## #9862 — config: `apply-groups-except H` is ignored when H is inherited through another group (`groups { G { apply-groups H; } }`) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## Defect

`apply-groups-except <name>` is honoured for a group applied **directly**, and ignored for one inherited **through another group**. Group expansion merges G's already-expanded body under the name `G`, so `nodesExcludeGroup(..., "G", ...)` never sees `apply-groups-except H`, and H's content is inherited anyway.

Measured at master `ad2ba883a` through `config.CompileConfigLenient`. Strict commit accepts every row below. The configuration shape is:

```junos
groups { H { security { zones { security-zone zgh; } } } G { apply-groups H; } }
apply-groups G;
security { zones { apply-groups-except H; <inline zone> } }
```

| Group H's zone | How H is applied | Inline zone | Compiled zones |
|---|---|---|---|
| `security-zone zgh;` | nested in G | `security-zone trust { }` | `[trust zgh]`: not excluded |
| `security-zone zgh { tcp-rst; }` | nested in G | `security-zone trust { }` | `[trust zgh]`: not excluded |
| `security-zone zgh;` | directly, `apply-groups H;` | `security-zone trust { }` | `[trust]`: excluded, correct |
| `security-zone zgh;` | directly | `security-zone trust;` | `[trust]`: excluded, correct |

The nested rows with a **leaf** inline zone (`security-zone trust;`) compiled `[trust]` at master, but not because the exclusion was honoured: the leaf branch's keyword-only override dropped the group's zone, which is #9831. Once that is repaired (the #9801/#9831 branch), the nested rows compile `[trust zgh]` in both inline spellings, matching the braced rows above.

## Cause

`expandGroupsRecursive` (`pkg/config/ast_groups.go`) expands G's own `apply-groups H` into G's cloned body **before** merging that body into the destination, and the outer `mergeNodes` call carries `group = "G"`. The destination's `apply-groups-except H` is therefore never matched. Nodes inherited from a nested group are tagged with that group's name only on the display path (`ExpandGroupsTagged`), not on the compile path, so the provenance a correct check needs is not there.

## Consequence

- Group content the operator explicitly excluded is inherited.
- When the excluded content carries a reserved zone name (`security-zone any;`), strict commit is refused, so the operator cannot suppress it by the documented means.

## Expected

`apply-groups-except H` excludes H's content wherever H is applied, directly or through another group, consistent with #9422.

Severity: Medium.

## #9872 — dataplane: a fabric interface with configured members but no local member gets its interface MTU planned by the wrong owner [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What happens

`planPhysDesired` excludes a fabric interface from the #9761 tagged-parent MTU plan by testing `LocalFabricMember == ""` alone (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:113`). That field is a DERIVED one, not the configured one. `compiler_derivations.go:129-141` sets it only when both hold:

- `cfg.Chassis.Cluster != nil`, and
- some member's `InterfaceSlot()` maps to this node's `NodeID` (slot 0 to node 0, slot 7 to node 1).

The CONFIGURED membership lives in `FabricMembers`, populated from `fabric-options member-interfaces` at `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:185`.

So a fabric interface whose members do not include one for this node — no chassis cluster configured, or members whose slots map to neither node — has `FabricMembers` non-empty and `LocalFabricMember` empty. The exception does not fire, and the planner writes the interface-level `mtu` onto `fab0` itself, a device whose MTU the fabric IPVLAN setup owns.

```
set chassis cluster node 0
set interfaces fab0 mtu 1400
set interfaces fab0 vlan-tagging
set interfaces fab0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-1/0/0
set interfaces fab0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-2/0/0
set interfaces fab0 unit 10 vlan-id 10
set security zones security-zone fabric interfaces fab0.10
```

Slots 1 and 2 map to neither node, so `LocalFabricMember` stays empty and the plan contains `fab0: mtu 1400`.

The same hole exists in the resolver: `resolveInterfaceRef` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:117`) also branches on `LocalFabricMember != ""`, so the reference resolves to `fab0` rather than to a member.

## Why it matters

Two components then write the same device's MTU, which is the class of alternating-state defect #8119/#8120 removed for the untagged path. It is a wrong write rather than a missing one.

## Fix

Exclude an interface with `len(FabricMembers) > 0` as well, in the planner and in the resolver, so the exception follows the CONFIGURED membership rather than the local-node derivation.

## Cells this needs

`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_tagged_parent_mtu_9761_test.go` has no row that builds real `FabricMembers` — the fabric rows inject `LocalFabricMember` directly, so the "fabric membership" claim in that file is currently tested only in its derived form. With the fix it wants:

- a compiled legacy/bond fabric config, members present, no local member;
- a remote-only fabric config on a configured cluster.


*(truncated — 47 lines total)*

## #9873 — dataplane: the lexical st<N> fallback resolves a configured tagged unit as a physical netdev, so its parent MTU is never planned [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What happens

`resolveInterfaceRef` has a lexical secure-tunnel fallback (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:103-114`): for a two-part reference whose base name looks like a secure tunnel, it returns immediately with

```go
physName = config.LinuxIfName(ref)   // "st10.5"
unitNum, _ = strconv.Atoi(parts[1])  // 5
// vlanID is left 0
```

It returns BEFORE the ordinary path that reads the configured unit's `vlan-id`. So for a configured, compiler-accepted interface:

```
set interfaces st10 mtu 1400
set interfaces st10 vlan-tagging
set interfaces st10 unit 5 vlan-id 100
set interfaces st10 unit 5 family inet mtu 1300
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces st10.5
```

the reference resolves as physical netdev `st10.5` with VLAN 0, not as unit 5 / VLAN 100 on parent `st10`.

## Why it matters now

Before #9761 this was a resolution oddity. Since #9761 the tagged branch is what plans a parent's interface-level `mtu`, and this reference never reaches it:

- `st10` gets no `mtu 1400` plan, though the config asks for one;
- the unit-level `mtu 1300` is planned onto a netdev named `st10.5`, which is not the VLAN child the rest of the config describes.

Both are silent.

## Scope, stated honestly

This predates #9761 — the fallback is unchanged by it, and the comment there marks the in-range `st<N>` PHYSICAL question as deliberately out of scope, pointing at #6737 (now closed, and about a different symptom: an in-range `st<N>` physical interface losing transit zone adjudication). What #9761 changed is the consequence: a missing parent MTU is now a real missing write rather than a no-op.

I have not established how reachable this is in practice. `st<N>` interfaces are XFRM secure-tunnel devices, and `vlan-tagging` with a unit `vlan-id` on one is accepted by the compiler but unusual; whether any real configuration does it is exactly the question a fix should answer first. Filing at LOW on that basis.

## Fix

When the exact reference is not secure-tunnel-owned (`SecureTunnelUnitNetdev` misses) but the base interface IS configured, fall through to ordinary configured-unit resolution before the lexical fallback, so a configured `vlan-id` is honoured. Keep the lexical fallback for a reference whose base is not configured, which is what it exists for.

## #9874 — config/nat: an authored-but-empty source-NAT `match` ships as an UNCONSTRAINED catch-all translator on the tolerant path — #8430 rejects it at commit and nothing poisons it on the wire [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

A boot or peer-sync installs a catch-all translator after only a warning: every flow the rule is probed for is source-translated, which breaks return-path identity and can defeat policy expectations built on NAT scope.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/nat_match_unconstrained_8430.go:46-114 (`natMatchIsConstrained`, and the `r.matchAuthored && !natMatchIsConstrained(r.Match)` tests at :96 and :107); pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_nat.go:112-121 (strict error vs tolerant warning); consumer side userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:1287 `rule.source_constrained = !snap.source_addresses.is_empty();` with the match at :1083-1088 — empty means match-anything.

## Contract

#8430 established that an authored-but-empty NAT `match` is a different thing from an omitted one and must not install a catch-all translator. Strict commit rejects it; the tolerant path must not ship an unconstrained rule without a fail-closed marker, which is the doctrine every sibling dimension follows (#3406/#6459/#6463).

## Reachability and actor

Protection: NAT is an enforcement surface — an unconstrained source-NAT rule translates every flow it is probed for. Actor: no network actor needed; the ingress is a persisted config written by an older build, an HA peer config sync, or a hand-edited DB, i.e. exactly what the tolerant path exists to ingest. Challenged: whether any snapshot-side poison exists. None does.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (coordinator) + EXECUTED (source report's P4 probe; all three lanes re-located the mechanism at the pin)
- `Probe`: No new execution (the Rust leg cannot be built on this host). The Go half is pinned by the source report's P4 probe and re-read at the pin by all three lanes.
- `Trace`: tolerant load/peer-sync -> compileNATSource (matchAuthored=true, empty match) -> warning only -> snapshot -> Rust source-NAT table with source_constrained=false -> every probed flow translated.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked for a NAT equivalent of the filter `LenientContentDropped` poison flag and for any snapshot-side rejection; there is none at the pin (`grep` over pkg/dataplane and userspace-dp for a NAT match-authored marker returns nothing). The strict path does reject, which bounds the ingress to the tolerant path.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Give the typed rule a poison marker when `matchAuthored && !natMatchIsConstrained`, carry it on the wire, and have the Rust table drop the rule closed (or skip it inert with a loud warning). Strict behavior unchanged. Acceptance: a leniently-loaded empty-match rule is inert or refused, and a populated rule is byte-identical.

## Deduplication

#8430 (CLOSED) owns the strict reject and is cited by the code; no open owner for the tolerant-path ship. Distinct from F-007 (partial match loss) and from F-004/F-005 (firewall filter dimension).

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.
- Origin run ID `review-work.7n9FuGPsdt`; report base SHA `3b24fe26e8356963893d151d4dedaa1aa27a7e48`. The report was `Mode: report-only, Filed: 0`, so this is the finding's FIRST filing.
- Finding ID(s): F-003 (source finding E04-04 (slice-E04.md)).
- Discovering model: `muse-spark-unknown` — family-only identity (the report's header records `WHOAMI: muse-spark-unknown` and exposes no exact model identifier). The report attributes the finding to the slice above; no separate slice-worker model identity is evidenced, so the discoverer stays the report's derived identity.

## #9875 — firewall: an unrepresentable or valueless `from` leaf widens the term on the tolerant path with no wire marker — every sibling match dimension got one, whole-leaf drops did not [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

An accept term over-permits and a discard term over-drops, with no operator-visible signal after the boot warning scrolls past — on exactly the path that exists to ingest configs the current build cannot fully represent.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:1217-1228 appends the dropped leaf name to `term.UnknownFrom`; pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:1319-1356 is the strict gate that rejects it at commit; pkg/config/schema_walk.go:380-388 records that Store.Load and Store.SyncApply downgrade schema violations to warnings; `grep -rn UnknownFrom pkg/dataplane/` (non-test) returns nothing, so no snapshot/helper marker exists.

## Contract

A `from` match leaf the dataplane cannot enforce must not widen the term. Every sibling dimension got a fail-closed wire marker (#3406/#6459/#6463, #9020, #3307); whole-leaf drops got a warning only.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: firewall-filter enforcement. Actor: no network actor — the ingress is the tolerant path (persisted config from an older build, HA peer sync). Challenged whether the grep-by-absence is blind: it is not. Positive control: `term.UnknownFrom` IS read outside pkg/config (pkg/routing/rules.go:1547 consults it for the #4422 PBR degradation), so the search can find consumers; it still finds none under pkg/dataplane.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (coordinator + three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's P2 probe)
- `Probe`: No new execution. Three independent lanes re-located the mechanism at the pin; the source report's P2 probe recorded `Protocols=["tcp"] UnknownFrom=["ttl"] Action="accept"` on the lenient path at its base.
- `Trace`: tolerant load -> compileFilterFrom drops the unrepresentable leaf, records UnknownFrom -> warning -> snapshot -> Rust filter term with the remaining (wider) match set.
- `Refutation attempt`: Searched for a snapshot-side `FromUnrepresentable`-style marker and for a Rust preflight that refuses a term carrying one; neither exists at the pin. The strict gate covers the operator path only.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Carry a `FromUnrepresentable` marker on the typed term and the wire, and fail the snapshot closed (or poison the term to match nothing) when set. Strict unchanged. Acceptance: a leniently-loaded term with non-empty UnknownFrom is inert/refused; representable terms byte-identical. This issue also covers F-005 (the valueless-`from` spelling), which Claude SMR independently judged a DUP of this one: same missing poison channel, same corrective scope.

## Deduplication

#3307 and #9020 (both CLOSED) fixed sibling dimensions with markers; #8480 (CLOSED) owns the valueless strict reject. No open owner for the filter from-leaf tolerant ship.

## #9876 — firewall: the #8480 valueless-`from` gate does not walk the braced `family { inet { filter ... } }` shape the compiler compiles, so a valueless prefix-list leaf commits strict-clean as match-ANY [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What is wrong

A `then discard` term over-drops every packet on that criterion, and a `then accept` term opens it, on a strict commit that reports success.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

Gate: pkg/config/compiler_firewall_valueless_from_8480.go:145-156 takes `fam.Children` as the filter level and requires `filt.Name() == "filter"`, with a special case only for the family-less spelling. Compiler: pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:201-215 compiles BOTH `family inet {…}` (len(Keys)>=2) and the nested `family { inet {…} }` (children are the AF nodes). Generic guard that partially covers it: pkg/config/schema_walk.go:691-706 (#8597) requires `missingArgs > 0`, which is false for the args-0 prefix-list leaves.

## Contract

A commit-time gate must enumerate the same AST shapes its compiler enumerates; otherwise a shape the compiler accepts escapes the gate (the #2419/#6526 doctrine).

## Reachability and actor

Protection: firewall-filter enforcement at the operator boundary. Actor: an operator or template loading a braced-nested `family { inet { ... } }` file (hand-authored or a `load merge` fragment). Flat `set` cannot produce that shape (`family` is compoundKey), which bounds reachability. Challenged: whether any generic gate covers it — the #8597 guard does, but only for leaves that declare an argument.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: EXECUTED (Claude SMR, through the real strict pipeline `configstore.CheckText` at the pin) + STATIC
- `Probe`: Claude SMR built a scratch Go module with a `replace` against the pinned worktree and drove `configstore.CheckText` (SchemaValidate-on-expanded-tree then strict compile) over 18 fixtures: `firewall { family { inet { filter F { term T { from { source-prefix-list; } then { discard; } } } } } }` returns CheckText=nil and compiles a match-ANY `discard` term, while the `protocol;` spelling is refused by #8597. No cargo was run.
- `Trace`: braced file -> hierarchical parser -> apply-groups expansion -> SchemaValidate (#8597 misses args-0 leaves) -> #8480 gate (skips the shape) -> compileFirewall (descends) -> match-ANY term.
- `Refutation attempt`: Codex's #8597 refutation was taken seriously and is correct for the argument-declaring leaves; the residual is exactly the two args-0 prefix-list leaves, measured.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Have the #8480 gate enumerate the shapes `compileFirewall` enumerates (share one walker), so gate and compiler cannot drift; keep the #8597 guard as the generic belt. Acceptance: the braced-nested prefix-list fixture strict-rejects naming the leaf; existing #8480 cells stay green.

## Deduplication

#8480 (CLOSED) is the gate's owner; #8597 (in base) is the generic guard. The residual shape has no owner. F-104's diagnostic bug lives in the same function and rides this fix.

#4313 built the closed-world keyword gate as opt-in; #8882 then armed the TOP-LEVEL stanza case and recorded that the deep case stays open deliberately. The subtree that decides enforcement is not among the 37 armed ones.

- `Refutation attempt`: #8882's fix (PR #8887) rejects unknown TOP-LEVEL stanzas; its own closing comment measures why the blanket deep rule was rejected. So the refutation 'this was already fixed' fails for this subtree, and the refutation 'arming it is unsafe' is about the ROOT, not about these two subtrees.

Arm `closedWorld` on `security policies` and `security zones` (narrow, not the root), or reject/warn naming the unknown token, and measure the shipped + example configs in the same change as #8882's closing comment did. ## #9879 — nat: a destination-NAT `off` exemption loses to a NARROWER later translate rule, so exempted traffic is translated — specificity-first precedence with no commit gate for the losing shape [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

Traffic an operator exempted from destination NAT is translated anyway when a narrower rule appears later in the rule-set, with a clean commit and no warning. The blast radius is the exempted flow class (typically a management or hairpin exclusion).

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs:706-789 — the cross-tier `.or_else` chain probes exact `(protocol, dst_ip, dst_port)`, then `dst_port: 0`, then `PROTO_ANY`, then the LPM prefix tier, and `:779-789` maps `Some(Exempt) | None => return None`. An `off` entry therefore short-circuits only the tiers probed AFTER it. userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs:842-848 states the precedence outright: across tiers this is MOST-SPECIFIC-WINS. userspace-dp/src/protocol/nat.rs:293-309 carries the exemption variant.

## Contract

`destination-nat rule ... then destination-nat off` is an exemption. Junos evaluates NAT rule-sets first-match-wins and stops; the snapshot promises that semantic for `off`. docs/vsrx-gaps.md:119 records that xpf uses implicit rather than explicit NAT ordering.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: NAT exemption — traffic an operator deliberately excluded from translation. Actor: none required; an ordinary configuration with a broad `off` and a narrower later translate. Prerequisite: both rules present in the same snapshot. Fail direction is OPEN (exempted traffic is translated).

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three independent lanes at the pin; the behaviour is stated verbatim in-source)
- `Probe`: No execution (the Rust leg cannot be built on this host). All three lanes independently located the chain and the precedence comment at the pin. The Go-side half — whether the compiler accepts the losing shape — is the unresolved part: no commit gate rejecting or warning about a broad-`off`-before-narrow-translate config was found.
- `Trace`: snapshot build -> DnatTable tiers -> per-packet probe exact -> wildcard-port -> proto-any -> LPM; an `off` in a broader tier is never consulted once a narrower tier hits.
- `Refutation attempt`: The strongest refutation is that this is documented as a deliberate, reviewed choice and that the same specificity order governs translate-vs-translate (#3164), so changing it for `off` alone would make `off` behave unlike every other DNAT rule. That establishes INTENT; it does not establish that the operator is told. There is no commit-time gate and no `NOT INSTALLED`-style annotation (#6534 shape) for the losing shape.
- `HPC/invariant check`: The tiered hash design is what buys O(1) per-packet DNAT lookup; any fix must not turn it into an ordered scan. That is the real constraint on the fix, and it argues for a commit-time gate rather than a dataplane reordering.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Preferred, given the HPC constraint: a commit-time gate that rejects or warns on a broad `off` whose space is re-entered by a narrower later translate, with the #6534 `NOT INSTALLED` annotation on `show`. Alternative: evaluate `off` in config order ahead of specificity (costlier). Acceptance: the losing shape is refused or annotated; a dataplane test names the precedence either way; translate-vs-translate specificity unchanged.

## Deduplication

#5145 and #4161 (both CLOSED) cover DNAT/source-NAT rule-set precedence generally; neither covers the `off` exemption losing to a narrower later translate, which is the fail-open direction. #3444 (CLOSED) is the accepted-but-dropped `to` scope.

## #9880 — config: the strict schema gate refuses every VALUED modifier on a generic typed leaf, so Junos NTP authentication (`key`/`version`/`routing-instance`) and `threshold action` cannot be committed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

A supported, security-relevant Junos configuration (NTP authentication keys) cannot be committed, and the diagnostic misnames the cause, so the operator is steered away from the feature rather than toward the fix.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/schema_system.go:192-207 declares the modifiers with `args: 1`. pkg/config/schema_walk.go:804-826 `validateModifierChild` is presence-only — 'A modifier is presence-only: it must be a known child keyword of the leaf, carry NO extra tokens in its Keys' — and returns `typedLeafErrorf(leafPath, "unknown modifier %q", node.Keys[1])` for any trailing token, never consulting the modifier's own `args`/`valueType`. pkg/config/schema_walk.go:1005-1012 routes generic typed leaves there. pkg/configstore/store.go:516-522 runs the schema gate BEFORE compile on every operator commit, so the reject is terminal; store.go:680 shows the lenient path compiling the same tree correctly.

## Contract

Valid Junos must commit. `ntp server <addr> key <n>` / `version <n>` / `routing-instance <ri>` and `threshold ... action <a>` are valued modifiers; the schema declares them with one argument each.

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial: an operator writing valid Junos NTP authentication cannot commit it. Consequence is integrity loss by workaround (operators drop NTP auth) or a strict/lenient-divergent persisted config. Actor: none.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's TestE03 probes at base)
- `Probe`: No new execution. The source report recorded `key 5`/`version 4`/`routing-instance foo`/`action accept` rejected strict and compiled lenient (`Key=5`), with `prefer` (genuinely presence-only) passing as the control. Three lanes re-located the mechanism at the pin; Claude SMR additionally checked for a `tailValidator` opt-out, a blockValue escape and the multi-value path, and found none.
- `Trace`: operator commit -> schemaValidateExpandedTreeForNode -> validateSingleValueLeafWithModifiers -> validateModifierChild -> reject with a misleading `unknown modifier` diagnostic.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked: `prefer` passes (correct, presence-only); the CoS heterogeneous-tail path has its own validator; the lenient path compiles it. None of these makes the strict path correct, and the existing tests use lenient-only compilation, which is why the suite stays green.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Teach `validateModifierChild` to validate a modifier's value against the modifier's own `args`/`valueType` instead of refusing every trailing token, so each valued modifier commits in both spellings with value validation and garbage is rejected naming the leaf. Acceptance: regression tests drive `SchemaValidate` (not lenient compile) for every valued modifier, plus the `prefer` presence-only control.

## Deduplication

#7132 (CLOSED) modelled per-value MODIFIER keywords in setSchema — this is the validator half that was not carried with it. #9156/#9157 (CLOSED) are untyped-leaf admission, a different failure direction.

## #9881 — config: an UNQUOTED leading-bracket as-path regex is lexed as list sugar and silently compiles to a different, still-valid POSIX regex — `[0-9]+` becomes `0-9 +` [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

A `then accept` term matches nothing and a `then reject` hijack filter rejects nothing, with a clean commit. Routing loss or an unenforced route filter, depending on the term.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/lexer.go:138-158 consumes `[`/`]` as list sugar; the #8453 mid-token rule at lexer.go:409-425 is gated on `bracketDepth == 0` and never fires on a LEADING bracket — 'Deliberately NOT fixed here: a LEADING \'[\' … is genuinely indistinguishable from a one-element list by any local rule'. pkg/config/aspath_regex.go:55-63,94-102 then compiles the joined tokens: `[0-9]+` becomes `0-9 +`, which is valid POSIX, so the strict gate at pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_routing.go:1515-1532 (which rejects invalid or empty reconstructions with a quoting diagnostic) does not fire.

## Contract

An as-path regex the operator authored must compile to that regex or be refused. The lexer's own comment states that a leading `[` 'still requires quoting'.

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial authoring fault with routing consequences. Actor: an operator writing a standard POSIX as-path regex without quotes. The mangled result is still valid POSIX, so the gate accepts it.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's TestE03 probe at base; Claude SMR measured the display rendering at the pin)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator. Claude SMR measured the display path at the pin: `show configuration` renders `as-path AP1 0-9 +;` and `display set` renders `set policy-options as-path AP1 0-9 +` — the MANGLED form, not the authored text. That REFUTES the report's '#6686 display-verified-but-wrong' framing and is the correct, narrower consequence.
- `Trace`: unquoted regex -> lexer list sugar -> joined tokens -> aspath_regex compile -> valid-but-different regex -> FRR as-path filter matching a different set.
- `Refutation attempt`: Two partial refutations were checked and recorded: the strict gate does catch invalid reconstructions (so the residual is exactly the ones that stay valid), and the display renders the mangled form (so the operator can in principle see it). Neither prevents the silent miscompile at commit.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Reject an unquoted leading-`[` as-path regex at strict commit with a 'quote the regex' diagnostic (the lexer comment already names quoting as the requirement), or reconstruct it faithfully. Acceptance: quoted and unquoted spellings are pinned against each other; the existing #8453 mid-token fixture stays green.

## Deduplication

#8453 (CLOSED) fixed the MID-token bracket case and its comment declares the leading case out of scope; #6523/#4097 (CLOSED) are FRR render-quoting, a different layer.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9882 — firewall: an unknown policer `then` token is dropped on every path and a lone `forwarding-class` commits as `discard`, contradicting #8445's own meter-only message [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What is wrong

A typo'd policer action silently becomes `discard` — an availability over-drop with zero diagnostic — and a Junos-correct lone `forwarding-class` drops traffic the operator asked to be marked and forwarded, while the product's own error text says it meters only.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:22-25 initialises `PolicerConfig{ThenAction: "discard"}`; :49-70 records `discard`/`loss-priority`/`forwarding-class` into `ThenActions` but only writes `ThenAction` for `discard`, and unknown tokens are ignored entirely (no UnknownActions channel, unlike filter terms #2399); :160-177 consumes it. pkg/config/schema_cos.go:480-484 advertises only `discard` and `loss-priority` and is not closed-world. pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:1960-1973 (#8445) rejects only discard+marking COMBINED and its own message calls lone `forwarding-class` meter-only. pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:788-790 maps the result to `DiscardExcess`.

## Contract

Junos policer `then forwarding-class <fc>` marks and forwards; `then discard` drops. A policer `then` token the compiler does not understand must not silently select the most destructive action, and #8445's own diagnostic calls lone `forwarding-class` a meter-only supported spelling.

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial: an operator typo (`discrad`) or a valid lone `forwarding-class`. Both commit clean on EVERY path including strict. Fail direction for the typo is closed with respect to the rate limit but sharply over-drops versus intent.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's R1/S2 probes at base; Claude SMR re-measured both halves at the pin through the real strict pipeline)
- `Probe`: Claude SMR re-measured both halves at the pin via a scratch Go module driving the real strict pipeline: a policer `then { foo; }` commits clean with `ThenAction="discard"`, and a lone `forwarding-class` commits as `discard` — contradicting the #8445 message's own 'METERS ONLY' remedy text. No cargo was run.
- `Trace`: policer `then` -> unknown token ignored / lone forwarding-class recorded but not acted on -> ThenAction stays "discard" -> snapshot DiscardExcess=true -> excess traffic dropped.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked #8445's gate and the snapshot mapping: neither the unknown token nor the lone `forwarding-class` prevents `DiscardExcess`. The 'fail-closed is safer' argument is recorded, but it contradicts the project's own message and Junos semantics, so it is not a refutation of the claim.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Record unknown policer `then` tokens (mirroring filter terms' UnknownActions) and reject them at strict commit / warn on the tolerant path; give lone `forwarding-class` Junos mark-and-forward semantics or refuse it explicitly, so #8445's message and the behaviour agree. Acceptance: a cell per spelling (typo, lone FC, lone LP, discard+FC) pinning commit outcome AND the compiled ThenAction.

## Deduplication

#8445 (CLOSED) owns the discard+marking combination; #2399 (CLOSED) is the filter-term UnknownActions channel this path never got; #9503 (CLOSED) is the three-colour policer loss-priority case.

## #9883 — firewall: a braced filter under an UNKNOWN address family folds into the IPv4 pool while the #9017 warning tells the operator it compiles to NOTHING [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What is wrong

An operator who reads the warning believes the filter is inert and leaves it in place; IPv4 traffic is being filtered by a rule they think does nothing. Whichever way the operator acts on that belief is wrong.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:245-251 — `dests := []map[string]*FirewallFilter{fw.FiltersInet}` with a switch that special-cases only `inet6` and `any`, so every other token lands in the IPv4 pool. pkg/config/compiler_firewall_family_9017.go:91-95 emits the message 'the filter under it compiles to NOTHING' and :99 rejects on the strict path. The two statements contradict each other on the hierarchical route.

## Contract

A filter under an unknown address family must either be refused or be installed where the operator is told it is installed. #9017 chose refusal on the strict path and a warning on the tolerant path.

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial: an operator typo in a braced config, or a tolerant-path load of one. The consequence is an INVERTED diagnostic: the operator is told the filter compiles to nothing while the IPv4 pool enforces it.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin; Claude SMR established which ingress route the mechanism is reachable on)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator; the source report's P6 probe recorded `inInet=true inInet6=false` with the NOTHING warning at base, and Claude SMR re-derived the reachable route at the pin.
- `Trace`: braced `firewall family <typo> filter F` -> tolerant compile -> default-fold into FiltersInet -> V4 enforcement, while the warning says NOTHING is installed.
- `Refutation attempt`: Strict commit rejects the token (#9017), which bounds the ingress to the tolerant path; and a V6 hook cannot forward unfiltered because the snapshot refuses the dangling reference. Neither addresses the inverted warning on the V4 side.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Either quarantine an unknown-family filter out of BOTH pools on the tolerant path (making the existing message true), or change the message to state the actual V4-only installation. Acceptance: a cell per route (flat-set and braced) asserting the message and the pool membership agree.

## Deduplication

#9017 (CLOSED) owns the strict reject and the message; #3884 is the pre-existing default-fold. No owner for the message/behaviour contradiction on the braced route.

## #9884 — configstore: a Load whose active tree fails to compile skips pending-confirm recovery entirely, so a node sits with no policy AND a stranded commit-confirmed record [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

The node comes up with no compiled policy AND a stranded rollback opportunity: the recovery that exists to restore the last good configuration is skipped precisely when it is needed.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:82-108 — `compiled, err := s.compileTreeLenient(tree); if err != nil { ... s.active = tree; s.loadRollbackHistory(); return fmt.Errorf("compile config: %w: %w", ErrConfigCompile, err) }` — an unconditional return. `recoverPendingConfirmLocked()` is reached only on the success path at :111-118.

## Contract

A pending `commit confirmed` must be resolved at boot — expired records roll back, live ones re-arm — so a node cannot be left enforcing an unconfirmed configuration with no timer.

## Reachability and actor

No attacker. A previously committed config that stops compiling (a deleted group, a tightened validator) plus a pending confirm window is enough. Availability, not confidentiality.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's probe at base: Load -> ErrConfigCompile with the expired confirm.json still on disk)
- `Probe`: No new execution. All three lanes confirmed the early return terminates Load before recovery; Codex also established the consequence chain into bootstrap/lifeline mode (pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:285, pkg/daemon/daemon_run_bringup.go:381).
- `Trace`: boot -> Load -> lenient compile fails -> early return -> confirm recovery never runs -> the record stays on disk with no in-memory timer -> indefinite safe state.
- `Refutation attempt`: Claude SMR recorded the partial self-limit: after the operator fixes the config and commits, the NEXT boot's Load succeeds and recovery runs. That bounds the duration to 'until the next successful boot', not to 'until an operator notices', but the window is exactly the one where the node is already in a degraded state.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Run confirm recovery on the compile-failure path too (expired -> roll back and persist; live -> re-arm or surface), or document-and-journal the drop and remove the record. Acceptance: cells pin both arms of a compile-failing Load with an expired and with a live confirm record.

## Deduplication

#9615 (CLOSED) covers a confirm window re-armed at boot skipping the #6707 rollback — adjacent leg, different path (that one is the success path). #9058 (CLOSED) is the WriteConfirm-failure leg.

## Review origin

## #9885 — networkd: a leading-dash interface name commits strict-clean and poisons the whole `networkctl reconfigure` batch — `--help` exits 0, applies nothing, and clears the retry debt [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

One badly named interface silently disarms the whole batch apply: every interface in that invocation is left unconfigured while the commit reports success and the retry debt is cleared.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/validate_interface_name.go:58-66 `interfaceNameAllowed` admits `-` at any position, and :76 is wired as the `interfaces` wildcard keyValidator (pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:46). pkg/networkd/networkd.go:560-576 builds `["reconfigure", names...]` with no `--` separator.

## Contract

An interface name that reaches an argv position must not be interpretable as an option. The repo already applies the `--` belt for scp (#4589).

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial authoring/operator fault with an availability consequence. Actor: whoever writes the config. `--help`/`--version` exit 0 WITHOUT acting, which is what makes it silent; `-x` would fail noisily.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's probes at base: strict commit of `interfaces --help` accepted; argv without `--`; `networkctl reconfigure --help` exits 0)
- `Probe`: No new execution. Claude SMR additionally bounded the route: the physical-interface path requires `physIface != nil` (pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1259) and xpf's own naming never produces a leading dash, so the reachable route is the netdev-creating one.
- `Trace`: committed name `--help` -> networkd apply -> one shared `networkctl reconfigure` argv -> networkctl prints help and exits 0 -> no interface reconfigured, retry debt cleared, commit reports success.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked the render belt (`confinedInterfaceName`, networkd.go:1009-1013) — it rejects only empty/slash/NUL — and the strict validator — it rejects whitespace and globs but not a leading dash. Neither stops this.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Put `--` ahead of the operands in the reconfigure argv (and the `ip link set` sibling), and reject a leading-dash interface name at commit-check. Acceptance: a stubbed-seam unit test asserts `--` in the argv; a commit-check cell refuses `interfaces --help`.

## Deduplication

#4589 (CLOSED) established the `--` belt for scp; this is the networkctl/ip sibling. No open owner.

## #9886 — networkd: no render-side refusal for an interface name that is not exactly one `[Match]` pattern — the repo argues refusal is the only safe posture and wrote the predicate, but never calls it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

If such a name is ever ingested, one unit claims devices it must not and the intended device gets none — and the project has already concluded in-source that no substitution is safe here, so the absence of the refusal is the defect.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/config/freetext.go:83-95 `sanitizeControlChars` replaces each control byte with a SPACE; :324-330 `sanitizeNodesControlCharsAt` rewrites EVERY key including identity keys, armed on the lenient compile only (pkg/config/compiler_prewalk.go:33-42). Sink with no belt: pkg/networkd/networkd.go:817-818 `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Name=%s\n", ifc.Name)`; `confinedInterfaceName` (:1009-1013) checks only empty/slash/NUL. The predicate that would express the refusal already exists and has NO production caller: pkg/config/validate_interface_name.go:110-112 `interfaceNameRendersAsOnePattern`.

## Contract

`pkg/config/validate_interface_name.go:18-27` and `pkg/networkd/networkd.go:722-730` state the rule in the repo's own words: a sanitizer whose replacement character is the sink's SEPARATOR manufactures a second pattern out of one, which is strictly worse than rendering raw — so the renderer must REFUSE a name that is not exactly one pattern.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: none established. The ingress would be a persisted or peer-synced identity key containing a control byte. The consequence if it occurs: a `.network`/`.link` unit whose `[Match] Name=` is a whitespace-separated list claiming devices other than the intended one, and the intended device left with no unit.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (Claude SMR measured the lenient compile at the pin: compiled name `"ge 0"`, two whitespace-separated fields, warning only)
- `Probe`: Claude SMR, at the pin: `interfaces { "ge\n0" { unit 0 { family inet { address 10.0.0.1/24; } } } }` — strict SchemaValidate REJECTS with the message that names this exact hazard; `CompileConfigLenient` yields the compiled name `"ge 0"` (`len(strings.Fields()) == 2`) with only a #1798 sanitize warning. Render path read, not run.
- `Trace`: tolerant ingest -> sanitize-in-place rewrites the identity key to `ge 0` -> networkd renders `[Match] Name=ge 0` raw -> systemd reads two globs.
- `Refutation attempt`: Recorded in full above: the ordering claim fails, and reachability is unestablished. What survives refutation is that the repo argues refusal is the only safe posture, wrote the predicate for it, and never called it.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Take Claude SMR's acceptance route and skip the reachability question: make `generateLink`/`generateNetDev`/`generateNetwork` return an error and write no file when `len(strings.Fields(name)) != 1`, reusing the existing `interfaceNameRendersAsOnePattern` predicate; additionally re-run `ValidateInterfaceName` as a HARD error for identity keys on the lenient path. Acceptance: a unit test per generator asserting refusal + no file written.

## Deduplication

#6834 (CLOSED) named the 'strictly worse than rendering raw' rule that this render path still does not implement; #6833 (CLOSED) is the shared-sanitizer shape issue. Distinct from F-048 (argv quoting), per Claude SMR's explicit not-DUP finding.

## #9887 — configstore: a plain commit does not clear the #8566 confirm-read-failure flag, so /health stays 503 after the window it describes has been superseded [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

An operator sees a node reporting unhealthy indefinitely after they have already fixed it, with no action available except a `commit confirmed` they have no reason to run.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:178-187 sets `s.confirmRecoveryReadFailed = true` and returns nil so Load SUCCEEDS. It is cleared in exactly two places: pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:688 (`writeConfirmState`, reached only by a NEW `commit confirmed`) and :789 (tombstone removal). pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:946-950 `clearPendingConfirmLocked` returns early when `cancelPendingConfirmTimerLocked` reports nothing to cancel — which is the case here, because no timer was ever armed.

## Contract

A health degradation must clear when the condition that raised it is superseded. #8566's flag says 'an unconfirmed config stands with no timer'; a later plain commit makes that false.

## Reachability and actor

No attacker — a corrupt/unreadable confirm record at boot. Operator-visible availability signal, not data loss.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's probe at base: corrupt confirm.json -> Load ok + flag true -> commit ok, flag still true)
- `Probe`: No new execution; three lanes traced the clear sites at the pin.
- `Trace`: boot with unreadable confirm.json -> flag set, Load succeeds -> /health 503 + gauge asserted -> plain commit promotes a new tree -> flag still set -> 503 persists until a future `commit confirmed`.
- `Refutation attempt`: Claude SMR recorded the defensible reading: the unreadable record is still on disk, so a real removal debt persists and the next boot re-sets the flag anyway. That argues for clearing the debt, not for keeping a stale 503 after the window has been superseded.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Low** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Any commit or sync that supersedes the lost window clears `confirmRecoveryReadFailed`, best-effort removing the unreadable record and retaining removal debt on failure. Acceptance: cells pin plain-commit and sync clearing.

## Deduplication

#8566 (the flag's owner) and #9058 (CLOSED, the WriteConfirm leg). Distinct from F-039 (recovery skipped on compile-fail Load): different site, different fix.

## #9888 — userspace-xdp: a DOUBLE-TAGGED frame is XDP_PASSed to the kernel unadjudicated, and on a bridged port the kernel forwards it with no zone policy — the transit barrier is removed while armed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

An L2-adjacent sender can move frames across a bridged xpf topology without zone policy, screens or session accounting, by adding a second VLAN tag — no configuration on the firewall required. Independently, a load-bearing in-source contract statement is false, which is how the next reader concludes this path is already closed.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

Shim: userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1453-1461 unwraps exactly ONE tag (`if`, not `while`) and recognizes only 0x8100/0x88a8 (lib.rs:17-18); lib.rs:484-486 returns `pass_non_ip_l2_direct()` for any other ethertype and lib.rs:1289-1294 is `XDP_PASS`. That test sits ABOVE the ingress-ifindex gate (lib.rs:524), so it is total. Armed kernel path: pkg/nftables/transit_barrier.go:25-39 — the forward-hook DROP is scoped 'STRICTLY TO THE UNARMED WINDOW' because 'Several ARMED paths deliberately rely on the kernel forward path being OPEN and UNFILTERED'; the same comment records that `ip_forward` does not govern bridged frames at all and that this repo creates Linux bridge domains. Bridge members are created and bound in pkg/networkd/networkd.go:72-73,776,860 / pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go. Live stale contract statement: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/parser.rs:62-63 asserts 'the upstream XDP shim drops double-tagged frames before they reach userspace' — false at the pin; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/README.md:376-378 corrected exactly that sentence for its own copy and this one was not updated.

## Contract

Every transit frame on a bound interface is adjudicated by the userspace dataplane (zone policy, screens, session accounting). An XDP_PASS is a handoff to the kernel, and while the dataplane is ARMED the kernel forward path is deliberately open and unfiltered.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: zone-policy enforcement on transit. Actor: any L2-adjacent sender — it needs no configuration on the firewall, only a frame. Prerequisite for the established shape: a bridged topology (bridge domains are a shipped feature). Challenged assumptions: (1) 'the commit gate blocks this' — it blocks the CONFIG, not the frame; (2) 'ip_forward/nft barrier closes it' — the barrier is installed only while UNARMED, by design.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes + coordinator at the pin; two kernel-behaviour steps are inference, marked below)
- `Probe`: No execution (no lab; frame injection is out of scope). The repo-side chain is read at the pin by three lanes and re-verified by the coordinator. The two kernel steps — a bridge forwarding by MAC irrespective of ethertype, and the vid-0 inner-tag path reaching ip_forward — are reasoning about Linux behaviour, not measurements, and bound the confidence to Medium.
- `Trace`: double-tagged or 0x9100 frame -> shim parse_l2 (one unwrap) -> non-IP ethertype -> XDP_PASS -> kernel; on a bridged port the bridge forwards it between members with no xpf adjudication and no bridge-family barrier (removed while armed).
- `Refutation attempt`: Retained in full: 0x9100 frames are dropped by the kernel (`eth_type_vlan()` covers only 0x8100/0x88A8, no packet_type handler) and a double tag with inner vid != 0 finds no vlan netdev and is discarded by ip_rcv as PACKET_OTHERHOST. Those shapes are blind-but-not-forwarded. The residual is the bridged port, plus the vid-0 routed shape.
- `HPC/invariant check`: The single-unwrap `if` is deliberate for BPF verifier cost; a loop-unwrap needs a documented bound. That is a constraint on the fix, not a defence.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Decide and implement the shim's fate for a frame whose inner ethertype is still a VLAN TPID (loop-unwrap with a documented bound and correct l3_offset/VLAN identity, or an explicit DROP with a counter) rather than a silent XDP_PASS; and correct parser.rs:62-63 in the same change. Acceptance: a double-tagged frame on a bound bridged port is either adjudicated or dropped-and-counted, never handed to the kernel; the l2-offset canary is extended to the double-tag shape; no single-tag behaviour changes.

## Deduplication

#2354 (CLOSED) is the QinQ TRANSIT FEATURE request and #5879 (CLOSED) is the commit-time honesty gate — neither is the unadjudicated-handoff defect, and the gate's own rationale assumes the handoff is harmless. #9522 and #9506 (both OPEN) are the same 'delegated to the kernel with no adjudication' class at different sites (learned-route cap, route-based-VPN ingress), which is corroboration that the class is accepted as real, not a duplicate of this site.

## #9889 — grpcapi: ShowCompare is priced PermView and diffs against the CANDIDATE, so a view-only caller reads another session's uncommitted configuration — on BOTH the rollback_n=0 and rollback_n>0 arms [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

A view-only account reads an administrator's in-progress configuration change before it is committed: planned ACL changes, new addresses and zones, staged NAT, and the shape of the next maintenance — everything except the redacted secrets.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/grpcapi/authz_methods.go:87 prices `"ShowCompare": config.PermView`. pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_target_9324.go:47-67 `configTargetReadPermission` switches on `"ShowConfig"` ONLY, so the stricter target gate never fires for ShowCompare. pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:401-418: `RollbackN == 0` returns `s.store.ShowCompareRedacted()`, which is `config.FormatCompare(forDisplay(s.active), forDisplay(s.candidate))` (pkg/configstore/store_format.go:448-459).

## Contract

#9324 established the rule: reading a CANDIDATE configuration is a configure-mode activity and must cost `PermConfig`; a class without `configure` cannot get there. The REST twin agrees on the price.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: confidentiality of another session's uncommitted candidate. Actor: any authenticated principal holding only `view` — including read-only shell accounts. Prerequisite: another session is in configure mode with a candidate (otherwise the handler returns empty). Secrets are redacted, so this is reconnaissance, not credential theft.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (coordinator at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's loopback-listener probe at base: ShowConfig as read-only -> PermissionDenied control; ShowCompare{rollback_n:0} -> OK with the uncommitted canary)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator; the mechanism was read at the pin and independently located by all three lanes. The source report's probe used a real loopback gRPC listener with a read-only principal and a staged canary.
- `Trace`: view-only principal -> interceptor prices ShowCompare at PermView -> target gate skips it -> handler diffs active vs candidate -> candidate content returned.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked whether the method-table completeness guard covers this property: it proves every method HAS a price, not that every candidate read is priced, so it is vacuous here — the same vacuity #9324 was filed about for a different RPC.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

**Coordinator correction to the report's acceptance criterion, which is insufficient.** The report asks for `rollback_n == 0` at PermConfig with `> 0` left at PermView. But `ShowCompareRollbackRedacted` (pkg/configstore/store_format.go:461-470) also diffs the chosen rollback slot **against the candidate** — its own doc says so — so the `> 0` path discloses candidate content too. Price the WHOLE RPC at PermConfig (or make the `>0` path diff against the active tree). Acceptance: a view-only principal is denied on BOTH arms with a staged candidate present; a configure-class principal still gets both; the completeness census is rewritten to enumerate candidate-READING RPCs from handler behaviour rather than from the price table.

## Deduplication

#9324 (CLOSED) priced ShowConfig's target and did not reach this sibling RPC; this is its residual. #5812 and #9119 are unrelated configure-mode legs.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9890 — api: the deny-configuration regex gate enumerates only `set` and `delete`, so a restricted principal can deactivate, activate or annotate a DENIED path over REST [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

A deny-configuration restriction is bypassable by choosing a different verb on the same path — and the verb that bypasses it can disable enforcement rather than merely edit it.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:46-49 — `restConfigMutationRoutes` contains exactly `POST /api/v1/config/set` and `POST /api/v1/config/delete`; the surrounding comment explains only why `load`, `commit` and `rollback` are absent. Registered and candidate-mutating at the pin: pkg/api/server.go:799 `POST /api/v1/config/deactivate` -> `configDeactivateHandler` (pkg/api/config.go:181-199, `DeactivateFromInputAs`); server.go:800 activate -> (config.go:203-221, `ActivateFromInputAs`); server.go:813 annotate -> (config.go:616-645, `AnnotateAs`, path parsed from `{"path"}` not `{"input"}`).

## Contract

`deny-configuration` regexes are an authorization control over configuration mutation. The CLI/oracle model evaluates all path-carrying verbs; the REST surface must match it.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: the deny-configuration boundary for a `configure`-class principal restricted by regex. Actor: that authenticated, restricted operator. `deactivate` is the sharp one: inactive nodes are excluded from compilation, so deactivating a denied subtree REMOVES its enforcement, and a later legitimate commit by anyone ships the change.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (coordinator at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's probe at base: denied `set` -> 403 control; deactivate/activate/annotate on the same denied path -> 200)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator; three lanes located all three routes at the pin.
- `Trace`: restricted principal -> POST /api/v1/config/deactivate -> route not in the gate's map -> no regex evaluation -> candidate mutated on a denied path.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked whether the generic REST mutation gate or the candidate-ownership check covers it: they require `PermConfig` and candidate ownership, neither of which is the regex control. No other evaluation point exists on these routes.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Evaluate all five path-carrying REST routes against `AuthorizeConfigMutation` with the applied verb, parsing `annotate`'s path from `{"path"}`. Acceptance: a denied path returns 403 on all five; a completeness test derives the gated route set from handler behaviour (which mutate the candidate with a caller-supplied path) rather than from a hand-maintained map.

## Deduplication

#9154 (CLOSED) is the owner of the regex evaluation and stated `load`'s absence; it did not enumerate deactivate/activate/annotate. F-053 (the `load` verb) is a DIFFERENT corrective scope — content path-matching rather than route enumeration — and is filed separately.

## #9891 — grpcapi: MonitorInterface is the one monitor stream with no subscriber budget and no send deadline — it degrades under subscriber pressure instead of refusing [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What is wrong

The one uncapped monitor stream degrades the whole management surface under subscriber pressure instead of refusing, and a slow consumer parks a goroutine indefinitely.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:405-570 — no admission call of any kind: `ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)` (:504-506), an unbounded `for` loop, per-interface counter reads each tick (:545), and a blocking `stream.Send(resp)` (:560) with no deadline and no TrySubscribe/limiter. `git log 3b24fe26e8..HEAD -- pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go` is empty, so nothing changed since the claim's base.

## Contract

Every sibling monitor stream on this server caps its subscribers; MonitorInterface is the one that does not. A server under subscriber pressure should refuse with ResourceExhausted rather than degrade.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: any `PermView` holder, including a read-only shell account, plus fabric-segment hosts while dual-accept admits them (MonitorInterface is on the fabric allowlist). Prerequisite: authenticated access to the management surface. Blast radius is the management/telemetry surface, not forwarding.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin; the absence of any admission bound is proven, the degradation magnitude is NOT measured) + EXECUTED (source report's 400-stream probe at base: 287-329 admitted, 0 refused, against siblings that cap at 256/128)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator. The three lanes bounded the claim: `grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams(256)` (pkg/grpcapi/server.go:59) caps streams per CONNECTION but nothing caps connections; the #5707 `monitorStatusCache` (pkg/grpcapi/monitor_status_cache.go:49) coalesces dataplane Status() reads within a 1s TTL, so the per-tick cost is lower than the claim assumes; proxying is one hop.
- `Trace`: N connections x 256 streams -> N*256 goroutines + tickers -> per-tick counter reads -> blocking Send with no deadline; a slow consumer holds its goroutine.
- `Refutation attempt`: Recorded above and it genuinely narrows the claim's cost model — but none of it is an ADMISSION bound, which is what the siblings have and what the server needs to refuse rather than degrade.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Per-subscriber cost at the pin is one goroutine + one 1s ticker + cached status reads; the unbounded dimension is subscriber COUNT, not per-tick work. No measured throughput or latency degradation is claimed.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Give MonitorInterface a bounded subscriber budget sized like MonitorPacketDrop's and refuse past it with ResourceExhausted; add a send deadline or flow-control bound for slow consumers. Acceptance: a regression test asserts refusal past the cap AND continued service for admitted subscribers.

## Deduplication

The sibling caps this one is missing were added by earlier issues on MonitorPacketDrop and the other diag streams; no open owner covers MonitorInterface.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9892 — authz: the `load` verb still bypasses deny-configuration regexes on the REST and CLI surfaces (#9633 fixed the gRPC third before the pin) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

The regex control is bypassable on two of three surfaces by the one verb that can carry every denied path at once, and the gRPC fix shows the content-matching mechanism already exists and can be reused.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

FIXED third: pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:45-47 now delegates to `authorizeRPCLoadAndRollback` (pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_rpc_9633.go:62-95), which evaluates `load set`/`load merge` content line-by-line through `config.AuthorizeConfigMutation` and refuses `load override` for restricted classes. Remaining surfaces at the pin: pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:41-45 still records `load` as deliberately ABSENT, and pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:68-80 carries the shared evaluator's whole-verb exception for the CLI path.

## Contract

A regex-restricted principal's denied paths must be denied whatever verb carries them. `load` replaces or merges whole configuration content, so it is strictly more powerful than the per-path verbs.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: an authenticated `configure`-class principal restricted by deny-configuration regexes. `load override` replaces the entire candidate; `load merge` can carry the whole denied subtree in one call (up to 16 MiB on REST).

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin, all three independently finding the same partial fix)

## #9893 — userspace-dp: NDP neighbor learning parses a Neighbor Advertisement out of a NON-FIRST IPv6 FRAGMENT (RFC 6980 §5 says MUST discard) and never validates the IPv6 source [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

An L2-adjacent sender can steer a neighbor entry — and therefore the next-hop MAC for forwarded traffic — by shaping a single non-first fragment, bypassing the kernel-diversion path that would otherwise apply the kernel's own RFC 6980 handling.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

userspace-dp/src/afxdp/parser.rs:210-246 resolves the NA through the shared walk `frame::packet_rel_l4_offset_and_protocol(l3_slice, AF_INET6)`; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:222-265 `walk_ipv6_ext_chain` traverses Fragment (44) as a traversable type — its own contract says it walks 'even past a Fragment header' (inspect.rs:144). No Fragment-header refusal exists on the NDP learn path. Source validation: parser.rs:261,264,269 check hop-limit 255, code 0, non-multicast target and checksum — but NOT that the IPv6 SOURCE is a valid on-link unicast. Override=0 handling is a read-then-insert re-lock in userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:289-296.

## Contract

RFC 6980 §5: 'IPv6 Neighbor Discovery [RFC4861] messages MUST NOT be fragmented. A node MUST discard any Neighbor Discovery messages that contain a Fragment header.' RFC 4861 additionally requires a valid on-link unicast source for NA processing.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: the neighbor table that decides the forwarding next-hop MAC. Actor: an L2-adjacent sender; no credentials. Reachability (Claude SMR): the shim normally DIVERTS NDP to the kernel (userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:694-699 returns early for ICMPv6 types 133-137), so the userspace learner is not normally reached — but a NON-FIRST IPv6 fragment is deliberately sent to AF_XDP as a flowless session miss (lib.rs:1581,1605), and the userspace walk then continues PAST the Fragment header to a terminal 'L4', so attacker-shaped payload in a non-first fragment is parsed as an NA-136 with an attacker TLLA. The ICMPv6 checksum is computable by the sender.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin; RFC 6980 consulted as the primary source)
- `Probe`: No execution (no frame injection, no Rust build). Three lanes read the chain at the pin; the learnability gates (`neighbor_mac_is_learnable`, `neighbor_ip_is_learnable`, `owns_configured_ip`, poll_stages.rs:279-281) were checked and do bound the target set without covering the fragment or source-validity questions.
- `Trace`: non-first IPv6 fragment -> shim flowless miss -> AF_XDP -> parse_ndp_neighbor_advert -> ext walk past Fragment -> NA accepted -> neighbor entry replaced with the attacker's TLLA.
- `Refutation attempt`: The strongest refutation found is partial and is recorded: hop-limit 255 bounds the sender to the local link, and the learnability gates refuse unspecified/loopback/multicast targets and unlearnable MACs. Neither implements the RFC 6980 MUST, and neither validates the source address.
- `HPC/invariant check`: The Override=0 read-then-insert re-lock is an admitted best-effort TOCTOU; an atomic compare-and-swap under the shard lock is the cheap fix and costs nothing on the normal path.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Refuse an NDP learn when any Fragment header is sighted on the chain (the RFC 6980 MUST), require a valid on-link unicast IPv6 source, and make the Override=0 replace an atomic compare-and-swap under the shard lock. Acceptance: a fragmented NA is dropped and counted; a legitimate unfragmented NA still learns; a regression test drives the Override=0 interleave.

## Deduplication

#2368 (CLOSED) added RFC 4861 validity checks (hop-limit/code/checksum) to NA learning and #2369 (CLOSED) the ARP sibling; neither added the RFC 6980 fragment refusal or source validation, so this is their residual. #2150 (CLOSED) unified the parsers.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9894 — userspace-dp: the TCP/UDP metadata fast path admits a 5-tuple read from out-of-datagram SLACK bytes — the declared-length bound the frame README calls closed is not applied there [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What is wrong

Sessions, NAT bindings, policy decisions, flow-cache entries and flow logs are created for a 5-tuple that never existed on the wire, which both corrupts the audit record and gives an attacker a handle for screen evasion.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:1327-1332 — the TCP/UDP fast path returns the shim's metadata tuple verbatim when `metadata_tuple_complete(meta, meta_flow)` holds, and that predicate (inspect.rs:880-932) carries NO length dimension. The shim's own parse bounds L4 reads by the frame end including slack (userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1881-1962) and never reads IPv4 total-length (lib.rs:1475-1484). The ordinary (non-fast) parser DOES apply the declared-end guard (inspect.rs:966, :1094), and the ICMP metadata arm has an explicit declared-end check — so the fast path is the one site that skips it.

## Contract

The frame module's README states the invariant as CLOSED: 'L4 ports are bounded by the IP-DECLARED packet length (#2361) … The 4 port bytes MUST lie inside the declared end.' The ICMP metadata path implements exactly that check.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: session/admission/audit integrity. Actor: any sender that can reach a bound interface; it needs only a short `total_len` with chosen trailing bytes. Forwarded bytes are trimmed elsewhere, so the consequence is state and audit integrity plus screen-evasion leverage, not wrong-port delivery.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (source report's probe at base: the production path returned the slack tuple (1111,443) while the declared-end parse returned None)
- `Probe`: No new execution by the coordinator. All three lanes independently found no length test on the admission path; Codex and Claude SMR each enumerated the guards they checked (`metadata_tuple_complete`, `frame_is_non_first_fragment`, `classify_metadata`, `try_parse_metadata`, the #5150 declared-length helper).
- `Trace`: short total_len + chosen slack -> shim parse_l4 reads the slack bytes as ports -> metadata tuple -> fast path returns it verbatim -> session, policy, NAT, flow cache and logs all seeded on the phantom tuple.
- `Refutation attempt`: Non-first fragments are rejected before the fast return and ICMP has its own gate; neither covers TCP/UDP. No admission-path length guard exists.
- `HPC/invariant check`: The fast path exists to avoid a re-parse on the hot path; the fix is one comparison against the declared end, not a re-parse, so the cost argument does not defend the gap.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Accept the metadata tuple only when `[l4, l4+4)` lies within the IP-declared end — the same test the ICMP arm and the ordinary parser already apply. Acceptance: the probe frame resolves flowless; parity/property tests stay green.

## Deduplication

#2361 (CLOSED) established the declared-length bound and the README claims it closed; #5150/#6748 are adjacent slack/trailer fixes at other sites. This is the metadata fast path's residual.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9895 — userspace-dp: the reverse session lookup's pass-2 fallback admits a reply from ANOTHER non-zero routing domain, so a zone-matching tenant-B reply lands in tenant A's flow [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

A tenant's reply stream can be injected into another tenant's flow where the address space overlaps and the zones line up — the reverse-direction counterpart of the forward collision #7160 addressed.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:326-341 — pass 2 keeps the first validating candidate from ANOTHER routing domain as a fallback and returns it when no same-domain candidate exists: `if record.key.routing_domain == reply_key.routing_domain { return Some(matched); } if fallback.is_none() { fallback = Some(matched); }`. The reverse index is keyed with `routing_domain = 0` (userspace-dp/src/session/key.rs:127-133), and the validation compares the domain-neutral reverse tuple (key.rs:127-155). No check refuses the fallback when both domains are non-zero and different.

## Contract

Two routing instances are isolation domains. A reply must not be matched against a session belonging to a different non-zero domain.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: cross-tenant isolation on the reverse path. Actor: a server-side or spoofing sender in tenant B whose reverse tuple collides with tenant A's flow AND whose arrival zone matches A's egress zone. Prerequisite: overlapping address space across two non-zero domains — a supported multi-VRF CGNAT posture.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin)
- `Probe`: No execution (Rust build prohibited here; the two-domain collision cell is the decisive check and is named below).
- `Trace`: tenant B reply -> pass 1 finds no same-domain candidate -> pass 2 returns tenant A's session -> reply admitted and NAT-reversed into A's flow, polluting A's accounting.
- `Refutation attempt`: Recorded and it bounds the claim: a same-domain candidate always wins; the full translated tuple must validate; and since #7169/#9383 the arrival zone must match the forward session's egress zone. What remains is that a zone-matching, tuple-matching foreign-domain reply is admitted by construction.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Pass 2 exists to make a domain-0 reverse index usable; a per-domain index or an explicit refusal is the fix, and neither adds per-packet cost on the same-domain path.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Refuse the pass-2 fallback when both domains are non-zero and different (or require an explicit non-contained-flow marker); single-VRF behaviour unchanged. Acceptance: a two-domain overlapping-tuple regression test admits the same-domain reply and refuses the foreign-domain one.

## Deduplication

The sibling review's SYN-FWD-05 (the FORWARD leg, in the finished virtual-router-routing result) was left NEEDS_VALIDATION and NOT_FILED, so there is no owner for either leg; its detector half is filed as #9809. #7160 (CLOSED) is the forward collision; #9680 (CLOSED) is the NAT64 BIB scope-0 sibling. This is the reverse-path leg, distinct from all of them.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9896 — natpoolalarm: pool utilization is computed against nominal address x port capacity, not the live-tracked-flow cap that actually refuses new flows [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What is wrong

The pools that most need an early warning are the large ones, and for them the alarm's denominator is not the constraint that refuses flows, so the operator learns about exhaustion from dropped traffic.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

pkg/natpoolalarm/natpoolalarm.go:321-325 — `capacity := uint64(s.AddressCount) * (uint64(s.PortHigh) - uint64(s.PortLow) + 1)` then `pct := s.UsedPorts * 100 / capacity`. The binding constraint is elsewhere: userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:105 caps live tracked flows per pool (`MAX_SOURCE_NAT_POOL_TRACKED_FLOWS`), and admission refuses exactly when `live_by_flow` reaches it (allocator.rs:2036). The sample struct (natpoolalarm.go:49) carries only address count, range and UsedPorts; pkg/daemon/daemon_natpoolalarm.go:44-50 and pkg/dataplane/userspace/applied_nat_view.go:139-145 do not pass live-flow counts, although the snapshot has them.

## Contract

A pool-utilization alarm must be computed against the constraint that actually refuses new flows.

## Reachability and actor

Non-adversarial: a large CGNAT pool under ordinary load. The first signal of exhaustion becomes dropped flows rather than an alarm.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin)
- `Probe`: No execution. Three lanes read the arithmetic and the admission site; Claude SMR additionally checked for a commit-time validation refusing a pool whose nominal capacity exceeds the cap and found none.
- `Trace`: allocator refuses at live_by_flow == cap -> alarm divides used_ports by nominal capacity -> the ratio can stay below the raise threshold while the pool is refusing.
- `Refutation attempt`: Codex's arithmetic refutation is accepted for the plain PAT mode and is why this is filed with the mode qualified: the divergence is real where one translated tuple carries many live flows (persistent NAT) or where used-ports and live-flows are otherwise decoupled.
- `HPC/invariant check`: The fix is a second ratio on an already-shipped snapshot field; no new sampling cost.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Alarm on `max(used_ports/capacity, live_flows/max_tracked_flows)` using the fields the snapshot already carries, and mark utilization inapplicable where it cannot bind. Acceptance: a synthetic at-cap fixture raises; the plain-PAT goldens are unchanged; no double-syslog.

## Deduplication

#7361 (CLOSED) covers the address-only pool's structural inability to fire — a different denominator problem on a different pool mode; #2938 (CLOSED) is the show/stats capacity computation. No open owner for the tracked-flow cap.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.
