## #9897 — [cohort] configstore/journal: four link-following paths that the same O_NOFOLLOW/Lstat discipline already applied elsewhere would close [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What this groups

Four sites in `pkg/configstore` operate on a path without first establishing that it is a regular file the daemon owns. The write-side counterparts already refuse links — journal append uses `O_NOFOLLOW`, the factory-reset wipe has a `SymlinkTarget` check, `chmodOwnerOnly` refuses — so each member here is the same class at the one sibling that was not converted. None of them grants privilege: planting requires write access to the parent directory (the `-config <dir>` under a shared parent that `ValidateFactoryResetRoot` was written for) or an operator's stale symlink.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-037 | `pkg/configstore/db.go:53-61` — `NewDB` does `fsatomic.MkdirAllDurable(dir, 0700)` then `os.Chmod(dir, 0700)` with no `Lstat`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, so a symlinked `.configdb` has the TARGET's mode changed to 0700 | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-038 | `pkg/configstore/journal/journal.go:619-633` — `tailSegment` opens with a bare `os.Open`: no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no `IsRegular()` check, so `show system commit`/history can render attacker-chosen JSONL as genuine history while the append path (`:406`) correctly refuses the same link | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-108 | `pkg/configstore/journal/journal.go:503-527` — `maybeRotateLocked` stats through the link (the target's size drives rotation) and then renames the LINK into `.N`, so the planted link is laundered into a segment every later read follows; `migratePermsLocked` only warns | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-040 | `pkg/configstore/factory_reset.go:278-296` — `ValidateFactoryResetRoot` is lexical by its own doc, and `os.ReadDir` follows intermediate links, so a zeroize can delete xpf-named files under another directory and report success. Claude SMR's correction: the two copies differ, and the PRODUCTION one is not the one the claim cited — record both in the fix | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

One fix shape closes all four: resolve or refuse before acting (`Lstat` + `O_NOFOLLOW` + `IsRegular`, or `EvalSymlinks` then re-validate), and the repo already contains the pattern at the sibling call sites. Fixing them separately would mean four reviews of the same argument.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. Two lanes (AGY, Claude SMR) scored each member COHORT/Low; Codex scored F-037/F-038/F-040 MATERIAL/Medium on the integrity consequence. The conservative grade is used because every member needs parent-directory write access or an operator mistake, and the #1960 posture already treats an unreadable store as fatal. The audit-integrity member (F-038/F-108) is the one with a real consequence that does not need a privileged planter to matter: a spoofed commit history survives rotation.

## Fix direction and acceptance

Convert each site to the discipline its own write-side sibling uses, and keep the two factory-reset copies in one change so the mirror cannot drift. Acceptance, per member: a planted-symlink fixture is refused with an error naming the link and the target, and the ordinary path is byte-identical — including `DeleteConfirm`-style absent-file cases. For F-040, resolve `configDir` before BOTH validation and wipe, and assert the grpcapi mirror behaves identically.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

F-040's cited site is not the production one (Claude SMR) — the claim's mechanism is right and its citation is off by one copy. Nothing in the group was refuted outright; no member claims privilege escalation, and that bound is kept rather than inflated.

## Deduplication

#9013 (CLOSED) fixed `RemoveAll` on a symlinked archive dir and #5188 the journal append leg — this group is the set of siblings those two did not reach. #1893/#1894 are the constructor/fsync owners.

| F-115 | `pkg/fsatomic/fsatomic.go:323` — the short-write count is discarded (`if _, err := writeTemp(...)`), so no `n == len(data)` assertion exists, and one close path bypasses the `closeTemp` seam that the durability tests cover | Codex NEG Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

Every member is 'the property is owned by this boundary, and the boundary does not assert it'. The journal trio (F-110/F-113/F-114) share one file and one fix review; the two db.go body guards (F-001/F-035) are two halves of one read; the durability trio (F-111/F-112/F-115) share the temp/rename/remove seam. Filing eight issues would spend eight reviews on one argument.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. Per member, two of three lanes scored Low; Codex scored F-001 COHORT/Low, F-035/F-110-class members MATERIAL/Medium or NEG depending on the member, and those splits are in the table. No member is reachable by a remote actor: the reachable ones need privileged write, a power cut, or a future caller. The group's value is that each one fails in the dangerous direction (accept, lose, or expose) rather than refusing.

## Fix direction and acceptance

Move each property to its boundary: a key-set check on the final plaintext body (case-folded) for F-001; integrity over the unencrypted header for F-035; a documented byte bound inside `Journal.Log` for F-110; a visible degraded state (or a fail-closed append) for F-113; the bounded reverse scan plus `O_NOFOLLOW` for F-114; `O_EXCL`/flock for F-111; `rbRemove`/`rbSyncDir` (or deletion of the dead API) for F-112; an explicit `n == len(data)` check and one close seam for F-115. Acceptance per member is a cell that fails before the change and passes after, including the `{}` decision for F-001 and an absent-file case for F-112.

Codex scored F-110/F-114/F-115 NEG on the ground that no production caller reaches them today, and F-112 STALE because the rollback slots are dead; AGY and Claude SMR kept them as COHORT precisely because a boundary property with no current caller is a trap for the next one. Both readings are recorded; the group is filed at the conservative severity rather than at Codex's higher one for F-035/F-037.

## Severity and reachability

## #9900 — [cohort] userspace-dp: six frame-ownership and fault-containment invariants the datapath assumes and nothing asserts [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What this groups

Six places where the AF_XDP datapath assumes a property of a descriptor, an offset or a thread and nothing checks it. All six are trusted-kernel/driver or local-fault models, not remote attack surfaces — but each converts a recoverable fault into packet corruption, a cross-flow byte leak, or a permanent blackhole.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-091 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:165-171` + `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:169-187` — `MmapArea::slice` checks WHOLE-MAPPING containment only; nothing enforces `len <= FRAME`, alignment, or single-chunk containment, so a cross-frame descriptor forwards adjacent-frame bytes instead of failing closed. TX staging re-verify repeats the same UMEM-only check | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-092 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/rings.rs:20-71,246-261` — every kernel-returned completion offset is pushed into the free/fill lists with no range, alignment, ownership or already-free check, and `outstanding_tx` uses `saturating_sub` so skew is hidden and `== 0` early-returns without draining | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-093 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/supervisor.rs:86-119` — a panicking worker is caught, marked `dead`, and never respawned; its SessionTable dies with it, so any packet-path panic becomes a permanent per-worker forwarding outage | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-094 | `userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs:587-597,639-649` — neither accept loop wraps the handler in `catch_unwind`, and five `.expect("server state poisoned")` sites mean one panic while holding the lock wedges every later request | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-095 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:668-673` — the rewrite plan trusts a stamped `meta.l3_offset` of 14/18 with no version-nibble check, unlike the #2344 sites, so a wrong-but-plausible stamp mutates TTL/checksum/NAT at the wrong offset | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-150 | `userspace-xdp/src/binding_index.rs:243-248` — the binding slot composes `ifindex * stride` in plain `u32`; the module comment documents the >= 2^28 wrap as a known residual, and the high-ifindex row then fails closed as BINDING_MISSING while the interface still reads up | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

Two pairs and two singletons that share one review: descriptor/offset validation at the UMEM boundary (F-091/F-092/F-150 — all 'compose or slice first, check later or never'), and fault containment (F-093/F-094 — 'the supervisor observes the fault and nothing recovers'), with F-095 the one remaining meta-offset consumer that does not re-derive.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group and all three lanes agree on that. None has a demonstrated remote trigger: F-091/F-092 need a driver or kernel fault, F-093/F-094 need a panic that the hot-path audits did not find, F-095 needs a shim stamping bug, F-150 needs an ifindex >= 2^28. The group's value is that each one is the amplifier that makes the NEXT fault unrecoverable, and each fix is cheap (a bound check, a debug bitmap, a respawn-or-shed decision, a nibble check, a checked multiply).

## Fix direction and acceptance

F-091: reject and recycle a descriptor not contained in one frame, and mirror the bound in the TX staging re-verify. F-092: validate reaped offsets (in-mapping, frame-aligned, not already free — a debug bitmap at minimum, a release counter on violation) and surface `outstanding_tx` skew instead of saturating. F-093: respawn with a defined state resync, or decisively shed the worker's queues with an alert. F-094: serve each accepted connection under `catch_unwind` and use poison recovery on the state lock. F-095: nibble-check the stamped offset and fall back to `frame_l3_offset`. F-150: checked/saturating multiply returning `None`, plus a planner refusal for an ifindex past the addressable rows. Acceptance per member is a unit test that pins the new refusal and leaves the normal path byte-identical.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

Nothing was refuted outright, and two claims were narrowed: F-093/F-094's hot-path panic censuses came back negative (no live `.expect`/`panic!` on the packet path; production uses fallible preflight), so these are structural-amplification findings rather than live crashes — which is how they are filed.

## Deduplication

#2344 (CLOSED) is the nibble-check precedent F-095 is missing; #5716 and the ring-hygiene family are the adjacent owners for F-091/F-092; #9499 (OPEN) is the cohort for 'no executed gate turns a Rust integer wrap into a test failure', which is the ASSURANCE half of F-150 rather than the bound itself.

## #9901 — [cohort] userspace-dp: six places where an admitted packet's identity or authority is inherited, split across two walkers, or signalled by a learnable value [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-15)

## What this groups

Six datapath findings about identity and authority rather than about a single wrong branch: an association that renews its own permit, two IPv6 walks that must agree by convention, a fabric stamp whose authenticator is learnable, a PMTUD decision that fails open on an unknown MTU, an ingress length/TTL discipline split across layers, and an ICMP quote trusted as a session key.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-010 | `userspace-dp/src/fragment_assoc/mod.rs:623-627` — `lookup` re-stamps `deadline_ns` on every hit, so the 2 s TTL is an IDLE timeout with NO absolute bound, and the key is port-free, so within one config generation a spoofing sender on the same logical ingress can hold a permitted datagram's forwarding+NAT decision open indefinitely | Codex FIXED Low; AGY NEG Medium; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-072 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:155-288` vs `screen/extract.rs` — forwarding and screen keep independent IPv6 extension walks whose agreement (every forwarding-`Truncated` chain is also a screen-`Err`) is a convention, not a shared verdict, so any future drift reopens an ext-header IDS evasion | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-073 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:1923-1966` + `forwarding/fabric.rs:289-316` — the fabric zone stamp is a MAC magic plus a PUBLIC name hash, both learnable on the L2 segment, and `routing_table` is inert at every production assignment | Codex FIXED Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR NEG Low |
| F-074 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_ptb.rs:117-123,150-156` — `mtu == 0` (unknown) returns Forward, so an oversize frame is submitted and dropped downstream with no PTB; per-reason per-zone buckets also share one bucket across all sources in a zone | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-075 | `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1475-1484` — the shim validates version and IHL only and never reads IPv4 total-length, so a lying length reaches shim classification and flow stamping before any declared-end discipline; the TTL half has changed since the claim and is narrower | Codex DUP Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-077 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/parse.rs:171,313` — quote bounds correctly follow the quoted declared length (#5568), but the outer ICMP error carries no authentication, so an off-path sender who guesses a live 5-tuple gets the error matched to the session and NAT-reversed | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

All six are 'the identity or authority this packet is adjudicated under was established elsewhere and is not re-established here'. F-010/F-073 are inherited authority; F-072/F-075 are split verdicts that must agree; F-074/F-077 are decisions taken on attacker-shaped or absent inputs. They share a review, and three of them share the same fix lever (derive the verdict once, in one place).

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. The severities split and the splits are in the table: Codex scored F-074 MATERIAL/Medium and F-075 DUP; AGY scored most of the group COHORT/Low; Claude SMR refuted F-010's load-bearing half and F-073's primary consequence. What is left in each member is real but bounded, and none has an executed end-to-end demonstration.

## Fix direction and acceptance

F-010: add an absolute lifetime bound beside the idle TTL (`created_ns` + cap). F-072: share ONE walker verdict, or add a differential property test sweeping all 256 next-header values x truncation points. F-073: authenticate fabric redirects (or bind acceptance to a peer-authenticated channel) and wire or remove `routing_table`. F-074: populate egress/tunnel MTU from one SSOT with an explicit unknown-MTU counter, and make the zone buckets per-source-fair. F-075: one ingress declared-length gate shared by shim and userspace. F-077: stricter quote adequacy plus a per-session error-delivery rate limit. Acceptance per member is named in the corresponding report finding.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

Two of the report's load-bearing consequences are REFUTED at the pin and the members are filed narrower: (1) F-010's 'a mid-datagram deny-policy commit is never re-applied' is false — the #5624 generation fence at `fragment_assoc/mod.rs:601-604` evicts the association on ANY config commit, and `nat64_tests.rs:5310-5323` pins it; only the missing absolute bound survives. (2) F-073's stamp is gated twice, so the re-homing requires more than the claim states. F-075's TTL half changed since the claim's base.

## Deduplication

#5798 (CLOSED) added the interface-filter re-check on the frag-assoc hit arm and #6835 the owner-RG re-enforcement — F-010 is their stated residual. #2361/#5150/#6748 are the declared-length family for F-075. #5568 (CLOSED) is the quote-bounds owner for F-077. #9519 (CLOSED) is the session-table analogue of F-010's inheritance question.

Five bounded items around the NAT pools and the SYN-cookie path. Each is a cost, signal or honesty gap rather than a wrong verdict.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. AGY scored F-026 and F-023 at the lower end (NEG for F-026, refuted-cost for F-023), Codex and Claude SMR kept them as bounded hardening, and Claude SMR refuted the HARM half of F-096 while keeping its facts. Four small gates where the failure direction is permissive or the signal is wrong. Two are in the nftables plan builder, two are in the API/authz observability layer.

| --- | --- | --- |
| F-126 | `pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go:684-688` — `ifname16` copies into a 16-byte field with no length check and no `p.fail`, so an explicit junos-host DROP for a >= 15-char interface never matches and falls through to zone policy. Claude SMR scored the CONSEQUENCE refuted and the code exactly as described | Codex FIXED Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR NEG Low |
| F-127 | `pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go:375-393` — `pfxAddrMatch` `continue`s past any unparseable or wrong-family token with no error, so a wholly-unparseable list renders a rule with NO address predicate (fail-open for accepts), below a #6512 contract that says never install a rule built from a narrowed subset | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-128 | `pkg/grpcapi/authz_stream_reauth_9051.go:104-115` — on revoke the wrapper cancels the stream ctx, so `if herr != nil { return herr }` returns the handler's ctx error and identical revocations surface as `PermissionDenied` or `Canceled`/`Unavailable` by timing; the client retries instead of surfacing the authorization event | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-129 | `pkg/api/authz.go:894-899` — `readAuthz` fails OPEN for an unlisted safe-method route (`if !known { next.ServeHTTP(w, r); return }`), and the only guard is a source census over ONE registration shape, so a route registered via `mux.Handle`, a method-less pattern or a trailing-slash variant evades both | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

All four are single-site gates with a permissive failure direction and a cheap structural fix; the two nftables members share one builder and one review, and the two authz members share the observability argument (the enforcement is correct, the SIGNAL is not).

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group, with all three lanes agreeing for F-127/F-128/F-129. F-126 splits (Codex FIXED, AGY COHORT, Claude SMR NEG-on-consequence) and is kept as a member for its builder-posture inconsistency rather than for the never-match claim. F-129 has NO live instance today — every current `/api/v1` GET uses the censused shape — so it is filed as a trap for the next route author, which is how #9134 actually fired.

## Fix direction and acceptance

F-126: `p.fail` when a rendered ifname exceeds 15 bytes (mirroring #6512) or pre-validate at the converter, plus a parity cell asserting both builders agree. F-127: fail the plan on any unparseable or wrong-family token, with a unit test feeding `["garbage"]`. F-128: consult the `revoked` channel BEFORE returning a handler error, with a regression test that demotes a class mid-stream and asserts a deterministic `PermissionDenied`. F-129: either fail closed for unknown `/api/v1` paths with an explicit exempt set, or census the LIVE mux (all patterns and methods) and fail on an uncensused shape.

F-126's never-match proof is analytic (key byte[15] != NUL vs the kernel's NUL-padded field) and the oracle divergence was never measured against `nft(8)`; Claude SMR treats the consequence as refuted on that ground. Claude SMR REFUTED the claim's mechanism: the masking is AF_XDP CORE (`xp_check_aligned`), not mlx5-specific, so the surviving item is that the repo depends on a core contract it never cites — and its own reference harness masks before refill | Codex NEG Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR no pass |

Claude SMR found the claim's preferred remedy is explicitly FORBIDDEN by `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/README.md:83-84`, so the fix needs a different shape | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR no pass |
| F-151 | `userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:332` — bind resolves ifindex->name with `if_indextoname` and then creates the socket BY NAME, so a concurrent rename in the window can bind another interface's queue, and nothing downstream re-checks the bound identity. Claude SMR's correction: the rename actor is the PRODUCT itself (xpf renames interfaces at startup), not an operator — which makes the window a real product-internal ordering question rather than a hypothetical | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR no pass |

## #9905 — [cohort] daemon/dataplane: the Go HA session-delta hot path converts binary to string and back and rebuilds per-delta state on the event-stream reader [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What this groups

Two findings on the same hot path: the Go side of HA session-delta handling, which runs on the event-stream reader goroutine that paces the helper's replay-buffer ACK. Both are source-proven per-delta costs, not measured bottlenecks, and they share one corrective scope.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-083 | `pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go:1509,1518` — binary IPs and MACs are formatted into strings and re-parsed on the delta path (~13-15 format/parse ops per IPv4 delta; the measured micro-benchmark in the source report put the round trip at ~429-506 ns/op against ~0.85-1.3 ns for a 4-byte copy), although the binary frame already carries the raw bytes | Codex NEEDS_VALIDATION Medium; AGY MATERIAL Medium; SMR no pass |
| F-152 | `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:352` — every binary delta calls `ActiveConfig`, rebuilds the whole `zoneIDs` map (FNV-1a per zone name) and wraps the single delta in a fresh one-element slice, while zone ids change only on commit | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR no pass |

## Why these belong together

The source report grouped these itself (F-152 'same corrective scope as F-083, smaller magnitude'), all three lanes kept them together, and the fix is one change to the same call path: carry binary through and hoist the per-commit state out of the per-delta loop.

## Severity and reachability

Low. Both are proven per-operation costs on a path that paces HA ACKs; neither is a measured throughput or failover-latency regression, and this is stated rather than implied. The reason it is worth doing is that the cost is paid twice per connection (open and close) and K times serially during a FullResync bulk export, which is the path that is already degraded.

## Fix direction and acceptance

Carry binary addresses through `SessionDeltaInfo` (or a parallel binary struct) so no format/parse round trip remains; at minimum parse each NAT IP once per delta. Cache the zone-id map across deltas, rebuilding only on a config-generation change, and hoist `ActiveConfig()` out of the per-delta path the way `queueUserspaceSessionDeltas` already hoists `getSessionSync()`. Acceptance: an allocs/op regression budget on decode plus the V4 convert, and a cell asserting the zone map is not rebuilt when the generation is unchanged.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

Nothing refuted; both claims' cost arithmetic was checked by all three lanes. The magnitude framing is deliberately kept at 'proven per-delta cost', since no end-to-end failover measurement exists.

## Deduplication

#9053 (CLOSED) is the RUST-side per-new-flow cost cohort with a recorded deferral on a cluster blocker — the five Rust cost claims in this report (F-078/F-079/F-080/F-081/F-084) are its enumerated sites and are linked there rather than refiled. These two are the GO side and are not in that enumeration.

## #9906 — ipsec: `#`/`{`/`}`/`=` in a committed algorithm value reach the UNQUOTED `proposals`/`esp_proposals` slots verbatim — a silent crypto downgrade, and #9495 measured that an injected swanctl setting is applied [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

The established harm is a silent crypto downgrade: the offered proposal list is truncated at the `#`, so the trailing integrity and PFS terms disappear and charon negotiates whatever the truncated list permits (or its compiled-in defaults for a `#`-leading value) — the exact outcome #2270 fails closed for, reached without an error and without an audit trail. With `}` and `=`, the same ungated bytes reach a root-parsed file in which the project has MEASURED that an injected setting is applied, which is why F-018 is folded in here rather than filed separately.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:707-709` — `sanitizeSwanctlValue` is `rendersafe.ReplaceControlBytes(s, ' ')`, which touches only `c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f`; `#`, `{`, `}`, `=` and SPACE pass verbatim. The two unquoted list slots that take attacker-or-operator-supplied algorithm tokens are `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:246` (`proposals = %s`) and `:307` (`esp_proposals = %s`). `pkg/ipsec/ike.go:485-517` appends `prop.EncryptionAlg`/`AuthAlg` VERBATIM on the unknown-algorithm fall-through, and the non-AEAD branch collapses `-cbc`/`-` without filtering anything else.

## Contract

#2270 establishes that a crypto downgrade must fail closed. A rendered swanctl value must not be able to change the meaning of the line it sits in: `#` starts a charon comment, and `{`/`}`/`=` are structural.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: the negotiated ESP/IKE transform, and the integrity of a root-parsed config file. Actor: whoever can get a value into a proposal field — an operator with commit rights, a persisted config from an older build, or an HA peer config sync. The algorithm leaves are deliberately untyped (`pkg/config/schema_security.go:1004`), so a quoted value carrying `#` or `}` survives to the renderer.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes + coordinator at the pin) + EXECUTED (the source report's emission probe at base; and an IN-TREE measurement of charon's lexer recorded by commit 8d0aa6207/#9495)
- `Probe`: No new execution here. The decisive external fact is MEASURED IN-TREE rather than assumed: commit `8d0aa6207` (#9495) records, on the pinned strongSwan, that 'whitespace, a brace, \'#\', \'=\', \',\', a quote or \'.\' makes the whole file unparsable' and that `x { children { p { mode = transport } } } y` **injects a connection and the setting is applied**. That measurement was taken in the section-NAME position; applying it to a VALUE position is ONE inference step (Claude SMR's caveat, recorded rather than elided).
- `Trace`: committed/persisted algorithm value with `#` or `}` -> buildIKEProposal/buildESPProposal append it verbatim -> sanitizeSwanctlValue leaves it -> `esp_proposals = aes256 #-sha256-modp2048` -> charon reads `aes256` and a comment (silent downgrade), or, with `}` and `=`, additional settings in the enclosing section.
- `Refutation attempt`: Two real narrowings, both applied: the VPN-name legs are gated at the pin by #9495 (commit allowlist `pkg/ipsecname/ipsecname.go:119-132` wired at `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_ipsec_event.go:221`, plus the render belt at `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:129-136`), and `local_ts`/`remote_ts` are not the live surface. No structural guard exists on the two proposal slots, so the emission itself is unrefuted.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **High** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Gate the rendered proposal token: an allowlist at commit (the #9495 `SectionSafe` pattern applied to algorithm values) plus a render-side reject-or-skip with a loud log, so no committed-or-tolerated value with swanctl-significant bytes reaches an unquoted slot. Acceptance: a cell per metacharacter per slot asserting the value is refused at commit and the render refuses-or-skips on the tolerant path; legitimate comma-lists and `-`-joined tokens render byte-identically. **This issue covers F-016 and F-018**, which Claude SMR found to be one defect with one corrective scope — F-018 contributes the injection consequence and the charon measurement.

## Deduplication

#9495 (CLOSED) gated the section NAMES and supplied the measurement; #6833 (CLOSED) named this sanitizer's shape problem and left 'whether any swanctl key is whitespace-list-valued' open — it is: these two; #4098 (CLOSED) is the local_ts/remote_ts leg. No open owner for the value slots.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.
- Origin run ID `review-work.7n9FuGPsdt`; report base SHA `3b24fe26e8356963893d151d4dedaa1aa27a7e48`. The report was `Mode: report-only, Filed: 0`, so this is the finding's FIRST filing.
- Finding ID(s): F-016 (source finding E15C-01 (slice-E15crypto.md)).
- Discovering model: `muse-spark-unknown` — family-only identity (the report's header records `WHOAMI: muse-spark-unknown` and exposes no exact model identifier). The report attributes the finding to the slice above; no separate slice-worker model identity is evidenced, so the discoverer stays the report's derived identity.

## #9907 — ipsec: a non-AEAD ESP proposal with no `authentication-algorithm` renders as a bare cipher with no integrity term, and nothing requires one at commit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

Either the firewall silently negotiates ESP with no integrity for an operator who simply omitted a leaf, or it fails to load a tunnel with a diagnostic that points at charon rather than at the missing leaf. The operator is not told which.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`pkg/ipsec/ike.go:485-517` `buildESPProposal`: for a non-AEAD cipher it appends the encryption token and then `if prop.AuthAlg != "" { parts = append(parts, normalizeAuthAlg(prop.AuthAlg)) }` — the integrity term is conditional, and the default when `EncryptionAlg` is empty is `aes256` (`ike.go:489-492`). `authentication-algorithm` is an optional untyped leaf under `ipsec proposal` (`pkg/config/schema_security.go:1199`) and no validator requires it for a non-AEAD cipher (a grep of pkg/config for `AuthAlg` finds only the compiler's reader).

## Contract

Missing crypto intent must not render the weakest legal transform. Every sibling (IKE, AH, WireGuard) fails closed when intent is absent; #4298 established 'never fabricate a suite'.

## Reachability and actor

Actor for the severe branch: an on-path attacker against a CBC ESP SA with no integrity (bit-flipping, known-plaintext forgery). Actor for the defect itself: an operator who omits `authentication-algorithm`, which commits clean.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes + coordinator at the pin); the consequence branch is NEEDS_VALIDATION and is stated as such
- `Probe`: No execution: no strongSwan on this host. The source report's probe recorded the rendered string `"esp_proposals = aes256-modp2048"` at its base.
- `Trace`: commit `encryption-algorithm aes-256-cbc` with no authentication-algorithm -> buildESPProposal -> `esp_proposals = aes256[-modp...]` -> charon either negotiates an integrity-less ESP SA (severe) or refuses the proposal (misleading tunnel-down).
- `Refutation attempt`: The severe consequence is unmeasured and is NOT asserted here. Claude SMR's refutation is adopted as the severity bound. Both branches are bad and the remedy is identical, which is why this is filed rather than deferred.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Reject a non-AEAD ESP proposal with an empty `authentication-algorithm` at strict commit, naming the proposal; skip-or-warn (never bare-cipher render) on the tolerant path; AEAD/GCM without a separate integrity term still renders. Acceptance: a renderer test asserts no bare non-AEAD cipher token is ever emitted without an integrity term, plus a commit-check cell. Next measurement that would settle the severity: load `esp_proposals = aes256` into the shipped charon and record accept-vs-refuse.

## Deduplication

#4298 (CLOSED) is the 'never fabricate a suite' precedent for the AH skip; #4117 (CLOSED) is the ESP default-suite fallback; #9008 (CLOSED) is the negative-lifetime sibling. None requires integrity for a non-AEAD ESP proposal.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.
- Origin run ID `review-work.7n9FuGPsdt`; report base SHA `3b24fe26e8356963893d151d4dedaa1aa27a7e48`. The report was `Mode: report-only, Filed: 0`, so this is the finding's FIRST filing.

## #9908 — userspace-dp/wireguard: no per-source bound on valid-MAC2 handshake ADMISSIONS — a replayed initiation costs a full responder DH before the TAI64N replay drop, on the per-tunnel control thread [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

One non-spoofed host can hold a tunnel's control thread in a DH loop with replayed bytes, degrading keepalive and rekey processing for that tunnel, and the mitigation the design relies on is applied to the wrong packet class.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:619-680` — under load the admission path reaches `Process` for a valid-MAC2 packet with no per-source bound; `wg/cookie.rs:436-479` is reply-only and is invoked at `engine.rs:652`; `wg/handshake_session.rs:585-587` performs the DH before the TAI64N drop at `:615-617`; the coordinator dispatch is `coordinator/wg_control/dispatch.rs:76-137`. `WG_RX_BURST=64` bounds one poll iteration, but `did_work` skips the poll wait, so a flood drives a CPU-bound loop.

## Contract

The WireGuard cookie design assumes that a spoofed source never obtains a cookie; it does not bound a NON-spoofed host that obtains one legitimately and replays it. wireguard-go answers that with a per-source HANDSHAKE-packet ratelimiter, which #4332 cites while applying its bucket to cookie REPLIES only.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: any non-spoofed host that can reach the WireGuard listen port — it obtains one cookie at its real address and then replays valid-MAC2 bytes. Cost to the responder: ~2 X25519 plus the AEAD/BLAKE chain per replay, because the Noise read happens BEFORE the TAI64N replay drop, inline on the per-tunnel control thread that also runs timers, keepalives, rekeys and socket IO.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (the source report's E11 probe at base showed a replayed valid-MAC2 initiation classified and Noise-read a SECOND time before the TAI64N replay drop)
- `Probe`: No new execution (cargo prohibited here). The source report's `e11_mac2_valid_replay_costs_full_handshake_under_load` recorded `hs_rx_under_load_mac2_ok == 2` — the replayed bytes were classified `Process` a second time and only then failed `ReplayedInitiation`.
- `Trace`: attacker obtains a cookie -> replays valid-MAC2 initiation -> engine consumes it as a fresh Process -> full responder DH -> TAI64N replay drop, after the cost is paid -> repeat.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked the #4332 bucket and the global budget: both gate cookie REPLIES, not handshake admissions; and the burst bound does not rate-limit because `did_work` skips the wait. No handshake-path ratelimit exists anywhere in the tree.
- `HPC/invariant check`: This is a CPU-cost finding with a proven per-packet cost (2 X25519 + AEAD/BLAKE) and an unmeasured saturation rate: no flood benchmark was run. The contended resource is the per-tunnel control thread, which also owns timers and socket IO, so the degradation mode is missed keepalives and delayed rekeys rather than data-plane loss.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Bound under-load `Process` admissions per source — extend the #4332 bucket to handshake admissions, or keep a bounded recent-(source, MAC1) cache consulted BEFORE the Noise read. Acceptance: replaying one valid-MAC2 initiation N times consumes at most K expensive handshakes while a fresh initiation from another source still completes under load; a flood test shows a bounded DH count with live timer processing.

## Deduplication

#4332 (CLOSED) is the cookie-reply bucket this finding shows is pointed at the wrong class. #9644 (OPEN) is a different WireGuard hot-path lock (per-decap roaming mutex), not this admission path.

## #9909 — userspace-dp/wireguard: a tunnel in a routing-instance binds its OUTER UDP socket in the main table, so handshake and transport leave the VRF the operator scoped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

An operator who scopes a WireGuard tunnel into a VRF gets a tunnel whose transport is not scoped, with no diagnostic — either silently broken (VRF-only peer route) or silently wider than configured.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/wg_control/sock.rs:86-91,99-104` — the outer UDP socket is created without `SO_BINDTODEVICE` and with no VRF binding, so the handshake and transport use main-table routing; the inner `wgN` device IS VRF-bound (`pkg/routing/tunnel_wireguard.go:251`). The S2a comment calls the gap known, but nothing at commit time tells the operator.

## Contract

A tunnel configured inside a `routing-instance` must either have its outer transport in that VRF or be refused. The Go side models WireGuard + routing-instance as supported: the schema sibling commits clean and no validator rejects it.

## Reachability and actor

Protection: VRF containment for tunnel transport. Actor: for the containment-break case, any host reachable in the MAIN table that can complete a handshake — AEAD and AllowedIPs still hold, so authentication is intact and containment is not. Non-adversarial cases: a VRF-only peer route silently blackholes the handshake, and handshake/transport egress leaves the wrong VRF.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin, both sides of the boundary)
- `Probe`: No execution. Three lanes read both sides (Rust socket creation, Go schema/compiler/routing/VRF claim and snapshot rows).
- `Trace`: `routing-instance` + WireGuard commit -> inner device in the VRF, outer socket in main -> (1) VRF-only peer route never reached; (2) outer traffic in the wrong VRF's policy domain; (3) a main-table-reachable peer handshakes a nominally VRF-scoped tunnel and injects into the VRF.
- `Refutation attempt`: Checked whether AllowedIPs or the AEAD bound the containment question: they bound AUTHENTICITY, not which VRF the outer packet traverses, so they are not a refutation. Checked for a commit-time rejection: none.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

EITHER reject WireGuard + routing-instance at commit with a naming diagnostic, OR VRF-bind the outer socket and route its egress in that VRF. Acceptance: a regression test asserts whichever is chosen — refusal, or a VRF-correct bind observed on the socket.

## Deduplication

#9506 (OPEN) is the route-based-IPsec analogue (decrypted ingress kernel-forwarded with no zone policy) — same family, different tunnel type and different code path, so corroboration rather than duplication. #9587 (OPEN) is the WireGuard listen-port steering feature.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9911 — logging: a hung syslog collector stalls the EVENT READER ~4s per event because the write-timeout arm never arms the cooldown, and a concurrent Close serializes the commit behind it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

One degraded collector converts every logged event into a 4-second stall on the goroutine that also paces HA session-sync and flow export, and makes a routine reconfigure commit wait on a dead peer.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`pkg/logging/syslog.go:48` `defaultWriteTimeout = 4 * time.Second`; `:754` `writeMsg` runs unconditionally on every `Send`; `:765-768` the timeout arm drops the message WITHOUT arming `lastReconnectFailure`, so nothing ever fails fast. `pkg/logging/ringbuf.go:725,838` are the two callers on the event path. Claude SMR ruled out the adjacent gates: the #4806 closed-gate short-circuit (`:749-752`) only applies after Close, and `reconnectCooldown` (`:522-527`) is consulted only inside `reconnect()`, which this path does not reach.

## Contract

#2302 added a reconnect cooldown so a dead collector fails fast. A write timeout is the same fault and must arm the same cooldown.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: none required — a hung, blackholing or degraded collector. A MITM that blackholes the TCP syslog port produces the same effect. The stall lands on the event-reader goroutine AND the HA userspace-stream callback.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (the source report's two probes at base: 2 sends -> 2 attempts with droppedCooldown=0, and both sends blocking the full deadline)
- `Probe`: No new execution. This issue also covers **F-060**: `Close` (`pkg/logging/syslog.go:1392-1399`) takes the same `s.mu` that a stalled `Send` holds across the write deadline (`:746-747`), so a reconfigure-time client swap serializes behind a hung peer — the source report measured 0.30 s for a 300 ms stalled write, and the worst case is ~13 s per client (4 s write + 5 s dial + 4 s retry). Closing the socket does not release the mutex waiter.
- `Trace`: hung collector -> every Send blocks up to writeTimeout on the event-reader goroutine -> HA session-sync queueing, flow-export, trace and aggregation callbacks all wait -> a concurrent Close waits on the same mutex, so the commit path waits too.
- `Refutation attempt`: No fail-fast path exists for the timeout case; the cooldown that would provide it is unreachable from here. For the Close half, no mark-closed-without-lock fast path and no async close exist (both checked at the pin).
- `HPC/invariant check`: Per-event cost is bounded by the deadline but unbounded in repetition: ~4 s per event per hung client, indefinitely.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Arm the cooldown (or an equivalent fail-fast) when a write times out, so at most one writeTimeout is paid per cooldown window per client; and make swap/close never block a commit on a stalled peer (mark-closed plus socket close to unblock, with a bounded deferred join). Acceptance: the second send inside the window returns without blocking, and a client swap against a hung server completes in bounded time.

## Deduplication

#2302 (CLOSED) added the reconnect cooldown and left the timeout arm unwired; #9326 (CLOSED) bounded the syslog DIAL at 5 s, which is the sibling fix F-058 is missing in flowexport. No open owner.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9912 — feeds: the fetcher follows cross-origin redirects and honours ambient HTTP(S)_PROXY, so an untrusted feed server chooses the firewall's next hop [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

An untrusted feed server chooses what the firewall connects to, from inside the management network — and an ambient proxy variable silently re-routes feed traffic and its credentials.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`pkg/feeds/feeds.go:191-193` — `client: &http.Client{Timeout: httpClientTimeout}` with no `CheckRedirect` and no `Transport`, so Go's default follows up to 10 redirects and `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` applies; the fetch is a plain `m.client.Do(req)` at `:793`.

## Contract

#3934 states that a plaintext feed server is UNTRUSTED. Commit-time validation of the configured URL therefore bounds only the FIRST hop; the fetcher must not let that server choose subsequent hops.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: a compromised or malicious feed server — explicitly in the threat model. It returns a 302 to an arbitrary internal `http(s)` endpoint and the firewall fetches it from its own vantage point. Ambient `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` additionally route fetches (and any query-string token) through a proxy the operator did not configure here.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (the source report's probe at base: a 302 to a second httptest origin was followed and the second origin's prefixes were returned)
- `Probe`: No new execution. Claude SMR bounded the consequence: the body is parsed into prefixes and never echoed to the redirect issuer, so the SSRF is BLIND, and the 32 MiB / 1M-entry caps bound its cost.
- `Trace`: malicious feed server -> 302 -> fetcher follows to an internal endpoint -> response parsed as a prefix list -> blind SSRF from the firewall's vantage point, plus any ambient proxy in the path.
- `Refutation attempt`: The blindness and the caps are real and are recorded; they bound the information gained per request, not the reachability of internal endpoints.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: High

## Fix direction and acceptance

Disable redirects or pin them same-origin (and never to literal/link-local/internal targets unless explicitly configured), and set an explicit proxy policy (direct by default). Acceptance: a cross-origin 302 is not followed and is counted; a same-origin redirect still works if that is the chosen policy.

## Deduplication

#3934 (CLOSED) is the untrusted-feed threat model this relies on; the commit-time URL validation is its own owner and covers only hop one. No open owner for redirect/proxy policy.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.
- Origin run ID `review-work.7n9FuGPsdt`; report base SHA `3b24fe26e8356963893d151d4dedaa1aa27a7e48`. The report was `Mode: report-only, Filed: 0`, so this is the finding's FIRST filing.

## #9913 — flowexport: collector dial and DNS resolve are unbounded and run while the reconcile holds the mutex, so a slow resolver parks the COMMIT — the syslog sibling was bounded at 5s by #9326 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

A DNS outage or one mistyped collector hostname parks an operator's commit for the resolver's full budget, on a path whose sibling was bounded for this exact reason.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`pkg/flowexport/transport.go:117-122,149-159` — `dialUDP = net.DialUDP` / `resolveUDPAddr = net.ResolveUDPAddr` and a bare `net.Dial("udp", c.Address)`, with no `net.Dialer{Timeout}` and no context anywhere; called from `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:159-227` on every apply while the mutex is held. Contrast `pkg/logging/syslog.go:470,475,488` where the 5 s dialers live.

## Contract

#9326 bounded the syslog dial at 5 s for exactly this reason. The flow-export collector dial is the same operation on the same commit path and did not get the same bound.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: none — a DNS outage, a slow resolver, or an operator typo in a collector hostname. The stall is taken while the reconcile holds the manager mutex, so the COMMIT waits.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin; exact stall duration is resolv.conf-dependent and is not measured)
- `Probe`: No execution. Claude SMR checked for a pre-dial resolve/validate gate, a context-carrying dial seam and an async reconcile, and found none.
- `Trace`: commit -> flowexport reconcile holds the mutex -> NewExporter -> unbounded resolve/dial -> the commit and everything behind the mutex wait for the resolver's full budget.
- `Refutation attempt`: None found. The bound on the claim is that the duration depends on the resolver configuration, which is why the severity is Medium and the confidence is Medium.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Not applicable.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Bound the collector dial and resolve at <= 5 s (matching syslog) and pass a context. Acceptance: a commit with an unresolvable collector completes in bounded time, asserted by a regression test.

## Deduplication

#9326 (CLOSED) is the syslog sibling fix. No open owner for flowexport.

- Discovery source: `source:deep-review` — external deep-review report `muse-spark-unknown-review-full-firewall-001.md` (SHA-256 `e70255f6c46b6045123bc4cb4940e7dfd036be9c921182a78a2938c533e0040a`), review name "full firewall (maximal expert coverage)", slug `full-firewall`.

## #9914 — [cohort] vrrp/ra: four out-of-domain values that reach the wire or silently skip an instance instead of being clamped at the one boundary that owns them [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What this groups

Four HA/RA values where the domain check lives somewhere other than the sink that puts the value on the wire. Each is individually narrow; together they are the same omission, and three of them have the clamp already written a few lines away.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-042 | `pkg/vrrp/instance_send.go:82-85,89,104` + `pkg/vrrp/packet.go:75` — #9039 clamped the advertise interval at the TOP only. A lenient-loaded NEGATIVE interval makes the timer fall back to 1000 ms while the WIRE value wraps: Claude SMR's arithmetic run gives `ms=-40950` -> 10 ms advertised (false master-down, dual-master, VIP flap) and `ms=-10` -> ~41 s (≈2 min to notice a real failure). All three lanes confirmed the files are unchanged since the claim's base | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Medium; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-119 | `pkg/ra/sender.go:994-997` — LinkMTU is advertised verbatim and `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:632-637` is floor-only (1280) with NO ceiling, so a lenient 1-1279 blackholes honouring hosts and a plain operator typo commits an unusable MTU; the saturating-clamp template for sibling fields is in the same file | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-120 | `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:789-805` — `UpdateRGPriority` is the one writer that bypasses `clampConfigPriority`, and the sink narrows with `uint8(priority)`: 256 aliases to 0, which IS the resign value, so a priority update would read as a resignation. Latent: current callers pass only 100/200 | Codex NEG Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-121 | `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:236,259` (`GroupID: 100 + rgID`) against the `MinVRID=1..MaxVRID=255` bound — a lenient-loaded RG id > 155 yields an out-of-range VRID, the instance is SKIPPED with a Warn, and the cluster manager still elects that RG primary, so manager state and VIP reality diverge behind one log line. The same `100 + rgID` arithmetic appears at five manager call sites with no shared constructor | Codex FIXED Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

All four are 'the value's domain is checked at one layer and spent at another'. F-042/F-120/F-121 are all in `pkg/vrrp` and two of them share the `100 + rgID`/clamp surface; F-119 is the same shape in `pkg/ra`. One review, four small diffs.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. Codex scored F-042 and F-120-class members MATERIAL/Medium; AGY and Claude SMR scored the group COHORT/Low-Medium, and the splits are per-member in the table. Every member needs either a lenient-loaded (persisted or peer-synced) out-of-domain value or a future caller; none is reachable by an operator commit at the pin, because the strict schema rejects them.

## Fix direction and acceptance

Saturate or refuse at the sink, not only at the author boundary: clamp the VRRP wire value at BOTH ends so wire and timer can never disagree (F-042); a send-side saturating clamp plus a commit ceiling for LinkMTU (F-119); route `UpdateRGPriority` through `clampConfigPriority` (F-120); one shared checked VRID constructor, and mark the RG not-ready/degraded in manager state when an instance is refused (F-121). Acceptance per member: a cell pins the negative/zero/over-max inputs and the in-range control stays byte-identical.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

Nothing refuted. F-121's refusal is deliberate and correct (a wrapped VRID would join the wrong virtual router) — the defect is the divergence it leaves in manager state, not the refusal.

## Deduplication

#9039 (CLOSED) clamped F-042's top end only. #5834 (CLOSED) is the lenient-VRRP-auth sibling. #2384 is the v6 VRRP schema. No open owner for any member.

| F-131 | `pkg/eventengine/engine.go:588-600` — `Close`'s docstring says it 'drains in-flight retries'; the body closes `stopCh` and the worker returns with buffered actions still queued. None run, none are counted, the gauge is never decremented, and nothing is logged | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-132 | `pkg/logging/audit_async_writer_9025.go:154-168` — `enqueue` checks `stopped` then does a non-blocking send; the worker drains until a momentarily-empty `default` and exits, so a send that passes the check and lands after the final drain sits in the channel forever: the caller saw success, no drop was counted, the audit line was never written | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-133 | `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:390-395` — `Apply` cancels each old producer and swaps the map WITHOUT joining (unlike `StopAll`, fixed by #7174), so an in-flight old fetch can complete post-swap and call `onUpdate` against the NEW state — a spurious dataplane apply | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-135 | `pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:303-382` — `withinMatches` and `pruneWindow` dereference a `*EventWithin` with no nil test while two of the four consumers do check, so a nil clause panics `HandleEvent` on a probe goroutine and takes the daemon down. No reachable producer today (the compiler always appends a non-nil clause and no JSON/gob decode of EventPolicy exists) | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Severity and reachability

## What this groups

Seven WireGuard findings that are not protocol violations and not live exposures: a reliability edge on simultaneous open, three key-hygiene residuals, a flood-path cost ordering, a DNS-steering trust boundary, and the missing interop oracle that would catch a transcript regression.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-141 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/handshake_session.rs:200-211` — the at-most-one-pending DoS bound (sound against floods) over-fires against a concurrent VALID handshake: two individually valid crossed initiations deterministically establish nothing, both sides reach `pending_count() == 0`, and recovery needs a fresh trigger (~1 s via the NoSession edge, <= 5 s via REKEY_TIMEOUT) | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-142 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:422-427` — the engine comment claims key material is wiped, but `snow 0.10.0` has no `zeroize` and no `impl Drop` (verified by Claude SMR against the locked registry copy with a positive control), so session/handshake keys persist in freed heap. The false comment is itself the hazard: a reviewer will not add wiping they believe exists | Codex NEEDS_VALIDATION Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-143 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:1569-1572` — the `CryptoFailed` arm returns without zeroing `out`, leaving attacker-influenced unauthenticated plaintext in the caller's buffer; every sibling post-AEAD arm wipes, and one sibling's comment claims a new arm 'cannot accidentally skip the wipe' while this pre-existing arm does | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-144 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:628-644` + `wg/cookie.rs:552-577` — under load MAC2 is verified before MAC1 and the MAC1 key is derived per message, so one bad-MAC1 junk packet costs 4-6 hashes where MAC1-first with a precomputed key would cost ~1.5 — a 2-3x cut on exactly the path the under-load mitigation exists to cheapen | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-145 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/cookie.rs:494` — `secrets()` returns a bare `[u8; 32]` pair, copying the responder cookie secret out of its `Zeroizing` guard on every under-load initiation; that secret is the root of the anti-flood property | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-146 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/handshake_tests.rs:118-126` — the in-tree KAT concedes its own scope (the Noise body is a fixed pattern, not real snow output), and `wg-interop.sh` is GATE-class but declared unreached, so a systematic transcript deviation shared by both sides of a self-handshake cannot be detected in-tree | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-162 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/wg_control/mod.rs:807-844` — a DNS-resolved peer endpoint can redirect tunnel egress after 90 s of peer silence; the attacker cannot decrypt or handshake, but the tunnel blackholes and they learn traffic timing and handshake cadence. The 90 s roam-hold and first-authenticated-datagram re-win are sound mitigations, and hostname endpoints are opt-in | Codex COHORT Low; AGY NEG Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

All seven are in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg` (plus its coordinator) and none is a protocol violation; they share one reviewer's context and several share one file. F-142/F-143/F-145 are one key-hygiene pass.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group; all three lanes agree. F-146's POTENTIAL impact is high (a systematic transcript deviation means total interop failure) but NO deviation is evidenced — it is an assurance gap, filed as such. F-162's preconditions (attacker controls DNS for the DDNS name AND the peer is silent > 90 s) are strong, which is why AGY scored it NEG and the group keeps it at Low.

## Fix direction and acceptance

F-141: make crossed valid initiations yield a usable tunnel without a fresh trigger (or have the loser retry deterministically), or document the stall with a regression test pinning the recovery bound. F-142: correct the comment AND wipe at end of life (wrap with explicit wipe-on-drop, or rekey-to-random before drop), or record the accepted residual with its rationale. F-143: zero `out[..n]` on the `CryptoFailed` arm and invert the existing probe to assert all-zero staging. F-144: check MAC1 before MAC2 under load and derive the MAC1 key once per engine, with an op-count test pinning the per-junk-packet hash budget (all existing KATs must stay byte-identical). F-145: keep both secrets inside the locked `SecretState` — no plaintext `[u8; 32]` escapes. F-146: pin deterministic byte-exact handshake vectors in-tree, OR run `wg-interop.sh` on a recorded cadence with the last-green SHA visible to reviewers. F-162: document that hostname endpoints trust DNS for egress steering and surface resolver-driven moves in status.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

Nothing refuted outright. Two scope corrections are carried: F-142's claim is about the DEPENDENCY (snow), not first-party code, which already uses `Zeroizing` for PSKs and private keys; and F-143 has no live leak because in-tree callers honour 'on Err do not inspect out'.

## Deduplication

#4103-F12 is the key-hygiene standard F-142/F-143/F-145 are measured against; #4332 is the cookie bucket F-144 reorders around; `test/incus/HARNESSES.unreached:38` is F-146's registry entry. #9644 (OPEN) is a different WireGuard hot-path lock and is not a duplicate of any member.

## Why these belong together

## Severity and reachability

Low-to-Medium as a group; Codex and Claude SMR scored F-063 MATERIAL/Medium and AGY agreed, while F-064 split (Codex COHORT, AGY and Claude SMR MATERIAL). The actor for F-063/F-064 is the publisher or an operator running a recovery step, not a remote party, and `publish.py` remains fail-closed downstream — which is why the group is filed at the lower grade.

F-148: add `userspace-dp/rust-toolchain.toml` (or a `rust-version` plus a build-time `rustc --version` assert), make `make build-userspace-dp` fail loudly on a non-pinned toolchain, and correct the `debian/rules` comments.

Nothing refuted. The bound that matters is recorded: `publish.py`'s gate still refuses a tampered set, so F-063 is a break of the invariant at the signing step rather than a path to a published bad artifact.

## What this groups

Four release/install findings: two where publisher- or operator-controlled environment values reach a root-owned file without validation, and two where a guard and the read it protects are separate syscalls.

## Members, each located at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

The repo's own #5685/M40 rule is enforced at stamp time, not here | Codex NEEDS_VALIDATION Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-066 | `scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh:33-38,54` — SUITE is allowlisted; COMPONENT, ARCH and ORIGIN are not, so publisher-env control writes repo files outside `--out` (`COMPONENT='../../../../p4-escaped'`) and injects `Release` fields, including a leading duplicate `Valid-Until: 2099` ahead of the genuine one the build asserts — then GPG-signed into the published repo | Codex MATERIAL Medium; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-068 | `scripts/image/validate.py:888-927` — `verify_signatures` hashes the LIVE qcow2/metadata paths and the subsequent boot, import and `write_manifest` re-read those same re-openable paths minutes later, so a concurrent host writer during the gate window can make `validated: true` attest to never-validated bytes. Claude SMR found the asserted consequence CHANGED since the claim's base and the member is filed on the surviving window | Codex NEEDS_VALIDATION Medium; AGY NEG Low; SMR COHORT Low |
| F-147 | `scripts/image/xpf-day0-config:122,142` — the `-f`/`! -L` guard and the `head -c` read are separate syscalls against a medium whose backing store the hypervisor can mutate (the script's own threat model), so a mid-probe swap defeats the two-fixed-filenames guard: a fifo stalls the copy (bounded by the unit's 120 s timeout) and a symlink redirects the read to a host-side path | Codex COHORT Low; AGY COHORT Low; SMR COHORT Low |

## Why these belong together

Two pairs that share one review: unvalidated environment input reaching a root-owned file (F-065/F-066), and check-then-use against mutable media (F-068/F-147). Both pairs have the same fix grammar — validate before any host mutation; open once and operate on the fd.

## Severity and reachability

Low as a group. Codex scored F-065 NEEDS_VALIDATION and F-066 MATERIAL/Medium; AGY and Claude SMR scored the group COHORT/Low. The actor is a publisher, an operator, or a host writer with concurrent access to the bake directory — not a remote party. For F-147 the downstream backstops hold (size cap, strict commit-check on the private copy, nothing installed on reject), so it is guard-bypass hardening rather than config injection.

## Fix direction and acceptance

F-065: mirror `validate_apt_url` in `install.sh:validate()` (https-only; no whitespace, controls, metacharacters, userinfo, query, fragment or `%`) and die before any host mutation, keeping env > baked precedence. F-066: allowlist COMPONENT/ARCH (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*`) and ORIGIN (single-line printable), die before any write, and assert the emitted `Release` contains exactly one `Valid-Until` equal to the `ValidTime`-derived value. F-068: verify-then-freeze (private 0700 staging; import, scenarios and manifest hashing against the staged copies), or re-assert the digest immediately before `write_manifest` and die on drift. F-147: open media files with `O_NOFOLLOW` and `fstat` the fd, treating a symlink or `ENXIO` as skip, with a small per-file timeout.

## What was refuted or narrowed along the way

F-068's asserted consequence changed since the claim's base and is filed narrower. F-147's injection framing is refuted by the downstream backstops and it is filed as guard-bypass plus bounded-stall hardening.

## #9923 — config: the #9871 group-container change drops a scalar wildcard leaf, silently accepts a compact zone member that was strictly refused, and loses a split-stanza group body [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## Summary

The group-container work that landed in PR #9871 (merge `4cc9b66e6`) introduced
three regressions. They are measured, not traced: verified at `ef390f3ac`
against `4cc9b66e6`.

This issue exists so master's state is visible on the board while the forward
fix is built. The owning lane is fixing forward on a branch off current master
(not reverting), and this issue closes with that fix.

## Measured behaviour

| case | before `4cc9b66e6` | after |
|---|---|---|
| `description "<*>"` inside a wholesale-adopted group container | kept | **dropped silently** |
| compact zone member `interfaces <ge-*>;` | strict **REFUSES** (`references interface <ge-*>`) | **commits clean, member gone** |
| block member `interfaces { <ge-*>; }` | refuses | refuses (unchanged) |
| group body with `screen` AND `zones`, target splitting them across two stanzas | `trust.ScreenProfile = edge` | **`edge` lost** |

## Causes

**1. The prune keys on node SHAPE, not on position.** The predicate is
`!IsLeaf || len(Keys) >= 2`. An ordinary two-key leaf (`description "<*>"`) and a
compact member (`interfaces <ge-*>`, `Keys = [interfaces, <ge-*>]`) both satisfy
it. The second is the serious one: it converts a **loud strict refusal into a
silent acceptance**, which is the failure direction that does not get noticed.

**2. The routing bundles all non-wildcard children to a single receiving
stanza.** The design said route each child to where its match lives; the
implementation sends them all to the stanza that matched first, so the other
stanza is never reached. For the split-stanza shape this is **worse than the
pre-change behaviour**.

## Why the matrix did not catch it

The change shipped a 6/6-killed mutation matrix. **Every cell used the BLOCK
spelling** (`interfaces { <ge-*>; }`), which is the row that did not regress.
The log described "three spellings"; they were three *placements* of one
spelling. A fixture set pinned to one value of a parameter the code varies over
is a denominator, not a control — no cell could have caught this, however well

## #9924 — userspace-dp: the shared-secondary and AUTO XSK bind rows do not request XDP_BIND_NEED_WAKEUP (or zero-copy), relying on an unstated kernel pool-inheritance rule [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

Small, but it is the second place in this review where the tree depends on an AF_XDP kernel rule it does not write down; the cost of making the request explicit is one flag.

## Mechanism, at `5fe2964417c3cebdd72402e733efb8a141d32e7c`

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bind.rs:5,9,195-205` — the shared-secondary and AUTO rows omit `XDP_BIND_NEED_WAKEUP`; `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/rings.rs:145-149` is the 500 microsecond `FILL_WAKE_SAFETY_INTERVAL_NS` net that covers the case when `needs_wakeup()` is false. The post-hoc zero-copy check means ZC is negotiated by auto-mode outcome and then refused group-wide rather than requested.

## Contract

A socket that drives a fill ring should request the bind flags its wake path depends on, and the repo should not depend on a kernel inheritance rule it never states.

## Reachability and actor

Not adversarial — a configuration with shared-UMEM secondary sockets or AUTO mode under fill pressure.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC (three lanes at the pin) + EXECUTED (the source report's hermetic flag-matrix probe at base)
- `Probe`: No new execution (no kernel AF_XDP interaction available here). The source report's probe is hermetic and only pins the flag matrix, not kernel behaviour.
- `Trace`: secondary/AUTO bind without the flag -> `needs_wakeup()` false -> fill submits rely on the 500 microsecond safety net rather than a prompt kick, UNLESS the owner pool already set the flag (Claude SMR's point).
- `Refutation attempt`: Recorded and decisive for severity: the NEED_WAKEUP flag lives on the UMEM pool, so a socket sharing that pool behaves as the pool was bound. AGY's own refutation adds that the safety-net timer fires regardless, and TX always force-kicks. What survives is an inconsistency in what the rows REQUEST and a dependency on an unstated kernel rule.
- `HPC/invariant check`: Worst case without the flag and without inheritance is up to 500 microseconds of added fill latency per cycle under pressure; no RX drop was measured, and the mlx5 `rx_xsk_buff_alloc_err` signal the claim predicts was not observed here.
- `Severity`: **Low** — see Reachability
- `Confidence`: Medium

## Fix direction and acceptance

Add NEED_WAKEUP (and an explicit zero-copy request, consistent with the post-hoc check) to the secondary and AUTO bind rows, or record the pool-inheritance rule beside them with a citation; extend the existing flag-matrix probe to whichever is chosen. No primary-row behaviour change. Acceptance: the probe pins the new matrix and the 500 microsecond net is left as a net, not as the mechanism.

## Deduplication

Same 'unstated external contract' family as the members of the AF_XDP contract cohort filed in this run; kept separate because its fix is a bind-flag change rather than a documentation change.

## #9925 — userspace: a fabric interface with no local member gets no AF_XDP ingress target, so it forwards nothing [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## What happens

A fabric interface with configured `fabric-options member-interfaces` but NO resolved local member gets no AF_XDP ingress target at all, so traffic on it never reaches userspace forwarding. Two independent mechanisms combine:

1. **No fabric snapshot.** `buildFabricSnapshotsFrom` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/fabric.go:79-81`) returns `nil` when `cfg.Chassis.Cluster == nil`. With a cluster it builds only from `cc.FabricInterface` / `cc.Fabric1Interface` — and `pkg/config/compiler_derivations.go` auto-populates those "only if the local node has a member", i.e. only when `LocalFabricMember` resolved. So a fabric with members and no local one produces no snapshot **with or without a cluster**.
2. **The interface row is excluded by name.** `netdevExclusionClasses` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/ingress_exclusions.go:139-141`) drops every interface whose base name starts with `fab`.

The members themselves are not zoned — the zone references `fab0.10` — so nothing else supplies a target either. The Rust helper then binds neither the bond nor its member NICs.

```
set interfaces fab0 mtu 1400
set interfaces fab0 vlan-tagging
set interfaces fab0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-1/0/0
set interfaces fab0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-2/0/0
set interfaces fab0 unit 10 vlan-id 10
set security zones security-zone fabric interfaces fab0.10
```

L3 state is correct for this shape — `pkg/routing/bond.go` builds the bond, and addresses and MTU are actuated against it — which is what makes the gap quiet: the interface looks configured and carries no forwarding.

## Why it is filed separately

Found by an adversarial review of #9872, which is an MTU-ownership fix in the same shape. This is a MISSING BINDING, not a wrong write, it predates #9872, and fixing it means deciding what the AF_XDP attachment target for a bond even is — the bond master or the member NICs — which is a dataplane design question rather than a planner one.

## What a fix has to decide

- **Which netdev carries the XDP program for a bond fabric.** A bond master's XDP support is driver-dependent; attaching per member is the other option and interacts with the `redirect_capable` fallback.
- **Whether the `fab` name exclusion should be keyed on the name at all.** It currently excludes by prefix, which is why a legitimately zoned fabric row disappears; keying it on "this interface is handled by the fabric snapshot path" would exclude only what is actually handled elsewhere.
- **Whether this shape should be refused at commit instead.** If a fabric with no local member is not a supported deployment, rejecting it with a clear message is cheaper than binding it — but that is a product decision, and the config compiler accepts it today.

Severity MED: it is silent, and the affected configuration is accepted by strict compilation.

## #9927 — dataplane: a directly zoned fabric member still plans its own MTU over the fabric's, because ownership is decided per reference [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What happens

MTU ownership in `planPhysDesired` is decided per zone REFERENCE, not per resolved netdev. A zone can reference both a fabric interface and, directly, the physical member that fabric resolves to — and strict compilation accepts it:

```
set chassis cluster cluster-id 1
set chassis cluster node 0
set interfaces fab0 mtu 9000
set interfaces fab0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-0/0/0
set interfaces fab0 unit 0
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 mtu 1500
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/24
set security zones security-zone fabric interfaces fab0.0
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
```

Both references resolve to `ge-0-0-0`. The fabric one is correctly suppressed — the fabric setup renames that member and builds the IPVLAN on it, so it owns the MTU (#9872). The DIRECT reference is not a fabric reference at all: `ge-0/0/0` has no `FabricMembers` and no `LocalFabricMember`, so the ownership test returns false and the plan writes its 1500 over the fabric's 9000.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed in #9872

#9872 made the exception ask about the RESOLVED netdev rather than the configuration, which is the right shape, but it still asks that question one reference at a time. Closing this needs a pre-pass: compute the set of netdevs a fabric component owns for the whole config first, then suppress EVERY reference that targets one, whichever interface it came through. That is a structural change to the planner's shape rather than a predicate fix, and it is worth doing on its own with its own cells.

It also predates #9872: the direct reference was never suppressed on master either.

## What a fix has to get right

- The pre-pass must be keyed on the resolved netdev, since that is the thing with one owner. Two references resolving to one netdev is exactly the case #8119/#8120 addressed for addresses and unit MTUs.
- It must not suppress a write on a netdev whose fabric interface is itself not owned by anything — the slash-bearing-name case in #9872, where `bond.go` cannot create the device because Linux rejects the name.
- A cell should carry both references in one config, in both zone orders, since the planner walks zones in sorted order and the defect is order-independent only if the suppression is global.

Severity MED: it is silent, both references are accepted by strict compilation, and the losing value is the fabric MTU, which is the one that matters for fabric forwarding. Found by an adversarial review of #9872.

## #9928 — routing: an adopted bond keeps its old MTU, because bond.go writes MTU only on create [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What happens

`pkg/routing/bond.go` adopts an existing bond device without reconciling its MTU. When the reconciler finds a bond already present whose signature it can track, it keeps it (`LinkByName` hit, `isBond`, tracked or KEEP) — but the MTU is only ever set on CREATE, in `createBond` (`bond.LinkAttrs.MTU = ifc.MTU`, under `if ifc.MTU > 0`).

So a bond left at 1500 by a previous configuration, or by a previous daemon run, stays at 1500 while the committed config asks for 1400. Nothing reports a difference: the bond's members, mode and name all match, so the signature comparison is satisfied and the device is adopted as-is.

```
# previous config, applied, bond created at 1500
set interfaces bond0 mtu 1500
set interfaces bond0 fabric-options member-interfaces ge-0/0/4

# then, on a running box or after a daemon restart
set interfaces bond0 mtu 1400          # bond0 stays at 1500
```

## Why it matters more now

It has always been true, but #9872 makes it the only path to that device's MTU. Before, the zone-interface planner also wrote an MTU onto a bond-owned device; that was a SECOND writer with a different value (the alternating state #8119/#8120 removed for the untagged path), so #9872 made the bond manager the single writer. A single writer that only writes on create leaves the device on whatever it was.

The same applies to the `KEEP` path.

## Fix

Reconcile the observed MTU on adopt and on KEEP: read the existing link's MTU, compare against `ifc.MTU`, and `LinkSetMTU` when they differ — the same shape the fabric IPVLAN path already uses (`daemon_ha_fabric.go` raises the parent to 9000 whenever it is lower). Decide explicitly what `ifc.MTU == 0` means for an adopted bond: today it means "write nothing on create", and it should probably keep meaning "leave it alone" rather than reset to a default.

## Cells

- an existing bond at 1500 adopted under a config asking 1400 ends at 1400;
- an existing bond at 1400 under the same config issues no write (no churn per apply);
- `ifc.MTU == 0` leaves an adopted bond's MTU untouched;
- the KEEP path carries the same two.

Found by an adversarial review of #9872, which classified it FOLLOW-UP: pre-existing, and not a reason to withhold that fix. Severity MED — it is silent, and the surviving value is the stale one.
