## #9931 — userspace-dp: libelf, zlib and zstd are linked from the host with no recorded version, no range and no shadowing guard [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is missing

#9726 gives libxdp and libbpf provenance: each is snapshotted into `OUT_DIR` under a unique name, linked by that name, range-checked, and reported in `ProcessStatus`. Three statically linked siblings get none of that.

`userspace-dp/build.rs` emits them as bare names:

```rust
println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=elf");
println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=z");
println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=zstd");
```

A `-Wl,-Map` trace of a real build shows where they come from — the host, via the compiler's own search path:

```
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15/../../../x86_64-linux-gnu/libelf.a
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15/../../../x86_64-linux-gnu/libz.a
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15/../../../x86_64-linux-gnu/libzstd.a
```

So for these three the binary has: no recorded version, no declared range, and no `debian/control` build-dependency bound of the kind libxdp carries.

## Why it is worth an issue rather than a README line

They are **bare `-l` names**, which is precisely the defect #9726's round 6 found for libbpf: any `-L` landing ahead of the build-script paths — `cargo rustc -- -Lnative=...`, RUSTFLAGS, a rustc wrapper, a dependency's search directory — resolves the name from there instead. For libbpf that was demonstrated, not argued: under `-Lnative=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` the link took 17 distinct members from the host's libbpf 1.7.0 while the build reported the vendored 1.6.3. The same mechanism applies to `-lelf`, `-lz` and `-lzstd` because they are resolved the same way.

Stated honestly: I have NOT measured the substitution for these three. The mechanism is identical and the libbpf case is measured, but the claim here is structural, and a fix should start by reproducing it the same way — a link map under a hostile `-L`, with the negative case shown.

The reason this needs an owner is that #9726's merged PR reads as "provenance is solved for the helper's static libraries". It is solved for the two that the issue named. Someone reading `ProcessStatus` later will reasonably assume the rest are covered.

## What a fix has to decide

- **Is provenance wanted for all three, or only recording?** libelf/zlib/zstd are ordinary distro libraries with stable ABIs; a recorded version plus a `debian/control` bound may be enough, without the snapshot machinery.
- **If snapshotting: is the unique-name treatment worth three more copies?** It is ~10 MB per build and the same `prepare_snapshot_dir` sweep already exists. The alternative is accepting them as host-supplied and saying so in `ProcessStatus` explicitly, which at least makes the boundary visible at runtime rather than only in a README.
- **Where the versions come from.** Unlike libxdp there is no pkg-config `--modversion` guarantee for a static-only install of these; the fix needs to establish what it can actually read before promising a recorded version.

Severity MED: nothing is wrong in a normal build, and the exposure is the same class #9726 closed for its two named libraries. Found while closing #9726's round 6; the README there states the gap, and this issue is what owns it.

## #9932 — config: `family inet dhcp;` with the brace elided compiles DHCP=false and commits clean — the flat-set spelling is correct, the text spelling is not [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

`interfaces <if> unit 0 family inet dhcp;` written with the `family` brace elided
compiles to `DHCP=false`, commits clean, and emits no warning. The interface ends
up with no address and no DHCP client.

## Measured

At `5aad283ea` (the #9620 H11 fix applied — this member SURVIVES it), lenient
compile, reading the whole compiled JSON:

| spelling | strict | `DHCP` |
|---|---|---|
| `unit 0 { family inet { dhcp; } }` — fully braced | OK | **true** |
| `unit 0 { family inet dhcp; }` — `family` brace elided | OK | **false** |
| `unit 0 family inet dhcp;` — `unit` and `family` elided | OK | **false** |

## The flat-set path is NOT affected

This is the fact that bounds the blast radius, so it is worth stating plainly —
the `set` spelling an operator types interactively is correct:

| input | `DHCP` |
|---|---|
| `set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet dhcp` | **true** |
| the same, then `… family inet address 10.0.0.1/24` | **true** |

`SetPath` builds `family inet` with `dhcp` as a CHILD. The hierarchical text
parser puts it on the container head's `Keys` instead.

So the exposure is configuration TEXT — a saved config, a `load merge`, a config
restored from backup, a golden file in the tree — not the interactive CLI.

## Cause

`compiler_interfaces.go:456` reads the family node with
`afNode.FindChild("dhcp")`. In the elided text spelling the parser produces one
node with `Keys=["family","inet","dhcp"]` and no children, because `family` is
`compoundKey: true` and the trailing token lands on `Keys`. The family node is
still matched on its first two keys, so the compiler finds the family and the
third key is simply never read.

## #9937 — [cohort] three in-code comments assert facts that are false — including an import cycle that does not hold for the leg it names [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## Summary

Three in-code comments assert facts about the code that are **false at `b2c0c4c1b`**. Each was verified individually; one of them actively deters a valid refactor, which is what makes this a defect rather than tidiness.

This is the same class as the four Miri-coverage comments corrected in #9499: a comment that states a constraint or a protection which does not exist is read as authoritative, and the cost is paid by whoever believes it.

## The three

**1. `pkg/api/exec_timeout.go:9-18` — an import cycle that does not hold for the leg it names.**

The comment says the shared helper "cannot be imported here: pkg/daemon imports pkg/api (daemon_run.go), so a shared helper would create an import cycle", and then points at `pkg/grpcapi` as carrying the sibling copy.

The `pkg/daemon` half is true. The implication that the duplication is therefore forced is **not**: `pkg/api/dhcp.go:11` **already imports `github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/grpcapi`**, so there is no cycle on that leg and the two copies could share. Verified by reading both files at `b2c0c4c1b`.

Consequence: a maintainer who reads this comment concludes the duplication is structural and leaves it. That is a false constraint, and it is the most expensive of the three because it is load-bearing for a decision.

**2. `pkg/config/sync_auth.go:67` — a legacy set stated as "<=26" that now runs to 37.**

The bound is stale. A reader sizing anything against it, or writing a cell that asserts it, inherits a number that the code has already passed.

**3. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:562` — names a hook that is never wired.**

The comment describes a mechanism by name; no wiring for it exists. Same shape as the #9499 case: the sentence is about the code's *shape* and false about the world.

## Why file rather than fold into a passing PR

A comment asserting a false constraint is not a formatting matter — item 1 changes what a maintainer believes is possible. Filing keeps it visible rather than dependent on someone remembering; the fix is small and this issue closes with it.

## Acceptance

- Item 1: the comment states which leg the cycle actually blocks (`pkg/daemon`) and that the `pkg/grpcapi` leg is not blocked, or the duplication is removed on that leg.
- Items 2 and 3: corrected to what is true at the head they are fixed on, with the tree named — a bound restated without its tree rots the same way.
- No claim in any of the three asserts a protection or constraint that cannot be pointed at in the source.

## Provenance

Found during research on the modularity refactor audit (`muse-spark-unknown`, REVIEW_SLUG `modularity-refactor-audit`). The audit itself produced **zero** filable defects across 99 claims; these three were coordinator residuals found while verifying it, and were deliberately held back from the audit's own ledger because they are not modularity findings. Each verified independently at `b2c0c4c1b` before filing.

## #9938 — [cohort] authz: the deny-configuration gate adjudicates the RAW WIRE STRING, not the path the store acts on — three escapes on one lever [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What this groups

Three ways a `deny-configuration` regex is evaluated against a string that is not the path the
configuration store actually edits. They are one defect with three heads: `config.AuthorizeConfigMutation`
receives **raw transport text**, while every dispatcher receives a **lexed, verb-routed, possibly-two-path**
structure. A fix that adjudicates one string leaves the other two open.

## Members, each located at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts (independent first passes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-019 | `cmd/cli/shared.go:326-328` — the production `set` case sends `SetRequest{Input: strings.Join(fullPath, " ")}`, a **bare path with the verb stripped**. `pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:66-71` returns it verbatim (`case "Set": … return line, true`), unlike `case "Delete"` at `:72-78` which prepends `"delete "`. `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:99` splits it and `:72-74` returns `gated=false` because `parts[0]` is `security`, not a mutation verb — so `AuthorizeConfigMutation` returns nil = **allowed** | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR MATERIAL |
| F-020 | `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:99` — `parts := strings.Fields(line)` keeps quote characters, while the store lexes them away: `pkg/config/lexer.go:337-365` `readString` returns `b.String()` with the quotes consumed, reached through `ParseSetVerbGrouped` (`pkg/config/parser.go:244`) → `SetPathQuoted` (`pkg/config/ast_edit.go:355`). `deactivate security "policies" p1` is therefore **gated as** `security "policies" p1` and **applied as** `security policies p1` | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR MATERIAL |
| F-029 | `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:82-85` joins copy/rename into ONE string (`<verb> <src> to <dst>`), while `pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:155-180` `handleCopyRename` splits it into `srcPath` and `dstPath` and calls `RenameAs`/`CopyAs` on **two real paths**. The CLI twin is `pkg/cli/cli_config.go:52-61`. No per-endpoint adjudication exists anywhere — `grep srcPath\|dstPath` intersected with the authz files returns zero | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR PARTIAL |

## Why these belong together

All three are "the gate decided about a string the dispatcher never acts on". The structurally sound shape
is for the gate to receive what the dispatcher resolved — verb plus lexed token slice, **one decision per
acted-upon path** — rather than the wire text. Three separate string-level patches would each leave the
others open, which is why they are filed as one lever.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: an authenticated `configure`-class principal restricted by `deny-configuration` regexes — the exact
principal the feature exists to contain. F-019 needs no special condition on gRPC/CLI. F-020 needs a
multi-token denied path. F-029 carries a **stated precondition**: `CompiledLoginRegexes.EvaluateForms`
matching is UNANCHORED partial (`pkg/config/login_regex.go:35-43`, which cites Juniper's own guidance that
"You must use anchors when specifying complex regular expressions"), so a plain substring deny incidentally
catches both rename endpoints. The escape needs an **anchored** deny (`^security policies p1$`) — which is
the idiom Junos documents for complex expressions. Both directions (`rename <denied> to <allowed>` and
`rename <allowed> to <denied>`) are open under that condition.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin, three independent lanes; two lanes traced F-019 end to end through the
  production CLI path personally.
- `Probe`: no new execution. The source report records EXECUTED gRPC/REST E2E probes for F-019/F-020 at its
  own base; this run did not re-execute them (read-only research scope) and does not claim it did.
- `Refutation attempt`: F-019's **non-instance control passed** — this is not a surface-wide gap. REST

## #9939 — eventengine: a `then change-configuration` payload is never authorized against the planter's class and commits as root on a routine event [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

`event-options policy … then change-configuration commands "delete security policies …"` stores its payload
as DATA. The edit that plants it is gated by `deny-configuration`; the payload it carries is not gated by
anything, at plant time or at fire time. When the event fires, the engine applies the embedded
`set`/`delete` and commits with explicit **internal (root) authority**. A class denied `security policies`
but permitted `event-options` can therefore delete a guard policy autonomously on a routine RPM event.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- Extractor: `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:2175` → `EventPolicy.ThenCommands` (`pkg/config/types_chassis.go:212`).
  No class is recorded with the payload.
- Classification: `pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:24-30` `classifyPlan` walks `pol.ThenCommands`.
- Application: `pkg/eventengine/engine.go:772` `e.store.Delete(op.delPath)` and `:798`
  `e.store.SetFromInput(op.setInput)` — **no class argument, no authz call**.
- Commit: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:698` — `return d.commitAndApply(ctx, configstore.InternalCommitter(), comment, peerSyncNever)`,
  and `pkg/configstore/commit_authority.go:111-112` — `case authorityInternal: return nil`, i.e. no authority
  check runs at all on that path.

**Positive control for the absence claim.** `config.AuthorizeConfigMutation` has exactly **4 non-test call
sites at 1be0079** — `pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_rpc_9633.go:91`, `pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:48`,
`pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:167`, `pkg/cli/permissions_config_regex.go:94` — and **zero** in
`pkg/eventengine`. The same grep finds all four surfaces, so the pattern and path set resolve; the absence
is real rather than a bad search. (At the report's base the count was 3; `#9633` added the fourth.)

## Contract

A restricted principal's denied subtrees must stay denied whatever mechanism carries the edit. An
operator-authored automation payload is a deferred edit by that operator, not a privilege escalation into
root authority.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: an authenticated `configure`-class principal whose `deny-configuration` regexes exclude
`security policies` but permit `event-options`. Trigger: any configured event — the report names
`ping_test_completed`, which fires on an ordinary RPM probe cycle. No second principal, no race, no network
position. This is a classic confused deputy: the engine holds authority the planter does not.

## #9940 — nftables: a zero-rule lo0 render atomically replaces the live RE-protection table with an empty `policy accept` shell and reports commit success [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

When the lo0 filter spec lowers to zero rules, the installer still runs the atomic table replacement. The
live `xpf_lo0` table is deleted and recreated as an empty base chain whose policy is **accept**, inside one
netlink `Flush`. The caller records `lo0Enforced=false`, emits a warning, and returns `nil` — so the commit
reports success while every explicit host-bound deny that table carried is gone.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:205` — `if rules == 0 {` … `:226` `d.lo0Enforced.Store(false)` … `:234` `return nil`.
  The in-tree comment on that arm says the path deliberately installs no fence, because fencing on a
  SUCCESSFUL install would deny host-bound traffic on a clean commit.
- `pkg/nftables/netlink_installer.go:136` `InstallLo0` → `:149` `replaceTable`, which is `DelTable(tbl)` +
  `AddTable` + chain creation in a single `Flush`.
- **The decisive line:** `pkg/nftables/netlink_installer.go:164` — `policy := nftables.ChainPolicyAccept`.
  The sibling barrier chain chooses the other value at `pkg/nftables/transit_barrier.go:96` —
  `ChainPolicyDrop`. Accept here is a **choice**, not a library default.
- How a zero-rule spec arises: `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:175` `toNftLo0Spec` looks the filter up by
  name (`if f, ok := cfg.Firewall.FiltersInet[filterV4]; ok`), so a **dangling filter name** silently yields
  no terms. The door is `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_firewall_nat2.go:316-322`, where
  `validateFirewallFilterReferencesStrict` is downgraded to a warning under `opts.lenientFirewallRefs`.

Both cited files are **byte-identical** between the report's base and the pin; the `rules == 0` block is at
line 205 in both trees.

## Contract

A commit that reports success must leave enforcement at least as strong as it found it. An RE-protection
table that renders to nothing is a configuration error, not an instruction to open the host.

## Reachability and actor

Not adversary-initiated at the door: the strict commit path REJECTS a dangling filter reference. The
reachable doors are the tolerant ones — boot `Store.Load` of a persisted config and HA `SyncApply` from a
peer — which is exactly where a config authored under an older binary, or a peer running a different build,
arrives. Blast radius is bounded to the `xpf_lo0` table: `xpf_hostinbound` is a separate table with its own
transaction and is unaffected, so the source report's "all host denies evaporate" is **too broad** and is
filed narrower here.

## #9941 — userspace-dp: an unzoned tunnel's decap re-ingress resolves to zone 0, which host-inbound treats as ADMIT-ALL, so decap-inner traffic to the firewall skips two of the three LocalDelivery gates [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

A logical ingress that is not in `ifindex_to_zone_id` resolves its zone with `unwrap_or_default()` — zone
**0**. Zone 0 is not a deny sentinel: the host-inbound table treats an absent zone as *admit*, and the
junos-host policy evaluator returns early for `from_id == 0`. So a decapsulated tunnel packet addressed to
the firewall itself is admitted past both zone-keyed host gates.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/logical_ingress.rs:145-149` — `let ingress_zone = forwarding.ifindex_to_zone_id.get(&params.logical_ifindex).copied().unwrap_or_default();`
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:799-801` — the lookup's `None` arm is `true`, with the
  in-file comment stating such traffic "keeps the **admit** default".
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:3444` — `if !state.has_junos_host_rules || from_id == 0 { return None; }`.

The path is exercised, not theoretical: the shim sends **native** host-bound traffic to the kernel
(`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:757`), so the userspace LocalDelivery gates are reached precisely by
decap/worker-claimed inner packets — which is this finding's path.

## Two corrections to the original claim, both verified

1. **"All three LocalDelivery gates" is wrong by one.** The lo0 filter gate
   (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/filter.rs:1134-1184`) is zone-independent and still runs on any
   admitted packet; `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs:768-785` returns a default result only when no
   lo0 filter is configured at all. Two zone-keyed gates are bypassed, not three. A finding whose stated
   blast radius exceeds its evidence is the shape that gets laundered into an over-broad fix, so it is
   corrected here rather than repeated.
2. **A narrowing the report does not state.** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:643-649`
   arms a deny-all `ifindex_host_inbound` sentinel (#5659) for a zoneless interface **that registered a
   local address** and is not a lifeline. So an *addressed* unzoned tunnel unit is denied. The bypass needs
   a logical unit that registers no local target — an unnumbered tunnel.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: a remote peer of an established tunnel (GRE / IPsec / WireGuard) whose inner packet targets a
firewall-local address, where the tunnel's logical unit is unzoned and unnumbered. Consequence: direct
reach to RE-local services that a `host-inbound-traffic` or `to-zone junos-host` policy was written to
deny.

## #9942 — frr: the static-route renderer strips a `.0` unit suffix, so a `bind-interface st0.0` secure tunnel's route names a device that does not exist and LAN→tunnel traffic falls to the default route in clear [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

The xfrmi reconciler creates the secure-tunnel netdev under the **authored** `bind-interface` string
verbatim. The FRR static-route renderer unconditionally strips a trailing `.0` before emitting the route's
interface operand. With `set security ipsec vpn V bind-interface st0.0` the device is named `st0.0` and the
route is rendered against `st0` — a device that exists on no box. The route never installs, and LAN→tunnel
traffic follows the remaining default route out the WAN **in clear**.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

The two strings, verbatim:

- Device name: `pkg/routing/xfrm.go:106` calls `config.XFRMIfNameAndID(vpn.BindInterface)`, which returns
  `LinuxIfName(bindIface)` (`pkg/config/xfrmi.go:77`), and `LinuxIfName` replaces **only** `/` with `-`
  (`pkg/config/types.go:12-14`). Dots survive. `bind-interface st0.0` → netdev `st0.0`.
- Route operand: `pkg/frr/config_render.go:206-209` — `if strings.HasSuffix(ifName, ".0") { ifName = ifName[:len(ifName)-2] }`.
  Emits `st0`.

The repository states this rule itself, in the resolver's own doc at `pkg/config/xfrmi.go:84-91`:

> A secure tunnel is materialized by the xfrmi reconciler (pkg/routing/xfrm.go) under exactly
> `LinuxIfName(bindInterface)` — the AUTHORED string. … `bind-interface st0.0` creates a netdev named
> `st0.0` but `bind-interface st0` creates one named `st0`, and the unit ref is `st0.0` in both cases.

`pkg/frr/config_render.go` is byte-identical between the report's base and the pin for this arm.

## This is an un-owned site in a CLOSED migration

`Config.SecureTunnelUnitNetdev` (`pkg/config/xfrmi.go:142+`) is the canonical resolver introduced precisely
for this defect, and its own doc narrates the identical failure at the nft renderer: the snapshot said
`st0.0` while the renderer emitted `iifname st0`, so "a junos-host deny was scoped to a netdev that does not
exist … A security guard that cannot fire."

**Positive control for the absence claim:** `grep -rn 'SecureTunnelUnitNetdev' --include='*.go'` DOES hit
`pkg/config/types.go:321` and `pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go:1160` — the symbol and the search resolve — and
returns **zero** hits under `pkg/frr/`. Siblings `#6729`, `#6738`, `#6955` are CLOSED issues for this exact
defect at *other* resolvers; `#8994` (CLOSED) records that the centralizing migration was closed. The FRR
renderer was never in the tracked set (`#6728`–`#6731`).

## #9943 — dhcp/frr: option-121 classless routes defeat the DOCUMENTED "DHCP-learned routes are lower priority than static routes" contract — a rogue server's /1 pair beats a configured static default [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

The project documents, in four places, that DHCP-learned default routes sit at admin distance 200 and are
therefore lower priority than configured static routes. That mechanism protects only the **exact default**.
Option-121 classless static routes are installed with no prefix sanity, no override gate and no trust knob,
and a `0.0.0.0/1` + `128.0.0.0/1` pair from the DHCP server beats a configured static `0.0.0.0/0` by
longest-prefix match — at any admin distance. The documented precedence promise is unenforceable for the
route shape that matters.

## The documented contract

- `CLAUDE.md:435` — "DHCP-learned default routes get admin distance 200 in FRR (lower priority than static routes)"
- `docs/critical-patterns.md:180`, `pkg/dhcp/README.md:267`, `testing-docs/regression-checklist.md:63` — same claim.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:418-496` `classlessStaticRoutes` rejects only unparseable addresses and non-IPv4 masks.
  **Any prefix length is accepted.** (Positive control that syntactic validation exists and simply does not
  cover this: the same parser rejects `bits != 32` and folds `ones == 0` to the default gateway.)
- `pkg/frr/config_render.go:406-409` states the rule outright — the static-default suppression applies ONLY
  to the default route, because "classless static routes are more-specific and must not be dropped by a
  static default".
- Emission at `:447`/`:453` with distance 200. Distance is irrelevant to a `/1`: longest-prefix wins before
  distance is consulted.
- Management-VRF twin: `pkg/daemon/daemon_flow.go:358-380` `RouteReplace`s classless entries into table 999
  with no validation.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: a rogue or compromised DHCP server on a DHCP-enabled WAN interface — the ordinary untrusted position
for a WAN uplink. No authentication exists in DHCP, so no additional capability is required.

## The strongest refutation, and why the claim survives it in a narrower form

One reviewer refuted this as "the expressly implemented RFC 3442 contract — option 121 supersedes option 3,
and longest-prefix selection over a static default is normal routing, not a firewall bypass." That is
correct **about option 3 versus option 121** and is not the claim being made. The claim is about
**learned versus operator-configured-static** precedence, which is an xpf contract written in four in-tree
documents and implemented only for the exact-default shape. Filed accordingly: this is a
documented-contract-versus-behaviour defect plus a missing trust boundary, not an RFC 3442 complaint.

## #9944 — dhcp: RENEW/REBIND replies and NAKs are accepted on message type alone, with no binding to the server that granted the lease (RFC 2131 §4.4.5) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

The DHCPv4 renewal path accepts any ACK or NAK that matches the transaction id, and the DHCPv6 path accepts
any Reply. Neither compares the responder's server-identifier against the server that granted the lease
before accepting new parameters — or, for a NAK, before revoking the lease to INIT. The stored
`serverID` is used only as the RENEW *destination*, never as an acceptance predicate.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:289-290` — `resp, err := client.SendAndRead(exCtx, dest, req, nclient4.IsMessageType(dhcpv4.MessageTypeAck, dhcpv4.MessageTypeNak))`.
  Message type only.
- `pkg/dhcp/renew.go:95-100` `v4RenewDest` uses `serverID` to choose the unicast destination, and nothing else does.
- NAK arm `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:294-300` revokes to INIT on any xid-matching NAK.
- DHCPv6 twin: `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6.go:364-365`, matcher `IsMessageType(Reply)`; `v6ServerDUID` is echoed
  outbound only.
- Lease rewrite on acceptance: `leaseFromACKv4` (`pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:358-363`) replaces address, gateway,
  DNS and classless routes wholesale, and stores the new `serverID` unvalidated.

**Positive control for the absence claim.** The vendored client library ships exactly the missing matcher —
`nclient4.IsCorrectServer` at `client.go:420`, checking `p.ServerIdentifier().Equal(s)` — and uses it on its
own OFFER path at `:529`. The predicate exists, is in scope, and is simply not applied to the renew reply.
That is why this is an omission rather than an unimplementable ask.

## Contract

RFC 2131 §4.4.5: a client in RENEWING unicasts to the server that granted the lease and processes that
server's reply. A reply from a different server is not the renewal the client asked for. The practical
security contract is narrower and sufficient: a lease's parameters should not be replaceable, and a lease
should not be revoked, by a party other than the one that granted it.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: a DHCP-adjacent attacker — on-path, or able to guess the 32-bit transaction id inside the reply
window. RENEW is unicast, which is the only real mitigation and is not an authorization control. Once
accepted, the attacker owns the address, gateway, DNS and classless routes for that interface, which is the
entry point for the option-121 route-steering defect filed separately by this run.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin, three independent lanes, all three MATERIAL.

## #9945 — userspace-dp/screen: a SYN-cookie-validated client skips `syn_flood_gate` entirely, so the per-destination SYN-flood cap and every aggregate never charge [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

PHASE 0 of the screen pipeline short-circuits for a client present in the SYN-cookie validated cache. That
short-circuit skips `zstate.syn_flood_gate` completely — not just the per-source limiter, but the
**per-destination cap** and the aggregate accounting. The cap that exists to shield one victim host never
fires for a validated source, and the counters that would show it never move.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:938-940` — `if syn_cookie_validated { syn_cookie_bypassed = true; } else { … zstate.syn_flood_gate(…) }`.
- The in-source comment at `userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:910-911` states it verbatim: *"A validated
  returning SYN-cookie client bypasses the gate entirely."*
- The gate that is skipped, including the per-destination arm: `userspace-dp/src/screen/zone.rs:351-375,405-433`.

This arm is **unchanged** between the report's base and the pin, despite substantial churn in the same file
and in `zone.rs` — the three SYN-cookie PRs that merged in the window (`d278eb1da` #9173 key derivation,
`7c9278c71` #9740 zone-tag base, `3b7b85af3`/#9712 rollback policy) all touch key/zone-tag plumbing and
none charges the validated path.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: **one non-spoofed source** that has completed a genuine SYN-cookie round trip. The validated-cache
key is `(src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port)` (`userspace-dp/src/screen/syncookie.rs:138-142`), so this is not an
arbitrary-source flood — it is "a client that proved reachability once then floods that destination
unmetered for the cache's lifetime". That is exactly the population a per-destination cap exists to bound,
and it is the population an attacker with a single real host has.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin, three independent lanes, all three MATERIAL.
- `Probe`: no new execution in this run. The source report records EXECUTED evasion and control probes at
  its base (cap fires on the control, silent on the validated path).
- `Refutation attempt`: the bypass being source-scoped and requiring a completed handshake is the strongest
  refutation and is accepted — it is why the actor above is stated narrowly rather than as "any attacker".
  The refutation does not restore a rate limit; it changes who can reach it.
- `HPC/invariant check`: the fix is on the per-SYN path; charging the gate is the same atomic work the
  non-validated arm already does, so the cost is the existing gate's, not a new one.
- `Severity`: **High** — the flood shield does not fire for the one class of traffic the cookie mechanism
  labels trustworthy, and no counter shows it.
- `Confidence`: High for the mechanism; Medium for the blast radius, which depends on the validated-cache

## #9946 — daemon: the post-link-cycle `ethtool -K rxvlan off` re-disable is warn-only, so a failure silently re-opens the #5268 cross-zone VLAN-strip bypass while the commit reports success [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

Hardware VLAN RX offload strips the 802.1Q tag before the dataplane classifies the frame, which is why #5268
made it a **fail-closed compile gate**. But `programRethMemberMAC` cycles the member link (down → set MAC →
up), and several drivers restore offload defaults across that cycle. The tail that re-disables offload
afterwards only logs a warning and falls through, so a failure there leaves the NIC stripping tags while the
commit reports success and no fault is raised.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:717-722` — the re-disable in `finishRethMemberLinkTail`:
  `if out, err := runCommandTimeout("ethtool","-K",linuxName,"rxvlan","off"); err != nil { slog.Warn(…) }`,
  then fall-through. (The function returns an error only for the #6980 `LinkList` leg.)
- The fail-closed gate it is supposed to mirror: `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:898-912`, which calls
  `rxVlanOffloadActivationError` — and runs at **compile time**, i.e. *before* the link cycle. It cannot
  observe post-cycle state.
- Only one commit touched this file in the 462-commit window (`b1944b50b`, a heartbeat-restart change);
  the arm is otherwise unchanged from the report's base, where it sat at `:708-717`.

**Dedup search, with its control:** `gh search issues --state open "rxvlan"` returns **0** results; the same
search form for `"link-local"` returns 6, so the search resolves and the absence is real.

## Contract

A commit that reports success must not leave a NIC in a state the project's own compile gate classifies as a
cross-zone bypass. #5268 established that classification; this path does not honour it.

## Reachability and actor

Not attacker-initiated at the door, but attacker-*influenced*: a peer or a link flap causes the RETH member
cycle, and any `ethtool` failure at that moment (driver refusal, transient ENODEV during the up transition)
leaves offload on. The operator sees a green commit. No alarm is wired — positive control: this daemon does
raise alarms for other conditions (#9530, #2079 alarm paths exist), so the absence here is a choice rather
than a missing facility.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin; three independent lanes, all three MATERIAL.
- `Probe`: no new execution in this run. The source report records a STATIC tail-versus-compile-gate analysis
  plus an EXECUTED compile-gate contrast probe at its base.

## #9947 — [cohort] frr: two render/reload paths that keep a permit alive — a degraded additive reload defers stale removal, and a narrowed policy chain ships a permit-terminated subset [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

## What this groups

Two `pkg/frr` paths where a configuration change that should remove or tighten a permit instead leaves one
standing, with the commit reporting success and only a `slog.Warn` to show for it. Both files are
byte-identical between the report's base and the pin.

## Members, each located at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-007 | `pkg/frr/manager.go:1043-1064` — when the full-diff reload fails, the fallback is an **additive** `vtysh -f`, which cannot remove stale configuration; it returns `ErrFRRReloadDegraded`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:233` maps degraded → `nil`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go:224-227` warns and continues. An operator removing a permit-bearing route or BGP stanza gets a green commit with the old state still installed | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR PARTIAL |
| F-008 | `pkg/frr/bgp_policy_chain.go:71-83` — the file states it in-tree: *"A NARROWED chain -- some members survive -- is still rendered as the surviving subset here … Do not read the drop below as 'the reference is safely discarded.'"* The only handling is `warnNarrowedChains` (`pkg/frr/policy_chain_narrowing_warn_8363.go:147-171`), a pure `slog.Warn` whose own text says *"It changes no rendered output"*. A dropped deny-bearing member therefore vanishes and the surviving subset falls through to permit | Codex PARTIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR MATERIAL |

## Why these belong together

Both are `pkg/frr` renderers that answer "I cannot express what was authored" with "ship something weaker and
warn". They share an acceptance shape — the tolerant outcome must be deny-terminated or must fail the
commit — even though the code paths differ.

## Reachability and actor

Neither is adversary-initiated. F-007 triggers on any `frr-reload.py` failure during an operator commit.
F-008's reachable door is a dangling policy-statement name arriving through a tolerant path (boot
`Store.Load`, HA `SyncApply`, rollback), since the strict commit path rejects an undefined reference. Both
are ordinary-fault findings; no attacker is required and none is claimed.

## Evidence quality and the bounds that matter

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin; three lanes.
- `Probe`: no new execution. The source report records EXECUTED probes for both at its base.
- **F-007 is narrower than the report states, and the narrowing is load-bearing.** It is *not* silent:
  `pkg/frr/manager.go:119-123` sets the `xpf_frr_reload_degraded` Prometheus gauge and an in-manager retry
  loop reconverges, with `degradedRetrySlowDelay = 5 * time.Minute` (`pkg/frr/manager.go:79`). The exposure
  is therefore a bounded ≤5-minute stale-permit window with a metric, not an indefinite invisible one. That
  is why this is filed at Medium, not High, and why the acceptance below asks whether the gauge is actually
  alerted on rather than whether it exists.
- **F-008's consequence is asserted, not measured.** Whether FRR 10.6 falls through to permit on the
  surviving subset is the measurement `#7625` explicitly deferred. The *rendering* behaviour is certain; the
  RIB outcome is not.
- `Severity`: **Medium** for both — material but bounded incorrect behaviour on a supported path.

## #9948 — userspace-dp: a reversed embedded-ICMP error is queued as a prebuilt forward and `continue`s past the only zone-policy evaluation on that arm [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

Same-family embedded-ICMP reversal matches a quoted 5-tuple against a live NAT'd session, rewrites the error,
and queues it as a prebuilt forward. The queue arm then `continue`s — skipping the flowless transit
enforcement block that is the **only** site applying zone security policy on that path. An off-path sender
who guesses a live translated tuple therefore gets a packet delivered into the victim's zone without a
policy decision.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- Match, deliberately unconstrained: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/nat_match_v4.rs:80-92` passes
  `ReverseIngress::Unconstrained`; v6 twin at `nat_match_v6.rs:140`.
- **The decisive line:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4152-4157` —
  `EmbeddedIcmpReversal::Queued => { telemetry.counters.touched = true; continue; }`. That `continue` skips
  the `#3291 flowless transit enforcement` block beginning at `mod.rs:4171`.
- The queued frame carries a pre-computed resolution from `embedded_icmp/return_resolution.rs:20-30`
  (session-resolution reuse or a plain FIB + neighbor lookup — no policy) and `flow_key: None`
  (`embedded_icmp.rs:269-272`).
- **Positive control for the policy absence:** `poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs` contains zero occurrences
  of `policy` or `zone`, while the same grep over the same file DOES hit `egress` (:34,:102,:167) and
  `filter`/`cos` (:189,:216) — so the pattern and file resolve, and the rebuild genuinely runs no policy.

## What DOES run first, and why the claim is still filed

Two bounds that the source report omits and that a fix must preserve:

- **Interface input filters and PBR filters run before both ICMP arms**, deliberately hoisted there by
  `#7359` (`mod.rs:3975-4016`) and `#9528` (`:4020-4062`). An operator's `filter input … discard` is honoured.
- The path is **opt-in** via `set security flow allow-embedded-icmp`
  (`pkg/config/compiler_security_flow.go:717-718`). One reviewer went looking for the non-instance here and
  found the opposite: every reference configuration in-tree enables it (`docs/ha-cluster.conf:140`,
  `docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:149`, `docs/ha-cluster-loss.conf:152`). Treat it as effectively on.

## The recorded counter-rationale, and what it actually covers

`icmp_embed/nat_match_v4.rs:85-92` carries an explicit issue-7169 rationale for the unconstrained match: no
session is installed, and off-path ICMP errors are legitimate for PMTUD. That is correct and it justifies
the **match**. It says nothing about the **delivery** being un-adjudicated, which is what this issue is.
Two reviewers traced the caller-to-TX path independently and both reported the trace as decisive.

## #9949 — userspace-dp: the ICMP session key carries no query type, and an owner-zone session hit re-derives no policy, so a denied ICMP type rides a permitted type's live session [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

`SessionKey` has no ICMP type field, and the type is used only as an *admission gate* at parse time. Once a
session exists for a permitted type, a packet of a **different, denied** type with the same identifier
matches that session — and the session-hit path re-derives nothing, so the denied type inherits the permit.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `userspace-dp/src/session/key.rs:65-92` — `SessionKey` carries address family, protocol, addresses, ports,
  discriminator and routing domain. No type.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:1138` — the ICMP arm returns `Some((ident, 0))`; the type is
  consumed by the admission list (`:1103-1140`, `:1030-1039`), which for IPv4 admits types {0, 8, 13, 14,
  15, 16}. `junos-ping` (type 8) and an `icmp-type 13` term therefore share one key.
- **The #9519 authority check does not cover this actor.**
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_hit_authority.rs:154-156` —
  `if arrival_zone == metadata.ingress_zone { return HitAuthority::Owner; }` — and an Owner hit re-evaluates
  nothing. Only the `Foreign` arm reaches `foreign_hit_verdict`, which *does* pass `policy_packet_icmp`
  (`:216-241`). The attacker here sends from the same source on the same ingress, so the hit is Owner.
- **Positive control that the type dimension is a live concept and is simply not consulted here:** the same
  file calls `forwarding.policy.icmp_verdict_may_depend_on_type(meta.protocol)` at `:237` — on the Foreign
  arm only.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/policy_revalidation.rs:249-252` declines ICMP entirely when a
  type-constrained permit exists, and its stamp is generation-keyed — so in steady state (no commit) nothing
  is re-evaluated at all.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: a host that already holds one permitted ICMP query type to a destination. No spoofing is required.
The escalation is "may ping X" → "may timestamp / address-mask X" — same source pair, so it is not a
cross-host bypass. That bound is stated deliberately rather than left implied.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin; three independent lanes, all three MATERIAL.
- `Probe`: no new execution in this run. The source report records an EXECUTED 3-half probe at its base.
- `Refutation attempt`: the strongest — "#9519 re-runs policy on every session hit" — was checked and
  **does not reach this actor**, per the Owner arm above. The IPv6 surface is echo-request/reply only, so
  this is a v4 finding.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — bounded incorrect enforcement: a type-constrained deny is not enforced for a
  source that holds any permitted type.

## #9950 — [cohort] userspace-dp/fragments: enforcement runs before any overlap check, and the fragment association is forward-only, so reply non-first fragments leave untranslated [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What this groups

Three consequences of the same architectural fact — xpf associates fragments rather than reassembling them,
and the association it builds is one-directional. One is an enforcement-ordering gap, two are a
reverse-translation gap sharing a single root.

## Members, each located at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

| Claim | Site and mechanism at the pin | Three-way verdicts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-035 | `userspace-dp/src/screen/stateless.rs:49-51` — `if pkt.is_fragment && !pkt.is_first_fragment { return None; }`, so TCP-flag screens never see a non-first fragment; `:190-193` states the check "does NOT make [this] an overlap detector"; `userspace-dp/src/fragment_assoc/mod.rs:51` states "we ASSOCIATE, we do not RFC-reassemble". A first fragment earns the verdict; a later overlapping fragment rewrites the bytes the receiver reassembles, after enforcement | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR MATERIAL |
| F-036 | `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/frag_assoc.rs:213-219` — asserted in-tree (#7899): **both installs pass `reverse: None` and no caller anywhere passes `Some`**; `:256-258` the reverse association is a deferred increment. A DNAT **reply** non-first fragment therefore forwards untranslated, putting the internal server address on the wire | Codex MATERIAL; AGY MATERIAL; SMR MATERIAL (scoped) |
| F-053 | Same root, different placement: a pool-SNAT reply non-first fragment. The #6122 fail-closed probe `flowless_fragment_requires_nat_translation` (`frag_assoc.rs:346-453`) has five arms — src-SNAT/NPTv6-out and dst-DNAT/NPTv6-in/static-DNAT — and a reply fragment matches none of them, so it returns `false` and the packet forwards | Codex DUP of F-036; AGY DUP; SMR PARTIAL/COHORT |

## Scope corrections that a fix should not re-inherit

- **F-036 is `security nat destination` (pool/rule) only.** `security nat static` IS covered, via
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/nat_exception.rs:110-123`. One reviewer established this; the source report did not
  state it.
- **F-053's stated consequence is overstated.** For interface-mode SNAT the pool address *is* the egress
  interface address, so the packet resolves to `LocalDelivery` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/nat.rs:158-210`),
  not an L2 re-emission; for a distinct pool the FIB yields next-hop = destination → ARP →
  `MissingNeighbor` drop at least as readily as a loop, and the TTL is decremented
  (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:949,1009`) so any loop is bounded. And the untranslated field in the
  pool-SNAT reply is the **destination**, not an internal source — so F-053 carries no topology disclosure.
  It is filed as a cohort member of F-036's root, with its own placement cell, not as a second disclosure.
- **F-035 is a documented gap, and the issue is the ordering, not the missing feature.**
  `docs/feature-gaps.md:426` and `:360-367` already record that xpf does not reassemble, and
  `force-ip-reassembly` is accepted-only (`pkg/config/types_security.go:254`) with a commit advisory
  (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:719-741`). RFC 5722 binds the *reassembler*, and xpf never
  reassembles — so the RFC is not the lever. What is filed is that enforcement is applied to bytes the
  receiver may not be the ones to reassemble, with `application any` as the realistic permit.

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin; three independent lanes. One lane wrote its expected confound down

## #9951 — userspace-dp: an established session keeps its cached forwarding resolution across REMOVAL OF THE INTER-VRF LEAK it rides — a tenancy revocation the documented WAN-failover pinning was not scoped to cover [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

A session hit returns the resolution stored at flow creation and never re-runs the FIB. That pinning is a
**documented, deliberate** choice for WAN-failover parity. It was not scoped to inter-VRF leak removal,
which is a tenancy revocation rather than a next-hop preference change — and the policy-revalidation
machinery cannot see it, because removing a leak changes no zone.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/mod.rs:136-140` — `if allow_cached_fast_path { if let Some(cached) = cached_session_resolution(forwarding, decision.resolution) { return cached; } }`;
  `cached_session_resolution` (`:20-44`) accepts any `ForwardCandidate` with `egress_ifindex > 0` and a
  neighbor MAC, with **no generation term**. It is on the hit path (`mod.rs:1850`, `:1984`).
- The tree has two revalidate-on-session-hit hooks and neither covers routing:
  `revalidate_static_input_filter_on_session_hit` (`poll_descriptor/filter.rs:826`, #7212) and
  `revalidate_zone_policy_on_session_hit` (`poll_descriptor/policy_revalidation.rs:183`, #8356) — both keyed
  on `config_generation`, which `session/mod.rs:769-773` states explicitly does **not** advance on a
  `BumpFIBGeneration`.
- **Positive control for the absence:** `fib_generation` appears once in `poll_descriptor/` + `session/`
  non-test code at the pin, and that once is a doc comment (`session/mod.rs:771`); the identical grep for
  `config_generation` in the same directories returns 8 hits including a live write
  (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:158`). The routing dimension genuinely is not consulted on the hit path.

## The documented behaviour this issue is careful NOT to re-litigate

`docs/multi-wan.md:545-562` names `cached_session_resolution` and asserts Junos parity for established-flow
pinning across a WAN next-hop change, and `docs/pr/1827-pr3-nat/plan.md:130-143` concluded "No code change
required" for that case. This issue accepts all of that. The claim is that **removing an inter-VRF leak is a
different question**: the operator is withdrawing a tenant's permission to reach another VRF, not expressing
a preference between two paths to the same destination. A pinned session carries that permission forward
indefinitely, and #8356 cannot notice because the zones are unchanged.

## A correction to the source report, because it points a fix at the wrong file

The report names `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go:343-368,405-414` and `pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:371-384`
as "unfulfilled contracts". They are the **fulfilled** actuators: `daemon_apply_routing.go:426` and
`daemon_ipmon.go:375` each call `pub.BumpFIBGeneration()` after a real publish, and `daemon_ipmon.go:376-382`
carries a `pendingFIBBump` dirty-retry. The bump does invalidate the flow cache
(`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache.rs:999`). What it does not do is invalidate a session entry's stored
resolution — which is the actual gap, and is in `session_glue`, not in `pkg/daemon`.

## #9952 — api: REST never evaluates deny-commands / allow-commands at all, and `docs/system-login.md` claims it enforces all four regex statements [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

The REST surface enforces the coarse permission bits and the configuration-mutation regexes, and **nothing
else**. The operational command regexes — `deny-commands` / `allow-commands` — have no enforcement point in
`pkg/api` at all, so a principal whose class narrows its command set by regex has that narrowing ignored on
every REST endpoint. The documentation says the opposite.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- `pkg/api/authz.go:894` `readAuthz` → `readPermissionFor` — the coarse bit plus the #9324 candidate
  repricing at `:887-889`. No command evaluation.
- `pkg/api/authz.go:928` `mutationAuthzGuard` → `authz.Authorize(cfg, p, required)` then

## #9953 — nftables: a port-only lo0 filter term renders `th sport/dport` with no `meta l4proto` guard, so the transport-offset bytes of SCTP/GRE/ICMP are compared as ports [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-12)

## What is wrong

When an lo0 filter term names ports but no protocol, both render paths emit a bare transport-header port
match. `th sport`/`th dport` compare bytes at the transport-header offset **without any protocol
qualification**, so a non-TCP/UDP packet whose first four payload bytes happen to match is treated as
matching the term — turning a port-scoped deny or accept into a collision on the host path.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- Text oracle: `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_term_lower.go:217` — `parts = append(parts, "th sport "+term.SourcePorts[0])`.
  `nftTermProtocolPredicates(term)` at `:213` contributes nothing when the term names no protocol
  (`meta l4proto` is emitted only when `term.Protocols` is non-empty, `:119-149`).
- Netlink mirror, with the behaviour stated in its own comments:
  `pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go:225-237` — *"thPort appends a transport-agnostic 'th sport|dport [!=] <spec>' match (lo0, no l4proto guard …)"* — and `:443-446` — *"portMatch renders the transport-header port comparison … WITHOUT any l4proto guard"*.
- Sole lo0 caller: `pkg/nftables/netlink_lo0.go:141` `a.thPort(dir, ports, except)`, reached whenever
  `len(ports) > 0`.
- **Positive control that the guarded shape exists and is simply conditional:**
  `pkg/daemon/lo0_filter_test.go:1097` pins `want3 := "meta l4proto 17 th sport != 123 drop"` — produced only
  when the term *does* declare a protocol — and `pkg/nftables/netlink_golden_test.go:129` pins the unguarded
  `thPort` golden. Both render paths are unchanged between the report's base and the pin.
- The project applies the opposite rule elsewhere: tcp-flags matches are protocol-qualified
  (`pkg/daemon/lo0_filter_test.go:919-943`), so this is an inconsistency within one renderer, not a
  house style.

## Reachability and actor

Actor: anyone who can send SCTP, GRE or ICMP to a firewall-local address, where an lo0 term is written with
ports and no protocol. Direction matters and is the open question: the chain is priority-0 `input`, and for
AF_XDP-adjudicated traffic the userspace lo0 gate runs first, so an over-permissive accept grants nothing
*there*. The exposure is on host-bound paths that reach `xpf_lo0` **without** a userspace lo0 gate.

## Evidence quality

- `Verification`: STATIC at the pin; three independent lanes, all three MATERIAL.
- `Probe`: no new execution in this run. The source report records EXECUTED render and live-kernel netns
  probes at its base.
- `Refutation attempt`: checked and partially lands — see the direction question above, which is why the
  first acceptance item is an enumeration rather than a code change.
- `Severity`: **Medium** — a deny-to-permit (or permit-to-deny) collision on the host path, bounded by which
  ingress paths reach the kernel chain unadjudicated.

## #9954 — userspace-dp: `tcp-mss all-tcp` is applied only on the frame-BUILD path, so the generic in-place TX rewrite — the default path on a shared-UMEM mlx5 pair — emits unclamped MSS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What is wrong

The configured TCP MSS clamp is applied at exactly two sites, both on the copy/build TX path. The generic
in-place rewrite path applies none, and it is the path selected whenever the ingress and egress bindings
share a UMEM — which is the default grouping for eligible mlx5_core NICs, i.e. the normal transit path on
the cluster this project validates on.

## Mechanism, at `1be007963bf8188a5d06d96b974b60bf46794731`

- **Exactly two non-test call sites** of `clamp_tcp_mss_frame` in the whole crate:
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/build/ipv4.rs:87` and `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/build/ipv6.rs:70`, both
  guarded `if selected_tcp_mss > 0`. Definition at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/tcp.rs:787`.
  (The grep that produced that count hits both build sites, which is the control that the symbol and paths
  resolve.)
- `rewrite_apply_v4` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:901`) and `rewrite_apply_v6` (`:972`) contain no
  MSS call; `rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place` (`:1025-1105`) takes no `ForwardingState` and therefore
  **cannot** read `tcp_mss_all_tcp` even if it wanted to.
- Selection: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1022-1027` takes the in-place path when the bindings
  share a UMEM; the default `CrossNic` mode groups all eligible NICs
  (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/shared_umem.rs:52-58,92-148,250-252`).
- **Why this survives lab validation:** `shared_umem.rs:262-264` rejects `virtio_net`, so the standalone
  test VM always takes the build path and always clamps. The mlx5_core pair on the loss cluster is the
  configuration that does not. That is an explanation of the blind spot, not a mitigation.

All of these files are byte-identical between the report's base and the pin.

## Contract

`set security flow tcp-mss all-tcp <n>` is documented as clamping all forwarded TCP. A path-dependent clamp
means the configuration is honoured on some hardware and silently not on others.

## Reachability and actor

Not adversary-initiated. Endpoints behind the in-place path negotiate an unclamped MSS, which produces
PMTU blackholes and forces fragmentation on tunnel or lower-MTU egress paths — the failure `tcp-mss` exists
to prevent. One reviewer notes this is a configuration-enforcement and availability defect rather than an
admission bypass, and that framing is adopted here.

## #9955 — routing: the helper models the kernel's TWO-STAGE leak resolution (priority-ordered rules WITH FALL-THROUGH, then per-table LPM) as one sorted list — three divergences, worst is a blackhole needing no overlap [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

> **RE-SCOPED 2026-09-12 after the differential this issue asked for was built and run.**
> The original claim — overlapping leaks resolve differently — is **true but is one of three
> heads on a single modelling error**, and it is not the most consequential one. The differential
> is landed (PR #9982, `Refs`), and the acceptance below is rewritten accordingly. The original
> text is preserved at the bottom.
>
> Two things inverted during the investigation. The old body used the kernel's **fall-through on a
> table miss** to *narrow* the claim — "a divergence needs both candidate tables to resolve the
> probe". Nobody checked whether the helper models fall-through. **It does not**, and that is the
> worst of the three divergences. And the fix point the old body named — carry the ordering key
> through at the `routes.go` boundary — is **necessary but not sufficient**, for a structural
> reason given below.

## The defect: a two-stage mechanism modelled as one sorted list

The kernel resolves an inter-VRF leak in **two stages**:

1. **ip rules, in priority order, first match wins, WITH FALL-THROUGH** — a matching rule sends the
   lookup to its table; if that table has no route, evaluation *continues with the next rule* and
   eventually reaches `from all lookup main` at priority 32766. Prefix length plays no part.
2. **then per-table longest-prefix-match** inside whichever table was selected.

The helper models this as **one sorted list per table** — `sort_routes` orders by descending prefix
length then ascending preference, and the lookup is `routes.iter().find(|e| e.prefix.contains(ip))`
— with the leak arm ending in an **unconditional** `return lookup_forwarding_resolution_v4_inner(…)`.

Everything below follows from that one mismatch.

## Divergence 3 first, because it is the worst and needs no overlap at all

**A leak into a table that MISSES is blackholed, where the kernel forwards the packet.**

`lookup_forwarding_resolution_v4_inner` returns the recursive result unconditionally, so a
target-table miss becomes the final answer (`NoRoute`) instead of falling through to main. A single
leak is enough — no overlapping configuration is required, so this is reachable by configurations
the original title does not describe.

Measured: `a_leak_into_a_table_that_misses_does_not_fall_through_9955`.

## #9960 — userspace-dp/HA: a DECLINED synced delete tears the session down anyway and reports Applied — steering row, DNAT hold, worker fan-out and the return value ignore the decision [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary

`delete_synced_session_gen_marked` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/session_import.rs`) binds the **shared-map removal** to the under-lock decision, and nothing else. When that decision **declines**, five of the six teardown steps proceed anyway and the function still returns `SyncedDeleteOutcome::Applied`.

The session is left **torn** — neither kept nor cleanly deleted.

## Verified at `origin/master` = `590bffcfb`

`let removal = remove_shared_session_if(…)` is bound at line 940 and read as a gate at **exactly one** site, line 978. The final statement is an unconditional `SyncedDeleteOutcome::Applied`.

| teardown step | line | observes the decision? |
|---|---|---|
| kernel steering row deleted | 896 | **no** — runs *before* the decision exists |
| DNAT hold released | 924 | **no** — runs *before* the decision exists |
| shared entry removed | 940 | yes — declines |
| reverse companion removed | 977–978 | yes |
| worker fan-out `DeleteSynced` to every worker | 1025 | **no** |
| return value | ~1073 | **no** — unconditional `Applied` |

## Consequence

In the decline window — a local replacement appearing between the clone and the removal, which is the race the guard exists to close — the live local session:

- **keeps** shared authority and its reverse half;
- **loses** its kernel steering row, its DNAT hold, and every sibling worker's replica;
- and, because the function reports `Applied`, Go deletes its BPF mirror row too. The applied-set inversion faithfully carries the wrong answer onward.

Shared authority still lists the session, so **bulk export ships it to the peer**, and a **failover restores a session with no local forwarding state behind it**. The first symptom is an outage, not an error.

## Relationship to #9714 / PR #9935

**This is not a defect in #9935's stated claim.** That PR claimed the shared-map decision is bound to the entry it removes; that is true, and its F3a/F3b mutants measure it.

It is the **adjacent claim nobody made**: that the *rest* of the teardown is bound to the same decision. It is not — round 3 bound two of six.

The narrow regression is that `SharedRemoval::Declined` **did not exist before** #9935. Adding a decision without threading it created a state the surrounding code cannot represent: a refusal that reports itself as an apply. In the common path #9935 is strictly an improvement; this is a new window.

It also explains a row recorded there as *"unkillable single-threaded"* more narrowly than stated: F3c short-circuits the predicate, and single-threaded the predicate never declines, so nothing downstream can differ. The row is unkillable **because the decline path is unreachable in that harness**, not because the guard is inert — and this is the shape a concurrent harness would expose.

## #9975 — daemon: the fabric MTU floor is attempted, not guaranteed — all three LinkSetMTU(9000) calls are warn-only [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What happens

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_fabric.go` establishes the fabric MTU floor with three `LinkSetMTU(..., 9000)` calls, and **none of them can fail the apply**:

- the parent raise logs `slog.Warn("fabric: failed to set parent MTU 9000", ...)` and continues;
- the existing-IPVLAN reconcile calls `netlink.LinkSetMTU(existing, 9000)` and does not check the error at all;
- the created-IPVLAN write logs `slog.Warn("fabric IPVLAN: failed to set MTU 9000", ...)` and continues.

So the floor is ATTEMPTED, not guaranteed. On a NIC that cannot carry 9000 — hardware capped at 1500, a driver that refuses jumbo, an MTU an upstream bridge rejects — every write fails, the commit succeeds, and the fabric parent stays where it was.

## Why it matters now

#9872 made the tagged-parent MTU plan defer to that floor: a unit MTU **below** 9000 on a local-member fabric is suppressed, because the fabric would raise the parent and the two writers would alternate. That reasoning assumes the raise SUCCEEDS.

When it does not, the outcome is the one nobody chose. An accepted `set interfaces fab0 unit 0 family inet mtu 1300` on a 1500-capped member is suppressed by the planner, the fabric's 9000 write fails and is logged at warn, and the link keeps 1500 — the operator's 1300 is never written by anyone, and the only signal is a warn line.

The suppression is still the right default: at plan time nothing knows whether the raise will succeed, and planning 1300 against a fabric that will raise to 9000 is the alternating state #8119/#8120 removed. This issue is about the FAILURE path being silent, not about reversing that choice.

## What a fix has to decide

- **Propagate or retain?** The three writes could fail the apply, or record retry debt the way other daemon paths do (`recordDataplaneWorkerArmDebt` is the local precedent), or stay best-effort while REPORTING the divergence so an operator can see the floor was not reached.
- **What the planner should do when the floor is known unreachable.** If the daemon knows the parent cannot carry 9000, the ownership argument for suppressing a sub-floor unit MTU no longer holds — but that knowledge is on the daemon side, after the plan.
- **Whether "floor" is the right contract at all** for hardware that cannot meet it, or whether the fabric should adopt the highest MTU the member supports.

Until then the qualification belongs in the docs: the floor is what the fabric attempts, and #9872's suppression is justified by that attempt rather than by a guarantee. That wording is in `pkg/dataplane/README.md` and the planner comment.

Severity MED: silent, on a configuration strict compilation accepts, and the surviving value is neither the one the operator asked for nor the one the fabric wants. Found by an adversarial review of #9872, which classified it FOLLOW-UP: pre-existing daemon behaviour, not a reason to hold that fix.

## #9984 — eventengine: a change-configuration payload persisted before #9939 still fires as root, because the policy records no planting class [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## What remains after #9939

#9939 closed the PLANT: a `then change-configuration commands` payload is now
adjudicated against the planting class's own `*-configuration` regexes, at the
one moment a class is in scope, from the single evaluator every surface already
routes through (`config.AuthorizeConfigMutation`, so gRPC, REST, the on-box CLI
and `load` all get it from one implementation).

**A payload ALREADY PERSISTED before that gate existed still fires as root.**

## Why the engine cannot re-adjudicate it

At fire time there is no principal. `pkg/eventengine/engine.go` applies the
embedded `set`/`delete` and `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go` commits with
`configstore.InternalCommitter()`; `pkg/configstore/commit_authority.go` answers
`case authorityInternal: return nil`, so no authority check runs on that path at
all. That is not an oversight — the daemon really is acting on its own behalf.

The policy does not record **who planted it**, so the engine has nothing to
evaluate the payload against. Every substitute is unsound:

- *"refuse a payload denied to any regex-restricted class"* — over-denies a
  payload a superuser legitimately planted;
- *"refuse a payload that could not be planted today"* — that is the same
  question, and it still needs a planter;
- *"refuse every persisted payload"* — breaks every legitimate
  `change-configuration` policy on upgrade.

## What closing it takes

Record the authoring principal's class **with the policy**, and re-evaluate every
target path against it at fire time before applying.

That is a **config-type change**: the class has to survive persistence, `show
configuration`, rollback, and HA config-sync, which puts it on the helper wire
and in the peer's compiled tree. This repo's own record on that shape is that a
config-type field has repo-wide blast radius, which is why it was not folded into
#9939's fix rather than shipped as a smaller version of itself.

## Reachability, bounded honestly

## #9985 — dataplane: MTU ownership is decided per zone-reference, not per netdev, and the owner it defers to is a floor [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary

`planPhysDesired` decides **who owns a netdev's MTU** with a predicate evaluated
**per zone reference**, not per netdev. The same physical device therefore gets a
different answer depending on which reference reaches it, and the component it
defers to does not guarantee the configured value.

Found by a post-landing hostile review of the change for issue 9761 (round 14).
Not a regression from that change — the asymmetric half is older — but that
change is what makes the two halves visibly disagree, so this is filed against
master rather than reopening a closed issue.

All three consequences below are **measured**, not read off the source. Probe
output is at the end.

## The mechanism

`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go`, inside the per-zone-reference loop:

- the **tagged** branch (`vlanID != 0`) plans the interface-level MTU only when
  `ifCfg.MTU > 0 && ifCfg.LocalFabricMember == ""`, with a comment explaining the
  yield: *"another component owns the MTU of the device they resolve to … a
  fabric interface resolves to the local fabric member, whose MTU the fabric
  setup owns"*;
- the **untagged** branch, a few lines below, tests
  `ifCfg.RedundancyGroup > 0 || ifCfg.LocalFabricMember != ""` only to set
  `skipAddrs`, and then writes `pd.mtu = ifCfg.MTU` **with no ownership check at
  all**.

So the ownership premise is applied on one branch and not the other. One of the
two must be wrong: either the fabric owns the device's MTU and the untagged
branch is trampling it, or it does not and the tagged branch is dropping the
operator's configuration.

## Three measured consequences

**1. The MTU a fabric device gets depends on the taggedness of an unrelated zone
reference.** Same device, same `LocalFabricMember`, same `mtu 9500`:

| zone reference | planned MTU |

## #9988 — nat: a NON-NUMERIC static-NAT match destination-port is discarded to 0, which is the whole-address wildcard — installs every port, and both the warning and the 5101 fail-closed drop are structurally blind to it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

**Severity:** Medium-High | **Confidence:** High (executed) | **Source:** gemini-review-049 `GEMINI-049-036`, validated during the 8869 adjudication

## Problem

A static-NAT `match destination-port` token that does not parse as an integer is **discarded**, leaving `rule.MatchDestinationPort` at `0` — which every layer below defines as the whole-address 1:1 wildcard. An intended single-port rule therefore installs as "every port of the external address reaches the internal host".

`pkg/config/compiler_nat_static.go` (the `case "destination-port"` arm):

```go
if p, err := strconv.Atoi(nodeVal(m)); err == nil {
    rule.MatchDestinationPort = p
}
```

On an `err != nil` the token is dropped and the field keeps its zero value. Nothing preserves the raw token, so no layer below can tell **invalid** from **absent**.

## Measured, at `origin/master` 394aec7e2

Through `CompileConfigLenient` then the real `buildStaticNATSnapshots`:

```
case                                 stored  mapped  ExcludedReason                              outcome
well-formed  destination-port 443     443      0     ""                                          ROW INSTALLED port-scoped
NON-NUMERIC  destination-port http      0      0     ""                                          ROW INSTALLED as WHOLE-ADDRESS 1:1
NON-NUMERIC  http + mapped-port 443     0    443     ""                                          ROW INSTALLED as WHOLE-ADDRESS 1:1
OUT-OF-RANGE 70000 + mapped-port 443  70000  443     "destination-port / mapped-port outside…"   NO ROW (fail-closed)
no port statement at all (legit 1:1)    0      0     ""                                          ROW INSTALLED as WHOLE-ADDRESS 1:1
```

Rows 2 and 5 are **indistinguishable** — same stored values, same exclusion verdict, same snapshot row. The datum that separates them was destroyed at the config layer.

The wire contract confirms the reading. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_nat.go`: *"0 = match any port (whole-address 1:1, the legacy behaviour)"*, and `userspace-dp/src/nat/static_nat.rs`:

```rust
let (match_dst_port, mapped_port) = match (snap.match_destination_port, snap.mapped_port) {
    (0, _) => (None, None),
    ...
```

## Two guards exist and BOTH are blind, for the same structural reason

Enforcement is correct (Deny) and a dedicated `UNZONED_INGRESS_DENIED` counter exists -- the defect is attribution only. (Distinct from #8318, which covered enforcement parity; this is the record/render scope. In-source comment calls a distinct log reason 'worth doing on its own'.)

Diagnostic misattribution; enforcement correct.

Map the unzoned deny to the reserved unattributed id (a mapping change, not a new sentinel) or document the attribution contract; bind emission and rendering.

## #9990 — userspace-dp: refused peer delete and ICMP-error quote lookups mutate session lifetime state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
Two read-path lookups mutate the session they inspect. `handle_delete_synced` calls `lookup_with_origin(&key, now_ns, 0)` (delete_synced.rs:37) *before* the #9048 ownership-refusal check (:86-93), and the NAT64 ICMP-error matcher calls `lookup_session_across_scopes(..., 0)` (nat64_match.rs:272-279). The hit path in `session/lookup.rs:185-214` unconditionally re-stamps `last_seen_ns = now_ns` (:189) and completes `handshake_pending` for a forward TCP entry (:185-188), promoting it from the ~20 s opening window to the 300 s established window. A refused delete therefore leaves lifetime fields changed, contradicting the #9048 "lingers until it ages out" promise; an ICMP error quoting a flow can change its timeout class.

## Evidence (all three reviewers, independent reads)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/commands/delete_synced.rs:37-40,86-93` — lookup precedes refusal; refused arm returns without touching NAT/session-map, but the lookup already ran.
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:184-214` — unconditional `last_seen_ns` re-stamp; flagless handshake completion for forward `handshake_pending` entries.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/nat64_match.rs:250-281` — error-path quote lookup with flags=0 shares the mutating hit path.
- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Low, conservative)
Dual-primary HA (refused delete) or ordinary ICMP-error traffic (quote path) extends session lifetime and can complete handshakes without handshake traffic. Bounded: promotion requires an already-`handshake_pending` forward TCP entry, not any half-open entry.

## Corrective direction
Use a non-mutating probe for pre-decision inspection on both paths (or document refresh intent and narrow the timeout-class change). Keep the #9048 refusal semantics.

## Acceptance
- A refused peer delete leaves `last_seen_ns` and `handshake_pending` byte-identical; regression pins the 20 s window + unchanged stamp.
- An ICMP-error quote lookup does not refresh activity or complete handshakes.
- Coordinate F-004/F-069 acceptance (shared `lookup.rs` root) without assuming identical callers.

## Reviewer agreement
Unanimous MATERIAL (Low) across GLM-5.3-FLASH, gpt-6-astra, muse-spark-1.3 SMR. No dissent on mechanism; residual: ordinary PMTUD liveness-refresh intent is arguably correct for the stamp, but not for the timeout-class change.

## Provenance
Discovered by muse-spark-unknown deep-review `review-work.Hc25JksDtW` (full-firewall-002); validated through /research run `research-work.nyMnlhxBKd` (GLM-5.3-FLASH + gpt-6-astra + muse-spark-1.3 SMR, evidence rev 3). Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; cited files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## #9991 — session: lookup hit path never checks expiry -- traffic re-stamps idle-crossed sessions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
No `now > last_seen + expires` gate exists anywhere on the lookup hit path; every hit unconditionally re-stamps a fresh full window instead of re-admitting (no policy/NAT re-verdict). The 1 s wheel GC bounds the practical extension and #8356 re-validates verdicts, but the inspected lookup behavior contradicts a strict deadline reading, and the README 'lazy-delete on lookup' language is ambiguous (the phrase sits in the wheel bullet; expire.rs defines lazy-delete as the sweep's own discriminator).

## Evidence
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:60-229` (no expiry gate; unconditional re-stamp).
- `userspace-dp/src/session/expire.rs:70-169` (1 s GC gate ~:154-157).
- `userspace-dp/src/session/README.md:45-53,450-457` (ambiguous lazy-delete language).
- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Low)
Short windows affected most; wheel GC + #8356 bound the blast radius. Primary gap is specified-vs-actual deadline semantics.

## Corrective direction
Reconcile documented lazy expiry with lookup behavior, preserving HA retention; explicitly define deadline and sweep semantics.

## Acceptance
- Documented deadline semantics match lookup behavior (or lookup enforces the deadline); regression: hit 1 s past deadline is a miss (or explicitly specified otherwise).
- HA hold behavior preserved.

Unanimous COHORT. No dissent.

## #10004 — cluster: failed targeted/batch failover does not restore the cleared ManualFailover hold [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
Targeted failover clears the local manual hold (:360-365) *before* `commitRequestedPeerFailover`; on failure the arm calls `abortRequestedPeerFailover` (:374), which never re-arms the hold. Batch path (:900-907 + three failure arms) has the same shape. `ManualFailover = true` occurs only at the request-setters (failover.go:183,224,809) — no abort path restores it. The :352-354 comment promises hold preservation through preflight/send only.

## Evidence
- `pkg/cluster/failover.go:340-374` (targeted), `:890-921` (batch), `:975-984` (abort), `:183,224,809` (only hold setters).
- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Medium)
A failed operator-initiated transfer silently drops the operator's hold: the node no longer holds, with no record that intent was consumed by failure rather than success. Preflight/send failures preserve the hold; only the commit-failure arm loses it.

## Corrective direction
Failed targeted/batch transfers must restore preexisting hold state with request-matched ownership.

## Acceptance
- Commit-failure on targeted and batch paths restores `ManualFailover` + timestamp; regression drives failure after hold-clear and asserts restoration.
- Successful transfers still consume the hold exactly once.

## Reviewer agreement
Unanimous MATERIAL (Medium). No dissent.

## #10009 — termsafe: threshold emission can escape a trailing partial rune (chunk-dependent render) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
At the #7389 bound the writer emits the whole buffer (`line := s.buf; s.buf = nil`) with no truncation -- so the writer itself never splits a rune (continuation bytes cannot equal newline). The residual path is an upstream-truncated stream: an incomplete trailing rune is escaped bytewise by the sanitizer, so valid streaming text can render differently depending on write boundaries. Sanitization remains safe (never emits raw invalid UTF-8); the artifact is display-only escaped bytes.

## Evidence
- `pkg/termsafe/writer.go:45-114` (bound emission :74-80; whole-line vs whole-buffer).
- `pkg/termsafe/termsafe.go:140-179` (rune walk + hex-escape of invalid sequences).

## Impact (Low)
Display-only: byte-identical valid streams can render differently across chunk boundaries.

## Corrective direction
Optionally retain a bounded incomplete UTF-8 suffix during threshold emission.

## Acceptance
- Equivalent valid streams render identically across chunk boundaries (or the byte-fidelity/display-only behavior is pinned as accepted).
- Sanitizer never emits raw invalid UTF-8 (preserved).

## Reviewer agreement
Unanimous COHORT. No dissent.
