## Summary
`classifyFilterAddrFamily` uses bare `netip.ParsePrefix/ParseAddr`, which accept `%zone`; no `%` rejection exists. `recordFilterAddrTokens` keys on the same classifier, so the zone literal is never recorded and the Go-set `address_unrepresentable` marker (#6463 fail-closed path) never fires. At runtime `parse_address` (`std::net::Ipv6Addr`) rejects `%zone` and the Err arm pushes nothing — a silent per-token drop. #5875 closed the identical divergence for SNAT pools; filters still have it.

- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

A filter term over a scoped address silently loses tokens: the committed filter does not match what the operator wrote, with no diagnostic. Strict gate passes it.

Align address classification with runtime representability (reject `%zone` like #5875, or propagate unrepresentability through the marker) on strict and tolerant paths.

## Acceptance

## Impact (Low)
Fail-safe direction, but drop-state silently lost across reconfigs; repeated failure after no-op reconfig never re-establishes the published drop.

## Corrective direction
Preserve or explicitly rederive persisted drop-state semantics across reconfiguration.

## Acceptance
- Regression: hold-dropped feed + continued failure after no-op reconfiguration preserves drop semantics; recovery is not bounded by another hold interval.
- Documented non-carry rationale updated to cover #9689.

## #10015 — feeds: hold-drop warning and debug arms log unredacted transport errors (credential-bearing URLs) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
Go transport errors quote the URL dialed, and a dynamic-address feed routinely carries a per-tenant bearer token in its query string (#9164 comment). The hold-drop Warn arm (feeds.go:1150-1156) logs raw `ferr` unconditionally, and the default Debug arm (:1191-1195) logs raw `ferr`; meanwhile `enteredStale` (:1182-1190) redacts via `redactFeedURLInError9164`, which exists immediately below. The production-visible Warn path leaks credential-bearing URLs to logs.

## Evidence
- `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:1150-1156` (hold-drop Warn, raw `ferr`), `:1182-1190` (redacted arm + #9164 rationale), `:1191-1195` (Debug raw), `:1197+` (redactor exists).
- Stored error and stale-entry warning are redacted; transport errors reaching hold-drop are not.
- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Medium)
Per-tenant bearer tokens written to logs on a production-visible path. No exploit needed: ordinary feed failures emit it.

## Corrective direction
Route both raw-`ferr` arms through `redactFeedURLInError9164`; apply credential redaction uniformly at every logging boundary including hold-drop and repeated failure.

## Acceptance
- Hold-drop and repeated-failure log lines contain no query string / token material; regression feeds a token-bearing URL through failure and asserts redaction.
- Debug arm covered or proven mute in production.

## Reviewer agreement
Unanimous MATERIAL (Medium). No dissent. (This report contains no token material and no reproduction recipe.)

## Provenance
Discovered by muse-spark-unknown deep-review `review-work.Hc25JksDtW` (full-firewall-002); validated through /research run `research-work.nyMnlhxBKd` (GLM-5.3-FLASH + gpt-6-astra + muse-spark-1.3 SMR, evidence rev 3). Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; cited files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Summary
The worker send-failure arm logs Warn only — no `trapsDropped` increment — while abandoned/drain arms count. ## #10017 — snmp: GET of unknown-class OID returns noSuchInstance instead of noSuchObject [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
`getOIDValueSnap` collapses unknown objects and absent instances into nil, and both v2c (`agent.go:1340-1348`, whose own comment says "return noSuchObject exception" while the code emits `tagNoSuchInstance`) and v3 (`v3.go:375-414`, including unconditional noSuchInstance for non-default context) render one tag. RFC 3416 requires noSuchObject for unknown-class OIDs.

## Evidence
- `pkg/snmp/agent.go:1340-1348` (comment/code mismatch), `:1623-1684` (lookup collapse).
- `pkg/snmp/v3.go:375-414` (same collapse on v3/default-context + non-default paths).
- Coordinator-confirmed at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Low)
Protocol-conformance nit; no availability impact. Fix needs care: blindly swapping the tag fixes one class while breaking the other.

## Corrective direction
Return typed object/instance absence from the shared lookup and render the appropriate exception in v2c/v3.

## Acceptance
- Unknown-class OID → noSuchObject; missing instance of known object → noSuchInstance; regression covers v2c + v3 (do not infer v1 coverage).
- No regression on existing SNMP surfaces.

Defect agreed (2 MATERIAL + 1 COHORT — severity-only dissent, filed Low conservative).

## #10018 — nat: PersistentSourceKey omits routing_scope — cross-VRF persistent-lease sharing [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-17)

## Summary
`SourceNatFlowKey` carries `routing_scope: u32` (#9062, with docs requiring active/standby agreement), but `persistent_source_key()` builds `PersistentSourceKey { protocol, src_ip, src_port, remote }` WITHOUT scope. Allocators are not routing-domain-partitioned (#9389 removed that split). Tenants in different VRFs with overlapping subscriber IP space and `permit any-remote-host` persistent NAT therefore share one translation lease. Related family: #2387/#7160 (session keys, closed); this is the distinct NAT-lease corrective scope (allocator + #8121 idle-lease sync).

## Evidence
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/source/keys.rs:44-73` (scope on flow key, absent from persistent key); constructor docs never state the drop is intentional.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:107-119` (`PersistentSourceKey` fields), `:2041-2065,2172-2298`.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/idle_lease_sync_8121.rs:218-227`; `userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:293-327,380-389`.
- Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## Impact (Medium)
Cross-VRF lease collision/availability impact demonstrated; reverse-identity protection may refuse the second flow, bounding proven impact below confirmed misdelivery. Realistic reachability: overlapping subscriber space across VRFs with persistent NAT.

## Corrective direction
Include routing scope in `PersistentSourceKey` (and the #8121 idle-lease record) while retaining shared public-port occupancy; cover lease sync and address-only collision behavior.

## Acceptance
- Cross-VRF overlapping-subscriber persistent-NAT test shows distinct leases; HA active/standby agreement test passes.
- No regression in shared-port occupancy or single-VRF behavior.

## Reviewer agreement
Unanimous MATERIAL (Medium). No mechanism dissent; residual: full misdelivery vs collision-only impact needs the allocator-instance + #8121 sync trace (next check, not a filing blocker).

## Provenance
Discovered by muse-spark-unknown deep-review `review-work.Hc25JksDtW` (full-firewall-002); validated through /research run `research-work.nyMnlhxBKd` (GLM-5.3-FLASH + gpt-6-astra + muse-spark-1.3 SMR, evidence rev 3). Verified at 2ff10ecb7fd6; cited files byte-identical at master tip 7ef2264747e6.

## #10034 — userspace: replay HA inventory when snapshot retry-debt converges [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up residual of #9642 (filed per its plan review).

When a timeout-but-landed apply_snapshot is retained as retry debt, convergence happens through syncSnapshotLocked, which repeats only a subset of Compile's success tail: it does not replay HA inventory (refreshHAStateFromMapsLocked + syncHAStateLocked) and does not run the standalone clear. Convergence currently relies on the same consumers as the shipped pendingXSKStartup deferral path (UpdateRGActive on election + the 5s watchdog-only tick sync), plus — under the 9642 fix — a recorded pendingHAStateClear on standalone adopt.

That precedent argument may be sufficient, but it has never been asserted by a test: a clustered node whose helper was respawned by the debt path gets its HA inventory only via UpdateRGActive/watchdog, and the standalone transition relies on the newly recorded clear debt.

Ask: either add an explicit HA replay (or clear verification) to the debt-clearing success path with a fault-injected cell, or close this with evidence that UpdateRGActive + watchdog-only sync covers every bootstrap interleaving (clustered first apply, cluster-to-standalone with helper reuse, respawn mid-debt).

Refs #9642, #7468, #7465, #5487, #5873.

## #10035 — userspace: neighbor-replace exact-match fence (gen == applied) is indistinguishable from applied in the Go ACK [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Residual from #9696 (filed as the owned follow-up action from its plan review)

**Severity: very low** (structural hardening; no live path in-tree).

The Rust helper fences a replace when `generation != 0 && generation <= applied_manager_generation` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/mod.rs:712-716`, explicitly exercised for equality at `forwarding/tests.rs:1008-1010`) and ACKs `last_applied_manager_neighbor_generation()` — so a fenced `gen == applied` send is answered with an ACK **equal** to the sent generation, byte-identical to a successful apply. The response carries no applied-bit, and Go cannot tell the two apart.

Why this is not #9696: #9696 widens the Go arm to `ack != 0 && ack != gen`, which captures every DISTINGUISHABLE fence. Under the seeded single-writer invariant (strictly increasing per-manager generations, one `Boot()` writer, ordered synchronous control socket, helper applied taking only accepted sent values) every in-tree send has `gen > applied`, so exact-match implies applied and the residual is structurally closed in-tree — latent only for a hypothetical future pre-seed sender.

## Fix direction

Add an explicit applied signal to the neighbor-replace response (e.g. an applied-bit or an echo distinct from the applied-generation counter), version-gated like the other protocol evolutions, and key the Go success path on it instead of ACK equality. Low priority; file now so the analysis is not lost.

## #10050 — config: family inet arm unconditionally overwrites unit.MTU, so mixed-family MTU depends on statement order [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Found during #9837 parent review (2026-09-14; parent-filed). Pre-existing compiler quirk, independent of the #9837 gate (which correctly rejects exactly what the runtime would write).

## Observed
Families are visited in authored order (pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:404). The inet6 arm min-folds into unit.MTU (:570); the inet arm UNCONDITIONALLY overwrites it (:506). So with parent MTU 1400, family inet6 mtu 1300 before family inet mtu 9000 compiles unit.MTU=9000, while the reverse order compiles 1300. The compiled unit MTU - consumed by both the #9837 strict gate and the runtime writer (applyVLANSubInterfaceMTU9757) - depends on statement order.

## Acceptance
unit.MTU is order-independent (documented min-of-families, or a specified precedence); both authoring orders covered by cells asserting the compiled value; gate and runtime stay consistent.

## #10053 — config: per-member apply-groups-except for cross-group leaf-list unions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Defect

`apply-groups-except` through nested groups is node-atomic for leaf-lists: when a nested expansion unions members across groups into one node (`mergeLeafListInto`), per-member provenance is lost, so excluding one contributor keeps the whole union (under-exclusion, today's behavior preserved by #9862's tag-clearing) rather than dropping just that group's members.

## Measured

At the #9862 branch, with `G { apply-groups [ H1 H2 ]; }`, `H1 { system { name-server { 1.1.1.1; } } }`, `H2 { system { name-server { 2.2.2.2; } } }`, top-level `apply-groups G`, and `system { apply-groups-except H2; }`:

- compiled `NameServers = [1.1.1.1 2.2.2.2]`; per-member Junos union expects `[1.1.1.1]`.
- The direct (`apply-groups [ H1 H2 ]`, no nesting) shape filters per-group exactly, so nesting is what collapses it.

## Scope

Per-member provenance for leaf-list unions. The collapsed shape (`name-server 1.1.1.1 2.2.2.2`) carries members on `Keys` with no node to tag, so a fix must either track a parallel member-contributor structure or normalize before filtering — and it must keep the block and collapsed shapes identical (#4070 posture). Firewall leaf-lists (`match application`, `source-address`) under-excluded into a permit policy fail open, which is why this is its own issue rather than a shrug.

Pinned safety side (must stay green): `TestApplyGroupsExceptNestedLeafListUnionKeepsSurvivor9862` asserts a surviving group's members are never dropped, with follow-up-compatible superset assertions.

## #10054 — config: nested <*> group template never fans out at the destination [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Defect

A `<*>` template inherited through another group never fans out at the destination: the nested group's body is merged into the outer group's cloned body first (#4474 pre-expansion), and that inner merge wholesale-adopts into an empty clone — where `pruneWildcardInstances9802` drops the wildcard-keyed node as matching nothing by construction. The wildcard is consumed before the outer merge ever sees it.

## Measured

On base `68a4ec6fd` (verified by stash: fails identically with and without the #9862 fix):

```junos
groups {
  H { interfaces { <*> { description FROM-H; } } }
  G { apply-groups H; }
}
apply-groups G;
interfaces {
  ge-0/0/0 { unit 0 { family inet { address 10.0.0.1/24; } } }
  ge-0/0/1 { unit 0 { family inet { address 10.0.1.1/24; } } }
}
```

Both interfaces compile `Description == ""`; the direct (`apply-groups H`) shape from `TestApplyGroupsExceptIsPerDestination9422` delivers the description. Found while cell-writing for #9862 (a per-destination-through-nesting cell had to use concrete instance names instead); independent pre-existing hole, not a #9862 regression.

## Scope

Nested wildcard templates should fan out at the destination like direct ones. The inner adopt cannot prune what the outer destination would match — likely needs the wildcard to survive the inner merge (deferred matching) or the nested body to merge per-destination rather than pre-merged. Untouched by #9862 on purpose: fan-out surgery with its own blast radius and cells.

## #10066 — userspace: tick retry adoption can write stale m.cfg in diverged spawn state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Found during #10064 plan review (verified in source by lane; filed per review recommendation, not folded: discriminating Compile-differ from tick-differ needs a signature change the 4959/5488 call-text pins forbid).

Mechanism: ensureProcessLocked(ucfg) spawns the NEW identity and writes m.cfg at process.go:300; a subsequent protocol-gate failure (manager_compile.go:511), disarm failure (:523), or publish refusal (:540, adopt arm skipped on refusals) returns with lastSnapshot still OLD, so m.cfg (NEW) != lastSnapshot.Userspace (OLD). With pre-existing debt the tick gate is open; if the tick republish hits a content conflict and the retry lands-but-loses-its-response, the retry generation differs from retained, so the adopt arm fully adopts - including m.cfg = adopted.Userspace (OLD) - clobbering the correct NEW identity. #10064's same-generation skip fixes the no-retry case; the retry case still adopts stale.

Consequence: crash respawn restarts the stale identity (restartHelperAfterCrash -> ensureProcessLocked(m.cfg), process_supervisor.go:371, whose contract is 'm.cfg is the CURRENT desired config'); the next NEW commit sees a configEqual mismatch and does an unnecessary kill+respawn (plus a spurious #8899 restart in the startup window).

Repair directions: thread the publisher (Compile vs tick) into publishSnapshotFailClosedLocked so the tick adopts generations without the m.cfg write (requires updating the 4959/5488 call-text pins); or snapshot m.cfg across tick publishes and restore on failure; or re-derive m.cfg from the spawn record instead of the snapshot. Rare (needs diverged state + tick conflict + lost retry); low priority.

## #10084 — config: LoadMergeAs-hierarchical drops leaf bracket provenance through FormatSet, blinding provenance-based strict gates (follows #9881) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## What is wrong

`LoadMergeAs` with hierarchical input silently miscompiles `policy-options as-path AP1 [0-9]+` to `0-9 +` and commits STRICT-clean — the exact defect #9881 closes on every other authoring path.

## Mechanism (measured on fix/9881-aspath-bracket @ 2456a1fcb + lane)

`LoadMergeAs`-hierarchical parses the file (provenance intact), renders the tree with `FormatSet`, and replays the flat lines through `applyEditLine` (`pkg/configstore/store_command.go:490-510`). `FormatSet` drops leaf bracket provenance unconditionally: `nodeKeyBracketMask` returns nil for every leaf (`pkg/config/ast_format.go:219-224`), and single-key runs render bare (`ast_format.go:403-407`, pinned as anti-churn by #6668). As-path definition nodes are always leaves, so the replayed tree carries no `KeysBracketed` and the #9881 strict gate sees a clean tail.

Probe (throwaway, since removed): `LoadMergeAs("", "policy-options { as-path AP1 [0-9]+; }")` yields candidate text `set policy-options as-path AP1 0-9 +` and `CompileConfig` returns nil error.

Scope note: this is broader than single-key runs — ALL leaf bracket provenance is lost through any `FormatSet` round trip. `load override` (raw tree install), `SyncApply` (direct parse), flat `load merge` / `load set` (grouped replay), interactive `set`/`delete` (grouped since #9881), and JSON persistence/rollback (mask survives, #6668 pin) are all unaffected. The lossy set is exactly the `FormatSet`-replay paths.

## Fix direction

Preserve the bit through the hierarchical-merge replay without churning operator-visible `display set` output: either a lossless internal set renderer used only by the merge replay (emitting single-key/leaf brackets the grouped re-parse restores), or a direct hierarchical tree merge preserving masks. Filing, not fixing, here: either option changes load-merge results for every bracketed hierarchical config and deserves its own review cycle.

## Acceptance

`LoadMergeAs` of hierarchical `as-path AP1 [0-9]+` is strict-rejected with the #9881 quote-the-regex diagnostic; the #6668 no-churn pins (`TestBracketedValueLeavesRenderUnchanged_6668`) stay green.

## #10089 — networkd: no render-side refusal for single-pattern glob interface names (F-049 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## What is wrong

#9886 (F-049) closes the render-side refusal for interface names that are not exactly one `[Match]` pattern (whitespace/multi-pattern). The adjacent single-pattern class — glob metacharacters — passes the same gates and renders the same device-claiming harm with success reported. Found during #9886 plan review (hostile review, verified against base `15be546a1`); filed so the #9886 belt's scope boundary (whitespace only) is honest and this class has an owner.

## Mechanism

`strings.Fields("ge*") == ["ge*"]`, so a one-pattern glob passes the #9886 belt predicate and renders raw:

- `pkg/networkd/networkd.go:846` `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Name=%s\n", ifc.Name)` writes `Name=ge*` into the `.network` with `Apply` returning nil. systemd reads `[Match] Name=` as shell-style globs, so the unit claims every `ge*` device (addresses/VRF applied to wrong NICs) while success is reported. Trigger and harm are identical in shape to F-049 (persisted or peer-synced pre-#6834 value arriving via the lenient path, where strict `ValidateInterfaceName` never runs).
- The repo's own test states the ground truth (`pkg/config/validate_interface_name_6834_test.go`, `TestValidateInterfaceNameRejectsGlobs_6834`): a glob is a legal kernel name that nothing downstream rejects — it silently matches everything it globs.

## Second hole: strict-path bridge-domain globs commit today

`pkg/config/schema_validators_bridge_domain_9494.go:14-24` `ValidateBridgeDomainName` checks separators/NUL/whitespace but has NO glob arm, so `bridge-domains "ge*"` commits on the strict path today. The dataplane names the bridge `"br-" + name` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1551`) and the belt-exempted `Name=br-ge*` glob-claims from a fully committed config. The #9886 lenient drop covers whitespace for bridge-domains; globs stay open on both paths.

## Suggested direction

- Extend the #9886 render belt to refuse ASCII glob metacharacters (`*?[]`) in `ifc.Name` — UTF-8-safe (no charset class involved), and a glob `Name=` never matched only its device so the #6564 over-rejection analysis holds.
- Add the missing glob arm to `ValidateBridgeDomainName` (strict), mirroring `ValidateInterfaceName`'s glob message.
- The #9886 predicate carries a deferral note pointing here; its tests pin glob pass-through as known-deferred.

## Deduplication

Split out of F-049 (#9886): that issue's acceptance is explicitly `len(strings.Fields(name)) != 1`, which globs satisfy. Distinct scope, same sink and harm class.

## #10094 — console: operational show system rollback compare N reads the shared candidate at PermView [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## What is wrong

A view-only console user reads another session's staged, uncommitted configuration through operational `show system rollback compare N` — the same candidate disclosure #9889 closes on gRPC, on the in-process console surface.

## Mechanism (base `363c21dc2`, verified by reading)

- `pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go:1024` (`show system rollback compare N`) and `:1059` (`show system rollback N ... compare`) call `c.store.ShowCompareRollbackRedacted(n)`, which diffs rollback slot N against the CANDIDATE (`pkg/configstore/store_format.go:461-473`).
- The console gate prices the whole `show` family at `PermView` (`pkg/cli/permissions.go:161-162`, via `checkPermission`), with no compare-aware upgrade.
- The console shares the DAEMON's store: `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:782` builds the shell with `cli.New(d.store, ...)`, and the RBAC class comes from the kernel (`daemon_run.go:897`, `cli_rbac.go`, #6701). So `s.candidate` is the live shared candidate — another session's WIP whenever anyone holds configure mode.

Precondition (same as #9889): some session holds a candidate; otherwise the call errors with `not in configuration mode`. Secrets are redacted, so reconnaissance, not credential theft.

NOT affected: console config-mode `show | compare` (`pkg/cli/cli_config.go:484-488`) — console `configure` already requires `PermConfig` (`permissions.go:167-168`), so that reader holds configure, matching the contract.

## Suggested direction

Subcommand-aware console pricing mirroring the gRPC/REST contract (reading a candidate costs `configure`): a `show ... compare` selector prices at `PermConfig` while the rest of `show` stays `PermView`. Suggested cells: read-only console principal denied on `show system rollback compare N` with a staged candidate on the shared store; configure-class console principal still served with the canary in the output; plain `show system rollback N` (committed archive) still served to read-only.

## Notes

- The `cli_show_system.go:1013` comment claimed rollback-vs-active; corrected to candidate semantics in PR #10093 (no behavior change).
- Discovered as review follow-up SPARK-1 on #9889; filed before that PR merges so the residual is tracked, not dropped.

## #10100 — [cohort] zeroize wipe: interior and rendered-leg symlinks survive silently [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-16)

## What this groups

Two wipe-time link-following residuals found during the #9897 plan review (security pass), split out because the cohort's four members are root/segment-level while these are interior/rendered-leg level. Both report clean while secrets survive (the #9013 under-wipe shape). Located at base 0f69a6164.

## Members

| # | Site and mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| R-1 | Interior symlinks under wiped trees survive silently. The #9013 guards check only the top paths: `pkg/configstore/factory_reset.go` `eraseConfigDB` checks `.configdb` + `master.key` only (:470-492), then `RemoveAll(dbDir)` (:509); `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go` checks `tls/` only (:216-222), then `RemoveAll` (:222). A real `tls/` containing symlinked `key.pem`/`cert.pem`, or a real `.configdb` containing a symlinked `active.json`/rollback slot (other than `master.key`), has the link unlinked while the target bytes (HTTPS private key, config text) survive on the target volume with no `FactoryResetSymlinkError` entry. Same for `zeroizeDBCopyDir` (`.old`/`.restore.partial`, dir+key only). |
| R-2 | Rendered-config wipe follows links. `zeroizeRenderedConfigs` (`pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go:369-404`) `os.Remove`s the swanctl snippet + kea4/kea6 with no `SymlinkTarget` check: a symlinked snippet unlinks the link while the IKE/Kea secrets survive, nil returned. `sweepFsatomicTemps` (:415-426) `ReadDir`s fixed rendered dirs and `Remove`s temp-shaped names with no link check. `frr.StripManagedSectionFile` (`pkg/frr/manager.go:900+`) `ReadFile`s through a link and rewrites with `WithResolveSymlinks`, replacing content AT THE TARGET (privileged modification of a victim file carrying managed markers; needs `/etc/frr` parent write, root-only in production). |

## Suggested direction

Pre-walk `tls/`, `.configdb` (+ `.old`/`.restore.partial`) with `Lstat`; collect ANY interior symlink into `Skipped` (still erasing regulars), mirroring the `master.key` inverse-shape handling. `Lstat`+refuse (report `Skipped`) symlinked `frrConf`/swanctl/kea4/kea6; drop `WithResolveSymlinks` on the zeroize write path (no-follow write or refuse); add `SymlinkTarget` checks to the temp-sweep removes. Acceptance per member: planted-interior-link fixture reports the surviving target path and never nil; ordinary wipe byte-identical.

## Reachability note

R-1 needs write access inside the config root (stronger than the #9897 parent-write planter); R-2's frr leg needs `/etc/frr` parent write (root-only in production). Low severity, same bound as #9897 (no privilege escalation claimed).

## #10113 — snmp Serve budget residual: worst-case PDU flood below the rate (follows #9917 F-139) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## What

#9917 F-139 bounds the SNMP Serve loop by per-source request RATE (100/s sustained + 200 burst). Rate alone cannot bound loop share across PDU shapes: the in-tree worst case (a max-size GETNEXT of 239 deep ifXTable OIDs, ~33 ms per pkg/snmp/README.md and the agent.go comment) saturates the serial loop at ~30 requests/s -- below the budget. A valid-credential flood of worst-case PDUs at that pace still stalls all polling.

## Accepted residual, tracked here

Bounding that shape needs per-PDU cost charging (e.g. token cost proportional to varbind count, decoded cheaply pre-budget) or a request varbind-count cap, both of which exceed the Low cohort scope and need their own measurement + NMS-compat analysis. The residual is documented in pkg/snmp/README.md (Serve budget bullet); this issue tracks the follow-up.

Also documented there: a distributed flood saturates the UDP socket buffer ahead of any userspace budget -- the per-source budget bounds the single-source actor only.

Raised during hostile plan review of #9917 (reviewer findings B-P1-2, A-P3-18).

## #10120 — [follow-up] dist: re-sign re-hashes live bytes, so a content-swap preserving sidecar flags gets a fresh valid signature [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #9920 (parent review on PR #10119, acknowledged residual — do not close thinking re-sign is content-swap-safe).

## Mechanism
`sign.assert_bake_set()` (`scripts/dist/sign.py`) checks SET MEMBERSHIP (basenames equal the bake four-file set) plus sidecar FLAGS (`validated`/`base_image_pinned`/`guest_kernel`). It never compares current disk bytes to the recorded hashes, and `write_and_sign_manifest()` then re-hashes whatever is on disk. So a qcow2/metadata/sidecar byte tamper that preserves the flag VALUES is re-hashed and signed; publish hash checks then pass against the NEW manifest.

## Actor
Publisher/operator running `make dist-sign` recovery, or anyone able to write `dist/` between bake and re-sign. NOT closed by the #9920 gates: the CLI gate is shape+flags, and `gate_images` completeness (added in review) is membership — neither binds bytes to a prior trusted record.

## Why it was left open
F-063's letter is set/provenance shape. Old-signature verification before re-sign is impossible on rotation without the old key (the rotation scenario exists because the old key is gone/untrusted). Fixing this needs key-management or out-of-band expected-hash decisions beyond the cohort.

## Possible directions (undecided)
- Require old-pubkey verification when the old key IS available (rotation-with-overlap), refuse-or-warn on drift.
- Compare live bytes to recorded hashes pre-sign and refuse/warn when they differ (catches sloppy tamper; a careful tamperer rewrites both).
- Record expected artifact hashes out-of-band (e.g. in the release ticket) and check re-sign output against them.

## Acceptance sketch
A test that mutates artifact bytes (flags intact) then re-signs must either refuse or surface an explicit, operator-visible drift warning — not a silent fresh signature.

## #10129 — frr: narrowed BGP policy chain renders a permit-terminated surviving subset (F-008 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Follow-up to #9947 (F-008), split out per parent review: the cohort PR ships F-007 only. This is the OPEN tracker for the narrowed-chain surviving permit. It supersedes the deferred #8369 (CLOSED-as-DEFERRED) with a corrected measurement.

## Surviving-permit behavior

`filterDefinedPolicies` (pkg/frr/bgp_policy_chain.go) drops undefined chain members and renders the surviving subset. A narrowed chain — some members survive — still attaches a filter, but a weaker one than authored, and the attachment is permit-terminated (Junos BGP default-accept, #2998). The only handling is `warnNarrowedChains` (warn + `xpf_frr_policy_chains_narrowed` gauges); rendered output is unchanged. A dropped deny-bearing member vanishes and the survivor falls through to permit.

Reachability: strict commit rejects undefined policy references, so 100% of narrowed chains arrive via the tolerant path (boot Store.Load, HA SyncApply, rollback). No attacker required; ordinary fault.

## Corrected measurement (settles #8369 reason 3)

#8369 reasoned that an empty-but-defined survivor renders match-all permit-10, making a synthesized deny UNREACHABLE, and that the deny-safe gauge therefore over-counts. That inference assumed a trailing deny APPENDED behind permit-10. Measured against the actual synthesis shape — a chain MEMBER with a terminating default — EMPTY contributes zero sequences, so [EMPTY,SYNTH-DENY] renders lone deny-10, reachable by every route (TestEmptySurvivorSynthesizedDenyIsReachable9947, #9947). The shape flips permit-all to deny-all: highest-impact member of the denominator, not an over-count. Excluding it would hide an outage case.

Established (kept): #8363 suffix rule — a member-synthesis deny at a non-final ghost position DELETES later survivors (renderComposedRouteMap breaks on the first terminating default), so member synthesis is safe only for GhostsAreSuffix. Code-read, NOT yet pinned: terminating-default survivors and match-all-final-term survivors need per-shape reachability cells before any deny ships.

## Migration decision (owed)

Any deny (or render-side rejection) lands on reboot/peer-sync/rollback for configs the operator did not just edit, and a route-map deny is silent (first symptom: prefix absent from adj-rib). Decide with the fleet split (narrowed vs deny-safe counts, empty-survivor share) plus a migration story: warn-first release vs immediate deny, per-shape rollout (suffix-only first), operator comms. #7625 (emptied -> deny-all) is precedent for the SHAPE of the fix, not for its cost: emptied replaced no filter at all; narrowed replaces a working filter.

## Render-vs-compile consequences (no conflation)

- Compile-side rejection on the LENIENT path would brick boot/HA-sync (#1960) — must stay warn-only there. Strict already rejects.
- Render-side rejection (ApplyFull returns an error pre-write, like the redist/composed/emptied collision belts at manager.go) does NOT take the Store.Load path and does NOT brick the daemon or management (#1993 fail-closed boot preserves mgmt reachability): boot/background applies log and continue, operator commits fail. Its consequence is FORWARDING-plane: FRR keeps last-good — on cold boot with a narrowed config that is EMPTY (no managed section, no filters), which permits everything and is WORSE than the narrowed filter. So render-reject is fail-open on cold boot, not fail-closed.
- Rendered deny alias: no brick; the cost is the load-time silent routing change above.

## Collision handling (solvable, recipe)

A narrowed-deny alias needs the standard reserved-name machinery (same recipe as #5277/#5116/#7625): reserved suffix/namespace + strict commit validator forbidding operator spellings + render-side collision belts failing the apply closed on the lenient path + dedupe rule for same surviving chain shared across neighbors/VRFs/instances. Four pairs: alias-vs-operator-policy, alias-vs-composed, alias-vs-emptied-deny, alias-vs-alias on distinct kept chains. Reference and definition emitted together (#6807 by-construction).

## Acceptance

- Narrowed suffix-safe chains (populated survivors) deny the fall-through the dropped member covered, measured against the FRR version in the image (terminating accept stops; trailing/member deny catches the rest), with ghost-first/middle cells proving survivors are NOT deleted and a deny-not-emitted cell proving the decision is a discriminator.
- Empty-survivor narrowing covered explicitly (permit-all -> deny-all flip named in the migration notes).
- Single-policy (standalone alias, never mutating the shared map) and composed (distinct alias, never mutating the shared composed map) both deny-terminate the ATTACHED map; VRF/global instances covered; nil PolicyOptions and oversized (#5701/#5732 quarantine) paths defined.
- Fleet split + migration decision recorded here before rollout.

## #10130 — [follow-up #9950] session-gated reverse discriminator for reply-fragment misses [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #9950 (parent review of PR #10128, item 6).

#9950 installs reply fragment associations on the session-hit tail, fixing the IN-ORDER case (first-then-tail, wire-asserted). The MISS path still fails open for replies: flowless_fragment_requires_nat_translation sees FORWARD-direction rules only (src SNAT/NPTv6-out, dst DNAT/NPTv6-in/static-DNAT), so a DNAT-reply tail arriving before its first (reorder, TTL straddle, shard eviction under flood, config-generation bump, HA non-sync, LAG/ECMP L4-hash split) matches no arm and forwards with the internal source on the wire (F-036 leak).

A rules-only reverse arm over-drops (plain outbound from a DNAT target IP matches naive src-in-pool checks). The sound fix is session-gated: drop the reply tail iff a forward session exists whose reverse would translate it (forward.src==reply.dst plus rewrite match), else forward. Needs a session L3/reverse index readable from the flowless miss path plus hot-path cost analysis.

Precise residual scope (verified in #9950 lane):
- DNAT-without-SNAT reply reorder: DISCLOSES internal src (the filed leak).
- SNAT-covered reply misses: already drop via source_nat_would_translate_fragment.
- Distinct-pool misses: MissingNeighbor buffers/retries toward the pool next-hop (not terminal drop); with a pool neighbor/route present the fragment forwards untranslated to the pool (misdelivery, dst field — no topology disclosure; demonstrated by the F-053 fixture).

## #10135 — [follow-up #10100] zeroize wipe does not attest hardlinked interior content [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #10100 (GPT-4 adjudication, choice b).

## Gap

`configstore.CollectInteriorSymlinks` censuses SYMLINKS only. A same-filesystem HARDLINK (nlink>1) to wiped interior content (tls/key.pem, .configdb/active.json, archive snapshots, DB copies) survives `RemoveAll` via its other name with no report: the wipe certifies MANAGED-NAME removal only. Stated as the narrowed contract in the census doc comment (factory_reset.go), not silently assumed.

## Why a follow-up, not this change

Presence (nlink>1 via Lstat) is detectable, but the OTHER names sharing the inode are not enumerable from the wiped path — there is nothing actionable to hand the operator in a Skipped-style entry (no target path exists). Failing closed on any nlink>1 needs a new error shape (not FactoryResetSymlinkError) and a decision on what the operator does next; that design is its own change.

## Suggested direction

Link-count attestation pass over wiped trees: Lstat each managed file, and on nlink>1 either (a) fail the wipe closed as incomplete-erasure with the offending managed paths named, or (b) resolve sibling names via a bounded directory scan where feasible. Plant: hardlink tls/key.pem to a second name, wipe, assert the wipe reports incomplete (or names the survivor).

## Reachability

Needs write access inside the config root (same bound as #10100 R-1) plus same-filesystem link; low severity, no privilege escalation claimed.

## Origin

#10100 parent review (GPT-4 vs spark-§3): both half-right — presence detectable, location isn't.

## #10136 — test: live wire deny gate for routing-instance separation (VAL-04 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

## Acceptance

- Recorded PASS row on a healthy build and FAIL row on a fault-injected leak (VRF miss transits another table).
- Near-miss control differs from the probe only in the routed-table dimension.
- §3 row's ledger gate has measured rows; no new unreached GATE without a shrink-only declaration.

Parent: #9812. Requires loss-cluster access (not available in the #9812 lane, hence this split).

## #10190 — userspace-dp/NAT: address-only and PAT rules sharing one allocator can mint the same public tuple (GEMINI-049-026) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Research disposition for #8869 / GEMINI-049-026

At report base `b0f3aba21` and current `43e7038a1`, the shared allocator key is `pool_name + addresses + port range` and omits `no_translation` (`userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:398-405`). Address-only reservations record only `address_only_owners` and no PAT occupancy bit (`userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:2516-2525`, `3699-3729`); the PAT arm claims only the bitmap (`userspace-dp/src/nat/source/match_rules.rs:851-879`). The cross-allocator guard intentionally skips owners from the same allocator (`userspace-dp/src/nat/source/overlap.rs:156-163`), so two rules over one shared allocator can admit an address-only flow preserving port P and a PAT flow allocated at the same public address and P. That duplicate reverse tuple is fail-open and can misdeliver replies.

This is distinct from #5269/#5341 (address-only versus address-only/deterministic token coverage) and #8115 (cross-allocator peer guard). The existing #6528 fixture proves allocator sharing and mode-correct teardown but not simultaneous PAT/address-only collision.

Requested follow-up: add a same-allocator simultaneous collision regression cell and either make the two occupancy domains mutually exclusive at admission or reject the candidate against the other domain. Do not widen `allocator_key` without preserving lease carry-over semantics.

Static adjudication only; no production code changed in this research pass. Report base: `b0f3aba21`; checked HEAD: `43e7038a1`.

## #10191 — userspace-dp/NAT64: guard IPv6-to-IPv4 total-length narrowing above 65515 bytes (GEMINI-049-096) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Research disposition for #8869 / GEMINI-049-096

At report base `b0f3aba21` and current `43e7038a1`, NAT64 v6-to-v4 translation narrows `20 + l4_len` into the IPv4 16-bit Total Length without a bound check at the outer translator (`userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:2517-2518`) and the non-first-fragment translator (`:3858-3859`). The embedded quote arm has the same cast (`:3261-3262`) but is bounded by `MAX_EMBEDDED_LEN = 1300` (`:1886`, `:3217`), so that arm cannot reach the wrap. IPv6 payload lengths 65516..65535 are valid ordinary 16-bit payloads (not IPv6 jumbograms); when an unusually large ingress MTU or GRO-delivered buffer carries one whole, the wire header carries a value below 20 while the function returns the unwrapped `usize`, producing an incoherent/corrupt IPv4 datagram. Standard 1500/9000 MTUs do not reach this branch.

Requested follow-up: fail closed before every v6-to-v4 `20 + L` cast when `L > 65515`, with the RFC 7915 §5.1 packet-too-big/drop policy selected by the caller; add a synthetic 65516..65535 regression cell asserting no wrapped packet escapes. Saturating the field would emit a different invalid datagram and is not a fix.

Static adjudication only; no production code changed in this research pass. Report base: `b0f3aba21`; checked HEAD: `43e7038a1`.

## #10198 — [follow-up #9553] DHCPv6 relay has no link-local link-address fallback (RFC 8415 §19.1.1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #9553 (merged #10159), found during round-3 review. RFC 8415 §19.1.1 permits a link-local Relay-Forw link-address when no GUA/ULA exists (not recommended; Interface-Id required when the link-address cannot identify the return link). Current code: defaultDHCPV6LinkResolver (relay6.go:348-370) feeds selectDHCPv6LinkAddress (:373-386), which skips IsLinkLocalUnicast and returns 'no usable global IPv6 link-address'; supervisor run (:510-548) logs resolve failure and retries forever — no Relay-Forw is ever sent on a link-local-only interface. Even with resolver fallback, buildRelayForwardV6 (:451-479, guard :459-460) rejects link-local. Minimal fix (lane-proposed): deterministic link-local fallback after GUA/ULA scan; allow for direct-client Relay-Forw with nested validation retained; decouple Relay-Forw link identity from upstream socket bind/source selection in defaultDHCPV6ConnFactory (:293-327, upstream bind :319-322) using unspecified/route-selected bind; add resolver/build/supervisor integration tests; document the RFC fallback. Repro: DHCPv6 relay on fe80::/64-only interface with reachable configured server. Provenance: Fin9553 round-3 investigation.

## #10244 — cluster: failover-hold restore is not bound to RG incarnation; stale restore + reservation wipe across remove/re-add (follow-up #10004) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #10004 (PR #10243), filed per delta review (non-blocking; fails safe). Mechanism: UpdateConfig holds m.mu (group_state.go:17) but never reads failoverInProgress, so a remove+re-add (two commits) can land while RequestPeerFailover(Batch) sits unlocked in hooks. Purge deletes failoverGen/failoverInProgress/RG object (:134-139); re-add allocates a FRESH RedundancyGroupState (:33-43, ManualFailover=false, gen 0). An in-flight gen-0 snapshot then passes all restore gates (0==0, groups[rgID] exists, flag false) and the abort installs the OLD incarnation's hold/At/state/weight on the NEW RG. Independently, the old request's deferred unconditional delete(failoverInProgress, rgID) (:368 targeted, :930 batch) can wipe a new request's reservation. Trigger: RG gen 0 + hold → request clears + blocks → remove → re-add → hook fails → stale restore; defer wipes new reservation.\n\nRecommended fix: bind the snapshot to incarnation (capture *RedundancyGroupState at snapshot time, failover.go:412-418/:972-980; skip restore when m.groups[rgID] != snapshot.rg); then bind reservation cleanup to request identity (owner token/reqID, delete-only-if-match) across Request + Manual paths. Do NOT refuse removal while guarded (wedging risk; purge exists to avoid wedges).\n\nSeverity rationale: fails safe (stale holds park secondary per group_state.go:105-116 taxonomy; no dual-primary/data loss); needs a double-commit inside one request window. Patch-introduced only in that restore-to-RG-by-ID is new.\n\nAcceptance: remove/re-add mid-flight cannot install a stale hold (incarnation-bound restore); reservation cleanup is request-identity-bound; regressions pin both.

## #10245 — cluster: stacked ForceSecondary→ManualFailover weight pin missed by restore predicate (follow-up #10004) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up to #10004 (PR #10243), filed per delta review (non-blocking P3). Gap: restoreWeight predicate (failover.go:417 targeted, :978 batch: StateSecondary && Weight==0) misses the stacked shape — ManualFailover sets flag+At+SecondaryHold and never writes weight, so ForceSecondary (pins 0, Secondary) then ManualFailover yields a flagged Hold-state hold with pinned 0. A failed request clears (recalcWeight 0→debt-derived) and the abort restores flag+timestamp+Hold but skips weight (predicate false on Hold). Trigger: ForceSecondary → ManualFailover → failed RequestPeerFailover, same RG.\n\nRecommended fix: key restoreWeight on pin provenance, not state shape — at capture compare rg.Weight against debt-derived weight from m.monitorWeights (all under m.mu); differ → pinned → restore; equal → derived → skip (preserves the no-over-restore 155-cell property). Alternative: provenance bool set by ForceSecondary, cleared by recalcWeight/Reset.\n\nNot blocking: 3-action chain, latent while held (election blocked on flag), pin already fragile on master.\n\nAcceptance: stacked-shape weight pin restored; regression pins it; no-over-restore preserved.

## #10261 — userspace HA: secondary cut drain strands established TCP streams at cwnd floor [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

Follow-up from #10023 / #9486 measurement.

The Sep-13 loss userspace rolling-cut run kept one iperf3 TCP session and all four streams alive, but the secondary-node cut produced asymmetric per-stream starvation:

* streams [7], [9], and [11] fell to 0.00 bits/sec from t=12 through t=42 (30 s), with snd_cwnd pinned at 1.41 KiB and roughly one failed RTO probe per second;
* stream [5] continued at about 95–102 Mbit/sec until t=38, then fell to 0.00 bits/sec from t=39 through t=54 (15 s), recovering with a 445-retransmit burst;
* the SUM row hid 39 s of per-stream zero time because another stream remained healthy; the only aggregate zero window was 3 s;
* no TCP reset, stream death, or iperf error occurred.

Clock-corrected journal alignment is important: the three-stream gap begins at approximately host 19:51:25.215, about 1.46 s after fw1's forced-secondary/drain marker (19:51:23.755 host-equivalent) and 1.78 s before fw1's shutdown signal (19:51:26.995 host-equivalent). The fw1 restart is therefore only one candidate phase, not an established cause. The journal later records new process at +3.016 s, helper connection at +5.452 s, and session-sync readiness at +7.900 s; the streams remained starved through those milestones. Existing evidence is at `docs/pr/9486/evidence/iperf.log`, `docs/pr/9486/RESULTS.md`, and the #10023 follow-up evidence.

Please characterize and fix the flow/state-specific cause across the secondary cut drain/ownership transition and restart (session import/installation, dataplane flow attachment, or another forwarding-path condition) so an established session cannot strand only some streams at the TCP congestion floor. Acceptance should be per-stream, not SUM-only: no reset/death and no multi-second per-stream zero interval across a rolling cut.

## #10267 — userspace conntrack ignores per-application inactivity-timeout on live loss cluster [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Summary

The live wire conntrack lifecycle gate cannot distinguish the configured per-application inactivity timeout from the default TCP timeout on the loss userspace cluster.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `applications application wire-manual-timeout` with `protocol tcp`, `destination-port 54921`, and `inactivity-timeout 300`.
2. Permit only that application from `lan` to `wan`.
3. Open `10.0.61.102:58123 -> 172.16.80.201:54921`, send one payload, then remain connected and silent.
4. At t+5, `show security flow session destination-prefix 172.16.80.201/32` reports `Timeout: 20` for the session.
5. At t+45, the same session query reports `Total sessions: 0`.

The CLI configuration itself is retained:

```
set applications application wire-manual-timeout protocol tcp
set applications application wire-manual-timeout destination-port 54921
set applications application wire-manual-timeout inactivity-timeout 300
```

## Evidence

The same behavior was observed while running the #10030 harness with `APP_TIMEOUT=10` and `IDLE_WAIT=15`: the lifecycle session remained present (`stale_present=1`) instead of expiring at 10 seconds, causing:

```
WIRE_GATE wire_conntrack_lifecycle FAIL reason=-- created=1 witnessed=1 evicted=0 stale_present=1 exp_offered=1000 exp_leaked=0 fresh_offered=1000 fresh_leaked=0 syn_offered=1500 syn_observed=1500 ctrl_sess=3002 lifecycle_bad=1 cksum_bad=0
```

This is a product/runtime defect, not a harness workaround: the gate intentionally observes between the configured 10-second timeout and the default 20-second timeout so ignored application metadata is fail-closed.

## Expected

A session matched to `inactivity-timeout 300` must retain that timeout, and a session matched to `inactivity-timeout 10` must be evicted after 10 seconds of inactivity. The live session display should report the application timeout rather than the default TCP timeout.

The #10030 test infrastructure records this as a live gate failure; this issue tracks the dataplane/configuration defect separately.

## #10270 — userspace conntrack admits non-SYN midstream packets without a session [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Summary

The new #10030 `wire_conntrack_lifecycle` gate exposes that a TCP ACK/PSH tuple with no SYN can transit when the destination application is policy-permitted but no matching conntrack session exists.

## Loss-cluster evidence

On 2026-09-17, with `lan -> wan` narrowed to a temporary TCP application for destination port 54921:

- A subject TCP session was created and witnessed in `show security flow session`.
- After the idle window, the expired subject tuple and a never-created fresh source tuple each sent 1,000 valid raw ACK/PSH frames.
- The temporary lifecycle application remained permitted, so a policy deny cannot explain the result.
- Peer-side capture observed `exp_leaked=1000` and `fresh_leaked=1000`.
- A same-destination-port SYN control observed 1,500/1,500 SYNs, proving capture liveness.

The gate row was:

```
WIRE_GATE wire_conntrack_lifecycle FAIL reason=-- created=1 witnessed=1 evicted=0 stale_present=1 exp_offered=1000 exp_leaked=1000 fresh_offered=1000 fresh_leaked=1000 syn_offered=1500 syn_observed=1500 ctrl_sess=3002 lifecycle_bad=2001 cksum_bad=0
```

The stale-session result is tracked separately in #10267. This issue tracks the independent mid-stream admission: the never-created fresh tuple's non-SYN payload was observed on the peer wire despite no SYN and no session.

## Expected behavior

The `wire_conntrack_lifecycle` contract in `docs/firewall-validation-harness-design.md` requires “mid-stream without SYN” to drop. Only a SYN-created, policy-permitted flow should produce a peer-side packet.

No product code was changed in the test-infrastructure lane.

## #10283 — [w01-ha-F1] bulk snapshot read BEFORE BulkStart; gap-born session deleted at BulkEnd [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
cluster: the bulk snapshot is read BEFORE BulkStart is written and incrementals are not held across the gap, so a session that opens in that window is synced ahead of the window, omitted from it, and DELETED on the standby by the BulkEnd reconcile

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: cluster: the bulk snapshot is read BEFORE BulkStart is written and incrementals are not held across the gap, so a session that opens in that window is synced ahead of the window, omitted from it, and DELETED on the standby by the BulkEnd reconcile
Code references: pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:68-79; pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:242-255; pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:292-294; pkg/cluster/sync_conn_write.go:14-31; pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go:91-92; pkg/cluster/sync_conn_read.go:120-126; pkg/cluster/sync_conn_read.go:168-174; pkg/cluster/sync.go:2119-2200; pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:1008-1025; pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go:155-158; pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager.go:825-831; pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager.go:844-844.

## Impact
live session deleted on standby. Snapshot IS read before BulkStart and incrementals are NOT held. Residual race: a session opening after the snapshot read whose incremental is TRANSMITTED BEFORE BulkStart hits the wire installs on the standby unrecorded (bulkInProgress false), then the window (omitting it) completes and BulkEnd reconcile deletes it. Prerequisites: HA bulk (cold-prime/resync) + session open in the snapshot->BulkStart gap + sendCh/ direct-write interleave putting the incremental first.

## Acceptance / next check
open sessions continuously across a bulk; assert a sample of gap-opened sessions is deleted on the standby; fix by recording pre-window installs (grace set) or holding incrementals across snapshot->BulkStart.

## #10285 — [w02-pktpath-F1] fragment-overlap tracker has no completion reclaim; box-wide fragmented-transit cap; drops counted as forwarded [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
The #9950 fragment-overlap tracker never reclaims a completed datagram, so its 1024-entry, fail-closed, box-global table caps ALL fragmented transit at ~34 datagrams/s (~17/s with address NAT); above that, well-formed permitted fragments are silently dropped, and ~35 pps from one tenant blackholes fragments in every other VRF/zone

## Evidence

## Impact
availability, fail-closed direction. No completion-based reclaim: entries live 30 s idle (`OVERLAP_TTL_NS`) / 60 s absolute, so the 1024-slot table (16 shards x 64) sustains ~34 new datagrams/s box-wide (~17/s when the post-NAT second key plants). Above that, well-formed permitted fragments drop via SHARD_FULL. Shard index excludes routing domain, so one tenant's fragment flood evicts/blocks other tenants sharing those shards (availability, not bypass). Prerequisites: fragmented transit above the rate, or an adversarial same-shard flood (FNV-1a unkeyed); NAT doubles plant rate for re-addressed flows.

## Acceptance / next check
measure `FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED` under a 50-datagram/s fragmented iperf run + a single-tenant ident-varying flood; confirm victim-VRF drops and 30 s recovery.

## #10286 — [w02-pktpath-F2] related ICMP errors admitted only for NAT'd sessions; un-NAT'd flows lose PMTUD/traceroute [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
`allow-embedded-icmp` related-error admission exists only for NAT-translated sessions; an ICMP/ICMPv6 error (Frag-Needed / Packet-Too-Big / Unreachable / Time-Exceeded) quoting a live, permitted, UN-NAT'd session is judged as a brand-new flowless ICMP packet under the reverse zone pair and dropped by the default deny — PMTUD and traceroute black-hole for every un-NAT'd flow, which is essentially all IPv6

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: `allow-embedded-icmp` related-error admission exists only for NAT-translated sessions; an ICMP/ICMPv6 error (Frag-Needed / Packet-Too-Big / Unreachable / Time-Exceeded) quoting a live, permitted, UN-NAT'd session is judged as a brand-new flowless ICMP packet under the reverse zone pair and dropped by the default deny — PMTUD and traceroute black-hole for every un-NAT'd flow, which is essentially all IPv6
Code references: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs:116-147; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs:39-41; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs:50-70; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4422-4503; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/session_match.rs:15-17; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/session_match.rs:27-35.
Reviewer artifact: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ZWgbAoHBen/reviewers/shard-1/final.md` (shard 1); retained Codex supporting verdict: `MATERIAL`.

## Impact
with `allow-embedded-icmp` enabled, an ICMP error quoting a live permitted un-NAT'd session is recognized but then sent through ordinary flowless zone policy. Under a default-deny reverse zone pair, PMTUD/Time Exceeded can therefore be dropped despite the existing-session knob contract. This is not an all-flow blackhole: an explicit ICMP policy permit can deliver while the matched session's error budget remains; over-budget matches are dropped before fallback, and a NAT rewrite path takes a different route. Prerequisites: knob enabled, matching un-NAT'd session, and no explicit flowless ICMP permit (with budget not already exhausted).

## Acceptance / next check
add a dataplane case with the knob enabled, an existing un-NAT'd session, default-deny reverse zones, and a quoted PTB/Time-Exceeded; assert whether the intended contract is delivery or policy drop, then pin that decision in a regression test.

## #10288 — [w03-nat-F1] delete-drop sweep vs still-QUEUED DeleteSynced strands NAT holder bits (active node too) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
The delete-drop sweep removes a worker's peer-synced session while that session's `DeleteSynced` is still QUEUED; the sweep releases no NAT, and the late `DeleteSynced` then finds no entry and releases none either — the worker's holder bit, the pool port and the `live_by_flow` slot are stranded for the life of the allocator.

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: The delete-drop sweep removes a worker's peer-synced session while that session's `DeleteSynced` is still QUEUED; the sweep releases no NAT, and the late `DeleteSynced` then finds no entry and releases none either — the worker's holder bit, the pool port and the `live_by_flow` slot are stranded for the life of the allocator.
Code references: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/delete_drop_sweep.rs:72-118; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/commands/delete_synced.rs:86-93; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/commands/delete_synced.rs:94-139.
Reviewer artifact: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ZWgbAoHBen/reviewers/shard-1/final.md` (shard 1); retained Codex supporting verdict: `MATERIAL`.

## Impact
NAT pool port + holder-bit + `live_by_flow` slot stranded for the allocator's life per race hit; cumulative pool exhaustion. The sweep removes the worker entry directly with steering-only release (no NAT release); the late (queued, accepted) `DeleteSynced` then finds no entry and takes the no-entry branch, which releases steering rows only — no NAT release either. Neither path drops the evicted worker's holder bit, so last-worker-wins free never fires. Prerequisites: HA peer-synced SNAT session + armed sweep (epoch bump from refused delete/RG churn elsewhere) racing an accepted-but-undelivered DeleteSynced + per-worker pool NAT.

## Acceptance / next check
deterministic test (arm sweep with queued DeleteSynced pending); assert port reuse after race; fix by NAT-releasing in sweep step or reaping holder bits for swept keys.

## Problem
A destination-NAT pool written in valid Junos range grammar (`address A to B`) commits clean under strict validation with zero warnings and compiles to the single host **B**; any extra token (`address A bogus B`, `address [ A B ]`) is likewise swallowed last-token-wins.

For `address A to B` the token stream is `[A to B]`, so `Address=B`. `B` is a bare IP, so `validateDNATPoolStrict` (`compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:493-530`, `isHostMaskAddress`) accepts it with zero warnings, and the snapshot builder installs host B (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_destination.go:148` via `DNATPoolHostIP`, which takes the already-collapsed string). Same for `address A bogus B` → B. The strict gate validates the collapsed string, never the raw token count, so the swallowed tokens are invisible to every downstream check. fails closed on unparseable/wide values — but it receives `B`, a valid host, so the guard cannot fire. Junos pool grammar does not define `address A to B` for DNAT pools (range…

medium. Silent wrong-backend translation: traffic intended for a range/pool is delivered to a single host B with no commit signal. Prerequisites: operator authors (or a tool emits) a multi-token address value; strict commit; referencing DNAT rule.

## Problem
NPTv6 with a /64 rule always adjusts IID word 4, violating RFC 6296 §3.5's MUST (inspect words 64..79, 80..95, 96..111, 112..127 and use the first not initially 0xFFFF): a host whose first IID word is `0xFFFF` is translated to the SAME external address as its `0x0000` sibling and inbound traffic for it is delivered to the sibling.

## #10302 — [w06-hostsys-F1] addressed interface in NO zone is kernel-routed while armed (no forward-hook fence) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
A netdev with no XDP shim (a configured-but-UNZONED interface, or a device-map `leave-alone` NIC) is a policy-free router port while the dataplane is armed — its transit is kernel-forwarded into zoned networks.

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: A netdev with no XDP shim (a configured-but-UNZONED interface, or a device-map `leave-alone` NIC) is a policy-free router port while the dataplane is armed — its transit is kernel-forwarded into zoned networks.
Code references: pkg/daemon/README.md:3498-3503; pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:692-693; docs/bare-metal-device-map.md:214-216; pkg/daemon/daemon_transit_gate.go:69-80; pkg/nftables/transit_barrier.go:25-39; pkg/networkd/networkd.go:895-932.
Reviewer artifact: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ZWgbAoHBen/reviewers/shard-1/final.md` (shard 1); retained Codex supporting verdict: `MATERIAL`.

## Impact
policy bypass (routing). While ARMED: `ip_forward=1` is kept (required by XDP_PASS paths) and the transit barrier is REMOVED (strictly unarmed-window scoped); the repo has no other `hook forward` policy. A device-map `leave-alone` NIC (never downed/stripped, stays L3-up) or a configured-but-UNZONED interface (never AF_XDP-bound, still addressed) therefore kernel-forwards transit into zoned networks with no zone policy. Prerequisites: armed dataplane + such an interface with L3 + kernel routes (connected routes suffice).

## Acceptance / next check
on armed node with leave-alone NIC, send inter-subnet transit via that NIC; capture kernel forward + absence of policy verdict; decide armed-state forward default-drop with explicit XDP_PASS pinholes.

## #10303 — [w06-hostsys-F2] RETH stable link-local absent from host-inbound sets after any render while BACKUP [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
The daemon-derived "stable RETH link-local" `fe80::bf72:<cluster>:<rg>` (MASTER-only, the RA router address) is in the host-inbound daddr sets only if it happened to be live at the last apply — after a failover (and after a cold boot until the first commit) it has no rule and falls to `policy accept`.

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: The daemon-derived "stable RETH link-local" `fe80::bf72:<cluster>:<rg>` (MASTER-only, the RA router address) is in the host-inbound daddr sets only if it happened to be live at the last apply — after a failover (and after a cold boot until the first commit) it has no rule and falls to `policy accept`.
Code references: pkg/cluster/reth.go:140-149; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:278-335; pkg/ra/sender.go:1110-1150.
Reviewer artifact: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ZWgbAoHBen/reviewers/shard-1/final.md` (shard 1); retained Codex supporting verdict: `MATERIAL`.

## Impact
fail-open host exposure. `fe80::bf72:<cluster>:<rg>` exists only on the MASTER (added/removed with mastership) but is neither a configured address nor a VRRP VIP, so daddr sets (live snapshot + configured VIPs) include it only if it happened to be live at the last apply. After a failover (new master's last apply predates its LL) and after cold boot until the first commit, host-bound traffic to the RA router address misses every deny and hits `policy accept`. Prerequisites: RETH/HA + IPv6 + host-inbound enforcement.

## Acceptance / next check
failover + cold-boot tests with LL host-service probes and nft dumps before/after commit; union the deterministic stable LL into daddr sets like VIPs.

## #10309 — [w10-pressure-cos-F1] expiry pass overflows the 4096-slot delta ring; dropped Close deltas strand shared-map entries that are later honoured [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
The session-expiry pass emits Close deltas into a 4096-slot ring with no drain-as-you-expire; when one 1-second GC tick expires more owned forward sessions than the ring holds, the excess Close deltas are dropped — and that delta is the ONLY expiry-path carrier of the shared-session-map removal, the sibling `DeleteSynced` fan-out, the `dnat_table` delete, the HA close and the SESSION_CLOSE record. The stranded shared entry is then honoured as a session hit, with no age check, on any worker, indefinitely.

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: The session-expiry pass emits Close deltas into a 4096-slot ring with no drain-as-you-expire; when one 1-second GC tick expires more owned forward sessions than the ring holds, the excess Close deltas are dropped — and that delta is the ONLY expiry-path carrier of the shared-session-map removal, the sibling `DeleteSynced` fan-out, the `dnat_table` delete, the HA close and the SESSION_CLOSE record. The stranded shared entry is then honoured as a session hit, with no age check, on any worker, indefinitely.
Code references: userspace-dp/src/session/expire.rs:157-157.
Reviewer artifact: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ZWgbAoHBen/reviewers/shard-1/final.md` (shard 1); retained Codex supporting verdict: `MATERIAL`.

## Impact
state leak + resurrection + peer/telemetry loss under burst expiry. One GC tick expiring >4096 owned forward sessions overflows `MAX_SESSION_DELTAS` (4096); excess Closes drop (latched, #2442). The delta flush is the ONLY carrier of: shared-map removal, sibling `DeleteSynced` fan-out, `dnat_table` delete, HA close, SESSION_CLOSE record. Stranded shared entries are honored as session hits with NO age check (any worker without a stale local record) indefinitely; `dnat_table` (HASH, non-LRU) leaks; HA peer never learns the close (resync re-emits Opens only — cannot convey deletes). Prerequisites: >4096 forward-session expirations in one 1 s GC tick (burst/churn/timeout cliff).

## Acceptance / next check
induce >4096 forward expirations in one GC tick; assert the overflow/latch, then inspect shared lookup, dnat map, sibling `DeleteSynced`, HA close, and SESSION_CLOSE telemetry both immediately and after later GC.

## #10315 — [w13-ha-transport-F1] heartbeat auth: a KEYED node admits an unsigned heartbeat until the peer has authenticated in THIS process; the admitted frame feeds election [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
On a keyed node whose peer has not authenticated since this xpfd process started, an UNSIGNED heartbeat is admitted and drives election — it demotes a sole-surviving primary to secondary (total forwarding outage), marks a dead peer alive and refreshes liveness. Session-sync removed the identical first-contact grace as a security bug (#5078); the heartbeat kept it, and #5639's fix is keyed on PROCESS lifetime.

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.

On accept, `admitFrame` refreshes `lastSeen` and calls `m.handlePeerHeartbeat(pkt)` (1807-1811), which sets `peerAlive=true`, rebuilds peer RG state from the packet, and runs election (654-713). Election resolves dual-primary by priority/node-id and can demote the local node (`pkg/cluster/election.go:215-223`). The dual-accept is pinned as intended by test (`pkg/cluster/heartbeat_auth_test.go:396`) and documented as rollout grace (`docs/architecture.md:179-185`) — but the arming signal requires a prior AUTHENT…

## #10316 — [w13-ha-transport-F3] heartbeat readLoop warns per datagram pre-auth on two reject paths (siblings are rate-limited); proxy-ARP responder captures the interface MAC once and keeps answering after a live virtual-MAC change [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-18)

## Problem
The proxy-ARP responder captures the interface MAC ONCE per responder lifetime and reconcile keeps a running responder ("swap the snapshot rather than restart"); a later virtual-MAC change applied by the LIVE-set path (no link cycle) leaves it answering pool-address ARP with a MAC the NIC no longer owns. `r.rgID`/`r.junosRef` are also written under a lock the reader never takes.

## #10319 — [w15-pktpath2-F2] ip-sweep counts any protocol; count-min flood cap admits up to 4x; same-family embedded-ICMP TTL not decremented; allow-dns-reply sport-53 forward with no session [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

## Problem
The ICMP/UDP per-destination flood cap is a count-min sketch over CONSUME-ON-ADMIT token buckets, so a destination whose row cells sit at different fractional token phases is admitted at up to `ROWS` (4) times the configured threshold, sustained — measured exactly 4.00x — while the module doc still claims the sketch "never lets a real flood through"

## Evidence
Current comparison target: `c96e0b24dbdb0c62e963608f3dbf9f228a3d051c` (`origin/master`); evidence pin: `8f7563c8a42486f8fac57091b625118cdf6c19f4`.
Reviewer evidence: ** flood sketches use `SynRateSketch<TokenBucket>` (zone.rs:93-97; syn_rate.rs:368-371). `increment` charges ALL rows and ANDs over-limit (syn_rate.rs:263-271); `TokenBucket::charge` consumes only on admit (syn_rate.rs:143-152; rate.rs:237-242). Admit ⟺ ANY row admits. Each row refills at `threshold`/s; round-robin phase stagger (each admission consuming from exactly one row, refilled at threshold rate) is self-consistent at 4x sustained, so the cap is `threshold` only in the synchronized-phase case and up to `ROWS×threshold` otherwise. The doc's monotonic-increase invariant is false for consume-on-admit cells.
Code references: userspace-dp/src/screen/syn_rate.rs:263-271; userspace-dp/src/screen/syn_rate.rs:295-309; userspace-dp/src/screen/syn_rate.rs:143-152; userspace-dp/src/screen/rate.rs:213-243; userspace-dp/src/screen/syn_rate.rs:61-74; userspace-dp/src/screen/zone.rs:281-311; userspace-dp/src/screen/zone.rs:368-378.

## Impact
** attacker sustains (threshold,4×threshold]/worker/destination with paced arrivals; flood in that window passes steadily. Above 4×/worker all rows dry → trips.

## #10387 — drain barrier vacuous when bulk never queued (follow-up #10261) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Follow-up to #10261 (residual from Rev10361 delta review of PR #10361, accepted as non-blocking).

## The gap
The demotion barrier gates on bulk-primed status, but if a bulk was never queued (bulk-source failure with nothing pending) the barrier is vacuous: drain proceeds during retry-wait with no prime ever demanded. References: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go` bulk-skip + `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:781-855` BarrierAck-only path.

## Why it did not block #10261
The hole needs a bulk-source failure with zero pending plus a drain landing exactly in retry-wait; no codebase path gates on `syncPeerBulkPrimed` today; the #10261 patch strictly narrows exposure (ForceSecondary barriered, rejoin bulk-first). Pre-existing with an identical base barrier.

## Fix direction
An outbound `needColdPrime`/`Pending` gate: demand a prime (or refuse drain) when no bulk is pending/acked, rather than treating absence-of-bulk as primed.

## #10391 — fence residual: demux adjudicated vs delegated traffic on xpf-usp1 (follow-up #10302) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Follow-up to #10302 (residual documented in PR #10390, accepted at merge).

## The gap
The armed FORWARD fence allowlists `xpf-usp1` (required: xfrm plaintext + slow-path reinject transit arrives with iifname `xpf-usp1`). But `xpf-usp1` multiplexes adjudicated passthrough AND delegated no-policy traffic (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/slow_path.rs:150-174` maps NoRoute/MissingNeighbor/ForwardCandidate fallback + synthetic IPsec passthrough to usp1), indistinguishable by iifname. Pinholing usp1 preserves status quo for usp1 while the fence closes unzoned-NIC transit — strictly an improvement, but the delegated share is still unpoliced.

## Fix direction
Demultiplex by mark (or equivalent): tag adjudicated passthrough at the slow-path outlet so the fence can admit marks, not the whole interface — or move delegated traffic to a fenced outlet. See `poll_stages.rs:1405-1424`, `neighbor_dispatch.rs:377-380`, and the NO-accept contract notes in `afxdp/mod.rs:504-514`.

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg_control/tun_origin.rs` (TUN-origin publication path)

A non-default-NAT TUN-origin entry is published into all three aliases. Demotion then retags each alias as `SyncImport`, allowing a node-local TUN-derived session to enter peer-synced/materialization paths and potentially cross HA after failback. This is distinct from the `SessionTable::demote_owner_rg` provenance guard in PR #10402.

## Evidence

The fail-on-revert regression `demote_shared_owner_rgs_preserves_tun_origin_10402` removed the primary-map guard and failed with `SyncImport` instead of `TunOrigin` (`artifact://42273`). With guards in the shared, NAT-alias, and forward-wire loops, the same test passed and verified all three aliases (`artifact://42283`).

## Requested outcome

Preserve `SessionOrigin::TunOrigin` in every shared-map demotion alias while continuing to retag ordinary local origins. Keep a regression covering primary, NAT-alias, and forward-wire copies.

This issue is separate from #10317 and #10318; it was discovered while reviewing their HA bulk/sweep provenance changes.

## #10421 — Loss cluster misses pref2000 after xpfd restart with sfmix committed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

## Summary

On the locked loss userspace cluster, xpfd did not reinstall the managed VRF-miss terminator after a clean service restart when the committed `sfmix` virtual-router remained present. A managed temporary-RI commit restored both families, so the cluster was returned clean, but the startup/recovery path remains unresolved.

## Locked reproduction

Readiness-gated, 30-second convergence probe archive: `/var/tmp/xpf-10342-probe-20260919T044647Z`

- Before mutation, both `loss:xpf-userspace-fw0` and `loss:xpf-userspace-fw1` had IPv4 and IPv6 `pref 2000 ... l3mdev-table unreachable`, `vrf-sfmix` table 488570, and the committed sfmix stanza.
- Exact `ip -4/-6 rule del pref 2000 l3mdev unreachable` commands returned rc=0 on both nodes; post-delete checks were empty for both families on both nodes.
- `systemctl restart xpfd` returned rc=0 on both nodes without any config commit or temporary RI. PIDs changed from 24133 to 24604 (fw0) and 46342 to 46733 (fw1).
- The probe waited until `systemctl ActiveState=active` and the CLI successfully returned the committed sfmix stanza on each node (five CLI polls after each restart), then polled both families on both nodes once per second for 30 seconds. Every sample remained empty (`settle.txt`, seconds 1–30).
- After that readiness and convergence window, `fw0-postrestart.txt` and `fw1-postrestart.txt` still show IPv4 and IPv6 pref-2000 absent on both nodes, while `vrf-sfmix` table 488570 and routes remained.
- The running binary SHA was `4a196d927c91b5d65d07caaf1a8d6738eb3c56412daaffa330651cba18509748`; `go version -m` reports vcs revision `ed4a7c10e04d0a41e95dacad492985f14fce26e1` and `vcs.modified=true`, so deployed-build provenance must be corrected/confirmed.
- Managed fallback add/delete through xpfd then restored IPv4+IPv6 pref-2000 on both nodes. `final-assert.txt` proves final rules, `vrf-sfmix`/`vrf-mgmt`, no `vrf-wire-10342`, and no committed `wire-10342` path; `/tmp/xpf-cluster.owner` was absent after the cell.

## Expected

When committed configuration declares a virtual-router, startup/reconcile must install the IPv4 and IPv6 pref-2000 `l3mdev unreachable` terminators before/with VRF realization, consistent with `pkg/routing/vrf.go` and `pkg/routing/vrf_miss_terminator_9819.go`.

## Actual

A fresh xpfd restart leaves both terminators absent even after the daemon is active, the committed `sfmix` stanza is queryable, and a 30-second convergence window elapses. A later managed RI commit restores them. This can leave VRF misses falling through the normal rule chain after restart.

## Scope

No product-code change was made in the #10342 lane. The harness parser correction merged separately in PR #10415; #10342 is the originating baseline incident. Refs #10342

## #10426 — [GEMINI-049-055] Preempt dual-active winner suppresses direct-VIP GARP [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

**Finding:** GEMINI-049-055 (round-3 high-lane adjudication for #8869).
Correct when written (base `b0f3aba21`); still RED at master `6fa3310c0`.

## Mechanism

`electRG` (`pkg/cluster/election.go:177-208`) handles `rg.Preempt` in an early
arm. A dual-active winner that is already primary (`rg.State == StatePrimary`,
`peerGroup.State == StatePrimary`, `localEff > peerEff`, or the winning side of
a node-ID tie) falls through every transition and hits `:208`:

```go
return electNoChange, ""
```

The non-preempt arm's dual-active reaffirm (`:236`
`return electNoChange, "Dual-active: winner stays"`) is unreachable when
preempt is on. `runElection` (`:364-407`) keys the reaffirm event on the exact
reason string, so no `ClusterEvent{DualActiveWin: true}` is emitted, and the
normal state-change path (`:410`, `oldState != rg.State`) also skips because
nothing changed.

## Consequence

`handleClusterEvent` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:612-617`) maps
`DualActiveWin -> scheduleDirectAnnounce`. Suppressed, no GARP/NA refresh runs
after split-brain healing under the recommended `preempt: true`, and the
ownership-change announce (`applyDirectVIPOwnership`, `daemon_ha_vip.go:167`)
does not fire either — a dual-active winner is already the steady owner
(`announce = !prev || added > 0`; the election.go comment at :386-390 records
exactly this). Upstream keeps the losing node's MAC until ARP/NDP expiry.

Bounded: direct-VIP (`noRethVRRP`) deployments only — RETH-VRRP setups rely on
VRRP advertisements. The loser still yields normally (state-change event), so
only the winner's refresh is missing. No periodic GARP ticker exists; announces
are event-driven.
