## #10427 — [GEMINI-049-076] Route-based IPsec local-only selector suppresses remote wildcard [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

**Finding:** GEMINI-049-076 (round-3 high-lane adjudication for #8869).
Correct when written (base `b0f3aba21`); still RED at master `6fa3310c0`.

## Mechanism

`effectiveTrafficSelectors` (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:604-612`) applies the
route-based wildcard default only when BOTH sides are empty:

```go
if local == "" && remote == "" && xfrmiIfID(vpn.BindInterface) > 0 {
    local, remote = routeBasedDefaultTS, routeBasedDefaultTS
}
```

An operator who sets `local-identity 10.10.0.0/16` (selector-shaped, so it
survives the #8003 gate and the `IsTrafficSelectorShape` filter) while omitting
`remote-identity` renders `local_ts = 10.10.0.0/16` with NO `remote_ts`.
strongSwan applies its `dynamic` default — the peer's /32 endpoint IP
(measured in-tree on strongSwan 6.0.5, policy.go comment block above the
condition) — and installs e.g.
`src 10.10.0.0/16 dst <peer>/32`. The in-tree comment defends selector-shaped
local-identity as "the operator said what they wanted", but the operator said
nothing about remote: `""` is an omission, and nothing in xpf documents that an
omitted remote means /32.

## Consequence

Routed transit traffic via the XFRM interface does not match the /32 remote
policy and is dropped by the kernel — silent blackhole of transit over a
route-based VPN configured the ordinary Junos way (bind-interface +
asymmetric identities). The commit gate (#8003) rejects non-selector identity
values but does not require symmetric identities, so this commits cleanly with
no warning (no diagnostic at the render site).

## Master measurement

- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:607-608` — condition byte-identical at base and tip.
- `routeBasedDefaultTS = "0.0.0.0/0,::/0"` (`:539`); render is silent (no
  warn on the asymmetric path).

## #10428 — [GEMINI-049-093] DHCP HA memfile fallback drops IPv4 hardware address [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

**Finding:** GEMINI-049-093 (round-3 high-lane adjudication for #8869).
Correct when written (base `b0f3aba21`); still RED at master `6fa3310c0`.

## Mechanism

Lossy pack/unpack round-trip on the DHCP HA memfile fallback path:

1. `ddns_leases.go:483` packs BOTH memfile columns into one string:
   `l.Identity = identity4(client_id, hwaddr)`. `identity4` (`:527-535`)
   prefers client-id and drops the MAC from the packed form (`"cid:..."`).
2. `readSyncLeasesViaMemfile` (`lease_sync.go:432-434`) unpacks with
   `splitV4Identity` (`:465-473`), which returns `hwaddr = ""` for any
   `"cid:..."` identity. The comment at :462-464 acknowledges the collapse
   ("we recover whichever was present") — but the consumer needs BOTH.
3. `syncLeaseToKea` (`:703-704`) passes `HWAddress`/`ClientID` through with no
   guard, and `keaLeaseJSON.HWAddress` carries `json:"hw-address,omitempty"`,
   so an empty MAC is OMITTED from the `lease4-add` arguments.

## Consequence

Kea documents `hw-address` as "a mandatory parameter for an IPv4 lease"
(`lease4-add`; `client-id` is optional). Every memfile-sourced v4 lease that
carries Option 61 is therefore rejected on takeover seeding, exactly when the
fallback exists to save us (control socket down: crash/restart/hang).
Reservations are lost; Kea re-offers allocated addresses; collisions. Leases
without client-id take the `"mac:"` branch and survive, so the blast radius is
"all Option-61-bearing v4 leases", not "all leases".

- Required v4 memfile columns include both `client_id` and `hwaddr`
  (`ddns_leases.go:75-78`), so the data is present and then discarded.

## #10429 — [GEMINI-049-083] Fabric HMAC tokens replay across RPC methods [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

**Finding:** GEMINI-049-083 (round-3 high-lane adjudication for #8869).
Mechanism CONFIRMED (executed through the full interceptor chain on #8869);
consequence CONFIRMED SMALLER than reported. Still RED at master `6fa3310c0`.

## Mechanism (unchanged at tip)

- `computeFabricAuthToken` (`pkg/grpcapi/fabric_auth.go:122-129`) signs
  `domain || LE64(window)` and nothing else — no method, peer, request, or
  nonce binding.
- `checkFabricAuth` (`:269-330`) receives `method` and uses it ONLY for
  logging (`:320,325`); verification (`verifyFabricAuthToken`, `:144-160`)
  still accepts windows ±1.
- Fabric listener still plaintext (`buildFabricServer`, `server.go:959-976`:
  no `grpc.Creds`).
- No nonce, no replay cache. A token minted for `GetStatus` verifies for
  `ClearSessions`, both proxied failover forms, `MonitorInterface`, and the
  allowlisted `ShowText` topic (allowlist `server.go:1115-1121` + request-action
  gates `isFabricSafeSystemAction` / `isFabricSafeShowText`).

## Consequence, bounded (per the executed merits analysis on #8869)

- Replay window is 30–59s, not 60–90s (verifier-relative ±1).
- No periodic token feed: `GetStatus` dials are operator-driven, so capture
  requires sniffing during an operator cross-node RPC, then acting in-window.
- Heartbeat MACs are domain-separated (`heartbeat.go`, `fabric_auth.go:109-112`
  rationale) and not substitute tokens.
- Reach is bounded: 5 unary + 2 failover forms + 1 stream + 1 ShowText topic;
  node lifecycle (`zeroize`/reboot) is NOT reachable; hardened configuration
  only (no key = no auth to replay).
- Net: "an on-segment attacker sniffing during an operator's cross-node RPC
  gets 30–59s of ClearSessions + RG failover".

## Why file despite the Residual-1 comment

The file header now documents window-replay as an accepted statelessness
trade-off. That covers the HORIZON, not CROSS-METHOD reuse: binding
`info.FullMethod` into the HMAC preserves statelessness exactly while killing
the probe->destructive escalation. The residual comment does not bless that.

## #10431 — [GEMINI-049-071] Host-inbound zones can lose all matchable ingress scope [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

`hostInboundViewIngressNetdevs`

returns early when `len(v.IngressNetdevs) == 0`, and a zone whose EVERY netdev

host-bound packet arriving on the zone's netdev addressed to another zone's
interface IP reaches the bare-`daddr` accept. The merits analysis on #8869
executed this shape (empty `IngressNetdevs` -> untrust drop rule gone).
The current #6619/#6564 warning is useful observability but does not enforce
the configured host-inbound deny; the commit still succeeds and the packet
is admitted by another zone's destination-only rule.

## #10432 — GEMINI-049-028: NAT64 embedded ICMP rewrite uses captured quote length [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-028.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs derives the translated embedded header length from bytes actually present in the ICMP quote. The v6->v4 path caps the advertised payload end at quote_in.len() (lines 3251-3261) and writes total = 20 + l4_len (3263-3267). The v4->v6 path similarly caps total_len_field to quote_in.len() (3380-3383), then writes IPv6 Payload Length from frag_hdr_len + l4_len (3397-3406).

Consequence: A standards-compliant ICMP error commonly carries only the original IP header plus 8 L4 bytes. The translated embedded packet therefore advertises the quote length, not the original inner datagram length required by RFC 7915 §§4.2/5.2. PMTUD and error consumers that validate the embedded packet against the outstanding datagram can reject the translated error or associate it incorrectly. The current outer-message truncation is safe, but it does not justify changing the inner advertised length.

Acceptance: Preserve original IPv4 Total Length / IPv6 Payload Length semantics in the translated embedded header while copying only quoted bytes, bound all writes to the fixed scratch buffer, and add v4->v6 and v6->v4 tests for a 28-byte quote of a 1500-byte original packet.

## #10433 — GEMINI-049-060: fence wait can discard an acknowledgement at timeout [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-060.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/cluster/sync_fence_ack_7147.go SendFenceAwait (lines 546-566) selects directly between the buffered waiter channel and timer.C. The timeout arm unregisters and returns without a second nonblocking waiter check. If an ACK was delivered before the deadline but the waiter goroutine is scheduled after the timer becomes ready, both cases are ready and Go may select the timer case.

Consequence: A valid peer fence confirmation can be reported as a timeout, increment FenceAcksTimedOut, and drive an unconfirmed-takeover warning despite the peer having completed the requested fence within the configured deadline. This is a scheduler race in the takeover safety/telemetry path, not merely a log-order issue.

Acceptance: Linearize the deadline arm with a nonblocking drain (or equivalent synchronization) so an ACK already available at expiry is consumed as success; only unregister and report timeout when no ACK is available. Add a deterministic test that preloads the ACK and makes timer.C ready together, plus controls for a true timeout and disconnect.

## #10434 — GEMINI-049-044: SNMPv3 ignores authoritative and context engine IDs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-044.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/snmp/v3.go decodes the USM engine ID into `_` at lines 209-214 and the scopedPDU contextEngineID into `_` at lines 335-340. The only scoped-context gate checks contextName (347-370); no comparison to Agent.engineID is made. The empty-user discovery special case at line 243 is separate and must remain supported.

Consequence: An authenticated request carrying this agent's valid USM credentials but a foreign msgAuthoritativeEngineID or contextEngineID is not rejected at the engine/context boundary. Foreign context requests with the default context name can be answered from this agent's local MIB view, while a manager addressing the wrong authoritative engine cannot receive the RFC 3414 unknown-engine Report/discovery behavior. This is a protocol/interoperability and context-isolation defect, not a claim that arbitrary unauthenticated packets bypass USM authentication.

Acceptance: For non-discovery requests, compare msgAuthoritativeEngineID with the local authoritative engine and return the standard usmStatsUnknownEngineIDs Report when it differs; require contextEngineID to identify the local engine before serving the default view (and return the specified no-such/error behavior for foreign contexts). Preserve the empty-user discovery exchange and existing non-default context isolation.

## #10435 — GEMINI-049-078: networkd omits MTUBytes for VLAN child network units [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-078.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/networkd/networkd.go renders MTUBytes for netdev/link generators (835-836, 871-872, 890-892) but generateNetwork (905-1008) never emits MTUBytes. Apply intentionally gives VLAN subinterfaces only a .network file; a VLAN child has no MAC-backed .link file to carry its configured MTU.

Consequence: A configured VLAN logical unit such as ge-0-0-1.50 with MTU 9000 is written a networkd unit with no MTU directive and can remain at the kernel default 1500. Jumbo traffic then fragments, fails, or PMTUD-blackholes on that subinterface while the configuration appears accepted.

Acceptance: Emit MTUBytes in the [Link] section of the generated .network for VLAN/logical interfaces with MTU > 0, without regressing unmanaged/disabled or parent-specific handling. Add a generator/Apply test asserting the VLAN child .network contains the configured MTU and a control for an interface already covered by .link/netdev output.

## #10436 — GEMINI-049-068: delayed NAPI bootstrap is not process-generation scoped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-068.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go starts a goroutine at lines 310-324 that sleeps three seconds, locks m.mu, checks only m.proc != nil, and calls bootstrapNAPIQueuesAsyncLocked("startup"). stopLocked increments m.procGen (process.go:423-449), but the delayed goroutine captures neither procGen nor a generation-specific cancellation signal.

Consequence: If helper generation G1 exits before readiness and a replacement G2 starts before G1's three-second sleep expires, G1's callback sees G2 in m.proc and submits load-bearing NAPI bootstrap probes against the wrong/early helper generation. Repeated crash/restart sequences leave stale callbacks competing with current startup callbacks; the existing two-second throttle bounds frequency but does not establish generation ownership.

Acceptance: Capture the process generation (and preferably the process/supervisor identity) when scheduling startup bootstrap, cancel or fence the callback on stop/crash, and re-check that identity under m.mu before submitting probes. Add a crash-then-restart test proving G1 never bootstraps G2, while the successful same-generation startup still bootstraps once.

## #10437 — GEMINI-049-086: REST and gRPC destination NAT views drop plural/name matches [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-086.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/api/nat.go natDestHandler (211-214) and pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go GetNATDestination (74-77) copy only rule.Match.DestinationAddress. The parser stores bracketed/repeated prefixes in DestinationAddresses and address-book references in DestinationAddressNames; pkg/natshow.RuleMatchDestination (84-96) already handles the complete singular/plural/name set and is used by other surfaces.

Consequence: A destination NAT rule matching multiple prefixes or an address-book name is returned with a blank or first-only DstAddr, so REST/gRPC consumers cannot reconstruct the actual match and can produce false policy-compliance or routing audits. The translation action itself is not changed by this reporting defect.

Acceptance: Use the shared complete destination matcher in both handlers and make the structured schema carry its canonical complete rendering (additive field if necessary, preserving compatibility). Add REST/gRPC parity tests for a plural prefix list and a destination-address-name rule, asserting no criterion is silently dropped.

## #10438 — GEMINI-049-085: REST and gRPC source NAT views drop off and match data [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-085.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/api/nat.go natSourceHandler (183-188) and pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go GetNATSource (46-51) set Type only for Then.Interface or Then.PoolName. They do not use the shared pkg/natshow.SourceRuleAction helper (rule_action_8580.go:47-60), so Then.Off and actionless tolerant-load rules serialize with an empty Type.

Consequence: REST and gRPC configuration inspection cannot distinguish a no-NAT exemption (then source-nat off) from an incomplete/actionless rule, so automation and security audits can miss an active exemption or misclassify its action. This filing is deliberately limited to the proven empty action/type defect; NATSourceInfo has no source-match field, and adding per-rule match predicates would require a separate API-contract decision rather than being assumed here. The dataplane NAT action itself is not claimed to be wrong.

Acceptance: Route both handlers through the shared SourceRuleAction renderer and emit off/interface/pool/none consistently. Add REST/gRPC parity tests for off and actionless rules. Do not silently change the existing schema contract while fixing the action rendering.

## #10439 — GEMINI-049-082: REST show-text dereferences nil config map slots [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-082.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/api/show_text.go dereferences present-but-nil map values in SNMP communities/trap groups (96-106), DHCP relay groups (118-130), firewall filters and terms (139-144), dynamic-address feeds (189-196), address-book entries/sets (215-224), application entries (235-241), and flow-monitoring templates (267-279). The applications application-set loop is guarded by #5221, proving this tolerant-load shape is reachable and the remaining loops are inconsistent.

Consequence: A tolerantly loaded, restored, or peer-synced config containing one nil slot makes the affected REST show-text request panic and return a failed connection/500 under net/http (the net/http server recovers a handler panic; this does not by itself prove process termination). The affected topic is unavailable and repeated requests can create repeated panic/log/goroutine churn, even though the caller only has read permission.

Acceptance: Every show-text map/slice iteration must skip or safely render nil entries/terms without panicking, preserving all valid siblings and deterministic output. Add one live-handler regression covering each nil-valued map family (including nil firewall term) and assert a successful response; do not rely on process-wide panic recovery as the correctness mechanism.

## #10440 — GEMINI-049-088: dialPeer ignores caller cancellation during peer probes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-088.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/grpcapi/server_diag.go declares dialPeer with no context (28) and performs each GetStatus liveness probe under context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second) (77-81). Production callers such as server_show_forwarding.go:125-128 invoke it before their caller-scoped RPC, and server_show.go documents that the 5s post-dial timeout does not cover this up-to-two-fabric probe budget.

Consequence: A canceled or short-deadline inbound request can leave its server goroutine dialing/probing for up to roughly two seconds per fabric after the client is gone. Each probe reaches peer GetStatus, which consumes the session-walk limiter and can walk the peer v4/v6 session tables, wasting bounded but load-bearing control-plane work under cancellation storms.

Acceptance: Thread the caller context through every dialPeer call, derive each dial and probe deadline from it, stop immediately on cancellation, and add a test with an already-canceled context plus a blocked fake peer proving no probe proceeds. A cheaper health RPC may be a separate optimization, but cancellation propagation is required.

## #10441 — GEMINI-049-087: GetRoutes omits configured VRF routing tables [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Finding: GEMINI-049-087.

Mechanism: At both audit base b0f3aba21aede755573fb61714d3bfad15b795ab and current master 6fa3310c0609c4f2cb8547021db8cfa9ceda5883, pkg/grpcapi/server_routing.go GetRoutes (33-76) calls s.routing.GetRoutes(), and pkg/routing/routing.go defines that operation as the main kernel table only (148-149). The all-table implementation already exists at routing/routes.go:185-216 and is used by text show paths; it iterates configured VRF tables. GetRoutesResponse/RouteInfo currently have no table identity.

Consequence: Structured gRPC route consumers receive main-table entries but no entries from configured/learned VRF tables, so tenant routing topology and control-plane state are incomplete in multi-VRF deployments. This is an observability contract defect, not a claim that the kernel VRF tables themselves are absent.

Acceptance: Define the RPC contract to return all configured tables (including stable table/RIB identity in each route or a table selector), call the all-table path with the live routing-instance configuration, preserve partial-family/table error reporting, and add a fake-netlink test proving a VRF route appears with its table identity.

## #10458 — VRF terminator has no day-2 async-delete recovery (follow-up #10421) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Follow-up to #10421 (residual from Rev10430 post-merge review of PR #10430, accepted as non-blocking for the merge which strictly improves startup + in-apply coverage).

## The gap
Day-2 async-delete AFTER a successful reassert has zero recovery paths: cleanup can finish after Apply returns while the retry loop returns early when no error debt exists. A pref-2000 delete landing after a green reassert is never re-driven (no tail verifier, no always-on reconciler for the terminator).

## Fix direction
Either a synchronous networkd completion bound with deleter trace (prove the deleter cannot run post-Apply), or a day-2 tail/always-on verifier (periodic or event-driven reassert with RED cells). The merged in-apply + startup-tail + debt-loop coverage stays; this closes the post-success async window.

## #10467 — userspace FBF routing-instance steer not enforced: #10136 fixed leg leaks with PBR present [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-19)

Follow-up to #10136: the decisive fixed leg leaks at the userspace enforcement point.

## What is wrong

The `wire_routing_separation` fixed leg steers an exact probe tuple (owned LAN ingress `reth1`/`ge-0-0-1`, UDP) into an EMPTY temporary VRF via an exact `sfmix-pbr` input FBF term (`then routing-instance wire-10136`). The clean leg must therefore hit a userspace route miss and be denied. Instead the probe transits exactly like the control:

- Ledger `74322032d8e6fa8b` (`loss-userspace-cluster`, `2026-09-19T10:41:36Z`): FAIL, `probe_offered=1000 probe_leaked=1000 control_offered=1500 control_observed=1500 cksum_bad=0`.
- Attestation: `exe_check=MATCH`, `exe_scope=both`; build `eceb0a37c51262f2ca0d9ac8fede8391287f07d8085eb3df1016b2c19b0ccbc2` from clean master `11395ebd5` running on both nodes.
- Config archive: `/var/tmp/xpf-wire-routing-separation-1789814469`.

This is NOT a missing-kernel-rule harness artifact:

- `pbr-rules.set` records the live PBR rule at offer time: `31001: from 10.0.61.102 to 172.16.80.201 iif ge-0-0-1 ipproto udp dport 48741 lookup 210564` (exact tuple, table `210564` = the empty temporary VRF, verified empty pre-offer).
- `session-0.txt` / `session-1.txt` record `Total sessions: 0` for BOTH node stanzas each (destination/port-scoped clear + exact-absence proof ran on both cluster nodes before the FBF term was installed).
- The near-miss control differs only in the routed-table dimension and emerged 1500/1500, proving the capture window.

## Mechanism

The probe offered on the product-owned LAN/XDP ingress follows main's already-proven VLAN-80 route (`ge-0-0-2.80`) to the managed peer instead of being steered into the empty VRF at the userspace FBF enforcement point. Kernel PBR was present and the VRF table was empty, so the FBF `routing-instance` term was not enforced where the userspace dataplane makes its decision. Same shape as the #10466 diagnostic row `81aa0d69c9bb1c29`, now reproduced on clean current master with dual-node zero-session markers.

## Restore

Both nodes' normalized pre/post config SHA equal (`f40e51f2208fa6e70070e58475501bfc504a108ee04dffd7e415b113baf09d91`); kernel rule/link/table restore passed inside the gate (no harness-void demotion); a locked read-only post-check confirmed 0 `wire-10136` config lines, `vrf-wire-10136` absent, pref-2000 l3mdev rule present, and table 210564 empty on both nodes.

## Repro

Deploy current master to both loss-userspace nodes, then `make test-wire-routing-separation` (single fixed leg; no broken leg was run because the fixed leg must pass first).

Refs #10136

Follow-up to #10470 (S5, merged): post-merge review surfaced one narrow race + three test-hardening gaps in the new capture/reinject code.

## #10486 — REST, gRPC, and CLI session-filter contracts diverge [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The REST session-filter query builder takes `protocol` raw with no validation while fail-closing every other filter dimension, and the gRPC surface rejects the same token.

- `pkg/api/sessions.go:1358`: `q.proto = r.URL.Query().Get("protocol")` sits among the `zone` / `nat_only` / `snatPool` / `source_prefix` / `destination_prefix` / `source_port` / `destination_port` branches, which all return an HTTP-400 reason string on bad input.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go` validates with `appid.ProtocolNumberLenient` and raises `InvalidArgument`, with a comment stating the exact hazard ("an invalid protocol would otherwise iterate to an empty list and return as a *successful* RPC").

So REST answers `200` + empty list where gRPC rejects. The on-box CLI arm (`pkg/cli`) is a third contract that was not differenced token-by-token here.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `pkg/api/sessions.go:1350-1408` (unvalidated `protocol`, every sibling fail-closed)
- `pkg/api/sessions.go:1434,1478,1784-1792` (`protoFilterMatches`)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:436-446,494-503` (`ProtocolNumberLenient` validation + rationale comment)

Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. Same logical query returns success+empty on REST and a rejection on gRPC; automation cannot distinguish "no sessions" from "bad filter" on REST.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- Validate the REST `protocol` token with the same taxonomy as its sibling branches (400 + reason), or route all three surfaces through one shared `protoFilterMatches`-style helper.
- Add REST tests for valid, invalid, and numeric protocol tokens.
- Do not reintroduce delete-widening: the read path here is non-destructive.

## Limits

Token-by-token comparison across the three surfaces was not reproduced; the CLI arm was not differenced. Unverified 18/26 arithmetic from the source review is explicitly out of scope.

## Adjacent (not owners)

- #2935 (closed): REST case-sensitivity / numeric matching — different corrective scope.
- #3439 (closed): H5/L2 remote-CLI/gRPC strictness — the gRPC-side validation it asked for has since landed; the REST-side residual remains.

## Bug

`docs/refactoring-audit-accepted.txt` carries accepted entries that no longer describe live files, and the gate never re-checks them. `isAccepted` (`pkg/refactoraudit/audit_touched_test.go:187-197`) matches path plus tier only — no LOC re-check, no expiry — so accepted entries are permanent and silently pre-authorize future regrowth past their floors.

Two dead licences at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`:

- `pkg/api/metrics_userspace.go`, accepted `[REFACTOR]` "crossed 2000 at 2010 LOC" — measures **529** lines (split out under #7700, whose scope explicitly required pruning this entry once under the floor; the prune never happened).
- `pkg/vrrp/instance.go`, accepted `[WATCH]` at 1500 — measures **825** lines.

An independent heatmap recomputation corroborates from a second direction: `metrics_userspace.go` appears in the "left the heatmap" set.

- `docs/refactoring-audit-accepted.txt` lines 24 and 26; `wc -l` = 529 (`pkg/api/metrics_userspace.go`), 825 (`pkg/vrrp/instance.go`)
- `pkg/refactoraudit/audit_touched_test.go:183-197` (path+tier only)
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

Medium. Dead accepted entries silently pre-authorize any future regrowth of those files past their floors; the gate's decision record drifts from reality with no signal.

## #10488 — Touched modularity gate treats pure renames as new crossings [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The touched modularity gate treats pure renames as new crossings. Confirmed with a throwaway pure-rename control under Git's default configuration:

- `git diff --name-status` recognizes `R100 old.go -> new.go`,
- but the gate's `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d` (`scripts/refactoring-audit-touched.sh:100-115`) emits only the destination path. Its base lookup then probes `<merge-base>:new.go`, misses the old source blob, and sets `base_loc='-'` (`pkg/refactoraudit/audit_touched_test.go:63-65` measures a missing base path as `-`). The control probe produced `- 1701 pkg/rename_control/new.go`.

The false-positive mechanism survives default rename detection: the gate loses the old→new mapping before measuring.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `scripts/refactoring-audit-touched.sh:100-115` (`--name-only`, destination-only base lookup)
- `pkg/refactoraudit/audit_touched_test.go:63-65` (missing base path measured as `-`)
- Throwaway control (retained in research run dir, `q02-f6-rename-control.*`): default `diff.renames` unset, `--name-status` = `R100 old.go new.go`, `--name-only` = `new.go`, probe output `- 1701 .../new.go`
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Low. Developer-friction false positive, not a missed defect: pure renames get flagged as new modularity crossings.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- Carry the old→new mapping (`--name-status -M`) or resolve the merge-base blob/content hash before measuring.
- Adding `-M` to the existing `--name-only` command alone is insufficient (still destination-only output).
- Add a pure-rename control test: rename with no content change is not flagged.

## Limits

The 400-commit window is outside the evidence clone; the historical 11-rename census remains unverified.

## #10490 — Showaudit name discovery misses quarantined-state builders [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The showaudit gate discovers builder drop predicates purely by NAME, and `config.QuarantinedZoneNames` evades it. The contract is stated verbatim in `docs/engineering-style.md`: "A fail-closed exclusion owes a show-surface annotation (#6534)". `pkg/showaudit` is its gate.

`TestEveryBuilderDropPredicateIsRegistered6534` (`surface_gate_6534_test.go:232-281`) scans `pkg/dataplane/userspace` for `config.*` calls and keeps only those matching `dropPredicateName = /(?:Excluded|Unusable|Disarmed)Reason$|Exclusions$|Unsupported$|Undefined$/` (:214). `config.QuarantinedZoneNames` is called from the builder at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:145` and `zones_quarantine.go:65,236` — and its name matches none of those alternations. So zone quarantine, a fail-closed exclusion, passes the gate with no show family registered (the gate covers exactly 7 families at :82-194, with no zone row), and the degraded `ZoneIDCollisions` quarantine show omission persists.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `pkg/showaudit/surface_gate_6534_test.go:196-214` (name-only discovery regex + its own caveat), `:82-194` (exactly 7 families, no zone row), `:232-281` (exact-equality gate driven by that regex)
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:145`, `zones_quarantine.go:65,236` (`config.QuarantinedZoneNames` called by the builder)
- `docs/engineering-style.md` `#6534` section
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

High. The gate that enforces "every fail-closed exclusion has a show annotation" is blind to zone quarantine by construction (name discovery), so the exclusion ships with no operator visibility and the gate stays green.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- One of: rename the predicate to `*ExcludedReason`, register the zone family explicitly, or replace name-discovery with a type/marker mechanism (design decision).
- The exact-equality gate carries a zone family row and fails if quarantine loses its show registration.
- The `ZoneIDCollisions` quarantine show omission is linked to PR #3837's merged scope (regression); keep the independent `u04` `LastSnapshotRejectReasons` show gap separate.

## Limits

None material. The remediation choice is a design decision, not a verification gap.

## Adjacent

- PR #3837 (merged): quarantine implementation owner; the quarantine-show part of this finding is a regression against its scope.

## #10491 — VRRP VIP add and remove paths classify errno inconsistently [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The VRRP VIP add and remove paths classify errno inconsistently, and the failure direction is the dangerous one.

- Add path (`pkg/vrrp/instance_vip.go:208-216`): classifies `AddrAdd` failure by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "exists")` and on match records the VIP as APPLIED. No errno unwrap.
- Remove path 70 lines below (`:288-291`): uses `errors.Is(err, unix.EADDRNOTAVAIL)` first and documents why at `:285-287` ("errors.Is unwraps the netlink errno even when it is annotated with NLMSGERR_ATTR TLV text; the string check is a belt-and-suspenders match for wrappers that only expose Error()").

`res.failed` feeds `res.ok()` (:153), which gates `becomeMaster`'s fail-closed refusal to claim ownership (`instance_transition.go:108-137`). A text-only match can misclassify annotated netlink errors, recording a failed add as APPLIED (or vice versa) at the ownership gate.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `pkg/vrrp/instance_vip.go:208-216` (text-only EEXIST on add) vs `:271-293` (`errors.Is` + documented rationale on remove)
- `pkg/vrrp/instance_vip.go:153` (`res.ok()`); `pkg/vrrp/instance_transition.go:108-137` (fail-closed ownership refusal driven by `res.failed`)
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Low. Classification asymmetry at the ownership gate; a reachable non-EEXIST text mismatch remains unproven (see Limits).

## Fix direction / acceptance

- The add path unwraps with `errors.Is(err, unix.EEXIST)` first, keeping the string check only as a documented fallback mirroring the remove path's rationale.
- Symmetric unit coverage for annotated (`NLMSGERR_ATTR` TLV) netlink errors on both paths.

## Limits

No enumeration of netlink errno strings containing "exists"; no execution. File is the asymmetry only.

## Adjacent (not owner)

- #5082 (closed): VRRP VIP actuation / fail-closed ownership — broader scope, does not own this exact add/remove classification path.

## #10492 — Debug Rust cargo leg uses unanchored substring filters [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The only cargo test leg with overflow checks and live `debug_assert!` selects tests by unanchored substring. `Makefile:362-367` defines two cargo legs:

- line 364 runs `--release` (overflow checks off, `debug_assert!` compiled out);
- line 366 runs WITHOUT `--release` but with the trailing filter `-- --test-threads=1 frame nat session checksum`.

`cargo test` treats those as unanchored substring filters over test paths. The "coordinator contains nat" observation is literally true (c-o-o-r-d-i-**nat**-o-r), so coordinator tests are swept into the debug leg incidentally — the debug leg's membership is accidental substring matching, not intent.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `Makefile:362-367` (release leg at :364, unanchored-substring debug leg at :366-367)
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. Debug-assert/overflow coverage applies to an accidental test set: renaming a test module can silently drop it from (or sweep it into) the checked leg with no signal.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- The debug leg uses anchored/exact selectors (e.g. `--exact` with full test paths, or explicit test targets) with a comment stating each leg's purpose.
- Coordinator tests are selected intentionally or excluded deliberately — either way, by exact match, not substring accident.
- A test-name change that would silently leave the debug leg fails loudly (or the selection is by target, immune to renames).

## Limits

No execution; no `debug_assert!` census. Test-count denominators remain unverified.

## Review origin

## #10493 — Unused sync-auth helper remains load-bearing in security prose [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

`syncAuthDecision` has zero production callers, but live-tense documentation asserts it as the operative security mechanism. Confirmed by exhaustive call-site search: ``grep -rn 'syncAuthDecision(' pkg cmd --include='*.go' | grep -v _test`` returns only the declaration at `pkg/cluster/sync_auth.go:461`. The only other references are tests (`sync_auth_test.go:458`, `sync_auth_strict_7441_test.go:237`) and prose — and `sync_auth_test.go:188-193` acknowledges the function is not load-bearing.

Meanwhile live-tense prose asserts it as the mechanism in at least four places:

- `pkg/cluster/README.md:642-663` ("syncAuthDecision no longer consults peerAuthSeen ... An unkeyed/legacy peer is rejected")
- `README.md:2532-2535` and `:2615-2616` ("a hostile stream cannot, because syncAuthDecision refuses an unkeyed peer on a fresh connection")
- `pkg/cluster/sync_auth_strict_7441.go:59-61`, `pkg/cluster/status.go:771-773`, `pkg/cluster/sync_config_crypto.go:61-63`

A reader auditing the hostile-stream path is told the guard is `syncAuthDecision`; the guard that actually runs is `performSyncHandshake`.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- Call-site search as above (declaration only); live-tense citations listed above
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. Stale security prose over a dead helper misdirects auditors and incident responders about which code enforces unkeyed-peer rejection.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- Either delete `syncAuthDecision` (preferred, given the test acknowledgment) or wire it back into the live path — then sweep every live-tense citation to describe the mechanism that actually runs.
- A prose-cited security mechanism must have a production caller; add a guard (test or lint) or remove the claims.

## Limits

The rename-and-build proof was not run; a caller reachable only by reflection or code generation would evade grep (unlikely in this codebase). The "misled a prior reviewer" cost claim is unverified.

## Adjacent (not owner)

- #6881 (closed): prior `sync_auth.go` prose sweep — different sites; this residual is distinct.

## #10496 — Serial make test aborts before the Rust prerequisite [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The serial aggregate gate does not reach Rust. `Makefile:99` declares `test: test-go test-rust`; with default serial Make, a non-zero exit from `test-go` aborts before `test-rust`. The Makefile comment at `:88-98` states both the first-failing-prerequisite behavior and #4006's purpose.

`test-go` is red because `pkg/refactoraudit` runs uncached inside it (`Makefile:248-252`) and `TestStructMetricIsTypesNotFields6937` fails with 21 distinct `CompileResult` field types against a floor of 20. The bounded defect: default serial `make test` never reaches `test-rust`; `test-rust` remains runnable directly (`docs/log/9919.md:132-133` independently records direct `make test-rust`).

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `Makefile:88-99` (serial aggregate and first-failure semantics), `:248-252` (uncached refactoraudit in `test-go`), `:362-367` (`test-rust`)
- `pkg/refactoraudit/structs.go:76-99` plus `structs_6937_test.go:94-97` (the Go-leg red)
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. The default `make test` gate silently stops covering Rust whenever the Go leg is red — exactly when aggregate signal matters most.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- Default `make test` reaches `test-rust` despite a failing `test-go` prerequisite (e.g. continue-on-failure aggregate, `-k`-style semantics, or split default targets), while still failing overall.
- Document the aggregate semantics at the `test:` target.

## Limits

The 2026-09-14 date from the source review is outside the evidence window and unverified. Post-pin, the control checkout contains `.github/workflows/close-keyword-lint.yml`, which invalidates any broad no-CI premise — this issue claims only the serial composite-gate blockage. No claim is made about branch protection (not checked) or about Rust never having run.

## Adjacent (not owner)

- #4006 (closed): historical `make test` omission of the Rust suite — different mechanism (omission vs. serial blockage).

## #10497 — Live struct calibration can redden the Go gate without a floor gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The struct-watch calibration reddens the Go gate from live-tree drift, while nothing enforces the floor it calibrates. Two confirmed structural halves:

1. `StructRow.Tag()` has exactly two consumers in the tree: the calibration test (`pkg/refactoraudit/structs_6937_test.go:90,94,109`) and the heatmap generator (`pkg/refactoraudit/structaudit/main.go:63`). Nothing enforces `StructWatchFloor` as a gate — no test fails when an arbitrary struct crosses 20 distinct types; the only assertion is the three-point calibration (Engine must flag, CompileResult must not, xpfCollector must not).
2. The canary calibrates on LIVE structs: `structs_6937_test.go:65` calls `GoStructs` over the real `pkg/` tree, so any unrelated field addition to CompileResult, Engine, or xpfCollector can tip it.

Measured at evidence revision: CompileResult = 32 fields / 21 distinct types, of which `[]MTUUnconverged` is one — and removal yields 20, which still tags (`structs.go:76-99`, `>=` comparison), so the implied remediation does not even work.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `pkg/refactoraudit/structs.go:76-99` (floor 20, `>=` comparison)
- `pkg/refactoraudit/structs_6937_test.go:65` (live-tree scan), `:90,94,109` (the only `Tag()` assertions)
- `pkg/refactoraudit/structaudit/main.go:63` (the only other consumer)
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. Unrelated struct growth anywhere in `pkg/` can red the Go gate via the live calibration, while the floor itself is unenforced — the gate couples every contributor's build to `CompileResult`'s field count without buying the invariant.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- Either enforce the floor as a real gate (fail when any struct crosses 20 distinct types) or decouple calibration from live structs (fixture-based canaries).
- Adding a field to `CompileResult`/`Engine`/`xpfCollector` must not red an unrelated contributor's gate run unless the floor invariant itself is violated.

## Limits

#9841 is outside the evidence window, so the pre-commit count cannot be confirmed; the point stands regardless since the implied fix does not work at the evidence revision. Historical #9841 attribution remains unverified. (This is the Go-only split of the combined row; the Rust leg stays NEEDS_VALIDATION and is not filed.)

## Adjacent (not owner)

- #9841 (closed): `MTUUnconverged` implementation — different scope (implementation vs. calibration causality).

## #10498 — Named pre-L3 drops have no dedicated telemetry [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

Three named pre-L3 drops are silent: no dedicated counter, event, or log. In `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs`:

1. the UMEM slice failure at `:248-253` pushes the descriptor to `scratch_recycle` and continues with NO counter and not even a `touched` flag;
2. the #10313 unknown-VLAN drop at `:265-275` sets only `telemetry.counters.touched = true` before recycling;
3. the #10314 destination-MAC drop at `:281-290` does the same.

`touched` is not a tally — it is a boolean set in the same idempotent way at a dozen unrelated sites (`disposition.rs:607-740`, `icmp.rs:291,323`, `poll_stages.rs:887,1100`, `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1445`), i.e. a flush/liveness flag. This contradicts the `docs/engineering-style.md` runtime policy row requiring observable drops.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:248-253` (uncounted UMEM slice failure), `:265-275` (#10313, touched-only), `:281-290` (#10314, touched-only)
- `touched` set identically at the sites above (flag, not tally)
- `docs/engineering-style.md` runtime policy row
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Low. Silent packet drops in the pre-L3 path are invisible to operators: no counter distinguishes "no traffic" from "traffic dropped", complicating outage triage.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- A dedicated counter per named drop (UMEM slice failure, unknown-VLAN, dst-MAC guard), surfaced in `show`/telemetry.
- `touched` remains liveness-only; drop accounting does not rely on it.

## Limits

Not every drop site in the pre-L3 path was enumerated — no claim of "exactly three" drops total; only these three named sites are filed.

## Adjacent (not owners)

- #10313 (closed): unknown-VLAN classification — the causal guard owner, not the telemetry.
- #10314 (closed): destination-MAC / anti-loop guard — same; both must stay linked as causal owners.

- that test inserts only its own directory on `sys.path` (`_HERE = scripts/dist`, lines 48-49) and then loads `scripts/image/bake.py` by path as module `xpf_bake` (lines 52-54);
- executing `bake.py` runs its line 54, `sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "scripts", "dist"))`, and then line 56, `from bridge_floor_10171 import bridge_floor_offline_snippet`;
- but `bridge_floor_10171.py` lives at `scripts/image/bridge_floor_10171.py`, not `scripts/dist` — so the import resolves against the wrong directory and the signing gate goes unexecuted.

This root cause was established independently rather than accepting the source claim's attribution.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `scripts/run-selftests.sh` python self-test section (globs `scripts/dist/test_*.py`)
- `scripts/dist/test_dist_resign_9920.py:48-54` (`sys.path` = `scripts/dist` only; loads `scripts/image/bake.py` by path)
- `scripts/image/bake.py:54-56` (inserts `scripts/dist`, then imports `bridge_floor_10171`)
- `bridge_floor_10171.py` exists at `scripts/image/`, not `scripts/dist/`
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. The distribution re-sign gate is silently unexecuted: `run-selftests.sh` reports without ever running the signing test, so signing regressions ship undetected.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- The selftest resolves `bridge_floor_10171` (extend `sys.path` to include `scripts/image`, or make the bake import package-relative).
- `test_dist_resign_9920.py` executes under `run-selftests.sh` with red-on-revert proof (break the import → the runner fails).

## Limits

The script was not executed (out of scope). The `33a60fc49` attribution and the "38 tests / rc=0 after restore" figures are unverified.

## Adjacent (not owner)

- #9920 (closed): dist re-sign provenance / manifest enforcement — the enforcement owner; this issue is the unexecuted-test residual.

## #10500 — Degraded snapshot collision and rejection state lacks a show surface [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

The daemon knows it is in a degraded snapshot state and no `show` command on any surface reports it. `ProcessStatus.ZoneIDCollisions` and `ProcessStatus.LastSnapshotRejectReasons` are populated by the manager (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_status.go:27,31`, fed from `manager_compile.go:162-179,428`) and consumed in exactly two places: the Prometheus collector at `pkg/api/metrics_userspace.go:170` and `:184`, plus a one-shot log/warning path (`protocol.go:747`, `policies_reject_identity_9584.go:17`, `manager.go:233`).

A search of the operator render packages — `pkg/cli`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/format`, `pkg/natshow` — found zero references to either field.

**Bounded scope: this issue files only the `LastSnapshotRejectReasons` no-operator-show residual.** `ZoneIDCollisions` is excluded here because closed PR #3837 (referenced implementation merged) owns that show+metric observability/regression scope (see the `q04` findings filed alongside). Metrics/log consumers are existing partial observability.

## Evidence (pinned at `1a6952b61ef5f7dcf0fdd1786d91b14c9bb3f705`)

- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_status.go:27,31` (fields published on `ProcessStatus`)
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:162-179,428` (recording)
- `pkg/api/metrics_userspace.go:170,184` (Prometheus, one of two consumers)
- Zero occurrences of either identifier in `pkg/cli`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/format`, `pkg/natshow`
- Freshness: control HEAD `1b64806cf541978e26fda671b446fc2fdf2c2e78` touches none of these paths.

## Impact

Medium. A rejected/degraded snapshot is operator-invisible outside Prometheus scrapes and a one-shot warning: `show` on every surface reports a healthy system while the dataplane never took the config.

## Fix direction / acceptance

- An operator `show` surface (CLI, gRPC, or REST) reports `LastSnapshotRejectReasons` when a snapshot is rejected/degraded.
- Red-on-revert: produce a rejected snapshot → the show surface names the rejection reasons.

## Limits

Whether the one-shot warning reaches an operator-visible log by default was not verified.

## Adjacent (not owners)

- PR #3837 (merged): `ZoneIDCollisions` show+metric scope owner — explicitly out of this issue's scope.
- #9584 (closed): duplicate-policy-name `DuplicateRuleId` case — distinct corrective scope.

## #10507 — HA: standby FabricRedirect revalidation stamps recorded-egress Permit surviving promotion (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

# z07-ha-policy-F1: standby FabricRedirect revalidation stamps recorded-egress Permit at live generation; stamp survives promotion (fail-open)

## What
On a standby, every peer-owned session hit is rewritten
`HAInactive → FabricRedirect` before M2 (`redirect_via_fabric_if_needed`,
`fabric.rs:557-569`). `to_zone_override` keys on `disposition==FabricRedirect`
ALONE (`policy_revalidation.rs:738-740`) and wins over the live id (`:754`) —
substituting the PEER-RECORDED `metadata.egress_zone` for the live to-zone and
discarding a meaningful `live_to_id` that `#326` re-resolution computed from a
real local egress. A Permit on that weaker (live-from, recorded-to) pair calls
`mark_policy_revalidated`, stamping the LIVE generation. Promotion is an
in-place `refresh_for_ha_transition` rewriting decision/metadata/last_seen/
`first_held_ns`/`seen_rg_epoch` but NO revalidation field — the stamp survives,
so the promoted node forwards a flow the live policy denies until the next
config-generation publish or session end.

## Evidence (3/3 lanes, STATIC, High)
Full write/read chain verified at `b71c52d6` by all lanes (override keying,
redirect disposition, `#326` live re-resolution, stamp call, promotion field
preservation).

## Narrowed
- Population: peer-owned sessions judged on standby, promoted before the next
  generation-bumping publish. No claim about owner-side judgments.

## Acceptance
- Judge standby FabricRedirect hits against the live to-zone (or mark
  recorded-egress judgments so they cannot masquerade as live verdicts) +
  regression: standby Permit on diverged egress → promote → flow denied
  without waiting for a publish.

Severity: High (fail-open). Provenance: adversarial 3-lane research
(3/3 MATERIAL, High), pinned `b71c52d6`.

## #10508 — docs: fabric/session-sync docs deny the receiver-side per-hit policy contract + u16 zones as uint8 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

# z07-ha-policy-F2: fabric/session-sync docs misstate the receiver-side policy contract (established hits DO re-derive) + u16 zones documented as uint8

## What
Two live docs defects + one confirmed minor, all read at `b71c52d6`:
1. `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md:35-37`, in the lead "Solution —
   Three-Layer Fix" section of the named fabric entry point: "Established
   sessions skip policy evaluation (conntrack fast-path), so the zone mismatch
   ... doesn't matter." FALSE for the live userspace dataplane since
   `#8356`/`#9384`/`#9519`: an established hit DOES re-derive zone policy, and
   the mismatch owns dedicated machinery (`FromZoneSource::RecordedZone`,
   fabric ingress → `HitAuthority::Owner`). The section is eBPF-era (cites
   `bpf/xdp/xdp_zone.c`, absent at pin) with no historical marker; a repo-wide
   grep for `8356|9384|revalidat|RecordedZone|policy_revalidated` over the
   1326-line doc returns EMPTY. Link: F1 is a defect inside the mechanism the
   lead doc says does not exist.
2. `pkg/cluster/README.md` (4481 lines): EMPTY for
   `8356|policy revalidat|zone policy|7323` — no statement of the
   receiver-side per-hit re-judgment contract (import lands UNVALIDATED
   `policy_revalidated_gen: 0`, `install.rs:551`; receiver re-judges per hit).
   Narrowed: the README DOES document the `#3931` ConfigEpoch stale-install
   fence; the gap is specifically the per-hit re-judgment contract.
3. Minor CONFIRMED: `docs/session-sync-design.md:509-510` + `:534-535`
   document zone ids as uint8; code is u16 everywhere (Rust encoder
   `session_sync.rs:177-190` u16 LE `#3075`; Go decoder `eventstream.go`
   open/close arms; `SessionMetadata`/Zone types u16).

## #10509 — zone rename: commit-window transient foreign drops on every rename (deterministic, silent) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

# z07-ha-policy-F4-R1: commit-window transient foreign drops on every zone rename (deterministic, cluster-wide, silent)

## What
After a zone rename, the live arrival id (new `StableZoneID` hash, pure
function of name) can never equal recorded `metadata.ingress_zone` (old hash),
so `session_hit_authority` returns Foreign unavoidably; `foreign_hit_verdict`
judges (new arrival id → old recorded egress id) — a live+dead pair matching
no rule — falls to default deny and drops the packet (session untouched, no
revoke, no re-admit, silent but for `foreign_authority_drops`). The broader
"life-of-the-session outage" form is explicitly RETRACTED (refuted); what
stands is the bounded commit-window transient: a structurally-necessary window
with a deterministic trigger (every rename, cluster-wide, silent).

## Evidence (3/3 lanes; mechanism EXECUTED with control)
- Mechanism: rename → hash mismatch → Foreign → default-deny drop.
  Conceded by all lanes after dissent (Lane C conceded the key question).
- Magnitude unknown: affects precision-within-Low, not materiality.

## Narrowed (what is NOT claimed)
- NOT a persistent outage: transient window only. Siblings split separately:
  R2 partial-enumeration survivors NEEDS_VALIDATION (BPF BatchLookup failure
  reachability unproven); R3 mirror incompleteness NEG (closed by
  BPF-then-mirror-with-rollback); R4 first-policy/failover-before-rename
  separate filing.

## Acceptance
- Measuring follow-up (retained decisive check): quantify the window (packets/
  sessions affected per rename) + regression pinning the transient bound; then
  decide shrink-vs-accept on measured data.

Severity: Low (bounded transient). Provenance: adversarial 3-lane research
(3/3 MATERIAL Low), pinned `b71c52d6`.

## #10511 — policy-rematch extensive tears down renamed policies even when another policy permits (Junos parity gap) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

# policy-rematch extensive tears down renamed policies even when another policy permits (parity gap vs Junos; default/plain teardown is correct)

## What
`StablePolicyRuleID` embeds the policy name, so a rename makes the old key
disappear; `deletedPolicyRuntimeIDs` inserts the old nonzero id with no
rematch gate (`daemon_policy_invalidate.go:93-117`), `changedPolicyRuntimeIDs`
skips absent/deleted keys (`:643-665`), and `clearSessionsForDeletedPolicies`
tears down unconditionally (`:154-167`). Under `policy-rematch extensive` a
renamed policy's sessions die even when another policy still permits the flow.
Official Juniper Feature Explorer ("Policy rematch", feature/5004): DEFAULT
closes sessions on rename/deactivate/delete; PLAIN rematch covers changed
policies only; EXTENSIVE keeps the session when another allowing policy
matches. xpf matches default + plain and gaps extensive.

## Evidence (3/3 lanes)
- EXECUTED mechanism probes: middle rename → `deleted={1}`, `changed={}`
  (rematch off and on); zone rename → all nonzero old ids deleted; fake
  dataplane rename (id 1 removed, 2 retained). Existing daemon controls green.
- STATIC extensive reasoning: source proves `PolicyRematchExtensive` does not
  alter the unconditional deletion path (`:643-655` fingerprints common keys
  only). Existing probes did not exercise the alternate-policy preservation
  oracle — acceptance must.

## Narrowed (what is NOT claimed)
- Default/plain-rematch rename teardown is CORRECT Junos parity — REFUTED as a
  defect (source "cosmetic rename must preserve" framing rejected).
- Go deleted set is id>=1 only (id 0 excluded, `:37-66` overloaded wire rows);
  end-to-end first-policy policy-bound sessions are covered by the helper
  snapshot-rotation counter-handle purge (incl. rename); unrelated
  overloaded-zero sessions intentionally remain. Do not claim "every row".
- Zone rename shares the mechanism (same stable-key disappearance).
- M3 precedence included: arrival-zone mismatch sets Foreign before M2
  (`mod.rs:790-807`, `:1245-1280` dispatches `foreign_hit_verdict`, never
  session-hit revalidation); M1 normally deletes mirror-visible synced rows,
  leaving race/partial/mirror subsets.
- Log label (`change="deleted"`) dropped as an independent defect: Juniper
  models rename as delete/add; the internal label faithfully reports xpf's
  internal action absent a rename-event contract.
- U-1-extensive-gap (same run) cohorts here: same root.

## #10512 — commit invalidation misses deleted tenant on bare 5-tuple mirror collision; commit reports success [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

# Commit invalidation misses a deleted tenant on bare 5-tuple mirror collision (predicate shadow); commit reports success with helper sessions remaining

## What
`SessionKey` is the bare 5-tuple (no routing-domain axis); the BPF publisher
builds that key and overwrites with `BPF_ANY`
(`publish_conntrack.rs:118-145`), so two tenants sharing a tuple occupy ONE
row carrying the last publisher's value. The Go sweep enumerates that row and
matches only `val.PolicyID` (`daemon_policy_invalidate.go:449-461`): if the
surviving row carries tenant B's id while tenant A's policy was deleted, the
candidate set is empty, the empty delete returns nil, and the commit reports
success although A's domain-scoped helper session remains. The mirror's
`RoutingDomain` value cannot de-alias a key collision.

## Evidence (3/3 lanes, STATIC)
- In-repo measured: `docs/log/9146.md:16-40` (tenants A/B, domains
  100007/100008, two upserts, zero retractions on swap);
  `docs/log/9546.md:20-30` (enduring bound: BPF key has no domain axis).
- Scratch probes: fake mirror row with B's id survives an A-only id set with
  nil; A-row control deleted. Full daemon/userspace/configstore suites green.

## Narrowed (what is NOT claimed)
- Variant (b) under-targeting, DISTINCT from `#9364`'s fixed "once selected,
  scope the delete" variant (scoped delete names the surviving row's domain
  correctly) and from `#9526`'s first-policy/id-0 purge. Single-tenant and
  mirror-occupant-tenant deletes work.
- M2 fences many ordinary forward packets after deny/default changes, but
  conditionally — it does not repair the authoritative helper-table omission,
  especially for explicitly M2-declined populations; a standby has no packet
  to trigger M2.
- Requires exact same-5-tuple cross-domain overlap — but that is the supported
  overlapping-VRF case `9146.md` measures.

## Acceptance
Privileged two-domain same-tuple fixture: install both helper sessions, delete
only A's policy → A's helper rows deleted (or commit fails) while B remains;
repeat across standby/failover. (Bare-mirror discovery fix: per-domain
enumeration or de-aliasing — does NOT fix the sibling helper-error discard,
separate filing, same `#5578` contract.)

`Manager.BatchDeleteSessionsScoped` deletes the BPF mirror FIRST, then
discards the helper result (`_ = m.deleteHelperSessionsScopedV4(scoped)`,

"best-effort" comment). `deleteHelperSessionsScoped*Marked` DO retain

`manager_sessionsync_transmit.go:84-149`; `process_control.go:376-447`) — but
the caller drops it and returns the BPF `err` only. Mirror-success +
helper-failure → nil through `DeleteBatchKnownV4/V6` →
`deleteInvalidatedSessions` → daemon logs commit-clear success →
`applyAndSyncCommitted` sees `joined==nil` (`daemon_apply_commit.go:322-351`),

## #10514 — tolerant routing-instance + next-term contradiction renders without the ignored-next-term disclosure [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

# Tolerant routing-instance + next-term contradiction renders effective policy without the ignored-next-term disclosure (later terms silently dead)

## What
`filters.go:106-126` computes snapshot `NextTerm` as
`(term.NextTerm || term.Action == "") && term.RoutingInstance == ""`: a
tolerant term with empty action + `RoutingInstance=mgmt-vrf` + authored
`NextTerm=true` reaches the snapshot with `NextTerm=false`. The shared
renderer then prints `then routing-instance mgmt-vrf` + `then accept` and
never reaches its own `#10012` ignored-next-term disclosure branch
(`firewall_snapshot_render.go:135-160`). The strict gate rejects this shape —
only tolerant legacy/disk/older-ingress paths expose it. An operator reading
effective policy sees the real terminating accept but is never told the
persisted/authored next-term request was discarded, so later terms (e.g. an
SSH deny) can be dead without a diagnostic. (CLI + gRPC share the renderer:
`cli_show_security_filters.go:435-440`, `server_show_firewall.go:648-673`.)

## Evidence (3/3 lanes; EXECUTED)
- Scratch userspace probe: compiled `Action="" RI=mgmt-vrf NextTerm=true` →
  snapshot `NextTerm=false`; rendered output had RI + accept, no disclosure;
  discard+NextTerm control DID render the disclosure. Renderer controls green.

## Narrowed (what is NOT claimed)
- Enforcement-divergence REFUTED: Rust (`continue_term = action.is_empty() &&
  routing_instance.is_empty()`) and nft/runtime agree — RI terminating, empty
  action resolves accept, later terms dead. No data-plane fail-open. The
  effective render is truthful about enforcement; the defect is disclosure of
  the discarded authored bit. Not a duplicate of renderer-only `#10012`.

## Acceptance
Builder preserves the authored contradiction to the renderer (or renderer
re-derives it from raw): `show firewall effective` on a tolerant
RI+next-term fixture displays `(ignored — contradictory with terminating
action)` for the authored bit.

Severity: Low (operator disclosure). Provenance: adversarial 3-lane research
(3/3 MATERIAL, High), pinned `b71c52d6`.

`Exempt` for ESP/AH/ESP-in-UDP/NAT-T keepalives via `NotIsakmp` ("unconditional

verified `AttachedXDPIfindexes` over `xdpLinks` + `WithAttachedXDPFence` race
lease; ingress from `buildUserspaceIngressIfindexes`; attach from
`st.xdpIfindexes`). The fence builder appends every resolved tracked ifindex
name with NO link-type check (only xpf-usp1 gets a TUN-mode test). The sole
reconciler, `syncInterfaceAttachments`, returns VOID — on DetachXDP/DetachTC
error it warn-continues: no error return, no retry, no metric, no fail-closed
fallback, and neither caller can react.

## Evidence (3/3 lanes, STATIC)
All three sets + the void reconciler + warn-continue verified at `b71c52d6`.

## Narrowed (verified in code — the ledgered claim overgeneralizes)
DetachXDP has TWO failure modes; "the link stays in xdpLinks" holds for ONE:
- (a) `setXDPAttachedFlag` failure ⇒ link retained + still attached ⇒ fence
  keeps the pinhole ⇒ WIDENING as claimed. Precision: map and kernel AGREE
  (both attached) — "stale kernel truth" mislabels it; the staleness is
  intended-vs-actual (config intends detached).
- (b) `l.Close()` failure ⇒ `deleteXDPLink` still runs (`loader.go:719`) ⇒
  entry removed ⇒ fence omits ⇒ FAIL-CLOSED on the fence (residual:
  possibly-stranded kernel attachment + availability loss, not widening).
- Steady-state divergence unreachable (reconciler detaches the diff every
  compile); `#8279` keeps raw-L3 tunnels out of pendingXDP. Persistent
  widening needs a PERSISTENT BPF failure (plausible under map pressure,
  unproven). Confidence: Medium (2 lanes) / High (1 lane); verdict unanimous.

## Acceptance
Fault-inject both arms separately; read back `xdpLinks` + rendered
`AllowedIfnames` + forward verdict: (a) must currently pinhole (fix: fail-
closed fallback/retry/metric so callers can react); (b) must omit (pin the
fail-closed half). Then drive one descriptor with binding present but no
ingress-map entry and assert the `XDP_PASS` leg to replace the
comment-sourced arm with code.

Severity: Medium (structural + reachable-under-pressure widening).
Provenance: adversarial 3-lane research (3/3 MATERIAL, STATIC), `b71c52d6`.

## #10529 — [audit] dataplane interface address add classifies errno by text [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

## Bug

`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:418-429` reconciles desired interface addresses. On `addrAddSeam` failure it suppresses the warning and leaves `changed` false whenever `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "exists")` matches. The site therefore classifies a netlink add failure by text alone instead of unwrapping `unix.EEXIST`.

A non-EEXIST error whose text contains `exists` can be treated as an already-present address: the host-mutation flag is under-reported and the operator warning is skipped. A wrapped EEXIST whose text changes can be warned about and treated as a failed mutation. This is a separate failure policy from VRRP's ownership gate, but the taxonomy asymmetry is the same.

## Evidence

- Base `origin/master` at `b71c52d60`; exact production site: `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:418-426`.
- The add operation is independently test-seamed as `addrAddSeam` in `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_vlan_bringup_8122.go:84-90`.
- The site has no VRRP ownership publication, advert, GARP, or `vipDiverged` coupling; it only returns the `changed` mutation flag and controls the add warning. It is therefore separable from #10491 and should not be fixed as a drive-by in that VRRP change.
- The pinned `github.com/vishvananda/netlink v1.3.1` path preserves errno identity for NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG with `fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, msg)` (`nl/nl_linux.go:625-642`), but wrappers/future versions still motivate errno-first classification.

## Proposed fix and tests

Use `errors.Is(err, unix.EEXIST)` first and retain only a documented, narrow `file exists` fallback if the compatibility contract requires it. Add seam-driven tests for direct EEXIST, wrapped errno with annotation text, strerror-only fallback, non-EEXIST text containing bare `exists`, and other errno failures; assert both the returned mutation flag and warning behavior.

## Scope separation

#10491 remains limited to `pkg/vrrp/instance_vip.go` and its VRRP tests. This issue owns the dataplane compiler site and its own test fixtures. The fixes can land independently without shared production files.

## Provenance

Filed as the required separable follow-up from the #10491 plan review (2026-09-21).

## #10530 — Quarantined-zone annotations missing from adjacent show and telemetry surfaces [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

## Bug

Issue #10489 is limited to five zone-inventory show paths. The same StableZoneID quarantine can still be misrepresented by adjacent surfaces that iterate desired configuration or cr.ZoneIDs without consulting the quarantine verdict. The operator may see a quarantined zone's interface, screen, policy, metrics, session, or event state as if it were enforced.

## Evidence

- Interfaces: `pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces.go:117-125` derives iface-to-zone from desired config while `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_quarantine.go:96-99` unzones quarantined interfaces.
- Screen inventory: `pkg/cli/cli_show_security_screen.go:47-56` and `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_security_text.go:839-847` render `zonesByProfile` from desired config.
- Policy inventory: `pkg/api/security.go:193-203` and the gRPC policy inventory render authored policy rows; `ZoneDetailPolicySummary` (`pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:96-211`) does not consult quarantine even though `zoneKnown` does (`:1607-1615`).
- Prometheus per-zone series: `pkg/api/metrics_counters.go:620-657` reads `cr.ZoneIDs` and labels survivor-id counters with the quarantined name.
- Sessions/events: zone loops in `pkg/cli/session_filter.go:385`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:531`, and `pkg/api/sessions.go:1258` use desired/compiled maps without a quarantine annotation.
- Runtime fact: `assignZoneIDs` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:355-358`) assigns the same StableZoneID to both colliding names, so unqualified counters can be survivor traffic under the quarantined name.

## Scope

Sweep the listed interfaces, screen-zone reverse maps, policy inventory and zone-detail policy summaries, Prometheus per-zone series, and sessions/events filters/renderers. Reuse #10489's shared `ZoneQuarantineExclusions` / `ZoneQuarantineExcludedReason` verdict and define conservative marker, counter, and absent-state behavior per surface. Add fail-on-revert tests for a `z174`/`z214` collision and ordinary no-collision configs.

## Relationship

This is an adjacent-surface follow-up to #10489, which covers only local CLI zone inventory, gRPC structured zones, gRPC text zones-detail, REST security/statistics zones, and the remote CLI zone view. Do not widen #10489's behavior scope; land this separately after its shared verdict contract is available.

## Provenance

Filed during the #10489 plan delta review after adversarial review identified the residual surfaces. The quarantine runtime is #3719 / merged PR #3837; the missing operator annotation is #10489.

## #10531 — Structured zone inventory lacks truthful quarantine state over GetZones and REST [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

## Bug

Issue #10489's text inventory surfaces can be annotated from the shared quarantine verdict, but structured zone inventory handlers still have no truthful quarantine state on the wire. `GetZones` and REST `/api/v1/security/zones` currently serialize authored `ZoneInfo` rows while the dataplane may have dropped a colliding zone; old or new structured consumers cannot distinguish an enforced survivor from a quarantined loser.

## Evidence

- gRPC `GetZones` builds `pb.ZoneInfo` from `cfg.Security.Zones` at `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go:18-141`; `proto/xpf/v1/xpf.proto:244-301` has no quarantine state fields.
- REST `zonesHandler` builds `api.ZoneInfo` from `cfg.Security.Zones` at `pkg/api/security.go:19-147`; `pkg/api/types.go:107-184` has no quarantine state/presence field.
- `assignZoneIDs` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:355-358`) assigns the same StableZoneID to both colliding names, so structured responses can carry survivor counters under the quarantined name.
- Runtime enforcement is explicit: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_quarantine.go:57-118` drops the loser, unzones interfaces, and scrubs policies.
- The safe compatibility contract is an UNKNOWN/NO/YES enum for protobuf (UNKNOWN=0) plus REST presence where absence=UNKNOWN; a bool false default would false-clean under old-server/new-client skew. Quarantined counters must be zero/unavailable server-side so old clients do not render survivor traffic.

## Scope

Add the structured quarantine state and survivor identity to GetZones and REST zone inventory, with explicit UNKNOWN/old-client behavior, server-side counter suppression, wire regeneration, and fail-on-revert tests for z174/z214 plus no-collision and skew cases. Reuse the shared `ZoneQuarantineExclusions` / `ZoneQuarantineExcludedReason` verdict from #10489.

## Relationship

This is intentionally separate from #10489's text-surface plan: local CLI zone inventory, gRPC text zones-detail, and remote CLI text views can be annotated without claiming structured-wire truth. Do not close this issue by adding a bool or by changing the bare REST array into an envelope.

## Provenance

Filed during the #10489 delta plan review after adversarial review required the two structured handlers to remain explicitly exempt from the gate drain. The quarantine runtime is #3719 / merged PR #3837; #10489 is the text-surface follow-up.

## #10566 — flow-cache: static INPUT then-count not charged on Fresh session/cache seed (SYN→ACK undercounts 2 vs 3) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

Follow-up split out of #10504 implementation (out of fixture-MAC scope; production behavior gap exposed by strict-SYN test seeding).

Context: after strict-SYN admission, a SYN creates a session; the next ACK reaches the established-session path and seeds the flow cache. For a static count-only INPUT filter, userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/filter.rs:753-758 returns None on FilterRevalidationTarget::Fresh, so no counted evaluator runs. userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_seed.rs:111-119 captures input-filter counter handles while assuming the seed packet was charged on the cold path.

Repro: in afxdp/tests_txn_flow_cache.rs::txn_flow_cache_hit_replays_input_filter_then_count_3777 with strict-SYN seeding: SYN counter=1/cache=0; ACK seed leaves counter=1/cache=1; second ACK hit leaves counter=2, while the full-path invariant requires 2 then 3. The existing pure-ACK-first fixture hid this gap.

Proposed design: thread an explicit already_counted/result signal from established-session input-filter evaluation into flow-cache seed; when the static Fresh path returns no counted evaluation, charge captured INPUT counter handles exactly once for the seed packet before caching; preserve no extra charge for stale/static revalidation or per-packet evaluators that already count.

Acceptance: regression covering SYN admission + ACK seed + cache hit asserting 1->2->3; targeted review for charge-once/double-count and stale-generation semantics.

## #10579 — [follow-up #10519] DetachXDP/DetachTC ignore Unpin failure; pinned-link bpffs-unlink failure strands attachment invisibly [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-22)

Found during PR #10578 code review (reviewer deep-dive, disposition: not a merge-blocker, follow-up scope).

## Mechanism
`Unpin()` failure is ignored on detach paths (XDP loader.go:715 context, TC :1207, Teardown :1415-1417, re-pin shim_pins.go:112). Common case is ENOENT/no-pin and MUST stay ignored (attach-time Pin is WARN-only best-effort :609-613/:1206-1210; unpinned links are normal).

Harmful sub-case: pin EXISTS + bpffs unlink fails + Close ok → registry entry deleted, reconciler nil, no debt/alarm (even post-#10519) → stranded pinned link invisible to the reconciler (no handle left to retry), resurrects via pin-reuse on next AttachXDP (loader.go:571-590: a pin holds a kernel ref, so Close drops only the fd ref). Forwarding stays fail-closed (fence omits; stranded shim passes into a closed fence = drop — same residual shape as arm-(b)).

## Reachability
Negligible: needs bpffs-unlink failure with healthy everything-else — more exotic than the map-pressure arm-(a) #10519 rates unproven.

## Fix sketch
ENOENT-vs-real discrimination on Unpin failure: ignore ENOENT (no-pin normal), surface real unlink failures into the #10519 debt/alarm/ApplyResult path. Pre-existing in all detach paths; no test injects Unpin failure today.

## #10598 — conntrack GC prefix-vs-holes: return exact deleted set from store (follow-up to #10528) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

Follow-up to #10528 (PR #10596, reviewer item M1).

## Problem

`pkg/conntrack/gc.go` error branches (`:362-369` V4, `:447-454` V6) notify
`toDelete[:deleted]` on `(partial, err)`, assuming the count is a prefix.
Since #10528 surfaces recovery-loop errors, partials can have holes: 5 keys
with missing@1 + boom@2 yields `deleted=3` for the actually-deleted set
`{0,3,4}`, but GC HA-syncs `{0,1,2}` — a still-present key is synced as
deleted while deleted keys are omitted until the next sweep/bulk heal.

## Transient (current, documented at the call sites)

Failed keys stay expired in the table, so the next 10s sweep re-enumerates
and retries them; periodic cluster bulk reconcile heals the peer. The
divergence window is bounded and self-healing, which is why #10596 documents
rather than restructures.

## Exact fix

Return the exact deleted set from the store (`DeleteBatchKnownV4/V6` or a new
method) and sync exactly that set on the error path. Blast radius: every
`DeleteBatchKnownV4/V6` caller (invalidation, GC x2, bulk reconcile,
singular paths) — restructure, not a minor fold, hence this issue.

## Acceptance

- Error-path HA-sync covers exactly the deleted keys (boom-mid-tail + later
  successes regression test at the GC level).
- Store-level hole shape already pinned by
  `TestBatchDeleteV4/V6SurfacesPerKeyErrorAfterNotFound` (deleted==3 with the
  boom key retained).

## #10620 — [follow-up #10612] replay fence admits cross-generation zone-id reuse that the purge deletes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-24)

Found by 10619/CodeA-M3 during PR #10619 review (parent-ruled: no stateless fix exists; needs entry-vintage architecture — deferred from the #10612 fold, which closes the wide holes).

Mechanism: `removed_zone_ids_for_rotation` treats same-id/different-name as REMOVED (purge deletes those rows; pinned by the #10510 reuse test). The #10612 fence checks `contains_key(id)` against the CURRENT set only — a reused id is PRESENT, so the fence ADMITS a stale replay the purge deleted. The replayed row (dead zone-A session, id-3) installs under zone-B's live id-3 = cross-zone session confusion (fail-open direction).

Why not stateless: the entry records zone IDs, not the name/vintage it was stamped under. A's-stale id-3 and B's-live id-3 have IDENTICAL observables at the fence (id + current map). No stateless predicate can distinguish them. The scout's Option-A stateless design has this hole by construction.

Fix shape (architectural): stamp entries with zone-generation at install; fence drops entries with stale generation (or equivalent vintage mechanism). Must also cover: retained-removed-set alternative was considered and rejected (cannot distinguish live-reuse from stale without vintage).

Acceptance: reuse-race cell (rename with id-reuse + stale replay naming the reused id does not resurrect) green; RED (vintage-check removal resurrects); no regression to legit reuse (B's live rows install).

Window accepted meanwhile: requires zone-id reuse AND a stale replay racing the rename; documented in the fence code + #10619 body.
