## #10630 — [follow-up #10605] PBR Accept->Accept retarget does not revoke established tunnel flows (hit-path (0,0) exemption) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-24)

The #10605 hit-path tunnel exemption (filter.rs: mirror of install_table_stamp_for_miss) forces desired=(0,0) whenever the STORED decision is tunneled. Correct for the steady state (pre-fix: 100% blackhole — every PBR-steered tunnel TCP flow revoked on packet 2), but it also suppresses revocation on REAL post-commit PBR add/remove/retarget for established tunnels: (0,0)==(0,0)->None->no revoke, and the ordinary evaluator returns None for PBR Accept (no backstop for Accept->Accept moves), so the stale tunnel decision persists until session churn. Same for tunnel->different-tunnel and native-unresolvable transitions on tunneled flows. Fix direction: stamp the desired PBR identity separately from the (0,0) table stamp (or compare fresh outer/tunnel resolution on hit) so genuine retargets revoke while steady-state tunnels stay pinned. Deny direction unaffected (Drop/Reject still revokes via the ordinary evaluator; exemption sits after the Drop early-return).

## #10635 — [regression] companion_needs_live revokes permitted ICMP first-replies box-wide and lone-reverse worker replies (#10507) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-23)

## What
#10507's reverse fence (`companion_needs_live`, commit `085695ffa`) revokes **permitted** sessions in two shapes with one predicate:

1. With any type-constrained ICMP permit configured anywhere, the **first reply of every ICMP query session revokes its own session and is dropped, box-wide**. GATE 1b returns before `mark_policy_revalidated`, so a locally installed forward can never become `LiveEgress` (`policy_revalidation.rs:427-435` vs `:533`); the reply then always sees `companion_needs_live` and takes the fail-closed exit (`:1175-1183`). Trigger is stock (`junos-ping`, `test/incus/xpf-test.conf:153`).
2. Any reply landing on a worker holding only the reverse half is dropped and its half torn down (`:1105-1116`, no `Unvalidated && !fresh` carve-out); shared-map materialization installs only the hit half (`session_glue/mod.rs:2597-2662`), creating exactly that shape.

## #10639 — Policy-based IPsec (no bind-interface) plaintext traverses the armed fence with no zone policy [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-24)

## What
Policy-based IPsec (a VPN with no `bind-interface`) plaintext is kernel-forwarded through the armed fence with no zone policy. The VPN passes strict commit and renders an SA with no `if_id` (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:343,408-411`); tunnel-mode decap re-injects plaintext on the XDP-owned physical ingress, and the armed fence's only allow rule (`iifname {tracked XDP names} accept`) admits it — no policy, session, NAT or screen. The #9506 divert is keyed on xfrmi names only (no secpath match), and the #5619 plaintext advisory skips bind-interface-less VPNs.

CONDITIONAL/latent in steady state (masked by the box-wide quarantine while it holds — which is itself a defect, see linked trigger issue), LIVE during every standalone-stop window: stop removes divert+quarantine tables while leaving the fence + `ip_forward=1` and charon running, with SAs up.

Related (not owner): #9506 (route-based xfrmi plaintext, different population/mechanism).

## Evidence
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:343,408-411,604-607`, `pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert.go:822-827` (xfrmi-only), `:557-572` (stop removes quarantine), `pkg/nftables/transit_barrier.go:228-229` (fence pinhole), `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:145,190-212` (stop path), `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_plaintext_warn.go:142-145` (advisory skip) @465c5870 (identical @bbd1bc11)
- Kernel steps (decap keeps skb->dev; no XDP re-run on reinject) are standard-Linux inference, unexecuted

## Acceptance
- Bind-interface-less VPN either rejected at strict commit (joint fix with the quarantine-trigger issue) or its plaintext diverted/adjudicated (xfrmi-independent match, e.g. secpath/mark)
- Regression: no-bind SA plaintext does not traverse the armed fence unadjudicated in steady state AND across a standalone stop/start cycle

## #10650 — Same-incarnation refused_identity merges as benign stale success; revoked forward survives silently [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-24)

## What
A same-incarnation `refused_identity` from policy delete is counted as a benign "stale" no-op, so a revoked forward can survive while the commit reports success (violates the #5578 surfaced-gap contract).

Mechanism: when the captured forward is the live same-incarnation entry but a companion the capture didn't name exists (reply installed between capture READ and the delete batch — window ms-to-seconds per match, no cross-process serialization), both Rust envelopes refuse WITHOUT removing the forward (`delete_synced.rs:43-60`, `session_import.rs:1103-1121`) and Go merges it as `Stale` success (`manager_sessions.go:269-274`, no error). The merge path is unpinned (no test feeds a refused_identity outcome).

## Evidence
- Cited sites @465c5870 (identical @bbd1bc11); invalidation window bounds (64 matches/128 keys/micro-batch, 30s deadline, 250ms fanouts) make per-invalidation straddling routine at scale
- Dissent recorded: 2 lanes wanted executed race proof; the acceptance cell below supplies it empirically

## Acceptance
- Unit cell: worker table with forward+companion (same session_id) + PolicyDeleteItem with captured_companion None → refused_identity → DeletePolicySessions surfaces a gap error (not nil)
- Race repro (capture→reply→delete) or documented rationale if the unit cell + window analysis is accepted as sufficient
- Refused-same-incarnation no longer merges to silent success

## #10673 — Type-constrained ICMP deny poisons L4-need recording, dropping errors under later permits [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
A type-constrained ICMP DENY ahead of a permit drops ICMP ERRORS on the flowless path: `has_l4_constrained_term` counts ICMP-type terms as needing L4 and the discriminator is called with the real packet type, so a `junos-ping` deny skipped because the TYPE differs is recorded as if skipped for lack of L4, overriding the later permit. The classic "deny ping, permit junos-icmp-all for PMTUD" config breaks PMTUD (narrowed to IPv4; order-dependent — the reordered set forwards).

## Evidence
- `policy.rs:1270,3109,3317,3836-3843` @465c5870 (identical @bbd1bc11); executed (v4 Frag-Needed incl. SNAT'd flows; v4 traceroute/unreachable)

## Acceptance
- Type-mismatch skips no longer poison L4-need recording (distinguish "wrong type" from "needs L4"); deny-ping/permit-icmp-all forwards errors; order-independent cells

- Discovery source: deep-review `zone-policy-bypass` (run `review-work.8ME6xrTFa2`), finding `b06-flowless-order-F1`

With no SA, no XFRM policy exists (start_action=start, never trap), so there is no kernel-DROP expectation to split from. The steady-state availability half (silent accept → box-wide quarantine) is owned by #10638; THIS issue owns the model gap + conditional cleartext.

## Acceptance
- Bind-less VPN selectors either rejected/surfaced at commit or fenced on the dataplane (no silent cleartext in SA-up windows); divert-withheld + autoload windows covered by cells

## #10696 — configstore: commit-confirmed promotes durably before its crash-recovery record [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

order is `writeActive(candidate)` (durable) â†’ in-memory promote â†’ `journalLog` (fsync) â†’ `saveRollbackFiles` (up to 50 Ã— durable temp+fsync+rename+dir-fsync + metadata) â†’ arm in-memory timer â†’ only then `writeConfirmState`. A crash/power-loss in that span leaves the unconfirmed config as durable `active.json` with no `confirm.json`; `Store.Load` recovery finds no record, arms nothing, returns success. The in-code comment calls the window "microseconds" (`store_commit.go:695-697`); it structurally spans a journal fsync plus ~50 durable slot rewrites.
- Adversarial analysis: protection owed = commit-confirmed's guarantee that an unconfirmed (possibly management-stranding) config auto-rolls back. - Fix acceptance: crash injected at every inter-stage boundary never leaves an active unconfirmed config without (a) a durable confirm record recovery can re-arm/roll back from, or (b) an explicit persisted degraded state. ## #10699 — dhcprelay: DHCPv6 relay forwards server replies with no request binding [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

a Relay-Reply is accepted iff source IP+port equals a configured server, `Interface-ID` matches (default = authored interface name, e.g. `ge-0/0/0.0` â€” public, zero entropy), and not nested. Destination comes from the packet's own `PeerAddr`. No xid/DUID/IA binding is recorded on Relay-Forw. The shared upstream socket binds `[::]:547` without `SO_BINDTODEVICE`. The v4 relay implements exactly the missing pending binding, and `pkg/dhcprelay/pending.go:10` states the threat model: source IP is spoofable, a reply must match a forwarded request.
- Adversarial analysis: protection owed = only genuine server replies to real client requests reach clients. Actor = any host able to route/spoof UDP to the relay's :547 (on-path, same-L2, spoof-permitting upstream). Consequence: forged Advertise/Reply unicasted to victim clients (rogue address/gateway/DNS assignment), xid is 24-bit with no rate limit or drop counter.

- Probe / next check: unit-drive `processDHCPV6ServerPacket` with a forged Relay-Reply (spoofed allowed source, correct IID, no prior Relay-Forw) â€” currently forwarded (`repliesForwarded++`).
- Fix acceptance: v6 pending table (bounded/TTL'd like v4) keyed (xid, client-DUID, IAID/type), inserted before forwarding Relay-Forw; unmatched replies dropped + counted; regression: forged-unbound dropped, legitimate Solicitâ†’Advertiseâ†’Requestâ†’Reply passes.

## #10702 — dataplane: post-teardown apply refusal misclassified as state-retained [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

Rust distinguishes pre-teardown integrity faults (workers alive) from post-teardown spawn/bind/SA failures (workers dead, dataplane down) only in free error text. Go classifies both as `helperRejectedError`, whose documented invariant is "helper still holds prior state". On the same-plan retainable path Go rolls classifier maps back and leaves control enabled, logging "transit continues on it", while Rust workers are dead. No Go code matches the `after teardown`/`dataplane down` text.
- Refutation attempt: shim binding-READY sync should drop transit on unbound slots (fail-closed) and the 1 Hz wedge detector auto-rebinds â€” consequence is delayed recovery + false status, not silent forwarding. Non-same-plan leg is safe.
- Probe / fix acceptance: machine-readable refusal kind (lockstep-pinned like `SNAPSHOT_CONTENT_CONFLICT_PREFIX`); Go treats post-teardown as unknown-outcome (ctrl-disable, no retain, retry armed); fake-helper test pins both classes.

Severity: Medium (research-confirmed impact; see result report for per-lane grades).

## #10717 — cluster: pre-key session-sync connections are never evicted unless default-off strict auth is set [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

Residual of closed #7441/#9717: a session-sync connection installed pre-key (or from a peer that never completes the #6628 upgrade) keeps nil keys and stays pass-through for life. `SessionSync.strictSessionAuth` zero value is false = "pre-#7441 behaviour exactly: nothing is ever evicted" (`pkg/cluster/sync.go:697`); `enforceStrictSessionAuth` returns without action unless the operator declares the posture (`sync_auth_strict_7441.go:162-163`). Such a peer can send fence, config payloads, failover requests, session installs/deletes with no HMAC/sequence. ## #10718 — networkd: renderer interpolates unit fields raw; belt pinned to Description only (defence-in-depth + doc correction) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

NARROWED from the report's injection claim: the literal newline-injection mechanism is REFUTED — the #1798 pre-walk gate (`runPreWalkGates`, strict hard-reject / lenient scrub+warn) runs first in `compileExpanded` on every compile path including load/peer-sync, so no config-channel newline reaches the renderer. Two lanes + coordinator primary verification confirm.

Surviving residue (this issue): units are line-oriented `Key=Value`; a lexer-materialised `\n` in a raw field (`VRF/Bond/Bridge/Duplex/MAC/Address/Mode`) injects whole directives (`DHCP=yes`, re-addressing), defeating zone/VRF intent. `sanitizeUnitValue` is deliberately pinned to `Description=` only (pinned by test `TestUnitValueSanitizerIsAppliedOnlyToDescription_6833`). Sibling renderers (FRR/swanctl) belt every field; provenance copies several fields verbatim with no renderer-side re-validation. Tolerant load/rollback channels are the exposure if strict canonicalisation misses a field.
- Refutation attempt: strict-commit enum/IP validation may cover several fields; not proven for `VRF/Bond/Bridge/Address/MAC`, and `parseDuplex` canonicalisation is used for ethtool, not networkd.
- Probe / fix acceptance: render unit test with `\n`-carrying `VRFName/Duplex/Addresses` + `systemd-analyze verify`; every interpolated field single-token/no-control validated (refuse + sweep poisoned file) or escaped; inventory test fails on new raw sinks.

## #10816 — GRE decap attribution across inherited multi-unit endpoints is first-sorting-wins [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-24)

Follow-up to #10654 (filed from that lane).

## Shape
One interface-level GRE tunnel with N units carrying no tunnel stanza. The emitter fans the single `*TunnelConfig` out to N endpoints (`gr-0/0/0.0`, `gr-0/0/0.1`, ...), the snapshot builder installs N rows, and all N land in one Rust `gre_decap_index` bucket with identical (source, destination, key, VRF). `match_tunnel_endpoint` returns the first key-matching endpoint in snapshot order, so unit 0 wins every inbound frame: the losing units' counters, zone ingress, and session ownership silently describe traffic the operator assigned to them.

## Why #10654 exempts it
The #10654 commit gate dedupes endpoints by `*TunnelConfig` object: pure inheritance is ONE tunnel definition fanned out to the multi-unit logical model (the #7509 real-cluster shape), not a duplicate definition. Rejecting it would brick legitimate configs whose subject (zone advisories, unit aliases, address collection) requires tunnel-less units.

## Question for this issue
What SHOULD per-unit decap identity be? Options include per-unit rows keyed by inner demux (Junos demuxes units post-decap by inner addressing, not by outer endpoint), a single shared row for inherited units, or documenting first-sorting-wins as the model. Needs a dataplane-modeling decision, not a gate tweak.

## Acceptance
- Decide and document the intended attribution model for inherited multi-unit GRE endpoints.
- Cells pinning the decided behavior (or an explicit wontfix with rationale referencing the #10654 exemption).

## #10821 — frr: non-suffix ghost in narrowed BGP chain keeps permit-default fall-off (no deny alias) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
A tolerant-load/peer-sync BGP import/export chain whose ghosts are NOT in suffix position (ghost first/middle, e.g. `import [GHOST-DENY, REAL]`) renders the surviving subset with Junos BGP fall-off `permit` and no deny alias — prefixes the missing filter existed to reject are accepted/advertised. Residual of #10129, which shipped the suffix-only alias (`GhostsAreSuffix`); this is the deliberately-deferred non-suffix remainder.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- `filterDefinedPolicies` drops ghosts (`pkg/frr/bgp_policy_chain.go:83-91`); the narrowed-deny alias is taken only for suffix-ghost shapes (`pkg/frr/policy_chain_narrowed_deny_10129.go:112-118,255-282`).
- A non-suffix survivor chain attaches and falls through to BGP permit-default (`pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:589-606`); strict commit rejects undefined refs so 100% of cases arrive via the tolerant path (boot/HA-sync/rollback).
- Inserting a deny at a non-suffix ghost position would delete legitimate later survivors (the #8363 suffix rule) — real tradeoff, but the current outcome is fail-open, not fail-closed.

## Fix acceptance
Non-suffix narrowed attachments get a deny-terminated private alias (or the apply fails closed) unless the ghost position is provably after a terminating term; regression cells for ghost-first/ghost-middle × import/export × v4/v6 asserting the attached route-map trailing action. Follow #10129's migration decision (warn-first vs immediate deny) for rollout.

## Review origin

- Research validation: run `research-work.XBjjl5jSP7`, 3/3 MATERIAL High, base `53931de6b`, verified `cdb7b5a24` (one lane EXECUTED the bounded survivor-attachment cell; trailing-action assertion is the exact next check)

## #10822 — frr: community-list omission dangles match community with no as-path-equivalent belt [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
A community definition with a member failing `ValidCommunityMember` is omitted entirely at render on the tolerant path, but referencing terms still emit `match community <name>` — a dangling match with no as-path-equivalent guard. The strict name gate (`validatePolicyCommunityReferencesStrict`) passes defined names, and the member gate (`validatePolicyCommunityRegexStrict`) only warns on tolerant load, so the defined-name/invalid-member shape reaches emission. Sibling of #9881 (as-path got `asPathListMissingAtRender` + deny-all; community got nothing).

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- Omission: `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:310-319`; dangling emit: `:773-775`; as-path-only skip: `:981-991`; as-path belt contrast: `:489-498,576-587`.
- Consequence is BOUNDED but not fully settled (3/3 agreed split): the renderer comment claims missing-list NO-MATCH at evaluation, while README #2881 doctrine says a dangling match fails the whole frr-reload (stale routing). Both can be true at different stages (load-time admission vs route-decision evaluation). Floor consequence: availability/staleness (Medium). The silent-accept (reject-never-fires → fall-through permit) consequence needs an FRR 10.6 fixture: tolerant-rendered invalid-member/omitted-list + reject-term config through a managed-section add-batch — record admission, then (only if admitted) route evaluation.

## Fix acceptance
Mirror the as-path rule: a reject term over an omitted/undefined community renders a deny-all sequence (or the apply fails closed with the belt); accept/non-terminating terms skip the dangling branch. Tests: omitted-member, undefined-name, and valid-list controls.

## What
`policy-options prefix-list` definitions with malformed entries (`999.0.0.0/8`, `10.0.0.0/33`, `foo`) are emitted verbatim into `frr.conf` (control-char sanitize only): `ip prefix-list X seq 5 permit <bad>`. The strict gate is firewall-scoped, and the definition loop has no ParseCIDR/omit/quarantine — unlike route-filter entries (ParseCIDR) and community/as-path definitions (omit unrenderable). A poisoned managed section fails reload per the project's #1880 model, so a commit removing a compromised neighbor/route never converges while config says removed. Distinct from #7273 (firewall-filter wire marker, different consumer).

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- Emission without belt: `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:245-261`; route-filter belt contrast: `prefix_list_render.go:43-54`; strict gate firewall-scoped: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_prefix_list_entries_7273.go:8-15`; no entry validator: `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:173-174`.
- EXECUTED during research: strict compile ACCEPTED `set policy-options prefix-list PL 10.0.0.0/33` (rejected=false, no error) — routing-only lists reach FRR even on the strict path.
- Reload-failure consequence at medium confidence (FRR 10.6 batch behavior unexecuted): feed the exact line into a minimal managed-section reload; confirm non-zero exit + sibling route-map loss + stale routing after withdrawing an existing route.

## Fix acceptance
Malformed entries omitted (match-nothing, fail-closed) or whole policy quarantined-deny like #6807, with warn; no FRR-invalid line emitted on any path; sibling policies still reload. Cells: `/33`, bad-octet, non-IP entries × strict/tolerant.

## #10824 — routing: single global learned-route cap lets one peer flood evict all protocols' routes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
The learned-route cap is one count over all tables/protocols (`maxLearnedRoutes`, ~64,956 by the 10s-publish budget math). A peer without prefix-limit flooding past it makes `learnedRouteCapExceeded` decline the ENTIRE import — OSPF/ISIS/DHCP destinations vanish from the helper FIB and resolve NoRoute (policy-denials on deny-default). One rogue peer DoSes forwarding for routes it does not own; full-table peering may trip this without malice. Distinct from #8355 (which decided the ceiling exists, not its blast radius).

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- Single global count + decline-all: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:1146-1158`; cap rationale: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/learned_route_cap_8355.go:60-73,83-139` (loud + documented, avoids partial-subset arbitrariness — the tradeoff is real; the cross-protocol eviction is the residual).
- Config-derived routes survive; only learned routes evict.

## Fix acceptance
Per-table/per-protocol quotas (or BGP-only excess shed) so one protocol's flood cannot evict unrelated learned routes; per-protocol cap-hit counter. Test: cap-1 OSPF routes + BGP flood over cap → OSPF snapshots survive.

## #10825 — api: no brute-force throttling/lockout on REST password surfaces; failures uncounted [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-28)

## What
REST Basic/API-key checks are constant-time but unlimited-rate: no delay, lockout, source cap, or failure counter. `writeAuthChallenge` emits a bare 401 with no log/counter, and nothing enforces API-key entropy/length. Off-loopback, this is network online-guessing of human-chosen Basic passwords and invisible API keys. SSH side: xpf renders no `MaxAuthTries`/`LoginGraceTime`/`PermitEmptyPasswords` and installs/checks no faillock (base-image PAM mitigation unverified).

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- `pkg/api/auth.go:196-260` (`authCheck`/`checkAuthorization`/`writeAuthChallenge`); schema leaves without validators: `pkg/config/schema_system.go:592-602`; strict gate checks auth presence only.
- Negative grep over `pkg/api` for lockout/throttle/backoff/per-source attempt accounting: no credential-attempt accounting exists. denyaudit surfaces exclude REST login-class + api-auth (see AAA-08 companion).
- SSH: `buildSSHDConfig` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:807-858`) emits no auth-tries/grace limits.

## Fix acceptance
Per-source+account failure budget with lockout/backoff on REST and sshd drop-in; minimum api-auth secret length at strict commit+apply; counted rate-limited failure audit (new surface `rest_api_auth`). Tests: N bad Basics → lockout + counter; SSH tries bounded (or base-image faillock verified + documented).

## #10826 — api/authz: api-auth is an unscoped unexpiring plaintext superuser token, also over clear HTTP [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-28)

## What
Any one Basic user/API key authorizes EVERYTHING (no login-class binding, no read-only variant, no expiry/scope) including `POST /api/v1/system/action` (PermMaint). Passwords/keys are plaintext-equivalent in compiled config (`Secret` redacts marshal only), unlike login passwords (crypt hashes): DB/archive/backup disclosure or one sniff = replayable full-power credential until manual rotation. The same credential is accepted on the plain-HTTP leg. Live revocation works; the defect is scope+storage+cleartext.

NOTE: the discovering report excluded this as known (campaign-1 DR-26 family), but research could not resolve that reference to an actionable owner (#4047 is presence-clamp only; #5561/#5866 cover revocation mechanics, not scope/storage). Filing as validated-unowned; close as duplicate if the DR-26 owner surfaces.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- `CredentialPrincipal{Superuser:true}` (`pkg/authz/authz.go:281-282`); `Authorize` superuser bypass satisfies `PermMaint` (`:171-174`).
- Storage: `APIAuthUser.Password Secret` (`pkg/config/types_system.go:537-546`); `daemon_run_servers.go:437-444` copies `Reveal()`ed cleartext into runtime `AuthConfig`.
- Transport: port-80 HTTP leg and HTTPS leg independently enabled with ONE shared credential (`daemon_run_servers.go:375-456`).

## Fix acceptance
Bind each api-auth identity to a login class (default least-privilege, PermMaint excluded unless granted); store salted hash only; refuse/warn-clamp api-auth on clear-HTTP legs; credential expiry. Tests: view-scoped key 403s on `/config/set`+`/system/action`; DB dump holds no usable secret.

## #10827 — api: expired/revoked TLS cert served forever; no custom cert, rotation, or revocation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
An expired (or not-yet-valid) on-disk TLS pair loads and serves indefinitely with no warning/re-mint/metric — Go `tls.Config` does not reject an expired leaf, and xpf never checks `NotBefore`/`NotAfter` on load or on any timer. Revocation is impossible by construction (self-signed, serial 1, no CRL/OCSP); compromise is remedied only by manually deleting `/etc/xpf/tls`. No stanza installs a CA-issued cert, so strict-verifying clients can never be satisfied — operators are trained to `-k`/TOFU. Expired-serving breaks strict clients (availability); TOFU/no-rotation is the confidentiality failure.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24; base 53931de6b)
- `generateSelfSignedCertAt` returns `tls.LoadX509KeyPair` success as-is (`pkg/api/server.go:1974-1990`); `warnStaleLoadedCert` (`:1783-1797`) checks SAN coverage only, never validity dates.
- Grep `NotAfter|expired` in non-test `pkg/api`: only the mint template (`:2058-2062`, SerialNumber 1, +10y, self-signed). Schema offers only `https system-generated-certificate`.

## Fix acceptance
On load AND on a timer, alarm (error+metric) and re-mint/refuse when `now` is outside `[NotBefore,NotAfter]`; config-installable cert/key + documented rotation-as-revocation. Test: expired fixture is not served silently.

## Review origin
- Discovery source: deep-review `hundred-issue-loop` (run `review-work.Z4WV3ZjzCM`), finding `AAA-03`
- Discovering model: `muse-spark` (`source:deep-review`)
- Research validation: run `research-work.XBjjl5jSP7`, 3/3 MATERIAL Medium, base `53931de6b`, verified `cdb7b5a24`
- Report: `report-muse-spark-review-hundred-issue-loop-003.md` (pending publication at filing time)

## #10830 — config: ValidateCryptHash accepts md5crypt and structurally impossible hashes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
ValidateCryptHash accepts md5crypt ($1$) and structurally impossible hashes (e.g. $6$a$b, truncated-checksum bcrypt): it checks only modular shape + known id + non-empty salt/checksum + alphabet. No salt/rounds/checksum floor, no aging. Two consequences: (a) usable-but-weak hashes crack fast after any shadow/backup disclosure (1-char salts precomputable); (b) unusable-at-PAM hashes are written verbatim via chpasswd -e with apply reporting success — password login (incl. root) silently dead, discovered at console in an outage, with no post-write verify catching it.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- cryptModularIDs admits 1/5 (pkg/config/schema_validators_system.go:41-44, documented permissive); ValidateCryptHash shape-only (:89-148).
- Apply writes verbatim, success on exit 0, no shadow readback/PAM check (pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:513-527); chage/aging never invoked.
- The validator's threat model ("reject plaintext, never corrupt shadow, never brick boot") is achieved but does not cover strength or silent-dead-login.

## Fix acceptance
Drop $1$/$5$; floor $6$/$y$/bcrypt with salt >= 8, exact checksum length per id, min rounds; verify after chpasswd. Tests: $1$..., $6$a$b rejected strict AND at the apply boundary; valid $y$ applies. (PAM-refusal-of-malformed + aging enforcement need base-image confirmation — recorded as next checks, not blocking the validator floor.)

## Review origin
- Discovery source: deep-review hundred-issue-loop (run review-work.Z4WV3ZjzCM), finding AAA-06
- Discovering model: muse-spark (source:deep-review)
- Research validation: run research-work.XBjjl5jSP7, 3/3 MATERIAL Medium-Low (acceptance floor High; PAM-impact Medium), base 53931de6b, verified cdb7b5a24
- Report: report-muse-spark-review-hundred-issue-loop-003.md (pending publication at filing time)

## #10833 — daemon: every login user including unauthorized and read-only gets full /bin/bash [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Classes constrain only xpf CLI/API; the OS account is general-purpose. applySystemLogin loops ALL configured users with no class check and runs useradd -m -s /bin/bash. A class unauthorized (perms {}, Junos: no operational access) or read-only user with a key/password SSHes to bash: arbitrary binaries, world-readable state, local privesc staging, attacks on local sockets. Peer-UID API authz correctly denies these classes at the APIs — but the shell was never part of the class decision. Sudo correctly limited to super-user bounds but does not eliminate.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- No class check: pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:61-100 (:94 useradd -s /bin/bash); sudo super-user-only (:328-339, visudo-gated, revoked on downgrade).
- Negative greps: no ForceCommand/nologin/restricted-shell/shell-class directive anywhere (buildSSHDConfig emits none); applyCLILoginClass is in-process console RBAC, not a shell restriction. No in-tree disproving mechanism (base-image global ForceCommand would equally cage super-users, contradicting documented use).

## Fix acceptance
Non-super classes get the xpf CLI as shell (or restricted wrapper), unauthorized gets nologin; document exceptions. Test: read-only SSH lands in CLI, bash unavailable. (Base-image sshd effective config is the residual next check, not blocking.)

## #10834 — cli: flow-trace and packet-drop streams ignore Overrun-Dropped and present gapped audit as complete [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Flow-trace + packet-drop consumers ignore the producer gap signal: a deny/screen storm fills the 256-record subscriber channel, the trace loses precisely the attack records, and the file/stream is treated as forensic-complete while show still reads Active with no gap marker. Distinct from #5064 (which BUILT the gap signal on the producer side); this is the consumer side ignoring it. Lane C additionally found the same omission in both SSE consumers (5 production subscribers, none consume the signal).

- CLI flow-trace writer consumes sub.C, never reads rec.Overrun/sub.Dropped() (pkg/cli/monitor.go:695-750,775-803); same omission CLI packet-drop (:978-1040) and gRPC MonitorPacketDrop (pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:409-505).
- Producer contract: channel-full drops counted per-sub, next record carries Overrun=true, BufSeq gap (pkg/logging/eventbuf.go:199-250) — built exactly so consumers can report loss.
- Aggregate Prometheus drop metrics exist but are not surfaced in the terminal/file/stream paths under review.

## Fix acceptance
Writer + both packet-drop paths (+ SSE consumers, or a centralized gap signal) check Overrun/Dropped()/BufSeq gaps; emit in-band "** records lost (overrun) **" line / final dropped=N; show-status exposes trace-sub Dropped(). Test: bounded storm → published/received/dropped accounting + operator-visible gap indication.

## #10842 — fwdstatus: sampler presents aged data as current and trusts hardcoded HZ and page size [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

Build/Format takes snapshot age; age>2xinterval → windows invalid (-/stale note); worker-held samples invalid not 0%; obtain HZ/pagesize at runtime or mark rows approx (assumes HZ=100/4K). Annotate the busy-poll false-positive.

## #10848 — upgrade: no anti-rollback floor on binary and kernel channels - signed old code cuts as upgrade [OPEN]

## What
No anti-rollback floor anywhere on binary/kernel channels: validly-signed OLD code is a first-class upgrade (replay/downgrade — distinct from F-05 forgery, whose gate is satisfied). Binary: staged version from the staged binary's self-report, only ValidateVersionSegment + same-version/gen refusals; no ordering vs current, no security/DB floor. Kernel: Arm preflight refuses only candidate==running; any older linux-image arms and promotes on dataplane+beacon. Apt: VALID_DAYS=365 default Valid-Until; old Release/Packages/.deb stay validly signed a year, pool never pruned. postinst standalone publish-OK auto-cuts. A floor need not ban rollback (RollbackTo stays journalled/operator-named): refuse forward-cut/arm below max(DB floor, high-water) unless the rollback verb/flag is used.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- cutover.go:318-324 (shape not order); kernel_run.go:90,242-243 (only ==running refused); build-apt-repo.sh:37,150,195,205,225 (365-day validity + retained pool); postinst auto-cut. postrm floors are layout/teardown floors, not downgrade refusals.
- Narrowed in research: apt-NORMAL-upgrade automatic downgrade via stale-mirror replay specifically remains NEEDS_VALIDATION (isolated apt-root probe); the no-floor forward/kernel channels are established.

## Fix acceptance
Persisted high-water under /var/lib/xpf checked in Run INIT and Arm; older forward target dies pre-STOP/pre-apt without a named override; shorten Valid-Until/snapshot-pin. Replay cell (old signed repo+gen) refused without override; named rollback still works.

## #10849 — deploy: latest.json freshness unenforced - signed date written never read [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Image latest.json freshness is unenforced: the signed date is written and never read; anti-rollback is deletable per-user local state only. make_latest signs {channel,version,manifest,date} with no comparison to the existing signed pointer; _gate_one_latest checks signature + presence only; the deploy consumer verifies signature/channel/version-shape, never date (no expiry, no max-age). The only guard is the watermark: per-user ~/.local/state/xpf/image-watermark.json, code-admitted best-effort — a fresh workstation has no watermark. Stale mirror replays an old validly-signed latest.json set to a fresh/reimaged workstation, new operator, CI, or after rm of the watermark → silent vulnerable install. Distinct from #9238 (concurrent-fetch inversion): cross-host/time replay where no watermark ever existed.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- scripts/dist/publish.py:899-920 (sign w/o comparison), :758-785 (gate signature/presence only); scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:1651-1716 (consumer ignores date), :1883-1909 (best-effort watermark). Project's own §5.6 calls this a freshness pointer — unenforced freshness is a contract gap.

## Fix acceptance
Consumer enforces date (max-age or monotonic-vs-server/pinned epoch); make_latest/publish refuse non-advancing version/date per channel; fresh-state fetch of a pointer older than X or below a git-pinned minimum stable version warns/dies. Replay-old-pointer cell on empty XDG_STATE_HOME must fail post-fix.

## #10850 — image: bake signs newest-mtime deb without binding version and commit identity [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Bake signs whatever .deb is newest-by-mtime in dist-deb/; signed provenance (version, git_commit) is never bound to that .deb. debs sorted by getmtime, last taken — mtime, not version, filename-version unparsed. --skip-build skips make deb entirely and still takes this pick. Guest proof runs xpfd version but never compares output to --version/deb filename. Plant or leave an old/vulnerable .deb with fresh mtime (touch, partial build, restored backup), run a --skip-build bake labelled new: the old binaries boot+validate (genuine xpf, honestly earning validated:true/base_image_pinned:true) — then minisign attests them as the new release with HEAD's commit. - scripts/image/bake.py:959-972 (mtime pick, incl. --skip-build), :917,:1040-1042 (independent --version), :1071-1074 (HEAD/unknown commit), :694-696 (xpfd version executed, output uncompared); scripts/dist/publish.py:628-756 (no version-identity cross-check).

Bake parses deb filename / dpkg-deb -f Version + staged xpfd version and dies unless deb-version == --version (and non-skip commit consistency or sidecar records deb's own commit, never unknown-free mismatch); publish gate cross-checks inventory xpf version == set version. ## #10851 — upgrade: default rollback target is newest-mtime dir, can select the just-failed version [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Default operator-rollback target is the newest-mtime restorable dir — it can select the just-FAILED (or a touched ancient) version, not the previous good one. defaultRollbackTarget filters only validateRestorableVersion (presence/ELF/lockstep shape), sorts by ModTime desc, picks [0]. No use of journal PreviousVersion, committed-state, health history, or version order. (a) After a failed cut + auto-rollback, the failed dir remains complete/restorable with newest mtime: bare --rollback flips ONTO the failed build (health gate catches it only after another STOP/outage). (b) Anything copying/touching an old dir (cp -a, backup restore) makes an ancient vulnerable version the default and can evict the genuine intermediate target past N=3 (same mtime heuristic orders GC retention in flip.go gc).

- pkg/upgrade/rollback.go:252-280 (mtime pick, no journal use); pkg/upgrade/flip.go:463-529 (mtime GC ranking). Explicit --rollback <ver> unaffected; restorable+post-start health bound (a) to an outage loop rather than silent bad service.

## Fix acceptance
Default = last committed predecessor (persisted at COMMIT/flip, e.g. journal-derived stamp inside versions/<ver>), mtime only as tie-break with a loud listing; failed-cut dirs stamped non-committed and excluded. Cells: after failed cut, default != failed target; touched-old-dir does not change default.

All remote fetches are unbounded curl -fsSL: no scheme/proto restriction, redirect-downgrade protection, timeout, or size cap — in _download_to (manifest, sig, latest, multi-GB qcow2; base URL from --image-url/XPF_IMAGE_BASE_URL with no https check) and in bake.py (base image + SHA256SUMS + release listing). A hostile/slow mirror holds a fetch/bake indefinitely or fills the disk with an oversized qcow2 BEFORE verification runs; an https base can redirect to http. Integrity explicitly NOT affected (signatures + base pin) — availability only. The discovering report excluded this as ungraded; research validates the availability mechanism 3/3.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:1719-1738 (_download_to), :1858-1861 (no https validation); scripts/image/bake.py:347,374,378. No --proto/--proto-redir/--max-time/--max-filesize anywhere on these paths.

## Fix acceptance
--proto/--proto-redir =https, --max-time, plus a signed size field in SHA256SUMS to bound downloads; strict URL validation on image + bake-base URLs. Test: oversized/slow-mirror fixtures refuse/hang-bounded pre-verification.

## #10854 — dataplane: pre-policy RX source-learn overwrites live v6 neighbours, bypassing ND hardening [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Every parsed frame learns (ingress_ifindex,flow.src_ip)->eth src MAC, overwriting a differing live entry unconditionally — BEFORE screen/policy (stage_parse_flow_and_learn runs before screen; per-shard cap refuses only NEW keys, updates never refused). Gates are learnable-unicast class, not-own-IP, learnable MAC only: no zone/screen/policy verdict, no solicitation, no connected-prefix check. On-link actor sends ONE packet (policy-dropped is fine) src=<v6 gateway/server on that link> with attacker src-MAC: entry flips, transit to that next hop egresses to attacker (MITM/blackhole). Quiet victims stay poisoned until they transmit; refresh is trivial. Survives a complete X2P-06 fix — no NA parse path is used. Distinct from X2P-06 (unsolicited-NA) by mechanism.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:459 (learn) before :560 (screen); neighbor_dispatch.rs:739,806,930; sharded_neighbor.rs:41-57 (cap refuses new keys; updates overwrite); types/forwarding.rs:1114 NeighborEntry{mac} only (no TTL); forwarding/fib.rs:804,872 consume the map for egress dst MAC.

## Fix acceptance
Learn post-admission only, or RX-learn create-only vs resolver/kernel-confirmed entries; count refused overwrites. Cells: policy-denied spoofed-src packet leaves neighbor unchanged; genuine permitted MAC move still updates.

## #10855 — dataplane: DAD attack permanently kills configured global v6 and reconciler reports converged [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
DAD attack permanently kills configured global v6 on non-RETH interfaces, and the reconciler counts dadfailed as present. Plain ge/xe/et + VLAN subs keep accept_dad=1 with no dadfailed repair (accept_dad=0 only for RETH members; clearDadFailed link-local-only, RETH-tail-only). DAD attacker answers the DAD NS for the firewall's configured global (gateway/VIP/mgmt) at link-up/apply → address dadfailed forever, every reconcile reports converged, commits succeed, no counter/alarm. Dead until manual del/add or reboot. X2P-06's DAD dual named downstream victims, not xpf's own configured-address lifecycle/reconciler blindness.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:458,482-485 planAddressReconcile (matching IPNet key = already present; Flags never inspected — no del/re-add for IFA_F_DADFAILED); pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:23-28 (accept_dad=0 RETH-only); daemon_reth.go:424-452 + daemon_apply_dataplane.go:765 (clearDadFailed link-local-only).

## Fix acceptance
Plan treats dadfailed/stuck-tentative desired v6 as del+re-add (extend clearDadFailed to global + all iface classes), with a dadfailed counter. Cell: existing=[2001:db8::1/64 dadfailed] → plan emits del+add.

## #10856 — dhcpv6: IA_PD prefix class and scope never validated before LAN RA advertisement [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

## What
DHCPv6 IA_PD prefix address class/scope never validated: only mask sanity; the address is stored unchecked, derived, and re-advertised on-link+autonomous. fe80::/64, ff00::/8, ::1/128, ULA, documentation, the LAN's own prefix, or the WAN connected prefix are all accepted live PDs. Hosts autoconfigure in link-local/multicast-derived space, treat off-link dsts as on-link, or collide with the real LAN prefix. Rogue/compromised upstream (or M-V6-06 race winner) delegating the LAN's own prefix causes segment-wide on-link/default-router confusion under xpf's trusted router identity. A10-02 covered IA_NA address only; /0+mask were #6531/#6587.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6.go:735-818 extractDelegatedPrefixes (mask sanity :791-799; address :800-810 unchecked), :905 DeriveSubPrefix; daemon/daemon_ra.go:30-51 (OnLink+Autonomous); pkg/ra/sender.go:940-953 (sole floor: Delegated && Bits()==0 refused).

## Fix acceptance
At extract + RA sink require global-unicast (ULA only if pinned); reject link-local/multicast/loopback/unspecified/documentation and any overlap with configured iface/RA/NAT64 prefixes unless operator-pinned. Per-class tests.

## #10857 — dhcpv6: lease DNS installed without class validation, hijacking host resolution [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
DHCPv6 DNS option reaches host /etc/resolv.conf with no class validation: server supplying ff02::1, ::1, fe80::x (zoneless, unusable) or an attacker global resolver is written as the firewall's own nameserver (mgmt/DDNS/update lookups), retained across transient renew failures. Rogue server needs no bad leased address (evades A10-02-class fixes) — DNS-only hijack of host resolution. (Loopback-for-local-resolver explicitly carved out as product decision; static-path laxity out of scope — different actor.)

## Fix acceptance
Filter lease DNS to global-unicast (drop+log) at parse or merge. Cell: DNS=[ff02::1,::1,fe80::1,2001:4860:4860::8888] → only last installed.

## #10858 — dhcpv6: acquire and stateless acceptance is xid-only with no IAID, status, or server binding [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
DHCPv6 acquire/stateless acceptance is xid-only: no IAID, StatusCode, Preference, or server binding (renew was hardened by #9944, acquire was not). parseV6Reply iterates ALL IA_NA/IA_PD regardless of IAID and never reads OptStatusCode or Preference. Fastest on-link responder with a parseable Reply — wrong IAID, StatusCode NoAddrsAvail/NoPrefixAvail plus stray IAADDR, a wholly different server — is committed (address, DNS, PD). First-reply-wins discards RFC 8415 Preference selection by construction; the legitimate server need only be slower.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6.go:338 stateless SendAndRead(nil matcher), :377 RapidSolicit (library first-reply), :459-533 parse (all IAs, no IAID/status); contrast renew.go:60-86 v6RenewMatcher (xid+client DUID+granting-server DUID, #9944).

## Fix acceptance
IAID equality, message+IA StatusCode handling, Advertise collection honouring Preference off rapid-commit. Fixtures: wrong-IAID, status+stray-option, fast-low-preference all rejected.

## #10860 — nat64: fragmented geometry broken with post-Fragment ext headers, tracker invariant false [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
NAT64 fragmented geometry breaks when the fragmentable part starts with an extension header, and the tracker's "translation preserves fragmentation geometry" invariant is false. (a) First fragment: translator strips all walked ext headers, copying only L4, yet non-first fragments copy frag offset verbatim — offsets relative to the fragmentable part INCLUDING the stripped header, so every tail lands ≥8B too far; receiver reassembly has a permanent hole and drops the whole legitimate datagram. (b) Non-first: payload_off derived from a walker that walks PAST the Fragment header interpreting frag NextHdr, consuming real payload bytes as a DestOpt header and demanding a TCP/UDP terminal. Direction is fail-safe (corruption→receiver drop): availability + falsified tracker invariant (post ranges overstate first-frag length → spurious post-NAT overlap drops).

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- Invariant claim: fragment_overlap/mod.rs:59-70; TX re-check: poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5987-6015 (verify :5995-6023, +8 unrelated). NAT64 frag eligibility incl. ext headers: nat64.rs:2061-2065,2112-2128. First: :2439-2515 (strip) vs :3898-3908 (verbatim offsets). Non-first: :3869-3887 (payload_off walker). Correct frag+8 use: fragment_overlap/mod.rs:882-885.

## Fix acceptance
NAT64-drop fragmented datagrams whose frag NextHdr is an ext header (RFC 7915 §5.1.1 SHOULD-drop posture already used for AH), or adjust offsets/lengths. Cells: v6 frag train with DestOpt-after-Frag translates and reassembles byte-identical, both directions. (Reachable shape needs a header-complete first fragment: 8B DestOpt + full TCP header per research refinement.)

## #10861 — nat64: post-translation overlap key protocol-0 conflates TCP and UDP under shared pool [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
NAT64 post-translation overlap key has protocol=0: v6 pre-keys pin protocol to 0 by design, and translated_overlap_key maps that 0 unchanged — but IPv4 reassembly keys include protocol. Under a shared SNAT64 pool (normal): (i) an admitted inside sender crafting UDP fragments to server S with low-16 ident equal to a victim's TCP datagram plants ranges in the conflated entry — victim's fragments drop as post-NAT overlaps (targeted fragmented-flow DoS, no ident guess beyond 16 bits, pool src shared); (ii) two live datagrams' ranges union into one entry, so commit_admission completion/coverage can retire the union while one datagram is incomplete. Adjacent flaw (same fn, reachability caveat): v6→v4 arm returns None (post-check silently skipped, fail-open) if either rewrite_src/rewrite_dst is None — production NAT64 decisions carry both rewrites on the traced path, so treat missing-rewrite as hardening (drop), not proven-bypassed.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- fragment_overlap/mod.rs:925-935 (post key), :113-125 (v6 pre-key proto 0), :734-756 (commit_admission).

## Fix acceptance
Carry the real frag NextHdr into the post key (parse, not key field); treat missing rewrite pair on a nat64 fragment as drop. Verify: concurrent TCP+UDP NAT64 frag trains, same dst, colliding low-16 idents, both complete; missing-rewrite fixture drops.

## #10862 — nfqueue: FragPool holds-vs-pool deadline desync plus Stats.Fragments undercount [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What (capture/measurement scope only — #9506 capture tooling, not forwarding enforcement)
Go FragPool/pipeline fragment-state desync + stats undercount: (a) Deadline split-brain: pipeline expiry uses fragTimes (first-seen absolute) and drops held frames at deadline, but FragPool.Expire evicts by updatedAt (idle) — a set refreshed by late fragments survives in the pool after its holds were verdict-dropped; next fragment re-Inserts into the zombie set and can reach complete, releasing only surviving holds while earlier pieces are already dropped. (b) Accounting EXECUTED: insertIPv6Locked appends the piece and bumps set.bytes BEFORE the conflicting-terminal check returns ErrFragmentOverlap; Insert's error path dropSetLocked subtracts len(set.pieces) though that piece was never added to p.fragments — Stats().Fragments undercounts (clamped only at 0). Reproduced in research scratch test: Flows=1, Fragments=0 with one live piece retained.

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go:510-513,904-930 (fragTimes expiry); pkg/nfqueue/fragpool.go:336-350 (updatedAt eviction), :197-205 (append-before-check), :311-317 (wrong subtraction).

## Fix acceptance
One deadline authority (holds and pool agree); check terminal-conflict before append. Tests: old-fragTimes + refreshed-updatedAt (holds expire, pool does not complete on zombie); multi-set Stats().Fragments invariant.

## #10872 — rpm: predictable unauthenticated probes allow forged PASS suppressing failover [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

Predictable unauthenticated probes can be forged: ICMP id=pid^counter, Seq=1, constant data; reply accepted on type+id+seq+src-IP only. Each forged success zeroes SuccFail and sets pass — on-path/L2 attacker forging per-cycle replies suppresses failover edges indefinitely. http-get defaults to plaintext http:// (>=400 = fail, so a hostile target invokes B-EVENT-2 at will); tcp-ping is bare connect. ## Fix acceptance
Design decision: authenticated probing (TCP-MD5/AO option, HTTPS-only guidance, multi-target quorum) or documented accepted risk with deployment guidance. Test: forged per-cycle replies against each probe type → failover still trips (or explicit documented acceptance).

## #10873 — scheduler: replace during failed apply strands active permit with no retry bound [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What (narrowed; slew-evasion half refuted)
Scheduler replacement during a failed initial apply clears retry and fail-closed state while a nil/skipped initial publication never latches scheduler retry: the old dataplane permit can remain live without a fixed recovery bound until a window transition or successful apply. Stale-permit latch reset on ordinary nil-result apply failure is the same class. (Slew-evasion as originally framed is REFUTED 3/3: wall-semantic scheduling inherently follows wall time; ~500ppm NTP slew needs ~2.8h per 5s; large steps trip the guard; 2m-then-trust is a bounded tradeoff.)

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- Daemon REPLACES Scheduler wholesale on scheduler-hash change (pkg/daemon/daemon_scheduler.go:29-64), zeroing unsafeUntil/republish streak/fail-closed latch; nil result skips initial schedule publish (daemon_apply_dataplane.go:201-224,238-239; daemon_apply_tail.go:740-743; scheduler.go:238-256). Guard trips only on |wall-mono|>5s per 60s tick (scheduler.go:328-354); hold 2m then trust (:232-233).

## Fix acceptance
Carry retry/fail-closed state across scheduler replacement, or latch initial-publish failure into the new scheduler; consider a long-baseline slew-rate alarm. Test: clock-step hold + 5-minute republish failure + scheduler-hash change + nil-result apply → old permit expires/retries on a bound.

The event engine lacks the HA publication gate ipmon has: on a read-only secondary, EnterConfigure fails via ensureWritableLocked → remediation permanently rejected, consumed, no retry/requeue. Decide: HA publish gate + defer-on-readonly vs document-and-close as design tradeoff; add divergence notation to commit history; measure gated-probe takeover re-trip delay (threshold × interval) against remediation criticality.

## #10878 — ipsec: changed connection never terminated - rotation and hardening do not evict established SAs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-27)

## What
Apply reloads changed config, then diffs loaded connection NAMES only; surviving names with rotated PSKs, hardened proposals, changed selectors, or identities are never terminated. Established IKE/CHILD SAs continue under old credentials/selectors until expiry. PSK rotation after compromise is the headline: Apply succeeds, operator believes the peer is cut off, but the SA never re-authenticates (RFC 7296 §2.8: rekey derives new keys WITHOUT re-verifying authentication; CHILD rekeys continue under the old IKE SA). Junos commit on IKE policy change brings the tunnel down and renegotiates. (New negotiations use reloaded settings, bounding exposure to SA expiry absent extreme lifetime — see IKE-07.)

## Mechanism (verified @cdb7b5a24, base 53931de6b)
- ApplyGeneration → applyConfig renders + swanctl --load-all (pkg/ipsec/manager.go:353-387) → promoteConnNames(loadedNames) (:320,443-471) diffs NAMES ONLY → terminateRemovedConns(removed) (:324,524-564). No per-connection content hash exists (grep contentHash over pkg/ipsec = zero). Only manual TerminateAllSAs evicts (pkg/ipsec/ike.go:794-809). The removed-conn rationale comments (#3941/#5494: live child under stale selectors/credentials is fail-open, must tear down) apply verbatim to changed conns, unextended.

## Fix acceptance
Content-hash scoping (proposals/auth/secret/TS/endpoints/lifetimes — not cosmetic fields, to avoid flapping on description reorder): changed conns terminate + renegotiate on Apply. Test: establish, rotate PSK + narrow TS under same name, apply → old SPI/selectors dead (swanctl --list-sas + ip xfrm state/pol).

## #10915 — dataplane: no disable path or fail-closed gate for S-tag HW-strip offload (rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
Follow-up to #10655 (filed from the #10655 lane during parent review). The in-frame S-tag drop (userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs) assumes the S-tag is visible in-frame — but on iavf VFs advertising VIRTCHNL_VLAN_ETHERTYPE_88A8 outer stripping, the NIC can strip 0x88a8 into skb->vlan_tci (unreadable to XDP) via the rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse offload. A stripped frame bypasses the in-frame drop and adjudicates as untagged/unit-0. The repo has NO disable path for this offload (ensureRxVlanOff covers the 802.1Q-only rxvlan control, deliberately left untouched) and no fail-closed gate on disable failure.

## Evidence
- Upstream iavf advertises NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_STAG_RX conditional on PF/VF virtchnl support (drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c); ethtool maps it to rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse (net/ethtool/common.c). iavf is a documented supported deployment (docs/deploy-quickstart.md, docs/ha-cluster-test-plan.md).
- Limitation (honest): capability is PF-conditional; repo has no captured ethtool output proving it ON for any appliance; host ethtool unavailable in this environment.

## Fix acceptance
- Query + disable path for rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse mirroring ensureRxVlanOff (shared classifier incl. absent/off/fixed handling), applied wherever the S-tag in-frame drop is load-bearing (every XDP-adjudicated parent).
- Fail-closed gate on disable failure (mirror rxVlanOffloadActivationError structure with S-tag-specific scope + comment).
- Exact check to run first: ethtool rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse state on iavf deployments (on/off/absent per PF); if universally absent/off, downgrade to a documented probe + test pinning the disable path.

## #10949 — scheduler: committed system time-zone change never takes effect in the running daemon (process-cached time.Local) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
A committed system time-zone change never affects the scheduler in the running daemon: applyTimezone rewrites /etc/localtime + /etc/timezone and logs success, but Go loads time.Local once per process (localOnce/initLocal) and nothing restarts/re-execs/replaces the scheduler or warns. Windows fire in the old zone indefinitely; show surfaces agree (same daemon state) while host date shows the new zone (actively misleading). HA arm: a restarted peer flips zones while the un-restarted peer stays - identical config+hash, hours-offset verdicts, flipping on failover.

## Evidence
- Every scheduler now carries time.Local (Run/ticker, New/Update/evaluate, ParseInLocation(now.Location())); SchedulerConfig has no zone field and the config hash has no TZ term (hash-unchanged returns live state); zero time.Local assignment / production LoadLocation worktree-wide; no timezone owed-latch exists (unlike rsyslog/chrony/sshd debt latches). Go 1.24.9 zoneinfo source: localOnce.
- All three research lanes concur MATERIAL (MEDIUM-HIGH).

## Acceptance
- Running-daemon TZ A-to-B cell: window boundary follows B within one tick (restart latch or per-eval cached LoadLocation); peers agree regardless of restart history.

## #10967 — [follow-up #10696] nested no-op re-arm equal-hash alias bypasses expired prior deadline on crash recovery [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
After #10954: a nested no-op re-arm (candidate identical to active) writes a provisional record with GuardedHash == PreviousHash. On crash between provisional write and active write, recovery's alias branch (GuardedHash != activeHash && PreviousHash == activeHash) is FALSE by equality, so it selects the future candidate Deadline instead of the expired PreviousDeadline - re-arming an expired window instead of rolling back to Base.

## Evidence
- store_commit.go provisional write (~553-615): previousHash=guardedConfigHash(s.active), GuardedHash=guardedConfigHash(s.candidate); equal when candidate==active.
- store_persist.go:295-309: alias condition requires GuardedHash != activeHash.
- Integration repro (lane-verified logic, not yet an automated test): persist Base; arm Pending 10m; expire its deadline; stage unchanged candidate; crash at commitConfirmedStageRecord; restart Load. Expected: rollback to Base. Actual: Pending re-armed with new deadline.
- Found by delayed hostile review on merged 99813fce.

## Acceptance
- Equal-hash nested re-arm crash recovers against the EXPIRED prior deadline (rolls back); regression test with crash-hook at Record stage + expired prior deadline; full configstore suite green.

## #11004 — policymatch: directed-broadcast permits lack the route-drop advisory [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
For a policy match query targeting a connected subnet-directed broadcast (for example 10.2.0.255 on a connected 10.2.0.0/24 egress), the simulator returns an unqualified policy permit. It omits the route-drop caveat it gives for multicast and limited broadcast, so the result does not communicate that this packet is not normally deliverable through the configured dataplane. This is a low-severity operator-truth gap, not a policy bypass.

## Evidence
- At review verification 36b4e35a, `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:928-944` classifies multicast, limited broadcast, unspecified, and loopback, but has no connected-prefix directed-broadcast case. `dest_is_directed_broadcast` is used for ICMP-error suppression, not simulator classification (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/addr_class.rs:95-105`, callers in `icmp.rs:105` and `icmp_ptb.rs:474`).
- The accepted-only `targeted-broadcast` warning (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_routing.go:101`) does not annotate this tuple query. The local directed-broadcast negative test covers the ingress subnet only (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_bind_forward.rs:2497`).
- Freshness: current `origin/master` c76da215 still lacks the simulator classification; #10690 separately prevents a NOARP neighbor from promoting a directed-broadcast destination into an L2 broadcast, but does not add the simulator caveat.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three find the simulator truth-surface mismatch; no forwarding-bypass claim is made.

## Acceptance
For a connected egress prefix, a directed-broadcast destination query must identify the route/drop limitation rather than return a plain permit/deny. Add deterministic simulator coverage for a normal unicast control and the egress-prefix directed broadcast. Preserve the independent #10690 NOARP-neighbor rejection behavior.

## #11005 — dataplane: rebuilds the address-book table and policy state during one snapshot apply [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
A normal userspace policy snapshot apply repeats control-plane work: Go policy lowering builds an address-book table and discards it before the snapshot builder builds the same table again; Rust parses policy state for preflight and then parses it again for the successful forwarding-state build. Fingerprint and rejection consumers also rebuild policy snapshots. The cost is configuration/feed/apply CPU and latency, not per-packet forwarding; previous-good state remains the fail-closed fallback.

## Evidence
- At review verification 36b4e35a, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_lower.go:28` builds and discards the table; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:139-149` builds policy snapshots and then the table again. Scheduler republish repeats the pair (`manager_compile.go:1027-1051`).
- Rust preflight parses with scratch counters (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:233`), then the successful forwarding-state build parses again (`:283`). Extensive policy-rematch and rename fingerprint paths perform further builds (`daemon_policy_invalidate.go:782`, `daemon_policy_rename.go:114`).
- Freshness: `origin/master` c76da215 changes the snapshot diagnostic ordering but does not remove the discarded-and-rebuilt Go table or Rust preflight/final parse pair; the builder change adds address-book validation work.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three confirm redundant work; none claims a measured latency or throughput regression.

## Acceptance
On successful apply, thread/reuse the built address-book table and parsed policy state without weakening preflight failure-atomicity. Instrumented representative and feed-backed apply cells show one Go table build and one Rust policy parse on the success path; rejection and previous-good behavior remain unchanged. Share per-commit fingerprints/rejection work where safe.

## What

Large accepted feed sets therefore amplify parsing and allocation during feed refresh and snapshot rebuild. This is an update/control-plane availability cost; no runtime throughput measurement is claimed.

- At review verification 36b4e35a, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:444-447` calls `net.ParseCIDR` for both `sort.Slice` operands; IPv6 delegates to the same sorter (`:460`). Each expanded name bucket is sorted (`:230`) and canonicalization reparses every prefix (`:474-490`).
- Feed input is capped at 1,048,576 prefixes (`pkg/feeds/feeds.go:96`) and a feed update recompiles the active dataplane (`pkg/daemon/daemon_feeds.go:15`). The cost bound is source-derived; the near-cap scenario has not been benchmarked.
- Freshness: `origin/master` c76da215 retains the comparator and canonicalization paths; #10711 adds a whole-space refusal but does not reduce parsing per comparator.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three confirm repeated parsing; all distinguish the source bound from measured production latency.

## Acceptance
Parse each CIDR into a sortable canonical key once, reuse parsed values for ordering/canonicalization, and preserve deterministic bucket/ID output. A deterministic large-feed check must show O(F) parses per table build with byte-identical canonical output; exercise a nested-set case and a normal control.

- Freshness: these quarantine and host-inbound consumers are unchanged at `origin/master` c76da215. Existing #10530/#10531 concern quarantine visibility/inventory APIs, not the host-inbound accept path.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three bound exposure to tolerant collision recovery, not normal strict commits.

## Acceptance
Use the same quarantine exclusion set for kernel host-inbound views, unzoned drop addresses, VIP handling, and AF_XDP per-interface stamps. A lenient colliding-zone fixture with an addressed interface and a per-interface override must produce no view or accept for the quarantined zone, put its addresses in the unzoned drop set, and publish no host-inbound stamp; non-colliding configs remain unchanged.

Strict Store validation rejects the unsupported token; the affected behavior is tolerant Load/SyncApply and direct-compiler consumers.

- At review verification 36b4e35a, `pkg/config/compiler_security_policy.go:283-337` handles permit/deny/reject/log/count without a fallback for unknown `then` children. `UnknownChildren` only scans direct policy children (`:375-381`), and the poison predicate omits unknown then siblings (`:425-429`).
- `pkg/config/schema_security.go:145` has a closed-world `then` schema; Store strict validation rejects it (`pkg/configstore/store.go:593-610`), while tolerant loading downgrades the schema failure (`:778-811`) and compiles the policy. The report probe observed a terminal permit and no typed warning/poison for this child.
- Freshness: the compiler/schema paths are unchanged at `origin/master` c76da215.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three bound the issue to tolerant/compatibility paths and require preserving fail-closed policy behavior.

## Acceptance
An unrecognized `then` sibling must either be implemented as supported policy semantics or produce a named diagnostic and poison/reject the enforcement rule on tolerant load; it must not silently leave an earlier terminal permit active. Add a security-policy fixture for permit plus next-term through Store.Load/SyncApply, confirm no widened rule installs, and keep firewall-filter `next term` behavior unchanged.

- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three agree the failure is bounded to D11 attestation and fail-closed.

On an apply that changes only the `st` interface zone, refresh the tunnel-zone authority or rotate capture state before accepting the new generation. ## #11016 — ipsec: reject D11 ingress candidates before claiming capture resources [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
The shared ipsec queue normalizes inet input/output families as capture candidates, so a D11 candidate on the input hook can pass Go-side planning and reserve/fill capture-ring resources. The Rust delivery/admission path only implements output-hook adjudication, rejects ingress candidates, and cannot produce the promised D11 result. This does not create an allow or bypass: forwarding is fail-closed; the defect is an inconsistent and wasteful production capture contract.

## Evidence
- At review verification 36b4e35a, queue owner normalization accepts `inet`/`input` (`pkg/daemon/ipsec_queue_owner.go:148-153`); queue lifecycle and the lower-level hook-kind contract also admit it (`ipsec_queue_lifecycle.go:98-118`, `:120-126`).
- In production, the Go callback checks the marker/tuple, validates outer family, charges candidate work and reserves a lease (`ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1067-1117`). The Rust userspace D11 path checks `HookOutput` and discards other hook classes (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ipsec_inner.rs:305-308`).
- Freshness: these Go candidate and Rust admission paths are unchanged at `origin/master` c76da215.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three agree that the gap is admission/attestation consistency, not an enforcement bypass.

## Acceptance
Before charging or leasing D11 capture resources, reject hook/family candidates that the Rust consumer cannot adjudicate, or implement the matching input-hook decision contract end-to-end. Exercise production capture and dry-run validation with identical `inet/input` and `inet/output` candidates; unsupported input must fail explicitly before lease/charge, while supported output retains the existing behavior.

## Review origin
- Discovery source: deep-review `zone-policy-critical` (run `review-work.VKSOFqPzgw`), finding V2-NFQ-03; report `muse-spark-review-zone-policy-critical-002.md`.
- Discovering model: `muse-spark` (`source:deep-review`).
- Validation: B3 three-way review in `research-work.6SXuD6JOvF`; source base `a7e61c0f23a67b647fcc4cf1e205b89c114d04e1`; reviewed revision `36b4e35ab86e6bbafddd0d238da04d76206f0bab`; freshness comparison `origin/master` `c76da215364a11607580c0f765d9ed284c8d6d43`. Research lanes: Design (reported `meta/muse-spark-1.3`, identity unverified), HPC and subject-matter (runtime-reported `openai-codex/gpt-6-luna`).}

## #11017 — nfqueue: emit D11 deny events instead of counting validator accepts [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
The only production `DenyEvents` sink for D11 capture is a validator stub: it returns true when the reason is valid but records, logs, and forwards no operator-visible event. The `D11Deny52` metric increments when `emitDeny` returns true and is exported as a count of emitted reason-52 deny events, so it reports emission even though no event reached an operator. This is an audit/observability gap only; forwarding is unaffected.

## Evidence
- At review verification 36b4e35a, `pkg/daemon/ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1224` installs the validator-only sink. Production deny handling calls it from `pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go:590`; aggregate pipeline counters remain.
- The D11 WouldPermit path increments `D11Deny52` iff `emitDeny` returns true (`pipeline.go:1073`); the metric is described/exported as emitted reason-52 events (`pkg/api/metrics_descriptors_controlplane.go:347`).
- Freshness: the sink and metric increment/export paths are unchanged at `origin/master` c76da215.
- Three-way disposition: dom/SMR MATERIAL; des/design MATERIAL; sys/HPC MATERIAL. All three agree impact is the D11 operator-audit contract, not forwarding.

## Acceptance
Install a production sink that persists/forwards each D11 denial to the existing operator-visible event path, and increment the emitted-event metric only after successful delivery. If delivery is intentionally unsupported, rename/document the metric as validation/attempts rather than emitted events and expose a distinct delivery-failure signal. Exercise zone-unzoned, stale-generation, evaluator-unavailable, and unsupported-hook denials and confirm both the event and metric describe actual delivery.

## #11033 — [follow-up #11004] snapshot neighbor path may resolve directed broadcast the event path rejects [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-25)

## What
Post-merge review (Eng11004 lane, credited) found the merged #11004 note overclaims: it states categorically that no usable neighbor resolves for a directed broadcast (#10690 NOARP rejection). That rejection covers the dynamic-neighbor EVENT path, but the SNAPSHOT path has no broadcast-IP restriction:

- Go buildNeighborSnapshots samples all kernel neighbors; neighborSnapshotPublishable has no broadcast-IP restriction; no config validator forbids it.
- Rust installs snapshot neighbors for arbitrary parsed IPs (forwarding_build/fib.rs:292-333); lookup_neighbor_entry consults state.neighbors first (forwarding/tunnel.rs:120-138); the connected arm returns ForwardCandidate when one exists (forwarding/fib.rs:557-563). forwarding/fabric.rs:147-167 even treats NUD_NOARP as usable.

So with a usable snapshot neighbor present (e.g., static ARP for the broadcast IP), the packet likely forwards and the permit DOES describe real forwarding - the note's categorical cannot-forward is false in that case.

## Questions to adjudicate
1. Can a broadcast-IP snapshot neighbor exist WITHOUT operator static-ARP (synthesis/proxy/stale paths)? If yes, this is a snapshot/event gate-asymmetry with smurf-adjacent forwarding impact, and the snapshot import likely needs the broadcast-IP gate - not just a note fix.
2. If only via explicit static ARP, condition the #11004 note sentence (unless a snapshot neighbor resolves it) with deterministic coverage.

## Acceptance
- Q1 answered with evidence; snapshot import gated if spontaneously reachable.
- Note text exactly truthful in all reachable cases, with coverage for the snapshot-neighbor-present shape.

## #11053 — [cohort] pptp: unauthenticated pre-policy learn + alias clobber + no control-close teardown (3 findings) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-27)

## What (3 cells, one ALG)
(a) PPTP ALG association learned from an UNAUTHENTICATED pre-policy TCP segment: any TCP flow with src-or-dst port 1723 is captured at flow-parse time (before screens/policy/session), parsed for cookie/msg-type/ctrl-8/len/Result-1 only, and installed+broadcast — a single spoofed policy-denied segment teaches an attacker-chosen (call-id A, call-id B) pair. (b) Install refuses handle collisions but SILENTLY OVERWRITES the by_allocator alias: two calls sharing one (allocator, call-id) re-point data resolution to the newest handle. (c) Associations are NEVER torn down on control-channel close: forget_control_channel has no production caller (self-documented), and data packets renew via resolve_and_touch indefinitely.

## Mechanism (verified @239976f3f)
- (a) userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:452-455 capture unconditional on is_pptp_control_flow (:467-471, port-only, deliberately not gated); caller order poll_descriptor/mod.rs:560 (parse+learn) precedes :671 (screen) and all adjudication; session/pptp_control.rs:235-267 parse checks only cookie/type/ctrl-8/declared-len/Result-1; afxdp/worker_queue.rs:764-795 drain installs+broadcasts with no session/policy check (caller worker/loop_body/mod.rs:1968).
- (b) session/pptp.rs:217-245: by_handle collision refused, but by_allocator.insert (:243-244) overwrites with no check; data resolve is by allocator+call-id (:254).
- (c) session/pptp.rs:299-341: forget_control_channel documents 'Still no production caller'; only expire_idle runs, and resolve_and_touch (:279-287) refreshes last_seen on every data packet.

## Acceptance
Spoofed policy-denied TCP/1723 Outgoing-Call-Reply installs nothing and subsequent GRE stays unassociated; alias-collision second install refused (not re-pointed); control FIN/RST (or control-session timeout) tears down all channel associations on every worker while data-only renewal still expires.

## Review origin
- Discovery: deep-review HOST zero-day sweep (149 findings + 42 dismissals/U-items), F-001/F-017/F-018
- Research validation: run research-work.CW5Oqkh4P0, 3/3 MATERIAL per cell (High/Medium/Medium), source base 32bb1e72, verified 239976f3f

## #11054 — gre: native decap matches tuple+key+VRF only — no ingress zone/interface or outer host-inbound gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-27)

## What
Native GRE decap authorizes on (family, outer-dst, outer-src) + transport VRF + GRE key ONLY. No ingress interface/zone check, no outer host-inbound admission, no outer policy/screens — stage 6 runs before FIB/policy/host-inbound. An unauthenticated remote spoofs outer-src + key (0/absent accepted when endpoint key is 0) and injects arbitrary inner packets that are decapped and adjudicated under the tunnel's logical ingress zone.

## Mechanism (verified @239976f3f)
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/gre.rs:744-779 match_tunnel_endpoint: index on (family,dst,src), VRF check (:768-771), key check (:772-777, key==0 accepts absent/zero); no ingress-ifindex/zone parameter at all. Caller has no ingress field to pass.
- Decap at poll_descriptor/mod.rs:497 stage_native_gre_decap (stage 6), before policy/host-inbound; inner stamped via logical_ingress build and judged as tunnel ingress.
- Distinct from #10865 (PT-nibble observability): this is the authorization predicate, not the nibble check.

## Acceptance
Outer GRE arriving on a non-tunnel-member interface / non-served ingress zone, or denied by outer host-inbound, is not decapped; key-0 endpoints require key-absent (not merely key-0-present)? — at minimum the VRF+key predicate gains ingress-zone binding. Cells: spoofed-outer decap refused; legitimate tunnel traffic unaffected.

(a) Session-hit ICMP recheck arms ONLY on type-constrained PERMITs: a deny-constrained type (deny echo + permit icmp-any) rides the typeless session — deny never enforced on established flows. (b) Same mechanism, no-config-change angle: within-session type switching shares the SessionKey (no type in key). (c) Fabric-ingress session hits skip the owner ICMP verdict ENTIRELY (early None). (d) Source-NAT match has no ICMP-type dimension (DNAT does): junos-ping SNAT term matches every ICMP type. (e) junos-host deny projection drops ICMP type/code for NUMERIC-protocol applications (protocol '1'/'58' + icmp-type loses the constraint; named icmp keeps it).

- (a) userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2565-2578 arm set only by Permit; session/key.rs:66-81 key carries identifier, no type; afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_hit_authority.rs:246-267 recheck gated on the arm.
- (b) Same key + 'typeless session key' named at session_hit_authority.rs:~280.
- (c) session_hit_authority.rs:260-262 packet_fabric_ingress → None (orig #10670).
- (d) userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:176-180 SourceNatAppTerm protocol+ports only; l4_matches :1132-1188 no icmp param; Go SNAT builder emits no icmp (contrast DNAT destination.rs:182 + protocol_nat.go:307 MatchICMPType).
- (e) pkg/config/junos_host_deny_resolve.go:274-286 named icmp arms set ICMPType/Code, numeric default sets Proto only.

## #11065 — host-inbound: to-zone junos-host PERMIT has no implicit deny-non-permitted half (re-file, was #9504) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-29)

## What
A committed to-zone junos-host PERMIT program enforces its permits but nothing denies the non-permitted remainder: the kernel projection is DROP-only (deny/reject render; permits never suppress), and the runtime has no implicit junos-host default-deny. Direct-to-firewall packets are handed to the kernel before userspace policy runs, so the kernel chain is the only enforcement point — and for permit-shaped traffic it contains nothing.

## Mechanism (verified @239976f3f)
- pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go:281-284 self-admits: 'A PERMIT is NEVER suppressed: its deny non-permitted half is enforced on no path, because the runtime has no implicit junos-host default-deny (#9504).'
- Lineage: #9504 (same defect) CLOSED 2026-09-12 by owner with no comment and no fix; mechanism still live at verify-master. No open issue tracks it — this re-files.

## Acceptance
to-zone junos-host permit programs gain an enforced deny-non-permitted half on the kernel path (or an explicit operator-acked unenforceable warning blocks commit); cells: non-permitted dst to firewall dropped, permitted admitted, un-projectable shapes fail closed or loudly.
