Unsolicited Override=1 NA against a live differing entry refused (or verified via solicited probe) with counter+alarm; legitimate LLA change (solicited / revalidated) still converges; cells: unsolicited hijack refused, solicited failover works.

## #11070 — [cohort] ha-sync: voided reconcile still acks + first-prime resets gens + fabric deltas zone-ANY + counter misattribute + stale-gate window + fold skips reth members (6 findings) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-29)

## What (6 cells, session-sync correctness)
(a) Any config apply during a bulk silently VOIDS stale-session reconcile (map-gen mismatch → keep-all), yet BulkEnd still ACKs + fires OnBulkSyncReceived (failover-gate release) — ack claims a reconcile that never ran. (b) First INCARNATED bulk prime (not a reboot — no recorded incarnation → switched) runs the full resetRecvGen: applied/received config generations zeroed, stale-config barriers lowered. (c) Fabric-redirect session deltas judged by zone-ANY ShouldSyncZone, bypassing the per-RG ownership #11012 fixed for bulk/sweep — multi-RG zones over-sync peer-RG handoffs. (d) Peer-synced sessions (bound=None) resolve hit counters POSITIONALLY: a policy reorder/insert credits the wrong rule; successor rule falsely proves firing. (e) PeerConfigStale gate opens on re-push WRITE: lastSent advances at send, the old nack no longer matches — manual failover allowed while the standby still holds/applies the older generation. (f) buildZoneFoldRGMap skips RETH members (RG only on RedundantParent) → per-session reconcile falls back to zone-ANY: multi-RG zones keep peer-owned stale sessions.

- (a) pkg/cluster/sync.go:2382-2386 void + :512-516 unconditional sendBulkAck/OnBulkSyncReceived (sync_conn_read.go).
- (b) sync_conn_read.go:350-354 '!inc.known() || switched → resetRecvGen'; sync_conn_gen.go:1172-1192 zeroes session+config marks.
- (c) pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:125-133 fabric branch uses ShouldSyncZone; bulk/sweep use ShouldSyncSession (sync_bulk.go:240-252, sync_conn_sweep.go:100-119).
- (d) userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:1856-1862 bound.or_else(hit_counter_by_idx); doc :1817-1820 admits staleness.
- (e) sync_conn_config.go:370 lastSent stored on write; peer_config_stale_9569.go:54-60 nack-vs-lastSent comparison.
- (f) pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace.go:60-90 no RedundantParent walk (contrast buildZoneRGMap :37-42); consumer sync_zone_rg.go:130-155 falls back to shouldSync(zone).

## Acceptance
Voided reconcile withholds ack (or marks bulk non-authoritative + re-drives); first-prime distinguishes reboot from first-contact; fabric deltas use per-session RG; synced rows carry stable rule_id (unresolvable → unattributed bucket); stale gate keys on standby-APPLIED generation; fold map walks RedundantParent. Bounded deny cache (short TTL, generation-fenced like the forward cache, deny-type keyed) with cells: repeated denied packets hit cache, policy change invalidates, no stale-deny past commit.

(b) Explicit @interface static next-hop resolves ifindex UNCHECKED (no table scope), unlike the #4446 bare-gateway arm: an RI-A route with an RI-B interface bakes foreign-VRF egress; to_zone re-pairs from the foreign egress. (c) connected_v4_directed_broadcasts is ONE global set: overlapping VRFs poison each other (A's broadcast is B's unicast → false martian drops). - (d) neighbor_dispatch.rs:485-499 fence recheck present, no martian recheck; TX dispatch likewise unarmed.

## Acceptance
Mirror skips selector-carrying rules fail-closed (PBR-band precedent) or carries selectors; @interface next-hop gated to the route's instance; broadcast set table/zone-scoped; replay + TX recheck martian under the current snapshot. Cells per finding.

## #11087 — dataplane: established local-delivery flows bypass per-packet screens — shim PASS_TO_KERNEL rows never reach the worker [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-01)

## What
Screens run per-packet in the WORKER (stage 10). Transit REDIRECT sessions send every packet to the worker → screened per-packet. But local-delivery sessions publish PASS_TO_KERNEL shim rows: once installed, ALL subsequent packets go to the kernel WITHOUT the worker — established host-bound flows skip icmp/udp-flood accounting, LAND, and every per-packet screen. A host-bound UDP flood to an established local 5-tuple (DNS/NTP to the firewall) never trips udp-flood; the host stack takes the full flood the screens exist to shed.

## Mechanism (verified @239976f3f)
- userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:788-803 PASS_TO_KERNEL hit → cpumap_or_pass, no screen checks in shim.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bpf_map/mod.rs:1689-1700 worker publishes PASS rows for local-delivery sessions.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:671 + poll_stages.rs:661 stage_screen_check is worker-only (every worker packet screened; shim-passed packets never arrive).

## Acceptance
Local-delivery fast path screened (shim-side flood/LAND counters, periodic worker re-admission, or documented + alarmed exemption with kernel-side backstop); cells: established-flow flood trips udp-flood, transit parity preserved.

## Review origin
- Discovery: deep-review HOST zero-day sweep, F-069... (F-090)
- Research validation: run research-work.CW5Oqkh4P0, ruled MATERIAL Medium (L2-M + completed screen-placement trace; L1/L3-NV overcautious), source base 32bb1e72, verified 239976f3f

## #11225 — dataplane: xfrm-sa-monitor GETSA dump request triggers kernel netlink leftover warning every poll [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-26)

## What
The XFRM SA monitor's periodic GETSA dump request is malformed: it appends a bare 24-byte zero xfrm_usersa_id where the kernel expects netlink attributes. Every 30s poll logs `netlink: 24 bytes leftover after parsing attributes in process 'xfrm-sa-monitor'` on both HA firewalls (dmesg spam; found during 2026-09-26 HA validation).

## Mechanism (verified on loss:xpf-userspace-fw0)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ipsec_sa.rs` `full_dump` builds nlmsghdr (16B) + 24 zero bytes, flags REQUEST|ROOT|MATCH.
- Kernel parses the 24 bytes as attrs; the first zero-length pseudo-attribute stops the parse → 24 bytes leftover → warning.
- `ip xfrm state` (strace) sends nlmsg_len=56: nlmsghdr + NLA(XFRMA_ADDRESS_FILTER=26, len=40, zeroed match-all filter) — no warning.
- Replay check: sending the iproute2-shaped request via python returns a clean dump with zero dmesg output.
- Old bug (#10516-era code), newly exercised: the lab helpers were disarmed/not-enabled for days, so the monitor was not running until the 2026-09-26 deploy healed both nodes.

## Fix acceptance
Build the dump request as nlmsghdr + zeroed XFRMA_ADDRESS_FILTER attr (iproute2 shape); factor the builder so a unit test pins the exact bytes (len 56, NLA type 26 len 40); no dmesg warning on a live poll. Do NOT change dump semantics (still unfiltered match-all).

## Review origin
- Discovery source: HA validation dmesg review (2026-09-26 campaign)

## #11298 — dataplane: reverse-path RI admission is wrong in both directions — mixed-zero over-admits, cross-instance replies over-refused [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-30)

## What
The #9895 reverse-lookup predicate fails in BOTH directions (residual of #9895, CLOSED). (a) Mixed-zero over-admit: a zone-matching reply arriving on any RI-B interface is admitted into a default-instance session (and vice versa) with no policy — local/shared lookups refuse only when BOTH domains are nonzero, then gate arrival by zone only. (b) Cross-instance over-refuse: flows ingressing on RI-A and egressing on an RI-B member (PBR then routing-instance, @interface next-hop, SNAT to RI-B, next-table leak) get their first reply refused by the both-nonzero pass-2 predicate; the reply misses the A-keyed companion and falls to new-flow handling (end-to-end outcome policy-dependent — universal connection failure NOT established; a separate B->A permit may admit an independent flow). The NAT arm (s01-F1) and IPv6/NAT64 twins (g2-F1) are the same predicate.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- session/lookup.rs:672-690, shared_ops.rs:694-699 + 1199-1214 (zone-only gate); reply fragments lookup.rs:719-732; HA-synced path shared_ops.rs:694-699.
- Executed: reverse_domain_9895 4/4 (both mixed-zero controls admit), pbr_install_table_9752 37/37, SYN|ACK no-drop at the SYN-first gate.
- Corrective direction (preserves legitimate asymmetric flows): compare the reply domain against the forward egress domain (domain of forward.decision.resolution.egress_ifindex), already cheaply derivable, instead of the both-nonzero/mixed-zero test.

## Acceptance
- Mixed-zero cross-instance replies refused; A-ingress/B-egress replies matched to their companion; legitimate asymmetric flows preserved; cells for both directions + NAT/IPv6 twins.

## #11299 — dataplane: every session close runs O(n) slab scans plus a full shared-map scan under mutex [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-30)

## What
Every session close drained on the packet worker loop can run two O(n) slab scans (session_id_for_bare_tuple, contains_bare_tuple; session/mod.rs:2499-2527) plus a full scan of the shared synced map under its mutex (session_delta.rs:154-175). Cost is linear in live sessions (up to 131,072/worker), churn-driven, and the shared-lock hold starves installs. Worst case per Close: four slab walks + two shared-map walks (checked at both worker drain sites).

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- Ordinary Close with absent bare tuple and no earlier skip reaches the scans at both drain sites (session_delta.rs:243,638; worker/loop_body/mod.rs:870,900,1823,1920,2566). Non-Close, detected replacements, and stale purge-retirement closes can bypass some/all scans — not literally every Close pays all three.
- Debug microbench (ancestor base, scan code + call sites unchanged at pin — timing NOT remeasured at pin): 682us@10k -> 8.6-9.2ms@100k vs indexed 0.4us flat. Release-build / loaded-node churn impact needs measurement.

## Acceptance
- Close-path scan cost indexed or bounded; loaded-node churn measurement shows no install starvation; regression cell pins the bound.

## #11310 — frr: protocol interface references not gated to routing-instance membership — stanza activates in wrong instance or nowhere [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-30)

## What
Protocol interface references are not gated to routing-instance membership. FRR binds interface blocks by the interface's kernel VRF (ospf_vty.c:8986, ospf6_interface.c:1821, isis_circuit.c:74), so a per-instance OSPF/OSPFv3/RIP/IS-IS stanza naming a default-instance interface (or a global stanza naming a tenant member) activates in the WRONG instance or silently nowhere — on a green commit with no warning.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- Rendered stanza is instance-blind; no membership gate; FRR activates the interface in the process of the interface's KERNEL VRF, not the authored instance. 3/3 MATERIAL Medium (potential High), EXECUTED+STATIC. Closest closed (#9405 name canonicalisation, #9409 protocols-under-instance refusal) key on different predicates.

## Acceptance
- Cross-instance protocol/interface references rejected or warned at commit; per-instance stanzas render only for member interfaces; cells for both mismatch directions.

## #11312 — routing: 'interface' accepted under 'instance-type forwarding' — kernel keeps it in main, userspace files it into the instance [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-30)

## What
'interface' is accepted under 'instance-type forwarding' (Junos: forwarding instances own no interfaces). Kernel leaves the member in main while userspace stamps the instance domain and files its connected prefix + ingress domain into <fwd>.inet.0 — so forwarding/zone pairing differs per plane, inet.0 loses the subnet on the fast path, and IPv6 is terminal on the fast path. Found independently by two lanes (r02-F3, r05-F2) — single mechanism. Adjacent OPEN #11060 keys on an interface claimed by TWO configured instances; this single-forwarding-instance shape is invisible to it.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- Compile fixture accepts the member with zero membership warnings; daemon bind loops skip forwarding RIs, but userspace route/domain construction includes member keys + connected routes. 3/3 MATERIAL (Medium / High-potential), EXECUTED+STATIC.

## Acceptance
- Member interfaces under forwarding instances rejected or warned at commit with per-plane-consistent handling; cells for v4 + v6.

## #11337 — nat: fabric-punted session-miss loses interface/RI NAT scope — scoped DNAT dead, scoped SNAT skipped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-30)

## What
Fabric-punted session-miss packets keep only the peer's ZONE stamp: prerouting_ingress_scope reads 'from interface'/'from routing-instance' NAT-scope NAMES from the local fabric link ('') and SNAT gets meta.ingress_ifindex=fabric, while ingress_routing_domain routes the same packet as the tenant via zone_routing_domain. Result: RI-/interface-scoped DNAT/static VIPs are not translated (service dead for punted connections) and RI-scoped SNAT is skipped (untranslated private source or mis-pooled by a broader/other-tenant rule). Same ROOT as OPEN #11061 (only the zone crosses the fabric) but a distinct NAT consumer — not DUP.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- Fabric zone stamp supplies tenant routing identity while NAT scope reads the local fabric-link identity (empty). 3/3 MATERIAL Medium (potential High in multi-tenant CGNAT active/active), EXECUTED (unit: real prerouting_ingress_scope/ingress_routing_domain/nat_scope_ctx/DnatTable on build_forwarding) + STATIC. Zone-scoped rules still match; the interface/RI axes are broken; fabric-punt path is the minority case.

## Acceptance
- Fabric arrivals carry (or recover) ingress interface/RI identity for NAT scoping; scoped DNAT/SNAT correct on punted connections; cells.

## #11338 — filter: native-fragment proto-255 wildcard over-matches — wrong-protocol tails match any 'from protocol' term [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-01)

## What
#10676 made the native-fragment proto sentinel 255 a match-any wildcard in the shared filter/PBR/CoS matcher (matching.rs:175-183): a native non-first fragment of protocol A matches a 'from protocol B' term. Consequences: 'from protocol icmp then discard' drops ALL fragmented transit on that hook; protocol-scoped accepts admit every tail; PBR mis-steers wrong-protocol fragments into another routing-instance. The real protocol is in every fragment's IP header (#10677 proves recoverability). Found as z01-F1 and s02-F1 (same matcher) — single mechanism, counted once. Residual of #10676 (CLOSED): the wildcard fixed the bypass, the residual is over-match.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- '!term.protocol_match_enabled OR protocol == SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4 OR bitmap_has(protocol)' — 255 unconditional match-any. 3/3 MATERIAL Medium (potential High for the PBR leg), EXECUTED (filter engine witness + 4 #10676 evaluator cells) + STATIC (PBR/CoS via same matcher).

## Acceptance
- Non-first fragments judged by header protocol (or wildcard narrowed to documented cases); filter + PBR + CoS cells; #10676 bypass stays fixed.

## What
The ListSessionsByPolicy worker arm iterates the worker-LOCAL table only, then reports COMPLETE with 0 matches when the forward row lives only in the shared synced map — while SessionPolicyComplete is treated/documented as the authoritative helper-owned READ result. - READ reports INCOMPLETE (or scans shared state) when worker-local coverage is partial; revocation never silently misses; cells.

## #11351 — nat: DNAT/static-NAT rule-set context precedence ignores interface>zone>RI hierarchy [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-01)

## What
DNAT and static-NAT rule-set CONTEXT precedence is zone-tier-then-config-order: an interface-scoped rule-set never beats a zone-scoped one, and ties with a routing-instance-scoped one by text order. Junos: interface > zone > routing-instance (NAT Configuration Overview: the more specific rule set wins). Wrong DNAT backend changes post-translation policy/routing, silent at commit. (SNAT already implements the hierarchy per #4161 CLOSED; DNAT/static were explicit follow-up.)

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- DnatTable::match_entries zone-find before wildcard-find (interface scope lands in wildcard tier); static pick_scoped same; Go DNAT/static builders append by config order without the SNAT scope sort. 3/3 MATERIAL Medium, EXECUTED (Rust table probes both orders: zone pool wins either way; RI-vs-interface follows insertion) + STATIC + Juniper contract. s01 NEG-3 read scope_ok (eligibility) only, not precedence.

## Acceptance
- DNAT/static honor interface > zone > RI (+ unscoped) independent of config order; SNAT parity preserved; cells per pair + order controls.

## #11353 — nat64: missing RFC 7915 §5.1 size-keyed DF rule + fragment-if-needed; unconditional DF=1 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-01)

## What
Re-date + correction of nat-001 FZ-07 (prior-unfiled): FZ-07's premise was wrong (the NAT64 PTB clamp max(1280,...) IS RFC 7915 §4.2's own MUST NOT — its fix would introduce non-conformance). The real gaps are §5.1's size-keyed DF rule (DF=0 when translated size <= 1260) and the §5.1 MUST to fragment a <=1280 v6 packet whose translation exceeds the v4 next-hop MTU. xpf defaults to DF=1 unconditionally (option-gated no-v6-frag-header; code comment admits it is not the RFC algorithm). Narrowed to NAT64 IPv4 egress paths with MTU below 1300; §4.2 clamp itself is conformant. No wire/MTU probe at pin.

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- 3/3 MATERIAL Low (potential; v4 paths below 1260 MTU), EXECUTED (default-DF test + Rust DF/atomic-fragment/MTU-clamp tests) + STATIC (RFC 7915/source comparison).

## Acceptance
- Size-keyed DF + fragment-if-needed per §5.1 on NAT64 egress; constrained-MTU packet cells.

A single member add/remove/flap (3→2) remaps ~2/3 of RE-RESOLVED flows (new, policy-revalidated per-gen, RG-refresh/demote, synced-promoted — narrowed to re-resolved flows only, not cached hits), not just the dead member's 1/3. Moved flows change egress ISP/zone/RG mid-session. (Established cache-hit flows unaffected until re-resolution.)

## Mechanism (verified @467a52da4)
- fib.rs:1282 pick over live set (:1280-1294); re-resolve at session_glue/mod.rs:371. 3/3 MATERIAL Medium (narrowed), STATIC.

## Acceptance
- Consistent hashing (Maglev/rendezvous per candidate id): 3-member fixture, kill one, survivors' flows keep member, only dead share moves; v4+v6.

## #11475 — nat: idle-lease import bypasses table cap enabling exhaustion [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-28)

Found during #10789-F4 review (Rev11473Sec, filed as follow-up to keep F4 scope tight).

import_idle_lease never checks max_tracked_flows and never runs GC pressure, unlike every local mint (allocator.rs:2367-2376 PAT, :4790-4797 address-only); address_only skips bitmap claiming entirely (key-exists + in-pool check only). Repeated unique source keys with in-pool translated address + huge lifetime grow persistent_by_source + lease_expirations + lease_expirations_by_addr beyond the cap across batches (per-batch bounded by ~16MiB frame, cumulative unbounded), starving future local leases (AllocatorExhausted after GC finds nothing expirable) and growing memory unbounded.

Fix direction: fail-closed admission on import — if len >= max_tracked_flows (after one bounded gc_expired_locked pressure pass) refuse with new IdleLeaseImport::SkippedCapacity + coordinator count (not PortBusy reuse); address_only consults address_only_owners/pat contention or explicit per-pool imported quota. Cells: table-at-cap refuses import while local mints still fail AllocatorExhausted (no starvation inversion); repeated unique-key batches cannot grow beyond cap.

## #11478 — nat: atomic holder capture+evict for synced replacement rollback (11476 residual) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-09-27)

Follow-up to #10788-F1 (merged 3be469bc3). Round-2 review (Rev11476Opus2 MATERIAL, Rev11476Sec2 finding 11476-R2-holder-capture-gap-early-free) established: holder-mask capture and replacement eviction are separate allocator-lock operations (synced.rs port arm ~778-795 + address-only/interface arms + NAT64 twin). Two residuals: (a) a worker release landing between capture and reserve is replayed by rollback as a phantom holder bit (bounded leak until retire sweeps); (b) a worker processing a queued prior upsert in the gap ORs a bit the eviction destroys, so rollback restores a stale mask and a sibling's last release can free the tuple early (NAT reuse while forwarding) — requires gap-race + mirror failure + release-before-refresh conjunction. Fix: single-lock PortAllocator capture_and_replace (read mask + evict + install under one lock_live guard) threaded through all four synced-reserve arms, + barrier-injected interleaving test proving a gap worker OR is captured-or-preserved, + regression for capture-release-replace-refuse-rollback-release ordering. Pre-merge behavior (no rollback at all) was strictly worse, hence merge-then-harden.

## #11487 — fabric: exclude state-changing verbs from dual-accept grace window (tiered auth) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

Follow-up from #10784 review (Rev11474Sec F1, non-blocking for #11474 per verdict — pre-existing posture). Dual-accept grace (pkg/grpcapi/fabric_auth.go:283-296,373-422): keyed + tokenless + unarmed accepts; armed only via prior valid token or authenticated heartbeat. The grace applies to EVERY keyed method, and #11474's exact clear-persistent-nat addition means the grace window now admits an unauthenticated cluster-state clear. Worse: one grace-window request to node A fans out to node B over A's authenticated peer channel, revoking BOTH nodes' leases when B is keyed. Chain order (auth before allowlist) proves the fix belongs in auth, not the allowlist. Fix: tiered auth — state-changing verbs (clear-persistent-nat at minimum; audit others) require armed (valid token/heartbeat), not grace; or narrow grace to read-only verbs.

## #11495 — nat: synced-session mints insert persistent leases without the max_tracked_flows table cap [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

Follow-up filed from PR #11484 review (Rev11484Opus1, confirmed in source at 3e827e750). Pre-existing gap, NOT introduced by #11484 (which correctly scopes its cap to idle imports + local mints).

**Gap:** synced-session mint paths insert into persistent_by_source without checking the table cap:
- reserve_flow_maybe_persistent checks live_by_flow.len() (allocator.rs:4668) then inserts a new persistent lease (:4483).
- Address-only reserve checks live_by_flow.len() (:4874) and inserts a new persistent lease (:4768).
- No persistent_by_source.len() cap on either path. Production synced paths reachable via source/synced.rs:669-687, 793-813.

**Effect:** idle imports individually obey the cap, but a table filled by capped imports can then be exceeded by an imported synced session (up to separately bounded live flows) — neither new flow count nor lease count shares one budget. max_tracked_flows is therefore not a hard invariant over all persistent table entries today.

**Scope note:** #11484's docs correctly claim only that idle imports share the cap with local persistent mints — no doc overclaim. This issue tracks extending the invariant (or explicitly bounding the exception) for synced-session rebuilding.

## #11497 — host-inbound: retry/convergence owner for failed gap-failure applies (unbounded #3698 fault residual after double nft failure) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-03)

**Residual:** day-2 double failure (real install AND gap install both fail in the same apply) leaves a newcomer address (VRF-enslaved unzoned DHCP lease sharpest — no backstop either) reachable until the next trigger, with NO wall-clock retry owner. Negative trace verified link-by-link: joined error dies at applyConfigUnderSem warn+void (daemon_apply.go:220-222, no debt latch); #9811 scope explicitly excludes caller-less paths (rollback + loop self-latch only); conntrack/routing/proxyARP/fabric/service loops never re-drive host-inbound; identical-content T1 renew gated at commitLease (commit.go:198-203,246-247 + #1777).

**Why separate scope:** retry-while-subsystem-down is futile; the real need is a post-repair trigger, which belongs to #9811's retry-ownership scope (currently excludes caller-less paths). Widening it inside #11466 would expand #9811's contract.

**Security note (Sec10):** trigger is fault-only (kernel nft transactions not remotely fail-able), but routine REMOTE renewals (T1 gate) can sustain the open window indefinitely after nft heals with zero install attempts — remotely discoverable (port scan on W), deliberately extendable by a rogue server. Single-failure (real fails, gap installs) is PROVEN bounded (TestVRFLeaseWindowBoundedByGapAfterFailedRerender10751) — this issue covers double-failure only.

**Acceptance:** a bounded retry/convergence owner for failed host-inbound applies (e.g. 30s retry scoped to the gap-failure join, or #9811 caller-less widening), proven by failure-injection (double-fail → automatic convergence with no new external event).

The userspace dataplane has process-local `UNZONED_INGRESS_DENIED` and `UNZONED_EGRESS_DENIED` cause counters, but they are not currently included in `ProcessStatus`, Prometheus metrics, or policy hit-count snapshots. Production visibility is therefore limited to the unattributed RT_FLOW event and aggregate `xpf_policy_denies_total`; the dedicated Rust counters are currently test/in-process diagnostics only.

Expose both directions through a stable status/metrics surface and add an end-to-end surfacing test. Preserve direction separation and ensure side-effect-free policy re-derivation does not increment either cause counter.

Related: #11067, #11499.

## #11530 — dataplane: link-change-triggered snapshot rebuild for interface rows (follow-up #11086) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-06)

Part 1 (apply-time name↔ifindex revalidation) ships under #11086. Residual: STEADY-STATE staleness — link churn with no subsequent apply leaves the helper enforcing a pre-churn snapshot indefinitely (the #9848 watcher is transit-gate-scoped and triggers no rebuild).

Design sketch: extend the RTNL link subscription (or a second watcher on NEWLINK/DELLINK for snapshot-row netdevs) to trigger a snapshot refresh through the apply semaphore, following the reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange precedent (applySem + health signal + single-flight retry). Needs: debounce/coalescing (churn storms), row-scoped change detection (ignore unrelated links — no flap), generation fencing so a rebuild cannot resurrect older content. Acceptance: recreate-with-reuse triggers rebuild and stamps correctly; delete drops the row; unrelated churn causes no republish (cells + netns harness).

## #11565 — daemon: route-listener learned-route republish never bumps FIB generation; established flows pinned to stale routes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-01)

## What
actuateLearnedRouteRefresh publishes a learned-route overlay and returns converged, but discards the published flag and never calls BumpFIBGeneration, violating the publisher contract (caller must bump after published=true). The helper gets a newer route snapshot while existing flow entries keep the previous FIB generation/next-hop. Only established flows are affected; new flows see the update. Related to #11373 (hit-path generation gating): that fix keys off generation bumps, so this missing bump would defeat it for listener-driven refreshes — distinct corrective work in daemon_route_listener.go.

## Mechanism (verified at b7450692fb19)
- pkg/daemon/daemon_route_listener.go:232-264 publishes and returns converged on nil error; pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go:79-96 requires the bump after published=true; snapshot carries current FIB generation at :204-207. Sibling actuators bump and retain pending retry state; the listener has no pending-bump bookkeeping for a publish/bump split.

## Acceptance
- Mirror the sibling actuator: bump only after actual publish, keep dirty/pending on bump failure, retry even after duplicate-skip. Changed overlay publication increments FIB generation before route-hit use; injected bump failure remains dirty and a later retry invalidates caches.

## #11567 — dataplane: GRE decap has no transport-interface binding; spoofed peer IP on any same-VRF GRE-admitted interface adopts tunnel zone [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What
match_tunnel_endpoint matches outer tuple, GRE mode, transport-table RI, key, and GRE host-inbound on the ingress interface, then stamps the endpoint logical interface — but never compares ingress ifindex/zone with the resolved transport egress. A second same-VR GRE-admitted interface with matching tuple/key gets its inner packet reattributed to the tunnel zone before policy. #10653 (VR check) and #11054 (host-inbound) constrain but do not bind ingress to the configured transport path. Requires spoofing/injecting peer outer addresses on that interface.

## Mechanism (verified at b7450692fb19)
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/gre.rs:826-865 (match, no ingress-bind compare), :1114-1124 (stamp); stage-6 decap precedes screen/session/policy (poll_stages.rs:339).

## Acceptance
- Require ingress ifindex or ingress zone to match resolved transport egress identity: correct tuple/key on a non-transport same-VR GRE-admitted ingress is not decapped (v4 and v6); the same packet on the transport ingress decaps.

## What
wg_endpoint_for_listen_port matches only listen port and WG mode; the caller passes only the destination port, although the snapshot carries transport_table. AEAD/AllowedIPs protect the cryptographic peer, then logical ingress is stamped from the endpoint interface — with no ingress-VR or outer local-destination comparison in the demux. ## #11571 — host-inbound: host-bound routing multicast ungated by zone protocols (no destination-group dimension) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-03)

## What
With a zone not configured to admit OSPF/VRRP/PIM/RIP, multicast addressed to a host-joined routing group still reaches the local daemon: the enforced catalog covers host-local unicast only, the Rust classifier has no destination-group dimension, and the nft builders emit no multicast-group + ingress-zone rule — unmatched local multicast reaches the input policy-accept path. Requires an enabled daemon + joined group (group membership narrows delivery to the segment, not to an opted-in zone); protocol auth is optional and is not a zone guard. Junos gates this via zone host-inbound protocols ospf (per Juniper OSPF interface docs).

## Mechanism (verified at b7450692fb19)
- pkg/config/host_inbound_multicast.go:11-41 (multicast-group enforcement deferred); zones_host_inbound.go:390 (unicast views); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:724-732 (admit on zone/protocol/port/family/type, no group dimension).

## Acceptance
- With OSPF/VRRP daemon joined and empty zone host-inbound, proto 89 to 224.0.0.5 and proto 112 to 224.0.0.18 drop in that zone; same traffic accepted only on a zone configured for that protocol. Both families/builders + Rust classifier; default-deny catalog groups.

## #11574 — dataplane: XDP WireGuard claim/decap has no ingress-zone check; authenticated peer accepted cross-zone before #11076 gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-06)

Narrow authenticated-peer boundary gap: XDP routes local UDP on a steered listen port to the helper and the worker claim/decap checks tunnel presence, UDP, type, listen port and AEAD — with no ingress zone/ifindex input — then constructs logical tunnel ingress. A valid authenticated peer can send type-4 transport data to a local address in a different zone and get it claimed/decapped without consulting that arrival zone, while the normal nft path has no accept there. Cryptokey/AllowedIPs + tunnel-zone screen/policy still constrain inner traffic, so impact is outer-ingress service scope only. #11076's explicit per-zone host-inbound admission is evidence cross-zone roam is not the intended blanket exception; roaming-intent confirmation remains open.

- userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:824-847, wg_classify.rs:113-143 (XDP steer without zone); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/decap.rs:180-212 (claim without zone input).

## Acceptance
- Carry/resolve outer ingress zone or netdev and apply configured zone-port admission before WG decap (or explicitly document + test cross-zone roaming as the exception): same valid transport record decaps on its serving-zone ingress, not on an unconfigured zone's local address; denied case reaches the kernel host-inbound drop. Retain AllowedIPs/inner-policy positive controls.

- daemon_ipmon.go:389-393 (intent + bump); coordinator/mod.rs:1953-1964 (Arc reuse); poll_descriptor/mod.rs:445 (config-gen-only stamp); session_glue hit path re-pin + flow_cache re-seed.

Repeated weekday blocks with complementary, non-conflicting boundaries silently discard an earlier boundary. Strict compilation accepts the input and emits no warning. This is a compiler composition defect in operator-authored configuration; no network attacker or live traffic scenario is assumed.

## Evidence

Verification revision: e6204b2bf6f87a95be0ea64d3a43a51846c64f9c (PR #11628 merged with baseline f5584e77d5f03474bf722a2518e8fbffc09277d6). The affected compileSchedulers weekday assembly is unchanged by that PR.

STATIC: pkg/config/compiler_system.go:2882-2887 parses each weekday fragment into a fresh SchedulerDayWindow and unconditionally assigns sched.Days[name] = &w. In contrast, daily fragments at 2871-2878 preserve previously supplied start/stop fields when a later fragment omits them.

EXECUTED: a bounded local program called the real parser and CompileConfig, with no policy attachment or network activity. Observed:
- Combined weekday start/stop control: 09:00:00 / 17:00:00; warnings empty.
- The same weekday boundaries split across two blocks: start empty / stop 17:00:00; warnings empty.
- Complementary daily-block control: 09:00:00 / 17:00:00; warnings empty.

Command: go run /var/worktrees/resume-scheduler-fragments-smoke.go, from the pinned review checkout. This verifies compiled values only; no deployed policy or Junos parity claim is made.

## Deduplication

- #5825 fixed replacement of the whole named SchedulerConfig across scheduler instances. This residual occurs one level below, when replacing an entry in its Days map.
- #11358 / #11628 diagnose conflicting repeated values and multiple-pair loss. Here each boundary occurs only once and the fragments are complementary, so that new conflict check does not address the loss.
- Closed broad parser/coalescing issues were searched; no open owner for this remaining weekday assembly defect was found.

## Corrective direction and acceptance

Preserve all accepted non-conflicting fragments of one weekday as the equivalent single-window/flat form, or explicitly reject an unsupported composition; never silently erase the earlier field. Do not invent multi-window union semantics.

Cover complementary boundaries in both orders, the combined-window and daily controls, equivalent flat input, and existing identical/conflicting/day-flag behavior. Retain the separately reviewed strict/tolerant repeated-window diagnostic contract. Validate through the exported compiler API rather than source-text assertions.

## Assessment and provenance

Gate: MATERIAL. Severity: Low, bounded compiler-value loss; potential policy consequences are not measured here. Confidence: High for the stated local property. Verification: EXECUTED component check plus STATIC assignment trace.

Discovery: native Claude Code review of PR #11628, session c301ca69-b25e-42fb-a88d-689fd6e6c500; runtime reports claude-opus-5-5, firstParty, 1M context. Parent verification: openai-codex/gpt-6-astra in the resumed campaign. Independent full source-review passes otherwise marked PR #11628 READY; this pre-existing residual is not attributed to that PR's new diagnostic.

## #11650 — userspace-dp: scope-aware link-local candidate filter for bare-gateway inference (follow-up #11322) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-03)

## What
PR #11648 (issue #11322) made bare IPv6 link-local next-hop inference fail closed: it infers an egress only when same-table connected IPv6 rows collapse to one (ifindex, tunnel) candidate, else NoRoute. That eliminates wrong-egress binding, but the candidate set over-counts: the helper builds a connected row for EVERY kernel address including autoconf fe80::/64 on managed IPv4-only/VLAN-parent/mgmt interfaces (networkd LinkLocalAddressing=ipv6), while the daemon counts only configured v6 addresses/VIPs. Result: single-configured-v6-unit deployments (daemon-unique, FRR installs) can read as helper-ambiguous (NoRoute) purely from kernel-LL extras. Patch-introduced availability divergence in the daemon-unique corner; the ambiguous corner is correctly fail-closed either way.

## Fix direction (from ScoutLinklocalFallback11648 section F — verify, do not blindly adopt)
A scope-aware Rust filter (skip nonzero non-UNIVERSE rows) is wire-compatible (scope rides the snapshot today, Rust ignores it) and fixes the kernel-LL axis while preserving explicit fe80::/64 under unit.Addresses. Do NOT do a content-based 'count only non-link-local' (drops explicit-LL capability). Open sub-decisions: (a) which Scope wins when the live/configured merge collapses copies (provenance check); (b) DHCP/kernel-only GUA rows (UNIVERSE scope, daemon does not count them) — needs a capability decision; (c) VRRP-VIP-only and RA/PD rows. Overlay bare-LL reachability (ip-monitoring overlays bypass the #11317 config-static gate) and mixed-member ECMP rescue need pinned cells; add a VRF/table-scoping cell for the new arm.

## Acceptance
Daemon-unique + kernel-LL extras resolves (no false ambiguity); genuinely ambiguous stays NoRoute; explicit scopes authoritative; global-LPM/IPv4 unchanged; overlay + mixed + VRF cells pin production shapes.

## Origin
Campaign PR-to-zero merge review of #11648; native CODE review section B + independent scout carrier analysis (preserved in campaign run). Fail-closed safety fix merged first; this is the availability refinement.

feedOverlay-extended names and match-application-any pairs are analyzed (warn when overlap is possible; never hard-reject on unproven overlap, preserving #11670's exact/potential split). Regression cells per shape; no change to exact-witness hard rejects.

Campaign follow-up reported by the #11352 lane post-merge; deliberately not folded into #11670 (merged) — separate corrective scope.

## #11765 — harness: ha-smoke exe attestation structurally VOID — rebuild-vs-deployed comparison cannot MATCH [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What
Every HA gate (test-failover etc.) records VOID via exe_check=MISMATCH even when the test itself passes, because build_exe_sha256 is hashed from a fresh local $root/xpfd rebuild while running_exe_sha256 comes from the deployed deb. Two stamped LDFLAGS make any rebuild differ from the deployed bits:

1. main.buildTime second-granularity (Makefile:10 BUILD_TIME ?= date now) — deploy build and gate rebuild always differ.
2. main.version dirty flag — deployed builds carry -dirty (e.g. working-17244-g8bffc4ed5-dirty) that a clean-tree gate rebuild will not reproduce.

Evidence: loss-userspace-cluster test-failover 2026-10-02, 22 PASS / 3 FAIL(iperf-artifact, see stream note), verdict VOID solely on exe_check=MISMATCH. Reosz across runs.

## Direction (lane decides)
Record-at-deploy attestation: deploy writes the built xpfd (+helper) shas to a manifest; the gate compares running vs the manifest instead of vs a fresh rebuild. That attests deployment identity rather than build reproducibility. Alternative (pin BUILD_TIME + enforce clean-tree deploys) is fragile — dirty-flag alone re-breaks it.

## Acceptance
- Same-commit deploy + gate run yields exe_check=MATCH (or a principled non-VOID path) on loss-userspace-cluster.

## #11767 — [follow-up #11370] fib_dump consistency + response caps (RuntimeView snapshot, over-budget refusal) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (post-#11763 hardening, spec from DriveBatchAR)
1. **Stale-view read**: dump_fib reads retained self.forwarding/self.validation instead of the published RuntimeView. Fix: take exactly one self.ha.runtime.load() and derive both forwarding() and validation().fib_generation from it. Regression: publish route/gen 9, mutate retained fields to empty/gen 10, dump must still return route/gen 9.
2. **Unbounded response**: no cap on FIB snapshot bytes. Fix: Rust MAX_CONTROL_RESPONSE_BYTES = MAX_CONTROL_REQUEST_BYTES; count serialized route-row bytes incrementally; refuse over-budget snapshots (1 MiB framing/status reserve) with Result::Err, dropping partial rows. Handler sets ok=false + explicit error, then counts final JSON and refuses/clears routes if it reaches the Go 64 MiB cap. Go must never decode a truncated FIB as empty/success.
3. **Lockstep + docs**: Go cap test pins Go response cap to Rust response cap; Go manager test confirms helper refusal surfaces as error with no generation/routes; pkg/cli/README documents explicit refusal / no partial list.

## Acceptance
- Rust fib_dump cells + full server::tests green; Go FIB/cap cells + 5x canary green; rebase + PR.
- Lost once by parent force-removing the worktree (reubo undocumented edits); this issue tracks the redo.

## #11836 — harness: test-failover Phase-5 samples iperf log before summary → false did-not-complete + no-SUM FAILs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What
Phase 5 waits up to IPERF_DURATION iterations for main_iperf_running to go false, then reads /tmp/iperf3-failover.log ONCE. If iperf3's final control exchange (broken-pipe retries after failover) pushes completion past the wait, the sampled log ends mid-stream (e.g. 118-119s intervals, no final [SUM] sender) and the gate emits two false FAILs: 'iperf3 did not complete' and 'no [SUM] sender line'.

Evidence: loss-userspace-cluster run 06525c4ca58ca308 (2026-10-02): gate sampled at 118-119s; the completed log afterwards shows a full 0-120s run with [SUM] 259 GBytes / 18.5 Gbits/sec sender. On complete data both cells would PASS via the control-disrupted branch. Verdict impact: FAIL on a healthy run (this instance additionally VOIDed by #11765 exe MISMATCH).

## Fix direction
Wait for the summary line (or iperf Done), not just process exit / fixed iterations: poll until grep -q 'iperf Done' or [SUM].*sender appears, with the existing duration as the timeout budget.

## Secondary observation (same run)
Stream 19 silent 3 intervals vs 2-interval aggregate outage → 'did not resume within 3s'. Single-stream tail under 33k-retransmit crash failover; carried 29.6 GB total. Needs a rerun datapoint to judge flake vs systematic; do not soften the oracle without it.

## #11840 — [follow-up #11767] fib_dump needs a controlVerbDeadlineFloors9344 floor — 3 s base vs 64 MiB serialize [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What
fib_dump is asked with a ~60-byte request so controlWorkDeadline grants it controlBaseDeadline (3 s). But a dump can serialize up to MAX_CONTROL_RESPONSE_BYTES (64 MiB) of JSON; on a loaded box the serialize + unix-socket write can exceed 3 s, so Go abandons a round trip the helper is still legitimately performing — the exact #9344 failure shape (there: export_owner_rg_sessions).

Spotted by DriveBatchAR during #11837 review (advisory, verified by parent against control_work_deadline_9344.go on 0034c5e6f).

## Fix
Add a fib_dump entry to controlVerbDeadlineFloors9344 sized for worst-case serialize + write + margin (mirror any helper-side bound by READING the Rust constant per the file's agreement-test convention, not a restated literal), plus a floor test. Keep the floor far below controlMaxDeadline per the file's SCOPE note.

## #11845 — [follow-up #11765] deploy manifest is single-slot: rolling per-node rebuilds overwrite each other, peer attestation cannot MATCH [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (live finding, loss-userspace-cluster 2026-10-02)
Each NODE deploy rebuilds (BUILD_TIME differs), so fw0 and fw1 run different xpfd bits (08238e52… vs 0ed8df7b…). The manifest at dist-deb/xpf-deploy-manifest.json is single-slot: fw1's deploy overwrote fw0's entry. The HA gate checks BOTH nodes (#9044 peer attestation), so fw0 can never MATCH — VOID forever on rolling deploys.

## Fix direction (lane decides)
(a) Per-node manifest slots (node → binaries), recorded per deploy without clobbering siblings; gate looks up each node's slot. (b) Or: build once, deploy the identical deb to all nodes. (a) is smaller and preserves the rolling flow; (b) is operationally nicer but bigger. Either way, stale/missing-slot must fail closed per the existing contract, selftests must cover two-node rolling (deploy 0, deploy 1, assert both slots + both MATCH), and docs/log/11765.md + schema note updated.

## Acceptance
Two-node rolling deploy + gate run shows MATCH for both nodes (live loss proof by parent post-merge), hermetic selftests cover the rolling case.

## #11861 — [follow-up #11836] failover iperf3 client can hang forever in the final control exchange — needs a wall-clock killer [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (live, loss-userspace-cluster run 9eec5af7a2f1a64b, 2026-10-02)
The -t 120 client finished 118-119s of data intervals, then hung 6+ min in the final control exchange (no SUM, no 'iperf Done', process alive, log frozen). --connect-timeout covers connect only. The Phase-5 marker wait (#11836) correctly exhausted and sampled pre-summary → FAIL (honest), but the hang wastes the full budget and leaves a stuck client (manually pkill'd). Server is external lab hardware (172.16.80.200, no mgmt path) — flaky far end must be assumed.

## Fix
Wrap the gate's iperf3 client in timeout(1) (e.g. timeout 150 for a -t 120 run + exchange margin) so it always terminates; ensure cleanup pkills by pidfile; the existing control-disrupted PASS branch already handles the truncated-but-measured case. Add a hermetic cell if the harness has a client-lifecycle seam.

## #11872 — harness: test-failover should resync node clocks after the crash reboot (no-NTP lab loses 2+ min) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (live, run fbd19d88, 2026-10-02)
fw0's crash reboot came back 2m18s behind (no NTP anywhere in the loss lab). The skew broke fabric-auth windows/heartbeat freshness, stretched the rejoin bulk past the failback budget, and all 3 manual failbacks were refused ('cold prime owed without pending outbound bulk' — peer barrier never satisfied). Manual clock resync → all 3 transfers committed immediately. Not a code regression; purely environmental. But every crash test in this lab will eat it.

## Fix
After the crash-reboot wait in test-failover.sh (and double-failover), resync both nodes' clocks from the host (incus exec date -u -s) before the failback phase. Small, hermetic-testable sequencing; live-provable on the next run.

## #11896 — [follow-up #11507] lenient poison installs a real drop instead of refusing via FromUnrepresentable (no-brick violation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (post-merge advisory from DriveBatchBS, verified by inspection claim)
#11893's lenient poison overwrites term.Action="discard". toNftLo0Term propagates term.Action directly, so the conflict installs a REAL DROP in nft/lo0 rendering. The existing no-brick marker flow uses FromUnrepresentable to refuse whole userspace snapshots/lo0 plans and retain prior-good state; #11507 adds no such marker.

## Direction (lane decides, confirm against #11063a)
The poison should set FromUnrepresentable (refuse snapshot, retain prior-good) instead of — or in addition to, with render suppression — Action=discard. Check what #11063a (the cited parallel) actually does and match it. Consider the peer-sync path: refusing must stall-and-retain, not wedge sync.

## Acceptance
Conflicting lenient terminals neither install accept (old fail-open) nor install a fresh drop (current over-correction); prior-good retained with warning. Red-before/green-after cells + full battery. No revert of #11893 (discard is the safe direction meanwhile).

## #11928 — [follow-up #11701] boot success stamp races concurrent failed promotion (MarkActiveApplied outside applySem) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-02)

## What (post-merge catch by DriveBatchCK on #11925, already merged)
Boot calls applyActiveConfigResult (which releases applySem), then MarkActiveApplied stamps success. A concurrent commit whose apply FAILS in between leaves failed state stamped as applied — TOCTOU between result return and stamp.

## Fix
Move the success stamp under applySem (or otherwise make result+stamp atomic w.r.t. concurrent applies); add an interleaving regression cell (concurrent failed promotion vs boot success → no applied stamp on failure).

## Acceptance
Interleaving cell red-before/green-after; full battery; PR. No revert of #11925 (the debt-latch behavior is correct; only the stamp needs the lock).

## #12007 — [cfg-appid-cmdtree] Preserve keyword-looking CoS filter values [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-03)

## Dependency

This follow-up was blocked on the fail-closed parser work in #11834 landing. Its fix merged as PR #11998 (merge commit 37b733ceb), so the dependency is satisfied and this follow-up is now unblocked.

## Problem

`ParseCoSNameTypeArgs` treats `name` and `type` as keywords even when they occupy the value position. Consequently, valid explicit filters such as `name name` and `name type` are rejected, even though configured classifier/rewrite-rule names are opaque values and may literally equal either keyword. The same issue affects type-filter values equal to a keyword.

## Fix

Recognize `name` and `type` only in key positions. Consume the next token as the value regardless of spelling; report a dangling filter only when its keyword is the final token. Keep rejecting unconsumed unknown tokens. Add grammar cells for literal `name`/`type` values and dangling/unknown controls.

## Provenance

Post-merge review of #11834 / PR #11998 found this valid-input regression.

## #12034 — [R2-05+R2-03] shared-VRF-master host-inbound: destination-owner admit + missing fine junos-host deny (one sdifname fix) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-06)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL High.

### R2-05: On a VRF master shared by two zones with different host-inbound sets, the kernel host-inbound gate admits a host-bound packet by the zone that owns the destination address, not the ingress zone — an untrusted-zone peer reaches a service opened only on the trusted zone's firewall address, and a trusted-zone peer is refused on the co-member's address.
Junos `host-inbound-traffic` is an ingress-zone control; the tree states that contract and the #9637 defect in the comment at `pkg/daemon/host_inbound_ingress_9637.go:66-120`, and closed #9637 fixed admission-by-destination. `pkg/daemon/README.md:3799-3815` calls the kernel chain "the PRIMARY host-inbound enforcement path" and, ten lines below the contract, documents "#11331: … the kernel applies each destination owner's service rights". This is a **deliberate choice of the #11331 fix**, made to end an instance-wide outage (the pre-fix behaviour was an unconditional drop) and documented in the daemon README; it contradicts the ingress-zone contract in the same file and closed #9637.

Fix: render per-zone ingress rules on a shared master scoped by `iifname <master>` + `meta sdifname {<zone's own slaves>}`, keeping destination-owner rights only where slave identity is genuinely unavailable. **One fix with R2-03** (same slave match gives the fine junos-host deny its scope). Acceptance criterion (verifier's): real-kernel cell with two slaves of one VRF and differing host-inbound sets: untrusted-slave → trusted address:22 dropped and counted against the untrusted zone; trusted-slave → either address:22 accepted; a port neither zone allows dropped; the same matrix for IPv6; text and netlink renderers in parity; R2-03's fine deny scoped by the same slave match. Remaining validation: IPv6, netlink renderer, unzoned/lifeline co-member variant, shim run.

## #12037 — [R1-04] #11323's preference-aware gap-fill compares the config route's preference with the constant 200, not the learned protocol's distance: a floating static at preference 21.... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-06)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### R1-04: #11323's preference-aware gap-fill compares the config route's preference with the constant 200, not the learned protocol's distance: a floating static at preference 21..200 (eBGP), 111..200 (OSPF), 116..200 (IS-IS), 121..200 (RIP) or exactly 200 (iBGP) suppresses the kernel-selected protocol route, so the helper forwards on the static while FRR / the kernel use the protocol route.

#11323 acceptance: "Helper honors route preference (or declines so the kernel's selected route wins)". Against it, `pkg/routing/fibimport.go:77-86` and `TestLearnedRouteDoesNotOverrideABetterPreferenceConfigRoute` pin "config at <= 200 stays sole" as intended — a documented simplification that contradicts the issue's own acceptance for any protocol whose distance is below 200.

Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/0.93/STATIC; smr MATERIAL/Medium/0.8/STATIC (both; spark MATERIAL/High/0.88/EXECUTED

Evidence:
- BASE afb887cb3 pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:1343-1355,1428-1444@base; pkg/routing/fibimport.go:77-86,181-191@base; pkg/frr/config_render.go:512-519@base

- pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:332-358,385-421@both (diff starts at 425) — config static emitted at route.Preference / qualified nh.Preference independent of FRR selection; only all-recursive bare gateways are withheld (332-341, #11317).
- pkg/routing/fibimport.go:77-86 and 181-191@both (file identical) — LearnedRouteImportPreference=200; import set includes RTPROT_BGP/ISIS/OSPF/RIP and ZSTATIC(196), so a bgp/ospf/isis/rip row for a prefix exists in the kernel only when zebra selected it over the static.
- pkg/frr/config_render.go:512-520@both — static rendered with distance sr.Preference / nh.Preference; `git grep 'distance (bgp|ospf|isis|rip)'` empty at both pins (positive control `dist := sr.Preference` hits) => FRR defaults eBGP 20, OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, RIP 120, iBGP 200.

- pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:1428-1435@base == :1442-1449@verify: `best <= routing.LearnedRouteImportPreference { continue }`, no use of lr.Protocol (logged only :1411@:1425)

Fix: when the import reports a dynamic-protocol row for a prefix that config also covers, keep the learned row ordered ahead of the static (or stamp it with the protocol's distance), keeping the `<=` suppression only for the static's own echo. - poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5457-5490@BASE and :5486-5519@VERIFY sends the stamped incoming packet_frame to deny_reply_and_emit with binding.ifindex, including the fabric parent in the owning node's flow-miss policy-reject branch.

- tx/transmit/mod.rs:218-273@BASE and @VERIFY optionally rewrites DSCP then copies TxRequest.bytes to UMEM unchanged at Ethernet destination. test_fixtures.rs:1029-1064@BASE and @VERIFY uses fabric parent ifindex 21; native client's MAC is on a different ingress binding.
- Mechanism: for a stamped fabric punt the RG owner evaluates new-flow policy; on Reject the TCP RST is built by reflecting the inbound frame's L2 header (dst = inbound src = zone stamp) and queued on the arrival fabric binding, then counted policy_reject_sent and logged REJECT.
- Ingress node never enforces policy for FabricRedirect: policy only for ForwardCandidate (poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4148-4150@base / :4170@verify); 'FabricRedirect is HA peer-owned and enforced on the peer' (:6458@base / :6487@verify).
- forwarding/fabric.rs:574-592@base/@verify stamp src_mac = [0x02,0xbf,0x72,FABRIC_ZONE_MAC_MAGIC,hi,lo].
- Call sites pass binding.ifindex and packet_frame with no fabric condition: mod.rs:5469-5490@base / :5498-5519@verify; MissingNeighbor twin :8106@base / :8135@verify.
- poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs (unchanged): TCP -> build_reject_rst_frame(packet_frame) :304-305; TxRequest{egress_ifindex: ingress_ifindex} :456-468; policy_reject_sent += 1 :471; deny_reply_and_emit :194-236 passes enqueued=true so event_emit.rs:551-552 logs REJECT.
- frame/tcp.rs:746-758@base/@verify write_reply_eth_header: reply dst = frame[6..12] (stamp), reply src = frame[0..6].

Fix: For fabric-ingress triggers, either route the generated reply via a normal forwarding lookup toward the source, or suppress it and log a truthful DENY. Consumers: `enqueue_reject_reply` and both call sites. Acceptance criterion (v10): the run7 cell — for a stamped fabric punt under `then reject`, either no reply is queued and the event is DENY with `policy_reject_sent == 0`, or the reply's L2 destination comes from a forwarding lookup toward the source (never `02:bf:72:fe:*`) on a non-fabric egress; native control unchanged. Remaining validation: peer-side handling; a fabric unit that carries an address of the packet's family (v10: would source an ICMP error from the fabric address — not exercised).

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### W03-02: `system-services any-service` + `<svc> except` silently discards the exclusion.

`pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:166-170` — the function's own rule that a malformed modifier must "never [be] silently accept[ed] as an empty exclusion". The doc contract (`host-inbound-service-matrix.md:1682-1688`) only speaks of `all`; `~:1983` states `any-service` is deliberately never expanded.

Gate: codex NEEDS_VALIDATION/Low/0.82/STATIC: inde; smr MATERIAL/Low/0.6/EXECUTED (v4; spark MATERIAL/Low/0.75/STATIC

Evidence:
- pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:126-171@afb887cb3 ; pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:126-171@425e83f93 — only literal `all` is expanded; unfiltered `any-service` survives the exact-name exclusion
- pkg/config/host_inbound_tokens.go:526-543@afb887cb3 ; pkg/config/host_inbound_tokens.go:526-543@425e83f93 — `any-service` expressly stands only for itself, not a subtractable union
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:256-269@afb887cb3 ; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:256-269@425e83f93 — full-admit flag is set from the surviving token
- pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_host_inbound.go:929-965@afb887cb3 ; pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_host_inbound.go:929-965@425e83f93 — generic full-admit advisory warns of breadth, does not identify dropped exclusions
- Mechanism: only literal `all` is expanded/filtered; `any-service` passes through as a packet-wide full admit, so an authored `<svc> except` is consumed with zero enforcement effect and no diagnostic.
- pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:148-171@afb887cb3=@425e83f93: excluded token removed from the list (:153-155), only `token == "all"` is expanded (:156-162), `any-service` appended verbatim (:164); :166-170 keeps only malformed bare `except` visible to strict validation.
- Doctrine of rejecting inert `except`: compiler_host_inbound_except_10292_test.go:146-152 (standalone modifier fails) and :231-239 (double modifier fails) @afb887cb3=@425e83f93.
- Enforcement: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:269@afb887cb3/@425e83f93 `"any-service" => hi.all_services = true`; daemon_nft.go hostInboundAllowsAll :2570@afb887cb3 / :2695@425e83f93 -> bare accept, no catch-all, so tcp/22 stays admitted.
- Advisory names breadth, not the dropped exclusion: compiler_validate_warn_host_inbound.go fullAdmitAdvice :1032-1049@afb887cb3 / :950-967@425e83f93.
- Junos: reference syntax defines `except` only under `all` (`all <service-name except>`); YANG `leaf except` ('traffic to disallow') is present on every entry, so the pair is YANG-valid but Junos semantics under any-service are not established in-tree.

Fix: Diagnostic or reject in the same filter. Acceptance: `any-service` + `<svc> except` either fails strict commit or yields a warning containing the excluded token; lenient load keeps `[any-service]` and warns.

- Lead only (not run by me): verify/v3/frr-live-w07-08.txt (FRR 10.7.1) per-daemon `show route-map` matches those tables exactly (isisd seq10/20 address-only; ospf6d seq10 no match + `metric 500`; ospfd/ripd seq20 no match + `metric 500`); frr-reload rc=0 and idempotent.

The reporter also cites the same file's header ("Identity is the stable string key …", "clears ONLY sessions whose stored policy_id matches a deleted policy") at old-base lines `:16-19` / `:129-131` (504ada249 lines only). v4: the comment at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:160-170` ("the helper's #3395 refresh re-stamps established rows") is stale for the userspace read path.

Evidence:
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:48-69 and policies_ids.go:60-75@BASE and @VERIFY assign positional PolicySetID*MaxRulesPerPolicy+RuleIndex by stable key: inserting a preceding rule renumbers the unchanged later rule.

- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/mod.rs:1615-1648,1719-1734@BASE and @VERIFY matches frozen SessionMetadata.policy_id against requested numbers. ha/session_domain.rs:490-505@BASE and @VERIFY serializes that scalar; session/mod.rs:3460-3505@BASE and :3532-3576@VERIFY changes it only in explicit po
- userspace-dp/src/protocol/security.rs:473-477@BASE and @VERIFY has stable rule_id in policy snapshots; it is not the discriminator of the helper's session list. A re-resolved policy ID for BPF rows is a different surface from the stored SessionTable metadata.
- Mechanism: commit-time invalidation computes target ids in the OLD config's positional numbering and asks the helper for sessions whose STORED session-table policy_id equals them; the stored id is frozen at admission, so after an earlier renumbering commit the two id spaces differ: an unrelated rule
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:67-69@base/@verify policyID = PolicySetID*MaxRulesPerPolicy + RuleIndex (positional).

Both pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go:120-135,259-263 and pkg/cli/cli_sho
- Counterexample to a nonexistent table: pkg/routing/routes.go:89-105,264-275@afb887cb3 and :89-105,264-275@425e83f93 can read the numeric table directly; pkg/cli/cli_show_routing.go:129-165 at both pins resolves 'show route instance <ri>' via cfg.RoutingInstances[*].TableID. - No listed fresh open owner addresses these readers. Closed #9409 concerns routing protocols incorrectly assigned to global FRR, not route-display name resolution. No performance effect is asserted: the failed lookup is a management diagnostic, not a packet hot path.
- Forwarding instances never get a VRF device: pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:186-191 ('forwarding instance, skipping VRF creation'), :345 (member binding skips forwarding), :520 (hasDesiredVRF excludes forwarding); file identical at both pins.

- Name-keyed readers resolve ONLY via the vrf-<name> link: pkg/routing/routes.go:184-198 (GetVRFRoutes -> LinkByName("vrf-"+name) -> 'VRF %q not found'), :204-237 (GetTableRoutes sends every non-inet.0/inet6.0 name to GetVRFRoutes); Manager wrappers pkg/routing/routing.go:192-199 add no table-id fallb
- Callers without fallback: pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go:125 (route-table topic) and :260 (test-routing instance); pkg/cli/cli_show_routing.go:26 -> :169-175 (showRoutesForVRF -> GetTableRoutes); pkg/cli/cli_request_testcmd.go:327 (GetVRFRoutes); remote cmd/cli/show.go:186@afb887cb3 / :194@4

## #12077 — [W09-04] Both CLI `test routing` parsers ignore unknown tokens and valueless selectors, so a mistyped `instance` silently becomes a main-table lookup. [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-07)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### W09-04: Both CLI `test routing` parsers ignore unknown tokens and valueless selectors, so a mistyped `instance` silently becomes a main-table lookup.

The #4589 comment in `showTestRouting`: a typo must not silently widen the query to the wrong table.

Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/0.98/STATIC; smr MATERIAL/Low/0.9/STATIC; spark MATERIAL/medium/0.9/STATIC

Evidence:
- Mechanism: after recognizing a valid destination, either on-box or remote test-routing CLI silently ignores an unknown selector or a trailing 'instance' with no value. That leaves instance empty and performs a main-table query, although the operator typed a different query.
- pkg/cli/cli_request_testcmd.go:296-330@afb887cb3 and :296-330@425e83f93 have no switch default or missing-value error. cmd/cli/main.go:780-806@afb887cb3 and :780-806@425e83f93 repeat the same loop and emit only dest=... when instance stays empty. pkg/cli/cli_request_testcmd.go:373-385 at both pins p
- The on-box dispatch at pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:248-275,299-312@afb887cb3 and :248-275,299-312@425e83f93 checks top-level command, coarse permission and optional command regex but does not validate routing subarguments before handleTest. pkg/cli/cli_request_testcmd.go:16-37@both pins only validates t
- The server is not a rescue for dropped CLI tokens: pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go:213-251@afb887cb3 and :213-251@425e83f93 rejects malformed/unknown keys only if they reach the 'test-routing:' topic. The remote CLI strips 'instnace dmz' and forwards a perfectly formed dest-only topic. Closed
- The optional on-box regex gate bypasses an uncanonicalizable line only for a class with operational regexes: pkg/cli/permissions_regex.go:62-108@afb887cb3 and :62-108@425e83f93 returns nil if no regexes exist. This is a reliability/diagnostic problem, not a demonstrated authentication bypass or hot-
- Local parser: pkg/cli/cli_request_testcmd.go:303-317 (identical at both pins) — `switch args[i] { case "destination": if i+1 < len(args) {...}; case "instance": if i+1 < len(args) {...} }` with no default arm and no missing-value error; :319-322 print usage only when dest is empty; :324-330 then pic
- Remote parser is the same loop: cmd/cli/main.go:780-806 (case "instance" at :789), building `test-routing:dest=D[,instance=I]` at :802-805, so unknown, misspelled or valueless tokens never reach the server.
- The strict parser exists only server-side: pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go:192-250 (#4589 comment: a typo'd `instnace=dmz` left instance empty and fell back to the MAIN table; selector switch :234 with unknown-key default arm :239-243, parseErr reported before any lookup :246-252) — it only s
- No pre-dispatch guard on the default path: pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:248-312 runs only checkPermission and checkCommandRegex before handleTest (the regex gate returns nil for classes without operational regexes); handleTest (cli_request_testcmd.go:17-39) resolves only the sub-command word; remote cmd/
- Consequence (static): `test routing destination D instnace dmz`, `... instance` (no value), `... bogus`, and a Junos-style abbreviation `... inst dmz` (case labels are exact strings) all run a main-table lookup and print 'Routing lookup for D:' with success on both CLIs.

Fix: Add `default:` and missing-value errors to both parsers. Acceptance criterion (v5): `test routing destination D instnace dmz`, `… instance` (no value) and `… bogus` each return an error on both CLIs and perform no lookup.

Dedup note (source): #4589 CLOSED fixed the server-side parser only; #4921, #4832 are server-side / test coverage. Archive lost. Residual of #4589.

The ICMP socket binds only tc.Source in the default/global context, while an anchored GRE endpoint can resolve the actual outer destination in X.inet.0; an
- BASE pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive.go:96-105,137-143 and pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive_runner.go:280-305; VERIFY same paths and lines. - Mechanism: GRE keepalive opens an unprivileged ICMP datagram socket bound to tc.Source with no SO_BINDTODEVICE/VRF scope; when the underlay is a routing instance (stanza = transport, as the dataplane encapsulates) a VRF-held source makes bind fail EADDRNOTAVAIL -> UnsupportedStructural -> hold-on-un
- pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive.go:58-106 (contract: probe 'routed in the GLOBAL/underlay FIB exactly like the tunnel's encapsulated traffic (section 5b - NO overlay-VRF bind)'; 'No SO_BINDTODEVICE'), :131-144 (listen on source), :234-255 (EADDRNOTAVAIL -> structural) @afb887cb3 = same @425e83f93 (unch
- pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive_runner.go:148 startKeepalive(tunnelName, source, remoteAddr, interval, maxRetries) - no instance; :271-306 ProbeUnsupported: no Failures, no transition @both; pkg/routing/tunnel.go:654-674@both anchor path starts the runner with tc.Source/tc.Destination only.

## #12088 — [W14-02] RPM next-hop probe pin is verified only at install time — the kernel deletes the pinned table-7000 route on an admin link down/up or last-IPv4-address removal, the fwma... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### W14-02: RPM next-hop probe pin is verified only at install time — the kernel deletes the pinned table-7000 route on an admin link down/up or last-IPv4-address removal, the fwmark rule survives, and nothing re-installs the route until the RPM config hash changes. Corrected form: "link flap" is narrowed (carrier-only loss keeps the route), and "falls through to the main table" is replaced by the measured on-link behaviour.

`pkg/routing/probe_pin.go:160-245` and `pkg/rpm/rpm.go:808-829` — an unbacked SO_MARK is the state #1895 made a held-probe condition; `probe_pin.go` itself calls "a rule over an empty band table … stale state" (reporter's cite `:235-238`).

Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/0.86/STATIC at bo; smr MATERIAL/Medium/0.8/STATIC at bo; spark MATERIAL/Medium/0.85/STATIC

Evidence:
- BASE and VERIFY pkg/routing/probe_pin.go:176-253 builds mark rule plus ONLINK gateway host route and reports only install failures, with no readback or link subscription.
- BASE and VERIFY pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go:267-275,288-295,393-445 retries/restarts only for failed installs or a changed RPM hash; successful installs clear rpmPinsFailed; pkg/rpm/rpm.go:795-828 obtains SO_MARK from cache and gates only pinFailed/zero mark.
- Prior artifact verify/v6/w14_02_netns_output_7.2.8.txt:17-52,69-102 shows an installed route removed by admin down/up or last-address deletion while fwmark rules survive, but carrier-only down leaves it; BASE and VERIFY source supplies no route-loss notification path into pin re-install.
- pkg/routing/probe_pin.go:176-254@afb887cb3 == @425e83f93 (identical): pin = ONLINK Gw+LinkIndex /32 (/128) route in per-test table, installed once in Apply; :159-175@both comment: an unbacked SO_MARK is the #1895 false-PASS class
- pkg/rpm/rpm.go:795-806@both probe socket SO_BINDTODEVICE + SO_MARK; :808-829@both pinInstallError reads only in-memory pinFailed/marks (no kernel readback)
- pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go:262-279@both retry runs only while rpmPinsFailed; :403-407@both hash gate returns before any re-install; rpmPinsFailed written only at :275,:435@both; activeRPMHash sole writer :445@both
- callers daemon_apply_tail.go:301, daemon_run.go:490, daemon_ipmon.go:599@both all pass the same gate; route listener (daemon_route_listener.go) never touches pins
- verify/v6/w14_02_netns_output_7.2.8.txt (lead, read): link down/up empties table 7000 v4+v6 while control table 7001 and rule '50: from all fwmark 0x1000 lookup 7000' survive; last v4 addr del empties table, not restored on re-add; lookup falls to on-link 'dev wan1' or to a main route via wan1 .254
- pkg/routing/probe_pin.go:176@both Apply, :224-229@both Gw+LinkIndex+ONLINK band-table route, :235-238@both stale-rule comment — identical
- pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go:267@both retry only while rpmPinsFailed (:269 early return), :403@both hash gate, :275/:435@both rpmPinsFailed from install results only, :445@both sole activeRPMHash writer — identical

Fix: Make the pin a reconciled object (read back rule + route per pin on reconcile / link-address event / the existing ticker; hold and re-install when missing). Acceptance (verifier): a netns test that installs a pin, bounces the egress link, then drives the reconcile with an UNCHANGED hash and asserts (a) the test is held (`ErrProbeSetup`, no probe sent) while the route is absent and (b) the route is back after one retry interval; same for last-address removal and re-add. Remaining validation: end-to-end through `reconcileRPM`; the `programRethMAC` trigger.

Dedup note (source): Searched `probe.pin|pinned|probe table|fwmark|7000|rpm`. #1895 (CLOSED) is nearest — covers failed installs only. #6561, #5852, #9026 are different wrong-verdict causes. ## #12112 — [follow-up #11815] BGP SAFI diagnostics: warn every unsupported name, fix sibling/inherited 'not activated' + strict mixed wording [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## What
Post-merge delta review (Review12109b) of #11815 found the activation gate + fail-closed behavior correct, but three diagnostic gaps in pkg/config/compiler_bgp_safi_11815.go:

1. **P1 — only the first unsupported SAFI is named.** The gate retains one `unsupportedName` while the open-world hook suppresses every SAFI warning, so a family with two unsupported SAFIs (braced labeled-unicast + bogus-leaf, or flat labeled-unicast + bogus-safi) warns once naming only the first; the second goes inert with no record. Pre-fold code warned twice.
2. **P2 — false 'not activated' for sibling/inherited mixed SAFIs.** The message is picked from the single node's unicast flag, but group siblings + neighbor inheritance OR activation across nodes: sibling one-liners (`family inet labeled-unicast;` + `family inet unicast;`) and neighbor-level override inheriting group unicast warn 'this family is not activated' while the compiled neighbor has inet=true. Intra-node mixed text is accurate.
3. **P2 — strict mixed-SAFI error reuses lenient wording.** A family carrying unicast + unsupported SAFI on the strict path returns 'is skipped; explicitly configured unicast remains activated' as a HARD error although strict rejects and activates nothing.

## Acceptance
- Lenient diagnostic names EVERY unsupported SAFI on the family (multi-name message or one warning per name).
- Sibling/inherited mixed shapes report unicast-active accurately (message reflects merged activation, not the single node).
- Strict mixed-SAFI error states rejection (no 'remains activated').
- Regression cells for all three shapes, strict + lenient.

## Review origin
Parent-review follow-up from PR #12109 delta (Review12109b, merged as 10e8ea36f). Activation/fail-closed behavior verified correct; diagnostics only.

## #12128 — nftables: large host-inbound batches fail with EMSGSIZE/ENOBUFS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Observed defect

The production netlink installer cannot install the existing large host-inbound parity fixture with the current transport defaults. During PR #12127 verification at `6ff8f637e7a8a45d65844e68cb77decfc11362f7`, real private-netns T1 execution failed before a ruleset comparison:

```text
TestNftNetlinkParity/host_inbound:
  nftables flush xpf_hostinbound: SendMessages: netlink send-messages: sendmsg: message too long
TestNftNetlinkParity/cold_boot_fence:
  nftables flush xpf_hostinbound: netlink receive: recvmsg: no buffer space available
```

The screen-alarm, stale-gate, no-programs and several mutation cases also hit EMSGSIZE. The focused DHCP lease-transition packet proof passed five times, and the new DHCP VRF-backstop parity case passed. Full T1 is **FAILED**, not a green gate. Recorded output is retained locally as artifact://151836. A separate #11574 run also recorded netlink message-size/buffer failures; that report is corroboration, not a second isolated reproduction.

## Source boundary

- [NewNetlinkInstaller](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/blob/a4bdf49ca950d7b463f331d59949e3fad463cd3d/pkg/nftables/netlink_installer.go#L156-L165) constructs an ordinary google/nftables connection.
- [replaceTable](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/blob/a4bdf49ca950d7b463f331d59949e3fad463cd3d/pkg/nftables/netlink_installer.go#L305-L343) emits delete/add/rules in one Flush, preserving the intended atomic table transaction.
- The failing host_inbound fixture does not supply the new DHCP backstop argument; the new VRF-specific case passes. The exact broader regression age has not been established by a rerun and is not asserted here.
- Observed dependencies: google/nftables v0.3.0 and mdlayher/netlink v1.7.3-0.20250113171957-fbb4dce95f42. Observed host defaults: wmem_default=rmem_default=212992; wmem_max=rmem_max=4194304. These values do not, alone, prove which transport change is correct.

## Impact and required fix

Reachable config installation fails through the production installer; the mandatory security-parity gate cannot measure those cases. There is no demonstrated fail-open packet result. Investigate actual send/ACK sizing and implement a bounded transport correction without changing rule semantics or splitting one atomic table replacement into multiple committed transactions. Do not merely shrink the fixture, skip failures, or globally tune host buffers to make the gate green. Receive-side loss must not be mistaken for proof that the kernel rolled back: establish the installed state for uncertain ACK outcomes.

## Acceptance

1. The existing complete T1 matrix runs on a real private netns and reaches its comparisons, including negative mutations.
2. Exercise a production-shaped large ruleset install/replace plus a rejected replacement; prove old-or-new atomic ruleset behavior and readback on transport uncertainty.
3. Record exact limits, packet/message sizes and environment. Keep no-DHCP and DHCP/VRF behavior unchanged.

Campaign-owned residual discovered while reviewing #12127; distinct from the Rust broad-suite tracker #11649. Do not hide it inside the DHCP API fold. No duplicate open issue was found in the complete campaign inventory or all-state exact-error searches.
