## #12133 — PPTP install broadcast shortfall ignored by the drain [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### W4A1-022 <- a1-worker-queues (finder A1-08; re-exam L215; L254)
- Codex defect: Broadcast returns the number of accepted queues, but the production caller discards the return and records no install retry. The missed worker does not receive the association from this event and its GRE uses an undifferentiated, flowless path until another learn; neither forget-retry mechanism repairs a missed install.
- Codex locators: worker_queue.rs:981-1008,1105-1110: accepted-count return from broadcast is ignored after successful local install.; worker_queue.rs:1038-1075,1125-1126: forget notifications have explicit unsent-queue retry handling, unlike install.; gre_discriminator.rs:819-824,843-854: unassociated call is counted and forwarded without a PPTP session discriminator.
- Codex refutation/limits: `learned` is documented as local associations learned, so its increment is not by itself an incorrect global-acknowledgement counter. Unassociated GRE is explicitly forwarded and counted, not categorically dropped; a later control reply could relearn the call.
- Spark defect: drain_pptp_control_inbox ignores broadcast_pptp_install's accepted-count and increments learned unconditionally, with no install retry record or shortfall counter — unlike the forget paths that record unsent_queue_ids and retry. A worker whose queue was full at broadcast never learns the call and resolves its GRE as unassociated for the association lifetime with no republish trigger.
- Spark refutation/limits: Unassociated is the forward-and-count path, not a drop (gre_discriminator.rs:819-822; worker_queue.rs:982-984), so the missed worker forwards flowless rather than blackholing — survivable per the broadcast test doc. Associations expire on idle via the periodic sweep (pptp.rs:expire_idle wired into expire_stale_entries_ha), bounding stale-handle risk on the teardown side; the residual is missing discriminator/session/policy attribution, not demonstrated loss.
- SMR defect: broadcast_pptp_install returns the accepted count, and its doc obliges callers to retry or surface a shortfall (worker_queue.rs:975-986). drain_pptp_control_inbox ignores the count and increments `learned` unconditionally (:1105-1110). It is the only InstallPptpCall producer (grep), with no retry ledger, unlike the forget paths (:1038-1076, 1119-1126). A worker whose queue is full (4096) at broadcast never learns the call; only the generic WORKER_COMMAND_QUEUE_DROPS moves (:788-791). That worker resolves the call's GRE as unassociated, flowless and counted for the association lifetime (gre_discriminator.rs:818-852; gated by gre_acceleration at poll_descriptor/mod.rs:789-796; EXECUTED an_unassociated_call_is_flowless_and_counted_7699), losing the per-call discriminator.
- SMR refutation/limits: The unassociated path is a designed degradation: forwarding continues. The precondition is a full peer command queue at broadcast time (replication burst, import or stalled worker).
- Next check: With one of several peer queues full at the CallReply, later drain it and show whether that worker ever learns the handle without another reply; distinguish local learned count, worker-specific shortfall and GRE discriminator.

Fix direction: see packet acceptance + reviewer next-checks above; regression cell must fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.

## #12134 — RDNSS/PREF64 lifetimes derive from the unclamped router lifetime (PREF64 silently dropped) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### W4A567-008 <- C08 (finder 544-553; ref 654-657)
- Codex refutation/limits: Strict commits bound both configured leaves. An RDNSS lifetime need not equal the 16-bit Router Lifetime: the sender deliberately maintains independent DNS lifetime when Router Lifetime is explicitly zero, and RDNSS has a wider field. PREF64 pruning deliberately preserves the rest of the RA, so it prevents the larger all-RA outage.
- Spark refutation/limits: Same tolerant-ingress precondition as A567-007 (strict bounds both leaves). Per-option library wrap/drop read but not executed (RDNSS wrap vs prune-drop ambiguous; PREF64 fail-to-prune confirmed via schema :300-302 + sender :1018-1024). Prune is intentional #3895 defense (drop bad option vs abort entire RA); dropping preserves rest of RA (safe vs blackhole). Fix (resolve shared lifetime through header clamp once at source; saturate PREF64 to 65528 + warn-once not prune-drop) is safe. Inconsistency confirmed regardless of wrap-vs-drop.
- SMR defect: Valid narrower form, reachable on the STRICT path, not only via tolerant ingress as the packet assumed. optLifetime copies the raw router lifetime (sender.go:809-826). PREF64 falls back to it when the NAT64 lifetime is unset (sender.go:980-983); the schema documents 'lifetime 0 = router lifetime' (schema_routing.go:749-751, 760-762). Strict commit accepts default-lifetime up to 65535 (schema_routing.go:667-669; RFC 8319 allows up to 65535), but PREF64 can encode at most 65528 (schema_routing.go:298-303). ndp computes uint16(round(L/8)) and errors when >8191 (ndp option.go:803-808). round(65532/8)=8192, so any committed default-lifetime of 65532-65535 with nat64prefix/nat-prefix and no explicit lifetime makes pruneUnmarshalableOptions drop PREF64 from every RA with only a WARN (sender.go:10
- SMR locators: pkg/ra/sender.go:809-826, 859, 956-992, 1003-1045; pkg/config/schema_routing.go:298-314, 667-669, 742-763; ~/go/pkg/mod/github.com/mdlayher/ndp@v1.1.0/option.go:415-432, 803-808; pkg/ra/sender_marshal_3895_test.go:114-119 (only the explicit 65528 boundary is tested)
- SMR refutation/limits: No guard covers the fallback path. The prune exists to avoid aborting the whole RA, and it causes the silent option loss here. The strict-path trigger is a legitimate but unusual near-maximum router lifetime. Hosts with DNS64 may still discover the NAT64 prefix via RFC 7050.
- Next check: Marshal-decode bounded tolerant configs with router lifetime 2^32, explicit router lifetime 0 plus DNS, and PREF64 life 100000; inspect individual wire lifetimes and option presence. Apply the appropriate PIO/RDNSS/PREF64 field bounds rather than assuming all options must numerically equal the header.

## #12135 — External .network glob/multi-pattern Name= missed; xpf always-down file wins [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### W4A567-032 <- F1 (finder 801; ref 869-878)
- Codex defect: A matching external glob/list is stored as one literal map key, so Apply emits an earlier 10-xpf-*.network with always-down policy. More importantly, even an EXACT external Name= only suppresses networkd emission: the earlier compiler has already stripped the interface addresses and brought it down. The bounded defect is inconsistent external ownership across compile and networkd, with an additional durable override for pattern matches; the claimed sole-management-NIC outage is conditional.
- Codex locators: pkg/networkd/networkd.go:788-794 `result[ifName] = true` stores whole Name=; :353 `external[ifc.Name]` is literal; :357-362 describes Name= as whitespace-separated globs; :530-532 writes network file.; pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1816-1853 strips non-link-local addresses and calls LinkSetDown BEFORE daemon_apply_dataplane.go:332-337 calls networkd.Apply; pkg/networkd/networkd.go:1022-1029 renders ActivationPolicy=always-down.; pkg/config/types_chassis.go:76-89 establishes the active-device-m
- Codex refutation/limits: In device-map leave-alone mode unmapped NICs never reach the unmanaged sweep (compiler_iface.go:1773-1810); positional mode is explicitly documented to rename and claim unconfigured NICs (docs/bare-metal-device-map.md:3-29), so an unchanged enp3s0 on an ordinary positional boot and protection of every foreign NIC are NOT established. Protected management names are also skipped at compiler_iface.go:1756-1771.
- Spark defect: Parser keys whole Name value; exact lookup misses glob/list. Compiler already strips/downs before networkd skip; 10-xpf-* sorts before 20-* and wins first-match.
- Spark locators: pkg/networkd/networkd.go:773-799 `ifName := TrimSpace(TrimPrefix(line,"Name=")); result[ifName]=true` — no split, no glob; pkg/networkd/networkd.go:353 `if ifc.Unmanaged && external[ifc.Name]` — exact map lookup; pkg/networkd/networkd.go:357-367 comment admits `Name=` is `WHITESPACE-SEPARATED LIST OF GLOBS` — same function knows semantics parser ignores; pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1831-1853 Unmanaged row + `AddrDel` + `LinkSetDown` immediate; pkg/networkd/networkd.go:1022-1030 `ActivationPo
- Spark refutation/limits: Device-map leave-alone skips unmapped NICs (compiler_iface.go:1804-1810) and protected resolver spares lifeline/fxp0 (:1765-1771) — but both require device-map Active (types_chassis.go:88-90 entries>0) or mgmt identity; positional mode and mapped-but-unconfigured NICs still claimed. Configured NICs intentionally always claimed (networkd.go:340-343) — not this path. Ordering premise (first-match wins) is standard systemd.network(5) and in-repo comment treats glob semantics as load-bearing; no source guard contradicts. Compiler never consults external map even for exact names — skip only suppres
- SMR defect: FindExternallyManaged keys the whole trimmed Name= value (networkd.go:773-799). Apply checks external[ifc.Name] by exact key (networkd.go:353-356). The stated contract is that unmanaged interfaces with external configs are skipped (networkd.go:330-331, 340-343). Per systemd.network(5), Name= is a whitespace-separated list of shell globs (a leading '!' inverts), and the first matching file in alphanumeric order wins. For `Name=enp*` or `Name=ens1 ens2`, xpf writes 10-xpf-<if>.network with always-down, which beats any external file sorting after '10-xpf-'. xpf's own renderer already refuses globs in its names because Name= is a glob list (networkd.go:357-367, ~401-405 #10089). Same-scope extension: external files that match by MACAddress= (or other [Match] keys) are invisible to this reader.
- SMR locators: pkg/networkd/networkd.go:330-367, 773-799; pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1713-1855; systemd.network(5): Name= glob list; first matching file in alphanumeric order applied, later ignored (freedesktop.org)
- SMR refutation/limits: Device-map leave-alone (the bare-metal default when a device map exists) makes unmapped NICs invisible (compiler_iface.go:1773-1810), and the management lifeline and protected set are never stripped (compiler_iface.go:1756-1771). In claim-all mode the compiler strips and downs every unconfigured NIC at runtime regardless of external files, including exact-name ones (compiler_iface.go:1791-1854). The glob gap's incremental harm is therefore persistence: the NIC stays down while xpfd is stopped or before it starts. External names sorting before '10-xpf-' (for example '10-netplan-*') still win.
- Next check: Using isolated source-level fixtures, compare exact Name= and glob/list Name= with the SAME post-naming, present NIC under an explicitly chosen naming/unmapped policy; record compiler address/link effects and generated units separately. Check deployed networkd first-match behavior; a networkd-only parser fix cannot protect the earlier compiler operation.

## #12136 — VRF adopt path swallows LinkSetUp failure; commit green with VRF down [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-09)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### W4A567-035 <- F4 (finder 807; ref 902-907)
- Codex defect: On LinkSetUp failure, adoption still tracks the VRF and returns no link-reconcile error; IsManaged checks tracked names, so consumers can treat a down VRF as ready after a green apply. No periodic link-up reassert was established; later applies can retry.
- Codex locators: pkg/routing/vrf.go:434-439 `LinkSetUp` failure is Debug-only followed by `newTracked = append(...)` and `continue`; :108-118 IsManaged reads the tracked name.; pkg/routing/vrf.go:570-572 RETURNS the identical LinkSetUp error on creation; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:209-218 only propagates an error actually returned by ReconcileVRFs; :253-268 publishes management membership conditional on IsManaged.; pkg/daemon/mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:61-85 checks interface MasterIndex, not VRF admin
- Codex refutation/limits: The existing link has the correct table and remains tracked, so retry on a later Reconcile is possible; management member rebinding failures have a separate commit-error path. Those do not turn an unsuccessful VRF LinkSetUp into success or prove the VRF is up.
- Spark defect: Adopt swallows LinkSetUp (Debug, nil return) while create returns it; tracked+nil lets IsManagedVRF admit mgmt bind/FRR render into down VRF — #5700 false-convergence shape.
- Spark locators: pkg/routing/vrf.go:434-439 adopt: `if err:=LinkSetUp; err!=nil { slog.Debug(non-fatal) }; newTracked append; continue` — no recordErr; pkg/routing/vrf.go:570-572 create: `return true, fmt.Errorf(set VRF %s up)` — asymmetry directly confirmed; pkg/routing/routing.go:130 `IsManagedVRF`; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:253 `if IsManagedVRF(mgmtVRFName)` gates mgmtSet bind; :149-156 #5700 false-convergence comment threads vrfErr to commit — but here err is nil
- Spark refutation/limits: Next Reconcile re-runs adopt LinkSetUp, so later apply retries (self-heals on next commit, not hung forever). Trigger needs down-but-present correct-table VRF + transient LinkSetUp failure (driver reset, external down) — narrow. Mgmt-VRF reassert (mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go) rebinds members, not VRF LinkSetUp itself, so no faster owner — but commit-driven retry bounds window to next apply. Severity capped; no evidence of permanent blackhole.
- SMR defect: Adopt path: a LinkSetUp failure is logged at Debug, the name is tracked, and no error is returned (vrf.go:433-439). The create path returns the same error (vrf.go:570-572). No periodic owner re-asserts VRF admin state. The mgmt-VRF reassert loop checks member MasterIndex only (mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:61-85), as does the RI member reassert (ri_member_vrf_reassert_9813.go). A down VRF therefore persists after a green commit until the next apply, while IsManagedVRF-gated consumers proceed (daemon_apply_interfaces.go:253).
- SMR locators: pkg/routing/vrf.go:431-439, 549-575; pkg/daemon/mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:12-86; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:253
- SMR refutation/limits: This needs an existing correct-table VRF that is already admin-down and a transient LinkSetUp failure; a successful LinkSetUp repairs it. The next apply retries. The codebase's own discipline (#5578, #6792, #6871) treats swallowed apply errors as defects.
- Next check: Fake an already-present correct-table DOWN VRF whose LinkSetUp errors; assert a failed reconcile/commit despite retained tracking, and assert a later healthy reconcile converges.

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### A89-024 <- P-06 (finder 301–302; ref 382–386)
- Codex defect: MATERIAL: installer replaces an existing package trust key in place without an atomic write or cleanup restoration. An interruption or a non-placeholder, invalid locally stamped key can strand Signed-By verification even if subsequent installation fails.
- Codex locators: scripts/dist/install.sh:261-281 checks is_placeholder_key only; :284-294 `printf '%s\n' "$ARCHIVE_KEY" > "$KEYRING"` truncates the live path.; scripts/dist/install.sh:83-115 cleanup restores source/channel pin state, not KEYRING; :443-449 writes key before apt update/install.; scripts/dist/install.sh:343-365 shows separate atomic-ish pin temp/backup discipline; scripts/dist/publish.py:319-338 fingerprints imported keys in apt agreement gate.
- Codex refutation/limits: A normal combined release checks signed install.sh and apt signer/package/installer key agreement via publish.py:360-434,869-906; unauthenticated remote substitution of a Tier-B signed installer is not established. But the installer itself checks only its placeholder marker, `_read_real_archive_key` at publish.py:211-228 checks armor shape rather than full import, and an interrupted local write needs no signature forgery.
- Spark defect: Installer truncates live keyring in place without parse, atomic replace, or rollback, violating its own fail-clean/host-untouched contract. Garbage-but-non-placeholder key (valid armor) passes validate, or kill/power mid-write truncates; apt-get update then fails and cleanup leaves broken keyring (SRC removed, pin restored, keyring stays). Corrupt local stamp / interrupted write / hand-edit need no signature forgery. Bounded to xpf Signed-By key but leaves host worse than before, self-heals only by re-running corrected installer.
- Spark locators:  printf '%s\n' "$ARCHIVE_KEY" > "$KEYRING"; chmod 0644 "$KEYRING"  # in-place truncate, no temp+rename/fsync/symlink refu;  if is_placeholder_key; then ... else die placeholder ... fi  # only placeholder check, no PGP/gpg parse;  cleanup_on_fail removes SRC + restores/removes pin; no keyring arm (PIN_TEMP/PIN_BACKUP only);  write_channel_pin: symlink/non-regular refusal + mktemp-in-dir + backup + mv + PIN_WRITTEN restore arm (owed discipline ;  validate: ALL input checks first — no host mutation yet (H-16); main: validate -> install_keyring -> write_source -> do_;  _read_real_archive_key PGP-block-parses before stamping; _key_fingerprints gpg-imports (publish-side discipline absent i
- Spark refutation/limits: Remote forgery out (minisign covers Tier-A/B); hand-edited local run is already-operator. Window tiny; impact single-key availability with re-run healing. But in-file precedent (pin temp+backup+restore, publish PGP/gpg parse) proves owed discipline, and the file's own H-16 contract promises bad input fails with host untouched — garbage key violates it by mutating before failing.
- SMR defect: install_keyring truncates the file in place (install.sh:284-294), and validate checks only for the placeholder (271-280). cleanup_on_fail restores the channel pin byte-for-byte but has no keyring arm, and it deletes SRC outright (83-115); write_source keeps no backup (298-316). Re-runs are supported (pin rollback, 80-82; #11133). A failed re-run, for example a transient apt-get update failure (409-411), therefore leaves no xpf apt source at all (the update channel is silently lost) and an overwritten keyring, while the pin is restored. That is an inconsistent rollback against the H-16 contract (257-260).
- SMR locators: scripts/dist/install.sh:75-115,257-316,409-411,443-450; scripts/dist/publish.py:211-228,360-434
- SMR refutation/limits: For publishes that include apt, publish's key-agreement gpg import catches a corrupt-but-armoured key (publish.py:360-434). The interrupted-write window is tiny. The installer exits non-zero, and a successful re-run recovers.
- Next check: Bounded installer fixture: use a valid-armor/non-importable embedded key and a preexisting keyring; simulate apt-update failure and interruption during writing, then compare keyring bytes. Protect production host paths by fixture instrumentation; do not run the installer on a host.

## #12143 — postinst publish/cut failure exits 0 with no durable surfaced staged-vs-running skew state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### A89-028 <- P-10 (finder 313–314; ref 406–410)
- Codex defect: MATERIAL: a generic publish failure and non-lock cut failure log and continue to postinst exit 0, potentially leaving old running binaries without durable machine-readable staged-vs-running failure status. Existing best-effort `/run` marker covers only selected contention paths and is not consumed by the inspected Go/CLI status paths.
- Codex locators: debian/xpf.postinst:262-278 marks publish rc=2 but only logs generic rc; :306-318 skips cut if unpublished or intentionally staged.; debian/xpf.postinst:331-335 marks explicit contention; :347-361 marks failed cut only if lock remains busy; :394-396 exits 0.; pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:283-295 refuses an unpublished fresh generation; repository search found upgrade-deferred reads only in postinst/docs, not cmd/ or pkg/ status code.
- Codex refutation/limits: This is intentionally nonfatal to avoid half-configuring dpkg; logs give immediate operator recovery commands, and clustered stage-only and XPF_NO_POSTINST_CUT stage-only are intentional, not errors to flag indiscriminately. A local journal may be persistent depending on host configuration, so 'only transient journal evidence' is overstated. A failed cut attempts to restart an inactive xpfd (:363-379), protecting availability but not surfacing version skew.
- Spark defect: Non-lock publish failure (copy/ENOSPC/corrupt staged) and non-lock cut failure (verify/copy reject) log and exit 0 with no marker, while lock-busy arms drop write-only volatile markers. Dpkg/apt report success on old generation; no daemon health/upgrade status/deferred consumer surfaces skew (unlike rollback/journal degraded latches). Rolling operator proceeds on peer assumption never staged; only evidence is install-time journal line, discovered at next incident/audit. No external assumption needed — storage fault or verify-reject at apt time suffices.
- Spark locators:  if staged/xpfd publish-generation -> PUBLISH_OK=1 else rc=$?; if rc==2 marker+defer else log only (no marker);  if PUBLISH_OK!=1 skip cut (recover hint) # exits 0, dpkg success while old gen active;  cut-contention drops marker (331-335); cut failure drops only if lock still busy at recheck (356-359) — verify/copy fail;  grep upgrade-deferred: only debian/xpf.postinst + docs (Log/history/docs); no pkg/cmd/Python/shell consumer; /run tmpfs ;  publish failure does NOT fail configure (non-zero half-configures dpkg, worse than deferred cut) — exit 0 by design
- Spark refutation/limits: Journal/hints exist, and exit-0 avoids half-configured dpkg. But journal is neither durable-surfaced to status/health nor checked by rolling automation that keys on apt exit 0; manual version comparison is not a surface. Lock-busy markers prove project wants consistent recovery recording, yet generic arms omit it and all markers are write-only/volatile — internal inconsistency, not external misunderstanding.
- SMR defect: The generic publish-failure arm only logs (postinst:274-278). A cut failure drops the marker only if the lock is still busy (347-362), and the marker exists only in the lock-busy arms (267-273, 331-335). upgrade-deferred has no reader anywhere in pkg, cmd or scripts. No staged-versus-running surface exists for the binary channel; only the kernel channel has one (#6495). Exit 0 is deliberate (242-245). So apt and fleet tooling report a successful upgrade, possibly a security fix, while the node keeps the old generation. This includes a standalone verify-dataplane REJECT.
- SMR locators: debian/xpf.postinst:242-278,306-362; grep upgrade-deferred: only postinst and docs; pkg/daemon/kernel_upgrade_status.go (kernel only)
- SMR refutation/limits: Exiting 0 is a deliberate dpkg-safety choice. apt term.log keeps the stderr lines. `show version` reveals the old version. The next manual cut refuses or no-ops visibly (cutover.go:291-294).
- Next check: Inspect postinst's existing hermetic harness for generic publish rc=1 and verify-failed cut: identify staged/current and running versions after exit 0, and test a durable status consumer for skew. Exclude intentional cluster/manual stage-only from failure classification.

## #12144 — flat apt builder pools/signs any xpf-named deb with no identity binding, never prunes pool [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### A89-029 <- P-11 (finder 316–317; ref 412–416)
- Codex defect: MATERIAL on the default flat builder: it selects every matching dist-deb basename, adds rather than replaces pool content, and indexes the entire persistent suite pool. Thus a superseded or additional valid xpf .deb can remain in signed Packages after omission/removal from the selected input set; no current package-version/identity allowlist excludes a higher-version extra.
- Codex locators: scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh:90-105 selects `dist-deb/xpf_*.deb` and uses persistent pool; :193-207 only charset-checks, cp -f, then apt-ftparchive indexes all pool content.; scripts/dist/publish.py:875-906 extracts pooled debs for keyring presence and signer agreement, not Package/Version/Architecture or expected set.; scripts/image/bake.py:353-380 independently implements exact version binding for the image selection, but apt builder does not use it.
- Codex refutation/limits: Per-suite pools prevent cross-channel contamination (:96-104), signing is still authentic to the publisher, and gate_apt rejects uninspectable or placeholder-bearing debs (:875-903). A completely keyring-less extra passes only if another pooled package provides a valid keyring (:379-382). Deliberate older-version retention might be a desired repo policy, but then it needs an explicit manifest/retention contract rather than implying `--debs` is the entire released set. The optional reprepro branch has different retention semantics.
- Spark defect: Flat repo pools every dist-deb/xpf_*.deb by glob with no Package/Version/Arch binding or expected-set allowlist, cp -f into never-cleaned per-suite pool; Packages rescans pool so removals never unpublish. Gate extracts pooled debs but only keyring-carrying enter agreement; keyring-less (and even agreeing-keyring) extra at higher Version publishes under valid Release signature. Stale accumulation needs no malice (make deb only adds); planted high-Version needs dist-deb/pool writer (compromised leg/shared CI/stale artifact) and yields fleet-wide signed delivery via apt upgrade.
- Spark locators:  DEBS=$(ls ROOT/dist-deb/xpf_*.deb ROOT/dist-deb/xpf-appliance_*.deb ...) # all accumulated debs;  POOL=APT/pool/SUITE/COMPONENT/x/xpf; mkdir -p POOL DISTDIR # never pruned;  case d in charset; cp -f d POOL/ # pathname charset only, no dpkg-deb Package/Version/Arch, no allowlist;  (cd APT && apt-ftparchive packages pool/SUITE/COMPONENT > Packages) # rescans whole persistent pool;  for pooled .deb: extract; if keyring present check placeholder + collect; keyring-less ignored beyond extraction; _gate_;  select_xpf_deb binds filename+dpkg Version and refuses ambiguity/mismatch (bake discipline absent in apt path); make deb
- Spark refutation/limits: Old-version retention alone is weak (normal, not auto-installed). High-Version plant needs malicious writer. But stale-withdrawn retention arm needs no malice and is fixture-decisive, and no-identity-binding + never-cleaned + gate-blind-to-extras is source-conclusive inconsistency vs bake's binding — removals never unpublish is a correctness gap regardless of malice.
- SMR defect: By default DEBS globs every xpf deb in dist-deb (build-apt-repo.sh:90-93), although the comment says 'freshly built'. make deb only adds to dist-deb (Makefile:1563-1570), and make dist-repo uses the default (716-717). The pool persists and only grows (102-105, 193-200), and the whole suite pool is indexed (205-208). gate_apt does not bind Package/Version to the release (publish.py:811-906), unlike bake's select_xpf_deb. Stale builds are therefore signed, including a leftover deb from another branch whose higher commit-count version makes it the newest. A rebuild cannot withdraw a version.

## #12146 — snmp: v3 AES response IV can use a different engineTime than the carried USM value [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### A89-001 <- A9S-01 (finder 1025–1034; ref 1203–1206)
- Codex defect: AES encryption IV uses one integer engineTime, then the authenticated USM header independently reads engineTime. Crossing a one-second boundary between those reads yields an IV the receiver cannot reproduce from the wire; an otherwise valid response becomes undecryptable.
- Codex locators: pkg/snmp/v3.go:890-895,944-954,1137-1174; pkg/snmp/agent.go:671-673; RFC 3826 §3.1.2.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3826
- Codex refutation/limits: Boundary crossing is rare and DES uses a different IV scheme; neither point removes the deterministic AES mismatch.
- Spark defect: Two unpinned engineTime() reads per authPriv response (encrypt-then-stamp order) violate RFC 3826 IV-carried-time contract on 1s tick.
- Spark locators: pkg/snmp/v3.go:891 enc, err := encryptAES128(user.privKey, scopedPDU, salt, a.engineBoots, a.engineTime()); pkg/snmp/v3.go:951-954 binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(iv[0:4], uint32(boots)); binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(iv[4:8], uint32(time)); copy(iv[8:16], sa; pkg/snmp/v3.go:1141 vs 1168-1174 enc, pp, err := a.encryptPDU(user, scopedPDU) // :1141 ... usmFields = append(usmFields, berEncodeIntegerTLV(a.engineTim; pkg/snmp/agent.go:672-673 func (a *Agent) engineTime() int { return int(time.Since(a.startTime).Seconds()) }; pkg/snmp/v3.go:340 + decryptPDU:753 comment RFC 3826 3.1.2.1 decrypted := a.decryptPDU(user, privParams, encData, reqBoots, reqTime) // carried values
- Spark refutation/limits: No refutation of mechanism; only frequency/severity mitigation. Retries mask rare polls but stepping clock makes deterministic.
- SMR defect: buildV3Response encrypts first. Inside encryptPDU, v3.go:891 calls encryptAES128(..., a.engineBoots, a.engineTime()). It then reads the clock a second time for msgAuthoritativeEngineTime at v3.go:1171. engineTime() is int(time.Since(startTime).Seconds()) (agent.go:672-674), so a second boundary, a preemption or a GC pause between the two reads makes the carried time = IV time + 1. The receiver builds the IV from the carried boots/time (README:214-218). In CFB the wrong IV corrupts the first block, so the scopedPDU cannot be decoded and the response is lost. README:229-234 says the IV and header agree 'by construction'; the code does not do that.
- SMR locators: pkg/snmp/v3.go:891; pkg/snmp/v3.go:1140-1141; pkg/snmp/v3.go:1168-1174; pkg/snmp/agent.go:672-674; pkg/snmp/README.md:229-234
- SMR refutation/limits: The window is microseconds (encryptAES128 plus a few BER encodes), so it is rare, and a manager retry masks it. DES is unaffected (v3.go:882-889). The request decrypt path correctly uses the carried values (v3.go:340, 753). The HMAC covers the carried value consistently, so there is no security impact.
- Next check: Inject a clock that advances between encryption and USM construction; decrypt the emitted packet using only its carried boots/time/salt. Capture one time value per response.

## #12148 — flowexport: stableExporterID omits family, dual-family groups share SourceID/ODID [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-10)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### A89-008 <- A9S-08 (finder 1102–1111; ref 1240–1243)
- Codex defect: Resolver can instantiate two same-template, same-collector exporters split by family, each with its own v9 sequence but identical SourceID. RFC 3954 §5.1 says collectors SHOULD separate v9 streams using source IP plus Source ID, so independent UDP source ports do not disambiguate v9 when both use the same outbound source IP.
- Codex locators: pkg/flowexport/exporterid.go:44-56; pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:585-610,765-784; pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:788-801; pkg/flowexport/manager.go:455-458,507-534,602-616,667-680,1064-1074; pkg/flowexport/transport.go:194-207,219-263; pkg/flowexport/family_fanout_6811_test.go:198-220; RFC 3954 §5.1 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3954.txt; RFC 7011 §§2,3.1 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7011.txt
- Codex refutation/limits: The IPFIX half is materially different: RFC 7011 §§2,3.1 defines a UDP Transport Session by both endpoint IPs and ports and says collectors SHOULD use Transport Session plus ODID. Separate default UDP dials normally use distinct ephemeral ports [INFERENCE]; thus identical ODID does not, by itself, prove colliding IPFIX streams in a conforming collector. Different v9 source IPs/collectors also avoid the reported collision, and identical template definitions alone do not establish template-cache corruption.
- Spark defect: SourceID/ODID ignores address family; dual-family same-collector groups collide.
- Spark locators: pkg/flowexport/exporterid.go:44-57 func stableExporterID(protocol, instance, template string) uint32 // family absent from signature and hash; pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:794 sourceID := stableExporterID("ipfix", cfg.InstanceName, cfg.TemplateName); pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:595 sourceID: stableExporterID("netflow9", cfg.InstanceName, cfg.TemplateName); pkg/flowexport/manager.go:455-458 + 507-534 + ExportConfig.GroupIsV6 :88-97 set :606/:671 never read by constructors type collectorGroupKey struct { Template string; IsV6 bool } // grouping IS family-split; pkg/flowexport/manager.go:1064-1074 + dedupeCollectors:312-323 keeps both func collectorKey(c CollectorConfig) // family part of identity: sa
- Spark refutation/limits: No refutation of collision reachability; only severity bound and collector-display variance.
- SMR defect: stableExporterID hashes only protocol|instance|template (exporterid.go:44-57); its callers are ipfix.go:794 and netflow.go:595. Groups split by family (manager.go:446-458, 507-516, 606, 671). collectorKey keeps the same address configured under both families as two destinations (manager.go:1064-1073, 312-323). A dual-family instance with the same (or empty) template sending to one collector therefore gets two exporters with the same ID and independent sequence counters. For NetFlow v9, RFC 3954 §5.1 tells collectors to key on (source IP, Source ID), so they see interleaved sequences and false loss — the #3740 defect again (exporterid.go:13-22).
- SMR locators: pkg/flowexport/exporterid.go:13-22,44-57; pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:794; pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:595; pkg/flowexport/manager.go:312-323,446-458,507-516,1064-1073; RFC 3954 §5.1; RFC 7011 Transport Session
- SMR refutation/limits: For IPFIX over UDP, the RFC 7011 Transport Session includes UDP ports, and each exporter has its own socket (transport.go:121-122, 197-207), so RFC-compliant collectors keep the streams apart. Harmless when collectors differ by family. Template definitions are identical, so any template churn is benign.
- Next check: In a bounded two-family same-destination fixture, inspect v9 packets' actual source IP/SourceID and independent sequence streams, and separately the IPFIX transport four-tuples and collector key. A config-derived family suffix fixes v9 without a per-record hot-path cost; document any ID migration.

## #12149 — snmp: ifTable/ifXTable omit loopback lo and ifNumber undercounts it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-09)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### A89-009 <- A9S-09 (finder 1113–1122; ref 1245–1248)

- Codex locators: pkg/daemon/daemon_snmp_reconcile.go:356-427; pkg/snmp/agent.go:766-771,1792-1853; RFC 2863 IF-MIB https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2863
- Codex refutation/limits: Remaining rows and ifNumber agree internally; gaps in ifIndex are permitted. A deliberately limited appliance interface presentation could justify omitting host lo, and Linux lo is not automatically a Junos lo0 unit, but no inspected code comment or documented inventory contract establishes that exemption. If included, lo needs softwareLoopback ifType 24, not the ordinary ethernet default.
- Spark defect: ifTable/ifXTable silently omit loopback, ifNumber undercounts.
- Spark locators: pkg/daemon/daemon_snmp_reconcile.go:392-394 in buildSNMPIfData if attrs.Name == "lo" { continue } // no comment/doc at site; pkg/snmp/agent.go:1793-1795 via getOIDValueSnap if oidEqual(oid, oidIfNumber) { ifaces := snap.get(); return berEncodeIntegerValue(len(ifaces)) } // undercounts; pkg/daemon/daemon_snmp_reconcile.go:212 if attrs.Name == "lo" || attrs.Index <=0 { continue } // ethtool speed-only skip, harmless contrast

The skip has had no rationale since it was introduced (commit fb7aaae77). RFC 2863 defines ifNumber as 'the number of network interfaces ... present on this system', and Junos IF-MIB lists lo0 (softwareLoopback). So ifNumber undercounts and lo0 is missing from ifTable and ifXTable.

- SMR refutation/limits: Gaps in ifIndex are legal. Linux lo counters do not carry the meaning of Junos lo0 counters (traffic to the routing engine). No other table references ifIndex.

A short successful restart bounds the outage, and an operator transfer can recover it. The source separately exposes helper-crash status, so claiming every operator signal is healthy would be false. The cluster forwarding-consistency field compares applied rg_active/VRRP against ownership, not live helper forwarding, so it can nonetheless say consistent while th
- Spark defect: On active helper death the daemon predicate stays true (armed latched + xpfd-owned XDP count unchanged), so reassertTransitGate keeps kernel gate open and applies no __dataplane-arm__ debt; weight stays 255. Crash path only makes TakeoverReady false -> SetRGReady(false), which blocks future promotions and never demotes the incumbent. Non-preempt incumbent stays primary by rule; preempt tie at 255 stays by nodeID. Marking the RG not-ready only blocks new promotions; it never demotes the current primary (election.go:407-412; readiness.go:56-141). The crash-loop state is only shown in status output (fwdstatus/builder.go:245-255).

- Codex refutation/limits: The standby is NOT immediately ready: reset clears its status and XSK proof, and a real helper must first bind, arm and meet readiness gates; standby-ready bindings can alternatively waive the traffic-derived XSK proof. A specific in-flight per-session request may be restamped/retried after generation churn. The Go/kernel BPF conntrack mirror can retain synced rows across restart, but the production userspace bulk path treats Rust session-table export—not that display mirror—as authoritative; retaining a row is not proof it was restored to Rust. Snapshot/HA-group re-publication and same-proces
- Spark defect: Helper-only replacement starts with empty process-local session/NAT tables; in-process replay hooks cannot cross the process boundary and no BPF/state-file/pull restore exists. Go clears HA inventory/liveness but replays no session table; per-session installs are forward-only deltas with no bulk owner. TakeoverReady lacks any synced-inventory-for-generation term (overflow and HA-inventory gates cover other debts), so gen2 becomes ready once XSK/bindings/listener pass with zero old sessions. Daemon bulk-primed and xpfd-to-xpfd sync stay connected, so no cold-prime/fence bulk fires and peer sends only future deltas; FullResync exports local owner sessions outward and is empty on standby. Failover before age-out then misses long-lived flows. Active-side twin: reset NAT cursor reissues ghost-held tuples the peer refuses (RejectedReserve).
- Spark refutation/limits: Strongest alternative is narrow gating, not inventory healing: overflow, HA-membership, XSK/bindings, snapshot-debt and listener gates all pass on a restarted helper with zero sessions (by design they cover other debts). No Go BPF-mirror pull, no Rust BPF/state-file restore, and no peer bulk on helper-only restart was found; incremental deltas cannot backfill long-lived flows. Refutation would need a replay owner or generation-keyed readiness term covering the same standby-restart state — none exists. Remaining uncertainty is impact magnitude (age-out window, re-adjudication vs drop per flow) and ghost-path end-to-end proof, not the empty-with-ready core.
- SMR defect: When the helper goes away, the manager resets its helper state and replays no sessions (process.go:676-726). The only replay it has is for HA state (manager_ha.go:188-212). The Rust replay hooks read the in-process shared map (bringup.rs:549-659), which a new process does not have. Takeover readiness has no check for the session inventory (manager_ha.go:404-465). The node-to-node sync connection is untouched, so no fresh bulk is sent, and sessions are not resent otherwise (see D0HA-001).
- SMR locators: pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go:668-726; pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:188-212,404-465,538-547; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/bringup.rs:549-659; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/session_import.rs:1108-1119

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

The gate can subsequently discard the candidate, remove its journal/lease/marker, and continue without rebooting. The ordinary hold's periodic reconcile checks only whether the promotion marker equals the running kernel; its journal-clean self-heal applies solely to the separate unreadable-journal hold. Thus, if daemon-first ordering occurs, a healthy, undrained node remains ineligible even after a discarded outcome; peer failure cannot promote it.

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low.

### C-054 <- D11-03
- Codex refutation/limits: If /dev/watchdog is absent, exclusive-owned, or the driver's ordinary-close semantics stop it, this exact hardware consequence does not occur. The retained fake models arm/disarm calls, not Linux driver behavior, kernel configuration or eventual reset; a strict-mode SETTIMEOUT failure is a different, unexecuted subcase. BootNext-clear failures would add a separate NVRAM hazard, not explain away the missing watchdog cleanup.
- Spark refutation/limits: Unreachable without a present /dev/watchdog with the assumed magic-close/nowayout semantics and not owned by systemd RuntimeWatchdogSec; VMs and systemd-owned hosts cannot arm. Driver close semantics and the strict SETTIMEOUT hypothesis are untested, the probe uses a fake watchdog without hardware reset timing, and a coincident ClearBootNext failure would be needed for a candidate-side reset.
- SMR defect: ArmWatchdog runs before the fallible steps and closes without the magic 'V' (kernel_linux.go:488-519; kernel_run.go:331). Failure returns at 375-377, 379-386 and 392-416 never call DisarmWatchdog; disarmAfterArmFailure clears BootNext only (453-461). No product RuntimeWatchdogSec exists. With magic-close drivers the box resets about one timeout later.

Each post-acquisition failure exits without DisarmWatchdog: the shared `disarmAfterArmFailure` only deletes BootNext. A failed Reboot likewise returns from Arm with the watchdog still acquired/armed. The real ArmWatchdog writes keepalive and merely closes its fd; unlike the product's explicit DisarmWatchdog, it does not write magic `V`. But non-preempt election keeps an incumbent unless weight <= 0 (election.go:146-160, 267-290). Helper death is not itself evidence of this debt: transit_gate_tick_9725.go:52-53 depends on armed/XDP-link count, not helper liveness. No observed appliance outage was supplied.

Loss scope is trigger-dependent

The 'dataplane not ready' debt lowers the weight only to 1, and the comment that 'a ready peer at 255 outbids this node at 1' is true only for preempt RGs (election.go:745-764; daemon_transit_gate.go:286-326). The canonical config does not enable preempt (docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:75-96).

## #12165 — Heartbeat suppression cap never re-armed; second gap promotes secondary [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-09)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### C-029 <- D5-06
- Codex refutation/limits: A sync disconnect or more than two seconds of sync silence resets the stamp; normal restart gaps might be shorter than a heartbeat timeout. The retained result demonstrates manager behavior under imposed gaps, not their field frequency.
- Spark refutation/limits: Stamp clears if sync also drops or goes quiet >2s; post-guard freshness recheck helps when heartbeats arrive; restart grace protects the restarting node. Real restart gap lengths unmeasured; probe gaps are synthetic (2.5s) with netns UDP.
- SMR defect: hbSuppressStart is reset only on sync connect, disconnect or silence (daemon_ha_sync.go:66, 175, 180), not when heartbeats recover. A later heartbeat-only gap on the same connection finds the cap already consumed, which violates the 'continuous suppression' intent (comment at :184-188).
- SMR locators: pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:54-66,170-215
- SMR refutation/limits: The stamp clears if sync also drops. The real restart gap length is unmeasured.
- Next check: Trace the stamp through normal heartbeat admission/restart and examine existing production gap durations; a bounded repeat-gap fixture should assert election states rather than relying on the rounded sentinel timing log.

### U-018 <- D5-06
- Codex refutation/limits: A renewed sync connection or a sync outage/quiet period clears the stamp, and heartbeat_manager.go:824-826 prevents demotion when a heartbeat returned during the guard. An ordinary clean rebind may be much shorter than 500 ms, so production exposure depends on a distinct long second outage. The retained probe uses synthetic LastPeerReceiveAge, stops both A heartbeat roles, contains no production traffic or real bind failure, and its PASS does not quantify field incidence.
- Spark refutation/limits: Trigger needs a narrow shape: sync stays connected AND fresh (<2s peer-receive age) across both gaps (any sync drop/quiet re-arms at :175/:180), first gap ends by heartbeat recovery (not sync loss), second gap >500ms occurs >5s after the first stamp on the same connection. Clean RestartHeartbeat rebind is milliseconds (docs/bug-heartbeat-vrf-rebind-split-brain.md:52-59 verification), so production gaps may rarely exceed 500ms unless a bind retry fails (1s each, heartbeatRestartRetryDelay, heartbeat_manager.go:371-383, up to ~5s) or networkd stripped em0 from VRF. Outcome is a single-primary fl
- SMR defect: The suppression start time is cleared only on a new sync connection, a sync disconnect, or sync silence (daemon_ha_sync.go:66, 175, 180). Heartbeat recovery does not clear it. A later heartbeat-only gap therefore starts with the 5s cap already used up, is not suppressed, and the peer takes over.
- SMR locators: pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:54-66,170-215
- SMR refutation/limits: The second gap still has to exceed the heartbeat threshold.
- Next check: Drive two heartbeat-only interruptions separated by recovery across an actual connected session-sync lifecycle and a bounded failed RestartHeartbeat bind retry; verify whether the second interval is independently capped, whether node A continues forwarding, and the duration of any two-owner period. This measures operational frequency, not the already established missing reset.

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

- Codex refutation/limits: Persisted deadlines are explicitly wall-clock based and arm provenance is diagnostic, not a durable monotonic clock; elapsed real time across power loss cannot be reconstructed exactly without a trusted source. - Spark refutation/limits: Forward steps fail safe (immediate rollback); the cited contract bars permanence, not delay, and rollback still eventually fires; ArmedAt-as-diagnostic is documented. Cluster branch behavior (possibly over-eager rollback without NTP) was read, not run.
- SMR defect: remaining = deadline.Sub(now) has no clamp (store_persist.go:911). The skew alarm is cluster-only; standalone returns false (daemon_clockskew.go:46-51, 97-101). A clock behind ArmedAt re-arms for more than the original window, and the monotonic AfterFunc keeps that after NTP corrects the clock.
- SMR locators: pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:789-811,905-943; pkg/daemon/daemon_clockskew.go:36-51,94-114; pkg/configstore/README.md:837-866
- SMR refutation/limits: Forward steps fail safe. The README calls ArmedAt and bootid diagnostic only (configstore README:860-866).
- Next check: Clarify the confirmed-commit rollback invariant when reboot time is untrustworthy and inspect a bounded persisted-record/boot-clock scenario for a safe failure policy; the current wall-clock calculation demonstrably cannot preserve a 10-minute maximum.

### D0HA-005 <- D9-04
- Codex defect: Recovery uses the persisted wall deadline, and a standalone configuration makes the skew callback return false. A backward step before Load therefore yields an arbitrarily enlarged deadline-now timer despite the original short confirm window; arm-time and boot-ID provenance are not used to cap it.

- SMR locators: pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:1170-1176,1255-1288,1520-1563; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:22-66; pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go:210-233,404-494; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:436-490; pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:451-456
- SMR refutation/limits: Requires a boot apply that fails before the VRF step, on an HA node that has a management VRF.

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

- Codex refutation/limits: A primary self-election before reconcile preserves the window, and an actual peer takeover should confirm on demotion by design. Clock-skew recovery can roll back first; the retained probe drives production reconcile directly rather than a complete live daemon boot with all scheduling conditions.

Store clusterReadOnly starts false and is set only in applyRG0OwnershipTransition (daemon_ha.go:936, 974). reconcileRGState calls reconcileRG0ConfigOwnership first on every 2 s pass (daemon_ha.go:1207-1215). The mismatch drives applyRG0OwnershipTransition(Secondary), which calls ConfirmPendingOnDemotion unconditionally (daemon_ha.go:963-975; store_commit.go:1121-1134). A window recovered at Load is therefore confirmed even when no peer took over.
- SMR locators: pkg/cluster/group_state.go:28-45; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:883-914,932-976,1207-1215; pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:1110-1134; pkg/configstore/store.go:384,596; pkg/daemon/daemon_clockskew.go:97-114

- Next check: Bounded integrated Run boot with configured cluster and NTP, recovered pending record, no peer, and controlled election/reconcile scheduling; compare initial Secondary, self-elected Primary, and genuine peer-takeover branches.

A different target takes the stale-STOPPED recovery branch (cutover.go:383-414); a resume after FLIP boots the new path; a still-stopped unit starts the target successfully in the control. `debian/xpf.postinst:374-377` can restart a stopped unit after a failed cut, but is not a boot-time journal resume or a guard against the described active-unit state.
- Spark refutation/limits: Requires a crash in a sub-second window plus an out-of-band restart plus a same-version rerun; in-band Restart=on-failure does not fire on a clean stop, and the postinst restart fires only when the unit is inactive after a failed cut. Health is wired fail-closed (NewSystemWithHelperHealth), so the outcome is a revert, never a commit of the wrong binary. A deliberately restaged running version can clear the stale journal via superseded-cut recovery plus a distinct refusal (cutover.go:331-414,472-505), and snapshot compatibility is checked separately by rollback.go:192-212. Those facts limit reachability and offer recovery, but do not make the initially refused STAGED journal an active destructive cut or provide a direct rollback path.
- Spark refutation/limits: No traffic outage; recovery exists via manual journal removal or the accidental same-version verify-fail rewind, and existing tests pass on unit-not-stopped. The stamp-demotion variant needs a min-reader rise between gates or a resume plus tag reuse, making it rare, while the main STAGED wedge needs an envelope-gated downgrade.
- SMR defect: The journal is transitioned to STAGED (cutover.go:539) before preflight's envelope gate (916-920). The refusal leaves an in-flight journal, a rerun re-refuses, and rollback refuses any non-INIT state (rollback.go:107-110). REFUSE-AT-INIT is applied only to the no-target case (cutover.go:448-470).
- SMR locators: pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:448-470,536-541,869-920; pkg/upgrade/rollback.go:88-112

## #12179 — Per-source session quota bypass via uncounted missing-neighbor/fabric seeds [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### DSM-024 <- SHORT[C1 | finder 2323-2324 | ref 2409-2412] // DEEP[C1 | finder 2323–2324 | ref 2409–2412]
- Codex defect: A new-flow source-quota check reads only counted sessions; MissingNeighborSeed and FabricPuntSeed consume table slots without increasing that count. In the missing-neighbor arm, installation and BPF/shared publication precede pending-neighbor duplicate/capacity rejection. Consequently even different tuples to the SAME unresolved next hop can leave uncounted seeds when their frames are immediately recycled; a single permitted source can pass a limit of 10 more than 10 times and ultimately exhaust its worker's finite table.
- Codex locators: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_admission.rs:39-45; userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:38-45,267-270,422-439; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3508-3559,9049-9058,9086-9119,9149-9174,9199-9225,9280-9315,9407-9421; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neg_neigh.rs:80-90,138-160; userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:3501-3510
- Codex refutation/limits: A seed represents unresolved delivery rather than a fully forwarded session, a table-wide hard cap still rejects inserts, and later promotion balances counted origin transitions. Negative neighbor caching eventually fast-fails a timed-out next hop; none of these enforce the per-source quota during the initial pending interval.
- Spark defect: One source can install MissingNeighborSeed/FabricPuntSeed sessions that never increment the per-source count, so the (zone,worker) quota (default 4096) never trips for seeds. Distinct on-link dst/port tuples (or NAT-free FabricRedirect punts) each install a worker-table entry (slot, wheel, shared/BPF publishes) until protocol timeout, up to max_sessions (131072/worker), starving legitimate new flows. Packet's 'promotion transitions accounting' is unsupported — no seed promotion path exists, so seeds stay uncounted for life (worse than stated, but no double-count risk).
- Spark refutation/limits: Seeds cannot exceed the worker table cap; fabric seeds need a sustained RG split plus permit; repeats per hop are coalesced/fast-failed. The quota bypass is scoped to seeds, not counted ForwardFlow/LocalMiss (which the 3551 check dominates per its own comment).
- SMR defect: Seeds are excluded from limit-session counting, and the per-source check reads only counted sessions. Each policy-permitted new flow to an unresolved on-link destination installs a MissingNeighborSeed before pending-neighbor admission, and the seed survives a CapacityDrop or DuplicateDrop. It lives for the protocol timeout (UDP 60 s, TCP opening 20 s) and publishes BPF conntrack and shared rows. One source can therefore exceed the default 4096/zone/worker quota up to the worker cap (131072). The negative cache only throttles repeated next hops (TTL 3 s, cap 256), and IPv6 /64 on-link space makes distinct destinations free.
- SMR locators: userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:30-45,267-270; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_admission.rs:29-46; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3546-3561,9047-9056,9172-9195,9302-9420; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neg_neigh.rs:1-35; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs:554,572,590,612; userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:190-224,3501-3509
- SMR refutation/limits: Promotion accounting is correct (no double count). The flow must be policy-permitted toward unresolved on-link addresses, and the worker cap still bounds the table.
- Next check: In a bounded source-controlled fixture with quota 10, admit 11 distinct 5-tuples to one pending unresolved hop; inspect live seed count, source count, duplicate-buffer drops, and an optional subsequent seed promotion. Confirm count rises exactly once on promotion, without executing this check during this review.

## #12182 — Auth-throttle pressure evicts live lockouts; /64 refill forgives brute-force [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium.

### DSM-056 <- SHORT[N-14 | finder 1982-1983 | ref 2067-2069] // DEEP[N-11 | finder 1973–1974 | ref 2053–2055]
- Codex defect: At 4096 buckets, eviction's second phase disregards lockedUntil and can remove a live completed lockout. Account-pair buckets are scanned *first*, so an active per-pair lockout is straightforwardly evictable under serial table pressure; when the account category offers no evictable entries, global and source locks also become candidates. This violates the lockout-preservation invariant.
- Codex locators: pkg/api/auth_throttle_10825.go:57-77,174-246,345-390,526-583; pkg/api/auth.go:249-263; pkg/daemon/daemon_run_servers.go:509-545
- Codex refutation/limits: The packet's approximately 1365 completed attempts do *not* establish renewed guesses against a locked Basic username: the global Basic threshold is also five and its bucket generally survives because account buckets are evicted first; the source bucket is scanned last. Global/source loss under pressure needs the account buckets unavailable, e.g. in-flight work, and its practical cost is unmeasured. Go map order is arbitrary *within* each category, not across categories; expired-first sweep and inFlight protection are real safeguards.
- Spark defect: Strongest defect reading: makeRoomLocked phase two (auth_throttle_10825.go:354-363) deletes ANY authThrottleBucketEvictable bucket — and evictable (:381-391) excludes only inFlight/protected, NOT lockedUntil-future buckets; the expired-first sweep (:371-379) requires quiet+expired so ACTIVE lockouts survive it, only to die in the random phase; reserve() calls makeRoomLocked BEFORE inserting the new triple (:206-219), so each fresh-source failure (IPv6 /64 key at :563-582, three buckets per Basic attempt) can evict a victim's live account/global/source lockout; global-Basic bucket shares the same pool; attacker repeats ~1365 cheap failures to refill at will — probabilistic per round, attacker-controlled across rounds.
- Spark locators: auth_throttle_10825.go:381-391 evictable ignores lockedUntil; :354-363 random-phase delete; :371-379 sweep spares active lockouts (quietSince=lockedUntil at :393-401); reserve() :178-219 lockout check → makeRoomLocked → insert: eviction precedes the new buckets; normalizeAuthThrottleSource :563-582 /64 keying enables distinct-source refill; header comment :34-37 documents fail-open without addressing lockout loss; sweepIfFullLocked :493-511 same evictable predicate on the legacy path
- Spark refutation/limits: Requires api-auth enabled on a reachable non-loopback REST listener plus attacker IPv6 /64 rotation — loopback-nil-auth path never consults the tracker (:39-43); per-round eviction is probabilistic Go-map order, so a single fill may miss the victim; no live test demonstrates end-to-end lockout forgiveness; the bound itself (4096) is a deliberate anti-OOM doctrine. None of these change the code fact that active lockouts are evictable — they bound its reachability, not its existence.
- SMR defect: The makeRoomLocked phase-2 loop deletes any authThrottleBucketEvictable bucket. Evictability checks only inFlight and protected status, while the expired-only lockedUntil condition exists only in the sweep. Pressure from rotated /64 sources can therefore evict live account, global-Basic and source lockouts.
- SMR locators: pkg/api/auth_throttle_10825.go:89-98,347-388
- SMR refutation/limits: Victim loss is probabilistic, which the attacker overcomes by refilling. Requires api-auth on a reachable non-loopback listener.
- Next check: A fake-clock reservation fixture should first show which live lockout evicts under serial distinct identities; then hold other account reservations in-flight to test global/source protection separately. A full table of live locked buckets should refuse new admission without erasing their Retry-After.

The FRR export skips them (qnh_metric_11447.go:99-101). The explicit IPv4-disabled arm correctly protects family-less IPv6 peers and IPv4 inet6-only peers; it does not match this one.
- Spark refutation/limits: Mirror case (IPv4+inet6-only) is handled via the disabled arm, and validNeighbors excludes remote-as-0/malformed so the section still loads; group-inherited cross-family is fenced by #2454. - SMR defect: Confirmed. The per-neighbor family path sets FamilyInet with no address-family gating (compiler_bgp_neighbor_merge_9192.go:199-245; group inheritance is gated at compiler_protocols.go:607-614). Classification (protocols_render.go:639-658) puts the peer in none of inet4, inet4Disabled or inet6, so no activate, no deactivate, no route-maps and no prefix-limit are rendered. FRR's default `bgp default ipv4-unicast` activates IPv6-addressed neighbors in IPv4 unicast (docs.frrouting.org stable-8.1 bgp.html). An iBGP peer then exchanges IPv4 routes with no import or export policy.

- SMR refutation/limits: For eBGP, FRR's default `bgp ebgp-requires-policy` (on in the traditional profile since 7.4) blocks all prefixes, so the effect is a route-less AF, not a leak. No strict gate rejecting this shape was found.
- Next check: Render an IPv6-address peer explicitly configured only for inet with import/export and validate the actual FRR 10.6 accepted config and AF operational state; determine whether FRR ever default-activates this peer before alleging unfiltered exchange. A strict-commit diagnostic/control for family-less IPv6 would distinguish intended unsupported syntax.

The packet's proposed `--skip-validate` seal-mode publish fixture is invalid: bake.py:909-917 returns validated=false and publish.py:672-679 rejects it.

Fleet ships signed image whose xpf keyring cannot verify repo: every imaged host apt upgrade fails until fixed package via another channel; install.sh vs image trust diverges.

- Spark refutation/limits: Combined publish from same checkout is protected via pooled-deb check, and placeholder fails closed (no bad package installed). Preconditions narrow likelihood, and recovery via image-roll exists. But image-only is a supported mode, drop-in is manual/silent, and no code binds pooled keyring to in-image keyring — the image-side hole survives the partial guard.

Images configure no xpf apt source; install.sh writes the source (install.sh:75-77, 298-316). install.sh overwrites the keyring with its own embedded key before use (284-294). apt fails closed (debian/rules:130-131). The impact needs four conditions at once. This is a real gap in an existing protection, reached through another delivery path.

## #12189 — Fragment-overlap shard index unseeded; precomputable FNV allows targeted ShardFull [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-11)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### DSM-027 <- SHORT[C4 | finder 2332-2333 | ref 2424-2427] // DEEP[C4 | finder 2332–2333 | ref 2424–2427]
- Codex defect: Overlap tracking picks one of 16 shared shards using fixed, externally computable FNV-1a over family/source/destination/fragment ID. In one routing domain, four permitted source addresses can each hold eight distinct incomplete datagram anchors in the target shard, reaching its 32-entry domain cap; further unrelated first fragments in that domain/shard fail closed as ShardFull. The keyed association-shard hash does not protect this distinct overlap index.
- Codex locators: userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs:110-119,201-224,645-650,708-733; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:7023-7050; userspace-dp/src/fragment_assoc/mod.rs:432-450; userspace-dp/src/hot_path_hash_seed.rs:127-142; userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs:1943-2042
- Codex refutation/limits: Fragments must already pass policy and source-address restrictions; one sender is limited to eight, other routing domains retain half-shard headroom, old anchors expire after 30 seconds idle or 60 seconds absolute, and the result is availability loss only, never overlap admission or policy bypass. Shared-lock costs are unmeasured.
- Spark defect: Offline-precomputable shard placement lets an attacker with >=4 sender IPs in one routing domain (8/shard each) fill the 32-entry domain quota of a chosen shard with ~32 fragments, fail-closing legitimate fragments in that domain/shard for as long as colliders are refreshed per 30s TTL. Seeding raises targeted-attack cost ~16x and matches the assoc precedent.
- Spark refutation/limits: Impact is a narrow availability-only collateral DoS (one shard/domain, fragments-only, needs multiple sources + policy permit + sustained refresh), with fail-closed direction retained.
- SMR defect: An offline-computable FNV-1a hash with no boot seed (fragment-assoc is seeded) allows targeted exhaustion of one shard and domain, with fail-closed ShardFull.
- SMR locators: userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs:110-121,198-224,715-733; userspace-dp/src/fragment_assoc/mod.rs:431-450; userspace-dp/src/hot_hash_seed.rs:127-143
- SMR refutation/limits: The marginal value is low: whole-domain exhaustion across all 16 shards needs only about 512 entries per 30 s without precomputation (lead L4), and the per-sender cap of 8 still requires at least 4 permitted sources in both cases.
- Next check: Use a bounded deterministic collision fixture to show four allowed sources' keys exhaust one domain's shard and drop a legitimate distinct key. A candidate seeded index must keep all fragments of the same datagram co-located and retain the domain/sender fairness invariants; none was run here.

## #12192 — Session replication fans out to dead workers; refusal counted as generic drops [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### W4A1-029 <- a1-worker-queues (finder A1-15; re-exam L229; L268)
- Codex defect: Peer-worker slices carry bare queue Arcs and remain captured by surviving workers; each new-flow replica is cloned and pushed toward a dead consumer until the 4096 cap, after which refusals count as generic queue drops rather than dead-worker sheds. This is ongoing per-replication wasted work and misleading failure attribution, distinct from live-queue contention.
- Codex locators: worker_queue.rs:59-81,95-105: dead records persist, slice producers can feed dead queues, bound 4096, and SHED versus DROPS have different operational meanings.; coordinator/reconcile/bringup.rs:863-868 and session_glue/mod.rs:2197-2223: survivor captures peer bare handles; replication clones and ignores `push_bounded` refusal.; coordinator/worker_manager.rs:46-70 and worker_queue.rs:784-793: record-keyed producers use `shed_if_dead`; bare-handle bounded refusal increments generic DROPS.
- Codex refutation/limits: Records are intentionally retained, queues are bounded, and the comments expressly say bare-handle slice producers do not implement dead checks. The source does not measure clone cost or prove an additional forwarding failure beyond the worker's already-reported death; per-call `SESSION_REPLICATION_ENQUEUED` counts attempts, not accepted delivery.
- Spark defect: Slice-based upsert replication fans out over bare queue handles with no dead check, cloning per queue and ignoring push_bounded refusal. After a worker death (record retained, #925) the dead queue fills to 4096 and later drops use the generic DROPS counter rather than SHED_TOTAL — exactly the folding the SHED doc forbids — with wasted hot-path clone per flow and no dead-vs-overload signal. The delete path already resolves IDs via Arc identity (worker_id_for_command_queue) for repair.
- Spark refutation/limits: Bare-handle pushes to dead workers are explicitly documented as accepted and bounded (4096 cap, never unbounded), and dead workers are rare (panic/supervisor path). Slice shape avoids per-packet record lookup on the hot new-flow path; associating each queue with worker identity (BTreeMap scan with Arc::ptr_eq per queue per flow) has its own cost. Remaining questions narrow to accounting precision and unmeasured clone waste, not unbounded growth.
- SMR defect: replicate_session_upsert uses bare handles with no dead check and ignores the push_bounded result (session_glue/mod.rs:2196-2223). Once a dead worker's queue fills (4096, held forever), each new flow increments the generic WORKER_COMMAND_QUEUE_DROPS (worker_queue.rs:784-794). That is exactly the misreport the SHED counter exists to prevent ('opposite remediations', worker_queue.rs:95-105). Record-keyed producers do shed (ha/state.rs:89-91; ha/session_import.rs:1330; EXECUTED record_keyed_fan_out_sheds_dead_workers_9900).
- SMR refutation/limits: The bare-handle push is documented and bounded (worker_queue.rs:70-75). It arises only after a worker panic, which is already flagged. The per-flow wasted clone and lock is negligible.
- Next check: Under a marked-dead sibling with surviving peer new-flow traffic, verify continued dead-target attempts, generic-versus-shed deltas and actual clone cost. Design identity-aware shedding with safe worker-ID reuse/retirement semantics; do not infer live-throughput improvement without measurement.

## #12193 — RA PIO valid/preferred lifetimes unclamped; 2^32 wraps to 0 on tolerant ingress [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### W4A567-007 <- C07 (finder 533-542; ref 649-652)
- Codex refutation/limits: A fresh strict commit is rejected. The packet overstates 'instant invalidation' for all existing hosts: host lifetime safety rules and RA header/default-router state are distinct; this does not make the unclamped tolerant PIO sink correct.
- Spark refutation/limits: Strict commit correctly gated; only stale pre-bound/hand-edited/older-peer configs reach tolerant path (narrow). Warning emitted at load; next commit fixes. Display-vs-wire mismatch requires ignoring warning. Window bounded to boot/HA-sync of stale config. Fix (saturate [0,0xFFFFFFFF] at sink after default substitution + pref clamp, or sanitize on lenient compile with per-prefix warning) is safe, monotone, in-range byte-identical, mirroring header clamp.
- SMR defect: PIO lifetimes reach ndp without a sink clamp: ValidLifetime is time.Duration(validLife)*time.Second (sender.go:946-953), and ndp writes uint32(valid.Seconds()) (ndp option.go:212-216). The strict bound exists only at commit (schema_routing.go:727-732). The repo says tolerant Load and peer-sync downgrade typed-leaf violations (schema_routing.go:308-311; sender.go:832-836). The compiler stores bare Atoi values (compiler_protocols.go:1143-1154). The header, MTU and VRRP sinks are all clamped under the same doctrine (sender.go:859-865, 999-1001, 1177-1218); PIO is the outlier. A value of exactly 2^32 (or 2^32+k) yields 0 (or k) on amd64 [INFERENCE: implementation-dependent float→uint32].
- SMR locators: pkg/ra/sender.go:893-953, 832-866, 1177-1218; ~/go/pkg/mod/github.com/mdlayher/ndp@v1.1.0/option.go:212-216; pkg/config/schema_routing.go:308-318, 727-732; pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:1143-1154
- SMR refutation/limits: Reachability is narrow. It needs a persisted or peer config carrying a value above 0xFFFFFFFF, for example from a pre-#3895 build, and most such values wrap to a large harmless lifetime. DHCPv6-PD-derived lifetimes cannot exceed uint32 (daemon_ra.go:46-50). RFC 4862 §5.5.3(e) keeps the remaining lifetime of existing SLAAC addresses at a 2-hour floor. However, RFC 4861 §6.3.4 times out the on-link prefix immediately at 0.
- Next check: In an isolated buildRA/ndp marshal-decode fixture, pass tolerant positive valid/preferred values 4294967296 and larger values that overflow Duration, plus 4294967295 and ordinary defaults. Check the exact PIO wire seconds and consistency of preferred<=valid; retain existing <=0-as-default semantics.

## #12194 — VLAN-alias binding rows lack pre-multiply ifindex guard; large child wraps slot [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### W4A567-018 <- LOCAL-a6-pos-01-ref1 (finder 701; ref 736-737)
- Codex defect: The alias loop lacks the primary row's pre-multiply ifindex bound. A live child ifindex of 2^28+17 with queue zero wraps its uint32 binding index to the valid primary row for ifindex 17 and can replace that row's XSK binding. Child indices are refreshed without this upper bound. An unrelated low-ifindex interface can then suffer binding/redirect failure.
- Codex locators: pkg/dataplane/userspace/helper_status_apply.go:503-519 primary bindingIfindexInRange precedes multiplication; :588-631 alias checks queue/slot but not child ifindex before multiplication, then UpdateAny.; pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1718-1735 mints child key without maximum; userspace-xdp/src/binding_index.rs:247-259 checked_mul prevents high-index packet-side wrap.
- Codex refutation/limits: This requires extraordinary kernel ifindex churn; ordinary out-of-range children fail the post-multiply cap. The specific packet example 2^28 maps to slot zero, and the shim uses checked_mul on incoming ifindex: it does not redirect that high-index child's packets via a wrapped row. Wrong-socket XSK redirect is expected to fail, not prove cross-interface delivery.
- SMR defect: Confirmed parity gap. Primary rows check bindingIfindexInRange before the multiply (helper_status_apply.go:509-519). The alias loop computes childIfindex*16+queue with only the post-multiply cap (helper_status_apply.go:607-616). An alias child at 2^28 would wrap into slot space. The #9698 helper documents exactly this wrap (binding_index_bounds_9698.go:13-29).
- SMR locators: pkg/dataplane/userspace/helper_status_apply.go:494-530, 588-616; pkg/dataplane/userspace/binding_index_bounds_9698.go:13-29; pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1708-1737
- SMR refutation/limits: Alias children come from the Go snapshot's kernel ifindex, not helper input, and LogicalOnly synthetic rows are excluded (maps_sync.go:1708-1737, esp. :1718). Linux allocates ifindex sequentially, so the wrap needs ≥2^28 interface creations in the netns. The reachable out-of-range band (65536 ≤ ifindex < 2^28) already fails closed loudly via the #814 cap (helper_status_apply.go:611-616). MaxInterfaces is 65536 and the stride 16 (pkg/dataplane/constants_test.go:21-29).
- Next check: A bounded fake-map fixture with a valid low-ifindex primary and child ifindex 268435473: assert alias does not overwrite the primary, failure disables forwarding as required, and the 268435456/slot-zero control does not falsely claim packet-side steering. Do not require zero total map writes: primaries precede aliases.

## #12195 — update_neighbors skips persisted snapshot fold; state file keeps stale neighbors [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### W4A567-025 <- LOCAL-a6-pos-08-ref8 (finder 715; ref 757-758)
- Codex defect: A successful incremental neighbor replace updates coordinator forwarding and clears digest, but never folds accepted neighbors into guard.snapshot.neighbors. Subsequent periodic/status or other persist serializes the old neighbor set as current state; the documented state-file show surface therefore can misreport its neighbor snapshot indefinitely until a full apply.
- Codex locators: userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/neighbors.rs:49-68 omits snapshot.neighbors write; userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/mod.rs:436-456 folds changed fabrics but not neighbors; :360-368 periodically requests state persistence.; userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/persistence.rs:57-63 persists the stored snapshot; docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md:566-585 describes the state file as the Go show/observability snapshot, not a restore source.
- Codex refutation/limits: Coordinator forwarding is authoritative, Go caches accepted neighbors, and helper restart does not restore from the state file; there is no demonstrated packet loss or failed restart. Persisting on every unchanged update is unnecessary and can add I/O; distinguish changed folds from unconditional writes.
- SMR defect: update_neighbors clears content_digest without writing snapshot.neighbors or setting persist_state (neighbors.rs:61-67). update_fabrics folds, clears the digest and persists (handlers/mod.rs:436-446, #3773). The state payload serializes status plus snapshot (persistence.rs:25-63), so a later unrelated write persists apply-time neighbors.
- SMR locators: userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/neighbors.rs:49-68; userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/mod.rs:400-456; userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/persistence.rs:25-110
- SMR refutation/limits: Forwarding is unaffected: the coordinator tables are authoritative, and the helper never restores from state.json; restart continuity is owned by Go (handlers/mod.rs:429-435). There is no in-tree reader of the helper state file. Go reads status over the control socket, and a grep finds no Go reads of the state JSON, so the effect is limited to manual or forensic inspection.
- Next check: Update-neighbors with changed accepted rows, then trigger an ordinary subsequent persist and inspect decoded state.snapshot.neighbors; include unchanged-set control to distinguish correctness from needless disk writes.

The argv0-directory candidate is the packaged location, and a broken file there is also the PATH entry. Shadowing therefore needs a stray artifact at a root-level candidate path. - Next check: Isolated discovery fixture containing an implicit 0644 cwd candidate plus executable PATH candidate: expect the PATH candidate; explicit 0644 path should return an informative error rather than silently fall back.

## Summary
Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (severity-dissent cohort: all three reviewers agree the defect exists; SMR rates COHORT/Low).

### C-033 <- D9-02
- Codex refutation/limits: A retry can update an already existing session-sync object's ownership, so the ordinary retry is not proof of immediate session loss. The constructor consequence requires a comms rebuild at a particular point; that sequence has not been executed.
- Spark refutation/limits: The common retry path updates the existing live session-sync object through applyConfigLocked's SetZoneOwnership, so only the narrow construct-after-restart case is exposed; probe shows the missing stamp but never drives the comms-restart consequence.
- SMR defect: configApplyReassertFn (config_apply_debt_9811.go:50-56) and executeConfirmedRollback (daemon_apply_commit.go:1125-1126) call applyConfigLocked without MarkActiveApplied. The stamp is written only at daemon_apply.go:215, 242 and daemon_apply_commit.go:432. Consumers are the sync shortcut (daemon_ha_sync.go:903, 926) and session-sync ownership seeding (daemon_ha_userspace.go:51-69).
- SMR locators: pkg/daemon/config_apply_debt_9811.go:45-56; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:1118-1129; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:200-243; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace.go:36-72
- SMR refutation/limits: Consequences are redundant re-apply and the narrow comms-restart seeding case.

### D0HA-003 <- D9-02
- Codex defect: The retry invokes applyConfigLocked and clears debt on nil without MarkActiveApplied; the successful auto-rollback does likewise. Thus a converged active config can still read unapplied, making an identical standby config push take the full apply path. Constructor seeding also requires ActiveApplied, so an object created in that state would lack authoritative zone ownership and withhold BulkAck.

No dataplane throughput or repeated-reapply cost was measured.

Census finds stamps only on boot/background (daemon_apply.go:215,242), commit (daemon_apply_commit.go:432), and sync capture/replay (daemon_apply_commit.go:785). After a failed boot + converging retry, owed=false while ActiveApplied()=false.
