- Spark locators: Source census of MarkActiveApplied/MarkAppliedDigest writers vs applyConfigLocked callers (retry + auto-rollback are the unstamped active-config applies).; Packet probe with control: boot-ok ActiveApplied=true; failed boot owed=true ActiveApplied=false; converging retry owed=false ActiveApplied=false — directly measures the claimed disagreeing state; stubbed apply body is sufficient for marker assertion because stamping is outside applyConfigLocked.; Code-verified consumers: handleConfigSync sho

The store's contract says that marker is set after every successful active apply (store.go:523-526, 1192-1197), and the other apply paths do set it (daemon_apply.go:211-216, 241-243; daemon_apply_commit.go:432). A newly created session-sync object only gets its zone-ownership map if the config is marked applied (daemon_ha_userspace.go:39-72), and that object is built in a background goroutine that can wait about 60s for an address (daemon_ha_sync.go:1183-1266). If the retry converges first, the new object starts with no zone map, so reconcile is skipped and BulkAck and 'primed' are withheld (sync.go:2517-2520; READM
- SMR locators: pkg/daemon/config_apply_debt_9811.go:44-153; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:1118-1129; pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:195-243; pkg/configstore/store.go:523-534,1192-1220; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace.go:12-73; pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:900-935,1183-1270
- SMR refutation/limits: If the session-sync object already exists, the apply installs the zone map itself (daemon_apply_dataplane.go:280-286). A secondary repairs itself through config sync at the cost of one redundant apply.

## #12212 — dataplane: fabric punt-seed adjudication uses the counting evaluator, double-counting the first packet of every punted flow [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC).

### Fabric punt-seed adjudication uses the counting evaluator, double-counting the first packet of every punted flow

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fabric.rs:939` calls `evaluate_policy_result_with_icmp_at` (the counting evaluator) to adjudicate a punt seed, then drops the returned counter handle (`policy_counter_idx: 0`, `fabric.rs:~985`). Dropping the handle cannot undo the atomic increment already performed inside `try_match_rule` (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:4349`). The owner node then re-evaluates and counts again at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4208`. One redirected admitted packet increments a policy hit counter on both legs.

This contradicts the function's own contract at `fabric.rs:906-912` ("the PEER counts the policy hit ... stamping the counter here as well would double-count"). A side-effect-free evaluator already exists (`evaluate_policy_result_without_counting_at`, `policy.rs:3392`) but is unused here.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fabric.rs:906-912` (no-double-count contract), `:939-951` (counting call), `:988-989` (handle dropped).
- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:4345-4350` (count-bearing matcher), `:3392-3421` (`WithoutCounting` variant).
- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4208-4220` (owner recount).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/STATIC (Low/High).

## Acceptance

- A punted flow's first packet increments the policy hit counter exactly once (owner leg only).
- The punt-seed adjudication path uses the non-counting evaluator; existing punt + counter tests stay green.

## #12213 — dataplane: failed partial publish mutates the retained snapshot via shared-slice aliasing; stored plan key predates revalidation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low-Medium (unanimous 3xMATERIAL on both members, STATIC + probes). Cohort: PA-01 + PA-04 share one root (send-time in-place revalidation after plan/map decisions).

### Failed partial publish mutates the retained snapshot via shared-slice aliasing, and the stored plan key predates revalidation

Struct copies share one `Interfaces` backing array: `next := *m.lastSnapshot` (`manager_overlay.go:194`, `manager_compile.go:1168`, `process_status.go:94`) then `publishSnap := next` clones tunnel endpoints but not Interfaces. The sole send site revalidates in place (`kept := snap.Interfaces[:0]` + shift + zero tail, `interfaces.go:1433-1486`) before the digest/send (`apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:89`). On failure the caller keeps `m.lastSnapshot` whose backing now holds revalidated rows under the old header while the stored hash describes pre-mutation content; on success the retained header can include a zero tail row the helper never saw. Consumers: classifier re-sync from retained rows (`maps_sync.go:618`), same-generation retry digest divergence (#9520 conflict path), `prevPlanKey` computed from mutated rows (`manager_compile.go:534`).

PA-04 leg: Compile stores the pre-revalidation `newPlanKey` (`manager_compile.go:535,720`) and uses it for same-plan verdict + map sync, so Go can classify same-plan while the helper rebinds; a stale stored key also triggers a spurious helper restart on the next FIB bump. Route-overlay and scheduler paths recompute post-send (partially guarded); Compile/deferred paths do not.

Severity rationale: retained-authority corruption with availability/churn consequences. No fail-open shown (zero rows are inert in the helper; ingress re-sync moves toward kernel truth). Probe `TestProbeRevalidateAliasing001` PASS confirmed the aliasing.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` alias sites (`manager_overlay.go:194,212,280,287,298,303`; `manager_compile.go:685,1168,1201`; `process_status.go:94,161`), in-place revalidation (`interfaces.go:1433-1486`), send site (`apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:89`), consumers (`maps_sync.go:618`; `manager_compile.go:534-535,541,720`).
- Gate PA-01: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/High/probed + smr MATERIAL/Low/STATIC. Gate PA-04: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Low/STATIC.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- Deep-copy Interfaces (slice + LinkUp ptrs) before revalidation, or make revalidation pure and write the result back into publishSnap AND (on ACK only) the retained snapshot.
- Single revalidation sample at the apply boundary before plan-key classification; store the key of the exact sent struct on every path.
- Regression cells: failed partial publish leaves retained rows + hash byte-identical; stored plan key equals sent key on Compile/deferred paths.

## #12214 — config: strictly admissible deep/cyclic address-set chains abort the live userspace apply in the shared prepass [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (2xMATERIAL + NV on both members, STATIC; coordinator-verified live path). Cohort: AB-08 + P10 (same root — shared-prepass depth/cycle abort).

### Strictly admissible deep/cyclic address-set chains abort the live userspace apply in the shared compiler prepass

`ExpandAddressSet` errors past depth 5 and on revisit (`pkg/config/predefined.go:425-484`). The shared compiler expands every set, referenced or not (`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:794-809`), and the live userspace path calls it (`CompileUserspaceShim` ← `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:335` ← `pkg/dataplane/loader.go:270-287`). No strict book-wide depth/cycle bound exists (the members gate checks definedness only, `compiler_validate_strict_addrset_members_9490.go`), so a strictly admissible chain with 6+ nested edges (or a mutual cycle) commits green and then aborts the production apply. The userspace snapshot resolver itself is unbounded (`policies_addrbook.go:454-490`) — the snapshot path could handle the chain, but the shared prepass fails first.

Availability/commit-apply split: persisted config fails every subsequent apply including boot.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` depth/cycle error (`predefined.go:425-484`), book-wide expansion (`compiler.go:794-809`), live caller chain (`loader.go:270-287`; `manager_compile.go:335`), members-gate scope (`compiler_validate_strict_addrset_members_9490.go`), unbounded snapshot resolver (`policies_addrbook.go:454-490`).
- Gate AB-08: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/STATIC + spark NV. Gate P10: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark NV.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- Either the strict gate bounds book-wide depth/cycles (commit-time diagnostic), or the shared prepass skips unreferenced sets / the userspace path exempts them, so a green commit always applies.
- Regression cells: 6-deep chain + mutual cycle with concrete members; both either reject at commit with the set named or apply cleanly — never commit-green/apply-red.

## #12216 — nat/host-inbound: non-policy expanders skip policy-path quarantines (NAT ignores CollidingNames; junos-host projection ignores collisions) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (2xMATERIAL + NV, STATIC + live NAT probes). Residuals of #12049 outside the policy path (P13 legs 2–3 fold here as evidence).

### Non-policy expanders skip policy-path quarantines: NAT expansion ignores `CollidingNames`/dangling/unready-feed, and junos-host projection ignores collisions

`CollidingNames` has exactly three consumers, all policy-path (`policies_lower.go:74`, `capabilities.go:339`, `policies_representable.go:151`). Outside it:

- NAT: `expandBookNameRecursive` (`policies_addrbook.go:454-491`) has no `CollidingNames` test, no dangling-member poison (a dangling member contributes nothing, returns `(out,false)`), and no declared-but-unready-feed test. Live probes: a colliding name expands address-first and a dangling member is silently dropped, while the same shape on the policy path sentinel-refuses. A NAT-only reference publishes a prefix set no channel accepted (translation scope narrowed/aliased).
- Junos-host: `junos_host_deny_resolve.go:112-116` resolves address-first with ok=true on an address-vs-set collision (re-read confirmed), emitting an incomplete deny and suppressing the no-representable signal; the kernel projection ignores address AND application `CollidingNames` (`:112-116`, `:198-281`), under-projecting a host-bound deny. (The host-dangling arm is fail-closed: ok=false → unrepresentable → key excluded; only the collision arm survives.)

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` consumer census (`policies_lower.go:74`; `capabilities.go:339`; `policies_representable.go:151`), NAT expander (`policies_addrbook.go:454-491`), host resolve (`junos_host_deny_resolve.go:108-129` → `junos_host_deny.go:437-474,562-588`), live NAT probes (good+ghost, colliding X).
- Gate AB-04: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark NV (NAT arms live-probed; host coupling narrowed).
- Dedup: #12049 is the policy-path fix; no open owner for the NAT/host residuals (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- NAT expansion honors `CollidingNames` + dangling/unready-feed poison exactly like the policy path (sentinel-refuse, not partial publish).
- Junos-host projection honors address/application `CollidingNames` on collisions (complete deny or explicit unrepresentable, never silent address-first subset).
- Regression cells: colliding/dangling shapes referenced NAT-only and host-only; both refuse like the policy-path control.

## #12223 — dataplane: application-list any short-circuits validation in list order ([any,bad] arms, [bad,any] poisons) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC + probes).

### `any` short-circuits application-list validation in list order: `[any, <bad>]` arms as match-any while `[<bad>, any]` poisons

The application lowerer returns `nil,true` immediately on `any` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/capabilities.go:384-408`), skipping subsequent `ApplicationReferenceMatchDrops` validation; the reversed list hits the drop and poisons the policy (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_lower.go:162-178`). The surviving tolerated-config case is a defined, representable-but-dropped application (e.g. ICMP carrying an inapplicable port, `pkg/config/application_match_drops_9525.go:67-90`): strict refuses it, but the lenient path silently absorbs it when `any` comes first.

Scope note: a nonexistent BAD is independently rejected by the unconditional legacy `compileApplications` prepass (`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:451-485,840-862`), so only defined-but-dropped members exhibit the order dependence. The bad-set arm was killed for the same reason.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` lowerer short-circuit (`capabilities.go:384-408`), poison arm (`policies_lower.go:162-178`), match-drops (`application_match_drops_9525.go:67-90`), legacy prepass (`compiler.go:451-485,840-862`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/narrowed/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/probed + smr MATERIAL/Low/STATIC.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- Application-list validation is order-insensitive: `[any, <defined-but-dropped>]` and `[<defined-but-dropped>, any]` produce the same snapshot outcome (both poison, or both arm with a diagnostic).
- Regression cell pins both orders plus the `[any, <nonexistent>]` control (still rejected by the prepass).

## #12226 — dataplane: fragment-deny override leaves the dropped fragment counted on the overridden PERMIT rule [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC).

### Fragment-deny override leaves the dropped fragment counted on the overridden PERMIT rule

`try_match_rule` increments the matched rule's hit counter (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:4345-4350`) before the caller applies the fragment-deny override (`policy.rs:3451-3495` and siblings). A flowless non-first fragment that matches a PERMIT on L3 but is then denied by an earlier port-bearing DENY (FragmentDenyOverlap) leaves the count on the PERMIT rule, which looks exercised although the packet was denied. The attributing DENY rule is deliberately never counted (`policy.rs:4265-4270`).

Scope note: the reject-label half of the source claim was killed (a suppressed reject reply truthfully logs DENY per #3615). This issue covers the provable counter-accounting component only.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:4345-4350` (count on match), `:3451-3495` + siblings (override applied after), `:4265-4270` (deny deliberately uncounted).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/STATIC (Low).

## Acceptance

- A fragment overridden from PERMIT to DENY does not accrue a hit on the overridden PERMIT rule (defer counting until after the override, or move the count).
- Counter regression cell: fragment-overlap deny leaves the permit count unchanged and the deny count unchanged (deliberate), with no double-count on the flowless path.

## #12229 — host-inbound: lifeline-shared address withheld from deny-all view, missing the kernel ingress drop [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC).

### A lifeline-shared address is withheld from a deny-all host-inbound view, so the zone's ingress drop misses it and the kernel input chain accepts

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:677-708` withholds a lifeline-shared address from an empty-admit view. `pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound_ingress_9637.go:8-28` builds ingress destination guards from those post-withhold views, and `pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound.go:94-121` falls through to the input chain's accept when no address remains. Packets arriving on a deny-all data-zone interface toward the shared local address therefore miss the intended kernel drop. Rust's empty host view is stricter but does not guard direct kernel delivery.

The lifeline exemption itself (preventing management lockout) and the duplicate-address strict checker's lifeline skip (`pkg/config/dup_host_local_address.go:306-354`) are legitimate; neither restores an ingress-only deny for the data zone.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:677-708` (withhold), `pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound_ingress_9637.go:8-28` (guards from post-withhold views), `pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound.go:94-121` (fallthrough accept).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/High/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC.

## Acceptance

- A deny-all data-zone interface drops host-bound traffic to a lifeline-shared local address at ingress (lifeline reachability preserved via its own interface), or the limitation is documented with an operator-visible warning.
- Regression cell: fxp0 address shared onto an untrust interface with no host-inbound stanza; ssh from untrust to the shared address is dropped while fxp0 management still works.

## #12233 — config: cross-kind set member fails or passes the production apply depending on sorted name order [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-09)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (NEG/NEG/MAT; coordinator-verified order-dependent apply failure, STATIC). Availability/commit-apply split.

The strict member gate explicitly accepts either kind ("matching that resolver", `compiler_validate_strict_addrset_members_9490.go:16-18`), and the runtime resolver is kind-agnostic by construction (`policies_addrbook.go:465-488`). So `address-set A { address B; }` with set `B` (A<B) fails the whole apply (`member not found`), while `Z { address B; }` passes: order-dependent commit-green/apply-red. Host-deny turns the shape into `ok=false` (unrepresentable) and static-NAT yields no target — inconsistent with both the strict gate and the runtime resolver.

Arm (a) (multi-zone scoped-global) is NEG (verified fail-closed via sentinel-refuse, as AB-10).

- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

- `compileAddressBook` resolves cross-kind members independent of sorted processing order (two-pass, or resolve-then-lookup), matching the strict gate and runtime resolver.

## #12235 — dataplane: deferred startup publish is recorded as applied before the helper enforces it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC).

### Deferred startup publish is recorded as applied before the helper enforces it

The deferred arm stores the unpublished snapshot as retained and returns nil (`manager_compile.go:627-653`). Only four daemon consumers read the deferred bit (host-inbound freshness, rx-VLAN retention: `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:198-199,244-245,1285,1303`). Ungated: commit/sync applied-digest stamp (`daemon_apply_commit.go:784-786`), HA ACK + high-water (`pkg/cluster/sync_conn_config.go:801-807`), takeover readiness (`manager_ha.go:428-430`). Health/convergence surfaces thus treat an unpublished generation as converged, contradicting the #4957 invariant and #9637's own premise that deferred success is not running.

Bounded window (seconds: same-plan deferrals publish on the next 1s tick; changed-plan ends at liveness), so Low. Rare sharper sub-case: a deferred publish later refused in-band is never surfaced to HA (refusals are not adopted as debt, `manager_compile.go:854-855`), and each tick re-enables ctrl + re-syncs maps to the refused snapshot before retrying and failing again.

Scope note: the session-invalidation sub-claim is DUP #12073 (OPEN) and is linked, not refiled, here.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` deferred arm (`manager_compile.go:627-653`), gated consumers (`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:198-199,244-245,1285,1303`), ungated stamp/ACK/takeover (`daemon_apply_commit.go:784-786`; `sync_conn_config.go:801-807`; `manager_ha.go:428-430,443-451,467-485`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Low/STATIC.
- Dedup: no open owner for the applied-marking leg (session leg -> #12073).

## Acceptance

- Thread the deferred bit (or PublishedGeneration < Generation) into the applied-digest stamp, HA ACK/high-water, and takeover readiness; a deferred generation is never reported converged.
- Regression cell: deferred startup publish shows pending (not applied) on commit status + HA high-water until the tick lands it; in-band refusal after deferral surfaces to HA.

## #12238 — config: weekday scheduler merge is sticky-OR for AllDay/Exclude; specific window stays all-day [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

The daily-window arm overwrites `AllDay` (`compiler_system.go:2885-2893`), but the weekday merge preserves `AllDay`/`Exclude` by OR after replacing a time boundary (`:2900-2912`: `w.AllDay = w.AllDay || win.AllDay`). An earlier `exclude` likewise cannot be superseded. Repeated distinct weekdays and complementary start/stop fragments merge properly — only contradictory flags stick.

- Later weekday blocks supersede (not OR) contradictory `AllDay`/`Exclude` flags — or the compiler rejects contradictory repeats with the scheduler named.

## #12240 — feeds: failed hold-drop publish is single-shot; dataplane keeps stale contents while manager reports dropped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (2xMATERIAL + NV, STATIC).

### Failed feed hold-drop publish is single-shot: the dataplane keeps stale last-good contents indefinitely while the manager reports dropped

`feeds.go:2099-2119` flips `hasSnapshot` to false before calling the drop publish; `:2135-2155` returns on callback failure without a retry; later failures skip the transition because `hasSnapshot` is already false. `:1101-1109` exposes publication debt but does not republish it. After hold-expiry publication is rejected, the dataplane keeps stale last-good contents indefinitely while the feed manager reports dropped. Ordinary good-content publication retries on identical refetch (`:1815-1825`), but that retry condition is not used for failed drops. A subsequent successful provider fetch replaces the desired empty state — it does not repair the dropped-state retry contract.

SMR's open leg (whether manager retry-debt republish carries the dropped overlay, `manager_compile.go:830-938`) was not traced; no lane found such a carry.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` single-shot drop (`feeds.go:2099-2121,2135-2156`), debt without republish (`:1101-1109`), good-content retry (`:1815-1825`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr NV (mechanism confirmed; overlay-carry open).
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- A rejected hold-drop publish retries until the empty state lands (or the debt overlay carries it on the next manager republish); manager-reported dropped always matches dataplane contents.
- Regression cell: hold-expiry with a failing publish callback; the drop is retried and the dataplane converges to empty; debt surface reflects the pending drop until then.

## #12241 — feeds: hold-expiry evaluated only inside failure recording; time-to-drop is not a real-time bound [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (2xMATERIAL + NV, STATIC).

### Feed hold-expiry is evaluated only inside failure recording, so the configured time-to-drop is not a real-time bound

`feeds.go:1254-1275` invokes fetch only initially and on its interval; `:2088-2107` checks `holdInterval` only when recording another failure. A 300-second hold with a 3600-second fetch cadence drops on the next failed fetch — roughly an hour after the first detected failure, potentially nearly two hours after actual upstream outage. `:1936-1970` also routes guard refusals through that clock. The configured hold is documented as a time-to-drop but behaves as a failure-count-gated drop.

Opt-in `fail-mode drop` and treating a rejected candidate as a feed failure are documented choices (not disputed); the defect is the wall-clock-vs-failure-clock gap. The packet's ~65-minute estimate is not a sound upper bound from actual outage onset (coordinator agrees with Codex).

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` fetch cadence (`feeds.go:1254-1275`), hold-inside-recordFailure (`:2088-2107`), guard-refusal routing (`:1936-1970`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr NV (mechanism confirmed; fail-mode semantics unverified).
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- Hold-expiry is evaluated on a wall-clock timer (or the documented contract states the failure-gated semantics explicitly with the worst-case bound).
- Regression cell: 300s hold + 3600s fetch + upstream outage at T0; the drop lands within hold+epsilon of T0 (or the documented bound), not at the next fetch failure.

## #12246 — policymatch: match-policies evaluates the operator tuple with no NAT stage; VIP query can certify the opposite [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (NZ-013: MAT/NV/NEG; AT-06: 2xMAT/NEG; STATIC). Cohort: header-merged simulator-NAT group (AT-06 + NZ-13).

### `match-policies` evaluates the operator tuple with no NAT translation stage, so a VIP query can certify the opposite of what the dataplane enforces

CLI `show security match-policies` passes literal source/destination/ports to `policymatch.Match` (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:531-561,565-610`); `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:23-27,724-739` matches the supplied tuple and never DNATs it (NAT refs in the package are family hints only; no `rewrite_dst`/DNAT/NPTv6 pre-stage). The dataplane evaluates zone policy after destination translation (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3103-3159`, `policy_dst_ip = effective_resolution_target`). With a VIP-vs-real-server policy distinction, the simulator can report a permitted VIP query while the real incoming VIP packet maps to a denied server. CLI usage does not require or label post-NAT inputs.

The package contract promises to "replicate the runtime precedence and semantics exactly" (`policymatch.go:1-30`); the NAT stage is the missing piece. Entering the post-DNAT address manually can produce a correct policy-only answer, so this is a missing specified input/translation context on the advertised packet-check surface.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` CLI tuple pass-through (`cli_show_security.go:531-561,565-610`), simulator no-translate (`policymatch.go:23-27,724-739,794`), dataplane post-translation policy (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3103-3159`), contract text (`policymatch.go:1-30`).
- Gate NZ-013: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark NV (input-contract decision) + smr NEG (Junos-inference). Gate AT-006: codex MATERIAL/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr NEG. Coordinator: the in-tree contract text decides over the Junos inference.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- Either the simulator translates VIP inputs through DNAT before matching (or requires post-NAT inputs with a banner), and the usage text states which tuple is expected.
- Regression cell: VIP with VIP-permit + server-deny; the VIP query reports the translated (deny) verdict or an explicit post-NAT-input requirement.

## #12247 — cluster: tolerant quarantine recomputes per-snapshot while the strict gate unions node views; peers differ [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Medium (2xMATERIAL + NV, STATIC).

### Tolerant collision quarantine recomputes per-snapshot while the strict gate unions node views: peers can enforce different survivors

The strict AST collision gate unions main + node0/node1 names (`zoneid.go:126-158,169-190`), but tolerant dataplane quarantine recomputes from each snapshot's names (`zones_quarantine.go:63-88`; `zoneid.go:219-247`, from the node-expanded lenient compile, `zones_snapshot.go:10-21`). If one node expands both colliding names and the other expands only the later-sorting name, the latter retains a zone the former drops: peer zone enforcement differs on old/tolerant-loaded configuration. The HA-symmetry claim (`zoneid.go:214-217`) assumes identical name sets, which node-scoped configs violate.

Strict commits reject the union (tolerant/HA-sync path only). One name per node without both on either node does not reproduce the disparity.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` union gate (`zoneid.go:126-158,169-190`), per-snapshot recompute (`zones_quarantine.go:63-88`; `zoneid.go:219-247`), node-expanded compile (`zones_snapshot.go:10-21`; `compiler.go:773-775,918-923`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + smr NV (mechanism confirmed; needs node-scoped colliding-pair test).
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- The runtime quarantine computes over the 3-view union (or ships the union name set in the snapshot), so peers quarantine identically on node-scoped configs.
- Regression cell: node0-only zA / node1-only zB with colliding StableZoneID, tolerant load; both nodes quarantine the same survivor.

## Review origin

- Discovery source: deep-review, review-work.gueCgw0dbL, muse-spark-review-security-zone-policies-focused-hunt-001.md (ZB-10).
- Validation: research-work.ZUHKCVTbaV @ f07859287 (evidence == comparison; zero-diff preflight 2026-10-06).

## #12248 — config: native VLAN with no unique matching unit blackholes untagged ingress with no diagnostic [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-12)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low (2xMATERIAL + NEG-fail-closed, STATIC). Fail-closed blackhole without a commit-time diagnostic — availability/diagnosability only, no zone leak.

### Native VLAN with no unique matching unit blackholes untagged ingress with no commit-time explanation

`compiler_interfaces.go:173-181` accepts an integer `native-vlan-id` without requiring an associated configured/zoned unit, while `forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:1549-1593` maps VID 0 only to a unique matching unit and otherwise marks the parent tagged-only (`forwarding/mod.rs:373-381`). An otherwise green configuration with an unmatched native VLAN blackholes untagged ingress silently. Malformed non-integer input is handled by the typed strict schema — the gap is the missing native-binding diagnostic on syntactically valid configs.

SMR's NEG (deliberate fail-closed contract per #11434) is acknowledged for the enforcement direction; the filed defect is the missing commit advisory, which SMR also names as the residual.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` unguarded accept (`compiler_interfaces.go:176-182`; `schema_interfaces.go:89-91`), unique-unit mapping (`interfaces.rs:1548-1593`), tagged-only mark (`forwarding/mod.rs:373-381`), no `NativeVlanID` advisory consumer (grep).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/Medium/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/Low/STATIC + smr NEG (fail-closed) with advisory residual.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- A commit-time advisory names the native VLAN without a unique matching unit (or the gate rejects it); untagged ingress is never silently blackholed on a green commit.
- Regression cell: native-vlan-id with no/ambiguous unit; commit warns (or rejects) naming the interface; matched-unit control stays silent.

- Discovery source: deep-review, review-work.gueCgw0dbL, muse-spark-review-security-zone-policies-focused-hunt-001.md (ZB-12 availability half; security half NEG).
- Validation: research-work.ZUHKCVTbaV @ f07859287 (evidence == comparison; zero-diff preflight 2026-10-06).

## #12249 — dataplane: tolerated defined zone any is dropped but its policies survive as wildcards [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-09)

## Summary

Research disposition: MATERIAL Low-Medium (unanimous 3xMATERIAL, STATIC; one-wave tolerant window).

### Tolerant zone `any`: a defined zone named `any` is dropped but its policies survive as wildcards

`pkg/config/zoneid.go:250-265` excludes a defined reserved `any` zone; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_quarantine.go:122-130` scrubs only collision losers, retaining reserved-token policies (`policyQuarantined = QuarantinedZoneNames`, keep-rationale `:124`); `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2705-2715` indexes `from_zone == "any"` as wildcard. A tolerated persisted definition of zone `any` loses its interfaces while a purportedly zone-specific permit naming it becomes a from-any permit. #9570 poison covers `junos-global` only (`zone_pair_global_sentinel_9570.go:38`).

Window: definition allowed until `10881c18b` #3055 (2026-06-25), wildcard enforcement landed `1726ea415` #3090 (2026-06-26) — one wave wide. Current strict commit prevents creating the definition (`compiler_validate_strict_zones.go:50-54`); a wildcard policy with no zone definition must remain legal. Only pre-#3055 persisted configs booting tolerantly today are affected.

## Evidence

- BASE/VERIFY `f07859287` exclusion (`zoneid.go:250-265`), collision-only scrub (`zones_quarantine.go:122-130`), wildcard index (`policy.rs:2705-2715`), #9570 junos-global-only poison (`zone_pair_global_sentinel_9570.go:38`), strict prevention (`compiler_validate_strict_zones.go:50-54`).
- Gate: codex MATERIAL/High/STATIC + spark MATERIAL/STATIC + smr MATERIAL/Low-Medium/STATIC.
- Dedup: no open owner found (2026-10-06).

## Acceptance

- When a reserved-name zone was actually defined, scrub/poison zone-pair policies naming it (mirror #9570); wildcard policies with no such zone defined stay untouched.
- Regression cell: pre-#3055-shaped persisted config defining zone `any` + `from-zone any` permit; tolerant boot scrubs/poisons the policy instead of widening it.

- Discovery source: deep-review, review-work.gueCgw0dbL, muse-spark-review-security-zone-policies-focused-hunt-001.md (ZB-13).

## #12312 — frr: QNH static-source predicate misses whitespace/case protocol variants, silently drops metric (follow-up #12311) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## What
`policyHasStaticSource11447` (`pkg/frr/qnh_metric_11447.go:215-226`) compares `term.FromProtocols` against exact `"static"`. Strict compilation accepts whitespace/case variants (`STATIC`, `"static "`, `" Static "`) without rewriting the stored token, so those spellings compile clean but fail the predicate: the qualified-next-hop metric map is not created/attached, and redistribution silently uses the ordinary map without the configured metric.

## Mechanism (verified on `cbcec8cad`, pre-existing on base `a714c90d4`)
- Predicate: `if source == "static"` — no canonicalization.
- The protocol domain (`config.FRRRoutingProtocolKeyword`) trims whitespace + folds case; PR #12311's `config.CanonicalSourceProtocol` shares that SSOT for renderer/count/redistribute naming, but QNH predates it and was never wired in.
- Reproduced by reviewer (compile→render): `from protocol STATIC` attaches `EXP-static-xpf-redist` (empty body) instead of the QNH metric map carrying `set metric 10`. Lowercase `static` attaches correctly.

## Acceptance
- Route the predicate through `config.CanonicalSourceProtocol` (or the domain keyword directly); `STATIC`/`"static "`/`" Static "` attach the QNH map.
- Compile→managed-section regression following the actual redistribution attachment (not just section grep — the metric text appears in the unattached map, a false-green shape).
- Existing QNH + redistribute + IS-IS suites green; gofmt clean.

## Provenance
Found by Codex/Astra hostile review round 3 on PR #12311 (#12066). Ruled follow-up (not fold): the predicate is byte-identical on base, untouched by #12311's diff, and a different symptom class (silent metric omission vs duplicate-prepend). Parent verified pre-existence via `git show origin/master:pkg/frr/qnh_metric_11447.go`.

## #12313 — config: cross-scope any-service + except union stays silent (follow-up #12310) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## What
PR #12310's per-stanza full-admit/except gate covers zone-level stanzas and per-interface overrides individually, but a cross-scope combination stays silent on BOTH strict and lenient paths: `any-service` on one scope (e.g. a physical interface or the zone) unioned at runtime with an `except` on another scope (e.g. a unit-level override). The runtime union admits everything while the exclusion is inert, with no diagnostic.

## Mechanism
- The gate (`validateHostInboundFullAdmitExceptStrict`) walks each stanza independently; it never correlates a full-admit token in one stanza with exclusions in another.
- The runtime host-inbound view unions tokens across scopes, so the cross-scope `any-service` full-admits before the other scope's exclusion is consulted.
- Reproduced live by GLM-5.3 hostile review R2 on PR #12310 (silent on strict AND lenient); the #12310 fold commit Risk section discloses it as outside that fold. Opus R3 confirmed no follow-up existed and requested this filing.

## Acceptance
- Strict commit rejects (or lenient warns naming both scopes) when a retained `any-service` in any in-scope stanza unions with an `except` in another stanza of the same zone/interface family.
- Regressions: physical-interface any-service + unit except (strict reject + lenient warn), zone any-service + interface except; controls proving same-stanza behavior unchanged.
- Document the cross-scope rule in `docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md`.

## Provenance
Follow-up from PR #12310 (#12054) hostile review residuals (GLM R2 + Opus R3). Not a regression: the combination was silent before #12310 too; #12310 narrowed the per-stanza case only.

## #12317 — config: cross-scope override union re-admits alias-excluded tuples (follow-up #12316) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## What
`MergeHostInboundTraffic` (pkg/config/host_inbound_effective_view.go:178-205) unions physical-interface + unit-level override token lists by exact string, discarding exclusion provenance. A unit stanza `all; ssh except` (correctly tuple-subtracted per #12053 within its own stanza) unioned with a physical-interface stanza carrying `netconf-ssh` re-admits tcp/22 through the alias — the cross-scope twin of W03-01.

## Mechanism (reviewer-verified on PR #12316 head 4cf2b731a, memory-only probes)
- Config: physical interface `netconf-ssh` + same unit `all; ssh except` passes strict compile.
- The merge unions alias back; emitted nft: `ip daddr 192.0.2.1 tcp dport { 22, 830 } accept` (+ IPv6 twin); netlink builder lookup set [0016,033e] ACCEPT both families.
- Same defect family as #12313 (cross-scope any-service + except): per-stanza gates correct, cross-stanza union drops the constraint. #12053's acceptance is single-stanza (`all` + `T except` emission); this combination is outside it.

## Acceptance
- Cross-scope union must preserve tuple-subtraction: an exclusion in any merged stanza removes the tuple from the union (or the combination is rejected/warned with both scopes named).
- Regressions: physical alias + unit except (strict + lenient), reversed scopes, zone+interface combinations; controls proving single-stanza behavior unchanged.
- Document in `docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md`.

## Provenance
Found by Codex/Astra hostile review on PR #12316 (#12053). Ruled follow-up (not fold): outside #12053's single-stanza acceptance; sibling of #12313. Parent verified the merge function drops provenance by code read.

## #12319 — userspace-dp: stamped-fabric UDP reject sends ICMP to stamp MAC, counted as sent (follow-up #12314) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## What
Stamped-fabric UDP policy rejects emit ICMP port-unreachable addressed to the synthetic stamp MAC — unreachable backscatter counted as sent with a REJECT event. Same defect class as #12051 (TCP), different leg, explicitly unexercised there.

## Mechanism (reviewer-proven on PR #12314 head 616300ba6)
- The #12051 gate is TCP-only by design (reject_reply.rs:259-266); UDP falls through to ICMP construction.
- `icmp.rs:417-418` copies the inbound source MAC (the stamp) into the ICMP L2 destination.
- Throwaway probe on the M3 fixture (fabric ifindex 21 with primary_v4): sent=true, policy_reject_sent=1, reply L2 dst=02:bf:72:fe:00:02, ICMP 3/3 — confirmed undeliverable, counted, and logged REJECT, against the #3615 "never logs a reject that did not happen" contract.
- The M3 negative control (`stamped_fabric_udp_policy_reject_keeps_port_unreachable_12051`) records this as current behavior pending this follow-up; dropping the TCP-only condition is the natural fix shape.

## Acceptance
- Stamped-fabric UDP reject: no stamp-addressed ICMP queued or counted; truthful DENY event (mirroring the #12051 TCP contract).
- Extend the shared gate or add the ICMP leg with V1+V2 + session-miss-equivalent coverage; real-poll regression with producer-minted stamps.
- Reword/extend the M3 control to the fixed behavior.

## Provenance
Found by Claude Opus hostile review R2 on PR #12314 (#12051, finding F1). Sibling SYN-cookie leg (cookie_reply.rs, no fabric gate) noted as unexecuted residual — assess in the same slice.

## #12503 — userspace-dp: stale-generation re-resolve loses TUN-origin VRF reverse LocalDelivery (follow-up #12269) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up to #12269 (PR #12484 fixes the host-inbound forward cell; these two VRF residuals are product-path, not fixture).

## What
`gre_tun_origin_vrf_reverse_resolves_local_10038` (decap_tests.rs:3138) and `wg_tun_origin_domain_vrf_hit_delivers_10038` (:3633) still fail: session_hit=1, policy_deny=1, no_route=1, local=0.

## Mechanism (fold-lane trace, firsthand)
Both builders synthesize the reverse as LocalDelivery in the tunnel named-instance table (tunnel.rs:724-742; tun_origin.rs:315-329), while the reverse decision carries the intentional zero install-table stamp (shared_ops.rs:1699-1709). The descriptor pass publishes validation generation (7,9), but `upsert_synced_with_origin` installs an invalid default forwarding-generation stamp (session/install.rs:681-690), making the session stale (session/mod.rs:1986-1992). `resolve_flow_session_decision_with_conntrack` re-resolves it BEFORE the poll-loop TUN-origin PBR guard (session_glue/mod.rs:3099-3145; guard at poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1819-1841). The zero install-table stamp selects Default rather than the table-scoped `cust` lookup (session_glue/mod.rs:144-163), losing the VRF LocalDelivery → NoRoute. The TUN-origin reverse marker is valid and the PBR guard skips correctly; the failure is the earlier generic refresh.

## Acceptance
Both cells green via product fix (stale-refresh preserving TUN-origin table scope, or valid install stamps on synced reverse installs); no assertion weakening.

Parent: #12269.

## Acceptance

For compact term-line forms, verify strict compilation retains each action in the correct typed field and FRR rendering emits it; verify `accept` and `reject` controls still set only the terminal action. ## #12515 — daemon: reconcile lost-ACK rollback sessions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Parent issue: #12072

## Summary
A confirmed timeout rollback can report convergence while a session admitted only by the rolled-back policy remains live if the policy publish ACK was lost after the helper actually applied the new snapshot. This is pre-existing on master and is not caused by PR #12323.

## Reproduction
1. Start from C1 and commit-confirm C2, which adds policy x. The helper applies C2 but its apply_snapshot ACK is lost, leaving authority unknown.
2. Add session 1099 admitted by x while the helper enforces C2.
3. Let the confirm timer fire before authority is reconciled.
4. The rollback arm resolves to {C1->C1} from debt.oldCfg; the empty diff performs no READ or authority refusal.

Observed result: session 1099 remains live although the rolled-back C1 forbids it, while ActiveApplied is true. Reproduced on master 4a284d9d8 with a compatibility-patched harness, and identically on the PR head.

## Expected
An empty C1-to-C1 plan must not establish convergence while the preceding C2 publication outcome is unknown. Reconcile the helper authority and ensure sessions admitted only by rolled-back policy are revoked before reporting ActiveApplied.

## #12516 — config: then-first LoadMerge/LoadSet drops from clause and permits all [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Parent: #12067

## Problem

The then-first spelling is handled by LoadOverride, but LoadMerge, LoadSet, and direct `set` replay lose the entire `from` clause. For example:

```
term T then accept from route-filter 10.0.0.0/8 exact;
```

`FormatSetForLoadMerge` emits a set path with `from ...` nested below `then/accept`. `SetPath` then drops that child, and `CommitCheck` / `Commit` succeed with `Action=accept` and no route filters: a match-all permit. The same mechanism affects bare `upto`, protocol, and bare `route-filter` forms.

This reproduces on the #12067 true parent `912499f05` and the merged stack with #12324 `9d6a61955` plus #12325 `922c7828b`. The then-first Store coverage in #12325 uses `LoadOverride` only, so it does not exercise the affected replay paths.

## Expected

Preserve the whole `from` clause through LoadMerge, LoadSet, and direct set-path replay, or reject the operation; it must never commit as an unconstrained permit. Add Store regressions for route-filter and the affected bare-upto/protocol forms across these paths.

## References

Found during Opus R3 review of #12325; unrelated to the R3 fold and filed as a follow-up.

## #12520 — config/userspace: validate tunnel routing-instance stanza targets (#12082 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Parent: #12082. Related reserved-name work: #9622.

Strict CompileConfig currently accepts an explicit tunnel `routing-instance destination` naming an undefined instance, a `forwarding` instance, or reserved `mgmt`. These targets do not all have an active VRF owner, but the kernel tunnel manager still derives a VRF device name from the stanza. In particular, a tunnel stanza naming `mgmt` binds its device to `vrf-mgmt`, while userspace snapshot rows remain in the default routing instance/domain. This violates #12082’s “for every tunnel” cross-plane ownership contract and can mis-scope connected routes and sessions.

Add a strict commit gate (with tolerant-load handling consistent with existing policy) for unsupported stanza targets. Cover undefined, forwarding, and reserved management targets, and prove accepted/rejected results agree with kernel tunnel binding and userspace interface snapshots. #9622 addresses a user routing-instance named `mgmt`; this follow-up is specifically the explicit tunnel-stanza target and the remaining invalid target classes.

## #12528 — config: is-fragment and flexible-match-range swallow fused then tails (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up to #12092. No owning issue was found for either leaf's fused-tail behavior.

`from is-fragment then discard` / `then reject` loses the terminal action. The resulting firewall term has `Action=""`; userspace treats that as continue/fall-through, whose default is Accept. The intended drop/reject therefore becomes fail-open.

Evidence (reproduced on base `83b5c9553` and the reviewed head):

1. **F13, flat LoadSet:** `set firewall family inet filter F term T from is-fragment then discard` (and `then reject`) plus a later allow term passes CommitCheck; T has Action `""`.
2. **N3, named LoadOverride:** `term T { from { is-fragment then discard; } }` passes with Action `""`.
3. **N4, named LoadOverride:** `term T { from { is-fragment { then { discard; } } } }` passes with Action `""`.
4. **N1, named packed round-trip:** `term T from is-fragment then discard;` loads correctly through LoadOverride with Action `discard`, but LoadMerge / `display set` → `load set` round-trip drops the action (Action `""`).
5. **N2, named compact hierarchical:** `term T { from is-fragment then discard; }` is rejected by LoadOverride with the #8437 fused-sibling diagnostic, but LoadMerge commits it with Action `""`.
6. **H1–H5, nameless forms:** `term { T from is-fragment { then { discard; } } }` (H1) commits through LoadMerge with Action `""`; replacing discard with reject, using leaf spelling `term { T from is-fragment then discard; }`, and the inet6 and any families (both pools) reproduce the same dropped-action behavior. LoadOverride rejects the nameless form.
7. **N6/F13c, related tail boundary:** `is-fragment foo` is also accepted silently; no gate rejects extra tokens after this no-argument leaf.

Mechanism: the #8437 gate in `pkg/config/schema_walk.go:602-656` checks only tokens that name siblings of the leaf (children of `from`). `then` is at term level, not a `from` sibling, so the fused tail gets through. `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:1780-1781` handles `is-fragment` by setting `IsFragment` and ignores the remaining tail. The same rows reproduce on base, so this is pre-existing; no production gate is changed by #12092.

## Additional affected leaf: `flexible-match-range`

`from flexible-match-range` also silently swallows a fused `then` tail. This is the same fail-open class: a requested discard is not stored on the term, leaving `Action=""` and allowing evaluation to fall through. Reproduced on the reviewed head with LoadSet, named LoadOverride, and nameless LoadMerge; parent reproduction also confirmed the LoadMerge case on base `83b5c9553`.

The flat LoadSet repro uses the following lines (plus `set firewall family inet filter F term allow then accept`):

```text
set firewall family inet filter F term T from flexible-match-range range R match-start layer-3
set firewall family inet filter F term T from flexible-match-range range R byte-offset 9
set firewall family inet filter F term T from flexible-match-range range R bit-length 8
set firewall family inet filter F term T from flexible-match-range range R match-value 0x11
set firewall family inet filter F term T from flexible-match-range range R then discard
```

It passes CommitCheck with T's `Action=""`; `FlexMatch` is populated as layer-3, offset 9, length 8, value 17, mask 255. Named LoadOverride also commits `term T { from { flexible-match-range { range R { match-start layer-3; byte-offset 9; bit-length 8; match-value 0x11; then discard; } } } }` with the same empty action. Nameless LoadMerge commits `term { T from flexible-match-range range R { match-start layer-3; byte-offset 9; bit-length 8; match-value 0x11; then { discard; } } }` likewise. In each form, the displayed set still contains `then discard` although the compiled term has no action.

Mechanism: `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:1782-1801` compiles `flexible-match-range` by iterating its named `range` children and reading range fields; the fused `then` tail is not mapped to the term action. The schema walk is open-world at this entry (`pkg/config/schema_walk.go:152-156`), so this ignored tail is not rejected. This behavior also reproduces on base; no production gate is changed by #12092.

## Tree-shape coverage required for the `is-fragment` gate

The tree representation differs by loading path. A firsthand dump on the reviewed head showed this H1 shape after LoadMerge and the same `is-fragment`-then-`discard` shape after flat LoadSet and interactive `SetFromInput`:

```text
["term" "T"] leaf=false
```

```
`prefix-length-range /16-/24`, `through`, `protocol static route-filter ... upto /24`, and a braced main `term T { then accept; }` lose the clause too. `exact`, `orlonger`, `prefix-list`, `protocol` merge correctly. ExpandGroups output keeps only `[\"term\" \"T\" \"then\" \"accept\"]`.

## Acceptance
Group-inherited route-filter clauses survive the merge (or the commit is rejected), with regression coverage. Or a disposition with evidence.

## #12530 — Preserve packed apply-group tails for inline container peers [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## #12532 — policy invalidation: nested confirmed rollback to root over-deletes sessions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Summary

Nested commit-confirmed rollback to the original confirmed config can over-delete sessions that the restored policy permits. This reproduces on both the base and PR #12323 head; it is pre-existing and remains out of scope for the single-level rollback fix.

## Reproduction (P3)

1. Start at C0, which permits rules `a` and `b`.
2. Commit-confirm C1, which forbids `a`; make its session deletion fail so debt records s1.
3. Before confirming C1, nest a commit-confirmed C2, which forbids `b`; make its deletion fail so debt also records s2.
4. Let the confirm timer restore the original confirmed C0. The store retains `confirmPrevCfg` as C0 across nested confirms.
5. Observe s1 and s2 both deleted, although C0 permits both rules.

## Mechanism

The retained debt has a depth-one landed predecessor link and `predecessorCfg == C1`. When the nested rollback restores C0, the exact-undo pointer predicate does not match (`C1 != C0`), so capture follows the carry path and includes candidates from both transitions. The result is over-deletion. See `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go` confirm-window handling (around lines 449-453) and rollback restoration (around 1209/1225), plus probe P3 from the F1-confirmation review.

## Requirement

Support multi-level rollback with per-candidate provenance (or equivalent policy-authorization evaluation) so the restored root config discharges candidates it permits while retaining only still-forbidden candidates. A depth-one landed chain cannot represent which target introduced each candidate. Add a permanent nested C0→C1→C2→C0 regression that fails on current behavior and passes with the provenance fix.

## #12543 — install: keyring rollback guard overwrites/deletes dpkg payload byte-identical to bootstrap key (follow-up #12142) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up to #12142 (Astra post-merge confirmation PC-F1 on PR #12358, merged as e67d7707c — real-dpkg repro + syscall trace + gpgv proof).

## What
The rollback guard (scripts/dist/install.sh:115-128) passes on byte equality alone: a regular non-symlink keyring whose bytes equal the bootstrap ARCHIVE_KEY is treated as still-the-installers file. Real dpkg can replace the bootstrap inode with a package-owned file containing those EXACT bytes (debian/rules copies the archive-key file directly — byte equality is a legitimate same-key release). The guard then renames the stale backup over the package payload (re-run) or deletes it (first install).

## Evidence (reviewer firsthand, retained harness at /var/tmp/PrincipalClam-12142)
Real .deb + private-root dpkg + postinst failing ENOTDIR after unpack: identical-payload existing-key case restores the OBSOLETE key; first-install case REMOVES the package file. After fixing only ENOTDIR + `dpkg --configure` (rc=0, install-ok-installed), the keyring stays stale/absent (dpkg does not re-unpack). Release signed by the new key: gpgv rc=0 against package payload, rc=2 NO_PUBKEY 4F8712E89E380EDC against live keyring. Syscall trace: dpkg .dpkg-new O_EXCL create + rename over live, then installer stale-backup rename over that. This REFUTES the merged PRs observationally-equivalent residual.

## Fix acceptance (reviewer direction)
Gate rollback on bootstrap file IDENTITY + byte equality: capture the bootstrap temps device/inode before arming rollback/rename; only restore/remove if the live file is still that object AND contents match (retained inode ref stronger). Preserve replacement inodes even when bytes identical. AVOID mtime-only, UID/GID/mode, naive dpkg-db ownership checks (all defeated per the verdict). Regressions: both equal-payload cases (existing-prior + first-install) with genuine unpack/inode-replacement + configure-only recovery asserting package bytes survive; retain distinct-payload + pre-unpack + interrupt-window cases.

## #12544 — Valid-Until exact-epoch assertion races apt-ftparchive wall clock [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Problem

`scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh` pins `APT::FTPArchive::Release::Date` to `NOWSTR` (line 330) and asks apt-ftparchive to emit `Valid-Until` with `ValidTime` (line 331). The exact-epoch assertion at lines 340–347 compares that field against `NOW + VALID_SECONDS`. In apt-utils 3.3.3, apt-ftparchive derives `Valid-Until` from `time(NULL)` and ignores the pinned `Date`; a second boundary can pass between reading `NOW` and apt-ftparchive sampling the wall clock.

## Reproduction / impact

A 12-worker × 25-build parallel repro against real apt-ftparchive repeatedly observed `Release Valid-Until ... != ValidTime-derived value` with `want epoch 1823156328, got 1823156329`. This is an intermittent CI/release build failure even though the emitted horizon is valid.

## Acceptance

- Keep the singleton `Valid-Until` and configured-horizon checks fail-closed.
- Make the assertion independent of this one-second wall-clock race (e.g. a narrowly tolerant window consistent with the emitted `Date`, or a wall-clock-independent assertion).
- Add deterministic coverage for the accepted boundary and malformed/missing/duplicate `Valid-Until` refusals.

Existing code is at `scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh` around lines 330–347.

## #12545 — bootstrap: multiport busAddr ties make the index-0 remedy never settle (mlx4/cxgb4/switchdev) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up from Opus round-1 on #12367 (R1 residual, live-probed in namespace).

NICs that put several netdevs on one PCI function (mlx4, cxgb4, switchdev representors) share one busAddr; enumeratePCINICs breaks those ties by current interface name. After a successful claim (enp1s0→fxp0), the next bootstrap run enumerates [enp1s0d1, fxp0], puts fxp0 at enum_index=1, and refuses — telling the operator to re-wire to enp1s0d1, the port they just left. The remedy never settles on such hardware. Positional naming at first commit would then map enp1s0d1→fxp0 and fxp0→ge-0-0-0 (INFERENCE from linksetup.go:276-281 + observed order; not live-probed) — a possible management port swap.

Suggested fix: break busAddr ties by dev_port/phys_port_name, not by name.

Probe: ExistingSalamander multiport_claimed (repro sources in review transcript).
```

```
## #12565 — master RED: TestControllerAdapterMethodsReachTheManager_6871 +5 fail bind/mkdir: untruncated t.TempDir names under CI go1.24.9 (follow-up #12553) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up of #12553 (per-test triage). Triaged firsthand on master `89223b7fa` and re-confirmed RED on tip `2f73d41da`.

## Classification
**(c) environment/toolchain-dependent — deterministic on CI, not a flake, not a product regression.** One cause, six tests:

| Test | Package | Failing subtest(s) | Symptom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TestControllerAdapterMethodsReachTheManager_6871` | `pkg/dataplane/userspace` | 13 subtests in CI (17 with a 4-byte-longer `TMPDIR`) | `listen unix …/control.sock: bind: invalid argument` |
| `TestEventStreamPolicyDenyGenerationAcrossBacklogAndReplay10978` | `pkg/dataplane/userspace` | `reader_backlog`, `reconnect_replay` | `…/policy-events.sock: bind: invalid argument` |
| `TestTakeoverReadyRequiresEventStreamListenerBound` | `pkg/dataplane/userspace` | `ListenerBoundHelperDisconnected`, `ListenerBoundHelperConnected` | `…/events.sock: bind: invalid argument` |
| `TestPeerCredentialReadFailsClosed9003` | `pkg/dataplane/userspace` | `a_closed_connection_is_refused,_not_defaulted` | `…/closed.sock: bind: invalid argument` |
| `TestLegacyReaderRepairWireFailsClosedWithoutRefusalClassification11360` | `pkg/dataplane/userspace` | `pending`, `overflow` | `…/events.sock: bind: invalid argument` |
| `TestCommitCheckRejectsSystemHostname10003` | `pkg/configstore` | the 300-char `bbbb…` host-name case | `TempDir: mkdir …: file name too long` |

## Cause
CI's Go job (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, added in 65bf0ec09 / #11185 on 2026-10-01) uses `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file: go.mod`. `go.mod` has said `go 1.24.9` since 7d171dd15, so CI runs **go1.24.9** (CI log: `go version go1.24.9 linux/amd64`). Developer hosts run go1.25+/go1.26.

`testing.(*common).TempDir` builds the directory name from the full test name:
- go1.24.9 `src/testing/testing.go:1262-1263`: `pattern := strings.Map(mapper, c.Name())`, then `os.MkdirTemp("", pattern)`. There is **no length cap**.
- go1.25.8 `testing.go:1341-1343` and go1.26.8 `testing.go:1450-1452`: `pattern = pattern[:min(len(pattern), 64)]`. The name is capped at 64 bytes.

These tests put an AF_UNIX socket under `t.TempDir()`. They were written and validated on go1.25+, where the name is capped. Under go1.24.9 the uncapped name pushes the socket path over the 108-byte `sun_path` limit, so `bind` returns `EINVAL`. In the host-name case, one path component grows past `NAME_MAX` (255), so `mkdir` returns `ENAMETOOLONG`.

CI path lengths with `TMPDIR=/tmp`, measured from the run 38086335279 log:

```
108 /tmp/TestControllerAdapterMethodsReachTheManager_6871managerHAOpsUpdateHAWatchdog2036417995/001/control.sock
108 /tmp/TestLegacyReaderRepairWireFailsClosedWithoutRefusalClassification11360pending1360571901/001/events.sock
108 /tmp/TestTakeoverReadyRequiresEventStreamListenerBoundListenerBoundHelperConnected2641886254/001/events.sock
113 /tmp/TestEventStreamPolicyDenyGenerationAcrossBacklogAndReplay10978reader_backlog588562828/001/policy-events.sock
113 /tmp/TestPeerCredentialReadFailsClosed9003a_closed_connection_is_refused,_not_defaulted3366138415/001/closed.sock
130 /tmp/TestControllerAdapterMethodsReachTheManager_6871userspaceLinkControllerRecordDeferredWorkerArmDebt2679286387/001/control.sock
(hostname case: a single 367-byte path component)
```

The minimum failing length is 108 even with the 4-byte `/tmp`. Under go1.24.9 these tests therefore fail for any `TMPDIR`. They were never green on the module's declared toolchain. Checked at the commits that introduced two of them: 8f928fffe (`TestPeerCredentialReadFailsClosed9003`) and dbd544598 (`TestCommitCheckRejectsSystemHostname10003`) both FAIL the same way on go1.24.9. The failure stayed hidden until CI began running go1.24.9 on 2026-10-01.

The package already knows this pattern. `shortSockDir9322`, `shortSockDir10005`, `shortSockDir9770`, `shortSocketDir` (5839) and `shortTempDir7139` all exist because "t.TempDir()'s long sub-test name pushes an AF_UNIX path past the 108-byte sun_path limit" (`response_cap_diagnostic_9322_test.go:118`). ## #12569 — master RED: TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets restart premise broken by #11443 orphan xfrmi reap (follow-up #12553) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)
```

Follow-up of #12553 (per-test triage). Triaged firsthand on master `89223b7fa` and re-confirmed RED on tip `2f73d41da`.

## Classification
**(b) stale fixture.** The premise of the `untracked after daemon restart` subtest was removed on purpose by #11443 "reap orphan tunnels on restart". The `LinkDel fails` subtest still passes.

## Firsthand RED (89223b7fa, go1.24.9)
Fails alone, `count=1` (1/1) and `count=3` (3/3). The result is the same on go1.26.8.

```
2026/10/10 17:19:54 INFO xfrmi orphan reaped name=st10
    secure_tunnel_parent_redirect_6691_test.go:957: premise broken: the xfrmi is gone, so there is nothing for the snapshot to adjudicate and this test proves nothing
--- FAIL: TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets/LinkDel_fails (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets/untracked_after_daemon_restart (0.00s)
```

## Cause (bisected)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/secure_tunnel_parent_redirect_6691_test.go:895-897` models route (b) as follows: "A fresh xfrmManager has EMPTY tracking, so the removed-desired delete pass has nothing to iterate and issues no LinkDel at all."

c66397134 `fix(11443): reap orphan tunnels on restart`, 2026-10-02, adds a `LinkList` orphan sweep to `xfrmManager.Apply` (`pkg/routing/xfrm.go`). It deletes every well-formed, untracked, undesired `*netlink.Xfrmi`. A fresh manager's `ApplyXfrmi(nil)` therefore now deletes `st10` from the fake kernel. That is exactly the post-restart leak #11443 set out to fix, so the subtest's precondition (line 956) can no longer hold.

Two-point bisect, go1.24.9, `go test -count=1 -run '^TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets$' ./pkg/dataplane/userspace`:
```
c66397134^ (9b4e15aea)  PASS
c66397134              FAIL  (untracked_after_daemon_restart: "premise broken: the xfrmi is gone")
```

This is not a product regression. After #11443, a retained live xfrmi after restart can still arise only when the orphan reap itself cannot delete the link. Two paths do that:
- `LinkDel` fails with something other than not-found. The sweep then returns `delete orphan xfrmi …`.
- `LinkList` fails. The sweep is skipped "retrying on next apply".

Those are the states the restart cell would need to model if F3 coverage of the restart route is kept.

## Repro
```
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.24.9 GOTMPDIR=/var/tmp TMPDIR=/var/tmp go test -count=1 -v -run '^TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets$' ./pkg/dataplane/userspace
```

## Fix direction (not implemented by this triage)
Re-express route (b) as "restart + orphan-reap LinkDel/LinkList failure", where the device genuinely survives. If the owner judges the restart route closed by #11443, delete the subtest and update the doc comment at lines 884-901. Either change is test-only.

## #12570 — master RED: TestUpdateInstances_TrackFieldChangeInPlace fails on hosts with eth0: unstubbed resolveIface hits #2294 drift probe (follow-up #12553) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up of #12553 (per-test triage). Triaged firsthand on master `89223b7fa`. The failing file is unchanged on tip `2f73d41da`.

## Classification
**(c) environment-dependent test.** It fails deterministically on any host that has an interface literally named `eth0`, such as GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners, and passes on hosts without one. It is not a flake: in every environment tried, the result is 3/3 one way or the other. It is not a product regression.

## Firsthand evidence (89223b7fa, go1.24.9, test binary from `go test -c ./pkg/vrrp`)
On the triage host, which has no `eth0`, the test PASSES alone, `count=1` (1/1) and `count=3` (3/3), with both go1.24.9 and go1.26.8. To match the CI runner, the same binary was run in a user+net namespace with a dummy `eth0` and `CAP_NET_RAW`/`CAP_NET_ADMIN` dropped, since CI runs the tests unprivileged.

```
=== netns WITH eth0, no CAP_NET_RAW (count=3) ===
INFO vrrp: restarting instance (ifindex changed) key=VI_eth0_101 old_ifindex=0
WARN vrrp: failed to open socket, keeping existing instance interface=eth0 have_existing=true err="listen ip4:112: listen ip4:112 0.0.0.0: socket: operation not permitted"
    track_test.go:176: track config = ""/0, want ge-0-0-9/50 (in-place update)
    track_test.go:179: trackDown not seeded from linkState on track-field change
    track_test.go:182: effective priority = 200, want 150
--- FAIL: TestUpdateInstances_TrackFieldChangeInPlace (0.00s)      x3

=== netns WITHOUT eth0, no CAP_NET_RAW (count=3) ===
INFO vrrp: in-place config update key=VI_eth0_101 old_pri=200 new_pri=200
--- PASS: TestUpdateInstances_TrackFieldChangeInPlace (0.00s)      x3
```

Full-package fidelity check (`vrrp.test -test.count=1`, no `-v`):
- With `eth0`: exactly one failure, `TestUpdateInstances_TrackFieldChangeInPlace`, with the same three `track_test.go:176/179/182` lines, preceded by the same `address watcher started` line as the CI log.
- Without `eth0`: `PASS`.

That matches CI run 38086335279, where this was the only failure in `pkg/vrrp`.

## Cause (bisected)
`pkg/vrrp/track_test.go:148-155` seeds an existing instance with `&net.Interface{Name: "eth0"}` (ifindex 0) but leaves `m.resolveIface` at its production default, `net.InterfaceByName` (`pkg/vrrp/manager.go:240`). `UpdateInstances` runs the #2294 ifindex-drift probe (`manager.go:600-602`): `probe, probeErr := m.resolveIface(inst.Interface); if probeErr == nil && probe.Index != existing.iface.Index { ifindexChanged = true }`.
- **No `eth0` on the host:** the probe errors, which is treated as no drift. The in-place update applies the track fields and the test passes.
- **`eth0` present:** its real ifindex is not 0, so `ifindexChanged = true`. The test takes the build-before-teardown restart path. Unprivileged, `openInstanceSocket` fails with EPERM and the old instance is kept untouched (`manager.go:755-763`). `vi.cfg` never receives the track fields, which produces the three assertions above. With `CAP_NET_RAW`, the replacement would be built and `stop()` called on the never-`run()` seeded instance; locally that hung until killed.

Two-point bisect in the eth0 netns (no `CAP_NET_RAW`, go1.24.9, `count=3`):
```
d8e9cd824^ (9382e4856)  with-eth0: 3 PASS   no-eth0: 3 PASS
d8e9cd824              with-eth0: 3 FAIL   no-eth0: 3 PASS
```
d8e9cd824 is `vrrp: restart instance on member ifindex drift under unchanged config (#2294)`, 2026-06-22. The test has depended on the host since then. The failure stayed latent because developer and lab hosts have no `eth0`; the CI Go job (#11185, 2026-10-01) is the first runner with one.

`mgmtBackupRouterRoute` sets no LinkIndex, but the kernel reads the route back WITH LinkIndex — so the desired key (`...|0|...`) never matches the live key (`...|9|...`). Every apply re-installs the route, and every apply starting with it present also deletes it. Through `applyMgmtVRFRoutesTo` the route is present after odd applies, absent after even ones (proven S14 on a real kernel; base shows the same REPLACE+DEL pair).

## Impact
Reconcile runs on every commit, every DHCP lease change, and debt retry — the backup-router route flaps continuously. The 11449 fake hides it (no LinkIndex fill).

## Fix direction
Normalize the LinkIndex out of the presence comparison (or set it on the desired route); add a real-kernel reconcile-stability cell (two applies → still present, no DEL).

## #12602 — [follow-up #12189] harden seeded shard indices: low-byte-only placement allows 1-in-256 offline precomputation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up from hostile R2 review of #12404 (F-A, verified firsthand on the real tracker).

Both `fragment_overlap::overlap_shard_index_seeded` (mod.rs:208 + :226-227) and `fragment_assoc::frag_shard_index_seeded` (fragment_assoc/mod.rs:435-447) XOR the seed into the FNV offset basis and finish with a fixed multiplier. An FNV-1a step commutes with +256m, so the seed high 56 bits rotate ALL keys together — shard-sharing is decided by the low byte alone. Proven: offline 32-key set + victim (low-byte guess 0x5c) → ShardFull 995/1000 on matching seeds vs 2/1000 random.

Consequence: precomputed set wins ~1 boot in 256; any low-byte leak (e.g. probing with drop feedback, or the shared global seed leaking at flow-cache/session/ratelimit sites — R2) restores deterministic targeting. Still strictly better than base (deterministic).

Fix options: keyed PRF, or mix seed material in AFTER the FNV loop, ideally with per-site derived keys (decouples overlap from the shared hot-path seed). Regression must fix the low byte, vary the high bits, and assert the set scatters. Note: hardening changes hash output — regenerate the seed-0 fixture premise at mod.rs:2171.

## #12603 — [follow-up #12189/R3] FxHasher seed-additive: v6 flow-cache set index + session-map buckets collide for EVERY seed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

Follow-up from hostile R2 review of #12404 (R3), validated REAL-DEFECT by adversarial research (Muse-Spark lens, firsthand probes on real layouts).

MECHANISM (verified in vendored rustc-hash 2.1.1): FxHasher::with_seed is seed-ADDITIVE — h=(h+w)*K per word, finish=rotl26. The seed contributes S*K^n, a key-independent constant; key-pair deltas are seed-free. Set index = rotl26(h)&1023 = h bits 38..48, so any pair with weighted-word-difference 0 mod 2^48 collides for EVERY seed.

V6 WEAPONIZATION (proven): v6 keys carry two full u64 words per address (write_u128 = lo,hi), so the top 16 bits of each half (src segments s3,s7; dst s3,s7) are attacker-controlled zero-cost collision bits: 2^16-flow single-set cliques (256/256 in one set under 3 pinned seeds; 16-flow flood single-set 5000/5000 seeds; s3 sweep 256/256 all-seed). Same pairs collide in session-map low-16 buckets 0/8000 divergences (all-seed) at every real table size (<=2^18 buckets).

V4 NOT weaponizable (verified counter-reading): (src,sport) cliques capped at 2 flows vs 5 needed for 4-way churn; existing #2364 port-sweep tests pass while missing the defect (deltas always span low significant bits).

SIBLINGS CLEAN: fabric boost-mix, frag FNV+XOR+mul-shift, icmp diffuse64(seed^fold), CoS boost-mix (seed XORed then avalanched), syn_rate (seed as WRITTEN words through avalanching hash_bytes). fib.rs:1317 ECMP fixed-seed use is FINE (stability, not secrecy).

FIX (proven pattern in-tree): do NOT use FxHasher::with_seed for attacker-keyed placement. (1) flow_cache.rs:1054 set_index_seeded — write seed as first word via FxHasher::default (syn_rate.rs:269-271 pattern); add the v6 s3-clique as fail-on-revert adversarial test. (2) session/mod.rs SeededKeyMap/Seeded*Index FxSeededState — same fix via custom BuildHasher (seed-first-word). Priority: flow cache first (direct churn), session maps second.

## #12609 — sessions: stop count and census walks on cancellation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Problem

Several O(table) session-count and census paths do not observe caller cancellation. `SessionCount()` synchronously traverses both address-family maps without a context or callback, so a disconnected caller can keep the full scan and its admission slot until EOF. The session-gauge collector similarly walks both tables with callbacks that always continue and does not bind a failed scrape to its context. The #8597 peer-liveness probe calls `GetStatus`, which performs a full `SessionCount()` walk; the caller can give up while the peer keeps scanning.

Confirmed call sites include:
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_status.go` (`GetStatus`) and `server_show_system.go` (`show system buffers[-detail]`).
- `pkg/api/health.go` (`/api/v1/status`).
- ~~pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go (`setSessionsTotal` on the unfiltered `GetSessions` path)~~ — FIXED by #12395 (merged 2026-10-12); unfiltered totals now run on cancellable sampled iterators.
- `pkg/api/metrics_sessions.go` (the cached session-gauge v4/v6 census).

Admission limits bound concurrency but do not make these individual walks cancellable. This is separate from the request-context-aware iterator fix in #12181.

## Acceptance

- Propagate the caller/scrape context to each count/census walk and stop during either address-family pass after cancellation; do not start v6 after an aborted v4 pass.
- Do not publish partial counts as successful: gRPC returns the mapped Canceled/DeadlineExceeded status, REST does not write a success body after cancellation, and metrics preserve the last good snapshot while exposing the failed-scrape signal.
- Release any acquired session-walk slot on every exit.
- Add deterministic cancellation/deadline tests for each public surface and the metrics census, including cancellation during v4 and v6, slot release, and no partial publication. Run the affected package suites and race tests.

References: #12181 (review residual), #5782 (SessionCount admission), #8597 (peer probe classification).

## #12611 — all.proxy_ndp unset — unicast NUD forwarded never answered [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Defect
xpf enables IPv6 proxy NDP through the per-interface `proxy_ndp` sysctl (`pkg/dataplane/proxyarp.go:139`), but does not set `net.ipv6.conf.all.proxy_ndp`. In a two-namespace reproduction with forwarding enabled, an NTF_PROXY entry installed, `reth0.proxy_ndp=1`, `all.proxy_ndp=0`, and a default route over `reth0`, the upstream Neighbor Solicitation for a proxied target was forwarded out `reth0` (hop limit decreased from 255 to 254) and received no Neighbor Advertisement; the neighbor entry reached FAILED. Repeating with `all.proxy_ndp=1` produced the proxy reply.

## Impact
When the FIB sends forwarded unicast NUD probes back through the proxy interface and the dataplane passes NDP to the kernel, stale upstream entries may fail to recover through NUD. The behavior depends on routing and dataplane forwarding; the reproduction demonstrates the kernel/sysctl case, not that every deployment is affected.

## Requested fix
Determine and implement the supported proxy-NDP policy so forwarded unicast NUD probes for configured targets are answered reliably (including the default-route case), or make the unsupported topology explicit. Add regression coverage for both the configured per-interface setting and the required all-interface setting, and document the operational behavior.

## Provenance
Opus R2 review of PR #12387, residual R3. Two-namespace repro used per-interface `proxy_ndp=1`, `all.proxy_ndp=0/1`, an installed proxy neighbor entry, forwarding, and a default route; the packet capture showed the forwarded unicast NS and whether a reply arrived.
