## #12613 — Expand recursive static ECMP resolution safely [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

Follow-up from PR #12398 / issue #12183 (B2).

## Reproduced order-dependent resolution

A Rust forwarding-build snapshot has one connected interface (`192.168.0.1/24`, ifindex 201), one reachable neighbor (`192.168.0.253`), and these static routes:

- `10.10.0.0/24` (Q), next hops `[192.168.0.254, 192.168.0.253]` (G1 has no neighbor; G2 is reachable).
- `10.20.0.0/24` (P), next hops `[192.168.0.99, 10.10.0.1]` (dead direct A plus recursive R through Q).

On the PR implementation, 256 distinct per-flow hashes with Q ordered `[G1,G2]` all resolve P as `MissingNeighbor` (256/256); reversing only Q's next-hop order to `[G2,G1]` changes the same 256 hashes to `ForwardCandidate` (256/256). A temporary Rust probe in `afxdp::forwarding_build::tests::b2_order_probe_12398` measured these counts; the probe was removed from the fix branch after recording the result. Resolution currently returns the first terminal spec rather than representing every resolved active ECMP member, so harmless config order determines forwarding versus neighbor-miss behavior.

## Self-match defect

The same snapshot route index contains P itself. If a recursive gateway R lies inside P, longest-prefix lookup can choose P as the route covering R and resolve R through P's sibling member rather than walking up to the next less-specific route. A pure one-member self-cycle control does not expose this mixed-row case. A separate 256-flow probe measured duplicate trust-member slots (`192.168.0.99`, ifindex 201) and `MissingNeighbor` on all 256 flows, rather than selecting the usable untrust default. Add a regression with a mixed self-covering row and a usable less-specific/default route; assert self is excluded and the resolver walks up.

## Required fix and acceptance

1. Expand every eligible next-hop from the selected covering row into terminal FIB candidates instead of stopping at the first resolvable spec.
2. Exclude the route currently being resolved from covering-route candidates (or otherwise walk up to the next less-specific prefix when the best match is the route itself).
3. Preserve configured weights across expansion using an explicit, deterministic weight policy compatible with the `weight` fields on `RouteNextHopV4` and `RouteNextHopV6`; do not silently discard or arbitrarily reweight members.
4. Add v4/v6 regression cells for the 256-flow ordering fixture, first-spec dead/live permutations, preference tiers, and self-match with a live default. Verify both orders produce the same valid candidate set/forwarding outcomes and never self-resolve.

Do not fold this semantic/weight-policy change into the fail-closed IPv6 link-local safety fix; PR #12398 references this follow-up.


---

## #12615 — upgrade: superseded STOPPED cut can roll back to an unverified version [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Defect

Stale STOPPED recovery assumes `current` still names the known-good old version when a newer staged package supersedes the interrupted cut. After FLIP 6a has already repointed `current`, that assumption is false. Recovery starts the unit, clears the stale journal, and a fresh INIT reads the repointed `current` (for example, 2.0.0) as `PreviousVersion` without establishing that the version ever passed health. The unit start uses systemd's currently loaded ExecStart, which can still be the earlier known-good executable.

If the superseding cut then fails target health, auto-rollback selects this unverified `PreviousVersion` instead of the previously known-good runtime; for example, it can roll back to 2.0.0 rather than 1.0.0.

## Reproduction

1. Start on healthy 1.0.0 and begin a cut to 2.0.0.
2. Persist STOPPED and complete FLIP 6a (`current` -> 2.0.0), then interrupt before confirming the new runtime healthy.
3. Stage 3.0.0 before resuming the stale 2.0.0 cut.
4. Resume and force 3.0.0 health to fail.

Observed during the R2 review of #12389 (probe P4): the fresh cut records 2.0.0 as `PreviousVersion`, and failed 3.0.0 rollback restores 2.0.0 instead of known-good 1.0.0. The defect is present on both the pre-fold and reviewed #12389 heads.

## Relevant code (pinned at master 7b4fc7b0d; same lines at f7074cbe7 are :338, :384-415, :418-420, :440, :514)

- `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:364` — supersede condition.
- `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:410-441` — STOPPED else-arm: stale invariant comment at :411-413 says 'STOPPED (unit down, `current` still OLD)'; StartUnit runs at :416-438, then partials are removed and INIT resets.
- `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:444-446` — fresh INIT records `prev := r.readCurrentVersion()`.
- `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:466` and `:551` — restorableCurrentTarget leading to j.PreviousVersion.
- `docs/in-place-upgrade.md:67-73` — user-facing 'never flipped `current`' assumption.

This is adjacent to, and outside, #12174 STOPPED-resume scope.

## #12617 — userspace-fib: quadratic recursive-build cost on large learned tables [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Context

Recursive static route resolution scans every route in the selected table for each gateway probe (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/fib.rs`, `recursive_static_target_v4` and `recursive_static_target_v6`). The 512-probe work budget limits probe count but does not bound the cost of each full-table scan; results for repeated `(table, gateway)` probes are not cached.

The release-build scaling probe used learned-style rows with a bare gateway outside the connected /32. Measurements were:

| Rows | Recursive resolution | Recursion-off baseline |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8,000 | 480 ms | 6.7 ms |
| 16,000 | 981 ms | 13.8 ms |
| 32,000 | 8.75 s | 84 ms |
| 65,000 | 21.7 s | 62 ms |

The import path can emit non-link-local gateways without an interface (`pkg/routing/fibimport.go:424-436`), and `build_forwarding_state` runs synchronously in reconcile preflight (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs:319-330`). The importer limit is approximately 64,955 learned routes.

## Follow-up

Cache top-level `(table, gateway)` resolution results for one build or replace table-wide candidate scans with a prefix index. Add a deterministic probe-count test that pins the 512-probe budget and verifies exhaustion fails closed. Preserve same-table, family-specific LPM, discard, cycle, and explicit-interface behavior.

## #12620 — [follow-up #12191] restamp reads every new connection's conntrack row; catalog-epoch gate would remove it [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Defect

#12406 restamps the forward AppID on stale reverse/forward session hits.
Installs stamp `policy_revalidated_gen: 0`, so EVERY new connection's
first hits are Stale and take the restamp path: a BPF lookup + (with
the skip-unchanged fold) no write in steady state.

The lookup itself still runs per connection (SYN-ACK + first forward
ACK for TCP; first packet for UDP). The repo's own measurement is
~1.0-1.4us per conntrack-map syscall.

## Fix

Gate the restamp on catalog change instead of connection birth, e.g.:

- (i) stamp a per-session app-label epoch at the 4 publish sites and
  restamp only when it differs from a ForwardingState app-catalog epoch
  bumped only on compiled-catalog change; or
- (ii) re-resolve the label from the local catalog only when the
  revalidation generation advanced since the row was stamped.

Either removes the per-connection BPF read in steady state.

## Provenance

Residual from the #12406 confirm (Opus R2 NEEDS-FOLD 2026-10-12, B2).
Minimum skip-unchanged fold merged in #12406; this tracks zero-syscall
steady state.

retired on this path.

## Fix

Run applyBootstrapHostAuthorizationCloseout from the #12155 boot
teardown when FirstCommitTeardownOwed, with the same durable-intent
discipline. Pin with a boot-expired FIRST probe (Load -> replay ->
assert revoked).

through to permit.

Default-case (unbind/deny) unknown book-level entries on the tolerant
path; qualify-or-warn zone-local refs; append a compiled warning.

## #12625 — [follow-up #12216] static NAT ignores CollidingNames (then static-nat prefix-name resolves to ambiguous winner) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

address winner on the lenient path: CollidingNames[X]=true and
rule.Then=10.0.0.5/32, so the 1:1 NAT maps to a target picked by an

exemptions as match-all) or never-match (current sentinel) everywhere,

## #12655 — perf: loss userspace cluster capped ~6 Gbps — fabric virtio NIC in generic-XDP/copy mode (split-RG hop) [OPEN]

## Summary

Loss userspace cluster throughput does not scale and is far below the documented
baseline (22+ Gbps IPv4 / 19+ Gbps IPv6 at -P4, 25G mlx5 native-XDP class).
Measured 2026-10-13 on deployed `d137348df` (`0.0.20988+gd137348df866`),
both nodes, RG0/RG1 primary node0, RG2 (LAN reth1) primary node1.

## Measured scaling (sender, iperf3 -t 10, LAN host -> VLAN80 targets)

Targets: `172.16.80.200` / `2001:559:8585:80::200` (loss-userspace-cluster.env).

| Proto | P1 | P4 | P8 | P16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 1.96 Gbps / 0 retr | 5.05 Gbps / 328 | 5.81 Gbps / 1528 | 6.33 Gbps / 3127 |
| IPv6 | 2.24 Gbps / 0 retr | 3.68 Gbps / 0 | 5.62 Gbps / 330 | 6.47 Gbps / 4009 |

P4 is ~4-5x below baseline; P16 only reaches ~6.5 Gbps. This is not a
single-stream-only or single-queue-only failure: **every** stream count is low.

## Root cause (measured, not inferred)

Every transit packet is forwarded **across the cluster fabric**, and the fabric
leg is capped at ~6 Gbps:

1. Path (counter-delta proof, 10s -P8): LAN ingress on fw1 `ge-7-0-1`
   (mlx5 native, zero-copy), forwarded over fabric `ge-7-0-0` -> fw0
   `ge-0-0-0`, egress fw0 `ge-0-0-2` (mlx5 native, zero-copy) to WAN.
   ~4.96M fabric packets in 10s on both fabric links; RG split
   (RG1/WAN on node0, RG2/LAN on node1) forces this hop for all LAN->WAN traffic.
2. `ge-0-0-0`/`ge-7-0-0` (fab0 member) is a **virtio_net** NIC (incus `eth2` on
   host bridge `bpu-fab0`, MTU 9000 in guest, 1500 on host bridge) attached in
   **generic (SKB) XDP mode**. xpfd log on fw0 (every boot, incl. 04:02
   d137348df deploy):
   `native XDP unavailable for userspace shim; falling back to generic (skb-mode) ifindex=4 err="attach XDP to ifindex 4: failed to attach link: create link: invalid argument" impact="higher CPU, ~6 Gbps cap; ..."`
   The loader's own warning (`pkg/dataplane/loader.go:391-393`) predicts the
   observed ~6 Gbps ceiling exactly.
3. Rust AF_XDP consequently binds the fabric interface COPY-only
   (`bind.rs: interface_uses_generic_xdp` -> COPY_ONLY for non-virtio... it is
   virtio so AUTO, but kernel XSK is generic: bindings show `zero_copy=False
   mode=copy` on ge-0-0-0/ge-7-0-0, vs `zero_copy=True` on all mlx5 ifaces).

*(truncated — 73 lines total)*

## #12658 — test/incus: post-deploy reassert never re-issues a refused RG transfer — cluster left split-RG, LAN↔WAN capped ~6 Gbps [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Summary

`deploy_reassert_primary_node0` (test/incus/deploy-lib.sh) sends **one** transfer per
redundancy group. It never re-sends a transfer that node0 refused. On the loss userspace
cluster, the RG2 (LAN `reth1`) transfer is routinely refused for about 2 s. As a result,
3 of the 4 rolling deploys on 2026-10-13 left the cluster **split-RG**: RG0/RG1 on node0,
RG2 on node1. With `preempt` off, nothing moves RG2 back. Every LAN→WAN flow then crosses
the virtio fabric, which runs generic XDP (#12655). Throughput stops scaling at about
6 Gbps. This is the "throughput doesn't scale / not line rate" report.

## Mechanism (from the logs, not inferred)

Per-deploy transfer requests that fw1 received from node0 (`remote failover request from peer`):

| deploy (UTC) | build | RGs transferred to node0 |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-02 01:53 / 02:12 / 12:39 | Oct-2 builds | 0, 1, 2 |
| 2026-10-13 03:25 | 948761f80 | 0, 1, 2 |
| 2026-10-13 03:33 | e81ddac8b | 0, 1 only |
| 2026-10-13 03:40 | c2aa3f8d9 | 0, 1 only |
| 2026-10-13 04:02 | d137348df | 0, 1 only, so RG2 stayed on node1 until a manual move at 04:30 |

fw0 journal for the 03:33 deploy:

```
03:33:05.036 cluster sync: failover ack received rg=1 req_id=2
03:33:05.233 cluster: RG readiness: not ready rg=2 reasons="[userspace XSK liveness not proven]"
03:33:05.910 cluster: failover reset rg=2          <- reassert's leading reset; the transfer that follows is refused
03:33:07.111 cluster: RG readiness: ready rg=2     <- ready again ~2 s later; no transfer is ever re-sent
```

- `RequestPeerFailover` refuses a request when `!rg.IsReadyForTakeover(...)`
  (`pkg/cluster/failover.go:468-482`). The default `takeoverHoldTime` is 0, so the
  refusal lasts only as long as the not-ready window.
- `takeoverReadyLocked` adds `userspace XSK liveness not proven` when
  `!xskLivenessProven && !standbyBindingsReadyLocked()`
  (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:477`). `standbyBindingsReadyLocked` returns
  false as soon as the node holds an active data RG (`manager_ha.go:533`). So a freshly
  cut node0 that has not yet proven XSK liveness flips RG2 to not-ready the moment RG1
  lands on it. WAN RX proves liveness about 2 s later. The 03:25 deploy and the Oct-2

*(truncated — 84 lines total)*

## #12659 — test/incus: #7962 liveness priming never runs from cluster-setup.sh deploy — CLUSTER_LAN_HOST is never set [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-13)

## Summary

The #7962 liveness priming in `deploy_reassert_prime_liveness`
(`test/incus/deploy-lib.sh`) never runs on the `make cluster-deploy` /
`cluster-setup.sh deploy all` path. Every real deploy therefore verifies in the
**fallback** regime, which is the 150 s degraded-promotion budget.

## Evidence

- `deploy_reassert_prime_liveness` returns 1 unless `CLUSTER_LAN_HOST` and
  `IPERF_TARGET4` are both set (`deploy-lib.sh`, `local lan="${CLUSTER_LAN_HOST:-}"`).
- `cluster-setup.sh` sources the env file (`$BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV`),
  `cluster-lock.sh`, `cluster-build-identity.sh` and `deploy-lib.sh`. None of
  them sets `CLUSTER_LAN_HOST`. Only `cluster-env.sh` derives it from
  `LAN_HOST`, and the deploy path never sources that file. The env file sets
  `LAN_HOST="cluster-userspace-host"`, but nothing reads that name here.
- A live rolling deploy on 2026-10-13
  (`XPF_CLUSTER_SKIP_BUILD=1 BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV=test/incus/loss-userspace-cluster.env ./test/incus/cluster-setup.sh deploy all`)
  printed:
  `==> Re-asserted node0 primary for all redundancy groups (post-deploy, verified; fallback regime).`

## Impact

- The priming that ha-failover-status.md (#7962) describes as "converges the
  common case in seconds" is dead code for deploys. On an idle cluster the
  reassert waits on the 120 s degraded fallback.
- When a deploy fails, the diagnosis always takes the "precondition was absent"
  branch, even when a LAN host and target exist.
- This did not cause #12658: on the loss cluster, ambient WAN RX proved node0
  XSK liveness about 2 s after RG1 landed. But it removes the one mechanism
  meant to supply that proof on a quiet cluster.

## Expected

The deploy path resolves the LAN host the same way the HA smokes do (the
`cluster-env.sh` `LAN_HOST` → `CLUSTER_LAN_HOST` bridge, remote-qualified), so
priming runs. A wiring selftest cell should fail if `cluster-setup.sh` stops
supplying it.

Origin claim D8-07 from Gemini deep-review run review-work.B6GmJdbjWS (verified at 29456d1e5; re-validated today).

Evidence (lane synthesis, full text in research result report-gemini-4-argon-high-review-security-policies-and-zone-policies-001.md):

## D8-07 — MATERIAL; Medium
**Strongest defect:** On scheduler-config change, the daemon constructs a fresh primed scheduler before carrying the previous evaluation timestamp and wall-recovery state (`pkg/daemon/daemon_scheduler.go:41-81`). Initial `evaluate` sees zero `lastEval`, cannot recognize a jump between previous tick and commit, and `CarryRecoveryStateFrom` copies timestamps/holds and only forces inactive on a **previously existing** hold/latch; it does not compare current `now` to the copied history (`pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go:109-133,397-429,443-469`). The replacement can publish a permissive window until a later tick detects the discontinuity. **Best refutation/limit:** A hold *already set* is copied and actively suppresses new state (`scheduler.go:423-427`); this is a fresh jump since the previous evaluation, not every commit. Current tolerance is **5 seconds**, not the old claim's 90 seconds (`scheduler.go:89-92`). Work is at apply/tick time, not per-packet. **Decisive check:** Two `time.Time` values preserving their monotonic interval but with wall jump >5s across old lastEval→changed-config prime; inspect the very first published active map *before* any background tick.


Severity (origin): Medium. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## D8-08 — MATERIAL; High
**Strongest defect:** Before applying a changed scheduler config, `policySchedulerActiveStateAndFailClosedForApplyLocked` asks the previous scheduler for `(activeState, failClosed)` then primes **new** active states, suppressing them only when `republishFailClosed` is true (`pkg/daemon/daemon_scheduler.go:89-109`). `ActiveStateWithFailClosed` returns only that republish latch, not `unsafeUntil` (`pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go:196-207`). Consequently an existing wall-clock recovery hold with `republishFailClosed=false` can seed scheduled permits active in the snapshot applied **before** reconciliation (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:116-118,203-208,277-278`); the replacement's later `CarryRecoveryStateFrom` suppression (`pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go:397-429`) is too late for that publish. **Best refutation/limit:** Same-hash config returns previous already-inactive map; an independent republish-failure latch also suppresses. Only changed scheduler hash during an active clock hold escapes. Helper heartbeat lease is not a guard against a newly published, fresh-but-incorrect active map. **Decisive check:** Force old scheduler into unsafe hold, modify scheduler configuration so new window is active at apply time, examine the snapshot actually passed to `ApplyConfig`, then post-reconcile state and rollback invalidation decisions.

FRR discards non-IP `nh.Address` (`pkg/frr/config_render.go:515-527`), rather than rendering an interface route. The IPsec route-selector validator skips interface-only entries, but checks full destination coverage within individual VPN candidate lists (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_ipsec_route_ts_11422.go:53-86,103-134`); two different VPNs each covering a complementary half of a destination can be rejected despite their aggregate coverage. The newly landed `#12790` guard only rejects a **dangling QNH keyword tail** (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_static_route_interface_qnh_tail_12790.go:5-30`); it does not normalize a complete interface-valued QNH.
- **Best refutation:** plain `next-hop st0.0` works; IP-based qualified next hops and the new `#12790` syntax gate work for their distinct cases. A union of complementary VPN selectors must also be deployable in routing terms; this is not a license to install an ambiguous VPN route.
- **Decisive check:** strict and tolerant compile/render matrices for `qualified-next-h

Severity (origin): Medium. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## #12910 — [research D10-09] screen-probe.sh` queries labeled Prometheus metric `xpf_screen_drops_by_reason_total` with an exact `$1 == m`  [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

What happens: screen-probe.sh` queries labeled Prometheus metric `xpf_screen_drops_by_reason_total` with an exact `$1 == m` awk match, making the witness counter permanently unreadable (`VOID`) on every live run

Validated by three-way adversarial research (Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus + Muse-Spark lanes, blinded, at origin/master 255bd90c3): all three independently confirm this defect at current master. Origin claim D10-09 from Gemini deep-review run review-work.B6GmJdbjWS (verified at 29456d1e5; re-validated today).

Evidence (lane synthesis, full text in research result report-gemini-4-argon-high-review-security-policies-and-zone-policies-001.md):

## D10-09 — MATERIAL, Medium: screen witness metric parser cannot read labeled series
- **Defect/evidence:** `test/incus/screen-probe.sh:60-65,139-149` passes metric name `xpf_screen_drops_by_reason_total` to an awk equality test on `$1`. The exporter declares **only labeled** `xpf_screen_drops_by_reason_total{reason=...}` (`pkg/api/metrics_descriptors_global.go:148-162`); bare `$1 == m` cannot match those series, so the witness samples are empty and verdict is VOID despite actual counter increases.
- **Best refutation:** the **subject** is already the correct aggregate `xpf_screen_drops_total` (`screen-probe.sh:140,149`), and the per-reason metric is appropriate *for a deliberately triggered named-screen witness* (closed issue #8336). The packet's reference to `pkg/dataplane/userspace/exporter.go` is not a current file; actual metric descriptor is `pkg/api/metrics_descriptors_global.go`.
- **Decisive check:** feed a bounded Prometheus text fixture with a labeled per-reason witness increment to the shell metric extractor/verdict library; confirm witness detected and the intended DROP/PASS polarity.


Severity (origin): High. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## #12911 — [research D10-10] screen-probe.sh` exits `0` (false PASS) when `screen_probe_verdict` returns `PASSED` (screen bypass), masks `c [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

What happens: screen-probe.sh` exits `0` (false PASS) when `screen_probe_verdict` returns `PASSED` (screen bypass), masks `cleanup FAIL` with `exit 2` on `VOID`, and never acquires the `cluster-cell.sh` lock it claims to take

Validated by three-way adversarial research (Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus + Muse-Spark lanes, blinded, at origin/master 255bd90c3): all three independently confirm this defect at current master. Origin claim D10-10 from Gemini deep-review run review-work.B6GmJdbjWS (verified at 29456d1e5; re-validated today).

Evidence (lane synthesis, full text in research result report-gemini-4-argon-high-review-security-policies-and-zone-policies-001.md):

## D10-10 — MATERIAL, Medium for mutation-without-lock, Low for exit contract
- **Defect/evidence:** live screen probe's own header promises shared cluster-cell locking (`test/incus/screen-probe.sh:43-45`) but its script never sources/enters that cell before mutating both firewalls; its diagnostic can collide with another lane. It only fails process status for `VOID` or cleanup `FAIL` (`:151-169`); a witnessed subject `PASSED` falls through with rc0 and can be mistaken for a green DROP gate by an exit-code-only caller.
- **Best refutation:** `PASSED` is a distinct **diagnostic result**, not necessarily a failed process contract if operators consume the printed verdict. The script does call `disarm` before normal exit (`:155-158`) and uses an EXIT cleanup trap; the packet's assertion of wholly unguarded cleanup is too broad. `test/incus/HARNESSES.unreached:95` calls the live script diagnostic; do not assert an existing CI target actually interprets rc0 as a successful block.
- **Decisive check:** inspect the *actual* invoking workflow for required DROP outcome, then a hermetic exit-status cell for `PASSED`; separately verify shared-lock entry on the live command path, without running it.


Severity (origin): High. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## #12912 — [research D10-11] test-host-inbound.sh` shares one `HI_SSH_LISTENER_MARK` across ports 22 and 23 and omits a non-empty `sockpids [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

What happens: test-host-inbound.sh` shares one `HI_SSH_LISTENER_MARK` across ports 22 and 23 and omits a non-empty `sockpids` check in `start_ssh_probe_listener`, allowing a missing port-23 listener to pass all telnet `DENY` cells vacuously

Validated by three-way adversarial research (Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus + Muse-Spark lanes, blinded, at origin/master 255bd90c3): all three independently confirm this defect at current master. Origin claim D10-11 from Gemini deep-review run review-work.B6GmJdbjWS (verified at 29456d1e5; re-validated today).

Evidence (lane synthesis, full text in research result report-gemini-4-argon-high-review-security-policies-and-zone-policies-001.md):

## D10-11 — MATERIAL, Medium: host-inbound listener presence gate passes on zero sockets
- **Defect/evidence:** `test/incus/test-host-inbound.sh:174-182` starts both TCP/22 and /23 children under the **same** marker; `:192-206` gets *any* owned marker PID and then iterates `for spid in $sockpids` for each port. If /23 has no wildcard listener, its empty `sockpids` produces zero checks while /22 keeps `owned` nonempty; despite its comment `:184-191`, the gate reaches `:209` and claims both sockets verified.
- **Best refutation:** a nonempty wrong-owner socket PID is correctly rejected and loopback-only sockets are excluded by `hi_wildcard_socket_pids`; the bug is the **empty** list and lack of port-specific ownership, not every foreign socket.
- **Decisive check:** hermetic `ss`/`pgrep` fixtures with owned TCP/22 only (no /23), foreign TCP/23, and both owned; assert only the last passes before host-inbound verdicts are scored.


Severity (origin): High. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## #12913 — [research D10-12] policy_scheduler_validate.py` lacks any positive traffic or deny control during the `inactive` scheduler windo [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-14)

What happens: policy_scheduler_validate.py` lacks any positive traffic or deny control during the `inactive` scheduler window, coerces JSON boolean `true` to integer `1` in `_as_int`, and omits byte-monotonicity validation on `failover

Validated by three-way adversarial research (Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus + Muse-Spark lanes, blinded, at origin/master 255bd90c3): all three independently confirm this defect at current master. Origin claim D10-12 from Gemini deep-review run review-work.B6GmJdbjWS (verified at 29456d1e5; re-validated today).

Evidence (lane synthesis, full text in research result report-gemini-4-argon-high-review-security-policies-and-zone-policies-001.md):

## D10-12 — MATERIAL, Medium for absent inactive witness, Low for schema/bytes nuances
- **Defect/evidence:** `test/incus/policy_scheduler_validate.py:135-167` requires active traffic, monotonic active→rebuild and exact inactive==rebuild counters, but no evidence that traffic was *offered* during the inactive scheduler period. An inactive artifact copied from rebuild can pass with zero probe traffic. Failover tests packets advancing but not bytes (`:159-167`). `_as_int:46-54` explicitly coerces JSON booleans into 0/1 and defaults invalid numbers to zero.
- **Best refutation:** it *does* enforce an active positive packet count (`:139-142`), active→rebuild byte monotonicity (`:148-151`), userspace runtime identity (`:57-68`) and a strict missing-scheduler negative artifact (`:169-176`). It is an artifact validator, not proof that its upstream traffic generator actually omitted inactive traffic; the missing witness is the source-supported assurance gap.
- **Decisive check:** hermetic copy of rebuild status to inactive status while keeping all other valid artifacts, plus failover packets incremented/bytes regressed and boolean `rule_id`/counter fields; determine intended schema and whether a separate accepted inactive-window traffic witness exists.


Severity (origin): Medium. Fix direction and acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed.

## #13404 — [regression] stale-reply VRF fallback ANDs multiple VRF masters into one unsatisfiable guard (199c972f1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

## Verified defect (hostile review of `git log origin/master -30`)

Commit `199c972f102abb96964af70a15cc721e73ce3505` (nftables: scope stale-reply guards to VRF members, #13170) introduced per-master VRF fallback guards in `HostInboundStaleReplyGuardRules`. On current `origin/master` (`f7492bd5c`), the **daemon text oracle** renders each `IngressVRFScopes` entry of a *single* rule as conjunctive predicates on that same rule, while the netlink emitter does the same — so a rule carrying **two** VRF scopes can never match.

### Evidence (exact lines on f7492bd5c)

- `pkg/nftables/stale_reply_catalog.go` — fallback loop emits **one guard per master** (correct, one scope per rule): `appendOwnerGuards(nil, false, []config.HostInboundVRFIngressScope{{Master: master, Slaves: slaves}}, true)`. So catalog output itself has ≤1 scope/rule today.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:1446-1453` (`hostInboundStaleReplyGuardText`): 
  ```go
  for _, vrf := range guard.IngressVRFScopes {
      scope += "iifname " + nftIifnameSet([]string{vrf.Master}) + " "
      ... meta sdifname (!)= ...
  }
  ```
  Two scopes ⇒ `iifname {masterA} iifname {masterB} meta sdifname != {...} meta sdifname != {...}` — a packet has exactly one iifname, so the rule is **unsatisfiable / dead**.
- `pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound.go:162-169` (`emitHostInboundStaleReplyGuards`) has the identical loop: `rule.iifname([]string{scope.Master})` per scope on one rule — same AND semantics.

### Why this is filed despite catalog emitting 1 scope/rule today
The rule struct `StaleReplyGuardRule.IngressVRFScopes []config.HostInboundVRFIngressScope` (slice, `pkg/nftables/stale_reply_catalog.go:139`) plus both renderers silently produce dead rules for the multi-scope shape, and no test covers it: `pkg/nftables/stale_reply_vrf_13170_test.go` only exercises a **single** master (`vrf-blue`). Any future (or out-of-tree/test) construction with 2 scopes — the natural coalescing a follow-up would do to reduce rule count — silently drops stale-reply protection (fail-open for denied-service replies) with no error from `nft -c` (repeated iifname matches are syntactically valid).

### Expected
Renderers must either (a) reject/ignore >1 scope with an explicit error, or (b) expand multi-scope rules into one rule per scope. Add a regression with two distinct VRF masters in one guard asserting each rendered rule contains exactly one `iifname` master predicate (text + netlink parity).

### Severity / scope
Latent fail-open in stale-reply guard rendering; not triggered by today's catalog (1 scope/rule). No production path currently emits multi-scope guards — verified by reading all `StaleReplyGuardRule{` constructions on f7492bd5c.

## #13405 — [review] last-30 squash commits da763c1bb + c3be1ffc4 lack PR-number suffix required by commit standard [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

## Commit-message standard defect (hostile review of `git log origin/master -30`)

Campaign standard: every squash-commit subject is `<area>: <imperative summary> (#NNNN)` where the trailing `(#NNNN)` is the **PR number**, plus Why/What/Validation/Risk body. On current `origin/master` `f7492bd5c`, 28/30 in-window subjects carry both issue `(#13xxx)` and PR `(#13yyy)`; two carry only the issue number and no PR suffix:

- `da763c1bb62e47a904a1b82fa06efdd8534553a6` — `userspace-dp: deny unzoned VRRP VIPs (#13158)` (single `(#13158)`, no PR number)
- `c3be1ffc4749cf33bc51b784daa22f3279e832fe` — `firewall: protect lifeline-shared host inbound addresses (#13159)` (single `(#13159)`, no PR number)

Both have complete Why/What/Validation/Risk bodies (verified), so this is subject-format only. Contrast in-window conforming examples: `72c7bc91a ... (#13176) (#13399)`, `bca57f7d9 ... (#13174) (#13398)` (also note `bca57f7d9` uses capitalised `Track` after `daemon:` — imperative but capitalised, minor style drift vs lower-case peers).

Impact: traceability only — `git log --grep` by PR number and PR↔commit linkage miss these two landings. No code defect. Suggest: enforce subject regex in the squash-merge template; cannot rewrite landed master history.

Filed by hostile final review; read-only, no history rewritten.

## #13411 — [regression #13170] direct stale-reply fallback also matches covered VRF ingress [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

Astra hostile review of f7492bd5c. Evidence: pkg/nftables/stale_reply_catalog.go:285-313 (fallback excludes direct ingress names but not VRF masters); pkg/nftables/netlink_hostinbound.go:154-172. With trusted reinjection the fallback exclusion list is nonempty even in VRF-only configs, so iifname != xpf-usp0 ... drop matches iifname=vrf-blue covered slaves whose ingress zone permits the service — defeating #13170. ## #13419 — preserve endpoint-pinned GRE TUN-origin forwards [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

# Context

PR #13410 stamped the forward GRE TUN-origin `SessionDecision` with the tunnel's inner routing-instance identity, based on source finding D6-08 / issue #13182. That premise is incorrect for endpoint-pinned tunnel sessions: `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_session_with_cache` validates nonzero install-table stamps before its tunnel branch, then the tunnel branch re-resolves through `resolve_tunnel_forwarding_resolution` and does not perform a destination-table lookup. The ordinary miss stamp policy also explicitly keeps tunnel outcomes at `(0,0)` (`install_table_stamp_for_miss`, #9752/#12056).

Consequently, if the tunnel endpoint and underlay remain usable but the unrelated inner `cust` install-table row is absent, the new forward stamp returns `TableUnavailable` before endpoint re-resolution. The unstamped endpoint-pinned decision still resolves to the configured GRE endpoint. This is an unnecessary fail-closed regression, not a route-leak fix.

# Expected behavior

Keep GRE TUN-origin forward decisions table-free at `(0,0)` and preserve the existing table-scoped reverse synthesis. Pin the behavior with a real builder/session-resolver regression: start with a present `cust.inet.0` row, remove that row while retaining the GRE endpoint and underlay, and assert the forward decision re-resolves to `ForwardCandidate` on that endpoint. The same test must fail against #13410's nonzero forward stamp.

This corrects a regression introduced by #13410 and records that D6-08's source claim overlooked the endpoint-pinned tunnel re-resolution contract.

## #13443 — [regression #13414] validate native VLAN ownership against surviving zone [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

Regression introduced by the #13414 native-VLAN host-inbound fix (PR #13433). A unique matching native VLAN unit is not sufficient to prove that the unit owns the parent traffic in the inherited zone.

Reproduction: configure tagged unit .200 in security zone lan and `native-vlan-id 100`, while unit .100 (`vlan-id 100`) is unzoned (or belongs to a different zone). `InterfaceZoneMap` fans lan from .200 onto the base. `nativeVLANUnitRefs` sees the unique VID match on .100 without checking its surviving snapshot zone, so hostInboundUnzonedFanUpBaseRows suppresses the unzoned parent guard; the host-inbound view then uses the inherited base zone with .100 policy lookup and falsely claims parent traffic for lan. This is fail-open/misclassification.

Acceptance: native parent ownership must derive from the matching unit row’s surviving zone, not a fan-up base label. If native unit is unzoned/quarantined/owned by a different zone than the base’s surviving zone, keep parent ingress and addresses on the unzoned fail-closed path. Preserve valid same-zone native access, no-native/unresolved/ambiguous behavior, and test unit-specific host-inbound overrides. Include regression for mixed-zone and unzoned native units.

## #13444 — VRF lifeline stale-reply fallback misses lifeline-only masters [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

A review after #13413 landed found one remaining stale-reply fallback path. When a VRF has only lifeline slaves, `LifelineVRFScopes` is not added to `coveredDirect`, so the direct negated fallback still matches the VRF master (`iifname vrf-blue`) before the scoped `sdifname` exclusion can preserve `fxp0`. This drops shared-address management replies.

The correction must exclude lifeline-only VRF masters from the direct fallback for `IngressDenyV4/V6` addresses, retain the existing direct fallback for ordinary owner-denied addresses, apply the VRF-scoped fallback to non-lifeline members, and avoid emitting empty-slave VRF guards for ordinary addresses.

Regression acceptance: a lifeline-only VRF shared address preserves the lifeline reply and still guards data/non-lifeline ingress; ordinary owner-denied addresses retain the existing direct fallback and do not gain an empty-slave VRF guard. Follow-up discovered during review of PR #13442.

## #13476 — [nfqueue] Atomically claim eligible flow heads before dispatch [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

## Summary
`CapturePipeline.dispatchEligible` can dispatch the same flow head concurrently. The helper snapshots eligible heads under `p.mu`, unlocks, then invokes phase dispatch; it does not claim/reserve heads before releasing the lock.

## Evidence
On current `master`, `pipeline.go:637-655` snapshots `p.eligibleLocked()` and unlocks before dispatching. `Poll` calls this helper at line 1228; ingress `consumeFrames` calls it at line 630; scoped `Cancel` also calls it (added in #13233). These are not serialized by a shared dispatch lock.

For enforcing work, `submitEligible` performs zone evaluation before locking to inspect/reserve the flow head (`pipeline.go:933-950`). Two callers can snapshot the same frame. If one reserves first, the other sees `flow.pending != nil` and calls `finishFrame(frame, VerdictDrop)` at lines 939-945, removing/terminalizing the same original while the first caller is still admitting it. D11 attestation has the analogous flow-pending check in `attestSubmit` (`pipeline_attest_10484.go:925-943`), where the losing dispatcher records a failure and terminalizes the packet while the winner's submission continues.

Interleavings include scoped Cancel dispatch overlapping Poll after a completion makes a queued follower eligible, and Poll dispatch overlapping ingress dispatch. This can cause duplicate admission attempts, premature DROP of an in-flight original, inconsistent ledger/completion state, or double terminalization.

## Fix direction
Add an atomic eligibility claim under the pipeline lock before dispatch (or equivalent per-flow dispatch state), and ensure only the claim owner can release/terminalize that head. Preserve Poll progress while a submitter call is in flight; do not make Poll wait on the broad drain/submit lock.

## Provenance
Adjacent concurrency risk observed while implementing #13233 (research-validated finding D5-02). Source-level interleaving trace above is reproducible by concurrent dispatcher invocation; no code change for this separate issue is included in #13233.

## #13627 — cli: remote 'show system storage' broken by dispatch-parity change (#13551) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

## Defect

Commit `cc0e2df0a5f55535deb0715b738ef0fef10a3382` (`cli: restore remote command dispatch parity (#13551) (#13610)`, on `origin/master`) removed the remote-CLI dispatch for `show system storage` while reworking `cmd/cli/show_system.go` for `processes summary` / `configuration rescue`.

## Evidence (origin/master @ b99ed2bce)

- Before `cc0e2df0a`: `cmd/cli/show_system.go` had `case "storage": return c.showCommand("show system storage")`, which resolves via `pkg/cmdtree/showtext_topic.go:167` (`"storage": "show system storage"`) to the `storage` ShowText topic rendered by `pkg/grpcapi/server_show.go` (`case "storage": s.showStorage(&buf)`).
- After `cc0e2df0a` (current `origin/master:cmd/cli/show_system.go`): the `handleShowSystem` switch has cases `uptime/memory/processes/configuration/alarms/users/connections/.../boot-messages/...` but **no `storage` case** (verified: `git grep "\"storage\"" origin/master -- cmd/cli` returns nothing). The `default:` arm returns `unknown show system target: storage`.
- The server side is fully intact: `GetSystemInfo` still handles `case "storage":` in `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_status.go`, `systemInfoCanonicalCommand` still maps `"storage" -> "show system storage"` in `pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_gate_7172.go`, and the ShowText `storage` topic still exists. Only the remote client dispatch was dropped.
- The commit message claims "No unrelated dispatches changed" — this removal is an unrelated dispatch change/regression.

## Consequence

Remote operators running `show system storage` via the shipped `cli` binary now get `unknown show system target: storage` instead of filesystem usage. The embedded/on-box CLI (`pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go:989` `case "storage"`) still works, so this is a remote-only regression — the exact parity class #13551 was fixing.

## Expected

Restore `case "storage": return c.showCommand("show system storage")` (or `showSystemInfo("storage")`) in `cmd/cli/show_system.go` `handleShowSystem`, with a dispatch-parity regression test alongside the existing `dispatch_parity_13551_test.go` cases.

Found by hostile review of `git log origin/master -25`.

## #13628 — cli: remote annotate truncates comments containing embedded double quotes (#13554) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-15)

## Defect

Commit `73ea9f1dfc9d63adaf9130eadee248e88fe5735a` (`cli: dispatch annotate mutations remotely (#13554) (#13625)`) rebuilds the annotate line in `cmd/cli/shared.go` by interpolating the parsed comment verbatim into double quotes:

```go
input := "annotate " + strings.Join(fullPath, " ") + " \"" + comment + "\""
```

`cliterm.AnnotateCommentFromLine` (`pkg/cliterm/terminal.go`) splits on the **first** `"` and strips only one matching outer quote layer (`StripSurroundingQuotes`). A comment containing an embedded double quote therefore does not round-trip.

## Evidence (origin/master @ b99ed2bce)

- `origin/master:pkg/cliterm/terminal.go`: `AnnotateCommentFromLine` returns `StripSurroundingQuotes(line[quoteIdx:])`; for input `system "say "hi" team"` the captured comment is `say "hi" team` (outer quotes stripped, inner quote retained).
- `origin/master:cmd/cli/shared.go` (annotate case): re-emits `"say "hi" team"` wrapped in fresh double quotes.
- Server side `pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go` (`Server.Set` annotate arm) re-parses with the same `AnnotateCommentFromLine`, which again splits on the first quote and strips one outer layer — recovering only `say ` (up to the embedded quote; the remainder `hi" team"` is not part of the stripped string because `StripSurroundingQuotes` requires first==last quote, so it returns the raw segment, and tokenization via `lexConfigMutationLine9938` in `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go` treats `"say "` as one string token and `hi"` / `team"` as subsequent tokens).

Net effect: the stored annotation is silently truncated/corrupted relative to what the operator typed, and the authz gate (`AuthorizeConfigMutation` annotate arm, which drops the last token only when `quoted[last]`) adjudicates a different token stream than the store applies. The on-box CLI path (`pkg/cli/quote_strip.go: annotateCommentFromLine`, same helper) shares the first-quote split, but it does **not** re-serialize and re-parse the comment, so the remote path is strictly worse: it adds a lossy serialize→parse round-trip.

## Consequence

Remote `annotate <path> "say "hi" team"` (or any comment with an embedded `"`, e.g. quoting a Junos description) stores a mangled annotation without error. No validation rejects embedded quotes: `config.ValidateAnnotationText` (`pkg/config/freetext.go`) rejects only control chars and `/*`/`*/` delimiters.

## Expected

Either reject comments containing `"` at the remote dispatch (usage error), or transmit path/comment without re-serializing into a quoted line (e.g. structured fields), or escape embedded quotes consistently with the lexer (`NewLexer` string handling). Add a regression with an embedded-quote comment through `cmd/cli` dispatch → `Server.Set` → `AnnotateAsPlantClass`.

Found by hostile review of `git log origin/master -25`.

The #10988/#4800 newflow-ceiling harness cannot drive the pool-mode SNAT
path on the loss userspace cluster because the traffic generator client
cannot source from the prefix the pool rule matches. The committed rule
`pool-snat` in rule-set `lan-to-wan` matches only
`source-address 10.0.61.240/28` (deliberately unassigned: LAN host is
`10.0.61.102`, VIP `.1`, DHCP range `.100-.199`; see
`docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf` pool-snat comments and
`docs/userspace-newflow-ceiling.md` blocker 1, verified at source).
Adding a `.240/28` address to the LAN host for the duration (the
documented workaround) is not enough: the client never binds it.

## Source (origin/master 761931ff6)
- `test/incus/newflow-gen/src/main.rs`: `--bind` is parsed only for sink
  mode (binds the listener). Client mode connects with
  `TcpStream::connect_timeout(&addr, ...)` and no local bind, so the
  kernel picks the host's primary address (`10.0.61.102`) and traffic
  takes the sibling `rule snat` (interface mode) instead of the pool.
- `test/incus/newflow-ceiling-harness.sh` (line ~215) invokes
  `--mode client --target ... --dst-ports ... --rate ...` with no
  source-address option to pass through even if the generator had one.
- Result: pool sees ZERO allocations, which is the harness's first named
  refusal condition — every cell refuses, no ceiling number is possible.

Verified by a read-only probe on 2026-10-15 (since reverted): with
`10.0.61.241/28` temporarily on the LAN host, gateway+target pings
sourced from that address succeeded and one pool allocation appeared,
proving the prefix path works when traffic actually sources from it.

## Fix acceptance
- `newflow-gen` client mode accepts a source-bind option (e.g.
  `--src-bind <IP>`); the harness exposes/passes it (env or flag) so a
  run can bind the `.240/28` address added for the duration.
- Unit/synthetic coverage: client connects from the requested source
  address (loopback cell), and the analyzer's zero-pool-allocation
  refusal still fires when the pool path is not actually taken.
- No change to the committed cluster config or the pool rule's
  non-interference construction.

## Provenance

*(truncated — 45 lines total)*

## #13757 — test: harness census fails on master — test/incus/active-fw.sh is a sourced library, not a runnable harness [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Summary

`scripts/harness-census.sh` fails on current `origin/master`: `test/incus/active-fw.sh` is classified UNREACHED and undeclared — invoked by no Makefile recipe and not listed in `test/incus/HARNESSES.unreached`.

## Evidence

- Observed while landing PR #13756 (#13641): the `Harness census and self-test` CI job failed in 12s.
- Reproduced locally on a pristine `origin/master` worktree: `sh scripts/harness-census.sh` → `harness census: 66 runnable harnesses -- 33 reached, 30 declared unreached`, `FAILED (1 problem(s))`, sole complaint `test/incus/active-fw.sh`.
- #13756's diff touches only `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/` + `docs/log/13641.md`, so this is a pre-existing master condition, not PR-introduced.

## Mechanism

`test/incus/active-fw.sh` (added by #13069, deep-review D10-14) is a **sourced library**, not a runnable harness: it defines `active_fw_detect()` and is meant to be `source`d by CoS/fairness harnesses. The census classifies every `test/incus/*.sh` as a runnable harness and demands either a Makefile invocation or an `HARNESSES.unreached` declaration; a sourced library satisfies neither, and the census output itself notes that a mention/comment does not count as invocation.

## Suggested fix (pick one, census-sanctioned)

1. Add a line to `test/incus/HARNESSES.unreached`: `test/incus/active-fw.sh  sourced library (active_fw_detect) for CoS/fairness harnesses, #13069 — not a standalone harness`, or
2. Teach `scripts/harness-census.sh` to exempt sourced libraries (e.g. files with no `main`/execution guard), if the project prefers the census to model libraries.

Option 1 is the census's own documented remedy and is the smaller change.

## Acceptance

`sh scripts/harness-census.sh` passes on master; the `Harness census and self-test` CI job goes green on an unrelated PR.

## #13760 — [afxdp #13637] Stage 11 IPsec passthrough double-counts fall-through input-filter counters (counted non-PBR walk + counted PBR walk) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Verdict evidence (hostile review of origin/master 8738dc25c, 88914413a + 04173fe58)

### Defect
Stage 11 IPsec passthrough now runs TWO counted filter walks for one packet, double-charging every matched `then count` fall-through (`continue_term`) term that precedes a routing-instance term.

### Mechanism (file:line on reviewed head 8738dc25c)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/filter.rs:1829-1845` `stage11_input_filter_terminal` calls `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter(..., routing_eval_follows=true)`. Per `filter.rs:197-260`, `true` selects `NonRoutingCountPolicy::OnlyTerminalNonAccept` ONLY when `interface_filter_affects_route_lookup` is true — that policy still counts matched fall-through terms on the Accept/defer exit (it suppresses only the terminal-term charge the routing walk will own). See `evaluate_filter_ref_non_routing_counted` semantics documented at filter.rs:220-235.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1251-1277` (Passthrough arm, added 04173fe58) then unconditionally calls counted `ingress_route_table_override(...)` for the SAME packet/flow. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/pbr.rs:89-113,165+` counted mode calls `evaluate_filter_ref_routing_instance_event_counted`, which counts every matched term including the same fall-through `then count` terms (`filter/engine/eval.rs:615-660`: `if count && term.has_count { record_filter_counter }` before the continue_term branch).
- Net: a filter like `term1 { from {...} then { count c1; next term; } } term2 { then { routing-instance X; discard; } }` (or accept) charges `c1` twice for one Stage-11 ESP/AH/IKE packet to a local IP. On the ordinary session-miss path this cannot happen: the non-PBR precheck and the routing walk are sequenced so the routing walk runs only after an Accept AND the precheck used OnlyTerminalNonAccept precisely to avoid this — but Stage 11 runs both unconditionally even when the non-PBR verdict is Accept (filter_terminal returns false) — and even on Discard/Reject the routing walk is skipped only because filter_terminal returns true; the double-count hits the ACCEPT path, which is the common passthrough case.

This is exactly the double-count class #13648 (16313f8d6) fixed on the session-hit path by deriving the PBR verdict uncounted first and replaying only one counted walk; Stage 11 was not given the same treatment. The 04173fe58 regression asserts a routing-instance discard counter ==1 on the DROP path (where the non-PBR walk counts only terminal-non-accept, so no double) — it does not cover a preceding fall-through count term on an ACCEPT/passthrough packet, so it is test-only-green for this defect.

### Consequence
Operator-visible `then count` counters for any input filter mixing a counted fall-through term with a routing-instance term are inflated 2x on every IPsec passthrough packet (ESP/AH/IKE to a local destination). Counters are the billing/visibility surface Junos operators rely on; silent 2x is a correctness defect, not cosmetics.

### Suggested fix shape (not prescribed)
Mirror #13648: derive routing verdict uncounted at Stage 11, then run exactly one counted walk (routing-counted on PBR outcome, non-PBR counted otherwise), or pass routing_eval_follows=false-equivalent sequencing with explicit ownership. Add a regression: Stage-11 IKE/ESP packet, filter with counted next-term + routing-instance accept/discard, assert counter ==1.

Labels: bug,audit per campaign instruction.

## #13761 — [afxdp #13655] declined-ICMP zone rebind failure purges a session pre-fix code retained [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Verdict evidence (hostile review of origin/master 8738dc25c, commit 7fa1c0a84)

### Defect
When a type-dependent ICMP rematch is declined, the new zone-rebind path can turn a session the pre-fix code RETAINED into a PURGED (torn-down) session if the BPF conntrack restamp fails or the pair entries cannot be read back.

### Mechanism (file:line on reviewed head 8738dc25c)
- Pre-fix (7fa1c0a84^): the `icmp_packet_verdict_may_depend_on_type` branch set `retained=true; declined=true;` unconditionally — session kept, packet-scoped adjudication later.
- Post-fix `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/reconcile.rs:322-383`: `retained = sessions.rebind_zones_pair(...)`; if local rebind succeeds but `restamp_bpf_conntrack_policy` returns false for any entry, or `policy_rebind_pair_entries` returns None, code sets `retained=false` (reconcile.rs:~371,374).
- Caller at reconcile.rs:~440-465: `if !retained { delete_terminal_filtered_session(...); purged+=1 }` — full pair teardown, NAT release, shared/BPF deletion.
- restamp failure is reachable in production: conntrack map fd absent/full, entry raced-expired between rebind and restamp. The zone IDs in the local table were already mutated by rebind_zones_pair (session/mod.rs rebind_zones_pair) and are NOT rolled back on this path, so even the surviving mirrors are inconsistent before teardown.

### Consequence
A config commit that merely renames zones (the exact scenario #13655 fixes) can now DELETE live ICMP sessions (e.g. long-lived ICMP-monitor / PMTUD state) on a transient BPF restamp failure, where before the commit they were silently retained. Session teardown on a rename commit is an availability regression; the failure mode is timing-dependent and will not appear in the added regression (which uses a healthy in-test BPF stub).

### Suggested fix shape (not prescribed)
On restamp/readback failure after a successful local zone rebind, keep the pre-fix posture: retained=true, declined=true (packet-scoped adjudication with new zones already in the local table), and log/count the restamp failure; or roll back the local zone mutation before purging. Add a regression injecting a failing restamp.

Labels: bug,audit per campaign instruction.

## #13762 — test: #13646 missing-neighbor throttle regression is source-string only; capacity/NAT64 probe paths untested behaviorally [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Summary
#13646 (commit c9543ac8b, `sessions: bound missing-neighbor probes`) claims to bound **every** MissingNeighbor kernel probe, but its only poll-path regression is a source-string assertion that passes without exercising the mechanism, and the two sibling probe paths keep their per-packet behaviour:

- The **behavioral** test (`throttle_reclaim_preserves_live_rate_limits`, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/resolver_enqueue_tests.rs`) only exercises `note_kernel_probe`/`probe_throttled` helpers in isolation.
- The **poll-path** test (`missing_neighbor_probe_path_is_globally_throttled_and_borrows_name`, same file) is `include_str!("mod.rs")` + substring checks (`probe.contains("let is_probe_throttled = probe_throttled(")`, `.map(String::as_str)`, `!.cloned()`, `!throttle.clear()`). It never drives a descriptor through `poll_binding_process_descriptor_with_injection`, so inverting the `!is_probe_throttled` guard, deleting the capacity/NAT64 `note_kernel_probe` branch, or breaking the throttle-key construction would keep it green (only renamed variables / reintroduced `.cloned()` / `.clear()` trip it).

## Uncovered sibling paths (same descriptor arm, `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` on origin/master @ 8738dc25c)
1. **Capacity-drop / NAT64 branch untested behaviorally.** The `else if !tunnel_marked && !already_probing && !is_probe_throttled { note_kernel_probe(...) }` arm records the window, but no test sends two same-key capacity/NAT64 misses and asserts the second does not re-probe. The commit message's RED evidence is only "the isolated poll-path source regression failed" — i.e. the string test, not a behavioural failure.
2. The failure-mode claim "failed probe syscalls also consume the window" (Risk section) has no test: `note_kernel_probe` return/failure is discarded (`let _ =`) and never asserted.

This is a test-quality/coverage defect, not (on current reading) a production-code defect: the production wiring in `mod.rs` does apply `probe_throttled` before `trigger_kernel_arp_probe` and does call `note_kernel_probe` on the capacity/NAT64 arm. The fix merges with false confidence because the regression cannot fail for the claimed mechanism.

## Acceptance
- Add a behavioural poll-loop regression (existing `txn_run_descriptor*` / mirror-test harness) that: sends two same-(ifindex,next-hop) MissingNeighbor packets in the capacity-drop and/or NAT64-miss shape within one 100 ms window and asserts only one kernel-probe / throttle-window consumption; or an equivalent seam-level test that fails if the `!is_probe_throttled` guard or the `note_kernel_probe` call is removed/reverted.
- Keep or delete the `include_str!` test; if kept, it must not be the sole coverage for the throttling claim.
- RED evidence: test fails with the poll-loop gate reverted (not merely with helper functions removed).

## #13763 — test: #13632 raw-L3 ingress-gate regression skips unprivileged; only source-order coverage executes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Summary
#13632 (commit 2883d2a48, `dataplane: gate disabled parsing on ingress authority`) ships two regressions, but neither can run-and-fail for the claimed mechanism in CI:

1. **Privileged BPF test never executes unprivileged.** `TestUserspaceXDPDegradedCtrlDisabledRawL3CannotTakeLocalExemption13632` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/xdp_shim_decouple_test.go`) loads a real eBPF collection via `loadUserspaceXDPTestCollection`, which `t.Skipf`s on `rlimit.RemoveMemlock` failure. The commit's own log (`docs/log/13632.md`) records: "Focused Go raw-L3 regression completed but was skipped because RemoveMemlock is denied in this environment." So the only behavioural test of the raw-L3→local-exemption mechanism has zero recorded non-skip execution; a revert of the `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs` gate would be invisible wherever the suite runs unprivileged (the normal `make test-go` lane).
2. **Rust coverage is pure source-order.** `shim_degraded_ctrl_disabled_tests_adjudicated_before_parse_13632` (`userspace-dp/src/main_tests.rs`) tokenises `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs` and asserts the ADJUDICATED bit-test precedes `parse_l2`/`parse_ipv4`/`parse_ipv6`/`is_degraded_local_or_control` and is followed within 40 tokens by `drop_degraded_transit`. It compiles/executes no XDP program. It would pass if e.g. `userspace_ingress_metadata` returned flags for the wrong ifindex/map, if the refreshed BPF object were stale, or if the gate tested the right token in dead code — and the shipped `.o`/manifest refresh is only verifier-checked, not behaviour-checked against this test.

Net: on an unprivileged CI runner the 13632 gate has **no executing regression at all**; the fail-on-revert evidence in the commit is the source-token test turning red because a token disappears, which proves ordering of tokens, not that a raw-L3 packet is dropped.

## Acceptance
- Make the raw-L3 BPF test execute in at least one recorded lane (privileged CI job, or a non-BPF behavioural seam — e.g. extract the degraded-action decision over parsed inputs and test unadjudicated→DROP vs adjudicated-local→PASS in Rust), and record a non-skip PASS plus a RED-on-revert run in the issue log.
- Until then, do not cite the Go test as behavioural coverage for #13632; the source-order test may remain as a supplementary pin.

## Summary
#13643 (commit 9d9725d4c, `userspace-dp: retry pressure-shed teardown after tuple contention`) claims in its commit body and `docs/log/13643.md`: "Cover both pressure admission paths". Production does defer on both sites in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (normal SYN admission ~line 5374 and guarded missing-neighbor admission ~line 10155, both `sessions.defer_pressure_shed(...)` on lease failure). But the regression covers **only one**:

- The sole extended test, `txn_pressure_shed_gate_failure_keeps_shared_row_and_nat_hold_12862` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_txn_flow_cache.rs::txn_pressure_shed_nat_pool_hold_behavior(gate_blocks_cleanup=true)`), drives an ordinary TCP SYN through `txn_run_descriptor_checked` — the normal admission path. It then calls `retry_deferred_pressure_sheds` directly.
- No test drives the **missing-neighbor admission** path (`can_admit_new_syn(1, ...)` under `MissingNeighbor`, `pending_capacity_available` arm) with the tuple gate contended, so deleting/reverting the second `defer_pressure_shed` call (mod.rs ~10155) — stranding NAT64/NAT holds and shared rows exactly as in the original bug — keeps the whole suite green.
- Relatedly, the retry test asserts only shared-row removal + SNAT pool `used_ports 2 -> 1`; the commit claims retry also cleans "BPF, conntrack, flow-cache, NAT64, and replica state" (`retry_deferred_pressure_sheds` in `worker/loop_body/gc_teardown.rs` calls `release_coordinator_session_rows`, `delete_bpf_conntrack_entry_under_gate`, `delete_dnat_table_entry`, `invalidate_slot`, `release_nat64_allocation_for_worker`, `replicate_session_delete_repairing`) — none of those effects is asserted, so a regression that dropped e.g. the NAT64 release or conntrack delete from the retry would pass.

## Acceptance

## #13765 — afxdp: #13648 session-hit PBR deny double-counts preceding counted fall-through terms [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect
#13648 (commit 4d6a70bc) session-hit PBR deny path double-charges matched `then count` fall-through terms that precede the routing-instance deny term.

## Mechanism (reviewed range 4d6a70bc)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/filter.rs` `evaluate_input_filter_on_session_hit` per-packet arm now calls `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter(..., routing_eval_follows=false)` first. With `false`, `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter` (filter.rs:197+) selects `NonRoutingCountPolicy::Always` (sole-counter doctrine), so every matched `then count` fall-through term is recorded inline via `evaluate_filter_ref_non_routing_counted_v4/v6` (`counting() == (true,false)`).
- If that walk returns Accept (it defers at the routing-instance term, returning default Accept), the new code then calls `evaluate_filter_ref_routing_instance_event_counted`, whose v4/v6 walks (`userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs:638-640` / v6 twin) again do `if count && term.has_count { record_filter_counter(...) }` for every matched term, including the same fall-through terms, before reaching the routing-instance term.
- Session-miss path avoids this via `OnlyTerminalNonAccept` (`counting()==(false,true)`): counts only replayed on terminal deny. The new session-hit arm does not use it, and the uncounted probe (`evaluate_filter_ref_routing_instance_uncounted`) does not suppress the counted replay's re-charge.

## Consequence
One established-session packet hitting a per-packet (DSCP etc.) filter with `term count-before { then count; next term; } term pbr { then { routing-instance X; discard; } }` increments `count-before` twice (and its byte count twice). Filter counters inflate 2x for exactly the PBR-deny population #13648 fixed. Analogous double-count was filed as #13760 for stage-11.

## Test gap
`filter_revalidation_7212_tests.rs` #13648 tests assert only `filter.terms[1]` (the PBR term) counter ==1; fixture terms carry no preceding counted fall-through term, so double-charge is unobserved.

## Fix direction
Count fall-through terms once: e.g. run non-routing walk with `OnlyTerminalNonAccept`-equivalent when `affects_route_lookup`, or make counted PBR walk skip terms already charged, mirroring #2620 ownership split.

## #13767 — sessions: #13654 requeue overflow drops deltas while flush reports in-sync (no LossResync) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect
#13654 (commit c452631f) `flush_session_deltas` treats a requeue whose ring is full as fully preserved, suppressing LossResync even though deltas were dropped.

## Mechanism
- `session_delta.rs:622-645`: on tuple-gate contention, `let requeued = if let Some(sessions) = current_sessions { sessions.requeue_deltas_front(&deltas[delta_index..]); true } else { false }; event_stream_out_of_sync |= !requeued;`
- `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:4069-4079` `requeue_deltas_front`: per delta, `if self.deltas.len() >= MAX_SESSION_DELTAS (4096) { self.delta_drops+=1; self.delta_loss_pending=true; continue; }` — dropped deltas are NOT requeued.
- So when the session delta ring is at/near capacity (the overload condition where contention is most likely), some/all of the suffix is dropped, `delta_loss_pending` is set on the table, but `flush_session_deltas` returns `event_stream_out_of_sync=false` (and does not set `*worker_lossless_wedged`).
- Worker loop (`worker/loop_body/mod.rs:214-219` `flush_session_deltas_loop`) only calls `sessions.set_delta_loss()` when flush returns true. The table's `delta_loss_pending` set by requeue overflow is read via `sessions.take_delta_loss()` in `delta_recovery.rs:228` — need verify that path runs unconditionally per cycle; if the only arming is via flush return / binding live latch, dropped requeue deltas raise no resync. Even if `take_delta_loss` is polled, the flush contract ("requeued==true means preserved") is false and the new tests assert `!slot.take_delta_loss()`-style invariants only for non-full rings.

## Test gap
`flush_tuple_gate_contention_13654` tests use an empty `SessionTable::new()` retry slot; no test fills the delta ring to `MAX_SESSION_DELTAS` before contention, so overflow-drop-while-claiming-requeued is unobserved.

## Fix direction
Make `requeue_deltas_front` return preserved count/bool (all-or-nothing), and `event_stream_out_of_sync |= !fully_preserved`; add full-ring contention regression.

## #13867 — HA: reject delayed equal-generation persistent-NAT lease batches after local clear [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Context
Follow-up to #13693 / PR #13855. #13693 narrows the post-clear fence so a generation-accepted lease import for a different subscriber is not blocked by an unrelated per-key clear tombstone.

## Evidence
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_idle_leases_8121.go:150-167` rejects a batch only when `batch.Generation < RemoteGenerations[origin]`; equality proceeds without advancing the generation. The accepted path reaches the indexed generation-authorized importer (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/idle_lease_sync_8121.rs`) which sets `generation_validated`; `userspace-dp/src/nat/idle_lease_sync_8121.rs` then checks only the per-key tombstone and bypasses the batch-wide clear fence. Consequently, an old equal-generation batch for a key that was not individually tombstoned can restore a pre-clear lease after local clear.

## Acceptance
- Add a regression with an already-known remote generation, local clear, and delayed equal-generation batch containing a previously unknown lease key; show current behavior installs it.
- Define and persist a clear-generation/lease freshness rule that rejects that delayed batch while still allowing legitimate post-clear HA lease imports.
- Preserve older-generation rejection and post-clear new-subscriber import behavior; cover restart persistence if the rule is durable.

## Relation
This is intentionally separate from #13693 because its fix requires additional generation/freshness semantics beyond the narrowed per-key post-clear import behavior. Track it before shipping deployments that rely on preventing delayed equal-generation replay.

## #13898 — afxdp: IPv6 neighbor arm still burns one-shot probe token on same-MAC refresh (#13661 parity gap) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect

On `origin/master` (`9a8b957d312ba55eb13cdd7c0a050371f2b48921`), the IPv6 `RTM_NEWNEIGH` arm in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neighbor.rs:875` still consumes the one-shot solicitation token unconditionally:

```rust
let solicited = dynamic_neighbors.take_arp_reply_solicited(&key, now_ns)
    || (state & NUD_PERMANENT) != 0;
let result = dynamic_neighbors.insert_arp_reply_if_solicited_allows(key, NeighborEntry { mac }, solicited);
```

This is the exact bug #13661 fixed for IPv4 and the RX ARP path in `797c39195` (#13838): peek before insert, consume only when the insert actually changes the map (`Some(true)`). The IPv4 kernel arm at `neighbor.rs:829,837` and `poll_stages.rs` do this; the IPv6 arm added by #13660 (`5018cb759`, landed before #13661) was never updated.

## Mechanism

`insert_arp_reply_if_solicited_allows` returns `Some(false)` for a same-MAC refresh (no change, no authorization needed). The IPv6 arm has already removed the token via `take_arp_reply_solicited`, so a same-MAC `NUD_DELAY`/`NUD_STALE` refresh inside the 5s solicitation window burns the token. A genuine failover MAC change milliseconds later is then refused as unsolicited (`NeighborMsgEffect::None`, NA refusal counted), blackholing IPv6 forwarding until the next probe — the identical failover interruption #13661 describes for IPv4.

Sequence: `record_neighbor_probe` → same-MAC usable-state RTM_NEWNEIGH (token consumed, `Some(false)`) → differing-MAC RTM_NEWNEIGH (refused).

## Evidence

- `neighbor.rs:829/837` (v4): `peek_arp_reply_solicited`, then `take_...` only `if matches!(result, Some(true))`.
- `neighbor.rs:875` (v6): unconditional `take_arp_reply_solicited` before insert; no conditional consume.
- `sharded_neighbor.rs`: `peek_arp_reply_solicited` exists precisely for this; same-MAC insert returns `Some(false)`.
- Existing v6 tests (`kernel_neighbor_v6_unsolicited_13660_tests`) cover probe→failover and one-shot second-replacement, but never same-MAC-refresh→failover, so the suite is green without exercising this.

## Fix direction

Mirror the v4 arm: peek, insert, consume only on `Some(true)`. Add the v6 analogue of `same_mac_nud_delay_refresh_preserves_solicitation_token_13661`.

Found by hostile review of `8738dc25c..origin/master`.

## #13899 — afxdp: WG try_encap now serializes all senders per session behind tx_lock through AEAD (#13667 perf regression) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect / regression risk

`e550d5ffb` (#13667, in `8738dc25c..origin/master`) changed `WgEngine::try_encap` in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs` (~line 1613 on `origin/master` 9a8b957d3) to hold a new per-session `Mutex<()>` (`WgSession::tx_lock`, `wg/session.rs`) across the AEAD `write_message` call:

```rust
let _tx_guard = session.tx_lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
let counter = session.tx_counter.load(Relaxed);
...
let n = session.transport.write_message(counter, plaintext, payload)?;
session.tx_counter.store(counter + 1, Relaxed);
drop(_tx_guard);
```

## Mechanism / consequence

Previously the counter was reserved with a lock-free atomic (`next_tx_counter` / `reserve_next_counter`), so concurrent workers could encrypt in parallel and only the counter fetch-add serialized. Now every sender for the same peer session serializes through the full ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption of up to `PADDED_PLAINTEXT_MAX` bytes. On multi-queue RSS deployments where many workers forward to one popular WG peer, this is a per-peer throughput ceiling and tail-latency cliff on the hot path — the compiled-code no-avoidable-serialization concern. The stated goal (do not consume a nonce on AEAD failure) does not require holding the lock during encryption: reserve the counter atomically as before, and on AEAD failure the counter has advanced — but WireGuard nonces must never repeat, and gaps are legal (receiver replay window tolerates skipped counters; indeed the commit itself accepts gaps when submission fails after successful AEAD). Alternatively stage with a reserved counter and only publish, but encryption itself need not be inside the critical section.

Note the commit message acknowledges nonce gaps after successful encryption are acceptable for safety, which undermines the need to avoid gaps on the (practically unreachable for valid keys/buffers) AEAD-failure path at the cost of serializing all successful encryptions.

## Evidence

- `engine.rs` try_encap: `_tx_guard` spans `write_message`.
- `session.rs`: `tx_lock: Mutex<()>` added; comment says lock serializes reservation through AEAD.
- Pre-range code at `8738dc25c`: `next_tx_counter()` atomic reserve, no lock.

At minimum this needs a perf justification / measurement, or restructure to atomic reservation. Filed as audit finding from hostile review of the campaign range; severity is production throughput risk, not correctness — nonce uniqueness is preserved.

Found by hostile review of `8738dc25c..origin/master`.

## #13909 — nat: local persistent-NAT clear permanently fences known peers' post-clear leases (#13867 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect

`ClearPersistentNATLeasesWithGeneration` records `LocalClearRemoteGenerations[origin] = generation` for **every** origin already in `RemoteGenerations` (pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_idle_leases_8121.go, the loop just before `state.Generation++`), and the map is never pruned or refreshed afterwards. Admission in `ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch` drops any batch with `batch.Generation <= clearGeneration`.

A sender's durable generation only advances when **that sender** clears (`state.Generation++` in its own `ClearPersistentNATLeasesWithGeneration`). Idle-lease re-advertisement (`runPersistentNatLeaseSyncLoop`, 30s tick) re-exports at the sender's **unchanged** generation.

## Consequence

After a purely local clear on node B (no peer involvement):

1. B fences peer A at A's current generation G.
2. Every subsequent A batch at generation G — including idle leases A creates *after* B's clear, re-advertised every 30s — is silently dropped (`return nil`) at B forever.
3. This lasts until A itself happens to run a persistent-NAT clear, which most peers never do. Failover to B then finds no rebuilt idle persistent-NAT leases for A's clients: clients lose their translated port on takeover, indefinitely and silently (import returns success).

The #13867 regression (`TestLocalClearEqualGenerationFence13867`) pins generation-9 admission only for the integer following the fenced generation, but nothing in the protocol makes a non-clearing peer ever reach generation 9. The commit message acknowledges only the symmetric gap ("peer first observed after clear"); the post-clear starvation of already-known peers is not bounded or documented.

Note the tension: same-generation batches are additive by design (the regression itself asserts a post-clear equal-generation additive import at generation 9 is accepted after the generation-9 barrier batch clears), so the fence cannot distinguish a delayed pre-clear snapshot from a fresh post-clear lease at the same generation — which is exactly why fencing *all future* same-generation traffic is over-broad once the delayed snapshot window has passed.

## Expected

Post-clear leases from a fenced peer become importable again without requiring that peer to clear — e.g. fence only until the peer's next post-clear barrier/empty batch is observed, or advance/expire the watermark on a defined condition — while delayed pre-clear equal-generation snapshots remain rejected. At minimum, the starvation must be bounded and operator-visible rather than a silent permanent `return nil`.

## Evidence

- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_idle_leases_8121.go`: fence written for all known origins on any clear (local or forwarded); `ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch` drops `batch.Generation <= clearGeneration` with `return nil`; no deletion of `LocalClearRemoteGenerations` entries anywhere in the tree.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_persistent_nat_lease_sync_8121.go`: sender re-advertises at its unchanged durable generation every 30s; the only generation increment in the tree is the sender's own clear.
- Introduced by 991d96905 (#13867, #13903) on origin/master.

## #13910 — userspace-dp: companion-less reverse provenance fail-closed now depends on reconstructed rewrite shape (#13789 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect

In the NoLocalEntry (companion-less) reverse arm of `source_nat_revocation_on_session_hit_with_ingress` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/policy_revalidation.rs`), the early return added by 9a8b957d3 (#13789) fires before the forward-VLAN provenance fail-closed arm:

```rust
if forward_decision.nat.rewrite_src.is_none()
    || forward_decision.nat.nat64
    || forward_decision.nat.nptv6
{
    return None;
}
```

Pre-fix, **every** companion-less reverse hit with `forward_ingress_vlan_id == None` returned a drop-only `StaleSourceNat` revocation ("absent NAT provenance deliberately fails closed for translated source-NAT state"). Verified against 9a8b957d3^: the provenance check was unconditional in this arm.

## Verified scope

- `rewrite_src.is_none()`: passing through to the ordinary policy gate is #13789's stated intent. Only the missing regression pin is asked for below.
- `nat64` / `nptv6`: `source_nat_translation_still_valid` returns `(true, None)` for these shapes unconditionally, so the provenance arm was the **only** stale-translation guard for companion-less NAT64/NPTv6 reverse hits. It is now gone: such a hit with missing forward VLAN provenance receives no SNAT-arm validation or drop at all and proceeds to the zone-policy gates, even though NAT64/NPTv6 state is translated state the fail-closed posture was written for. No test in 9a8b957d3 distinguishes the nat64/nptv6 + missing-provenance shape.

## Ask

1. Restore the provenance fail-closed drop for companion-less NAT64/NPTv6 reverse hits (or document + pin why they are exempt), and
2. Pin with a regression that a companion-less reverse hit with `rewrite_src.is_none()` and missing forward VLAN provenance is intentionally permitted through to the policy gate, so the narrowed fail-closed posture is explicit.

## Evidence

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/policy_revalidation.rs` on origin/master (62f3d1885): early `return None` precedes the `forward_ingress_vlan_id` fail-closed arm in the `NoLocalEntry` branch.
- Same file: `source_nat_translation_still_valid` head returns `(true, None)` for `rewrite_src` absent / NAT64 / NPTv6 — the validator never substitutes for the removed drop.
- 9a8b957d3 validation covers reverse-SNAT and lone-reverse regressions; no no-companion NAT64/NPTv6 missing-provenance case.

## #13999 — IPv6 MTU gate must use referenced shared-link MTU (#13936 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

Follow-up to #13936: the IPv6 minimum-MTU gate currently checks the IPv6 unit MTU or interface MTU only. Untagged logical units share one physical link, and `planPhysDesired` selects the MTU from the lowest-numbered referenced untagged unit with an MTU. Therefore unit 0 IPv4 `mtu 1000` and unit 1 IPv6 with no family MTU both zoned plans a 1000-byte physical MTU, but the current gate accepts it.

Acceptance: add a regression with both units zoned, reject the IPv6 unit based on the actual planned parent-link MTU, and zone the existing unit-MTU-overrides-low-interface-MTU acceptance control so it proves the override is active. Preserve tagged-child behavior and IPv4-only allowance.
