## #14009 — [follow-up #13992] Completed fragment anchors starve other routing domains [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Mechanism

PR #13992 merged as 34277bb excludes completed fragment-overlap entries from both sender and routing-domain fairness quotas in userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs (OverlapTracker::check_and_record_fragment_detailed). The sender exclusion fixes #13937 H08-05, but the routing-domain exclusion breaks #10658: one routing domain can fill all 64 slots of a shard with settled completed anchors (sender/domain quotas see zero), so another domain's new key is refused ShardFull until the 30s TTL expires. Existing cross_vrf_attacker_cannot_starve_victim_10658 only floods incomplete entries.

## Acceptance

- New regression: one domain fills a shard with completed anchors; another domain's key is still admitted and bounded; attacker domain cannot exceed its fair reserve via completions.
- #13937 rate regression still passes (conformant completed datagrams do not exhaust sender quota).
- #13680 replay protection still passes (same-ident overlap after completion still dropped when anchor retained).
- #10658 incomplete fairness tests still pass unmodified.
- RED on merged code, GREEN after fix; full fragment_overlap module green.

Discovered by post-merge advisory review of #13992.

## #14012 — [regression] Preserve DHCP backstops across static-address applies [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

The #13927 pre-networkd static-address fence reused InstallGapFence, which atomically replaces xpf_hostinbound_gap. On a consecutive apply after a prior failed host-inbound render, the previous gap can carry DHCP unleased-interface backstops. If a later config removes DHCP intent while adding a static address, rebuilding from incoming-only backstop fields drops the old DHCP guard while the DHCP address can still be active.

The first reproduction showed the pre-networkd replacement itself dropped the prior backstop. A separate temporary address-activation table is required so installing new static-address drops does not replace the active coverage-gap table.

A second boundary matters too: if the full host-inbound render fails in the apply tail, its incoming-config-only coverage-gap replacement must retain the old DHCP backstop inputs until a later successful real render removes the gap. Consecutive temporary address drops must likewise stay guarded until successful full-render cleanup.

Required: keep the active DHCP backstop across both the pre-networkd and failed-tail replacements when incoming DHCP intent is removed; preserve fail-closed host-service denial for newly added static addresses. Regression coverage must assert the old backstop remains in the active gap before networkd and is carried into a failed-tail gap replacement.

## #14021 — userspace dataplane: generate ICMP for reject routes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Summary

The route snapshot and Rust FIB now preserve `reject` separately from `discard`, and IPv4/IPv6 route selection treats reject as terminal. The slow-path disposition handling still has no `RejectRoute` poll arm that generates a reply; the existing reject-reply helper is session-flow-backed and currently uses TCP RST for TCP policy rejects. Route rejects therefore still need a flowless, protocol-independent ICMP/ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable path.

## Acceptance

- Transit packets matching reject routes emit ICMPv4 Destination Unreachable or ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable (including TCP and flowless packets).
- Discard routes remain silent.
- Reuse existing suppression, output classification, reply budget, and per-zone generated-reject limiter gates.
- Cover IPv4/IPv6 parity and test suppressed and permitted reply paths.

## Evidence

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs` has `DiscardRoute` handling at the slow-path disposition match, but no route-reject response handling.
- Existing ICMP reply builder is `build_reject_icmp_unreachable` in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp.rs`; the policy helper `enqueue_reject_reply` in `poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs` requires `&SessionFlow` and emits TCP RST for TCP, so it cannot directly satisfy flowless route reject behavior.

## #14084 — HA session import with no registered workers bypasses the #13944 interface control-tuple guard and later installs the forbidden identity [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Origin
Astra hostile review of PR #14016 (merge 1c625e6c2) — VERDICT: DEFECT. Opus lane returned CLEAN on direct allocator paths; Astra traced the HA publication path. Mechanism verified firsthand on origin/master d99419b66.

## Mechanism
1. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/session_import.rs`: `translation_reserved` requires `!worker_records.is_empty()`. With zero registered workers (boot/reconcile), `reserve_synced_translation` is never called, so the #13944 guard in `reserve_interface_identity` (nat/allocator.rs:5276) never runs — yet the forward entry (publish_shared_session), its synthesized reverse companion, and an `Applied` outcome all proceed.
2. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/bringup.rs` (`replay_late_synced_sessions`) later queues `UpsertSynced` for newly registered workers from those shared entries.
3. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/commands/upsert_synced.rs`: installs the session (`upsert_synced_with_origin`) BEFORE reservation, discards the bool from `reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation_for_worker` (an `IdentityConflict` from the #13944 guard does not remove the installed entry), and publishes the worker session-map entry regardless. Reverse companions skip reservation.
4. First-hit validation (`nat/source/mod.rs`, interface mode) accepts by egress-address equality only; it does not check the translated control port.

Consequence: an older/unpatched peer supplying H:5000 -> P:4500 translated to E:4500 is accepted by a patched receiver with no registered workers, and the reverse key P:4500 -> E:4500 (the prohibited host-local NAT-T identity from #13944) is installed on bring-up/failover. [INFERENCE: source-traced, not runtime-reproduced]

## Scope note
Direct allocator mint/reserve paths are correctly guarded by #13995/#14016 (verified). This is the HA admission/publication path only. #13944's own regression calls the allocator directly, so it cannot detect this bypass.

## Acceptance
- Enforce the interface control-tuple eligibility check before shared/mirror publication, independent of worker registration. Do not merely move reservation into the no-worker branch without addressing its holder-lifetime contract.
- Coordinator-level regression: import the forbidden tuple with zero workers; assert rejection and absence of forward+reverse authority, and that later replay/drain installs neither.
- Regression fails on current master, passes after.

## #14088 — P-Mech local selector projection diverges on tunnel and mixed-ECMP routes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Context
Follow-up to merged #13956 / PR #14079. The Go snapshot producer and Rust validator compute the local-selector destination projection differently, so valid local routes can make a tunnel inventory fail closed, and the Rust validator can accept a destination projection that the producer is intended to exclude.

## Exact mechanism
- Go `pkg/dataplane/userspace/pmech_snapshot.go` builds `c.tunnelIfindexes` from every tunnel row. In the local projection loop (`stamp`, around lines 534-544), it skips routes with `pmechRouteHasMixedEgress(route)` and skips every next-hop ifindex found in `c.tunnelIfindexes`.
- Rust `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/runtime_view.rs::recompute_local_selector_projection` (around lines 653-680) iterates `route_index.owned_routes_by_ifindex`, skips only `tunnel.logical_ifindex`, and does not skip mixed-egress routes.
- `has_mixed_tunnel_egress` invalidates mixed routes involving a tunnel, but does not cover a mixed ECMP route whose legs are all non-tunnel. For such a local-selector route, Go omits the prefix while Rust recomputes it, so `PMechInventory::from_snapshot` reports `SELECTOR_PROJECTION_MISMATCH` and rejects the row. Routes through a second tunnel likewise disagree: the producer excludes them, while the validator includes them. This violates the contract that destination authority is local-selector intersection with non-tunnel main-table routes and breaks Go/Rust projection lockstep.

Evidence: #14079 changed Go to exclude all tunnel ifindexes and mixed-egress routes; the merged Rust helper excludes only the current tunnel ifindex and has no mixed-egress predicate. No open issue was found by searching the repository for #13956/local-selector/tunnel-projection follow-ups.

## Acceptance
- Make the Rust local projection use the same complete tunnel-ifindex set and mixed-egress exclusion as Go.
- Add regression coverage with two tunnel interfaces proving a route via the other tunnel is excluded, and with a non-tunnel mixed-ECMP route proving both Go and Rust derive the same projection without invalidating an otherwise valid row.
- Verify existing IPv4/IPv6 destination projection and decrypted-ingress policy tests remain green.

## #14090 — Preserve L4 port matching in decrypted IPsec zone-policy evaluation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Context
Follow-up to merged #13956 / PR #14079, separate from route projection parity tracked by #14088. The decrypted-ingress policy gate currently evaluates every packet as flowless, which can deny valid TCP/UDP traffic under a port-specific VPN-to-LAN permit rule.

## Exact mechanism
In merged `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ipsec_inner.rs`, `d14_zone_gate` calls `evaluate_policy_result_l3_aware` after selector/route checks (the added block around lines 407-431). It supplies source/destination ports `0, 0` and `l4_present=false` unconditionally. The policy evaluator therefore cannot match a TCP/UDP rule that requires ports, although a complete decrypted packet can carry parseable L4 ports. Existing policy behavior deliberately fails flowless packets closed against port-bearing rules; `flowless_ports_fail_closed_against_a_port_bearing_term_7480` covers that contract.

This is a functional regression introduced by the new H14-02 policy gate: an otherwise permitted remote-to-local TCP/UDP packet with a port-specific zone rule is denied because the gate discards its L4 tuple.

## Acceptance
- Carry parsed L4 ports and the correct `l4_present` state into the policy decision for decrypted IPsec traffic; preserve flowless handling only when ports are genuinely unavailable (for example non-first fragments or protocols without ports).
- Keep the existing fail-closed behavior for flowless packets against port-bearing policy terms.
- Add IPv4 and IPv6 regression coverage showing a matching TCP/UDP port rule permits and a nonmatching port denies; include fragment/flowless coverage.
- Run focused IPsec adjudication and policy tests.

## #14091 — [follow-up H10-05] deterministic NAPT64 still allocates per remote flow [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

Follow-up to #13946. The #13946 fix makes the standard round-robin NAT64 allocator use the endpoint-independent AnyRemoteHost BIB key. The separate deterministic NAPT64 mode (`Nat64Prefix::deterministic_v6`, `allocate_deterministic_v6`) still indexes `live_by_flow` by the full `SourceNatFlowKey` and claims a new free port from the subscriber block for each remote endpoint.

Observed in `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs::allocate_deterministic_v6`: the exact-flow reentry check only runs after claiming a block port; different remote IP/port means a different flow key and therefore a second port. The existing deterministic test `napt64_deterministic_v6_routes_through_block_allocator` pins block placement and intentionally expects distinct ports for distinct source ports, but does not cover two remotes for one source transport. The archived H10-05 review explicitly noted this deterministic-path residual.

Acceptance:
- Same `(protocol, IPv6 subscriber, source port/ICMP identifier, routing scope)` uses one external IPv4 address and port across different remote addresses and ports, while each session retains its full remote-specific key.
- Binding remains inside the subscriber's deterministic IPv4/port block, tracks active flows independently, and retains its configured BIB idle lifetime; unrelated source transports remain distinct.
- HA active-session reserve joins the same BIB; idle BIB sync/failover preserves it when configuration identity matches and rejects stale/out-of-block records without stealing a live tuple.
- Deterministic block release/GC/rollback uses no-recycle semantics; test concurrency of two destinations racing for the same BIB.
- Add local, teardown/expiry, HA reserve/failover, configuration identity, and fail-on-revert tests; do not claim #13946 covers deterministic NAPT64 until this is fixed.

Implementation note: reuse allocator-integrated persistent lease ownership rather than an unbounded side table. The standard NAT64 BIB timeout is 300 seconds; deterministic and source `persistent-nat` config are mutually exclusive.

## #14110 — [research D4-09] compileNAT persistent-NAT pool registration ignores pool.Address / CIDR expansion [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## compileNAT persistent-NAT pool registration ignores pool.Address / CIDR expansion

Research-validated defect from deep-review source report (three-way adversarial research: Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus SMR + Muse-Spark, blinded; coordinator aggregate).

## Review origin
- Discovery source: deep-review (gemini-4-argon-high review of major security/forwarding defects, 100 claims D1-01..D10-10)
- Finding ID: D4-09
- Validated by: /research three-way gate — codex=MISSING, opus=MATERIAL, spark=COHORT (gate: >=2 MATERIAL, or 1 MATERIAL + 1 COHORT/NEEDS_VALIDATION leaning defect; no open-issue duplicate found 2026-10-16)
- Reviewer evidence: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.ccsxHW6SyD/{codex,opus,spark}-b*.md` sections D4-09 (audited 24b16aeb7, checked vs master ac21746fc; aggregate re-verified cited paths at origin/master e0c8e9913)

## Defect mechanism (at origin/master)
Cited code:
- `pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:496–560`
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:134–175`
- `pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:1079–1125`

Traced mechanism (codex-b3 lane, strongest-defect reading): ** `compileNAT` registers persistent pool IPs from **only** `pool.Addresses`, and for CIDRs registers parsed **network/base IP**, not all members: **A=M** `pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:496–560`. Userspace SNAT uses `config.SourceNATPoolMembers(pool)` instead (**A=M** `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:134–175`), including the singular `pool.Address` form. The Go session-store preservation hook looks up that table by translated IP before saving (**A=M** `pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:1079–1125`), so on a *reachable Go session deletion* its table can omit a binding. This is not the malformed address expansion at report's `compiler_nat.go:562–605`; those lines have another purpose. - **Best refutation / scope:** The actual production userspace helper owns source-NAT translation and persistent lease reuse, not `PersistentNATTable.Lookup

## Decisive regression check
compile a `/29` persistent pool + singular-`address` pool and inspect RegisterNATIP set vs allocated binding preservation across recompile. Downgrade to COHORT if compiler proves it normalizes all pools to per-IP Addresses before compileNAT (then only CIDR form remains, still defect).

Fix acceptance: remove the defect mechanism cited above; add a regression that fails on current master and passes with the fix; keep tolerant/strict doctrines fail-closed. Do not special-case the test input.

## #14113 — nat: clear stale permissions when removing persistent leases [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

Follow-up found while reviewing #14046 after merge.

`PortAllocatorLiveState::remove_persistent_lease` removes the lease and reverse-index owner but leaves `persistent_permissions[key]`. When the expired source key is recreated for a different remote, `record_persistent_permission` adds the new permission to the old set. `persistent_inbound_lookup` then still permits the old remote under the new lease.

Reproduction: allocate persistent PAT for `10.0.61.50:40000 -> 8.8.8.8:443`, release it, let the lease expire, then reallocate the same source key to `9.9.9.9:8443`. The current master regression failed: the old remote returned `Permitted` instead of `Denied` after the replacement lease was created.

Acceptance: lease removal must clear its permissions without breaking rollback/restoration paths; add a fail-on-revert expiry/recreate test that asserts the prior remote is denied and the new lease's remote remains permitted. Run the full `nat::tests_idle_lease_sync_8121` module and attribute existing failures on base.

Found while reviewing merged PR #14106 / issue #14046.

When the deferred `sendGARP` finally runs, `garpSendAllowedForOwner` (`instance_garp.go:59-65`) sees `lastGARPEpoch == garpEpoch == 2` and suppresses the burst — V1/V2 never receive a failover GARP/NA, so neighbours keep stale ARP/NDP pointing at the old master until cache expiry. **Strongest

## Decisive regression check
deterministic test with a scheduling seam: hold `sendGARP` before its `vipMu` acquisition, run `updateVIPs(+V3)`, release, and assert GARP frames emitted for V1,V2 — plus populate-pending-in-`becomeMaster` as the fix direction.

## #14217 — userspace-dp: preserve IPv6 AH protocol identity in IPsec-inner zone policy (#14211) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Summary

Merged PR #14211 (squash `f05541e8e`, original PR head `ae2a683ab`) claims in its PR body to "Preserve IPv6 AH as protocol 51 for policy evaluation; ignore shim-stamped inner TCP/UDP ports on AH-sighted chains" and to add an IPv6 AH-to-TCP/443 denial regression (`d14_ipv6_ah_sighted_tcp_443_does_not_match_tcp_term_14090`). The merged code does neither: an IPv6 inner packet whose extension chain sights an Authentication Header (51) before TCP is evaluated as TCP with its inner ports, so a `tcp dst-port 443 permit` term can admit AH traffic that every other flowless/policy path classifies as protocol 51.

## Evidence (origin/master @ 60dc8ef2e)

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ipsec_inner.rs:411-433` (`d14_zone_gate`): ports are taken from `live_frame_ports_from_meta_bytes(&owned, meta)` whenever the packet is not a non-first fragment, and the result is passed to `evaluate_policy_result_l3_aware(..., input.protocol, src_port, dst_port, ..., l4_present)`. `input.protocol` is used verbatim; there is no AH sighting check (grep `ah_sighted` in this file: no hits).
- Production protocol derivation: `userspace-dp/src/slowpath.rs:775` builds the descriptor via `packet_rel_l4_offset_and_protocol_for_ipsec`, which is `packet_rel_l4_offset_and_protocol` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs:310-316`). For IPv6 that walker (`walk_ipv6_ext_chain`, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:197`) walks *through* AH (protocol 51 arm records `ah_present` and continues) and returns `ExtChainOutcome::L4(offset, protocol)` with the terminal protocol — TCP (6) for an AH→TCP chain. So the descriptor's `protocol` is 6 and `rel_l4_offset` points at the TCP header after AH.
- The shared parser has the same behaviour by design and documents the required correction elsewhere: `parse_session_flow_from_bytes` explicitly refuses to mint a ported flow when `ipv6_ah_sighted(...)` (see `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs` around the AH gate, "a v6 chain sighting AH classifies as AH, not as its inner protocol"), and `flowless_effective_protocol` (`inspect.rs:419`) maps AH-sighted chains to `PROTO_AH` (51) — used by PBR, noroute adjudication, embedded-ICMP and poll paths (`forwarding/pbr.rs:243`, `poll_descriptor/noroute_adjudication.rs:61`, etc.). The D14 gate uses neither helper.
- `build_logical_ingress_packet` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/logical_ingress.rs:96`) calls `parse_session_flow_from_frame` for the flow, but D14 ignores that flow entirely and re-derives ports with `live_frame_ports_from_meta_bytes`, which also walks through AH (its byte-led fallback `live_frame_ports_bytes` → `frame_l4_offset` returns the post-AH TCP offset).
- Claimed regression is absent: `grep d14_ipv6_ah_sighted userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ipsec_inner.rs` returns nothing on master; the merged tests cover only plain IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP and IPv4 fragments. The PR body's "RED on previous PR head ae2a683ab ... GREEN ... (30 passed)" AH validation therefore does not correspond to any code or test in the merged squash (29 tests in the merged module per docs/log/14090.md, which also omits the AH bullet present in the PR body).

## Consequence

Fail-open against operator policy: decrypted IPv6 traffic carrying AH before TCP/UDP is admitted by a port-specific TCP/UDP permit term in the VPN→LAN zone policy, where the dataplane's own invariant (#10729 X2-F6) classifies it as protocol 51, which cannot match that term. This is exactly the cleartext-aliasing shape the AH gates elsewhere exist to prevent.

## Expected

In `d14_zone_gate`, when the inner IPv6 chain sights AH, evaluate with effective protocol 51 and `l4_present=false` (flowless), mirroring `flowless_effective_protocol`; or reuse that helper for the protocol argument. Add the claimed `d14_ipv6_ah_sighted_tcp_443_does_not_match_tcp_term_14090` regression (AH→TCP/443 must deny against a tcp/443 permit, and a protocol-51 term should be the only way to admit it).

`route_reject_suppresses_synthetic_fabric_source_14021` (`reject_reply_tests.rs`) calls `enqueue_route_reject_reply(..., 21, ...)` directly — the **post-fix** argument. - Tests-only transplant onto pristine parent `7a4cc2ccdf10` (only `reject_reply_tests.rs` applied): `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp route_reject_suppresses_synthetic_fabric_source_14021` → **PASS** (1 passed). - Source check: pristine `mod.rs` RejectRoute arm computed `ingress_logical = resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex(...).unwrap_or(meta.ingress_ifindex)` and passed it; all sibling reject callers (`enqueue_filter_reject_reply`, `enqueue_session_miss_rst`, `deny_reply_and_emit`) pass `binding.ifindex`. The production fix itself is correct and complete — this issue is only about test validity/coverage.

### Acceptance
- Add a regression that fails on pristine `7a4cc2ccdf10` and passes with the fix, exercising the disposition→reply path (or an extracted seam asserting the route arm supplies the physical binding ifindex to the synthetic-source gate), with the physical(21)/logical(5) VLAN distinction the current fixture sets up.

## #14302 — config: dotted lifeline hb.1 loses ingress exception for its only declared unit after #14192 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect (merged in #14241, commit d40f1f29e, at origin/master a52586a2a)

`pkg/config/lifeline.go` (HostInboundLifelineSet, #14192 change) registers every declared unit as an explicit `false` key before the cluster walk. For a dotted lifeline `hb.1` (ControlInterface=hb.1) whose only declared unit is 7:

- Registration sets `hb.1.7=false`; the role==name arm sets `hb.1=true`, but nothing re-marks `hb.1.7`.
- The cluster walk sets `hb.1=true` and `hb.1.0=true`, then the non-zero-unit guard treats `hb.1` as 'role at unit 1 of bare parent hb' and the SplitInterfaceUnitRef arm does not restore unit 7.
- Result: `HostInboundLifelineInterface("hb.1.7", set) == false` (exact key false).

## Consequence

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:1515 HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs` enumerates only declared-unit spellings (`hb.1.7`), so it yields `[fxp0]` — the control-link netdev loses its host-inbound ingress exception (management/HA reachability gap; documented in docs/log/14192.md as a known follow-up but no issue was filed). The pinned test `TestHostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevsDoesNotAddUnitParent12848` (pkg/dataplane/userspace/host_inbound_lifeline_12848_test.go:64) now fails on master: it expects `hb.1.7` present without parent `hb.1`.

Note the direction is fail-closed for traffic (deny applies) but breaks the lifeline's own ingress exception — an availability defect for the cluster control link.

## Evidence

- pkg/config/lifeline.go:57-73 (declared-unit false registration + role==name only re-marks the base key)
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/host_inbound_lifeline_12848_test.go:64-79 (failing expectation)
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:1515-1545 (helper probes only `ifName.unit` spellings)

## Fix direction (not prescribed)

Either the lifeline set must not register a dotted lifeline's own units false when the interface name itself is the designated lifeline (hb.1 is an interface, not 'hb unit 1'), or HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs must also probe the lifeline base. Must preserve #14192: declared transit VLAN unit ge-0/0/0.100 of a bare lifeline parent stays non-lifeline, and #12848: no bare parent netdev added.

## #14303 — userspace-dp: HA bulk export and tunnel purge stamp pptp_call_ids=0, withholding synced PPTP sessions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect (merged in #14228, commit 7c60f3d04, at origin/master a52586a2a)

#14228 taught the incremental SessionDelta producers to stamp `pptp_call_ids` from the live association table (session/install.rs, session/expire.rs via `pptp_call_ids_wire_for`), and the HA import gate withholds any Pptp(handle) record whose pair is absent/0 (`PPTP_CALL_IDS_ABSENT`). Two delta producers were missed:

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/export.rs:307` — HA bulk export (`snapshot_all_sessions_export`, the full-resync Open deltas) hardcodes `pptp_call_ids: 0`.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/tunnel_purge.rs:110` — tunnel-purge Close delta hardcodes `pptp_call_ids: 0` (less harmful for a close, but inconsistent).

## Consequence

A PPTP session that reaches the standby only via bulk export / full resync (e.g. after event-stream reconnect or peer restart, precisely when incremental deltas were missed) arrives with pair=0 and is withheld as `pptp-call-ids-not-carried` — the exact failure #13965/#14228 set out to eliminate, surviving on the resync path. Fail-closed (no aliasing), so impact is PPTP session loss on failover-after-resync rather than misdelivery.

## Evidence

- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/export.rs:307 `pptp_call_ids: 0` in bulk-export Open delta construction
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/tunnel_purge.rs:110 same in purge Close delta
- Contrast: userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:741 and expire.rs:432 stamp via `pptp_call_ids_wire_for(&key)`
- Import gate: userspace-dp/src/session/pptp.rs `from_wire_call_ids*` returns None for absent pair; session_import withholds

## Fix direction (not prescribed)

Stamp bulk-export (and purge, for symmetry) deltas from the same association lookup the incremental producers use, where the export path has access to it; if the export snapshot genuinely lacks the association table, thread it. Add a regression: bulk-exported PPTP session imports on the peer instead of being withheld.

## #14304 — test: #14253 (14253-review) daemon S1 cell TestIPsecAttributionFollowsLoadedGenerationOnFailedAddition9511 left failing by design — premise superseded, needs re-expression [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect: PR #14253 knowingly leaves a daemon test failing; its premise no longer holds

Post-merge hostile review of merged PR #14253 (`f016b89a`, \`ipsec: skip PSK connections with no secret and split multi-address selectors (#14139)\`).

### Evidence

`docs/log/14139.md` (merged in the same PR) records, verbatim in substance:

> `pkg/config` IPsec cells pass, and the `pkg/daemon` IPsec cells pass except `TestIPsecAttributionFollowsLoadedGenerationOnFailedAddition9511` (S1), whose premise is that the promoted C1's blue-red VPN is one charon never loaded. Under #14139 the C1 fixture VPN now carries a key (as a real config must) and therefore DOES render, so the name is genuinely ambiguous in both generations and owning RG1 alone correctly skips it. The S1 cell needs its premise re-expressed (e.g. blue-red rendered in C0 only via a child name, not a loaded C1 connection); that is a test-design fold for review, not a renderer exception.

The fixture change that breaks the premise is in the same PR: `pkg/daemon/ipsec_sa_rg_9511_test.go` now appends `set security ipsec vpn blue-red pre-shared-key fixture-secret` to the C1 tree (visible at `origin/master:pkg/daemon/ipsec_sa_rg_9511_test.go:502`). Before #14139 the PSK-less C1 VPN rendered a live `auth = psk` connection with no secret (the #14139 defect itself), so charon "never loaded" it for a different reason than the test intended; after the render belt correctly skips PSK-less VPNs, the fixture had to gain a key to keep its other measurements, which makes blue-red genuinely rendered in C1 and defeats the S1 attribution premise.

### Why this is a defect (not a renderer bug)

- The production change is correct: skipping an uncredentialed PSK connection is the fail-closed fix for #14139, and the log correctly refuses to add a renderer exception for the test.
- But the merged state ships a known-red cell in `pkg/daemon`. A permanently failing test trains reviewers to ignore that suite's failures and masks future real regressions in IPsec SA attribution (#9511 loaded-generation attribution is exactly the kind of subtle HA behaviour that needs a green guard).

### Decisive check / fix direction

Re-express the S1 premise so blue-red is rendered in C0 only via a child name (not a loaded C1 connection), per the log's own suggestion, and restore `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestIPsecAttributionFollowsLoadedGenerationOnFailedAddition9511 -count=1` to green without weakening the #9511 attribution assertions. Do not special-case the renderer.

### Scope note

This is a test-premise repair only. No production behaviour change is requested; the #14139 render belt and commit gate are correct as merged.

## #14305 — userspace-dp: #14115 slow-path NAT64 guard in build_nat64_l3_packet_for_slow_path is unreachable dead code (family test contradicts is_non_first_fragment) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-16)

## Defect: the #14115 fail-closed guard added by PR #14243 can never fire

Post-merge hostile review of merged PR #14243 (`c6f05867`, `afxdp: skip NAT64 port rewrite on reverse non-first fragments (#14115)`).

### Evidence (file:line at origin/master)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:543-548` (in `build_nat64_l3_packet_for_slow_path`):

```rust
if !matches!(meta.addr_family as i32, libc::AF_INET6 | libc::AF_INET)
    && is_non_first_fragment(packet, meta.addr_family)
{
    return None;
}
```

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:1029-1035`:

```rust
pub(in crate::afxdp) fn is_non_first_fragment(packet: &[u8], addr_family: u8) -> bool {
    match addr_family as i32 {
        libc::AF_INET => ipv4_is_non_first_fragment(packet),
        libc::AF_INET6 => ipv6_is_non_first_fragment(packet),
        _ => false,
    }
}
```

The first conjunct requires `addr_family` to be neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6; the second conjunct returns `false` for exactly those families. The conjunction is therefore always `false` and the `return None` is unreachable. The comment above it ("Fail closed if either arm declines to classify it as non-first") describes protection that does not exist.

### Impact assessment (why this is a defect, not just dead code)

- No live fail-open was found: for AF_INET/AF_INET6 the match arms below classify `non_first` themselves and return before the port rewrite, and for any other family the `match` falls to `_ => return None`. So today the dead guard is benign.
- It is still a defect: (a) it is misleading safety theatre — a future editor who trusts the comment may weaken an arm believing this guard catches the residue; (b) it is exactly the "regression that passes on pristine (vacuous)" shape — the #14115 slow-path regression test passes with or without this guard, so nothing pins the stated invariant; (c) dead code in a NAT64 fragment path (a historically bug-dense area: #14114/#14115/#2562) invites misreading during the next fragment fix.

### Decisive check / fix direction

Impact ceiling is a wrong application name in logs/telemetry, not the report's "Wrong-Zone Classification / High".

TermMatchExtra::default() may still match L3-only terms — only L4-qualified terms are lost.

Root cause (source report):
`SessionTable::revalidate_forwarding_resolution` (`session/mod.rs:2114-2147`) and `mark_policy_revalidated` (`policy_revalidation.rs:1165`) leave `forward.metadata.egress_zone` and `reverse.metadata.ingress_zone` stale when a forward flow's egress zone changes, and `foreign_hit_verdict` (`session_hit_authority.rs:362-415`) evaluates reverse-flow hits in the reversed `(arrival_zone -> egress_zone)` direction instead of the initiating forward direction.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D2-09 — Cross-zone reroute leaves reverse companion ingress_zone stale

**Strongest supported defect reading:** `session/mod.rs:2114-2147 revalidate_forwarding_resolution` only swaps `decision.resolution`, `forwarding_generation`, `owner_rg_id` — it does **not** update `metadata.egress_zone` on the forward entry nor `ingress_zone` on the reverse companion (nor *_zone_check). After a permitted cross-zone reroute (lan→wan1 becomes lan→wan2) or egress re-zoning, the reverse entry still claims ingress=wan1. Replies arriving on wan2 then hit `session_hit_authority` (:190-208): `arrival_zone(wan2) != metadata.ingress_zone(wan1)` → `Foreign`, and `foreign_hit_verdict` (:394-403) evaluates policy as `(arrival_zone → hit_egress_zone)` — the reversed pair (wan2→lan), which under a normal one-way permit (lan→wan2 permit, wan2→lan deny) drops 100% of replies; under the asymmetric opposite it forwards replies for a now-denied forward pair.

**Strongest refutation:** Some callers may rebind zones separately (`rebind_zones_pair` exists, D3-03) before/after calling `revalidate_forwarding_resolution`, making this fn's narrowness correct-by-contract ("resolution only"). The claim must show at least one cross-zone reroute caller (#11373/#12074/#9384 path) that calls this fn *without* a companion zone rebind. Also `foreign_hit_verdict` evaluating (arrival→egress) for a reverse hit is arguably the intended #9604 design — the defect is the stale metadata, not the verdict direction; claim's "additionally fix foreign_hit_verdict" is wrong direction.

## D3-03 — Rebind helpers leave stale zone checks

**Strongest supported defect reading:** Source-proven, cleanest claim in batch. `session/mod.rs` `rebind_policy_pair` (~3960-3985) and `rebind_zones_pair` (~3990-4035) set `metadata.ingress_zone/egress_zone` (and policy fields) on forward+reverse companion but never touch `ingress_zone_check/egress_zone_check` (u32 fields, `session/mod.rs:1377`). `shared_ops/store.rs:794-850 restamp_shared_policy_entries::apply` likewise copies zones without checks. After a legitimate rebind to a different zone *name*, the (id, check) pair is inconsistent; any later `synced_entry_is_stale_replay` vintage comparison (`stamped != zone_identity_check(current_name)`) false-positives and evicts a live session on shared promotion/prewarm/BPF republish — self-inflicted DoS on config reload. Note: checks only matter where the vintage arm applies (policy_id==0 sync-family entries) — rebind paths that set `policy_counter=Some(...)` (rebind_policy_pair sets it!) may exempt the entry from the fence anyway; `rebind_zones_pair` (policy untouched) is the cleaner exposure.

**Strongest refutation:** If every rebind caller also restamps checks via `policy_rebind_pair_entries` consumers or the entries always carry policy_counter (exempt), impact is nil. Requires caller audit — but the helpers' own contract ("restamp only zone identity") should include the check half of zone identity.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL (Medium, availability/state-corruption, not a bypass).** Distinct corrective scope from #10620 (closed) — file as residual.

Trivial cross-zone fragmentation denial of service: 32 fragments per shard every 30 seconds from 4 IPs in an untrusted zone blackholes all IPv4/IPv6 fragmented traffic across every security zone sharing the VRF, and spoofed `(src, dst, id)` fragments from an untrusted zone corrupt `OverlapTracker` state for flows in trusted zones.

Root cause (source report):
`OverlapTracker` omits `ingress_zone` from `OverlapKey` / `overlap_same_datagram` and enforces its non-evictable 32-entry cap per `routing_table` rather than per `(routing_table, ingress_zone)`, while `FragAssoc` enforces only a 32-entry per-session cap out of 64 entries per shard with no per-zone cap.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D3-08 — Frag Overlap/FragAssoc omit per-zone quotas and `ingress_zone` — **MATERIAL**

**Strongest supported defect reading.** `OverlapKey` (`fragment_overlap/mod.rs:140ff`, both SHAs) contains `addr_family, src, dst, ident, protocol, routing_domain, fairness_origin` — no `ingress_zone`; `overlap_same_datagram` therefore merges datagrams across zones sharing `(src,dst,ident,protocol,domain)`. Quotas are `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_SENDER_PER_SHARD=8`, `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_SHARD=32`, `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_SHARD=64` (mod.rs:122-135) — keyed by sender and *routing domain*, not zone. Four sender IPs in one zone can hold all 32 domain slots for the 30 s TTL, refusing new fragmented datagrams (`ShardFull`) for every other zone in the same VRF. `FragAssoc` (`fragment_assoc/mod.rs:167-180,437-553`) caps per *session* (32) and per shard (64) with no zone partition.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** Per-sender cap (8/shard, seeded shard by source) means a *single* IP cannot blackhole; the attack needs ≥4 distinct sources sustained at fragment rate — cheap for a botnet/DDoS source but not "trivial 32-packet" from one host: entries expire on 30 s idle / 60 s absolute TTL and completed entries are reclaimable at the domain cap (`check_and_record_fragment_detailed` reclaim path). Zone-blind overlap merging mirrors receiver reassembly semantics (an end host also merges by tuple alone); cross-zone poisoning additionally requires spoofing the victim's exact `(src,dst,ident)` and arriving while its datagram is tracked. FragAssoc entries are only installed for an *admitted* first fragment with a session, so its shard pressure is post-policy.

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — domain-granular (not zone-granular) non-evictable quota plus zone-blind overlap key is a genuine cross-zone DoS/poisoning surface on a pre-policy tracker; "trivial" and "all fragmented traffic" overstate (needs 4+ senders, sustained, same VRF, and only new datagram admission is refused).

**File:line (both SHAs, unchanged):** `fragment_overlap/mod.rs:122-165 (caps+OverlapKey), 862-925 (quota enforcement)`, `fragment_assoc/mod.rs:167-180, 437-453, 533-553`.

**Decisive unresolved check:** Test in `fragment_overlap

Spark:
## D3-08 — FragAssoc / OverlapTracker per-zone quotas

**Strongest defect reading.** `OverlapKey` (fragment_overlap/mod.rs:144-160) has addr_family/src/dst/ident/protocol/routing_domain — no zone; `overlap_same_datagram` (277-284) likewise. Post-commit admission enforces `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_SENDER_PER_SHARD = 8` and `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_SHARD = 32` keyed on routing_domain only (862-925). Two zones sharing VRF 0 therefore share one overlap entry for the same (src,dst,id,proto): a spoofed overlapping fragment from zone A poisons zone B's datagram entry (dropped as Overlap), and 32 incomplete entries in the domain exhaust the reserve for all zones in that VRF (completed entries reclaimable, incomplete not).

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** (1) The FragAssoc half is mostly wrong: `FragKey` carries `FragAuthority { ingress_ifindex, ingress_vlan_id, ingress_zone, routing_table }` (fragment_assoc/mod.rs:253-341, #5798) precisely so cross-zone fragments MISS; per-session cap is 32 *per admitting session* (FRAG_CAP_PER_SESSION_PER_SHARD, mod.rs:179,533-552), so one session cannot consume another zone's associations — the residual is only the shared 64/shard ceiling, reachable only if many sessions in other zones are idle (entries have 2s idle / 10s absolute TTL). (2) Claim's "32 fragments from 4 IPs" ignores the per-sender cap of 8/shard and 16 shards keyed by src: 4 IPs × 8 = 32 only if all four hash to the same shard and same domain and stay incomplete for the TTL; the tracker also runs a pure pre-check that records nothing for refused traffic ("refused traffic can never plant ranges", poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1114-1122). (3) Overlap aliasing requires identical (src,dst,ident,protocol,domain) — the receiver-side reassembly identity; downstream receivers merge on exactly that tuple (mod.rs:272-275, #14127), so keying overlap membership by zone would arguably be wrong for the translated path.

Sharing an SNAT pool across zones (or rules with different `persistent-nat` permit modes) leaks reflexive `(translated_ip, translated_port)` bindings and escalates `target-host` / `target-host-port` permissions to `any-remote-host` across security zones.

Root cause (source report):
`PersistentSourceKey`, `PersistentPermissions`, and `persistent_inbound_lookup` in `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs` are zone-unaware while `parse_source_nat_rules_with_previous` shares a single `PortAllocator` across rules with different `(from_zone, to_zone)` pairs and different `PersistentNatPermitMode` settings.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D3-10 — Shared `PortAllocator` leaks Persistent-NAT permissions across zones — **MATERIAL (bounded)**

**Strongest supported defect reading.** `PersistentSourceKey` (`nat/allocator.rs:124-145`, both SHAs) = `{protocol, src_ip, src_port, routing_scope, remote: None}` — scoped by VRF (`#10018`) but not by egress zone/rule. `PersistentPermissions { any_remote, remotes }` (allocator.rs:148ff) is stored per that key in the single shared `PortAllocator`; `allocate_flow_with_holder` records the *admitting rule's* permit mode into the shared entry (`record_persistent_permission`, allocator.rs:~3180), and inbound lookup checks `permits()` against the same zone-blind key. Two source-NAT rules sharing one pool with different `persistent-nat` permit modes (e.g. `trust→dmz: any-remote-host`, `trust→wan: target-host-port`) therefore merge: an `any_remote=true` grant minted via the dmz rule authorizes arbitrary remote hosts inbound on the wan-side reflexive binding for the same `(proto, src_ip, src_port, routing_scope)`.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** Sharing the *allocator* is deliberate and correct — `(translated_ip, port)` is one wire identity (`nat/source/mod.rs:302-337` comment, `#9389`: splitting allocators caused double-minting and #6979/#8115 overlap refusals). The leak requires the *same internal host* `(src_ip, src_port)` egressing through two different zones in the same routing instance with the same pool — overlapping-IP multi-zone egress of one host is an unusual topology, and Junos itself scopes persistent NAT by rule/rule-set on one egress context. Inbound persistent-NAT traffic still needs a route/zone path back to the host; whether the leaked permission alone admits a session without further policy depends on the inbound persistent-NAT call site [not fully traced]. Lease *identity* sharing (same translated tuple) is intended endpoint-independent NAT behavior; only the *permission widening* (`target-host*` → `any-remote`) is the defect.

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — permission-merging across rules with different permit modes in one shared allocator is code-proven and security-relevant (reflexive pinhole widening); bounded by the same-host/two-zone/

Spark:
## D3-10 — Shared PortAllocator leaks PersistentNat across zones

**Strongest defect reading.** `PersistentSourceKey { protocol, src_ip, src_port, routing_scope, remote: None }` (allocator.rs:124-141) and `PersistentPermissions { any_remote, remotes }` (146-189) are keyed without zone; `record_persistent_permission` merges permits into the per-key record, and `persistent_inbound_lookup` (2301-2345) checks only translated tuple + remote permission. The production inbound loop (poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3455-3500) iterates **every** persistent pool-mode rule whose pool contains the target, with no zone check. So if rule A (zone trust→dmz, AnyRemoteHost) and rule B (zone trust→wan, TargetHostPort) share one pool and one internal host, A's outbound flow records `any_remote=true` on the shared key, and an arbitrary remote can then initiate inbound via the translated tuple that B's stricter policy intended to limit — permissions escalate across egress zones sharing the pool.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** (1) Allocator sharing is deliberate and load-bearing: #9389/#9428 (nat/source/mod.rs:290-337) — splitting allocators per zone/VRF caused double-minting of the same (addr,port) wire identity and #6979/#8115 overlap refusals; "two rule-sets naming one pool must share one allocator, because the pool is one shared resource of wire identities." The claim's fix (zone in PersistentSourceKey) reintroduces exactly that split for the lease layer — though leases ≠ occupancy, so it is not automatically wrong. (2) Persistent NAT semantics (RFC 6888 / Junos `persistent-nat permit any-remote-host|target-host|target-host-port`) attach to the *mapping*, not the zone; Junos enforces the permit mode per rule-set matching the outbound flow, and the mapping is then endpoint-independent by design. The defect needs the conjunction: same pool deliberately shared across two rule-sets with *different* permit modes + same internal (src_ip,src_port,protocol,routing_scope) originating through both. (3) Inbound still must pass zone policy/host-inbound after DNAT translation; persistent lookup only supplies the translation candidate (and conflicting candidates → Denied, allocator.rs:2339-23

## Decisive regression

On little-endian (x86/arm64 LE) exactly one of these encodings can match the map writer. The writer is Go: `binary.BigEndian.Uint32(v4)` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1136, 1423, 1929`) — matching `parse_ipv4`, **not** the GRE-inner classifier. Likewise `shim_v4_key` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/wg_control/kernel_path.rs:125-130`) uses `from_ne_bytes` under a comment claiming "userspace-xdp `parse_ipv4`" does so — false at lib.rs:1932 — and its test `v4_key_matches_the_shims_native_endian_parse_9594` asserts the buggy encoding against itself instead of against the Go/BE encoding. `early_filter.rs:43-48` documents the correct BE convention explicitly ("the same encoding Go uses for the `userspace_local_v4` keys").

## D4-01 — Endian mismatch in GRE-inner / WG kernel-path local maps

**Strongest defect reading.** On x86_64 (little-endian), `u32::from_ne_bytes([172,16,80,8])` = 0x0850_10AC while the Go writer stores `binary.BigEndian.Uint32` = 0xAC10_5008. **Strongest refutation / alternative.** Checked and it fails: the healthy main path uses the be encoding everywhere — parse_ipv4 `dst_v4: u32::from_be_bytes` (lib.rs:1932), probes at 1555/2146/2172/2198 use pkt.dst_v4; Go writers use BigEndian at maps_sync.go:1271,1427,1596,2106 and tests pin BigEndian keys (maps_sync_addrlist_prune_3924_test.go:55, maps_sync_cap_test.go:198-199,232). early_filter.rs:43-48 documents "parse_ipv4 stores dst_v4 big-endian… the same encoding Go uses" and #3087 fixed the sibling site. One caveat: BPF map keys are raw memory — Go's `ebpf` marshals uint32 in native (little) endian, so the *stored integer value* BigEndian.Uint32(octets) is what makes the in-memory bytes equal wire order; the Rust XDP side reading the same map memory must produce the identical integer value on the same host, which is from_be_bytes of the octets. from_ne_bytes coincides only for palindromic addresses. Claim stands.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL, High.** (Palindromic/reverse-symmetric addresses unaffected; that narrows, not negates.)

**Decisive unresolved check.** None needed for existence — static oracle is complete (Go writer + heal

## D4-03 — Pre-MAC SYN-cookie ACK sketch reintroduces spoofed-ACK starvation — **MATERIAL**

Spoofed-ACK starvation requires source-IP spoofing capability toward the firewall and knowledge of the victim (src,dst,dport); on ingress-filtered networks spoofing a *specific* internal/NAT source may be blocked. Sketch is per-zone per-worker, so aggregate budget scales with workers [INFERENCE], softening the "16/s per service" NAT figure per worker — but equally, hash/RSS placement means a given client's budget is whichever worker it lands on. The pre-MAC bound has a genuine DoS-protection purpose (SipHash exhaustion), so the fix is ordering/refund (validate-then-charge-failures), not removal.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D4-05 — Chained IPv6 fragment headers bypass flag + sizing screens — **MATERIAL (first leg only; second leg refuted in part)**

**Strongest supported defect reading.** In `extract_screen_info` (`screen/extract.rs:489-550`, both SHAs), the `#14129` refinement for a *second* Fragment header with non-zero offset executes only `info.is_first_fragment = false` (extract.rs:514-518) — it does **not** update `info.ip_frag_off`/`frag_data_off`, which retain the first header's values (offset 0). The two consumer families then split predicates: `check_tcp_flag_screens` (`screen/stateless.rs:49-51`) skips when `is_fragment && !is_first_fragment` ⇒ syn-frag/flag screens off; `check_ping_of_death`/`check_teardrop` (stateless.rs:145-152, 250-269) test `(ip_frag_off & 0xFFF8) > 0` ⇒ 0 ⇒ sizing screens off. A `[Frag(off=0,M=1), Frag(off>0)]` packet is in neither family — the dual bypass is a direct field-level proof.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** (1) Multiple IPv6 Fragment headers in one packet violate RFC 8200 ("each extension header at most once"); the receiving stack (Linux reassembly) keys on the first fragment header and treats the second as payload — the "non-first fragment with offset 65528" never reassembles into a ping-of-death at the end host, so screen evasion ≠ end-host exploit delivery; the residual harm is screen-accounting evasion on a malformed packet other layers may drop. (2) The report's second leg is **largely already fixed in the audited code**: for a genuine non-first fragment, extract.rs (the `#9114` block) sets `info.protocol = frame[offset]` (the Fragment header's NextHdr) when the protocol is the no-L4 sentinel, specifically so `check_icmp_fragment`/icmp-flood/udp-flood fire — the claim "non-first fragments bypass icmp-fragment/icmp-flood/udp-flood" is not supported for the sentinel case; it survives only if `info.protocol` was pre-set to something else by an earlier header.

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL (narrow) — the chained-header `is_first_fragment`/`ip_frag_off` inconsistency is real and should be fixed by rejecting multi-Fragment-header packets or keeping fields consistent; the broader "simultaneously bypasses five screens + flood scre

Spark:
## D4-05 — Chained IPv6 Fragment headers bypass screens

**Strongest defect reading.** extract.rs:489-503 (#14129 sticky logic): first non-atomic Frag header governs ip_frag_off/frag_data_off; a later non-zero-offset header only sets `is_first_fragment = false`. For chain [Frag#1(off=0,M=1), Frag#2(off>0)]: ip_frag_off remains Frag#1's value (offset bits 0). Then stateless.rs v6 ping-of-death (142-153) and teardrop (246-270) compute offset from `pkt.ip_frag_off & 0xFFF8` = 0, so a Frag#2 with huge offset never triggers them; while check_tcp_flag_screens (49-51) *does* skip via !is_first_fragment. Net: neither family adjudicates the packet as the non-first fragment it (also) is. Multiple Fragment headers are RFC 8200-nonconformant, so fail-closed handling is the expected posture.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** (1) Second leg refuted: for a (single) non-first fragment, extract.rs:546-549 already recovers `info.protocol = frame[offset]` (FragHdr.NextHdr) when the shim protocol is the no-L4 sentinel (#9114) — so icmp-fragment/icmp-flood/udp-flood do fire; the claim's "Non-First Fragment Extension Headers Bypass…" leg describes pre-#9114 behaviour or requires protocol preset to something else, not shown. In the chained case the walk breaks at Frag#2 (528-549) with protocol recovery from Frag#2's NextHdr if sentinel — again not a clean bypass. (2) First-leg impact is bounded: the packet still faces overlap tracker (which parses fragment headers independently), fragment association, and policy; the bypass is of two *screen profiles* (ping-of-death/teardrop) for a malformed double-Fragment-header packet, and only when those profiles are enabled. (3) Frag#2's data is not part of this packet's reassembly contribution in any sane receiver (second fragment header inside a fragment payload is payload bytes, not a header) — [INFERENCE] real receivers treat the bytes after Frag#1 as fragment data, so the "non-first fragment" the screens miss may never be reassembled as such; the evasion is against the screen's own model.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL (narrowed to leg 1).** Inconsistent fragment state (is_first_fragment=false while ip_frag_off reports first) is a real ext

## D4-07 — WG endpoint lookup ignores dst_ip / zone — **MATERIAL (functional; zone-bypass framing refuted)**

**Strongest supported defect reading.** `wg_endpoint_for_listen_port` (`afxdp/wg/decap.rs:165-185`, both SHAs) scans `wg_engines` (a hash map — iteration order not config order) and returns the **first** entry matching only `(wg_listen_port, transport_instance)`; it takes no `dst_ip`. With two WG tunnels sharing a listen port in one transport instance bound to different local IPs, decap/underlay-exemption can select the wrong engine; WireGuard's authenticated encryption then fails (drop), or the wrong `logical_ifindex`/inner zone is used for the attempt. `is_wg_listener_tuple` (decap.rs:131-155) inherits the mis-selection.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** This is fail-closed, not a zone-isolation breach: `wg_outer_zone_matches` (decap.rs:87-129) *is* applied by callers after selection and requires `local_zone(dst_ip) == ingress_zone && source_zone(endpoint.source) == ingress_zone`; a wrong-zone endpoint is rejected, and a wrong same-zone endpoint cannot decrypt another tunnel's traffic (WG keys), so no cross-tunnel traffic acceptance or inner-zone confusion for *admitted* traffic results — packets drop. The comment (decap.rs:158) documents the assumption "0, 1 or 2 [tunnels] in practice"; same-port multi-tunnel on one instance is the unhandled config. Harm: non-deterministic decap failure / listener-exemption misses (availability, config-dependent), not "breaking zone isolation" in the permissive direction.

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL as a correctness/availability defect for same-port multi-tunnel configs (plus the `?`-vs-`continue` lookup abort); the Wrong-Zone Classification/security framing is refuted — every downstream check fails closed.

## D5-03 — Fingerprints/identity maps omit quarantine scrub; rematch suppression

**Defect reading.** Publish path scrubs: `builder.go` → `quarantineCollidingZones` → `scrubPoliciesForQuarantinedZones`, and partial republishes re-scrub (`manager_compile.go:1123`, `policies_reject.go:205` via `policySnapshotAfterZoneQuarantine`). Consumer `daemon_policy_invalidate.go:902-916` diffs old/new via exactly these four functions to decide policy-rematch re-evaluation. A commit whose *only* enforcement-relevant change is a zone becoming quarantined (StableZoneID collision introduced, or poisoned child added) therefore produces identical fingerprints/ID maps while the published snapshot drops/narrows the rule — live sessions of the dropped rule are never re-evaluated.

**Refutation/alternative.** The hash DOES capture the quarantined zone's *name* disappearing from a Match set only if the config text changes; a pure collision (two zones folding to one StableZoneID) changes no policy text, so the gap is real but requires a quarantine-set transition between the two compared commits. Ordinary zone edits (rename, interface moves) change fingerprints through other fields. Impact is stale-session persistence until session timeout/reaper, not new-flow admission — new flows see the scrubbed snapshot.

Root cause (source report):
`buildInterfaceSnapshotsFrom` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:384-418`) emits a base row (`IsUnit: false`) that shares the unit `.0` netdev (`Ifindex` and live kernel `Addresses` from `buildLinkSnapshot(linuxName)`) while computing `RoutingInstance` / `RoutingDomain` from the bare interface key `name` (`RoutingDomain: 0`), and neither `localAddressRoutingDomain` nor `buildLocalAddressEntriesWithExclusions` skips non-unit base rows that collapse onto a unit or have fan-up-only identity.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D5-04 — Base-row default domain leaks VRF locals; `localAddressRoutingDomain` rejects untagged VRF ifaces

**Defect reading.** `interfaces.go:380-418` (`buildInterfaceSnapshotsFrom`): the base row (`IsUnit:false`) gets `Ifindex`/`Addresses` from `buildLinkSnapshot(linuxName)` — for an untagged `.0`, `snapshotLinuxName(base)==snapshotLinuxName(unit.0)`, so base and unit share ifindex AND live addresses — but `RoutingDomain: routingDomainForInterfaceKey(name /*bare*/, ...)` where the bare name is typically absent from `ifaceRoutingInstance` (the unit `.0` key is present), yielding domain 0. Consequences, both traced: (a) `buildLocalAddressEntriesWithExclusions` (`maps_sync.go:1579ff`) iterates ALL rows including the base row and emits `(Domain:0, addr)` for every VRF address → Rust `local_v4/v6` treats a VRF IP as inet.0-local → `XDP_PASS` to kernel instead of zone adjudication. (b) `localAddressRoutingDomain` (`maps_sync.go:138-155`) sees the same ifindex with domains {0,1} → `found && domain != iface.RoutingDomain` → returns `(0,false)` → `syncIngressIfaceMapLocked` (941-953) DELETES the `userspace_ingress_domains` entry (fail-closed comment notwithstanding, this also kills correct local classification for that ifindex).

**Refutation/alternative.** Partial guard exists: `localAddressRoutingDomain` ambiguity is *intentionally* fail-closed (delete domain, traffic goes through userspace policy, not kernel PASS) — so consequence (b) is degraded classification, not a bypass. Consequence (a) is the security-relevant one and has no equivalent guard in `buildLocalAddressEntriesWithExclusions` (it only skips `AdminDisabled`/`unresolvedLo0LocalAddressOwner`). Whether the base row truly duplicates addresses depends on `buildLinkSnapshot` returning unit addresses for the base linux name — true for untagged (same netdev), false for VLAN units (distinct child netdev, disjoint addresses). Claim correctly scopes to untagged.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL (leak (a) is the defect; (b) is fail-closed fallout of the same root). Not FIXED. Parent issues #13929/#14031 closed — they added domain scoping; this is the base-row hole they missed, not a DUP.**

Is base row perhaps suppressed when units exist? Loop emits base unconditionally before units. - Severity (source): `High`

Adding a lifeline interface to a VRF silently suppresses both `#10431` ambiguous-ingress fail-closed drop rules (`IngressDenyNetdevs`) and zone flood-screen rules (`IngressNetdevs`) for all non-lifeline interfaces in that VRF, failing open on host-bound traffic arriving on unzoned or conflicting-zone VRF members.

Root cause (source report):
`hostInboundIngressClaims` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:808-833`) collapses `lifelineNetdevs` to their VRF master (`effectiveLifelines["vrf-mgmt"] = true`) and then discards every non-lifeline slave whose `vrfMasters[netdev]` equals that VRF master, directly contradicting the per-slave `meta sdifname` architecture documented at `HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs` (`lines 1510-1514`, `"the set carries NO vrf-mgmt blanket"`).

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D5-06 — `hostInboundIngressClaims` VRF-master lifeline blanket

**Defect reading.** `zones_host_inbound.go:803-841`: `effectiveLifelines` rewrites each lifeline netdev to `vrfMasters[netdev]` when VRF-enslaved, marking the MASTER lifeline; then every non-lifeline claim with `vrfEnslaved[netdev]` gets `target=vrfMasters[netdev]` and is dropped by `if effectiveLifelines[target] { continue }`. So one lifeline slave in a VRF suppresses ALL co-VRF claims. Both consumers inherit it: `hostInboundViewIngressNetdevsWithMasters` (846ff, flood-screen `IngressNetdevs`) and `hostInboundViewIngressDenyNetdevs` (889ff, #10431 ambiguous-ingress fail-closed `IngressDenyNetdevs`). This directly contradicts the per-slave `sdifname` design documented at `HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs` (1510ff: "the set carries NO vrf-mgmt blanket").

**Refutation/alternative.** Two partial mitigations exist in the same builder: `IngressVRFScopes` (`hostInboundViewVRFIngressScopes`, 861ff) and `view.LifelineVRFScopes` are computed per-slave from raw `netdevSigs`/`lifelineNetdevs`, NOT via `hostInboundIngressClaims` — so the VRF-scope rendering path still adjudicates non-lifeline slaves correctly where nftables renders scopes. The bug bites only the flat `IngressNetdevs`/`IngressDenyNetdevs` lists. Whether the renderer prefers scopes over flat lists for VRF-enslaved netdevs determines real-world impact; the claim asserts both lists are used, which is true, but doesn't show the flat-list rendering is reached for VRF members.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL (narrowed: flat-list suppression is code-proven; end-to-end fail-open depends on renderer precedence). Not FIXED. #13413/#10751 closed are the parent fixes that missed this site, not DUPs.**

**Decisive check:** Go test `TestHostInboundIngressClaims…`: netdevSigs with lifeline slave + non-lifeline slave sharing `vrf-mgmt` master; assert non-lifeline sig survives in claims (expected) — then check the nftables renderer for whether `IngressDenyNetdevs` (flat) is emitted for VRF-enslaved targets alongside scopes.

Spark:
## D5-06 — Lifeline VRF-master blanket in `hostInboundIngressClaims`

**Defect reading:** `zones_host_inbound.go:803-841` verbatim: `effectiveLifelines` maps each lifeline netdev through `vrfMasters[netdev]` when enslaved; then loop drops any netdev with `effectiveLifelines[netdev]` **and** any whose rewritten `target` is an effective lifeline. So one lifeline slave in `vrf-mgmt` marks `vrf-mgmt` itself lifeline → every non-lifeline slave in that VRF is discarded from claims → absent from both `hostInboundViewIngressNetdevsWithMasters` (flood-screen IngressNetdevs) and `hostInboundViewIngressDenyNetdevs` (ambiguous fail-closed drops). Directly contradicts documented invariant at 1510-1514: "the set carries NO vrf-mgmt blanket… a non-lifeline member stays denied" (for the *lifeline* rendering path, #10751) — the claims path kept the pre-sdifname blanket.

**Refutation/alternative:** Could suppression be harmless because VRF-ingress *scopes* (`hostInboundViewVRFIngressScopes`, per-slave, lifeline-aware) still render rules for those slaves? That path handles *unambiguous single-sig* members for view ingress; the DenyNetdevs (ambiguous, multi-sig) path has no per-slave fallback — ambiguous host-bound traffic on a co-VRF interface loses its fail-closed drop. Flood-screen IngressNetdevs similarly list-based. So at minimum the #10431 ambiguous-drop half is a genuine fail-open.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL. Not FIXED.**

- Symbols: `buildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes`, `syncIngressIfaceMapLocked`
- Severity (source): `High`

On any VLAN trunk that also has an unzoned, quarantined, or disabled `.0` unit stanza (or a disabled native-VLAN unit), `USERSPACE_INGRESS_IFACE_FLAG_TAGGED_ONLY` is stripped from the trunk parent `ifindex`, allowing untagged (`VID 0`) spoofed frames on the trunk to bypass `TAGGED_ONLY_LOCAL_DROP` in XDP and enter the kernel local-delivery path for any tagged unit's IP address in the same routing domain.

Root cause (source report):
`buildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1788, 1811-1823`) records `untaggedUnitIfindexes` and `nativeVLANUnitCounts` without checking `!iface.AdminDisabled && iface.Zone != ""`.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D5-09 — Tagged-only flag cleared by unzoned/disabled `.0`

**Defect reading.** `maps_sync.go:1779-1851` (`buildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes`): second loop records `untaggedUnitIfindexes[bindIfindex]` for any `IsUnit && HasSuffix(Name,".0") && VLANID==0` row — no `AdminDisabled`/`Zone` check; native loop (1811ff) likewise counts units without survival checks. Final loop `delete(taggedOnly, ifindex)` for every untagged-unit ifindex. So a trunk with tagged units (which set `taggedOnly[parent]`) plus a default stub `.0` (unzoned, or `AdminDisabled`, or quarantined-unzoned) loses `USERSPACE_INGRESS_IFACE_FLAG_TAGGED_ONLY`. XDP (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1545ff`): flag off → VID-0 frame to a firewall-owned dst (local in the ingress domain, or interface-NAT) is NOT `TAGGED_ONLY_LOCAL_DROP`ped and takes a local PASS arm.

**Refutation/alternative.** Scope limit: the drop only protects firewall-owned destinations (`is_firewall_owned_destination` = local ∪ interface-NAT); untagged *transit* was never dropped by this flag, and local delivery still meets nftables `hook input` host-inbound chains. Also, is a stub `.0` actually emitted with `VLANID==0` and the parent's bind ifindex when unzoned? The builder emits unit rows regardless of zone (zone is a separate map), and `userspaceSkipsIngressInterface`/adjudication happens elsewhere — so yes, the row exists. Whether Junos semantics even want tagged-only treatment when a `.0` stanza exists-but-is-disabled is debatable: a *zoned, enabled* `.0` legitimately owns VID-0 (that's the existing correct arm); the defect is only that disabled/unzoned `.0` — which owns nothing — also clears it.

**Gate verdict: MATERIAL (narrowed to disabled/unzoned/quarantined `.0` and disabled native units). Not FIXED. #12055 closed is the introducing fix, not a DUP.**

**Decisive check:** Go test `buildUserspaceTaggedOnlyIngressIfindexes` with trunk(parent, `.100` zoned) + (`.0` unzoned) vs (`.0` disabled): assert parent absent today (bug) for both, present-as-untagged-owner only for zoned+enabled `.0`.

**Defect reading:** `maps_sync.go:1811-1823`: `if iface.IsUnit && strings.HasSuffix(iface.Name,".0") && iface.VLANID==0 { untaggedUnitIfindexes[bindIfindex]=... }` — no `Zone`/`AdminDisabled` predicate; final loop deletes those ifindexes from `taggedOnly`. Native-VLAN counting similarly unguarded. So a trunk with tagged units + a stub/disabled/unzoned `unit 0` (JunOS default) loses `TAGGED_ONLY` → XDP `TAGGED_ONLY_LOCAL_DROP` not applied → untagged frames can reach local IPs of tagged units in same domain (per XDP shim semantics [cited, not re-read in XDP]).

**Refutation/alternative:** Is an unzoned `.0` row actually emitted with `VLANID==0, IsUnit==true` and same bind ifindex? **Strongest refutation / alternative:** Minor: the same "rejects what programming would skip" shape could be defended as strictness (an operator typo in a quarantined zone still signals config rot), and quarantined zones arise only on StableZoneID collisions or reserved/poisoned names, so the trigger is an already-degenerate config. But the function's own doc comment states the contract — "this sweep must reject exactly what the loop rejects, never more" (written for the nil-zone case) — and `programZoneMaps` + `userspace/screens.go:22-37` both apply the exclusion, so the pre-pass is broader than production by the codebase's own stated invariant. Fail-closed (apply blocked, old config retained): availability, not bypass.

Instead the pairs vanish and traffic for them falls to the next tier (single-wildcard/both-any/global/default) — if the dropped pair carried the only deny, that is a fail-open; if it carried a permit, an outage. Direction depends on config, which the claim does not bound.

**Strongest refutation / alternative:** Severity and framing only. "Critical" requires broad catastrophic loss with an actor story; here the prerequisite is an operator authoring a non-JunOS bracketed zone list in container form, the commit is the operator's own, and the fall-through tier is still policy-evaluated (default deny unless a broader permit exists). Real Junos would reject the syntax at commit — the defect is that xpf accepts-and-truncates instead of rejecting. That is a High config-integrity defect (silent loss of authored policy on a clean commit), not Critical. Note also the tolerant path: the claim shows the strict-clean compile; whether the lenient/HA-sync path records `MalformedZonePairs` poison for these shapes (the :168 branch records several #12633 poisons for *other* nested shapes) determines whether the snapshot builder also drops them silently — worth one check, but the strict result alone sustains th

- Severity (source): `High`

When a security zone's `to-zone junos-host` policy program consists of `then permit` term(s) that either have an empty cross-family intersection in both IPv4 and IPv6 (e.g., `source-address admin-v4` + `application junos-pingv6`) or are skipped on tolerant load via `#12040` (`skipPermit == true` due to `LenientContentDropped` or `ApplicationReferenceMatchDrops`), `BuildJunosHostDenyProjection` returns `Representable = true` with `RulesV4 = nil` and `RulesV6 = nil`, omitting the `#11065` implicit terminal deny in both families and failing open to coarse `host-inbound-traffic` admission for 100% of IPv4 and IPv6 traffic.

Root cause (source report):
In `junosHostProjectProgram` (`pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go:657-698`), `hasPermitV4` and `hasPermitV6` are only set to `true` inside `add()` (`lines 669-676`) *after* `if t.action == PolicyPermit && t.skipPermit { continue }` (`lines 679-681`) and *after* `junosHostBuildRule` returns `ok == true` (`lines 586-605`). When no `permit` term emits a concrete `JunosHostReturn` rule in either family, `hasPermitProgram := hasPermitV4 || hasPermitV6` (`line 691`) evaluates to `false`, so lines 691-697 skip appending the `#11065` terminal `JunosHostDrop` rule in both `RulesV4` and `RulesV6`.

Meanwhile, `portInSpec` calls `canonicalPort(parts[0])` (`n < 1`) instead of `config.NormalizeExplicitPortRange(tok)`.

## Lane evidence (narrowed scope governs)
Opus:
## D8-09 — pkg/appid dropped-constraint catalog, 0-N range, icmp-v6

**Strongest supported defect reading.** `BuildCatalog` (`pkg/appid/catalog.go:79ff` both SHAs) and `resolveTupleFallbackWithIndex` (`pkg/appid/runtime.go:~411ff`) never call `config.ApplicationMatchDrops`. `ApplicationMatchDrops` (`pkg/config/application_match_drops_9525.go:67`, both SHAs) returns non-empty for e.g. value-less match leaves (`IncompleteDirectLeaves` on `destination-port`), malformed ICMP (`UnknownICMP`), unimplemented leaves (#9603). For `application broken-tcp { protocol tcp; destination-port; }` the compiled `DestinationPort==""`, `ICMPType==nil`, so `!icmpTypeConstrained(app)` passes, `parsePortRange("")=(0,0,nil)`, `emittable=true` → protocol-wide `(0,0)` row; tuple fallback likewise matches via `portInSpec(dst,"")==true`. That contradicts the documented #9525 contract ("a leniently-loaded bad app is inert") enforced in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go`/`junos_host_deny.go` but not here. Impact is mis-labelling (AppID stamp / session name), not policy verdict — severity should be downgraded from High toward Medium, existence unaffected.

**Strongest refutation / alternative.** (a) *0-N leg is false*: `canonicalPort` (`runtime.go:580`, both SHAs) rejects `0` (`n<1`), but strict `validatePortSpec` (`pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:1108`) *allows* lo=0 in ranges (`must be 0-65535 in a range`; only bare `0` is rejected), and `BuildCatalog` deliberately preserves `0-N` (`NormalizeExplicitPortRange`, `catalog.go:524`, pinned by `catalog_port_zero_5194_test.go`: "A 0-N range stays emittable"). So `portInSpec(x,"0-1023")==false` is a real Go↔Rust/Go↔catalog inconsistency for dst/src port 0 only — real sessions essentially never have dst port 0, and the fallback failing closed (no label) is the safe direction. At most a low-severity parity nit, not the claimed rejection bug; suggested fix direction (use `NormalizeExplicitPortRange` in `portInSpec`) would make port-0 match, debatable. (b) *icmp-v6 leg is false as a defect*: `ProtocolNumber` (`catalog.go:318-326`) maps `icmpv6|icmp6|junos-icmp6-all|junos-pingv6→58` but not hyphenated `icmp-v6`; `junos_host_deny_resolve.go:337`

- **Strongest defect:** Real executed behaviour (overlay test, exit 0, both SHAs — `pkg/appid` untouched in delta). (1) Lenient `destination-port;` leaves `IncompleteDirectLeaves=["destination-port"]`, i.e. `config.ApplicationMatchDrops(app)!=∅` (`pkg/config/application_match_drops_9525.go:67`), yet `BuildCatalog` (`pkg/appid/catalog.go:140-267`) gates only on `protoOK/srcOK/dstOK`/reversed-range and `icmpTypeConstrained` (`catalog.go:482`) — never `ApplicationMatchDrops` — so it emits `CatalogEntry{DstPortLow:0,DstPortHigh:0}` (the unconstrained sentinel) for `broken-tcp`, and `resolveTupleFallbackWithIndex` (`runtime.go:411+`, `consider` checks only nil/`icmpTypeConstrained`/`matchTuple`) stamps TCP/8443 `broken-tcp` when AppID stamping is off. ## D9-05 — Post-promotion early returns bypass host-auth closeout, strand preactivation fence

**Strongest supported defect reading.** `closeoutHostAuthOnCancel` (`daemon_apply_hostauth.go:202-223`, both SHAs) runs `applyHostAuthorizationCloseout` **only** for `context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded`; non-cancel errors return unchanged. Meanwhile :510 `applyHostInboundPreNetworkdAddressFence` may already have installed the preactivation drop fence. Result: committed tightening (lo0/host-inbound/credentials) not enforced in kernel/OS files until a later successful apply, while ActiveConfig claims it — a monotonic-revocation gap. #5679's ordinary-compile-error path runs the tail, but abort-class errors by definition don't.

## Defect (at origin/master)
- Files: `pkg/cluster/sync_zone_rg.go:52-154`, `pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:401-544, 1159-1215`, `pkg/dataplane/session_node_local.go:42-50, 99-107`, `pkg/dataplane/bpf_session_value.go:215-260`
- Symbols: `SessionSync.ShouldSyncSessionV4`, `SessionSync.ShouldSyncSessionV6`, `zoneOwnershipSnapshot.shouldSyncV4`, `zoneOwnershipSnapshot.shouldSyncV6`, `SessionSync.resolveSessionRG`, `zoneOwnershipSnapshot.resolveRG`, `dataPlaneSessionStore.ReconcileClusterBulk`
- Severity (source): `High`

1. **Stale/revoked session retention across `BulkEnd`:** When sessions owned by RG 2 on node 1 close or are revoked by security policy while the sync link is disconnected, the subsequent bulk sync to node 0 omits them, and `ReconcileClusterBulk` (`pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:1171, 1207`) calls `input.ShouldSyncV4(key, val)`. Because `shouldSyncV4` returns `true` (treating node 1's RG 2 sessions as locally owned by node 0), `!shouldSyncV4(...)` is `false`, so `ReconcileClusterBulk` skips deleting every stale RG 2 session in that multi-RG zone. 2. **Split-brain echo loop:** Node 0's periodic `SessionSync.sweep()` and `storeBulkWalk()` treat those peer-synced RG 2 rows as locally owned (`ShouldSyncSessionV4 == true`) and re-transmit them back to node 1 with a freshly incremented `SyncGeneration` and `IngressIfaceFold = 0`, overwriting node 1's authoritative session state or resurrecting sessions closed on node 1.

Root cause (source report):
`ShouldSyncSessionV4/V6` (`pkg/cluster/sync_zone_rg.go:55-71`) and `zoneOwnershipSnapshot.shouldSyncV4/V6` (`:111-129`) assume that peer-synced sessions read back from `ForEachV4/V6` or `IterateSessions` still carry `val.IngressIfaceFold != 0` (`#7095`), and neither predicate checks `val.Flags&dataplane.SessFlagClusterSynced != 0`. In reality, `IngressIfaceFold` is a Go-only field on `SessionValue`/`SessionValueV6` (`pkg/dataplane/types.go:295, 742`) that is never persisted in `bpfSessionValue`/`bpfSessionValueV6` (`pkg/dataplane/bpf_session_value.go:215-260`), and `SessionSync` maintains no receiver-side memo for `IngressIfaceFold`. Because `ScrubNodeLocal()` simultaneously zeroes `IngressIfindex` and `IngressVlanID` on peer-installed rows, both the `(IngressIfindex, IngressVlanID)` lookup and the `IngressIfaceFold` lookup fail (`ok == false`), triggering the zone-wide OR fallback (`s.zoneSetSyncs(ingressZone)` / `z.shouldSync(ingressZone)`), which evaluates `true` whenever ANY RG in that multi-RG zone is locally primary.

In `ReconcileClusterBulk` (`session_store.go:1171,1207`) that `true` short-circuits the stale check (`if shouldSync || … { return true }`) despite `SessFlagClusterSynced` being set — so stale RG2 rows are never bulk-purged and are re-exported by sweep (echo). Existing #11012 tests construct `SessionValue` in memory (fold populated) or use full-struct mock stores, exactly the blind spot the claim identifies.
- **Strongest refutation / alternative:** Severity hinges on multi-RG zones (`len(rgs)>1`) with split RG primaries — in single-RG or co-primary deployments the zone fallback gives the correct answer, so this is not a general HA defect. 1. Preserve a receiver-side memo for `(IngressIfaceFold, EgressIfaceFold)` keyed by `(SessionKey, SessionID)` alongside `installTableRecvV4/V6` and `sourceNatICMPRecvV4/V6` in `SessionSync`, restoring it on sweep/bulk read-back and `ReconcileClusterBulk`. 2. - Severity (source): `High`

1. **Complete loss of standby policy hit accounting after 15 seconds:** Every session that survives one 15s `SessionSync.sweep()` cycle has its `metadata.policy_counter` and `metadata.policy_counter_idx` wiped to `(None, 0)` on the standby; after failover, post-failover packets on those sessions never increment per-policy hit counters. 2. **Bypass of `#9526` deleted first-policy session purge after failover:** For the first compiled policy rule (`policy_id == 0`), `entry.metadata.policy_id` is `0` (indistinguishable from "no policy ID"), so `purge_sessions_bound_to_deleted_first_policy` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/revalidation.rs:348-354`) identifies sessions admitted by that first policy exclusively via `entry.metadata.policy_counter == Some(old_first_counter_idx)`. Because `SessionSync.sweep()` wipes `entry.metadata.policy_counter` to `None` within 15s, if a failover occurs and the operator deletes that first security policy (leaving remaining policies), `purge_sessions_bound_to_deleted_first_policy` misses every synced session whose `policy_counter` was wiped, allowing reverse-sustained flows admitted only by the deleted policy to survive policy deletion indefinitely.

Root cause (source report):
`PolicyRuleID` (`#11070`) and `PolicyCounterIdx` (`#3301`) are sync-only fields on `dataplane.SessionValue` and `dataplane.SessionValueV6` that are not stored in `bpfSessionValue` / `bpfSessionValueV6`. When `#9412`, `#9752`, `#10888`, and `#11064` fixed periodic `SessionSync.sweep()` erasing sync-only fields by adding per-session memos in `stampInstallGenV4/V6` and `installClusterSyncedV4/V6`, `PolicyRuleID` and `PolicyCounterIdx` were omitted from both the sender and receiver memos.
