## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end in source. Update path: new drop-in is written, `sshd -t` passes, reload fails transiently → `noteSSHDReloadResult(err)` latches `sshdReload=true` **and** `revertDropIn("reload-failed")` restores the prior (permissive) bytes (or deletes the drop-in). The #6800 comment claims this path "has its own retry owner" because the file now differs from desired — but the only background retry owner, `reassertServiceReloadDebtOnce`, does **not** re-render: it validates and reloads whatever is on disk (the reverted file) and on success calls `noteSSHDReloadResult(nil)`, clearing the debt and logging "sshd reload re-asserted". Net effect after one transient failure during a hardening commit (`root-login allow`→`deny`, ciphers/MACs, limits): commit reports success, disk + running sshd both enforce the old permissive policy indefinitely, telemetry shows no owed reload. Second arm also verified: the no-change early return (`prior == content && !legacyPresent`, :1040) does not check `!d.sshdReloadOwed()` (unlike the removal branch at :1007), so even a later identical apply will not reload while a debt is outstanding. - Strongest refutation / alternative: The revert-on-reload-failure itself is defensible (don't leave a drop-in the running daemon hasn't accepted), and the failure needs a transient `systemctl reload sshd` error at exactly the hardening commit; the next *config-changing* apply would rewrite and reload correctly, so "permanent" means "until the next ssh-config change or daemon restart", not eternal. But the debt-clearing reassert is the indefensible part: it 
- Spark: Verified control flow both revs: reload failure → `noteSSHDReloadResult(err)` latches debt (`:1129`) AND `revertDropIn("reload-failed")` restores permissive prior (`:1133`); `reassertServiceReloadDebtOnce:358-383` then validates+reloads the *on-disk reverted* file and clears debt (`noteSSHDReloadResult(nil):380`) without ever re-driving `applySSHConfig(ActiveConfig)`; plus `applySSHConfig:1040-1042` early-return lacks `!sshdReloadOwed()` (removal branch at `:1007` has it — asymmetry is in-tree evidence of oversight). Net: hardening commit permanently reverts + falsely reports convergence.

- Opus: Verified on master: `rematchRenamedV4/V6/Match` build `policymatch.Query` with no `ICMPType/ICMPCode` (session keys store echo identifier in ports; no type/code field exists on `SessionKey`/`SessionPolicyTuple`), and `reauthorizePolicyCandidates`'s `isPermitted` does the same and additionally never calls `capturedTunnelDiscriminatorValid` (the GRE guard the rename paths call at entry). `matchSingleApp` returns false for any app with `ICMPType != nil` when the query type is nil — so in first-match order, an earlier `deny junos-icmp-ping` is skipped and a later broader permit matches. In `reauthorizePolicyCandidates` the `RuleID == key` requirement does not save it: the kept session's own permit rule is exactly the key, and the newly-inserted deny (different rule, earlier order) is what nil-type evaluation skips. The asymmetry with GRE — explicitly failed closed at `daemon_policy_rename.go:517` because the tuple lacks the discriminator — proves the pattern was understood and ICMP was missed. - Strongest refutation / alternative: Impact needs a live ICMP/ICMPv6 session present at rename/rollback time with an icmp-type-constrained deny ordered before the session's permit; ICMP sessions are short-lived and operators rarely order `deny junos-icmp-ping` before `permit junos-icmp-all`. `reauthorizePolicyCandidates` is rollback-only. None of that negates the mechanism — extensive rematch exists precisely to re-judge live sessions against new policy, and it silently mis-judges this protocol class in the fail-open direction. - Decisive unresolved check: proposed `TestRematchRenamedV4F
- Spark: Grep confirms neither `daemon_policy_rename.go` nor `daemon_policy_invalidate_capture.go` ever sets `ICMPType` (zero hits, both revs); queries are built from 5-tuple only. `policymatch.go:2725-2746`: `app.ICMPType!=nil && icmpType==nil → false`. Hence an icmp-type-constrained deny can never match in rematch/reauthorize, while unconstrained permit can — first-match fall-through keeps a session the deny would kill. GRE got `capturedTunnelDiscriminatorValid`; ICMP (1/58) stores identifier in ports, no type/code — same lossy-tuple class, unguarded. ## #14705 — [gemini-hostile D14-03] Pre-Authentication NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat in heartbeatReceiver.readLoop Allows Unauthen… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
Pre-Authentication `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat` in `heartbeatReceiver.readLoop` Allows Unauthenticated Spoofed UDP Packets to Forge Cluster History Events and Suppress Duplicate-Identity Alarms

Finding `D14-03` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Order verified: `srcIsConfiguredPeer` → `UnmarshalHeartbeat` → ClusterID → `NodeID==own → NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat(); continue` (:1763) → only then `admitFrame` HMAC (:1768). `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat`, `warnDuplicateNodeIDLocked` and the authenticated `NoteDuplicateNodeIDBeacon` all consume the *same* `duplicateNodeIDWarningDueLocked` 30 s limiter and write `EventRG` history. So a frame that never passes HMAC can (i) forge a "duplicate node-id: invalid cluster configuration" history/syslog event and (ii) keep the limiter fresh, suppressing the richer authenticated beacon diagnostic (iface/boot-id/src-mac). Packet's fix direction (verify HMAC against accepted ring for same-NodeID frames, still `continue` before replay-state admission) is correct and safe. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Packet overstates the actor: "any unauthenticated sender with spoofed source IP to UDP/4784" ignores the #6888 peer pin at :1730 — off-peer-IP datagrams are dropped *before* unmarshal. Exploitation therefore requires source-IP spoofing of the configured peer on the control link (or a compromised/misconfigured peer), i.e. an on-link attacker able to spoof the peer address — still unauthenticated w.r.t. the PSK, but a narrower boundary than claimed. History pollution is also rate-limited to 1/30 s (≤100-entry ring churn is slow). No election/liveness state is mutated (frame is discarded), so impact is alarm-suppression/forged-history, not split-brain. - Decisive check: receiver test feeding an unsigned same-NodeID frame *from the peer IP* on a keyed manager: assert no history recor
- Spark: Verified line-exact at both revs. `heartbeat.go:1735` unmarshals (header only), `:1746` checks cluster ID, `:1763-1766` calls `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat()` and drops the frame — **before** `admitFrame` (`:1768`) runs HMAC verification (`:1815-1853`). The source pin (`:1730`, #6888) checks source IP only and its own comment states "This is NOT an authentication boundary". `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat` (`election.go:441-458`) consumes the shared 30s limiter `duplicateNodeIDWarningDueLocked` (`:395-402`), logs at Error, and records a forged `EventRG` history entry. The same limiter gates the authenticated beacon path `NoteDuplicateNodeIDBeacon` (`dupaddr_watch_10745.go:580-585`) and `warnDuplicateNodeIDLocked` (`election.go:414-417`), so one spoofed datagram per 30s from the peer's IP (or any source if `peerAddr` is nil — `srcIsConfiguredPeer:1600-1608` fails open) perpetually suppresses genuine duplicate-identity alarms including their forensic `iface` detail.

## #14706 — [gemini-hostile D14-05] VRRP recordMasterAdvert Unconditionally Overwrites Master Priority, Source IP, and Master_Adv… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
VRRP `recordMasterAdvert` Unconditionally Overwrites Master Priority, Source IP, and `Master_Adver_Interval` on Rejected Lower-Priority Advertisements

Finding `D14-05` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified: `handleBackupRx`/`handleMasterRx` call `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` then `recordMasterAdvert` *before* any priority comparison, and `recordMasterAdvert` unconditionally sets `lastMasterPriority`, `lastMasterSeen`, per-family source (with a priority-255 carve-out), and `masterAdverInterval` (floored, not capped). Those fields feed `shouldPreemptObservedMaster` (`effective > lastMasterPriority`, staleness from `masterAdverInterval`) and the #10719 detector's known-source. A lower-priority advert therefore (a) lowers the bar the #2082 sync-hold gate compares against — a BACKUP that should not preempt a higher master can pass `effective > lastMasterPriority` after a low advert overwrites it — and (b) refreshes `lastMasterSeen`, keeping a bogus master "live". VRRP (RFC 5798) has no authentication, so any L2 speaker can send such adverts; that is the protocol's trust model, but the *local* gate must only learn from the advert it actually accepted as master. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Packet's three arms are not equal. (i) Preempt-gate arm: real, but requires sync-hold release/`preemptNowCh` or hold-expiry racing the bogus advert; ordinary Backup handling already ignores lower adverts for timer purposes. (ii) Spoof-detector arm is partly self-defeating: `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` runs *before* recording and only warns on priority 0/255; overwriting the known source with an ordinary lower-priority source is arguably correct learning (that sender *is* advertising as master). (iii) Interval arm is weakest: RFC 5798 §6.4.2 *requires* a Backup to learn Master_Adver_Inter
- Spark: Verified at both revs: `handleBackupRx:152-153` and `handleMasterRx:205-206` call `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` then `recordMasterAdvert` **before** any priority/state decision, and `recordMasterAdvert` (`:24-71`) unconditionally overwrites `lastMasterPriority`, `lastMasterSeen`, per-family master source IP (any priority 1–254), and `masterAdverInterval` (floor-clamped only, no ceiling — wire max 4095×10ms = 40.95s). All three claimed arms trace: (1) `shouldPreemptObservedMaster` (`instance_preempt.go:95-148`) returns `effective > lastMasterPriority` against the clobbered value — a Backup(100, preempt) that heard the real Master(200) and then one rogue Priority-50 advert will preempt on sync-hold release → dual-master. (2) `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` (`:78-122`) only fires for priority 0/255 from a source ≠ learned master; a prior rogue Priority-1 advert *becomes* the learned master (`:31-39`), so the follow-up rogue 255/0 from the same IP is silent (`:106-108`) — the #10719 detector is primed off by the very packet class it ignores. (3) `masterAdverInterval=40.95s` inflates `masterDownInterval()` to ~122.85s (Backup watchdog / preempt-hold staleness, `instance_preempt.go:175-297`) and `ResignRG`'s `3×masterDownInterval` safety timeout. RFC 5798 §6.4.2/§6.4.3 indeed forbid adopting `Master_Adver_Interval` from a discarded advert.

## #14707 — [gemini-hostile D15-01] ShowConfig, ShowCompare, and ShowRollback Bypass allow-configuration / deny-configuration Sub… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
`ShowConfig`, `ShowCompare`, and `ShowRollback` Bypass `allow-configuration` / `deny-configuration` Subtree Restrictions and Path/Format-Scoped `deny-commands` Rules

Finding `D15-01` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end. Handlers take `_ context.Context` and render full (secret-redacted) active/candidate/rollback subtrees with no class filtering. `authorizeRPCConfigMutation` only adjudicates Set/Delete (via `configMutationLineFor`) and Load/Rollback; Show* return nil. `ShowConfig`/`ShowCompare`/`ShowRollback` are *not* in `configModeMethods9633`, so `authorizeRPCCommand` evaluates the bare canonical `"show configuration"` — a class with `deny-commands "^show configuration security"` or `"display set"`, or with only `deny-configuration "^security"`, still receives the `security` subtree via `Path:["security"]` (ACTIVE = PermView; candidate/compare = PermConfig via #9324/#9889 pricing). This contradicts the codebase's own stated invariant (#14144 header: subtrees `ShowConfig`/`Set` "conceal"). Redaction (#4051) masks secret *values* only; topology, zones, policies, address books and user/class names are disclosed. - Strongest refutation/alternative: `deny-configuration` is Junos-wise a *configuration-mode* (mutation/session) control; one could argue it was never a read-visibility control and `show configuration` is governed solely by `deny-commands`. That argument fails on this codebase's own terms: #14144 implements read-concealment for Complete explicitly by reference to what "ShowConfig/Set conceal", the CLI applies config regexes to `show` in config mode, and path/format-scoped `deny-commands` (`^show configuration security`) is unambiguously a read control that the canonical-command flattening defeats regardless. Severity is disclosure-to-authenticated-restricted-ope
- Spark: Verified at both revs. All three handlers discard ctx (`server_config.go:401,439,458`: `_ context.Context`) and render the requested subtree (or whole tree / candidate diff / rollback slot) with only secret *redaction* (`ShowActive*Redacted` etc.), never subtree authorization. The interceptor (`authz.go:288-298`) runs two gates, neither covers this: `authorizeRPCCommand` maps the methods to the bare literals `"show configuration"`/`"show configuration"`/`"show configuration"` (`authz_command_table.go:81-83` — note the report's transcription "show system rollback" is stale; actual is `"show configuration"`, which makes the path-scoping gap *worse*, not better), ignoring `Path` and `Format`; and `authorizeRPCConfigMutation` (`authz_config_regex_9154.go:39-52`) only adjudicates `Set`/`Delete`/`Load`/`Rollback` — for these three it returns nil. So `deny-configuration "^security"` (which demonstrably denies `Set` under security) and `deny-commands "^show configuration security"` / `"display set"` both fail to conceal anything on the read RPCs, in every format. The in-code assumption the claim cites is real: `authz_complete_14144.go:11-38` documents #14144 as fixing completion disclosure of "exactly the subtree those gates conceal from ShowConfig/Set" — ShowConfig does not, in fact, conceal it.

## Summary

Finding `D16-02` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Both sub-vectors verified by bounded lexer test on master: `lexConfigMutationLine9938("annotate system\u00a0login")` returns `["annotate","system"]` (TokenError truncates, login dropped) and the `\v` variant likewise, while the handler's `strings.Fields(req.Path)` (unicode-aware) splits to `["system","login"]` and annotates the denied node. Quoted arm: `lex…("annotate system \"login\"")` yields quoted=[…,true], so `configMutationPaths` strips the final token as the "comment" and adjudicates only `system`. Third arm verified in code: REST handler calls `store.AnnotateAs` (plantClass="") whereas every sibling mutation handler resolves `mutationPlantClass(r)` and master’s gRPC Set-annotate path uses `AnnotateAsPlantClass` — REST annotate loses plant-class attribution. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Impact is annotation-only: the caller can attach a comment to a denied subtree and dirty the candidate, not change configuration values; privilege-escalation framing should not be borrowed from D16-01. `AnnotateAs` still enforces session-holder ownership. But deny-configuration bypass + missing attribution on a candidate mutation is precisely what #9154/#9892 exist to prevent, and the gate/handler tokenizer mismatch is the canonical fail-open shape. Fix direction in packet (join Fields + synthetic empty quoted comment; use `AnnotateAsPlantClass`) is sound. - Decisive check: REST test — class `deny-configuration "system login"`: NBSP, VT, and `system "login"` annotate bodies must 403; normal `system login` control already 403s; success case must record plant class.
- Spark: Verified at both revs, both sub-vectors. Gate: `authorizeRESTConfigMutation` (`pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:242-260`) builds `"annotate " + strings.TrimSpace(req.Path)` with **no comment argument**, and `AuthorizeConfigMutation` lexes it with the real lexer (`lexConfigMutationLine9938`, `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:172-189`). (A) Unicode whitespace: for `system\u00a0login`, `readIdentifier` stops `system` at byte `0xC2` (not `isIdentChar`, `pkg/config/lexer.go:511-519`), `skipWhitespaceAndComments` skips only `' ' \t \n \r` (`:353`), so `Next()` returns `TokenError` and the gate lexer **stops** (`default: return tokens, quoted`) having seen only `[annotate, system]` — the deny on `system login` never matches. Handler: `strings.Fields` (`pkg/api/config.go:687`) splits on `unicode.IsSpace`, yielding `[system login]`, and annotates the forbidden node. Same for `\v`, `\f`, NBSP, U+2000s, U+3000. (B) Quoted leaf: `system "login"` lexes to `[annotate, system, login]` with `quoted=[F,F,T]`; `configMutationPaths`' annotate arm (`:139-152`) treats a quoted final token as the comment and adjudicates only `system`. Additionally the handler calls `s.store.AnnotateAs` (`config.go:691`) — `plantClass=""` — while every sibling mutating handler resolves `s.mutationPlantClass(r)` and calls the `*AsPlantClass` variant (`config.go:172,196,226,253,348,543`; store: `AnnotateAs`→`AnnotateAsPlantClass(sessionID,"",…)`, `store_command.go:382-388`), so the annotation is planted with superuser attribution, defeating the #9939 embedded-command recheck provenance.

## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified by bounded test on master: `throttleIdentity` with both headers returns `basic:dummy` (X-API-Key branch unreachable), key-only returns `api-key`; `authCheckCredential` with failing `Digest` + bad key evaluates *both* (`authorizationFailed=true`, key also checked). So failures charge `(source, basic:<rotating>)` and the source bucket only — `(source, api-key)` is never charged, and a previously-locked `(source, api-key)` is never consulted when an Authorization header is present. Rotating dummy usernames gives the source-bucket budget (20) instead of the account budget (5) per window — 4× key-guessing — and dual-header presentation of the *valid* key bypasses an active api-key lockout outright. Double-verify CPU (`1 + len(APIKeys)` bcrypt-ish compares under one reservation) is the secondary arm; note `constantTimeAPIKeyMatch` cost depends on key store, so "bcrypt per key" should be stated as per-key compare cost, not assumed bcrypt for every deployment. - Strongest refutation/alternative: The fall-through itself was deliberate (#11492-era): a failing Authorization with a *valid* key still authorizes, and `complete` charges the failed claimed identity and clears only the verified bucket — changing to fail-fast on any Authorization presence would break clients that send a stale Authorization alongside a valid key (the packet's own fix does exactly that and should be flagged as a behaviour change needing intent). But no design comment justifies *never charging the api-key bucket for key evaluations*, nor bypassing an active api-key lockout; the minimal fix (reserve/cha
- Spark: Verified at both revs. `throttleIdentity` (`auth_throttle_10825.go:539-561`) picks exactly one identity, `Authorization` first (`:542`), so a dual-header request reserves/charges only e.g. `(source,"basic:dummy")` or `(source,"authorization-invalid")` — never `(source,"api-key")`. `authCheckCredential` (`pkg/api/auth.go:295-309`) then evaluates **both**: failed `Authorization` sets `authorizationFailed=true` (`:303`) and *falls through* to `X-API-Key` (`:305`). On dual failure, `complete` (`auth_throttle_10825.go:274-311`) charges the reservation's claimed bucket + source bucket; the api-key pair bucket is never created or charged. Consequences as claimed: (i) per-account api-key lockout (5 failures) is bypassed indefinitely from one source — only the 20-failure source budget (`:65,310`) applies, i.e. ~4× the intended guesses per window, rotating dummy Basic usernames to also dodge pair buckets; (ii) a source whose `(source,"api-key")` bucket *is* locked can keep testing keys — and a valid key still authenticates (`complete:303-305` even clears the verified api-key bucket on the fallback success) — by stapling any junk `Authorization` header; (iii) each attempt costs the failed-Authorization bcrypt (when Basic/Bearer-shaped) plus a full `constantTimeAPIKeyMatch` sweep over configured keys under one reservation.

- Spark: At audit, `readPermissionFor` (`pkg/api/authz.go:932-936`) aliases any safe method to the `GET` entry, but `authorizeRESTCommand` (`authz_command_regex_9952.go:291`) keys `restRoutesNoCommand`/`restRouteCommand`/`restRequestCommand9952` on raw `r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path`. ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: (Echo arm — verified) `LoadMergeAsPlantClass`/`parseOverrideContent` return `fmt.Errorf("line %d: %q is not a set/delete/…", trimmed)` and `line %d: %q: %w` with the raw line (:610-613, :681-684; `LoadSetAsPlantClass` same pattern). A non-superuser with `PermConfig` — whose `show configuration` is redacted under #4099 — can `load merge /etc/xpf/rescue.conf` (or any readable-by-daemon file with ≥1 flat verb line to select the flat branch) and read off denied file lines one error at a time. The rescue loader in the same package deliberately scrubs exactly this (`rescueParseError`, coordinates only), proving the intended discipline. (Ordering arm — verified) `handleLoad` calls `ReadBoundedConfigFile(source)` (:204) *before* `AuthorizeConfigLoad` (:234), so even a `deny-configuration ".*"` class (and any restricted class using `override`, which the load gate refuses categorically) triggers a root-privileged open and gets distinguishable errors (not-exist vs non-regular vs empty vs parse), i.e. a filesystem existence/type oracle plus the echo channel above. - Strongest refutation / alternative: The read itself is bounded and safe against hangs (`O_NOFOLLOW`, regular-file check, 16 MiB cap, #6753) — no unbounded allocation or FIFO block. Files with no flat-verb line take the hierarchical parser whose errors are coordinate-only, so bulk exfiltration requires target files containing a `set/delete/…` line before the secret line (true of xpf config/rescue files — the realistic targets — not of e.g. `/etc/shadow`, whose lines would go hierarchical and not echo [needs the packet's bran
- Spark: (two separable parts):** 1. *Verbatim echo (MATERIAL):* `LoadMergeAsPlantClass`/`parseOverrideContent` return `line %d: %q is not a set/… command` with the raw line (`store_command.go:610-614,681-685`; same pattern in `LoadSetAsPlantClass`). `LoadRescue` deliberately scrubs this (`rescueParseError`, coordinates only). A non-superuser `PermConfig` class that is denied cleartext secrets (#4099 redaction) can therefore extract individual lines of any file it can get parsed as flat input, one error per load — a real, if slow, exfiltration oracle for files containing a valid first `set` line followed by a secret line. 2. *Pre-auth unconfined read (weaker):* `handleLoad` (`cli_config.go:200-213`) calls `ReadBoundedConfigFile(source)` before `AuthorizeConfigLoad` (:234), inside root-privileged `xpfd`, with no directory confinement. Existence/empty/non-regular distinctions leak via distinct errors even under `deny-configuration ".*"`. But "load a config file by path" is the feature's purpose, Junos `load merge <file>` inherently reads operator-named files, and `ReadBoundedConfigFile` already enforces regular-file + 16 MiB + `O_NOFOLLOW` (#6753). Confinement to a staging dir is a design/policy change, not a clear contract violation — this half is a hardening question.

## Summary

## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end. #14172's cover lives only in `DB.writeConfirmCover`, set at `store_commit.go:638` from the guarded tree and cleared by `defer` on return (:639) — the in-code comment even asserts the false premise ("cleared on return so no later tombstone/migration/retry write silently inherits it", and crypto.go:315-319 "keeps those records exactly under the PrevTree profile they were armed with"). In the #14172 scenario the record was *not* armed under the PrevTree profile (PrevTree has none); every later `WriteConfirm` — resolution tombstone (`markConfirmResolvedLocked`, :929, via `WriteConfirm→encodeConfirm` with cover `""`), phase-3 retry (`store_persist.go:1465`), boot rebind/migration (:392,438,999), FIRST sentinel (:1039,1574) — marshals the full PrevTree (all secret leaves) and, with `confirmEncryptionPRF(prevTree, "")==""`, writes it unencrypted and fsyncs it. The tombstone arm fires on *every* confirm resolution in this configuration, not an edge case; crash/delete-failure leaves it indefinitely, and even on success cleartext blocks were durably written. This directly defeats the operator's act of enabling master-password. - Strongest refutation / alternative: File is `0600` in the config DB dir alongside `master.key` — an attacker who can read `confirm.json` cleartext may be near the key material anyway [INFERENCE on deployment perms]. That mitigates remote-attacker severity but not the defect: #14172's whole purpose was at-rest encryption of this record, backups/snapshots/support-bundles routinely carry config DB files without keys, and the encrypted-then-c
- Spark: `commitConfirmedLocked` sets `s.db.writeConfirmCover = {profile: masterPasswordPRF(committedTree)}` with `defer` clearing it on return (`store_commit.go:638-639`) — the comment at :635-637 says clearing is deliberate so later writes don't "silently inherit" it. But `encodeConfirm` (`db.go:781`) computes `confirmEncryptionPRF(rec.PrevTree, db.writeConfirmCover)` = PrevTree's own PRF, else cover, else `""` = plaintext (`crypto.go:351-356`). In the exact #14172 scenario (PrevTree has *no* master-password; the guarded commit *adds* one), every subsequent `WriteConfirm` therefore writes plaintext: resolution tombstone (`markConfirmResolvedLocked`, `store_commit.go:923-933`), finalization retry (`store_persist.go:1465`), FIRST-rollback sentinel (:1039), boot-recovery/migration rewrites. The tombstone case is the cleanest: it rewrites the *same* `PrevTree` (with its secrets) unencrypted and fsyncs it.

## #14720 — [gemini-hostile D18-03] Cutover Pre-STOP Stamp and Pre-FLIP Guard Confusion Delete the Committed Rollback Target on Verify/Start Failure [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
**ID:** `D18-03`

Finding `D18-03` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: The identity confusion is real. For a fresh cut, `j.PreviousVersion = restorablePrev` = the *live* version (`cutover.go:520,605`), so `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`'s guard `ver == j.PreviousVersion || ver == cur` (:1749) protects only the live dir — never live's committed predecessor. Re-stage predecessor `1.0.0` (running `2.0.0`) under a new generation: (a) if bytes differ, `copyStaged`'s predecessor-preservation (`committedPredecessorStamp`, commit_stamp.go:80-94) is explicitly *demoted* on mismatch — `stampInFlightVersion(ver)` + `removeStaleVersionDir` (:1543-1553) — deleting the rollback target before verify; (b) if the copy lands and verify fails, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` `os.RemoveAll(versions/1.0.0)` + `.<ver>.dbsnap` (:1756,1803) with no predecessor check. Either way `defaultRollbackTarget("2.0.0")` then finds `.1.0.0.committed` gone/non-committed and reports no restorable target. The packet's proof log ("replacing stale version dir … removed copied version dir … defaultRollbackTarget err") matches arms (a)+(b) chained. - Strongest refutation / alternative: Two packet arms need narrowing. (1) "Byte-identical reuse then cleanup deletes it": at audit, same-generation reuse skips the copy and *cleanup still deletes the pre-existing dir* — that sub-arm holds and is the worst form; but the generation-mismatch-as-mismatch claim (packet Cross-Domain note) is stale: current `existingVersionDirMismatch`/`mismatchedManagedBinary` compare SHA-256 of binaries, generation difference routes through the refuse/replace logic at :1483-1553, not a pure generation-string mismatch. (2) C
- Spark: When `v1` (committed predecessor of live `v2`) is re-staged under a *new* generation, `copyStaged` preserves its stamp only while `preservedPredecessorStamp != nil` and `ver == j.PreviousVersion` (`cutover.go:1471-1481`); the pre-STOP gate likewise keeps it a candidate only until the envelope recheck (:826-833). If `verify(j)` then fails, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` guards deletion with `ver == j.PreviousVersion || ver == cur` (:1749) — but in this journal `j.PreviousVersion == "v2"` (the *current* version, since the cut targets v1), so the guard does **not** fire for the re-staged v1 dir, and `os.RemoveAll(versionDir(ver))` (:1756) plus `.<ver>.dbsnap` removal (:1803) destroy the very directory `defaultRollbackTarget("v2")` would restore. The report's executed proof (dir gone, `defaultRollbackTarget` errors "no restorable… target") matches this path.

## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified both arms. (1) `rollback()` (:288-295) does `StartUnit` then `clearJournal()` with no `HelperHealthy`, while the forward path (:1031-1034) and operator `executeRollback` (rollback.go:259-263, #5286) both gate on it — for a `Type=simple` unit, start-success says nothing about the dataplane helper, so a dead-helper rollback is declared clean and the journal (the only resume record) is destroyed. (2) `Run`'s resume branch (:276-297) calls `rollback(j)` and `return nil` (:296); `runRollingWith` treats nil as a successful cut and proceeds to re-sync + `RejoinAndConfirm`/`ResetFailover`, logging "cut complete" for a node that actually went *backwards* — the packet proof (err=nil, resetCalled=true, helper dead) is consistent. Real consumers read the pair atomically in the window: `pkg/daemon/daemon_route_listener.go:271`, `daemon_scheduler.go:98`, `daemon_ipmon.go:494` all call `ActiveStateWithFailClosed()`. - Spark: Legs 1 and 3 proven by probe. ## #14731 — [gemini-hostile D20-04] Dual-Stack DDNS Manager.currentAuthorityLocked Collapses Per-Family Authority Fingerprints to… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
Dual-Stack DDNS `Manager.currentAuthorityLocked` Collapses Per-Family Authority Fingerprints to Only IPv4 (`pol4.authority`), Breaking Cross-Surface Co-Ownership (`#5748`/`#6755`) for IPv6 `AAAA` Records and Deleting Live Router `AAAA` Records on DHCPv6 Lease Expiry

Finding `D20-04` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: .** Confirmed on master despite refactor: `ReconcileScoped` builds `agg := pol4; if !agg.enabled { agg = pol6 }` and stores single `m.lastPolicy`; `currentAuthorityLocked()` (`manager.go:1196`) returns the one `p.authority`; both `wireRRSharedWithOther` (`:1147`) and `rebuildWireRRClaimsLocked` (`:1209`) stamp it on records of *both* families (`wireRRClaim(r.FQDN, r.ForwardType, ...)` — ForwardType derives from family, authority does not). With distinct ddns4/ddns6 RFC2136 servers, every v6 claim carries the v4 fingerprint. `coOwns` requires exact `Authority` equality — so (a) false negative: v6 lease expiry deletes a live Surface-A AAAA on the v6 server; (b) false positive: cross-server co-ownership suppresses a needed delete, orphaning the record. The code's own comment acknowledges the current-authority approximation but only argues policy-*change* boundedness, not dual-stack distinct endpoints — the exact #2663-supported config. **Strongest refutation/alternative.** Requires dual-stack DDNS with *different* UpdateServers *and* a Surface-A record colliding on (FQDN, type, rdata) with a lease record — a narrow but explicitly supported topology (#5748/#6755 machinery exists for it). If both families share one server, fingerprints coincide and there is no defect. `leaseAuthorityFingerprint` on master may already be per-config — check whether `policyFromConfig` fingerprints incorporate family endpoint correctly for single-family case (yes) — defect is only the dual-stack collapse. **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL. **Decisive unresolved check:** master test: dual-stack Reconcile wi
- Spark: `ReconcileScoped` collapses the aggregate policy to `agg := pol4` whenever v4 is enabled (audit `manager.go:833-840`; master retains pol4-first collapse), so `currentAuthorityLocked()` — the single scalar used to stamp *every* lease claim in `rebuildWireRRClaimsLocked` and to build the owned claim in `wireRRSharedWithOther` — is always the v4 endpoint fingerprint. An AAAA lease published to the distinct ddns6 server is stamped with the v4 fingerprint; Surface A's teardown compares it against the AAAA record's own `BackendFingerprint` (the v6 server) via `coOwns`, gets a mismatch, and deletes a live co-owned AAAA record (and symmetrically, lease teardown can delete a Surface-A co-owned RR). `coOwns` itself is correct — its inputs are wrong per-family.

- Spark: All three legs code-verified, leg 2 probe-verified. (1) `LocalLogWriter.Send` formats `msg` raw into the audit file; its syslog twin sanitizes with `termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay` (#6585). `formatSyslogMsg` interpolates zone/reason fields raw, so `\n`/`\r`/ESC reaching it forges audit lines. The revalidation helper currently receives only (forwarding, forward_key, now_ns) — it has session metadata available at its caller `destination_nat_translation_still_valid` (metadata.ingress_zone etc.), so the fix needs to thread the arrival zone + rule zones mirroring mod.rs:3539, or pass empty strings only if unscoped semantics are intended (allocator treats empty as UNSCOPED — that would re-open the #14322 cross-zone leak on the revalidation path, so threading real zones is likely required).

This blocks every Rust test build on master. #14643 works around it locally only for test execution and does NOT include the fix in its PR (separate scope).

## #14831 — userspace-dp: session-miss TE arm double-queues TE + Live forward for TTL=1 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Found while implementing #14643 (witness control).

On the session-miss arm, a buildable TTL=1 TCP SYN queues BOTH a Prebuilt Time Exceeded (from build_local_time_exceeded_request at poll_descriptor/mod.rs ~5529) AND a Live forward (from build_live_forward_request_from_frame at ~8902). Descriptor harness evidence (nat_snapshot, pool SNAT, ifindex 24): scratch_forwards=[Prebuilt(target=24), Live(target=11)], dbg.forward=1, sessions=0. The Live frame is later refused at rewrite for TTL<=1, so no wire leak today, but the packet is counted as forwarded and occupies TX queue state.

Likely mechanism: the miss arm does not suppress the trailing Live-forward tail after queueing the TE (recycle_now=false is insufficient because the tail at ~8430 checks only disposition). Flow-cache sibling returns Consumed. Session-hit TE arm at ~3311 continues correctly.

Out of scope for #14643 (which fixes the suppressed-TE install). File + fix separately: after queueing TE on miss arm, skip the Live tail (e.g. continue or a consumed flag).

## #14850 — [build] origin/master userspace-xdp shim has a duplicate closing brace from #14645 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Symptom

`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs` on origin/master does not parse. rustc and rustfmt both report `unexpected closing delimiter` at the end of `try_xdp_userspace`: the session-miss block introduced by #14645 (13905b0650) closes the match arm, the match, and the enclosing if, then has one extra `        }` before `    } else if native_gre_fragment {`.

## Evidence

- `git show origin/master:userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs | sed -n '1015,1022p'` shows three consecutive closes (`            }`, `        }`, `        }`) where sibling pre-#14645 code has two (closes the `_` arm and the match; the if is closed by the `else if` line).
- `rustfmt +nightly-2026-05-23 --edition 2024 --check` on the pristine HEAD file: `error: unexpected closing delimiter: } at 1162`, citing `if !native_gre && !native_gre_fragment` at 905.
- The sibling worktree at 4c6c8fb2da (pre-#14645) parses cleanly.
- The shipped `pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_bpfel.o` and gate verdict predate #14645, so the stranded source was never regenerated; the manifest lists the new gre sources but the object was built from the pre-#14645 source. This is why CI stayed green.

## Impact

Any PR touching the shim cannot run `make build-userspace-xdp` without first removing the duplicate brace. Found while implementing #14842 (per-VLAN ingress domains); that lane removes the duplicate line as a drive-by and calls it out in its PR body.

## Fix

Delete the extra `        }` line. Regenerate the shim object afterward; note the regenerated object will measure the true current verifier headroom, which the stale verdict (620456 insns, 2026-10-17) does not reflect.

## #14935 — userspace-dp: closing-state sessions frozen on fixed 30s fuse - active data flows idle-reaped mid-transfer (#14300 root cause) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Root cause of #14300 (loss cluster live repro, deployed 06f2d276f; mechanism byte-identical on master 27b8cba22d).

Mechanism: first FIN/RST sighting stamps closing=true + tcp_close_window (30s) on the pair (session lookup stamp_tcp_close/propagate_tcp_state_to_companion). Afterwards the FIN-owning direction can never refresh last_seen/expires: slow-path refresh predicate (lookup.rs) and flow-cache touch_if_stale both gate on !fin_own/!reset. Reaper (expire_stale_entries_ha, 1s wheel) removes the entry at FIN+30s regardless of traffic volume. Live evidence: iperf3 -P12 streams 17-20 Gbps stall to 0 at ~28-30s flow age; fw0 session count 13-17 -> 0; journal SESSION_CLOSE reason=idle Timeout on flows with 200k+ packets; per-worker survival (queues 1,3).

Fix shape: data-bearing segments (payload progress) must re-stamp expiry even in closing state; keep fixed fuse only for TIME_WAIT (both FINs) and RST. Regression: FIN one direction -> data at intervals past closing+30s -> both halves alive; stop data -> reap at last-data+window. Existing close_refresh_gate_10885 tests pin ACK-only frozen behavior - split ACK-only vs data-bearing.

Acceptance: loss-cluster long iperf3 (60s+, -P12, both directions, v4+v6) stable >=18 Gbps with no stream stall.

## #14937 — userspace-dp: payload-less keepalive wrappers still reachable from poll loop - closing sessions die at 20-30s on subset of workers (follow-up #14935) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Follow-up to #14935 / root of #14300. Live loss evidence on build b4464fda30 (includes #14936): iperf -P12 push decays per-stream all-or-nothing at 20-30s; dead workers go CPU-idle; sessions close idle Timeout with multi-GB counters. Diagnosis: #14935 threaded payload progress through main paths but kept payload_len=0 compatibility wrappers; a subset of hit paths (per-worker bimodal) still invokes them, so those closing entries keep the frozen #10885 fuse.

Fix: thread payload progress through every production lookup/touch call site; remove payload-less wrappers from poll loop reachability; regression per hit path (flow-cache, deferred-owner, fabric/shared, slow path). Acceptance: loss 60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, zero 0-byte streams, zero idle-Timeout closes on multi-GB sessions.

## #14939 — userspace-dp: established TCP sessions never promote out of handshake_pending - stuck on 20s OPENING window, reaped mid-flow (#14300 root) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Live discriminator on loss (master 8cece4238a): during iperf -P12, ALL sessions show Timeout: 20 (OPENING window) mid-flow instead of 300 (established). handshake_pending never clears for these installs, so sessions live on the 20s opening window; combined with 30s-scale reap they die mid-transfer (idle Timeout closes, all-stream stall ~30s, SYN-less packets then fail strict-syn-check - permanent stall).

Per Code30s analysis: local-install promotion requires a forward non-SYN ACK reaching lookup while handshake_pending (lookup.rs promotion arm); candidates that break it: completing ACK served by flow-cache hit (never reaches lookup), deferred-owner/Owner-replay path not applying promotion, or synced/materialized replicas (upsert_synced maps HandshakePending -> established=true, handshake_pending=true and completion depends on that worker seeing the ACK via lookup).

Fix: ensure handshake completion is applied on every hit path that can consume the completing ACK (flow-cache hit must complete promotion or not swallow the ACK; deferred owner replay likewise). Regression: install SYN/SYN-ACK, drive completing ACK via flow-cache hit path, assert Timeout becomes established window (300) and session survives past opening+closing windows under data traffic. Acceptance: loss 60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, sessions show Timeout:300 mid-flow, zero idle-Timeout closes.

## #14941 — userspace-dp: reverse-direction revalidation writes forward egress zone into reverse ingress - ACKs go Foreign and stall at ~28s (#14300) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

From #14300 wire diagnosis (build 1b2aab09b4): reverse ACKs silently dropped in fw0 ~28s into every TCP stream; forward data still passes; sessions idle-Timeout close.

Code defect (Rev14300): reverse metadata is direction-relative (shared_ops/reverse_synth.rs:90-91), resolver derives new_egress_zone from matched packet direction incl. reverse hits (session_glue/resolve.rs:514-553), but recipient writes it as forward egress_zone / reverse ingress_zone unconditionally (session/mod.rs:2231-2257; poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2278-2283). A reverse (WAN->LAN) revalidation can flip reverse ingress zone WAN->LAN; next ACK becomes Foreign (session_hit_authority.rs:190-206), skips refresh, cannot re-seed cache, may policy-drop. Fix orientation: when matched direction is reverse, map resolved zones direction-relatively. Regression: reverse-hit revalidation preserves reverse ingress=original forward egress zone; ACK stream keeps refreshing past 30s. Also check neighbor-generation flow-cache invalidation lead (flow_cache_hit.rs:160-196) as contributing trigger for the ~28s transition timing.

## #14943 — userspace-dp: flow-cache HA lease stamp frozen at insert (10s) - entries self-evict and demote to HAInactive mid-flow (#14300) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Code-provable (Lease14300 hunt, head d90ea9ff65): FlowCacheStamp::capture copies HAForwardingLease::ActiveUntil into owner_rg_lease_until at insert (flow_cache.rs:165,188-194,714); hits never refresh it (flow_cache.rs:1315-1331). Lease is 10s (afxdp/mod.rs:544, types/runtime.rs:523-531). Every seeded entry self-evicts <=~10s after seeding (flow_cache.rs:1286-1294) and before that the hit validator demotes cached resolution to HAInactive when the runtime lease expired (flow_cache_hit.rs:160-196, forwarding/ha.rs:248-262), failing closed to slow-path redirect/drop. try_refresh_ha_leases never resurrects an expired stored-active lease (ha/session_domain.rs:1681,1704-1716), so one lapse is permanent for the entry.

Live correlation (#14300): all flows cache-evict in a burst at session age ~26-28s, session-hit burst, then no re-seed/refresh, ACKs dropped, idle-Timeout closes. Fix direction: cache hits re-stamp owner_rg_lease_until from the CURRENT runtime lease (or validate against current lease, not insert stamp); allow lease refresh to resurrect stored-active when heartbeat is fresh again. Regression: seeded entry hit past insert+10s with fresh runtime lease stays cached/valid; expired-runtime-lease still fails closed. Acceptance: loss 60s -P12 both directions stable.

## #14945 — perf: userspace RSS queue imbalance - 2 of 6 workers idle while contended queues micro-drop (loss -P12 ceiling 16-19G) [OPEN]

### Summary

- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:343`, `pkg/config/aspath_regex.go:59-67`, `aspath_regex.go:30-36`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): Observed: pkg/frr/policy_render.go:343 `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "bgp as-path access-list %s permit %s\n", frrName(name), sanitizeFRRValue(ap.Regex))`. Observed: pkg/config/aspath_regex.go:59-67 joins the tokens, and :98-106 `ValidASPathRegex` checks only non-empty + `regexp.CompilePOSIX`. Observed: the comment at aspath_regex.go:30-36 itself reads `.* 65000 .*` with Junos meaning. Inference: FRR evaluates as-path lists as unanchored POSIX ERE over the path string (confirmed empirically).

### Fix direction

## #15045 — config: fix — next-header icmp (proto 1) with icmp-type in an inet6 filter, or protocol icmpv6/58 with icmp-type in an inet filter, passes… (A05-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A05-01** — `next-header icmp` (proto 1) with `icmp-type` in an inet6 filter, or `protocol icmpv6`/`58` with `icmp-type` in an inet filter, passes strict commit with no warning, and the discard/reject term never matches real traffic (report severity: Medium — an operator-authored stateless discard/reject is silently inert and falls through to later terms or the implicit accept. This is the fail-open class #3723 closed for other protocols, here lim; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A05-01` (Part v1-v28).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:131`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:131` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:2035-2045`, `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1180-1192`, `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/matching.rs:61-68`, `compiler_firewall.go:1842`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:2035-2045` `protocolIsICMPFamily` returns true for icmp/icmpv6/1/58 with no family input; `:776-788` uses `family` only in the error text. `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1180-1192` accepts protocol 1 OR 58 in either family; `:1380` `protocol_bitmap: build_u8_match_bitmap(&protocols)`. `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/matching.rs:61-68`: icmp-type needs `is_icmp` and set membership. `compiler_firewall.go:1842` resolves the icmp-type by the filter family (`echo-request` becomes 128 in inet6).

## #15061 — vrrp: fix — A standalone vrrp-group VIP is foreign to networkd and is stripped by xpf's reconfigure while VRRP stays MASTER (A37-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:463-480`: the snapshot writes `Hash: highWaterHash` with `Prefixes: epochPrefixes`. `:450-455`: the restore keeps the prefixes only if `hashPrefixes(canon) == hash` (the high-water hash). `:2273-2276`: an install with newCount >= highWater moves highWaterHash. `:2282-2291`: the epoch moves only on bootstrap or ack, so the two hashes diverge after one ordinary rotation (observed). `:2111-2125`: shrink and churn trips both require `fs.hasSnapshot`, which is false on cold boot. `:2282`: `if wasBootstrap || guardBypass` rebases the epoch to the candidate. `:2125-2127`: the warn

### Fix direction
- **A50-01:** Persist an `EpochHash` separately and validate the prefixes against it. Update the README. Acceptance: a restart cell bootstrapping a disjoint set against a restored epoch is refused; a restore after a non-rebasing rotation keeps 100 epoch prefixes; both go red if the Apply epoch copy is deleted.

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): Observed, xpf @51d355c1d. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bind.rs:604-622` loops `for attempt in 0..BIND_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` calling `xsk_ffi::create_xsk_binding_shared(worker_umem.as_raw_umem_ptr(), …)` for `XskCreateMode::SharedUmem` on the same `worker_umem`, and `:690-695` retries on "Device or resource busy". `bind.rs:74-78` maps `SharedOwner` to `SharedUmem`. `xsk_ffi.rs:1293-1392` allocates fresh zeroed `fill_ring`/`comp_ring` boxes per call, passes them to `bridge_xsk_socket_create_shared` (`csrc/xsk_bridge.c:214-232` → `xsk_socket__create_shared(…, fill, comp, …)`), and keeps them as the device's

### Fix direction

Acceptance: a namespaced test forces EBUSY on the owner's first attempt, frees the queue, and asserts the kernel FILL producer equals the primed count and that the fill/comp ring pointers are inside a live mapping of the UMEM fd (the M1 → M2 contrast)

### Summary
- **A57-02** — xpf-input-closed.service and xpf-transit-closed.service are DefaultDependencies=no with no mount ordering. ## #15097 — userspace-dp: fix — The kernel-monitor NUD_PROBE token is minted even when the kernel is probing a MAC the dataplane just refused, so one… (A66-05) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A66-05** — The kernel-monitor NUD_PROBE token is minted even when the kernel is probing a MAC the dataplane just refused, so one spoofed ARP reply (or NA) plus the kernel's own unicast re-probe turns a refused hijack into an authorized one (report severity: Medium — this defeats the #10704/#13660 live-binding protection, allowing next-hop hijack (MITM or blackhole, e.g. of the WAN gateway) by an L2-adjacent host. ### Fix direction
- **A66-05:** On a refused overwrite, re-assert the dataplane's MAC into the kernel (`add_kernel_neighbor(key, G)` REPLACE, rate-limited) so the kernel probes G rather than A. A genuinely moved G then fails to FAILED and resolves fresh. Additionally, bind the NUD_PROBE token to the probed lladdr and accept only replies consistent with a probe of the MAC the dataplane holds. Acceptance: the v23 Rust cell keeps G at step 3. The #10704 positive control (PROBE G then REACHABLE G2) still converges. A netns run of the attack leaves both the kernel entry and the dataplane entry at G.

## #15115 — config: fix — The #9727 jumbo-MTU commit advisory omits the kernel's 256-byte XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM, so MTUs 3567..3822 commit silently… (A80-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A80-01** — The #9727 jumbo-MTU commit advisory omits the kernel's 256-byte XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM, so MTUs 3567..3822 commit silently while full-size frames are dropped (report severity: Low — the advisory that exists to prevent silent jumbo-frame loss is wrong by 256 bytes. Within that window full-size frames never reach a worker (copy mode: kernel `rx_dropped`) or the ZC bind is ref; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A80-01` (Part v1-v28).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:383`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:383` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/config/userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727.go:23-28`, `afxdp/umem/mod.rs:59`, `afxdp/mod.rs:440-441`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/config/userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727.go:23-28` `userspaceRxMTUBudget = 4096 - 256 - 14 - 4` (3822). `/usr/src/linux-headers-6.18.5+deb14-common/include/net/xdp_sock_drv.h:35-48` `xsk_pool_get_headroom = XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM + pool->headroom`, `rx_frame_size = chunk - headroom` (4096 - 512 = 3584). Kernel `net/xdp/xsk.c:335-337` `if (len > xsk_pool_get_rx_frame_size(pool) && !xs->sg) { rx_dropped++; return -ENOSPC; }`. `afxdp/umem/mod.rs:59,83` headroom = `UMEM_HEADROOM` (256). Bind flags have no XDP_USE_SG (`afxdp/mod.rs:440-441`).

### Fix direction
- **A80-01:** Set `userspaceRxMTUBudget = 4096 - (256 + 256) - 14 - 4` (3566), name both headroom terms in the warning text, and add a test that derives the budget from XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM independently. Acceptance: 3567 warns, 3566 does not.
- Change only the cited mechanism in the anchored file(s)/symbol(s) above; fail closed (deny/drop/reject the operation) wherever the current path fails open, and preserve all neighbouring legitimate behaviour.

### Acceptance
- A regression test/fixture exercising the exact `A80-01` mechanism above (same path/spelling/state as claimed, surviving leg only) **fails on current `origin/master` and passes after the fix**; test-only-green coverage that does not exercise the mechanism does not close this issue.
- Named control cases adjacent to the mechanism (legitimate traffic/config/operations through the same code path) stay green; no behaviour change outside the cited mechanism.
- Fix, regression, and docs/changelog land together; stale narrowed/refuted sub-legs are not reintroduced.

### Dedup
- **A80-01:** Residual of #9727 (CLOSED), which introduced the advisory with this formula. Prior H06-02 assigned the over-MTU drop to #9727 without examining the budget. No issue or prior finding mentions headroom/3822.

## #15150 — userspace-dp: fix — IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::try_post treats lock contention as "queue full". post_worker_verdict then posts an Uncertain deny,… (B12-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **B12-02** — `IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::try_post` treats lock contention as "queue full". `post_worker_verdict` then posts an Uncertain deny, which terminalizes the still-Queued ReinjectCore entry, so the writer's pre-write check cancels the armed permitted write. Every worker takes the same mutex every loop iteration. (report severity: Medium — permitted traffic is lost (availability, not enforcement) at a rate set by lock contention. The E24 "verdict queue full" counter lies (the queue is empty). The production rate is unmeasured. ; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `B12-02` (Part v29-v63).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus2.md:160`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus2.md:160` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `ipsec_inner_queue.rs:634-645`, `worker/loop_body/mod.rs:833-838`, `worker/loop_body/reconcile.rs:761-778`, `loop_body/mod.rs:788-826`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `ipsec_inner_queue.rs:634-645` (`try_lock` failure → E24++ and Err). `:1872-1903` (fallback `Deny { stage: "d11_verdict_queue_full", reason: VERDICT_UNCERTAIN }`). `:656-662` `drain_into` takes `pending.lock()`. It is called from `worker/loop_body/mod.rs:833-838` inside `refresh_runtime_view`'s `between` closure, which runs on every iteration (`worker/loop_body/reconcile.rs:761-778`). The FORWARD permit is armed before the post (`loop_body/mod.rs:788-826`). `slowpath_reinject_9506.rs:1154-1192` spares an armed entry only for WouldPermit. `:487-501` returns Cancelled for a Terminal entry.

### Fix direction
- **B12-02:** Do not convert contention into a verdict change. Use a lock-free bounded MPSC, or a blocking `lock()` on the producer side. Treat a true-full queue for an armed WouldPermit as "leave armed". Count contention separately. Acceptance: the v41 rewrite cell yields WouldPermit with the lock held, and E24 moves only at `len() >= DEPTH`.
- Change only the cited mechanism in the anchored file(s)/symbol(s) above; fail closed (deny/drop/reject the operation) wherever the current path fails open, and preserve all neighbouring legitimate behaviour.

### Acceptance
- A regression test/fixture exercising the exact `B12-02` mechanism above (same path/spelling/state as claimed, surviving leg only) **fails on current `origin/master` and passes after the fix**; test-only-green coverage that does not exercise the mechanism does not close this issue.
- Named control cases adjacent to the mechanism (legitimate traffic/config/operations through the same code path) stay green; no behaviour change outside the cited mechanism.
- Fix, regression, and docs/changelog land together; stale narrowed/refuted sub-legs are not reintroduced.

### Dedup
- **B12-02:** No issue or draft for D11 verdict contention. #13550 is the Go batch cap; #9644 and #5163 are the same lock class in other modules. Shares its root mechanism with B12-03 (admission side); file together.

### Summary

(report severity: Medium — admissible IPsec-inner frames are refused and dropped at a contention rate whose synthetic upper bound is 22–50%. - Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `ipsec_inner_queue.rs:1793-1805` (`queues.try_lock()` failure → WORKER_QUEUE_FULL). `:1822-1832` (`drain_worker` takes `queues.lock()`, then `active.lock()` even for an empty batch). `:1942-1960` (`drain_verdicts_into` takes `verdicts`, `uncertain` (try) and `active`). Every iteration: `worker/loop_body/mod.rs:719-838` via `reconcile.rs:761-778`. The transport is always present (`loop_body/mod.rs:369-371`). Acceptance: the v41 refusal cell admits with the lock held (or returns a distinct retryable busy), and an idle iteration takes zero shared locks.

## #15163 — daemon: fix — When an IPv6 single-path management static or an IPv6 system backup-router is deleted or changed, the old route stays in… (B21-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **B21-01** — When an IPv6 single-path management static or an IPv6 `system backup-router` is deleted or changed, the old route stays in table 999 forever. The IPv6 FIB drops the RTA_FLOW realm that the stale-route reaper relies on to recognise xpf-owned routes. (report severity: Medium — config integrity in the management VRF lasts across restarts. A deleted or re-pointed IPv6 management route keeps steering management-plane traffic to the old gateway until reboot or a manual; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `B21-01` (Part v29-v63).

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus2.md:203` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/daemon/mgmtvrf_static_routes.go:29-30`, `daemon_flow.go:828`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): pkg/daemon/mgmtvrf_static_routes.go:29-30 says `IPv6 routes do not store RTA_FLOW, so an IPv6 single-path route reads back unmarked and is never reaped`. Lines :586-597 have `case unix.RTPROT_STATIC: return route.Realm == mgmtStaticRouteRealm`, and :104-107 has `if !mgmtStaticRouteOwned(route) { continue }`. Single-path routes are built as RTPROT_STATIC plus a realm (:268-275). The only other delete path is daemon_flow.go:828 reconcileMgmtVRFRouteDeletes, which handles RTPROT_DHCP only.

### Fix direction
- **B21-01:** Use a protocol marker instead of the realm for IPv6 single-path routes (for example ManagementVRFMultipathStaticProtocol or a dedicated one). Optionally add a one-time migration that adopts (RTPROT_STATIC, realm 0) routes matching a previously applied key. Acceptance: the probe passes for both the IPv6 static and the backup-router, operator RTPROT_STATIC IPv6 routes stay untouched, and a priority-change step leaves only the new slot.

## #15164 — cluster: fix — After RequestPeerFailover aborts locally, the requester reports an error and demotes. The owner keeps advertising… (B22-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **B22-01** — After RequestPeerFailover aborts locally, the requester reports an error and demotes. The owner keeps advertising StateSecondaryHold under its #5079 lease (no abort frame exists), and electRG's "Peer transfer out" rule promotes the requester on the next heartbeat. Under preempt, the owner takes the RG back when the lease expires. (report severity: Medium — HA ownership moves contrary to the reported outcome. The fail-closed commit-ready/settle guard is bypassed within one heartbeat, and preempt clusters get an unrequested second RG move about 2; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `B22-01` (Part v29-v63).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus2.md:205`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus2.md:205` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/cluster/failover.go:544-563`, `failover.go:209`, `daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:516`, `election.go:178-182`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): pkg/cluster/failover.go:544-563 calls abortRequestedPeerFailover and returns err on the commit, ready and commitFn failures. Lines :592-602 restore the pre-request snapshot of the peer state. The owner enters StateSecondaryHold (failover.go:209) and arms a lease of `2*localFailoverCommitTimeout + 20*time.Second` (daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:516, :604). election.go:178-182 has `if peerGroup.State == StateSecondaryHold && !clearedManualFailover { ... return electLocalPrimary, "Peer transfer out" }`, which does not check whether that hold belongs to a request this node aborted.

### Fix direction
- **B22-01:** Add a reqID-bound abort frame that restores the owner, keeping the lease as the crash fallback. Alternatively, have the requester record the aborted reqID and refuse "Peer transfer out" while the peer's hold belongs to it. Acceptance: in the b22 probes the requester stays non-primary after the abort, and the owner is restored promptly.

### Summary

### Summary

The #10878 teardown is lost for changes to that VPN's own block, and edits to the other VPN tear it down spuriously. (report severity: Low — the #10878 guarantee is lost for selector, proposal, local-address, lifetime, start/DPD and if_id changes on that VPN: the established SA keeps forwarding under the superseded config with no war; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1144-1150 @51d355c1d `marker := " " + name + " {\n"; start := strings.Index(section, marker)`. policy.go:413/431/490 render `" local {\n"`, `" remote {\n"`, `" children {\n"` inside every connection. policy.go:1125-1136 hashes that slice plus the `ike-<name>` secret. Observation: the block printed for VPN `remote` is `aaa`'s `remote { auth = psk } children { aaa {...} }` tail.

Acceptance: the three keyword names are evicted like the control, and editing `aaa` leaves `remote`'s hash unchanged.

### Summary

## #15186 — upgrade: fix — When the staged version is already live and committed, a bare re-run of xpfd upgrade (or --rolling) performs a full… (D05-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **D05-01** — When the staged version is already live and committed, a bare re-run of `xpfd upgrade` (or `--rolling`) performs a full same-version cut. It stops and restarts xpfd, replaces `.<ver>.dbsnap` with the current DB, and stamps `{version:<ver>, predecessor:<ver>}`, which the reader rejects. Operator rollback to the real predecessor then falls back to mtime and can refuse outright. If the re-run fails VERIFY, the cleanup deletes the live version's snapshot while the error says "live dataplane untouched". The neighbouring same-version refusal (new generation) tells the operator to run `dpkg-reconfigure xpf` to realign. That command always mints a new generation, so it is refused again every time. D05-03 is merged here because it shares the decision point and the fix. (report severity: Medium — no fault is needed, only a re-run of the documented verb. The cost is an unplanned xpfd stop/start (on HA, `--rolling` also runs a ForceSecondary failover). The pre-upgrade rollback snapshot ; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `D05-01` (Part v29-v63).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus2.md:302`.

- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:365`, `commit_stamp.go:67-72`, `stagedgen/stagedgen.go:208`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): Read at 51d355c1d. `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:365`: resume-vs-fresh runs only when `j.TargetVersion != stagedVer`. The INIT block (:497-635) has no no-op for `stagedVer == prev`. The only same-version check, :577-588 `existingGen != srcGen && stagedVer == prev`, refuses only on a different generation. The COMMITTED no-op (:637-648) needs an uncleared journal. `:1376`: `snapDir := ... "."+j.TargetVersion+".dbsnap"` is replaced. `commit_stamp.go:67-72` writes `Predecessor: j.PreviousVersion` (= ver), and `:131` rejects `stamp.Predecessor == ver`. Arm 2: `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` protects the dir wh

### Fix direction
- **D05-01:** In INIT, when `stagedVer == prev`, compare the pinned generation's managed binaries with the live dir (`mismatchedManagedBinary`, or `.srcgen` equality). If they are identical and a valid committed stamp exists, return "already at <ver>; nothing to do" before writing a journal or a snapshot. Apply the same check in `runRollingWith` before ForceSecondary. When the bytes differ, refuse with re-version guidance only, and drop the dpkg-reconfigure advice from code and docs. As defence in depth, never write `Predecessor == Version`, and guard the dbsnap removal with `ver == cur || ver == j.PreviousVersion`. Acceptance: the probe's re-run makes no stop/start calls, `.2.0.0.dbsnap` stays byte-ident
- Change only the cited mechanism in the anchored file(s)/symbol(s) above; fail closed (deny/drop/reject the operation) wherever the current path fails open, and preserve all neighbouring legitimate behaviour.

## #15193 — ipsec: fix — The #3952 PSK id selector scopes the secret to the peer ADDRESS only, and no remote.id is rendered for a fixed-address… (D04-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **D04-01** — The #3952 PSK id selector scopes the secret to the peer ADDRESS only, and no `remote.id` is rendered for a fixed-address gateway. With no `remote-identity`/`local-identity` (the Junos default shape, accepted by strict commit), charon acting as INITIATOR looks the key up as (`<local ip>`, `%any`), finds none, and aborts IKE_AUTH. Every xpf-initiated path (`establish-tunnels immediately`, the default `trap`, #14140 changed-VPN re-initiation, HA takeover re-initiation) fails; only peer-initiated SAs come up, and two xpf boxes in this shape never establish the tunnel in either direction. (report severity: High — availability of a committed security service on the default configuration shape. Demonstrated: xpf-initiated IKE_AUTH fails with real charon on the strict-commit render; xpf-to-xpf in this shap; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Fix direction

## #15194 — ipsec: fix — On RG demotion xpf removes the VIP but never terminates the IKE/CHILD SAs anchored on it. The stale SAs survive in charon… (D04-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **D04-02** — On RG demotion xpf removes the VIP but never terminates the IKE/CHILD SAs anchored on it. The stale SAs survive in charon (MOBIKE defers, and a non-MOBIKE peer generates no IKE traffic). When the RG fails back, `reinitiateIPsecSAs` → `swanctl --initiate --child` is refused with `not establishing CHILD_SA ... due to existing duplicate`, and the returning owner keeps encrypting with SPIs the peer has already deleted. The black hole lasted 160 s with a MOBIKE peer and `trap`, and over 220 s (still down when the window ended) with a non-MOBIKE peer; it is bounded only by DPD (if configured), the next rekey, or peer initiation. (report severity: High — HA ownership/availability on a routine planned failover + failback (manual `request chassis cluster failover`, preempt, monitor-driven demotion without a reboot). ### Summary

- **A44-05** — `allInterfaceNames` unions config base names with zone unit names without normalization, so `ge-0/0/0` and `ge-0/0/0.0` both export the same kernel ifindex counters (report severity: Low — metric truthfulness: any sum/per-zone aggregation double-counts unit-0 interfaces; no protection loss; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

## #15231 — logging: fix cohort — syslog client lifecycle (A47-02, A47-03, A47-04, A47-05, A47-06) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A47-02** — SyslogClient captures os.Hostname() at construction, and the #9326 fingerprint has no hostname term. After a rename with an unchanged stream stanza, every RT_FLOW record carries the previous device name until the stanza changes or xpfd restarts. (report severity: Low — this is a wrong attribution on the audit channel only. There is no enforcement or delivery loss. [reporter: Low+]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A47-03** — slogLevelToSyslog has no debug arm, so Debug becomes SyslogInfo. An `any info` host receives the whole debug firehose labelled severity 6, and a debug host cannot tell the two apart. (report severity: Low — a severity mislabel and filter bypass, bounded to --debug. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A47-04** — applySystemSyslog `continue`s on a client build error (source-address not yet local, or a hostname collector unresolvable at boot) and arms no retry debt, so the off-box system log stays off until any later commit. (report severity: Low — the system log (not the security audit stream) is lost after boot, and any commit recovers it. [reporter: Low-Medium]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A47-05** — pkg/cli reloadSyslog unconditionally replaces the daemon's client set with clients built by the dialing constructor. Each console commit pays a TCP/TLS dial per stream, tears down healthy connections, and installs a set the daemon's latch does not own. (report severity: Low — it affects only the in-process root console (#10833). The costs are commit latency (up to 5 s per blackholed stream), reconnect churn and dropped queued records. [reporter: Low-Medium]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A47-06** — applySyslogConfig is all-or-nothing. Any skipped stream leaves the fingerprint unset and the debt armed, so every 30 s tick replaces the whole client set and re-warms (redials) every healthy TCP/TLS stream, forever. (report severity: Low — the cost is reconnect churn (a TLS handshake per collector every 30 s), dropped queued records and lost drop counters. There is no delivery loss beyond each tick. [reporter: Low-Medium]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

## #15235 — cli: fix cohort — remote-cli diag (A51-02, A51-03, A51-04, A51-06) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A51-02** — `cmd/cli` wraps Ping in `context.WithTimeout(60s)`, while the server sizes the budget at count×1 s + 15 s (up to 115 s), so long counts lose their summary. (report severity: Low — diagnostic UX only. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A51-03** — ParsePingOptions accepts any int and cmd/cli casts it with `int32(...)`. `count 4294967297` sends 1 probe, where the local console sends 100. (report severity: Low — the operator types an absurd value, and the result is still a bounded, valid ping. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A51-04** — The LLDP TX socket is created with protocol ETH_P_ALL and never bound or read. With N LLDP ports there are N global taps, so every kernel-path frame is cloned to each until its receive buffer fills, then dropped. (report severity: Low — kernel-path CPU and memory overhead only. The AF_XDP fast path is not affected. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A51-06** — sysinfo reads the cumulative `cpu ` jiffies once and prints their ratios as `CPU: x% user, y% system, z% idle`, unlike Junos/top's current-interval figure. (report severity: Low — a misreport on a troubleshooting surface. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Summary
- **A58-01** — A changed .go file seeds only its owning package plus reverse importers. Tests that read another package's Go source by relative path (for example pkg/denyaudit scanning ../grpcapi/authz.go) are never selected for that package's changes. This is a residual of #14647. (report severity: Low — CI is non-blocking and `make test-go` runs everything. The effect is a false-green "affected tests" signal on PRs touching the targets of security-shape canaries. [reporter: Low, upper Medium]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A58-02** — The close-keyword lint workflow lints the PR body and the branch commits, but not the PR title. The squash-landed master commit's subject is the title, so a negated close keyword in the title can close an issue unchecked. (report severity: Low — the impact is a wrongly closed issue (tracking integrity), recoverable by reopening. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A58-03** — ci_affected_go_tests.sh's `git diff --name-only` reports only the destination of a rename. The source package, whose tests may no longer compile, is not selected. (report severity: Low — a non-blocking CI false-green on cross-package moves, which are routine in this repo's refactors. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A58-04** — Makefile:378's -run alternative `HeartbeatStartSuperseded` has its words in the wrong order. TestStartHeartbeatSupersededByStopDoesNotPublish7257 therefore never runs under the race detector, and the leg has no check that each name matches a test. [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A58-06** — The pkg/daemon host-inbound real-kernel cells (9637 x2, 12034, 12229, 12087) honour XPF_REQUIRE_NETNS only on the netns-start arm. No runner sets it for pkg/daemon, and the tool-absent arms (nft/unshare/ip...) skip before the forcing check. The #9812/#11418 forcing covers pkg/routing only. (report severity: Low — these cells pass on capable hosts. On runners without userns or tools they skip inside an ok package. Unit-level shape tests remain.
