## #15243 — userspace-dp: fix cohort — dataplane hold/replay fidelity (A60-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A60-01** — `PendingPMechReversePacket` stores the outer descriptor with the post-decap inner meta and discards the owned inner frame, so replay mis-parses the outer frame and the held packet is never delivered or forwarded (report severity: Low — fail-closed loss of a bounded number of held packets (at most 4 per token, 512 per binding) during an IPsec install window. It is limited to reverse packets that arrived decapsulated from native; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A60-01` (Part v1-v28).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:263`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:263` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:737-787`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:737-787` (`GreDecapStage::Decapped(m, f) => (m, Some(f), false)`) and `:811-866` (the WG equivalent) set `meta` to the inner meta. `:1772-1807` pushes `PendingPMechReversePacket { desc, meta, …, is_injected }` with no frame field and no `owned_packet_frame.is_some()` refusal. `:592-606` replays with `(held.desc, Some(held.meta), held.is_injected, true)`. `:613-624` uses the held meta and slices the outer UMEM frame. `:737` re-runs `stage_native_gre_decap(raw_frame, inner meta)`, which returns NotGre because the inner protocol is not GRE.

### Fix direction
- **A60-01:** Either refuse to hold when `owned_packet_frame.is_some()` (recycle and count, as in the over-cap branch), or store the owned inner frame in `PendingPMechReversePacket` and replay it via the injected-style `(meta, Some(frame))` path while recycling the native outer descriptor. Acceptance: the v16 cell delivers the inner packet once on replay (or counts a refusal), and the native control is unchanged.

### Summary

## #15247 — userspace-dp: fix cohort — neighbor-cache learn hygiene / #11406 residual (A66-03, A66-04) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A66-03** — XSK NA-learned neighbors carry no RX lease and no on-link target gate, so unsolicited NAs create authoritative entries that never age and pin the per-shard learn cap (report severity: Low — the effect is bounded: per-shard cap pinning in the dynamic map. Genuine neighbors still arrive through the Go mirror and the resolver, so forwarding degrades rather than fails [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).
- **A66-04** — Kernel-neighbor program limiter permanently drops a genuine change that arrives while every way of its bucket is hot; the "retried on a later advert" claim is false (report severity: Low — the only effect is kernel-table lag for host-originated traffic. The dataplane map is already correct, and the kernel's own NUD eventually resolves the neighbor [reporter: Low]; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A66-03` (Part v1-v28).

- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:333`.
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:334`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:333` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `poll_stages.rs:304-306`, `sharded_neighbor.rs:669`, `poll_stages.rs:337`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `poll_stages.rs:304-306` gates only MAC/IP learnability and the own-IP check, with no on-link test of `na.target_ip`. `sharded_neighbor.rs:669` inserts `NeighborRecord::authoritative(val)` with `last_rx_learned_ns: None` (:149-154). `age_rx_learned_neighbors` (:695-719) retains every lease-None record. Kernel programming is skipped by the #5288 limiter (`poll_stages.rs:337`) or refused by a full kernel table (no xpf gc_thresh tuning), so no DELNEIGH ever arrives for those entries.
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:334` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `neighbor_program_limiter.rs:254-261`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `neighbor_program_limiter.rs:254-261` returns false without claiming or marking any way. On the next advert no way owns the key, and `:239-241` `if !map_changed { return false; }` applies.

### Fix direction
- **A66-03:** Give NA/ARP-learned records an RX-style lease unless kernel-backed (`mark_kernel_backed_if_same` already exists), and gate the target with `src_ip_on_link_for_ingress` (or allow link-local only). Acceptance: the v23 cell drains the shard after aging.
- **A66-04:** On refusal, record the owed key (e.g. a small owed list, or mark the LRU way as owed without programming), or re-check the map on the next advert. Acceptance: the v23 cell's later-advert assertion turns true and the #5288 bound tests stay green.

### Summary

## #15274 — cluster: fix cohort — #9818 incarnation-retirement residuals (C03-02, C03-03) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## #15277 — release-tooling: fix cohort — release-tooling publish-gate completeness (C11-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **C11-02** — `publish.gate_apt` verifies the signature and the Packages binding for every suite but never reads `Valid-Until`/`Date`. An expired suite in the dist tree (for example a stale non-target suite) passes the gate and is published, after which apt clients refuse the channel. (report severity: Low — availability of the update channel only (no updates, and fresh Tier-A installs fail at `apt-get update`). There is no integrity loss. The default Valid-Until is 365 days, so the trigger is a sta; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

## #15284 — cli: DisableAutoSaveHistory breaks in-memory recall - wrong/empty history entries and spurious Ctrl-D exit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

Reproduced (PTY, production config): cliterm.DisableReadlineHistoryAutoSave sets readline DisableAutoSaveHistory=true (pkg/cliterm/terminal.go:45-50; pkg/cli/cli.go:480-490; cmd/cli/main.go:200-212), intending only to stop credential lines reaching disk (#10743). In chzyer/readline v1.5.1 that flag also skips history.New() on Enter - the only path committing the submitted line in memory and writing the file. Consequences: (1) Up after submitting a new command recalls the last seeded entry, not the command just run (off-by-one/stale); duplicate-submit then Up returns an EMPTY line; (2) no new command ever persists across sessions; (3) Ctrl-D on the manufactured empty line emits EOF/'exit' - CLI constantly wants to exit.

Fix direction: keep in-memory history commit enabled; suppress persistence selectively - e.g. custom history saver that skips credential-bearing lines, or DisableAutoSaveHistory=false + filter on save. Regression: PTY/unit test with seeded history: submit new cmd -> Up recalls it; dup-submit -> Up recalls it (not empty); new commands persist (non-sensitive) next session; credential line does NOT reach disk.

## #15285 — userspace-dp: publish rx_ring_full XSK statistic - RX ring-full drops currently invisible [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

From #14300 perf hunt (PerfCodex, deployed e480baa5a4): kernel XDP ABI distinguishes rx_ring_full from rx_dropped (if_xdp.h:93-99); the bridge reads all six socket stats (userspace-dp/csrc/xsk_bridge.c:365-385) but the publisher discards rx_ring_full (afxdp/binding_state/kernel_stats.rs:35-70), and sampling errors leave last value unchanged (worker/loop_body/mod.rs:2884-2900). 'Kernel RX dropped: 0' therefore does not establish zero ring-full loss - the suspected silent micro-drop point for -P12 retransmit bursts. Fix: publish rx_ring_full per binding/queue as a counter metric + surface in status; regression pin. Then use it to confirm/refute ring-full as the burst source on loss.

## #15649 — Show-surface renderer divergence (no SSOT) across CLI/gRPC/REST: policy detail, screen, flow timeouts, applications, flow-monitoring (V2-02, V10-04, V11-04, V12-04, V17-04) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

Cohort C1 (synthesis §5a) — Show-surface renderer divergence (no SSOT): member claims V2-02, V10-04, V11-04, V12-04, V17-04. Independent CLI/gRPC/REST renderers of policy/flow/screen/monitoring state with hardcoded literals diverge by construction (`pkg/cli/cli_show_*`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_*`, `pkg/api/show_text.go`).

Member titles (full, from source report master index / detailed headings):

- V2-02 — Local operational CLI `show security policies` and `show security policies detail` omit `then count` and live `Session statistics` (`packets`/`bytes`) even when `then count` or `policy-stats` is enabled
- V10-04 — `alarm-without-drop` is omitted from all screen inventory and `show security screen` surfaces, while local CLI `show security screen` omits unresolved/inert profile warnings and ignores invalid arguments
- V11-04 — `show security flow timeouts` / `show security flow` Disagrees Across Local CLI, gRPC, and REST on ICMP Default (`30s` vs `60s`), Unset Timeouts (`0s` vs Defaults), Stale `#5804` GRE Text, and Omitted Flow Fields
- V12-04 — `show security policies detail` and `show security applications` Bypass `ResolveApplication` / `ExpandApplicationSet`, Omitting Protocol/Port/ALG Details for Predefined, Term-Based, and Set-Backed Applications
- V17-04 — `show services flow-monitoring` and `show forwarding-options` diverge between gRPC and CLI, reporting `"No flow monitoring configured"` for IPFIX-only configs over gRPC, omitting IPFIX template bindings and `inline-jflow` source addresses, and rendering un-resolvable collectors as installed

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `72435eac8d7e4c4d59d9e8fffca8756682ea99af`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.j7oANJBkLs/synthesis.md` §3/§5a — all members final MATERIAL.

Note narrowed live forms at verification revision (synthesis §7): V12-04 predefined apps/sets are now explicitly rendered with shadow labels (#15207) — live defect is raw user/term/set expansion, not wholesale predefined omission. V17-04 gRPC forwarding-options now shows inline-jflow source and an exclusion suffix for uninstalled collectors — live defect is the IPFIX-only gRPC flow-monitoring leg (and template bindings). File/fix the narrowed forms, not the broader report wording.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `f214fac62ba2b38108baf824fc5a4f43a5c8fcda` (codex | smr | spark | final), synthesis §3: V2-02 M|M|M MATERIAL; V10-04 M|M|M MATERIAL; V11-04 M|M|M MATERIAL; V12-04 M|M|M MATERIAL; V17-04 M|M|M MATERIAL.

Decisive file:line from ledgers (codex-a / smr-a / spark-a):

- V2-02: codex-a — local detail/hit-count omit live counters although gRPC renders them (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security_dispatch.go:629-639,694-701`, `pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:355-519`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_policies_text.go:549-575,651-694`); smr-a — `cli_show_security.go:355` `showPoliciesDetail` prints Session log + quarantined line only, no `pol.Count`, no counter reader; spark-a — gRPC twin prints `count` and `Session statistics` via counter reader, local standard view builds `actionStr` from action+log only, never `pol.Count`.
- V10-04: codex-a — inventory has no audit modifier (`pkg/config/screen_inventory.go:26-44,65-121`), local `handleShowScreen` ignores extra/unknown arguments (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security_dispatch.go:767-792`); smr-a — grep `alarm-without-drop|AlarmWithoutDrop` in `screen_inventory.go` = 0 hits while profile field exists; spark-a — `ScreenChecks` has no alarm-without-drop token, inventory is SSOT for REST/gRPC show so modifier is invisible operationally. (Closed #15175 / B18-04 checked — closed, not an open duplicate; unanimous MATERIAL at f214fac is the inventory/show residual.)
- V11-04: codex-a/smr-a/spark-a — local hardcodes ICMP default `30s` against Rust `60s`, gRPC/REST print zero/omit unset (`pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:916-999` esp. :970-973, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_flow.go:109-157`, `pkg/api/show_text.go:387-425`, `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:220-222`); spark-a — three independent renderers with hardcoded literals, divergence by construction.
- V12-04: codex-a — local `show security applications` direct map loop prints raw user definitions, does not expand term/set via resolver (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security_objects.go:114-160,163-235`), predefined now rendered at :239-266 (#15207); smr-a — grep `ResolveApplication` in `cli_show_security_dispatch.go` = 0; spark-a — `printAppDetail` indexes `cfg.Applications.Applications[appName]` directly (nil-map early return).
- V17-04: codex-a/spark-a — gRPC returns `No flow monitoring configured` if Version9 nil even for IPFIX-only (`pkg/grpcapi/server_show_flow.go:26-47`, spark :28-30); smr-a — same, CLI handles more; codex-a refutes inline-jflow/collector subclaims at f214 (`server_show_forwarding.go:166-185,217-225`).

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --search` for V2-02 / V10-04 / V11-04 / V12-04 / V17-04 / cohort terms — no open issue covers this cohort (only unrelated closed screen issue #15175 noted above).

## Acceptance

Fix direction (report § "Complete Fix Specification" / §5 per member): introduce/reuse a single shared renderer/formatter (SSOT) for each object across local CLI, gRPC text, and REST — shared policy-detail counter rendering (V2-02), screen inventory including `alarm-without-drop` + unresolved/inert warnings + arg validation (V10-04), shared flow-timeout formatter next to `TCPSessionTimeoutDataplaneDefault` with ICMP `60s (default)` (V11-04), `ExpandApplicationSet`/`ResolveApplication` in all show paths (V12-04, narrowed), and gRPC flow-monitoring rendering for IPFIX-only configs (V17-04, narrowed).

Regression criterion: parity tests asserting identical (byte-for-byte where report specifies) output across CLI/gRPC/REST for the same fixture config — policy with `then count` + stub counters (packets/bytes), audit+inert screen profile, unset/configured flow timeouts, custom multi-term + nested application-set, and IPFIX-only flow-monitoring config. Tests must fail on the pre-fix divergent renderers, not merely pass on one surface.

## #15650 — V18-01: `compileForwardingOptionsWithOpts` and `compilePortMirroring` Overwrite and Drop Repeated `forwarding-options`, `port-mirroring`, `instance`, `input`, and `output` Stanzas Instead of Merging Them [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim
Repeated forwarding-options/port-mirroring/instance/input/output stanzas are overwritten/dropped instead of merged (MATERIAL, unanimous codex/smr/spark at f214fac62b). Report ID: V18-01 (source report: gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md, verified at f214fac62b).

## Evidence
- codex-b: MATERIAL — each port-mirroring stanza creates a new object, traverses only first child, overwrites named instance in map (`pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1864-1881,1919-1970,2022-2032`); userspace has no ingress to emit if incomplete object survives (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/mirrors.go:113-176`). Narrowing: strict #15256 shape check rejects zero-ingress object, so report's clean strict commit of input-only/second output-only is not proved; independently valid repeated-input stanza can still be lost.
- smr-b: MATERIAL — split `instance span1` input/output blocks overwrite; probe strict err `no ingress interfaces` because 2nd block's fresh `mi` replaces 1st (`compiler_services.go:1919-22,2022 pm.Instances[mi.Name]=mi`); Junos merges; `dup_block_merge_9023.go:48-84` omits port-mirroring.
- spark-b: MATERIAL (narrowed) — `compiler_services.go:1864` uses `FindChild("port-mirroring")` (first only) vs sampling `FindChildren` :1777; `compilePortMirroring:1879-1881,2022,2032` allocates fresh `pm` and overwrites; probe hierarchical split → strict error (second wins, first lost) — data loss confirmed but fail-closes at f214fac62b instead of silently installing zero mirrors; flat-set equivalent compiles correctly.
- Synthesis §3: V18-01 codex M / smr M / spark M → MATERIAL. Decisive file:line: `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1864,1919-1970,2022-2032`.

## Acceptance
Fix direction (report §V18-01): register `{"port-mirroring","instance"}` in `dupBlockMergeSites9023` (`pkg/config/dup_block_merge_9023.go:48-84`), iterate `FindChildren("port-mirroring")` in `compileForwardingOptionsWithOpts`, reuse/merge `fo.PortMirroring` + find-or-create instances and iterate all `input`/`ingress`/`output` children in `compilePortMirroring`. Use narrowed live form: repeated individually-valid stanzas must merge (not fail-close misleadingly nor drop on lenient load).
Regression criterion: hierarchical split `instance span1{input}` + `instance span1{output}` (and repeated forwarding-options/port-mirroring blocks) compiles strict with merged instance retaining both input and output; no instance/ingress lost.

## #15651 — V18-02: Port-Mirroring Interface Resolution Uses Raw `config.LinuxIfName` Instead of `ResolveKernelIfName`, Dropping Linux Unit Spellings (`ge-0-0-0.0`), Failing Junos Unit Spellings in `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go`, and Bypassing Commit-Time Duplicate-Ingress Checks on Interface Aliases [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim
Port-mirroring resolution uses raw LinuxIfName instead of ResolveKernelIfName, dropping/failing unit spellings and bypassing alias duplicate-ingress checks (MATERIAL unanimous at f214fac62b). Report ID: V18-02 (source report: gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md, verified at f214fac62b).

## Evidence
- codex-b: MATERIAL, narrower — compiler aliases input names by Linux spelling (`compiler_services.go:1971-1980`), userspace resolves configured names and key `(ifindex,VLAN,unitScope)` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/mirrors.go:70-95,121-155`; Linux-spelled `.0` alias not represented by configured unit/physical key can disappear. Narrowing: scoped-key code distinguishes bare physical from logical unit zero; blanket same-ifindex duplicate-loss obsolete; `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go` is legacy.
- smr-b: MATERIAL — `mirrors.go:60-79,121-41` indexes only Name/LinuxName (unit rows share parent LinuxName) so `ge-0-0-0.0` misses; `dataplane/compiler.go:2344 cachedInterfaceByName(LinuxIfName(ref))` fails Junos `ge-0/0/0.0`; commit dedup `LinuxIfName` key (`compiler_services.go:1972`) lets `ge-0/0/0` vs `ge-0/0/0.0` compile both yet same ifindex; `ResolveKernelIfName` (`types.go:357`) unused here.
- spark-b: MATERIAL — `compiler_services.go:1972` dedups on `LinuxIfName(v)` only; `mirrors.go:123,139-140` and `compiler.go:2344,2354` resolve via LinuxIfName+ifindexByName, never `ResolveKernelIfName` (`pkg/config/types.go:357`); VLAN-unit/RETH/tunnel spellings cannot map through slash→dash alone.
- Synthesis §3: V18-02 M/M/M → MATERIAL. Decisive: `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1972`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/mirrors.go:70-95,121-155`.

## Acceptance
Fix direction (report §V18-02): in `buildMirrorConfigSnapshots` index `LinuxIfName(iface.Name)` and fall back to `cfg.ResolveKernelIfName(ref)` for output/input; in `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go` resolve via `resolveInterfaceRef`/`ResolveKernelIfName`; add post-section validation normalizing each Input through `ResolveKernelIfName` so aliased ingress across instances is rejected at commit (#3972). Apply narrowed scope (legacy compiler.go leg noted by codex).
Regression criterion: `buildMirrorConfigSnapshots` unit test with Linux unit spelling (`ge-0-0-0.0`), Junos/VLAN/RETH spellings resolves to correct ifindex; aliased `ge-0/0/0` vs `ge-0/0/0.0` duplicate ingress rejected at commit.

## #15652 — Application-resolution bypass: compiler drops elided application leaves, show bypasses ResolveApplication, junos-host advisory predefined-first (V5-04, V12-04, V5-03) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

Cohort C2 (synthesis §5a) — Application-resolution bypass: member claims V5-04, V12-04, V5-03. Three consumers, three different application resolvers: direct-leaf compiler drop (`compiler_applications.go`), show bypassing resolver (`cli_show_security_objects.go`), predefined-first advisory (`junos_host_app_gap_7374.go`). V12-04 also appears in cohort C1 (show-surface divergence) — cross-reference that issue; the shared root here is that no consumer consistently uses `ResolveApplication`/`ExpandApplicationSet`.

Member titles (full, from source report master index / detailed headings):

- V5-04 — `applicationDirectLeaves` and `compileApplications` Silently Drop Header-Elided `application` Tokens and Value-in-Child Tails (`destination-port { [ 80 443 ]; }`, `protocol { tcp destination-port 8080; }`), Compiling All-Port / All-ICMP Applications on Clean Strict Commits
- V12-04 — `show security policies detail` and `show security applications` Bypass `ResolveApplication` / `ExpandApplicationSet`, Omitting Protocol/Port/ALG Details for Predefined, Term-Based, and Set-Backed Applications
- V5-03 — `to-zone junos-host` Application-Narrowed Permit Advisory (`#7374`) Checks `PredefinedApplications` Before User Definitions (Ignoring Shadowed `junos-*` Apps) and Aborts on Any `application-set` or Multi-Term Application

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `72435eac8d7e4c4d59d9e8fffca8756682ea99af`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.j7oANJBkLs/synthesis.md` §3/§5a — all members final MATERIAL.

Note narrowed live form at verification revision (synthesis §7): V12-04 predefined apps/sets are now explicitly rendered with shadow labels (#15207) — live defect is raw user/term/set expansion in show paths, not wholesale predefined omission.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `f214fac62ba2b38108baf824fc5a4f43a5c8fcda` (codex | smr | spark | final), synthesis §3: V5-04 M|M|M MATERIAL; V12-04 M|M|M MATERIAL; V5-03 M|M|M MATERIAL.

Decisive file:line from ledgers (codex-a / smr-a / spark-a):

- V5-04: codex-a — hierarchical direct attributes remain in named app node's own Keys while compiler only walks children (`pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:145-306`, `schema_security.go:1752-1767`); smr-a — MATERIAL, same flat-set/compact class with `applicationDirectLeaves` as consumer; spark-a — probes at f214fac: `protocol { tcp destination-port 8080; }` → `proto=tcp dport=""` (all-port, no error/warning), `destination-port { [ 80 443 ]; }` → `dport="80"` (443 silently lost).
- V12-04: codex-a — local `show security applications` direct map loop prints raw user definitions, no term/set expansion (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security_objects.go:114-160,163-235`); smr-a — grep `ResolveApplication` in `cli_show_security_dispatch.go` = 0; spark-a — `printAppDetail` indexes `cfg.Applications.Applications[appName]` directly (nil-map early return), replicated in gRPC text renderer.
- V5-03: codex-a — advisory checks predefined before shadowing custom and aborts on unexpandable sets (`pkg/config/junos_host_app_gap_7374.go:47-76,199-214`) though runtime resolver uses user-first set expansion (`pkg/config/capabilities.go:445-527`); smr-a — `junos_host_app_gap_7374.go:51` reads `PredefinedApplications[name]` before user map (inverse of `ResolveApplication` in `predefined.go:234ff`), set/multi-term returns `ok=false` → no warning; spark-a — same at :50-54, `appL4Matches` has no ApplicationSet/multi-term expansion.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --search` for V5-04 / V12-04 / V5-03 / application-resolution terms — no open issue covers this cohort.

## Acceptance

Fix direction (report fix specifications per member): make all three consumers use the canonical resolver — compiler must honour header-elided/value-in-child application leaves instead of silently widening to all-port/all-ICMP (V5-04; fail-closed or preserve ports, never silent widening on strict commit); show paths expand via `ExpandApplicationSet` + `ResolveApplication` (V12-04, narrowed); #7374 advisory resolves user definitions before predefined (honouring shadowed `junos-*`) and expands application-sets/multi-term applications instead of aborting (V5-03).

Regression criterion: compiler tests in `pkg/config/compiler_application_specs_test.go` asserting header-elided `destination-port` and `protocol { tcp destination-port 8080; }` preserve protocol+port (and bracket-list form does not silently drop ports); show tests asserting predefined, term-based, and set-backed applications render protocol/port/ALG in policy detail and `show security applications`; advisory tests in `pkg/config/junos_host_app_gap_7374_test.go` asserting a user-shadowed `junos-ssh` (tcp/2222) warns for uncovered system-services ssh (tcp/22) and multi-term/set permits warn for uncovered services. Each test must fail against the current divergent resolver.

Non-first primary installs as IFA_F_SECONDARY, primary flips are no-ops, and inet6 primary is dropped on dual-stack units (MATERIAL unanimous at f214fac62b). Report ID: V19-01 (source report: gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md, verified at f214fac62b).

- codex-b: MATERIAL — `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:796-805,924-925` overwrites IPv4 primary and only fills IPv6 when scalar empty; `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:484-527,1571-1596` uses addresses/order rather than per-family primary; IPsec `pkg/ipsec/policy_addr.go:349-370` consumes scalar.

## #15657 — Rollback-compare surface: operational compare wrong baseline/rollback 0 rejected, local CLI compare unreachable, display formats dropped (V45-03, V47-02, V48-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

Cohort C4 (synthesis §5a) — Rollback-compare surface: member claims V45-03, V47-02, V48-02. Same rollback-compare surface: operational `show system rollback compare` wrong baseline/unreachable pipe (`store_format.go`, `cli_show_system.go`) — spark-c flags V47-02 cohort with V45-03/V48-02.

Member titles (full, from source report master index / detailed headings):

- V45-03 — Operational `show system rollback compare <N>` Fails Outside Configuration Mode and Diffs Against Uncommitted `s.candidate` Instead of `s.active`, While `rollback 0` Is Rejected Across Compare/Show Surfaces
- V47-02 — Local CLI `show system rollback <N> | compare` Always Fails Due to Unreachable `case isCompare:` After `case rbPiped:` and `authorizablePipe` Rejection, While Pre-Pipe Tokens Are Silently Ignored
- V48-02 — `show system rollback <N> | display xml|json|inheritance` and REST `/api/v1/config/show` & `/api/v1/config/show-rollback` Drop Display Formats and Subtree Path Selectors

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-001.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `72435eac8d7e4c4d59d9e8fffca8756682ea99af`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.j7oANJBkLs/synthesis.md` §3/§5a — all members final MATERIAL.

Note severity dissent at verification revision: codex-c and spark-c rate V47-02/V48-02 Low/Medium (parity/UX, no config mutation/enforcement impact), V45-03 remains the substantive wrong-baseline defect.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `f214fac62ba2b38108baf824fc5a4f43a5c8fcda` (codex | smr | spark | final), synthesis §3: V45-03 M|M|M MATERIAL; V47-02 M|M|M MATERIAL; V48-02 M|M|M MATERIAL. (Slice C lanes: codex-c / smr-c / spark-c.)

Decisive file:line from ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c):

- V45-03: codex-c — `pkg/configstore/store_format.go:304-328` compares rollback against candidate and requires config mode; operational `pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go:895-920` uses this despite needing active, rollback 0 rejected; smr-c — `store_format.go:281` ShowRollback, :480 ShowRollbackRedacted, candidate-vs-active + config-mode-only compare; spark-c — `ShowCompareRollback` (store_format.go:305ff) requires candidate ("not in configuration mode") and diffs candidate not active, `rollbackEntry(n)=history.Get(n-1)` so n=0 → Get(-1) error, CLI :904,926 reject n<1.
- V47-02: codex-c — `pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go:929-976` evaluates rollback-piped branch before compare; smr-c — showSystemRollback case ordering (rbPiped before isCompare unreachable), authorizablePipe rejection; spark-c — :942ff switch: `case rbPiped` (unknown pipe) BEFORE `case isCompare`, so `rollback 1 | compare` hits unknown-pipe, `authorizablePipe("compare")` false (permissions_regex.go) → regex classes denied.
- V48-02: codex-c — `pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:465-481` rollback show only differentiates set vs hierarchical, ignoring XML/JSON/inheritance; REST `pkg/api/config.go:379-400` passes nil path; smr-c — `server_config.go:465` only Set/Redacted switch, REST drops format+path; spark-c — gRPC leg code-verified, REST `restShowFormat` at `authz_config_read_14707.go:59ff`.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --search` for V45-03 / V47-02 / V48-02 / rollback-compare terms — no open issue covers this cohort (hits were unrelated anti-rollback/closed configstore issues).

## Acceptance

Fix direction (report fix specifications per member): add active-baseline compare (`ShowCompareRollbackActive`/`...Redacted` comparing against `s.active`, no candidate requirement) and route operational-mode compare to it; handle `n == 0` as active config in rollbackEntry/show paths (V45-03); reorder local CLI switch so `isCompare` is evaluated before the generic `rbPiped` unknown-pipe case and permit `compare` in `authorizablePipe`, failing loudly on ignored pre-pipe tokens (V47-02); honour `display xml|json|inheritance` and subtree path selectors across gRPC `ShowRollback` and REST `/api/v1/config/show` & `/api/v1/config/show-rollback`, rejecting unknown formats (V48-02).

Regression criterion: store/CLI/API tests asserting (a) operational (non-config-mode) `show system rollback compare 1` diffs against active even with a dirty candidate, and `compare 0` succeeds; (b) local CLI `show system rollback 1 | compare` returns the diff (not unknown-pipe error) for both unrestricted and regex-restricted classes; (c) `display xml|json|inheritance` and subtree paths are honoured on CLI/gRPC/REST rollback+config show and unknown format is rejected (e.g. HTTP 400). Each must fail on the current candidate-baseline/unreachable-case/format-dropping code.

- **spark (spark-c)**: V49-03 rstDropExprs ct state 0 — MATERIAL (kernel-semantics NEEDS live validation, source-strong) - Code rst_suppress.go:211-225 Ct STATE & 0x4f == 0. nft_ct: for untracked packet ct state register = NF_CT_STATE_UNTRACKED_BIT (0x40) in kernel (ct state includes UNTRACKED bit when no ct) — actually kernel sets state = NF_CT_STATE_BIT(IPS_...)?? Report claims from 6.18 nft_ct.ko disassembly state never 0: untracked → 1<<6? If UNTRACKED bit (64, in mask) set, &0x4f !=0 → predicate fails for exactly target packets. Existing test TestRSTDropExprsScopedToConntrackless14949 PASSES at f214fac but only asserts expr shape (mask/cmp zero), not kernel evaluation — false-green oracle, itself evidence-quality finding. - Strongest refutation: kernel may return 0 when skb->_nfct==0 (nft_ct_get_eval zeroes reg when no ct in some versions) — version-dependent. Hence gate MATERIAL on report's disassembly +…


## Acceptance

#### Concrete Fix Plan - In `rstDropExprs` (`pkg/nftables/rst_suppress.go:211-225`), match `CtStateBitINVALID` (which is what `nft_ct_get_eval` produces when `ct == NULL` / no conntrack entry exists for an outgoing TCP RST on `NF_INET_LOCAL_OUT`) by masking with `expr.CtStateBitINVALID` and comparing `CmpOpEq` against `binaryutil.NativeEndian.PutUint32(expr.CtStateBitINVALID)` (or excluding only tracked states `CtStateBitESTABLISHED | CtStateBitRELATED | CtStateBitNEW` so `state & (ESTABLISHED|RELATED|NEW) == 0`), while also ensuring that `nf_conntrack_tcp_loose=1` mid-stream pickup on ingress does not promote foreign SNAT-address TCP packets into tracked conntrack entries before `tcp_v4_send_reset` / `tcp_v6_send_reset`. Update `TestRSTDropExprsScopedToConntrackless14949` (`pkg/nftables/rst_suppress_14949_test.go`) and add a live-netns nftables evaluation test that verifies the rule actually increments its counter and drops a conntrack-less outgoing TCP RST. --- ---

## #15730 — userspace-dp: worker_loop panics 'single-owner umem' on shared-UMEM owner bind after zero-copy EINVAL, helper never arms (loss cluster, master 7d95e004cb) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

Found by smoke-matrix lane 2026-10-19 on loss cluster converged to master 7d95e004cb (working-20694-g7d95e004cb, wire v3).

## Defect
On both xpf-userspace-fw0/fw1, the userspace helper (xpf-userspace-dp) worker threads panic deterministically:
```
thread 'xpf-userspace-worker-N' panicked at src/afxdp/umem/mod.rs:106:14: single-owner umem
xpf-userspace-dp: worker bring-up FAILED (worker_bind_incomplete:0:timeout:planned=3)
```
umem_mut() does Rc::get_mut().expect("single-owner umem") — the WorkerUmem Rc is still shared at create time. Sequence in journal: zero-copy bind fails EINVAL (flags=0x000c) -> copy-mode fallback binds several slots OK (role=private, shared_umem=false in status) -> remaining workers panic -> worker 0 incomplete -> reconcile fails closed -> helper enabled=false, forwarding_armed=false -> RG1/RG2 Takeover=no (helper not enabled / forwarding not armed / XSK liveness not proven), no forwarding primary.

Default policy is CrossNic (SharedUmemPolicy::auto), so shared-UMEM groups are attempted. Related: #15088 (SharedOwner create mode), #15244 (post-create ladder terminal).

## Workaround (applied live, config only)
`set system dataplane shared-umem mode off` + daemon restart on both nodes: panics 0/min, helper arms, RG0/1/2 primary node0 forwarding active, iperf matrix runs (v4 push 14.8G/3702 retr — degraded vs 22-23G bar, likely shared-off/private-UMEM + copy-mode cost; see smoke report).

## Acceptance
- No worker panic under default CrossNic policy on mlx5 SR-IOV loss cluster; helper arms on fresh daemon start.
- Regression test: a WorkerUmem whose Rc is shared must not reach umem_mut() expect — clone/ownership precondition enforced or handled.
- Loss cluster re-test with stanza removed (mode auto) PASS.

Refs smoke report /var/worktrees/smoke/security-matrix-2026-10-19.md

## #15734 — cluster: RG2 on node1 blackholes IPv6 transit and failback holds past 300s (recorded #12495 gate FAIL) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## What happens
Recorded 2026-10-19 on the loss userspace cluster, converged build `working-20694-g7d95e004cb` (origin/master `7d95e004cb`), via `test/incus/test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` (the #12495/#13058 acceptance gate; FAIL exit shape per #13058's disposition rule):

```
==> RG2 primary before: node0
  baseline: 2001:559:8585:ef00::1 -> 02:bf:72:16:02:02; fe80::bf72:16:2 -> 02:bf:72:16:02:02
  capture armed: tcpdump: listening on eth0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet), snapshot length 262144 bytes
==> requesting RG2 failover on loss:xpf-userspace-fw0 (node0 is primary)
  transit: 0/5 replies from 2001:559:8585:80::200
INSTRUMENT: LIVE-NA
GW-ENTRY: NA-ATTRIBUTED (fe80::bf72:16:2)
TRANSIT: BLACKHOLED (0/5 to the WAN-side v6 target, min 3)
VIP-ENTRY: ATTRIBUTED-NA (2001:559:8585:ef00::1)
V6NA-VERDICT: FAIL neighbor recovery is NA-attributed but v6 transit is blackholed — a separate (route/fabric-class) defect
FAILBACK: RG2 did not return to node0 within 300s — the shared cluster is left failed over
GATE_EXIT: 3
```

Two coupled defects from this single recorded run:

1. **IPv6 transit blackholed while RG2 owned by node1.** Neighbor recovery itself worked and is NA-attributed (VIP entry flipped `02:bf:72:16:02:02` → `02:bf:72:16:02:03` with a preceding Override NA; GW entry likewise NA-attributed), but the LAN host's IPv6 transit to `2001:559:8585:80::200` was 0/5 in the measurement window and still 0/2 ~40 min later while RG2 remained on node1. Read-only route snapshot in that state: LAN host default via `fe80::bf72:16:2` lladdr `02:bf:72:16:02:03` (node1) REACHABLE; fw1 `inet6.0` showed `::/0 → discard via lo` and only the LAN `/64` direct — the node0 view retained the WAN v6 routes (`2001:559:8585:80::/64` via `ge-0-0-2.80`). After manual failback to node0, transit immediately recovered 3/3. Needs root-cause per the verdict guidance: capture `ip -6 route`/`neigh` on both nodes + LAN host while RG2 is on node1 (the #6934 instrument table) — is the WAN-side route/fabric path simply not active for the RG2 owner on node1, or does ownership of the transit path not follow the RG?

2. **Failback did not complete within the 300 s deadline (reproduces #13058's failback half).** After the harness requested return, node0 sat in `secondary-hold` with `Manual=yes` and RG2 stayed on node1 past `FAILOVER_DEADLINE=300` (script exit 3, cluster left failed over). Cluster owner (SmokeMatrix) recovered manually: `request chassis cluster failover reset redundancy-group 2` (cleared hold), then `request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group 2 node 0` → node0 primary, forwarding active (`/var/worktrees/smoke/rg2-failback.log`). This is exactly the 2026-10-14 shape ("node0 remained secondary-hold past deadline; manual failover restored") that #13058 dispositioned by widening 120 s → 300 s; per #13058's closing note, a >300 s exceedance "should be filed as its own defect rather than widening again" — hold-release timing, not deadline width.

## Evidence limits
The harness's EXIT trap deleted its temp dir (pcap + neighbor timeline), so only the stdout verdict cells above survive; the NA/route attribution is as the gate computed it, not independently re-parseable. (Instrument improvement, not asked for here: preserve the evidence dir on FAIL/exit-3.)

## Cluster state after
Restored and verified: RG0/1/2 primary node0, node1 secondary, takeover/transfer ready yes (both views), forwarding active on node0, v6 transit 3/3, VIP6 2/2, lock free. `shared-umem mode off` live-config workaround for #15730 was in effect during the run.

Parent: #12495, #13058.

## #15740 — perf: __memmove 13.6% under poll_binding — copy-fallback/decap copies while shared-UMEM off; needs post-#15735 re-profile attribution (#14300) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Profile evidence (loss cluster, user-supplied)
`poll_binding_process_descriptor_with_injection` 16.18%, `__memmove_evex_unaligned_erms` (libc) **13.60%**, `enqueue_pending_forwards_with_dynamic` 3.65%, `build_live_forward_request_from_frame_with_dynamic` 2.36%, `build_forwarded_frame_into_from_frame` 1.20%.

## Attribution (source audit at 6372394b1, perf lane #14300)
The established fast path is already **zero-copy**:
- Flow-cache hit: `apply_rewrite_descriptor` / `rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place` in UMEM (`poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:716ff`) — 0 frame copies.
- Slow path `enqueue_pending_forwards` (`tx/dispatch/mod.rs`): in-place rewrite when `target.umem.allocation_ptr() == ingress` (L1262ff), else **direct-TX** `build_forwarded_frame_into_from_frame` straight into the egress UMEM frame (L1386ff) — 1 payload memcpy (unavoidable cross-UMEM).

Remaining per-packet copies (memmove candidates), in likely order **while shared-UMEM is OFF** (the cluster's current workaround for #15730; fix PR #15735 is MERGED on master but the cluster still runs the pre-fix `working-20694` build):
1. **Copy fallback** (`enqueue_copy_fallback_frame`, tx/dispatch/mod.rs:549): `build_forwarded_frame_from_frame` allocates `vec![0u8; len+4]` (`frame/mod.rs:684`, zero-fill + payload memcpy in `frame/build/mod.rs:91-93`), then `transmit/mod.rs:273` memcpys the Vec into the TX UMEM frame. **2 full-frame copies + 1 alloc + zero-fill per packet** whenever in-place and direct-TX are both unavailable — which, with shared-UMEM off, is every cross-NIC forward whose free-TX pool is momentarily empty, and every NAT64/native-tunnel forward.
2. **Decap/injected owned frames**: GRE/WG decap and WG injection `to_vec()` the inner frame (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:756`), then it is copied again at TX.
3. **Mirror clones**: sampled `packet_frame.to_vec()` (`flow_cache_hit.rs:712`) + staged mirror in dispatch.
4. **TCP segmentation** copies per segment (`tx/tcp_segmentation.rs:209ff`) — only oversized TCP.

## What is needed (do NOT guess-fix)
1. Re-profile on a **#15735-or-later build with shared-UMEM re-enabled** (smoke lane owns cluster scheduling) and confirm whether `__memmove` collapses — if yes, this is a deployment/validation task, not a code task.
2. If it persists: `perf report` call-graph attribution of `__memmove` (which of the 4 sites above), then target that site (e.g. direct-TX pool sizing, or building NAT64 frames directly into TX UMEM instead of the allocating `build_forwarded_frame_from_frame`).

Refs #14300. SessionKey-hash and PTB-parse wins split into PR #15739.

## #15742 — cluster: split-RG (RG2 node1 / RG1 node0) transit blackholes v4+v6 and gate-timing failback strands past 300s on 8871e79a9d (#12495 gate still FAIL) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

## What happens
Recorded 2026-10-19 round-2 on loss cluster converged to origin/master `8871e79a9d69dc7cb076f45b21b32ce837e494a1` (`working-20699-g8871e79a9d`, xpfd sha `7fd2379d…` both nodes, wire v3), which includes PR #15738 fixing #15734. The #12495 gate (`test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh`) still FAILs identically, and a controlled RG2-only diagnostic reproduces the split-RG blackhole:

```
==> RG2 primary before: node0
  capture armed: tcpdump: listening on eth0
==> requesting RG2 failover
  transit: 0/5 replies from 2001:559:8585:80::200
INSTRUMENT: LIVE-NA
GW-ENTRY: NA-ATTRIBUTED
TRANSIT: BLACKHOLED (0/5)
VIP-ENTRY: ATTRIBUTED-NA
V6NA-VERDICT: FAIL neighbor recovery is NA-attributed but v6 transit is blackholed
FAILBACK: RG2 did not return to node0 within 300s (exit 3)
```
Preserved evidence (#15737 working): `test/incus/logs/v6na-12495-*/{cap.pcap,events.txt,neigh.txt}` — NA burst at …785715 flips VIP+GW `02:bf:72:16:02:02`→`…:03`, entries REACHABLE, transit still 0/5.

## Controlled diagnostic (RG2 only, RG1 left on node0) — `/var/worktrees/smoke/r2-diag.log`
- RG2→node1 succeeds; LAN v6 transit 0/5 **and v4 transit 0/3** (both blackholed in split ownership, not v6-only).
- fw1 zebra while RG2-owner/RG1-non-owner: `S>* ::/0 [250/0] unreachable (blackhole)` selected; **no** `2001:559:8585:50::/64` or `80::/64` connected routes (WAN RETH prefixes stayed with RG1/node0); LAN `ef00::/64` connected present. Kernel: `blackhole default`.
- fw0 zebra healthy: `S>* ::/0 [5/0] via 2001:559:8585:50::1, ge-0-0-2.50` + WAN connected.
- So #15738's static-filtering removed the inactive WAN statics on node1 (correct), but split-RG transit still has no working path: LAN-owner (node1) must forward via fabric/cross-node to WAN-owner (node0), and does not. Either intra-cluster forwarding for split RGs is broken, or the gate's expectation needs a fabric route the dataplane/kernel never installs.
- HA matrix earlier same build: mid-iperf RG1+RG2→node1 ping v4/v6 3/3 ttl=63 passed (both RGs together move works); split RG2-alone does not.

## Failback half
- Gate failback (plain failover request, no reset) again stranded: node0 `secondary-hold Manual=yes` past 300s. Recovery needed `failover reset` + re-request (round-2 recovery log).
- BUT controlled failbacks succeed instantly: matrix RG1+RG2 failback `RG2_BACK iter=1`, diag RG2 failback `RG2_BACK iter=1`. Difference vs gate: [INFERENCE] gate failback issued ~20s after failover while matrix/diag waited longer / different hold state. #15738's hold-release fix does not cover the gate's early-failback timing shape.

## Acceptance
- Split-RG (RG2 on node1, RG1/WAN on node0) LAN→WAN transit v4+v6 works, OR gate/matrix document+enforce co-moving RG1+RG2 and the product declares split-RG transit unsupported with a fail-closed operator signal (not silent blackhole).
- Gate failback at its actual timing returns within deadline without manual reset.
- Re-run `test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` to PASS.

Refs: #12495 (gate), #13058 (failback timing), #15734/#15738 (prior fix, insufficient for split shape). Round-2 report: `/var/worktrees/smoke/security-matrix-2026-10-19.md`.

## #15753 — TCP-session fidelity knobs: zero seq/window state with rst-sequence-check/maximum-window schema-rejected, rst-invalidate-session + no-syn-check-in-tunnel dropped by buildFlowSnapshot (G29-03, G29-04) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

Cohort K3 — TCP-session fidelity knobs (report-002 G29-03, G29-04; both final-MATERIAL, unanimous M/M/M, in synthesis2 §5a/§5c, verification rev `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Full report titles:

- **G29-03:** TCP Session State Machine Tracks Zero Sequence or Window State (`rst-sequence-check` / `maximum-window` / `time-wait-state` Rejected by Schema; Any Blind Off-Path `RST` or `FIN` Matching the 5-Tuple Closes the Session)
- **G29-04:** `[edit security flow tcp-session rst-invalidate-session]` and `no-syn-check-in-tunnel` Are Dropped by `buildFlowSnapshot`, Leaving `should_teardown_tcp_rst` Hardcoded to `false` and Dropping Asymmetric Tunnel TCP Traffic

Source: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (G29-03/04). Shared mechanism (synthesis2 §5c K3): `security flow tcp-session` fidelity — zero seq/window tracking + schema-rejected `rst-sequence-check`/`maximum-window` (G29-03) and dropped `rst-invalidate-session`/`no-syn-check-in-tunnel` in `buildFlowSnapshot` (G29-04). Corrective scopes differ (state machine vs snapshot plumbing); this issue tracks both knob-groups.

Note on prior art: closed #6461 already covered blind off-path RST/FIN demoting a live session on session *hit* (`session/lookup.rs`). G29-03 as validated is the schema/state-machine limb: the Junos knobs that would control this are rejected by schema and `SessionEntry` carries no seq/window state at all (lanes' grep at d316277c). If #6461's fix already added sequence validation, close the G29-03 seq limb with a pointer; the schema-rejection limb (`rst-sequence-check`/`maximum-window`/`time-wait-state` unknown keywords) remains.

## Evidence (3-lane verdicts at d316277cb4)

- **codex-b** (`codex-b/ledger.md:86-87`): G29-03 MATERIAL under the firewall's intentionally lightweight TCP model — `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:951-1274` stores flags/handshake and close state, not sequence/window bounds; an admitted same-5-tuple RST/FIN can close a live session regardless of TCP sequence (refutation noted: off-path packets still need an allowed zone/interface and guessed tuple; do not present as guaranteed Internet-wide attack). G29-04 MATERIAL if advertised knobs are accepted and forwarded — `pkg/dataplane/userspace/flow.go:76-117` flow snapshot lacks `rst-invalidate-session` and `no-syn-check-in-tunnel` while the TCP dataplane consumes only selected flags (global `tcp_no_syn_check`/`tcp_strict_syn_check` in `afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4725-4772` are real, so not every no-SYN knob is inert — the two named knobs are the defect).
- **smr-b** (`smr-b/ledger.md:72-73`): G29-03 MATERIAL (parity, narrowed) — `should_teardown_tcp_rst` hardcoded `false` (`tx_cancel.rs`, deliberate, with documented HA rationale — tradeoff, not oversight); schema grep: no `rst-sequence-check`/`maximum-window` leaves (only timeouts); `session/mod.rs` seq tracking not found (grep seq/window nil). G29-04 MATERIAL — `buildFlowSnapshot` (`flow.go:76-118`) carries `NoSynCheck`/`StrictSynCheck` (#10703) but NOT `NoSynCheckInTunnel`/`RstInvalidateSession` despite config fields `types_security.go:352-353` + compiler `compiler_security_flow.go:711-715` — compiled-then-dropped CONFIRMED at the Go→wire boundary; Rust `should_teardown_tcp_rst=false` stub confirms the RST arm is dead; no alternate Rust snapshot field for either name (grepped, absent).
- **spark-b** (`spark-b/ledger.md:323-333`): G29-03 MATERIAL* — grep `rst-sequence-check|maximum-window` in `schema_security.go` = none; any 5-tuple RST kills the session (spoofable with guessed 5-tuple); severity High if default-on Junos semantics confirmed, else Medium parity — explicitly "cohort-able thematically, distinct knobs/paths" with G29-04. G29-04 MATERIAL* narrowed — `compiler_validate_warn.go:710-735` lists these as *unenforced* with warnings, so not fully silent: warned-but-still-misbehaving; forwarding impact is asymmetric tunnel TCP traffic dropped beyond knob cosmetics, plus default-behaviour divergence (`rst-invalidate-session` default on in Junos vs hardcoded `false`).

Dedup: `gh issue list --search` for G29-03/04, `rst-invalidate-session`, `rst-sequence-check`, `tcp-session` found no open issue; closed #10703 (syn-check knobs inert — the `NoSynCheck`/`StrictSynCheck` siblings that *were* plumbed) and closed #6461 (session-hit RST demotion) are adjacent, not covering the schema-rejected knobs or the `buildFlowSnapshot` drop.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `security flow tcp-session rst-sequence-check` and `maximum-window` (and `time-wait-state` if Junos-canonical) are either implemented — `SessionEntry` tracks sequence/window bounds and an out-of-window blind RST/FIN on an admitted 5-tuple does not close/demote the live session — or explicitly rejected/warned as unsupported at commit with no silent schema dead-end. Add a Rust unit test: in-window RST closes, out-of-window RST (seq=0 blind) does not.
- [ ] `buildFlowSnapshot` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/flow.go`) threads `RstInvalidateSession` and `NoSynCheckInTunnel` from `types_security.go:352-353` / `compiler_security_flow.go:711-715` through the wire snapshot to the Rust consumer (snapshot round-trip test asserting both fields).
- [ ] With `rst-invalidate-session` configured (or by Junos-default equivalence), an RST invalidates the session: `should_teardown_tcp_rst` is driven by the snapshot value, not hardcoded `false` — respecting the documented HA stray-RST rationale in `tx_cancel.rs` (i.e. knob-controlled, default behaviour explicitly decided and documented).
- [ ] With `no-syn-check-in-tunnel` configured, asymmetric tunnel mid-stream TCP (ACK without seen SYN) is admitted instead of dropped; without it, current strict behaviour is retained. Regression test on the tunnel ACK fixture from G29-04.
- [ ] The `compiler_validate_warn.go:719-735` unenforced-knob warnings for these leaves are removed once enforced (warned-but-inert is not an acceptable end state).

## #15757 — Bare-destination `copy`/`rename` (`#15237`) skips `BareDestinationParent` in `AuthorizeConfigMutation` and `Store.RenameAsPlantClass` session-rematch lineage [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

Bare-destination `copy`/`rename` (`#15237`) skips `BareDestinationParent` in `AuthorizeConfigMutation` and `Store.RenameAsPlantClass` session-rematch lineage

## Claim

G2-01 — Bare-destination `copy`/`rename` (`#15237`) skips `BareDestinationParent` in `AuthorizeConfigMutation` and `Store.RenameAsPlantClass` session-rematch lineage

Report: `gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` § Detailed Findings G2-01; synthesis `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a final verdict **MATERIAL** (codex/smr/spark at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`).

Cross-reference: unfiled prior claim V2-01 (prior synthesis NEEDS_VALIDATION) — same mechanism family, not a filed issue; file as new per synthesis §5a/§5b note.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at d316277cb4 (ledgers in `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/`):

- **codex-a:** G2-01 — MATERIAL, related but not identical to V2-01.** Defect: authorization resolves source and destination exactly as supplied, but executor derives bare destination from source parent; session rename lineage records the bare path too (`pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:118-140`; `pkg/config/ast_edit.go:82-87,130-143,191-205`; `pkg/configstore/store_command.go:320-329`). Refutation: full absolute destination has no mismatch; V2-01 is the older executor misplacement, now corrected, not necessarily this new authorization/rematch gap. Decisive check: anchored deny and session ancestry using *same* bare rename, independently checking copy vs rename.
- **G2-02 — MATERIAL.** Defect: scoped compare extracts only `m.Children` for non-leaves; a leaf, a container's own inactive flag, and an empty container produce identical empty child lists, so no diff (`pkg/config/ast_format.go:568-589`). Refutation: global compare still compares actual nodes; child edits within a scoped container render. Decisive check: compare each changed target node itself, including duplicate same-path matches, against `FormatCompare` node-level output (`pkg/config/ast_format.go:557-560`).

## #15768 — Session-Miss Scoped-NAT FIB Lookup (`#15118`) Ignores `route_table_override`, Clears `resolved_in_table` Provenance, Loses 5-Tuple ECMP Hashing, and Deep-Clones `ForwardingState` [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

G35-01 — Session-Miss Scoped-NAT FIB Lookup (`#15118`) Ignores `route_table_override`, Clears `resolved_in_table` Provenance, Loses 5-Tuple ECMP Hashing, and Deep-Clones `ForwardingState`

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form (synthesis §7 — file this, not the broader report wording):** MATERIAL for PBR/native-VRF wrong-table resolution + `resolved_in_table` stamp loss on ordinary untranslated session-miss flows. The "loses 5-tuple ECMP hashing" limb is **refuted** for the non-NAT-local branch (spark-c: `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic_for_flow` does pass `Some(ecmp_hash_flow(flow_key))` at fib.rs:241-258; smr-c agrees ECMP loss is only on the NAT-local-suppressed branch) — do not claim ECMP loss on ordinary flows. The deep-clone limb is scoped to the cold NAT-local miss path for an unclaimed registered NAT address only (`is_nat_local` gate), not every flow.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL, cold path. Defect: an unclaimed registered-NAT destination enters `lookup_forwarding_resolution_without_nat_local(..., dst, None)` without the caller's PBR/VRF table, without the five-tuple dynamic ECMP selection, and its returned `selected_route` is discarded; `state.clone()` copies the *whole* forwarding state, not the "small local sets" claimed by its comment (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:339-379,383-415`; caller `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4297-4339`). Counter: only when `is_nat_local && !nat_destination_claims_local`; ordinary claimed destinations use the flow-based lookup, and no measured CPU cost is established. Check: bounded VRF/PBR, ECMP and table-provenance test with registered but unclaimed NAT address.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL (narrowed). Defect: `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4297-4322` — untranslated arm calls `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow(forwarding, neighbors, flow, zone,ifname,ri)` with NO table arg, returns `resolved_in_table=false` (4321) vs else-arm 4323-4338 passing `route_table_override.as_deref()` + true. `fib.rs:339` nat_flow helper hardcodes `table=None` in both branches; `without_nat_local` clones whole `ForwardingState` (`state.clone()`). Refutation: for non-NAT-local dst, helper delegates to `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic_for_flow` which DOES preserve 5-tuple ECMP hash — report's "loses ECMP" only true on NAT-local-suppressed branch (`without_nat_local`→`inner_ecmp None`). Clone is cold miss path for unclaimed NAT addr only, not every flow (`is_nat_local` gate fib.rs:~355). Verdict: MATERIAL for PBR/native-VRF (`route_table_override` ignored + install_table stamp cleared → re-resolve in wrong table, VRF leak/blackhole) on ordinary untranslated flows; ECMP/clone subclaims narrowed.
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL (narrowed). Defect (strongest): in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` the untranslated arm (`pre_routing_dnat.is_none() && nptv6_inbound.is_none() && nat64_match.is_none()`, ~:4297) calls `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow(forwarding, dyn, &flow, zone, ifname, ri)` — no table parameter. That helper (`forwarding/fib.rs:338-380`) for the non-NAT-local case calls `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic_for_flow(state, neighbors, dst, &flow.forward_key)` → `lookup_forwarding_resolution_inner_ecmp(..., None, Some(ecmp_hash_flow))` (fib.rs:241-258), i.e. default table `inet.0/inet6.0`, *not* `route_table_override`. Refutation: flowless path was fixed to thread `route_override` (`flowless_verdict.rs:339-350`); ECMP-hash sub-claim is *wrong* on that branch; deep-clone exists but is bounded/cold. Decisive: construct `ForwardingState` with diverging inet.0 vs tenant route, call `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` with a flow whose override table differs; observed egress follows inet.0.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G35-01"` and keyword searches (`scoped-NAT FIB route_table_override`) — no issue covers this claim. Hits #12086/#9752 are distinct table-free local-resolution / PBR-installing-table mechanisms, not the session-miss scoped-NAT `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` table threading. Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- Thread the caller's table (and ICMP context where the report fix specifies it) into the session-miss scoped-NAT FIB lookup so an untranslated flow resolves in `route_table_override` (its PBR/VRF table) rather than default `inet.0`/`inet6.0`, and return correct `resolved_in_table` provenance instead of clearing the stamp — i.e. implement the report §G35-01 Fix Direction narrowed as above (pass `route_table_override.as_deref()` from `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`, use the in-table lookup variants in `fib.rs`, stop discarding `selected_route` provenance).
- Do **not** regress the refuted limb: ordinary non-NAT-local flows must retain 5-tuple ECMP hashing; any clone-elimination must be scoped to the NAT-local-suppressed branch without changing claimed-destination behaviour.
- Regression criterion: a bounded VRF/PBR test with diverging default vs tenant routes and a registered-but-unclaimed NAT destination (plus a non-NAT flow in an override table) must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` (egress/table follows `inet.0`, `resolved_in_table=false`) and pass after the fix; neighbouring claimed-NAT and flowless (`flowless_verdict.rs` route_override) paths must not regress.

## #15769 — XSK Neighbor Lease (`#15247` / `#15624`) Demotes Kernel-Backed Neighbors on Same-MAC ARP/NA and Self-Promotes Unsolicited XSK Learns via Echoed `NUD_STALE` Netlink Events [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

G35-02 — XSK Neighbor Lease (`#15247` / `#15624`) Demotes Kernel-Backed Neighbors on Same-MAC ARP/NA and Self-Promotes Unsolicited XSK Learns via Echoed `NUD_STALE` Netlink Events

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form:** MATERIAL primarily for the demotion half (source-complete in all three lanes): a same-MAC XSK ARP/NA refresh demotes a kernel-backed (authoritative, `last_rx_learned_ns=None`) neighbor to a 60s RX lease that can then be aged out. The self-promotion half (echoed `NUD_STALE` clearing the lease) is retained inside the claim but smr-c notes it needs the monitor-socket check (does the monitor receive its own netlink requests?) — do not present self-promotion as independently proven beyond the cited `USABLE_NUD`/`mark_kernel_backed_if_same` path.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL, narrower than unconditional poisoning. Defect: same-MAC XSK NA sets `last_rx_learned_ns=Some` even on an authoritative row; later an RTM_NEWNEIGH echo of userspace-programmed `NUD_STALE` can `mark_kernel_backed_if_same` without independently confirming reachability (`sharded_neighbor.rs:789-802,885-919`; `neighbor.rs:530-545,947-953`). Counter: on-link/ARP solicited and NDP override guards constrain acquisition, the kernel uses `NUD_STALE` rather than REACHABLE, and a genuinely kernel-backed same-MAC update clears the lease. Check: order a backed row → same-MAC XSK learn → kernel event/expiry, distinguishing kernel's own echo from independent resolution, and inspect resulting map/epoch.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: `sharded_neighbor.rs:789-802` same-MAC XSK re-advert with `learn_now_ns=Some` unconditionally sets `last_rx_learned_ns=Some(now)` even if prior was None (kernel-backed authoritative) → demotes to 60s RX lease, aged by `age_rx_learned_neighbors`. Return `Some(false)` so no kernel reprogram. Refutation (self-promotion half): `neighbor.rs:948-952,1008-1012` monitor calls `mark_kernel_backed_if_same` on echoed RTM_NEWNEIGH — but monitor requires solicited/PERMANENT gate (`insert_arp_reply_if_solicited_allows`, 914/985); unsolicited XSK learn echoed as NUD_STALE still passes USABLE_NUD and same-MAC → mark clears lease. So self-promotion plausible via own `add_kernel_neighbor` echo. Kernel may not echo own netlink req to same socket group — depends on monitor socket registration (decisive: check monitor binds RTNLGRP_NEIGH and receives own requests). Verdict: MATERIAL demotion half (source-complete); self-promotion NEEDS that socket check, retained inside claim.
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: (1) `sharded_neighbor.rs:789-803`: same-MAC arm does `record.last_rx_learned_ns = Some(record.last_rx_learned_ns.map_or(now_ns, |s| s.max(now_ns)))` when `learn_now_ns=Some` — a `None` (kernel-backed/authoritative) record becomes `Some(now)`. Since it returns `Some(false)` (unchanged), `should_program` is false, no `add_kernel_neighbor`, so no monitor event re-marks it; `age_rx_learned_neighbors` (sharded_neighbor.rs:859-883) then evicts once age ≥ 60s+grace unless in `manager_keys`. (2) Self-promotion: data-path learn calls `add_kernel_neighbor` (poll_stages.rs ARP ~:253 / NA ~:358) which installs NUD_STALE; monitor `parse_neighbor_msg` treats `USABLE_NUD = REACHABLE|STALE|DELAY|PROBE|PERMANENT` (neighbor.rs:886-887) and on usable state calls `mark_kernel_backed_if_same`. Refutation: `refresh_rx_learned_pair` preserves None (`if is_some()` guard, sharded_neighbor.rs:901-917), and continued traffic refreshes the lease so eviction needs 60s of silence for that IP; gateway may be in manager_keys (exempt from aging). But neither refutes the state inversion: a same-MAC refresh must not demote, and a self-installed STALE must not confirm. Decisive check (not run): unit test — insert kernel-backed (None), call insert same-MAC with learn_now_ns, assert still None; plus monitor test feeding own STALE echo asserting no promotion.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G35-02"` and keyword search (`XSK neighbor lease`) — no issue covers this claim. Hit #15247 is the prior neighbor-hygiene cohort that introduced the cited machinery, not this demotion/self-promotion defect. Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- A same-MAC XSK refresh must not demote a kernel-backed neighbor: only refresh `last_rx_learned_ns` when it is already `Some(_)` (matching `refresh_rx_learned_pair`), per report §G35-02 Fix Direction step 1 (`sharded_neighbor.rs:793-801`).
- A self-installed `NUD_STALE` echo must not self-promote an unsolicited XSK learn to kernel-backed: gate `mark_kernel_backed_if_same` on independently confirmed states (excluding unconfirmed `NUD_STALE` echoes for currently-leased entries), per report Fix Direction step 2 — after confirming the monitor socket-registration behaviour smr-c names.
- Regression criterion: unit tests that (a) insert a kernel-backed (`None`) record, apply a same-MAC XSK learn with `learn_now_ns`, and assert it remains `None`/not aged out, and (b) feed the monitor its own `NUD_STALE` echo and assert no promotion — must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` and pass after; solicited/kernel-confirmed neighbor acquisition must not regress.

## Claim

G35-03 — `KernelNeighborProgramLimiter` (`#15247` / `#15624`) Single-Slot `self.owed` Overwrite and Way-Eviction Drop Lose Owed Kernel Neighbor Programs Under Hot-Bucket Contention

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form:** MATERIAL as a bounded correctness defect of the owed-retry mechanism under hot-bucket contention (all three lanes), not a steady-state bug. Severity is contested downward by the lanes (smr-c: report High overstated, Medium-bounded; spark-c/codex-c: bounded to overloaded same-bucket ways in a per-worker best-effort kernel-neighbor mirror; transit forwarding via the userspace map is unaffected — impact is kernel neighbor-table lag). Related closed #6129 tracked a distinct earlier direct-mapped slot-collision starvation in the same limiter lineage; the present claim is the successor single-`owed`-slot overwrite / way-eviction loss at `d316277c` — cross-reference #6129, do not treat as its duplicate without a scope check against its closed fix.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: one `owed: Option` is newest-wins: two fresh keys colliding in a hot limiter bucket overwrite debt, while the first key's subsequent unchanged-map advert exits before programming (`neighbor_program_limiter.rs:159-172,207-279`). Counter: limited to overloaded same-bucket ways in a per-worker best-effort kernel-neighbor mirror; later changed bindings may eventually repair it, and no rate/traffic impact has been measured. Check: bounded two-key hot-bucket sequence, a later unchanged advert for each, and actual program-decision recovery.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL (bounded). Defect: `neighbor_program_limiter.rs:172` single `owed: Option<((key),mac)>` newest-wins; 266-269 every-way-hot sets owed, next hot key overwrites; in-owned-way rate-limited MAC change (227-229 return false) never records owed, slot.mac stays old, way eviction (choose_victim) loses it, later `map_changed=false` advert hits `!owed_map_changed` skip (257). Refutation: bounded — requires ≥4-5 colliding keys in same bucket within 50ms + MAC change; kernel entry stays stale until re-advert with change/solicited probe; NUD_STALE self-heal on host path only, userspace FIB uses userspace map (correct MAC) so transit forwarding unaffected; impact is kernel neighbor table lag. Verdict: MATERIAL, Medium-bounded (report High overstated). Distinct from limiter tests present (owed tests cover single owed, not multi-victim overwrite).
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL (narrowed: correctness of owed-retry under contention; not a steady-state bug). Defect: `neighbor_program_limiter.rs:169-173` `owed: Option<((i32,IpAddr),[u8;6])>` single table-wide slot; set only in the no-way/all-hot branch (~:259-263). A 5th colliding changed key overwrites victim's owed; victim's later `map_changed=false` advert returns false at the `!owed_map_changed` early return — kernel never programmed. Second limb: key owning a way with stale MAC, rate-limited inside interval returns false without recording owed (fast-path owns-key branch) — if ways later evicted, new MAC never reaches kernel. Refutation: limiter is explicitly newest-wins by design comment ("One slot: newest-wins"); most losses self-heal on next *changed* advert or kernel probe/reassert paths; impact needs hot-bucket contention within 50ms + silence. But "newest-wins" is a documented lossy contract for a must-not-lose obligation (kernel neighbor programming) — the owed mechanism does not compose under the flood it was built for. Decisive: existing limiter unit-test harness — add 5-key same-bucket collision sequence; deterministic.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G35-03"` — no hit. Keyword search (`KernelNeighborProgramLimiter`) hits only closed #6129 (earlier direct-mapped slot-collision facet, closed 2026-07-21); synthesis2 lanes unanimously affirm the distinct single-`owed`-slot mechanism live at `d316277c` with no DUP flag, and §5a lists G35-03 as fileable — filed as new with the #6129 cross-reference above. Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- Owed kernel-neighbor programs must not be lost under hot-bucket contention: eliminate or bound the lossy single-slot `self.owed` overwrite and the in-owned-way rate-limited MAC-change / way-eviction drop (report §G35-03 Fix Direction: track kernel-programming state on the neighbor record, e.g. `kernel_programmed_mac`, and derive `needs_kernel_program` from it rather than a single external owed slot — or an equivalent per-key owed design).
- Regression criterion: limiter unit tests with a ≥5-key same-bucket collision sequence (victim owed, then overwritten by a later hot key, then an unchanged-map re-advert for the victim; plus an in-owned-way MAC change followed by way eviction) must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` (victim never programmed) and pass after; single-owed and normal changed-advert programming must not regress, and the rate-limit (anti-netlink-DoS) bound must be preserved.

## #15771 — `embedded_icmp_return_resolution` and `embedded_icmp_quoted_reply_resolution` Fall Back to Default Routing Table `inet.0`/`inet6.0` (`table = None`), Breaking VRF Isolation and Return Routing When Companion Session Is Absent [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

G36-03 — `embedded_icmp_return_resolution` and `embedded_icmp_quoted_reply_resolution` Fall Back to Default Routing Table `inet.0`/`inet6.0` (`table = None`), Breaking VRF Isolation and Return Routing When Companion Session Is Absent

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form:** MATERIAL for the companion-absent fallback path only (all three lanes). When a forward/reverse companion session is present its resolution is preferred and unaffected; default-table-only deployments are unaffected. The safe fallback must be domain-scoped or fail-closed (drop), never the default table.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL, missing-companion case. Both embedded-return helpers can fall back to a dynamic route lookup without a routing-table argument, despite carrying related forward-flow identity (`icmp_embed/return_resolution.rs:12-32,52-72`). Counter: existing forward/reverse companions provide preferred resolution, and default-table deployments are unaffected. Check: force only the companion-absent path for an error associated with a VRF flow and assert selected table/route identity.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL (narrowed). `return_resolution.rs:30,70` fallback `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic(forwarding, neighbors, original_src)` — table-free overload defaults inet.0/inet6.0 (fib.rs inner defaults). When companion absent, VRF tenant src resolves in default table — VRF cross-talk/blackhole. Refutation: session normally present (fallback rare); flow's routing domain could be recovered from ingress metadata not passed to ctx — function signature lacks table/domain, so defect is API omission. Verdict: MATERIAL (fallback path only).
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: `icmp_embed/return_resolution.rs:12-32,52-72` (full file read): both fns fall back to `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic(ctx.forwarding, ctx.dynamic_neighbors, dst)` → `table=None` → DEFAULT_V4/V6_TABLE (fib.rs:229-240). Neither maps `forward_key.routing_domain`/`install_table_domain` to a table, though `lookup_…_for_flow_in_table` exists (fib.rs:260+). Cross-VRF leak + VRF blackhole follow when companion absent. Refutation: fallback only fires when companion session absent (error for expired/unknown session) — Junos would arguably drop anyway; cross-VRF leak needs overlapping prefixes + neighbor present in default table. Design verdict: a *fallback lookup* must still be domain-scoped; using default table is never the safe fallback (fail-closed drop is). Decisive: test with route only in tenant table + conflicting default route, no companion; assert resolution egress.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G36-03"` and keyword search (`embedded_icmp_return_resolution`) — no defect issue covers this claim (hit #1348 is a code-refactor task for the same file, not the VRF fallback defect). Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- Both embedded-ICMP return helpers must resolve the fallback in the flow's own routing domain/table (map `forward_key.routing_domain` / `install_table_domain` via `routing_domain_to_instance` / `table_name_for_domain` to the in-table lookup, per report §G36-03 Fix Direction), or fail closed (drop) when no domain-scoped resolution exists — never fall back to default `inet.0`/`inet6.0`.
- Regression criterion: a test with a route present only in a tenant table plus a conflicting default-table route and **no** companion session (the report §G36-03 regression shape: tenant route on ifindex 11 vs default on 99, assert egress 11) must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` and pass after, for both `embedded_icmp_return_resolution` and `embedded_icmp_quoted_reply_resolution` (v4 and v6); companion-present resolution must not regress.
