## #15772 — `build_logical_ingress_packet_with_ethernet` Leaves `flow_src_addr` and `flow_dst_addr` Zeroed (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) When `parse_session_flow_from_frame` Returns `None`, Blackholing and Mis-Adjudicating All Flowless Inner Traffic Decapsulated from GRE and WireGuard [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

G37-01 — `build_logical_ingress_packet_with_ethernet` Leaves `flow_src_addr` and `flow_dst_addr` Zeroed (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) When `parse_session_flow_from_frame` Returns `None`, Blackholing and Mis-Adjudicating All Flowless Inner Traffic Decapsulated from GRE and WireGuard

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form:** MATERIAL as narrowed by the lanes — not literally every flowless packet in every shape. Live scope: inner traffic for which `parse_session_flow_from_frame` returns `None` (non-first fragments, ICMP-control shapes, and any non-TCP/UDP/ICMP-query inner protocol such as ESP/GRE/OSPF/VRRP/SCTP per spark-c) decapsulated from GRE/WireGuard, where consumers adjudicate on the zeroed meta addresses. Parseable TCP/UDP inner records are stamped and unaffected (codex-c counter); codex-c decisive shape is valid tunnel-inner non-first fragments and ICMP errors with nonzero wire IPs.

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL, not every flowless packet. Synthetic Ethernet ingress stamps source/destination metadata only when `parse_session_flow_from_frame` succeeds; ICMP-control/fragment no-flow shapes can retain zero source/destination and be routed/adjudicated as unspecified addresses (`afxdp/logical_ingress.rs:135-194`; `afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:1796-1852,2341-2410`; `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:7607-7616,8012-8049`). Counter: parseable TCP/UDP inner records are stamped, and other stages can reject malformed flowless input independently. Check: valid tunnel inner non-first fragments and ICMP errors with nonzero wire IPs, then inspect synthetic frame meta and final routing/zone verdict.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL (narrowed). `logical_ingress.rs:149-164` flow_src/dst zeroed when `parse_session_flow_from_frame` None, stamped into meta 191-194. Flowless inner (OSPF proto89, ICMP, non-first frag) decapsulated GRE/WG gets 0.0.0.0/:: in meta flow addrs. Refutation: consumers may parse addrs from frame not meta for flowless path; ports also zeroed by design. Need consumer that trusts `meta.flow_src_addr` for policy/session (poll flowless_verdict). Verdict: MATERIAL if meta consumers adjudicate on zero addr (spot: flowless path uses meta addrs) — confidence Medium; decisive consumer trace named: grep `flow_src_addr` readers in poll_descriptor.
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: `logical_ingress.rs:136-165` at d316277: `flow_src_addr/flow_dst_addr` zero arrays, populated only `if let Some(flow)`. Consumers: `l3_session_flow_from_meta` returns None on unspecified (inspect.rs:2510-2542), but `l3_enforcement_flow_from_meta` (2586-2614) then builds a *synthetic* flow from `l3_addrs_unfiltered()` — which reads the same zeroed meta addrs — and if both unspecified it falls through and *creates* SessionFlow with 0.0.0.0/:: src/dst. Transit martian drop (`transit_source_class_drop`) / local-delivery misjudgement follow. XDP shim always fills addrs from L3 header (lib.rs:2110-2126 v4, v6 ip6[8..24]) even for fragments — contract confirmed divergent. Refutation: `parse_session_flow_from_frame` returns None mainly for non-first fragments/flowless protocols — for inner *first* fragments with L4 it succeeds; but any non-TCP/UDP/ICMP-query inner protocol (ESP=50, GRE=47, OSPF=89, VRRP=112, SCTP=132) yields no ported flow → None. Also meta could be reconstructed by callers from frame — inspected call sites (poll_descriptor flowless path) consume meta addrs, not re-parse. Fix is local (parse L3 addrs independently of flow success). Decisive: unit test `build_logical_ingress_packet_with_ethernet` with inner ESP packet; assert meta addrs == inner header addrs.

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G37-01"` and keyword search (`build_logical_ingress_packet_with_ethernet`) — no issue covers this claim. Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- `build_logical_ingress_packet_with_ethernet` must stamp `flow_src_addr`/`flow_dst_addr` from the packet's L3 header independently of `parse_session_flow_from_frame` success (matching the XDP-shim contract cited by spark-c), so flowless GRE/WireGuard inner traffic is routed/adjudicated on its real addresses — per report §G37-01 Fix Direction (`logical_ingress.rs:146-165` coupling is the defect).
- Regression criterion: unit tests with flowless inner packets with nonzero wire IPs (report shape: inner ESP/OSPF packet asserting meta addrs == inner header addrs; plus codex-c's non-first-fragment and ICMP-error shapes through to the final routing/zone verdict) must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` (meta addrs 0.0.0.0/::, synthetic 0.0.0.0/:: enforcement flow) and pass after; TCP/UDP inner stamping must not regress.

## #15773 — Both CLIs Silently Ignore `<rule-name>` on `show security nat {source,destination} rule <name>`, and Remote CLI (`cmd/cli/show_nat.go`) Ignores `NotInstalled` / `PortNoTranslation` and Hides Unreferenced DNAT Pools [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

## Claim

G46-04 — Both CLIs Silently Ignore `<rule-name>` on `show security nat {source,destination} rule <name>`, and Remote CLI (`cmd/cli/show_nat.go`) Ignores `NotInstalled` / `PortNoTranslation` and Hides Unreferenced DNAT Pools

Source report: `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-vsrx-parity-every-command-option-feature-002.md` (origin `gemini-4-argon-high`, report base `5a80697d`, comparison `4db87ff6`). Synthesis: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uqc7qG9uJc/synthesis2.md` §5a (verification revision `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674`). Issue bodies below use the *narrowed live form* from the three blind ledgers (codex-c / smr-c / spark-c) per synthesis §7, not the source report's broader wording where a lane refuted a limb.

**Narrowed live form:** Unanimously MATERIAL for the core limb — both CLIs silently ignore an explicit `<rule-name>` selector on `show security nat {source,destination} rule <name>` and print all rules. The remote `NotInstalled`/`PortNoTranslation` rendering limb is supported by codex-c (and the report) but smr-c explicitly marks the remote subclaims *not verified*; the unreferenced-DNAT-pool limb may be an intentional "installed pools" view (codex-c counter) — acceptance below requires verifying those two limbs before treating them as defects, and does not claim dataplane NAT bypass (output is a superset; harm is operator/automation parity).

## Evidence

Three-way verdicts at `d316277cb4eb446c3968f3f2cc73261a55b64674` (codex-c | smr-c | spark-c | final), synthesis2 §3/§5a: **M | M | M | MATERIAL**.

- **codex-c**: MATERIAL bounded CLI parity. Both NAT rule views parse `<rule-name>` yet do not apply a name predicate; remote view ignores NotInstalled/PortNoTranslation in rendered output (`cmd/cli/show_nat.go:48-101`; `pkg/cli/cli_show_nat.go:79-85`). Counter: exposing all matching rules is not dataplane NAT bypass; omitted unreferenced DNAT pools may be an intentional "installed pools" view rather than hidden configured resources. Check: two named rules, one disarmed and one `port no-translation`, compare exact local/remote selections and runtime state.
- **smr-c**: MATERIAL (local rule-name, narrowed). `cli_show_nat.go:79` case "rule": if `args[1]=="detail"` → detail else `showNATSourceRuleAll` — rule NAME (`args[1]=name`) silently ignored, prints all. Verified pattern. Remote NotInstalled/pool subclaims not verified. Verdict: MATERIAL (silent ignore of selector, operator-facing).
- **spark-c**: MATERIAL (silent-ignore of an explicit selector argument is the exact anti-pattern this codebase elsewhere rejects — cf. parsePolicyShowQuery default-error). Defect: `cli_show_nat.go:79-85 + :729-735` read verbatim: `case "rule": if args[1]=="detail" …; return showNATSourceRuleAll` — a rule *name* argument falls to All. Remote `show_nat.go:48-60`: `args[1]=="rule"` → `showNATRuleStats("")` (empty name) regardless of args[2] unless detail. Junos filters by name; static rule *does* implement it (cited :1170) — internal precedent. Refutation: output is a superset (all rules) — operator gets more, not less; harm is parity/automation parsing. Fail-open display, not silent drop of data. Other limbs NEEDS_VALIDATION (in spark-c's per-limb split; final remains MATERIAL on the selector limb).

Duplicate check: `gh issue list --state all --search "G46-04"` and keyword search (`show security nat rule`) — no issue covers this selector defect (hits are unrelated address-book/NAT64/authz issues). Nothing skipped as duplicate.

## Acceptance

- `show security nat source rule <name>` and `show security nat destination rule <name>` must filter to the named rule (or fail loudly on an unknown name) on **both** the local CLI (`pkg/cli/cli_show_nat.go`) and the remote CLI (`cmd/cli/show_nat.go`), following the existing static-rule name-filter precedent — no silent fall-through to "all rules".
- Verify, then fix if confirmed: remote rendering of `NotInstalled` / `PortNoTranslation` state and visibility of unreferenced DNAT pools (codex-c check: two named rules, one disarmed and one `port no-translation`, compare exact local/remote selections and runtime state). If the pool view is intentionally installed-only, document that instead of changing it.
- Regression criterion: CLI tests invoking both CLIs with a named rule among ≥2 rules (including the disarmed / `port no-translation` fixtures) must fail on pre-fix code at `d316277c` (all rules printed regardless of name) and pass after; `rule all` / bare `rule` listings must not regress.

- **spark-c**: MATERIAL. Defect: `tree.go:318` `"fence-status": {Desc: "Show peer fencing…"}` present; grep found *no* fence handler in cli/grpc/cmd (only unrelated "fences"). Local `showChassisCluster` (cli_show_cluster.go:158-210 read): switch on args[0] with *no default* → falls to `showChassisClusterStatus()` for `fence-status` and any typo — silently renders status, exit 0. Remote `clusterSubsystemView` (show.go:478-513) *does* error on unknown subsystem — so typo limb is local-only; bare-subsystem default-view divergence as claimed. V40-02: per-interface disable merge, brace-elided disable drop, sibling blocks, chained-after-disable. G50-01 adds packed top-level leaves (transmit-interval/hold-multiplier) + duplicate interface fail-open. Verdict: DUP-candidate V40-02; transmit-interval/hold-multiplier packed-leaf residual NEEDS if not in V40-02 acceptance.

## #15927 — vrrp: preempt-hold arm conditional note preserves stale 1s hold on in-window revert [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## What happens
On current master (post-#15922, 85058d1abb), `armPreemptHold`'s
conditional note (`pkg/vrrp/instance_preempt.go:329`) skips the
baseline note when `newHoldSec != snapSec`. In the accumulated
in-window-revert interleaving — commit 60→1 pending, timer fires,
snapshot is 1s, revert 1→60 lands before the arm — the pending
record nets 60→60 and the config consumer PRESERVES the 1s hold:
takeover ~59s early against a live lower-priority master.

Reproduced run-verified at dbdf3d0118, 7d08d595de, and the merged
head 85058d1abb (instance_preempt.go byte-identical). Found by GLM
round-3 review running parallel to the merge gate; Codex/Opus/GLM4
passes at the same head did not cover this interleaving.

Minor (same review): the consumer's trailing `armAdvertTimer` note
can erase a priority-only commit landing during the consumer's
`sendAdvert` (stale wire priority ≤ one interval; fails at head,
passes with the hunk reverted).

## Evidence
`/var/worktrees/retro-review/15922r3-glm.md` — deterministic probes
fail at all three heads above.

## Fix direction
One line: note `oldHoldSec := snapSec` unconditionally when valid.
Add regression for the in-window-revert interleaving. Merged PR
#15922 closed the coalescing defect; this residual stays open here
until the fix merges. (Discovered by campaign retro review.)

## #15929 — vrrp: inherited coalescing gaps - peer cadence on interval growth, unbaselined priority sends, hold-expiry select race [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## What happens
Inherited gaps in the #15920/#15922 coalescing machinery, surfaced by
Codex review of PR #15928 (ledger 15928-codex.md); NOT introduced by
that PR. GLM bounds both as non-blocking (15928-glm.md):

1. Interval growth applied via a cfg-derived arm can leave a peer
   expecting the old (shorter) advert cadence: a BACKUP that learned
   100ms from an actual packet may expire ~0.3s before the next 60s
   advert if its local config grows while the learned timer stays
   armed (dual-MASTER window).
2. Some priority-bearing send paths (promotion
   instance_transition.go:176, VIP announce
   instance_vipupdate.go:320, resign 0-burst) do not baseline the
   pending priority record; consequence bounded to redundant
   correction adverts, never suppression.
3. Scheduling gap (Codex, [INFERENCE]): if the run loop is blocked
   until both preemptHoldTimer.C and configUpdatedCh are ready,
   select can fire the hold expiry first; instance.go:876-899 does
   not recheck a changed PreemptHoldTime before promoting.

## Disposition
Follow-up hardening; the #15927 fix merges independently. Reproduce
gap 1 with a two-instance harness before designing the fix.
(Discovered by campaign retro review.)

## #15937 — harden: empty/mismatched policy snapshot must fail loudly at builder, send site, and helper (never silent default-deny) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

## What happened
Commit 670274c712 (#15707) dropped `Policies: policies` from the
full snapshot builder literal. Every full Compile then published
`policies == []` while `summary.policy_count == 2`. The helper
installed the empty set and default-denied ALL transit
(`policy_denied zones=lan->wan`, session creates +0). Nothing
logged, nothing refused, no metric moved - the outage was found
by live traffic probes, not by the system. Fixed by PR #15921;
the co-located leg is verified live, but the CLASS is unguarded.

## Requirement (user-directed)
Any snapshot whose policy payload contradicts its declared
counts - or any builder path that drops a snapshot field - must
fail loudly and immediately:
1. Builder invariant: len(Policies)==PolicyCount and non-empty
   when the compiled config has policy rules; violation = compile
   error, prior snapshot retained.
2. Send-site gate at the single apply_snapshot boundary: refuse
   count/payload mismatch as known-unsent (no generation burn).
3. Helper (Rust): refuse an empty policy install when the
   snapshot declares rules or a prior non-empty set exists; keep
   prior policies; ERROR log + dedicated mismatch counter.
4. Observability: structured ERROR at every refusal; mismatch
   counter on the existing stats surface; policy count visible in
   daemon status/health.
5. Field-coverage census test: representative config through the
   full builder must populate every ConfigSnapshot field, so the
   NEXT dropped literal field fails in CI, not on the wire.

## Acceptance
Regression fails at each layer independently with the
`Policies: policies` line removed; census test green on master;
no protocol bump unless separately approved; no packet-path
allocation added. (Campaign hardening.)

## #15939 — userspace: recursive m.mu deadlock in syncSnapshotLocked -> rgPrimaryNow on link revalidation (full-suite hang) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

process_status.go:507/540) and calls `prepareSnapshotForApply`
(process_status.go:152). When link revalidation moves or drops an
interface row, `rebuildDerivedSectionsAfterRevalidate`
(apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:134-166) calls

(manager.go:879-887) - recursive lock, deadlock, no cluster
needed. This is the recurring pkg/dataplane/userspace full-suite
timeout repeatedly observed during this campaign (the
TestCompileUsesPostCompileVLAN11080 hang shares this stack).

fixture + prior Opus full-suite stack (15938r-opus.md,
15938r3-codex.md). Pre-existing on master; NOT introduced by
PR #15938.

## Fix direction
Make rgPrimaryNow lock-free under held m.mu (split locked/unlocked
variants like rgProviderWiredForLocked in PR #15924), audit other
m.mu-held callers of prepareSnapshotForApply for the same shape,
add a regression driving syncSnapshotLocked with a moved interface
row. (Campaign retro.)

  4.02ms/20.4ms at 20.7KB/202KB/1.5MB JSON; publish computes it
  ~3x (manager_overlay.go:276,313 + apply stamp). Measured waste
  15.6ms @202KB, 112ms @1.5MB PER PUBLISH under m.mu (scratch A/B
  dedup is semantics-identical: hash(next)==hash(publishSnap)).
  PerfExpHashFlow + PerfExpGoControl, /var/worktrees/retro-review/
  perf-exp-{hashflow,go}.md.

  compile (205-715us vs 10.5-29.6ms total compile, measured with
  instrumented counters, 3 config shapes).
- FlowCache hit = 106ns/op release (report's 442ns was debug
  profile, ~4x overstated); descriptor clone on hits REFUTED
  (hit binds &descriptor, 0 clones).

## #15958 — userspace: split-RG return leg counted as forward-candidate on LAN-owner fabric binding but never transmitted on LAN egress (no counter, no ring entry) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

## SmokeFinal3 (round 3) — split-RG counter evidence on 9e94cf62ab: NO #15941 counter moves; the sink is now named on the RETURN leg (fw1 fabric→LAN egress), upstream of every #15941 site

Deployed current origin/master `9e94cf62ab51808174a5aca6e5f9de38d6585db9` from clean `/var/worktrees/smoke/final3-wt` via `make cluster-deploy` (DEPLOY_RC=0, log `/var/worktrees/smoke/final3-deploy.log`). Both nodes `working-20841-g9e94cf62ab`, xpfd sha256 `2504c6452ccecfdd7bf2c0da701171637cc2137faf7cc4e4ed102742ac7af59b` == local manifest on BOTH nodes, helper `8301170eeb87ca1e75a60594dbc745e8f45d714c3cea6d459fcdc44365ced590` both, helper snapshot `Last snapshot policies: 2` on both nodes, **0 panics** both nodes.

EXACT gate `test/incus/test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` re-run (log `/var/worktrees/smoke/final3-v6na.log`, evidence `final3-wt/test/incus/logs/v6na-12495-xpf-v6na-12495.aUzkqm/`):

```
V6NA_RC=3
INSTRUMENT: LIVE-NA
GW-ENTRY: NA-ATTRIBUTED (fe80::bf72:16:2)
TRANSIT: BLACKHOLED (0/5 to the WAN-side v6 target, min 3)
VIP-ENTRY: ATTRIBUTED-NA (2001:559:8585:ef00::1)
V6NA-VERDICT: FAIL neighbor recovery is NA-attributed but v6 transit is blackholed
FAILBACK: RG2 did not return to node0 within 300s — the shared cluster is left failed over
```

Named gate file:line: `test/incus/test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` (verdict logic `test/incus/v6-na-recovery-lib-12495.sh:241,291`).

### Split-state counter capture (RG2@node1 / RG1@node0), probes LAN→WAN -c5/-c3 both families, 0% replies

fw0 (WAN owner) AND fw1 (LAN owner) aggregate + per-binding deltas of the NEW #15941 counters (helper `/run/xpf/userspace-dp.json` `status.bindings[]`, script `/tmp/final3-{delta,perbind,solo}.py`, logs `/var/worktrees/smoke/final3-{clean,perbind,solo}-delta.log`):

- `transit_output_filter_drops` Δ0, `transit_source_martian_drops` Δ0, `transit_ipsec_fence_drops` Δ0, `transit_l2_group_drops` Δ0, `forward_build_failures` Δ0, `no_egress_binding_drops` Δ0 — **on both nodes, every binding**. Exception ring: no new entry for the probes on either node (fw0 ring unchanged — only the standing 15s `policy_denied` wan→wan cadence; fw1 ring shows only background `discard_route` 10.0.61.102→10.255.192.41).

So **none of the #15941-named sinks fires**. The blackhole is NOT output-filter, NOT source-martian, NOT IPsec fence, NOT forward-build, NOT no-egress-binding.

### Where the packets actually go (forward leg healthy, return leg dies at fw1 LAN egress)

1. Forward leg WORKS end-to-end: fw0 WAN tcpdump (`ge-0-0-2`, `/var/worktrees/smoke/final3-wan2-cap.log`) shows `172.16.80.8 > 172.16.80.200 ICMP echo request` AND `172.16.80.200 > 172.16.80.8 ICMP echo reply` on the wire (both families); destination capture confirms replies. fw0 session table counts the reply leg (`Out: 172.16.80.200/0 --> 172.16.80.8/0 Pkts: 5`).
2. Return leg reaches fw1's fabric bindings: fw1 `ge-7-0-0` (ifindex 4) `tx_packets` Δ+3/+5 per probe batch (fabric TX toward LAN owner), fw0 fabric `rx/forward_candidate/snat` Δ equal.
3. **Return leg never leaves fw1's LAN interface**: fw1 `ge-7-0-1` (ifindex 5) bindings keep `tx_packets = 0` cumulatively (all 6 queues) while `forward_candidate` rises; fw1 LAN tcpdump (`ge-7-0-1`) during probes shows NO `172.16.80.8 > 10.0.61.102` reply frames — only unrelated host traffic. LAN host receives 0/5.

**Named sink: the fw1 (split LAN-owner) fabric-ingress → LAN-egress forwarding step — a forward-candidate on fw1's fabric binding whose egress (LAN ifindex 5) TX never happens, with no counted drop and no exception-ring entry.** This is upstream of / disjoint from every site #15941 instrumented (those all sit on the ForwardCandidate/WAN-egress path). Candidate mechanisms for the fix lane: flow-cache-hit inline path resolving the fabric target via `BindingLookup::fabric_target_index(target_ifindex, hash)` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/forwarding.rs:2028`) / cached-descriptor `target_binding_index` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:739`) landing on a binding that never transmits, or the CoS no-owner-binding drop (`cos_no_owner_binding_drops_total`, status-only, not per-binding) — both currently uncounted at the point of loss. The fix issue should add a named counter + ring entry at that fabric→LAN egress resolution and fix the resolution itself.

Failback leg + co-located spot (iperf -P12) and restoration to RG0/1/2 node0 reported in the follow-up comment / coordinator summary.

## #15979 — config: scoped display inheritance renders leak context-gated secrets (H-6, regression from #15973) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Summary

Scoped `display inheritance` redacted renders leak context-gated secrets to any authenticated PermView caller. `FormatPathInheritanceRedactedForNode` passes a `nil` ancestor prefix to `redactMatches15942`, so every context-gated predicate in `secretIndices` / `urlLeafIndices` sees a truncated flattened path and never fires. Distinctive-name secrets (`pre-shared-key`, `authentication-key`, …) still mask; the leak is exactly the ancestor-gated set: SNMP v1/v2c communities, archive-site passwords, OSPF MD5 keys, AAA/API-key `secret`s, and credential-bearing URLs.

Regression introduced by #15942, merged as PR #15973 (merge commit `0d96f179f095cde5da8e6fade1c0c7c1e0bfa905`). Confirmed unanimously MATERIAL High by three independent research passes (Codex / Opus / Wonder) at `origin/master` `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9`. Origin of the hypothesis: muse-spark hostile security review (`muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001.md`, claim H-6 / R15942-01).

## Mechanism (at `c1b86e87`)

- `pkg/config/ast_redact.go:242-262` — `FormatPathInheritanceRedactedForNode` expands the **unredacted** tree (`expandForInheritance`), navigates the caller's path, clones the matches, explicitly discards the consumed width (`_ = width`, :261) and calls `redactMatches15942(clones, nil)` (:262). The in-code comment at :258-260 ("node's own flattened key path as context") is the defect's rationale and is backwards: `redactMatches15942`'s `idx >= len(base)` rule (:352-367) means identity tokens beyond the consumed width already live in `n.Keys`, not in `base`, so passing the real prefix cannot unmask the navigation path.
- Working sibling: `redactedScopedMatches` at `pkg/config/ast_redact.go:317-318` computes `parentPrefix := path[:len(path)-width]` and passes it as base; the compare path does the same at :117-124. The inheritance arm is the only scoped renderer passing `nil`.

### Gates defeated by the nil base

- **SNMP community** — `secretIndices` `case "community"` (`ast_redact.go:926-933`) requires `i >= 1 && fp[i-1] == "snmp"`. For scope `["snmp","community"]`, `navigatePathWidth` returns all terminal `community` siblings with `width=1`; the clone's keys begin `community,<actual string>`, so `community` sits at `i=0` and the gate can never fire. The community string prints clear.
- **`password`** — ancestor allowlist `api-auth|dynamic-dns|archive-sites|user-identification|access|active-directory-access|identity-management|local-authentication-table` over `fp[:i]` (`ast_redact.go:888-889`), e.g. `system archival configuration archive-sites <url> password <secret>` scoped at/above the stanza.
- **OSPF MD5 `key`** — `keyHasOSPFMD5Ancestor` requires a consecutive `("authentication","md5")` pair strictly before `key` (`ast_redact.go:921,943-949`).
- **`secret`** under AAA / API-key ancestry (`isAAASecretPath` / `isAPIAuthNamedKeySecretPath` on `fp[:i]`, :898).
- **Gated URL leaves** (`urlLeafIndices`, :980+) — `server`/`update-server` ← `dynamic-dns`, `target` ← `rpm`, `path`/`hostname` ← `feed-server`, `endpoint` ← `wireguard`: credential-bearing URLs print un-`RedactURL`'d whenever the gating token sits at/above the matched node.

## Reachability

- Store entry points: `ShowActiveInheritanceRedacted` (`pkg/configstore/store_format.go:493-498`), `ShowCandidateInheritanceRedacted` (:553-561), `ShowRollbackInheritanceRedactedPath` (:642-651) — active, candidate, and every rollback slot.
- Remote dispatch: gRPC `ShowConfig` / `ShowRollback` INHERITANCE arms (`pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:429,439,501`), REST (`pkg/api/config.go:398,420,690`), plus local CLI (`cli_show.go:177`, `cli_config.go:617`, `cli_show_system.go:1044`).
- Authorization prices the requested allowed path/format, not a substitute value redactor (`pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_read_14707.go:60-64,81-82`; `pkg/api/authz_config_read_14707.go:31-39,54-59`). Redaction on these surfaces is unconditional for remote callers, including PermAll.
- Actor: any authenticated PermView principal — strictly below config-edit authority. The scope names the *container* (`snmp community`, an interface, an apply-groups node); the leaked token is the community/key/password **value**, which the caller need not know in advance. `apply-groups`-inherited copies are exactly the ones whose ancestors are most likely above the scope, because expansion happens before the nil-base mask.

Yield: SNMP v1/v2c communities (often RW and fleet-shared), archive scp passwords, OSPF MD5 keys, feed/DDNS URL tokens.

## Why the obvious refutations fail

1. *"Fixed after base by #15973"* — false. `git diff 0d96f179..c1b86e87 -- pkg/config/ast_redact.go` is empty; PR #15973's merge commit **is** `0d96f179`, the commit that introduced the renderer. `git log origin/master -- pkg/config/ast_redact.go` tops out at `0d96f179`. The unmerged `cd1dd3421d` on `origin/fix/15942-authz-parity` fixes the *opposite* leak (descendant-scope output context) and still calls `redactMatches15942(clones, nil)` in this arm.
2. *"PermView holders are trusted with config anyway"* — contradicts the subsystem's own contract: the entire `secretIndices` / `RedactedClone` apparatus and a dozen prior issues (#7511, #10948, #14389, #15019, …) exist precisely because these surfaces must not print these values to view-only principals. The unscoped and sibling scoped renders mask them; only this renderer does not.
3. *"Scope must name the secret"* — the scope names the container; the secret is the value token inside the matched node.

Residual narrowing (does not change severity): distinctive-name secrets mask correctly even with a nil base because they need no ancestor. The leak is exactly the context-gated, fleet-shared, off-box-valid set.

## Decisive check / acceptance

A scoped INHERITANCE regression fixture at `["snmp","community"]` plus an OSPF `authentication md5 … key` scope (including an `apply-groups`-inherited community) asserting the value token renders as `SecretDataPlaceholder`, while non-secret text still renders. The vacuous `["snmp","community","public","authorization"]` row must not be used as acceptance (the `public` token is not rendered at that scope either way).

## #15989 — ipsec: gateway-less PSK VPN renders lone `%any` secret — any on-box PSK holder authenticates (High) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15982 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **H-4 / VPN-C2** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-high-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` (H-4 sections) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 3 + `MATRIX.md` H-4 row

## Severity
**High** — finder High → validated High, unanimous, no downgrade. Cross-key consequence moderate-high confidence (static chain closed; charon selection asserted from codebase's own #3952/#14139/#14591 doctrine, not live-measured).

## Mechanism
A VPN whose `gateway` leaf is omitted (`vpn.Gateway == ""`, PSK auth, e.g. `bind-interface st0.0`) evades all three #14591-era defenses, each keyed on a *defined* gateway:
1. Strict responder gate looks up `ipsec.Gateways[vpn.Gateway]` — lookup of `""` misses, gate `continue`s.
2. Gateway-references gate `continue`s on empty gateway ("may legitimately omit the remote endpoint").
3. Render belt `responderOnlyGateway(nil)==false` (nil-safe), so the unscoped-responder skip never fires.
Render then emits a connection with **no `remote_addrs`** (charon `%any` responder default) and the secret-scoping walk (`pskIDSelectorsLocal`): remote side splits `remoteAddr==""` into nothing, local-owner arm with `gw==nil` falls to `add("%any")` as the *sole* selector. Result: `id-1 = "%any"` — the PSK matches any peer identity. A holder of *any* PSK configured on the box (e.g. a decommissioned low-trust site's key) can initiate claiming an identity that selects their known secret and IKE_AUTH completes into this tunnel; route-based default TS is `0.0.0.0/0,::/0`, traffic then governed only by the st0 zone policy scoped for the intended peer. Deterministic on both HA nodes (same render). Actor: network reachability to UDP 500/4500 + possession of any on-box PSK; no admin access.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
- *"Defined-responder idiom is gated (#14591)"* — true and irrelevant: gateway-less has no gateway object to carry any identity, so there is nothing to scope by. The renderer itself (`policy.go:1145-1157`) says an unscoped `%any` owner is only safe as one selector *among* peer selectors; lone `%any` is the precise shape #14139/#14591 eliminated.
- *"charon won't select a lone `%any` secret"* — backwards: `%any` as secret id matches any IDi/IDr; that is its documented purpose as local-owner fallback when a concrete peer selector also exists. The defect is absence of the peer selector.
- *"Requires bind-interface/route-based"* — narrows blast radius (policy-based gateway-less VPNs still authenticate the wrong peer into their configured TS), does not kill the auth bypass.
Distinct residual of closed #14591, not DUP/FIXED: #14591's acceptance left variants without a responder-only gateway unverified.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_responder_identity_14591.go:41-49` (lookup `""` misses)
- `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go:980-985` (`continue` on empty gateway)
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:699-730` (`responderOnlyGateway` nil-false :699-701; `resolveRemoteAddr` returns `("",localAddr,nil,true)` :727-730), belt `:420`, lone `add("%any")` in `pskIDSelectorsLocal` `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1165-1211` (add at :1207)

## Decisive check / acceptance
Strict fixture: route-based (st0.0) PSK VPN with no gateway → strict-reject **or** rendered swanctl contains no secret whose sole selector is `%any` (render via existing `pkg/ipsec` harness; no live charon needed). Fix direction: treat `gw==nil && remote==""` as responder-only in both gates + render belt, or refuse to render gateway-less PSK VPNs.

## #15990 — config: `$9$` decode-to-empty (`$9$i`/`$9$!`) erases credentials — BGP neighbor rendered passwordless, IPsec renders `secret = ""` (Medium) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15982 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **K1 (+ VPN-C1 render leg, shared decoder fix)** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w23-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` (K1) + `sec-high-*.md` (VPN C1) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 3

## Severity
**Medium** — unanimous MATERIAL Medium for K1. VPN-C1 charon grade is NV (see notes/dissents); the decoder fix is owed regardless.

## Mechanism
`decodeJunos9` returns `("", nil)` for `$9$i` / `$9$!`: the first char's skip is consumed, zero nibble groups remain, the decode loop never runs, and empty output is not an error. Every presence gate tests the *encoded* form only (`"$9$i" != ""` passes), so compile stores `Secret("")`.
- **BGP arm (K1):** FRR render gates `if n.AuthPassword != ""` *before* the #14977 unrenderable-password belt — an emptied password skips the belt and the neighbor is emitted with **no `password` line**; a peer tolerating no-MD5 establishes unauthenticated BGP.
- **IPsec arm (VPN-C1 render leg, same root):** render tests encoded non-emptiness, stores `decodedPSKs[name]=""` with no decoded-empty check, the #14139 no-secret skip tests encoded form and never fires, and emission renders `secret = ""`. Stock strongSwan 6.0.5 rejects zero-length key data at load (`load_creds.c`/`vici_cred.c`) — so C1's High (empty-key IKE_AUTH) is **NV/rejected for stock 6.0.5**, narrowed to uncredentialed/undetected tunnel load; do not file C1 as High without a shipped-version + isolated charon check.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Presence checks test encoded form only — fails at every layer (strict gate, compile decoder, render belt). Spoofable-neighbor exposure needs a malformed/truncated operator credential + peer allowing no-MD5 — caps K1 at Medium. The charon refutation bounds C1's grade, not the decoder defect: rendering an empty credential is never legitimate.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/config/junos9_15051.go:66-134,158-190` (`decodeJunos9` :98-134; compile decoder :164-189)
- `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:650-656,774-777` (password gate pre-belt, neighbor emitted passwordless)
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:331-385,630-665` (encoded test :355-364, grouped fold, `secret=""` emission :644-651)
- Strict PSK gate tests encoded form: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_psk_14139.go:46-50,65-75`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Strict rejects empty *decoded* output on every credential leaf; `$9$i` BGP neighbor is not rendered passwordless; `$9$i` IPsec render emits no `secret = ""`. A valid `$9$` credential renders byte-identical to today. Fix: `decodeJunos9` errors on empty decoded output (or all callers reject `decoded==""`); strict validators decode before emptiness tests.

## Dissents / notes
- C1 severity split only: Codex grades the IPsec arm Medium-narrowed (6.0.5 rejects empty key); Opus/Wonder keep NEEDS_VALIDATION High-if-confirmed pending shipped charon check. K1's Medium is unanimous. The decisive charon check (shipped strongSwan version + isolated load of `secret=""` + IKE_AUTH attempt) remains owed for C1's grade — it does not block the decoder fix.

## #15991 — ipsec: ASCII PSK `0x…` loses provenance and is re-derived as raw hex bytes (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15982 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **IKE-DEEP-2** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w23-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` (IKE-DEEP-2) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 3

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low (finder Medium downgraded, sustained). Second instance of wave-1 VPN-C7 grammar class — count once with that family.

## Mechanism
An `ascii-text` PSK spelled `0x61626364` loses its ASCII provenance at decode; the grouped-secret emitter re-derives raw hex bytes (prefixes `0x` onto the decoded value and emits it unquoted), so charon interprets the credential as the raw bytes `61 62 63 64`'s hex decoding rather than the literal ASCII string the operator authored. Typically the tunnel simply fails against a peer using the literal string; very short weak ASCII PSKs are already weak (bounds severity).

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Operator intent is unambiguous (ascii qualifier); the render silently changes the credential's byte value. No gate re-checks provenance after decode — the emitter's hex re-derivation is the defect.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:472-491` (`hexPSKs[name]` arm prefixes `0x` onto decoded value)
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:638-644` (unquoted hex emission; FILING-DRAFTS cites :638-651 region)

## Decisive check / acceptance

## #15992 — ddns: RFC2136 without TSIG — forgeable rcode drives durable DDNS ownership state (Medium) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15982 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A10-03** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1d-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` (A10-03) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 3

## Severity
**Medium** (Opus/Wonder) / **Low** (Codex narrowed) — file at Medium with dissent recorded. Unanimous MATERIAL on direction.

## Mechanism
RFC2136 DDNS without TSIG is warn-only: the runtime unsigned warning logs once per server per process, and response validation is a no-op when no TSIG is configured, so the unsigned exchange proceeds and its rcode is trusted. A forged NOERROR records **durable ownership** of an unwritten name in DDNS state that survives restart (silent blackhole of the published name); a forged REFUSED/YXDOMAIN suppresses legitimate publishes. Blast radius is the names xpf itself publishes.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Warnings exist on both commit surfaces and the runtime warns once — bounds but does not kill: durable ownership is still recorded on a forgeable rcode after warnings. TSIG-configured path is strong (unsigned/wrong-key/wrong-algo replies rejected, #14603). Spoof needs DNS-ID+port match or true on-path position; spoofed-UPDATE additionally needs the authoritative server configured for source-IP-ACL unsigned updates (server-side operator choice).

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/ddns/backend_rfc2136.go:1385-1470` (`warnUnsignedOnce` :1385-1411; `validateTSIGResponse` no-op without TSIG :1424-1427; unsigned exchange :1454-1470)
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_ddns.go:100-113,369-380` (commit warnings, both surfaces)
- Durable state: `pkg/ddns/state.go`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Alarm/metric visible for as long as any non-loopback unsigned update-server is active (not once-per-process); `require-tsig` knob + no key refuses commit, default posture unchanged (legitimate ACL'd internal BIND must keep working).

## Dissents
- Codex: Low (deliberate ACL-based unsigned UPDATE support; warnings on both surfaces). Opus/Wonder: Medium (durable ownership on forgeable rcode). Direction unanimous.

What survives is defense-in-depth: `CompileConfig` (the strict entry point) itself drops unknown roots with no error, so any future direct caller without the pre-pass inherits a silent drop. Low stands. Fix: strict `compileSections` default arm errors on schema-unknown roots — the compiler should own its belt, not borrow the caller's.

## Full ledger evidence (verbatim excerpts, file:line at `c1b86e871b`)

### Ledger `sec-w1a-opus.md` — `### A3-M2 dangling`

### A3-M2 dangling screen-profile reference fails open — MATERIAL (Low, finder overstated via stale comment)
- The finder's Rust claim is stale at master: since #7168/#7888 an unresolved reference is evaluated against `ScreenProfile::conservative_default()` — nine threshold-free malformed-packet checks — via `missing_profile_verdict` (`screen/mod.rs:55-59,896,1197` at master), with Go threading missing-profile zones + WARN/metrics. "Pass for every packet / complete loss" is killed. Surviving residual: flood/scan/sweep/session-limit thresholds genuinely lost on the tolerant leg until the config is fixed; strict rejects. The Go comment at `compiler_opts.go:2490-2506` still describes the old fail-open and is itself now wrong.
- Verdict: **MATERIAL, Low** (residual = threshold loss + stale-comment cleanup; no dataplane code fix owed).

### Ledger `sec-w1a-wonder.md` — `**A3-M2 dangling screen-profile`

**A3-M2 dangling screen-profile reference — MATERIAL Low (was Med; finder relied on a stale comment).** The Go comment at `compiler_opts.go:2490-2506` at master STILL says the dataplane "fails OPEN (screen/mod.rs returns ScreenVerdict::Pass for a missing profile)" — and it is still stale: Rust `missing_profile_verdict` evaluates unresolved refs against `ScreenProfile::conservative_default()` (nine threshold-free malformed-packet checks), with Go threading `screen_missing_profile_zones` + WARN/metrics. So the flood/scan/session-limit thresholds are genuinely lost on the tolerant leg, but malformed-packet screening is not, and strict rejects. Residual Low is (a) threshold loss until the config is fixed and (b) an actively misleading comment at the exact site a future maintainer will read before touching this gate — design-lens, the comment is part of the defect. Fix owed is mostly the comment; optional alarm-grade surfacing.

**A3-M3 tolerant screen numeric fallback — MATERIAL Low (was Med, narrower).** At master `compiler_security_screen.go` still guards each syn-flood subfield with `if n, ok := parseThresh(...); ok { ... }` (:463-505 region) so a bad `source/destination-threshold`/`timeout`/`limit-session` silently leaves 0/disabled, while `attack-threshold` defaults to 200 (:505-512) and icmp/udp flood, sweep, port-scan take Junos defaults. The finder's headline example (`attack-threshold 1o00` zeroes the profile) is refuted by the default arm. Surviving leg: per-source/per-destination caps silently off on tolerant compile, warning exists. Low stands.

**A3-M4 unknown top-level stanza dropped by compiler — MATERIAL Low (was Med; "silently" mostly killed).** At master the dispatch default arm (`compiler_dispatch.go:106-108`) records `ToleratedUnknownTopLevelStanzaWarning` into `cfg.Warnings` under `lenientUnknownTopLevelStanza`, and store dedups it — the tolerant leg is warned, not silent. Every production strict admission pre-validates via configstore SchemaValidate or the peer-strict pipeline. What survives is defense-in-depth: `CompileConfig` (the strict entry point) itself drops unknown roots with no error, so any future direct caller without the pre-pass inherits a silent drop. Low stands. Fix: strict `compileSections` default arm errors on schema-unknown roots — the compiler should own its belt, not borrow the caller's.

**A3-M5 candidate-edit double lenient compile under store lock — NEEDS_VALIDATION (carried from refuter; I did not run the benchmark).** Mechanism confirmed statically at base and nothing post-base touches `event_plant_class_9984.go`/`store_command.go`'s Stamp path: `StampChangedEventPlantClasses` lenient-compiles before AND after trees unconditionally (no event-options presence short-circuit), under `s.mu`, which also serializes SyncApply/Commit. Magnitude is entirely empirical. Decisive check (refuter's, still owed): benchmark one `set` on a ≥50k-node candidate with no event-options; >~1 s/edit ⇒ Med, <100 ms ⇒ Low/NEG. I record this as NV rather than echoing the refuter, because the design lens cannot settle it — an unconditional O(tree) compile per keystroke under the HA lock is architecturally wrong regardless, but severity is the number. NV.

**A3-M6 LoadSet/SetPath has no node-count budget — MATERIAL Med.** At master `LoadSetAsPlantClass` (`store_command.go:849`) still caps only bytes, then replays unbounded per-line `applyEditLine`→`SetPathQuotedGrouped` (`ast_edit.go:576`, no budget) under `s.mu`; the parser's `maxParseNodes = 200_000` covers only hierarchical text. ~16 MiB of short valid `set` lines yields several× the parser's node budget, and sibling-linear SetPath search makes replay super-linear under the lock, stalling SyncApply/commit. Every later compile/clone/format/sync re-pays. Actor is a config-mode holder — but availability of the HA control plane against an authenticated low-privilege config user is in scope. Med stands. Fix: shared node budget mirroring `maxParseNodes` in SetPath/LoadSet.

Parent cohort: #15985 (`research-sec: dataplane session/NAT/packet path - validated defects batch`)

Validated via three adversarial passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0; coordinator synthesis in MATRIX.md). Base re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Evidence ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` + `MATRIX.md`.

## Validated severity
Medium (finder High refuted/downgraded; unanimous MATERIAL)

## Mechanism
`first_fragment_l4` stamps `flags=0` when declared L4 <14 bytes, so `syn-frag` (SYN-gated) cannot fire and SYN-flood/cookie logic keys on absent flags. Residual arms: operator `no-syn-check` zones and LocalDelivery (exempt from transit SYN gate).

## Evidence (file:line at `c1b86e871b`)
- `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:2556-2582` (flags=0 on <14B)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_admission.rs:78-101` (`strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow_tunnel` gate)
- `userspace-dp/src/screen/stateless.rs` SYN-gated syn-frag (Opus: `screen/stateless.rs:70-74`)

## Refutation considered / bounding
Strongest refutation (sustained, bounds severity): default-config transit new-flow is dropped anyway by strict SYN check — non-closing TCP miss without SYN drops unless `no_syn_check`; finder headline 'complete evasion / session installed' is false in default config (Opus+Wonder+Codex agree). Survives only in no-syn-check / LocalDelivery arms, hence Medium not High.

## Fix direction
Encode flags-UNKNOWN for declared L4<14 and fail closed in screen + admission incl. LocalDelivery; co-design with A1-C9 (see separate issue).

## Decisive regression check
8-byte first-frag + offset-1 second frag in (a) default, (b) `no-syn-check`, (c) LocalDelivery configs — must drop with syn-frag/malformed counter in all three (today: misclassifies in b/c).

## #16009 — userspace-xdp: shim kernel-PASS bypasses worker malformed screens for host-bound traffic (A1-C2) [OPEN]

## Per-claim split from #15985

Parent cohort: #15985 (`research-sec: dataplane session/NAT/packet path - validated defects batch`)
Claim ID: **A1-C2** — split into this single-claim issue per user rule (one issue per claim, full evidence in body). RN-01..06 and SI-2/3/4/5/6 are filed as separate issues.

Validated via three adversarial passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0; coordinator synthesis in MATRIX.md). Base re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Evidence ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` + `MATRIX.md`.

## Validated severity
Medium (flood headline refuted; unanimous MATERIAL)

## Mechanism
Shim PASS arms (kernel-pass/local/WG/session) precede worker stage-10 screens; only LAND is replicated in shim. Host-bound traffic therefore never executes worker stateless malformed screens (teardrop/POD/icmp-fragment/syn-frag/source-route), port-scan/ip-sweep, SYN-cookie challenge semantics, or worker screen counters.

## Evidence (file:line at `c1b86e871b`)
- `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:901-1030` (PASS arms; Codex: :901-918,943-963,979-1030)
- `pkg/nftables/host_inbound_screens.go:22-163` (flood meters replicated in nft)
- Shim LAND gate `lib.rs:730-754` (Opus/Wonder)

## Refutation considered / bounding
Refutation: flood leg is replicated in kernel — `host_inbound_screens.go:22-34,106-163` builds per-zone UDP/ICMP/TCP-SYN meters, ingress-scoped catch-all drop before ct-established, so SYN/UDP/ICMP flood to host is NOT unscreened. Surviving loss is narrower: malformed set + scan/sweep + cookie challenge + counter fidelity. Hence Medium, not High.

## Fix direction
Restore screen parity for host-bound path (shim/kernel equivalent of malformed screens or redirect to worker), with screen counters. Do not duplicate flood meters already in nft.

## Decisive regression check
Overlapping-frag / LSRR / ICMP-frag to firewall-local address with screens on untrust — must drop at shim/kernel with a screen counter (transit twin as control).

## #16011 — nat: sequential PAT allocation is predictable, RFC 6056 failure (A2-C1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Per-claim split from #15985

Parent cohort: #15985 (`research-sec: dataplane session/NAT/packet path - validated defects batch`)
Claim ID: **A2-C1** — split into this single-claim issue per user rule (one issue per claim, full evidence in body). RN-01..06 and SI-2/3/4/5/6 are filed as separate issues.

Validated via three adversarial passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0; coordinator synthesis in MATRIX.md). Base re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Evidence ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` + `MATRIX.md`.

## Validated severity
Medium (unanimous MATERIAL)

## Mechanism
Fresh PAT ports handed out in ascending CAS order, `try_next_port` is `fetch_add % range`, address pick round-robin, interface PAT seeded from shared counter, `claim_in_block` lowest-free-bit. No secret/hash/keyed choice anywhere. Colluding endpoint (attacker's own server sees remote ip/port) gets the only unknown — the port — given away; multiplies A2-C11/A2-C12. C16/DOS re-counts fold here.

## Evidence (file:line at `c1b86e871b`)
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:1902-1939,3215-3239` (also :1908-1932, :3219)
- Interface PAT seeded :6211-6217 (Codex)

## Refutation considered / bounding
Refutation/bounding: TCP still capped by sequence window; exact remote tuple required. Atomic Relaxed is adequate for uniqueness, not entropy (Codex). RFC6056 advice is design guidance, but colluding-UDP leg is real. Medium upheld by all three passes.

## Fix direction
Keyed/randomized port choice (RFC6056 Alg 3/5) with per-boot, ideally cluster-shared, secret (same secret can serve A2-C4 sticky). Bounded fail-closed probe behaviour.

## Decisive regression check
Next-port prediction advantage ≈ random over 10k varied tuples with concurrent worker mix and 5-tuple controls; compare translated UDP reply admissibility.

Parent: #15985

## #16013 — nat: one host exhausts pool — no per-source fairness beyond zone/worker quota, persistent leases retain (A2-C2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Per-claim split from #15985

Parent cohort: #15985 (`research-sec: dataplane session/NAT/packet path - validated defects batch`)
Claim ID: **A2-C2** — split into this single-claim issue per user rule (one issue per claim, full evidence in body). RN-01..06 and SI-2/3/4/5/6 are filed as separate issues.

Validated via three adversarial passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0; coordinator synthesis in MATRIX.md). Base re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Evidence ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` + `MATRIX.md`.

## Validated severity
Medium (downgraded from High; unanimous MATERIAL)

## Mechanism
Pool-global cap only in allocator; per-source session quota is per (ingress zone, pre-NAT src) per worker, so 4096×workers can approach a single-address pool. Persistent-NAT idle leases (300s–24h) survive flow close, count against pool-global `max_tracked_flows`, and are NOT charged to session quota — open/close churn accumulates. DOS-1/3 re-counts fold here.

## Evidence (file:line at `c1b86e871b`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/session_admission.rs:21-45` (also :29-54)
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:2413-2707` (persistent leases :2413-2426, grants :2681-2707)
- `session/mod.rs:268-271` quota shape (Codex)

## Refutation considered / bounding
Refutation (kills High): `new_flow_session_limit_drop` defaults to `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_SOURCE=4096` per (zone,src) when profile sets no positive limit — NOT merely opt-in screen. Residual legs (per-worker multiplication, persistent-lease retention, spoofed sources on SAV-less LANs) stand. Medium.

## Fix direction
Per-source fairness in allocator (charge persistent leases to source budget / global unreplied+lease budget not keyed solely on claimed src where spoofable); see also S2-01 separate issue.

## Decisive regression check
Single-host persistent-churn: after quota-many *closed* flows, new leases from that source refused while a second source still allocates (small-pool poll test).

## #16014 — sessions: same-domain reverse-NAT ambiguity first-wins instead of ambiguous-drop (A2-C6) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Per-claim split from #15985

Parent cohort: #15985 (`research-sec: dataplane session/NAT/packet path - validated defects batch`)
Claim ID: **A2-C6** — split into this single-claim issue per user rule (one issue per claim, full evidence in body). RN-01..06 and SI-2/3/4/5/6 are filed as separate issues.

Validated via three adversarial passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0; coordinator synthesis in MATRIX.md). Base re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Evidence ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` + `MATRIX.md`.

## Validated severity
Medium (downgraded from High; unanimous MATERIAL)

## Mechanism
Both ordinary matchers treat a second candidate as ambiguous ONLY if `prev.key != m.key && prev.key.routing_domain != m.key.routing_domain` (#14374); same-domain second hit `continue`s, first wins — while quote matcher (#14375) and `find_unique_established_forward_nat_match_at` apply any-distinct rule. Asymmetry is indefensible as code matter.

## Evidence (file:line at `c1b86e871b`)
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:1125-1345` (Wonder master rewrite: ambiguity only cross-domain :1336; Codex :1125-1141,1327-1345)
- Quote matcher #14375 distinct (`lookup.rs:1158-1217`)

## Refutation considered / bounding
Refutation/bounding (downgrades High→Medium): reverse key carries client ip:port as dst, so canonical DNAT VIP1/VIP2→one-backend collision needs same client talking to both VIPs; first-wins returns reply to same client with wrong VIP source, its stack drops. Cross-host confidentiality loss does not survive. Non-bijective static duplicates inherently ambiguous. Prior owner named DR4-H2 in source packet (not #14375, which is quote matcher) — reconcile if duplicate found.

## Fix direction
Mirror #14375 in both matchers: distinct key OR NAT decision ⇒ ambiguous ⇒ drop + `NAT_REVERSE_AMBIGUOUS_TOTAL`.

## Decisive regression check
Same client tuple to two VIPs (same-domain, two live candidates) must drop ambiguous + counter, not misdeliver to first winner; cross-domain control unchanged.

## #16016 — cluster: legacy-unkeyed cluster retains full authority indefinitely — forged heartbeat/sync displaces peer, replaces standby config (PSK not preserved), reconciles away sessions (Medium; High in precondition) [OPEN]

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-01 family (A5-01/A5-08/A5-09/A5-10 = W-HA1, 1 work item, 4 claim IDs)** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1b-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4 + `MATRIX.md`

## Severity
**Medium standalone; High inside (legacy-unkeyed or pre-key) + shared control segment.** Unanimous MATERIAL family. Dissents: Codex grades facets individually (A5-01 High-cond, A5-09 High-cond, A5-10 Low/Med availability-only) vs family Medium — same fix, recorded below.

## Mechanism
A cluster persisted from the pre-key era (pre-#6611 DB via lenient/tolerant load) stays **unkeyed indefinitely** — no expiry, no opt-in leaf, warnings only:
- **A5-01:** heartbeat dual-accept is unconditional when no key is configured (`if !keyConfigured { return true }`); sync handshake is a no-op unkeyed; pre-key eviction is inert unkeyed.
- **A5-08:** a third host's TCP sync connection is admitted to the general pool (no peer-IP pin; `isPeerRemote` only rations slots), handshake no-ops, and `installConn` unconditionally closes/installs over the genuine peer.
- **A5-09:** forged config-sync frames are `SyncApply`-promoted (lenient wholesale promote) on the standby. Provenance *is* plumbed end-to-end (`readAuthed` -> `OnConfigReceivedWithProvenance`), but the only unauthenticated-conn mitigation quarantines event-plant classes only — it does not reject the frame, does not protect security policies/zones/`system login`, and **does not preserve the local PSK** (node-local preserve list holds only `strict-session-auth`), so a forged tree can strip cluster auth during first-keying/unkeyed windows.
- **A5-10 (availability arm):** a forged *empty* authoritative bulk sync reconciles away peer-owned standby sessions, so they disappear on takeover.
Actor: any host with L3 reachability to control/fabric IPs, no credential. Entry is a pre-#6611 persisted DB or a pre-key connection during first-keying/rolling upgrade.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Keyed steady state genuinely holds (Noise + key-confirm *before* `installConn`; strict commit/day-0/`check-config` require PSK; unkeyed fabric is GetStatus-only) — that kills the keyed arm, not the lenient/pre-key population this claim is scoped to. The earlier policy-bypass arm of A5-10 is **killed by #8356** (receiver-local policy revalidation on session hits) and is NOT claimed here; the surviving arms are election/availability/config/PSK-preservation. Reference deployments use a dedicated fabric (`examples/deploy/ha-pair.conf`), which weakens default actor realism but does not remove the shared-segment case.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- Strict lenient downgrade: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_cluster_auth.go:28-104` (tolerant downgrade :54-63); lenient gate `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_cluster_zone.go:564-568`
- Heartbeat dual-accept: `pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:1317-1359` (`heartbeatAuthDecision` :1317-1335), source pin not auth :1742-1762
- Sync handshake/install: `pkg/cluster/sync_auth.go:478-564`, `pkg/cluster/sync_admission.go:41-52,80-98,224-252`, `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:983ff,1031-1101`
- Config-sync provenance/quarantine-only: `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_read.go:1388-1581`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:254-268`, `pkg/config/event_plant_class_9984.go:308ff`
- PSK not node-local: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_node_local_7441.go:19-95` (preserve list :95 = only `strict-session-auth`)
- Policy revalidation (killed arm, for scope): `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/policy_revalidation.rs:1-17`

## Decisive check / acceptance
On an unkeyed-after-grace node and on a keyed node over an unauthenticated connection, a third host must not: drive election, displace the genuine sync connection, replace standby config, strip/alter the local PSK, or reconcile away standby sessions. Fix (W-HA1, one work item): reject config/session authority on unauthenticated conns once locally keyed (provenance already plumbed — the rejection check is the missing piece); refuse non-peer-IP install when peer addresses are literals; add `authentication-key` to node-local preserve; grace-bound/alarm the lenient unkeyed posture.

## Dissents
- Codex facet grades: A5-01 High-conditional, A5-08 Medium facet, A5-09 High-conditional, A5-10 Low/Medium availability-only. Opus/Wonder grade the family once at Medium standalone / High in precondition. Same corrective work.

## #16018 — vrrp: unknown-source priority-0/255 adverts are logged then applied — forged takeover/demotion after master learned; no commit gate for AF_PACKET VRRP (Medium / Low fold) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-03 (+ A7-03 folded)** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1b-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4 + `MATRIX.md`

## Severity
**Medium** (A5-03) with **Low** A7-03 gate-gap folded in (one corrective work; count once). Unanimous MATERIAL.

## Mechanism
**A5-03:** xpf already learns the legitimate master source per address family, but unknown-source handling is detection-only: the receive path warns (`unrecognizedMasterAdverts`) and then *still applies* RFC priority/state-machine behaviour — a priority-0 advert from any source arms the near-immediate (~1ms) backup takeover, and a higher-priority advert demotes the current master unconditionally. The recorded-master gate and priority-255 source carve-out protect only recorded master state, not state transitions; equal-priority tie-break trusts the spoofed source IP. This holds even *after* the genuine master is learned and fresh.
**A7-03 (folded):** native VRRP is consumed via AF_PACKET before netfilter input and no commit-time gate covers `vrrp` (the managed-routing mismatch gate covers only FRR ospf/ospf3/rip), so a zone denying `vrrp` never warns that VRRP bypasses it.
Actor: any L2 neighbour on the RETH/VIP data segment (typically far less trusted than the control link) with the configured VRID.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
TTL/hop-limit 255 + ifindex/VRID checks bound the actor to the segment + configured instance (kills routed injection) — Medium not High. Generic VRRPv3-has-no-auth is A5-02/#4288 protocol floor and is NOT claimed; the incremental defect is that xpf *learns* the master source and chooses to log-and-apply. Spoofing the learned source itself remains the protocol floor, not this item.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- Detection-only comment + apply: `pkg/vrrp/instance_rx.go:24-77` (gate :24-46), `handleBackupRx` :151-220 (warn-then-takeover :151-173), `handleMasterRx` :204-220, tie-break :307-334
- AF_PACKET receive: `pkg/vrrp/instance_socket.go:143-155`; TTL255 paths `pkg/vrrp/instance_receive.go:166-173,272-283,458-460`
- Commit-gate gap: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_host_inbound.go:30-46` (ospf/rip only, no vrrp)
- In-tree restatement: `pkg/vrrp/README.md:269-272`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Learn a master, then inject unknown-source priority-0: no takeover, drop counter increments; genuine priority-0 resign from the learned source still takes over in ~1ms. A7-03: commit with a VRRP group + zone denying `vrrp` warns/errors naming the AF_PACKET bypass. Fix: once a master source is learned and fresh, ignore priority-0/255 from other sources (count drops); extend the managed-routing commit gate to vrrp.

## #16020 — fabric: gRPC has no TLS and HMAC tokens are replayable byte-identically within the window — ClearSessions/failover replay + plaintext session tuples (Medium) [OPEN]

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A8-04 ≡ A5-05 (W-FAB, count once)** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1c-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `sec-w1b-*.md` (A5-05) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4

## Severity
**Medium** (combined plaintext+replay, w1c grading). Replay-arm alone graded Low by w1b — dissent recorded. Unanimous MATERIAL, count once (A8-04≡A5-05).

## Mechanism
The fabric gRPC server installs no transport credentials (`RequireTransportSecurity()=false`, insecure dial), so session tuples/NAT/status cross the control segment in plaintext. The HMAC token binds method + args-digest + 30s window with **no nonce/jti/single-use store**, and ±1 adjacent windows are accepted — a byte-identical captured request (e.g. `ClearSessions`, failover) replays successfully within ~60–90s. The fabric header itself documents this as Residual 1. In-tree threat model posits any host on the shared control segment; no peer compromise is assumed. Scope correction vs finder: MonitorInterface carries interface *statistics*, not packet capture — sensitive payload is GetSessions tuples/NAT + status plus the replayable verbs.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Replay duplicates an already-authorized action rather than creating a new capability, and cross-method/cross-args substitution is digest-bound (#10709) — that bounds the replay arm to Low standalone. Combined plaintext disclosure + replay is Medium. mTLS is the deferred #4047 direction; #4047 is not asserted as the fabric owner — do not file against it by assumption.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/grpcapi/fabric_auth.go:25-94` (threat model :27-33, Residual 1 :78-94), token/window :137-261, `RequireTransportSecurity()=false` :780
- Server/dial: `pkg/grpcapi/server.go:1086-1106`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag.go:50-55` (`insecure.NewCredentials()` :51)

## Decisive check / acceptance
Same valid unary request bytes presented twice inside the window: accepted today, must be rejected post-fix (single-use (window,digest) cache for mutating methods, or mTLS). Acceptance also: fabric traffic is TLS on the wire if the mTLS route is taken.

## Dissents
- w1b (A5-05): Low for identical mutating-RPC replay alone (capture + live authorized write + short window preconditions). w1c: Medium for plaintext+replay combined. Filed at Medium per FILING-DRAFTS.

## #16022 — cluster: heartbeat anti-replay latch is process-scoped — restart clears it and 65 captured incarnations churn the 64-entry ring (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-06** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1b-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4 + `MATRIX.md`

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low.

## Mechanism
Heartbeat anti-replay remembers only 64 sender incarnations in a FIFO ring, and the 'peer ever proved epoch-capable' latch/floor is **process-scoped** — a receiver daemon restart clears it (an in-tree header records a durable latch was priced and removed). With ≥65 captured sender incarnations (now per-daemon-incarnation, so 65 peer restarts' worth of captures) replayed after a receiver restart while the peer is down, archived epochless frames are admitted and can delay takeover. Epoch-bearing steady state itself is bounded (floor checked before ring, per-epoch session bound).

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Compound precondition (captured incarnation set + receiver restart + peer dead) and availability-only payoff (delayed takeover while actively replaying) cap this at Low; no generic single-frame replay exists.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_epoch_admit.go:71-92` (process-scoped latch/floor)
- `pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:681-780` (64-incarnation ring)

## Decisive check / acceptance
Restart the receiver, replay a pre-upgrade epochless capture set: rejected once the persisted bit is restored. Fix: persist the epoch-capable bit + floor across daemon restart (alongside `ha-boot-epoch`); the fix must engage the in-tree rationale for removing the durable latch, not ignore it.

## #16024 — cluster: two-node partition has no quorum — dual-primary is the default posture, fencing is opt-in and fail-open (Low) [OPEN]

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-11** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1b-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4 + `MATRIX.md`

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low (default posture, not a code-defect Medium).

## Mechanism
After heartbeat loss (sync-recency suppresses peer-lost for only ~5s, deliberately capped), peer-lost election promotes the eligible local redundancy group with no witness/quorum. The mitigations are opt-in: `peer-fencing disable-rg|disable-rg-confirmed` defaults unset/disabled, and even confirmed mode 'always returns and never blocks the takeover indefinitely' — every failure path proceeds. A genuine partition (or heartbeat-only suppression past the cap) therefore yields dual-primary by default, with no default alarm.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Two-node no-quorum failover is inherent vSRX-parity semantics and an explicit availability tradeoff, and sync-recency suppression + opt-in fencing are real guards — Low posture item, not a bypass. No guarantee an attacker can drop only heartbeats on a dedicated segment.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:172-219` (suppression + promotion)
- `pkg/cluster/fence_confirm_7147.go:12-22` (opt-in, fail-open header)
- `pkg/cluster/election.go:134-150`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Drop UDP heartbeat only (sync alive) in default config: no dual-primary, or an explicit dual-primary-risk alarm fires. Fix: default fence-confirmed when sync fabric is configured, or alarm on fence-unconfirmed takeover by default.

## #16027 — fabric: tokenless grace re-anchors per restart/commit via ControlLinkAuthKeyConfiguredAt — repeated 5-minute tokenless windows (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-14** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1c-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `sec-w1b-*.md` (A5-05) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low. Mechanism restated at master vs original finder description; exposure stands (see dissent note).

## Mechanism
The fabric tokenless grace (read-only set) anchors at `cluster.ControlLinkAuthKeyConfiguredAt()` — the most recent no-key→key transition — falling back to a process-scoped first-observation timestamp, with persist-failure logging but grace still opening. Key-touching commits/restarts during rollout therefore re-open fresh 5-minute tokenless windows on a keyed node whose peer is not yet armed, instead of the grace being a one-time rollout event. Grace is read-only and closed early once the peer arms via heartbeat/token.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Read-only scope, early-close on arming, and fabric reachability precondition bound this to Low. The original finder's '/var/lib/xpf unwritable persist file' mechanism is stale at master (no persist file; anchor moved to `ControlLinkAuthKeyConfiguredAt`) — w1b-Opus restated the mechanism and the exposure stands; w1c-Wonder notes restart does not reopen where the anchor persisted (#15262). Filed on the restated mechanism per FILING-DRAFTS.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/grpcapi/fabric_auth.go:314-475` (grace set/anchor :314-355, remaining :440-475)
- `pkg/cluster/manager.go:918-945,926-929` (`ControlLinkAuthKeyConfiguredAt`)

## Decisive check / acceptance
Keyed <5m with peer down, daemon restart (and separately a key-touching commit): tokenless read-only request rejected after the first grace, or the re-opened grace is alarmed/visible in status.

## #16029 — cluster: key-rotation additional key has no expiry or age alarm — a forgotten rotation leaves the old PSK valid indefinitely (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A5-15** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1b-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4 + `MATRIX.md`

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low (visibility gap).

## Mechanism
Control-key rotation accepts signing + additional keys with no timer: the accepted set holds both keys until the operator manually finalizes, `ControlLinkRotationSafeToFinalize` answers only 'safe yet' with no age/elapsed field, and no alarm fires however long the rotation stays open. A compromised old key (ex-admin, old backup/config capture) therefore remains valid indefinitely if finalization is forgotten.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Manual rotation overlap is documented by design and status reports an open rotation; software cannot infer when a node is ready to abandon the old key. Requires a separate old-key-compromise precondition — visibility only, Low.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/cluster/control_key_rotation.go:20-149` (mechanism :20-29, finalize check :140-149, no age field)
- `pkg/cluster/manager.go:918-945`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Rotation open beyond a threshold (days) produces a visible status alarm naming the open rotation. Fix: record rotation-open-since and alarm on age.

## #16031 — fabric: legacy method-only stream token is counted, never rejected, and fabric streams have no continuous re-auth (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **A8-05** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w1c-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `sec-w1b-*.md` (A5-05) + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low (narrowed).

## Mechanism
Fabric streaming handlers still accept a legacy method-only (not args-bound) token: absence of the args-bound token is counted (`fabricStreamArgsUnboundTotal`) but never rejected, as follow-up #11524's Phase-2 removal (see also open #11524) tracks. The fabric interceptor chain also has no counterpart to the primary server's 5-second continuous stream re-auth, so key *removal*/decommission mid-stream does not end a fabric stream. Current peers always mint args-bound tokens, so the legacy arm serves only pre-#11082 peers in a rolling-upgrade window; payload is counters/statistics, not capture; rotation accepting both keys means only removal (not rotation) is the revocation gap.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Bounded Low: counters-only payload, legacy arm is a metric-observable rolling-upgrade window (#11524), proxied streams die with the origin's primary re-auth.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/grpcapi/fabric_auth.go:277-315` (legacy token design)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:804-833` (counted-not-rejected :818-832)
- No fabric re-auth: `pkg/grpcapi/server.go:1099-1100` vs primary `pkg/grpcapi/authz_stream_reauth_9051.go:67-112`

## Decisive check / acceptance
Remove the PSK entirely (not rotate) while a fabric stream is open: stream ends within one re-auth tick; legacy unbound token rejected once the #11524 sunset lands. Fix: key-epoch recheck in the fabric stream loop + sunset for the unbound arm.

## #16036 — cluster: DHCP lease-chunk `totalLeases` is only `!=0`-checked — `make(cap 0xFFFFFFFF)` runs before the count check (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **CW-1** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w23-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4

## Severity
**Low** — unanimous MATERIAL Low. Medium iff the unrun NV-1 check proves fatal under shipped GOMEMLIMIT — grade hinge recorded, fix owed regardless.

## Mechanism
`decodeDHCPLeaseChunkHeader` bounds `total` to [1,1<<20] but checks `totalLeases` only for `!= 0`; at assembly completion `make([]SyncLease, 0, totalLeases)` executes **before** the `len(complete) != totalLeases` refusal. One chunk header with `total=1, totalLeases=0xFFFFFFFF` requests ~4.29e9-record capacity (~721GiB virtual under the sibling analysis). Assemblies also survive disconnect. Actor class: keyed-mode genuine-peer fault; in the unkeyed precondition this is dominated by the A5-01 family, not a separate High.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
Go makeslice under overcommit may survive unbacked and touch one element before rejection (sibling `sync_persistent_nat_lease_8121.go` analysis) — the crash/Medium arm is exactly the unrun NV-1 (shipped GOMEMLIMIT/overcommit behaviour) and may not be asserted. The unbounded request + retention leg stands regardless.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/cluster/sync_dhcp_chunk_15160.go:112` (`totalLeases` only `!=0`), make-before-check :181-214 (make :204, count check :214)

## Decisive check / acceptance
One-chunk fixture (`total=1,totalLeases=0xFFFFFFFF`) under shipped GOMEMLIMIT/overcommit settles Medium-vs-Low; the fix is owed either way: bound `totalLeases` to [1,1<<20] like `total` and refuse `received > totalLeases` before allocating.

## Dissents / hinge
- NV-1 (fatal under shipped GOMEMLIMIT?) unresolved by all three passes — do not grade above Low until the one-chunk fixture runs.

## #16039 — cluster: bulk-sync receive maps insert before the install verdict with no per-window cap (Low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

Insert-before-verdict is the same shape as state mutation preceding the verdict that authorises it.

Authenticated/keyed peer + entry-by-entry wire cost + disconnect clearing the main maps bound this to Low; it is not an unauthenticated remote DoS as filed. Unkeyed rate question is owned by the A5-01 family.
