## #16041 — cluster: any well-framed frame refreshes peer liveness before semantic accept; no per-type payload caps (Low, narrowed) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Provenance
- Parent cohort: #15984 (split per user rule: one issue per claim, full evidence)
- Claim: **CW-4** — unanimous MATERIAL per MATRIX.md at `c1b86e871bb535bb302cbfb5f0cdf8e36746aeb9` (three adversarial passes: Codex / Opus / Wonder; file:line re-verified at that SHA)
- Ledgers: `sec-w23-{codex,opus,wonder}.md` + `FILING-DRAFTS.md` Cohort 4

## Severity
**Low (narrowed)** — unanimous MATERIAL Low on the narrowed legs. Killed legs are NOT claimed (see dissents).

## Mechanism
In the sync read loop, `missedHeartbeats=0` + last-peer-receive timestamp update run for **any well-framed frame before `handleMessage` semantic accept**, so junk frames refresh peer liveness and can mask a dead peer's failover trigger. There are also no per-type payload caps on accepted frame types. Surviving legs only: (1) liveness-before-accept, (2) no per-type caps.

## Why the obvious refutations fail / bounds
HMAC + monotonic sequence mean 'junk' is a real (keyed) peer's frames, bounding this to the keyed-peer fault class; fixed-type HMAC cost approximates wire bytes. These bounds cap severity at Low.

## Evidence (at `c1b86e871b`)
- `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_read.go:95-129` (pre-accept liveness refresh), `:1192-1280` (per-type handling without caps)

## Decisive check / acceptance
Well-framed but semantically rejected frames must not refresh liveness; per-type payload beyond cap refused with a counter. Fix: refresh liveness only on semantic accept; add per-type header caps.

## Dissents
- w23-Opus: 2 of 4 finder legs survive (liveness, per-type caps); failover-goroutine coalescing and ack-detail truncation legs were already bounded/killed. Codex adds failover-goroutine/log legs — narrowed filing follows the Opus/Wonder narrowed form; do not re-add killed legs without re-derivation.

## #16046 — research-sec: AV-9 — fsatomic preserve keeps 0644 frr.conf world-readable forever (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim AV-9 — validated severity: Medium
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
fsatomic WithPreserveExisting lifts the existing file mode wholesale, replacing the caller-requested mode. The FRR writer requests 0640 for frr.conf (which carries BGP TCP-MD5 / OSPF / IS-IS keys, #4484) but always passes WithPreserveExisting, so a legacy 0644 frr.conf stays 0644 after every managed apply and routing keys remain world-readable to any local account.

## Refutation considered
Preserving owner/group is legitimate (#4484 must not override operator ownership) — but that justifies preserving owner, not widening mode past the caller perm. The managed section's secrets are xpf-written, and 0640 root:frr keeps frr-daemon group read, so tightening breaks no legitimate reader. The stat→rename race sub-claim was killed (needs write in /etc/frr). Fresh-create tests are test-only-green: they never seed a pre-existing 0644 file.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/fsatomic/fsatomic.go:284-308 (preserve lifts fi.Mode().Perm(), chmodTemp at :342); pkg/frr/manager.go:1456-1508, :1371-1391, :1412-1424 (owner override only on fresh create) @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1b-opus AV-9, sec-w1b-wonder AV-9, sec-w1b-codex AV-9.

## Decisive regression check
Seed a pre-existing 0644 frr.conf with a routing-auth leaf, run the next writer apply → file must be ≤0640 with frr group read kept. Fails pre-fix (stays 0644).

## Fix shape
Never widen beyond caller perm in WithPreserveExisting (mode = existing &^ ^perm / min), or drop preserve for secret-bearing frr.conf; add the 0644-seeded row to frrconf_mode_4484_test.go (today only 0600 is seeded).

## #16048 — research-sec: A6-01 — userspace-dp state file has no asserted mode; full snapshot world-readable (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A6-01 — validated severity: Medium
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Both state-writer transports create the temp file with no .mode() (default 0666 & umask 022 = 0644) then atomically rename it, with no chmod anywhere. The persisted pretty JSON clones the entire snapshot including the opaque compiled config Value (topology/policy/NAT/routes/tunnel endpoints, secrets redacted via Secret types), refreshed ~1/s on every status verb, inside a directory that can pre-exist at 0755 — any local account can read the full posture continuously.

## Refutation considered
Secret-content kill caps at Medium: WG privkeys/PSKs/SYN-cookie keys are skip_serializing and IKE/cluster/DDNS/API secrets redact via Secret MarshalJSON — no key material leaks, only posture. Wonder/Opus differ on how often the dir is 0755 (clean boot creates 0750; upgrade/preinst path can leave 0755) — filing is scoped to the unasserted file mode, which is wrong regardless of dir mode.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
userspace-dp/src/state_writer.rs:413-519; userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/persistence.rs:30-63; pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:303-345; pkg/daemon/daemon_singleton_15085.go:14-44 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1b-opus/wonder/codex A6-01.

## Decisive regression check
Call write_state in a 0755 dir under umask 022 → dest file and temps must be 0600. Fails pre-fix (0644).

## Fix shape
Create state temps with mode 0600 (OpenOptionsExt::mode) in both transports, and/or drop the opaque config from the persisted payload (Rust has no consumer of it).

## #16050 — research-sec: F2 — /run/xpf 0755 + flock files 0644 let a local user block upgrades (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim F2 — validated severity: Medium
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
/run/xpf is created 0755 and upgrade/epoch/kernel-roll flock files are created 0644. On Linux an exclusive flock can be taken on a readable O_RDONLY fd, so any local unprivileged user can open and exclusively flock the upgrade lock (and kernel-roll/heartbeat-epoch locks) and block all upgrades indefinitely — no write permission needed.

## Refutation considered
Actor needs a local shell/service account and the shipped image's actual umask/modes must be confirmed (a restrictive umask could narrow this) — hence the built-image decisive check rather than assuming. Users cannot create files under the root dir, but they do not need to: read+flock suffices. Go-only chmod is insufficient because shell package scripts can be first creator.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/upgrade/lock/lock.go:155-175; pkg/daemon/daemon_singleton_15085.go:14-44; pkg/cluster/heartbeat_epoch_lock.go:147; pkg/upgrade/kernel_selfrecover.go:207-215 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w23-opus/wonder/codex F2.

## Decisive regression check
On the built image: stat /run/xpf and the lock files + record xpfd umask; as an unprivileged user, attempt exclusive flock on the upgrade lock → must fail post-fix (0750 dir / 0600 locks). Pre-fix it succeeds.

## Fix shape
0750 (or 0700) /run/xpf and 0600 lock files, asserted on use as well as at creation (shell first-creators included).

## #16052 — research-sec: F1 — reinject Go client never verifies the helper peer; squatter gets decrypted payloads and lying success (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim F1 — validated severity: Medium
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The Go reinject client dials both helper unix sockets with a bare net.DialTimeout and never checks SO_PEERCRED. A squatter listening on the socket path in a non-default (operator-selected, writable/sticky) socket dir receives ANNOUNCE plus decrypted IPsec-inner payloads, and can return spoofed completions that the client reports as success while every packet is actually dropped (all completion paths are VerdictDrop — blackhole with lying success, no fail-open forwarding).

## Refutation considered
Default root-owned /run/xpf disallows squatting, so the precondition is a non-default socket dir plus a local squatter — that caps at Medium and kills any fail-open claim (bounded: DROP only). The #9171 census verified the Rust helper side, never the Go client's peer — census counted sockets, not trust direction. #15950's reinject_9506.rs change is server-side and does not fix this.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/nfqueue/reinject_socket.go:144-202 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w23-opus/wonder/codex F1.

## Decisive regression check
Peercred-on-connect test with a trusted-dir /tmp-style alternative socket dir: squatter must see zero bytes including ANNOUNCE, and the client must refuse the connection. Pre-fix the squatter receives payloads.

## Fix shape
Verify peer credentials (uid 0 / daemon uid) via SO_PEERCRED on both dials immediately after connect, before ANNOUNCE.

Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. ## Claim A6-03 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
findBinary's candidate list starts with ./xpf-userspace-dp (then a target/release path, argv0-dir, PATH) and admission checks only stat + exec-bit/faccessat — no owner or writability check. A root xpfd hand-run without a binary leaf from a low-privilege-writable CWD executes a planted ./xpf-userspace-dp as root, and then trusts its uid-0 peercred.

## Refutation considered
Shipped service has no WorkingDirectory= and an absolute daemon executable (systemd CWD=/, root-owned), and shipped configs pin an absolute binary — so the packaged path is safe. The surviving arm is the hand-run/lab workflow from a writable CWD; that precondition caps at Low. #12196 only skips non-executable/dir candidates and a test pins CWD preference.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go:461-629 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1b-opus/wonder/codex A6-03.

## Decisive regression check
Plant an executable user-owned ./xpf-userspace-dp in a writable CWD and run findBinary with default config → candidate must be refused/skipped with a loud log post-fix. Pre-fix it wins over PATH.

## Fix shape
Drop CWD-relative candidates outside an explicit dev flag, or require root-owned && !group/world-writable on every resolved candidate including LookPath results.

## #16056 — research-sec: A6-06 — snapshot summary counts unverified; joint interface/zone omission installs and unbinds (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Claim A6-06 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The Rust snapshot apply handler checks protocol version, generation monotonicity, same-generation digest and policy preflight, but never compares summary.interface_count/zone_count/scheduler_count against the built sections. A producer shape with interface_count>0 but interfaces=[] passes all gates, builds forwarding with zero bindings, unbinds all workers, ACKs ok and persists as baseline (same for zones=[] in a global-only config).

## Refutation considered
The fail-open headline was killed: zones dropped while policies reference them fails closed in preflight (UnresolvableZoneReference, default Deny), so no extra authority is created. The surviving arm is availability-only and producer-bug preconditioned — hence Low. Fix hazard: Go sets Summary.ZoneCount before quarantineCollidingZones, so counts must be reconciled post-quarantine before adding a Rust equality check or legitimate snapshots will be refused.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:17-178; pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:303-345 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1b-opus/wonder/codex A6-06.

## Decisive regression check
Over an installed snapshot, apply zone_count=2/zones=[] (global-only policies) and interface_count=2/interfaces=[] → both must be refused with prior bindings intact. Pre-fix the interfaces shape installs and unbinds.

## Fix shape
Extend count-mismatch + empty-over-nonempty refusals to zones/interfaces Rust-side (keep prior forwarding on refusal); reconcile the pre-quarantine ZoneCount Go-side.

## #16058 — research-sec: F3 — Kea lease-sync client bare-dials the pathname with no peer verification (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. ## Claim F3 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The Kea lease-sync client dials the Kea control socket by pathname with no SO_PEERCRED verification of the server. A wrong/squatted server on that path is trusted as Kea; returned leases are sanitized but sanitization cannot authenticate the wrong server, so fabricated lease data can be fed into HA lease sync.

## Refutation considered
Legit peer is _kea and existing sanitization caps impact; the likely actor needs _kea compromise or bad /run/kea perms, HA-only — hence Low. The permissions arm of this claim is DUP A10-06 (still NV) and is not filed here; only the peer-verification arm is in scope.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/dhcpserver/lease_sync.go:375-412 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w23-opus/wonder/codex F3.

## Decisive regression check
Point the client at a squatter socket → it must refuse on peer-cred (expected _kea/daemon uid) and sync zero leases. Pre-fix it consumes squatter data.

## Fix shape
Verify SO_PEERCRED (expected _kea uid) on connect in the lease-sync dial, mirroring the reinject fix shape.

## #16060 — research-sec: K3 — management TLS key permissions asserted only at mint, loaded as-is (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim K3 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The generated management TLS key/dir get 0600/0700 only on the mint path; the load path does LoadX509KeyPair with no stat, fchmod or refusal. A pre-existing loose key (loosened dir/key, restored backup, operator chmod) is silently loaded and served forever, so the mint-time invariant gives false assurance.

## Refutation considered
Generated dir is normally 0700, so a local reader needs a prior root-side loosening and no MITM follows solely from reading — local-actor precondition caps at Low. User-supplied keys must not be chmodded blindly; the fix must distinguish generated vs operator-supplied material.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/api/server.go:2376-2532 (mint) and load path loadManagementTLSCertificateLocked @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w23-opus/wonder/codex K3.

## Decisive regression check
Restart production against a pre-existing loose (0644) generated key → daemon must fchmod to 0600 or loudly refuse. Pre-fix it loads silently.

## Fix shape
Stat + fchmod-or-refuse on load for generated keys (assert-on-use, same invariant family as F2); do not chmod user-supplied private keys indiscriminately.

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. ## Claim A10-07 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Every Kea config render creates the directory 0755 and the file 0644 (fresh files start world-readable; the atomic helper may preserve a stricter existing mode but never tightens a fresh one). The file carries the full static-reservation inventory (MAC ↔ IP ↔ hostname), harvestable by any local account for later spoofing.

## Refutation considered
These are topology identifiers, not passwords, and incremental harm beyond L2 discovery is conditional — hence Low. Inconsistent with the configstore 0700/0600 discipline. Kea's reading UID must be confirmed on the image before choosing the group.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:1480-1494,1755-1767 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A10-07.

## Decisive regression check
Fresh install/render → non-root account must not read the Kea config; stat must show 0640 root:_kea (including tightening a pre-existing 0644 file). Pre-fix a non-root read succeeds.

## Fix shape
Render 0640 root:_kea on every render including pre-existing-file chmod (verify Kea reads as _kea on the image).

## #16064 — research-sec: AV-11 — crash between active rename and rollback-meta publish tombstones all rollback slots (#15986) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15986 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim AV-11 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Config commit writes rollback metadata last. A power cut after the active DB rename+dirsync but before/within saveRollbackFiles leaves the sidecar binding the old active identity; on next Load the generation mismatch refuses every one of the 50 rollback slots (tombstone entry appended, loop continues) — history is gone exactly when the just-committed config misbehaves.

## Refutation considered
This is deliberate #10723 fail-closed anti-spoofing, and every non-crash rewrite rebinds metadata, so only a power-cut in the narrow window strands history (and history survives in memory until restart) — that caps at Low. The PostRename 'failed commit secretly live' leg is already FIXED in-tree (commit converges on PostRenameSyncError) and is not part of this claim.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:1641-1855; pkg/configstore/rollback_metadata.go:132-153 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1b-opus/wonder/codex AV-11.

## Decisive regression check
Fault-injection kill in the active-rename→meta-publish window → slots whose bytes match in-memory history must survive Load. Pre-fix all slots tombstone. (Needs fault injection, not a plain unit run.)

## Fix shape
Write meta with a pending-active-hash dual binding (like confirm's PreviousHash) so one-generation skew degrades to per-slot verification instead of mass tombstone.

## #16066 — research-sec: MGMT-06 — ValidateCryptHash errors interpolate the raw secret into daemon logs/syslog (#15987) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15987 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim MGMT-06 — validated severity: Medium
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
ValidateCryptHash interpolates the raw value with %q in every error arm, including the plaintext branch ('not an encrypted password hash (got %q)'). Redaction exists only on the typed-leaf schema path; the daemon apply boundary logs and returns the error verbatim (slog.Warn + fail), so a plaintext password pasted into the wrong leaf lands in journal/syslog and is forwarded off-box to log-aggregation tenants and support-bundle consumers with lower privilege than the author.

## Refutation considered
 'The value is already in the config store' fails: the config DB is root-only on-box while journal/syslog forwarding widens the audience — exactly why the project forbids secrets in errors (secret_in_error_6625_test.go, schema_walk #8434). Bound: a malformed/plaintext value must survive tolerant ingress (lenient Load/SyncApply downgrades schema errors to warnings) — that path exists and is the point. Fix first in cohort: the payload is the secret itself.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/config/schema_validators_system.go:91-206; pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:805-821; redacted twin pkg/config/schema_walk.go:1686-1710 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex MGMT-06.

## Decisive regression check
Tolerant-apply encrypted-password "hunter2-plaintext" → daemon logs and the returned error contain no trace of the string; valid hashes still apply. Pre-fix the string appears verbatim.

## Fix shape
Strip raw values from ValidateCryptHash messages centrally (name the defect class + expected form only) so every present/future caller is safe.

## #16067 — research-sec: A8-02 — argument-scoped allow/deny-commands regexes never fire remotely (#15987) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15987 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. ## Claim A8-02 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Canonical command strings carry no arguments, and both the gRPC and REST gates evaluate the bare topic — so operator-authored argument-scoped regexes like ^ping 10\.99\., ^show route table secret-vrf or ^show log .* never match anything remotely. The restriction the operator believes is enforced is silently inoperative on the remote surfaces.

## Refutation considered
Not silent at commit time: a commit-time advisory names the unenforceable surface plus a once-per-class runtime warning — that demotes this to Low and makes it advisory-only (commit succeeds). Base #15942 closed selector-addressable forms (route-table:<name>) and anchored-path agreement, but not free-argument text.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_table_topics.go:63-98; pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_gate_7172.go:132-140; pkg/config/login_command_surface_8189.go:86-111 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1c-opus/wonder/codex A8-02.

## Decisive regression check
Class with deny ^show route table secret-vrf connecting remotely → the command must be denied post-fix (or strict-commit must reject the pattern). Pre-fix it is allowed.

## Fix shape
Build the matched command from topic + canonicalised request arguments on both surfaces, or escalate the advisory to a strict-commit error for argument-bearing patterns.

## Claim A8-08 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The REST Basic throttle reserves against a global per-username bucket before verification (5 failures/10min → 5min lockout doubling to 1h; failures during lockout are dropped, so sustaining needs a re-spray after each expiry). Anyone who can reach an off-loopback web-mgmt leg and knows a username can keep that user locked out of REST Basic auth indefinitely.

## Refutation considered
The global bucket is the deliberate anti-spray control (#11492); blast radius is one Basic username on REST only (API-key namespace separate; gRPC/CLI/SSH unaffected) and a restart clears it — a textbook lockout-vs-spray tradeoff taken knowingly, hence Low.

## Decisive regression check
Spray 5 bad passwords for a username, then present the correct password from another source → must succeed post-fix. Pre-fix it is refused by the global bucket.

## Fix shape
Successful verify clears-then-admits the global bucket (keep the bcrypt cost cap).

Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
The REST config-session token is 128-bit random but restConfigSessionID validates format only; the store holder is the bare sessionID string and the principal is recorded only for journal. Any equally-privileged insider who obtains another operator's token can prematurely commit or release that operator's candidate. The gRPC twin binds the holder to kernel connection identity; REST does not.

## Refutation considered
The second principal still needs PermConfig and passes mutation regexes as themselves; journal names the actual committer and commit-time adjudication runs for the committing class — so this is attribution/workflow integrity, not privilege gain. Low.

## Decisive regression check
Mint a session as principal A, present the token as principal B → commit/release must be denied post-fix. Pre-fix it succeeds.

## Fix shape
Bind (principal, token) at mint and verify per use.

flowExportCallback's SESSION_OPEN arm tracks the flow into every family-matching group of both exporter bundles with no instance/zone/interface eligibility test, while CloseFlow runs only inside the ServesFamily && ShouldExportIface sampled branch. TouchFlow has zero callers under pkg/daemon. A flow opened in a non-sampled zone/instance, or sampled-out at close, is therefore never closed in the other instance's tracker and emits a zero-counter phantom SESSION_OPEN/timeout record at the inactive timeout to a collector the operator excluded that zone/instance from.

## Refutation considered
SESSION_OPEN is producer-gated (userspace emits SESSION_CREATE only for log_session_init policies), so the population is session-init-logged policies, not all traffic; the record is a zero-counter 5-tuple only, delivered to another operator-configured collector, not to the traffic actor. That bounds severity to Medium (finder High downgraded) but does not kill it — audited zones are exactly the ones enabling session-init logging.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:815-977; pkg/flowexport/tracker_15655.go:80-149; pkg/flowexport/manager.go:504-510; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:1079-1081 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A9-01.

## Decisive regression check
Two instances/zones (rate 10 on A, pci unsampled, log session-init policy): open+close in pci and sampled-out in A → zero records at either collector after >inactive timeout, sampled closes exported exactly once. Pre-fix phantom records arrive at the excluded collector.

## Fix shape
Apply instance/zone/sampling eligibility on SESSION_OPEN symmetric to CloseFlow (track only where the flow is eligible), or close/expire ineligible opens immediately without emission.

## #16083 — research-sec: A9-06 — synchronous syslog forwarding blocks daemon goroutines on a slow collector (#15988) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15988 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A9-06 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Non-event slog forwarding is synchronous: SyslogSlogHandler.Handle calls c.Send directly for every non-EventReader caller. A blackholed TCP/TLS collector can park arbitrary daemon goroutines (commit/apply, reconcile, API handlers) that log, serialised behind the client mutex.

## Refutation considered
The stall is recurrently bounded, not per-call: after a write timeout the client arms a reconnect cooldown and does not retry, and during cooldown non-UDP sends fail fast. Worst case ≈ one 4s write (or 5s dial+retry) per 1s cooldown window per client, and default UDP does not stall this way. Finder Medium → Low upheld.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/logging/slog_handler.go:226-241; pkg/logging/syslog.go:1024-1184 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A9-06.

## Decisive regression check
Fake slow/blackhole TCP collector latency test: a logging daemon goroutine must return promptly (bounded by the queue, not the collector). Pre-fix it parks for the write/dial timeout.

## Fix shape
Route all slog through the existing bounded per-client writer (SendFromEventReader queue) regardless of caller context.

## #16084 — research-sec: A9-09 — SNMPv3 accepts weak passphrases with no length floor (source-throttle leg rides NV-1) (#15988) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15988 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A9-09 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Three verified absences: SNMPv3User has no Clients field (unlike communities), v3 dispatch discards srcIP, and the strict key gate is presence-only — a 1-character SNMPv3 passphrase compiles. The only throttling is a 100/s/source + 2000/s global token budget keyed on spoofable UDP source, giving an online HMAC oracle with no lockout/per-user backoff (partially offset by the ~1MiB passwordToKey cost per guess).

## Refutation considered
Junos USM users likewise have no per-user clients — source scoping there is host-inbound/firewall-filter, and xpf has an snmp host-inbound token; whether that gates this socket on every backend is A9-NV1, unresolved, and gates severity only (Low today, Medium if NV-1 shows UDP/161 reachable from untrusted zones), not existence. The durable defect is the missing password-length floor; the oracle pays only against operator-chosen weak passwords.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_snmpv3_keys_7530.go:54-85; pkg/snmp/agent.go:1079-1085; pkg/config/types_system.go:973-979 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A9-09.

## Decisive regression check
Strict-compile an SNMPv3 user with a 1-character passphrase → must be rejected by a length floor. Pre-fix it compiles.

## Fix shape
Enforce an SNMPv3 passphrase length floor at strict compile (and consider per-user throttle); severity re-check owed if A9-NV1 resolves reachable-from-untrusted.

## #16085 — research-sec: A9-14 — malformed lines silently shrink small deny feeds below the shrink-guard floor (#15988) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15988 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A9-14 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Malformed feed lines are skipped and the valid subset installs; the shrink guard is inert below its default floors (old <32 or drop <16). A deny feed with <32 entries that loses entries to origin corruption therefore silently stops enforcing those prefixes — fail-open in exactly the direction the guard exists to prevent (e.g. a 10-entry feed losing 3).

## Refutation considered
Thresholds are operator-tunable down to 1 and the degraded state is counted/surfaced, which bounds but does not kill it: by default the failure is silent enforcement loss from mere origin corruption, no compromise needed. Low.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/feeds/feeds.go:1729-1758,2111-2119 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A9-14.

## Decisive regression check
Feed a 10-entry deny feed with 3 malformed lines → last-good must be retained or the shrink refused/alarmed by default. Pre-fix only 7 entries enforce, silently.

## Fix shape
Retain last-good when invalid lines remove previously-enforced prefixes at any size, or alarm the degraded state by default.

## #16086 — research-sec: A10-16 — DDNS withdraw deletes foreign same-content records (Cloudflare/Route53) (#15988) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15988 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A10-16 — validated severity: Low
Unanimous MATERIAL across the three passes (validated severity; downgrades/dissents recorded in the refutation section where applicable).

## Mechanism
Cloudflare DeleteLease deletes every row with Content==owned; Route53 strips the owned value from the live RRset. Value equality is the only ownership proof in both backends, so when xpf withdraws it also deletes a foreign publisher's identical record; the victim's name dies until its engine's forced-refresh republishes.

## Refutation considered
The hostile variant needs zone-API write credentials for the same zone (that actor can delete records directly, so xpf adds no capability); same name+type+value is arguably the same DNS datum and two autonomous publishers are undefined shared ownership (an HA pair is a coordinated single writer). The finder's record-ID fix only half-works because upsert adopts an existing same-content row. The non-hostile flap (redundant appliances, one withdraws) is real — finder Medium → Low upheld.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/ddns/backend_cloudflare.go:340-433; pkg/ddns/backend_route53.go:419-546 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder/codex A10-16.

## Decisive regression check
Two publishers of the same name+IP where xpf adopted an unmanaged record, then xpf withdraws → the foreign record must survive (with a logged value-scoped fallback). Pre-fix it is deleted.

## Fix shape
Cloudflare comment-tag ownership (delete only tagged-or-self-created rows; legacy untagged = value-scoped fallback, logged); document the Route53 value-scoped limitation.

## #16087 — research-sec: A10-17 — DHCP relay aggregate token bucket starves legitimate clients (fairness leg; eviction leg refuted) (#15988) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Parent cohort
Split from #15988 (per-claim split of the deep-review security cohorts; one issue per validated claim). Source: muse-spark-review-hostile-security-complete-001, three adversarial validation passes (Codex GPT-6-Sol, Opus-5.5, Muse-Wonder-1.0) + coordinator synthesis; every claim re-verified at master `c1b86e871b`. Full ledgers: `/var/tmp/deep-review-work/research-work.uOwanxdwXl/sec-*.md`, `MATRIX.md`, `FILING-DRAFTS.md`.

## Claim A10-17 — validated severity: Low
Cohort-listed MATERIAL Low (Opus/Wonder) with Codex NEG dissent on the remediation — see Refutation; MATRIX records 2M/1NEG split. Filed for parent disposition, not as unanimous.

## Mechanism
The relay limiter is one aggregate token bucket per interface, so a sustained flood at ≥rate from a single sender starves legitimate DISCOVERs proportionally for the flood's duration — no per-sender fairness exists.

## Refutation considered
DISSENT RECORDED: Codex graded NEG for the proposed per-client remediation (aggregate bound is a necessary, explicitly-configured CPU/amplification control; chaddr/client-id are attacker-chosen so per-chaddr fairness only stops a naive single-MAC flooder) while Opus/Wonder graded MATERIAL Low on the fairness leg — MATRIX records 2M/1NEG split, cohort #15988 lists it Low. The eviction leg is refuted by all: pending capacity is rate×30s+burst (floor 4096, ceiling 131072) so limiter-admitted packets have slots, and retransmission self-heals. Filed as the cohort lists it, with this dissent explicit for the parent to disposition.

## Evidence @ c1b86e871b
pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:1627-1670; capacity pkg/dhcprelay/pending.go:98-175 @c1b86e871b. Ledgers: sec-w1d-opus/wonder A10-17 (MATERIAL Low), sec-w1d-codex A10-17 (NEG on remediation).

## Decisive regression check
1-MAC flood at the rate cap while a second MAC attempts DORA → second MAC must complete DORA post-fix. Pre-fix it starves for the flood's duration. (Multi-MAC floods need switch controls — document.)

## Fix shape
Bounded per-sender fairness within the aggregate bucket (accepting it only stops naive single-MAC flooders), or document the aggregate-fairness limit explicitly.

## #16109 — ha: established flows permanently blackhole after RG failover despite synced sessions present on new owner [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Validated on cluster (build working-20873-g69c7c69af6, master 69c7c69af6, both nodes)

Loss userspace cluster, P4 iperf3 to 172.16.80.200:5211, manual failover every ~5-7s (evidence: `/var/worktrees/fz-repro/EVIDENCE-TABLE.txt`, `analysis-*.json`, `midzero-*/fw{0,1}.txt`; plus FZDiag single-failover runs `/var/worktrees/fz-diag/diag2-012558`, `diag3-012722`, `diag4-012841`, `diag5-012958`):

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| RG1 IPv4 forward | SUM zero 88/90 intervals after failover #1 (+2s), never recovers in 90s despite 14 completed failovers |
| RG2 IPv4 reverse (`-R`) | SUM zero 88/90, same permanent death |
| RG2 IPv4 forward | 13 SUM-zero / 17 <1Gbps of 150; a 12s zero window (42-54s), then partial recovery |
| RG2 IPv6 forward | 7 SUM-zero, episodic |
| Start-during-failover (RG2) | only 2 SUM-zero; largely survives |

## Single-failover decisive reproduction (FZDiag, RG1 node0->node1)

- Pre-failover: 13-18 Gbps. Failover completes ~1.3s (`Manual failover completed ... transfer committed`).
- iperf: 4 healthy intervals, then **1 partial interval (~1-2.5 Gbps), then permanent 0.00 bits/sec**, TCP cwnd collapsed to 1.41K on all 4 streams, retransmits continuing (sender alive, ACK clock dead).
- New owner helper log: `RG activation detected: [1], workers=6, shared_sessions=65`, `republished 27 USERSPACE_SESSIONS entries for activated RGs [1]` — activation republish DID run.
- New owner daemon log: VIPs added, **6 direct-mode GARP bursts sent** for RG1 (172.16.80.8/172.16.50.8 + IPv6 NA + pool .7) — GARP/NA DID run. GARP hypothesis refuted.
- Kernel tcpdump on the AF_XDP-bound interfaces captures **0 packets** (XDP redirects before AF_PACKET taps): per-node tcpdump cannot split forward vs return; stats-based discrimination is required (see fix shape).

## Session-display evidence (midzero, taken during zero window)

- On the RG1-non-owner node, live iperf sessions render `HA State: Backup, Timeout: 1800` with the **real SNAT port** preserved (`Out: ... --> 172.16.80.8/57566` etc.).
- On the RG1-owner node the same session IDs render `HA State: Active, Timeout: 20`, some with `Out: ... --> 172.16.80.8/0` (port 0) and tiny packet counts, while one older session (ID 16) carries the bulk counters.
- `Pkts: 0` on the new owner's synced rows while sessions exist — consistent with the tasking brief (SNAT packets 193-194 on the standby vs 85.8M/117M on the owner in midzero snapshots).

[INFERENCE] Labels below are diagnosis, not yet code-proven; see "What is NOT yet known".

## Diagnosis

Candidates from the brief, evaluated against code at 69c7c69af6 (paths in `pkg/`, `userspace-dp/`):

1. **"Synced session lacks functional NAT binding" — NOT supported as the primary mechanism.** The import path reserves the translated tuple before publishing: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/session_import.rs:1224-1239` (`reserve_synced_translation`, refusal = `RejectedReserve`), per-worker adoption in `session_glue/commands/upsert_synced.rs:257-306`, reverse companion synthesized at import (`session_import.rs:1057-1067` -> `shared_ops/reverse_synth.rs:191-235`), and the reverse-SNAT `dnat_table` steering entry is published at import (`session_import.rs:1348-1363`). Standby display rows carry the real translated port. A pure missing-binding defect would also break the start-during-failover cell, which survives.
2. **"Not pushed to fast path on RG activation" — refuted in its coarse form.** `ha/state.rs:166-178,276-303` runs RefreshOwnerRGS + reverse prewarm + BPF republish on activation; the live log above confirms 27 entries republished. Any defect here must be per-entry/per-worker (see below), not a missing republish.
3. **Gratuitous ARP/NA not refreshed — refuted** (6 bursts logged; `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:447-490,567-717`). Private RG election is the default (`pkg/config/compiler_system.go:4429-4434`), so the direct-mode announce path is the operative one and it fires.
4. **What the code does guarantee:** packet-time HA is enforced against the *stored* session decision on every hit — `session_glue/resolve.rs:496-503` (`enforce_session_ha_resolution`), backed by `forwarding/ha.rs:87-197` (`HAInactive` when the egress owner RG is not `is_forwarding_active`, where active requires a live watchdog lease: `types/runtime.rs:534-536`, lease = watchdog+10s `HA_WATCHDOG_STALE_AFTER_SECS`). Synced hits are re-resolved from local FIB (`resolve.rs:474-481`) and materialized into the worker table (`resolve.rs:35-56`); promotion requires a `ForwardCandidate` disposition (`session_glue/promote.rs:96-99`). Worker-local copies are installed by fan-out **at import time** (`session_import.rs:1441-1453`) and by activation prewarm (`shared_ops/store.rs:540-590,598-631`), each via bounded queues with counted drops.

## What is NOT yet known (the open root cause)

Which of these per-entry legs fails for the iperf tuples on the new owner, and why it differs by variant:

## #16110 — cli: show security flow session renders divergent NAT port/counters for the same synced session on the two nodes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary

`show security flow session` renders **the same synced session** on the two cluster nodes with different NAT ports and different packet counters, with no marker that one row is a standby copy whose forward direction has never been locally observed. During a failover blackhole this makes the authoritative-looking row (`HA State: Active`) the *least* informative one, and the standby row the one carrying the real translated port.

## Evidence (midzero snapshot during RG1 zero window, /var/worktrees/fz-repro/midzero-rg1-20261021T005131/fw0.txt vs fw1.txt)

Same session ID 562949953421325 (`10.0.61.102/57566 -> 172.16.80.200/5211`):

- fw0 (RG2 owner / RG1 non-owner view): `HA State: Active, Timeout: 20`, `In: ... Pkts: 7777627`, `Out: 172.16.80.200/5211 --> 172.16.80.8/0` (dst port **0**).
- fw1 (peer view of same ID): `HA State: Backup, Timeout: 1800`, `In: ... Pkts: 0`, `Out: ... --> 172.16.80.8/57566` (real SNAT port **57566**).

Other rows on the owner render `Out: .../0` with `Pkts: 0-12` while the flow is supposedly live. The `HA State` column is not read from the session at all: it is *derived at render time* from the session's ingress/egress interface RETH ownership vs local primary state — `pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:289-300` calling `config.SessionHAState` (`pkg/config/reth_rg_owner.go:118-186`), first matching interface wins. `Timeout` likewise renders the row's stored value with no indication it is the standby's 1800s retention window vs the owner's 20s window.

## Why it matters

- Operators (and automated failover harnesses grepping this output) conclude "sessions exist on the new owner, Pkts: 0" and stop there; the display cannot answer the next question — *is this row forwarding-ready, NAT-reserved, worker-installed?* — which is the actual failover question.
- The `/0` port rendering invites a wrong "NAT binding lost" diagnosis: the port is present in the synced value (the standby row proves it) but the owner-side row renders 0, suggesting the mirror row and the forwarding row have diverged — exactly the split-truth the sync code works hard to avoid, now hidden by the display.

## Fix shape

- Render the session's own provenance on each row: origin (local / cluster-synced / promoted), the stored translated port as-is (never a synthesized 0), and whether the local helper holds a forwarding-ready entry (e.g. suffix the HA column with the dataplane's view rather than re-deriving it from config ownership).
- Add a `show security flow session` self-check: when the same session ID renders different translated ports on the two nodes' *local* views, surface that divergence explicitly instead of leaving it to be spotted by eye across two CLI outputs.

## Repro

1. Loss userspace cluster; start any SNAT'd flow; sync it.
2. On both nodes: `show security flow session destination-prefix 172.16.80.200` and compare the same session ID's `Out:` port and `Timeout:`.

## #16111 — docs: in-VM tcpdump captures zero packets for AF_XDP fast-path flows; failover playbooks need working observation points [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Summary

Kernel `tcpdump` inside the firewall VMs captures **zero packets** for live, multi-Gbps transit flows, on every interface including the AF_XDP-bound physical NICs, the `.80` VLAN sub-interfaces, and `xpf-usp0/1`. Failover debugging that relies on in-VM captures (the standard "capture on both nodes" play) therefore produces empty files and can be misread as "traffic never arrived".

## Evidence (FZDiag, build working-20873-g69c7c69af6)

Three separate runs during a live 10-18 Gbps iperf3 flow with a mid-flow RG1 failover:

- `tcpdump -i any 'tcp port 5211'` on both FWs: `0 packets captured` (diag2).
- `tcpdump -i ge-0-0-1`, `-i ge-0-0-2.80`, `-i ge-0-0-0`, and fw1 twins `ge-7-0-1`, `ge-7-0-2.80`, `ge-7-0-0`: all `0 packets captured` (diag3/diag4).
- `tcpdump -i xpf-usp0` / `xpf-usp1`: 0 packets (diag5). The same run's capture on the **parent** `ge-7-0-2` (pre-VLAN-split) did capture wire traffic — but only broadcast/other-VLAN background (5,697 frames of lab ARP), still 0 frames of the VLAN-80 iperf flow: the XDP program (`xdp_userspace_p`, xdpgeneric on the sub-interfaces per `ip link`) redirects the flow before any AF_PACKET tap sees it.

Meanwhile the LAN-host capture of the same flow works fine (3,985+ frames), and helper statistics (`RX packets`, `Flow cache hits`) prove the packets traverse the FW.

## Why it matters

- Every HA failover investigation runbook that says "capture on both nodes" silently gets no data exactly for the fast-path flows that fail over badly; investigators then chase L2/neighbor theories that captures can neither confirm nor refute.
- The one diagnostic that *would* discriminate (which node/direction dies) is unavailable, which materially slowed the FZ zero-throughput diagnosis.

## Fix shape (any one is sufficient; first preferred)

1. Document in `testing-docs/ha-failover-validation.md` (and the failover skills) that in-VM tcpdump is blind to AF_XDP fast-path traffic, and name the working observation points: LAN/WAN host captures, helper statistics deltas (`show chassis cluster status` data-plane section), and exception/recent-exception records.
2. Or add a helper-side per-flow packet tap / counters export that can answer "did node X see flow Y in direction Z after time T" (e.g. extend the existing `Recent exceptions` / last-resolution telemetry with per-session first/last-seen node-local timestamps).
3. Or support capturing on the XDP redirect path (AF_XDP socket tap) for a filtered flow during diagnosis.

## Repro

1. Loss userspace cluster, start `iperf3 -c 172.16.80.200 -p 5211 -P 4` from LAN host.
2. In either FW VM: `tcpdump -i any -c 10 'tcp port 5211'` → `0 packets captured` while iperf reports Gbps.

## #16124 — daemon: extract shrunk failoverActuationRegistry + forEachRGState (equivalence test first) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Claim
- **ID:** W2.7 (daemon R6 shrunk; R5/R3 opportunistic-only, not standalone) — Daemon HA registry shrunk
- **Source report:** muse-spark refactoring audit, Wave 2

## Narrowed survivor form (not the as-written proposal)
Extract only the shrunk `failoverActuationRegistry` (arm/disarm/resolve/fail/wait + its 4 fields) plus one `forEachRGState` snapshot helper. VIP resign stays on `Daemon`. Field-continent grouping (R5) and typed `nftFamily`/`hostFamily` (R3) are **opportunistic-when-touching only, never standalone PRs** — do not file or do them standalone. Precondition, test-only, before any actuation move: an event-vs-reconcile equivalence test.

## Mechanism / pain (file:line at current origin/master 0976d8be74)
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:76-103` — `syncRGSyncHold` / `syncRGKernelUpgradeHold` repeat take-lock/copy-slice/release-lock RG iteration; no `forEachRGState`.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:329-500` — arm/consume/timeout barrier lifecycle on `Daemon` fields (`failoverActuateMu`, wait map, Consumed distinction); state declared `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1693-1708`.
- `grep failoverActuationRegistry|forEachRGState` = 0 at master. `daemon_ha.go` still 3,168 lines.
- Pain is maintenance (Low): ownership/inspection of actuation state is entangled with the 970-method `Daemon`.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives
Refutation: holding `rgMu` across per-state calls serialises HA reconcile; adding another slice allocation in the helper adds cost; splitting `failoverActuateMu` or moving VIP resign (`daemon_ha.go:584-598`, touches `resignRethRGFn`/`vrrpMgr`) breaks lifecycle. Codex A/C correction: R3's claimed production-ingress pain is false — production netlink already typed (`pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go:39-57` `famV4/famV6`); string family lives in the independent textual oracle (`host_inbound_ingress_9637.go:93-383`) which must stay untouched, and the one prod conntrack callsite passes hard-coded literals then converts back at the `pkg/config` boundary. Additive `error_code` / `error_retry_class` fields beside the existing prose (old binaries retain the message), **one string-prefix site converted per PR**, with a per-prefix differential (old prefix branch vs new code) proven before the old branch is deleted, and error/panic canaries in the same train. **NO serde tagged-enum rewrite. NO blanket unknown⇒never-retry rule** (see refutation — that rule is UNSOUND and is explicitly excluded; HA retry debt is preserved).

## Mechanism / pain (current origin/master `1f3e4e130e`)

- Prose-prefix branching: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_control.go:367` (`snapshotPostTeardownPrefix`, defined :309), `:495` (`syncedImportRepairPrefix`, :106), `:509` (`syncedImportRefusedPrefix`, :100), `:516-523` (unknown/mirror-write-failed left retryable); `pkg/dataplane/userspace/apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:40-48` (`snapshotContentConflictPrefix` matched against Rust `userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs` `SNAPSHOT_CONTENT_CONFLICT_PREFIX` #9520, plus `SNAPSHOT_POST_TEARDOWN_PREFIX` #10702).

An unrecognized future code may coexist with an old **known message prefix**, which must still classify correctly on new-Go/old-Rust and old-Go/new-Rust skew. Blanket no-retry can strand a torn-down dataplane or acknowledge a write that never reached authority."* The additive, per-site form survives because it never removes a prefix arm until the differential (including **unknown typed code + known legacy prefix**, and truly-unknown post-teardown) proves equivalent retry/rollback/debt behavior in both mixed-version directions.

## Validated severity

**Low (maintenance)** — no real defect demonstrated; classification-drift risk only. (Explicitly NOT a fail-open claim.)

## Decisive acceptance check

#9520/#10702 classification suites stay green. Per converted site: differential matrix over success, false-positive prefix, nil/missing field, each existing prefix, refusal/repair/post-teardown/transport distinction, and both old/new Go×Rust cross-pairs — old prefix branch deleted only after equivalence. Panic canaries preserve existing panic→quarantine/restart (`userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs` already implements containment; only the ratchet/canary part is pending per A-codex P7).

## #16134 — dataplane: validate u8 protocol carriers against poison and version bump first [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Claim

**W1.3 (data-model P3) — Protocol tokens → `u8` — DOWNGRADED to NEEDS_VALIDATION.** As scheduled in the synthesis wave row, this carrier change is **UNSOUND without atomic `__unsupported__` poison preservation and a version bump / rolling mixed-version cell BEFORE any carrier change**. This issue files the validation prerequisite, not the conversion.

## Narrowed survivor form (file ONLY this)

A NEEDS_VALIDATION-flavored investigation issue: before any of the three string carriers changes type, prove (a) atomic whole-snapshot poison preservation for the `__unsupported__` sentinel, (b) `ProtocolVersion` bump + rolling cell (old Rust + new Go and new Rust + old Go), and (c) protocol-0 semantics per carrier. No carrier is retyped, no Rust mirror table is deleted, until those cells exist and pass.

Three carriers (current origin/master `1f3e4e130e`): filter `pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_policies.go:43` `Protocols []string`; app `pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_policies.go:298` `Protocol string` (`PolicyApplicationSnapshot`); DNAT `pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_nat.go:258` `Protocol string`. Rust mirrors: `userspace-dp/src/protocol/security.rs:206-207,642-644`, `userspace-dp/src/protocol/nat.rs:269-270` (expect JSON strings); parsers `userspace-dp/src/ip_proto.rs:86` `proto_number`, `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:5164` `parse_protocol`. Go SSOT: `pkg/appid/catalog.go:316-353` `ProtocolNumber` (protocol 0/HOPOPT is `(0, true)`, distinct from unrepresentable).

## Mechanism / pain

Name-table skew between Go `appid.ProtocolNumber` and the Rust tables is real, but the app carrier doubles as the fail-closed poison channel — see refutation. Exact-equality versioning (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol.go:464` `ProtocolVersion = 63`; `userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs:295` `= 63`) means a numeric field under unchanged 63 is admitted by the version check and then refused by old Rust string decoders, stranding the previous image.

## Strongest refutation considered + why the downgraded form survives

**Codex dissent (A-codex P3, verbatim):** *"**New decisive omission:** `PolicyApplicationSnapshot.Protocol` is also security *poison* `"__unsupported__"`, injected for unrepresentable terms AND lenient bad policy/scheduler (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_lower.go:192-208,211-245`); Rust `policy.rs:2926-2945,5065-5074` rejects the **entire** snapshot so prior-good stays/fresh boot denies. `u8` has no encoding for poison; merely skipping/coercing a bad term (especially a DENY) can fail open."* (Current master: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:19` `unsupportedApplicationSentinel = "__unsupported__"`, injected at `policies_lower.go:206-207,229-230,243-244`; Rust rejects whole snapshot via `SnapshotIntegrityError`, `policy.rs` `parse_applications`/`dropped_any`; Go mirror check `policies_reject.go:59-110`.)

**CodexE dissent (E-codex W1.3, verbatim):** *"`pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol.go:10-16,464` and Rust `protocol/control.rs:27-30,295` enforce *exact* version 63 only; a new Go numeric field under **unchanged 63** passes version admission then old Rust `String`/`Vec<String>` decode refuses the snapshot, leaving the previous image (not assured safe/current)."* Decisive check (E-codex): *"Cross-pair actual old-v63 helper/new-Go snapshot with the **current required-protocol gate** and prove rejection/disarm before claim of apply, then version-bump both sides and preserve proto-0 semantics."*

The narrowed form survives precisely because it does not schedule the conversion: it requires the poison/mixed-version/proto-0 cells first. A-opus/A-wonder rated data-P3 STILL-VALID as "strongest data-model survivor" on the refuter's proto-0/3-carrier narrowing — that rating does not override the two Codex dissents on atomic poison + version bump, which are adopted here as gating prerequisites.

## Validated severity

**Low (maintenance)** as a refactor; the underlying poison channel is a security fail-closed mechanism — mishandling it would be a real fail-open defect, which is why this is filed as validation-first rather than as a scheduled conversion.

## Decisive acceptance check

Per-carrier builder tests proving: every poison path (unrepresentable term, lenient bad policy/scheduler, partial-drop DENY as well as permit) aborts publication atomically and preserves prior-good/fresh-boot deny **and** mirror rejection reason (`policies_reject.go:59-110`); protocol-0 (HOPOPT) stays valid and distinct from unknown (never default `0` for unknown); empty filter `[]u8` = unconstrained vs app/DNAT optional-numeric semantics; `""`+port≠0⇒TCP builder default; Junos aliases; both mixed-version orders under a bumped `ProtocolVersion` with rejection/disarm proven before apply. Rust backstop table not deleted until these pass.

Extract one parser returning **raw suffix** `(name string, suffix string, hasSuffix bool)`-equivalent, adopted per-caller only where that caller already treats the suffix as raw. Newtypes DEFERRED. A universal `(name, unit int, hasUnit bool)` parser is UNSOUND and NOT part of this issue.

## Mechanism / pain (current origin/master 0976d8be74)
- Divergent ad-hoc dot parsing `pkg/config/types.go:240-271,376-399,513-530` (`ResolveReth`/`ResolveFab`/`ResolveKernelIfName`/`DHCPLeaseKey`); same shape recurs at `pkg/flowexport/manager.go:1176 parseIfaceRef`.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives
Codex A: `ResolveReth`/`ResolveFab` copy an **arbitrary raw suffix** including non-decimal/multiple dots; `DHCPLeaseKey` discards suffix and uses separately supplied unit/VLAN; `resolveKernelIfNameWith` prioritizes a **declared dotted interface name** over any parse (`types.go:376-395`). A universal integer parser normalizes/refuses previously carried refs or misroutes an authored `gr-0/0/0.0`. Also note duplicate-adjacent closed #9821 (dotted interface names parsed as unit refs) — this issue is parser extraction only, not re-fixing #9821 semantics. Survives per-caller with raw suffix preserved and `TestResolverAgreement8994` as pin.

## Validated severity
Low (maintenance).

## Decisive acceptance check
Per-caller adoption list with suffix-semantics table (raw/discard/declared-name-wins); resolver-agreement tests green; authored dotted-name case (`gr-0/0/0.0`) unchanged; marshal-diff (G1).

## #16145 — config: gate registry per sub-run gated by lenient-census PR-0 (W2.1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Claim

- **Claim ID + title:** W2.1 (config-compiler P1 + cross P5-narrowed) — Gate registry per sub-run, gated by W1.7 PR-0
- **Validated severity:** Low (maintenance). No real defect is claimed; this is duplicated/drift-prone gate plumbing, not a correctness bug on current code.
- **Source report:** `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/muse-spark-review-refactoring-audit-code-quality-modularity-001.md`, base `cbfdd5462e`, verification `0976d8be74`, current `origin/master` `1f3e4e130e` (file:line below re-pinned at current master; drift since verification is unrelated).

## Narrowed survivor form (not the as-written proposal)

Per-sub-run gate registry **only**, in increments, **gated by the W1.7 PR-0 reflection/completeness test** over the `lenient*` bools. NAT first. Essays/comments travel verbatim; gate order is censused. A baseline regen or essay deletion = stop, no longer a refactor. Structured `Diagnostic` is additive; prose stays.

Explicitly **not** in scope: the cross-P5 general registry rewrite (REJECTED there), a generic `Check(*Config)` registry that cannot represent scrub/prune/order, and any claim that PR-0 alone proves the fourth link.

## Mechanism / pain at current origin/master

- `pkg/config/compiler_opts.go:18` `type compileOpts struct` (3,906-line file at base; ~297 `lenient* bool` fields — validators counted 297 at base, 295–300 distinct at verification, still growing) and `lenientCompileOpts()` at `pkg/config/compiler_opts.go:3602`. Each lenient bool needs four links: strict gate, tolerant gate, builder backstop, show/reason surface. Today that completeness is enforced by reviewer memory only; no census/completeness test exists.
- Ordered dispatch is hand-maintained at `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates.go:34` `runUniformGates(tree, cfg, opts)` with per-sub-run files `compiler_uniformgates_*.go` (16 files). First-error/warning order is observable (strict path: first failing gate wins).
- `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_nat.go:24-58` repeats explicit gate logic; gates consume AST/offenders (`compiler_uniformgates_nat.go:113-117`), not just `func(*Config) error`.

Pain: adding a lenient bool without its fourth link compiles green; gate extraction without an order census can silently change which diagnostic an operator sees first.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives

- **Refutation (Codex B / cross P5):** a general `Check(*Config)` registry cannot represent scrub/prune/order without extra per-gate hooks; `Diagnostic` alone does not prove the strict/tolerant/builder/show links; reflection PR-0 checks only that fields are `true` in `lenientCompileOpts`, not that a guard reads the right field (swapping one `opts.lenientFoo` use to another already-true flag leaves reflection green). A blanket unknown-handling or registry rewrite is therefore unsound.
- **Why narrowed survives:** it does not claim PR-0 proves wiring. PR-0 is a completeness census (new bool without a census row fails); per-gate fail-on-revert tests prove wiring per gate; the registry arrives only per sub-run behind that census, with essays verbatim and an order census. The owning slice (config-compiler) wins over the cross-slice registry rejection only in this gated incremental form.

## Three-way validation

- Validators: Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus-5.5 SMR + Muse-Wonder-1.0. Ledgers: `/var/worktrees/research-refactor/{B-codex,B-opus,B-wonder}.md` (also A-* cross-P5 leg).
- All three: STILL-VALID in narrowed form. B-opus: count drifted 297→299 distinct (immaterial, population growing). B-codex dissent-in-part: *"reflection PR-0 cannot enforce the claimed fourth link"* — it checks the literal flag, not guard wiring; W1.7's "fails on missing fourth link" is mechanically overstated. B-wonder/B-opus concur PR-0 + per-gate tests are required together. No validator found ALREADY-DONE or a duplicate owner.

## Decisive acceptance check

- PR-0 first: reflection/completeness test fails when a `lenient*` bool is added without its census row (seeded-bool red test).
- Per sub-run (NAT first): 6-fixture golden byte-identical (necessary-not-sufficient) **plus** per-gate fail-on-revert tests, order census (strict first-error and warning order unchanged), strict/lenient × generic/node matrix unchanged, structured `Diagnostic` additive with prose retained.
- Stop rule: any baseline regen, essay deletion, or skipped gate aborts — it is no longer this refactor.

## #16146 — config: evict lodger compilers from compiler_system.go and unify NAT zone predicate (W2.2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Claim

- **Claim ID + title:** W2.2 (config-compiler P3 + P5) — Compiler evictions from `compiler_system.go` + NAT predicate unification
- **Validated severity:** Low (maintenance). No real defect claimed; navigability + predicate-drift maintenance only.

1. **Evictions only:** move lodger compilers out of `compiler_system.go` in-package, function-level, chassis first (then SNMP/DDNS/schedulers per validators). Stanza decomposition of `compileSystem` itself is DEFERRED. No `<800L` ratchet.
2. **NAT predicate unification only:** one predicate/axis projecting strict-errors / offenders / skip-set, preserving granularity (strict is per-missing-field in source→destination order; tolerant skip-set is per rule-set). Struct `{Kind,Name}` key may replace the `kind+"\x00"+name` string key. **Explicitly no by-kind split of `compiler_validate_strict_nat.go`** — the synthesis wave row's "split by NAT kind" exceeds its own hostile review and is not part of this filing (see dissent).

## Mechanism / pain at current origin/master

- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` is 5,729 lines: `compileSystem` at `:201`, lodgers `compileDDNSServices:1651`, `compileSNMP:2777`, `compileSchedulers:4093`, `compileChassis:4288`. `compiler_chassis.go` holds only `compileDeviceMap`.
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go` is 5,625 lines: `natUndefinedZoneOffenders:46` vs `NATUndefinedZoneRuleSetNames:86` re-derive the same undefined-zone predicate on separate walks; consumers at `compiler_uniformgates.go:263,267`; string key `kind+"\x00"+name` at `:82-110` with dataplane consumers `pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:380,659`.

Pain: reviewers must navigate unrelated stanzas in one file; the two NAT walks can drift so strict diagnostics and the tolerant skip-set disagree.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives

Stanza-splitting `compileSystem` could reorder AAA warnings and share `loginUserByName` incorrectly. For NAT: a shared boolean must not collapse per-field vs per-rule-set granularity or allocate an offender list on the key-check path; a by-kind file split is churn (P7-class).
- **Why narrowed survives:** function-level in-package moves with unchanged call graph change no semantics; the predicate projection is required to preserve both granularities, proven by the property test below. The by-kind split is excluded.

## Three-way validation

- Validators: Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus-5.5 SMR + Muse-Wonder-1.0. Ledgers: `/var/worktrees/research-refactor/{B-codex,B-opus,B-wonder}.md`.

The W2.2 row text "split `compiler_validate_strict_nat.go` by NAT kind + struct key" therefore over-claims; this issue files predicate + struct key only.

- NAT: property test — strict-rejected ⇔ offenders non-empty ⇔ skip-set exact — plus existing NAT gate suites; struct-key change updates both `\x00` consumers with no new map allocation per rule.

## #16147 — config: typed static SchemaRefs audit-first, init-panic last (W2.3 R3) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Claim

- **Claim ID + title:** W2.3 / config-schema R3 — Typed static `SchemaRef`s (audit-test FIRST, init-panic LAST)
- **Validated severity:** Low (maintenance), with a conditional real-defect trigger: if the audit surfaces a dead schema path, that is a silent-drop **bug** to file separately (not part of this refactor).
- **Source report:** `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/muse-spark-review-refactoring-audit-code-quality-modularity-001.md`, base `cbfdd5462e`, verification `0976d8be74`, current `origin/master` `1f3e4e130e` (file:line re-pinned at current master).

## Narrowed survivor form (not the as-written proposal)

Sequence is mandatory: (1) audit test FIRST (`TestSchemaRefsResolve` enumerating all resolvers, non-panicking), (2) static `SchemaRef`s only for no-arg resolvers, (3) init-panic LAST. Arg-taking resolvers stay functions. Any dead path the audit surfaces is filed as a separate silent-drop bug, not fixed inside this refactor.

## Mechanism / pain at current origin/master

- Stringly schema resolution is pervasive: ~79 non-test `schemaForPath(` calls (hostile-corrected 83→79), 29 files referencing `Schema8939/Schema9181`, resolver funcs such as `bgpMultipathSchema8939`, `bgpGroupSchema9181`, `ipsecVPNLeafSchema8939` in `pkg/config/`.
- `pkg/config/compact_tail.go:52-74` returns nil for an unresolved schema path, which can quietly disable a packed reader — a bad ref fails silently today rather than at init.
- `pkg/config/schema.go:464-472` mutates the groups wildcard in `init`, so caching group-subtree handles before that initialization would capture an incomplete schema.

Pain: a typo'd or rotted schema path is invisible until a packed/tolerant reader silently drops data.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives

- **Refutation:** panic-first is unsound — an init panic aborts ~45 importing packages and enumerates only one bad ref per run. Arg-dependent resolvers (`compiler_ipsec.go:1158-1172`, `compiler_class_of_service.go:1629-1645`, `cosBindingSchema8939(which)`, `gatewayLeafSchema8939(parent)`) cannot be static refs. Pre-init caching captures the incomplete groups wildcard.
- **Why narrowed survives:** audit-first produces the full dead-path list as the first deliverable without aborting anything; static refs cover only the no-arg population; panic arrives last, after burn-down, when it can only fire on a genuinely new bad ref.

## Three-way validation

- Validators: Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus-5.5 SMR + Muse-Wonder-1.0. Ledgers: `/var/worktrees/research-refactor/{B-codex,B-opus,B-wonder}.md`.
- All three STILL-VALID audit-first. B-codex adds the `schema.go:464-472` init-ordering constraint (above). B-wonder: *"Dead path surfaced = silent-drop BUG to file separately, not refactor fallout."* No ALREADY-DONE/DUPLICATE found.

## Decisive acceptance check

- Audit test lists every resolver outcome (dead-path list is deliverable #1); static-ref conversion keeps arg-taking resolvers as functions; init-panic added only after the audit list is empty, with a seeded bad ref turning the audit/init red; groups-wildcard init ordering preserved; tolerant path (#1960 no-brick) unchanged.

## Review origin

- Source report: `muse-spark-review-refactoring-audit-code-quality-modularity-001.md`; base `cbfdd5462e`; verification `0976d8be74`; discoverer `muse-spark`; validators Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus-5.5 SMR + Muse-Wonder-1.0. Dissents: none on the narrowed form; constraints above are verbatim from B-codex/B-wonder.

## #16153 — dataplane: extract partial-publisher pipeline, stamp dedup, typed actions; binding_plan canary-aware only (W2.4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Claim

- **Claim ID + title:** W2.4 (dataplane P3 ADOPT + P4-narrowed + P2-narrowed + P8-narrowed) — Partial-publisher pipeline extraction, stamp dedup, typed actions, `binding_plan.go`
- **Validated severity:** Low (maintenance), adjacent to a real measured perf issue #15955 (OPEN, triple `snapshotContentHash` per publish) — coordinate, do not double-fix the hash leg.
- **Source report:** `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/muse-spark-review-refactoring-audit-code-quality-modularity-001.md`, base `cbfdd5462e`, verification `0976d8be74`, current `origin/master` `1f3e4e130e` (file:line re-pinned at current master).

## Narrowed survivor form (not the as-written proposal)

Four bounded legs, each standalone:
1. **P3 (strongest in set):** extract the near-verbatim partial-publisher bookkeeping (clone→mutate→hash→dedup→publish) shared by the 4 clone sites, after characterizing the route-vs-capture dedup predicate difference. One publisher per PR.
2. **P4-narrowed:** stamp dedup via a capture-authority helper + **per-publisher** detach lists. No blanket deep clone.
3. **P2-narrowed:** typed policy actions with the **invariant check as the deliverable** (Go gives no exhaustiveness); do not unify permit/deny vs accept/discard vocabularies; Rust enum must not gate.
4. **P8-narrowed (canary-aware — see below):** keep pure binding-plan helpers **reachable where they are**; a `binding_plan.go` file move may proceed only with the source-text canaries updated in the same PR and proven non-vacuous. Pair-collapse is REJECTED (premise false: 3-line wrappers).

**Binding-plan UNSOUND as standalone motion (Codex C):** do not file or do a standalone "extract `binding_plan.go`" motion. See refutation.

## Mechanism / pain at current origin/master

- Four verbatim retained-clone sites: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go:215` and `:378`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:1282`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_worker_arm_5134.go:65` — each `next := *m.lastSnapshot` followed by generation/hash/ACK/cache bookkeeping. Documented bug farm: #15955 (hash drift under lock) / #9520. Route-vs-capture dedup gates differ (`manager_overlay.go:398-405` capture-only).
- Stamp duplication: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:123` `stampCaptureAuthorityWithRoutesMode` and `:148` `refreshCaptureAuthorityLocked` stamp the same four capture fields.
- Stringly actions: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol_policies.go:58` `Action string`, `:365` `Action string`; `snapshot_policy_invariant.go` checks count, not action soundness.
- Pure helpers live in the 2,552-line `pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go`: `buildUserspaceIngressDomainEntries:175`, `buildUserspaceIngressIfindexes:1773`, `snapshotBindingPlanKey:1973` — and are **already directly tested**: `plan_key_crossplane_9009_test.go:44-56` calls `snapshotBindingPlanKey` directly.

## Strongest refutation considered + why narrowed form survives

- **P3:** blanket extraction must not become an extra full-snapshot marshal under `m.mu`; route and capture dedup predicates differ and must be characterization-pinned first. Survives as: extract shared bookkeeping *after* per-publisher prep, preserving one hash/copy, ACK-then-retained-cache.
- **P4:** blind deep-cloning every field doubles copy/hash work under the manager lock and erases per-field intent (unmeasured FIB-churn rate). Survives as per-publisher detach lists only.
- **P2:** a string-derived Go enum is not exhaustive; rejecting unknown/empty wire actions instead of preserving fail-closed/default + nonterminal semantics could change admission. Survives as invariant-check-first.
- **P8 (Codex C, decisive):** *"The report's 'only reachable through Manager-level tests' is false"* — direct helper tests exist (above). Worse, `binding_plan_key_crossplane_8901_test.go:322-347` explicitly reads **`maps_sync.go`**, locates `func snapshotBindingPlanKey(` and verifies the emitted `"shared_umem=` key (also parser-based at `:100-102`). Moving the function as a standalone motion makes that security/availability liveness gate red while changing no package visibility or dependency. **Verdict: UNSOUND as standalone code-motion split. Keep existing pure helpers reachable.** Opus/Wonder rated the pure-only move STILL-VALID; this filing adopts the Codex-C constraint as binding: any eventual file move must update both source-text canaries in the same PR and prove they still locate and execute the moved function (canary-aware), and must not be scheduled as its own PR.

## Three-way validation

- Validators: Codex GPT-6-Sol + Opus-5.5 SMR + Muse-Wonder-1.0. Ledgers: `/var/worktrees/research-refactor/{C-codex,C-opus,C-wonder}.md`.
- P3/P4/P2: all three STILL-VALID as narrowed. **P8 material disagreement (stated, not smoothed):** C-codex UNSOUND as standalone motion (canary + false premise, quoted above); C-opus/C-wonder STILL-VALID pure-only. Resolution filed here: helpers stay reachable; move only canary-aware, never standalone. C-opus also flags #15955 overlap on the hash leg (coordinate, not duplicate).

## Decisive acceptance check

- P3: characterization of route-vs-capture dedup first; golden retained generation/hash + failed/partial ACK matrices per publisher; one hash/copy per publish; alloc/lock-hold comparison on a real-sized snapshot; snapshot goldens byte-identical.
- P4: snapshot immutability/alias test per publisher; retained-clone hash equivalence.
- P2: differential table (empty/malformed/future/terminal/nonterminal) across Go lowerer, wire JSON, Rust reader; every invalid accepted path fails closed.
