## #16270 — ha: aged RG1 failover strands ForwardCandidate-cached tuples on old owner — fw0 cache never supersedes locally-egressing decision after egress RG leaves (#16217) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary

Aged-flow (30 s) RG1 failover blackhole on PR #16217 head `78bc60d98c` (deb `99.16215.11.dirty`, DISC11 scratch instrumentation), diagnosed with per-stage DISC on fw1 for the 4 tuples post-failover. This is the residual after the #16215 FabricRedirect-SNAT decline closed live (snat_revoked 0 both nodes at every sample). **Stage of death: fw1 receives only 2 of 4 fabric-redirected tuples post-takeover; the 2 it receives are served correctly to WAN, the other 2 never arrive — fw0 stops fabric-redirecting them and keeps serving them locally as ForwardCandidate to a dead WAN egress.** Sessions stay established (Timeout 1800, est_wire=4) on both nodes; WAN-return is zero because fw0's local WAN TX goes nowhere after RG1 moves to fw1.

## Live cell (FZDiag11, hash-proven homogeneous)

- Scratch: PR head `78bc60d98c` + DISC11 `debug-log` instrumentation only (per-stage cache/session/NAT/slow-TX, tuple-gated to `10.0.61.102 -> 172.16.80.200:5211`, fabric-ingress only for cache/session stages; NAT stage ungated by ingress), deb repacked `99.16215.11.dirty` sha256 `ac025023…`, helper sha256 `6d7f85c8…` identical via `/proc/<pid>/exe` on BOTH nodes before traffic (8 DISC11 strings in binary on both). Evidence: `/var/worktrees/fzdiag11/cell/` (`iperf.log`, `disc-fw{0,1}.log`, `sess-*-fw{0,1}.txt`, `stats-*-fw{0,1}.txt`, `met-*-fw{0,1}.txt`, `cell.log`).
- Posture verified before traffic: RG0/1/2 all node0 primary (guard in cell). P4 60 s to `172.16.80.200:5211` (ports 46248/46262/46276/46280), RG1 fw0->fw1 at 30 s age.
- Result: **pre-FO throughput degraded by DISC logging to ~1 Gbps (instrumentation tax — the same cell shape on the uninstrumented fix build ran 11+ Gbps), first zero at interval 30-31 (failover+1 s), permanent zeros to end.** `snat_revoked` 0 on both nodes at every sample (pre/a10/d28/fo1/fo6/post) — the #16215 decline holds. Sessions post-run: Timeout 1800 rows on both nodes, forward counters live on fw0, WAN-return counters zero. Cluster restored clean master `2c8575b70e` (helper `2f2f5cbf…` both, RG0/1/2 node0, P4 13.8 Gbit/s verified).

## Per-stage evidence (fw1, post-takeover)

| Stage | 46246 | 46280 | 46248 / 46262 / 46276 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cache hit (fabric ingress) | `ForwardCandidate egress=14 tx=6 owner_rg=1 stamp_owner=1 nat_src=172.16.80.8 invalid=None outcome=serve-candidate` ×9 | same ×1 | **no DISC11 cache/session/slow lines at all** |
| Session hit | `SyncImport stored=MissingNeighbor egress=14 -> resolved ForwardCandidate egress=14 tx=6 next_hop=172.16.80.200 est_wire=4 (Established)` | `WorkerLocalImport stored=ForwardCandidate -> resolved ForwardCandidate` | none |
| NAT lookup | (reverse-hit samples pre-FO keep) — no REVOKE | `SyncImport judged=MissingNeighbor valid=true result=keep` | none |
| TX per binding | `cache-tx target_if=6 target_bi=Some(2) binding_index=0 cached_target_bi=Some(2)`; slow path `slow-built target_if=6 target_bi=Some(2) result=queued` | same | none |
| WAN egress TX | fw1 TX packets 229->255 (fo1) ->273 (fo6) — advances only for these 2 tuples | same | fw1 receives nothing |

fw1 totals: 53 DISC lines, only tuples 46246 (39) + 46280 (9+session/slow). **Tuples 46248, 46262, 46276 have zero fabric-ingress DISC11 lines on fw1** — they never cross the fabric.

## fw0 side (why the other tuples never leave)

- Pre-FO fw0 DISC16222 (existing #16222 line, ungated): all 4 tuples served `ForwardCandidate egress=14 owner_rg=1 outcome=serve` at full rate (~400k samples for 46248 alone).
- Post-FO, fw0's cached decisions for 46248/46262/46276 are **never evicted**: no `FabricRedirect` cache outcome, no session/slow re-resolve for these tuples post-FO. The flow-cache revalidation (`cached_flow_decision_invalid_reason_for_flow`) does not supersede a cached `ForwardCandidate` whose owner RG (RG1, egress 14) has become peer-owned after takeover — `enforce_ha_resolution_snapshot` on the *stored* resolution still compares equal (the stored ForwardCandidate is re-judged against the same FIB row; HAInactive demotion is not triggered for the cached-hit path because the invalid-reason check only handles FabricRedirect supersession, OwnerActiveRedirect, and DiscardRoute-now-local). So fw0 keeps transmitting client data on its local WAN binding (egress 14 / tx 6, ge-0/0-2) whose RG1 is now owned by fw1 — frames leave a non-owner interface / dead VRRP and are blackholed; TCP retransmits keep hitting the same cache entry forever.
- 46246/46280 took a different path: their fw0 entries were FabricRedirect-shaped (seeded `seeded_kind=FabricRedirect stamp_owner_rg=0/1 egress=4` in pre-FO DISC16222 samples; nat-pre `SyncImport stored=FabricRedirect egress=4` declining per #16215), so at takeover they cross the fabric and fw1 serves them (above). The split is per-tuple cache shape, not per-stream luck: FabricRedirect-seeded tuples survive, ForwardCandidate-seeded tuples strand on the old owner.

## Mechanism (proven chain)

1. Pre-failover (all RG on fw0), fw0 seeds flow-cache entries per tuple: some as `ForwardCandidate egress=14 (WAN reth0.80, RG1)`, some as `FabricRedirect egress=4`. Which shape a tuple gets depends on its seed-time resolution context.
2. At RG1 takeover (fw0->fw1), fw0 demotes RG1. FabricRedirect tuples: fw0 fabric-TXs retransmits to fw1; fw1 session/cache resolves `ForwardCandidate egress=14` (now locally active RG1) with SNAT `172.16.80.8` valid, TX queued to binding `target_bi=Some(2)` (ge-7-0-2 WAN) — **this leg works** (DISC11 session/slow-built/cache-tx above). No loop back to fw0, no DiscardRoute consumption, no NAT miss, no TX-ring miss for these tuples.
3. ForwardCandidate tuples: fw0's cache hit keeps serving the stored ForwardCandidate locally. No stage re-judges a cached ForwardCandidate against RG ownership change: `cached_flow_decision_invalid_reason_inner` returns `EnforceChanged` only if `enforce_ha_resolution_snapshot(stored) != stored`, but that enforcement demotes ForwardCandidate->HAInactive only via `owner_rg_for_resolution` + `is_forwarding_active` — and the observed live behavior shows these entries are NOT evicted (fw0 flow-cache evictions post-FO: only gen/rg_epoch/deny_expiry small counts, `enforce_changed=0`, `decision_invalid=0` in stats-fo1-fw0). The packet is TX'd on fw0's WAN binding to a next-hop whose RG fw0 no longer owns; WAN-return never comes; client retransmits hit the same entry permanently.
4. Result: 2/4 streams recover via fabric, 2/4 (in this cell 3 tuples show no fw1 arrival; 46248 also has no fw1 line — count is 2 arrived of 4) die at FO+1 s with established sessions everywhere — the blackhole is fw0 cache retention of a locally-egressing decision after its egress RG left the node, not any fw1 stage.

## What is ruled out (per suspect)

- **Fabric-ingress hit serves cached FabricRedirect back toward fw0 (loop):** ruled out — fw1 cache/session for arrived tuples resolve ForwardCandidate WAN, never FabricRedirect; fw1 TX advances.
- **Decision egress is fabric again on fw1:** ruled out — resolved egress=14 tx=6, next_hop=172.16.80.200.
- **TX ring/binding for WAN not armed on new owner:** ruled out for arrived tuples — `target_bi=Some(2)`, slow-built queued, fw1 TX packets advance 229->273 in fo window. (Note fw1 `Direct TX disallowed fb: 188` is pre-existing copy-path count, not post-FO growth.)

## #16288 — harness: Makefile HARNESS_ENV empty when CLUSTER_ENV is set on the command line — ledger env recorded as '--cluster' on tcp/udp gate runs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-22)

## Summary

When a cluster gate is invoked with an explicit non-default `CLUSTER_ENV` on the `make` command line (the documented tcp/udp-cluster workflow), the ledger row is recorded with `env="--cluster"` instead of the env file's basename (e.g. `tcp-userspace-cluster`). Every tcp/udp gate run in the 2026-10-22 evidence is corrupted this way, so no band comparison can ever use those rows — the ledger env label exists precisely to keep runs on different clusters from being compared (Makefile comment at the `HARNESS_ENV` definition).

## Evidence

Gate invocation echoed in the run logs (`/var/worktrees/tcpgate/evidence/cell3.log:53`, `/var/worktrees/udpgate/evidence/cell.log:71`, and every other tcp/udp cell):

```
BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV=test/incus/tcp-userspace-cluster.env ./test/incus/harness-result.sh run \
	--gate test-failover --adapter ha-smoke --env  --cluster \
	--require-helper-attestation \
	-- ./test/incus/test-failover.sh
```

Note `--env` followed by *nothing*, then `--cluster`. Ledger rows from the same runs confirm the corruption (`tcpgate/evidence/cell3.log:366-367`):

```
c0b3aeac3284ff04.json test-stress-failover --cluster VOID ...
7608c133945afa70.json test-failover --cluster VOID ...
```

## Root cause

`Makefile:1462-1476` (guard structure):

```make
NODE ?= all
ifeq ($(origin CLUSTER_ENV),undefined)
ifeq ($(origin BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV),undefined)
CLUSTER_ENV := test/incus/loss-userspace-cluster.env
else
CLUSTER_ENV := $(BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV)
endif

# Ledger `env` label ...
HARNESS_ENV := $(if $(CLUSTER_ENV),$(notdir $(basename $(CLUSTER_ENV))),local-cluster)
endif
```

## #16289 — harness: session-sync idle precondition compares absolute cumulative counters — fails forever on tcp cluster (source sent=15, target received=174, pending=0) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Summary

The test-failover session-sync idle precondition (`ha_session_sync_idle_sample`) compares *absolute cumulative* `Session create` counters across the two nodes (`source sent == target received`). On the tcp cluster those counters have different baselines — the target's `received` includes creates from before the source's current counting epoch (previous deploys / daemon restarts / earlier bulk syncs) — so the equality can never hold even when sync is fully caught up and `pending=0`. The gate burns its full 30 s timeout, reports FAIL "session sync did not become idle", and every downstream precondition-dependent cell is VOIDed.

This is distinct from closed #533/#586 (those were about requiring counters to stop *changing* / drained-counter behaviour on the old validator); the current harness code already dropped the stability requirement, but the absolute-equality requirement that replaced it is unsatisfiable whenever the two nodes' counters did not start from the same baseline.

## Evidence

`/var/worktrees/tcpgate/evidence/cell3.log:65-94` (identical line repeated for the whole 30 s window, counters never move):

```
session sync node0->node1 not idle: source sent=15, target received=174, pending=0
... (×30)
  FAIL  before traffic: session sync did not become idle within 30s (node0->node1)
```

Later in the same run the offset persists proportionally (`sent=74, received=233` — delta 159 in both samples), i.e. the target is keeping up in lockstep; it is the constant baseline offset (~159) that makes equality impossible, not lag. `pending=0` throughout.

Downstream damage in the same log: all RG1 precondition-gated cells VOID ("RG1 precondition session sync did not pass; RG1 did not move to fw0/node0", cell3.log:212-222), so the failover gate measures almost nothing.

## Root cause

`test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh:234-255` `ha_session_sync_idle_sample`:

```bash
if ! sent="$(ha_sync_stats_value "$source_path" "Session create" sent)"; then return 2; fi
if ! received="$(ha_sync_stats_value "$target_path" "Session create" received)"; then return 2; fi
...
if [[ "$sent" == "$received" && "$pending" == "0" ]]; then
    return 0
fi
```

`sent`/`received` are cumulative-since-daemon-start counters parsed from `show ... sync statistics` (`Services Synchronized: Session create <sent> <received>`). Nothing guarantees both nodes booted / last reset counters at the same moment or that the target has not received creates in a previous epoch (e.g. before a source restart zeroed its `sent`). The caller `ha_wait_for_session_sync_idle` (`test/incus/test-failover.sh:313-345`) requires 3 consecutive idle samples, so a permanent offset = permanent failure.

The hermetic selftest (`test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh:424-480`) only ever feeds fixtures whose baselines already match (5==5, 7==7), so this failure mode has no coverage.

## Impact

- `make test-failover` / `test-stress-failover` on tcp (and any cluster where the nodes' sync counters were not zeroed together) cannot pass the pre-traffic precondition; the gate FAILs and dependent cells VOID regardless of actual dataplane/HA health.

*(truncated — 56 lines total)*

## #16290 — harness: deploy version-tag refusal aborts before manifest write — invalidated xpf-deploy-manifest.json never rewritten, later gates record VOID [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Summary

`cluster-setup.sh deploy` invalidates the executable-attestation manifest *before* deploying, but only writes the new manifest *after* the deploy body succeeds. When the rolling cut refuses — e.g. `xpfd upgrade --rolling` rejects replacing the live version dir because the same version tag was re-staged with different bytes — `set -e` aborts the script before `deploy_write_manifest` runs, leaving **no** `dist-deb/xpf-deploy-manifest.json` at all. Every subsequent cluster gate then records VOID (`exe_check=UNAVAILABLE`, build under test unattributable) even for behaviour that has nothing to do with the refused re-stage, and the VOID gives no hint that a refused deploy is the cause.

## Evidence

Refusal (tcp: `/var/worktrees/tcpgate/evidence/cell2.log:95`, cell3.log:36; udp: `/var/worktrees/udpgate/evidence/cell2.log:47`):

```
upgrade --rolling: refuse-before-PREFLIGHT: cannot replace the live/rollback version dir /var/lib/xpf/versions/working-20908-g20ac8ba8c0-dirty (its bytes come from source generation "" but this cut pins "01792688566977636319-8afb4a62995d71bb"); re-stage under a DISTINCT version tag
```

Manifest never written (udp cell2.log:49, tcp cell4.log:24):

```
ls: cannot access 'dist-deb/xpf-deploy-manifest.json': No such file or directory
```

Resulting unattributable VOID ledger rows (tcpgate cell3.log:273-275, 360-367):

```
harness-result: test-failover gate verdict was FAIL but exe_check=UNAVAILABLE — the row is recorded VOID (unattributable)
harness-result: recorded test-failover --cluster verdict=VOID
```

## Root cause

`test/incus/cluster-setup.sh` `cmd_deploy` (with `set -euo pipefail` at :28):

1. `:665-666` — `deploy_manifest_invalidate "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$target"` runs first (correctly: a failed deploy must not leave stale provenance — design note in `deploy-lib.sh:278-281,299-302`).
2. `:688-694` — dispatch to `deploy_rolling_deb` / `deploy_vm_deb`, whose `incus exec ... xpfd upgrade --rolling` (`:761`, unguarded) exits nonzero on the version-tag refusal (`pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:580` `refuse-before-PREFLIGHT: cannot replace the live/rollback version dir ... re-stage under a DISTINCT version tag`). `set -e` aborts `cmd_deploy` here.
3. `:699-709` — `deploy_write_manifest ... || die ...` is never reached.

So on *any* mid-deploy failure the on-disk state is "manifest invalidated, nothing recorded". That part is intentional fail-closed design. The defect is what happens next: the nodes are still running the *previous, unchanged* build (the refusal happens before PREFLIGHT — nothing was cut), yet there is no manifest describing them, so gates VOID with generic `exe_check=UNAVAILABLE` instead of either (a) attesting the still-running build, or (b) naming the refused deploy as the void reason. The operator sees VOID rows with no pointer to the re-stage refusal that caused them.

Note the refusal itself is correct behaviour (same tag, different bytes must be refused); this issue is only about manifest/ledger handling around it. Prior manifest work: #11765 (closed, rebuild-vs-deployed VOID), #11845 (closed, single-slot manifest) — neither covers the invalidate→abort→no-manifest path.

## Impact

- One refused re-stage silently poisons attestation for all later gates until the next fully successful deploy; every row in between is VOID and unattributable.

## #16291 — lab: UDP iperf3 fails through udp-cluster firewall (unable to read from stream socket) while TCP via udp fw and UDP via tcp fw are clean [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Summary

Through the **udp** userspace cluster firewall, UDP-mode iperf3 cannot even complete its control handshake: `iperf3: error - unable to read from stream socket: Resource temporarily unavailable`. TCP-mode iperf3 through the *same* udp firewall is clean, and UDP-mode iperf3 through the **tcp** cluster firewall is also clean — so this is specific to UDP traffic through the udp-cluster firewall path, not a target/server problem. iperf3's control channel is TCP after the initial UDP test-port negotiation; the failure means the UDP datagrams (or the control connection they set up) are being dropped/reset in that one path, and no UDP throughput measurement through the udp cluster is possible at all.

## Evidence

All refs `/var/worktrees/targetprov/evidence/`, 2026-10-22, targets are the same iperf3-systemd service grid (ports 5200-5211) on both clusters:

- UDP via udp fw fails: `cell.log:315` and `cell4.log:44` — `iperf3: error - unable to read from stream socket: Resource temporarily unavailable` (`UDP_RC=1`); retries in `cell2.log:8,16,25` fail identically, and the target journal shows the server receiving nothing (`0.00 Bytes 0.00 bits/sec` intervals, cell2.log:30-49).
- Fresh-port retry also fails: `cell5.log` — UDP to previously-unused port 5205/5210 via udp fw: `unable to connect to server ... Connection refused`; cell6 (socket restore + retest): `unable to receive control message ... Connection reset by peer`.
- TCP via udp fw clean: same cells — `udp tcp5211 OK`, `udp tcp5202 OK`, grid check `24/24` ports OK.
- UDP via tcp fw clean (control): `cell5.log` — `UDP 5205 via tcp fw (control, target .210): 10.0 Mbits/sec, 0/2591 (0%)` loss, `iperf Done`; verify scripts record `tcp udp5211 OK` while `udp udp5211 FAIL` in the same run (cell4 final verify).

Config delta between the clusters is small (`docs/ha-cluster-tcp.conf` vs `docs/ha-cluster-udp.conf` in the harness worktree): hostnames, cluster-id 23 vs 24, auth key, and addressing/VLAN/IPs only — no policy difference that would intentionally deny UDP on one cluster and allow it on the other.

## Impact

- Any UDP throughput/loss gate against the udp cluster (test-failover UDP legs, perf cells) cannot run; the failure surfaces as an iperf3 client error, easily misread as a target-provisioning problem.
- Unknown whether this is (a) a real userspace-dp UDP forwarding defect that only the udp cluster's topology/config triggers, or (b) a udp-cluster environment/config defect (e.g. fabric/heartbeat addressing, zone/interface assignment). Either way it needs root-causing rather than working around; if (a), it is a product bug hiding behind a harness-looking symptom.

## Investigation so far / ruled out

- Target server provisioning ruled out as sole cause: identical systemd iperf3 grid passes TCP on both clusters and UDP on the tcp cluster; target-side sockets verified listening (cell6: 12 sockets, `ss` shows 5205/5210).
- Not a single-port/busy-server artifact: reproduced on 5211, then on fresh 5205/5210, and after socket-service restart.
- Not total UDP breakage on the udp host: the control runs above were from the LAN hosts *through* each firewall, isolating the firewall path as the variable.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified and stated on this issue (product dataplane vs cluster-config/environment), with packet-level evidence (capture on LAN/WAN sides of the udp firewall during a failing UDP run).
- `iperf3 -c 172.16.80.211 -p 5211 -u -b 10M -t 2` from `udp:cluster-udp-host` completes with 0% unexpected loss, matching the tcp-cluster control.
- If the root cause is product code, this issue links the fix; if environment/config, the env/config is corrected and the verify cell (`targetprov/evidence/verify-udp.sh` shape: grid + TCP + UDP) passes end-to-end.

## #16305 — harness: wire-zone-matrix + wire-policy-deny hardcode loss-cluster addressing (10.0.61.0/24, 172.16.80.201, mlx0) — VOID no-prober on tcp/udp envs; parameterize from cluster env [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Defect

`wire-zone-matrix.sh` and `wire-policy-deny.sh` hardcode loss-cluster addressing, so on the tcp (`10.0.62.0/24`, targets `.210`) and udp (`10.0.63.0/24`, targets `.211`) userspace clusters they always `VOID no-prober` / `env-void` before measuring — the gates can never PASS/FAIL there.

## Evidence (proven, not inferred)

Ledger rows in `/var/worktrees/tcp-smoke/test/results/ledger.d/` (build `51a8aea3a642`, 2026-10-23):

- `wire_zone_matrix tcp-userspace-cluster verdict=VOID void_reason=no-prober` — e.g. `4c5f8c1c94827c47.json`, `646cfe6a3add9415.json`, `8bf8d73fa171e9b5.json` (repeated, every run)
- `wire_policy_deny tcp-userspace-cluster verdict=VOID void_reason=no-prober` — `0e0d007f58998b6c.json`
- Same on udp: `/var/worktrees/udp-smoke-evidence/udp-cell4.log` GATE2: `WIRE_GATE wire_zone_matrix VOID reason=no-prober cells_measured=0 …` → `make: *** [Makefile:1179: test-wire-zone-matrix] Error 2`, ledger `93a13966ea32d883.json: wire_zone_matrix VOID no-prober`

## Root cause — hardcoded loss values (files at HEAD `6372394b1b`)

`test/incus/wire-zone-matrix.sh`:

- `:417-419` `TRUST_ADDR="${TRUST_ADDR:-${LAN_HOST_IP:-10.0.61.102}}"`, `UNTRUST_ADDR="${UNTRUST_ADDR:-${MOUSE_TARGET_V4:-172.16.80.201}}"` (partially parameterized), but `DMZ_ADDR="${DMZ_ADDR:-172.16.50.201}"` is a bare loss literal with no env fallback.
- `:463,623-635` route save/clear/replace hardcodes prefixes `10.0.61.0/24 172.16.50.0/24 172.16.80.0/24` and gateways `via 172.16.80.8` / `via 172.16.50.8` — loss LAN subnet and loss WAN VIPs. On tcp/udp the LAN is `10.0.62.0/24` / `10.0.63.0/24` (env `LAN_ADDR`) and the WAN VIP differs (`172.16.50.10`/`.11`), so `route_is_clear`/replace targets the wrong network and `fail_void no-prober` fires at `:632-635`.
- `:597-599` DMZ prober provisioning hardcodes `MOUSE_TARGET_V6="2001:559:8585:50::201" MOUSE_TARGET_PF="mlx0" MOUSE_TARGET_VLAN="50"` regardless of cluster env (`SRIOV_PARENT`, VLAN, v6 prefix all differ per cluster).
- Selftest fixture `:288` also pins loss addrs (acceptable in a hermetic fixture, but shows the assumption).

`test/incus/wire-policy-deny.sh`:

- `:241` `SINK="${SINK:-${MOUSE_TARGET_V4:-172.16.80.201}}"` — the mouse-target fallback is loss-only; tcp/udp envs set `MOUSE_TARGET_V4` to `.210`/`.211`, but the sink *instance* resolution at `:306-317` assumes the loss mouse container (`loss:xpf-mouse-target` via `MOUSE_TARGET_NAME` default in `mouse-target-setup.sh:50`, PF `mlx0` at `:56`) exists on the target remote. On tcp/udp remotes there is no such managed container at that address, hence `VOID no-prober` (`:299-312`).

Cluster envs that prove the mismatch: `test/incus/tcp-userspace-cluster.env:24-34` (`LAN_ADDR=10.0.62.102/24`, `IPERF_TARGET4=172.16.80.210`, `MOUSE_TARGET_V4=.210`), `/var/worktrees/udp-smoke-master/test/incus/udp-userspace-cluster.env:22-32` (`10.0.63.102/24`, `.211`).

## Fix required

Parameterize every loss literal in both gates from the sourced cluster env (`cluster-env.sh` / `BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV` file): LAN prefix from `LAN_ADDR`/`LAN_HOST_IP`, DMZ address+V6+PF+VLAN, route prefixes and `via` gateways (WAN VIP / LAN VIP per env), and the policy-deny sink instance/PF. No `10.0.61.0/24`, `172.16.80.201`, `172.16.50.201`, `172.16.80.8`, `172.16.50.8`, or `mlx0` literal should remain as a live-path default when a non-loss env is selected; loss behaviour must stay byte-identical under the loss env.

## Acceptance

- `wire-zone-matrix` and `wire-policy-deny` under `BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV=test/incus/tcp-userspace-cluster.env` (and udp env) reach measurement (PASS/FAIL on the wire, not `VOID no-prober` caused by wrong addressing).
- Loss-cluster runs unchanged.
- Hermetic `--selftest`/`--fixture` still pass.

Discovered during tcp/udp smoke evidence collection (FileHarness assignment); not a duplicate of #11056 (that cohort is about gates never having run live on *loss* at all — this is wrong-cluster addressing defeating tcp/udp runs).

## #16306 — harness: test-connectivity Group12 v6 cells ping ::200 while tcp/udp targets are ::210/::211 — parameterize from cluster env [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Defect

`test-connectivity.sh` Group12 IPv6 cells ping/route/neigh `2001:559:8585:80::200` (the loss target) while the same run's IPv4 Group12 cells and both iperf cells use the selected cluster's targets. On tcp/udp clusters the v6 cell therefore measures a host that is not that cluster's target (`::210`/`::211`), producing a spurious FAIL (or meaningless PASS).

## Evidence

`/var/worktrees/udp-smoke-evidence/udp-cell4.log` GATE1 (udp env, targets `.211`/`::211`):

```
FAIL  cluster: Group12 IPv6 controlled reachability (LC_ALL=C ping -6 -c 2 -W 1 2001:559:8585:80::200; rc=1; output=PING 2001:559:8585:80::200 … 2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss)
harness-result: recorded test-connectivity udp-userspace-cluster verdict=FAIL
```

Note the IPv4 side of the same run correctly targets `172.16.80.211` via env, and the tcp witness log shows the correct v6 form on tcp: `2001:559:8585:80::210 … via fe80::…` (`/var/worktrees/16284-witness/logs/master4.log`).

## Root cause

`test/incus/test-connectivity.sh` Group12 (`:484-609`) hardcodes both families, but only v4 happens to be reachable-by-coincidence on loss; there is no parameterization at all:

- `:488,528,561` v4: `172.16.80.200` (route/ping/neigh)
- `:508,544,571` v6: `2001:559:8585:80::200` (route/ping/neigh)
- Labels at `:500,520,540,556,609` embed the same literals, so even the evidence text lies on tcp/udp.

By contrast the iperf cells in the same file (`:386,397`) correctly use `$IPERF_TARGET6`/`$IPERF_TARGET4` from `cluster-env.sh`, and `cluster-env.sh:75-76` plus each cluster env (`loss: .200/::200`, `tcp: .210/::210`, `udp: .211/::211`) already provide the right values. Group12 was never wired to them. The hermetic stub in `test/incus/cluster-cell-selftest.sh:281-311` also keys on the literal `2001:559:8585:80::200`, masking the drift.

## Fix required

Drive all Group12 route/ping/neighbor targets (v4 and v6) and their labels from `IPERF_TARGET4`/`IPERF_TARGET6` (cluster env), for both families symmetrically. Update `cluster-cell-selftest.sh` stubs/expectations to match the parameterized form.

## Acceptance

- On tcp env, Group12 v6 pings `2001:559:8585:80::210`; on udp env, `::211`; on loss, `::200` (unchanged).
- No literal `172.16.80.200` / `2001:559:8585:80::200` remains in the Group12 live path.
- `cluster-cell-selftest.sh` passes.

## #16307 — harness: userspace-ha-validation assert_forwarding_route rejects two-line cache route output (ha_route_lookup_verdict) — VOID on udp host [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Defect

`ha_route_lookup_verdict` (used by `userspace-ha-validation.sh assert_forwarding_route`) rejects the normal two-line `ip route get` output that ends with a `    cache` line, returning VOID (2) — "route output missing or ambiguous" — instead of accepting the forwarding route. The gate therefore VOIDs on hosts where the route cache line is printed (observed on the udp cluster host), aborting the whole smoke before any iperf measurement.

## Evidence

`/var/worktrees/udp-smoke-evidence/udp-cell4.log` GATE3:

```
VOID: ipv4 forwarding forwarding-route evidence unavailable for 172.16.80.211: route lookup: route output missing or ambiguous
harness-result: recorded userspace-ha-validation udp-userspace-cluster verdict=VOID
```

Ledger: `test/results/ledger.d/a6a413fdb95f80f8.json: userspace-ha-validation VOID … (rc=77) — the smoke aborted before reaching i…`.

The two-line shape is real kernel output, reproduced in the tcp witness log (`/var/worktrees/16284-witness/logs/master4.log`):

```
172.16.80.210 via 10.0.62.1 dev eth0 src 10.0.62.102 uid 0 
    cache 
```

## Root cause

`test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh:994-997` (`ha_route_lookup_verdict`):

```python
lines = [line.split() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
if len(lines) != 1:
    print("route lookup: route output missing or ambiguous", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(2)
```

Any second non-empty line — including the single-token `cache` continuation that `ip route get` emits for a cached route — trips the `len != 1` VOID. The sibling `ha_route_device` at `:950-953` has the identical `len(lines) != 1` rejection, so it fails the same way in `test-connectivity.sh` Group12. `scripts/userspace-ha-validation.sh:483-509` (`assert_forwarding_route`) maps verdict 2 to `void … exit 77`, so one cosmetic line aborts the entire validation. The hermetic tests (`test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh:591-606`) only fixture single-line routes (`ROUTE_GOOD='172.16.80.200 dev eth0 src 10.0.0.1'`), so the defect is test-invisible; note `ROUTE_DEVICE_MULTILINE` there is a genuinely-ambiguous two-device output and must keep returning 2.

## Fix required

Accept a trailing `cache` continuation line (single token `cache`, optionally with flags) as part of the one route entry in both `ha_route_lookup_verdict` and `ha_route_device`; keep rejecting genuinely ambiguous multi-route/multi-device output. Add selftest fixtures for the two-line cache form (v4; v6 `ip -6 route get` form if it can emit it).

## Acceptance

## #16308 — build: make cluster-deploy silently rebuilds stock deb, defeating DEB_VERSION bump (downgrade refusal) — respect prebuilt deb [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Defect

`make cluster-deploy` silently rebuilds a stock-version `.deb` — its `deb` prerequisite is `.PHONY` — discarding a prebuilt high-version deb in `dist-deb/`. Deploying the rebuilt stock deb (`0.0.<count>+g<sha>`) onto nodes already running a force-bumped deb (e.g. `99.0.x`, the standard downgrade-avoidance workflow, #16219) is refused by apt ("Packages were downgraded and -y was used without --allow-downgrades"), so the deploy fails *and* the operator's `DEB_VERSION` bump is defeated with no warning that a rebuild happened.

## Evidence

`/var/worktrees/16284-witness/logs/master4.log`: prebuilt `xpf_99.0.16284+601c5462a991_amd64.deb` present in `dist-deb/` (built via `make deb DEB_VERSION=99.0.16284+…`, log line `DEB_VERSION=99.0.16284+601c5462a991` → `MAKE_DEB_RC=0`), then plain `make cluster-deploy` (run-witness4.sh: "build + deploy via make cluster-deploy (NOT skip-build; recipe builds deb then deploys it)"):

```
DEPLOY_RC=2
==> Rolling deb deploy: secondary=node1, primary=node0
0 upgraded, 0 newly installed, 1 downgraded, 0 to remove and 19 not upgraded.
E: Packages were downgraded and -y was used without --allow-downgrades.
```

Same refusal in `master2.log:127-128`, `master5.log:21-22`, `master6.log:103-104`, `master7.log:34-35`. The workaround agents actually use is bypassing `make cluster-deploy` entirely with `XPF_CLUSTER_SKIP_BUILD=1` + direct `cluster-setup.sh deploy` (see `16284-witness/deploy-only.sh`, `run-witness5/6/7.sh`) — i.e. the documented entry point is unusable with a prebuilt deb.

## Root cause

- `Makefile:1503-1507,1518-1528`: `cluster-deploy: $(CLUSTER_DEPLOY_PREREQS)` with `CLUSTER_DEPLOY_PREREQS = deb` (non-FAST path), and `deb` is `.PHONY` (`Makefile:1631-1632`), so *every* `make cluster-deploy` unconditionally rebuilds with the default `DEB_VERSION ?= 0.0.$(DEB_GIT_COUNT)+g$(DEB_GIT_SHA)` (`Makefile:1624`) unless the caller repeats `DEB_VERSION=` on the same command line. A deb prebuilt minutes earlier under `99.0.x` is silently superseded.
- `test/incus/cluster-setup.sh:743` (`deploy_vm_deb`) and `:704` then pick `ls -t dist-deb/xpf_*.deb | head -1` — newest mtime wins, which is the just-rebuilt stock deb, not the intended prebuilt one. No version comparison, no refusal, no message.
- #16290 is the sibling failure (manifest never rewritten after a refused deploy); this issue is the upstream cause: the rebuild itself should not happen / should not win.

## Fix required

Respect a prebuilt deb: when `dist-deb/` already contains an `xpf_*.deb` whose version is >= the version `make deb` would produce (or when `DEB_VERSION` was used to prebuild), `make cluster-deploy` must deploy that deb instead of rebuilding a stock one — or, at minimum, fail closed with an explicit message naming both versions rather than silently rebuilding and dying inside apt. Selection in `cluster-setup.sh` should be by version (authoritative `DEB_VERSION`), not `ls -t` mtime.

## Acceptance

- `make deb DEB_VERSION=99.0.x+… && make cluster-deploy` (no repeated `DEB_VERSION`) deploys the `99.0.x` deb (apt reports upgrade/same-version, no downgrade refusal, no stock rebuild in the log).
- Fresh-tree `make cluster-deploy` with no prebuilt deb still builds and deploys as today.
- Loss/tcp/udp env behaviour otherwise unchanged.

Related (not duplicate): #16219 (documents the DEB_VERSION force-bump workflow this defeats), #16290 (manifest consequence after refusal).

## #16328 — harness: tcp env target/prober instance names still default to loss xpf-mouse-target — wire gates VOID no-prober on tcp (xpf-tcp-target unnamed, DMZ prober creation targets loss remote) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Defect

On the tcp userspace cluster the wire gates still resolve their capture/prober instances to the loss-cluster names, so they `VOID no-prober` before measuring — and the one path that could create the missing DMZ prober cannot work on tcp at all:

1. `MOUSE_TARGET_NAME` defaults to `xpf-mouse-target` on every cluster. That instance is absent on tcp (the real VLAN-80 target is `xpf-tcp-target`); `xpf-tcp-target` does carry tcpdump today, but nothing in the harness names it, so the gates never find it.
2. `wire-zone-matrix.sh`'s DMZ prober creation fails on tcp for two independent reasons (below).

Follow-up to #16305 (closed): that issue parameterized *addressing* (prefixes, gateways, DMZ/mouse IPs) and its hermetic selftests assert the wrong instance name (see Evidence) — the *instance-name* parameterization was missed, and its live acceptance on tcp/udp was explicitly queued in the commit's Risk line.

## Evidence (proven, not inferred)

Worktree `/var/worktrees/tcp-ctcp` @ `5fc385cc985d21137002cb877fd1e75074e74635` (includes #16305 commit `678b581c41`), 2026-10-23.

Resolved tcp env (hermetic, `env -i ... BPFRX_CLUSTER_ENV=test/incus/tcp-userspace-cluster.env` + `source test/incus/cluster-env.sh`):

```
REMOTE=tcp MOUSE_NAME=xpf-mouse-target MOUSE_REF=tcp:xpf-mouse-target
MOUSE_V4=172.16.80.210 MOUSE_V6=2001:559:8585:80::210
DMZ_ADDR=172.16.50.211 DMZ_V6=2001:559:8585:50::211
```

Live tcp inventory (`incus list tcp:`): only `cluster-tcp-host`, `xpf-tcp-fw0`, `xpf-tcp-fw1`, `xpf-tcp-target` — all RUNNING. Both lookups fail:

```
$ incus exec tcp:xpf-mouse-target -- echo ok
Error: Failed to fetch instance "xpf-mouse-target" in project "default": Instance not found
$ incus exec tcp:xpf-zone-matrix-dmz -- echo ok

## #16329 — harness: wire-policy-deny capture timeout (120s) does not fire through incus exec — tcp runs hung 1263s/279s (rc=143) and left unkillable orphan tcpdumps on tcp target [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Defect

`wire-policy-deny.sh` wraps its peer-side captures in `timeout $STEP_TIMEOUT` (120 s) *inside* `incus exec`, but that timeout does not bound the capture: when the harness is killed, the in-container `timeout`+`tcpdump` survive as orphans, still capturing. Live tcp runs hung **>17 min (1263 s ≈ 10.5× the 120 s timeout)** and **279 s**, both ending only when the harness process was SIGTERMed (rc=143) — and the orphaned captures were still alive afterwards. The capture must be bounded differently: killing the local `incus exec` client does not propagate into the container.

## Evidence (proven, not inferred)

Ledger rows in `/var/worktrees/tcp-ctcp/test/results/ledger.d/` (env `tcp-userspace-cluster`, build `5fc385cc985d`, 2026-10-23):

| run | ts (UTC) | duration_s | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1e2a57e79b379493` | 07:26:33 | **1263** (21 min) | VOID `harness-void: no WIRE_GATE ... verdict line in the output (rc=143)` |
| `e8e0d0b9061a9cdd` | 07:41:03 | **279** | VOID, same rc=143 |

rc=143 = 128+SIGTERM: both runs were killed externally; neither produced a verdict line. STEP_TIMEOUT is 120 s (`wire-policy-deny.sh:300`).

Smoking gun — orphaned captures still running on `tcp:xpf-tcp-target` after the runs died (observed live, `ps -o pid,ppid,etime,args`):

```
10482  ppid=1  53:33  tcpdump -i any -n udp and dst host 172.16.80.210 and ( dst port 54901 or dst port 54902 )
10491  ppid=1  22:41  tcpdump -i any -n udp and dst host 172.16.80.210 and ( dst port 54901 or dst port 54902 )
10494  ppid=1  16:01  tcpdump -i any -n udp and dst host 172.16.80.210 and ( dst port 54901 or dst port 54902 )
```

The filter is verbatim the gate's baseline-capture invocation (`wire-policy-deny.sh:393`, ports 54901/54902 = PROBE_PORT/CONTROL_PORT defaults). Three orphans = three capture starts whose parents died. They are parented to PID 1, and — worse — they are **unkillable from subsequent `incus exec` sessions**: `kill`/`pkill` from root exec sessions return `Permission denied` (tcpdump's capability bounding set / cross-session pid-namespace view), and the gate's own cleanup (`wire-policy-deny.sh:484`, `pkill -f 'tcpdump.*$PROBE_PORT'`, stderr discarded) fails silently for the same reason. Cleanup of these three was attempted with `incus exec --user 0` and plain root `sh -c 'kill ...'`; both denied. They persist at filing time and need container restart or host-side removal.

Contrast (the timeout mechanism itself is fine): interactively, `incus exec tcp:xpf-tcp-target -- timeout 5 sleep 30` returns rc=124 at 5 s, and `timeout -k 2 5 tcpdump -c 1` exits cleanly. The 120 s `timeout` *does* fire for a foreground exec that stays attached. [INFERENCE] The failure is the composition: the gate backgrounds the exec (`... &`, `CAP_PID=$!` at `:393-394`, `:547-548`, `:510-511`), then stops it with a *local* `kill $CAP_PID` + `wait` (`:404-405`, `:568-569`, `:521-522`). Killing the local client leaves the in-container `timeout` orphaned to PID 1; the container-side `timeout` therefore keeps tcpdump alive until its own expiry from *its* start — and with a wedged/killed harness the last-resort local `wait` never runs either. `wire-gate-lib.sh:972` (`trap '' EXIT INT TERM` in `wire_gate_finalize`) additionally makes the finalizer ignore the very SIGTERM that killed these runs.

Same pattern in sibling gates (missed sites if only policy-deny is fixed): `wire-zone-matrix.sh:53` (backgrounded `incus exec ... timeout 300 tcpdump`, stopped via `pkill` from a *new* exec at `:59` — same cross-session kill problem), `wire-appmatch-twins.sh:274,359,405`.

## Consequence

- A hung capture converts a bounded 120 s step into an unbounded run: the two tcp cells burned 1263 s + 279 s and still recorded only `VOID harness-void (rc=143)` — no PASS/FAIL/VOID verdict from the gate itself.
- Orphaned tcpdumps accumulate on the target (3 at filing), each holding a BPF filter on the measured interface; later captures contend with them and the target's state no longer matches what any gate set up.
- The restore path cannot clean them up (cross-session `pkill` denied + output discarded), so the leak is permanent for the container's lifetime.

## Fix direction

Bound the capture differently — do not rely on `timeout` inside a backgrounded `incus exec` plus a local kill:

- Run tcpdump in-container under its own bounded lifetime that does not depend on the exec session staying attached (e.g. `tcpdump -c <count>` / `--time-stamp` self-termination sized to the burst, a detached in-container `timeout ... & echo $!` with the pid recorded and killed from the *same* session model that can actually signal it, or capture to a file in-container and `incus file pull` it with a bounded exec).

*(truncated — 49 lines total)*

## #16333 — test-host-inbound: hi_wildcard_socket_pids misses '*:port' wildcard spelling from modern ss — gate FAILs live listeners [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-23)

## Defect

`hi_wildcard_socket_pids` in `test/incus/host-inbound-lib.sh` matches only wildcard local addresses spelled `0.0.0.0:<port>` or `[::]:<port>`:

```awk
$4 ~ /^(0\.0\.0\.0|\[::\]):[0-9]+$/ { ... }
```

Modern `ss` (iproute2) prints a wildcard listener as `*:22` (e.g. `LISTEN 0 128 *:22 *:* users:(("python3",pid=...,fd=3))`). Such a row matches neither alternative, emits no pid, and `hi_socket_ownership_verdict` therefore returns FAIL ("port N has no wildcard-bound listener") even though a live, externally-reachable wildcard listener owned by this port's marker process is present.

## Consequence

The `test-host-inbound.sh` listener-presence gate (fail-closed per #9637/#12912) dies before any host-inbound cell is scored on nodes whose `ss` prints `*:<port>`. A live listener is reported as absent — fail-closed, but a false FAIL that blocks the whole smoke.

## Fix scope

- `hi_wildcard_socket_pids`: also accept `*:<port>` as a wildcard local address (exact port match retained via the existing `addrport == p` check; `*:220` must not satisfy port 22).
- `*` must not become fail-open: loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) and specific-address rows stay excluded; foreign pids still emitted for the caller's ownership rejection.
- Update the helper header comment to name the `*` wildcard spelling.
- Hermetic rows in `test/incus/host-inbound-selftest.sh`: `SS_*` rows for `*:22` matching, `*:220` near-miss exclusion, and a `checkg` gate row proving `*:23` owned passes (and/or foreign `*` holder fails).
- Validation: `bash test/incus/host-inbound-selftest.sh` (via `make test-host-inbound-lib`) passes; the negative rows still FAIL as before.

## Out of scope

No change to ownership verdict logic, prober, or cell scoring.

## #16417 — #14963 persistent-NAT batch peer cap is skipped for Generation==0 first contact, which still persists a new origin; 17+ gen-0 origins make the generation state file unloadable on restart [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14963 persistent-NAT batch peer cap is skipped for Generation==0 first contact, which still persists a new origin; 17+ gen-0 origins make the generation state file unloadable on restart

**Finding ID:** R3-F03-02
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — needs an authenticated HA sync peer that emits batches at generation 0 from 17+ distinct origin ids, i.e. a forged or corrupt sender. Genuine senders start at Generation 1. The consequence is the one #14963 set out to close: persistent-NAT lease export/import fails on every restart until the state file is removed by hand. There is no enforcement loss.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
a single bad peer build or a corrupt stream durably bricks persistent-NAT failover continuity on this node. A full map also refuses a re-imaged genuine peer's new origin ("peer limit reached").

**Contract:** ca901fc93e/#14963: "refuse a new distinct origin at/over maxPersistentNatGenerationPeers11486" so the state file cannot exceed the loader's peer limit. The forwarded-clear sibling caps every unseen origin regardless of generation.

**Trace:** peer sync message -> decodePersistentNatLeaseBatchPayloadLayout -> ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch -> gen-0 unseen arm persists origin -> after 17 origins the next restart's loadPersistentNatLeaseGenerationLocked fails -> every Export/Import returns that error.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_idle_leases_8121.go:300` `} else if !known && batch.Generation > 0 && len(state.RemoteGenerations) >= maxPersistentNatGenerationPeers11486 {`. `:312-317` `if !known && batch.Generation == 0 { ... state.RemoteGenerations[batch.OriginID] = 0; ... storePersistentNatLeaseGenerationLocked(state)`. `persistent_nat_generation_11486.go:15` cap = 16. `:93-95` the loader rejects `len(state.RemoteGenerations) > max`. The new-state init sets `Generation: 1`. `pkg/cluster/sync_persistent_nat_lease_8121.go:406-429` the decoder accepts any uint64 generation.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestR3F03Gen0 -count=1 -v` (fixture RUN/workers/f03/evidence/zz_r3f03_gen0_peercap_probe_test.go). Observed: `generation=1 accepted=16/20 remote_origins=16 restart_load_err=<fake-helper status error>` (control: capped; the load error is the fake helper's, not the peer limit) and `generation=0 accepted=20/20 remote_origins=20 restart_load_err=persistent-NAT lease generation state exceeds peer limit`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
apply the peer cap to every unseen origin (drop `batch.Generation > 0`), mirroring the clear path; consider age/LRU pruning. Acceptance: the generation=0 row caps at 16 and the restart load succeeds.

## Full validated claim

## #16418 — #14968 fold-semantics guard ignores a global policy's from-zone/to-zone match dimensions: cross-zone permit widening and scoped+unscoped deny narrowing fold unpoisoned [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14968 fold-semantics guard ignores a global policy's from-zone/to-zone match dimensions: cross-zone permit widening and scoped+unscoped deny narrowing fold unpoisoned

**Finding ID:** R3-F03-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — the tolerant path only (boot `Store.Load` and HA `SyncApply` of a config carrying duplicate same-named GLOBAL policy statements, which strict commit refuses under #3473). The consequence is a silent enforcement change. A permit applies to (zone, source) pairs no statement permitted, or a deny no longer covers traffic from zones its own statement denied, so that traffic falls to later globals or the default policy. #14968 was filed High at the same reach; the residual is rated Medium because reach needs a legacy or hand-placed config.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
it affects an appliance booting or receiving by HA sync a config with duplicate global policy names, e.g. a pre-#3473 persisted config. The widened permit or narrowed deny is enforced silently until the config is rewritten, with no warning that the fold changed semantics.

**Contract:** commit 1873289588 (#14968) and the doc block at `pkg/config/dup_instance_merge_8752.go:46-67`. `PolicyMatch.FromZones/ToZones` (`pkg/config/types_security.go:766-784`) are match predicates of a global policy, where an empty slice means all zones.

**Trace:** on-disk hierarchical config with two `global { policy p1 {...} policy p1 {...} }` -> lenient compile -> #8752 fold unions match children -> foldChangesPolicySemantics14968 returns false -> no LenientContentDropped -> helper accepts the snapshot -> the merged global enforces.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`dup_instance_merge_8752.go:661-676` `matchDimensionsDiffer14968` compares only `SourceAddresses`, `DestinationAddresses`, `Applications`. `:617-650` the restrictive-source leg compares excluded flags/lists and schedulers only, never zone scope. `types_security.go:769-774` "an empty slice means 'all zones' ... a packet's from-zone must be in FromZones AND its to-zone must be in ToZones".

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestVF03Fold$' -count=1 -v`; fixture RUN/verify/vf03/probes/zz_vf03_fold_probe_test.go, output RUN/verify/vf03/fold_probe.out. Controls: `gl same from-zone src-differ` poisoned=false (legitimate one-dimension union); `zp src-disjoint x dst-disjoint` poisoned=true. Defect: `gl permit from-zone-differ + src-differ` -> from=[trust untrust] src=[10.0.1.0/25 10.0.2.0/25] poisoned=false (now permits (trust,10.0.2/25) and (untrust,10.0.1/25)); `gl deny scoped + unscoped` -> act=deny from=[trust] poisoned=false (10.0.2.0/25 from untrust no longer denied). Identical on both entry points.

## Acceptance / fix direction
count FromZones and ToZones as match dimensions (empty or `any` = universal) in the cross-product check. Poison a surviving deny/reject when any restrictive source's zone scope is not a subset of the merged scope, and handle empty-as-universal before the union narrows it. Acceptance: both defect rows poisoned=true, both controls unchanged, and the existing #14968 tests stay green. Fix together with R3-F03-04 (same function).

## #16419 — #14968 cross-product predicate is unsound: the per-dimension containment exemption still mints new tuples ("ssh from 10.0.1.0/25" + "http from any" folds to ssh+http from any, unpoisoned) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14968 cross-product predicate is unsound: the per-dimension containment exemption still mints new tuples ("ssh from 10.0.1.0/25" + "http from any" folds to ssh+http from any, unpoisoned)

**Finding ID:** R3-F03-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — same tolerant-path reach as R3-F03-03. The consequence is a permit widened to tuples no statement permitted, e.g. a management protocol exposed to every source.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
an appliance tolerant-loading a duplicate-name zone-pair policy whose two statements trade a narrow and a wide dimension silently permits the cross product. This is the exact widening #14968 claims to refuse.

**Contract:** `dup_instance_merge_8752.go:63-67` "Folds whose merged semantics ARE the union of the statements — a permit pair differing in at most one dimension ... stay unpoisoned". The code comment `:654-660` claims a contained dimension "cannot contribute a new combination", which holds per dimension but not for the tuple.

**Trace:** as R3-F03-03, through zone-pair policies (`from-zone trust to-zone untrust`).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`dup_instance_merge_8752.go:661-676` (`n++` only when neither set contains the other); `:611` (`>= 2` threshold); `:680-697` (`any` is universal, so `any` contains everything and is never counted).

**Probe:** same run as R3-F03-03 (RUN/verify/vf03/fold_probe.out). Control `zp src-equal app-differ` poisoned=false (exact union, legitimate). Defect `zp src-contained + app-disjoint` (p1: src 10.0.1.0/25 app junos-ssh; p1: src any app junos-http) -> src=[10.0.1.0/25 any] app=[junos-ssh junos-http] poisoned=false, so ssh is now permitted from any source. The reporter's RUN/workers/f03/evidence/fold_subset_probe.out also shows src-superset + dst-disjoint unpoisoned.

## Acceptance / fix direction
poison a merged permit unless the explicit-permit sources are set-equal in all but at most one dimension, or one statement dominates the other in every dimension. Acceptance: the defect rows are poisoned, the controls are unchanged, and the existing #14968 controls stay green.

## #16420 — #14974's VRF master for the IPsec NFQUEUE divert is sampled at stageIpsecCapture, before the same apply enslaves a freshly created st0 into its routing-instance VRF; first deploy and every reboot install the iifname-only rule that never ... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14974's VRF master for the IPsec NFQUEUE divert is sampled at stageIpsecCapture, before the same apply enslaves a freshly created st0 into its routing-instance VRF; first deploy and every reboot install the iifname-only rule that never matches enslaved traffic

**Finding ID:** R3-F03-05
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The ordering defect is real at d1ea69f9aa, and I confirmed it again. daemon_apply.go:604 runs applyVRFReconcile, :641 runs applyInterfaceReconcile (ApplyXfrmi at daemon_apply_interfaces.go:464 has no VRF bind, and pkg/routing/xfrm.go never sets a master), and :662 runs stageIpsecCapture, which samples link MasterIndex in buildIpsecCaptureQueuePlan at ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1110-1118. Only after that does :676 applyDataplaneAndHACore call rebindRoutingInstanceMembers (daemon_apply_dataplane] Verifier text: — potential, inherited from #14974 (filed Critical, 3-way MATERIAL). VRF-enslaved route-based VPN traffic is not NFQUEUE-captured for userspace policy enforcement from the apply that creates the xfrmi (the first commit, and every boot because xfrmi devices do not survive reboot) until some later apply re-stages. The divert chain is policy ACCEPT, so uncaptured packets continue on the kernel path. This is demonstrated at the ordering and component level, not end-to-end.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
it reopens the #14974 bypass on every boot and on the commit that adds a VRF-scoped route-based VPN, for as long as no other apply runs. The divert table looks installed and healthy, so nothing surfaces the gap.

**Contract:** eedc0bf604 (#14974): `buildIpsecCaptureQueuePlan` resolves Master from the live link's MasterIndex, and `emitIpsecDivertRules` renders `iifname <master> meta sdifname <tunnel>` for enslaved tunnels so decrypted tunnel traffic is captured.

**Trace:** reboot -> boot apply -> step 0a cannot bind absent st0.0 (WARN) -> ApplyXfrmi creates st0.0 (no master) -> stage builds key{STN st0.0, Master ""} -> dataplane core rebinds st0.0 into vrf-X -> capture commit installs `iifname "st0.0" queue N` -> decrypted packets present iifname=vrf-X / sdifname=st0.0 -> no match -> chain ACCEPT -> not queued. This persists until the next apply (operator commit, DNS-address refresh, config sync, apply-debt retry).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:604` applyVRFReconcile (step 0a, st0 not yet created on boot) -> `:641` applyInterfaceReconcile (`daemon_apply_interfaces.go:464` ApplyXfrmi creates st0) -> `:662` `stageIpsecCapture(cfg)` -> `:676` applyDataplaneAndHACore (`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:621` `d.rebindRoutingInstanceMembers(cfg)`; comment `:608-613`: "Step 0a runs before applyInterfaceReconcile creates tunnel/xfrmi devices") -> `:716` `commitIpsecCaptureStage(captureOld, captureStaged)` with the staged spec. `ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1110-1118` `master := ""; if link.Attrs().MasterIndex > 0 {...}`. `:58` the rule copies `handle.Key.Master`. `pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert.go:872-880` renders `iifname st0.N` alone when Master=="" (chain policy accept, `:653`). The supervisor tick (`ipsec_supervisor_loop_9506.go:39` reconcileIpsecCaptureAuthority) only re-announces, and the topology census (`ipsec_topology_owner_9506.go:184-260`) marks a VRF master SAFE without comparing it to the installed divert.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestVF03StageSamplesMaster -count=1 -v`; fixture RUN/verify/vf03/probes/zz_vf03_stage_master_probe_test.go, output RUN/verify/vf03/stage_master_probe.out. Stage-time link MasterIndex=0 (fresh st0) -> `inet-forward rule: iifname="st0.0" sdifname-match=false`. Control MasterIndex=22 (later apply) -> `iifname="vrf-blue" sdifname-match=true`. Limits: it does not drive applyConfigLocked or a kernel. Lab check: on a node with `routing-instances X interface st0.0` and a route-based VPN, reboot, then compare `nft list table inet xpf_ipsec_divert` (expect only `iifname "st0.0"`) with `ip -d link show st0.0` (master vrf-X), and send tunnel traffic that policy should deny.

## Acceptance / fix direction
resolve Master after the RI member bind: bind freshly created xfrmi into their VRF inside applyInterfaceReconcile right after ApplyXfrmi, or re-stage capture after rebindRoutingInstanceMembers. Also have the topology census force a re-stage (or refuse OPEN) when a tuple's MasterIndex differs from the installed divert's Master. Acceptance: a daemon-level test where the apply creates the xfrmi and rebindRoutingInstanceMembers enslaves it ends with an `iifname vrf-X sdifname st0.0` divert rule. The lab check above shows the vrf rule after reboot.

## #16421 — #14973 SSH-apply rollback strips ALL managed faillock rules even when the failing apply only upgraded xpf's own pre-#14973 (legacy) rules, leaving the host with less lockout than before the apply [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14973 SSH-apply rollback strips ALL managed faillock rules even when the failing apply only upgraded xpf's own pre-#14973 (legacy) rules, leaving the host with less lockout than before the apply

**Finding ID:** R3-F04-03
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — this is a protection removed by a fix, but it is narrow. It needs a non-appliance install (appliance hosts skip faillock), xpf's legacy managed blocks still present, and a FIRST post-upgrade SSH apply that fails. The result: SSH cross-connection password lockout disappears with no alarm. A later successful apply re-installs it; a persistent apply failure keeps it off. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Pre-existing non-appliance deployments that hit an SSH apply error right after upgrading silently lose SSH brute-force lockout. That includes the root lockout #14973 set out to add. The apply error says nothing about PAM state.

**Contract:** the comment at pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1023-1035 says the rollback takes "the same posture as revertDropIn". revertDropIn restores the PRIOR file, at :1206-1219. The same comment says "stripping is a no-op when this apply changed nothing (pre-existing admin faillock survives)". stripPAMFaillockBlock recognises legacy bodies "so hosts carrying the old rules can be upgraded".

**Trace:** a host runs a pre-#14973 build with legacy managed blocks → upgrade → first applySSHConfig rewrites the blocks to the `even_deny_root` bodies (changed=true) → a later step fails (sshd -t, reload, drop-in write, or a #14111 render error) → the deferred strip removes every managed block → common-auth has no pam_faillock → sshd PAM auth runs with no lockout.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go@d1ea69f9aa:1014 `faillockInstalled, err := applySSHPAMFaillockChanged()` is true for a legacy→current rewrite. :1037 `stripSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback(faillockInstalled)` runs on any retErr. pkg/daemon/ssh_faillock_11492.go:270-274 `stripSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback` → `setSSHPAMFaillock(false)` strips both current and legacy blocks. No pre-apply bytes are kept.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestF04FaillockLegacyUpgradeStrippedOnFailedApply -count=1 -v`. Fixture: RUN/workers/f04/evidence/zz_f04_faillock_legacy_probe_test.go. Output: RUN/verify/vf04/F04-03.out. CONTROL: `success apply err=<nil> faillock-lines=3 hasCurrent=true`. Defect: `INFO stripped managed PAM faillock rules on SSH apply rollback`, then `faillock-lines-after=0 (were 3 before)`, and common-auth is left as bare pam_unix/pam_deny/pam_permit. Limit: the probe's key-exchange token is rejected at strict commit (pkg/config/schema_validators_system.go:439), so that exact trigger needs a tolerant config. Strict-path triggers are `sshd -t` and reload failures (not executed).

## Acceptance / fix direction
have applySSHPAMFaillockChanged return the pre-apply common-auth bytes, or a "managed-before" flag. On rollback, restore those bytes (or re-render the legacy body) instead of stripping. Acceptance: the probe's failed-apply row ends with the original 3 legacy lines, and the existing stock-stack rollback tests still end at stock.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf04.md)</summary>

## #16422 — On a tolerated (lenient-load or HA-sync) config, the pre-pass warn-skips the six #15002 shapes but the production real pass hard-rejects them. Apply aborts after the Phase 2 host mutation, so boot or peer-sync publishes no dataplane snap... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
On a tolerated (lenient-load or HA-sync) config, the pre-pass warn-skips the six #15002 shapes but the production real pass hard-rejects them. Apply aborts after the Phase 2 host mutation, so boot or peer-sync publishes no dataplane snapshot. This is the unfixed warn-skip half of #15943 H11-01.

**Finding ID:** R3-F04-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — It has the same consequence #15002 (A08-03, Medium) was filed for: a boot or HA-sync of such a config publishes no dataplane snapshot. At boot that means no snapshot at all. On sync the secondary stays on its previous snapshot while its interfaces/VLANs/addresses were already reconciled by Phase 2. Reach is the tolerant ingress only: a persisted pre-strict-gate config, or a push from an un-upgraded peer. The divergence-accounting half that #15943 called High was fixed by 2d8d1925f2 (the partial result now reaches `abortAfterHostMutation`). What remains is the abort itself. [reporter: Medium]

## Mechanism / impact
An upgraded node whose persisted active config carries one of these shapes boots with no dataplane snapshot. The operator was told by the compile warning that the rule would be skipped, and #15002 / #15943 are both closed as fixed. The HA secondary receiving such a config fails every sync apply after Phase 2 has moved its interfaces. Recovery requires an operator commit that removes the rule.

**Contract:** #15002 consequence/fix direction says a tolerated shape must not make boot/HA-sync "compile no dataplane snapshot", and asks for warn-plus-skip "matching the userspace builders". #15943 H11-01 §6 fix acceptance reads: "either the pre-pass rejects these shapes pre-mutation, or production warn-and-skips identically to the pre-pass; plus result (not nil) on all post-Phase-2 failures". The #4960 pre-pass contract (pkg/dataplane/compiler_validate_4960.go header) is that a pre-pass that accepts what a later phase rejects reproduces the #4960 post-mutation abort.

Make the six sites warn-and-skip on BOTH passes (drop the `isValidationPass` gate, or key it on a tolerant-config property), so the real pass omits the rule the way the userspace builder already disarms it. That is the regression #15943 §6 named (`TestCompileConfigTolerantNATShapesDoNotAbortPostZonePhase`).

## #16423 — #14997 REBIND gate keys on teardown content only: a non-granting REBIND Reply that omits the held IA_NA address and offers a different live one is accepted, and the held WAN address is removed in one packet [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#14997 REBIND gate keys on teardown content only: a non-granting REBIND Reply that omits the held IA_NA address and offers a different live one is accepted, and the held WAN address is removed in one packet

**Finding ID:** R3-F04-05
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — an on-link WAN host that answers the multicast REBIND (which requires the granting server to stay silent past T2, the same prerequisite as #14997, filed High) replaces the firewall's WAN IPv6 address with one of its choosing. The held address is deconfigured, so outbound IPv6 and inbound services, IPsec and DDNS on that address break until a fresh acquisition or a restart. The attacker's prefix is NOT adopted for IA_PD. Demonstrated at the matcher/parse layer; the kernel address removal is static. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A WAN-side on-link attacker (shared ISP segment or cable/DSL access LAN) can move the firewall's IPv6 WAN address to an unrouted or colliding value during any REBIND window. That breaks IPv6 egress and every service bound to the address. Recovery only comes through lease expiry and SOLICIT, or a restart.

**Contract:** RFC 8415 §18.2.10.1 (Reply for ... Renew, or Rebind), verified verbatim: "Leave unchanged any information about leases the client has recorded in the IA but that were not included in the IA from the server", and "Add any new leases in the IA option". The #14997 commit 0ab128349b says teardown content from a non-granting REBIND server must be refused, and that partners may only EXTEND. Its own control asserts that an accepted partner Reply keeps the HELD address.

**Trace:** the granting server is silent past T2 → the client multicasts REBIND → the attacker replies with its DUID, an IA_NA holding only a new live IAADDR, and an optional live IA_PD → v6RenewMatcher accepts (no teardown content) → parseV6ReplyChecked selects the new address and stores the attacker DUID → the run loop runs commitLease → removeAddress(held) and applyAddress(new) → recompile with the new WAN address.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/dhcp/renew.go@d1ea69f9aa:103 `if rebind && !sameDUID(serverID, expectedServer) && v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding(req, resp) {` is the only content gate. :123-160 v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding returns true only for a non-Success status or valid-lifetime-0 elements. It never checks that the held IAADDR is still present. pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6.go:533 `m.commitLease(key, renewed.lease, committed, ...)` on an accepted REBIND. pkg/dhcp/commit.go:259-260 `if prev != nil && prev.Address.IsValid() && prev.Address != lease.Address { m.removeAddress(key.iface, prev) }`.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run 'TestF04RebindReplacementFromNonGrantingServer|TestVF04RebindLegs' -count=1 -v`. Fixtures: RUN/workers/f04/evidence/zz_f04_rebind_replace_probe_test.go and RUN/verify/vf04/probes/zz_vf04_rebind_probe_test.go. Output: RUN/verify/vf04/F04-05.out. Control: attacker zero-lifetime REBIND `accepted=false`. Defect: `replace-IA_NA-only: rebindAccepted=true leaseAddr=2606:4700::bad/128 held=2606:4700::50/128 serverIsAttacker=true`. Handoff limit: `pure-extension: ... serverIsAttacker=true | nextRENEW attackerTeardownAccepted=true thirdDUIDTeardownAccepted=false`, where the third-DUID refusal is the RENEW identity-gate control. Limits: no wire capture and no kernel; the address removal is from commitLease source.

## Acceptance / fix direction
on a REBIND Reply from a non-granting server, treat a requested IA that omits a held binding element as not-an-extension. Either refuse it (count it as a teardown reject), or follow §18.2.10.1: keep the held address and record the new one only as an addition. Separately, decide whether a non-granting Reply should take over the RENEW binding when it changed content. Acceptance: the replace-IA_NA-only row is rejected (counter increments) or keeps the held address, and the #14997 partner-extension control is still accepted.

- **Refutation attempt:** I checked selectIANAAddress's blocked-class filter (#14185): it refuses loopback, link-local and protected ranges but accepts a global attacker address. ## #16425 — #15038 probeSourceFor picks the first VIP/unit address regardless of the target's family, so an interface-bound target whose family is not first on the unit is never measured on the primary [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#15038 probeSourceFor picks the first VIP/unit address regardless of the target's family, so an interface-bound target whose family is not first on the unit is never measured on the primary

**Finding ID:** R3-F05-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — the RG's ip-monitoring failover sensor is silently inert on the node that owns the RG, so loss of that upstream gateway never demotes the primary (HA ownership/recovery). Bounded: it needs the new #15038 `interface <unit>` binding plus a dual-stack unit whose `family inet6` precedes `family inet` in the tree (authoring order), or an IPv6 literal under `family inet` (whose missing address validation is owned by H23-03). Demonstrated at component level, not on a cluster [reporter: High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
On the primary, an operator who binds ip-monitoring to a dual-stack RETH unit gets a sensor that never fires. A dead upstream keeps traffic on the wrong node until manual failover, and status cannot show a failure that is never measured.

**Contract:** #15038 (fix d9e033dae0): "the primary probes from the RG VIP on the target interface ... On the primary it stays a completed failure". Losing that gateway must therefore demote the primary, as an unbound target does (pkg/cluster/README.md ip-monitoring section; CLAUDE.md HA monitor notes).

**Trace:** `interfaces reth0 unit 0 family inet6 address 2001:db8::2/64` then `family inet address 10.0.0.2/24`, plus `redundancy-group 1 ip-monitoring family inet 10.0.0.1 weight 255 interface reth0.0` → compileRGIPMonitoring (Interface=reth0.0) → Monitor.pollCycle → probeSourceFor (primary) → src=2001:db8::2 → defaultICMPDialer("udp4","2001:db8::2") fails → completed=false every cycle → no ip:10.0.0.1 debt → RG stays primary.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/cluster/monitor.go:684-701 `if vips := cfg.RethVIPsForRG(rg.ID)[device]; len(vips) > 0 { return stripCIDR(vips[0]), device }` / `:697 return stripCIDR(unitAddrs[0]), device`, with no family test against target.Address. pkg/config/reth_vips.go:56-75 appends unit.Addresses in tree order. pkg/cluster/monitor.go:1253 `conn, err := dialer(network, task.src)` → `return false, false` on bind failure. :491 `if !res.completed { continue }` leaves dampening untouched. Observed (configstore): with inet6 authored first, reth0.0 Addresses=[2001:db8::2/64 10.0.0.2/24], and an IPv4 target 10.0.0.1 with `interface reth0.0` commits clean.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run TestF05IPMonitorPrimaryDualStack -v` (workers/f05/evidence/zz_f05_ipmon_family_probe_test.go) → verify/vf05/cluster_ipmon.out: "defect: v4 target, unit lists inet6 first primary src=\"::1\" -> reachable=false completed=false"; control "v4 target, unit lists inet first src=\"127.0.0.1\" -> reachable=true completed=true"; end-to-end unreachable gateway, 5 polls: defect weight=255, control weight=0. Reachability: verify/vf05/probes/zz_vf05_ipmon_test.go → verify/vf05/configstore_probes.out rows v4-target-inet6-authored-first / control-v4-target-inet-first / v6-target-under-family-inet / family-inet6. Limits: loopback addresses are used so that binds are meaningful; ping_group_range is open on this host; no RETH member/VIP install was run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In probeSourceFor, select the first VIP/unit address of target.Address's family. Reject at strict commit a bound target whose unit has no address of that family, and validate that target.Address and secondary-ip-address are IPv4 under `family inet`. Consider treating a bind failure on the PRIMARY as an alarmed failure. Acceptance: the defect row yields completed=true and the end-to-end weight drops to 0; the control rows stay unchanged.

## #16426 — VRRP AF_PACKET receiver drops VID-0 priority-tagged native adverts as if they were tagged-sibling frames (#15049 regression) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
VRRP AF_PACKET receiver drops VID-0 priority-tagged native adverts as if they were tagged-sibling frames (#15049 regression)

**Finding ID:** R3-F05-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — when hit, the backup never hears the master, its master-down timer expires and both nodes hold the VIP (dual MASTER, ARP flapping). Bounded to VRRP-running modes (legacy `no-private-rg-election` RETH VRRP, standalone vrrp-group on untagged units/plain interfaces) on L2 paths that deliver priority-tagged frames (a peer VF/NIC or switch adding 802.1p with VID 0). Shown at the receive-loop level [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Split VIP ownership is an HA-ownership failure. It persists for as long as the tagging environment exists and recovers only when the tagging stops or the code changes.

**Contract:** #15049 (fix dd16fcc4d0) drops only frames that belong to a tagged sibling election and keeps untagged native adverts. Linux treats VID 0 as native (`__netif_receive_skb_core`: only a non-zero `skb_vlan_tag_get_id` marks OTHERHOST; the tag is cleared and the frame is delivered on the parent).

**Trace:** Peer advert, priority-tagged on the wire (VID 0, PCP 6) → NIC strip or skb_vlan_untag → ETH_P_ALL tap delivers with PACKET_AUXDATA VLAN_VALID tci=0xC000 → receiverAfPacket (!boundToVLAN) drops → no advert enqueued → master-down timer (≈3×advert) → backup becomes MASTER while the peer remains MASTER.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/vrrp/instance_receive.go:370-374 `if !boundToVLAN { if _, tagged := afPacketAuxdataVLANTag(oob, oobn); tagged { continue } }`; :435 `if aux.Status&unix.TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID == 0 { return 0, false }` then `return aux.Vlan_tci, true`. The VID is never tested. pkg/vrrp/manager.go:1550 `proto := htons(unix.ETH_P_ALL)`: the socket is a ptype_all tap that sees the skb before vlan_do_receive, with the tag in metadata, and af_packet sets VLAN_VALID whenever skb_vlan_tag_present. The 15049 harness treats tci 0 as "no auxdata", so no cell can express VID 0.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run TestF05 -v` (workers/f05/evidence/zz_f05_prio_tag_probe_test.go) → verify/vf05/vrrp_priotag.out: control (no auxdata) ge-0-0-1/reth1 "enqueued=[10.0.61.2]"; defect PCP6/VID0 tci=0xC000 "enqueued=[]" on both; reference VLAN-100 "enqueued=[]". Limits: kernel cmsg contents are synthesized from the af_packet source, not captured from a NIC.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Drop only when `aux.Vlan_tci & 0x0fff != 0` (and optionally only when the parent actually has tagged VRRP siblings). Add a VID-0 cell to vlan_tag_present_15049_test.go with an auxdata encoding that can express tci 0 plus VLAN_VALID. Acceptance: the VID-0 row enqueues and the VLAN-100 row still drops.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf05.md)</summary>

Shown at the receive-loop level [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High for the code and kernel behaviour; Medium for how common priority tagging is in the field.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — the reporter's harness drives the real receiverAfPacket loop through the afPacketRecvmsg seam with PACKET_AUXDATA cmsgs. Kernel delivery semantics are STATIC (source reasoning). No lab frames were sent.

Linux treats VID 0 as native (`__netif_receive_skb_core`: only a non-zero `skb_vlan_tag_get_id` marks OTHERHOST; the tag is cleared and the frame is delivered on the parent).
- **Adversarial analysis:** Protection: single VRRP master per VIP. Actor: an L2 element on the segment (NIC/VF port-priority config or switch QoS) that priority-tags. This is an environmental fault, not an attacker. Assumption challenged: "VLAN_VALID means the frame belongs to a VLAN sub-interface". VLAN_VALID is set for any 802.1Q header, including VID 0.
- **Evidence:** pkg/vrrp/instance_receive.go:370-374 `if !boundToVLAN { if _, tagged := afPacketAuxdataVLANTag(oob, oobn); tagged { continue } }`; :435 `if aux.Status&unix.TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID == 0 { return 0, false }` then `return aux.Vlan_tci, true`. The VID is never tested. pkg/vrrp/manager.go:1550 `proto := htons(unix.ETH_P_ALL)`: the socket is a ptype_all tap that sees the skb before vlan_do_receive, with the tag in metadata, and af_packet sets VLAN_VALID whenever skb_vlan_tag_present. The 15049 harness treats tci 0 as "no auxdata", so no cell can express VID 0.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run TestF05 -v` (workers/f05/evidence/zz_f05_prio_tag_probe_test.go) → verify/vf05/vrrp_priotag.out: control (no auxdata) ge-0-0-1/reth1 "enqueued=[10.0.61.2]"; defect PCP6/VID0 tci=0xC000 "enqueued=[]" on both; reference VLAN-100 "enqueued=[]". Limits: kernel cmsg contents are synthesized from the af_packet source, not captured from a NIC.
- **Trace:** Peer advert, priority-tagged on the wire (VID 0, PCP 6) → NIC strip or skb_vlan_untag → ETH_P_ALL tap delivers with PACKET_AUXDATA VLAN_VALID tci=0xC000 → receiverAfPacket (!boundToVLAN) drops → no advert enqueued → master-down timer (≈3×advert) → backup becomes MASTER while the peer remains MASTER.
- **Refutation attempt:** Checked the cBPF prefilter (reads in-data ethertype, which is untagged, so it accepts); checked for any VID test in the loop or the parser (none); confirmed the socket protocol is ETH_P_ALL (a protocol-bound ptype_base socket would see the frame after the VID-0 tag is cleared and would not be affected); checked that the drop applies to interfaces with no VLAN siblings at all (the predicate is only !boundToVLAN). Private-RG default mode suppresses RETH VRRP, which bounds the reach. The control and reference rows show the probe discriminates.
- **HPC/invariant check:** one extra mask on an already-parsed cmsg per received frame; negligible.

## #16427 — RestoreShrinkHighWater drops legacy (no epoch_hash) epoch sets whose high-water has rotated — a regression versus the #14994 restore [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
RestoreShrinkHighWater drops legacy (no epoch_hash) epoch sets whose high-water has rotated — a regression versus the #14994 restore

**Finding ID:** R3-F05-07
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — this is a one-shot window per affected feed (the restart after upgrading from a binary between #14395 and #15075 whose epoch had rotated). Within that window, a wholesale same-count content swap of an enforced feed installs without refusal. A WARN audit line is still logged. The epoch's later failure to re-bootstrap belongs to R3-A50-02 [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The first refresh after upgrade can replace an enforced deny/allow list wholesale with no refusal.

**Contract:** #14994 (parent comment, removed by 8f2bc3a4d5): "requiring equality silently dropped every restored epoch whose high-water had moved, leaving churn unanchored on cold restart"; pkg/feeds/README.md content-epoch section.

**Trace:** Pre-#15075 /var/lib/xpf/feed-shrink-history.json (Prefixes, no epoch_hash) → RestoreShrinkHighWater drops the epoch → first fetch of a disjoint equal-count set → count guard passes, churn guard has no epoch → installed → dataplane address book.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/feeds/feeds.go:343-355 `if record.EpochHash != "" { ... accept = digest == want } else { accept = digest == hash }` (:351). The parent `git show 8f2bc3a4d5^:pkg/feeds/feeds.go:456-459` accepted any canonical set.

**Probe:** workers/f05/evidence/zz_f05_legacy_epoch_probe_test.go → verify/vf05/feeds_epoch.out: "legacy-record=false restored-epoch-prefixes=100 -> ... installed=0 refused=true"; "legacy-record=true restored-epoch-prefixes=0 -> ... installed=100 refused=false". Reporter mutant (evidence/feeds_parent_semantics_mutation.diff): legacy restores 100 and refuses.

## Acceptance / fix direction
For records without epoch_hash, keep the #14994 acceptance (any canonical set within the cap). Acceptance: the legacy row restores 100 and refuses the swap. Coordinate with R3-A50-02's re-bootstrap fix.

## Full validated claim
