## #16428 — ExpandedMutationLines fails on the plain (no-vars) view of any `apply-groups "${node}"` tree, locking regex-restricted classes out of all commits on clusters [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
ExpandedMutationLines fails on the plain (no-vars) view of any `apply-groups "${node}"` tree, locking regex-restricted classes out of all commits on clusters

**Finding ID:** R3-F05-08
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — fail-closed lockout of every `*-configuration`-restricted (delegated) class on any chassis cluster that uses the canonical Junos `${node}` idiom, for commits unrelated to groups. Unrestricted classes are unaffected and there is no enforcement loss. This is an operator/API contract failure, demonstrated at the pkg/config decision layer [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Delegated operators cannot make any change on an HA cluster, which pushes administrators to hand out super-user, the opposite of the least privilege the feature exists for. It persists for as long as the cluster uses the idiom.

**Contract:** docs/system-login.md (#14981): restricted classes adjudicate the group-expanded configuration. `${node}` resolves per node, and the generic compile falls back to node0 (#15031, ExpandGroupsNodeFallback15031). The function's own comment says only a failure of "the authored inheritance itself" is fatal.

**Trace:** Cluster active config with `groups node0/node1` + `apply-groups "${node}"` → restricted principal (`permissions configure; deny-configuration "security policies"`) issues any set + Commit over gRPC/REST → AuthorizeExpandedCandidate → ExpandedMutationLines → plain ExpandGroups error → permission denied.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/config/authz_config_groups_14981.go:84-101 iterates `{nil, node0, node1}` and `if vars == nil { return nil, err }`; :211-215 → "permission denied: login class %q restricts configuration paths, and the group expansion cannot be resolved for adjudication". pkg/config/authz_config_read_14707.go:509-512 has the same error for reads. Callers: pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:52 (Commit/CommitConfirmed), pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:291/316. docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:61 `apply-groups "${node}";`. The existing TestGroupNodeVarExpansionDenied14981 (authz_config_groups_14981_test.go:177-185) passes because of this unresolvable-view refusal, not because of the denied leaf, and it has no allowed control.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestF05(ExpandedMutationLinesNodeGroups|RestrictedClassCommitOnNodeGroupCluster)' -v` (workers/f05/evidence/zz_f05_node_plainview_probe_test.go) → verify/vf05/config_probes.out: cluster ${node} "ExpandedMutationLines lines=0 err=apply-groups references undefined group \"${node}\""; commit of unrelated `set system services ssh` by netops → "permission denied ... group expansion cannot be resolved"; control plain group → lines=2, <nil>. Limits: the gRPC interceptor itself was not run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In ExpandedMutationLines (and the read gate), skip the plain view or use ExpandGroupsNodeFallback15031 when the only plain-view failure is the `${node}` trigger, and adjudicate the node0 and node1 views. Give TestGroupNodeVarExpansionDenied14981 an allowed control. Acceptance: the cluster row returns nil for the unrelated commit and still refuses a denied path delivered via a node group.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf05.md)</summary>

### R3-F05-08 — Group-expansion RBAC treats the plain-view `${node}` "undefined group" error as fatal: on every cluster using `apply-groups "${node}"`, every commit and whole-config read by a regex-restricted login class is refused
- **Finding ID:** R3-F05-08

- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker f05 (Fix-residual hunter (delta group 05)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vf05

The function's own comment says only a failure of "the authored inheritance itself" is fatal.

## #16429 — Port-mirroring: a bare-physical input in Linux spelling (`ge-0-0-1`) on a port with an untagged unit 0 is installed as a unit-0 VID-0-only row, so tagged sibling units are not mirrored [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Port-mirroring: a bare-physical input in Linux spelling (`ge-0-0-1`) on a port with an untagged unit 0 is installed as a unit-0 VID-0-only row, so tagged sibling units are not mirrored

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-01
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — the analyzer loses mirroring coverage of the tagged units for one accepted spelling, while no exclusion is recorded (so show reports the instance installed). Enforcement is unaffected. Recovery is to re-spell the input.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
an IDS fed from a trunk port silently sees only native/untagged traffic while the box reports the mirror armed.

**Contract:** #15113 (ccc2a6af55): a bare physical mirror input matches every unit on the port, and a unit input matches only its own VID. The compiler treats the Linux and Junos spellings as the same source (`pkg/config/compiler_services.go:2150-2160`, ingress owner keyed by `LinuxIfName(v)`).

**Trace:** `input ingress interface ge-0-0-1` resolves through `ifindexByName["ge-0-0-1"]`=11 to the unit-0 scope. That produces a snapshot row with `UnitScoped:true, IngressVLANID:0`, which Rust stores in `mirror_configs_scoped` only. A VID-100 packet's logical unit is 1, so the scoped lookups `(11,100,1)`/`(111,100,1)` miss, the bare map also misses, and nothing is mirrored.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:500-620`: the base row is appended before its unit rows, and an untagged unit 0's `LinuxName` equals the base netdev name. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/mirrors.go:95-132`: `scopeByName[iface.LinuxName] = scope` runs when `!nameKeyed[iface.LinuxName]`, so the unit-0 row overwrites the base row's `ge-0-0-1` scope with `{vlanID:0, unitScoped:true}`. `mirrors.go:207-212` looks up the raw input first. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mirror/mod.rs:58-105` matches a scoped row only on `(ifindex, vid, unit)`, and the bare fallback map does not contain scoped rows.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/zz_vf06_mirror_e2e_probe_test.go`, run with `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestVF06MirrorLinuxSpelledBareInputE2E -count=1 -v`; output `RUN/verify/vf06/probe01-mirror-e2e.out`. Positive control 1: `junos-bare+unit0` gives `UnitScoped:false`. Positive control 2: `linux-bare-no-unit0` gives `UnitScoped:false`. Defect: `linux-bare+unit0` gives `{IngressIfindex:11 ... IngressVLANID:0 UnitScoped:true IngressUnit:0}` with `excl=[]`. The reporter's synthetic-row probe (`RUN/workers/f06/evidence/zz_r3f06_mirror_linux_bare_probe_test.go`) reproduces it.

## Acceptance / fix direction
never let an `IsUnit` row overwrite a `LinuxName` key already written by a non-unit row (or key scope by the denoted row). Acceptance: the e2e probe gives `UnitScoped:false` for both spellings, and the 15113/15651/16063 cells stay green.

## #16430 — `xpfd cleanup` has no live-daemon interlock: run beside a running daemon it clears FRR's managed section, deletes fabric IPVLANs, closes kernel transit and unpins dataplane state while the daemon keeps reporting healthy [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`xpfd cleanup` has no live-daemon interlock: run beside a running daemon it clears FRR's managed section, deletes fabric IPVLANs, closes kernel transit and unpins dataplane state while the daemon keeps reporting healthy

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-02
**Severity (source):** Low — Low [reporter: Medium] — the trigger is root deliberately invoking a documented teardown verb. The only product text that recommends it (`pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go:71-83`) says to stop xpfd first and warns that cleanup is broad and causes downtime. Unlike #15085 (the product's own error text recommending a harmful bare `xpfd`), nothing steers an operator into it. The consequence is still real: the daemon's state diverges (routing withdrawn until the next apply, fabric overlay deleted) and the daemon reports healthy.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
one misremembered command on a live (possibly HA-primary) node withdraws FRR-managed routing and the fabric overlay without the daemon noticing. Recovery is a restart or commit.

**Contract:** `pkg/daemon/transit_cleanup_9725.go:11-14` assumes cleanup "runs in a short-lived process after the daemon has exited", which is a precondition that is never checked. #15085 (0e95cb82fb) introduced the singleton and a probe, `daemonLockHeldByLiveProcess` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_singleton_15085.go:106-125`). `cmd/xpfd/README.md:60-61` documents cleanup as the teardown that "Runs on uninstall".

**Trace:** with the daemon holding `/run/xpf/xpfd.lock`, `xpfd cleanup` writes forwarding sysctls 0 and installs the transit barrier, unpins links, deletes the fabric IPVLANs and rewrites frr.conf without the managed section and reloads, then exits 0. Refinement to the reporter's claim: the live daemon holds its XDP link FDs (`m.xdpLinks`), so unpinning does not detach AF_XDP forwarding. The transit gate's kernel-truth tick may re-converge the sysctls. The durable effects are the FRR routing withdrawal (until the next commit/apply) and the deleted fabric overlay.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`cmd/xpfd/main.go:238-280`: `parseCleanupArgs` → `daemon.CloseKernelTransitForCleanup()` → `dataplane.Cleanup()` (`pkg/dataplane/loader.go:1455-1475`, unpins every link and `RemoveAll(bpfPinPath)`) → `daemon.CleanupFabricIPVLANs()` → `frr.New().Clear()`. No step checks the singleton. A non-test grep for `daemonLockHeldByLiveProcess` returns only its definition. The sibling barrier verbs carry live guards (`cmd/xpfd/input_barrier_10751.go:76,113` `EarlyInputHandoffLive`).

**Probe:** none (destructive host verb). In-tree positive control for the available guard: `TestAcquireDaemonLockRejectsSecondOwner15085` shows `daemonLockHeldByLiveProcess` is true while a lease is held.

## Acceptance / fix direction
in cmdCleanup, refuse (non-zero, naming `systemctl stop xpfd`) when `daemonLockHeldByLiveProcess()` is true, or acquire the singleton for the duration of cleanup. Acceptance: a test holding a lease makes the cleanup entry refuse before any transit/pin/FRR mutation, and cleanup with no holder proceeds unchanged.

## #16431 — #15084 made xpfd ignore SIGHUP, but the Rust helper in the same unit still dies on it, so `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` fails node transit closed until the supervised respawn [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#15084 made xpfd ignore SIGHUP, but the Rust helper in the same unit still dies on it, so `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` fails node transit closed until the supervised respawn

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — this is the stray-signal scenario #15084 closed and documented as harmless. It still takes the forwarding process down. The node's userspace transit is fail-closed (shim disarmed) until the #5838 supervisor's backoff respawn completes, and helper-held per-worker state is rebuilt from scratch. The outage is bounded and self-recovering, needs no peer, and enforcement is not lost (it fails closed). Demonstrated at component level; the end-to-end outage duration was not measured.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
every node that receives the HUP drops userspace transit until respawn. On an HA primary that also drops takeover readiness for the window. Operators were told by #15084 and the changelog (`debian/changelog:793-802`) that SIGHUP is now a logged no-op.

**Contract:** #15084 (bf96eaf747) and the `ignoreSIGHUP` doc (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1063-1087`) say a SIGHUP must not take the firewall down: xpfd logs "SIGHUP received and ignored" and keeps forwarding. In userspace mode, forwarding is performed by `xpf-userspace-dp`, so the contract holds only if the helper survives too.

**Trace:** `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` sends HUP to every process of the unit. xpfd's `ignoreSIGHUP` logs and continues, while the helper (default disposition) terminates by signal. `superviseHelper` then runs `handleUnexpectedHelperExitLocked`: shim ctrl is disabled and binding rows cleared, so transit is dropped. `resetAfterHelperGoneLocked` runs, followed by the backoff restart. The new helper starts with empty worker tables and re-derives state from the Go-side replay and HA resync.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go:461-470` spawns with `exec.Command(binary, ...)` and no `SysProcAttr` (no Setpgid/Setsid). `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1087-1089` uses `signal.Notify(sighupCh, syscall.SIGHUP)`, which catches the signal and does not set SIG_IGN, so it is not inherited. `userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs:710-715` has `ctrlc::set_handler(move || running.store(false, ...))` as the only handler. `userspace-dp/Cargo.toml:13` declares `ctrlc = "3.5"` without features, and `Cargo.lock:327-336` pins ctrlc 3.5.2 as the single ctrlc package. In ctrlc-3.5.2 `src/platform/unix/mod.rs`, SIGTERM/SIGHUP are installed only under `#[cfg(feature = "termination")]`. A grep finds no SIGHUP in `userspace-dp/src`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_supervisor.go:347-407` (`handleUnexpectedHelperExitLocked`) runs `disableCtrlBeforeTeardownLocked` ("failing closed and scheduling restart (#5838)") and then `scheduleHelperRestartLocked`.

**Probe:** Sources are `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/hupprobe/` (Rust, `ctrlc = "=3.5.2"`) and `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/goparent/main.go`; output is `RUN/verify/vf06/probe03-sighup.out`. Positive control: SIGINT gives `graceful shutdown via handler` / `child exit: <nil> (state=exit status 0)`, which proves the handler is installed and the instrument can observe survival and graceful exit. Defect: SIGHUP to both pids gives `parent: SIGHUP received and ignored` and then `child exit: signal: hangup`. Limits: no real helper binary, no systemd, and restart latency not measured.

## Acceptance / fix direction
at helper start-up, install SIG_IGN (or log-and-ignore) for SIGHUP before workers spawn, and keep SIGTERM semantics unchanged. Optionally spawn the helper with `Setpgid` so terminal hangups do not reach it (this does not cover `systemctl kill`). Acceptance: a test spawns the real helper binary, sends SIGHUP, and asserts the process is alive and still answering the control socket. A sibling cell sends HUP to both PIDs and asserts no `exited unexpectedly` supervisor transition.

In ctrlc-3.5.2 `src/platform/unix/mod.rs`, SIGTERM/SIGHUP are installed only under `#[cfg(feature = "termination")]`. A grep finds no SIGHUP in `userspace-dp/src`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_supervisor.go:347-407` (`handleUnexpectedHelperExitLocked`) runs `disableCtrlBeforeTeardownLocked` ("failing closed and scheduling restart (#5838)") and then `scheduleHelperRestartLocked`.
- **Probe:** Sources are `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/hupprobe/` (Rust, `ctrlc = "=3.5.2"`) and `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/goparent/main.go`; output is `RUN/verify/vf06/probe03-sighup.out`. Positive control: SIGINT gives `graceful shutdown via handler` / `child exit: <nil> (state=exit status 0)`, which proves the handler is installed and the instrument can observe survival and graceful exit. Defect: SIGHUP to both pids gives `parent: SIGHUP received and ignored` and then `child exit: signal: hangup`. Limits: no real helper binary, no systemd, and restart latency not measured.
- **Trace:** `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` sends HUP to every process of the unit. xpfd's `ignoreSIGHUP` logs and continues, while the helper (default disposition) terminates by signal. `superviseHelper` then runs `handleUnexpectedHelperExitLocked`: shim ctrl is disabled and binding rows cleared, so transit is dropped. `resetAfterHelperGoneLocked` runs, followed by the backoff restart. The new helper starts with empty worker tables and re-derives state from the Go-side replay and HA resync.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked whether xpfd uses `signal.Ignore` (inherited SIG_IGN); it does not, it uses `Notify`. I checked the helper for any other signal installer (no signal-hook, `libc::signal` or SIGHUP), whether Cargo feature unification could enable `termination` (ctrlc has one consumer), whether the helper is spawned in its own process group or scope (no SysProcAttr), and whether `RestartForceExitStatus=SIGHUP` (`test/incus/xpfd.service:31`) helps; it covers the main PID only and is irrelevant here. Correction to the reporter: even with `termination` enabled, ctrlc would route SIGHUP to `running=false`, which is a graceful helper exit and still an outage, so the fix must ignore SIGHUP, not just enable the feature. The reporter's "drops all userspace sessions" is narrowed to "helper-held worker state is rebuilt", because the sessions themselves were not measured.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable to the hot path. The relevant invariant is lifecycle ownership: the helper is a separately signalled process whose disposition is not covered by the main-process fix.

## #16432 — A timed-out forwarded failover whose ownership did not move returns gRPC OK / REST 200: "outcome unknown" is distinguishable from "completed" only by message text [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
A timed-out forwarded failover whose ownership did not move returns gRPC OK / REST 200: "outcome unknown" is distinguishable from "completed" only by message text

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-04
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — an API/automation contract weakness. A status-checking client cannot tell a completed move from an unknown or not-moved one. The human-readable message is honest, and no in-tree automation consumes this status (the rolling upgrade uses other verbs, `pkg/upgrade/cluster_cli.go:116-127`).
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
a script that checks status may proceed (drain or reboot the old owner) although ownership did not move, which is the hazard the message itself warns about.

**Contract:** `SystemActionResponse` carries only `message`, so the RPC status is the only machine-readable verdict. #15081's goal (pkg/grpcapi/README.md:88-102) was "never a bare DeadlineExceeded after the peer may have committed", that is, to avoid a false failure, not to report a non-move as OK.

**Trace:** the forwarded failover hits the 46s proxy deadline. `Reconcile` reads heartbeat ownership, the peer is not primary, so the call returns the "outcome unknown … verify ownership" message with status OK. REST and the CLI print the message, and REST returns 200.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/peerclient/peerclient.go:96-145` (`Reconcile`): all arms return `(message, true)`, including "outcome unknown … not primary on node %d" and "peer is unreachable". `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:100-115`: `proxyClusterFailover` returns `(outcome, nil)`. `system_action_failover_proxy_deadline_15081_test.go:153-170` requires `err == nil` for a reachable peer still in `StateSecondary`.

**Probe:** the in-tree cells above. Positive control: `TestProxyFailoverTimeoutAfterPeerCommitReportsSuccess15081` (peer primary) also returns nil, which shows both outcomes share one status. Limit: REST serialization (200) was read, not executed.

## Acceptance / fix direction
keep committed-after-timeout as OK. Return a distinct non-OK status (for example `codes.Unknown` with the verify text) or add a structured outcome field for the unknown and peer-unreachable arms. Acceptance: the not-committed/unknown cells assert a non-OK or explicit-unknown outcome, and the committed cell stays OK.

## Full validated claim

## #16433 — `vlan-tags outer N <anything>` commits as single-tag VlanID=N: `inner-range`, `inner-list`, `inner-vlan-id-range` (and arbitrary trailing tokens) bypass the #5879 QinQ gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`vlan-tags outer N <anything>` commits as single-tag VlanID=N: `inner-range`, `inner-list`, `inner-vlan-id-range` (and arbitrary trailing tokens) bypass the #5879 QinQ gate

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-05
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — a stacked-VLAN unit that the dataplane cannot serve commits green through the operator commit-check (CheckText) in both AST shapes as an enabled single-tag VID-N unit. Single-tagged VID-N frames are then admitted into that unit's zone, which the authored config scoped to double-tagged traffic, and the configured QinQ traffic is not served. Bounded: zone policies still apply, and no other zone's isolation is lost.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
an operator gets a green commit on both HA nodes, wrong admission (S-VLAN-only frames enter the zone), and no QinQ service, with no warning. This is the "silent functional lie" class the #2354/#5879 gates exist to refuse.

**Contract:** `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_qinq.go:9-60` says any INNER (second) tag is unsupported and strict commit must hard-reject it (#2354, #5879). Junos parity: the Junos CLI reference for `vlan-tags (Stacked VLAN Tags)` lists the options `inner tpid.vlan-id`, `inner-list value` ("List or a set of VLAN identifiers. You can configure a maximum of 32 inner-lists for an interface") and `inner-range tpid. vid1–vid2` (juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/vlan-tags-edit-interfaces.html), so these are real second-tag spellings.

**Trace:** `unit 100 { vlan-tags outer 100 inner-range 1-200; }` passes the QinQ gate, which sees no `inner` token and counts outer only. #15035 sets `VlanID=100`, and the tagging gate is satisfied by `flexible-vlan-tagging`. The snapshot unit row then carries VLANID 100 and `<parent>.100`, so single-tagged VID-100 frames classify into this unit's zone. Double-tagged frames keep the inner 0x8100 after the single unwind and are not served as configured.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_qinq.go:109-121`: `vlanTagsHasToken` compares `k == token`. `:150-170` (`unitVLANStack`): a `vlan-tags` node is inner only if `vlanTagsHasToken(c, "inner")`; otherwise it is counted as an outer single S-tag. The #15035 compile loop in `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go` skips only `vlanTagsHasToken(vtNode, "inner")` and takes the outer value, ignoring the remaining tokens.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf06/probes/zz_vf06_vlantags_flat_probe_test.go` (pkg/configstore), run with `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestVF06VlanTagsInnerSpellings -count=1 -v`; output `RUN/verify/vf06/probe05-vlantags.out`. Positive controls: `outer 100` is ACCEPTED as VlanID=100 (hier and flat), and `outer 100 inner 200` is REJECTED "unsupported QinQ / stacked-VLAN stack" in both shapes. Defect: `outer 100 inner-range 1-200`, `outer 100 inner-list [ 10 20 ]` and `outer 100 inner-vlan-id-range 1-200` are each ACCEPTED with VlanID=100 InnerVlanID=0 in both shapes. Also `outer 100 bogus 7` is ACCEPTED, so the tail is not validated at all. The reporter's probes (`RUN/workers/f06/evidence/zz_r3f06_vlantags_*`) reproduce this.

## Acceptance / fix direction
close the statement's world. Accept exactly `outer <[tpid.]vid>` (either shape) and reject any other `vlan-tags` token, with `inner*` spellings (`inner`, `inner-list`, `inner-range`, `inner-vlan-id-range`) getting the existing QinQ reject text. Make the #15035 reader refuse trailing tokens after the outer VID. Acceptance: the four probe spellings are rejected by CheckText in both shapes, and `vlan-tags outer 100;` still compiles VlanID=100.

## #16434 — Changing verifyFrame's replay test from `seq <= recvSeq` to `seq < recvSeq` (accept an exact replay of the latest frame), or removing the 12-byte frame header (which carries the message type) from both seal and verify MACs, each leaves... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Changing verifyFrame's replay test from `seq <= recvSeq` to `seq < recvSeq` (accept an exact replay of the latest frame), or removing the 12-byte frame header (which carries the message type) from both seal and verify MACs, each leaves the whole green pkg/cluster suite passing. The only frame-auth cell replays a strictly older frame and tampers only the payload.

**Finding ID:** R3-A83-08
**Severity (source):** Low — an assurance gap only, because the production code is correct at HEAD. If either regression happened, an on-path party on the sync link could re-inject the latest authenticated frame indefinitely, or rewrite the type byte (for example install to delete, or between ack-shaped failover messages), because the link is MAC'd, not encrypted. That consequence is potential. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The #7163 redesign deleted three attack-guard cells and recorded where their coverage went. The frame-boundary cells that would keep that coverage honest were never added, so a seal/verify refactor can reopen replay or type forgery with every cell green.

**Contract:** pkg/cluster/sync_auth.go:401-407 verifyFrame "enforces the strictly-increasing per-connection sequence (replay/regression guard)". :385-399 sealFrame MACs `frame || seq` with frame = header||payload. :45 describes the per-frame HMAC keyed by the Noise Split() directional key. No module doc describes the trailer, so the code comment is the contract.

**Trace:** Peer A sealFrame(header||payload) → TCP → B receiveLoop reads header, payload and trailer → verifyFrame (MAC over header and payload, seq watermark) → handleMessage(hdr.Type).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
sync_auth.go:389-399 (sealFrame `mac.Write(out[:n+8])`), :407-427 (verifyFrame writes tag, header, payload and seq, then `if a.recvSeen && seq <= a.recvSeq { return errSyncFrameReplay }`). authConn (:266) embeds net.Conn and overrides neither Read nor Write, so frames are plaintext plus trailer. sync_auth_test.go:274-320 replays frame1 after frame2 (1 < 2), tampers p2[0], and uses a wrong key. The only production verifier is sync_conn_read.go:116.

**Probe:** Sandbox /var/tmp/va83/sb. MUT-R (`<=` to `<`) on the whole pkg/cluster gave a package `pass` (141.3 s) with 0 fail events. MUT-H (a83's cluster-header-mac-mutant.diff) gave a package `pass` (141.4 s) with 0 fail events. Probe RUN/verify/va83/probes/zz_va83_frame_auth_probe_test.go PASSes at HEAD (controls: frame1 and frame2 verify in order, and untampered frame1 verifies on a fresh receiver). Under MUT-R it FAILs with "exact replay of the latest frame (seq == watermark) accepted: err=<nil>", and under MUT-H it FAILs with "frame with rewritten message type verified: err=<nil>". sync_auth.go was restored and cmp-checked after each mutant.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Add the exact-replay and header-tamper assertions (plus a SessionV4/DeleteV4 type swap) to sync_auth_test.go. Acceptance: MUT-R and MUT-H each turn a named cell red.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (va83.md)</summary>

- **Trace:** Peer A sealFrame(header||payload) → TCP → B receiveLoop reads header, payload and trailer → verifyFrame (MAC over header and payload, seq watermark) → handleMessage(hdr.Type).
- **Refutation attempt:** The Noise handshake authenticates the peer but does not encrypt frames, so the MAC is the only integrity on the type byte. A changed length desynchronises framing loudly, but the type byte has no such side effect. The heartbeat and fabric auth cells do not exercise authConn.verifyFrame. The r2 finding "verifyFrame admits sequence gaps" is a different boundary.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — test coverage. verifyFrame is per-frame on the sync receive loop, and the probe adds no production cost.

## #16435 — #15087's `L3ReverseBucket` embeds `[u32; 256]` per NAT (server, translated-address) identity: measured 1104 B per index slot and about 310 MB per worker at the default session cap with distinct identities, versus about 15 MB pre-fix [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
#15087's `L3ReverseBucket` embeds `[u32; 256]` per NAT (server, translated-address) identity: measured 1104 B per index slot and about 310 MB per worker at the default session cap with distinct identities, versus about 15 MB pre-fix

**Finding ID:** R3-F06-06
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — measured, bounded resource amplification introduced by the fix. Every distinct NAT reply identity costs a 1104 B slot (plus a per-bucket HashSet heap allocation and a 1 KiB zero-fill on the session-install path) instead of about 60 B. The worst case at the default per-worker cap is about 310 MB per worker, multiplied by the worker count, on a VM appliance that shares memory with UMEM. Helper OOM (which would trigger the #5838 fail-closed restart) is a potential consequence, not demonstrated.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
busy NAT edges (many destinations per worker) pay hundreds of MB of helper RSS that pre-fix cost about 15 MB per worker, competing with UMEM on VM appliances. The memory is not released after a burst.

**Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md hot-path/working-set discipline (per-flow working-set growth). #15087's Risk paragraph asserts the cost is "bounded by distinct NAT destinations, not sessions". That is literally true, but in the worst case distinct identities approach the session count, and the per-identity constant is 1 KiB.

**Trace:** a NAT'd forward session install computes `l3_reverse_key_for_forward` (Some for rewrite_src/rewrite_dst/nat64), then `l3_reverse_index.entry(index_key).or_insert_with(L3ReverseBucket::new)`, which allocates a 1104 B slot and a HashSet for each new identity. The outer table grows to power-of-two capacity with hashbrown slack and does not shrink after a burst. Each worker owns its own `SessionTable`.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:53` has `type SeededL3ReverseIndex = HashMap<L3ReverseKey, L3ReverseBucket, HotPathSeededState>`, and `:71-74` has `struct L3ReverseBucket { handles: HashSet<u32, HotPathSeededState>, protocol_counts: [u32; 256] }`. `:5563-5575` inserts one bucket per `l3_reverse_fragment_index_key(l3_key)` (protocol-erased (family, server, translated addr)) for every non-reverse NAT/NAT64 session. Default cap: `:268` `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS = 131072`. Pre-fix `0d4f1dc808^:userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:39,44` has `type NatIndexBucket = SmallVec<[u32; 2]>` as the value type.

**Probe:** a temporary test appended to `userspace-dp/src/session/l3_reverse_bucket_15087_tests.rs` (`RUN/verify/vf06/probes/zz_vf06_l3_bucket_memory.diff`; file restored), run as `flock RUN/locks/cargo.lock timeout 1800 cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp zz_vf06_l3_reverse_bucket_memory -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, output `RUN/verify/vf06/probe06-l3-memory.out`. The size line is `size_of key=36 bucket=1064 slot(key,bucket)=1104`. Positive control: 131072 SNAT sessions to one server gives `l3_index.len=1 l3_index.capacity=3 rss_delta_kb=148156`. Defect shape: 131072 distinct servers gives `l3_index.len=131072 l3_index.capacity=229376 rss_delta_kb=457896`, about 310 MB more for the same session count. Limits: RSS deltas are approximate (allocator reuse after the control table was dropped), and the run used one table, not a 6-worker helper.

## Acceptance / fix direction
keep hashed membership but make the protocol counts sparse (for example `SmallVec<[(u8, u32); 2]>`, since real buckets carry 1-3 protocols), or keep only a total count plus the bounded verification walk. Acceptance: `size_of::<(L3ReverseKey, L3ReverseBucket)>()` is back under about 128 B, the 131072-identity RSS cell stays within about 2× the same-identity control, and all 15087 cells stay green.

## #16436 — The M4 cell fails when `loadedP99 > 5 * baseP99`, a ratio of durations, in the default `go test ./...` leg, with no retry, floor or load guard. Separately, requireNetNS ends every successful netns child with `t.Skip("netns child... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
The M4 cell fails when `loadedP99 > 5 * baseP99`, a ratio of durations, in the default `go test ./...` leg, with no retry, floor or load guard. Separately, requireNetNS ends every successful netns child with `t.Skip("netns child completed")`, so a green netns cell is reported as skipped.

**Finding ID:** R3-A83-09
**Severity (source):** Low — this is flakiness and verdict-reporting soundness. The ratio is noise-driven (it moved from 0.56 to 4.65 in my runs), so the gate can red unrelated PRs under load and cannot tell a real head-of-line regression of under ~5x from noise. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A non-deterministic red in a package that CI selects for IPsec and daemon changes trains reviewers to ignore pkg/nfqueue reds (see R3-A83-06). The Skip-on-success hides passing netns cells from every summary and from the skip census.

**Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md "Time in tests (#8218)" clause 1: "A pass criterion must never be a duration, or a ratio of durations." Clause 2: "A skip is indistinguishable from a pass in every summary line". measure_fragments_test.go:19-25 calls itself "the p99 <= 5x baseline kill gate", while the sibling M1 cell (measure_stages_test.go:23-27) is explicitly "baseline data, not a performance kill gate".

**Trace:** `go test ./...` / CI affected-package run → TestMeasureFragments9506 → two timing windows → ratio compare → FAIL under an unlucky schedule.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/nfqueue/measure_fragments_test.go:29-40 takes 128 samples each of baseline and loaded and runs `if loadedP99 > 5*maxInt64(baseP99, 1) { t.Fatalf("M4 IPv%d HOL gate: ...") }`. pkg/nfqueue/harness_test.go:37-56: after `cmd.CombinedOutput()` succeeds, it calls `t.Skip("netns child completed")`.

**Probe:** `go test ./pkg/nfqueue/ -run '^TestMeasureFragments9506$' -count=1 -v` x6, then `-count=30`. All 36 PASS, with ratios between 0.56 and 4.65 (the maximum is 7% under the threshold). The deterministic FragPool tail passed every time. a83's recorded FAIL lines (`loaded p99=132407 > 5x baseline p99=26088`, and an IPv6 ratio of 5.21) are in a83's report. I did not reproduce a failure.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Move the M4 ratio behind an opt-in measurement flag like M1, or replace it with a work-based assertion, keeping the deterministic FragPool checks in the default suite. Make requireNetNS return after logging instead of calling Skip. Acceptance: `-count=10` is green under shared-host load, and the parent of a passing netns child reports PASS.

## #16437 — The #15244 tripwire's "all three post-create arms are tagged" check counts the substring `post_create_bind_error(` anywhere in bind.rs. It finds 10 hits at base, and three of them (the fn definition, `is_post_create_bind_error(` and the... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
The #15244 tripwire's "all three post-create arms are tagged" check counts the substring `post_create_bind_error(` anywhere in bind.rs. It finds 10 hits at base, and three of them (the fn definition, `is_post_create_bind_error(` and the ladder gate) are already required by compilation or by the tripwire's own earlier check. So the `>= 3` assertion cannot fail, and the fill-prime and zero-copy arms have no guard.

**Finding ID:** R3-A84-01
**Severity (source):** Low — this is test assurance only. Production at d1ea69f9aa tags all three arms, and nothing is mis-tagged today. A future regression would bring back the #15244 misdiagnosis (bring-up reports "Bad address" instead of the true cause, and ladder candidates run against an unmapped UMEM). The outer reconcile loop retries on a fresh UMEM, which bounds that.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
this tripwire is the only guard #15244's fix (3a5e77eaf3) shipped for the fill-prime and zero-copy arms, and it reads as protection. If those arms regress, an operator sees a misleading "Bad address" bring-up failure.

**Contract:** the header at `userspace-dp/tests/post_create_bind_terminal_15244.rs:10-16` says "every post-create arm of `try_open_bind` (identity mismatch, fill-prime failure, non-zerocopy) returns a tagged error … Removing the tag, an arm, or the ladder check … does not satisfy this." CLAUDE.md says "a Rust dataplane regression fails `make test`".

**Trace:** a refactor writes the fill-prime arm (bind.rs:789) as a plain `format!(…).into()`. `open_binding_worker_rings` (:325) then no longer sees `PostCreateBindError` and continues the flag/strategy ladder on a UMEM whose rings the dropped socket unmapped. `last_err` becomes the follow-on create's `-EFAULT`. Meanwhile `make test-rust` leg 1 runs the tripwire green.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`tests/post_create_bind_terminal_15244.rs:63-69` reads `let tagged = bind_rs.matches("post_create_bind_error(").count(); assert!(tagged >= 3, …)`. The hits in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bind.rs` at d1ea69f9aa are: :154 `pub(super) fn post_create_bind_error(message: String)`, :161 `fn is_post_create_bind_error(` (substring), :325 `if is_post_create_bind_error(err.as_ref()) {` (the gate, which the tripwire already requires through `find(gate)`), :695 (mismatch helper), :789 `return Err(post_create_bind_error(format!("prime fill ring after socket create: {err}"` , :807 (zero-copy rejection), and the cfg(test) module at :1500, :1522, :1525 and :1527. The floor of 3 is met by :154, :161 and :325 alone.

**Probe:** `python3 -I RUN/verify/va84/probes/r01_tripwire_replica.py userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bind.rs` produced RUN/verify/va84/r01-replica.out. It shows `baseline -> GREEN(tagged=10)`, `M1 untag fill-prime -> GREEN(tagged=9)`, `M2 untag zero-copy -> GREEN(tagged=9)`, `M3 untag both inline arms -> GREEN(tagged=8)`, `M4 untag all three arms -> GREEN(tagged=7)` and `CONTROL delete ladder gate -> RED(order)`. The control shows the replica can red. The reporter's earlier probe (workers/a84/evidence/tripwire_15244_probe.out) agrees. Limit: the replica models only the source predicate. M4 is still caught by the behavioural cell `identity_mismatch_error_is_post_create_terminal_15244` (bind.rs:1490), but M1, M2 and M3 are caught by nothing.

## Acceptance / fix direction
in `try_open_bind`'s body only, with comments stripped and the fn definition and `is_` prefix excluded, require `return Err(post_create_bind_error(` inside the `prime_fill_ring_offsets` Err arm window and inside the `requires_zerocopy()` block. Acceptance: M1 and M2 each red the tripwire, and the baseline stays green.

## #16438 — With any WireGuard tunnel configured, the degraded shim drops every host-bound fragmented UDP datagram (heads included, interface-NAT addresses included), because the #15102 predicate runs ahead of the local check [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
With any WireGuard tunnel configured, the degraded shim drops every host-bound fragmented UDP datagram (heads included, interface-NAT addresses included), because the #15102 predicate runs ahead of the local check

**Finding ID:** R3-F07-01
**Severity (source):** Low — Low. The reporter's healthy-path leg is a DUP of G37-02 and is excluded here. The surviving leg is availability loss of fragmented host-bound UDP (for example IKE with certificates and no RFC 7383 fragmentation, NAT-T, large DNS/RADIUS replies to the box) only while the shim is degraded (helper down or restarting, queue binding not ready, heartbeat stale). It affects only boxes with at least one WireGuard tunnel. It is fail-closed (no enforcement loss), and TCP management and unfragmented UDP are unaffected. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator who adds one WireGuard tunnel loses the degraded-mode "local/control still reaches the kernel" floor for all fragmented UDP. That covers interface-NAT WAN addresses too, which work in healthy mode via the #13926 association. During helper restarts or ISSU, certificate-based IKE exchanges and large DNS answers to the box fail. Only a degraded-transit drop counter records it. Recovery is automatic when the helper is healthy again (where G37-02 still applies to non-ifnat addresses).

**Contract:** In degraded mode the shim still passes local/control traffic to the kernel and drops only transit (`is_degraded_local_or_control`, whose general local pass is `degraded_general_local_pass_applies`; `pass_local_control`). #15102's stated scope is WG outer datagrams: "degraded mode drops them with their head", and "NOT changed: the kernel socket path for handshakes and whole records". Before ada5f856da a host-bound UDP head or tail in degraded mode was local and was kernel-passed.

**Trace:** `set interfaces wg0 ... listen-port` → snapshot WG listen ports → `encodeSteeredPortSet` → ctrl.Flags |= WG_RX (both live and disabled ctrl, maps_sync.go:331-334,600-603) → shim degraded entry (ctrl disabled, or `binding_ready_slot` failure) → `is_degraded_local_or_control` → `wg_fragment_stays_on_helper(17,17,true,true)` true → `return false` → `drop_degraded_transit`. The same happens for the 255/17 tail. Nothing reaches the kernel, so the datagram is lost.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-xdp/src/gre_classify.rs:164-173` returns `wg_rx_armed && is_fragment && ((protocol == 17 && wire_protocol == 17) || (protocol == 255 && wire_protocol == 17))`. `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:2354` sets v4 `is_fragment: (frag_field & 0x2000) != 0 || non_first_fragment`, so a head (MF set) qualifies. `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1915-1922` (`is_degraded_local_or_control`) does `if wg_fragment_stays_on_helper(parsed.protocol, parsed.wire_protocol, parsed.is_fragment, WG_RX) { return false; }`. This comes BEFORE `should_fallback_early`, `is_local_destination` and `degraded_general_local_pass_applies`, and WITHOUT the `parsed.protocol == PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4` restriction the healthy path adds at `lib.rs:862-863`. Callers: `lib.rs:939-942` (binding/heartbeat not ready, else `drop_degraded_transit`) and `lib.rs:1800-1810` (ctrl disabled, `DropTransit`). `pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:600-603` sets WG_RX in the disabled ctrl whenever a WG listen port exists. The project test `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_wg_outer_frag_15102.rs` (truth-table row "first fragment (UDP head) stays on helper") pins the head row true. Observation: the predicate returns true for a head. Inference from the read order: the degraded path drops it.

**Probe:** `flock RUN/locks/cargo.lock timeout 1800 cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vf07 -- --nocapture` with temporary tests in `RUN/verify/vf07/probes/tests_wg_outer_frag_15102.vf07.diff` and `flowless_verdict_tests.vf07.diff` (reverted after the run). Output is in `RUN/verify/vf07/cargo_vf07.txt`, decisive lines in `cargo_vf07_decisive.txt`: `VF07 ike-head armed -> true`, `VF07 ike-tail armed -> true`; controls `VF07 ike-tail unarmed -> false`, `VF07 whole-udp armed -> false`; `2 passed`. The second probe ran the flowless host-inbound matrix (G37-02 leg, supporting): `zone=ike-only proto=17 -> HostInboundDeny`, `zone=all proto=17 -> HostInboundDeny`, positive control `zone=any-service proto=17 -> Deliver`. Limit: the XDP program was not loaded, so the degraded drop is established from the source order, not from a packet test.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In `is_degraded_local_or_control`, apply the WG-fragment exclusion only to datagrams that are provably WG. At minimum, restrict it to tails (`protocol == PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, mirroring lib.rs:862) and fix the head row of the truth table. Preferably, fix it together with G37-02 by keying the tail disposition on a "WG head claimed" record. Acceptance: a host-executed cell where a degraded fragmented UDP head to a local address with WG_RX armed is local/control (kernel pass); the WG tail row stays on the helper in healthy mode; `tests_wg_outer_frag_15102` stays green.

## #16439 — Every `cargo test` invocation in the tree runs default features. So `accumulate_carries_policy_revoked_sessions_10021`, whose module is gated `#[cfg(feature = "debug-log")]`, is absent from the test binary. The discriminating assertions... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Every `cargo test` invocation in the tree runs default features. So `accumulate_carries_policy_revoked_sessions_10021`, whose module is gated `#[cfg(feature = "debug-log")]`, is absent from the test binary. The discriminating assertions of `direct_tx_tuple_mismatch_recycles_frame_exactly_once` (#4041) and of the two #9782 no-false-mismatch cells are inside `if cfg!(feature = "debug-log")`, so they are dead in every leg.

**Finding ID:** R3-A84-02
**Severity (source):** Low — the unguarded code exists only in the opt-in diagnostic `debug-log` build, which is not the production target. In that build a #4041 recurrence would be on-wire corruption or a double-free of a TX frame, but only during lab diagnostics.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
the only build in which the #4041 aliasing bug can recur has no executed oracle, and #1678 already showed this feature rotting silently. The cells read as protection in a file listing.

**Contract:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/debug_report.rs:554-558` says "RED-on-revert: dropping the field or the `accumulate` line fails to compile (surface absent) or asserts here". `tx/dispatch/tests/enqueue_failure.rs:518-520` says "RED-on-revert (run with `--features debug-log`): reinstating the duplicate `push_front` …". CLAUDE.md says "a Rust dataplane regression fails `make test`".

**Trace:** a regression reintroduces the #4041 duplicate `push_front` in the debug-log arm of `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1768-1800`. Legs 1 and 2 compile that arm out, and the cell takes its `else` branch. `make test` stays green. A lab engineer then deploys a debug-log helper and gets aliased TX frames.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`worker/loop_body/mod.rs:51-52` reads `#[cfg(feature = "debug-log")] mod debug_report;`. `enqueue_failure.rs:605-630` is `if cfg!(feature = "debug-log") { assert_eq!(free.len(), egress_free_before, "#4041: …"); assert_eq!(dup, 1, …); … forward_tuple_mismatch … }`, and outside it only `dup <= 1` runs, which is vacuous when the mismatch branch is compiled out. `enqueue_failure.rs:740-751` and `tests/segmentation.rs:860-871` each hold a `cfg!(feature = "debug-log")`-only `!reasons…starts_with("forward_tuple_mismatch")`. The production branches are `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1768 if cfg!(feature = "debug-log") {` (direct TX) and `:1458` (segmented). Invocations: Makefile:466-472 (test-rust legs 0-2) has no `--features`, and Makefile:105-106 `build-userspace-dp-debug-log` is `cargo build … --features debug-log` (compile-only, and its header says "not an automated gate"). `.github/workflows/test.yml:97` runs only `cargo check`.

**Probe:** `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- --list` (CARGO_TARGET_DIR dr3-va84) produced RUN/verify/va84/r02-list-default.out: `9175 tests`. `accumulate_carries_policy_revoked_sessions_10021` does not appear. Positive control in the same listing: `afxdp::coordinator::status::tests::refresh_status_publishes_policy_revoked_sessions_total_10021`, `afxdp::tests_policy_revocation_8356::a_revoked_session_bumps_the_release_visible_live_atomic_10021`, `protocol::tests::process_status_policy_revoked_sessions_total_roundtrip_10021` and `afxdp::tx::dispatch::tests::enqueue_failure::direct_tx_tuple_mismatch_recycles_frame_exactly_once` are all listed, so the listing sees cells and only the gated module is missing. Limit: I did not show that the cells pass, or red on revert, under `--features debug-log`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
add one cheap leg, `cargo test --features debug-log --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- tx::dispatch loop_body::debug_report`, to `test-rust` or `make selftest`, or else correct the RED-on-revert comments. Acceptance: deleting `interval.policy_revoked_sessions` from `accumulate`, or restoring the #4041 double push, reds a registered leg.

## #16440 — DDNS rfc2136 LastError, journald warnings and gRPC/CLI status re-disclose the update-server userinfo that #15174 redacted on the field renderers [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
DDNS rfc2136 LastError, journald warnings and gRPC/CLI status re-disclose the update-server userinfo that #15174 redacted on the field renderers

**Finding ID:** R3-F07-02
**Severity (source):** Low — Low. The credential in `update-server` userinfo is shown to view-class CLI logins and gRPC readers, and is written to journald. This is the same audience and the same bound as #15174, which redacted the field itself. The trigger is an operator placing a credential in an rfc2136 host field, which RFC 2136 never uses. Such a value cannot work, so it re-discloses on every failed cycle.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The #15174 fix is incomplete for the same principals. The same credential appears in the error row next to the redacted field, and in journald, on every backoff cycle until the operator fixes the config.

**Contract:** #9497/#15174 redact `update-server` through `config.RedactURL` on every PermView surface (`pkg/cli/show_services_ddns.go:151-153` comment: "RedactURL, like the gRPC twin / show configuration / String / MarshalJSON"). The #9164 feeds precedent and the HTTP DDNS backends (`backend_http.go:646`, `backend_dyndns2.go:150-176`) treat error text as such a surface and redact URLs in it.

**Trace:** `set services dynamic-dns provider P backend rfc2136 update-server user:s3cr3t@host` → commit accepts it → `resolveBackend` → `newSurfaceARFC2136` → `newRFC2136Updater` (server unchanged) → publish → `exchange` → dial error embeds the address → `recordScopeError` → `rt.lastErr` → `StatusViews.LastError` → `show services dynamic-dns detail` (CLI and gRPC) and journald.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_ddns.go:154-166` (`ddnsUpdateServerParseable`: SplitHostPort or no-whitespace accept). `pkg/ddns/backend_rfc2136.go:234-252` (`normalizeUpdateServer` returns the value unchanged). `:1470-1473` (`resp, _, err := u.client.ExchangeContext(ctx, m, u.server); if err != nil { return nil, err }`). `:1434-1443` (TSIG errors format `u.server`). `pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:2179` (`rt.lastErr = err.Error()`) and `:2181` (`slog.Warn(... "err", err)`). `:2304` (`v.LastError = rt.lastErr`). `pkg/cli/show_services_ddns.go:104` and `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_dhcp_lldp_snmp.go:~514` (`termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay(v.LastError)`, no redaction). `grep RedactURL pkg/ddns` hits only the HTTP backends.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/ddns/ -run TestVF07 -count=1 -v` with `RUN/verify/vf07/probes/zz_vf07_lasterr_test.go` (removed from the worktree after the run). Output in `RUN/verify/vf07/go_ddns_lasterr.txt`. Positive control `server="127.0.0.1:38637" ... LastError="" leak=false`. Leak cases: `server="user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com" ... LastError="ddns surface-a: publish A wan.example.net=203.0.113.5: ddns: forward upsert A wan.example.net: dial udp: lookup udp/s3cr3t@dns.example.com: unknown port" leak=true redacted="<redacted>@dns.example.com"`; the `:53` form gives `lookup user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com:53: no such host` with leak=true. The journald line `WARN ddns: sending UNSIGNED DNS UPDATE ... server=user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com` was also observed. Limit: the CLI/gRPC renderers were not driven. The leak is shown at the status-view boundary they render from.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Render `u.server` through `config.RedactURL` in every rfc2136 error and log site (exchange wrapper, TSIG validation, `warnUnsignedOnce`). Alternatively redact `LastError` at the status boundary, or better, strict-reject userinfo in rfc2136 `update-server` at commit. Acceptance: the vf07 probe reports leak=false for both shapes while the positive control is unchanged, and `show services dynamic-dns detail` (CLI and gRPC) shows no `s3cr3t`.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf07.md)</summary>

### R3-F07-02 — DDNS rfc2136 LastError, journald warnings and gRPC/CLI status re-disclose the update-server userinfo that #15174 redacted on the field renderers
- **Finding ID:** R3-F07-02
- **Title:** DDNS rfc2136 LastError, journald warnings and gRPC/CLI status re-disclose the update-server userinfo that #15174 redacted on the field renderers
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker f07 (Fix-residual hunter (delta group 07)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vf07
- **Severity:** Low. The credential in `update-server` userinfo is shown to view-class CLI logins and gRPC readers, and is written to journald. This is the same audience and the same bound as #15174, which redacted the field itself. The trigger is an operator placing a credential in an rfc2136 host field, which RFC 2136 never uses. Such a value cannot work, so it re-discloses on every failed cycle.
- **Confidence:** High. The leak is executed end-to-end through the production rfc2136 constructor and `StatusViews`. The CLI/gRPC rendering through `termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay` (escaping only) is read statically.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — `pkg/ddns` probe through `newSurfaceARFC2136` → `Reconcile` → `StatusViews().LastError`, with a positive control (working fake DNS server). The renderer step is STATIC.
- **Gate verdict:** COHORT (credential-redaction residuals: #15174/#9497/#9164 class). It is a real residual of a closed redaction fix, bounded to a misconfiguration that already embeds a credential.
- **Contract:** #9497/#15174 redact `update-server` through `config.RedactURL` on every PermView surface (`pkg/cli/show_services_ddns.go:151-153` comment: "RedactURL, like the gRPC twin / show configuration / String / MarshalJSON"). The #9164 feeds precedent and the HTTP DDNS backends (`backend_http.go:646`, `backend_dyndns2.go:150-176`) treat error text as such a surface and redact URLs in it.
- **Adversarial analysis:** The boundary is configuration secrets vs. view-class principals (and journald readers). The actor is a low-privilege view login or a gRPC show caller; it controls nothing and only reads. The prerequisite is an operator-authored `update-server` with userinfo (accepted at commit: `ddnsUpdateServerParseable` passes both `user:s3cr3t@host` and `user:s3cr3t@host:53`). The challenged assumption is that redacting the field renderer redacts the value. The rfc2136 backend passes the raw server string to `net.Dialer` and to its own `fmt.Errorf` calls, and the errors flow unredacted into status.

"err", err)`). `:2304` (`v.LastError = rt.lastErr`). `pkg/cli/show_services_ddns.go:104` and `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_dhcp_lldp_snmp.go:~514` (`termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay(v.LastError)`, no redaction). `grep RedactURL pkg/ddns` hits only the HTTP backends.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/ddns/ -run TestVF07 -count=1 -v` with `RUN/verify/vf07/probes/zz_vf07_lasterr_test.go` (removed from the worktree after the run). Output in `RUN/verify/vf07/go_ddns_lasterr.txt`. Positive control `server="127.0.0.1:38637" ... LastError="" leak=false`. Leak cases: `server="user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com" ... LastError="ddns surface-a: publish A wan.example.net=203.0.113.5: ddns: forward upsert A wan.example.net: dial udp: lookup udp/s3cr3t@dns.example.com: unknown port" leak=true redacted="<redacted>@dns.example.com"`; the `:53` form gives `lookup user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com:53: no such host` with leak=true. The journald line `WARN ddns: sending UNSIGNED DNS UPDATE ... server=user:s3cr3t@dns.example.com` was also observed. Limit: the CLI/gRPC renderers were not driven. The leak is shown at the status-view boundary they render from.
- **Trace:** `set services dynamic-dns provider P backend rfc2136 update-server user:s3cr3t@host` → commit accepts it → `resolveBackend` → `newSurfaceARFC2136` → `newRFC2136Updater` (server unchanged) → publish → `exchange` → dial error embeds the address → `recordScopeError` → `rt.lastErr` → `StatusViews.LastError` → `show services dynamic-dns detail` (CLI and gRPC) and journald.
- **Refutation attempt:** Checked whether any status-boundary redactor exists: `SanitizeForDisplay` escapes control characters only. Checked whether commit rejects userinfo for rfc2136: it does not. Checked whether the dial error could omit the address: Go's net errors always include it in both shapes (EXECUTED). Checked the HTTP backends: they redact, so the gap is rfc2136-specific. I could not refute it; the reporter's claim stands as stated, plus the journald sink.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Not applicable. This is the control-plane error path, once per failed DDNS cycle.

## #16441 — `Promote` sends a `BootEntries()` error, and a missing candidate slot, straight to `revert`, which returns exit 3 and causes a reboot. It does not apply the RunningKernel discrimination that #4872-A added for the Boot... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`Promote` sends a `BootEntries()` error, and a missing candidate slot, straight to `revert`, which returns exit 3 and causes a reboot. It does not apply the RunningKernel discrimination that #4872-A added for the BootCurrent-unreadable sibling. A firmware-fallback boot that hits an NVRAM read timeout therefore reboots an already-safe firewall and records "reverted" where "discarded" is true.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low. One unnecessary reboot, which happens after xpfd has started (xpf-kernel-promote is ordered After=xpfd.service), plus a false last-roll record. It needs a firmware fallback combined with an efibootmgr failure or the 10 s timeout. The journal is cleared, so the attempt cap bounds it to a single reboot. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A56-05`
**Source part:** `parts/va56.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
An avoidable outage of one reboot on an appliance that was already safe, and an operator record that misstates the outcome.

**Contract:** `kernel_run.go:643-686` (#4872 A) says that when the booted slot cannot be read, "check RunningKernel first", and that positive evidence of a non-candidate kernel takes the no-reboot `cleanupAlreadyOnKnownGood` path, because "rebooting again would be redundant".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`kernel_run.go:634-637` `entries, err := sys.BootEntries(); if err != nil { return …, r.revert(j, fmt.Errorf("read boot entries: %w", err)) }`. `:638-641` sends the missing slot to revert the same way. revert returns `ErrKernelReverted`, which maps to exit 3, and xpf-kernel-promote then runs `systemctl reboot`.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED. Production Promote ran with the package fake system on an ARMED journal (BootCurrent=known-good, uname=known-good, BootEntries failing).

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** Gate 1 turns **any** `BootEntries` error or missing slot directly into `revert` (`pkg/upgrade/kernel_run.go:633-641`), even when `RunningKernel` proves already known-good. The adjacent BootCurrent-error path **does** discriminate and safely discards (`:642-675`). This produces an unnecessary reboot and inaccurate last-roll result.
- **Refutation:** If candidate is actually running, revert is necessary; if running kernel cannot be read, preserving uncertainty is necessary. One-shot journal clear bounds repeated reboot. **Decisive check:** BootEntries failure/missing-ID matrix crossed with candidate, known-good and unknown running kernel; preserve candidate fail-closed semantics and avoid unnecessary known-good reboot.

## #16442 — `isRustTestModuleFile15255` filters by basename (`tests_*`, `*_tests.rs`, `*_test.rs`, or `/tests/`). The 13 `tests.rs` files (2117 `#[test]` lines) and every inline test module in production files fall outside it, so the guard #15255... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`isRustTestModuleFile15255` filters by basename (`tests_*`, `*_tests.rs`, `*_test.rs`, or `/tests/`). The 13 `tests.rs` files (2117 `#[test]` lines) and every inline test module in production files fall outside it, so the guard #15255 added for displaced `#[test]` attributes is blind to roughly a third of the crate's cells.

**Finding ID:** R3-A84-03
**Severity (source):** Low — this is an assurance gap in a regression guard, and no cell is lost today (the reporter's crate-wide scan found no live orphan). The consequence is that the next #9962-style displacement in screen, session, filter, server, coordinator or forwarding tests would silently drop a cell.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
the largest Rust test files (screen 278 cells, session_glue 267 and others) are exactly where a merge-displaced attribute is likeliest, and there the census built for this class reads green.

**Contract:** `pkg/refactoraudit/duplicate_test_attribute_8393_test.go:223-249` describes the target as "a zero-arg asserting fn in a test module with NO attribute and no caller — silently never runs". #15255's fix commit 4d333d86f1 describes "a census for zero-arg asserting unregistered fns in Rust test modules".

**Trace:** a `#[test]` is displaced in a `tests.rs` module. rustc warns `dead_code`, which does not gate. `make test-rust` no longer runs the cell, and `make test-go` runs the census green because the file was never opened.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`duplicate_test_attribute_8393_test.go:251-257` reads `return strings.HasPrefix(base, "tests_") || strings.HasSuffix(base, "_tests.rs") || strings.HasSuffix(base, "_test.rs") || strings.Contains(rel, "/tests/")`. `TestNoUnregisteredAssertingTestFn15255` (:393 onward) returns early for any path the filter rejects. `find userspace-dp/src -name tests.rs` lists 13 files carrying 2117 `#[test]` lines, out of 9257 `#[test]` lines crate-wide. The reporter's wider count, which includes inline modules, is 3345 of 9218 (36%). I did not re-derive the inline-module share.

**Probe:** the baseline result was `ok` (RUN/verify/va84/r03-baseline.out). For the defect I deleted the `#[test]` at `userspace-dp/src/session/tests.rs:125`, above `pmech_install_reserves_reply_alias_and_local_capacity`. That name occurs once in the file and its body has 11 asserts. The result was `ok` (r03-defect.out, diff r03-mutant-defect.diff), so the lost cell went undetected. For the positive control I deleted the `#[test]` at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache_tests.rs:143`, above `cache_hit_with_matching_stamp`. That run FAILED with `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache_tests.rs:143 — fn cache_hit_with_matching_stamp() asserts but carries no #[test] and is never called` (r03-control.out). Both mutants were reverted and `git status` was clean. The reporter's independent pair (screen/tests.rs:4940 green, tests_slow_path_disposition.rs:4104 red) agrees.

## Acceptance / fix direction
scan every `.rs` file under `userspace-dp/` but only inside `#[cfg(test)]` regions, or at minimum add `base == "tests.rs"` plus inline `#[cfg(test)] mod` detection. Add detector-table rows for a `tests.rs` path and for an inline module. Acceptance: the session/tests.rs mutant above reds, and the baseline stays green.

## Full validated claim

## #16443 — `request system zeroize` (gRPC SystemAction or console) cannot complete while any process runs under an xpf-provisioned login account, and the operator's own SSH/CLI session is such a process. `userdel -r <name>` (no `-f`, no session ter... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`request system zeroize` (gRPC SystemAction or console) cannot complete while any process runs under an xpf-provisioned login account, and the operator's own SSH/CLI session is such a process. `userdel -r <name>` (no `-f`, no session termination) returns exit 8, the leg fails, and the remaining legs still run. Every retry from that session fails the same way. The box is left half-wiped: no SSH host keys, no root or xpf login keys, no xpf sudoers, no networkd drop-ins and no config DB. It can no longer persist a commit, and its next boot is the fail-closed pending-reset bootstrap.

**Finding ID:** R3-N01-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — the documented remote path for a super-user fails. That is an SSH session as a `system login user` account, which is the only key-based non-root login the image allows. Each attempt destroys remote access and persistence, so recovery is console-only and the next reboot leaves the box with no forwarding until a reset completes from the console. No enforcement or isolation is lost, and the box is recoverable from the console, so this is not High. The availability consequence is demonstrated at component level; the end-to-end SSH session is a lab check. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
This hits every operator who factory-resets remotely with an xpf-provisioned admin account. Each attempt leaves the box running on in-memory config with no way to persist a commit, no new SSH logins possible (root and xpf keys gone, the caller without sudo), and a bootstrap boot with no forwarding after any restart. Recovery needs the console, and zeroize must be retried from there.

**Contract:** zeroize is a super-user (maintenance) action (docs/system-login.md). The image allows SSH only by key, with `PasswordAuthentication no` and `PermitRootLogin prohibit-password` (scripts/image/bake.py:350-357), so a super-user normally reaches the CLI through a provisioned account. Three documents say a failed reset stays recoverable and can be retried: the handler comment ("the daemon … keeps running normally until a retried zeroize succeeds", pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:455-462), the Store.Load text ("retry zeroize to complete the interrupted factory reset"), and docs/system-login.md ("on a `userdel` failure the marker is retained so a retried `zeroize` re-attempts").

**Trace:** The operator SSHes in as a provisioned super-user and runs `cli` then `request system zeroize`. That goes to gRPC SystemAction "zeroize", then runZeroize, then daemon ZeroizeFn, then `PerformZeroizeWipePendingWithInventory`, then beginZeroize, which writes the pending marker. performWipe then runs the seal leg (host keys and /root/.ssh gone) and wipeLoginAccounts (sudoers gone, the caller's authorized_keys unlinked, `userdel -r caller` returns rc 8). Networkd, firewall logs and the config dir are still erased. Because errs is not empty, the markers stay, the daemon's resetFailed path runs, and the RPC returns "zeroize incomplete … exit status 8".

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/factoryreset/wipe.go:379-381 `wipeUserdel … "userdel", "-r", name` (no `-f`). wipe.go:818-831: the matched-UID branch unlinks authorized_keys, then calls `wipeUserdel`; on error it runs `fail(derr); removeMarker = false`. wipe.go:663-696 sweeps the `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-*` drop-ins before the account loop, so the caller loses sudo first. In `performWipe`, wipe.go:1400 runs the seal leg first (wipe_seal_10769.go:135 host keys, :140 `/root/.ssh` wholesale), then :1436 the login leg, then :1502 networkd. On the wrapper side, wipe_firewall_logs_10300.go:439 runs `beginZeroize` (pending marker), :461 erases the config dir last regardless of earlier errors, and :480 runs `completeZeroize` only when `len(errs)==0`. pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:436-475 runs `s.runZeroize(ctx)` synchronously inside the RPC. A grep for loginctl, pkill or terminate in pkg/factoryreset and pkg/daemon finds nothing. I observed all of these directly. The claim that the operator's sshd-session and cli processes run under its UID is standard OpenSSH privilege separation (inference).

**Probe:** First, `unshare --map-users=auto --map-groups=auto --map-root-user -m bash RUN/verify/vn01/probes/v_userdel_busy_uid1001_run.sh` (output RUN/verify/vn01/v_userdel_busy_uid1001_output.txt). Busy arm: `userdel: user admin is currently used by process 4129961`, `rc=8`, admin still in passwd. Control: idle account removed, and admin removed after its process exited. n01's original probe gave the busy account UID 0, which every process matches, so I replaced it. Second, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -run TestR3N01 -v` (RUN/verify/vn01/v_rerun_n01_probes_output.txt). Busy arm: `wipe err (admin busy): exit status 8`; ssh_host key, authorized_keys, `10-xpf-fxp0.network` and `.configdb` all absent; `.day0-config-applied` present; `Store.Load: factory reset is pending`; `retry err (still busy): exit status 8`. Idle control: `wipe err: <nil>` and the marker cleared. Post-failure commit: `persist active config … .configdb … no such file or directory`; the no-zeroize control commits and reloads `host-name "recovered"`. Limit: the Go arm injects rc 8 at the userdel seam, and the real userdel behaviour comes from the separate namespace probe.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Before any destructive leg, refuse the zeroize when a provisioned account to be deleted has live processes, naming the account. Alternatively, lock those accounts and terminate their sessions (for example `loginctl terminate-user` or `pkill -KILL -u <uid>` scoped to the marker UID) and then `userdel`. A third option is to defer the calling principal's account removal to the post-wipe stop or reboot. Consumers: the gRPC and console entry points share `performWipe`. Acceptance: with the userdel seam reporting busy for a provisioned account, the wipe either completes or fails with every surface intact. Twin: an idle account still completes.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn01.md)</summary>

### R3-N01-01 — Zeroize issued from an xpf-provisioned account's own session can never complete: `userdel -r` refuses the busy account (exit 8) after host keys, every login key, sudoers, networkd drop-ins and the config DB are already erased

A grep for loginctl, pkill or terminate in pkg/factoryreset and pkg/daemon finds nothing. I observed all of these directly. The claim that the operator's sshd-session and cli processes run under its UID is standard OpenSSH privilege separation (inference).
- **Probe:** First, `unshare --map-users=auto --map-groups=auto --map-root-user -m bash RUN/verify/vn01/probes/v_userdel_busy_uid1001_run.sh` (output RUN/verify/vn01/v_userdel_busy_uid1001_output.txt). Busy arm: `userdel: user admin is currently used by process 4129961`, `rc=8`, admin still in passwd. Control: idle account removed, and admin removed after its process exited. n01's original probe gave the busy account UID 0, which every process matches, so I replaced it. Second, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -run TestR3N01 -v` (RUN/verify/vn01/v_rerun_n01_probes_output.txt). Busy arm: `wipe err (admin busy): exit status 8`; ssh_host key, authorized_keys, `10-xpf-fxp0.network` and `.configdb` all absent; `.day0-config-applied` present; `Store.Load: factory reset is pending`; `retry err (still busy): exit status 8`. Idle control: `wipe err: <nil>` and the marker cleared. Post-failure commit: `persist active config … .configdb … no such file or directory`; the no-zeroize control commits and reloads `host-name "recovered"`. Limit: the Go arm injects rc 8 at the userdel seam, and the real userdel behaviour comes from the separate namespace probe.
- **Trace:** The operator SSHes in as a provisioned super-user and runs `cli` then `request system zeroize`. That goes to gRPC SystemAction "zeroize", then runZeroize, then daemon ZeroizeFn, then `PerformZeroizeWipePendingWithInventory`, then beginZeroize, which writes the pending marker. performWipe then runs the seal leg (host keys and /root/.ssh gone) and wipeLoginAccounts (sudoers gone, the caller's authorized_keys unlinked, `userdel -r caller` returns rc 8). Networkd, firewall logs and the config dir are still erased. Because errs is not empty, the markers stay, the daemon's resetFailed path runs, and the RPC returns "zeroize incomplete … exit status 8".
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for these escapes and none applies. Root is special-cased away from userdel (wipe.go:744-760), so only root and console sessions succeed. There is no `-f`, no `usermod -L` with a deferred delete, and no session kill. The UID-mismatch and absent branches do not apply to a live matched account. The daemon failure path does not restore host keys, login keys or sudoers. A later commit cannot re-provision anything because `.configdb` is gone, and the commit fails ENOENT (executed). I narrowed the claim: it is not only the caller's own session. Any live process under any provisioned account triggers it, and the caller's session is the deterministic case.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — this is an operator-triggered maintenance path. The invariant violated is "fail before the destructive legs, or complete": a leg that cannot succeed from the calling context runs after the irreversible legs.

Its "nothing gates on pkt_len" premise has also been stale since #8581.

**Finding ID:** R3-A84-04
**Severity (source):** Low — there is no production defect. The consequences are a standing master-red Rust cell, which stops `make test-rust` from distinguishing a new regression from this one, and IPv6 fixtures that drive CoS, policer and flow-cache byte paths 14 bytes short of production. The reporter's Python replica (workers/a84/evidence/r3-a84-04-{head,control}.out) agrees. Limit: the debug profile was run. The cell carries no debug_assertions gate, so the release leg 1 is red too (inferred, not run).

## Acceptance / fix direction
fix `resolver_enqueue_tests.rs:228` and `txn_meta_v6`. Replace the literal sinks with a comment-stripped pattern such as `pkt_len\s*[:=][^;\n]*-\s*14`, keeping the non-pkt_len wire-length invariants legal, and correct the stale header. Acceptance: the cell is green on the fixed tree and reds on each listed spelling reintroduced.
