## #16484 — In the fresh-allocator arm of `Nat64State::from_snapshots_with_previous`, the #6765 retained-address reseed takes its source allocator from the FIRST previous prefix with equal prefix bytes. `prev_prefix_is_deterministic` takes the same ... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
In the fresh-allocator arm of `Nat64State::from_snapshots_with_previous`, the #6765 retained-address reseed takes its source allocator from the FIRST previous prefix with equal prefix bytes. `prev_prefix_is_deterministic` takes the same first match. Since #15678 several zone- or RI-scoped rule-sets can share one /96 with disjoint pools. A pool edit on any rule-set after the first therefore reseeds from the wrong allocator (an empty index map, so nothing is carried, or the reseed is suppressed outright when the first rule-set is deterministic). That rule-set's live sessions stay valid, and the fresh allocator hands their (X, P) to other clients connecting to the same server.

**Finding ID:** R3-N05-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium. A routine pool edit on one tenant's rule-set silently voids that tenant's live reservations, and a DIFFERENT host is minted a live tuple (demonstrated). Replies are then potentially delivered to the wrong host, which is cross-host integrity and availability loss inside one tenant's client population. Pools are disjoint across rule-sets, so it is not cross-tenant, and it lasts only as long as the surviving sessions. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Per-tenant NAT64 under the well-known prefix is the layout #15678 enabled. Growing or shrinking any tenant's pool except the first one's silently strips its live reservations, and that tenant's other hosts' new flows to popular origins collide with live sessions. No counter or log reports it.

**Contract:** As for R3-N05-01, the `nat64/mod.rs` #4518 reload durability statement and the #6765 reseed contract at `nat64/state.rs:916-924` both require that THIS prefix's retained live ownership is carried. `nat64_revalidation_still_valid` documents same-/96 rule-sets in different zones or RIs with disjoint pools as a supported shape (#15678/#15932).

**Trace:** rule-sets `tenant-a` (zone trust-a, pool 198.51.100.1) and `tenant-b` (zone trust-b, pool 203.0.113.1), both `64:ff9b::/96`. Client c1 in trust-b mints F1 = (203.0.113.1, 1024). A commit appends 203.0.113.2 to tenant-b's pool → `forwarding_build/mod.rs:801` → `reuse_allocator` misses → fresh allocator → the reseed looks up tenant-a's previous prefix → empty index map → nothing carried → F1 revalidates valid (pool membership plus range) → client c2 in trust-b connects to the same server → `(203.0.113.1, 1024)`.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Observed @d1ea69f9aa:

**Probe:** Same run as R3-N05-01 (`RUN/verify/vn05/cargo_n05.log`, `12 passed`). Cells are in `RUN/workers/n05/evidence/nat64_tests_probe_snapshot.rs` and `RUN/verify/vn05/probes/vn05_nat64_tests_cells.rs`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Select the previous prefix by rule identity: the snapshot `name`, or prefix bytes plus normalized scope, in both the reseed lookup and `prev_prefix_is_deterministic`. Acceptance: `vn05_scoped_second_rule_pool_edit_reissues_live_tuple` and `r3n05_scoped_same_prefix_pool_edit_drops_second_rule_reservations` invert, `vn05_scoped_det_first_suppresses_rr_second_reseed` inverts (tenant-b reseeds), and the first-rule and single-rule controls stay green.

## #16485 — #15946 residual: `time-wait-state session-ageout` / `apply-to-half-closed-state` change the enforced close windows, but `RenderFlowTimeouts` (CLI/gRPC/REST SSOT) still prints `time-wait-timeout` / `closing-timeout`; `session-ageout` +... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
#15946 residual: `time-wait-state session-ageout` / `apply-to-half-closed-state` change the enforced close windows, but `RenderFlowTimeouts` (CLI/gRPC/REST SSOT) still prints `time-wait-timeout` / `closing-timeout`; `session-ageout` + `session-timeout` commit together and ageout silently wins

**Finding ID:** R3-A93-03
**Severity (source):** Low — the global summary on all three show surfaces is wrong. With `session-ageout`, closed TCP sessions are held for the established/app window (1800 s by default), while show prints the 30-150 s TIME_WAIT figure. No enforcement is lost, and per-session output (`timeout_secs_for`) shows the true expiry [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
`session-ageout` lengthens closed-session retention by roughly 12-60×. The global flow-timeout summary is where an operator checks that, and it shows the unchanged figure on every surface. Session-table pressure from closed sessions is then misdiagnosed. Recovery means reading per-session dumps.

**Contract:** `pkg/config/show_ssot_15649.go:10-15` makes the helpers "the single authority all three surfaces call", so they must describe what the dataplane enforces. Juniper `time-wait-state` (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/security-edit-flow-time-wait-state.html, fetched by va93): "`session-ageout`: Set a TCP session to age out, using the service based timeout value." and "`session-timeout` ... Range: 2 through 600 seconds". That the Junos syntax presents `session-ageout` and `session-timeout` as alternatives comes from the reporter (12.1X47 `security-edit-flow-security-flow.html`). va93 re-fetched the current `time-wait-state` page: its Syntax block is empty in the fetched rendering and it lists the two options as separate bullets, so the either/or is UNCONFIRMED. The commit-exclusion sub-leg is therefore weaker than the show leg, which rests on xpf's own SSOT contract.

**Trace:** `set security flow tcp-session time-wait-state session-ageout` → `compileFlow` `TimeWaitStateSessionAgeout=true` (`compiler_security_flow.go:801-802`) → `flow.go:129` `TCPTimeWaitSessionAgeout` (wire v67) → Rust `SessionTimeouts.tcp_time_wait_session_ageout` (`session/mod.rs:618`) → `tcp_close_window_ns_with_app` → entry expiry. In parallel, `RenderFlowTimeouts` reads `TimeWaitTimeout`/`ClosingTimeout` only → CLI/gRPC/REST.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Show @d1ea69f9aa, `pkg/config/show_ssot_15649.go:74-79`: the closing row is `tcpRow("TCP closing timeout", ..., tcp.ClosingTimeout)`, and the TIME_WAIT row uses `effectiveTimeWait := tcp.TimeWaitTimeout; if tcp.TimeWaitStateSessionTimeout > 0 { effectiveTimeWait = ... }`. Neither flag is read. A non-test grep of `pkg`/`cmd` for `SessionAgeout|ApplyToHalfClosed` finds only types, compiler and `flow.go:129-130`. The callers are `pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:921`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_flow.go:90` and `pkg/api/show_text.go:428`. Dataplane, `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:879-904`: the Closing class with half-closed returns `tcp_time_wait_ns`, or the app/established window under ageout. The TimeWait class with ageout returns `app_override_ns.unwrap_or(timeouts.tcp_established_ns)`. Its callers are `tcp_close_window_for_entry` (`mod.rs:862-871`) and the HA install at `session/install.rs:1047`. The doc comment at `mod.rs:874-877` says "an explicit TW session-timeout ... still wins when no app override exists", but the code returns `tcp_established_ns`, so ageout wins. That contradicts the comment.

**Probe:** EXECUTED `RUN/verify/va93/probes/va93_probe_test.go` `TestVA93TimeWaitShow` (output in `go_config_out.txt`). Control `time-wait-timeout 40` → `TCP time-wait timeout: 40s`. Positive control for the fixed leg: `+ time-wait-state session-timeout 90` → `90s`, so the #15946 override is shown. `time-wait-timeout 40` + `session-ageout` → `ageout=true` but show is still `40s`. `closing-timeout 10` + `apply-to-half-closed-state` + `session-timeout 120` → show `TCP closing timeout: 10s`. `session-ageout` + `session-timeout 120` → `schemaErr=<nil>`, show `120s`. Rust cell `va93_close_window_probe` (`rust_full.out`; decisive lines in `rust_decisive.txt`: `tw=40 ageout=true TimeWait=1800000000000`, `tw-session-timeout=120 + ageout TimeWait=1800000000000`, `closing=10 half_closed=true tw=120 Closing=120000000000`, control `Closing=10000000000`): TimeWait with tw=40 s and no ageout → 40 s (control). With ageout → `tcp_established_ns` (1800 s). With tw=120 s plus ageout → 1800 s, not 120 s. Closing with half-closed → the TW window (120 s), not 10 s. Control without half-closed → 10 s.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Derive the closing and TIME_WAIT rows in `RenderFlowTimeouts` from the same selector as `tcp_close_window_ns_with_app`, with annotations "service/established timeout (session-ageout)" and "time-wait window (apply-to-half-closed-state)". Reject `session-ageout` together with `session-timeout` at strict commit (warn on lenient), or document the precedence, and fix the contradicting Rust comment. Acceptance: the four probe cases render the dataplane-effective window, and the 40 s and 90 s controls are unchanged.

## #16486 — Sessions of every IP protocol other than TCP/UDP/ICMP (GRE, ESP, AH, SCTP, 6in4, OSPF) idle out after 30 s; the Junos protocol default for "Other" is 30 minutes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Sessions of every IP protocol other than TCP/UDP/ICMP (GRE, ESP, AH, SCTP, 6in4, OSPF) idle out after 30 s; the Junos protocol default for "Other" is 30 minutes

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — every permitted session of an "other" protocol that has no application `inactivity-timeout` is reaped after 30 s idle instead of 1800 s. On the usual one-way posture (trust->untrust permit only), the first remote-originated packet after a gap of more than 30 s matches no session and is policy-denied. For example, inbound ESP on an idle non-NAT-T IPsec passthrough tunnel is dropped until the inside peer sends again (DPD runs over IKE/UDP and does not refresh the ESP session). The impact is bounded: TCP, UDP and ICMP are unaffected, and an operator can work around it with a custom application `inactivity-timeout`. The 30 s reap is demonstrated in a unit probe. The end-to-end blackhole is inferred, not lab-run.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A62-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va62.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
IPsec ESP/AH passthrough, GRE and 6in4 tunnels, PPTP data channels, SCTP associations (heartbeat interval default 30 s + RTO exceeds 30 s) and OSPF transit all hit it. On one-way policies the remote side is blackholed after any lull until the inside sends again. With two-way policies each lull creates a new session, with SESSION_CLOSE/CREATE log and flow-export churn and loss of HA sync continuity. It persists for every idle gap, and recovery depends on inside traffic.

**Contract:** Junos Security 10.2, "Understanding Policy Application Timeout Configuration and Lookup", Table 13 "Protocol-Based Default Timeout", unit minutes: "TCP 30, UDP 1, ICMP 1, OSPF 1, Other 30". It is the last fallback after the application entry's configured timeout and any predefined-application default. xpf already treats this table as its contract for TCP (session/README.md:59 "1800 s (#15127, Junos default)"), UDP and ICMP (60 s).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:306 `const OTHER_SESSION_TIMEOUT_NS: u64 = 30_000_000_000;`. mod.rs:5890-5896 `_ => { if established { app_override_ns.unwrap_or(OTHER_SESSION_TIMEOUT_NS) } else { OTHER_SESSION_TIMEOUT_NS } }`. Every caller of `session_timeout_ns` goes through it: install.rs:652 (local install), install.rs:1048 (HA import), lookup.rs:794 and mod.rs:3785/3981/4237/4259/4582 (hit refresh and promotion). `SessionTimeouts` (mod.rs:495-620) has tcp/udp/icmp fields only. pkg/config/predefined.go:70 `"junos-gre": {Name: "junos-gre", Protocol: "gre"}` and :165 `junos-sctp-any` carry no timeout. Observation: the show-path `timeout_secs_for` (mod.rs:3601-3605) reports 30 for a GRE session.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a session-table unit probe (debug build, base d1ea69f9aa) ran `session_timeout_ns` for protocols 47/50/51/132/41/89 with TCP/UDP/ICMP positive controls, and installed and reaped a GRE session with a UDP twin as control. The end-to-end policy-deny consequence is STATIC.

## #16487 — Seconds-only legacy archive names (`config-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.conf`, 2026-02-14..06-28 builds) are invisible to `isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot`: the #10825 api-auth purge skips them and `rotateArchives` never prunes them [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Seconds-only legacy archive names (`config-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.conf`, 2026-02-14..06-28 builds) are invisible to `isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot`: the #10825 api-auth purge skips them and `rotateArchives` never prunes them

**Finding ID:** R3-B01-01
**Severity (source):** Low — demonstrated, but only on a narrow population. On affected boxes, cleartext superuser-equivalent REST credentials survive the #10825 purge silently, and (vb01 addition) these pre-#4056 files are 0644 in a possibly 0755 dir. Reach needs four things: `system archival` configured in the 2026-04-13..06-28 window (the first .deb was 06-16, and there are no release tags); REST api-auth configured; no more than max-archives (default 10) commits on any 06-28..10-02 build, whose pre-#11804 rotation would have pruned these files as oldest; and an upgrade to a build at or after #10825. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
On an affected long-lived box, the oldest archives keep cleartext REST superuser credentials, world-readable, with no warning or degraded flag, while the migration reports nothing left. Retention also exceeds max-archives forever. The fix is a one-line recognizer change.

**Contract:** store_persist.go:725-727: "isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot recognizes both the current sequenced filename and the legacy pre-sequence timestamp filename". :636-639: the purge removes "recognized xpf snapshots ... when api-auth material is cleartext". :2522-2525: rotation keeps at most maxArchives recognized snapshots. writeArchive's #4056 comment (:2406-2408): "the archive FILES are 0600 regardless".

**Trace:** xpfd `-config /etc/xpf/xpf.conf` → cmd/xpfd/main.go:559-563 opts in DefaultArchiveDir → Store.Load → purgeAPIAuthArchives → the name filter rejects `config-20260501-101500.conf` → silently skipped (not even the "preserving malformed" warning fires). On each commit, writeArchive → rotateArchives ignores the file.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`git show 9ab10042be` writeArchive: `fmt.Sprintf("config-%s.conf", time.Now().Format("20060102-150405"))`. 67f456300f diff: `-...Format("20060102-150405")` → `+...Format("20060102-150405.000000000")`. 848f54893d (#4056, 07-04) changed the mode from 0644 to 0600 for new writes only. Recognizer at store_persist.go:734 `time.Parse("20060102-150405.000000000", stampAndSequence)`, then the seq branch requires a dot plus 20 digits. The consumers filter on it: :670-673 (purge `continue`) and :2532-2536 (rotation). The archive is enabled only via `cfg.System.Archival` (pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:296-308, default dir /var/lib/xpf/archive, max 10). Pre-#11804 rotation (`git show 7789af01f7^:pkg/configstore/store_persist.go`) counted every `config-*.conf` and sorted legacy names oldest.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestVB01LoadSecondsOnlyArchiveEndToEnd -count=1 -v`. Source: verify/vb01/probes/zz_vb01_archive_probe_test.go. Output: verify/vb01/probes/vb01-configstore.out. Observed: `CONTROL nanosecond twin removed=true`; `seconds-only survived=true mode=0644 cleartext-password-present=true`; `recognizer(seconds-only)=false recognizer(nano)=true`. b01's TestB01SecondsOnlyLegacyArchive{Recognized,SurvivesAPIAuthPurge,NeverRotated} fail as designed (rotation with max 2 leaves 5 files). Limits: field population not measured.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Accept `time.Parse("20060102-150405", stamp)` as a legacy name in `isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot`, sorted oldest in rotation. Optionally tighten any legacy archive found at 0644 to 0600 during the Load sweep. Acceptance: the vb01 and b01 cells pass, and the #10825 owned-archive fixture gains the seconds-only name.

## #16488 — The coordinator's `export_idle_persistent_leases`, `export_display_persistent_leases` and `clear_persistent_nat_leases` iterate NAT64 prefixes only when `deterministic_v6` is set. Every round-robin NAT64 flow mints a persistent AnyRemote... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
The coordinator's `export_idle_persistent_leases`, `export_display_persistent_leases` and `clear_persistent_nat_leases` iterate NAT64 prefixes only when `deterministic_v6` is set. Every round-robin NAT64 flow mints a persistent AnyRemoteHost BIB lease with a 300 s timeout. Those leases are therefore invisible to `show security nat source persistent-nat-table`, are not revoked by `clear security nat source persistent-nat-table`, and are never exported to the HA peer while idle.

**Finding ID:** R3-N05-03
**Severity (source):** Low — Low. This is an operator-control and visibility gap with an HA continuity gap. The clear verb silently skips round-robin NAT64 BIBs and show hides them. After a failover an idle v6 socket gets a different mapping, which breaks EIM continuity. There is no collision (the standby never held the port), no enforcement loss, and the impact is bounded by the 300 s idle timeout. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The clear verb is the operator's remedy for a stuck binding, and the show table is the only view of it. Both are silent for the most common NAT64 mode. HA idle continuity is weaker than the gaps doc states.

**Contract:** `clear_persistent_nat_leases` doc: "Revoke every persistent source-NAT lease owned by the current forwarding snapshot". The `nat64/mod.rs` #4512 section says round-robin NAT64 "joins the same `AnyRemoteHost` persistent BIB lease … retains the BIB for 300 seconds". `docs/userspace-dataplane-gaps.md:45,76` say three sync routes (#7360/#8132/#8121) carry "the population" of persistent leases.

**Trace:** a round-robin NAT64 flow → `allocate_nat64_pool_port` (a persistent lease) → the flow closes → idle BIB pinned for 300 s. The operator runs `clear … persistent-nat-table` → the helper's `clear_persistent_nat_leases` skips the prefix and returns 0 for it → the BIB stays live. The 30 s HA idle push → `export_idle_persistent_leases` skips the prefix → the standby has no BIB → after failover the returning socket gets a fresh (X, P).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Observed @d1ea69f9aa:

**Probe:** Same run, `RUN/verify/vn05/cargo_n05.log`. Cells are in `RUN/workers/n05/evidence/idle_lease_sync_8121_tests_probe_snapshot.rs` and `RUN/verify/vn05/probes/vn05_idle_lease_sync_cells.rs`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Drop the `deterministic_v6` gate in all three loops, name round-robin prefixes distinctly (for example `nat64-{idx}`), and on import route them through round-robin tuple validation (pool membership, range, and peer/static/interface ownership) with the clear fence. Acceptance: the round-robin cells show display 1 and exported 1, the clear verb returns 1 and the port is freed, a pre-clear record is clear-fenced on import, and the deterministic 14676/14091 cells stay green.

## Full validated claim

## #16489 — closing_counters_keep_alive (#14937) has no baseline, so every idle half-closed TCP pair is retained one extra close window [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
closing_counters_keep_alive (#14937) has no baseline, so every idle half-closed TCP pair is retained one extra close window

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — this is over-retention of CLOSING (single-FIN, non-RST) pairs that go silent. The pair lives two close windows instead of one: about 60 s at the 30 s default, or a whole extra service timeout (for example 1800 s -> about 3600 s) under `time-wait-state apply-to-half-closed-state session-ageout`. It costs table-slot and pinhole lifetime with no enforcement loss, bounded to one extra window per session. The retention is demonstrated in a unit probe.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A62-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va62.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Half-closed sessions are the population a misbehaving or abusive client mints cheaply. Each holds its slot and pinhole twice as long, and with the #15946 apply-to-half-closed + session-ageout knobs it holds them for an extra full service timeout, which interacts with table-pressure limits.

**Contract:** expire.rs:554-562: "Change — not historic level — is the signal: counters advancing within the last GC interval prove activity at most one interval old ... a quiet flow (static counters) reaps on the next pass." mod.rs:1373-1377: "a quiet flow's historic volume must not retain it forever". The Junos closing-timeout (`security flow tcp-session` closing/time-wait) is the window the operator configures.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`closing_counters_seen` is set to 0 at install.rs:694 and :1088 and written only at expire.rs:597-600: `if forward.closing_counters_seen == total { false } else { forward.closing_counters_seen = total; true }`. On "advanced", expire.rs:606-611 sets `em.last_seen_ns = now_ns` and rebuckets. Unlike `companion_keeps_alive` (expire.rs:700-705), which copies the companion's real `last_seen_ns`, this manufactures freshness. The caller gate at expire.rs:373-381 is `companion_eligible && e_closing && !e_reset && !(e_fin_own && e_fin_peer)`.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a session-table unit matrix (debug build) ran three shapes: no counters (control), pre-FIN data only, and only the FIN packet accounted.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** `closing_counters_seen` starts zero (`userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:711-712,1136-1137`), and first expiry compares that baseline with already-counted FIN/traffic (`session/expire.rs:597-611`), fabricating a fresh `last_seen_ns` for a silent CLOSING pair and granting one extra close window. Packet's inherited 7s unit matrix controlled zero, data-before-FIN and FIN-only.
- **Refutation:** Bounded to one extra window, and active pair preservation is the original safety aim; not proof of orphaned reverse half or perpetual leak. **Decisive check:** seed baseline on actual closing transition, then retest FIN-only idle and genuine post-FIN activity; retain both halves on actual activity only.

**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Monitoring cannot learn that cleartext REST credentials survived in `.config.journal[.N]`, so nobody rotates them. Blast radius is small given the rarity.

**Contract:** journal.go:388-397 and :422-427 say failures "latch LegacyScrubDegraded", "mirroring the #9898 F-113 permission-repair discipline". docs/log/15143.md:55 and README.md:1966 say the flag is polled "like JournalPermsDegraded", and that twin is exported on /health and metrics.

**Trace:** Store.Load (:139/:158/:251) → journal.ScrubLegacyPayloads → migrateLegacyLocked → scrubSegmentLocked error → legacyDegraded=true → no reader outside configstore → /health and Prometheus silent.

Output: verify/vb01/probes/vb01-journal-scrub.out. Observed: `legacy-payload scrub failed ... create temp file ... permission denied`, `LegacyScrubDegraded=true, cleartext canary still on disk`, PASS including the writable-dir control (payload scrubbed, flag false). Limits: the read-only-dir trigger stands in for root-context ENOSPC/EIO.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Wire `JournalLegacyScrubDegradedFn` beside `JournalPermsDegradedFn` (health field plus `xpf_config_journal_legacy_scrub_degraded` gauge). Acceptance: a /health test with a failed scrub shows the field true, and the field is false after a successful retry.

## #16491 — retry_deferred_conntrack_deletes does a full shared-session-map scan per retry under the shared mutex, and is the one shared_sessions lock that panics on poison [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
retry_deferred_conntrack_deletes does a full shared-session-map scan per retry under the shared mutex, and is the one shared_sessions lock that panics on poison

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — the trigger is a deferred conntrack delete (tuple gate busy at GC/teardown time) retried while the shared map is large. Each permitted retry, up to 64 per housekeeping pass, holds the mutex shared by every worker's publish/miss path and HA import for one O(N) scan. Separately, a mutex poisoned by an earlier worker panic re-panics this worker, where 117 other sites recover. The impact is a bounded stall or a secondary panic. The frequency is unmeasured.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A62-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va62.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
A large HA-synced population plus a burst of deferred deletes stalls the retrying worker's housekeeping and blocks other workers' publishes for each scan. A poisoned mutex turns one worker panic into a second one on this path.

**Contract:** afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs:140-168: poisoned shared-session mutexes must be recovered ("recovering existing sessions and clearing poison"), not skipped or panicked on. The worker loop's control-path work must not stall other workers' installs (CLAUDE.md control-socket/contention rules; engineering-style hot-path discipline).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/gc_teardown.rs:483-488: `let shared_id = shared_sessions.lock().expect("shared sessions poisoned").values().find(|entry| entry.key.bare_tuple() == delete.key.bare_tuple()).map(|entry| entry.session_id);` inside `for delete in pending.by_ref().take(RETRY_BUDGET)` (RETRY_BUDGET = 64). The caller is housekeeping.rs:147-152. A census of non-test code finds no other `shared_sessions.lock().expect` and 117 `lock_shared_recover(` calls. An O(1) index exists: `SharedSessionOwnerRgIndexes.bare_tuple_sessions`, used by `close_delta_is_stale_incarnation` (afxdp/session_delta.rs:157-163).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — two unit probes in afxdp/worker/loop_body (debug build, loadavg about 4-6 on 16 cores): scan cost with a 10-row control, and a poison cell with a `lock_shared_recover` control.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** Each deferred delete up to budget 64 locks `shared_sessions` and linearly scans values for bare tuple (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/gc_teardown.rs:478-527`); ordinary shared-map access uses poison-recovery (`afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs:156-167`), whereas this uses `.expect` and can re-panic. The scan is under a contended cross-worker lock.
- **Refutation:** Each lock is dropped per iteration, **not** held for all 64; only deferred tuple-gate retries trigger it; kernel session-id guard narrows wrong-first-match effects. Packet's debug-mode 200k-row timings are **neither release upper bounds nor throughput evidence**; hash-table traversal, LLC/NUMA and mutex contention need measurement before any precise latency claim. **Decisive check:** replace scan with the already maintained bare-tuple index plus exact lookup under recover-on-poison, then measure production-sized release workload and verify stale/incarnation semantics.

## #16492 — A #15273-deferred api-auth migration strands `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json`, so the next plain commit or HA config sync makes the following boot fatal (ErrConfigDBUnreadable) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
A #15273-deferred api-auth migration strands `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json`, so the next plain commit or HA config sync makes the following boot fatal (ErrConfigDBUnreadable)

**Finding ID:** R3-B01-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — demonstrated: once the precondition holds, xpfd refuses to start on every later boot until an operator deletes a file that no message names (an appliance-availability consequence of High class). The precondition is narrow: the first boot that crosses the #10826 migration with legacy cleartext REST api-auth configured while `confirm.json` is present but unreadable. That keeps the severity at Medium. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The affected nodes are those that hit a confirm.json read failure on the upgrade boot crossing #10826 while REST api-auth is configured. The control plane and dataplane do not start until someone manually removes `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json`, and the health alarm itself prompts the triggering commit. On an HA secondary the routine RG0 config sync is enough. The outage lasts until manual repair.

**Contract:** `apiAuthMigrationStagingFile` doc (pkg/configstore/rollback_metadata.go:375-380) says staging "is deleted after the active binding and numbered slots converge". `ConfirmRecoveryReadFailed` doc (store_persist.go:1582-1588) says the lost-window state "clears only when ... a superseding plain commit or config-sync performs that removal (#9887)". /health returns 503 while it is set (store_persist.go:1570-1574). #15273's fix promised that the next boot restores the window "and only then does migration persist" (api_auth_migration_confirm_unreadable_15273_test.go:98-101). Nothing in that contract allows a commit to make the next boot unbootable.

**Trace:** upgrade boot1, legacy cleartext api-auth in active.json (H1), confirm.json unreadable → migrateActiveAPIAuthSecrets stages Old=H1/New=H2, keeps the hashed tree in memory and leaves active.json at H1; Load returns OK with ConfirmRecoveryReadFailed set → /health 503 → operator `commit` (or HA SyncApply) → writeActive H3 plus saveRollbackFiles rebinds the sidecar to H3; staging is untouched → restart → Load → loadRollbackHistory → apiAuthMigrationStagingConsistent: sidecar H3 matches neither New nor Old → ErrConfigDBUnreadable → classifyLoadError → loadFatalUnreadable → xpfd exits. Every restart repeats this.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Observed at d1ea69f9aa:

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestVB01Staging|TestB01DeferredStaging' -count=1 -v`. Source: verify/vb01/probes/zz_vb01_staging_probe_test.go. Output: verify/vb01/probes/vb01-configstore.out. The fixture is the #15273 seed with confirm.json overwritten by `{garbage-not-json`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
When a durable promotion of a new active generation succeeds after a deferred migration (commit, confirm, SyncApply, rollback, persist-retry heal), retire staging: discard it, or converge it once the new active hash is written and the sidecar is rebound. Alternatively, make `apiAuthMigrationStagingConsistent` treat a sidecar that exactly binds the current on-disk active (no generation mismatch) as superseding staging. Also name the staging path in the fatal message. Acceptance: arms A and SyncApply boot cleanly, api-auth is hashed on disk after boot2, and controls B and C still pass.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb01.md)</summary>

### R3-B01-03 — A #15273-deferred api-auth migration strands `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json`, so the next plain commit or HA config sync makes the following boot fatal (ErrConfigDBUnreadable)
- **Finding ID:** R3-B01-03
- **Title:** A #15273-deferred api-auth migration strands `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json`, so the next plain commit or HA config sync makes the following boot fatal (ErrConfigDBUnreadable)
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b01 (A4 storage engineer (second pass)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb01
- **Severity:** Medium — demonstrated: once the precondition holds, xpfd refuses to start on every later boot until an operator deletes a file that no message names (an appliance-availability consequence of High class). The precondition is narrow: the first boot that crosses the #10826 migration with legacy cleartext REST api-auth configured while `confirm.json` is present but unreadable. That keeps the severity at Medium. [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High — executed with a persistent on-disk corruption of confirm.json (realistic) as well as the reporter's transient seam. Two controls pass. Remaining assumption: the rare precondition happens in the field.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — Go probes in pkg/configstore (three arms by vb01 plus b01's commit, sync and no-promotion cells). The fatal daemon exit at the classifier is STATIC.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — reachable deterministic trigger (the documented remedy itself) leading to a concrete fail-closed boot outage, survives refutation and dedup.

Nothing in that contract allows a commit to make the next boot unbootable.
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection is the #10826/#15273 staged migration, which must stay restartable across every durable boundary without bricking boot. The fault is a disk/corruption fault on confirm.json (or a decrypt/oversize read failure) during the upgrade boot. ## #16494 — The #14833 scratch pin (Makefile:34-39, run-selftests.sh:34-38) exports `GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp` (28 characters) to every recipe. Go's `t.TempDir()` then exceeds the 108-byte sun_path limit, and on a clean tree `make test-... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The #14833 scratch pin (Makefile:34-39, run-selftests.sh:34-38) exports `GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp` (28 characters) to every recipe. Go's `t.TempDir()` then exceeds the 108-byte sun_path limit, and on a clean tree `make test-go` / `test-race-dp` fail 45+ socket tests with `bind: invalid argument`. scratch-pinning-selftest.sh checks a modelled 71-byte path that Go never produces.

**Finding ID:** R3-N06-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — a documented local gate now produces about 45 or more false reds in the helper control-socket, event-stream, HA-watchdog, reinject and gRPC teardown tests on every host that does not override GOTMPDIR. These are exactly the failures the project records as "reads like a dataplane defect and is not one" (Makefile:212-214). That removes the signal for those tests and invites wrong fixes. It is bounded: CI does not use make, the workaround is to export a short GOTMPDIR, and the packages are already red for unrelated fixture rot. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
every local `make test-go` / `make test` run (and `scripts/run-selftests.sh` Go legs) shows dozens of IPC/event-stream failures that look like dataplane regressions. Real regressions in that code are indistinguishable from them, and agents are known to "fix" these (the project memory records this trap twice). The effect persists until the root is shortened.

**Contract:** Makefile:210-215: "a long TMPDIR pushes the path past the 108-byte sun_path limit — 'bind: invalid argument', which reads like a dataplane defect and is not one. /var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp is 28 chars, so a Go test temp dir (<TMPDIR>/Test<Name><random>/sock) stays well under 108 bytes." The #14833 acceptance was "verify memlock guards + selftests pass with new TMPDIR".

**Trace:** make (any recipe) → exported GOTMPDIR (28 characters) → `go test` child → `t.TempDir()` = `$GOTMPDIR/<name[:64]><random>/001` → the test binds `<tempdir>/control.sock` (or a similar name) → 109-120 bytes → EINVAL from bind(2), or the config validator rejects a configured control-socket path → the test FAILs.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Makefile:34-39 @d1ea69f9aa: `TMPDIR ?= /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir`, `GOTMPDIR ?= /var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp`, `export TMPDIR GOCACHE GOTMPDIR CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. run-selftests.sh:34-38 has the same defaults. scripts/scratch-pinning-selftest.sh:93-97 has `sock=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp/TestMemlockGuard1234567890/0123456789.sock` with `[ "$n" -lt 108 ]`, and its comment budget "root(28)+testdir(60)+sock(20)" already sums to 108. Observed paths include `/var/tmp/vn06/p28/abcdefghij/TestReinjectSocketCompletionTimeoutResetsPartialFrame95061463570514/001/complete.sock: bind: invalid argument` and the gRPC validator message "socket path ... is 115 octets, over the 107-octet AF_UNIX sun_path limit".

Acceptance: the pinned and unpinned failure sets of `make test-go` are identical, and the canary reds when the root is lengthened past budget.

## #16495 — D11 IPsec-inner admission still refuses admissible frames on lock contention at the router in-flight map, the worker-set authority and the tombstone table, and labels them WORKER_QUEUE_FULL, ADMIT_SHUTDOWN and ADMIT_BAD_LEASE. [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
D11 IPsec-inner admission still refuses admissible frames on lock contention at the router in-flight map, the worker-set authority and the tombstone table, and labels them WORKER_QUEUE_FULL, ADMIT_SHUTDOWN and ADMIT_BAD_LEASE.

**Finding ID:** R3-B12-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — on the production enforcing route-based-VPN (st0/XFRM) D11 path, every refusal is a Go `finishFrame(VerdictDrop)` of a frame policy would permit. That is load-proportional availability loss, not an enforcement or isolation loss. A local harness with realistic per-descriptor work measured 1.9–5.9 % of admissible frames refused. The E23 "worker queue full" counter fires with an empty queue. The attestation ledger records the BAD_LEASE share as a contract FAIL. The production rate has not been measured in a lab. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Transit through a route-based IPsec VPN on the D11 enforcing path loses a share of permitted inner packets that grows with load. TCP over the tunnel sees spurious loss. Operators see "worker queue full", "shutdown" and attestation contract "FAIL" for a box that is none of those. The effect lasts as long as the load. There is no operator mitigation besides lowering load.

**Contract:** The #15151 fix (6a8f8df820) says "contention can no longer masquerade as a full queue" (`ipsec_inner_queue.rs:1999-2000`) and "Only `Full` counts E23 / `WORKER_QUEUE_FULL`" (`:485-488`). The module invariant `:13-14` says E23 means "full then DROP-and-count". The issue's fix direction was "retry or block briefly rather than refuse on contention; count busy separately from full". `docs/engineering-style.md` hot-path rules forbid shared mutex contention on the per-packet path.

**Trace:** NFQUEUE capture (enforcing) → Go `CapturePipeline` submits over the reinject socket → `submit_ipsec_inner_v1` (`slowpath.rs:1462`) → `admit_descriptor` (`ipsec_inner_queue.rs:1970`) → `router.admit` (two authority `try_lock`s, then the in-flight `try_lock`) → `tombstones.try_insert` (`try_lock`) → queue `try_enqueue`. A refusal goes to `refuse_queued_for` → AdmitDecision{admitted:false} → Go `applyAdmission` → `VerdictDrop`. Meanwhile any worker with D11 work holds `live` (per descriptor) and `inflight_by_flow` + `tombstones.entries` (per verdict).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`ipsec_inner_queue.rs:1663-1666`: `let Ok(mut inflight) = self.inflight_by_flow.try_lock() else { IPSEC_INNER_WORKER_QUEUE_FULL_TOTAL.fetch_add(1, ..); return Err(reason::WORKER_QUEUE_FULL); };`. The competing hold is `release()` at `:1676-1679` (blocking `lock()`), run per verdict in `drain_verdicts_into` (`:2230`) and per stale drop in `drain_worker` (`:2074`). At `:1578` and `:1583`, `self.live.try_lock().map_err(|_| ())?` returns `EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE` (`:1657,1661`). The competing hold is `is_live` (`:1604-1607`), run per drained descriptor from `drain_worker`'s `check_generation` (`:2064`). At `:1750`, `self.entries.try_lock()` returns false, and `admit_descriptor` returns `LEASE_EPOCH` (`:1988-1995`). The competing holds are `complete()`/`claim_stale()` (blocking, linear scan) per verdict. In `slowpath.rs:1513-1521`, `EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE => ADMIT_SHUTDOWN`, `WORKER_QUEUE_FULL | WORKER_QUEUE_BUSY | SLAB_EXHAUSTED => ADMIT_FULL` and `_ => ADMIT_BAD_LEASE`, then `refuse(..)`. In Go, `pipeline_attest_10484.go:1120-1154` calls `finishFrame(item.frame, VerdictDrop)` on `!admission.Admitted`. `d11AdmissionReason` (`:732-748`) maps `ADMIT_BAD_LEASE` to contract=true, and `UpdateAdmission` (`:483-500`) sets `TerminalState = "FAIL"`. The commit body of 6a8f8df820 says "NOT changed: depths, budgets, slab/tombstone/router".

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vb12/probes/d11/` has the production module copy, the reporter's `probe_cells.rs` plus the added `vb12_rate_with_eval_work`, and the build command `rustc --edition 2021 -O --test --extern arc_swap=libarc_swap.rlib probe_main.rs`. Deterministic cells (`r3_b12_rerun.out`), with the queue at 1/128 and 512 free slabs: holding `inflight_by_flow` gives `Err(47)` with `FULL_delta=1 BUSY_delta=0`; holding `authority.live` gives `Err(52)`; holding `tombstones.entries` gives `Err(50)`. Each cell admits `Ok(0)` before the hold and immediately after the release (positive control). Realistic rate cell (`vb12_rate.out`; worker spins 0.5–5 µs per descriptor between drain and post; producer spins 0.2–2 µs per frame; in-flight capped at 32×W, so no real depth refusal is possible): W=1 1.85 %, W=3 4.28 %, W=6 4.12 % / 3.23 % / 5.91 %, mostly reasons 47/52/50. Mutation control (`ctl/mutation.diff`, only the three sites changed to blocking `lock()`; `ctl/vb12_rate_ctl.out`): 0.04–0.53 % refused, all reason 61 (per-queue BUSY, the accepted risk), and zero 47/50/52. The reporter's tight-loop cell re-ran at 24.1 % / 13.0 % / 9.0 % (an upper bound). The module's own 29 tests pass in this harness when run serially. Limits: the `arc_swap` shim is a Mutex, which uses blocking loads only and cannot itself produce refusals. Spins stand in for the real D13/D14 work. No lab measurement.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Make admission non-refusing on contention at all three sites. Either replace the router `HashMap`, the authority `BTreeSet` and the tombstone `Vec` mutexes with slab-indexed or atomic state (in-flight and tombstone state are naturally fixed per-slab or per-flow-hash arrays; authority can be an ArcSwap snapshot like the queues), or take a blocking `lock()` where hold time is bounded. Acceptance: the three deterministic cells admit with the respective lock held by another thread (or the lock no longer exists), and the realistic rate cell shows zero reasons 47/50/52 below depth. E23 moves only at `len() >= IPSEC_INNER_QUEUE_DEPTH`.

## #16496 — `merge_matched_tx_modifiers` pushes `Arc::clone` of every matched term's counter and three-color policer into `TxSelectionFilterResult` on every walk. That includes the metered and counted live transit walks, which im... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
`merge_matched_tx_modifiers` pushes `Arc::clone` of every matched term's counter and three-color policer into `TxSelectionFilterResult` on every walk. That includes the metered and counted live transit walks, which immediately drop them. Each matched counted term costs a strong-count `fetch_add`/`fetch_sub` on the counter shared by all workers per packet, and ≥3 handles spill the inline-2 SmallVec to the heap.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — a per-packet CPU and cache-line cost on the non-flow-cache path only, with no enforcement or accounting effect. Magnitude is unmeasured. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A64-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va64.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Operators put DSCP or TCP-flag classifiers with `count` on high-rate egress, and those are exactly the filters that decline the flow cache. The regression re-adds the cross-worker line traffic that #3073/#14656 removed, on every worker. The effect is reduced throughput headroom, not wrong behaviour.

**Contract:** `docs/engineering-style.md` hot-path rules ("Never allocate per packet"; cross-core atomics must not share a hot line). `filter/mod.rs:786-799` and `:722-733` say the `CachedFilterCounters`/`CachedThreeColorPolicers` spill "happens off the packet hot path". The #3073/#14656 coalescer (`filter/mod.rs:1007-1058`) exists so that a per-packet `then count` does not do a shared RMW per packet.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/tx_selection.rs:304-310`: `if let Some(runtime) = term.three_color_policer.as_ref() { acc.three_color_policers.push(std::sync::Arc::clone(runtime)); } if term.has_count { acc.counters.push(term.counter.clone()); }` — unconditional, reached from both v4 (`:270`) and v6 (`:353`) walks for every matched term. `filter/mod.rs:389` `pub(crate) counter: Arc<FilterTermCounter>`. `filter/mod.rs:799-800` `SmallVec<[Arc<FilterTermCounter>; 2]>`. Consumers: `afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:1341-1345`, `:1432-1434` and `:1667-1672` keep the handles only `if defer_side_effects`. The live arms at `:1301-1314` and `:1561-1573` (`evaluate_filter_ref_tx_selection_runtime_counted`) discard them. `forward_request.rs:419-451` resolves live when no precomputed descriptor exists. Commit 716d512c2f (#15268) introduced the pushes (`git show` diff read) and is an ancestor of the base.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — component scope. An in-crate cell ran the production live counted walk and observed the strong counts and the SmallVec spill. No perf measurement was taken.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** `merge_matched_tx_modifiers` clones policer and counted-term `Arc`s regardless of live `now_ns` (`userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/tx_selection.rs:321-335`); live TX-classification keeps these handles only under `defer_side_effects` (`afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:1288-1345`), so noncached packet walks do two strong-refcount RMWs per counted term and may allocate when ≥3 handles overflow the inline-2 SmallVec (`filter/mod.rs:799-800`). Real production-code Arc/SmallVec behavior was exercised in inherited test.
- **Refutation:** Cached flows bypass the walk; multiple counted-term chains may already flush their coalesced counter on each switch, and live policers already mutate shared state. No release perf/NUMA/throughput measurement: **do not** equate two refcount ops with quantified throughput loss or infer a particular cache-line residency without layout measurement. **Decisive check:** live-path strong counts unchanged while result lives, deferred-generated-reply handles retained and charged exactly once; optional pinned-worker release perf comparison for practical severity.

## #16497 — #15149 residual: the dead-worker retire bumps the global worker-set generation, so descriptors already queued on SURVIVING workers are dropped as stale in `drain_worker` with no terminal verdict; and `stop_inner` reaps every queue into... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
#15149 residual: the dead-worker retire bumps the global worker-set generation, so descriptors already queued on SURVIVING workers are dropped as stale in `drain_worker` with no terminal verdict; and `stop_inner` reaps every queue into `reaped_verdicts` but never delivers them. Both sets of requests complete only by the Go ack deadline.

**Finding ID:** R3-B12-02
**Severity (source):** Low — the frame is dropped either way (fail-closed), so there is no enforcement change. The consequence is a per-request stall until the 5 ms default Go ack deadline (`pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go:355-357`) instead of an immediate Denied completion, the per-flow serialization delay behind it, ack-timeout mis-accounting of what are worker-death or teardown denies, and an undelivered-verdict list that grows by the reaped count on every full stop until the next dead-worker sweep flushes it. Triggered once per worker death (rare, #925 degraded posture) and on every non-same-plan reconcile with D11 work queued. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators chasing a worker panic see a burst of ack timeouts on healthy workers, i.e. the #15149 fix moved the ack-timeout completions rather than removing them; every full reconcile with D11 traffic adds ack-timeout drops that are really teardown denies.

**Contract:** #15149 acceptance: "reaped requests complete as Denied rather than by ack timeout". `ipsec_inner_queue.rs:2349-2355` doc: Go-facing requests "complete as Denied instead of by ack timeout". Module invariant `:23-24`: "every orphan descriptor terminalized exactly once (E34)".

**Trace:** worker A panics → coordinator status sweep → `transport.retire_worker(A)` → generation N→N+1 → survivor B's queue still holds descriptors stamped N (admitted just before, `slowpath.rs:1504-1509`) → B's next `drain_worker` claims them stale silently → no verdict reaches `complete_ipsec_inner_verdict` → the ReinjectCore entry stays Queued → Go deadline sweep expires them as ack timeout. Stop leg: reconcile → `stop_inner` → retire+join every worker → Deny pushed to `reaped_verdicts` → never taken → Go ack timeout; verdicts sit in the list until a later sweep.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`WorkerSetAuthority::retire_worker` (`ipsec_inner_queue.rs:1612-1621`) removes the worker and `generation.fetch_add(1)`; `is_live` (`:1604-1607`) requires `generation == self.generation()`. `drain_worker` (`:2064-2076`): on `check_generation(..).is_err()` it runs `tombstones.claim_stale`, `pool.force_release`, `router.release`, `continue` — no push to `reaped_verdicts` and no verdict. The sweep (`coordinator/status.rs:1666-1680`) calls `transport.retire_worker(id)` + `join_worker_after_termination(id)` and delivers `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts` only when `ipsec_inner_reaped > 0`, i.e. only the dead worker's own requests. `stop_inner` (`coordinator/mod.rs:1213-1228`) retires and joins every worker but never calls `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts`, whose only production caller is `status.rs:1676`. The slow path (and the transport) survives reconciles (`reconcile/snapshot.rs:661`). The #15149 regression test (`coordinator/ipsec_inner_dead_worker_15149_tests.rs:168-181`) asserts the survivor's request "stays pending" but never runs the survivor's drain, so it cannot see leg 1.

**Probe:** rustc harness `RUN/verify/vb12/probes/d11/` (re-run of `RUN/workers/b12/evidence/d11probe/probe_cells.rs`, output `r3_b12_rerun.out`): survivor cell control (no retire) `drained=8 terminals=[1..8] requests_with_NO_terminal=[]`; defect (`retire_worker(1)` + `join(1)` exactly as the sweep) `drained=0 terminals=[] requests_with_NO_terminal=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] free_slabs=512` (slabs reclaimed: accounting, not a leak). Stop cell: undelivered reaped Deny verdicts held `5 / 10 / 15` over three stop/start cycles. Cargo cell (`probes/d11/vb12_15149_survivor_cell.rs`, real `retire_dead_worker_holders` + `ReinjectCore`): EXECUTED, `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vb12_r3_b12_0` (`RUN/verify/vb12/cargo_vb12.out`, rc=0; cell source in `probes/worktree_probe_cells.diff`). Control (no death): both requests routed to workers 0 and 1 complete `Denied`. Defect (worker 0 marked dead, real sweep): the sweep completes only the dead worker's request `[151491]`; survivor worker 1 then drains 0 descriptors, and its request 151492 gets no completion (`completed_after_survivor_drain=[]`, free_slabs=512). Limits: no Go pipeline run; the ack-deadline completion is static.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In the `drain_worker` stale branch, when `claim_stale` wins, push `Deny{stage:"d11_stale_generation"}` to `reaped_verdicts` (or the normal verdict queue), and have the worker loop deliver it; in `stop_inner`, drain `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts` into `complete_ipsec_inner_verdict` right after the join loop. Acceptance: the survivor cell reports `requests_with_NO_terminal=[]` with each request completed Denied; the stop cell holds 0 undelivered after each cycle; the existing #15149 test is extended to run the survivor's drain.

## #16498 — `ScanCore::check` keeps inserting distinct destinations up to `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` (1024) after the fixed `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (10) has decided the verdict. A window reset `clear()`s but keeps capacity, and full set... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
`ScanCore::check` keeps inserting distinct destinations up to `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` (1024) after the fixed `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (10) has decided the verdict. A window reset `clear()`s but keeps capacity, and full sets survive least-suspicious eviction. A spoofed-source new-flow flood can therefore pin ~144 MiB (ip-sweep) and ~24 MiB (port-scan) of heap per worker per screened zone, about 100× what detection requires.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — attacker-driven, slowly-reclaimed memory growth in the forwarding helper. At the loss cluster's 6 workers that is ~1 GiB per zone with both screens on, multiplied by each screened zone. It is bounded and no OOM was demonstrated, so it is not High; it would become High only if an OOM or forwarding loss is shown on a real appliance memory budget. Potential, not demonstrated, end-to-end. [reporter: Medium, possibly High]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A64-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va64.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Screens are turned on to protect the box under attack. With `ip-sweep` on, an attacker can make the forwarding helper hold ~170 MiB × workers × screened zones of heap for minutes. On a VM appliance that shares RAM with xpfd, FRR and strongSwan, this can push the node toward the OOM killer. If the killer picks the helper, forwarding stops on that node (HA fails over; standalone loses forwarding). Recovery: the memory drains slowly after the attack ends, and a restart clears it.

**Contract:** `userspace-dp/src/screen/scan.rs:20-31` says the maps are "attacker-driven", "Both axes are capped", and "The maps never grow without bound". `:105-107` says "Memory stays bounded by the per-source/zone caps regardless". `:206-213` says the caps make the table "bounded regardless of the window". `:145-151` says `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` "is purely a MEMORY bound. Detection fires at the fixed SCAN_DETECT_COUNT (10)". `docs/engineering-style.md` bounds attacker-driven state. The sibling SYN sketches publish their per-zone × worker memory cost (`docs/syn-cookie-flood-protection.md`); the scan trackers publish none.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`screen/scan.rs:143` `const MAX_SOURCES_PER_ZONE: usize = 4096;` `:156` `const MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE: usize = 1024;` `:192` `pub(super) const SCAN_DETECT_COUNT: usize = 10;` `:452-455` `if now_micros.saturating_sub(entry.window_start) >= window_micros { entry.window_start = now_micros; entry.entries.clear(); }` `:459-467` `if entry.entries.len() >= MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE { ... skipped_pressure += 1 } else { entry.entries.insert(entry_val); } entry.entries.len() >= SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` — the insert does not depend on the source already being detected. `screen/mod.rs:1334-1358` calls `port_scan.check(zone_id, pkt.src_ip, pkt.dst_port, ...)` and `ip_sweep.check(zone_id, pkt.src_ip, pkt.dst_ip, ...)`. `screen/mod.rs:1384-1391` runs cleanup at most every 30 s. `afxdp/worker/loop_body/setup.rs:142` has `let mut screen_state = ScreenState::new();` (per worker). `afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5098-5104` calls `screen.scan_sweep_drop_on_new_flow(...)` in the session-miss arm, before session-limit and policy. Observations: the code excerpts above. Inference: the per-node total (workers × zones).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — component scope. In-crate `#[cfg(test)]` cells drove the production `ScanCore::check` (both `IpAddr` and `u16` instantiations) and measured `entries.len()`/`capacity()`. Heap bytes are computed from hashbrown's bucket layout (validated against a64's counting-allocator figure of 36880 B at n=1024). Helper RSS on a cluster was not measured.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** `ScanCore::check` keeps inserting distinct destination IPs/ports to 1024 *after* the verdict flips at ten (`userspace-dp/src/screen/scan.rs:143,156,192,452-467`). Per-source `clear()` retains allocation and saturation eviction prefers low-count victims (`:637-649`); inherited component probe measured ~144 MiB IP-sweep plus ~24 MiB port-scan inner sets **per worker per screened zone** at 4096 fully loaded sources. Attack-driven work also hashes entries 11–1024 although they add no verdict information.
- **Refutation:** Memory is strictly capped, worker-local (no shared-map lock), and filling all sources requires millions of varied destination/flow combinations inside configured windows; a restricted IPv4 /24 cannot fill 1024 distinct dst IPs; the typical 5ms window makes a full attack expensive. No observed helper RSS/OOM or measured packet-rate collapse. **Decisive check:** production-config per-worker memory peak/reclamation with actual MTU/zone/source/distinct-destination constraints, plus test capping at ten keeps identical verdict; keep bounded eviction behavior.

## #16499 — WireGuard TUN-origin egress pads every record to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap, unlike Linux and wireguard-go. An operator wgN `mtu` set by the standard underlay-minus-overhead formula (1420 on an IPv6/1500 underlay, 1432 on IPv4... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
WireGuard TUN-origin egress pads every record to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap, unlike Linux and wireguard-go. An operator wgN `mtu` set by the standard underlay-minus-overhead formula (1420 on an IPv6/1500 underlay, 1432 on IPv4 PPPoE 1492) makes every full-size firewall-originated packet too big by up to 15 bytes. Each one is dropped silently at `encap_mtu_drops` with no PTB.

**Finding ID:** R3-B12-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — deterministic, configuration-triggered loss of permitted firewall-originated traffic over WireGuard (BGP/OSPF over WG with full-size updates, SSH/scp, TCP syslog, management to a remote site): handshakes and small packets pass, full-size segments vanish. Transit traffic is not affected. The trigger is the documented override. Recovery is a lower `mtu` or removing the statement. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator who copies a peer's `MTU = 1420`, or applies the documented PPPoE/cloud override computed as underlay − overhead, gets a tunnel where the firewall's own control-plane sessions stall on the first full-size segment. BGP over WG flaps at hold-timer expiry under large updates. The only signal is `encap_mtu_drops`. It persists until the MTU is changed.

**Contract:** `docs/wireguard-interop.md:272-277` says "`wgTunMTUForEndpoint` honors an operator-set `mtu` on the tunnel interface (the supported sub-1500 override — PPPoE 1492, cloud overlays ~1450)". `docs/wireguard-interop.md:104-110` names silently dropped full-MSS segments at `encap_mtu_drops` as the failure class #2299/#1865 closed. Reference behaviour (copies in `RUN/workers/b12/evidence/wg/ref/`): Linux `drivers/net/wireguard/send.c` `calculate_skb_padding` uses `padded_size = min(PACKET_CB(skb)->mtu, ALIGN(last_unit, MESSAGE_PADDING_MULTIPLE))`, and wireguard-go `device/send.go` `calculatePaddingSize` uses `if paddedSize > mtu { paddedSize = mtu }`. Both cap the pad at the device MTU.

**Trace:** `set interfaces wg0 mtu 1420` with an IPv6 peer endpoint and a 1500 underlay → `collectAppliedTunnels` sets `tc.MTU=1420` → `wgTunMTUForEndpoint` returns 1420 → wgN device MTU 1420 → host TCP MSS 1380 → a full segment is a 1420-byte inner read off the TUN by the WG control thread → `encap_and_send` with per-peer outer MTU 1500: 16+1424+16+40+8 = 1504 > 1500 → `MtuDrop` (`encap_mtu_drops++`) → no PTB, so the kernel retransmits the same size. Reference WG would emit 1500.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/mod.rs:343-345` `pad_to_16(n) = (n + 15) & !15` (no cap). `wg/engine.rs:1726-1727` `let padded_len = pad_to_16(inner_ip.len()); let required = WG_DATA_HEADER_LEN + padded_len + POLY1305_TAG_LEN;`. `coordinator/wg_control/mtu.rs` `wg_encapped_size = 16 + pad_to_16(inner) + 16 + outer_ip + 8`, guard `<= outer_mtu`. `coordinator/wg_control/dispatch.rs:404-416`: on failure it bumps `encap_mtu_drops` and returns `EncapOutcome::MtuDrop`; nothing in `wg_control/{mod,dispatch,tun_origin}.rs` writes an ICMP PTB back to the TUN or clamps local MSS. `pkg/routing/tunnel_wireguard.go:89-91` `if tc.MTU > 0 { return min(tc.MTU, wgEngineMaxInnerMTU) }`, while the default branch `:109` subtracts `wgPadWorst` (15). `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_routehelpers.go:71` sets `tc.MTU = ifc.MTU`. `applyWireguardTunLocked` sets that value as the device MTU.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vb12/probes/wgmtu/` (`probe_main.rs` includes `gen_mtu.rs`, the production `mtu.rs` with only `//!`→`//`, and `gen_pad_to_16.rs`, the production function). Output `wgmtu.out`: v6 underlay 1500 with mtu 1420 drops inner sizes 1409..=1420 (full size gives outer 1504 vs 1500; reference gives 1500). v4 PPPoE 1492 with mtu 1432 drops 1425..=1432. v4 1450 with mtu 1390 drops 1377..=1390. v6 1450 with mtu 1370 drops 1361..=1370. Controls (v4/1500/mtu 1440, v6/1500/mtu 1400) drop none, and the reference never oversizes. Go probe (`go_probe.out`, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestR3B12ProbeOperatorWgMTUAccepted -count=1 -v`): `mtu=1432` v4 and `mtu=1420` with `[2001:db8::5]` both compile with err=nil and 0 mtu warnings, and the device MTU is 1432/1420. Control without `mtu` gives 1425 (the pad-aware default). Limits: `CompileConfig` stands in for commit, and end-to-end TCP stall was not lab-observed.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Cap the pad at the inner budget like the references, `padded = min(pad_to_16(len), max(len, inner_mtu))`, in `engine.rs` encap and in the `mtu.rs`/`frame/wg.rs` size models. And/or clamp an operator `mtu` in Go to the pad-aware underlay ceiling with a commit warning, and synthesize an ICMP Frag-Needed/PTB into the TUN on a TUN-origin `MtuDrop`. Acceptance: the probe reports no drops for the four standard-formula rows and the controls are unchanged. A cargo cell `encap_and_send(1420-byte inner, v6 peer, outer_mtu 1500)` returns `Sent` with a 1500-byte datagram.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb12.md)</summary>

### R3-B12-04 — WireGuard TUN-origin egress pads to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap, so a documented operator wgN `mtu` set by the standard formula silently drops every full-size firewall-originated packet
- **Finding ID:** R3-B12-04
- **Title:** WireGuard TUN-origin egress pads every record to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap, unlike Linux and wireguard-go. An operator wgN `mtu` set by the standard underlay-minus-overhead formula (1420 on an IPv6/1500 underlay, 1432 on IPv4 PPPoE 1492) makes every full-size firewall-originated packet too big by up to 15 bytes. Each one is dropped silently at `encap_mtu_drops` with no PTB.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b12 (A1 Rust tunnel-supervision engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb12
- **Severity:** Medium — deterministic, configuration-triggered loss of permitted firewall-originated traffic over WireGuard (BGP/OSPF over WG with full-size updates, SSH/scp, TCP syslog, management to a remote site): handshakes and small packets pass, full-size segments vanish. Transit traffic is not affected. The trigger is the documented override. Recovery is a lower `mtu` or removing the statement. [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High — the production guard was executed, commit acceptance was executed, and reference implementations were read. The remaining assumption is that the host TCP stack does not rescue itself, given the Linux default `tcp_mtu_probing=0`.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — the production `wg_control/mtu.rs` and `wg/mod.rs::pad_to_16` were compiled with rustc and swept over inner sizes. A Go `pkg/routing` test compiled the operator config and read `wgTunMTUForEndpoint`. The drop path in `encap_and_send` and the absence of a PTB are STATIC.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — a reachable, committable configuration silently drops every full-size local-origin packet over the tunnel. This is the "#1865 blackhole class" the docs describe, on the TUN-origin path.
- **Contract:** `docs/wireguard-interop.md:272-277` says "`wgTunMTUForEndpoint` honors an operator-set `mtu` on the tunnel interface (the supported sub-1500 override — PPPoE 1492, cloud overlays ~1450)". `docs/wireguard-interop.md:104-110` names silently dropped full-MSS segments at `encap_mtu_drops` as the failure class #2299/#1865 closed. Reference behaviour (copies in `RUN/workers/b12/evidence/wg/ref/`): Linux `drivers/net/wireguard/send.c` `calculate_skb_padding` uses `padded_size = min(PACKET_CB(skb)->mtu, ALIGN(last_unit, MESSAGE_PADDING_MULTIPLE))`, and wireguard-go `device/send.go` `calculatePaddingSize` uses `if paddedSize > mtu { paddedSize = mtu }`. Both cap the pad at the device MTU.
- **Adversarial analysis:** Protection owed: local-origin egress follows the same MTU model as the wgN device the kernel is told about, so the kernel never sends a packet the encap guard will drop without a PTB. Actor: the operator, applying the documented override with the conventional WG MTU (the wg-quick 1420 default, or underlay − 60/80). No adversary is needed. Assumption challenged: "the operator `mtu` is the inner wgN MTU directly". With an uncapped pad, the real inner ceiling is (underlay − overhead) rounded down to 16, minus 15 in the worst case. The docs do not say this, and commit does not warn.
- **Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/mod.rs:343-345` `pad_to_16(n) = (n + 15) & !15` (no cap). `wg/engine.rs:1726-1727` `let padded_len = pad_to_16(inner_ip.len()); let required = WG_DATA_HEADER_LEN + padded_len + POLY1305_TAG_LEN;`. `coordinator/wg_control/mtu.rs` `wg_encapped_size = 16 + pad_to_16(inner) + 16 + outer_ip + 8`, guard `<= outer_mtu`. `coordinator/wg_control/dispatch.rs:404-416`: on failure it bumps `encap_mtu_drops` and returns `EncapOutcome::MtuDrop`; nothing in `wg_control/{mod,dispatch,tun_origin}.rs` writes an ICMP PTB back to the TUN or clamps local MSS. `pkg/routing/tunnel_wireguard.go:89-91` `if tc.MTU > 0 { return min(tc.MTU, wgEngineMaxInnerMTU) }`, while the default branch `:109` subtracts `wgPadWorst` (15). `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_routehelpers.go:71` sets `tc.MTU = ifc.MTU`. `applyWireguardTunLocked` sets that value as the device MTU.
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/vb12/probes/wgmtu/` (`probe_main.rs` includes `gen_mtu.rs`, the production `mtu.rs` with only `//!`→`//`, and `gen_pad_to_16.rs`, the production function). Output `wgmtu.out`: v6 underlay 1500 with mtu 1420 drops inner sizes 1409..=1420 (full size gives outer 1504 vs 1500; reference gives 1500). v4 PPPoE 1492 with mtu 1432 drops 1425..=1432. v4 1450 with mtu 1390 drops 1377..=1390. v6 1450 with mtu 1370 drops 1361..=1370. Controls (v4/1500/mtu 1440, v6/1500/mtu 1400) drop none, and the reference never oversizes. Go probe (`go_probe.out`, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestR3B12ProbeOperatorWgMTUAccepted -count=1 -v`): `mtu=1432` v4 and `mtu=1420` with `[2001:db8::5]` both compile with err=nil and 0 mtu warnings, and the device MTU is 1432/1420. Control without `mtu` gives 1425 (the pad-aware default). Limits: `CompileConfig` stands in for commit, and end-to-end TCP stall was not lab-observed.
- **Trace:** `set interfaces wg0 mtu 1420` with an IPv6 peer endpoint and a 1500 underlay → `collectAppliedTunnels` sets `tc.MTU=1420` → `wgTunMTUForEndpoint` returns 1420 → wgN device MTU 1420 → host TCP MSS 1380 → a full segment is a 1420-byte inner read off the TUN by the WG control thread → `encap_and_send` with per-peer outer MTU 1500: 16+1424+16+40+8 = 1504 > 1500 → `MtuDrop` (`encap_mtu_drops++`) → no PTB, so the kernel retransmits the same size. Reference WG would emit 1500.
- **Refutation attempt:** (a) The Go default branch subtracts the worst-case pad, but only when no operator `mtu` is set. (b) The transit MSS clamp and PTB (`wg_inner_mtu`, #2330/#2684) are transit-only, and the TUN-origin path has no MSS or PTB handling (grepped `wg_control/*.rs`). (c) No commit-time warning: `CompileConfig` emitted none, and `pkg/config` has no WG MTU validation. (d) Decap accepts any padding (#2910), so only xpf's own TUN-origin sends are affected. (e) The trigger requires ceil16(mtu) + overhead > underlay. 1420 on an IPv4 underlay (1484) is fine, so the finding is narrowed to the IPv6-outer and sub-1500 standard-formula cases shown above. (f) Distinct from R3-A81-01 (downstream PMTU, which cites the operator `mtu` as its mitigation): here the mitigation itself blackholes, through xpf's own local guard.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Not applicable to hot-path cost. The invariant broken is MTU-model coherence between the Go-advertised wgN MTU and the Rust encap guard (the #2300 "same MTU model in both directions" contract).

## #16500 — The #16289 baseline-relative sync-idle predicate (`ha_session_sync_idle_sample`) asks whether the gap between sent and received is still the same as at the first sample. When creates are in flight at the first sample and are then deliver... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The #16289 baseline-relative sync-idle predicate (`ha_session_sync_idle_sample`) asks whether the gap between sent and received is still the same as at the first sample. When creates are in flight at the first sample and are then delivered, or when creates land between the source and target CLI captures, the gap shrinks and stays that way. The wait then never reads idle and times out with FAIL on a pair that has caught up.

**Finding ID:** R3-N06-02
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — this is a lab-gate liveness defect: a false precondition FAIL VOIDs the downstream RG1 cells of `make test-failover`. It has no product effect, and how often the trigger occurs on the cluster is unmeasured. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
the precondition guards "before traffic", "before RG1 failback" and "before fw0 crash" (test-failover.sh:906,1221,1508). The last two follow earlier failovers, when a bulk-sync backlog is most likely. A false FAIL there VOIDs the RG1 slice of the gate that CLAUDE.md makes mandatory for HA changes, and agents rerun or misattribute it.

**Contract:** test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh:234-251: "this helper is idle when every session created since the baseline has been received (sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received) with pending == 0". The #16289 purpose was to stop the gate timing out "forever on a fully caught-up pair".

**Trace:** `ha_wait_for_session_sync_idle` → first sample establishes the baseline (rc 1) → later samples compare deltas → the gap shrinks by k → rc 1 forever (baseline kept) → `fail "... did not become idle within ${SESSION_SYNC_IDLE_TIMEOUT}s"` → downstream RG1 precondition cells VOID.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
ha-assurance-lib.sh:291 @d1ea69f9aa: `if (( sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received )) && [[ "$pending" == "0" ]]; then return 0`. test-failover.sh:340-351 sets the baseline only when it is empty and keeps it on rc 1. Only rc 3 (a counter rewind, :352-358) re-baselines. scripts/userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh:445-452 has the same rule. Every ha-assurance-selftest.sh fixture (:435-574) has a zero or constant gap after the baseline.

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vn06/probes/sync-idle-vn06.sh sources the real library and replays 30 samples through the caller's rc handling (sync-idle-vn06.out). Control, the #16289 constant offset 15/174 → 40/199 → 74/233: PASS idle at sample 4. Control, new creates never received (20/20 → 25/20): FAIL, as it should. Defect, 3 creates in flight at the baseline and delivered (20/17 → 20/20): FAIL, never idle. Defect, non-atomic capture with 2 creates sent and received between the two reads (20/22 → 22/22): FAIL, never idle. The reporter's probe (workers/n06/evidence/probe-sync-idle-16289.sh) gives the same rc pattern. Limit: hermetic. The next decisive check is to log each wait's first-sample (sent, received) over several `make test-failover` runs and count waits whose gap later shrinks.

## Acceptance / fix direction
treat a shrinking gap as catching up: idle when `(sent - received) <= (baseline_sent - baseline_received)` and pending == 0. Alternatively, re-baseline whenever received outgrows sent since the baseline. Apply the same change to the userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh sibling. Acceptance: new selftest cells where 20/17 → 20/20 ×3 PASS and 20/22 → 22/22 ×3 PASS, while 20/20 → 25/20 stays not idle.

## Full validated claim

The reporter's probe (workers/n06/evidence/probe-sync-idle-16289.sh) gives the same rc pattern. Limit: hermetic. The next decisive check is to log each wait's first-sample (sent, received) over several `make test-failover` runs and count waits whose gap later shrinks.
- **Trace:** `ha_wait_for_session_sync_idle` → first sample establishes the baseline (rc 1) → later samples compare deltas → the gap shrinks by k → rc 1 forever (baseline kept) → `fail "... did not become idle within ${SESSION_SYNC_IDLE_TIMEOUT}s"` → downstream RG1 precondition cells VOID.
- **Refutation attempt:** rc 3 only fires when a counter decreases, not when received outgrows sent. Pending is checked separately but does not restore equality. No selftest cell feeds a shrinking gap. A backlog that is never delivered reads as idle, but that half is inherent to any baseline scheme and is not claimed. I found the additional non-atomic-capture trigger, which the reporter did not name and which does not need a sync backlog at all.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — lab harness arithmetic.

## #16501 — #16057 residual: an unconfigured unit casts no vote, so a configured sibling's per-interface host-inbound override governs every unit on the shared tunnel ifindex [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
#16057 residual: an unconfigured unit casts no vote, so a configured sibling's per-interface host-inbound override governs every unit on the shared tunnel ifindex

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — same class and bounding as the parent #16057 (filed Low): only interface-level tunnel units sharing one netdev, with an override on some units and none on others. On the Rust plane the unconfigured unit's peers gain the sibling's services (e.g. ssh) and lose the unconfigured unit's own zone services; the kernel nft plane still applies destination-owner rights to the ambiguous netdev, which bounds the end-to-end leak to the sibling's own addresses. Demonstrated on the Rust plane; end-to-end bounded statically [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A65-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va65.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
a partner/low-trust tunnel unit gains the management services of a sibling unit merely because the sibling was given an override, and the unconfigured unit silently loses its zone services on the Rust plane; authoring an explicit (even empty) override on the unconfigured unit is safer than authoring none, which is backwards. Bounded by the shared-netdev prerequisite and the nft destination-owner arm

**Contract:** #16057 decisive check: "Two same-zone units with distinct host-admit sets on shared ifindex: disputed override refused/warned, sibling admission not inherited." Junos host-inbound-traffic is per ingress interface (a per-interface stanza replaces the zone set for that interface only, #6515). The Go nft plane encodes this by claiming each unit netdev with its EFFECTIVE signature (zone set when no override) and treating a netdev with more than one signature as ambiguous (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:587-589,892-902`)

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:98-100` @d1ea69f9aa "An UNCONFIGURED unit row casts no vote: it would have fallen back to its zone set per-unit, so it cannot dispute a configured sibling."; `:488-495` `if iface.ifindex <= 0 || !iface.host_inbound_configured || !is_logical_unit_row(..) { continue; }`; `:1145` `state.ifindex_host_inbound.insert(iface.ifindex, ..)` for the agreed override. `forwarding/host_inbound.rs:905` and `:952` `if let Some(hi) = state.ifindex_host_inbound.get(&ingress_ifindex) { .. return hi.admits..(..) }` — the zone set is never consulted once the ifindex carries an override. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:737-748` `if ovr == nil && !zone.WithholdsZoneLevelDHCPFor(out[i].Name) { continue }` leaves an unconfigured unit `HostInboundConfigured=false`. `forwarding_build/tests.rs:4161-4190` case (b) pins the inheritance (asserts https denied on the shared ifindex although the unconfigured unit's zone is any-service)

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — Rust build-and-admit probe with two controls, plus Go producer probe from `set` lines
