## #16532 — The LocalDelivery session-miss install has no pressure-shed preflight. Since #15951 made refusal fail closed, a transit SYN flood that holds a worker's table at its cap drops every new host-bound TCP SYN or SYN|ACK and every UDP first pa... [OPEN]

## Summary
The LocalDelivery session-miss install has no pressure-shed preflight. Since #15951 made refusal fail closed, a transit SYN flood that holds a worker's table at its cap drops every new host-bound TCP SYN or SYN|ACK and every UDP first packet. On the same table a transit initial SYN would be admitted by shedding an embryo.

**Finding ID:** R3-N07-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — this is a remotely inducible denial of new control-plane and management sessions (BGP, SSH, IKE, DNAT-to-self, and the inbound SYN|ACK of firewall-originated TCP) on the saturated workers for as long as the flood lasts. It does not bypass enforcement, established cached host sessions are unaffected, and the plane recovers when the flood stops. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A remote unauthenticated flood through any allowed transit policy can stop BGP re-establishment, new SSH management sessions, IKE initiations and DNAT-to-self services on the affected workers, without touching host-inbound policy. Before #15951 these packets were delivered (fail-open). Now they are dropped while transit traffic still gets in.

**Contract:** The #10890 contract (`session/install.rs:281-286`): at high occupancy, reclaim handshake-incomplete local TCP sessions before refusing an initial SYN, and never evict established sessions. #15951 (docs/log/15951.md) intended "count the refusal and recycle" in place of sessionless delivery. It did not intend host-plane admission to be weaker than transit admission.

**Trace:** Config: any permit policy into a zone without syn-cookie, and host-inbound services or DNAT-to-self allowed. Runtime: flood SYNs install pairs until `can_admit` fails, then each new flood SYN sheds one embryo pair and installs one, so the table stays at or near the cap. A host-bound SYN (BGP, SSH or DNAT-to-self) goes LocalMiss → capacity "true" → install refused → `admission_refused` → recycled. A UDP first packet (IKE or DNS reply) is refused the same way, and so is the SYN|ACK of the firewall's own outbound TCP.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5953-5961` @d1ea69f9aa: `let local_session_capacity_available = if let Some(reuse_key) = owner_syn_reuse_key.as_ref() { sessions.can_admit_after_closing_tcp_pair_for_syn(..) } else { true };`. There is no shed. `mod.rs:6014-6031` installs through `install_helper_local_session_on_miss` (`forwarding/local_delivery.rs:94-104`), which reaches `session/install.rs:538-545` `if self.len().saturating_add(self.reserved_session_slots) >= self.max_sessions { self.create_drops += 1; return false; }`. On refusal, `mod.rs:6133-6144` runs `sessions.note_admission_refused(); … binding.scratch.scratch_recycle.push(desc.addr); continue;`. The transit sibling at `mod.rs:6763-6790` runs `if needed_sessions == 0 || reuse_fits { … } else { sessions.can_admit_new_syn(needed_sessions, meta.protocol, meta.tcp_flags) }`. The caching predicate `forwarding/local_delivery.rs:20-52` caches all non-TCP traffic and TCP SYN or SYN|ACK, so all of these reach the refusing install.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_localmiss_probe_tests.rs`, wired temporarily, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_localmiss -- --nocapture`. It uses the same DNAT-to-self fixture as tests_host_inbound_15951 (wan 198.51.100.10 → 203.0.113.9:443 → 10.0.61.1:8080) and a table capped at 16, filled with local ForwardFlow TCP-SYN embryos. Control `vn07_localmiss_one_free_slot_delivers_control` (15 embryos) printed `one-free: local=1 create=1 refused=0` and passed. Defect `vn07_localmiss_full_of_sheddable_embryos_refuses_host_syn` (16 embryos) printed `full: host local=0 create=0 refused=1 | transit-shaped can_admit_new_syn(2)=true shed=2` and failed. Output: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_localmiss.out`. n07's probe also failed with refused=1 (`RUN/verify/vn07/n07_localmiss.out`). Limits: the transit admission is shown at the `can_admit_new_syn` level, not by a transit frame through the poll path. That the transit call site calls it is static.

## Acceptance / fix direction
On the LocalMiss arm, run `can_admit_new_syn` for initial SYNs with the same NAT, BPF and shared-row release sequence as the transit site, and consider a small reserved host-local headroom for non-TCP and SYN|ACK. Only then fail closed. Acceptance: the vn07 defect cell turns green, the one-free-slot control and the #15951 cap-0 cells stay green, and a shed caused by a host SYN releases NAT holds exactly as the transit shed does.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn07.md)</summary>

### R3-N07-02 — LocalMiss fail-closed has no #10890 embryo shed: a table full of transit SYN embryos refuses every new host-bound session while transit SYNs are still admitted by shedding

On the same table a transit initial SYN would be admitted by shedding an embryo.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker n07 (A6/A1 session-glue + poll-descriptor engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vn07

It does not bypass enforcement, established cached host sessions are unaffected, and the plane recovers when the flood stops. [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High for the asymmetric admission, which is executed with a same-path control. Medium for the flood steady state staying at the cap, which is inferred from the shed-and-replace logic.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — I ran a verifier probe through the real poll path (`txn_run_descriptor_checked`) with a one-free-slot control, and n07's probe also reproduced. The steady state under flood is STATIC.

It did not intend host-plane admission to be weaker than transit admission.

- **Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5953-5961` @d1ea69f9aa: `let local_session_capacity_available = if let Some(reuse_key) = owner_syn_reuse_key.as_ref() { sessions.can_admit_after_closing_tcp_pair_for_syn(..) } else { true };`. There is no shed. `mod.rs:6014-6031` installs through `install_helper_local_session_on_miss` (`forwarding/local_delivery.rs:94-104`), which reaches `session/install.rs:538-545` `if self.len().saturating_add(self.reserved_session_slots) >= self.max_sessions { self.create_drops += 1; return false; }`. On refusal, `mod.rs:6133-6144` runs `sessions.note_admission_refused(); … binding.scratch.scratch_recycle.push(desc.addr); continue;`. The transit sibling at `mod.rs:6763-6790` runs `if needed_sessions == 0 || reuse_fits { … } else { sessions.can_admit_new_syn(needed_sessions, meta.protocol, meta.tcp_flags) }`. The caching predicate `forwarding/local_delivery.rs:20-52` caches all non-TCP traffic and TCP SYN or SYN|ACK, so all of these reach the refusing install.
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_localmiss_probe_tests.rs`, wired temporarily, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_localmiss -- --nocapture`. It uses the same DNAT-to-self fixture as tests_host_inbound_15951 (wan 198.51.100.10 → 203.0.113.9:443 → 10.0.61.1:8080) and a table capped at 16, filled with local ForwardFlow TCP-SYN embryos. Control `vn07_localmiss_one_free_slot_delivers_control` (15 embryos) printed `one-free: local=1 create=1 refused=0` and passed. Defect `vn07_localmiss_full_of_sheddable_embryos_refuses_host_syn` (16 embryos) printed `full: host local=0 create=0 refused=1 | transit-shaped can_admit_new_syn(2)=true shed=2` and failed. Output: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_localmiss.out`. n07's probe also failed with refused=1 (`RUN/verify/vn07/n07_localmiss.out`). Limits: the transit admission is shown at the `can_admit_new_syn` level, not by a transit frame through the poll path. That the transit call site calls it is static.
- **Trace:** Config: any permit policy into a zone without syn-cookie, and host-inbound services or DNAT-to-self allowed. Runtime: flood SYNs install pairs until `can_admit` fails, then each new flood SYN sheds one embryo pair and installs one, so the table stays at or near the cap. A host-bound SYN (BGP, SSH or DNAT-to-self) goes LocalMiss → capacity "true" → install refused → `admission_refused` → recycled. A UDP first packet (IKE or DNS reply) is refused the same way, and so is the SYN|ACK of the firewall's own outbound TCP.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked the following. (1) Under shed-and-replace, does the flood keep the table below the cap? No: the transit path sheds only after `can_admit` fails, so occupancy stays at max (or max-1, depending on install-group parity; a single 1-slot install puts it back at max). (2) `reserved_session_slots` is an IPsec reservation, not host headroom. (3) The syn-cookie screen avoids the condition only where the operator enabled it. (4) The #15951 tests cover only cap-0. (5) The #15951 log calls drops under pressure intended, but never considers shedding. The reporter's positive control did not run the same path, so I replaced it with a same-path one-free-slot control. The claim held. I narrowed it: UDP host traffic is also refused at a full table, but transit UDP is refused as well, so the asymmetry is TCP-initial-SYN only, while the outage covers all host-bound first packets.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Admission accounting: the fix must reuse the existing #12862 tuple-gate lease and NAT release for shed rows, as the transit site does. That path is cold because it runs only when the table is full. It needs no per-packet allocation beyond the existing `PressureShedSessions` vector.

## #16533 — A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose `then` tail carries any unmodelled token (typo, `next term`, `sample`) passes strict commit with zero warnings and installs a terminating ACCEPT [OPEN]

## Summary

A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose `then` tail carries any unmodelled token (typo, `next term`, `sample`) passes strict commit with zero warnings and installs a terminating ACCEPT

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The mechanism is real and I re-ran it at d1ea69f9aa. In worktree RUN/wt/a02 (production files untouched), TestVA02PackedThenStoreCommit and TestVA02PackedThenLenient reproduce every row. A term-line packed `then` tail with one un…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable with a documented spelling, it causes a concrete loss of enforcement, and both fail-closed gates are bypassed.

## Mechanism

Hierarchical text → parser: term node with Keys `[term t1 from ... then dicsard]` and no children → schema walk consumes the identity and ignores the tail → `packedBody` declines on `dicsard` → no `then` child → Action "", UnknownActions empty → strict `validateFilterActionsStrict` silent → `BuildFirewallFilterSnapshots` gives Action "" and NextTerm false → Rust gives terminating Accept for every packet matching the `from`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/compact_tail.go:186-189: `if childSchema == nil { // Outside the modelled grammar at every open level. Do not guess. return node.Children }`. A packed term has no children, so `then` vanishes. - pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:707-708: `termBody := packedBody(termInst.node, termSchema)`. - compiler_firewall.go:778-784: `for _, thenNode := range termBody.FindChildren("then") { compileFilterThen(...) }` followed by `failClosedUnknownFilterAction(term)`. - compiler_firewall.go:2526-2529: `if len(term.UnknownActions) > 0 { term.Action = FilterActionDiscard }`. Nothing populates it here. - userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1442: `"" => FilterAction::Accept`. - The `from` half survives only because of the #10071 raw re-scan, which has no `then` counterpart.

## Impact

Common lo0/transit filter idioms (`term count-all then count all next term; term block from ... then discard; term rest then accept;`) written compactly become accept-all, and a one-character typo in a packed `discard` turns a deny into a permit. The commit is clean and `show` reflects the intent. The blast radius is every interface the filter is bound to, plus the lo0 nft mirror that consumes the same term. It lasts until someone notices. Recovery is to rewrite the term braced.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `compileFirewall`, when the packed term tail is non-empty and `packedBody` declines, re-scan the raw `then` segment(s) as the #10071 `from` re-scan does, and record every unrecognised token in `UnknownActions`, so that strict rejects it and tolerant forces discard. Also model `next term` in the packed then grammar. Acceptance: - The probe's packed typo, `sample` and inet6 rows are strict-rejected naming the token, and compile to discard on the tolerant path. - `term t0 then count all next term;` compiles to `next_term=true count="all"` or is refused. - The packed `discard` and braced controls are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

- docs/config-schema.md "Compact (packed) stanza bodies": the packed and nested forms "are the same configuration". It names "a filter term with an empty action does not discard (#6685)" as the defect class. - #11357/#2399: an unknown `then` token must fail closed (strict reject; tolerant discard), never become the empty action. - userspace-dp/src/filter/README.md: fall-through is ONLY the authored `next term`, and an empty action TERMINATES as Accept (#14632).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A02-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A02-01 | Medium | A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose then tail carries any unmodelled token… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:16: - **R3-A02-01 — MATERIAL (Medium, conditional enforcement loss).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compact_tail.go:183-193` silently returns empty authored children when an unmodelled token breaks an otherwise packed filter term; `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:708-713,779-785` sees no `then` action, and `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1442` maps `""` to terminating `Accept`. The historical store test bound a compact filter and observed `warnings=0`, empty action and unknown-actions on a `dicsard` typo, with valid-packed and bad-braced controls. **Refutation:** requires an authorized author/peer, a specifically term-line packed spelling, and a bound filter; packet acceptance is source-derived from the Rust matcher, not newly measured, and a broad unconditional high-severity network claim is unwarranted. **Decisive check:** current end-to-end regression for typo/`next term` term-line tails, including strict rejection, lenient fail-closed action and snapshot-to-Rust action decoding.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L51: ### R3-A02-01 (+ merged A02-02) — packed filter term `then` tail with unmodelled token → terminating ACCEPT — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `pkg/config/compact_tail.go:192-193` @origin/master: packed body decline returns `node.Children` (empty for packed term) on first undeclared token — `then` vanishes silently. `compiler_firewall.go:709 packedBody(term…)`, `:785 failClosedUnknownFilterAction` keyed only on `UnknownActions` populated by surviving `then` nodes → typo `then dicsard` / `next term` / `sample` commits strict-clean, `Action=""` → Rust `"" => Accept` (filter/compiler.rs). Documented packed≡braced equivalence (docs/config-schema.md, #6685 class) makes spelling supported; braced typo is rejected (asymmetry). - Refutation: Requires packed one-line spelling + operator typo/unmodelled token; no external attacker authors config. But protection is enforcement integrity vs operator error/migration — the exact #11357/#2399 fail-closed doctrine; valid packed `then discard` works, so spelling cannot be dismissed as unsupported. - Evidence: Decline site + compiler call sites re-read at origin/master. ## #16534 — install.sh cleanup_on_fail `rm -f`s xpf.sources whenever this run wrote it, even when it overwrote an existing working source. A failed re-run (the documented channel-rebind procedure) leaves pin and keyring restored but no apt source... [OPEN]

## Summary
install.sh cleanup_on_fail `rm -f`s xpf.sources whenever this run wrote it, even when it overwrote an existing working source. A failed re-run (the documented channel-rebind procedure) leaves pin and keyring restored but no apt source, so the host stops receiving xpf updates

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-03
**Severity (source):** Low — the host silently stops receiving updates, but the failure is announced on stderr and a successful re-run restores the source [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/COHORT/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A perimeter firewall that silently drops off its update channel after a routine channel rebind.

**Contract:** docs/distribution.md:134-136: "Rerun `install.sh` to rebind channels ... rolls back its marked pin if installation fails". install.sh:83-90 describes restoring prior state. docs/distribution.md:377 says "removes the source", which literally matches the code but was written for the first-install shape. The asymmetry with #11133/#12543 is the defect.

**Trace:** existing install (stable) -> `curl … | sudo sh` with XPF_CHANNEL=edge -> install_keyring (backup) -> write_source overwrites -> apt-get update fails -> EXIT trap restores the keyring and pin and removes the source -> apt never sees xpf again.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
scripts/dist/install.sh:94-97 `if [ "$SRC_WRITTEN" = "1" ]; then ... rm -f "$SRC"`. :416-418 `printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$SRC"; SRC_WRITTEN=1`, with no backup. Pin backup at :463-466 (`PIN_BACKUP=... cp -p`) and restore at :101-109. main() (:548-555) runs write_source before do_install (:514-525: apt-get update, verify_channel, apt-get install). Only debian/xpf.postrm references xpf.sources, and no maintainer script recreates it.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_install_source_restore.py, re-run by vb17, output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/install_source_restore.out: `[re-run fails] ... source exists after: False`, `pin exists after: True  restored-to-old: True`. Controls: `control success keeps source: True | first-install failure removes source: True`. Limit: the apt failure is modelled with `false`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
back up a pre-existing source (same-dir temp plus rename), restore it on failure, and remove it only when it did not pre-exist. Update docs/distribution.md:377. Acceptance: the defect cell restores the source byte-for-byte, and both controls still pass.

## #16535 — The #6697/#7126 slot-escape and #2419 spelling gates omit the parser-admitted one-child multi-token block spelling `leaf { v1 v2; }`: 13 multi-value sites validate only `c.Keys[:1]`, so a rejected value commits or a valid one is silently dropped… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #6697/#7126 slot-escape and #2419 spelling gates omit the parser-admitted one-child multi-token block spelling `leaf { v1 v2; }`: 13 multi-value sites validate only `c.Keys[:1]`, so a rejected value commits or a valid one is silently dropped (e.g. a proxy-arp address)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — this is an assurance and validation gap on a non-Junos spelling. Measured consequences: a proxy-ARP address is silently dropped, and rejected tokens reach the compiled config for RA dns-server-address, login-class permissions and rip neighbor. The RA and sshd runtimes re-validate. [reporter: L…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (#2419/#6697 gate-completeness gaps on non-Junos spellings) — real, but a minor validation-gate hole.

## Mechanism

Text → parser: one child with Keys `[v1 v2]` → `validateMultiValueLeaf` checks v1 only → compiler reads Keys[0] (drop) or every key (unvalidated) → compiled config.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/schema_walk.go:1806-1818: `keys := c.Keys[:1]; if leafSchema.allChildKeysAreValues { keys = c.Keys }`. - pkg/config/compiler_nat_source.go `proxyARPAddressValues`: `for _, vn := range prop.Children { ... vals = append(vals, vn.Keys[0]) }`. Only Keys[0] of each block child is read.

## Impact

These gates are the evidence other lanes cite to close #2419-class issues. The uncovered form silently drops proxy-ARP entries, which makes the NAT'd address unreachable, and lets commit-check accept values its own validator rejects.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At the walker, refuse a multi-token statement inside a value-list block (one value per statement), or validate all of `c.Keys` wherever the compiler accumulates every key. Add form F to `TestSchemaSpellingDifferentialGate` and `TestSlotEscapeSweep`. Acceptance: 0 escapes in the sixth-form sweep, and the one-child proxy-arp row either compiles both addresses or is refused.

## Contract (where cited)

docs/config-schema.md and `schema_slot_escape_gate_test.go:239-242` claim the gates cover "all five spellings the grammar admits". The parser admits a sixth. #6659 says every authored proxy-arp address is installed or refused.

## Validation provenance

Thus the second value can escape a validator or disappear. **Refutation:** that sixth shape is not canonical Junos list spelling; many affected runtime consumers reparse/ignore malformed values, and no reported packet overpermit follows from this source chain. **Decisive check:** establish which multi-value leaves contractually allow a multi-token *single child*, then assert both values are validated and emitted, or reject that shape consistently before compile.

## #16536 — #11768 residual: the shared_exact per-flow admission cap computes its BDP floor from the class-wide rate over the worker-local flow count, so after per-shard buffer partitioning one flow can hold 75-100% of a worker's... [OPEN]

## Summary
#11768 residual: the shared_exact per-flow admission cap computes its BDP floor from the class-wide rate over the worker-local flow count, so after per-shard buffer partitioning one flow can hold 75-100% of a worker's admission budget

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — the #914 per-flow mouse protection inside a shared_exact (>= 2.5 Gb/s) class is weakened by about `active_shards`x at low-to-moderate local flow counts. The aggregate per-worker cap, the class rate and MQFQ dequeue order are unaffected, so there is no enforcement or isolation loss. The mouse drop consequence is inferred, not lab-measured. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A70-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va70.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=NEEDS_VALIDATION/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
On the 6-worker lab cluster, a >= 2.5 Gb/s exact class (iperf-b/c style) loses #914's mouse protection at the flow counts it was tuned for. A worker's elephant can fill 75-100 % of that worker's admission budget, and mice hashed to the same worker see `admission_buffer_drops` and extra queueing. This is bounded to one worker's share, and recovery is natural as the elephant backs off.

**Contract:** `cos/admission.rs:212-237` (#914): the shared_exact per-flow cap `max(fair_share*2, bdp_floor).clamp(MIN, buffer_limit)` exists because pass-through "allowed a single elephant to occupy the entire queue buffer, starving mice". `admission.rs:123-127` defines the BDP floor as "Per-flow BDP at the queue's rate divided across active_flows". `cos/README.md:300-306` (#11768) says the configured base "is divided by active shards".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`cos/admission.rs:242-257`: `let prospective = cos_queue_prospective_active_flows(queue, flow_bucket); let fair_share = flow_share_div_ceil(buffer_limit, prospective); let bdp = bdp_floor_bytes(queue.transmit_rate_bytes(), prospective); return clamp_flow_share_to_buffer(fair_share.saturating_mul(SHARED_EXACT_BURST_HEADROOM).max(bdp), buffer_limit);`. `admission.rs:137-140`: `per_flow_rate = transmit_rate_bytes / active_flows.max(1)`, multiplied by 10 ms. `tx/cos_classify.rs:2345-2361`: `buffer_limit = cos_shared_exact_buffer_limit(queue, flow_bucket, active_shards)`, with the shard count taken from the root lease. `admission.rs:355-375`: shard limit = `buffer_bytes / active_shards` (+ #707/#717). `flow_hash.rs:193-211`: prospective count = this worker's `active_flow_buckets` (+1 when the target bucket is empty).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a Rust unit probe called the production `cos_shared_exact_buffer_limit` + `cos_queue_flow_share_limit` with a single-shard positive control. The field consequence is NEEDS_VALIDATION.

## #16537 — `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindl... [OPEN]

## Summary
`candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindless IPsec fence is configured. With a /16 pool this costs milliseconds per SYN.

**Finding ID:** R3-N07-03
**Severity (source):** High — High — appliance availability. In the affected configuration, an unauthenticated flood of about 350 challenged SYN/s per worker (by the release-mode model) saturates a worker. RSS spreads the flood across all workers, so forwarding collapses appliance-wide, and the flood-defence feature is the amplifier. The configuration is a condition: syn-cookie active on the zone where the flood enters, plus a pool-mode SNAT rule matching the flooded flows with a large pool (/20 to /16). With a /24 pool the extra cost is about 2 µs per SYN, which is only a Medium-class degradation. [reporter: High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators enable SYN cookies precisely for hostile traffic. In a CGNAT-style deployment with a large pool, enabling them makes each flood SYN thousands of times more expensive than a normal packet, so a modest flood stalls RX servicing on every worker and every flow hashed to those workers starves.

**Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md hot-path discipline: no per-packet allocation on the hot path. SYN cookies exist to make the per-SYN cost of a flood constant and small. The call-site comment calls the rework "predicate-only … before any NAT allocation".

**Trace:** Config: `security screen ids-option X tcp syn-flood` on zone lan with syn-cookie protection mode, a lan→wan source-NAT rule with a pool of 198.51.0.0/16, and a permit policy lan→wan. Compile: the pool expands to 65536 `pool_addresses_v4`. Runtime: the zone goes over threshold, the screen mints a challenge, and the prescreen passes. On the session-miss arm, `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` builds 65536 NatDecisions (about 3 MB), merge-collects them, clones about 3 MB into `fence_candidates`, and scans all of them, only then emitting the SYN-ACK. This repeats for every flood SYN on every worker.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5256-5300` @d1ea69f9aa: `if let Some(challenge) = deferred_syn_cookie_challenge.take() { let candidate_nats = nat_exception::candidate_source_nats_for_challenge(…); let fence_candidates: Vec<NatDecision> = match &candidate_nats { Some(list) if !list.is_empty() => list.clone(), _ => vec![decision.nat] }; … fence_candidates.iter().any(|candidate| …bindless_ipsec_selector_fence.matches_with_nat(source, destination, *candidate))`. `poll_descriptor/nat_exception.rs:264-275` (NAT64: every `prefix.pool_v4`) and `:319-326` (`candidates.into_iter().map(|c| base_nat.merge(c)).collect()`). `nat/source/mod.rs:1509-1519`: "Every pool address" `rule.pool_addresses_v4.iter().map(|addr| NatDecision{…}).collect()`, with the same pattern for v6 at `:1521-1535`. `nat/source/expand.rs:21` `MAX_POOL_PREFIX_HOSTS: u64 = 65536`. The trigger is at `screen/zone.rs:518-545` (MintChallenge for every over-attack SYN, with no mint-rate cap) and `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1628-1652` (`deferred_syn_cookie_challenge = Some(challenge)` after the `syn_cookie_reply_admitted` prescreen, which does not consider NAT).

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_probe_tests.rs`, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_syncookie -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` (debug). Control, interface-mode SNAT: `1 candidates, 1.364µs per challenged SYN` (pass). Scaling: `/24: 256 candidates, 21.088µs`, `/20: 4096, 283.136µs`, `/16: 65536, 4.615138ms`. `size_of NatDecision = 48`. The bound cell failed. Release model `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_release_model.rs` (rustc -O): `/24 2.001µs`, `/20 126.219µs`, `/16 2.834877ms per SYN`. Outputs: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_syncookie.out` and `vn07_syncookie_release_model.out`. Limits: the probe calls the dominant function and the clone, not the whole poll iteration, so the real per-SYN cost is a superset. The model is a reconstruction, not production code.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Precompute, per source-NAT rule (and per NAT64 prefix) and per fence generation, whether any pool address intersects the bindless selector fence. Skip candidate enumeration entirely when the fence is empty. Keep the `is_some` allocation-failure shape check as an O(1) rule-level predicate. Never allocate per challenged SYN. Acceptance: the per-SYN challenge cost is independent of pool size (the vn07 bound cell turns green), the #15947 fence-suppression and allocation-failure cells stay green, and a lab flood with a /16 pool shows worker pps comparable to interface-mode SNAT.

- **Finding ID:** R3-N07-03
- **Title:** `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindless IPsec fence is configured. With a /16 pool this costs milliseconds per SYN.

The configuration is a condition: syn-cookie active on the zone where the flood enters, plus a pool-mode SNAT rule matching the flooded flows with a large pool (/20 to /16). With a /24 pool the extra cost is about 2 µs per SYN, which is only a Medium-class degradation. [reporter: High]

- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — the trigger is a reachable remote flood in a committable configuration (pools up to 65536 hosts are accepted), the cost is measured and linear, and it was introduced by c1b86e871b (#15947).
- **Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md hot-path discipline: no per-packet allocation on the hot path. SYN cookies exist to make the per-SYN cost of a flood constant and small. The call-site comment calls the rework "predicate-only … before any NAT allocation".
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection at stake is SYN-flood resistance and worker-loop availability. The actor is a host that can send SYNs that match a pool-SNAT rule through a permitted policy, for example a subscriber or inside host in a CGNAT-style deployment. Sources inside the matched range can be spoofed. The prerequisites are syn-cookie protection mode with the zone over its attack threshold, which is exactly the flood state. The trigger is at `screen/zone.rs:518-545` (MintChallenge for every over-attack SYN, with no mint-rate cap) and `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1628-1652` (`deferred_syn_cookie_challenge = Some(challenge)` after the `syn_cookie_reply_admitted` prescreen, which does not consider NAT).
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_probe_tests.rs`, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_syncookie -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` (debug). Control, interface-mode SNAT: `1 candidates, 1.364µs per challenged SYN` (pass). Scaling: `/24: 256 candidates, 21.088µs`, `/20: 4096, 283.136µs`, `/16: 65536, 4.615138ms`. `size_of NatDecision = 48`. The bound cell failed. Release model `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_release_model.rs` (rustc -O): `/24 2.001µs`, `/20 126.219µs`, `/16 2.834877ms per SYN`. Outputs: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_syncookie.out` and `vn07_syncookie_release_model.out`. Limits: the probe calls the dominant function and the clone, not the whole poll iteration, so the real per-SYN cost is a superset. The model is a reconstruction, not production code.
- **Trace:** Config: `security screen ids-option X tcp syn-flood` on zone lan with syn-cookie protection mode, a lan→wan source-NAT rule with a pool of 198.51.0.0/16, and a permit policy lan→wan. Compile: the pool expands to 65536 `pool_addresses_v4`. Runtime: the zone goes over threshold, the screen mints a challenge, and the prescreen passes. On the session-miss arm, `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` builds 65536 NatDecisions (about 3 MB), merge-collects them, clones about 3 MB into `fence_candidates`, and scans all of them, only then emitting the SYN-ACK. This repeats for every flood SYN on every worker.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked these possible guards. `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` affects only code layout. There is no early exit when the fence is empty: the scan runs, and the full vector is built because `candidate_nats.is_some()` is part of `admitted`. Only the deterministic-NAT arm is O(1). The screen has no cap on challenges per second, and per-source thresholds do not stop spoofed sources. In this run, a60 deferred this to n07. The reporter's claim held. I narrowed the severity condition to large pools (/20 and above) and noted that /24 is minor.
- **HPC/invariant check:** The cost unit is O(pool) work plus about 2×48×pool bytes of heap per challenged SYN on the worker's single-threaded loop. Large allocations are mmap-backed, so page faults dominate. There is no ownership or concurrency hazard; this is pure cost amplification.

## #16538 — Brace-elided `ssh no-password-authentication;` / `no-passwords;` and `api-auth metrics-require-auth;` pass strict commit and compile to false; the #2419/#8690 compact-block ratchet that should catch them is red at base (36 new compact-blind rows) [OPEN]

## Summary

Brace-elided `ssh no-password-authentication;` / `no-passwords;` and `api-auth metrics-require-auth;` pass strict commit and compile to false; the #2419/#8690 compact-block ratchet that should catch them is red at base (36 new compact-blind rows)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — management-plane authentication hardening the operator committed is silently not applied. sshd keeps PasswordAuthentication at the host default, so the password brute-force surface stays open. Loopback `/metrics` stays readable by any local UID (the #16072 exposure). The scope is bounded to…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable, strict-clean authoring spelling silently drops security hardening, and the guard designated for this class is red, so it detects nothing.

## Mechanism

Text → parser: `ssh` node with Keys `[ssh no-password-authentication]` → schema walk ignores tokens past the identity → compact normalizer does not admit the pair → `FindChild` finds nothing → `NoPasswordAuthentication=false` → sshd drop-in omits `PasswordAuthentication no` → host default (password auth on).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/compiler_system.go:1336-1338: a single `ssh` node "Preserve[s] the existing normalizer path". Only the multi-block arm (:1341-1344) calls `packedBodyChildren`. - :1429-1434: `sshNode.FindChild("no-password-authentication")` (children only). - pkg/config/compact_normalize_scope.go: the admitted ssh pairs do not include the two flags, and api-auth admits only `api-key`. - pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1401-1406: `if ssh.NoPasswordAuthentication || ssh.NoPasswords { lines = append(lines, "PasswordAuthentication no") }`.

## Impact

An operator hardening SSH or /metrics sees the hardening in `show configuration`, while sshd still accepts passwords and /metrics stays open to local users. This persists across reboots until the stanza is rewritten. More broadly, every new child-only leaf lands silently while the ratchet stays red.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Admit `(ssh, no-password-authentication)`, `(ssh, no-passwords)` and `(api-auth, metrics-require-auth)` to `compactNormalizeInScope`, or expand single `ssh`/`api-auth` nodes with `packedBodyChildren` as the multi-block arm does. Triage the other 33 rows (admit them or record a reasoned exclusion). Make the ratchet blocking for pkg/config. Acceptance: - `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` is green. - The elided ssh and api-auth probe rows compile to true. - The elided flag-only `metrics-require-auth` is refused like its braced twin.

## Contract (where cited)

- docs/config-schema.md, the #8690/#9056 admission rule: a brace-elided site that compiles to the empty stanza must be admitted to `compactNormalizeInScope` or recorded as a reasoned exclusion. - `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` is the ratchet that fails on a "NEW compact-blind site". - #15282/#15630 define `no-password-authentication`/`no-passwords` as rendering `PasswordAuthentication no`. - #16072 makes `metrics-require-auth` gate loopback /metrics, and refuses the flag without a credential.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A02-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A02-04 | Medium | Brace-elided ssh no-password-authentication; / no-passwords; and api-auth… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:18: - **R3-A02-04 — MATERIAL (Medium for lost explicit auth hardening; not proof of exposed login).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:1390-1404` retains a single `ssh` node unexpanded, then reads only children for `no-password-authentication`/`no-passwords` (`:1483-1488`); `api-auth` similarly reads `metrics-require-auth` only via `FindChild` (`:1563-1576`). The leaves exist in the schema (`schema_system.go:651-653,682-683`) but the compact normalizer has no matching rewrite for these flags. Historical #2419/#8690 regression had 36 red compact rows at report base; do not extrapolate that exact count to this master. **Refutation:** actual remote password acceptance requires a live sshd configuration, configured credentials and reachability; actual metrics exposure depends on bind/auth defaults. Both are unmeasured here, and unrelated `time-wait-state` rows belong elsewhere. **Decisive check:** commit both brace-elided and braced flags, inspect compiled booleans, generated sshd drop-in and /metrics gate, and make the compact spelling ratchet green.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L57: ### R3-A02-04 — brace-elided ssh/api-auth flags dropped; #2419 ratchet red — **MATERIAL (Medium)** - Defect: `ssh no-password-authentication;` / `no-passwords;`, `api-auth metrics-require-auth;` in elided form compile to false: compiler reads children only (`compiler_system.go:1484 FindChild`), `compact_normalize_scope.go` @origin/master admits `ssh root-login/ciphers/…` but grep shows no `no-password*`/`metrics-require-auth` admission. sshd renderer omits `PasswordAuthentication no`; /metrics gate (#16072) also bypassed incl. its credential precondition. - Refutation: Braced/flat spellings work; host sshd default assumption (passwords on) is stock-OpenSSH, not measured on image; scope = elided spelling only. Does not refute silent drop of committed hardening. - Evidence: Scope grep at origin/master confirms non-admission. [SMR-run] `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` at origin/master **FAILS** with NEW compact-blind rows explicitly including `system services ssh no-password-authentication`, `… no-passwords`, `system services web-management api-auth metrics-require-auth` (plus many others + 2 stale exclusions) — ratchet-red claim independently confirmed at current master, count drifted from report's 36 (do not reuse 36). - Unresolved: Image sshd effective default + whether CI non-blocking status changed; severity only. ### R3-A02-03 — one-child multi-token block `leaf { v1 v2; }` escapes slot/spelling gates — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: Gates enumerate 5 spellings; par

## #16539 — install.sh validate_archive_key (the #14833 pin) does `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir` and uses it as the GNUPGHOME parent whenever TMPDIR is unset, which is always the case under `curl … | sudo sh`. This leaves a... [OPEN]

## Summary
install.sh validate_archive_key (the #14833 pin) does `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir` and uses it as the GNUPGHOME parent whenever TMPDIR is unset, which is always the case under `curl … | sudo sh`. This leaves a developer-convention tree on every installed host, and the install aborts if that path cannot be created

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-04
**Severity (source):** Low — host hygiene, plus an unnecessary install-failure mode. The reporter's GNUPGHOME hijack needs a pre-existing group-writable /var/worktrees, which a production host does not have (root creates it 0755), so I give it no weight [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Every Tier-A install carries a stray developer directory. Hosts with an unusual or read-only /var layout fail to install.

**Contract:** #14833 is scoped to "build/test scratch". docs/distribution.md:360-377 enumerates what the installer mutates (keyring, apt source, pin, apt install), and a /var/worktrees tree is not on that list.

**Trace:** `curl … | sudo sh` -> validate() -> validate_archive_key -> mkdir under /var/worktrees -> gpg --show-keys under it -> rm of the key home only, so the tree is left behind.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
scripts/dist/install.sh:196-199 `if [ -z "${TMPDIR:-}" ]; then mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir || die "cannot create scratch dir."; fi` / `_key_home=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir}/xpf-archive-key-check.XXXXXX")`. The commit 99e8f3f26d (#14833, ancestor) message says "make dist/install.sh create the pinned dir only when TMPDIR is unset". scripts/scratch-pinning-selftest.sh:37 audits install.sh.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_install_scratch.sh, re-run by vb17 (stubs only, nothing mutated), output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/install_scratch.out: `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir`, `mktemp -d /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir/xpf-archive-key-check.XXXXXX`. Control (TMPDIR set): `mktemp -d /var/tmp/b17/...` only.

## Acceptance / fix direction
in shipped scripts, use `mktemp -d -t ...` (honours TMPDIR, otherwise /tmp), and exempt scripts/dist/install.sh from scratch-pinning-selftest. Acceptance: the probe's unset cell performs no /var/worktrees operation.

## Full validated claim

## #16540 — fairness-eval returns PASS (exit 0) when every flow delivers zero bytes across the whole steady-state window, and no harness arms the aggregate-throughput gate that would catch it [OPEN]

## Summary
fairness-eval returns PASS (exit 0) when every flow delivers zero bytes across the whole steady-state window, and no harness arms the aggregate-throughput gate that would catch it

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — a false green on the CoS fairness merge/regression gate in a narrow outage shape, with no dataplane effect. The sweep summary still prints avg_mbps of about 0, so a human reader can notice it. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A70-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va70.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
The fairness sweep is the regression gate for CoS scheduler changes, the area where wedge/stall defects (C08-01 class) have been found. A run that blackholes the class across the window is recorded as a fairness PASS. Automation keyed on `verdict` would accept it, and a human would have to notice avg_mbps of about 0.

**Contract:** `docs/fairness-regimes.md` "Acceptance gates" Gate 1 defines a starved flow as one below 1 % of the mean per-flow throughput for the whole window. The doc avoids the word "zero-throughput" only so as not to imply strictly 0 Mb/s, which makes 0 the canonical starved case. `userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/README.md` calls the tool "a merge gate for the CoS fairness contract". `fairness_eval/windowing.rs:113-127` (#7206) calls a near-total outage scoring PASS "a false PASS that can carry a merge decision".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/fairness.rs:84-90`: `if total_cells == 0 || total_bytes == 0 { return 0; }` (no flow counts as starved). `fairness.rs:58-63`: `if mean == 0.0 { return 0.0; }` (CoV 0). `fairness_eval/verdict.rs:204-218`: Gate 3 runs only `if input.expect_saturation`. `test/incus/fairness-harness.sh:726-757` (`run_eval`): `eval_args` never adds `--expect-saturation`. A repo-wide grep finds the flag only in `args.rs`/`verdict.rs`/`report.rs` and the blackbox test. `fairness-harness.sh:802-804` exits with iperf3's status before evaluating when iperf3 fails.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — the fresh `fairness-eval` ran on synthetic iperf3/binding inputs, with positive controls in both directions. Field reachability is STATIC.

## #16541 — A group leaf-list member is spliced into the FIRST of several same-key inline statements: inline BGP export written as two `set` lines `a`, `b` plus group `c` compiles and renders as the chain `[a c b]` [OPEN]

## Summary

A group leaf-list member is spliced into the FIRST of several same-key inline statements: inline BGP export written as two `set` lines `a`, `b` plus group `c` compiles and renders as the chain `[a c b]`

**Finding ID:** `R3-A03-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — export/import chains are evaluated in order, with the first terminal action winning (#5277). Moving a group policy ahead of later inline policies changes which routes are advertised or accepted. A template `accept` placed ahead of an inline `reject` leaks routes, and a template `reject` pla…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the CLI path yields a chain order that no reading of group semantics produces, and the commit gives no signal.

## Mechanism

`set protocols bgp group ext export a` + `... export b` → two sibling leaves. `set groups G protocols bgp group ext export c` + `set apply-groups G` → mergeNodes leaf arm → leafListPeer = `export a` → union → `export a c`, followed by `export b` → compiler concatenates siblings → BGPNeighbor.Export=[a c b] → pkg/frr bgpNeighborExportChain keeps the order (filterDefinedPolicies "in order") → composed route-map `a-c-b-xpf-chain` applied out.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1671-1684 @d1ea69f9aa: `leafListPeer` returns the first node with `Keys[0]==key` (`if n.IsLeaf || len(n.Keys) == 1 { return n }`). :1022-1024 calls `mergeLeafListInto(peer, s)` on that node. :1703-1760 `mergeLeafListInto` builds `seen` only from that node's members and appends new members to its Keys. Observation: ShowCandidateSet stores `set protocols bgp group ext export a` and `... export b` as two lines (two sibling leaves). Observation: with no group, the compiler concatenates the siblings in order to [a b].

## Impact

An operator who builds an export or import chain one `set` line per policy and has a site template that adds a common tail policy (`deny-bogons`, `default-reject`, or a catch-all accept) gets the template evaluated second instead of last. Depending on the template's action, routes leak to an eBGP peer or are withdrawn, with a green commit. The same splice applies to every order-sensitive leaf-list that uses this union (OSPF/RIP/routing-instance export and import).

## Acceptance / fix direction

In the union, compute `seen` over ALL same-key inline siblings (both shapes) and append new members to the LAST same-key sibling. Alternatively, coalesce same-key leaf-list siblings into one node before merging. Acceptance: TestVA03ExportOrder gives [a b c] for all three inline spellings, a group member equal to a later inline member is not duplicated, and the rendered route-map is `a-b-c-xpf-chain`.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/config/ast_groups.go:704-711 (mergeNodes doc): for a leaf-list "the group's members are inherited IN ADDITION to the inline members — UNION. Inline members keep precedence and order; group members not already present are appended, deduplicated ... yields exactly ONE node for the key". #5277 made export/import an ordered Junos policy chain. Under union-append the answer is [a b c], and under override it is [a b]. [a c b] is neither.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A03-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A03-01 | Medium | A group leaf-list member is spliced into the FIRST of several same-key inline statements:… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:24: - **R3-A03-01 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1667-1683` selects the **first** same-key leaf-list peer and `:1703+` appends inherited members there; for inline `export a; export b;` and group `export c;`, the read order becomes `a,c,b`, not the documented inline-first `a,b,c` chain. Historical FRR route-map output preserved the altered order. **Refutation:** no failure occurs unless ordered policies have different outcomes and two same-key inline nodes are authored; simple single-value and bracket-list forms are unaffected. **Decisive check:** compiled and rendered BGP export order, including a terminal accept/reject in `c` and a subsequent inline `b`.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L79: ### R3-A03-01 — group leaf-list member spliced into FIRST same-key statement → `[a c b]` — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `ast_groups.go:1671 leafListPeer` returns FIRST node with `Keys[0]==key`; `mergeLeafListInto` unions group members into it only, `seen` from that node alone. Two inline `set … export a` / `export b` sibling leaves + group `export c` → `[a c b]` (+ duplicate `[a b b]` case). Ordered policy chains (#5277, first terminal wins) → route leak/withdrawal potential. Neither union-append `[a b c]` nor override. - Refutation: Needs group+multi-statement inline list combo; route consequence via documented chain semantics, no peer advertisement run; duplicate case cosmetic. Ordering defect itself executed at compile+FRR render. - Evidence: `leafListPeer` first-match re-read at origin/master. Report controls (no-group `[a b]`, bracket `[a b c]`, defect `[a c b]` order-independent). - Unresolved: Lab BGP advertisement with terminal accept/reject template (impact proof); fix acceptance is compile-level `[a b c]`. ### R3-A03-04 — bare presence `set system services ssh` discards whole group container (#4325 guard) — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `ast_groups.go:1465ff` @origin/master: `len(s.Keys)==1 && hasMatchingLeaf(*dst,s.Keys) && !packedTailLeafExempts4325…` drops group container; `hasMatchingLeaf:2025` true for any same-keyword leaf; exemption only for packed tails (`len(Keys)>1`). ## #16542 — publish.py _gate_one_latest never checks `data["channel"] == channel`, and gate_apt never compares a suite's signed Suite/Codename with `dists/<suite>`. A mis-synced pointer or suite is reported as "gate PASSED" and then refused by... [OPEN]

## Summary
publish.py _gate_one_latest never checks `data["channel"] == channel`, and gate_apt never compares a suite's signed Suite/Codename with `dists/<suite>`. A mis-synced pointer or suite is reported as "gate PASSED" and then refused by every client, so the channel breaks until republished

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-05
**Severity (source):** Low — the client fails closed, so no wrong bytes are installed. The defects are a false gate verdict and a channel outage, and the trigger is a publisher mis-sync [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/COHORT/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
One mis-sync breaks channel fetch and install for every consumer until republished, while the publisher's log says the gate passed.

**Contract:** docs/distribution.md:165-167: a pointer "whose `channel` field disagrees with the channel it was served from is refused (... a mis-synced or swapped pointer verifies perfectly)". The publish gate is documented as the fail-closed release gate, and #4215 extended it to every channel's pointer.

**Trace:** a dist tree with edge/ and stable/ -> the signed edge pointer is copied to stable/latest.json -> gate_latest passes -> upload -> `xpf-deploy fetch --channel stable` dies with "says it is for channel 'edge'".

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
scripts/dist/publish.py:813-846 checks the signature (`verify_and_read`), dict shape, `validate_latest_date`, and `ver not in require_present` (target only). There is no channel check. scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:1752-1757 `if got_chan is not None and got_chan != channel: die(...)`. gate_apt (:1141-1272) reads Codename only to classify reprepro (:1215-1224) and never compares the signed Suite/Codename with the suite directory. install.sh verify_channel refuses that mismatch.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_latest_channel.py, re-run by vb17, output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/latest_channel.out: `[edge pointer served at stable/] gate PASSED stable -> 1.2.3; channel field = 'edge'`. Control: `[genuine stable pointer] gate PASSED`. The client-rule line in the probe is a re-implementation; I read the real client code at xpf-deploy.py:1752-1757 directly. No probe was run for the apt half.

## Acceptance / fix direction
require `data.get("channel") == channel` in _gate_one_latest, and refuse when it is absent. In gate_apt, require exactly one signed Suite and one Codename equal to the directory. Acceptance: the probe's defect cell is refused, the control passes, and a `dists/stable` signed `Suite: edge` fixture is refused.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb17.md)</summary>

- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b17 (A10 upgrade/release engineer, second pass); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb17
- **Severity:** Low — the client fails closed, so no wrong bytes are installed. The defects are a false gate verdict and a channel outage, and the trigger is a publisher mis-sync [reporter: Low]

- **Gate verdict:** COHORT (dist installer/publisher tooling fidelity: R3-B17-03, R3-B17-04, R3-B17-05) — a real gate-oracle gap with a bounded consequence.

The publish gate is documented as the fail-closed release gate, and #4215 extended it to every channel's pointer.

There is no channel check. scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:1752-1757 `if got_chan is not None and got_chan != channel: die(...)`. gate_apt (:1141-1272) reads Codename only to classify reprepro (:1215-1224) and never compares the signed Suite/Codename with the suite directory. install.sh verify_channel refuses that mismatch.

Control: `[genuine stable pointer] gate PASSED`. The client-rule line in the probe is a re-implementation; I read the real client code at xpf-deploy.py:1752-1757 directly. No probe was run for the apt half.

- **Refutation attempt:** make_latest checks the channel only on its own overwrite path, not on the gated bytes. require_present binds only the version, which is shared across channels. #4215 added signature and date checks only. The claim stands, narrowed to fail-closed consequences.

## #16543 — A `<*>` group never binds to a bare named OSPF interface or BGP neighbor leaf, so a wildcard OSPF-MD5 or neighbor-level BGP-MD5 template leaves those adjacencies and sessions unauthenticated on a clean commit [OPEN]

## Summary

A `<*>` group never binds to a bare named OSPF interface or BGP neighbor leaf, so a wildcard OSPF-MD5 or neighbor-level BGP-MD5 template leaves those adjacencies and sessions unauthenticated on a clean commit

**Finding ID:** `R3-A03-03`
**Severity (source report):** High — routing-protocol authentication that the operator configured is silently absent. The strict commit is green with zero warnings. The spelling that triggers it is the most common one: `set protocols ospf area 0 interface ge-0/0/0.0` with no attributes. If both ends run xpf with the same templat…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable through the ordinary CLI, it silently drops a configured security control, and it survived refutation and dedup.

## Mechanism

`set groups AUTH protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface <*> authentication md5 1 key K` + `set apply-groups AUTH` + bare `set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/0.0` → expandGroups → mergeNodes wildcard arm. `d` is a leaf and not a zone, so it is skipped. Compile gives OSPFInterface{AuthType:"", AuthKeyID:0}. pkg/frr emits no message-digest lines, and FRR runs the interface unauthenticated. The BGP neighbor-level path is the same, ending with an empty AuthPassword and no `neighbor X password`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1197-1243 @d1ea69f9aa is the wildcard fan-out loop. At :1213, `if matches && (!d.IsLeaf || zoneLeafTakesWildcard9801(ancestorPath, d))` skips every matching leaf destination except a zone. The #15032 pre-step at :1202-1207 promotes only `interfacePackedLeaf15032` destinations, and its comment says "Bare leaves have no tail and stay for #9838". pkg/config/group_merge_zone_leaf_9801.go:99-105 scopes the flip to `security-zone` because "An interface or a routing instance written as a leaf compiles no instance at all (#9838)". Observation: SetPath stores `interface ge-0/0/0.0` and `neighbor 192.0.2.2` as 2-key leaves. Observation: the compiler builds OSPFInterface and BGPNeighbor from those leaves (exact-name control).

## Impact

Any site that templates OSPF or neighbor-level BGP authentication with a `<*>` group and writes instances as bare lines (the usual spelling for an OSPF interface, and for a BGP neighbor that inherits everything from its group) runs those peers unauthenticated. The configuration shows the template, the commit is clean, and adding any attribute to the line "fixes" it, so the failure looks random. Recovery requires knowing about this defect.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Generalise #9801 in the wildcard arm. When `d.IsLeaf` and `d` is a bare named-instance leaf whose schema slot is a container that compiles from a leaf (OSPF/OSPFv3 interface, BGP neighbor, RA interface, and the like), promote it to an empty container before merging. Keep the #9838 exclusion for interfaces and routing-instances. Acceptance: the `def-bare-*` rows equal `ctl-attr-wild` for every instance, and the FRR render emits the auth lines. #9838's no-group rows stay unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

docs/feature-gaps.md:1019: "A group key of the form `<pattern>` is glob-matched against the instance name". #9801 established that a named instance written as a leaf takes a wildcard group exactly like its empty braced spelling. The exact-name arm of mergeNodes already binds a group to these same bare leaves.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A03-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A03-03 | High | A <*> group never binds to a bare named OSPF interface or BGP neighbor leaf, so a wildcard… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:23: - **R3-A03-03 — MATERIAL (Medium; high conditional adjacency significance).** **Defect:** wildcard merge binds matching destination nodes only when nonleaf or a narrowly special-cased zone leaf (`pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1198-1215`); a bare OSPF interface or BGP neighbor survives without inherited authentication while `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:248-288` still constructs the OSPF interface. Historical FRR rendering omitted the intended MD5. **Refutation:** adjacency/auth impact needs a corresponding peer, routing daemon and suitable host-inbound rule; grouped definitions may instead be braced or explicit. The source establishes inherited auth loss, not observed unauthenticated adjacency. **Decisive check:** identical bare-versus-braced OSPF/BGP peer fixtures through expansion and FRR output, followed by bounded existing integration test if available.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L73: ### R3-A03-03 — `<*>` group never binds to bare OSPF interface / BGP neighbor leaf — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1213` @origin/master: `if matches && (!d.IsLeaf || zoneLeafTakesWildcard9801(ancestorPath,d))` — wildcard fan-out skips every bare leaf except zones. OSPF interfaces/BGP neighbors compile instances from bare leaves (exact-name control binds), so wildcard MD5 template silently absent; clean commit, FRR renders no auth. OSPF has no group-level alternative. - Refutation: Junos binding of `<*>` to body-less statement is inferred from project's own #9801 zone equivalence + exact-name arm behaviour, not vendor-doc proven; if peer requires MD5, failure is visible outage (fail-closed-ish). But xpf-internal inconsistency (exact binds, wildcard doesn't; braced binds) is itself the defect regardless of Junos. - Evidence: Gate line re-read at origin/master; #15032 packed-only promotion noted in report. Report executed compiled+FRR controls (`ctl-attr-wild` md5 vs `def-bare-wild` auth=""). - Unresolved: Vendor-semantics citation for bare-instance wildcard binding (parity framing); internal-inconsistency claim needs no further check. ### R3-A03-01 — group leaf-list member spliced into FIRST same-key statement → `[a c b]` — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `ast_groups.go:1671 leafListPeer` returns FIRST node with `Keys[0]==key`; `mergeLeafListInto` unions group members into it only, `seen` from that node alone. ## #16544 — wildcard-address mask uses inverted (Cisco) polarity: every Junos wildcard is refused, and the masks that commit become a different address set (an all-ones host wildcard becomes 0.0.0.0/0 / ::/0) [OPEN]

## Summary
wildcard-address mask uses inverted (Cisco) polarity: every Junos wildcard is refused, and the masks that commit become a different address set (an all-ones host wildcard becomes 0.0.0.0/0 / ::/0)

**Finding ID:** R3-N08-01
**Severity (source):** High — High — enforcement is lost, because a policy address object is compiled to a different address set. The Junos exact-host wildcard `A.B.C.D/255.255.255.255` passes strict commit and reaches the userspace policy resolver as `0.0.0.0/0`, and the IPv6 all-ones mask as `::/0`. A `permit` naming that host then admits every source or destination, and a `deny` blocks everything. An inverted mask such as `/0.0.0.255` commits as a /24 that has nothing to do with the Junos meaning. Every Junos-polarity mask (both Juniper documentation examples, and contiguous masks such as 255.255.255.0) is refused at strict commit, which fails closed. On the tolerant or peer-sync path such an entry has no usable prefix. The severity is demonstrated at the compile and userspace-resolver layers; a wire test was not run [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator who writes a host wildcard gets a permit-any or deny-any policy with green strict commit. `show security address-book` prints a blank value for these forms (R3-B18-03), so the widening is invisible. Migrated configs that use Junos-polarity masks cannot commit. Blast radius: every policy and address-set that references the entry, across all zone pairs where it is used. Recovery: rewrite the entries as prefixes.

**Contract:** Juniper, *Address Books and Address Sets* (security-policies topic map, fetched): "A wildcard address is represented as A.B.C.D/wildcard-mask. The wildcard mask determines which of the bits in the IP address A.B.C.D should be ignored. For example, the source IP address 192.168.0.11/255.255.0.255 ... can discard the third octet ... (symbolically represented as 192.168.*.11)"; "You can configure any wildcard address." So a 1 bit in the mask is compared and a 0 bit is ignored. pkg/config/README.md promises the form "expands to the single wildcard-derived CIDR" (docs/log/15673.md:9-10).

**Trace:** `set security address-book ... address X wildcard-address A/M` -> mergeAddressNode -> applyWildcardAddress -> expandWildcardAddress -> Address.ExpandedPrefixes -> UsableValues() -> userspace buildAddressBookTable / expandBookNameRecursive -> policy snapshot address IDs -> Rust policy match. The same UsableValues feeds NAT expansion, the strict policy mirror and pkg/policymatch (README).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/config/address_forms_15673.go:17-21 (doc comment: "the bits set in the wildcard mask are 'don't care'"); :218-256 `expandWildcardAddress`; :241 `care[i] = ^maskB[i]`; :242 `network[i] = ipB[i] & care[i]`; :244-247 rejects only when `net.IPMask(care).Size()` is non-canonical; :300-307 `applyWildcardAddress` records failures as UnimplementedForms (strict reject). pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:517-520 consumes `addr.UsableValues()`. The test pkg/config/address_forms_15673_test.go:134-155 pins 10.1.2.3/0.0.0.255 -> 10.1.2.0/24. Observed directly: the outputs below. Inferred: wire behaviour follows the resolver output.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestVN08Wildcard -v` (RUN/verify/vn08/probes/config_zz_vn08_wildcard_test.go -> wildcard.out). Flat set plus a policy reference: 192.168.0.11/255.255.0.255, 10.0.0.0/255.0.0.0 and 10.1.2.3/255.255.255.0 give strict=REJECT; 10.1.2.3/0.0.0.255 gives strict=OK usable=[10.1.2.0/24], with Junos member 99.9.9.3 -> false and Junos non-member 10.1.2.77 -> true; control prefix 10.1.2.0/24 gives [10.1.2.0/24]. `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestVN08WildcardUserspace -v` (userspace_zz_vn08_wildcard_test.go -> wildcard-userspace.out): `10.1.2.3/255.255.255.255 strict=OK userspace v4=[0.0.0.0/0]`; `2001:db8::1/ffff:...:ffff strict=OK v6=[::/0]`; control `10.1.2.3/32 -> [10.1.2.3/32]`. Limit: no packet test.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Compare the bits where the mask is 1 (`network = ip & mask`). A canonical mask gives `network/ones`. A non-contiguous mask gives either the finite CIDR expansion (with a cap) or an explicit refusal naming non-contiguous masks. Refuse or define IPv6 explicitly. Flip TestWildcardAddressExpands15673. Acceptance: 10.1.2.3/255.255.255.0 -> 10.1.2.0/24; 10.1.2.3/255.255.255.255 -> 10.1.2.3/32; 10.1.2.3/0.0.0.255 never yields 10.1.2.0/24 or /0; the userspace resolver probe shows the same.

- **Contract:** Juniper, *Address Books and Address Sets* (security-policies topic map, fetched): "A wildcard address is represented as A.B.C.D/wildcard-mask. The wildcard mask determines which of the bits in the IP address A.B.C.D should be ignored. For example, the source IP address 192.168.0.11/255.255.0.255 ... can discard the third octet ... (symbolically represented as 192.168.*.11)"; "You can configure any wildcard address." So a 1 bit in the mask is compared and a 0 bit is ignored. pkg/config/README.md promises the form "expands to the single wildcard-derived CIDR" (docs/log/15673.md:9-10).
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection is policy match-set integrity for address-book objects. The actor is an authenticated operator migrating a vSRX/SRX config, or an HA peer config-sync carrying such text; no adversary is needed. The challenged assumption is that #15673 encoded the Junos mask polarity. It encoded the opposite, and the only guard (the non-contiguity refusal) is keyed on the inverted complement. That guard therefore refuses the correct forms and admits the wrong ones, including the degenerate all-ones mask, whose complement is the zero mask, i.e. /0.
- **Evidence:** pkg/config/address_forms_15673.go:17-21 (doc comment: "the bits set in the wildcard mask are 'don't care'"); :218-256 `expandWildcardAddress`; :241 `care[i] = ^maskB[i]`; :242 `network[i] = ipB[i] & care[i]`; :244-247 rejects only when `net.IPMask(care).Size()` is non-canonical; :300-307 `applyWildcardAddress` records failures as UnimplementedForms (strict reject). pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:517-520 consumes `addr.UsableValues()`. The test pkg/config/address_forms_15673_test.go:134-155 pins 10.1.2.3/0.0.0.255 -> 10.1.2.0/24. Observed directly: the outputs below. Inferred: wire behaviour follows the resolver output.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestVN08Wildcard -v` (RUN/verify/vn08/probes/config_zz_vn08_wildcard_test.go -> wildcard.out). Flat set plus a policy reference: 192.168.0.11/255.255.0.255, 10.0.0.0/255.0.0.0 and 10.1.2.3/255.255.255.0 give strict=REJECT; 10.1.2.3/0.0.0.255 gives strict=OK usable=[10.1.2.0/24], with Junos member 99.9.9.3 -> false and Junos non-member 10.1.2.77 -> true; control prefix 10.1.2.0/24 gives [10.1.2.0/24]. `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestVN08WildcardUserspace -v` (userspace_zz_vn08_wildcard_test.go -> wildcard-userspace.out): `10.1.2.3/255.255.255.255 strict=OK userspace v4=[0.0.0.0/0]`; `2001:db8::1/ffff:...:ffff strict=OK v6=[::/0]`; control `10.1.2.3/32 -> [10.1.2.3/32]`. Limit: no packet test.
- **Trace:** `set security address-book ... address X wildcard-address A/M` -> mergeAddressNode -> applyWildcardAddress -> expandWildcardAddress -> Address.ExpandedPrefixes -> UsableValues() -> userspace buildAddressBookTable / expandBookNameRecursive -> policy snapshot address IDs -> Rust policy match. The same UsableValues feeds NAT expansion, the strict policy mirror and pkg/policymatch (README).
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for strict-path normalization, a polarity flag, a schema validator on the mask and a later rewrite in userspace, and found none. I verified the Juniper text myself; it is not misattributed and the example is unambiguous. The reporter missed the all-ones case, which turns the claim from wrong set into match-any; workers a07 and f13 logged it as an addendum to this ID, and I re-executed it. I narrowed the IPv6 leg: Juniper documents only A.B.C.D, so the IPv6 wildcard is an xpf extension, yet it also expands to ::/0.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — compile-time expansion, no hot-path cost.

## #16545 — Explicit queue buffer-size (bytes/percent/temporal) and shaping-rate burst-size values below 96,000 B are silently raised to the 64x1500 runtime floor, so configured latency/burst bounds on low-rate classes are not en... [OPEN]

## Summary
Explicit queue buffer-size (bytes/percent/temporal) and shaping-rate burst-size values below 96,000 B are silently raised to the 64x1500 runtime floor, so configured latency/burst bounds on low-rate classes are not enforced

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — this is a material but bounded operator-contract failure. Under congestion, a documented "ENFORCED" queue-depth knob (`buffer-size temporal`) and the documented "tighter bursting" knob (`shaping-rate burst-size`) have no effect below 96 KB. On low-rate classes, queueing delay rises one to three orders of magnitude above the configured bound: a 10 ms target on a 1 Mb/s exact class admits 768 ms (demonstrated at the admission-limit layer). Rate caps and isolation are unaffected. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A70-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va70.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Operators porting Junos low-rate class configs (VoIP/network-control/WAN uplink) use these knobs precisely to bound latency. xpf commits them, reports success, and shows only a different buffer number in `show class-of-service`. Under congestion, the class adds hundreds of ms to seconds of delay (64 kb/s with a 20 ms target gives 12 s). It persists for as long as the config stands, and the only workaround is raising the rate.

**Contract:** `docs/cos-traffic-shaping.md:288-293` reads "Temporal resolution (#6846 — now ENFORCED). `buffer-size temporal <us>` sizes the queue by drain time ... Rounding and clamping mirror `buffer-size percent` exactly". `docs/cos-wan-sqm.md:145-148` reads burst "override with `... shaping-rate burst-size <bytes>` if you need tighter or looser bursting". `cos/admission.rs:145-151` (#4269) calls `buffer-size 16k` "a LEGAL operator configuration". The only acknowledgement of a floor is `docs/cos-traffic-shaping.md:~1101` ("runtime queues still retain a minimum burst floor", percent context, no value) and `cos/README.md:25` (developer doc, "universal floor").

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/token_bucket.rs:23-27`: `COS_MIN_BURST_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1500`, documented as "Sized so a single max-len frame can always fit". `cos/builders.rs:136`: `burst_bytes: config.burst_bytes.max(COS_MIN_BURST_BYTES)`. `cos/builders.rs:191`: `buffer_bytes: queue.buffer_bytes.max(COS_MIN_BURST_BYTES)`. `cos/admission.rs:313` and `:372`: `queue.config.buffer_bytes.max(COS_MIN_BURST_BYTES)`. `coordinator/cos_leases.rs:651`: `queue.buffer_bytes.max(64 * 1500)`. The builder resolves the value correctly: `forwarding_build/cos.rs:340-375` (`cos_scheduler_buffer_bytes`: bytes, then percent, then temporal) and `:879-883` (root burst = explicit `cos_shaping_burst_bytes` when > 0). `worker/cos/queue_row.rs:83` reports the floored `config.buffer_bytes` in status. No Go advisory flags a sub-96 KB value (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn*.go` grepped).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a Rust unit probe ran snapshot -> `build_cos_state` -> `build_cos_interface_runtime` -> `cos_flow_aware_buffer_limit` with a positive control. The end-to-end RTT inflation on a live class is STATIC (inferred from the admission limit / rate).

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-smr-batch07.md`: | R3-A70-01 shared_exact BDP floor class-rate/local-N | MATERIAL | Low |
| R3-A70-02 fairness-eval PASS on zero-throughput window | COHORT | Low |
| R3-A71-02 snapshot apply launders spoofed neighbor MAC | MATERIAL | Medium (potential High) |
| R3-A71-03 wire-owner roster latch never resets, O(table) removal | MATERIAL | High (potential) |

Executed snapshot→runtime probe: temporal 10ms @125kB/s resolves 1250 → runtime 96000 (768ms residence vs 10ms configured); bytes 16000→96000; above-floor control unchanged. Docs call temporal "ENFORCED" and burst-size "tighter bursting" — silent override with only `show` number differing.
- Refutation: floor is deliberate (#1398 test pins ≥ floor, README "universal floor") — but that pins liveness magnitude for defaults, not overriding an explicit operator bound; constant's own rationale is one frame (1500), and 96k = batch×frame conflates TX batching with admission buffer. Percent-collapse correction in part (≤76.8Mb/s all percents; else <96000/(rate/100)) is arithmetically right.
- Unresolved: none. Fix must keep ≥1 frame for liveness; applying floor only to unset values is the clean cut.
