## #16546 — A bare presence statement inline (`set system services ssh`, `set system syslog`) makes the #4325 cross-shape guard discard the whole same-keyword group container: a hardening group's root-login deny, ciphers and connection-limit never reach sshd [OPEN]

## Summary

A bare presence statement inline (`set system services ssh`, `set system syslog`) makes the #4325 cross-shape guard discard the whole same-keyword group container: a hardening group's root-login deny, ciphers and connection-limit never reach sshd

**Finding ID:** `R3-A03-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — management-plane hardening that the operator configured is silently absent. No `PermitRootLogin` is rendered (the sshd or factory default applies), the cipher restriction and MaxStartups are missing, and a group's remote syslog host is dropped beside a bare `system syslog`, which is an audi…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a common CLI spelling silently voids a hardening group, with a reachable trigger and a concrete loss of configured controls.

## Mechanism

`set system services ssh` → 1-key leaf `ssh`. Group `system services ssh { root-login deny; ciphers ...; connection-limit 10; }` → 1-key container. mergeNodes container branch: no same-key container found, so the #4325 guard fires and the container is skipped. Compile gives SSH{RootLogin:"", Ciphers:[], ConnectionLimit:0}. The sshd drop-in omits PermitRootLogin, Ciphers and MaxStartups.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1465-1470 @d1ea69f9aa: `if len(s.Keys) == 1 && hasMatchingLeaf(*dst, s.Keys) && ... && !packedTailLeafExempts4325(ancestorPath, *dst, s) && ...`. On this path the group container is dropped. hasMatchingLeaf (:2025-2042) returns true for any leaf with the same Keys[0]. packedTailLeafExempts4325 (:2075-2081) exempts only leaves with `len(Keys) > 1`. pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1338-1350 renders `PermitRootLogin` only when `ssh.RootLogin != ""`. A test pins the current behaviour: pkg/config/group_merge_ospf_auth_container_dr14h1_test.go `TestGroupBareLeafDuplicateStillDropped14414` asserts that a bare `rip;` suppresses the group's rip authentication ("a genuine duplicate stays dropped").

## Impact

`set system services ssh` appears in nearly every config, and a global SSH-hardening group is standard Junos practice. Under this guard the group's SSH policy is void, and remote syslog, SNMP and LLDP settings supplied by a group vanish whenever the inline side states the bare keyword. Nothing tells the operator. Recovery means deleting the bare inline statement or bracing it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Fire the #4325 guard only when the key is a leaf-list or the dst leaf carries values. For a bare `len(Keys)==1` leaf whose schema node is a container, promote it to an empty container and merge `s.Children` with inline precedence. Invert TestGroupBareLeafDuplicateStillDropped14414. Acceptance: the `def-bare-*` rows equal the controls, and the #4325/#4070 cells (`name-server` collapsed vs block) still yield one node.

## Contract (where cited)

In the mergeNodes doc (ast_groups.go:700-702), containers with matching keys merge recursively. A body-less presence statement is the same statement as its empty braced spelling (`ssh;` ≡ `ssh { }`), and the braced spelling inherits (control). In ast_groups.go:1454-1459, the #4325 guard's own premise is "a single-key group container whose LEAF-LIST counterpart exists inline as a collapsed leaf". `ssh` is not a leaf-list.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A03-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A03-04 | Medium | A bare presence statement inline (set system services ssh, set system syslog) makes the… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:25: - **R3-A03-04 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/ast_groups.go:1453-1496` drops a group's same-key container when an inline leaf shares its keyword (`hasMatchingLeaf`), so a bare `system services ssh;` can suppress an inherited block carrying root-login/cipher limits. The historical CheckText returned no explanatory warning. **Refutation:** bare `ssh` may intentionally override a group in a given Junos policy, so exact precedence is a contract question; this does not prove enabled password/root login without running host config. Other paths already exempt packed-tail leaf peers. **Decisive check:** compare bare versus empty braced inline ssh under the hardening group, and assert the final effective SSH config plus an explicit conflict diagnostic if override is intended.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L85: ### R3-A03-04 — bare presence `set system services ssh` discards whole group container (#4325 guard) — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `ast_groups.go:1465ff` @origin/master: `len(s.Keys)==1 && hasMatchingLeaf(*dst,s.Keys) && !packedTailLeafExempts4325…` drops group container; `hasMatchingLeaf:2025` true for any same-keyword leaf; exemption only for packed tails (`len(Keys)>1`). Bare `ssh;` (≡ `ssh {}` which inherits) voids group's root-login/ciphers/limit; same for syslog/snmp/lldp. Pinned test `TestGroupBareLeafDuplicateStillDropped14414` asserts the drop — pin encodes the wrong premise (bare leaf ≠ duplicate of container body). - Refutation: Bounded (needs bare inline + group container); base sshd default not measured; Junos merge of group container into bare presence inferred from #9801 equivalence. Internal braced-twin control (inherits) is the decisive asymmetry. - Evidence: Guard + hasMatchingLeaf re-read at origin/master. Report interactive-path probe: controls inherit, `def-bare-ssh` all-empty warnings=0. - Unresolved: Image sshd default (severity); census of affected keywords beyond demonstrated set. ### R3-A03-05 — brace-elided wildcard group statement compiled as phantom `<*>` interface — **COHORT** - Defect: Packed group leaf `interface <*> authentication …;` takes leaf arm (`ast_groups.go:856 IsLeaf`) which lacks the `keysContainWildcard:1182` check (container arm only, both re-read at origin/master) → adopted as literal instance `<*>`, real interfaces unauthenticated. S

**Wonder:** wonder batch00 L25: | R3-A03-01 | MATERIAL | MATERIAL | Medium | High | STATIC | | R3-A03-04 | MATERIAL | MATERIAL | Medium | High | STATIC (incl. pinning test executed) | | R3-A03-05 | COHORT (with A03-03) | COHORT | Medium | High | STATIC | | R3-A03-02 | DUP of gemini-003 H3-04 (scope checked in source report) | DUP | — | High | STATIC | | R3-A04-04 | MATERIAL | MATERIAL | Medium | High | STATIC |

## #16547 — The #7717 runtime interface-SNAT overlap quarantine (`iface_snat_egress_overlap`) disarms a source-NAT pool rule in the dataplane while every NAT show surface (CLI, gRPC/remote CLI, REST, Prometheus) still reports the rule and pool as... [OPEN]

## Summary
The #7717 runtime interface-SNAT overlap quarantine (`iface_snat_egress_overlap`) disarms a source-NAT pool rule in the dataplane while every NAT show surface (CLI, gRPC/remote CLI, REST, Prometheus) still reports the rule and pool as armed; `InterfaceSNATPoolOverlapStats` has no consumer

**Finding ID:** R3-B18-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — demonstrated at the builder/verdict layer: once a live interface address (DHCP/netlink) lands inside a pool used by a pool-mode rule that shares egress with an interface-mode rule, every new flow on that rule is refused (Rust `pool_failure` → `SourceNatFailure`), a fail-closed translation outage for that rule's subscribers, while `show security nat source rule|rule-set|rule detail|pool|summary`, gRPC GetNATSource/GetNATRuleStats and REST say the rule is installed with a 0 hit counter. Fail-closed direction (no protection loss) and a niche trigger keep it at Medium. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Subscribers on the quarantined rule lose new connections while every NAT view tells the operator the rule is healthy and idle, pointing diagnosis at traffic rather than at the quarantine; combined with the stale-quarantine defect reported in gemini vsrx-parity-002 the outage can persist after the overlap clears, still invisible. Recovery requires reading journald.

**Contract:** pkg/config/nat_not_installed_7473.go:14-18 — the shared composition exists so "the text renderers and the JSON/protobuf objects then cannot disagree about which rules are armed"; natshow/source.go:147-151 names this exact class (a pool the builder marks unusable rendered from config as if armed); docs/engineering-style.md "A fail-closed exclusion owes a show-surface annotation (#6534)". nat_iface_pool_overlap.go:59-74 says the scans/addresses pair exists so a reader can tell "no overlap" from "never ran".

**Trace:** DHCP lease E on ge-0/0/2.0 (zone wan) → full recompile → buildLinkSnapshot merges E into snapshot interface addresses → detectInterfaceSNATPoolOverlaps finds E in pool P of rule pool-snat and interface rule iface-snat egressing wan → PoolUnusable/iface_snat_egress_overlap on the wire → Rust pool_failure → every new mint for pool-snat refused (sampled exception reason source_nat_pool_iface_egress_overlap) → operator runs `show security nat source rule all`: no NOT INSTALLED line, Translation hits 0.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_iface_pool_overlap.go:331-375 `snap.SourceNAT[i].PoolUnusable = true` / `PoolUnusableReason = poolUnusableReasonIfaceOverlap` (const "iface_snat_egress_overlap", :389), NAT64 twin :364-374; callers builder.go:395, manager_link_refresh.go:168, apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:237. userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:2041-2044 maps pool_unusable to pool_failure; :1478-1480 `if let Some(reason) = rule.pool_failure { return Err(SourceNatFailure::for_rule(rule, reason)); }`. pkg/config/nat_not_installed_7473.go:73 `return SourceNATPoolUnusableReason(cfg.Security.NAT.SourcePools[rule.Then.PoolName])` (config-only), consumed by pkg/cli/cli_show_nat.go:697 (rule view, which then prints "Translation hits"), pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go:60,470, pkg/api/nat.go:196,548. `grep -rn PoolUnusable pkg cmd` outside the builder: no show reader. protocol_counters.go SourceNATPoolStatus carries no failure/unusable field. `InterfaceSNATPoolOverlapStats` (:74) has no non-test caller.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestB18RuntimeQuarantineInvisibleToShowVerdicts -count=1 -v` (RUN/verify/vb18/probes/zz_b18_probe_test.go, the worker's probe re-run by vb18): overlap row `dataplane PoolUnusable=true reason="iface_snat_egress_overlap" | rule-view="" detail-view="" pool-view="" ports=64512` → DEFECT; positive control (pool 198.51.100.7, no overlap) `PoolUnusable=false` PASS, so the probe separates the states. Limit: the overlap is created with a configured interface address (strict #7645 would reject that config); the runtime-learned case is inferred from the builder reading live link state.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Feed the applied snapshot's per-rule PoolUnusable/PoolUnusableReason (Manager's last snapshot) into the shared NAT verdict for the CLI, gRPC and REST rule/pool/summary views; add "iface_snat_egress_overlap" (and the NAT64 twin) to SourceNATDisarmReasonText; export InterfaceSNATPoolOverlapStats as scans/addresses metrics. Acceptance: the probe's overlap row reports a non-empty rule verdict and NOT INSTALLED text on all three surfaces while the control row stays empty; a gRPC GetNATRuleStats test sees not_installed=true.

## #16548 — A brace-elided wildcard group statement (`interface <*> authentication md5 1 key K;`) takes the leaf arm, which has no wildcard check, and is compiled as a phantom OSPF interface `<*>`; the real interfaces stay unauthenticated behind only an… [OPEN]

## Summary

A brace-elided wildcard group statement (`interface <*> authentication md5 1 key K;`) takes the leaf arm, which has no wildcard check, and is compiled as a phantom OSPF interface `<*>`; the real interfaces stay unauthenticated behind only an indirect #9405 warning

**Finding ID:** `R3-A03-05`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the consequence is the same as R3-A03-03 (an OSPF authentication template not applied), plus a phantom interface reaching the compiled config. Two things bound it. It is reachable only through hierarchical text (load override/merge, config file, day-0 CheckText), because the flat `set` spel…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (wildcard-group binding over leaf shapes in mergeNodes, with R3-A03-03) — real and reachable, but bounded by the load-only spelling and an existing warning. It shares the wildcard-over-leaf fix surface with R3-A03-03.

## Mechanism

hierarchical `groups { AUTH { protocols { ospf { area 0.0.0.0 { interface <*> authentication md5 1 key K; } } } } }` → packed leaf → mergeNodes leaf arm → no `<*>` peer, so the leaf is adopted → compiler builds OSPFInterface "<*>" with md5 → the #9405 advisory names it → the real ge-0/0/0.0 has AuthType "".

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/ast_groups.go @d1ea69f9aa: the only `keysContainWildcard(s.Keys)` check in mergeNodes is at :1182, after the `if s.IsLeaf {` arm (:856). That arm ends by adopting the group leaf (`*dst = append(*dst, s)`, :1177) when no inline peer is named `<*>`.

## Impact

A Junos-migrated or hand-written hierarchical config using the compact template spelling leaves every OSPF interface unauthenticated. The only signal is an advisory about an interface named `<*>`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Before the leaf arm, route a leaf whose identity span holds a `<...>` key through the wildcard branch after splitting it to its braced shape (identitySpan9855 knows the span). Alternatively, refuse it at strict commit with a named diagnostic. Acceptance: `def-packed` equals `ctl-braced`, and no compiled instance name contains `<`.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/config/group_key_wildcard_9423.go:44-53: "EVERY wildcard-shaped group key takes the wildcard branch in mergeNodes ... A pattern that matches nothing therefore applies nothing ... instead of inventing an instance named after the pattern". The compact spelling is documented as equivalent to the braced one (#8662/#7648).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A03-05` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:26: - **R3-A03-05 — COHORT (Low/Medium; related wildcard loss, separate branch).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/ast_groups.go:856-1178` processes source leaf nodes before the wildcard branch at `:1181-1215`; a packed `interface <*> authentication ...;` can be adopted literally as a phantom interface while actual OSPF interfaces receive no auth. The old test observed only an indirect warning. **Refutation:** requires a compact group wildcard as a leaf; a hierarchical/braced wildcard is handled differently, and the warning is a clue rather than zero signal. Fixing only A03-03's destination-leaf predicate would not close this source-leaf bypass. **Decisive check:** grouped bare/packed/braced OSPF interface matrix and compiled FRR config, with no literal `<*>` interface emitted.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L91: ### R3-A03-05 — brace-elided wildcard group statement compiled as phantom `<*>` interface — **COHORT** - Defect: Packed group leaf `interface <*> authentication …;` takes leaf arm (`ast_groups.go:856 IsLeaf`) which lacks the `keysContainWildcard:1182` check (container arm only, both re-read at origin/master) → adopted as literal instance `<*>`, real interfaces unauthenticated. Shares wildcard-over-leaf fix surface with A03-03. - Refutation/correction accepted: Commit is NOT silent — #9405 advisory fires (verifier corrected reporter), though it describes phantom interface, not unapplied template; hierarchical-text-only reach (flat `set` builds braced chain, works). Hence COHORT not MATERIAL. - Evidence: Leaf-arm-before-wildcard-check ordering confirmed at origin/master. ## #16549 — `stop_for_link_cycle` takes `forwarding` with `mem::take` before `stop_inner`, so holder retirement for the joined workers walks an empty default allocator set and their NAT holder bits survive on the preserved alloca... [OPEN]

## Summary
`stop_for_link_cycle` takes `forwarding` with `mem::take` before `stop_inner`, so holder retirement for the joined workers walks an empty default allocator set and their NAT holder bits survive on the preserved allocators

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — SNAT/NAT64 pool ports held by the stopped workers stay occupied after a RETH link-cycle stop. `retire_worker(id)` clears bit `id` on every flow, so the residue is cleared at the next correctly-retired stop of a worker with the same id. A durable leak remains only for ids absent from later plans and for reservations with no replayed shared entry. [reporter: Low (potential Medium)]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A71-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va71.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
RETH link cycles on cluster nodes leave pool ports occupied until a later stop of the same worker id, or forever after a plan shrink. Repeated cycles on a small pool add avoidable `AllocatorExhausted` pressure. The code comment asserts the opposite, which misleads maintainers.

**Contract:** The function's own doc at `coordinator/mod.rs:819-823` says: "the holder retirement inside `stop_inner` still frees worker-held bits on the SAME allocators the preserved forwarding ... will reuse — no leak". The #7092/#13669 holder-retirement contract is that a joined worker's bits are cleared. The #15950 sibling `stop_preserving_forwarding` (`mod.rs:837-849`) implements it correctly.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
Observed at d1ea69f9aa. `coordinator/mod.rs:851-854` `let preserved_forwarding = std::mem::take(&mut self.forwarding); ... self.stop_inner(false); self.forwarding = preserved_forwarding;`. `mod.rs:1231` `self.retire_worker_holders(&holder_snapshots);` runs inside `stop_inner`. `status.rs:1611-1628` spends the one-shot `holders_retired` CAS, then walks `self.forwarding.iface_nat_allocators/source_nat_rules/nat64`, which are defaults at that instant. `nat/allocator/mod.rs:3674-3700` `retire_worker` clears the worker's bit on every live flow.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `va71_01_*` cells call the real `stop_for_link_cycle` / `stop_preserving_forwarding` against a real `InterfaceNatAllocators` allocator. Production residue sizing is STATIC.

## #16550 — NAT64 `match source-address-name` strict gate checks only existence: an IPv4-only address-book entry or set commits clean and ships a never-match NAT64 scope, while the same prefix as a literal is rejected [OPEN]

## Summary

NAT64 `match source-address-name` strict gate checks only existence: an IPv4-only address-book entry or set commits clean and ships a never-match NAT64 scope, while the same prefix as a literal is rejected

**Finding ID:** `R3-A04-01`
**Severity (source report):** Low — fail-closed. The rule-set never translates, or traffic falls through to a later rule-set with the same /96. It needs an operator mistake, and there is no enforcement widening.
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (strict gates that admit a never-match scope) — the sibling literal arm rejects the same input. The defect is real but fail-closed.

## Mechanism

`address v4 10.0.0.0/8` + `nat64 rule-set rs1 match source-address-name v4` -> validateNAT64ScopeStrict (the name is defined, so OK) -> buildNAT64Snapshots resolves [10.0.0.0/8] unpoisoned -> wire constrained with no v6 prefix -> Rust prefix_scope_matches is false -> the rule-set never matches.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:3317-3323 (literal arm `if !pfx.Addr().Is6()` -> "is not IPv6; NAT64 sources are IPv6 (#15678)"); :3325-3351 (name arm: `ab.Addresses[n]` / `ab.AddressSets[n]` existence only). pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat64.go:218-238 resolves names through appendNATAddressNamesPoisoned and keeps the IPv4 prefix. userspace-dp/src/nat64/state.rs:1035-1056 keeps `source_constrained` and parses only Ipv6Net/Ipv6Addr; :1428-1462 then returns false for every source. :1466-1480 is first-match in config order.

## Impact

An operator scoping NAT64 by a book object gets a green commit and an inert rule-set. Subscribers either fall through to another rule-set's pool or get no NAT64, and no commit or apply surface flags it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In the name arm, resolve the closure with the builder's expander and reject when it yields no IPv6 prefix, while a mixed v4+v6 set still commits. The tolerant path should warn. Acceptance: `PROBE name v4` and `PROBE set all-v4` reject, and `CONTROL mixed set` still commits.

## Contract (where cited)

`validateNAT64ScopeStrict` (#15678) rejects a literal non-IPv6 source because "NAT64 sources are IPv6". A name that resolves only to IPv4 has the same never-match consequence and should get the same verdict.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A04-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A04-01 | Low | NAT64 match source-address-name strict gate checks only existence: an IPv4-only… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:32: - **R3-A04-01 — COHORT (Low).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:3317-3345` rejects literal IPv4 NAT64 source selectors but checks *only existence* of `source-address-name` (`:3346-3372`); all-v4 book values can pass strict commit, while `userspace-dp/src/nat64/state.rs:1037-1065,1443-1470` contains no matching IPv6 prefix. **Refutation:** the match is fail-closed; `any4` is deliberately never-match (#15930), and a mixed-family book with IPv6 entries is useful. **Decisive check:** resolve concrete named book/set members and distinguish all-v4 from mixed; strict-reject only the all-incompatible case, preserving intentional wildcard semantics.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L109: ### R3-A04-01 — NAT64 `source-address-name` gate existence-only; IPv4-only book commits never-match — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: `compiler_validate_strict_nat.go` @origin/master: literal arm rejects `!Is6()` (#15678, re-read ~:3345ff); name arm (~:3355ff) checks `ab.Addresses[n]`/sets existence only. IPv4-only name/set → wire `SourceConstrained=true [10.0.0.0/8]` → Rust nat64/state.rs parses only Ipv6Net/Ipv6Addr (`:1054ff`) → never matches, possible fall-through to later rule-set. Fail-closed. - Refutation: Operator error; no widening; `any4` admission is deliberate #15930 (verifier correctly narrowed it out, pinned by test). Mixed set commits correctly — gate should reject only zero-v6 closure. - Evidence: Both arms re-read at origin/master; Rust v6-only parse confirmed. Report executed strict + wire probes with controls. - Unresolved: Cargo-level `prefix_scope_matches` run (static read strong; execution closes it). ### R3-A04-02 — reserved `zone-local/<zone>/<name>` usable as match token cross-zone — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: Reserved-prefix checks cover entry/book NAMES only; post-fold global book contains synthetic `zone-local/trust/web` keys and match-token gates look up there → untrust→dmz policy binds trust's zone-local entry, commits, snapshot armed (SourceBookIDs set), display strips prefix (shows nonexistent `web`). Scoping contract advisory-only. - Refutation (strong): Operator must spell internal key; operator already has full config authority and could author

## #16551 — Junos AS-path translator: `<AS>{0}` / `{0,0}` on an unwrapped multi-digit AS binds to its last digit, and `B{m}` on a nullable group demands a separator for an empty copy [OPEN]

## Summary
Junos AS-path translator: `<AS>{0}` / `{0,0}` on an unwrapped multi-digit AS binds to its last digit, and `B{m}` on a nullable group demands a separator for an empty copy

**Finding ID:** R3-N08-03
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — a `from as-path` term matches a path set different from the Junos meaning, which affects BGP route acceptance, but only for unusual hand-written shapes (zero-count intervals, intervals on nullable groups). The common shapes are sound [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A reject or accept term written with these shapes matches the wrong routes (an unrelated AS such as 6500 for shape a). The population is narrow.

**Contract:** pkg/config/aspath_junos_translate.go:13-25 and :39-43: Junos matches whole AS numbers, and repetition repeats the term, never its digits.

**Trace:** `policy-options as-path N "<re>"` -> ValidJunosASPathRegex (strict gate) -> TranslateJunosASPathRegex -> pkg/frr/policy_render.go -> `bgp as-path access-list` -> bgpd regexec.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
aspath_junos_translate.go:297-300 (`wrapped := base`, wrapped only when the base contains a space or an unparenthesized `|`); :309 `case exact && lo == 0: return wrapped + "{0}"`; :317 `case lo == 0 && hi == 0`; :313 `%s( %s){%d}` regardless of baseNullable.

**Probe:** `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestVN08ASPath -v` (RUN/verify/vn08/probes/zz_vn08_aspath_test.go -> aspath.out). The three MISMATCH rows:

## Acceptance / fix direction
Always group a multi-character base before attaching a quantifier, or emit an explicit empty fragment for {0}. For a nullable base, fold the separator into each optional copy. Acceptance: the three mismatch rows match the Junos column, the controls are unchanged, and the reporter's differential oracle reports 0 mismatches on the full grammar.

- **Finding ID:** R3-N08-03

- **Confidence:** High — targeted cases EXECUTED with Go POSIX regexp, which has the same match semantics as FRR's ERE for a boolean match. FRR itself was not run.

## Summary
`show security address-book` (local CLI, gRPC ShowText, REST show-text) renders only `Address.Value`, so every #15673 `dns-name` / `range-address` / `wildcard-address` entry prints a blank value and a resolved and an unresolved (match-none) dns-name are byte-identical

**Severity (source):** Medium — demonstrated on all three surfaces: the operator's only operational view of address objects shows nothing for every entry using the three forms #15673 made enforceable, and cannot show what a dns-name currently resolves to or that it resolves to nothing (a deny policy referencing it then denies nothing). Enforcement itself is unchanged and the output is blank rather than a false value, so not High. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
After a DNS outage or a changed answer, the first diagnostic an operator runs shows blank lines for exactly the entries in question; a deny policy that silently stopped matching cannot be detected from the address view. Range and wildcard entries cannot be audited either.

**Contract:** pkg/config/types_security.go:1889-1891 — "Value itself remains available to show surfaces so they can render what the operator configured"; for these forms Value is empty by design (address_forms_15673.go:282-318), so the surfaces render nothing of what was configured. address_forms_15673.go:22-26 — an unresolvable dns-name "yields no usable prefixes (match-none, fail-closed)", a state the operator needs to see.

**Trace:** `set security address-book global address up dns-name up.example.com` → compiler applyDNSName sets DNSName, Value "" → daemon refresher fills DNSAddresses → policy/NAT resolvers enforce UsableValues → `show security address-book` on any surface prints the name with an empty value column, identical whether the name resolved or not.

pkg/cli/cli_show_security_objects.go:47 `fmt.Printf("  %-24s %s\n", addr.Name, addr.Value)` and :83 (set-member detail); pkg/grpcapi/server_show_security_text.go:1317 `fmt.Fprintf(buf, "  %-20s %s\n", name, addr.Value)`; pkg/api/show_text.go:352 same shape. types_security.go:1868-1882 DNSName/DNSFamily/DNSAddresses/ExpandedPrefixes/OversizedRange, all `json:"-"`. `grep -rn 'DNSAddresses\|\.DNSName\b\|ExpandedPrefixes\|UsableValues()' pkg cmd` outside pkg/config: only pkg/daemon/daemon_dnsaddr.go (refresher) and pkg/dataplane/userspace (resolvers) — no surface. pkg/cmdtree/tree.go:810 offers only "address-book" (no dns-cache style view). d42b0cc035 (#15673) is an ancestor of HEAD.

**Probe:** REST: `go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestB18AddressBookShowForms -v` (RUN/workers/b18/evidence/api_zz_b18_probe_test.go) → `h1 10.0.0.1/32`, `rng`, `wc`, `up`, `down` blank, while UsableValues are rng=[192.0.2.1/32 192.0.2.2/32 192.0.2.3/32], up=[198.51.100.10/32], down=[]. Local CLI: `go test ./pkg/cli/ -run TestVB18CLIAddressBookForms -v` (RUN/verify/vb18/probes/cli_zz_vb18_addrbook_probe_test.go) → "rng", "up", "down" blank in the listing and "up"/"down" blank in the `s1` member detail. gRPC: `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run TestVB18GRPCAddressBookForms -v` (RUN/verify/vb18/probes/grpcapi_zz_vb18_addrbook_probe_test.go) → "up"/"down" blank. Positive control h1 renders its prefix on every surface.

## Acceptance / fix direction
One shared renderer used by all three surfaces that prints the authored form (`dns-name X [ipv4-only]`, `range-address A to B`, `wildcard-address W`) plus the enforced set from UsableValues(), and an explicit "unresolved — matches nothing" / "NOT ENFORCED: <taint>" marker when empty. - **Title:** `show security address-book` (local CLI, gRPC ShowText, REST show-text) renders only `Address.Value`, so every #15673 `dns-name` / `range-address` / `wildcard-address` entry prints a blank value and a resolved and an unresolved (match-none) dns-name are byte-identical
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b18 (A10 show-output engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb18
- **Severity:** Medium — demonstrated on all three surfaces: the operator's only operational view of address objects shows nothing for every entry using the three forms #15673 made enforceable, and cannot show what a dns-name currently resolves to or that it resolves to nothing (a deny policy referencing it then denies nothing). Enforcement itself is unchanged and the output is blank rather than a false value, so not High. [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High — executed on the local CLI, gRPC and REST renderers with a positive control; the census of readers is a grep over the surface packages.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — REST via the worker's configstore-backed probe (re-run), local CLI via a strict commit through configstore, gRPC ShowText via the server renderer; all with a stub DNS resolver.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — an operator contract failure on a security-object audit surface for a supported, recently enabled feature, reachable by any strict commit.
- **Contract:** pkg/config/types_security.go:1889-1891 — "Value itself remains available to show surfaces so they can render what the operator configured"; for these forms Value is empty by design (address_forms_15673.go:282-318), so the surfaces render nothing of what was configured. address_forms_15673.go:22-26 — an unresolvable dns-name "yields no usable prefixes (match-none, fail-closed)", a state the operator needs to see.
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection is the operator's ability to audit what a policy object matches. For dns-name entries that is controlled by an external party (the FQDN's DNS operator) and changes at runtime via the daemon refresher, so a DNS outage or answer change silently changes enforcement. The challenged assumption is that #15673 threaded its new state to every consumer; it threaded the resolvers but not the show renderers.
- **Evidence:** pkg/cli/cli_show_security_objects.go:47 `fmt.Printf("  %-24s %s\n", addr.Name, addr.Value)` and :83 (set-member detail); pkg/grpcapi/server_show_security_text.go:1317 `fmt.Fprintf(buf, "  %-20s %s\n", name, addr.Value)`; pkg/api/show_text.go:352 same shape. types_security.go:1868-1882 DNSName/DNSFamily/DNSAddresses/ExpandedPrefixes/OversizedRange, all `json:"-"`. `grep -rn 'DNSAddresses\|\.DNSName\b\|ExpandedPrefixes\|UsableValues()' pkg cmd` outside pkg/config: only pkg/daemon/daemon_dnsaddr.go (refresher) and pkg/dataplane/userspace (resolvers) — no surface. pkg/cmdtree/tree.go:810 offers only "address-book" (no dns-cache style view). d42b0cc035 (#15673) is an ancestor of HEAD.
- **Probe:** REST: `go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestB18AddressBookShowForms -v` (RUN/workers/b18/evidence/api_zz_b18_probe_test.go) → `h1 10.0.0.1/32`, `rng`, `wc`, `up`, `down` blank, while UsableValues are rng=[192.0.2.1/32 192.0.2.2/32 192.0.2.3/32], up=[198.51.100.10/32], down=[]. Local CLI: `go test ./pkg/cli/ -run TestVB18CLIAddressBookForms -v` (RUN/verify/vb18/probes/cli_zz_vb18_addrbook_probe_test.go) → "rng", "up", "down" blank in the listing and "up"/"down" blank in the `s1` member detail. gRPC: `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run TestVB18GRPCAddressBookForms -v` (RUN/verify/vb18/probes/grpcapi_zz_vb18_addrbook_probe_test.go) → "up"/"down" blank. Positive control h1 renders its prefix on every surface.
- **Trace:** `set security address-book global address up dns-name up.example.com` → compiler applyDNSName sets DNSName, Value "" → daemon refresher fills DNSAddresses → policy/NAT resolvers enforce UsableValues → `show security address-book` on any surface prints the name with an empty value column, identical whether the name resolved or not.
- **Refutation attempt:** Looked for an alternate surface: `show configuration` shows the authored FQDN but not the answer; the commit-time unresolved warning (compiler_validate_warn.go:394-399) fires once and is not re-evaluated by the refresher; no cmdtree command reads DNSAddresses. Checked that the forms are committable under strict commit (the CLI probe commits strictly). The reporter's Junos-parity remark is not relied on; the product's own types_security.go contract is. ## #16553 — R3-A39-01: The client never reads server T1/T2 (IA_NA, IA_PD, or DHCPv4 options 58/59). `renewalTimers` is always 50%/87.5% of a single lease time, which is the IA_NA valid… [OPEN]

## Summary

The client never reads server T1/T2 (IA_NA, IA_PD, or DHCPv4 options 58/59). `renewalTimers` is always 50%/87.5% of a single lease time, which is the IA_NA valid lifetime whenever an IA_NA is held. A delegated prefix whose valid lifetime ends before that T1 lapses, is pruned and is withdrawn from LAN RA. It is only re-requested at the IA_NA T1, and this repeats every cycle.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — this is a recurring, attacker-free loss of the delegated LAN IPv6 prefix. Downstream SLAAC hosts lose the PIO for up to (IA_NA valid/2 − PD valid) per cycle. The client also ignores any server that uses a short T1 to drive renewal or renumbering. It is bounded because it needs a lifetime shape where PD valid < IA_NA T1, or a server T1 well below 50% of valid, and IPv4/IA_NA keep working. Demonstrated at component scope. The end-to-end RA withdrawal is inferred from the prune path that #14598 deliberately feeds into RA.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A39-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va39.md` (finding `R3-A39-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/dhcp/commit.go:74-85` `t1 = leaseTime / 2; t2Remaining = leaseTime / 8 * 3` is the sole schedule. `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6.go:1259-1264` `lease.LeaseTime = validLT` with the comment "#14598: IA_NA present — LeaseTime stays the IA_NA lifetime for T1/T2. PD expiry is tracked per-prefix ... not by shortening this lease". `dhcpv6.go:284` `renewalTimers(committed.LeaseTime)`. `dhcpv6.go:330-345` `case waitOutcomePDExpired: continue t1WaitLoop` prunes and keeps waiting for the IA_NA T1. `dhcpv4.go:653-654` takes option 51 only. A grep of non-test `pkg/dhcp` for `.T1`, `.T2`, `OptionRenewTimeValue` and `OptionRebindingTimeValue` returns nothing.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** RFC 8415 §18.2.4 (text checked): "the client MUST select T1 and T2 times from all IA options that will guarantee that the client initiates transmissions of Renew/Rebind messages not later than at the T1/T2 times associated with any of the client's bindings (earliest T1/T2)". RFC 2131 §4.4.5: T1/T2 "are configurable by the server through options", and the 0.5/0.875 values are only defaults. `pkg/dhcp/README.md:116-123` claims the renewal timer contract is RFC 2131 §4.4.5 / RFC 8415 §18.2.4.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — an RFC 8415 §18.2.4 MUST is violated, with a reachable, recurring consequence (LAN prefix withdrawal), and #14598's fix predicate does not cover it.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `runDHCPv6` ran through the exchange seam for a defect cell and a control cell, and `parseV6ReplyChecked` + `renewalTimers` ran on a Reply carrying T1=60s. The FRR/RA consumer chain is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High — the code behaviour is EXECUTED with a positive control, and the absence of any T1/T2 read was established by grep plus reading both timer inputs. Medium on how often real servers issue the triggering lifetime shape.

## Impact

Any deployment whose server grants IA_PD a shorter lifetime than half the IA_NA lifetime gets a recurring LAN-wide IPv6 outage for SLAAC hosts. It lasts hours per cycle on day-scale leases and recovers on its own at each T1, only to repeat.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Carry the server T1/T2 per IA on the lease. Schedule Renew at the earliest non-zero T1 across held IA_NA and IA_PD (and T2 likewise), falling back to 0.5/0.875 of the shortest held valid lifetime when T1/T2 are 0. Never schedule later than the earliest PD's T1. Use v4 options 58/59 when present. Acceptance: in the defect cell the Renew goes out before 1s and the PD never leaves `DelegatedPrefixesForRA`, the control cell is unchanged, and a Reply with T1=60s schedules the renew at 60s.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A39-01`, part `parts/va39.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16554 — The reserved `zone-local/<zone>/<name>` key is usable as a policy, NAT, or address-set-member token: an untrust->dmz policy can bind trust's zone-local entry, and strict commit accepts it [OPEN]

## Summary

The reserved `zone-local/<zone>/<name>` key is usable as a policy, NAT, or address-set-member token: an untrust->dmz policy can bind trust's zone-local entry, and strict commit accepts it

**Finding ID:** `R3-A04-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the operator must spell an internal key. The operator already has full config authority and could write the same prefix as a global object, so no privilege is gained. The impact is that the documented zone-scoping contract is bypassed, a later edit of trust's book silently changes another zone…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (reserved internal namespace reachable from authored tokens) — real, but needs an internal spelling and has no enforcement loss beyond what the operator could author openly.

## Mechanism

trust zone-local `web` -> the fold mints global `zone-local/trust/web` -> the untrust->dmz policy token is not rewritten (not in untrust's or dmz's book) -> the #2008 gate finds it in the global book -> commit OK -> the snapshot arms a trust-scoped object on an untrust->dmz rule -> show surfaces print `web`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:1159-1215 checkEntryName and the book-name check cover entry and book names only. Every other `zoneLocalNamePrefix` use (compiler_validate_strict_addrbook.go:308,:381; address_unimplemented_forms_9524.go:50) skips synthetic entries and never inspects tokens. policyMatchNamedAddressRefs (compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:44-60) builds the accepted-name set from the post-fold global book. DisplayAddressName (compiler_security_addressbook.go:133-138) strips the prefix for display.

## Impact

Zone-local books exist to scope object visibility per zone. This back door makes that scoping advisory and makes inventory displays name an object absent from the rule's zones, which misleads audits. The blast radius is limited to configs that spell the key.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Reject at strict commit any authored policy, global-policy, NAT, NAT64 or address-set-member token beginning with `zone-local/`, checked on the pristine tree before the fold. The tolerant path should warn and poison. Acceptance: both PROBE rows and a04's global and SNAT rows reject, and the own-zone authored-name control still commits and rewrites.

## Contract (where cited)

The resolveZoneLocalAddressBooks doc (pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go, the fold) says "A name present only in zone A's book is therefore invisible to a policy in zone B". validateAddressBookEntryNamesStrict (compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:1127-1160) says the `zone-local/` namespace "is reserved for the internal zone-local address book".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A04-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A04-02 | Low | The reserved zone-local/<zone>/<name> key is usable as a policy, NAT, or address-set-member… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:33: - **R3-A04-02 — COHORT (Low; namespace ambiguity).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go:464-480` rewrites a policy token to `zone-local/<zone>/<name>` whenever that local name exists; `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:1159-1215` reserves the prefix as a *definition* name but not as a reference, so another zone can explicitly name the synthetic global key. **Refutation:** only an authorized config author can write the cross-zone token, and zones do not thereby bypass an authority boundary; the ambiguity is namespace isolation/audit predictability, not attacker control of the parser. **Decisive check:** assert that a policy/NAT/set reference literally naming a folded internal key cannot access a different zone's entry, while generated compiler references continue to work.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L115: ### R3-A04-02 — reserved `zone-local/<zone>/<name>` usable as match token cross-zone — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: Reserved-prefix checks cover entry/book NAMES only; post-fold global book contains synthetic `zone-local/trust/web` keys and match-token gates look up there → untrust→dmz policy binds trust's zone-local entry, commits, snapshot armed (SourceBookIDs set), display strips prefix (shows nonexistent `web`). Scoping contract advisory-only. - Refutation (strong): Operator must spell internal key; operator already has full config authority and could author same prefix globally — no privilege/enforcement gain beyond authored intent. Real harm is audit/display misleading + edit-coupling. Correctly COHORT Low, not a security bypass. - Evidence: Gate asymmetry in report re-reads; `resolveZoneLocalAddressBooks`/`localDefines:477` at origin/master consistent. Report executed commit+snapshot, own-zone control rewrites correctly, undefined synthetic rejected (proves lookup). - Unresolved: Whether any non-operator surface (API/generator) can inject token without config authority — would raise severity; none found. ### R3-A04-03 — zone IDs 16-bit name hash; collisions hard-reject valid zone pairs — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: `pkg/config/zoneid.go:38-43` @origin/master FNV xor-fold to [1,65533]; collision = strict reject ("rename one zone"). Undocumented; birthday ~12%@128, ~39%@256 zones. - Refutation: Deliberate design (u16 on event-stream wire, pure function of name for HA deter

**Wonder:** wonder batch00 L30: | R3-A04-01 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A04-02 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A04-03 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A04-05 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A05-06 | MATERIAL | MATERIAL | High (potential, conditional) | High (mechanism) / Medium (prevalence) | STATIC |

## #16555 — #13951 residual: a config apply (and a rebind or arm rebuilt from the stored snapshot) installs the kernel's spoof-updated neighbor MAC as the static next-hop binding that the mirror fence refused, and the fence then ... [OPEN]

## Summary
#13951 residual: a config apply (and a rebind or arm rebuilt from the stored snapshot) installs the kernel's spoof-updated neighbor MAC as the static next-hop binding that the mirror fence refused, and the fence then defends the laundered MAC

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium (potential High) — the #10704/#13660/#13951 anti-spoof protection for transit next hops is lost at the next config apply. An on-link attacker's MAC becomes the static binding for every transit flow routed through that neighbor, typically the default gateway, which gives interception or a blackhole. Once laundered, the genuine MAC pushed by the mirror is refused. The component behaviour is demonstrated. The end-to-end attack timing is not, so High stays potential. [reporter: Medium (potential High)]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A71-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va71.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Any cluster or standalone node with an untrusted host on a transit L2 segment is exposed. The blast radius is every transit flow via the poisoned next hop, typically all egress through the default gateway. The window lasts from the first apply after poisoning until the kernel row reverts AND a fresh dynamic learn re-confirms G. A persistent spoofer keeps it poisoned. An ordinary operator commit during an attack completes it.

**Contract:** `docs/log/13951.md` says "The helper now treats a Go snapshot as a mirror, not independent evidence. It accepts a differing MAC only when the kernel row is NUD_PERMANENT or the monitor already has the same MAC in the dynamic cache", and notes that "static entries win lookup". The doc on `coordinator/mod.rs:983-985` says: "Apply a Go neighbor mirror without letting an unconfirmed kernel MAC change replace a live binding."

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
All observed at d1ea69f9aa. The fence exists only in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/mod.rs:1015-1033`, which keeps `prior_static` when `dynamic != Some(*entry) && prior.is_some_and(|prior| prior.mac != entry.mac)`. `forwarding_build/fib.rs:1056-1104` `populate_neighbors` runs `state.neighbors.insert((neigh.ifindex, ip), NeighborEntry { mac })` for every usable row, with no comparison against the previous generation. It is called from `forwarding_build/mod.rs:648` for every build, including the same-plan refresh at `coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:303` (`previous = Some(&self.forwarding)` is not consulted for neighbors). `forwarding/tunnel.rs:143-145` returns the static entry before consulting the dynamic map. `snapshot_refresh.rs:362-364` `bulk_replace_neighbors(&old_manager_keys, &[])` deletes the monitor's dynamic copy. `server/handlers/neighbors.rs:102-105` stores the raw request rows (`snapshot.neighbors = neighbors.to_vec()`), not the fenced `accepted` set, into the snapshot that `rebind` (`server/handlers/rebind.rs:70` `reconcile_status_bindings`) rebuilds from. On the Go side, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:268` `Neighbors: buildNeighborSnapshots(cfg)` reads `netlink.NeighList` (`neighbors.go:145-215`). The rebind/Go legs are inferred from the source; the refresh leg is observed.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `va71_02_snapshot_apply_launders_refused_mac` drives the real `Coordinator::refresh_runtime_snapshot`, `apply_manager_neighbors` and `lookup_neighbor_entry`. The Go-side publication and the rebind/arm rebuild-from-stored-snapshot legs are STATIC.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-smr-batch07.md`: | R3-A71-03 wire-owner roster latch never resets, O(table) removal | MATERIAL | High (potential) |
| R3-A71-01 stop_for_link_cycle mem::take defeats holder retirement | COHORT | Low |
| R3-A71-04 alias published during saturation never recorded | COHORT (w/ A71-03) | Low |
| R3-A72-01 telemetry kind budget held to 100ms ACK, 820 burst shed | MATERIAL | Medium |

| R3-A72-03 event-stream README SESSION_CREATE contract stale | COHORT | Low |
| R3-A73-02 unpaged idle-lease export >64MiB cap, standby gets none | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A73-01 drain_session_deltas write-fail loses batch, no latch | COHORT (w/ #15217) | Low |
| R3-A74-01 FragAssoc 32/session quota, no completion release, ~16/s cap | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A74-02 OverlapTracker abandoned entries count 30s vs sender quota | MATERIAL | Medium |

Timing window (apply while poisoned) is routine-commit frequent. Potential-High upgrade needs e2e attack timing; Medium (potential High) agreed.

## #16556 — On a tolerant load an interface claimed by two security zones is removed from the runtime interface→zone map and left without an XDP shim (#3072 fail-closed), but `show security zones` (local CLI, gRPC GetZones/ShowText) lists it as... [OPEN]

## Summary
On a tolerant load an interface claimed by two security zones is removed from the runtime interface→zone map and left without an XDP shim (#3072 fail-closed), but `show security zones` (local CLI, gRPC GetZones/ShowText) lists it as bound under BOTH zones, `show interfaces` prints a map-order-chosen "Security: Zone:", and no operational surface names it

**Finding ID:** R3-B18-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — the interface's transit and zone admission fail closed (a full outage of that interface) while every operator surface reports it bound and healthy. Reachable only on lenient compile paths (boot from a hand-edited or legacy stored config, HA peer-sync from a mixed-version peer); strict commit rejects (#3072). Fail-closed direction, so not High. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
After a lenient boot or peer-sync the operator sees the interface "in trust" and debugs policy, while every packet on it is dropped; the one place the truth appears is a load-time journal line. Recovery is easy once known (remove one claim and commit), but finding it is not.

**Contract:** pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_zones.go:376-378 — "On tolerant load / peer-sync paths the same key set is quarantined: neither zone claims that interface in the runtime map, so it matches no zone policy and fails closed." pkg/showaudit/doc.go:1-3 — an object the builder refuses to install must not be rendered as enforced. docs/engineering-style.md "A fail-closed exclusion owes a show-surface annotation (#6534)".

**Trace:** stored config (or peer-sync) lists ge-0/0/0.0 under trust and untrust → CompileConfigLenient downgrades the #3072 error to cfg.Warnings → QuarantinedZoneInterfaceKeys={ge-0/0/0.0} → runtime zone map omits it and programZoneMaps attaches no shim → #10302 forward-hook fence admits only runtime-owned XDP links, so transit through it is dropped → `show security zones` lists it under both zones, `show interfaces` names one at random, `show system alarms` (built from ValidateConfig + tolerated-leaf/stanza warnings) is silent.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:92 `conflictedInterfaces := config.QuarantinedZoneInterfaceKeys(cfg)` and :108-111 `if _, conflicted := conflictedInterfaces[key]; conflicted { continue }`; same omission in config.InterfaceZoneMap (host_inbound_effective_view.go:153). pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:885 and ~:940-952 skip mapZoneInterface and record `UnarmedSurface{Reason: "zone interface ... quarantined by duplicate membership"}` with StillForwarding=false (CoverageSkipped, so the #7191 arm gate does not disarm). pkg/cli/cli_show_security_zones.go:86 `Interfaces bound: %d` of len(zone.Interfaces) and :92-94 raw list; pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go:39 `Interfaces: zone.Interfaces`; pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces.go:126-133 ranges the zones map and overwrites ifaceZoneName per member (last writer wins in random order). QuarantinedZoneInterfaceKeys has no caller in pkg/cli, pkg/grpcapi, pkg/api or cmd/cli. pkg/showaudit/surface_gate_6534_test.go:251 dropPredicateName `(?:Excluded|Unusable|Disarmed)Reason$|Exclusions$|Unsupported$|Undefined$` does not match `...Keys`.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cli/ -run TestB18ConflictedZoneInterfaceShownBound -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/b18/evidence/cli_zz_b18_zone_conflict_probe_test.go, re-run by vb18): control-single-zone `runtimeZone[ge-0/0/0.0]="trust"`; conflict-two-zones `quarantinedKeys=map[ge-0/0/0.0:{}] runtimeZone[ge-0/0/0.0]="" compileWarn=true alarmMentionsIface=false`, trust "Interfaces bound: 1 / ge-0/0/0.0", untrust "Interfaces bound: 2 / ge-0/0/1.0 ge-0/0/0.0" → DEFECT. The control proves the probe distinguishes bound from quarantined. Limit: the packet-level outage is not executed.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Add a shared per-interface verdict (e.g. config.ZoneInterfaceQuarantineReason(cfg, zone, ref)) used by the CLI/gRPC zone renderers, GetZones and `show interfaces`; annotate the member `[UNBOUND — claimed by zones X and Y]` and exclude it from "Interfaces bound"; surface the downgraded warning in `show system alarms`; register the predicate in the #6534 "security zone" family or widen dropPredicateName; fix the stale comment. Acceptance: the probe's conflict row carries the annotation and "Interfaces bound: 1" for untrust, the control is unchanged, and TestEveryBuilderDropPredicateIsRegistered6534 reds if the predicate is unregistered.

## Full validated claim

## #16557 — Zone ids are a 16-bit hash of the zone name and any collision is a hard strict reject, so pairs like vlan163+vlan364 or zone109+zone237 cannot be committed, and the chance of a collision grows quickly with zone count [OPEN]

## Summary

Zone ids are a 16-bit hash of the zone name and any collision is a hard strict reject, so pairs like vlan163+vlan364 or zone109+zone237 cannot be committed, and the chance of a collision grows quickly with zone count

**Finding ID:** `R3-A04-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the commit fails closed with an explicit remedy (rename one zone), and there is no runtime enforcement loss. The tolerant quarantine is reachable only for a config that was never strictly committed. The consequence is a capacity and parity limit: about 12% collision probability at 128 zones an…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (commit-time capacity/admission limits that refuse valid configs) — a real, undocumented limit with a cheap per-instance workaround.

## Mechanism

two security-zone names -> collectZoneNamesAST -> StableZoneID equal -> validateZoneIDCollisionAST strict error -> commit refused.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/zoneid.go:38-44 `folded := uint16(s) ^ uint16(s>>16) ^ uint16(s>>32) ^ uint16(s>>48); return folded%(ZoneIDReservedMin-1) + 1`. :216-241 returns `"zone id collision between %q and %q (both fold to %d) — rename one zone (#3075)"` at strict (quarantine on the lenient path). :18-35 explains that the id must be a pure function of the name and is u16 on the event-stream wire. That is a deliberate design.

## Impact

Multi-tenant or zone-per-VLAN layouts and migrated configs hit a refusal unrelated to anything the operator did wrong, and at a few hundred zones the probability is significant.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Widen the zone-id carrier (u32) or resolve collisions deterministically, and at minimum document the limit in docs/config-schema.md. Acceptance: the three probe pairs commit, with ids stable across nodes and across unrelated zone add/remove.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos accepts any distinct security-zone names. xpf's operator docs (README, docs/config-schema.md) state no zone-name restriction beyond reserved names and `/`. validateZoneCountStrict states the cap as 65533 zones, and its own comment concedes the collision gate fires much sooner.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A04-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A04-03 | Low | Zone ids are a 16-bit hash of the zone name and any collision is a hard strict reject, so… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:34: - **R3-A04-03 — COHORT (Low; deliberate capacity tradeoff).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/zoneid.go:38-44,217-240` hashes names into a 16-bit zone ID and rejects collisions. Two individually valid zone names may fail together, with birthday exposure rising as zone count grows; the report's colliding pair is consistent with this admission gate. **Refutation:** rejection is fail-closed and explicitly protects stable session identities; random-collision probability is a model, not a measured field failure, and renaming one zone resolves it. **Decisive check:** validate supported zone counts and backward-compatible zone-ID/session migration before demanding a wider namespace.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L121: ### R3-A04-03 — zone IDs 16-bit name hash; collisions hard-reject valid zone pairs — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: `pkg/config/zoneid.go:38-43` @origin/master FNV xor-fold to [1,65533]; collision = strict reject ("rename one zone"). Undocumented; birthday ~12%@128, ~39%@256 zones. - Refutation: Deliberate design (u16 on event-stream wire, pure function of name for HA determinism #3075); fail-closed with explicit cheap remedy; no runtime loss. Design-limit, not hidden bug — COHORT is ceiling; a NEG-as-designed reading is defensible except undocumented admission refusal of valid configs keeps COHORT. - Evidence: [SMR-run] `StableZoneID("vlan163")==StableZoneID("vlan364")==51948`, `zone109==zone237==9074` at origin/master — report pairs reproduced exactly. - Unresolved: Wire-width change cost (u16 event-stream) — fix feasibility; tunnel-id sibling unexecuted. ### R3-A04-05 — address-book `range-address` reuses NAT-pool 256-host cap — **COHORT (Low, documented)** - Defect: `address_forms_15673.go:285ff applyRangeAddress → expandAddressRange`; `compiler_nat_helpers.go` expander caps 256 hosts per-IP (NAT occupancy bound #8814) → >256 range strict-rejected even unreferenced, while equal CIDR commits. ## Summary
Juniper's VRRP spelling (bare `virtual-address` / `virtual-inet6-address`) is strict-rejected even via flat `set` while the tolerant compile normalizes the same text, and `vrrp-inet6-group`'s `virtual-link-local-address` / `inet6-advertise-interval` are refused

**Severity (source):** Low — Low — fails closed at commit with no runtime loss. The cost is migration parity, plus a strict and tolerant disagreement over identical text (a tolerant peer normalizes what the strict primary refuses) [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

Every migrated Junos VRRP stanza needs hand-editing, and an IPv6 group cannot carry its Junos advertisement timer.

**Contract:** Junos accepts a bare VRRP virtual address. #15199 (A05-07) acceptance: "the Junos spelling compiles to the same VRRPGroup".

**Trace:** flat set -> SetPath -> compileInterfaces VRRPGroups -> tail gate validateVRRPVIPPrefixStrict (strict reject) or normalizeBareVRRPVIPs (tolerant) -> pkg/vrrp netlink.ParseAddr.

Apply normalizeBareVRRPVIPs on the strict path and reject only a bare VIP with no same-family enclosing prefix. Map inet6-advertise-interval and accept or name-refuse virtual-link-local-address. Fix the gate comment. Acceptance: the Juniper example commits to the same VRRPGroup as the CIDR form.

## #16559 — R3-A39-02: While host-inbound gap debt is owed, a content-identical renewal calls `onDHCPUnchangedLease` → `applyActiveConfig` inline on the client goroutine, which blocks… [OPEN]

## Summary

While host-inbound gap debt is owed, a content-identical renewal calls `onDHCPUnchangedLease` → `applyActiveConfig` inline on the client goroutine, which blocks uncancellably on `applySem`. An apply that holds applySem and reaches `reconcileDHCPClients`, where it removes or changes that client's stanza, then waits on `<-dc.done` forever. The same happens when the hook's own apply stops its caller. applySem never releases, and every later commit, rollback, config sync and background apply hangs until xpfd restarts.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the consequence when triggered is a permanent management-plane wedge: no commit, rollback or HA config sync, and the stopped DHCP client never renews again, so its WAN lease eventually expires. Recovery needs a daemon restart. It is not High because the trigger requires the #11497 double nft failure (debt owed) at the same time as a renewal and an apply that stops or changes that client. Demonstrated at component scope with the production hook. The full-daemon commit path was not driven.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A39-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va39.md` (finding `R3-A39-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/dhcp/commit.go:281` `m.notifyLeaseStateChanged(prev, lease, ..., true)` from `commitLease`, called by the renew/rebind arms (`dhcpv4.go:280,352`; `dhcpv6.go:389,533`) on the client goroutine. `commit.go:312-317` `onUnchangedLease := m.onUnchangedLease ... onUnchangedLease()` is inline. `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_bringup.go:182` `dm.SetUnchangedLeaseCallback(d.onDHCPUnchangedLease)`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:134-138` `if d.hostInboundGapOwed() { d.applyActiveConfig() }`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:219-220` `beginBackgroundApply(context.Background(), ...)`, and `:157` `d.applySem.Acquire(ctx, 1)` with a background ctx, so it is uncancellable. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go:185` `d.reconcileDHCPClients(cfg)` inside the apply. `pkg/dhcp/reconcile.go:137-145` `s.dc.cancel(); <-s.dc.done` with no timeout. Cancelling the client ctx does not wake a goroutine parked in `applySem.Acquire`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** applySem serializes every apply and must always be released. `pkg/dhcp/README.md` says the unchanged-lease hook fires "outside the manager lock", which only covers m.mu. The `Reconcile` doc says lease callbacks re-enter applyConfig and so must not depend on the client they call from.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable lock-cycle deadlock on the global apply semaphore, survived refutation, no owner.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — daemon-package probe using real `Daemon.onDHCPUnchangedLease`, `beginBackgroundApply`/`applySem` and `reconcileDHCPClients`. The client goroutine is modelled through `dhcp.NewManagerForTesting`. The worker's pkg/dhcp probe separately exercises the real `runDHCPv4` → `commitLease` → inline-hook path.

**Confidence:** High for the deadlock mechanics (real hook, real semaphore gate, real Reconcile, with a control). Low for production incidence.

## Impact

It strikes during an already-degraded state (host-inbound fence failure) and removes the operator's main recovery tool (commit/rollback). HA config sync to this node also stalls. The wedged client stops renewing, so the WAN lease eventually lapses as well.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Dispatch the unchanged-lease hook asynchronously, for example through the same debounced timer goroutine as `scheduleRecompile`, or have it signal the 30s reassert owner rather than applying inline. Optionally give the hook's acquire a context that client cancellation reaches. Acceptance: both va39 probe arms report `wedged=false`, the existing `commit_test.go` unchanged-lease test still passes, and the #11497 convergence test still converges.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A39-02`, part `parts/va39.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16560 — Strict commit caps each zone pair, and the whole global rulebase, at 256 expanded policy rules: the 257th trust->untrust policy is refused, because of the positional rule-ID block width [OPEN]

## Summary

Strict commit caps each zone pair, and the whole global rulebase, at 256 expanded policy rules: the 257th trust->untrust policy is refused, because of the positional rule-ID block width

**Finding ID:** `R3-A04-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — ordinary production rulebases cannot be committed. A zone pair with more than 256 rules (counted after application-set expansion) is rejected, and all global policies together share ONE 256-rule budget. The commit fails closed, so the previous config keeps running and enforcement is not los…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable trigger (the 257th policy in one zone pair, or about 9 policies each naming a 30-application set) with a concrete consequence (commit refused), far below vendor per-context scale, and documented nowhere in operator docs.

## Mechanism

N `set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy pK ...` -> compileTreeStrict -> compiler_tailgates.go:472 validatePolicyExpandedRuleCountStrict -> addSet("policy trust->untrust") -> span sum > 256 -> commit error. The mirror is walkPolicyRuleSlots at apply (pkg/dataplane/userspace), which is why #13921 moved the cap to commit.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_policy_expansion_13921.go:5-8 `const MaxPolicyRulesPerSet = 256` ("Policy rule IDs reserve one 256-ID block per zone-pair set and one for global policies"). :96-108 addSet does `if span > MaxPolicyRulesPerSet-setTotal { return fmt.Errorf("%s: expanded rules exceed MaxRulesPerPolicy (%d)", ...) }`. :112-139 runs one addSet per zone pair and ONE `addSet("global policy", globals)`. The span is the deduplicated application-set expansion (:27-55). The ID consumers are all positional `policySetID*dataplane.MaxRulesPerPolicy + uint32(i)` (pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1568, pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:144, pkg/grpcapi/server_show_policies_text.go:222, pkg/api/metrics.go:2425). That shows a layout constant, not a wire-width limit (inference: a u32 has room for a wider block).

## Impact

Any site whose trust->untrust (or any single pair) rulebase exceeds 256 rules after app-set expansion, or that consolidates onto global policies, cannot commit at all. The error names an internal constant and offers no remedy. The impact persists until the rulebase is rewritten.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Decouple per-set capacity from the 256-ID block: allocate contiguous per-set ranges, or widen the block inside the u32 space. Update every positional ID consumer (CLI/gRPC/REST/metrics/policymatch/daemon invalidation) through one helper. Keep the 65536 total bound. Document any remaining limit in docs/config-schema.md. Acceptance: the 257 and 1000-in-one-pair probes and the 257-global probe commit, and their rule IDs stay unique and stable across an unrelated policy edit and identical on both nodes.

## Contract (where cited)

The product claims Junos-style zone-based policy with Junos syntax (README, CLAUDE.md "What This Is"). Juniper's SRX4700 configuration essentials list "Policies per context: 100000" and "Policy contexts (zone pairs): 8192". The xpf README and docs/config-schema.md state no per-zone-pair or global-rulebase rule limit. docs/feature-gaps.md:1380-1420 discusses the 256 ID namespace only as an internal ID-collision guard (#3145/#3404).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A04-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A04-04 | Medium | Strict commit caps each zone pair, and the whole global rulebase, at 256 expanded policy… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:31: - **R3-A04-04 — MATERIAL (Medium product scale limit, NOT a security bypass).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_policy_expansion_13921.go:5-16,97-139` rejects the 257th expanded rule **per zone-pair or global set** even when the separate total allowance is 65,536; the report's historic 256/257 controls demonstrate the threshold. **Refutation:** this is an intentional positional 256-ID namespace (`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1568+`), not an accidental 16-bit overflow; raising it touches wire/HA session identities and linear new-flow policy evaluation. Vendor appliance 100k-rule marketing is not a same-hardware throughput guarantee, and no CPU/cache/NUMA performance figures were measured. **Decisive check:** agree on an operator-supported per-set scale and migration-safe ID layout, then test 257 rules with preserved session/HA identity and measured lookup cost, not merely a changed constant.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L103: ### R3-A04-04 — strict commit caps zone-pair & global rulebase at 256 expanded rules — **MATERIAL (Medium)** - Defect: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_policy_expansion_13921.go:8 MaxPolicyRulesPerSet=256`, `:104-105` reject; one `addSet` per zone pair + ONE for all globals. Positional ID layout (`policySetID*256+i`) is internal, u32 namespace has room; separate 65536 total bound (#11081) already caps evaluation cost. 257th policy (or ~9×30 app-sets) refused, undocumented in operator docs; fails closed (old config runs). - Refutation: Deliberate lineage (#3145/#3404/#13921 accepted 256 while fixing spill); widening touches ID consumers across CLI/gRPC/REST/metrics/HA session sync — compatibility cost unmeasured (reporter admits). ## #16561 — #15106 residual: the O(1) wire-owner roster is off whenever 16,384 or more NAT'd forward sessions with distinct wire keys are live, and its `wire_saturated` latch never resets short of a full stop, so every later NAT'... [OPEN]

## Summary
#15106 residual: the O(1) wire-owner roster is off whenever 16,384 or more NAT'd forward sessions with distinct wire keys are live, and its `wire_saturated` latch never resets short of a full stop, so every later NAT'd removal again scans the whole shared table under the global mutex (about 924x slower in the probe)

**Severity (source report):** High — High (potential) — this re-arms the exact consequence the project accepted as High and fixed in #15106: O(table) work per NAT'd close while holding the `shared_sessions` mutex that every worker's new-flow publish takes. At the component level, the measured per-removal cost at 100k rows is 21.5 µs on a fresh index vs 19.8 ms after one 16,385-session excursion (debug, loaded host). Appliance-level availability loss is not measured, so High stays potential. [reporter: High (potential)]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A71-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va71.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Nodes with large NAT tables (the case #15106 targeted) pay lock-held O(table) per close. Close rates of thousands per second at 100k rows serialize the publish path and contend new-flow setup. There is no counter for fallback-scan removals. Recovery requires a helper disarm or restart.

**Contract:** #15106 (CLOSED, fix 314f4587ff) required that NAT'd removal resolve survivors in O(1), with acceptance "the NAT ratio is at most 2x between 1k and 100k rows". #15104 (fix f5911e66c0) set the rule for the same struct at `types/mod.rs:95-97`: "saturation is a function of the LIVE population ... once removals drop it below the bound the index recovers without a helper restart."

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
Observed at d1ea69f9aa. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/mod.rs:232-249`: `if self.wire_saturated { return; } if self.saturated() { self.wire_saturated = true; return; }` and `if self.wire_owners.len() == Self::MAX_KEYS { self.wire_saturated = true; }`. `:278-280` defines `wire_owners_trusted() = !self.wire_saturated && !self.saturated()`. The only reset is `clear()` at `:216-221`, reached via `types/mod.rs:483` from `stop_inner(true)` (`coordinator/mod.rs:1346`). `shared_ops/store.rs:1113-1140`: untrusted leads to the "Legacy fallback" `sessions.values().filter(.. forward_wire_key(..) == wire_key).take(2)` while holding `shared_sessions` (`store.rs:1024`). With 0 or 1 survivors this visits every row. The reseed (`reset_wire_owners`) cannot clear the latch. The gauge `shared_wire_ambiguity_saturated` (`coordinator/status.rs:356-363`) reads `saturated()`, not the latch, so it reads 0 while the fallback persists. The #15106 cost cell (`session_glue/tests.rs:3190-3268`) gives every row `rewrite_src 203.0.113.9`/`rewrite_src_port 50_000`, which yields one wire key.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `va71_03_cell_a_*` (latch) and `va71_03_cell_b_cost_after_excursion` (cost) through the real `publish_shared_session` and `remove_shared_session_if`. The appliance-level throughput impact is NEEDS_VALIDATION (lab).

## #16562 — Local `show interfaces <if> detail|extensive` keys the zone map by `baseIfName(member)`, so a VLAN trunk whose units sit in different zones prints a map-order-random "Security zone:" (and #12899 qualifier) on the physical row — the... [OPEN]

## Summary
Local `show interfaces <if> detail|extensive` keys the zone map by `baseIfName(member)`, so a VLAN trunk whose units sit in different zones prints a map-order-random "Security zone:" (and #12899 qualifier) on the physical row — the misattribution the gRPC twin's #14364 `physicalRowZoneKey` avoids

**Finding ID:** R3-B18-05
**Severity (source):** Low — display only, no enforcement effect; the printed zone changes between consecutive runs and disagrees with the remote CLI. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator inspecting a trunk port is told it belongs to whichever zone map iteration picked, and a quarantined VLAN unit's tag appears or disappears run to run; local and remote CLI disagree.

**Contract:** pkg/grpcapi/server_show_interfaces_text.go:540-552 (#14364): a non-zero unit member "is NOT attributed to the physical row — that zone belongs to the logical unit ... claiming it here would misattribute a VLAN unit"; local and remote CLI twins are expected to agree (#4984/#5325 parity).

**Trace:** zones trust={ge-0/0/2.50}, dmz={ge-0/0/2.80} → local renderer maps both to key ge-0/0/2, last map iteration wins → physical row prints that zone and its quarantine qualifier; gRPC twin prints none.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_extensive.go:44-50 and pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_detail.go:40-46 `for _, z := range cfg.Security.Zones { ... ifZoneMap[baseIfName(ifName)] = z.Name }`, queried at extensive.go:95-100 by the physical display name; baseIfName strips any unit (cli_show_interfaces_shared.go:53-58). gRPC uses physicalRowZoneKey (server_show_interfaces_text.go:82,553-563), whose comment at :79-80 notes "the CLI twins key by baseIfName". Fix 04d772e847 (#14364) is in HEAD's history.

**Probe:** `go test -c -o /var/tmp/vb18/cli.test ./pkg/cli/` then `B18_NETNS=1 unshare -Urn sh -c 'ip link add ge-0-0-2 type dummy && ip link add ge-0-0-3 type dummy && /var/tmp/vb18/cli.test -test.run TestB18ExtensiveVLANUnitZoneMisattribution -test.v'` (RUN/workers/b18/evidence/cli_zz_b18_ifzone_probe_test.go): ge-0/0/2 (units .50 trust, .80 dmz) `map[Security zone: dmz:34 Security zone: trust:6]` over 40 runs; control ge-0/0/3 (unit 0 untrust) `map[Security zone: untrust:40]`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Move physicalRowZoneKey to pkg/config and use it in both local presenters; add a byte-equality cell against the gRPC renderer. Acceptance: no "Security zone:" on the trunk row, "untrust" on the unit-0 control, stable across runs.
