## #16580 — DHCPv4 relay rejects the Junos relay-level `active-server-group` (global default) under the #9552 closed-world gate with a misleading message, while DHCPv6 accepts and inherits the same family-level statement [OPEN]

## Summary

DHCPv4 relay rejects the Junos relay-level `active-server-group` (global default) under the #9552 closed-world gate with a misleading message, while DHCPv6 accepts and inherits the same family-level statement

**Finding ID:** `R3-A05-07`
**Severity (source report):** Low — valid Junos is refused at strict commit (fail-safe). The workaround is to repeat `active-server-group` in every v4 group. The refusal text ("it compiles to NOTHING: it commits clean ... and relays nothing") is printed as the reason for a rejection [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (Junos statement-spelling parity, fail-closed; with R3-A05-01/R3-N08-09) — v4/v6 asymmetry with a trivial workaround.

## Mechanism

`forwarding-options dhcp-relay { server-group sg { 10.0.0.5; } active-server-group sg; group rg { interface ge-0/0/1.0; } }` → #9552 child check → strict reject; the tolerant path warns and drops it.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/compiler_dhcp_relay_children_9552.go:57-66` `check` permits only the schema-declared tokens (`dhcpv6, group, server-group`) and otherwise returns the #9552 message. `DHCPRelayConfig` has no relay-level active-server-group field.

## Impact

migrated relay configs written the global way fail commit with a message that misdescribes the outcome. On a tolerant load, the global default is dropped and groups without their own server group relay nowhere. That second outcome is inferred and was not executed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

accept relay-level `active-server-group` for v4 and inherit it into groups lacking their own, mirroring the v6 compiler, with #11693 validation on the effective value. Reword the strict-path message. Acceptance: the relay-level row commits and the compiled group carries `sg`.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos relay-level `active-server-group` sets the default server group for groups that do not override it. xpf's own v6 compiler implements exactly that inheritance (`pkg/config/compiler_dhcp_relay_dhcpv6_9553.go:232-261`, docs/config-schema.md #9553 section).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A05-07` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A05-07 | Low | DHCPv4 relay rejects the Junos relay-level active-server-group (global default) under the… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:44: - **R3-A05-07 — COHORT (Low).** **Defect:** the DHCPv4 relay closed-world children list in `pkg/config/compiler_dhcp_relay_children_9552.go:44-66` omits relay-level `active-server-group`, while DHCPv6's compiler inherits it (`compiler_dhcp_relay_dhcpv6_9553.go:232-261`); a valid global-default spelling can fail v4 strict commit. **Refutation:** this is fail-closed; a group-local override exists, and no packet forwarding or lease regression follows from a config the gate refuses. **Decisive check:** one v4 relay with global default and a group override, strict check and compiled server group, against the equivalent v6 fixture.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L165: ### R3-A05-07 — DHCPv4 relay-level `active-server-group` rejected, v6 accepts/inherits — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: #9552 closed-world v4 check (`compiler_dhcp_relay_children_9552.go:57-66`) permits only schema tokens; relay-level active-server-group rejected with message describing clean-commit outcome (wrong for rejection path); v6 compiler implements same inheritance (#9553). Tolerant path drops global default → groups relay nowhere (inferred leg). - Refutation: Intentional closed world; per-group workaround trivial; fail-safe. Parity gap, correctly cohorted with A05-01/N08-09 spelling class. - Evidence: Allow-list + v6 twin in report re-reads; CheckText rows executed (v4 group OK, v4 relay reject, v6 family OK). - Unresolved: Tolerant-load drop executed proof (currently inferred). ### Part disposition A05-04 — **DUP of R3-A06-01** (same `compiler_interfaces_vlan_tagging.go:225` skip): concur, single filing unit under A06-01. ---

## #16582 — During a peer outage, any config apply (an unrelated operator commit, or the HA secondary applying synced config) brings a keepalive-down GRE tunnel back UP. The dataplane compile's zone loop (`mapZoneInterface`) brings it up, and the... [OPEN]

## Summary
During a peer outage, any config apply (an unrelated operator commit, or the HA secondary applying synced config) brings a keepalive-down GRE tunnel back UP. The dataplane compile's zone loop (`mapZoneInterface`) brings it up, and the keepalive runner never takes it down again until the peer answers. The interface therefore carries routes and FIB selection again while keepalive status still reads down.

**Finding ID:** R3-B21-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — This is a bounded loss of a failover mechanism. The GRE keepalive is the only dead-peer detector for the tunnel, and its LinkSetDown is what withdraws the tunnel's connected, static and IGP routes and removes the endpoint from the userspace FIB ECMP set. One routine commit during an outage cancels that for the rest of the outage, so traffic stays pointed at a dead peer instead of a backup path. The mechanism is demonstrated; the end-to-end route and traffic loss is inferred. Prerequisites are `keepalive` configured, a real outage, and an apply during it. Recovery is automatic when the peer returns. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators run GRE with keepalive so that a dead hub or peer is routed around, via a floating static, a backup tunnel or the IGP. On a cluster, the secondary's config-sync apply after any primary commit is enough. The blast radius is all traffic routed via that tunnel for the remainder of the outage, which is blackholed. `show interfaces` keepalive status still says down while the link is UP, which hides the cause. Recovery comes only when the peer answers again or the tunnel is recreated.

**Contract:** pkg/routing/README.md "Keepalives" says LinkSetUp "is SKIPPED when a retained runner holds the tunnel down (the down-transition in `keepaliveLoop` is gated on `state.Up`, so re-upping would strand the link admin UP)". The same README says peer death LinkSetDowns the anchor TUN so that dependent routes reconverge, which is Junos gr- interface-down semantics, and that "The Rust FIB excludes an endpoint reported down from ECMP". The tunnel manager's own comment (pkg/routing/tunnel.go:653-656) says "re-upping the link here would strand it admin UP forever while probes keep failing".

**Trace:** The peer dies. After MaxRetries dead ticks, keepaliveTick calls LinkSetDown(gr-0-0-0) and sets state.Up=false. An operator commit or a secondary config-sync apply then runs applyConfigLocked. ApplyTunnels correctly skips LinkSetUp because of skipUp. Next, applyDataplaneAndHACore runs userspace Compile, then compileZones, then mapZoneInterface(`security-zone X interfaces gr-0/0/0.0`), which calls LinkSetUp(gr-0-0-0). The kernel restores the connected route, zebra re-selects the statics and IGP via gr-, and the snapshot reports link_up=true, so the Rust FIB re-admits the endpoint. Later dead ticks see state.Up=false, so there is no down edge. The tunnel stays UP until a ProbeAlive arrives (wantUp leads to LinkSetUp and Up=true).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive_runner.go:304 `if state.Up && state.Failures >= state.MaxRetries { wantDown = true }` is the only down edge. pkg/routing/tunnel.go:657-665 (anchor) and :958-966 (legacy) set `skipUp = !runner.state.Up` for the tunnel manager's own finishTunnelLocked only. pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1290-1305 has `} else if nlErr == nil { if err := netlink.LinkSetUp(nl); ...` for any zoned interface without `Disable`. :1126-1132 shows that `IfaceFlagTunnel` changes only the flags and tx_port, not the bring-up. The apply order is pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:641 `applyInterfaceReconcile` (calls ApplyTunnels, daemon_apply_interfaces.go:454) and then :676 `applyDataplaneAndHACore`. That reaches daemon_apply_dataplane.go:222 `rt.ApplyConfig`, userspace/manager.go:947 `m.Compile(cfg)`, loader.go:285 `CompileConfig`, compiler.go:506 `compileZones`, and then mapZoneInterface. No keepalive reference exists in pkg/dataplane/*.go. The GRE local-origin thread opens and holds the anchor TUN (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tunnel.rs:260 `open_gre_tun`), so carrier is present after the re-up. `kernelLinkUp` (pkg/dataplane/userspace/fabric.go:266-280) then reports the link up and the helper re-admits the endpoint. The last link is an inference from the documented link_up contract (protocol_tunnels.go:20-27).

**Probe:** The zone-loop probe is RUN/verify/vb21/probes/dp_b21_r3_probe_keepalive_reup_test.go (identical to worker b21's). It ran as `go test -c -o /var/tmp/vb21/dp.test ./pkg/dataplane/ && B21_NETNS=1 PATH=/usr/sbin:$PATH unshare -Urn /var/tmp/vb21/dp.test -test.run TestB21R3ProbeZoneLoopReupsKeepaliveDownTunnel -test.v`, with output in RUN/verify/vb21/probe_zone_reup.out. Results: control-unzoned `adminUp before=false after=false`; control-zoned-disabled `before=false after=false` (log line "interface administratively disabled"); defect-zoned `before=false after=true` (log line "zone interface configured zone=vpn interface=gr-0/0/0.0"). The runner probe is RUN/verify/vb21/probes/routing_b21_r3_probe_keepalive_reup_test.go, run as `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestB21R3ProbeKeepaliveNeverRedownsAfterExternalReup -count=1 -v`, with output in RUN/verify/vb21/probe_routing.clean.out. The control gives `after 3 dead ticks: downs=1 ups=0 state.Up=false`; the defect gives `after 20 more dead ticks ...: downs=1 ups=0 state.Up=false failures=23`. Limit: the probe calls programZoneMaps directly rather than the full daemon apply, and no FRR or Rust FIB was running.

## Acceptance / fix direction
There are two options. The first is to have the routing manager export a "held down by keepalive" predicate (for example `TunnelHeldDown(name)`), consult it in `mapZoneInterface` before LinkSetUp, and record the surface as intentionally down. The second is to make the runner robust to external writers: derive wantDown from `Failures >= MaxRetries && link observed admin UP` rather than from `state.Up`, so a dead tick re-downs an externally re-upped link. Acceptance criteria: in the netns probe, the zoned arm stays DOWN while a runner holds it down; and a runner test with an external LinkSetUp after the down edge issues a second LinkSetDown on the next dead tick.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb21.md)</summary>

### R3-B21-01 — Any commit during a GRE keepalive outage re-ups the keepalive-DOWN tunnel. The dataplane zone loop `LinkSetUp`s every zoned netdev after the tunnel manager honoured `skipUp`, and the runner's down edge is gated on `state.Up`, so the dead tunnel stays admin UP for the rest of the outage.
- **Finding ID:** R3-B21-01

- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b21 (A7 management/routing engineer, second pass); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb21

The mechanism is demonstrated; the end-to-end route and traffic loss is inferred. Prerequisites are `keepalive` configured, a real outage, and an apply during it. There is none: userspace ApplyConfig always calls Compile, and CompileConfig always runs compileZones (Phase 2). Second, I checked whether the zone loop skips tunnels. It does not; the tunnel flag gates only tx_port and XDP/TC. Third, I checked for any post-compile keepalive reassertion. grep found only the route-listener nudge on a runner transition. - **HPC/invariant check:** This is an ownership invariant violation. Two writers act on one kernel attribute (link admin state) with no shared arbiter. The tunnel manager encodes "held down" only in runner state, which the dataplane compile does not read. There is no hot-path cost.

## #16583 — #15034 residual: on a vlan-tagging/flexible-vlan-tagging parent, a non-zero unit with no vlan-id (or vlan-id 0) commits strict-clean; its address lands on the parent while its zone/input filter bind to a never-created `<parent>.<unit>` device [OPEN]

## Summary

#15034 residual: on a vlan-tagging/flexible-vlan-tagging parent, a non-zero unit with no vlan-id (or vlan-id 0) commits strict-clean; its address lands on the parent while its zone/input filter bind to a never-created `<parent>.<unit>` device

**Finding ID:** `R3-A06-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. The unit's configured input filter is installed on no ifindex, and its subnet is configured on the untagged parent wire, where other rows classify it. This is the same consequence class #15034 was adjudicated at. The trigger is a misauthored unit that Junos rejects ("vlan-id required on tagg…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. A reachable strict-clean config silently drops an input filter; the #15034 predicate demonstrably excludes tagging parents.

## Mechanism

`vlan-tagging; unit 5 { family inet { filter input F; address 10.0.5.1/24 } }`, zone dmz `ge-0/0/1.5`. Strict commit accepts it, giving VlanID=0. ResolveKernelIfName returns `ge-0-0-1.5`. planPhysDesired puts 10.0.5.1/24 on `ge-0-0-1`, and networkd renders no address for it. The snapshot row `ge-0/0/1.5` has ifindex 0 and filterIn F. The Rust filter compiler skips the row, so F is armed nowhere.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_vlan_tagging.go:225` reads `if ifName == "" || ifaceTaggingEnabled(iface) { continue }`, so both the #14574 and #15034 arms skip tagging parents. `pkg/config/types.go:485-492` (`ResolveKernelIfName`) returns `kernelBase.<unit.Number>` when VlanID==0 and Number>0. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:218-295` (`planPhysDesired`) unions a vlanID==0 reference's addresses into the parent's set. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:999` creates a VLAN child only `if vlanID > 0`. `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:361,400` skip `iface.ifindex <= 0` rows when compiling filters. Observation: every Go leg above was executed. Inference: the Rust leg was read only.

## Impact

An operator on any tagged trunk who forgets one `vlan-id` gets a green commit, the unit's input filter silently disappears, and its subnet answers on the untagged wire. Every apply of the config is affected. Recovery is adding the vlan-id, but no diagnostic points there.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Extend the #15034 arm to tagging parents. A unit with Number>0, no positive tag and no tunnel/st/lo/irb exemption should be strict-rejected (tolerant-warned, #1960) regardless of parent tagging mode. Acceptance: all three defect arms REJECT naming `ge-0/0/1 unit 5`; the vlan-id control, unit 0 without vlan-id on a tagging parent (`test/incus/xpf-vlan-test.conf`), and tunnel units still compile.

## Contract (where cited)

#15034 (fix fb980ad435, ancestor of d1ea69f9aa) says a unit whose zone/filter writers name a device that nothing creates, while the address writers place its address elsewhere, must be strict-rejected and tolerant-warned (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_vlan_tagging.go:43-60`). The exemption list (tunnel, st, lo, irb) does not include tagging parents. They are simply never visited.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A06-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:45: - **R3-A05-04 — DUP of R3-A06-01.** **Defect:** the same `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_vlan_tagging.go:219-255` skip of tagging parents lets the nonzero untagged unit through. **Refutation:** it supplies no separate guard, independently affected consumer or remediation beyond the A06-01 VLAN/netdev case. **Decisive check:** keep A05-04's admission test in A06-01 acceptance rather than file a second issue.

## #16584 — `drain_session_deltas` pops up to `max` deltas from the per-binding RPC-fallback buffers and then writes the response. If the write fails, the handler just returns `Err`, which the accept loop logs. Nothing re-queues ... [OPEN]

## Summary
`drain_session_deltas` pops up to `max` deltas from the per-binding RPC-fallback buffers and then writes the response. If the write fails, the handler just returns `Err`, which the accept loop logs. Nothing re-queues the batch and no `set_delta_loss` is armed. This happens when Go has already hit its 3 s deadline and closed the connection, either because the request sat in the serial accept backlog behind a slow verb or because the drain's own `write_state` was slow. During an event-stream outage the opens in the batch are re-sent by the outage's own LossResync loop, but the closes are not.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low. The divergence is bounded to the standby: the closes in a lost batch leave stale peer rows until peer GC. The opens are lost only in the narrow case where no later incremental delta arrives before the stream reconnects. The trigger needs both an event-stream outage and a Go-side timeout on the drain round trip. Demonstrated at the dispatcher level; frequency in the field is unmeasured. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A73-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va73.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
It hits HA clusters during an event-stream outage when a control round trip stalls. The blast radius is one batch of 256 or fewer deltas per lost drain, which leaves stale standby rows. After a failover, those stale rows can briefly admit a reused 5-tuple until they time out. Recovery is peer GC, or a later owner-RG FullResync.

**Contract:** `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md` and `handlers/mod.rs:672-689` (#5294) say the drained-delta tail "must never strand an already-drained delta batch". The #2442/#2874/#5290 rule is deliver-or-resync: never a silent drop. The #15217 fix direction says "optionally latch loss on drain-response write failure in the helper".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
All at d1ea69f9aa.
  - Helper side:
    - `server/handlers/session_deltas.rs:14-16`: `response.session_deltas = guard.afxdp.drain_session_deltas(max); refresh_status(guard); *persist_state = true;`.
    - `server/handlers/mod.rs:699-712`: `write_state` runs first, then `serde_json::to_writer(...)?`, `write_all(b"\n")?` and `flush()?`. There is no latch on the error.
    - `server/helpers/guards.rs:110-113`: the accept loop only logs the error.
    - `server/lifecycle.rs:789-833`: one connection is served at a time.
    - `afxdp/coordinator/status.rs:1368-1399`: `set_delta_loss` is armed only on budget overflow.
  - Go side:
    - `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_status.go:376-399`: the drain is one request, with the deadline at `process_control.go:43` (3 s).
    - `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:1102-1105`: `if len(deltas) == 0 { return total, err }`. The callers at `:740` and `:763` discard the error.
  - Healing path, found by the verifier:
    - `event_stream/mod.rs:634-636`: an incremental push fails immediately when the stream is disconnected.
    - `afxdp/session_delta.rs:995-1001`, `worker/loop_body/mod.rs:226-228`: that failure arms the delta-loss latch.
    - `worker/loop_body/delta_recovery.rs:228+`: the latch drives a LossResync that re-emits an open for every owned session into the fallback buffer (`session_delta.rs:913`).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — the cell drives the real `handle_stream` dispatcher with a seeded binding: a connected control, an overflow-latch control, the closed-client defect arm, and a follow-up drain. The Go-side discard and the LossResync healing path are STATIC.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-smr-batch07.md`: | R3-A74-01 FragAssoc 32/session quota, no completion release, ~16/s cap | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A74-02 OverlapTracker abandoned entries count 30s vs sender quota | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A74-04 reinject epoch fence lost on queue withdrawal | NEEDS_VALIDATION | Low |
| R3-A75-02 Prebuilt mirror sends rewritten egress, not received frame | COHORT | Low |

| R3-A76-02 inbound+SNAT persistent session never takes hold | MATERIAL | Medium |

## #16585 — R3-A40-04: The Cloudflare instance tag is a zone-endpoint hash with no per-install component, so #16086 fold finding 1 (instance B withdraws instance A's record) stays open for… [OPEN]

## Summary

The Cloudflare instance tag is a zone-endpoint hash with no per-install component, so #16086 fold finding 1 (instance B withdraws instance A's record) stays open for the only shape where two routers can meet

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — the consequence and trigger are the ones #16086 graded. Two publishers of one name+IP: when one withdraws, the other's name disappears until that router's next forced refresh. It also arises when B's PrevAddr equals A's content. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A40-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va40.md` (finding `R3-A40-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

backend_cloudflare.go:204 `return cfInstanceTagProvider + backendFingerprint(p)`. surface_a.go:1965-1983 backendFingerprint hashes backend, UpdateServer, Server, Zone, HostedZoneID, AWSRegion and URLTemplate. Provider name, token and node identity are excluded. backend_cloudflare_foreign_withdraw_16086_test.go:46-51: the "other instance" fixture uses `Zone: "other.example.net"`. The residual documented at backend_cloudflare.go:181-182 and in PR #16114 reads "Routers that deliberately share one provider identity ARE one owner".

**Contract / expected behaviour:** backend_cloudflare.go:160-196: "A bare product marker ... is NOT ownership: every xpf instance stamps the same literal ... Two INDEPENDENT xpf instances have different providers/zones (different instance ids)". pkg/ddns/README.md:26: "A different instance's tagged row is FOREIGN: never adopted, never PATCHed, never deleted".

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (#16086 Cloudflare ownership residuals: R3-A40-04, with R3-A40-01 pending validation) — real and bounded. The fix's code comment and fixture claim closure that does not hold.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — two Cloudflare backends on one zone and the fake API.

**Confidence:** High — executed with a distinct-identity positive control. In production both routers leave `server` empty, so the tag is identical across all installs on a zone.

## Impact

This is exactly the non-hostile flap #16086 fixed, between two xpf routers, while the fix's tests report it closed. Recovery comes at the victim's next forced refresh.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Include a durable per-install (or per-cluster, config-synced) random id in the tag, and read the old zone-hash tag as legacy (value-scoped fallback). Fix the fixture to use the same zone. Acceptance: two backends with different install ids on one zone produce different tags, and B's withdraw leaves A's row; an HA pair still shares the id.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A40-04`, part `parts/va40.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16586 — A Junos reth LAG (two or more child links per node) commits strict-clean without a multi-child diagnostic; only the lexically-first local child is used and the others come up zoneless with a duplicate 169.254 RG source and no virtual MAC [OPEN]

## Summary

A Junos reth LAG (two or more child links per node) commits strict-clean without a multi-child diagnostic; only the lexically-first local child is used and the others come up zoneless with a duplicate 169.254 RG source and no virtual MAC

**Finding ID:** `R3-A06-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. A documented Junos chassis-cluster feature is accepted and silently not enforced. The configured intra-node link redundancy and bandwidth are lost. Demonstrated: the extra children are unused and zoneless, yet managed UP with an address. Potential, not demonstrated: with a static switch-side…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. An accepted-but-unenforced redundancy feature commits silently on the static spelling, contrary to the project's accepted-only doctrine (#6544 covers ae only).

## Mechanism

`ge-0/0/1` and `ge-0/0/2` both set `redundant-parent reth1`. Strict commit accepts it. RethToPhysical binds reth1 to ge-0/0/1. The VIP, virtual MAC (`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:437-505` loops over rethToPhys) and zone all land on ge-0-0-1. ge-0-0-2 is managed UP with 169.254.1.1/32, has no zone, and keeps its physical MAC.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/types.go:198-237` (`RethToPhysical`) keeps one member per reth: best slot score, then `ifc.Name < prev`. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1520-1528` gives every member with RedundantParent `effectiveCfg = rethCfg`, and `:1827-1834` renders `169.254.<rg>.<node+1>/32` for each. `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_reth_member.go` (#6722) has no member-count rule. `validateLinkAggregationWarnings` covers ae/802.3ad only. The schema `redundant-ether-options` (`pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:120-122`) models only `redundancy-group`.

## Impact

Reth LAG is a mainstream SRX deployment. On xpf, the first child failing leaves the RG on a dead link unless interface-monitor demotes it, and the switch may hash flows to an unzoned child. `show interfaces` shows the extra child up with an address, and the commit says nothing.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Until reth LAG exists, strict-reject (tolerant-warn, #1960) a reth with more than one local child per node, naming the reth, the node and the ignored children. Alternatively, emit an accepted-only advisory like #6544 and render the extra children down. Acceptance: the 2+2 arm REJECTs or warns naming `ge-0/0/2`, and the one-member control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper "Aggregated Ethernet Interfaces in a Chassis Cluster" (juniper.net, security-chassis-cluster-redundant-ethernet-lag-interfaces) says that two or more child interfaces per node on one reth form a reth LAG, with up to 8 per node, and "if one link in the primary aggregate fails, its traffic load is taken up by the remaining links". The xpf doctrine (#2078/#4231/#5804/#6544, `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn_routing.go:130-144`) says an accepted-but-inert redundancy configuration must carry an accepted-only advisory or be rejected. `docs/feature-gaps.md:705` lists reth runtime as Done and says nothing about reth LAG.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A06-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A06-02 | Medium | A Junos reth LAG (two or more child links per node) commits strict-clean without a… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:50: - **R3-A06-02 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/types.go:240-278` picks one lexicographically first local reth child, while `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1520-1528,1832-1836` still sets up other local members with redundant ownership/link-local address but no aggregate forwarding membership. Historical strict fixture and snapshot show the extra zoneless member. **Refutation:** no proof xpf promises full Junos reth LAG/LACP semantics, and the report did not observe a switch or traffic blackhole; a single-member reth is unaffected. **Decisive check:** decide whether multi-child per node is supported; either reject it clearly or exercise both links' bonding, MAC and RG takeover in an existing isolated-test setup.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L183: ### R3-A06-02 — reth LAG (2+ children/node) commits; extra children zoneless UP with duplicate 169.254, no vMAC — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `types.go:240 RethToPhysical` keeps one member (lexical best); no member-count gate (#6722 none, #6544 advisory ae-only); dataplane gives every redundant-parent member rethCfg + `169.254.<rg>.<node+1>/32` → extra child managed UP, zone="", physical MAC. ## #16587 — With the shipped HA config, the bond manager realizes the peer's fabric stanza as a local, slave-less, admin-UP bond. The cause is that the daemon selects every `len(FabricMembers)>0` interface, and bond.go skips only `LocalFabricMember... [OPEN]

## Summary
With the shipped HA config, the bond manager realizes the peer's fabric stanza as a local, slave-less, admin-UP bond. The cause is that the daemon selects every `len(FabricMembers)>0` interface, and bond.go skips only `LocalFabricMember != ""`. Neither fabric stale sweep removes it, because both delete only IPVLAN type. The phantom netdev is zoned and goes through the bring-up/XDP-queue path.

**Finding ID:** R3-B21-02
**Severity (source):** Low — The effect is a phantom kernel interface wearing the peer fabric's name, visible in `ip link`, `show interfaces` and SNMP. It is zoned into `control`, brought UP and queued for XDP attach. It has no address (fab addresses live only in the owning node's group) and no slaves, so no traffic was shown to be mis-forwarded. No consumer was found that treats it as a live fabric. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Every node of every cluster built from the shipped config carries a misleading interface named after the peer's fabric. That confuses troubleshooting (`ip link`, `show interfaces`, SNMP ifTable) and makes analyses that assume no fab1 netdev exists on node0 wrong. The surface is permanent while the config is present.

**Contract:** bond.go:15-17 says the bond manager owns the bond lifecycle for fabric member-interfaces and skips the vSRX single-local-member mode. compiler_derivations.go:126-141 resolves a fab's LOCAL member by FPC slot. Under Junos chassis-cluster semantics fab1 is node1's fabric and has no realization on node0. compiler_iface.go:153-158 describes the no-local-member shape as "the bond ApplyBonds creates" (#9872), which is the standalone multi-member shape, not a cluster peer.

**Trace:** The shipped HA config is compiled for node N, with LocalFabricMember set only on the local fab. applyInterfaceReconcile then calls ApplyBonds([fab0, fab1]). The bond manager creates the peer's fab as an empty bond and sets it UP. applyFabricIPVLAN creates the local IPVLAN and its stale sweep ignores the non-IPVLAN ghost. compileZones (`control` zone, `fab1`) resolves fab1 to itself (no local member) and finds the ghost netdev, so it runs the bring-up/XDP-queue path instead of the "not found, skipping" path.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:472-481 appends any `len(ifc.FabricMembers) > 0` interface to bondIfaces and calls `d.routing.ApplyBonds`. pkg/routing/bond.go:134 skips only `len(ifc.FabricMembers) == 0 || ifc.LocalFabricMember != ""`. In bond.go:395-410, createLocked reads the bond back, then `enslaveMembers` (where an absent member is a soft #4823 skip) and `b.ops.LinkSetUp(bondLink)`. pkg/config/compiler_derivations.go:129-141 sets LocalFabricMember only when `SlotToNodeID(slot) == cc.NodeID`. daemon_apply_interfaces.go:119-128 and daemon_fabric_reassert.go:134-147 both reap only when `link.(*netlink.IPVlan)`. docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:100-113 defines fab0 and fab1 globally, and :156 zones `fab0; fab1;` in `control`.

**Probe:** The probe is RUN/verify/vb21/probes/b21_r3_probe_peer_fabric_bond_test.go (identical to worker b21's), run as `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestB21R3ProbePeerFabricBecomesEmptyBond -count=1 -v`, with output in RUN/verify/vb21/probe_routing.clean.out. node0 shows `fab0 LocalFabricMember="ge-0/0/0"` and `fab1 LocalFabricMember=""`, then "bond created name=fab1 mode=active-backup" and `LinkAdd=[fab1] LinkSetUp=[fab1] master=[]`. node1 shows `LinkAdd=[fab0]`. The positive control in the same run is that the local fab on each node creates nothing. Limit: fake link ops were used, with no real kernel bond and no zone-loop run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In a chassis cluster, skip a fab whose members all belong to the peer: bond only when `cfg.Chassis.Cluster == nil`, or when two or more members are local. Also let ApplyBonds reap a tracked bond that leaves the desired set. Acceptance criteria: the per-node probe creates no bond on either node; a non-cluster multi-member fab still creates its bond; and upgrading a node that already carries the ghost removes it.

## Full validated claim

- **Finding ID:** R3-B21-02

The cause is that the daemon selects every `len(FabricMembers)>0` interface, and bond.go skips only `LocalFabricMember != ""`. Neither fabric stale sweep removes it, because both delete only IPVLAN type. The phantom netdev is zoned and goes through the bring-up/XDP-queue path.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b21 (A7 management/routing engineer, second pass); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb21
- **Severity:** Low — The effect is a phantom kernel interface wearing the peer fabric's name, visible in `ip link`, `show interfaces` and SNMP. It is zoned into `control`, brought UP and queued for XDP attach. It has no address (fab addresses live only in the owning node's group) and no slaves, so no traffic was shown to be mis-forwarded. No consumer was found that treats it as a live fabric. [reporter: Low]
- **Confidence:** High — Creation was executed at the bond-manager boundary using the shipped config compiled per node. That neither sweep reaps it was checked statically. The zone-loop follow-on and the XDP attach on an empty bond were not executed.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — `TestB21R3ProbePeerFabricBecomesEmptyBond` uses docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf with `ExpandGroupsWithVars` and `CompileConfigForNode`, the daemon's selection loop, and fake link ops seeded with only the local NIC. The sweep and zone-loop consequences are STATIC.
- **Gate verdict:** COHORT (interface-lifecycle hygiene / phantom netdevs realized from non-local config) — The defect is real and reachable on every cluster node with the shipped config, but its consequence is cosmetic and bounded.
- **Contract:** bond.go:15-17 says the bond manager owns the bond lifecycle for fabric member-interfaces and skips the vSRX single-local-member mode. compiler_derivations.go:126-141 resolves a fab's LOCAL member by FPC slot. Under Junos chassis-cluster semantics fab1 is node1's fabric and has no realization on node0. compiler_iface.go:153-158 describes the no-local-member shape as "the bond ApplyBonds creates" (#9872), which is the standalone multi-member shape, not a cluster peer.
- **Adversarial analysis:** The property concerned is the integrity of the kernel interface inventory and the operator's view. No actor is needed: the shipped HA config triggers it on every apply. The challenged assumption is that `LocalFabricMember == ""` implies a standalone LAG. In a cluster it also means "the peer's fabric".
- **Evidence:** pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:472-481 appends any `len(ifc.FabricMembers) > 0` interface to bondIfaces and calls `d.routing.ApplyBonds`. pkg/routing/bond.go:134 skips only `len(ifc.FabricMembers) == 0 || ifc.LocalFabricMember != ""`. In bond.go:395-410, createLocked reads the bond back, then `enslaveMembers` (where an absent member is a soft #4823 skip) and `b.ops.LinkSetUp(bondLink)`. pkg/config/compiler_derivations.go:129-141 sets LocalFabricMember only when `SlotToNodeID(slot) == cc.NodeID`. daemon_apply_interfaces.go:119-128 and daemon_fabric_reassert.go:134-147 both reap only when `link.(*netlink.IPVlan)`. docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:100-113 defines fab0 and fab1 globally, and :156 zones `fab0; fab1;` in `control`.
- **Probe:** The probe is RUN/verify/vb21/probes/b21_r3_probe_peer_fabric_bond_test.go (identical to worker b21's), run as `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestB21R3ProbePeerFabricBecomesEmptyBond -count=1 -v`, with output in RUN/verify/vb21/probe_routing.clean.out. node0 shows `fab0 LocalFabricMember="ge-0/0/0"` and `fab1 LocalFabricMember=""`, then "bond created name=fab1 mode=active-backup" and `LinkAdd=[fab1] LinkSetUp=[fab1] master=[]`. node1 shows `LinkAdd=[fab0]`. The positive control in the same run is that the local fab on each node creates nothing. Limit: fake link ops were used, with no real kernel bond and no zone-loop run.
- **Trace:** The shipped HA config is compiled for node N, with LocalFabricMember set only on the local fab. applyInterfaceReconcile then calls ApplyBonds([fab0, fab1]). The bond manager creates the peer's fab as an empty bond and sets it UP. applyFabricIPVLAN creates the local IPVLAN and its stale sweep ignores the non-IPVLAN ghost. compileZones (`control` zone, `fab1`) resolves fab1 to itself (no local member) and finds the ghost netdev, so it runs the bring-up/XDP-queue path instead of the "not found, skipping" path.
- **Refutation attempt:** First, I checked whether anything reaps it. The apply sweep and the 30 s reassert reaper both check the IPVLAN type, so neither does. Second, I checked whether the ghost acquires the peer's address. It does not, because addresses live in the per-node groups. Third, I checked whether Fabric1Interface or the dual-fabric listeners pick it up on node0. They do not (compiler_derivations.go:152-163 requires LocalFabricMember). Fourth, I checked AF_XDP binding: the fab* rows are excluded by name. Fifth, the early-input lifeline admits fab0/fab1 by name, but the ghost has no slaves and so receives nothing. Sixth, the only earlier mention (docs/pr/1879-pathc/deploy-delta-reviewer-ids.md:68-71, "AGY #5 ghost bonds ... REFUTED") argued only that the cluster still works, not that the bond does not exist. I narrowed the consequence to a phantom interface and wasted bring-up work.
- **HPC/invariant check:** This is an ownership/realization invariant violation: the node realizes a config object owned by the peer node. There is no hot-path cost. One extra netdev enters the zone loop and the arm set on each node.

## #16588 — #3898 residual: per-unit tunnel clones inherit every earlier inheriting unit's addresses from the interface tunnel, so the same IP/prefix is installed on several GRE/IPIP netdevs depending on authored unit order [OPEN]

## Summary

#3898 residual: per-unit tunnel clones inherit every earlier inheriting unit's addresses from the interface tunnel, so the same IP/prefix is installed on several GRE/IPIP netdevs depending on authored unit order

**Finding ID:** `R3-A06-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. The same address and connected prefix are installed on tunnel netdevs that have different remote endpoints, which is exactly the "duplicate IP on two tunnel netdevs" harm #3898 was closed for. Demonstrated: the applied tunnel state is wrong. Potential: the kernel picks between duplicate conn…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. The #3898 contract ("a per-unit override on one unit would [not] contaminate the others") is violated in the default authoring order, and its regression test cannot detect it.

## Mechanism

The `gr-0/0/0` interface tunnel serves unit 0 (10.1.0.1/30), and units 1 and 2 have their own tunnel stanzas. Compiling unit 0 appends its address to ifc.Tunnel. Units 1 and 2 then clone that list. The applied tunnels put 10.1.0.1/30 on gr-0-0-0, gr-0-0-0u1 and gr-0-0-0u2, and pkg/routing adds it to all three netdevs.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:576-578`: `if ifc.Tunnel != nil { tc = ifc.Tunnel.cloneForUnit(linuxName) }`. `pkg/config/types_routing.go:970-976`: `cloneForUnit` copies `tc.Addresses`. `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:1063-1069`: `unit.Tunnel.Addresses = append(...)` for a per-unit tunnel, else `ifc.Tunnel.Addresses = append(ifc.Tunnel.Addresses, unit.Addresses...)`. The interface tunnel has no address source of its own (the only writers are `:1065,1068`). `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_routehelpers.go:79-109` copies `*unit.Tunnel`, and `pkg/routing/tunnel.go:1004-1005` reconciles exactly `tc.Addresses` on the device.

## Impact

Multi-unit GRE with one inherited unit plus per-unit overrides is the shape the code comment documents. All later unit tunnels claim the inheriting unit's prefix, so unit 0's peer traffic can be encapsulated toward the wrong remote after link churn. Nothing diagnoses it, and the workaround (reordering) is undiscoverable.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Do not seed a per-unit tunnel's Addresses from ifc.Tunnel: clear Addresses in `cloneForUnit` for per-unit use, or accumulate interface-tunnel addresses after the unit loop. Acceptance: order 0,1,2 yields `u1=[10.2.0.1/30]` and `u2=[10.3.0.1/30]`. Extend `TestPerUnitTunnelAddressesIndependent` to assert the seed addresses are absent from u1 and u2 (that assertion fails at d1ea69f9aa).

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:567-575` (the #3898 fix comment) says each per-unit tunnel owns independent addresses. #3898 (CLOSED) names the harm as a duplicate IP on two tunnel netdevs.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A06-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

## #16589 — The helper builds `export_idle_leases` (and `export_persistent_lease_display`) as one unpaged JSON response. Once the idle population crosses the 64 MiB control-response cap, Go's bounded reader refuses the response. ... [OPEN]

## Summary
The helper builds `export_idle_leases` (and `export_persistent_lease_display`) as one unpaged JSON response. Once the idle population crosses the 64 MiB control-response cap, Go's bounded reader refuses the response. The #14607 cluster-frame chunking runs only after a successful export, so it never runs, and every 30 s idle-lease push delivers nothing to the standby. The operator's persistent-NAT show table fails the same way, and at a lower population.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium. The #8121 standby rebuild of idle persistent-NAT mappings fails completely, not partially, at a large but legal population, so after a failover every idle subscriber's persistent mapping is gone. Inbound connections from permitted remotes are refused, and new outbound flows may get a different mapping. Enforcement is not affected, and the failure shows up as a rate-limited Warn plus the `PersistentNatLeaseExportFailures` counter. The response size is measured; the end-to-end failover loss is inferred from the static path and not demonstrated on a cluster. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A73-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va73.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
It hits CGNAT- or subscriber-scale deployments that use persistent NAT, which is exactly the scale the feature exists for. The blast radius is every idle persistent mapping on failover, and the condition lasts as long as the population stays large. Recovery comes only when the population shrinks.

**Contract:** #8121 promises that the standby rebuilds idle persistent-NAT leases. #14607 (Y15-01) claimed the 64 MiB export-cap regime and named the helper `export_idle_leases` as a consumer to page "(with a cursor, as in #9344)". #9344 established that an unbounded helper export crossing the capped control transport must be paged. Its acceptance asked that 300k or more leases yield only sub-cap frames and that the peer decode every lease.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
All at d1ea69f9aa:
  - `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/idle_leases.rs:219-226`: `response.idle_leases = guard.afxdp.export_idle_persistent_leases_now().iter().map(to_wire).collect();` with no max and no cursor. `:623-630` is the same for `display_leases`.
  - `userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs:448-454`: `MAX_CONTROL_RESPONSE_BYTES = MAX_CONTROL_REQUEST_BYTES` (64 MiB). In the helper it is enforced only for fib_dump (`handlers/mod.rs:696-697`).
  - `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_idle_leases_8121.go:161-178`: a single `requestDetailedLocked{Type:"export_idle_leases", SuppressStatus:true}`.
  - `pkg/dataplane/userspace/control_work_deadline_9344.go:33-50`: work-deadline floors exist only for `list_sessions_by_policy`, `export_owner_rg_sessions` and `fib_dump`.
  - `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator/mod.rs:177` and `:1761-1762`: the per-pool `max_tracked_flows` is at most 262,144. `:297-305`: under TargetHost(Port), permitted remotes accumulate per lease up to 1024.
  - Commit 9e58892fba (#14784, an ancestor of HEAD): "NOT changed: Rust helper export, receiver import semantics, wire version".

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a temporary `#[cfg(test)]` cell serialized a real `ControlResponse` holding N `IdleLeaseWire` records with serde_json and compared the byte length to `MAX_CONTROL_RESPONSE_BYTES`. The unpaged handler path, the Go single-request caller, its missing work-deadline floor and the bounded reader are STATIC.

## #16590 — #14575 residual on RETH: RethVIPsForRG ignores unit/interface disable, so a disabled reth unit's address stays in the RG's VIP set; a disabled tagged unit blocks RG takeover readiness on both nodes, and when its link is up the disabled address is… [OPEN]

## Summary

#14575 residual on RETH: RethVIPsForRG ignores unit/interface disable, so a disabled reth unit's address stays in the RG's VIP set; a disabled tagged unit blocks RG takeover readiness on both nodes, and when its link is up the disabled address is installed and GARPed

**Finding ID:** `R3-A06-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. HA ownership is impaired by an ordinary admin action. Normal promotion of the whole RG is gated on both nodes. A cold boot leaves the RG unowned until peer-yield or the 2-minute degraded fallback, and every such promotion is DEGRADED. When the link is up, a disabled address is claimed by ARP…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. The single VIP derivation used for install, GARP and readiness misses the #14575 predicate, which has a concrete HA-readiness consequence.

## Mechanism

`reth0 vlan-tagging; unit 80 vlan-id 80 ...; unit 80 disable` puts `ge-0-0-2.80` into `RethVIPsForRG(1)` on both nodes. If the child is down (networkd), readiness is false and promotion is gated. If the child is up (ensureVLANSubInterface), the primary's `directAddVIPs`/`directSendGARPs` install and announce 172.16.80.8/24 on a VLAN the operator disabled.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/reth_vips.go:14-79` has no `ifc.Disable`/`unit.Disable` check in either the tagged arm (`:55-64`) or the untagged arm (`:66-75`). Compile only sets `unit.Disable = true` (`compiler_interfaces.go:534-536`) and does not clear Addresses. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:70-87` (`checkVIPReadinessForConfig`) iterates the map and reports `vip interface %s down`. It feeds `checkNoRethTakeoverReadiness` and then `takeoverReadinessForRG` (`daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go:230-237`). `pkg/cluster/election.go:497-525` blocks new promotions while not ready, except for the readinessGateVerdictLocked degraded path or peer-yield. `DefaultDegradedPromoteTimeout = 2 * time.Minute` (`pkg/cluster/manager.go:773`). networkd renders the disabled VLAN child `Disable: unitDisabled` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1724-1745`), but `ensureVLANSubInterface` brings an existing child UP with no disable test (`:268-279`).

## Impact

`disable` on one reth VLAN is the normal way to take a segment out of service. Here it degrades HA for every other VLAN in the RG and leaves the RG permanently "not ready" in readiness reasons. On an untagged reth, the disabled address can keep answering ARP after the operator has reassigned it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make `RethVIPsForRG` skip `ifc.Disable` and `unit.Disable` so install, GARP, readiness and probe source all follow, and stop `ensureVLANSubInterface` from bringing up a disabled unit's child. Acceptance: the `disable-unit80=true` arm is ready with `ge-0-0-2.80` absent; the untagged disabled arms give an empty map; the enabled control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

#14575 (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:528-535`) says unit `disable` is "Honoured end to end: the userspace snapshot marks the unit AdminDisabled with no addresses, and the networkd/legacy address planners skip it". #15763 removed disabled units from host-inbound scopes on the premise that they own no address. CLAUDE.md says private-RG election is the default and uses direct VIP ownership.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A06-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A06-04 | Medium | #14575 residual on RETH: RethVIPsForRG ignores unit/interface disable, so a disabled reth… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:52: - **R3-A06-04 — MATERIAL (Medium for disabled VIP retention; outage duration unverified).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/reth_vips.go:30-79` collects both interface and unit addresses without checking their `Disable` flags, despite address reconciliation skipping disabled units (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:264-273`). That collection feeds private-RG VIP installation, gratuitous ARP and takeover-readiness paths; historical synthetic readiness with disabled/tagged link down returned false. **Refutation:** a disabled device's real link state and install behavior determine whether an actual takeover stalls, so the report's categorical outage/timing claim is not source-proven. **Decisive check:** disabled parent and disabled tagged unit cases through VIP collection and a bounded RG readiness transition, controlling link up/down separately.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L195: ### R3-A06-04 — `RethVIPsForRG` ignores disable; disabled unit blocks RG takeover readiness — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `pkg/config/reth_vips.go:14-79` no `Disable` check (grep at origin/master: no Disable in file); compile sets unit.Disable without clearing addresses (#14575 honoured by other planners, not this one). Single derivation feeds VIP install/GARP/readiness/probe → disabled tagged unit down (networkd) → readiness false both nodes → election blocks new promotions (degraded 2-min/peer-yield bypasses bound outage; sitting primary not demoted — verifier narrowed correctly); if link up, disabled address installed+GARPed. - Refutation: Bypass paths exist; settled link state of disabled VLAN child is two-writer dependent (networkd always-down vs ensureVLANSubInterface) — Medium there; lab validation needed for which branch occurs in production. - Evidence: Absence-of-check + readiness/election chain in report re-reads; probe with netlink fake (readiness=false reasons=[vip interface …80 down], control true). - Unresolved/decisive: Lab settled link state + cold-boot RG ownership timing — the NEEDS_VALIDATION leg inside an otherwise MATERIAL claim. ### R3-A06-05 — interface `mtu` is Junos media MTU but applied as Linux L3 MTU verbatim — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: Compile `ifc.MTU=n` verbatim → netdev MTU n; Junos leaf is media MTU (GE 1514 = IP 1500). Explicit migrated values shift IP MTU +14/+18 vs Junos peer → giant-drop blackhole without PTB. Undocumented deviation; userspa

## #16591 — R3-A40-05: The #14995 device-DHCID digest change has no legacy match, so upgraded Surface B names can never be renumbered or refreshed and are orphaned on the wire [OPEN]

## Summary

The #14995 device-DHCID digest change has no legacy match, so upgraded Surface B names can never be renumbered or refreshed and are orphaned on the wire

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the consequence was demonstrated at the manager layer. On every Surface B (DHCP-lease DDNS, replace-owned) deployment upgraded past 909e852614, any client whose lease address changes keeps resolving to its OLD address. The pool may reassign that address to a different host, so the name points to the wrong LAN host. xpf drops ownership, and the stale A plus the legacy DHCID are never withdrawn. Repair is manual zone surgery per name. This is bounded to the DDNS zone, with no firewall enforcement impact. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A40-05`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va40.md` (finding `R3-A40-05`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

backend_rfc2136.go:795-799 `if key := pairedIdentityKey(clientID); key != "" { return "dev:" + key }`. state.go:437-469: every cid:/mac:/duid: form yields a non-empty key. Pre-fix `git show 909e852614^:pkg/ddns/backend_rfc2136.go` :652 `h.Write([]byte(clientID))`. :1086 Attempt B `mB.Used([]dns.RR{dns.Copy(dhcid)})` refuses on NXRRSET (:1091-1101). :1353 the guarded delete `m.Used(...)` fails, so it is a counted skip that returns nil (:1365-1376). manager.go:1875 a refused add deletes the intent (same key as the confirmed row). README.md:1019-1024 is the residual text. Observation: wire and ownership state after renumber. Inference: HA takeover and force follow the same refused-add path (static).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** RFC 4703 conflict resolution as implemented by sendAddOwned. Attempt B adopts "a name WE already own, refreshed" (pkg/ddns/backend_rfc2136.go:1001-1012 comment). pkg/ddns/README.md:1019-1024 records the pre-#14995 residual as delete-only and promises that "a same-device re-publish converges the name onto the device DHCID". The #5710 force-update contract is that `request system dynamic-dns update` re-asserts owned records.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — the trigger (an ordinary lease renumber after an upgrade) is reachable, the consequence is concrete (a stale name, ownership lost, the status reports success), and it contradicts the module README's convergence claim.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — two runs. The backend-level probe covers forced refresh, delete and add for cid:, mac: and duid: identities. The manager-level Reconcile renumber probe uses the stateful fake RFC 2136 server. Both include a current-digest positive control.

**Confidence:** High — the legacy digest is reproduced from the 909e852614^ dhcidRR, and dhcidIdentifierType is byte-identical before and after the change. The remaining assumption is that deployments carry records written by pre-#14995 builds, which holds for any upgrade of a running Surface B install.

## Impact

Every upgraded DHCP-DDNS LAN is affected. Names silently go stale per client as leases move, and the conflict counter blames a third party that is really xpf's previous build. This lasts until an operator hand-deletes each name's A + DHCID.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In Attempt B and in the guarded forward delete, also accept the pre-#14995 per-identity digest (raw clientID, including the IAID-bearing v6 form) as proof of ownership. On a legacy match, replace the legacy DHCID with the device DHCID in the same UPDATE. Correct the README residual. Acceptance: with a legacy wire DHCID, the manager probe ends with `old=false new=true ownedAfter=1`; a foreign (different-identity) DHCID is still refused; the #14995 hijack cells stay green.

A fix should:

## #16592 — On a node-targeted failover (`request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group N node <local>`), the owner's applied-ack can come back FAILED (fence barrier not actuated) or time out. The requester still promotes itself on the owner's... [OPEN]

## Summary
On a node-targeted failover (`request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group N node <local>`), the owner's applied-ack can come back FAILED (fence barrier not actuated) or time out. The requester still promotes itself on the owner's next secondary-hold heartbeat through electRG's "Peer transfer out" arm, after `RequestPeerFailover` has returned the error. The arm also fires before a successful ack whenever a heartbeat arrives first. The "peer holds instead of promoting" guarantee in the #5640/#6177/#6371 code comments and docs does not hold, and the request-ACK exit is a #15164 residual.

**Finding ID:** R3-B22-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — HA ownership moves even though the operator was told the failover failed. This happens on every request-ACK failure or timeout in which the owner had already entered secondary-hold. On the fence-failure arm, the requester also promotes while the old owner's demotion is known not to have landed (the rg_active clear was rejected or the RETH VIP release timed out). That is the two-owner window the barrier was written to prevent. The dual-forwarding consequence is potential, not demonstrated. The project's own #6371 research bounds it with the reconcile retry and the helper forwarding lease (~11 s). That bound is the reason this is not High. Under preempt the owner can later reclaim the RG at lease expiry, a second move nobody requested. [reporter: Medium, potential High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators and failover automation read the error as "nothing moved", so they retry, leave the RG alone or open a ticket, while the RG has in fact moved. On the fence-failure arms, both nodes can hold rg_active, and possibly VIPs, until the old owner's retry or lease ends the overlap. Possible effects are duplicate ARP/NA owners and asymmetric session ownership. `show chassis cluster status` shows the requester primary and the owner in secondary-hold for up to the 30 s lease. Under preempt, a second, unrequested move follows at lease expiry. Recovery is another manual failover or reset.

**Contract:** pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:329-334 (#6371) says "the sync layer downgrades the applied-ack to failed, and the peer holds instead of promoting into a two-owner window". daemon_ha.go:408-414 (#6177) says the peer "HOLDS rather than promoting into a window where both nodes answer for the VIP". daemon_ha.go:670-677 makes the same claim. sync_failover.go:413-419 (#5640) says "downgrade to failed so the peer holds rather than joining a split-brain". docs/session-sync-architecture.md:3264-3267 says the sender "treats that ack as authorization to run commitRequestedPeerFailover and become primary". Issue #15164's acceptance requires that "in the b22 probes the requester stays non-primary after the abort". Those probes included the request-ACK-timeout row.

**Trace:** CLI or gRPC `request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group N node <self>` (pkg/cli/cli_request_chassis.go:102, pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:898) → `Manager.RequestPeerFailover` → `SessionSync.SendFailover` → the owner's `OnRemoteFailover` runs `ManualFailover` (secondary-hold, event enqueued) and arms the lease → the owner's daemon demotion branch hits a SetRGActive error, a VIP-release expiry or the registry timeout → the ack comes back `failed`, or no ack arrives within 20 s → the requester returns the error with no marker. Meanwhile the owner's periodic heartbeat carries secondary-hold → the requester's `handlePeerHeartbeat` → `runElection` → electRG "Peer transfer out" → PRIMARY → the requester's daemon installs rg_active and VIPs while the old owner's fence has not landed.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
All at @d1ea69f9aa. pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:488-533: `OnRemoteFailover` calls `d.cluster.ManualFailover(rgID)` (owner goes to secondary-hold), then `ArmRemoteTransferOutLease`, then returns nil. pkg/cluster/sync_failover.go:420-425: `if err := s.WaitFailoverApplied(rgID, reqID); err != nil { ... sendFailoverResult(..., failoverAckFailed, ...); return }`; nothing undoes the owner's demotion. sync_failover.go:122 returns `0, fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for peer failover ack ...")` on timeout, so there is no reqID to bind an abort to. pkg/cluster/failover.go:557-560 has `reqID, err := fn(rgID); if err != nil { return err }`: no `abortedPeerTransferReqID` record and no abort frame. The #15164 marker is written only inside abortRequestedPeerFailover (failover.go:656), and the batch path has the same exit (failover.go:1202-1205). heartbeat_manager.go:550-555 builds the heartbeat with `State: uint8(rg.State)` and no actuation gate, and :825 runs `m.runElection()` on every peer heartbeat. election.go:198-211 has `if peerGroup.State == StateSecondaryHold && !clearedManualFailover { if _, aborted := m.abortedPeerTransferReqID[rg.GroupID]; !aborted { if rg.State != StatePrimary { return electLocalPrimary, "Peer transfer out" } ...` and consults no in-flight request or ack state. Inference: once a secondary-hold heartbeat arrives, the ack verdict cannot change the requester's election outcome.

**Probe:** `cd RUN/wt/b22 && TMPDIR=/var/tmp/vb22 GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run TestVB22AckFailurePromotes -count=1 -v`. Fixture: RUN/verify/vb22/probes/zz_vb22_probe_test.go (data RG1; owner node1 pri 200, primary; requester node0 pri 100; the requester is fed the owner's real `buildHeartbeat()`). Output: RUN/verify/vb22/probes/vb22-r3-b22-01.out. Observed rows: `SUBJECT ack-failed(fence) hb-after | err="peer failed failover request for redundancy group 1: timed out waiting for local fence actuation ..." | ownerWire=secondary-hold | reqPrimary ... afterErr=false afterOwnerHB=true`; `SUBJECT ack-failed(fence) hb-before | ... duringReq=true afterErr=true`, meaning the requester promoted while the fence was still pending; `SUBJECT ack-timeout hb-after | err="timed out waiting for peer failover ack for redundancy group 1" | ... afterOwnerHB=true`. The same results hold under preempt. Positive controls: `CONTROL ack-rejected(no demotion) | ownerWire=primary | ... afterOwnerHB=false | ownerPrimary=true`, which shows that delivering the heartbeat does not by itself promote; and `CONTROL fix-twin ... marker set | ownerWire=secondary-hold | ... afterOwnerHB=false`, which shows the instrument sees the fix direction. The reporter's probes were re-run (RUN/verify/vb22/probes/rerun-reporter-probes.out, RUN/workers/b22/evidence/zz_b22r3_probe_test.go): the DEFECT rows reproduce and the post-ACK-abort control passes. Limits: the sync transport and the daemon fence are not executed, and dataplane overlap is not measured.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Make the ack the real gate or make failure symmetric. (a) While `RequestPeerFailover` holds `failoverInProgress[rg]` and has not received `failoverAckApplied`, electRG must not take "Peer transfer out" for that RG. (b) On every `fn` error exit, single and batch, record the aborted request and send a reqID-bound abort. `SendFailover` should return the reqID on timeout so the abort can be bound. (c) Alternatively or additionally, the owner should undo its own `ManualFailover` (restore, clear the lease) when it downgrades the ack to failed. Correct the #5640/#6177/#6371 comments and docs/session-sync-architecture.md to match. Acceptance: in the vb22 probe, every SUBJECT row reports `afterOwnerHB=false` and `duringReq=false`, with the owner restored to primary; both controls are unchanged. The shipped #15164 and #6371 tests stay green. A shipped regression covers the ack-failed and ack-timeout exits on both the single and batch paths.

- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection is a single owner per RG across an operator transfer, with the old owner fenced (rg_active cleared, VIPs released) before the requester promotes, and an operator-visible outcome that matches the ownership that results. ## #16593 — FragAssoc refuses new associations at the 32-per-session quota and never releases a completed datagram's entry, so one NAT'd fragmented flow is capped at ~16 datagrams/s and starves same-zone sources sharing its shard... [OPEN]

## Summary
FragAssoc refuses new associations at the 32-per-session quota and never releases a completed datagram's entry, so one NAT'd fragmented flow is capped at ~16 datagrams/s and starves same-zone sources sharing its shard (regression of the #11058 fix)

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — conformant, policy-permitted fragmented traffic through any same-family NAT (interface/pool SNAT, DNAT, static NAT, NPTv6) or NAT64 loses the non-first fragments of every datagram above a fixed rate of about 16 datagrams/s per session. The NAT'd tails are dropped fail-closed, so the receiver cannot reassemble. This was demonstrated on the production module. The end-to-end throughput impact is inferred and was not run on the lab. There is no enforcement loss, and the impact is bounded to fragmented traffic.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A74-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va74.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Any client whose fragmented UDP through SNAT/NAT64 exceeds about 16 datagrams/s per session is hit: large-MTU tunnels, NFS/UDP, bulk UDP transfers, and EDNS-heavy resolvers on the reply side. The flow degrades to at most 16 reassemblable datagrams/s for as long as the rate persists. The only visible signal is the generic `nat_frag_untranslated_dropped` / `nat64_frag_dropped`, which the docs attribute to reorder or TTL. Recovery: none while the rate persists.

**Contract:** The `fragment_assoc/mod.rs:1-6` module doc says non-first fragments of an admitted datagram "inherit their translation" / the "admitted no-NAT session decision". The quota (`:49-54`) exists so "a spoofing session cannot spend another session's quota". It is an anti-DoS memory bound, and nothing documents a per-flow rate ceiling. Before ec59234a12 (#11058), the doc said "At its quota, a source replaces its own oldest association", so a busy flow recycled its own completed entries.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
At @d1ea69f9aa: `userspace-dp/src/fragment_assoc/mod.rs:179` `FRAG_CAP_PER_SESSION_PER_SHARD = FRAG_CAP_PER_SHARD / 2` (=32); `:186` per-zone 32; `:190` `FRAG_TTL_NS = 2_000_000_000`. `:443-455` shard index digests only `key.src`, so one flow's associations all land in one shard. `:542-578` at quota: `shard.retain(|e| frag_entry_live(e, now_ns))` then `if session_len >= FRAG_CAP_PER_SESSION_PER_SHARD || zone_len(&shard) >= ... { return false; }` — only EXPIRED entries are reclaimed. `:640-731` `lookup_with_session` removes an entry only on expiry, a dead session, a generation change or an inactive owner RG, and refreshes `deadline_ns` on every hit (`:727`). The FragAssoc API has no completion or MF-based release (method list: `new`, `install_with_session`, `install`[test], `lookup_with_session`, `lookup`[test], `len`). Every return of `install_with_session` is `false` (`:538`, `:578`, `:592`), so the caller's `record_nat64_frag_assoc_evicted()` (poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4083-4108) can never fire and refusals are uncounted. The heads of an existing flow install at the #9950 session-hit tail (poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4060-4108; frag_assoc.rs:224-227 doc "fires at BOTH the new-flow commit AND the session-hit tail").

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — cargo test `va74_frag_assoc_sustained_rate` in the real `xpf-userspace-dp` crate drove `FragAssoc::install_with_session` + `lookup_with_session`. The traffic consequence (NAT discriminator drop) is STATIC.

## #16594 — Interface-level mtu has Junos media-MTU semantics (GE default 1514 = IP 1500) but xpf applies it verbatim as the Linux L3 MTU, giving a 14-byte (18 tagged) larger IP MTU than a Junos peer with the same configured value, with no documented deviation [OPEN]

## Summary

Interface-level mtu has Junos media-MTU semantics (GE default 1514 = IP 1500) but xpf applies it verbatim as the Linux L3 MTU, giving a 14-byte (18 tagged) larger IP MTU than a Junos peer with the same configured value, with no documented deviation

**Finding ID:** `R3-A06-05`
**Severity (source report):** Low. This is a parity mapping error on a core leaf. Large-packet black-holing toward a Junos neighbour is possible only when an explicit value is copied from Junos and the neighbour's media MTU matches it. Default configs are unaffected, and the #16244 refusal already stops jumbo values on bound por…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (Junos interface/protocol-MTU semantics parity and documentation). The mapping is real and undocumented, but the consequence is bounded.

## Mechanism

Config `mtu N` becomes ifc.MTU=N, then netlink LinkSetMTU(N) and networkd MTUBytes=N. A Junos peer with the same `mtu N` has IP MTU N-14.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:177-184` sets `ifc.MTU = n` verbatim. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:253-256` sets `pd.mtu = ifCfg.MTU`. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1827-1831` passes it to networkd MTU (min-folded with the family MTU). `pkg/config/userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727.go:28-31` treats the value as L3 (frame budget minus 14 and 4).

## Impact

Migrated configs with explicit `mtu` lines get a silent 14/18-byte shift. Packets between N-14 and N bytes toward a Junos neighbour are dropped as giants with no PTB.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Either translate (netdev MTU = media MTU − 14 − 4×tags, keeping `family mtu` as L3), or document the L3 meaning in `docs/config-schema.md`/feature-gaps and in the leaf help and #16244 text. Acceptance: `mtu 1514` on an untagged port yields netdev 1500, or the docs and help state the deviation.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper "Media MTU and Protocol MTU" (juniper.net interfaces-fundamentals/media-mtu) says the `[edit interfaces <if>] mtu` is the media MTU, "specified as 1514 bytes" for GE, with a default IP protocol MTU of 1500. `family ... mtu` is the protocol MTU. The xpf README promises native Junos configuration syntax. The schema help (`pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:54-62`) says only "Maximum transmit packet size / MTU in bytes".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A06-05` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

## #16595 — A transient dns-name lookup failure discards the last answer. The userspace policy snapshot is refused as a whole, every strict commit fails, and the zone's kernel junos-host DENY program is silently withdrawn. [OPEN]

## Summary
A transient dns-name lookup failure discards the last answer. The userspace policy snapshot is refused as a whole, every strict commit fails, and the zone's kernel junos-host DENY program is silently withdrawn.

**Finding ID:** R3-N09-01
**Severity (source):** High — High. An external DNS fault, with no operator action, (1) withdraws every `to-zone junos-host` deny program of a zone that references the name. Host services that the zone's `host-inbound-traffic` admits (for example ssh) then become reachable from the sources those denies blocked; this is executed. (2) It makes the helper refuse every later policy snapshot, so feed updates, scheduler edges and other background applies stop being enforced. (3) It blocks every strict commit. (4) On a fresh boot with DNS unavailable, the first snapshot is refused and the node stays on the default-deny PolicyState for all transit; this leg is inferred from the documented #3261 design and was not run end to end.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Any deployment that uses dns-name objects, a feature Junos operators commonly use for SaaS endpoints, couples policy enforcement to the health of a third-party DNS zone. A resolver blip silently opens host services to blocked sources, freezes feed and scheduler enforcement, and blocks operator commits until the name resolves again or the entry is deleted. The outage lasts until the next successful resolution, at the 5-minute tick or the next apply.

**Contract:** `pkg/config/address_forms_15673.go:22-26` says "An unresolvable name yields no usable prefixes (match-none, fail-closed), never an error". `pkg/config/README.md` (#15673 paragraph) says "an unresolvable name matches nothing (fail-closed)". `compiler_validate_warn.go:394-397` warns "it will match nothing until DNS resolves". Per-entry match-none is the documented outcome. Withdrawing a whole to-self deny program, or refusing the whole policy snapshot, is not.

**Trace:** `address X dns-name fqdn` plus a `deny` policy, or a `to-zone junos-host` deny, that references X → compile resolves it (commit OK, no warning) → the resolver later fails → the refresher tick (5 min) or any apply runs `resolveDNSAddressEntry`, which sets `DNSAddresses=nil` → the snapshot rule gets `__unsupported_address__` → the Rust preflight refuses the whole snapshot (a running node keeps previous-good; a fresh boot keeps default-deny) → in the same apply's tail, `BuildJunosHostPrograms` drops the zone program and the kernel `xpf_hostinbound` chain loses the denies.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`address_forms_15673.go:98-101` `ips, err := lookupAddressDNSName(a.DNSName); if err != nil { a.DNSAddresses = nil; return }`. `types_security.go:1919-1921` `if a.DNSName != "" { return append([]string(nil), a.DNSAddresses...) }`. `policies_representable.go:207-215` makes an entry with no usable prefix return `(false,false)`. `policies_lower.go:164-176` turns that into `sourceAddresses/destinationAddresses = []string{unsupportedAddressSentinel}`. In userspace-dp, `src/policy.rs:2844` returns `Err(SnapshotIntegrityError::UnrepresentableAddress{rule_id})`, which fails `PreparedPolicyState::parse_snapshot` (:994-1022) for the whole snapshot. `daemon_dnsaddr.go:159-168` re-applies whenever the answers differ, and a failure-to-nil counts as a difference. `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:150` re-resolves inside every apply. `junos_host_deny_resolve.go:170-174` `if a, ok := ab.Addresses[name]; ok && a != nil && len(a.UsableValues()) == 0 { return true }`. `dataplane/userspace/junos_host_deny.go:68-71` skips programs that are not `Representable`. `daemon_nft.go:862-869` notes that the kernel delivers host-bound packets and userspace-dp never sees them. The nft render (`daemon_apply_tail.go:211`) runs after the core apply even when the dataplane phase errs (`daemon_apply.go:676-809`). The surrounding nft render code has no runtime warning.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestN09DNSName|TestN09Junos' -count=1 -v` with RUN/workers/n09/evidence/zz_n09_dnsname_poison_probe_test.go; rerun saved to RUN/verify/vn09/userspace-rerun.out. Snapshot: control `rules=3 sentinelRules=0 PolicyContentRejected=[]`; SERVFAIL `rules=3 sentinelRules=1 PolicyContentRejected=[policy trust->untrust/block-bad ... destination-address "bad"]`, with the unrelated trust->dmz permit in the same refused snapshot. Strict commit: control `err=<nil>`; resolver down `err=... "block-bad" match destination-address "bad" does not fully resolve`; lenient `err=<nil>`. Junos-host: control `kernel junos-host rules=2 programs=1`; after SERVFAIL `rules=0 programs=0`, with the static `deny-bad 10.0.0.5/32` withdrawn too. Limits: the helper and kernel were not run end to end, and no lab run was made.

## Acceptance / fix direction
On a lookup error, keep the previous `DNSAddresses` (stale-while-error, with an optional max-stale age), and keep "resolver failed" distinct from "name has no addresses". When no answer has ever been obtained, use per-entry match-none, plus a per-rule (not whole-snapshot) fail-closed for deny or excluded sides. A junos-host program should not be withdrawn because of a runtime-empty name. The strict commit gate should warn rather than depend on live DNS. Acceptance: in the probe's SERVFAIL arm, `sentinelRules=0` with the last good prefix retained, the junos-host program still renders `rules=2`, and a strict commit of an unrelated change succeeds while the resolver is down.

- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for a stale-while-error cache or last-known-good retention: there is none, and the DNS state is `json:"-"` runtime state that is never persisted. I looked for a commit-time warning on the junos-host path: the #4168 warning fires only at commit, when the name resolved. I looked for whether helper refusal aborts the nft tail: it does not, because the tail runs after a deferred dataplane error. I checked whether previous-good hides the effect on a running node, and it partly does. I corrected the reporter on two points. - **HPC/invariant check:** One failed lookup changes the enforcement of every rule in the snapshot, not just the rules that reference the name.
