## #16596 — A global policy scoped to one zone resolves address names against that zone's attached or local book, even when the global book has the same name (Junos requires the global book), so the enforced object changes silently and without a warning [OPEN]

## Summary

A global policy scoped to one zone resolves address names against that zone's attached or local book, even when the global book has the same name (Junos requires the global book), so the enforced object changes silently and without a warning

**Finding ID:** `R3-A07-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — a committed global deny or permit enforces a different address set than its authored Junos meaning, and no warning is given. Example: a global `deny BLOCKED` (global BLOCKED = 10.0.0.0/8) shrinks to the trust-attached BLOCKED (10.1.1.1/32) once the policy gains `match from-zone trust`, and …
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the trigger is reachable through strict commit, the consequence is concrete (the wrong address set is enforced), and the claim survived refutation and dedup.

## Mechanism

The `set security policies global policy P match from-zone trust` plus a same-named address in the global book and in the trust-attached book go through `compileSecurity`. Then `resolveNamedAddressBooks15672` folds the attached book into trust's book. Then `resolveZoneLocalAddressBooks` rewrites P's token to `zone-local/trust/BLOCKED`. Then `buildPolicySnapshots` / `classifyPolicyAddresses` give the rule the zone object's book ID. Then the Rust policy matcher enforces 10.1.1.1/32 instead of 10.0.0.0/8. `pkg/policymatch` reads the same folded book, so the simulator agrees and nothing flags the shift.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

In `pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go` @d1ea69f9aa, `rewrite` (:463-477) does `if localDefines(zone, t) { tokens[i] = zoneLocalQualify(zone, t) }` and never checks whether the global book defines `t`. The global loop (:510-517) calls `rewrite(p.Match.FromZones[0], p.Match.SourceAddresses)` when `len(p.Match.FromZones) == 1`, and likewise for ToZones. The comment at :497-508 keeps multi-zone scopes on the global book. `docs/config-schema.md:14029-14042` (#3287) describes only the case where a name is defined only zone-locally. The regression test `pkg/policymatch/scoped_global_zonelocal_test.go` covers only that case too. Observed: a strict compile succeeds with zero warnings. Inferred: operator views unqualify the synthetic key back to the bare name (`DisplayAddressName`), so the book swap is not visible.

## Impact

Anyone migrating vSRX configs that reuse object names across the global book and zone-attached books hits this when a global policy carries a single-zone scope. Adding or removing a second scope zone also changes which object the remaining zone's traffic is judged against. The effect lasts until the operator renames the objects, and no output tells the operator to do so.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Resolve global-policy address tokens against the global book only, per the Junos rule. A scoped-global token defined only in a zone book should be a strict commit error and a tolerant-load warning plus quarantine, which replaces the #3287 acceptance; this needs a deliberate update to `scoped_global_zonelocal_test.go` and to the docs/config-schema.md #3287 section. If the zone-local extension is kept on purpose, a same-name collision in a single-zone scoped global must at least be a strict commit error. Acceptance: the probe's `scope="trust"` row resolves to 10.0.0.0/8 (or the commit fails), matching the unscoped and multi-zone rows; zone-pair rows are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper, *Address Books and Address Sets* (fetched 2026-10-23): "Addresses used in a global policy must be defined in global address book." and "Global address book objects do not belong to any particular zone." The rule that "Addresses in a user-defined address book have a higher lookup priority than addresses in the global address book" applies to zone-scoped lookup. xpf states it only for zone-pair policies (`pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go:308-313`; `pkg/config/README.md:875-883`).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A07-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A07-01 | Medium | A global policy scoped to one zone resolves address names against that zone's attached or… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:57: - **R3-A07-01 — MATERIAL (Medium; intended match object silently changes).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go:464-480,494-519` rewrites a *single-zone scoped global* policy's token to that zone's local book even if an identically named global-book entry exists. [Juniper's address-books and sets documentation](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/security-policies/topics/topic-map/security-address-books-sets.html) says global policies refer to global-book entries. Historical probe used an attached named book and different global same-name object to show a changed address match. **Refutation:** xpf intentionally added local-only references for scoped globals (#3287), and local policy resolution is expected; parity only forces a distinction in the shadowed/global-twin case, not removal of all scoped local support. The original inline zone-book test was invalid Junos spelling; rely on the corrected attached-book case. **Decisive check:** strict-compile and snapshot-match global-only, local-only and same-name global/local fixtures for one-zone and multi-zone scoped global policies; choose explicit precedence/diagnostic.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L211: ### R3-A07-01 — single-zone-scoped global policy resolves names zone-first even when global book defines name — **MATERIAL** - Defect: `compiler_security_addressbook.go:463-477 rewrite` checks `localDefines(zone,t)` never global definition; `:510-517` applies for `len(FromZones)==1` (multi-zone stays global — internal inconsistency proving scope sensitivity). Junos: global-policy addresses must be in global book; same name in different books is legal Junos. Global deny BLOCKED 10.0.0.0/8 shrinks to trust-attached 10.1.1.1/32 silently (warnings=0); reverse widens permit. Policymatch simulator reads same folded book → no surface disagrees. - Refutation: Needs same-name collision across books + single-zone scope; reporter fixture (inline zone book + global) is Junos-refused shape — verifier correctly re-established with named attached-book shape Junos accepts. #3287 deliberately adopted zone-local resolution for scoped globals but only decided/tested the zone-local-only case; global-twin shadowing undecided there — residual, not overturning decided intent wholesale. Fix needs deliberate #3287 test/doc update (flagged). - Evidence: `localDefines` rewrite at origin/master (`:477` region) consistent. Executed strict compile + `buildPolicySnapshots`: scoped row → zone-local prefixes, unscoped/multi-zone → global. - Unresolved: Rust on-wire enforcement of snapshot prefixes (assumed from snapshot; other lanes cover matcher). --- ## va08

## #16597 — R3-A40-06: The device DHCID marker published under skip-existing/strict-fail has no owner and no delete path, and permanently burns the name for single-family and other-client… [OPEN]

## Summary

The device DHCID marker published under skip-existing/strict-fail has no owner and no delete path, and permanently burns the name for single-family and other-client claims

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — this needs a non-default conflict policy. The name is unclaimable by its own device returning single-stack, or by any later client, until manual zone cleanup. Refusals are counted as third-party conflicts. A dual-stack return still succeeds because the marker proves the sibling. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A40-06`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va40.md` (finding `R3-A40-06`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

backend_rfc2136.go:941-960, where a successful skip-existing add with a sibling candidate does `mark.Insert([]dns.RR{sib})` (:955) and tracks it only in the updater. :1336-1341 non-replace-owned deletes take `u.sendRemove` (:1340), an exact A/AAAA delete with no marker. :929-933 a claim with no proven sibling uses `m.NameNotUsed`, which the lone DHCID fails.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** backend_rfc2136.go:885-888 "skip-existing never writes a DHCID". :945-951 "The marker is a normal DHCID RR; a delete under these policies never replays a DHCID prerequisite, so it cannot poison a later delete". The sole-delete-authority contract says xpf removes what it created.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (#14995 device-DHCID lifecycle residuals, grouped with R3-A40-05) — real, bounded, non-default policy.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the stateful RFC 2136 fake under skip-existing.

**Confidence:** High — executed with a single-stack positive control.

## Impact

Operators who chose skip-existing to avoid claiming foreign names end up with xpf's own leftover acting as the "pre-existing" owner, permanently, with the conflict counter blaming a third party.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Track the marker with the owned records, or delete it value-specifically when the last same-name family of that device is withdrawn under skip-existing/strict-fail. Acceptance: the dual-stack probe row ends with no RR at the name and the re-claim is not refused; the #14995 hijack cells stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A40-06`, part `parts/va40.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16598 — deny-configuration / allow-configuration adjudicate a flat `set` (and flat `load set`/`load merge`) line as one joined path, but the store splits it into several statements at schema arity; a deny on a later statement is bypassed, so a... [OPEN]

## Summary
deny-configuration / allow-configuration adjudicate a flat `set` (and flat `load set`/`load merge`) line as one joined path, but the store splits it into several statements at schema arity; a deny on a later statement is bypassed, so a restricted class commits a super-user login or root-authentication change

**Finding ID:** R3-B23-01
**Severity (source):** High — loss of a configured privileged-authority boundary: a class with `configure` permission whose `deny-configuration` fences `system login` (anchored `^system login` or the plain substring `system login`) commits a new `login user … class super-user` account with a usable password, or a `root-authentication` change. Demonstrated end to end through the on-box CLI dispatcher, store and commit; gRPC/REST/event-engine reach the same gate and store call statically. Bounded by the prerequisite that a super-user authored such a restricted class, which is exactly the population the feature exists to contain.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
delegated/limited admin classes are exactly where a narrow `deny-configuration` fences `system login`/`root-authentication`; the bypass lets such a principal mint a super-user or reset root, i.e. take full control of the appliance (and, through config sync, both HA nodes). It is silent: the gate logged an allow and the journal records the operator's own line. Recovery requires noticing the rogue account. Applies to CLI, remote CLI, REST, flat `load set`/`load merge`, and event-options then-commands authored by a restricted plant class (static).

**Contract:** docs/system-login.md:446-450 says all four regex sub-statements are enforced on every dispatch surface, and :1079-1081 says deny/allow-configuration "apply to the configuration that takes effect, not only to the literal line typed"; :1049-1062 says `load merge`/`load set` content is "rendered to `set` lines" and each matched. The #9938 F-029 rule in authz_config_mutation_9154.go:477-481 is that "EVERY acted-upon path is adjudicated". A line that the store executes as two statements is two acted-upon paths.

**Trace:** class `limited` = `permissions [configure view]; deny-configuration "^system login"` → operator types `set system domain-search attacker.example login user evil class super-user` → `checkConfigRegex` → `AuthorizeConfigMutation` → `configMutationPaths` returns one joined path → `Evaluate` allows → `SetFromInputAsPlantClass` → `SetPathQuotedGrouped` writes `system domain-search attacker.example` AND `system login user evil class super-user` → `commit` (no per-statement re-adjudication for a group-free candidate) → active config contains a new super-user account → login/auth subsystems consume it.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:185` (set/delete fall-through) `return []string{resolve(parts[1:])}, true` — one joined string; `:480-492` `for _, path := range paths { decision := rules.Evaluate(path) …` — only that string is matched. `pkg/configstore/store_command.go:104-109` `SetFromInputAsPlantClass` → `config.ParseSetVerbGroupedClosed("set " + input)` → `:84 s.candidate.SetPathQuotedGrouped(...)`. `pkg/config/schema_system.go:85` `"domain-search": {… args: 1, multi: true, … allChildKeysAreValues: true}` — the leaf closes after its value and the next keyword (`login`) becomes a sibling of `domain-search` under `system`. Flat load: `pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go:252-260` returns the raw flat lines (only the hierarchical branch :262-271 renders through `tree.FormatSet()`). Executors: `pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:560`, `pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:201`, `pkg/api/config.go:177`, `pkg/eventengine/engine.go:1418` all call `SetFromInputAsPlantClass`; gates at `pkg/cli/permissions_config_regex.go:96`, `pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:59`, `pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:284`, `pkg/eventengine/engine.go:1356` all call `AuthorizeConfigMutation` on the line. Observation: the joined string for `set system domain-search attacker.example login user evil class super-user` is `system domain-search attacker.example login user evil class super-user`; neither `^system login` nor `system login` matches it.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cli/ -run TestVB23 -count=1 -v` with `RUN/verify/vb23/probes/zz_vb23_split_bypass_probe_test.go` (output `cli-e2e-rerun.out`, `cli-e2e-auth.out`): for deny `^system login` and `system login`, `set system login user evil class super-user` alone → `permission denied … denies set under "system"`; the split line → `err=<nil>`; `commit` → nil; ActiveConfig has `user evil class="super-user"`, and with a split `authentication encrypted-password` line `encpw-set=true` (a usable account). Positive control: deny `login` (substring present in the joined string) refuses the split line and the active config has no `evil`. `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestB23|TestVB23'` (`config-rerun.out`, probes `zz_vb23_load_probe_test.go`, `zz_vb23_allow_probe_test.go`, reporter's `RUN/workers/b23/evidence/zz_b23_multileaf_authz_probe_test.go`): `AuthorizeConfigLoad` mode set/merge on the flat split line → nil while the lone line → denied and the hierarchical form → denied; `allow-configuration "^system domain-search"` class: out-of-scope line alone → denied, split line → nil (allowlist mirror). `TestVB23SplitShapes` shows `set system domain-search a.example root-authentication plain-text-password-value x` lands as a separate `set system root-authentication …` statement (store split shown; a `^system root-authentication` deny bypass is inferred by the same mechanism, not separately executed). Limits: not exercised over a live gRPC/REST listener or on a VM.

## Acceptance / fix direction
adjudicate the executed statements rather than the input line: apply the parsed line to a scratch clone of the relevant subtree (the same `SetPathQuotedGrouped` the store runs) and match every resulting set-line (`FormatSet` diff) against the regexes, refusing the whole line on any denial; route flat `load set`/`load merge` through the same rendering that the hierarchical branch already uses. Acceptance: under `deny-configuration "^system login"` and `"system login"`, `set system domain-search x login user evil class super-user` is refused on CLI, gRPC and REST and via flat `load set`; `set system domain-search x` alone still succeeds; an `allow-configuration "^system domain-search"` class is refused the split line.

## #16599 — OverlapTracker's per-sender quota counts abandoned (tail-lost) datagrams for the full 30 s TTL, so a conformant sender with modest upstream fragment loss has most of its new fragmented datagrams ShardFull-dropped [OPEN]

## Summary
OverlapTracker's per-sender quota counts abandoned (tail-lost) datagrams for the full 30 s TTL, so a conformant sender with modest upstream fragment loss has most of its new fragmented datagrams ShardFull-dropped

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — this is fail-closed loss of permitted fragmented traffic for the whole sender, across all of its destinations, because the quota key is `(routing_domain, family, src)`. It is driven by ordinary loss or by the firewall's own tail drops, not by an attacker. The module behaviour is demonstrated; the real-world loss and rate mix is inferred. There is no enforcement loss.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A74-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va74.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=NEEDS_VALIDATION/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Any sender with lossy access and a fragmented UDP workload (VPN-over-UDP with large inner MTU, NFS/UDP, large DNS, video) is hit, as is any NAT'd flow already pushed over R3-A74-01's ceiling. The blast radius is the sender's fragmented traffic to every destination, plus its zone's per-shard reserve. It lasts 30 s after the loss stops.

**Contract:** `fragment_overlap/mod.rs:38-42`: "one sender ... holds at most 8 incomplete entries per shard ... Completed entries ... do not consume a sender's incomplete-datagram quota, avoiding modest-rate refusal of conformant completed traffic" (#13937). The quota exists against never-completing attack fill (#10658). The 30 s TTL is justified by Linux `ipfrag_time` (`:30-37`). A receiver drops such datagrams after its own timer, but it does not refuse the sender's new datagrams.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
At @d1ea69f9aa: `userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs:175` `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_SENDER_PER_SHARD: usize = 8`; `:183` `OVERLAP_TTL_NS = 30_000_000_000`. `:419-441` `overlap_entry_counts_for_sender_quota` returns false only for `overlap_entry_complete`, so head-only, pending and failed entries all count. `:291-311` the shard digest is `(family, src, dst, ident)`, so a sender's entries spread over 16 shards: 16 × 8 = 128 live abandoned entries ÷ 30 s ≈ 4.3/s. `:955-978` `if sender_entries >= OVERLAP_CAP_PER_SENDER_PER_SHARD { FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED...; return ... ShardFull }`, which returns before the zone/shard reclaims (`:979+`). Those reclaim only completed anchors, or another zone's incomplete ones (#15288), never the sender's own. A refused head's tail builds the same key, misses, and is refused the same way.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — cargo test `va74_overlap_sender_quota_under_loss` drove `OverlapTracker::check_and_record_fragment_detailed` + `commit_admission` exactly as the TX record site settles them. The production call site was read statically.

## #16600 — A source-NAT rule whose source match is single-family but whose pool has no member of that family (IPv6-only pool, or an IPv4-mapped `::ffff:` literal, for an IPv4 rule; or the reverse) commits clean; every matching flow is refused at runtime as… [OPEN]

## Summary

A source-NAT rule whose source match is single-family but whose pool has no member of that family (IPv6-only pool, or an IPv4-mapped `::ffff:` literal, for an IPv4 rule; or the reverse) commits clean; every matching flow is refused at runtime as WrongAddressFamily

**Finding ID:** `R3-A08-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — fail-closed: matching flows are refused by the allocator and counted. The commit is silent while the rule can never translate, and the #13922 DNAT twin is rejected. Operator-error trigger. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (NAT strict-commit gates that admit a rule which can never act as authored; with R3-A08-04, R3-A04-01 and b09's v4-mapped static/DNAT literal item) — real and fail-closed, the same corrective class as #13922.

## Mechanism

`pool P address 2001:db8::5` + `rule r1 match source-address 10.0.0.0/24 then source-nat pool P` -> strict clean -> SourceNATRuleSnapshot with a v6-only pool -> Rust rule.pool_addresses_v4 empty -> a v4 flow matches r1 -> WrongAddressFamily -> the packet is not forwarded (allocation-failure exception).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator/mod.rs:2760-2763 `let family_len = family_addresses.len(); if family_len == 0 { return Err(...WrongAddressFamily); }`. nat/source/match_rules.rs:1121-1126 `SourceNatLookup::Unavailable(... WrongAddressFamily)`. nat/source/mod.rs:1482-1489 (the v4 source with empty `pool_addresses_v4`). nat/source/expand.rs:137+ splits members by `IpAddr` variant, so `::ffff:192.0.2.1` lands in the v6 list. Go: no family check on the SNAT pool path (probe).

## Impact

a dual-stack migration that points a v4 rule at the v6 pool gets a clean commit and an outage of that rule's traffic, discoverable only through allocation-failure counters.

## Acceptance / fix direction

in the strict SNAT pool gate, reject a pool-mode rule whose authored source-address set is single-family F when the referenced pool has zero family-F members (warn on tolerant load). Use the colon-strict #13922 classifier and treat v4-mapped/compat literals per the #10686 identity rule. Acceptance: the three va08 DEFECT rows reject, while the control, a dual-family pool and an unconstrained rule still commit.

## Contract (where cited)

#13922 (CLOSED) made strict commit reject cross-family DNAT pools and static host pairs because they commit as a broken service (compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:540-552 "address family mismatch"). The SNAT pool path has no equivalent.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A08-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A08-02 | Low | A source-NAT rule whose source match is single-family but whose pool has no member of that… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:62: - **R3-A08-02 — COHORT (Low).** **Defect:** a single-family source-NAT rule can compile with an opposite-family-only pool; `userspace-dp/src/nat/source/match_rules.rs:946-948,1502-1507` then returns `Unavailable(WrongAddressFamily)` on a matching flow, whereas the relevant strict NAT validator (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go`) does not pair source match family to pool members. **Refutation:** an unconstrained/mixed-family rule can legitimately use pools covering both families; fail-unavailable is safer than translating to the wrong family and the actual traffic consequence depends on egress policy. **Decisive check:** source/pool family matrix, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 parsing and the rule's `off` cases, rejecting only single-family impossible rules.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L227: ### R3-A08-02 — SNAT pool family mismatch commits; runtime WrongAddressFamily — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: No SNAT-pool family gate (DNAT/static twin rejected #13922); v6-only or `::ffff:`-mapped pool for v4 rule (reverse too) strict-commits, lenient silent → Rust allocator empty family list → `WrongAddressFamily` refusal per flow (allocator/mod.rs sites at origin/master confirmed). Fail-closed, counted. - Refutation: Operator error; NAT46 designs use cross-family intentionally in Junos — no parity claim made; xpf cannot execute shape, so silent commit is the defect. Correctly cohorted. - Evidence: Rust refusal sites grep-confirmed at origin/master; #13922 gate text re-read. Report executed strict/lenient probe + DNAT twin control. - Unresolved: None decisive; single-family determination must handle unconstrained/dual rules (fix acceptance). ### R3-A08-04 — duplicate SNAT rule-set contexts commit; later exemption shadowed — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: No gate compares normalised (from,to) contexts across source-NAT rule-sets (dup gates key on name/rule-name; off-shadow is DNAT-only); snapshots stable-sorted by tier only (`nat_source.go:359`) → config-order concatenation, first-match (#4161) → later `source-nat off` exemption unreachable. Juniper text: cannot specify same source/destination conditions for source NAT rule sets. - Refutation: xpf #4161 comment asserts definition-order as designed within-tier behaviour — deliberate divergence from Junos, so this challenges docume

**Wonder:** wonder batch00 L47: | R3-A08-03 | MATERIAL | MATERIAL | Medium | High | STATIC | | R3-A08-02 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A08-04 | COHORT | COHORT | Low | High | STATIC | | R3-A08-01 | DUP of gemini-002 G43-04 (pool-SNAT leg matches; scope checked) | DUP | — | Medium | STATIC |

## #16601 — dns-name entries are resolved serially (5 s cap each) during compile while the configstore write lock is held, and again under applySem during apply, so a slow resolver stalls every ActiveConfig() reader, including HA readiness. [OPEN]

## Summary
dns-name entries are resolved serially (5 s cap each) during compile while the configstore write lock is held, and again under applySem during apply, so a slow resolver stalls every ActiveConfig() reader, including HA readiness.

**Finding ID:** R3-N09-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium. A blackholed resolver holds the global config write lock for names × 5 s × compiles per commit; a cluster commit compiles 3 times, and SyncApply on the standby does the same. Meanwhile every `ActiveConfig()` reader blocks: HA VIP readiness, VRRP reconcile, HA sync, gRPC show, and the commit RPC. The cost is bounded and needs dns-name entries plus a slow resolver; no enforcement is lost. The stall was demonstrated at 40 ms per lookup; the 5 s figure is the production cap.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
While a resolver stalls, a commit or a peer sync can park HA readiness and VRRP reconcile readers for tens of seconds or more (10 names × 5 s × 3 compiles = 150 s). That delays promotion and failover handling and freezes every show and commit RPC.

**Contract:** The project's control-plane serialisation rules (CLAUDE.md "Control socket contention", docs/engineering-style.md) and the #9913/#9326/#14613 precedents say external resolution must be bounded and must not run on a shared serialisation point. #15962's own design ("resolution runs outside the lock") states the same intent for the refresher.

**Trace:** commit/SyncApply → `s.mu.Lock` → compileTreeStrict/Lenient (local view plus peer views) → `applyDNSName` → `net.DefaultResolver.LookupIPAddr` (5 s each, serial) → every reader blocked in `RLock`. Then apply → applySem → `RefreshDNSAddressBooks` (serial again).

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`address_forms_15673.go:33-36` creates a new `context.WithTimeout(..., 5*time.Second)` per name. `applyDNSName` (:310-319) resolves during compile, and `RefreshDNSAddressBooks` (:118-141) loops sequentially. `configstore/store_commit.go:187-188` `s.mu.Lock(); defer s.mu.Unlock()` precedes the strict compile. `store.go:1113-1115` takes Lock and :1162 calls `compileTreeLenient` (SyncApply). `store_format.go:241-245` `ActiveConfig` takes `s.mu.RLock()`. `daemon_ha_vip.go:25` `checkVIPReadiness` calls `d.store.ActiveConfig()`. `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:150` re-resolves under applySem, including for the refresher's clone, which was already resolved outside the lock at `daemon_dnsaddr.go:159`.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestN09 -count=1 -v` with RUN/workers/n09/evidence/zz_n09_dns_commit_lock_probe_test.go; rerun saved to RUN/verify/vn09/lock-rerun.out. Control, 0 names: `lookups=0 commit=14ms max ActiveConfig() wait=12ms`. Standalone, 5 names: `lookups=5 commit=239ms wait=237ms`. Cluster node0, 5 names: `lookups=15 commit=649ms wait=649ms`. Userspace probe: 20 names gives a compile of `lookups=20 1.005s` and an apply-path refresh of `lookups=20 1.004s`. Limits: the 5 s production timeout and the HA consequence are extrapolated.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Resolve outside every lock with a bounded worker pool and an aggregate deadline. Compile should read a daemon-owned answer cache and perform no network I/O. The refresher's resolved clone should be applied without being resolved again. Acceptance: the probe's commit time and `ActiveConfig()` wait do not depend on lookup latency (0 lookups under the lock).

## #16602 — Both CLIs' `load merge|set|override` ignore every token after the source, including the Junos `relative` modifier. A snippet meant for the `[edit ...]` cursor is applied at the root, reported as `load <mode> complete`, and commits clean... [OPEN]

## Summary
Both CLIs' `load merge|set|override` ignore every token after the source, including the Junos `relative` modifier. A snippet meant for the `[edit ...]` cursor is applied at the root, reported as `load <mode> complete`, and commits clean whenever it is also valid at the root (for example a VRF default route that becomes a master-table route).

**Finding ID:** R3-B24-01
**Severity (source):** Low — an operator who types documented Junos syntax gets a different, equally valid hierarchy: a `routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0` meant for `[edit routing-instances RI1]` installs in the master table, and a group body pasted under `[edit groups G1]` applies device-wide. This is bounded. It is operator-triggered, only snippets that are valid at the root land silently (others fail commit), and the whole-tree `show | compare` shows the change. Demonstrated at the compiled-config boundary. [reporter: Low (upper); Medium if `relative` is in routine use]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
`load merge terminal relative` is the usual Junos way to paste a snippet into a routing-instance, group or policy context. Here a VRF route leaks into the master table, or a group body becomes a global change, and the success message gives no hint. Recovery is a rollback, once someone notices.

**Contract:** The Junos `load` reference (juniper.net junos12.3 command-summary/load.html, re-fetched) gives the syntax as `load (factory-default | merge | override | patch | replace | set | update) (filename | terminal) <relative>`. It defines relative as "(Optional) Use the merge or replace option without specifying the full hierarchy level", and otherwise "Your current location in the configuration hierarchy is ignored". xpf claims native Junos syntax (CLAUDE.md). The module refuses extra args on `load rescue` ("no source or extra arguments are accepted"), so a modifier it does not implement should be refused, not dropped.

**Trace:** `edit routing-instances RI1` → `load merge terminal relative` → handleLoad (mode=merge, source=terminal, `relative` dropped) → AuthorizeConfigLoad on the root content → LoadMerge at the root → `load merge complete` → commit check nil → compiled RoutingOptions.StaticRoutes=1 and RI1 routes=0 → FRR master-table default route.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/cli/cli_config.go:182-190 has `mode := args[0]` … `source := args[1]`, and args[2:] is never read. :271-289 apply via LoadSetAsPlantClass/LoadMergeAsPlantClass/LoadOverrideAsPlantClass, none of which takes the edit path. cmd/cli/main.go:628-669 has the same `mode := args[0]`, `source := args[1]` and sends `pb.LoadRequest{Mode, Content}` with no path field. cmd/cli/main.go:620-622 and the console rescue arm refuse extra arguments for `rescue` only.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b24/evidence/zz_b24_probe_loadrel_test.go and zz_b24_probe_loadrel2_test.go, re-run in RUN/verify/vb24/rerun-pkgcli.out. The control, `set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 192.0.2.1` under `[edit routing-instances RI1]`, gives `set routing-instances RI1 routing-options static route …`, commitCheckErr=nil, masterStatic=0, RI1Static=1. The defect arm, `load merge terminal relative`, gives `set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 192.0.2.1`, commitCheckErr=nil, masterStatic=1, RI1Static=0, and `load set terminal relative` gives the same. `load merge terminal bogus trailing tokens` prints `load merge complete`. Positive control for the guard shape: RUN/verify/vb24/probe-cursor-misc.out has `load rescue relative` → `load rescue: no source or extra arguments are accepted`. Limit: dataplane route installation is inferred from the compiled StaticRoutes.

## Acceptance / fix direction
On both CLIs, refuse any token after the source (`load: unexpected argument "relative"`). Or implement `relative` by prefixing the normalised cursor: wrap the hierarchical content, or prefix each set line, add a path field to LoadRequest, and have the server gate price the prefixed lines. Acceptance: the probe's defect rows either error with nothing loaded, or give RI1Static=1 and masterStatic=0, on both surfaces.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb24.md)</summary>

- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for an arity guard on merge/set/override and found one only on rescue. I checked whether `relative` reaches the server: LoadRequest has no field for it. The reporter said the scoped compare at the cursor (`[no changes]`) "lies". I narrowed that: it is correct scoping, because nothing changed under RI1, and the whole-tree compare shows the root change. Snippets not valid at the root (for example `static { … }` under `[edit routing-options]`) fail commit, so the silent case is limited to root-valid snippets.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — interactive config load path, no hot path.

## #16603 — For Prebuilt transit frames (embedded-ICMP NAT reversal, including NAT64), the #15251 mirror arm in `enqueue_pending_forwards` clones the already translated egress frame. The analyzer of the mirrored input therefore r... [OPEN]

## Summary
For Prebuilt transit frames (embedded-ICMP NAT reversal, including NAT64), the #15251 mirror arm in `enqueue_pending_forwards` clones the already translated egress frame. The analyzer of the mirrored input therefore receives a packet that never crossed that wire: the internal post-reversal address, the firewall's egress MACs and VLAN, a decremented TTL, and for NAT64 the other IP family. Every Live/Owned arm mirrors the received bytes instead.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — this is analyzer fidelity only. Forwarding, filtering and enforcement are unaffected, and the traffic class is rare (ICMP errors quoting NAT'd flows, Packet-Too-Big toward an SNAT pool). The demonstrated consequence is an internal inconsistency: for one NAT'd flow, the analyzer gets data packets pre-NAT and the flow's ICMP errors post-NAT, with L2 and VLAN identity from the egress side. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A75-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va75.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
An IDS or forensics capture on the outside port of a NAT edge sees inside addressing and egress L2/VLAN attributed to the outside port. It cannot match the error with the upstream router's real frame (TTL, MACs, VLAN and family differ), and NAT64 errors appear in the wrong family. The blast radius is small (rare ICMP class), and the defect persists as long as the configuration stays unchanged. There is no data-plane recovery issue.

**Contract:** docs/pr/1373-retire-ebpf-dataplane/plan-1376-port-mirroring.md:76 says "The mirrored bytes are the full original Ethernet frame, including VLAN tags and IPv4/IPv6 payload". The runtime-slice text says the dataplane "mirrors forwarded packets while the original frame bytes are still available". The Live arm implements this: tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1365-1373 stages `source_frame` (ingress UMEM), and :1618-1620 snapshots it before `rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place`.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs:1175-1178 @d1ea69f9aa: "the mirror clone must carry the rewritten wire frame ... `let mirror_frame = prebuilt.clone();`". The :1193-1201 comment says "The frame bytes are the already-rewritten wire frame". :1240-1264 calls `stage_sampled_mirror_clone(..., &mirror_frame, mirror_meta, ...)` and then `commit_staged_mirror_clone(..., &mirror_frame, ...)`. poll_descriptor/embedded_icmp.rs:442 queues `PendingForwardFrame::Prebuilt(rewritten_frame)`. tx/dispatch/tests/prebuilt_mirror_15251.rs:121-155 asserts "the mirror clone must carry the rewritten (NAT64) wire frame". The ingress frame is still readable at this point, because `recycle_ingress_frame` runs after the commit (:1266). Inference: the received bytes were available and were not used.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `prebuilt_nat64_frame_is_mirrored_15251`, which asserts clone == rewritten NAT64 wire frame, and the Live/neighbor control `retry_pending_neighbor_mirrors_original_frame_before_rewrite`, which asserts clone == original pre-rewrite frame, were both run at d1ea69f9aa through temporary zz_va75 wrappers. The lab analyzer view is STATIC.

## #16604 — NAT `from|to routing-instance default` is admitted as a defined scope by the #15278 gate, but nothing maps "default" to the dataplane's empty-string master-instance value, so every such SNAT/DNAT/static/NAT64 rule-set commits clean and never matches [OPEN]

## Summary

NAT `from|to routing-instance default` is admitted as a defined scope by the #15278 gate, but nothing maps "default" to the dataplane's empty-string master-instance value, so every such SNAT/DNAT/static/NAT64 rule-set commits clean and never matches

**Finding ID:** `R3-A08-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — an operator who names the master instance explicitly, as is usual in VRF-aware NAT (`from routing-instance cust-a to routing-instance default`), gets a rule-set that is inert. The consequences: SNAT never translates (main-instance egress leaves with untranslated internal sources, so connect…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable trigger (a spelling the strict gate deliberately admits and a test pins as a must-compile control) with a concrete consequence (the NAT rule-set never acts, with no error or warning).

## Mechanism

`set security nat source rule-set out to routing-instance default` -> SchemaValidate OK -> natUndefinedScopeOffenders skips "default" -> strict commit clean -> SourceNATRuleSnapshot.ToRoutingInstance="default" -> Rust SourceNatRule.to_routing_instance="default" -> NatScopeCtx.egress_routing_instance="" for a main-instance egress -> scope_matches false -> SourceNatLookup::NoMatch (untranslated). In parallel, the maps_sync registration scope's toRoutingInstance "default" never equals the interface's "", so the egress address gets no interface-NAT/RST registration.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:197-199 `func natRoutingInstanceDefined15278(cfg *Config, name string) bool { if name == "" || name == "default" { return true }` (callers :218-246 and the tolerant twin :262-298). pkg/config/nat_cohort_15278_test.go:137 `"set security nat source rule-set snat-ok to routing-instance default"` sits in the "control %d must compile strict" list. Go copies the string verbatim into the snapshots (observed in the probe: `ToRoutingInstance="default"`, `FromRoutingInstance="default"`). Rust: afxdp/forwarding/nat.rs:47-52 `forwarding.ifindex_to_routing_instance.get(&ifindex).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("")`. forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:856-868 stores `iface.routing_instance` from the snapshot, and pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:482-506 leaves `RoutingInstance` empty for interfaces not claimed by a routing instance. Matchers: nat/source/mod.rs:1106-1114 `if !self.to_routing_instance.is_empty() && self.to_routing_instance != scope.egress_routing_instance { return false; }`, nat/destination.rs:147-151 `scope_ok`, nat64/state.rs:1446-1452. The only Rust non-test "default" routing-instance literal is pbr.rs:62 (FBF). Inference: no NAT path normalises the name.

## Impact

VRF-aware NAT configs routinely name both sides. The master-instance side silently disables the whole rule-set: outbound SNAT goes untranslated, published services are unreachable, and nothing on commit, show or logs says why. Recovery: rewrite with zone/interface scopes.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Either strict-reject `routing-instance default` in NAT scopes with an operator message ("use a zone or interface scope, or omit"), warning on tolerant load, or carry an explicit master-instance token through compile and wire and make the Rust scope context emit it for main-instance interfaces, in SNAT/DNAT/static/NAT64 and the Go registration together. Acceptance: the va08 Rust cell's `rule=default egress=main` matches and `rule=default egress=VR1` does not, or the strict commit rejects. The zone control and named-VRF scopes are unchanged, and nat_cohort_15278_test.go:137 is updated deliberately.

## Contract (where cited)

#15278 (CLOSED, fix 41c18d7deb, an ancestor of the base) exists so that a NAT scope the dataplane can never match does not commit inert. Its commit body lists "Defined scopes, default RI" as intentionally accepted, so xpf asserts that `routing-instance default` is a meaningful NAT scope. pkg/config/routinginstance_reserved_name_9622.go:8-12 documents "default" as Juniper's alias for the global/master table, and FBF honours it (#11308; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/pbr.rs:62). I could not confirm from Juniper documentation how the literal `default` behaves in NAT `from routing-instance`, so this entry rests on xpf's own contract, not on a vSRX parity claim.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A08-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

## #16605 — R3-A41-01: The gRPC command gate charges GetIPsecSA, ShowInterfacesDetail, ShowRollback/ShowCompare/ListHistory, GetGlobalStats, GetVRRPStatus, GetNATPoolStats and… [OPEN]

## Summary

The gRPC command gate charges GetIPsecSA, ShowInterfacesDetail, ShowRollback/ShowCompare/ListHistory, GetGlobalStats, GetVRRPStatus, GetNATPoolStats and GetNATDestination one fixed canonical command each. The remote cli sends them for lines in a different command path (`show security ike security-associations`, `show interfaces [<name>|terse]`, `show system rollback ...`, `show security statistics`, `show security vrrp`, `show security nat source|destination summary`). As a result, a path-scoped `deny-commands` on the typed line is not enforced for remote users. For three realistic patterns the commit advisory says nothing.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the impact is read disclosure of view-tier data to a login class that is explicitly configured to be denied it, on the remote cli. That is the only surface restricted SSH users reach (their login shell is the remote cli, #10833). The data is IKE/IPsec SA names, states and peer addresses, the interface table, prior rollback configurations (redacted) and diffs, global flow statistics, VRRP state, and NAT pool summaries. There is no write, no secret disclosure and no privilege gain. The rating matches the round-2 parent (#15076, Medium). The rows where the #8189 advisory fires are loud fail-opens and would be Low on their own. The Medium rests on the silent rows. The reverse over-deny (allowlist lockout) is also present and is a bounded availability nuisance. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A41-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va41.md` (finding `R3-A41-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_table.go:63` `"GetGlobalStats": "show security flow statistics"`, :70 `"GetNATDestination": "show security nat destination pool"`, :74 `"ShowInterfacesDetail": "show interfaces detail"`, :78 `"GetIPsecSA": "show security ipsec security-associations"`, :79 `"GetNATPoolStats": "show security nat source pool"`, :83-86 ShowCompare/ShowRollback `"show configuration"`, ListHistory `"show system commit history"`, GetVRRPStatus `"show vrrp"`. `authz_command_gate_7172.go:270-300` `rpcCanonicalCommand` decodes only ShowText/SystemAction/GetSystemInfo/GetBGPStatus/GetNATRuleStats and otherwise returns the fixed string. Call sites: `cmd/cli/show_security.go:184-185,995-1007` (`case "ike"` → `showIKE` → `c.client.GetIPsecSA` when args[0]=="security-associations"), :179-181,945-946 (`statistics` → GetGlobalStats), :189 (`vrrp`); `cmd/cli/show_nat.go:31-32,254-255` (source summary → GetNATPoolStats), :90-91,407-408 (destination summary → GetNATDestination); `cmd/cli/show_interfaces.go:53-63,88-90` (no modifier or `terse` → ShowInterfacesDetail); `cmd/cli/show_system.go:40-105` (rollback compare/`| compare` → ShowCompare, `rollback N` → ShowRollback, bare → ListHistory). The handler `pkg/grpcapi/server_routing.go:379-399` GetIPsecSA renders SA name/state/local/remote. Observation: all call sites exist as cited. Inference: the over-deny leg also affects allowlist classes.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_gate_7172.go:43-45` @d1ea69f9aa says "a deny written against a command PATH — `deny-commands \"request system reboot\"` … — is enforced IDENTICALLY on both surfaces". Only ARGUMENT-text denies are documented as on-box-only (:46-49). Round-2 A41-01/#15076 fix direction: "the RPC's canonical command is a keyword prefix of that line's canonical form" for every cli call site. Junos `deny-commands` matches the operational command text, so `deny-commands "show system"` covers `show system rollback`.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — path-scoped login-class denies fail open on the only enforced remote surface, silently for three realistic patterns. This is an un-fixed residual of closed #15076, whose own evidence named the IKE leg.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — reporter probe re-read, plus an independent va41 probe with positive controls and two new silent shapes. End-to-end SSH on the lab cluster was not run.

**Confidence:** High — executed through the real compiled login regexes, the real `authorizeRPC` gate and the real advisory functions, with a committed config and the passwd fixture. The remaining assumption is the cli call-site mapping, which was read from source and not driven end to end over SSH.

## Impact

vSRX RBAC migrations write path-scoped denies like these for NOC/helpdesk classes (hide VPN peers, config history, NAT inventory). xpf accepts them and enforces them on the root-only console. Remote users are not bound by them, and for common patterns nothing warns the operator. The blast radius is every member of such a class, for as long as the config stays. Recovery requires knowing to also deny the charged sibling path.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make the charge call-site-aware. One option is a request selector per sharing line (`Terse`/filter on ShowInterfacesDetail, an `ike|ipsec` view on GetIPsecSA, summary selectors on the NAT RPCs). The other is to evaluate the class rules against all forms, the charged path plus the typed spelling, as in `EvaluateForms` (e.g. ShowRollback/ShowCompare/ListHistory also as `show system rollback`, GetGlobalStats also as `show security statistics`, GetVRRPStatus also as `show security vrrp`). Replace the hand-written census with one generated from every `c.client.<RPC>(` site in `cmd/cli` paired with its dispatching line. Acceptance: every admitted subject row of the va41/a41 probes becomes PermissionDenied, the over-deny row is admitted, and all controls are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A41-01`, part `parts/va41.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16606 — The dns-name refresher applies a private clone that the store never publishes. Scheduler and route-overlay republishes rebuild address-book rows from the stale published config, and the JSON-based #6480 skew guard cannot see the differen... [OPEN]

## Summary
The dns-name refresher applies a private clone that the store never publishes. Scheduler and route-overlay republishes rebuild address-book rows from the stale published config, and the JSON-based #6480 skew guard cannot see the difference, so the old answer is re-shipped.

**Finding ID:** R3-N09-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium. After a DNS answer change, the next scheduler window edge (or ip-monitoring route-overlay actuation) silently reverts dns-name enforcement to the previous answer. A `deny <dns-name>` stops covering the host's new address, and a permit to a moved service drops. The refresher baseline already records the new answer, so nothing repairs this until a full apply runs or the answer changes again. It needs dns-name plus a policy scheduler or ip-monitoring.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Sites that combine dns-name objects with scheduled policies or ip-monitoring are affected. Enforcement silently tracks a stale answer between full applies, which can be hours or days. `show` surfaces read the store config and also show the stale answer, so the divergence is not visible.

**Contract:** `manager_overlay.go:194-200` states the publishers' invariant ("cfg IS the applied config ... ApplyConfig stores the exact object ActiveConfig returns"). `daemon_dnsaddr.go:130-132` says the baseline equals the actually-applied answers. The #6480 guard exists to refuse a partial republish from a config that differs from the applied one.

**Trace:** answer A→B → refresher applies the clone with B (helper enforces B; baseline = B; store cfg still A) → scheduler edge → `UpdatePolicyScheduleState(store cfg = A)` → the hybrid guard sees JSON-equal configs → address-book rows are rebuilt with A → the helper enforces A → the next refresher tick resolves B, equal to the baseline, and does nothing.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`daemon_dnsaddr.go:156-168` resolves into `refreshed := cfg.CloneForDNSRefresh()` and calls `applyDNSRefreshedConfig(cfg, refreshed)`. :240-245 runs `d.applyConfigLocked(..., refreshed)` and then `recordDNSBaselineForce(base, snapshotDNSAnswers(refreshed))`. The store is never updated. `daemon_scheduler.go:363-367` reads `cfg := d.store.ActiveConfig()` and calls `updatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatchLocked(cfg, ...)`. `manager_compile.go:1188` `routeOnlyPublishHybrid(cfg, m.lastSnapshot.Config)` compares by JSON (`manager_overlay.go:418-453`). `types_security.go:1873-1875` declares `DNSAddresses []string json:"-"`. `manager_compile.go:1195` `buildAddressBookTableWithFeeds(cfg, ...)` and :1219 `next.AddressBooks = books`.

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vn09/probes/zz_vn09_sched_republish_stale_dns_test.go, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestVN09 -count=1 -v`; output in RUN/verify/vn09/userspace-rerun.out. The helper lastSnapshot, built from the refreshed clone, has `bad v4=[203.0.113.99/32]`. Control (republish cfg = clone): wire `bad v4=[203.0.113.99/32]`. Daemon shape (republish cfg = store active): wire `bad v4=[198.51.100.7/32]`. The reporter's daemon probe (rerun) shows `applied-cfg svc=[10.9.9.9/32] store.ActiveConfig() svc=[10.0.0.1/32] same-pointer=false`, and the next tick gives `applies=1` (no repair). `TestN09HybridGuardBlindToDNSAnswers` gives `routeOnlyPublishHybrid(cfg, refreshed)=false`, with the control (hostname differs) `=true`. Limits: Rust helper consumption was not run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Publish the refreshed DNS state as a new store generation, or move answers into a daemon-owned answer table that every builder reads, instead of applying an unpublished clone. Add the DNS answers to the `configsContentEqual` explicit comparison. Acceptance: in the verifier probe, the daemon-shape arm ships `203.0.113.99/32`, and `routeOnlyPublishHybrid(old, refreshed)` returns true.

## Full validated claim

## #16607 — Two source-NAT rule-sets with identical from/to context commit clean (Junos refuses this) and are concatenated in config order, so the later rule-set's rules, including a `source-nat off` exemption, are unreachable behind the earlier catch-all [OPEN]

## Summary

Two source-NAT rule-sets with identical from/to context commit clean (Junos refuses this) and are concatenated in config order, so the later rule-set's rules, including a `source-nat off` exemption, are unreachable behind the earlier catch-all

**Finding ID:** `R3-A08-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low — an operator-error shape that Junos refuses at commit. In xpf it becomes silent shadowing. The practical victim is a later exemption rule-set (for example no-NAT toward a VPN peer), whose traffic is still translated. Bounded to that config. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (NAT strict-commit gates that admit a rule which can never act as authored; with R3-A08-02 and R3-A04-01) — real, grounded parity gap with a bounded consequence.

## Mechanism

two `rule-set X/Y from zone lan to zone wan` blocks -> compileNATSource appends both -> strict clean -> snapshot sorted by tier (equal) in config order -> Rust first-match returns the catch-all `source-nat interface` -> the exemption is never consulted.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:359 `sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool { return sourceNATScopeTier(out[i]) < sourceNATScopeTier(out[j]) })` (equal contexts keep config order). dup_nat_ruleset_names.go (#6454) keys on rule-set NAME. nat_off_shadow_9879.go is DNAT-only ("Shared DNAT `off`-shadow analysis (#9879/#11352)"). Observed: no gate compares source-NAT (from, to) contexts across rule-sets.

## Impact

an exemption added later as its own rule-set silently does nothing. VPN or peer traffic gets translated, which breaks policy-based tunnels and partner allow-lists. A Junos-valid workflow (Junos would have refused the commit and forced a merge) becomes a silent misconfiguration.

## Acceptance / fix direction

strict-reject (lenient: warn) two source-NAT rule-sets whose normalised (from-kind, from-value-set, to-kind, to-value-set) are equal after #3096 list expansion, naming both rule-sets. Acceptance: the a08 probe config fails strict commit, and distinct contexts and single rule-sets still commit.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper NAT Overview (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/nat/topics/topic-map/security-nat-overview.html, fetched by va08) says: "You cannot specify the same source and destination conditions for source NAT rule sets." xpf's #4161 comment (pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:341-355) instead asserts "equal-specificity rule-set-definition order" as the within-tier behaviour.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A08-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A08-04 | Low | Two source-NAT rule-sets with identical from/to context commit clean (Junos refuses this)… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:63: - **R3-A08-04 — COHORT (Low).** **Defect:** `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:49-54,335-355` flattens source-NAT rule-sets then stable-sorts by specificity; two *identical* contexts preserve authored order and an early catch-all can shadow a later `source-nat off` exemption. [Juniper's source-NAT rule-set contract](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/nat/topics/topic-map/nat-security-source-and-source-pool.html) disallows duplicate from/to contexts, while the existing duplicate check is by rule-set name, not context. **Refutation:** xpf deliberately adopts first-match across equal scopes (#4161), and merged rules in one set can express the exemption if ordered first; no secret overpermit follows without an authored shadowing configuration. **Decisive check:** strict-reject *duplicate context tuples* (not merely equal specificity) or explicitly document alternate semantics, retaining tests for overlapping but distinct scope precedence.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L233: ### R3-A08-04 — duplicate SNAT rule-set contexts commit; later exemption shadowed — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: No gate compares normalised (from,to) contexts across source-NAT rule-sets (dup gates key on name/rule-name; off-shadow is DNAT-only); snapshots stable-sorted by tier only (`nat_source.go:359`) → config-order concatenation, first-match (#4161) → later `source-nat off` exemption unreachable. Juniper text: cannot specify same source/destination conditions for source NAT rule sets. - Refutation: xpf #4161 comment asserts definition-order as designed within-tier behaviour — deliberate divergence from Junos, so this challenges documented-in-code intent; harm needs duplicate-context authoring Junos would refuse. Not re-verified independently by this lane beyond report's rerun account; coordinator should keep Gemini ownership. [INFERENCE: DUP correctness depends on G43-04 text as quoted.] ---

## #16608 — NormalizeEditPathTokens re-lexes the space-joined cursor, so a quoted element with interior whitespace (`edit firewall family inet filter "lan in"`) is stored as two tokens. A discard term added from that cursor lands in a new, empty... [OPEN]

## Summary
NormalizeEditPathTokens re-lexes the space-joined cursor, so a quoted element with interior whitespace (`edit firewall family inet filter "lan in"`) is stored as two tokens. A discard term added from that cursor lands in a new, empty, unapplied filter `lan`, the applied filter `"lan in"` is unchanged, and commit check returns nil (both CLIs).

**Finding ID:** R3-B24-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — protection the operator added to an applied filter is silently absent while commit succeeds, so enforcement differs from intent. It is bounded by the trigger: the element name must contain whitespace, which the product accepts and compiles but which is uncommon. Closed-world subtrees (security policies, applications, address-book) refuse the misplaced result, so they fail closed. Demonstrated at the compiled-config boundary.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator hardening an applied filter from its edit level gets `commit complete` and an unchanged dataplane filter, on both console and remote CLI. The result persists across restart, HA sync and rollback history until someone audits the filter.

**Contract:** `[edit …]` navigation must address the node the operator named. #14716 stored the LEXED cursor "so the gate judges the executed path". #15237 A53-07 requires that "a quoted value with interior whitespace" survive as one token (cli_dispatch.go:554-556 comment).

**Trace:** `edit firewall family inet filter "lan in"` → ParseEditFragment gives [... filter, "lan in"] → NormalizeEditPathTokens re-lexes the joined text, giving [... filter, lan, in] → `set term block then discard` → JoinConfigPathTokens gives `firewall family inet filter lan in term block then discard` → SetPath creates `filter lan { in term block … }` → commit check nil → FiltersInet `"lan in"` (applied input on ge-0/0/0.0) unchanged.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:316-330: `if lexed, ok := ParseConfigPath(strings.Join(editPath, " ")); ok { return lexed }`. pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:520-521: `newPath := append(c.store.GetEditPath(), frag...)`; `c.store.SetEditPath(config.NormalizeEditPathTokens(newPath))`. :552: `fullPath := append(config.NormalizeEditPathTokens(c.store.GetEditPath()), toks[1:]...)`, then JoinConfigPathTokens. Other consumers: cli_dispatch.go:633 (annotate), cli_config.go:96,124 (copy/rename/insert), cmd/cli/shared.go:301,332,354,380,399,424,479, and gate permissions_config_regex.go:133.

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vb24/probes/zz_vb24_probe2_test.go TestVB24ProbeCursorWS, run with `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cli/ -run 'TestVB24ProbeCursorWS' -count=1 -v`, output RUN/verify/vb24/probe-cursor-misc.out. Positive control (`lanin`, same cursor lines): storedCursor=[firewall family inet filter lanin], filter "lanin" terms=[allow block], commitErr=nil. Defect (`"lan in"`): storedCursor=[firewall family inet filter lan in]; compiled `"lan in"` terms=[allow] and `"lan"` terms=[]; commitErr=nil; warnings=0. The reporter's zz_b24_probe_editws4_test.go (re-run, rerun-pkgcli.out) adds set lines `set firewall family inet filter lan in term block then discard`. Only an `insert` errors (`element not found`). Policies, applications and address-book are refused at commit.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Keep the cursor as lexed tokens and never re-lex the space-joined form. Where #14716's split-comment case needs a joined lex, join with JoinConfigPathTokens (quoting) instead of strings.Join, and quote tokens in `[edit …]` banners and compare headers. Acceptance: the defect arm compiles `"lan in"` terms=[allow block] on both CLIs, the `lanin` control is unchanged, and pkg/config/authz_editpath_lex_14716_test.go stays green.

## #16609 — PPTP first-learn install refused by a permanent alias collision is retained as a self-retry with no TTL/cap on a single-worker helper; the per-second retry walk re-attempts every entry on the forwarding worker and inf... [OPEN]

## Summary
PPTP first-learn install refused by a permanent alias collision is retained as a self-retry with no TTL/cap on a single-worker helper; the per-second retry walk re-attempts every entry on the forwarding worker and inflates `allocator_collisions` by N per second

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — a remote PPTP server on a policy-admitted TCP/1723 control channel can grow `pending_call_installs` by up to 64 entries/s (inbox capacity per 1 s drain) for the lifetime of the control channel, and each entry is cloned and re-installed (and re-fails) every second on the only forwarding worker; demonstrated: unbounded retention and the refusal counter advancing N/s; NOT demonstrated: the worker-loop stall magnitude or memory growth over hours (inferred O(N) per second under the inbox mutex). Bounded by the single-worker prerequisite (multi-worker clears) and by the channel's FIN/RST, a CDN for the alias, or ALG disable [reporter: Low (Medium on workers 1)]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A75-03`
**Source part:** `parts/vrc.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
single-worker appliances (small boxes, one-queue NICs) behind which any inside user can reach a hostile or buggy PPTP server: state and per-second worker work grow for as long as the control channel stays open (up to ~230k entries/hour at the inbox rate), degrading forwarding latency on the only worker, and `allocator_collisions` — the statistic an operator would use to diagnose it — reports a multiple of the real refusals; recovery requires closing the control connection, a CDN for the alias, ALG disable, or a helper restart

**Contract:** the self-retry exists only to avoid losing a TRANSIENT refusal (`afxdp/pptp_broadcast.rs:87-92`: "Retain the retry for the next interval on any error rather than lose a transient AllocatorCollision"), and the store's own field doc says it holds "PPTP installs refused by full worker queues" (`session/pptp_control.rs:165-166`); docs/engineering-style.md requires caps enforced before resource commitment and no unbounded per-tick work on the worker; `allocator_collisions` exists so a refusal is counted, i.e. once per refusal, not once per retry tick

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`afxdp/pptp_broadcast.rs:307-339` @d1ea69f9aa — on any local `install` error the drainer pushes its own `Arc::as_ptr(queue)` into `unsent` and calls `inbox.record_call_install_at(call, control, seg.captured_ns, seg.epoch, unsent)`; `afxdp/pptp_broadcast.rs:66-94` — `retry_pending_pptp_call_installs` takes every retry, and when the self queue is empty calls `install(...)`; on `Err(e)` it only logs "retaining retry" (no mark, no age check); `session/pptp_control.rs:404-440` — `record_call_install_at` does a linear `position()` keyed on `(call, control)` and `push`es when absent (no cap); `:530-549` `take_call_install_retries_at` clones every entry of the current epoch once per `CONTROL_DRAIN_INTERVAL_NS` (1 s, `:82`) while holding the inbox mutex; `:73` `PENDING_CONTROL_CAPACITY = 64`; `session/pptp.rs:403` each `AllocatorCollision` does `allocator_collisions = saturating_add(1)`. Removal only via `mark_call_install_sent`, `complete_call_install_broadcast`, `forget_call_installs_for_disconnect` (CDN), `forget_call_installs_for_channel` (control close), `purge_pending` (ALG disable) — no TTL. Observations: the lines above; inference: per-second cost and memory grow linearly in N

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — va75's temporary cargo cell `zz_va75_pptp_permanent_collision_self_retry_growth` (afxdp::worker_queue::tests) ran at d1ea69f9aa in RUN/wt/a75 (single worker, `peer_worker_commands = &[]`); vrc did not re-run cargo (task forbids it) and instead re-read the full chain at the base statically and checked the cell's fixture against production entry points

## Ledger validation (excerpt)

On every approximately one-second drain `:58-125`, an empty self queue retries `install`, and **every error** only logs, never clears the retry. `session/pptp_control.rs:404-440` appends a new `(call, control)` after a linear search without TTL/cap; `:529-547` clones every due entry, including its `Vec<usize>`, under the shared inbox mutex. `session/pptp.rs:397-408` counts each repeated alias collision. The retained actual Rust test reports 64 same-alias replies → 1 learned/63 pending and cumulative collisions 63,126,189,…,378; distinct aliases → 64 learned/zero retries; CDN removes the pending entries (`verify/va75/probes/cargo-zz_va75-r2.out:4945-4951`). The atomic `Relaxed` interval check avoids locking on *non-due* invocations but does not reduce **due** O(N) clone/heap allocations, retry attempts, shared-lock hold or initial linear insert/dedup. On a one-worker forwarding loop, those are source-proven recurring costs, although packet-latency degradation was not measured.
- **Strongest refutation/alternative:** The phrase “unbounded 230k entries/h

## #16610 — All four `firewall three-color-policer` burst leaves accept any positive byte count. `committed-burst-size`/`excess-burst-size` 64 or 1000 (single-rate), or a 1k `peak-burst-size` (two-rate), therefore commit with zero warnings. The meter then… [OPEN]

## Summary

All four `firewall three-color-policer` burst leaves accept any positive byte count. `committed-burst-size`/`excess-burst-size` 64 or 1000 (single-rate), or a 1k `peak-burst-size` (two-rate), therefore commit with zero warnings. The meter then colours every frame larger than max(CBS, EBS) (srTCM) or PBS (trTCM) red, and `then discard` drops it at any offered rate. The single-rate `firewall policer` rejects the same values under its #10310 1500-byte floor.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A09-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. The policed term turns into a size filter: every full-size TCP segment is dropped even at a small fraction of CIR, while small packets (ACKs, DNS) pass. Bulk transfers in that class stall, and the symptom looks like a PMTU problem. Drops at any rate were demonstrated at component level (Rust…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable clean commit silently converts a rate meter into a drop-every-full-size-frame filter. The sibling policer type already rejects the same values.

## Mechanism

`set firewall three-color-policer P single-rate committed-burst-size 1000; excess-burst-size 1000` -> SchemaValidate passes (`n != 0`) -> compileFirewall sets CBS=PBS=1000 -> `validateThreeColorPolicersStrict` passes -> snapshot `committed_burst_bytes=1000` / `peak_or_excess_burst_bytes=1000` -> `build_three_color_policer_state` -> srTCM buckets capped at 1000 -> a 1514-byte frame costs 1514, more than both buckets -> Red -> `then discard` drops it.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

The observations below are read at d1ea69f9aa. - `pkg/config/schema_cos.go:523,533,557,577`: `validator: validateThreeColorPolicerBurstSize11827` on all four burst leaves. - `pkg/config/schema_validators_cos.go:89-105`: "any positive, representable byte count is accepted. The legacy firewall policer validator also adds a 1500-byte minimum, which is outside this diagnostic-only change". The only check is `if n == 0`. - `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_cos.go:10-50`: `pol.CBS == 0` and `pol.PBS == 0`, plus `PIR < CIR` and `PBS < CBS`. There is no size floor. - `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:927-936`: `CommittedBurstBytes: pol.CBS`, `PeakOrExcessBurstBytes: pol.PBS`. - `userspace-dp/src/filter/policer.rs:286-291`: rejects only a zero rate or burst. - `policer.rs:490-497`: refill caps each bucket at its burst. - `policer.rs:601-685`: `consume` returns Green only on `committed >= cost`, Yellow only on `peak >= cost`, otherwise `return PacketColor::Red`. There is no deficit carry. - `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:750-757`: `discard` gives red `ColorTreatment::drop()`. - Cost unit: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:151` uses `meta.pkt_len as u64`. `afxdp/types/mod.rs:592-615` says `pkt_len` is the buffer length "not the L3 packet length (#8581)", meaning the full Ethernet frame. The threshold is therefore in frame bytes (L3 + 14 or 18).

## Impact

An operator importing a QFX-sized (512-byte) or mistyped burst gets a policer that black-holes full-size segments for that class with a green commit. The single-rate policer was hardened against exactly this in #10310, so the two policer kinds give opposite answers for one value. The fault lasts until someone reads the red/drop counters and edits the config.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Apply one shared one-frame floor to all four three-color burst leaves, either in the schema validator or the strict gate (strict rejects, tolerant load warns per #1960). At minimum enforce it on max(CBS, EBS) for single-rate and on PBS for two-rate. Express the floor in the meter's cost unit (see R3-VA09-S1). Acceptance: the probe's three srTCM/trTCM rows are rejected, and a twin at the new floor is accepted.

## Contract (where cited)

xpf's own #10310 invariant for policer buckets (`pkg/config/schema_validators_cos.go:56-67`): "a bucket smaller than one maximum-sized packet. A sub-packet bucket cannot admit an ordinary MTU frame and otherwise commits a configuration that drops/marks every such packet". Juniper "Policer Bandwidth and Burst-Size Limits" (MX) gives single-rate three-color committed-burst-size and excess-burst-size and two-rate committed-burst-size and peak-burst-size all as `1500..100000000000`. RFC 2697 §2: "It is recommended that when the value of the CBS or the EBS is larger than 0, it is larger than or equal to the size of the largest possible IP packet in the stream". RFC 2698 §2 says the same for CBS/PBS.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A09-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A09-01 | Medium | All four firewall three-color-policer burst leaves accept any positive byte count.… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:7: - **R3-A09-01 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** all four three-color bursts call the >0-only validator (`pkg/config/schema_cos.go:516-577`, `pkg/config/schema_validators_cos.go:88-104`); the compiled gate checks zero, rate ordering and CBS≤PBS, not one-frame capacity (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_cos.go:10-48`). Rust caps both buckets at the configured size and requires `tokens >= packet_bytes`; discard drops red (`userspace-dp/src/filter/policer.rs:490-497,601-680`, `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:750-756`). **Best alternative:** in single-rate mode a large EBS permits yellow even if CBS is tiny; only CBS *and* EBS smaller than the charged frame guarantee red; two-rate requires PBS smaller than the frame. This is a policing-choice error, not a generic traffic bypass. **Decisive remaining check:** repeat prior strict-commit/meter positive controls at current revision; cover >1500 configured MTUs and color treatment other than discard.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L12: | R3-A09-01 three-color burst no floor | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-VA09-S1 1500 floor < frame cost unit | MATERIAL (COHORT w/ A09-01, same fix) | Medium-Low | | R3-A10-01 next-table miss fall-through + LPM beat | MATERIAL (Junos-miss half NEEDS_VALIDATION on Junos contract) | Medium | | R3-A10-02 rib-group peer-return cross-VRF | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A10-04 static preference scale inversion | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-01 BGP auth unrendered spellings | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-02 flat-run heads bypass BGP validators | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-03 route-filter longest-match vs OR | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-04 community `\| ` vty pipe refusal | MATERIAL | Medium |

The meter charges frame bytes (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:151`), caps buckets to configured burst (`userspace-dp/src/filter/policer.rs:490-497`), and returns red when the cost exceeds available tokens (`:601-685`); red+discard drops (`userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:750-757`).
