## #16611 — R3-A42-01: #14981 commit-time expanded deny-configuration gate prices the candidate at interceptor time, but the daemon promotes whatever candidate exists after applySem (and… [OPEN]

## Summary

#14981 commit-time expanded deny-configuration gate prices the candidate at interceptor time, but the daemon promotes whatever candidate exists after applySem (and re-adopts a changed one on generation conflict); a same-holder `copy`/`rename` landing in between is committed unadjudicated

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — a restricted `configure` class (`deny-configuration`/`allow-configuration`) can get group-inherited configuration it is denied into the ACTIVE config, defeating the documented #14981 contract. I demonstrated this at component level. It is bounded because the class already holds config permission, the class cannot author the denied group body itself (the literal gate refuses it), so admin-authored group content it can copy or rename must already exist, and an ordinary rollback recovers. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A42-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va42.md` (finding `R3-A42-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

@d1ea69f9aa. pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:48-52: `return config.AuthorizeExpandedCandidate(cfg, class, s.store.CandidateTree(), s.store.ActiveTree())` runs in the interceptor (authz.go:295). Lines :97-100 have `case "copy", "rename", "insert", "annotate": … return nil` (no replay). pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:301 `authority, err := s.store.AuthorizeCommitAs(...)` and :324 `compiled, err := s.commitFn(ctx, authority, req.Comment)`. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:222 `d.applySem.Acquire(ctx, 1)`, then :271 `commitWithGenBinding`. Inside it, :127 `cand, gen, cerr := d.store.CompileCandidateGen()` snapshots AFTER the wait, and :170-173 retry on `ErrCandidateGenerationConflict` ("re-validating on the new generation", preflight only). The same applies to commit confirmed at :928. pkg/configstore/commit_authority.go:164 `if holder != a.sessionID || s.holderEpoch != a.epoch`: no candidate-generation term. pkg/grpcapi/config_session_lifecycle.go:128 connSessionID is per connection. server.go:945 allows 256 concurrent streams. I found no per-session config-RPC serialization. Observation: the probe promotes denied content. Inference: production behaves the same (the daemon loop matches the mirror line for line).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** docs/system-login.md:1077-1095 (#14981): "`deny-configuration` (and `allow-configuration`) apply to the configuration that takes effect … **Commit / CommitConfirmed**: the whole candidate is expanded and checked for the committing class". pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_regex_9154.go:97-100 delegates copy/rename/insert/annotate to that gate: "the commit-time expanded gate adjudicates their effective result". The promoted candidate is therefore the object the gate owes a verdict on.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable bypass of a documented authorization contract, executed with controls. No owner exists: every sibling finding is about gate content, not gate timing.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run TestVA42CommitGateTOCTOU -count=1 -v` drives the real interceptor gate function, Server.Commit, Server.Set and configstore promotion, with the daemon's generation-bound promote loop reproduced in the commitFn seam. The daemon's applySem/preflight placement, the REST twin and the CLI reachability are STATIC.

**Confidence:** Medium — the check/use gap and the bypass are executed with three controls. Remaining assumptions: the actor has a client that can put a second RPC on the same connection while the commit is in flight. That is deterministic for any restricted principal with code execution. On the shipped appliance (CLI login shell, no SSH forwarding) it reduces to a milliseconds-wide Ctrl-C race. The probe mirrors commitWithGenBinding rather than running the daemon.

## Impact

delegated-admin classes are the reason `*-configuration` regexes exist. A class barred from `system host-name`, `security policies`, `system login` and so on can move admin-authored protected group content into effect. The active config, persistence and HA peer sync then carry it until an unrestricted operator notices and rolls back. The gate reports nothing, because the gate never saw the promoted tree.

## Acceptance / fix direction

bind authorization to what is promoted. Either (a) record the candidate generation the commit gate priced, carry it in CommitAuthority (or a sibling token), and refuse promotion when `candidateGen` differs, with no adopt-on-conflict for authz-bound commits; or (b) run AuthorizeExpandedCandidate for the admitted class inside commitWithGenBinding's per-attempt preflight and again under the store lock in CommitWithDescriptionGenAs, for both commit and commit confirmed, on gRPC and REST. Acceptance: a Go cell where a same-session copy lands between gate and promotion is refused; the unchanged-candidate twin commits; the before-commit copy is still refused; and unrestricted classes are unaffected.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A42-01`, part `parts/va42.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16612 — A commit-confirmed window recovered at boot compiles its rollback target's dns-name answers once, at Store.Load. If resolution fails then, the deadline enters the bootstrap/lifeline safe state instead of rolling back, even after DNS reco... [OPEN]

## Summary
A commit-confirmed window recovered at boot compiles its rollback target's dns-name answers once, at Store.Load. If resolution fails then, the deadline enters the bootstrap/lifeline safe state instead of rolling back, even after DNS recovers.

**Finding ID:** R3-N09-04
**Severity (source):** High — High. The commit-confirmed auto-revert, the operator's "revert if I lose contact" safety net, turns into enterBootstrapMode: takeover files retired, FRR managed section cleared, dataplane detached, every RG resigned. Recovery needs a console or the lifeline. The bootstrap outcome is demonstrated; the trigger timing at real boot is not.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A reboot during a commit-confirmed window is the event the feature exists for. On a cluster the node resigns all RGs. Bootstrap also has no ordinary commit exit (see R3-A32-02, this run), so recovery is manual.

**Contract:** `confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:12-26,55-63` says the fire-time pre-flight exists so the timer does not make the unconfirmed commit permanent, and that a target waiting on a transient input is deferred. `rollback_target_appliable_6707.go:56-70` says the gate agrees with the mirror at this moment.

**Trace:** `commit confirmed N` with a target that has a dns-name policy → reboot → Store.Load recovers the window and compiles the target (resolution fails, empty answer) → deadline → preflight → `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` → not feed-only → PromoteRollback + enterBootstrapMode.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`configstore/store_persist.go:1362-1376` runs `compiled, cerr := s.compileTreeLenient(prevTree) ... s.confirmPrevCfg = compiled` once, at Load. `confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:81-82` calls `rollbackTargetAppliablePreflight(target, ...)` on that object. :87 shows the only deferral, `rollbackTargetRefusedOnlyForFeeds(target)`, which lists only `DynamicAddress.AddressBindings` (:40-53). :94-130 runs `PromoteRollback` and then `enterBootstrapMode()`. Nothing re-resolves `confirmPrevCfg`: the refresher touches only `ActiveConfig` (`daemon_dnsaddr.go:137`).

**Probe:** RUN/workers/n09/evidence/zz_n09_confirm_dns_bootstrap_probe_test.go, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestN09 -count=1 -v`; rerun saved to RUN/verify/vn09/daemon-rerun.out. Control (DNS up at Load): `applied=[dns-target] store host="dns-target" inBootstrap=false`. DNS down at Load and healthy at the deadline: `applied=[] store host="dns-target" inBootstrap=true`, plus `ERROR recovered commit-confirmed window ... the rollback target is refused by this build's dataplane` (a misdiagnosis) and `ERROR commit confirmed timed out ... the daemon enters the bootstrap/lifeline safe state`. Limits: no real reboot or lab run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Re-resolve or re-compile the pending target at fire time. Classify an empty answer caused by a failed resolution like the feed case (bounded deferral), and then apply with the last-known or empty answers as per-entry match-none rather than entering bootstrap. Acceptance: in the probe's DNS-down-at-Load arm, `dns-target` is applied with `inBootstrap=false`.

## Full validated claim

## #16613 — The console read gate discards RollbackCompareSnapshot's slotErr and stashes nil arms, so for a classed user `show <path> | compare rollback 40` prints nothing, `show system rollback 40 <path> | compare` prints `[no changes]`, and `show... [OPEN]

## Summary
The console read gate discards RollbackCompareSnapshot's slotErr and stashes nil arms, so for a classed user `show <path> | compare rollback 40` prints nothing, `show system rollback 40 <path> | compare` prints `[no changes]`, and `show system rollback 40 <path>` prints `configuration path not found`, where the unclassed console, gRPC and REST all report the missing slot.

**Finding ID:** R3-B24-03
**Severity (source):** Low — a change-control read gives an affirmative "nothing changed" for a slot that does not exist (a typo, or a slot aged out). It affects read surfaces only, for classed console users only, with no enforcement effect, and the gRPC/REST twins are correct.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A restricted reviewer checking "what changed since rollback N" after a burst of commits can conclude nothing changed. It is limited to the local console.

**Contract:** pkg/configstore/snapshot_render_15995.go:150-153: "gates price a nil snapshot as 'renders nothing', handlers must still surface the slot error". #3443/#5052 made a wrong rollback selector a hard error. gRPC (server_config.go:546) and REST (api/config.go:764) call RollbackSnapshotErr.

**Trace:** classed console `show … | compare rollback 40` → read gate → RollbackCompareSnapshot returns slotErr, which is discarded → nil arms stashed (captured=true) → handler takes the captured branch → empty diff, nil error.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/cli/permissions_config_read_14707.go:54 `scfg, slot, other, _, _, _ := c.store.RollbackCompareSnapshot(n, false)` → `c.setRenderSnapshots15995(slot, other)`. The same discard occurs at the operational sites (~:188, ~:251, ~:266). Handler cli_config.go:564-575 `case c.snapshotsCaptured15995():` → RenderCompareRedacted/Cleartext(nil, nil, …), with err left nil. cli_show_system.go:930-936 and 1014-1020 pass hasCandidate=true, so two nil arms diff to `[no changes]`. `grep RollbackSnapshotErr` finds callers only in grpcapi and api, none in pkg/cli.

**Probe:** Class "": `show interfaces | compare rollback 40` → `err=history position 39 out of range [0, 1)`. Class `limited`: the same line gives out="" err=<nil>, as does 99999999999. Operational, class `limited`: `show system rollback 40 interfaces | compare` → `[no changes]`, and `show system rollback 40 interfaces` → `configuration path not found: interfaces`. Positive control: slot 1 renders an identical diff for both classes.

## Acceptance / fix direction
At all four gate sites, stash the slotErr when it is non-nil, and have each handler return it (or `rollback slot N not found`, as gRPC does) before rendering. Acceptance: the probe's classed rows return an error, and the slot-1 rows are unchanged.

## #16614 — A `next-table` static is an ip rule ahead of `main`, not an inet.0 route. When the target table has no match, the lookup falls through to inet.0 (normally the WAN default) instead of stopping, and the leak overrides every more-specific inet.0… [OPEN]

## Summary

A `next-table` static is an ip rule ahead of `main`, not an inet.0 route. When the target table has no match, the lookup falls through to inet.0 (normally the WAN default) instead of stopping, and the leak overrides every more-specific inet.0 route. This holds on the kernel path and in the AF_XDP FIB.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A10-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — Shown on the kernel path and pinned in the helper: traffic the config sends into an internal VRF leaves through the default instance's routing (usually the Internet uplink) whenever the VRF has no covering route, for example because of an address hole, a withdrawn IGP/BGP route or a member …
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — The behaviour is reachable with an ordinary strict-commit-clean `next-table` config. It silently re-routes VRF-bound traffic out of the default instance, and no doc or warning discloses it.

## Mechanism

The static route `P next-table I` compiles to `StaticRoute{NextTable}`. The daemon calls `ApplyNextTableRules(..., DefaultInstanceIngressIfaces)`, which installs one `to P iif <if> lookup <I>` per ingress at a prefix-derived 30000+ priority. In the kernel RPDB this rule matches before main. On a miss in I the walk continues to `32766 main`, whose default is the WAN. The FIB snapshot carries a NextTable row in inet.0, and the Rust stage-1 leak walk does the same, `continue`-ing on a miss and then running inet.0 LPM.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/frr/config_render.go:413-414` has `if sr.NextTable != "" { return "" // handled via ip rule in routing package }`, so the static never enters zebra's RIB. `pkg/routing/rules.go:251-257` builds `rule.Dst = dst; rule.Table = tableID; rule.Priority = priority; rule.Family = family; rule.IifName = iif` at 30000-30999, ahead of `32766 lookup main`, with no unreachable shadow. Compare PBR, which has one under #11394. xpf installs no per-VRF default reject: `pkg/routing` has no `RTN_UNREACHABLE` install, and the only Null0 default is the global cluster one at `pkg/frr/config_render.go:940-947`. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:969-1007` reads "A matching leak whose target table has no route is a miss, not a terminal NoRoute; continue to the next leak and then to this table's LPM stage", and the leak walk runs before `select_v4_route`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:1599-1605` says "if the leak target misses, lookup continues to the next rule and eventually reaches this ordinary fallback". `tests_leak_overlap_9955.rs:271` (`leak_versus_ordinary_route_in_the_same_table_9955`) and `:339` (`a_leak_into_a_table_that_misses_falls_through_9955`) pin both behaviours.

## Impact

Sending an aggregate (10/8, a customer block) to an internal VRF is the canonical use of next-table. Any hole in that VRF silently becomes Internet egress of internal-destined traffic, often SNATed by a trust->untrust permit. An operator's more-specific carve-out is ignored. Recovery requires knowing to add a discard backstop inside the VRF, which no doc mentions.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make the target miss terminal: add a selector-identical `unreachable` rule after each next-table rule, or a per-target-VRF default reject, mirrored in the FIB as a terminal leak miss. Make inet.0 LPM decide: either install P as a zebra route with a table/VRF hand-off, or keep the rule but skip it when a more-specific inet.0 route exists. Flip the two #9955 Rust cells to Junos semantics. Acceptance: in the probe, 10.99.0.1 is unreachable and 172.16.5.9 resolves via xwan 203.0.113.253, the 10.1.0.5 control is unchanged, and the Rust helper agrees.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos `routing-options static route P next-table T.inet.0` puts a route P into inet.0 whose next hop hands the lookup to T. The Juniper static reference defines next-table as "Name of the next routing table to the destination". Because P is a route, it competes in inet.0 by longest-prefix match like any route, and the lookup is then done in T, whose forwarding table ends in a default reject. `docs/feature-gaps.md:612` advertises "next-table route leaking" with no semantic caveat. `pkg/routing/README.md:370-377,634-638` documents only leak-versus-leak LPM and the band order.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A10-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A10-01 | Medium | A next-table static is an ip rule ahead of main, not an inet.0 route. When the target table… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:13: - **R3-A10-01 — MATERIAL (Medium), strongest on LPM ordering; target-miss parity less independently established.** **Defect:** `next-table` is *omitted* from static routes rendered into zebra (`pkg/frr/config_render.go:412-415`) and instead becomes a destination-scoped early RPDB lookup (`pkg/routing/rules.go:251-257`). Userspace explicitly checks leaks before its own table's LPM and continues after an absent target route (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:969-1011`). Therefore even a *more-specific* main-table route can lose to a wider leak if the target covers that destination, and a target miss can reach main's WAN default. Previous netns probe on base observed both. **Best alternative:** `iif` scoping, zone policy and the l3mdev VRF miss terminator constrain some traffic, and the current kernel-model implementation intentionally mirrors RPDB semantics. Juniper describes `next-table` as a *static route next hop*, not an RPDB pre-route rule ([Junos static reference](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/static-edit-routing-options.html)); that is decisive for LPM but does not explicitly document target-table miss behavior. **Remaining check:** compare a Junos/vSRX target-table *miss* and a main more-specific competing route with current xpf kernel and AF_XDP paths; do not claim the former is proven by the vendor reference alone.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L14: | R3-A10-01 next-table miss fall-through + LPM beat | MATERIAL (Junos-miss half NEEDS_VALIDATION on Junos contract) | Medium | | R3-A10-02 rib-group peer-return cross-VRF | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A10-04 static preference scale inversion | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-01 BGP auth unrendered spellings | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-02 flat-run heads bypass BGP validators | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-03 route-filter longest-match vs OR | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-04 community `\| ` vty pipe refusal | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-05 community regex per-community vs joined | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-06 RR allow-outbound-policy missing | MATERIAL | Medium |

**Wonder:** wonder batch01 L16: | **R3-A09-02** | **NEG** | — | Current schema help states three-color `then discard` is the default (`pkg/config/schema_cos.go:582`), docs describe the color-blind behavior (`docs/feature-coverage.md:587`, `docs/feature-gaps.md:973`), and the supplied strict probe rejects Junos-only `then three-color-policer ...` syntax. The alleged silent Junos action/default divergence is therefore neither a supported spelling nor undisclosed. | | **R3-A10-01** | **MATERIAL** | Next-table statics are excluded from FRR routes and installed as prefix selectors/rules (`pkg/frr/config_render.go:413-414` per report; `pkg/routing/routing.go:256`, `pkg/routing/rules.go:251-257`). Rule priority precedes `main` and has no terminal miss rule; lookup can fall through to main/WAN. Userspace FIB mirrors a miss as a continuation (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:969-1007` per report). S…

## #16615 — The #15111 inbound-hold release rebuilds the lease key from the inbound session's arrival routing domain instead of the lease's routing_scope. A cross-domain persistent binding is never released: it never expires, it ... [OPEN]

## Summary
The #15111 inbound-hold release rebuilds the lease key from the inbound session's arrival routing domain instead of the lease's routing_scope. A cross-domain persistent binding is never released: it never expires, it leaks its pool port, and clear cannot remove it. With overlapping addresses, the release decrements another tenant's hold.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — needs routing instances with interface membership, an internal host in a different domain from the inbound arrival interface, and inbound reachability to the host in the arrival table. In that topology, `persistent-nat inactivity-timeout` no longer bounds inbound reachability through the binding (with `any-remote-host` that is any internet host), the pool port leaks, and `clear security nat source persistent-nat-table` leaves a revoked shell that never drains. The cross-tenant arm causes the original #15111 premature expiry on a different tenant. It is bounded to multi-instance persistent-NAT deployments, and it widens an exposure the operator already permitted rather than creating one, so it is not High. The infinite lifetime is demonstrated at allocator level. The full forwarding path is not.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A76-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va76.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Persistent NAT for a tenant VRF behind a shared uplink is a standard CGN/multi-tenant shape. The inactivity timeout is the operator's bound on an endpoint-independent inbound mapping, and here it silently becomes infinite, the clear does not remove the mapping, and pool ports leak until a helper restart or pool rebuild. With overlapping tenants, another tenant's live binding can expire and be reissued under its inbound session.

**Contract:** #15111/#15644: an inbound session through a persistent binding holds the lease, and its release re-arms the expiry so GC reclaims the lease `inactivity-timeout` later (`nat/tests_pool.rs:2237-2300` pins this for domain 0). `SourceNatFlowKey::routing_scope` is `SessionKey.routing_domain` of the flow that minted the lease (`nat/source/keys.rs:23-45`). `session/key.rs:116-131` states that routing_domain is a property of the ingress interface and is "NOT reply-direction symmetric".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/nat/source/release.rs:180-201` builds `PersistentSourceKey { protocol: key.protocol, src_ip: internal_ip, src_port: internal_port, routing_scope: key.routing_domain, remote: None }` and calls `release_persistent_inbound` on every pool rule. `key` is the inbound forward key (`afxdp/worker/loop_body/gc_teardown.rs:108-118`, `&expired_entry.key`). The acquire stores the lookup's `lease_key: Some(*key)` (`afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:4334-4344`, `nat/allocator/mod.rs:1940-1948`) and consumes it in `acquire_persistent_inbound_hold` (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:919-940`). The lookup is keyed by `ReverseIdentityBaseKey{protocol, translated_ip, translated_port}` (`allocator/mod.rs:1876-1882`). `persistent_rule_scope` (`nat/source/mod.rs:1144-1161`) folds only zone/interface/instance names and never the domain, so a cross-domain arrival is admitted. `release_persistent_inbound` (`allocator/mod.rs:2037-2054`) does a plain `get_mut(&key)`, so a miss is silent. GC `reclaim_expired_idle_lease_locked` refuses `inbound_flows != 0` (`:3344`). `clear_persistent_leases` stores the `u64::MAX` tombstone for a held lease (`:2186-2191`). The HA twin `nat/source/synced.rs:222-233` derives the same domain-0 key.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — Rust unit probe through `persistent_inbound_lookup_for_rule`, `acquire_persistent_inbound` and `release_source_nat_allocation_for_worker`, which is the gc_teardown entry point. The poll/forwarding path is STATIC.

## #16616 — The #11062 peer-return rules make two tenants reachable from each other, on the kernel path and in the AF_XDP FIB, when each one leaks only its own interface routes into inet.0. No import-rib authorizes this reach. [OPEN]

## Summary

The #11062 peer-return rules make two tenants reachable from each other, on the kernel path and in the AF_XDP FIB, when each one leaks only its own interface routes into inet.0. No import-rib authorizes this reach.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A10-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — Routing-instance separation is lost between tenants that follow the standard shared-services pattern. On the kernel path, VRF-context lookups (VRF-bound sockets and daemons, non-AF_XDP slaves, slow-path reinjects) reach the other tenant with no zone policy. On the AF_XDP path the FIB route …
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — The config is strict-commit clean with 0 warnings, the reach is reachable in practice and contradicts the import list, and nothing reported earlier claims it.

## Mechanism

Tenants A and B each have `routing-options interface-routes rib-group inet X-to-main` with `import-rib [ X.inet.0 inet.0 ]`. This gives `RibGroupConnectedPrefixes` and the daemon calls `ApplyRibGroupRules`, which installs per-prefix main leaks (30000 band) plus `to <peer-prefix> iif|oif vrf-<self> lookup <peer>` for each tenant at 1001-1999. A packet in VRF-A context for B's subnet misses table A at the `1000 l3mdev` rule, matches the return rule and is forwarded in table B. The FIB snapshot adds a row A.inet.0 -> B.inet.0 NextTable, consulted as a stage-1 leak.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/routing/rules.go:689-695` calls `ribGroupPeerReturnPrefixes(inst, instances, ...)` after A's own leak and then `addRibGroupReturnRules`. `rules.go:705-760` selects every peer with `ribGroupLeaksIntoMain(peer group)`, gated only on `len(installed[family]) > 0` for the source. No check asks whether any import-rib of A names B's table. `pkg/routing/rib_group_return_9819.go:84-139` emits `to <B-prefix> iif|oif vrf-A lookup <B-table>` at 1001-1999, before the 2000 terminator. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:566-581` mirrors each rule as `RouteSnapshot{Table: A.inet.0, Destination: <B-prefix>, NextTable: B.inet.0}`. `pkg/routing/vrf_miss_terminator_9819_test.go:556-561` pins `"lookup to another instance's leaked peer prefix", srcOtherLeak4, "table 300"` as a positive.

## Impact

Every tenant leaking its interfaces into inet.0 is the textbook shared-services design, and its whole point is that tenants do not see each other. VRF-bound services, kernel-path traffic and permissive intra-class zone policies lose isolation. The operator cannot express the intended config and must fall back to zone splits and deny policies.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Install return rules, and FIB reverse rows, only for peer prefixes that an import-rib of the source instance actually authorizes. That is the VRF->VRF import case, currently deferred to Phase 2. Update `docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md:89-126` and turn the 9819 test's peer-prefix positives into negatives. Acceptance: in the probe, A->B is `Network is unreachable` while main->A and main->B still resolve; the FIB snapshot has no A.inet.0 -> B.inet.0 row.

## Contract (where cited)

`docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md:3-6`: an interface-routes rib-group "installs the source instance's direct/interface (connected) routes into every secondary rib in the import list". With `b-to-main import-rib [ b.inet.0 inet.0 ]`, B's routes go into b.inet.0 and inet.0 only, never into a.inet.0. The same doc at :114-120 then states the opposite design ("traffic to a peer prefix that another instance leaked goes directly to that peer's table"), so the doc contradicts itself and Junos. The #9819 issue body classified "a VRF-context lookup that misses its own table, for a destination inside a leaked prefix, resolves in the leak's source-instance table" as defect SYN-RIB-03.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A10-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A10-02 | Medium | The #11062 peer-return rules make two tenants reachable from each other, on the kernel path… | votes codex/smr/wonder=NEEDS_VALIDATION/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:14: - **R3-A10-02 — NEEDS_VALIDATION (contract, not mechanics).** **Defect:** every source instance that successfully leaks its own prefix gains returns to every *other* instance that leaks to main; no source import-rib needs to name the peer (`pkg/routing/rules.go:690-755`, `pkg/routing/rib_group_return_9819.go:112-125`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:558-580`). This differs from Junos's per-secondary-RIB import list (`docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md:3-7`) and lets a VRF-bound process or traffic in tenant A resolve B without an A→B import. **Strong refutation:** xpf *expressly documents* precisely these peer-return rules and their intent (`docs/rib-group-route-leaking.md:89-129`), and an existing kernel test *requires* other-peer lookups to succeed (`pkg/routing/vrf_miss_terminator_9819_test.go:542-564`). Thus “surprising unannounced defect” and a simple removal of peer returns are unsupportable; these routes may have been deliberately chosen to make main→tenant return traffic work. **Decisive remaining check:** establish the product's security contract: is “leak into main only” supposed to permit VRF-A→VRF-B initiation/kernel sockets, or only stateful replies? Verify a supported main↔tenant return-flow scenario before changing this documented behavior. This is a real reachability difference, but MATERIAL as a *bug* requires that contract decision.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L15: | R3-A10-02 rib-group peer-return cross-VRF | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A10-04 static preference scale inversion | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-01 BGP auth unrendered spellings | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-02 flat-run heads bypass BGP validators | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-03 route-filter longest-match vs OR | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-04 community `\| ` vty pipe refusal | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-05 community regex per-community vs joined | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-06 RR allow-outbound-policy missing | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-01 duplicate OSPF router-id in RG split | MATERIAL | Medium |

**Wonder:** wonder batch01 L17: | **R3-A10-01** | **MATERIAL** | Next-table statics are excluded from FRR routes and installed as prefix selectors/rules (`pkg/frr/config_render.go:413-414` per report; `pkg/routing/routing.go:256`, `pkg/routing/rules.go:251-257`). Rule priority precedes `main` and has no terminal miss rule; lookup can fall through to main/WAN. Userspace FIB mirrors a miss as a continuation (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:969-1007` per report). Supplied real-kernel probe reports both target miss to WAN and leak precedence over a main more-specific. | My existing Go `TestVRFReconcileInstallsMissTerminatorBeforeAnyVRF9819` and Rust `leak_overlap_resolution_matches_the_kernel_9955` passed, pinning current XPF/kernel-aligned behavior, not Junos semantics. Zone policy still mediates egress, limiting impact. Junos table-default-reject behavior is the decisive external premise and…

## #16617 — R3-A43-01: `go test ./pkg/grpcapi` is red at d1ea69f9aa (51 top-level failures); the #15995, #9889-hop-2, #5278 positive-admission and #6532 meta cells die before asserting,… [OPEN]

## Summary

`go test ./pkg/grpcapi` is red at d1ea69f9aa (51 top-level failures); the #15995, #9889-hop-2, #5278 positive-admission and #6532 meta cells die before asserting, mostly in fixtures rejected by later strict gates or in guards rotted by renames

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — this is an assurance loss with no demonstrated runtime defect. For the two families repaired as controls (#15995, #9889), the production gates behave correctly. What is lost is the regression signal on the package that owns gRPC authorization and fabric disclosure, so a future regression of those properties changes nothing a reviewer sees. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A43-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va43.md` (finding `R3-A43-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

These are read or observed at d1ea69f9aa.
  - 51 top-level failures and 975 passes (verify/va43/grpcapi-failing-names.txt).
  - TestShowConfigRendersPricedSnapshot15995 → `authz_config_read_15995_test.go:170: Commit: commit check failed: security ipsec vpn "vpn1": no ike gateway configured; its pre-shared key cannot be scoped to a peer`.
  - TestPeerIdentityIsResolvedOncePerConnectionAtAccept_5278 → `principal_authz_5278_test.go:862: ... PermissionDenied (... configuration candidate is held by another session)`.
  - TestCandidateReadingRPCsCostConfigure_9889 → `show_compare_authz_9889_test.go:311` renderer enumeration (the guard names `ShowCompareRedacted`/`ShowCompareRollbackRedacted`, which were renamed `...AtPath`).
  - Commit order: 2082a45442 (#15989, 2026-10-20 19:36) is an ancestor of c6086d3c6d (#15995, 23:56), and both are ancestors of the base, so all 8 *15995 cells have been red since they landed.
  - The reporter's per-family catalogue is workers/a43/evidence/grpcapi-failing-tests.txt. Its NAT, vlan-tagging (#14574), RIP key (#15013), #15990 sweep and golden buckets were spot-checked, not each re-derived.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** CLAUDE.md "Test your code before declaring done". The cells' own guard-the-guard comments ("fails LOUDLY instead of certifying a shrunken set"). .github/workflows/test.yml:1-10: the Go job is not required while affected-package selections are red, with the stated owner action to require it once the baselines are green.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (master red-suite / dead-regression-cell cohort: R3-A83-03 pkg/api sibling, R3-A83-06, R3-A50-01, R3-A51-05, R3-A51-06, R3-N06-07) — real and bounded, with the same root practice (merging on base-identical failures) and the same fix shape.

**Confidence:** High — the whole-package run was executed and counted by test name from `-json`. The first errors were sampled per family, and the repair controls were executed. Remaining assumption: the ~41 cells not individually repaired guard properties that still hold. That is not shown.

## Impact

The package is the authorization boundary for every loopback gRPC caller and for the fabric-exposed surface. With 51 cells red for unrelated reasons, a genuine regression of #15995/#9889/#5278/#6532/#6960 is indistinguishable from the baseline, and the CI owner action (require the Go job) stays blocked.

## Acceptance / fix direction

## #16618 — The QuarantineAll guard retained after a failed guarded IPsec divert transition, and the daemon's ambiguous-removal and shutdown fallbacks, are built from lifeline-free normal specs. Their input chain is {lo accept, DROP} and drops fxp0... [OPEN]

## Summary
The QuarantineAll guard retained after a failed guarded IPsec divert transition, and the daemon's ambiguous-removal and shutdown fallbacks, are built from lifeline-free normal specs. Their input chain is {lo accept, DROP} and drops fxp0 and cluster control/fabric ingress.

**Finding ID:** R3-F01-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — management and cluster control/fabric input lockout until console intervention or a later successful commit, which cannot arrive over fxp0. Bounded because it needs a post-ACK transition failure (drain/old.close error, divert replace, readback or guard-removal failure) or a double failure on removal/shutdown. The HA effect (inbound heartbeat/sync loss on em0/fab) is potential and not executed. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A transient netlink or queue-close fault during a routine VPN change can lock out out-of-band management and cluster control/fabric ingress on that node, which leaves only console recovery.

**Contract:** #14696 scope: lifeline exemption for QuarantineAll on "queue/actor transient failures" and "orphaned quarantine/divert tables after a failed guarded transition". `pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert.go:692-697`: "on input only, lifeline ingress survives quarantine so management (fxp0 / configured control/fabric) is not blackholed ahead of host-inbound".

**Trace:** VPN change with an existing runtime → `commitIpsecCaptureStage` → `InstallIpsecDivertWithDrain` installs the lifeline-free guard (-200 input/forward, inet+bridge) → drain/replace/readback/guard-removal fails → guard retained, runtime nil, orphaned flag set → fxp0/em0/fab input dropped ahead of `xpf_hostinbound` until a later commit removes it.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1027-1031` stamps lifelines in `finalize`, then clears them when `!QuarantineAll` (normal plans). `ipsec_divert.go:513` `spec = normalizeIpsecQuarantineSpec(spec)` clears lifelines for a non-quarantine spec (`:150-151` `spec.LifelineNetdevs = nil`), and only then does `:530` build the guard with `LifelineNetdevs: append([]string(nil), spec.LifelineNetdevs...)` (always empty). The same holds in `installNormalUnderQuarantineGuard` `:405`. Failure retains the guard (`:544-557`); the daemon restores nil (`ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1694-1702`). Fallbacks `:1646` (`IpsecDivertSpec{QuarantineAll: true}` or `old.spec`), `:1733/:1741` (`staged.spec`), `:1854` (`active.spec`). Correction to the reporter: the actor-start arms (`:1733/:1741`) are effectively unreachable, because `IpsecCapturePipeline.Start` (`ipsec_capture_pipeline_9506.go:251-258`) fails only for a nil or already-started actor and the staged actor is always fresh.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf01/probes/zz_vf01_guard_kernel_test.go` under `unshare -Urn`: seed a normal divert, then `InstallIpsecDivertWithDrain(normal spec with LifelineNetdevs=[fxp0], drain → error)`. Output `vf01-01-nft-kernel.out`: "guarded transition err=quarantine recovery drain: injected old.close failure", "retained guard xpf_ipsec_quarantine_guard inet input: rules=2 fxp0-matches=0". `zz_vf01_actor_fail_lifeline_test.go` (output `vf01-01-daemon.out`) drives the real `commitIpsecCaptureStage` through its fallback seam: "fallback guard: QuarantineAll=true lifelines=[]". The control, a staged spec carrying fxp0, records `[fxp0]`. The kernel positive control (a guard WITH fxp0) failed to load with EOPNOTSUPP; that failure is R3-VF01-S1, and the guard-with-lifeline shape was instead validated at render level by f01's `TestR3F01QuarantineWithLifelineControl` (4 rules). Limits: no traffic was sent.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Carry the caller's lifelines into every QuarantineAll the daemon or installer builds: copy `LifelineNetdevs` into the transition guard BEFORE normalizing the normal spec (or keep them in a field normalize does not clear), and stamp them from the live config in `installIpsecQuarantine9506`, the ambiguous-removal fallback and the shutdown fallback. This must land with or after R3-VF01-S1's fix; otherwise every guard that gains lifelines will also fail to load on the bridge family. Acceptance: the kernel cell shows fxp0 iif/sdif accepts in the retained inet guard, and the daemon fallback cell records `[fxp0]`.

- **Refutation attempt:** I checked whether any lower-priority chain could rescue the packet (an ACCEPT in another base chain cannot override this chain's DROP), whether `HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs` could be empty (it always contains fxp0), whether the daemon re-stamps lifelines before the guard is built (it does not), and whether the transient guard during a SUCCESSFUL transition matters (tens of ms, not weighted). Fix a6ac0c1a46 is an ancestor of the base. I narrowed the reporter's claim by dropping the unreachable actor-start trigger.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Not a hot path. Ownership: the orphan flag is in-memory only (per the fix commit's own Risk note), so after a daemon restart, recovery depends on the next apply.

## #16619 — An inbound persistent-NAT session that is also source-NATed (for example by an untrust->trust source-nat rule-set) never takes the #15111 inbound hold. `acquire_persistent_inbound_hold` skips it on `rewrite_src.is_som... [OPEN]

## Summary
An inbound persistent-NAT session that is also source-NATed (for example by an untrust->trust source-nat rule-set) never takes the #15111 inbound hold. `acquire_persistent_inbound_hold` skips it on `rewrite_src.is_some()`, but the SNAT allocation is keyed by the remote and never joins the internal host's lease, so the binding expires and its tuple is reissued under the live inbound session.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — the same consequence class as #15111 (prior A76-04, Medium). The binding expires `inactivity-timeout` after the last outbound flow while an inbound session through it lives. The tuple is freed and can be minted for another host. New remotes then lose the mapping, or reach a different host's lease. The prerequisite is an operator config (inbound SNAT on the persistent-DNAT path, a common "make the server reply symmetric" pattern). It does not bypass policy.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A76-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va76.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
#15111 was fixed because inbound-only use let a binding expire and be reissued. This exemption reintroduces that for every deployment that source-NATs inbound traffic, while the code comment claims the case is covered.

**Contract:** #15111/#15644 commit text: "acquire ... once the final NAT decision is composed (skipped when SNAT joined via active_flows ...)". The intent is that every session using the binding keeps it alive. Junos persistent NAT starts the inactivity timer only when no session uses the binding.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:916-940`: "Skipped when SNAT composed a source rewrite (that flow joins the lease via active_flows instead)", followed by `if decision_nat.rewrite_src.is_some() || decision_nat.rewrite_dst.is_none() || ... { return false; }`. The call site comment at `:6551` repeats the premise. `:6420-6480`: `nat_match_flow = flow.with_destination(effective_resolution_target, policy_dst_port)` then `source_nat_decision_for_flow(..., &nat_match_flow, ...)` and `decision.nat.merge(snat_decision)`, so the source stays the remote's. `nat/source/keys.rs:53-63`: the lease key uses the flow's `src_ip/src_port`. The HA twin `nat/source/synced.rs:212-218` returns early on `nat.rewrite_src.is_some()`.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `acquire_persistent_inbound_hold` was called directly with the composed decision, together with an allocator probe that a remote-sourced SNAT through the same persistent pool does not touch X's lease. The composition in the poll loop is STATIC.

## #16620 — Static `preference` values written on the Junos scale are rendered verbatim as FRR distances, while OSPF, IS-IS, RIP and BGP keep FRR's default distances. A floating static backup can therefore become primary (against OSPF internal, IS-IS, RIP or… [OPEN]

## Summary

Static `preference` values written on the Junos scale are rendered verbatim as FRR distances, while OSPF, IS-IS, RIP and BGP keep FRR's default distances. A floating static backup can therefore become primary (against OSPF internal, IS-IS, RIP or iBGP), and a static meant to win can lose (against OSPF external).

**Finding ID:** `R3-A10-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — The wrong active route is selected for configs whose static preference falls between the two scales. Traffic takes the backup path, often a different uplink, while the dynamic route is healthy, and floating-static redundancy designs fail silently. The render is demonstrated; zebra's selecti…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — It is reachable with an ordinary strict-commit-clean config. Junos-scale preferences are the product's stated input language, and nothing documents or warns about the scale change.

## Mechanism

`routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 { next-hop G; preference 180; }` is a Junos backup to the iBGP default at 170. It compiles to `StaticRoute.Preference=180` and renders as `ip route 0.0.0.0/0 G 180`. Zebra compares 180 with iBGP 200, installs the static and demotes BGP; the kernel FIB, and the helper's FIB import, follow zebra. Likewise `preference 12` (a backup to OSPF internal 10) beats OSPF 110. In the other direction, `preference 120` meant to beat OSPF external 150 loses to OSPF 110.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/frr/config_render.go:568-577` does `dist := sr.Preference; if nh.HasPreference { dist = nh.Preference }; dist = clampFRRStaticRouteDistance(dist)` and then writes `"%s route %s %s %d%s"`. Discard and reject use the same distance at :466-476. No non-test file in `pkg/frr` renders a `distance` statement: grep hits only comments about the DHCP 200, cluster 250 and ip-monitoring 1 statics. `pkg/config/schema_routing.go` OSPF and BGP containers (:367-600) have no `preference` leaf; the only `preference` leaves are static/qnh (:121,:146) and RA (:779). Policy `then preference` is not rendered either: `policy_render.go` has only `set local-preference`.

## Impact

Floating statics are the standard Junos way to back up a dynamic route. A migrated vSRX config, which the product exists to accept, silently gets the opposite primary/backup choice in these windows, and `show route` shows nothing unusual. The blast radius is all traffic to the affected prefix, for as long as the config stands.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Render Junos default preferences into FRR, per instance and globally: `distance ospf intra-area 10 inter-area 10 external 150`, `distance bgp 170 170 170`, and IS-IS/RIP distances. Keep an omitted static preference at Junos 5, and keep the internal DHCP, cluster and ip-monitoring distances consistent with the new scale. Alternatively, translate static preferences onto FRR's scale. Acceptance: the managed section carries the protocol distances, and a zebra-level or table-driven check shows `preference 180` losing to iBGP and `preference 12` losing to OSPF internal.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper's "Understanding Route Preference Values" gives Static 5, OSPF internal 10, IS-IS L1 15 / L2 18, RIP 100, OSPF AS external 150 and BGP 170, "with a lower value indicating a more preferred route". FRR's zebra documentation gives Static 1, EBGP 20, OSPF 110, ISIS 115, RIP 120 and IBGP 200. `pkg/frr/README.md:821-841` presents `preference` as the Junos floating-static idiom rendered as the FRR admin distance, with no scale caveat.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A10-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A10-04 | Medium | Static preference values written on the Junos scale are rendered verbatim as FRR distances,… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:16: - **R3-A10-04 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** static and qualified-next-hop Junos `preference` is emitted as the *same integer* in FRR `ip route ... <distance>`; negative-route preference likewise (`pkg/frr/config_render.go:465-479,568-576`). The renderer offers no corresponding protocol-distance remapping: FRR's [default distances](https://docs.frrouting.org/en/stable-10.7/zebra.html) include OSPF 110, RIP 120, iBGP 200, versus different Junos preferences. Static 12 beats FRR OSPF 110 despite losing to Junos OSPF internal 10; static 180 beats FRR iBGP 200 despite losing to Junos BGP 170. **Best alternative:** no inversion for every peer protocol/value (eBGP at FRR 20 is a notable counterexample), and zebra arbitration was inferred/documented rather than run on the current checkout. **Remaining check:** render current assembled config and validate zebra winner with overlapping static and dynamic routes in representative VRFs, including inactive/qualified next hops.

## #16621 — BGP authentication xpf cannot render (top-level `protocols bgp authentication-key`, `authentication-key-chain` / `authentication-algorithm` at group and neighbor level) commits with only a generic advisory, and the peer is rendered without TCP-MD5 [OPEN]

## Summary

BGP authentication xpf cannot render (top-level `protocols bgp authentication-key`, `authentication-key-chain` / `authentication-algorithm` at group and neighbor level) commits with only a generic advisory, and the peer is rendered without TCP-MD5

**Finding ID:** `R3-A11-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the configured routing-protocol authentication is dropped while the config reads as protected. Against a keyed peer, the TCP-MD5 mismatch keeps the peering down (an outage of that session). When both ends drop the key (for example two xpf peers carrying the same migrated config), the sessio…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — authored credential statements are dropped with only a generic advisory, contrary to the #8443/#15136 refusal doctrine the project applies to every other routing protocol.

## Mechanism

`set protocols bgp authentication-key s3cret` → SetPath unknown child of `bgp` → SchemaValidate open-world skip → #10707 generic advisory → compileProtocols has no reader → `BGPNeighbor.AuthPassword` empty → `protocols_render_bgp.go` emits no `neighbor X password` → bgpd runs the session without TCP-MD5.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/schema_routing.go:488-505` (the `bgp` node declares local-as, router-id, cluster-id, graceful-restart, log-updown, multipath, damping, export, import and group; no auth leaf); `:506-590` (group and neighbor declare only `authentication-key`; no keychain or algorithm leaf and no refusal stub). `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:797` (group) and `compiler_bgp_neighbor_merge_9192.go:343` (neighbor) are the only `case "authentication-key"` readers for BGP; the top-level switch has none. `pkg/config/compiler_openworld_10707.go:79-84` emits the generic `unmodeled configuration keyword %q ... may be silently ignored (#10707)`. Contrast: OSPF `authentication keychain` is refused as a closed-world subtree.

## Impact

One key under `protocols bgp` for every peer is the canonical Junos spelling, and key-chains are the modern one. Migrated configs commit, then either lose every keyed peering or run them unauthenticated. `show configuration` still shows the key, and only `show bgp neighbor` reveals its absence.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Either implement top-level `authentication-key` inheritance (most-specific wins) or refuse it. Add refusal stubs, in the `unmodeledOSPFKeychainLeaf` shape, for `authentication-key-chain` and `authentication-algorithm` at bgp, group and neighbor level, in both `protocols bgp` and `routing-instances <ri> protocols bgp`, with a specific warning on the tolerant path. Acceptance: each probe row either renders `neighbor 10.0.0.2 password ...` or is strict-rejected naming the statement; the control rows are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos accepts `authentication-key`, `authentication-key-chain` and `authentication-algorithm` at `[edit protocols bgp]`, `group` and `neighbor` level; a top-level key is inherited by all groups and neighbors. In-tree doctrine: `pkg/config/schema_ospf_authentication_8443.go:1-45` says unmodelled authentication is "modeled here SOLELY so it is refused", because "the operator believes the adjacency is protected, and every surface they can check agrees with them". #15136 extended that refusal to OSPFv3 and virtual-links.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A11-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A11-01 | Medium | BGP authentication xpf cannot render (top-level protocols bgp authentication-key,… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:20: - **R3-A11-01 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** BGP top-level authentication-key and group/neighbor key-chain or algorithm are not schema fields or compiler readers (`pkg/config/schema_routing.go:488-595`, `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:790-800`, `pkg/config/compiler_bgp_neighbor_merge_9192.go:305-344`), and the open-world advisory is generic (`pkg/config/compiler_openworld_10707.go:78-84`). Only compiled `AuthPassword` renders a password (`pkg/frr/protocols_render_bgp.go:138-141`), so the prior strict-commit probe saw missing TCP-MD5 for these supported Junos spellings. **Best alternative:** unlike absolute silent acceptance, the base probe got a #10707 warning; a keyed remote peer will fail session establishment, not automatically create a working unauthenticated adjacency. **Remaining check:** run present-revision `CommitCheck` for top-level and group/neighbor variants in default and VRF BGP and require either explicit refusal or an inherited password line.

## #16622 — #16081 REST connection gate is one global 256-slot pool with no per-source share: one unauthenticated host holding 256 connections on any leg locks every operator out of every REST/HTTPS leg [OPEN]

## Summary
#16081 REST connection gate is one global 256-slot pool with no per-source share: one unauthenticated host holding 256 connections on any leg locks every operator out of every REST/HTTPS leg

**Finding ID:** R3-N10-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — demonstrated loss of the whole REST/J-Web management surface (HTTP and HTTPS, every bind family, loopback /metrics included) to any host the host-inbound `http`/`https` service admits, with no credential; bounded because SSH/CLI/gRPC are unaffected, enforcement is not loosened, and service returns when the attacker stops.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Any host on the management segment, or any local user, can deny every operator the REST API (config set/commit/rollback, system actions) and blind Prometheus scraping for as long as it holds 256 cheap sockets. Recovery means identifying and blocking the source. The appliance's own HTTPS management is the affected surface.

**Contract:** `pkg/api/conn_bound_16081.go:11-20` says the bound exists because "an attacker opening many idle or slow connections could ... den[y] legitimate management clients"; the fix is supposed to prevent that denial, not make it cheaper. REST is the documented remote management API (README / pkg/api/README.md).

**Trace:** commit `system services web-management http/https` (or default loopback API) → daemon management reconciler → `api.Server` legs → `boundListener(ln)` sharing one `apiConnGate` → `Accept` → `tryAcquire` false for every new connection on any leg while 256 are held → immediate close (RST) → operator's REST/J-Web/scrape refused.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/api/conn_bound_16081.go:62` `var apiMaxConnsTotal = 256`; `:83-93` `tryAcquire` is a global CAS on `g.active` with no peer identity; `:160-180` `boundedListener.Accept` closes any accept past the limit and returns a `Temporary()` error; `:39-42` holds the slot "for the connection's whole life, including keep-alive idle time". `pkg/api/listener.go:302` and `pkg/api/server.go:1604,1613` wrap every leg with the same `s.connGate`. `pkg/api/server.go:840-848`: ReadHeaderTimeout 10 s, IdleTimeout 120 s; any request renews the idle clock. `pkg/api/auth_throttle_10825.go` header: the throttle counts failed credential attempts per source/account and answers 429. It never closes the connection or releases a gate slot. I observed in the probe that 401/429 responses keep the connection alive. An inference, not executed: request-less connections recycled every <10 s also hold the pool.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestN10ConnBound -count=1 -v` with `RUN/verify/vn10/probes/zz_n10_connbound_probe_test.go` (the worker's probe, re-run unchanged), output `RUN/verify/vn10/connbound_rerun.out`: positive control 1 — operator with a valid API key on leg 127.0.0.1 → 200; attacker opens 256 credential-less keep-alive connections on leg 127.0.0.2, renews them after 1.5 s → `active=256`; operator with valid key on leg A → `connection reset by peer refusals=1`; positive control 2 — attacker closes → operator 200. Limits: loopback only; the remote-host and TLS-handshake shapes are not executed.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Partition the gate. Options: a per-source-IP (or per /64) sub-limit well below 256; a reserved share for loopback and for connections that have authenticated; `Connection: close` on 401/403/429 so an uncredentialed client cannot keep a slot; optionally evict the oldest unauthenticated idle connection when full. Consumers: `boundedListener`, `listenerHandler` auth path. Acceptance: the probe above leaves the authenticated operator on the other leg served (200) while one source holds its maximum, and the #16081 excess-refusal test still passes.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn10.md)</summary>

It never closes the connection or releases a gate slot. I observed in the probe that 401/429 responses keep the connection alive. An inference, not executed: request-less connections recycled every <10 s also hold the pool.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestN10ConnBound -count=1 -v` with `RUN/verify/vn10/probes/zz_n10_connbound_probe_test.go` (the worker's probe, re-run unchanged), output `RUN/verify/vn10/connbound_rerun.out`: positive control 1 — operator with a valid API key on leg 127.0.0.1 → 200; attacker opens 256 credential-less keep-alive connections on leg 127.0.0.2, renews them after 1.5 s → `active=256`; operator with valid key on leg A → `connection reset by peer refusals=1`; positive control 2 — attacker closes → operator 200. Limits: loopback only; the remote-host and TLS-handshake shapes are not executed.
- **Trace:** commit `system services web-management http/https` (or default loopback API) → daemon management reconciler → `api.Server` legs → `boundListener(ln)` sharing one `apiConnGate` → `Accept` → `tryAcquire` false for every new connection on any leg while 256 are held → immediate close (RST) → operator's REST/J-Web/scrape refused.
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for a per-source cap, a reserve for loopback or authenticated connections, or connection close on 401/403/429. None exists (whole file read; the throttle file never touches the gate). I checked the fix's own test: it only asserts that excess connections are refused. I checked the pre-fix cost: there is no LimitNOFILE in the shipped units and Go raises the soft fd limit to the hard limit, so before 94c3961658 the same 256 connections were harmless. Worker f15 dismissed this as a design tradeoff. I reject that: the tradeoff defeats the very property the file says it protects, and needs no credential. I narrowed the claim: keep-alive renewal is sufficient but not necessary.
- **HPC/invariant check:** The gate's accounting is correct (exactly-once release, TLS counted at raw TCP). The defect is the admission policy, not the counting. A sustained refusal flood also makes `http.Server` back off up to 1 s per refusal on the flooded leg (`Temporary()` path). That stretches recovery for legitimate clients on that leg after the attack.

## #16623 — `buildPBRFromFilter` records only terms with an explicit action or routing-instance as terminating, so a `then count`/`log`/`forwarding-class`-only carve-out (an implicit accept since #14632) does not shadow a later steer. The kernel... [OPEN]

## Summary
`buildPBRFromFilter` records only terms with an explicit action or routing-instance as terminating, so a `then count`/`log`/`forwarding-class`-only carve-out (an implicit accept since #14632) does not shadow a later steer. The kernel installs an ip rule into the routing instance for traffic userspace leaves in the main table.

**Finding ID:** R3-F01-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — plane divergence on kernel-forwarded (slow-path / XDP_PASS) ingress on the attached interface. Carved-out prefixes are policy-routed into another VRF/ISP, with no degraded signal. This is the #11325 carve-out-bypass class, bounded to the kernel path; userspace-forwarded traffic is correct. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Kernel-path traffic matching a carve-out (often management or local prefixes kept on the main table) is sent via another VRF or ISP. The divergence is silent: no degraded error, and `show firewall` / userspace counters say the carve-out accepted.

**Contract:** #14632 (3587ef059c): "Fall-through is now only the authored `then next term`"; a modifier-only term "terminates as implicit Accept". `pkg/routing/rules.go:1520-1523` (#11325): a prior terminating term that can match the same packet must suppress a later steer.

**Trace:** `set firewall family inet filter fbf term carve from source-address 10.0.0.0/8; then count mgmt; term steer from source-address 10.1.0.0/16 then routing-instance ISP2`, attached as an input filter → strict compile → `BuildPBRRules` → `buildPBRFromFilter` → carve not in `precedingTerminating` → steer emitted → kernel `ip rule from 10.1.0.0/16 iif ge-0-0-2 lookup <ISP2>`. Userspace terminates at carve with no override.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/routing/rules.go:1537` `if term.Action != config.FilterActionUnset || term.RoutingInstance != "" { precedingTerminating = append(...) }`. `grep NextTerm pkg/routing/*.go` (non-test) gives 0 hits. `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1588-1590` `continue_term: snap.next_term && snap.action.is_empty() && snap.routing_instance.is_empty()`. `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs:690-707`: a matched non-continue term with no routing-instance returns None via `?`. `pbrTermsMayOverlap` (`rules.go:1798-1825`) returns true for 10/8 vs 10.1/16.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf01/probes/zz_vf01_modonly_e2e_test.go`, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/routing/ -run TestVF01 -count=1 -v`, output `vf01-02-routing.out`. `then count mgmt` gives "Action=\"\" NextTerm=false Count=\"mgmt\" -> rules=1", "rule {Src:10.1.0.0/16 TableID:979494 Instance:ISP2 IifName:ge-0-0-2}". Control `count mgmt` + `accept` gives "rules=0 err=PBR filter fbf term steer is shadowed by a preceding terminating term". Twin `count mgmt` + `next term` gives rules=1 (correct). f01's direct-builder probe agrees.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In `buildPBRFromFilter` treat a term as terminating unless `term.NextTerm && term.Action == Unset && term.RoutingInstance == ""`, matching Rust. Acceptance: the count-only cell yields 0 rules plus the shadow degraded error; the next-term twin still yields 1 rule.

## #16624 — The cluster RA shared-identity predicate `isSharedStableRASource` matches only the auto `fe80::…bf72…` pattern. A configured RETH-unit link-local, which is installed as an RG VIP, therefore gets per-node goodbye handling on demotion and at cold-boot standby. This is the leg of #14978 its fix did not cover. [OPEN]

## Summary

The cluster RA shared-identity predicate `isSharedStableRASource` matches only the auto `fe80::…bf72…` pattern. A configured RETH-unit link-local, which is installed as an RG VIP, therefore gets per-node goodbye handling on demotion and at cold-boot standby. This is the leg of #14978 its fix did not cover.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A26-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — this is bounded HA IPv6 router-identity disruption for clusters that pin a router link-local on a RETH unit. That configuration is supported and documented: #15148 calls it "the operator's router link-local (installed as an RG VIP on the primary)". Demonstrated: the misclassification on all three paths. Potential, not re-run here: on demotion the goodbye is attempted after the VIP is removed, which fails and leaves a bind-retry stall plus goodbye debt on the HA event path (the Y48-01 netns measurement gave EINVAL/EADDRNOTAVAIL). A cold-boot standby logs a Warn on every reconcile tick. A retry that races promotion can send a lifetime-0 RA from the shared identity, so hosts drop the default router until the next RA. No enforcement loss. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the closed owner's fix predicate demonstrably misses the exact spelling its issue named, and its regression test pins the wrong behaviour.

## Mechanism

Shared config with fe80::1/64 on reth0.50 → both nodes run `buildRAConfigs` with SourceLinkLocal=fe80::1 (`daemon_ra.go:141-155`) → the primary holds the VIP → on demotion `applyDirectVIPOwnership(false)` removes fe80::1 → `clearRethRASendersWithoutGoodbye` clears none (predicate false) → `reconcileClusterRAServices` → `ra.Apply` without reth0.50 → graceful goodbye from the removed fe80::1, which fails and leaves retry debt. Separately, cold boot as secondary → `startupGoodbyeConfigs` keeps the config → `WithdrawOnce` binds fe80::1, which is absent → Warn and retry on every tick.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa:

## Impact

Pinning a router link-local so hosts' default router survives a hardware swap is common. Those clusters get the #10779 symptom class back: demotion-path stalls, permanent Warn churn on a healthy cold-boot secondary, and a possible lifetime-0 flash from the shared identity at promotion. That flash costs hosts their IPv6 default router until the next unsolicited RA.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Classify a source as shared when it is VIP-managed for the interface's RG (`cfg.RethVIPsForRG(rg)` contains it) or matches the stable pattern. Apply the same rule in `clusterRAConfigSets`, `sharedStableRAInterfaces` and `startupGoodbyeConfigs`. Change `TestDemotionPerNodeSourceNotSilentlyCleared14978` to a `groups nodeN` per-node fixture. Acceptance: with shared-section fe80::1/64, demotion silent-clears `[[ge-0-0-0.50]]` and `startupGoodbyeConfigs` returns nothing, while a `groups nodeN` per-node link-local keeps its graceful goodbye. The #10779/#10789/#14978 cells must stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

#14978's own title is "…Withdraws Shared Router Identity on Configured RETH Link-Locals…", and leg 1 of its source D34-01 is `fe80::1/64` on a RETH unit. Its acceptance requires "a regression test … exercising the exact D34-01 mechanism (same path/spelling/state as claimed)". `pkg/daemon/reth_configured_linklocal_15148_test.go:13-14` says a configured fe80::1/64 on a RETH unit is the router link-local installed as an RG VIP. Per the comment at `daemon_ha.go:1985-1987`, a shared identity must be stopped without a lifetime-0 RA.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A26-02` (parts file `parts/va26.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A26-02 | Medium | The cluster RA shared-identity predicate isSharedStableRASource matches only the auto…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): Same claim as D34-01 leg 1, filed as #14978 (CLOSED by `d060e38e95`, in base), whose fix predicate misses it. Also the same claim as prior unfiled Y48-01 (`/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-001.md`, the Y48-01 entry). Sibling #15148 (link-tail strip) is a different site. No open owner in gh-issues.tsv or this run's parts. File as a residual referencing #14978 and Y48-01; do not count it as a new root class.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A26-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16625 — RIP per-group `export` is flattened into one global ripd redistribute chain: two groups with different export policies commit strict-clean, and depending on stanza order one group loses its routes or the other receives routes its policy excludes [OPEN]

## Summary

RIP per-group `export` is flattened into one global ripd redistribute chain: two groups with different export policies commit strict-clean, and depending on stanza order one group loses its routes or the other receives routes its policy excludes

**Finding ID:** `R3-A12-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — this is a loss of routing-policy enforcement on a Junos-native shape. The per-group export boundary ("customers get only a default", "core gets the statics") is erased. One authoring order leaks internal statics to the restricted group's neighbours. The other drops the permissive group's ad…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a strict-clean commit enforces an export set different from the authored per-group policy, with an observed leak and an observed loss.

## Mechanism

`protocols rip group CUSTOMERS { export DEFAULT-ONLY; neighbor ge-0/0/1.0; } group CORE { export ALL-STATIC; neighbor ge-0/0/2.0; }` compiles to RIPConfig{Interfaces:[ge-0/0/1.0 ge-0/0/2.0], Redistribute:[DEFAULT-ONLY ALL-STATIC]}. The renderer emits one composed redistribute route-map per source protocol. ripd advertises that route set on every `network` interface.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:1116-1140` @d1ea69f9aa: `case "neighbor": proto.RIP.Interfaces = append(proto.RIP.Interfaces, firewallMatchValues(gc)...)` / `case "export": proto.RIP.Redistribute = append(proto.RIP.Redistribute, firewallMatchValues(gc)...)` inside the per-group loop. `pkg/config/types_routing.go:556-562`: `RIPConfig` has Interfaces, Passive, Redistribute, AuthKey and AuthType, with no group field. `pkg/frr/protocols_render_rip.go:90-97`: one `router rip` with `network` per interface and a single `resolveRedistributeChainCluster15158(rip.Redistribute, ...)`. No strict or warn validator compares exports across groups (grep of compiler_validate*.go).

## Impact

Operators use RIP groups toward customer or CPE edges, where the per-group export is the isolation mechanism. A green commit either advertises internal prefixes to customers or withdraws core advertisements, and which one happens depends only on stanza order. It persists until the config is changed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At strict commit, refuse RIP configs with two or more groups whose export lists differ (warn and fail closed on tolerant load), until per-group export is modelled. If it is modelled, carry the group to export association into RIPConfig and render per-interface output filtering (`distribute-list prefix … out <if>`) where expressible. Acceptance: the probe config is rejected, or the CUSTOMERS interface never receives 192.168.50.0/24 and the CORE interface receives it, in both orders.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper `group (Protocols RIP)` (fetched 2026-10-23): "Configure a set of RIP neighbors that share an export policy and metric. The export policy and metric govern what routes to advertise to neighbors in a given group … You should create a group for every export policy." The xpf schema describes group export as "Protocols redistributed into this group" (`pkg/config/schema_routing.go:634-640`). Chain semantics (first terminal action wins) come from #5277/#15156.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A12-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A12-03 | Medium | RIP per-group export is flattened into one global ripd redistribute chain: two groups with… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:30: - **R3-A12-03 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** group-specific RIP neighbor interfaces and `export` policies are separately appended into global lists, losing the group association (`pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:1113-1140`, `pkg/config/types_routing.go:555-562`). ripd uses one network/redistribute chain for every interface (`pkg/frr/protocols_render_rip.go:90-97`); the prior two-group RIP run observed a customer export leak or a core route omission depending on policy order. **Best alternative:** one group or identical policies has no association loss; generic policy-chain composition works on its own terms, so this is not evidence that *all* RIP export behavior is broken. **Remaining check:** current strict commit plus two opposite-order group policies, and prove current FRR per-neighbor advertisements or reject the unsupported shape.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L24: | R3-A12-03 RIP per-group export flattened | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-05 VL-only area on standby hard-fails apply | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-02 BFD-default perpetual --test diff | COHORT | Low | | R3-A12-04 OSPF key >16/>8 truncation + perpetual diff | COHORT | Low | | R3-A13-01 deny-* bracket list first-token only | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A13-02 permission fold widens to PermView vs doc | COHORT (doc/advisory only) | Low | | R3-A14-05 wakeAt never cleared busy-spin | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A14-01 parked direction skips windowing, until ceiling defeated | MATERIAL | Medium-Low | | R3-A14-04 within children escape closed-world gate | MATERIAL | Medium |

## #16626 — R3-A48-05: After vrf-mgmt is deleted and re-created (the #15223 reassert path), the running SNMP listener stays bound to the dead VRF ifindex and is deaf until a VRF-name… [OPEN]

## Summary

After vrf-mgmt is deleted and re-created (the #15223 reassert path), the running SNMP listener stays bound to the dead VRF ifindex and is deaf until a VRF-name change or daemon restart

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low. The trigger is an out-of-band root `ip link del vrf-mgmt`, the same class #15223 rated Low. The result is a silent, indefinite SNMP poll outage while the rest of management is healed. The outage is demonstrated at the socket level. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A48-05`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va48.md` (finding `R3-A48-05`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

At d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/daemon/mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:54-60` re-creates the device. `:70-79` re-binds members and `:88` calls `reconcileClusterTransportBinding`. There is no SNMP call. The only non-test SNMP restart callers are `reconcileSNMP` (`daemon_apply.go:523`) and the boot block (`daemon_run.go:601`). `daemon_snmp_reconcile.go:743`: `if d.snmpHashSet && h == d.snmpHash && d.snmpVRFDevice == vrfDevice { return false }`. `snmpConfigHash` hashes the device name (`:70-71`). `pkg/snmp/socket_vrf.go:20` binds once at `Bind`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #15223's acceptance is that one reassert tick re-creates vrf-mgmt and restores management-plane binding without a commit. `pkg/snmp/README.md` "Live reconfigure" says a changed management-VRF bind restarts the listener.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (SNMP agent lifecycle and IF-MIB conformance residuals; residual of #15223). It is a real, bounded residual with a root-only trigger.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED for the socket behaviour (netns probe). STATIC for the absence of an SNMP hook in the reassert and reconcile paths.

**Confidence:** High. It was executed with the production Agent and the reassert tick was read in full. The remaining assumption is that production re-creation matches the probe's `ip link add` sequence (`ensureVRFDeviceForReassert` + `BindInterfaceToVRF`).

## Impact

The operator sees management restored (ssh, DHCP and HA transport re-bound by #15223) while the NMS marks the box unreachable, and nothing logs that SNMP is deaf. Recovery needs a daemon restart or an unrelated edit that changes the SNMP hash or the VRF name.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When `reassertMgmtVRFOnce` re-creates the device, restart the agent under `snmpReconMu` (teardown + `startSNMPLocked`). Alternatively, record the bound VRF ifindex and compare it in `reconcileSNMP` and in the tick. Acceptance: in the probe's defect arm, one reassert tick restores the poll reply.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A48-05`, part `parts/va48.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).
