## #16643 — Two partial publishers, `UpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatch` and `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshotWithLatch`, return "converged" while the helper is down (crash or restart backoff), without writing their content into `m.lastSnapshot`. The supervisor's restart republishes `m.lastSnapshot` unchanged and re-seeds the scheduler lease. As a result, a closing-window permit stays enforced, or an opening-window deny never engages, and an ip-monitoring failover route is missing from the helper FIB. This lasts until the next scheduler transition, ip-monitoring transition or commit. [OPEN]

## Summary

Two partial publishers, `UpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatch` and `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshotWithLatch`, return "converged" while the helper is down (crash or restart backoff), without writing their content into `m.lastSnapshot`. The supervisor's restart republishes `m.lastSnapshot` unchanged and re-seeds the scheduler lease. As a result, a closing-window permit stays enforced, or an opening-window deny never engages, and an ip-monitoring failover route is missing from the helper FIB. This lasts until the next scheduler transition, ip-monitoring transition or commit.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A29-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. A time-boxed security policy silently becomes a standing one. In the permissive direction, a closing-window permit stays live; in the protective direction, an opening-window deny never engages. The duration is unbounded by any retry: it ends at the scheduler's next state change (hours for a work-hours window) or at an unrelated Compile or scheduler-aware overlay publish. The overlay sibling splits the FIB, so WAN failover is missing from the helper. The trigger needs a helper exit that overlaps a transition tick, which the 1-60 s restart backoff (process_supervisor.go) of a crash-looping helper makes more likely. The stale state is the last-good configured state, not arbitrary content, so this is not High. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable fault trigger (helper crash during a transition), concrete consequence (scheduled-policy enforcement wrong for hours), no retry owner, no existing issue.

## Mechanism

Window open, so the permit is active in `m.lastSnapshot`. The helper exits, and `resetAfterHelperGoneLocked` sets proc=nil and publishedSnapshot=0. The scheduler tick computes workhours=false and calls `publishPolicyScheduleStateWithLatch` → `UpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatch`, which stages the desired map and returns nil. The scheduler records the transition as converged. After the backoff, `restartHelperAfterCrash` → `ensureProcessLocked` (no publish) → `ensureStatusLoopLocked`. The status tick runs `syncSnapshotLocked`, which publishes `*m.lastSnapshot` (permit inactive=false) and sends a heartbeat. Later converged scheduler ticks only heartbeat, so the helper keeps enforcing the permit past its window.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:1261-1263` stages `m.policySchedulerDesired = activeCopy`. At `:1276-1281`, `if m.proc == nil || m.proc.Process == nil { ... return nil }` runs before any clone or rebuild. Grep for `policySchedulerDesired` readers finds only `manager_compile.go:232` (`policySchedulerDesiredStateAndFailClosedSnapshot`, used by Compile). `process_status.go:125` `retained := *m.lastSnapshot` is the publish source after restart; no scheduler-section rebuild occurs on that path. `apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go:465-472` `recordSchedulerSnapshotAppliedLocked` sends a scheduler heartbeat after the publish, which renews the lease around the stale bits. `pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go:345-353`: when nothing changed and nothing is pending, the tick calls only `heartbeatFn`. A nil `updateFn` result clears pending (`recordRepublishResultLocked`), so the 5-minute #5669 FAIL-OPEN-STALE escalation (scheduler.go:102) never arms. Overlay sibling: `manager_overlay.go:143-147` deferred-commits `m.routeOverlay` on a nil error, and `:168-170` returns `(false, nil)` when proc is nil. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:507-514` treats `!published && !d.pendingFIBBump` as "Converged".

## Impact

Deployments that use `scheduler-name` on policies (access windows) or `services ip-monitoring`, on a box whose helper crashes, are affected. A crash loop multiplies the exposure. The blast radius is every scheduled rule, or the failover prefix, box-wide. The stale state persists for hours with no metric: the scheduler reports converged and the republish-stale gauges stay clear. Recovery is any commit, or the next window or probe transition.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In both helperless arms, either return a retryable error, so the scheduler keeps `republishPending` and ipmon stays dirty (heartbeats then stop and the lease fails scheduled rules closed), or write the desired content into `m.lastSnapshot`. For the scheduler, use `rebuildScheduledPolicySectionsWithLatchLocked`; for the overlay, rebuild routes with the desired overlay, so the restart replay carries it. Keep the #3780 "no snapshot ever published" nil arm. Acceptance: the probe defect cells record `inactive=true` and the overlay route after restart, the helper-up controls stay green, and the existing #3780/#13717 tests pass.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go:336-342` (#3780) says a transition whose republish did not converge must be retried "so the stale enforcement (a permit past its window / a block that never engaged) converges instead of persisting until the next unrelated state change hours away". The helperless arm justifies returning nil only on the premise "The helper restart path re-applies the last snapshot. Converged." (manager_compile.go:1276-1281). That premise is true of the snapshot but false of the transition.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A29-03` (parts file `parts/va29.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A29-03 | Medium | Two partial publishers, UpdatePolicyScheduleStateWithLatch and…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked RUN/evidence/gh-issues.tsv for scheduler + restart/crash/helper/converged and overlay + restart. #3780 (CLOSED) introduced the helperless-converged arm. #13717 (CLOSED, 6f91c5024f) covers latch staging only. #5838 (CLOSED) is the restart path. #9684, #5306 and #9520 concern partial publishers reverting other sections, not desired state lost across a restart. Prior reports in /var/tmp/deep-review-reports/ and this run's drafts/parts have no match for a transition lost across a helper restart. This entry is new.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A29-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A29-03 — A scheduler window transition or an ip-monitoring overlay published while the helper is down is reported converged and then lost: the crash-restart republish sends the stale retained snapshot
- **Finding ID:** R3-A29-03

## #16644 — `test_postinst_triggered_runs_refresh_and_exits_zero` never runs the refresh. The postinst's absolute `/usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots` path is absent on the test host, so the cell asserts only rc 0, the same as its no-helper control. A wron [OPEN]

## Summary
`test_postinst_triggered_runs_refresh_and_exits_zero` never runs the refresh. The postinst's absolute `/usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots` path is absent on the test host, so the cell asserts only rc 0, the same as its no-helper control. A wrong or disabled helper invocation in the `triggered` arm still passes all 19 cells.

**Finding ID:** R3-N06-04
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — if the #15089 triggered-arm invocation broke, A/B ESP slot loaders would stay stale after a shim/grub update until the next boot-time sync in xpf-uefi-slots.service. That is bounded by the backstop, and per R3-A57-02 the trigger rarely fires for real updates anyway. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
the boot-chain refresh is security-relevant (shim/grub fixes), but the boot-time sync backstop bounds the window to one extra boot. The consequence is limited to future regressions of the wiring.

**Contract:** the cell name and its stale-slot ESP fixture (`_esp_with_stale_slot`) claim to verify that `postinst triggered` "runs refresh". debian/xpf.postinst:560-568 describes the arm's purpose: refresh both A/B slot copies so BootOrder does not keep booting the bake-time bootloader.

**Trace:** shim/grub update → dpkg file trigger → `xpf.postinst triggered` → `[ -x helper ]` → helper `--sync-only` refreshes the ESP slots. The test stops at the `-x` test on a build host, so the refresh and its effect on the stale slot are never observed.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
debian/xpf.postinst:569-570 @d1ea69f9aa: `if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots ]; then /usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots --sync-only || true`. scripts/image/test_slot_refresh_15089.py:279-289 builds the stale ESP, sets the env, runs `sh POSTINST triggered` and asserts only `returncode == 0`; its own comment says "in the hermetic run that path does not exist". :298-305 checks only that the substrings `xpf-uefi-slots` and `--sync-only` appear in the arm text. :307-315 is the no-helper control with the same assertion. `ls /usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots` gives "No such file or directory".

**Probe:** `python3 scripts/image/test_slot_refresh_15089.py` gives `OK`. With the mutant (RUN/verify/vn06/probes/postinst-mutant.diff, :570 → `/usr/local/sbin/xpf-uefi-slots.disabled --sync-only || true`) it also gives `OK`. The file was reverted and `git status` is clean. The reporter's identical mutant (workers/n06/evidence/mutant-postinst-triggered.diff) gave 19 tests OK.

## Acceptance / fix direction
make the helper path injectable (for example `XPF_UEFI_SLOTS_BIN` defaulting to the absolute path), or rewrite the path with sed as postinst-test.sh does for layout paths. Point it at the in-tree helper and assert that the stale slot is refreshed. Acceptance: the mutant above reds the cell.

## #16645 — `maybeDeferCooldownLocked` releases `e.mu` mid-loop, so a concurrent same-name redefinition pairs the old policy's commands and plant class with the new semantic revision and passes the #3750 "policy redefined" gate [OPEN]

## Summary

`maybeDeferCooldownLocked` releases `e.mu` mid-loop, so a concurrent same-name redefinition pairs the old policy's commands and plant class with the new semantic revision and passes the #3750 "policy redefined" gate

**Finding ID:** `R3-A14-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low. A retracted command set can commit once, under the new revision, and then its cooldown throttles the new definition. That is the #3750 H2 consequence, but it needs ≥2 policies on one event, an earlier one cooldown-parked, and a redefinition landing in the brief unlock window. The old batch is s…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (eventengine #15021 deferral state/concurrency residuals) — the defect is real, but the window is narrow and the impact is bounded to one stale batch.

## Mechanism

p1 and p2 both list `ping_test_failed`, and p1 is in cooldown → event → evaluate loop → p1 parks, which releases e.mu → `ApplyWithConfig` redefines p2 (new runtime and semRev) → relock → the old p2 object is evaluated and stamped with the new semRev → `HandleEvent` enqueues the old ops and old plant class → `staleReason` returns "" → commit.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:165` captures `e.eventIndex[ev.Name]` once. `:119-129` `e.mu.Unlock()` … `e.pendingMu.Lock()` … `e.mu.Lock()`. `:238` `triggeredPolicy{pol: pol, semRev: e.semRev[pol.Name], …}` reads the new map with the old pol. `engine.go:795` `e.classifyPlan(tp.pol)` and `:817` `plantClass: tp.pol.PlantClass`. `:1601` `if rev != a.semRev` compares revisions only.

## Impact

A redefinition is how an operator retracts a wrong remediation. In this window, exactly the retracted batch commits once and is attributed to the new revision.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Do not release e.mu inside the loop. Collect parked edges into a slice and insert them under pendingMu after evaluate returns. Acceptance: the probe's DEFECT arm yields `policy redefined` (or no p2 action), and the control stays green.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/eventengine/README.md` "Revalidate a queued action before commit (#3750)": "Policy redefined (H2) … the OLD command set must not commit under the new definition". `evaluate.go:19` "everything here runs under e.mu".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A14-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

## #16646 — `ReadInterfaceCounters` resolves a VLAN child's ifindex to its parent binding and returns the parent's full traffic as the unit's own counters with a nil error. There is no per-VLAN source, so sibling units report identical numbers. Prometheus, which dedupes by kernel ifindex, emits the parent's traffic under the parent label and again under every unit label. [OPEN]

## Summary

`ReadInterfaceCounters` resolves a VLAN child's ifindex to its parent binding and returns the parent's full traffic as the unit's own counters with a nil error. There is no per-VLAN source, so sibling units report identical numbers. Prometheus, which dedupes by kernel ifindex, emits the parent's traffic under the parent label and again under every unit label.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A30-01`
**Severity (source report):** Low — an operator-visible counter misstatement on CLI extensive, REST, gRPC, monitor and Prometheus that overstates per-unit traffic and multiplies summed totals. It does not hide missing enforcement. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (interface-counter attribution after #15656, with unfiled prior H5-03) — real but bounded observability lie, grouped with H5-03's disabled/unzoned/non-VLAN child attribution from the same resolver.

## Mechanism

config `ge-0/0/1` units `.50`/`.80` → `allInterfaceNames` → three kernel ifindexes → `ReadInterfaceCounters(99/100)` → `resolvedBindingIfindex` → parent 7 → parent sum returned under each unit label.

## Impact

Per-VLAN dashboards, alerting and capacity/billing on trunks show every unit carrying the whole trunk. `sum()` over the interface family jumps N+1-fold after #15656. DDoS triage cannot tell which VLAN carries the traffic. The state is steady and has no recovery.

## Acceptance / fix direction

For a VLAN child, return an explicit unavailable error until the helper exports per-(ifindex,vlan) counters, or export those counters. Fold H5-03's disabled/unzoned/non-VLAN rows into the same predicate. Acceptance: two sibling units with disjoint traffic never both report the parent total, and the Prometheus family sum equals real traffic.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos `show interfaces <ifd>.<unit>` reports per-logical-unit traffic. #15228 (A44-05) dedupes the Prometheus family so one interface's traffic is emitted once (`pkg/api/metrics_counters.go:524-545`). #15656's acceptance permitted "aggregated counters or explicit error". The aggregated arm is presented under each unit's own label, not as a parent figure.

## Summary
`show security nat source persistent-nat-table` renders every binding as `Permit: any-remote-host`, because the converter keys on `RemoteIP`, which has always been empty since #13945. It also merges distinct helper leases (TCP/UDP on one socket, overlapping-address tenants) into one row, because `persistentNATKey` and `PersistentNATBinding` drop Protocol and RoutingScope.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — an operator-display defect with no enforcement change. The permit line overstates exposure for target-host/target-host-port pools. The merge hides live bindings: the operator sees one of N leases, possibly for the wrong protocol or tenant.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A76-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va76.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
During an incident ("why can X reach H?"), the operator sees a single `any-remote-host` row, possibly for another protocol or tenant, and cannot see the binding that is actually admitting traffic.

**Contract:** #3193: render the three-way permit mode (`pkg/natshow/persistent.go:136-140`). #8607/#8615: the table is a faithful snapshot of the helper's leases. #10018 (`nat/idle_lease_sync_8121.rs:117-119`): "display rows retain the lease's routing domain too, so the operator can distinguish overlapping subscriber identities".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/nat/idle_lease_sync_8121.rs:236-279` sets `remote: None` on every row and fills `permit_any_remote`/`permitted_remotes`. `server/handlers/idle_leases.rs:556-560` maps `None => (String::new(), 0)`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_persistent_nat_show_8607.go:248-256` returns `PersistentNATPermitAnyRemoteHost` when `l.RemoteIP == ""` and ignores `PermitAnyRemote`/`PermittedRemotes`. The idle-export twin at `:358-366` has the same shape. `pkg/dataplane/persistent_nat.go:38-42` defines `persistentNATKey{SrcIP, SrcPort, Pool}`, and `:300-309` overwrites on collision. The conversion (`daemon_persistent_nat_show_8607.go:234-243`) discards `Protocol` and `RoutingScope`, although both are on the wire (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol.go:643-648`).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — Go probe over `persistentNatBindingsFromDisplayLeases` plus `PersistentNATTable.ReplaceAll`. The Rust side is STATIC.

## #16649 — Clear-all is a single-shot helper verb, and the helper hard-caps that verb at 262,144 shared entries (`CLEAR_MIRROR_KEY_CAP`). Above that, `clear security flow session` on CLI, gRPC and REST fails with `mirror-clear:clear-cap-exceeded` and revokes zero sessions. The peer clear is skipped and the policy-invalidation scan debt is not retired. There is no fallback, and no operator document states the ceiling. [OPEN]

## Summary

Clear-all is a single-shot helper verb, and the helper hard-caps that verb at 262,144 shared entries (`CLEAR_MIRROR_KEY_CAP`). Above that, `clear security flow session` on CLI, gRPC and REST fails with `mirror-clear:clear-cap-exceeded` and revokes zero sessions. The peer clear is skipped and the policy-invalidation scan debt is not retired. There is no fallback, and no operator document states the ceiling.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A30-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the operator's authoritative revoke-everything control (#5096: stop forwarding under revoked decisions) is unavailable above roughly 131k concurrent sessions. The shared table's own ceiling is 2 × workers × 131,072 entries, so on a 6-worker node clear-all works for only the first 1/6 of capacity. That is exactly the high-load incident (attack, policy tighten) in which clear-all is used. The failure is bounded: it fails closed and loudly, and filtered clears still work. Demonstrated at the production constant in a component test, not in the lab. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable table size disables the operator's authoritative clear-all and its debt-retirement side effect. No guard or fallback exists.

## Mechanism

operator `clear security flow session` → `cli_clear.go` → `liveDataPlane.ClearAllSessions` (under applySem) → `Manager.ClearAllSessions` → session socket `sync_session{mirror_clear_chunk}` → `SessionDomain::clear_mirror` → `keys.len() > 262144` → `Err` → `ok=false` → Go `(0,0,err)` → CLI error. Zero sessions are revoked, the peer is not cleared, and the scan debt is not retired.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha/session_import.rs:807` `pub(crate) const CLEAR_MIRROR_KEY_CAP: usize = 262_144;`. `:813-822` `let keys ... = lock_shared_recover(&self.sessions.synced).keys().take(cap.saturating_add(1))...; if keys.len() > cap { return Err("clear-cap-exceeded"); }` runs before the BPF sweep or any delete. `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/sync_session.rs:244-253` maps the error to `mirror-clear:{err}`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_sessions.go:1147-1153` sends one `mirror_clear_chunk` and on error returns `0, 0, fmt.Errorf("clear-all: authoritative helper session revocation failed: %w", err)`. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:7519` (forward) and `:7823` (reverse_entry) both call `publish_shared_session` into `worker_ctx.shared_sessions`, which is the coordinator `synced` map (`afxdp/worker/launch.rs:94-99`). `userspace-dp/src/session/README.md:1287` gives the shared ceiling as `2 * worker_count * DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS` (131072, `session/mod.rs:268`). Callers: `pkg/cli/cli_clear.go:178-181` (returns `clear sessions: ...` before `clearPeerSessions`), `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:1463`, `pkg/api/sessions.go:960`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_dp_live.go:440-465` retires scan debt only when `err == nil`.

## Impact

Any node above about 131k concurrent sessions, including the loss cluster at 6 workers × 131k per worker capacity, loses clear-all exactly during incidents. It also loses the documented debt-retirement path when commit-time invalidation was incomplete (#10512). The state lasts as long as the load does. Recovery is filtered clears by prefix or a helper restart, which drops all forwarding state.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Page the clear inside the helper under the existing clear fence (bounded key batches, loop until empty), or clear by generation without materialising a key Vec. At minimum, document the ceiling and have the CLI/gRPC fall back to a bounded filtered sweep. Acceptance: a clear-all of a shared table at 2× the cap revokes every entry and returns accurate counts. The over-cap cell becomes a multi-round success cell, and memory per round stays bounded.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos `clear security flow session` with no filter clears all sessions. The `ClearAllSessions` doc comment (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_sessions.go:1106-1139`) presents it as the authoritative revocation so that clear-all stops forwarding under revoked decisions (#5096/#5881). No README or docs/*.md states a size limit: `grep -rn 'clear-cap\|CLEAR_MIRROR_KEY_CAP' --include=*.md` finds nothing.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A30-02` (parts file `parts/va30.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A30-02 | Medium | Clear-all is a single-shot helper verb, and the helper hard-caps that verb at 262,144…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #5096/#5881/#5882/#5304 (CLOSED; earlier clear-all contracts) and #10512 (465c58701a, ancestor of base; introduced the cap; does not discuss the ceiling). Searched gh-issues.tsv for clear-all/clear security flow, prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports (the only hit, gemini hostile-experts-500-001 L60249, mentions the cap only as the fence duration for a worker-loop issue), and all RUN/drafts/parts and workers reports for `clear-cap`/`CLEAR_MIRROR_KEY_CAP`/262144: no owner.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A30-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A30-02 — `clear security flow session` (clear-all) refuses outright above 262,144 shared session entries (~131k bidirectional sessions) and revokes nothing, on every surface
- **Finding ID:** R3-A30-02

## #16650 — Parked-edge maps are keyed by policy name and not reconciled on `Apply`: a predecessor's parked entry occupies the key and silently swallows the redefined policy's in-cooldown edge [OPEN]

## Summary

Parked-edge maps are keyed by policy name and not reconciled on `Apply`: a predecessor's parked entry occupies the key and silently swallows the redefined policy's in-cooldown edge

**Finding ID:** `R3-A14-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low. One remediation edge is lost, and there is no counter for it. This is the #15021 "only edge" consequence on a narrow path: a same-name redefinition while the predecessor has a parked edge, then a successor commit followed by an in-cooldown successor edge before the stale entry drains. [reporter…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (eventengine #15021 deferral state/concurrency residuals) — real, but the trigger sequence is narrow and the impact is one lost edge.

## Mechanism

R1 commits at t=0 → R1 edge parks at t=5 → redefine at t=10 (fresh runtime, `pending` untouched) → R2 fires and commits at t=12 → R2 edge at t=15 finds the key occupied, is not stored, and its direction is suppressed → drain at t≥42 deletes the R1 entry on semRev mismatch → R2's edge is gone.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:118-127` `key := pol.Name + "\x00" + ev.Name` … `if _, exists := e.pending.cooldown[key]; !exists { … }`, while `:106` sets `suppressedDirection` unconditionally. `engine.go:624-` `apply` never touches `e.pending`. `engine.go:1066-1098` drain: the anchor comes from the successor's runtime, then the semRev mismatch gives `replay=false` and the entry is deleted. `engine.go:1550-1556` `deferBudget` returns false when `pending.budget[a.policyName]` exists (caller drops the successor's action).

## Impact

For `ping_test_failed`, which RPM emits only on a status change, the lost edge is not re-fired. The box stays unremediated until the next status change.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `apply`, purge `pending.cooldown`/`pending.budget` entries whose `action.semRev` no longer matches, adjusting the gauge. Alternatively, let a newer-revision edge replace an older-revision entry. Acceptance: the DEFECT arm replays once, like the control.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/eventengine/README.md` "Cross-policy global action budget": cooldown-suppressed edges are "parked per (policy,event) direction … and replayed after the 30 s cooldown". The reconcile section says "a redefined policy re-arms".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A14-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A14-03 | Low | Parked-edge maps are keyed by policy name and not reconciled on Apply: a predecessor's… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:47: - **R3-A14-03 — COHORT (Low, event-engine generation state).** **Defect:** cooldown key is just name+event; an existing entry is not replaced (`pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:117-127`), while `apply` resets a redefined policy's runtime and semRev without reconciling pending maps (`pkg/eventengine/engine.go:626-650`). Drain deletes old entry on revision mismatch and cannot replay a suppressed successor edge (`:1069-1100`); prior fake-clock probe saw that loss. **Best alternative:** if the background worker drains in the gap between redefine and next committed trigger the stale key is freed, and the first successor edge still executes; not a permanent/general inability to remediate. **Remaining check:** current deterministic fake clock across redefine, successor commit and second event, including the `pending.budget` map whose analogous effect remains source-only.

## #16651 — R3-A50-02: A feed restored with a count baseline but no usable content epoch never re-establishes the epoch. Three record shapes lead there: a legacy count-only record, a… [OPEN]

## Summary

A feed restored with a count baseline but no usable content epoch never re-establishes the epoch. Three record shapes lead there: a legacy count-only record, a record whose epoch digest did not match, and a pre-#15075 record whose epoch had rotated. Churn then stays predecessor-only for good, and the epoch-less record is persisted again on each restart.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — The #14395 content-churn epoch is the documented protection against whoever controls a feed's content (provider, CDN, DNS for the feed host) wholesale-replacing an enforced deny/allow set. For every affected feed that protection is silently disabled, with no expiry. Repeated equal-count rotations, each keeping 51% of the previous set, removed all 100 original prefixes with zero refusals (demonstrated). The count high-water still refuses a drastic shrink, and a provider can always add prefixes, so the exposure is withdrawal of enforced prefixes. That keeps it below High. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A50-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va50.md` (finding `R3-A50-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa. `feeds.go:1440` `hasRememberedBaseline := !fs.hasSnapshot && fs.shrinkHighWaterCount > 0`, which is true for every restored record (count > 0 is required to restore, `:315`). `:1671` `if (wasBootstrap && !hasRememberedBaseline) || guardBypass {` is the only unacknowledged epoch assignment; the others are the Apply copy at `:652` and carryForward at `:701`. `:1463-1469` reads `churnBaseline := fs.epochContentPrefixes; if len(churnBaseline) == 0 { churnBaseline = fs.prefixes }`. `:376` writes `Prefixes`/`EpochHash` only `if len(history.epochPrefixes) > 0`, so the epoch-less state is persisted again. `:342-355` drops an epoch on a digest mismatch.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/feeds/README.md:77-80 says "Records written before the epoch set was persisted restore the count epoch only; the content epoch then re-bootstraps on the first install." The ShrinkHighWater doc says the same (`pkg/feeds/feeds.go:137-139`). The comment at `feeds.go:1460-1462` reads "Fall back to fs.prefixes only while no epoch exists ...; the first install below then establishes the epoch". README (#14395) adds that successive 51%-retained rotations cannot cumulatively replace the set.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a documented anti-replacement guard is permanently off for a reachable population of feeds, contrary to the code's own comment and README.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/feeds unit probes (verifier's own plus the reporter's): the manager's install path plus the persistence round trip. The end-to-end dataplane install of the rotated set was not run on a helper.

**Confidence:** High — Executed through the real snapshot→restore round trip across two further restarts, with a valid-epoch control. The remaining assumption is that a count-only record exists on real boxes. It does wherever shrink-history persistence (#11755, 2026-10-02) ran before the epoch landed (#14395, 2026-10-16), and also wherever a digest mismatch drops the epoch.

## Impact

This affects every appliance that upgraded across #14395 with an existing feed, plus any feed whose epoch was dropped on restore. The documented human-in-the-loop guard against wholesale replacement of an enforced denylist (or allowlist) is off with nothing visible to the operator: AllFeeds and `show security dynamic-address` expose no epoch size. At the default hourly refresh, roughly 3 hours suffice. It lasts until an operator happens to acknowledge some later refusal.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `installSnapshot`, when `len(fs.epochContentPrefixes) == 0` and the candidate has passed every guard, including the restored count high-water, establish the epoch from the installed set and persist it. That means keying the rebase on "no epoch exists", not on `!hasRememberedBaseline`. Acceptance: both arms refuse at step 2 and persist 100 epoch prefixes; the controls are unchanged; TestColdRestartCountOnlyBootstrapShrinkRefused14994 and the #15075 cells stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16652 — `release_persistent_inbound` never downgrades the `u64::MAX` clear tombstone when the last inbound hold of a revoked lease drops, while its siblings `complete_persistent_lease_locked` and `rollback_flow` do. The sourc... [OPEN]

## Summary
`release_persistent_inbound` never downgrades the `u64::MAX` clear tombstone when the last inbound hold of a revoked lease drops, while its siblings `complete_persistent_lease_locked` and `rollback_flow` do. The source key then stays clear-fenced forever, which refuses idle-lease imports and strips persistence from synced sessions on that node.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — scoped to one source key per affected clear, and only when an inbound-only hold is the last holder at clear time. HA persistence for that internal socket is lost on that node (imports `SkippedClearFenced`, synced reserve without persistence), so after a failover the host loses its persistent mapping. Local mints still work. It heals on a pool reseed or restart. Each such key adds one `revoked_persistent` entry that is never pruned.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A76-04`
**Source part:** `parts/va76.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
After a clear during inbound-only use, that host's persistent mapping is not reconstructed on the peer, so a later failover silently loses it. Nothing shows that the key is fenced.

**Contract:** `clear_persistent_leases` (`nat/allocator/mod.rs:2186-2191`) stores `ACTIVE_PERSISTENT_NAT_CLEAR_TOMBSTONE_NS` for a lease with holders, and the last holder's release turns it into `now + PERSISTENT_NAT_CLEAR_REPLAY_HORIZON_NS`, as both outbound sites implement (`:3520-3528`, `:3765-3776`).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`nat/allocator/mod.rs:2037-2054` `release_persistent_inbound` sets `expires_at_ns = now_ns` for a revoked last holder and re-indexes, but never touches `live.revoked_persistent`. `rollback_persistent_inbound` (`:2056-2058`) delegates to it. `prune_expired_persistent_nat_clear_fences` (`:1100-1108`) keeps only `until > now`, so MAX is never pruned. The consumers are `persistent_nat_import_is_key_clear_fenced` (`:1110-1117`), the synced reserve None arm (`:4921-4940`) and the idle import (`idle_lease_sync_8121.rs:362-371`).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — Rust allocator probe. The HA consumer consequence is STATIC.

## #16653 — The status poll releases `m.mu` for its RPC and on re-lock fences only on helper process identity and the link-cycle lease. A status applied by a concurrent mutator (disarm, RG update, snapshot apply) is then overwritten by the older poll reply. After a durable fail-closed disarm, `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=1`, ready binding rows and `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` (a TakeoverReady input) return for up to one poll tick. [OPEN]

## Summary

The status poll releases `m.mu` for its RPC and on re-lock fences only on helper process identity and the link-cycle lease. A status applied by a concurrent mutator (disarm, RG update, snapshot apply) is then overwritten by the older poll reply. After a durable fail-closed disarm, `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=1`, ready binding rows and `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` (a TakeoverReady input) return for up to one poll tick.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A30-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the window is at most one 1 Hz tick per occurrence. During it, ctrl steers into a disarmed helper (the shim's 5 s heartbeat timeout does not stop it), and `takeoverReadyLocked` loses its "forwarding not armed" blocker. Each fresh tick self-corrects. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (stale helper-status apply after an off-lock RPC; with R3-B16-02, the export-pager site of the same missing fence) — real ordering defect, one-tick bounded.

## Mechanism

poll tick → unlock → `status` RPC (helper armed) → compile-path `disarmSnapshotProtocolFailureLocked`/unsupported disarm (under applySem, not poll-serialized) applies DISARMED status under `m.mu` → poll re-locks → proc/lease fences pass → stale ARMED status applied → ctrl=1, ready rows, `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` → `syncDesiredForwardingStateLocked` sees no delta → next tick corrects.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_status.go:520-540` captures `pollProc, pollProcGen`, unlocks, and issues the RPC. `:542-545` `if m.proc != pollProc || m.procGen != pollProcGen { ... continue }`. `:549-553` checks the link-cycle lease. `:562` `m.applyHelperStatusLocked(&status)`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_control.go:179-180` shows that `requestDetailedAtSocket` holds `controlReqMu`, so a mutator's RPC queues behind the poll's and the poll reply is older. `maps_sync.go:731-777` and `helper_status_apply.go:53-118` have no sequence/newer-status check. `manager.go:303-310` `lastStatusSeq` exists but is unused here. `manager_ha.go:366-394` shows that `desiredForwardingArmedLocked` is true for standalone and data-RG configs, which is why a plain operator disarm is not durable.

## Impact

Each overlap of a durable disarm with an in-flight poll briefly steers host and transit traffic into a disarmed helper, where it is dropped instead of reaching the kernel for local/control traffic. It also manufactures about 1 s of takeover-ready reading on an unsupported or protocol-stale helper. Recovery is automatic the next tick.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Snapshot `m.lastStatusSeq` (or a dedicated apply counter) before dropping `m.mu`. After re-lock, discard the reply if any other status was applied in between, using the same shape as the link-cycle discard. Apply the same fence to the owner-RG export pager (R3-B16-02). Acceptance: the probe's overlap arm leaves ctrl=0, and the twin and the #13093 cells still pass.

## Contract (where cited)

`applyHelperStatusLocked` is the single writer of `userspace_ctrl`/`userspace_bindings` from helper truth. #13093's risk note promises "worker and forwarding fail-closed gates unchanged". The poll body's own comment (process_status.go:500-507) claims level-triggered correctness, which holds for debt but not for applying an older truth over a newer one.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A30-03` (parts file `parts/va30.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A30-03 | Low | The status poll releases m.mu for its RPC and on re-lock fences only on helper process…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): #13093 (CLOSED, fb9da3296b/291c7746af, ancestors of base; its fence covers restart and link cycle only), #356, #512, #3970 (distinct). R3-B16-02 (this run) is the sibling site in owner_rg_export_paging_9344.go, so they are grouped as one cohort. No prior heading or report covers stale-reply ordering of the poll.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A30-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A30-03 — The #13093 off-lock status poll applies a reply older than a status another `m.mu` holder applied meanwhile, re-enabling `userspace_ctrl` and `ForwardingArmed` after a durable fail-closed disarm for up to one tick
- **Finding ID:** R3-A30-03

## #16654 — The #14660/#15134 closed-world gate does not descend into `within`: Junos correlation children (`events`, `not events`, or any bogus token) commit clean with no warning and are dropped, so a "fire only if X did NOT happen" policy fires… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #14660/#15134 closed-world gate does not descend into `within`: Junos correlation children (`events`, `not events`, or any bogus token) commit clean with no warning and are dropped, so a "fire only if X did NOT happen" policy fires unconditionally

**Finding ID:** `R3-A14-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. A negative gating condition on an autonomous config mutation is silently removed. That broadens when the remediation runs, which is the fail-open direction under the #2124 doctrine. It is the same class #14660 and #15134 were filed to close. Bounded: an operator must author the Junos correla…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a documented closed-world commit gate misses a whole child level, and the drop broadens an autonomous root-authority action.

## Mechanism

`set event-options policy p within 60 not events ping_test_completed` → SetPath (node under `within 60`) → SchemaValidate (open subtree) → `validateEventOptionsInertAST` (does not descend into within) → `validateEventWithinClause` (trigger only) → `compileEventOptions` (seconds + trigger) → `EventPolicy.WithinClauses = [{60, on 1}]` → engine fires on `ping_test_failed` regardless of `ping_test_completed`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/event_options_inert_14660.go:267-` `validateEventPolicyInert14660`: the `switch tok` handles only `events` and `then` (descending into `change-configuration`). `within` passes `permittedPolicy` and its children are never inspected. `pkg/config/event_options_within.go:211` `trigNodes := w.FindChildren("trigger")`: the within validator reads only trigger siblings. `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:2976-3032` `case "within":` reads `nodeVal(child)` and, at `:3000`, `FindChildren("trigger")`. `pkg/config/schema_system.go:1593-1595` declares `within` → `trigger` only, and that schema is not closed-world.

## Impact

A typical Junos remediation, "fail over only if the path did not recover in the last minute", commits clean and then fails over even when recovery just happened. Positive `events` correlation is also dropped, so a policy fires without its correlating event. The operator gets no warning, and the rendered config looks correct.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `validateEventPolicyInert14660` (or `validateEventWithinClause`), reject on the strict path, and warn on the lenient path, any `within` child other than `trigger`. Cover the hierarchical and flat shapes and packed Keys tails. Implementing correlation is an optional later step. Acceptance: all four probe cases are rejected by strict CompileConfig and by CommitCheck, naming the policy and the token. The policy-level control is unchanged, and `within 60 { trigger on 3; }` stays clean.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/eventengine/README.md` "Closed-world commit gate (#14660, #15134)": the gate "hard-rejects at commit / commit-check … any undeclared `event-options` or policy child, and (#15134) any `change-configuration` child other than `commands` … which `compileEventOptions` would otherwise drop". Junos `within` statement reference (juniper.net, Edit event-options): "Configure events that must (or must not) occur within a specified time interval before one of the trigger events."

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A14-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A14-04 | Medium | The #14660/#15134 closed-world gate does not descend into within: Junos correlation… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:45: - **R3-A14-04 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** event closed-world validator examines policy-level events/then only (`pkg/config/event_options_inert_14660.go:267-337`), while `within` schema declares only trigger but is not closed (`pkg/config/schema_system.go:1591-1608`); within validator reads trigger siblings (`pkg/config/event_options_within.go:198-235`), and compiler reads only within seconds/trigger (`pkg/config/compiler_services.go:3061-3091`). A supported parsed Junos `within ... not events ...` correlation is dropped; remediation may fire despite the authored negative prerequisite. **Best alternative:** invalid `trigger after` is rejected, and this needs a non-trigger *within child*, not arbitrary bad event clauses. **Remaining check:** current strict Store and hierarchical/flat forms for `within` unexpected children, plus control trigger-on; correlate runtime only if implementing rather than refusing.

## #16655 — pkg/daemon's test binary panics since e794bebb0b (#15745). `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` dereferences a nil `applySem` that HA test fixtures leave unset. A whole-package `go test ./pkg/daemon/` stops after 609 of 3,446 tests. `make test-go [OPEN]

## Summary
pkg/daemon's test binary panics since e794bebb0b (#15745). `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` dereferences a nil `applySem` that HA test fixtures leave unset. A whole-package `go test ./pkg/daemon/` stops after 609 of 3,446 tests. `make test-go`'s prerequisite `test-race-dp` also panics in its pkg/daemon leg. Together these hide 31 cells that genuinely fail.

**Finding ID:** R3-N06-07
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — this is a broad assurance loss with no production effect. About 82% of the largest daemon package (host-inbound, HA, IPsec attribution, flex-match, rx-vlan audit) has not executed in any whole-package run since 2026-10-19. 31 of the hidden cells fail when run on their own. Production is safe because the only store-bearing constructor sets `applySem`. Demonstrated, not potential. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
every developer or agent running `make test-go` gets a panic before the whole-tree leg, and every PR whose selection includes pkg/daemon (nearly all pkg/* changes) gets a panic instead of the real failure list. Regressions in host-inbound fencing, IPsec attribution, flex-match rendering and rx-vlan auditing have landed or can land unseen. This has lasted since 2026-10-19. Recovery is a one-line fix plus triage of the 31 failures.

**Contract:** `make test` / `make test-go` and the CI affected-package job are the Go regression gates (CLAUDE.md Quick Start, docs/ci-gate-contract.md). A test that never starts gives no signal. Every other background applySem consumer nil-checks the semaphore before `Acquire`, for example daemon_dhcp.go:156, daemon_ra_reconcile.go:176, daemon_syslog_retry_14597.go:57 and rxvlan_audit_11446.go:172. The sibling `scheduleFRRHAReconcile` stays out of these fixtures through its `d.frr != nil` gate.

**Trace:** test fixture `&Daemon{store, cluster}` → HA demotion or promotion handler (daemon_ha.go:544/760) or the RG reconcile (:1469) → `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` passes its guards → goroutine → `(*Weighted).Acquire` on nil → SIGSEGV in a non-test goroutine → the test binary exits → `go test` reports FAIL with a panic, and every later test in the package is neither run nor reported.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/daemon/daemon_route_listener.go:304-313 @d1ea69f9aa: `if d == nil || d.store == nil || d.isResetting() { return }` ... `go func() { if err := d.applySem.Acquire(ctx, 1); err != nil {` has no applySem guard. The call sites are daemon_ha.go:544 and :760 ("cluster-state") and :1469 ("rg-state-reconcile"). The fixture daemon_ha_actuation_6371_test.go:98-105 builds `&Daemon{store: fenceTestStore(...), cluster: cm, vrrpMgr: ..., rgStates: ..., failoverActuations: ..., userspaceDemotionPrepUntil: ...}` with no applySem. Production uses daemon.go:2210 `applySem: semaphore.NewWeighted(1)`. The other production `&Daemon{}` (daemon_ha.go:1952) has no store and returns at the first guard. The test-race-dp -run list at Makefile:392 includes `ReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot`, which selects TestReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot (reconcile_one_snapshot_6743_test.go:103).

**Probe:** First, `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '^TestFailoverActuation_FailedRGActiveClearDoesNotAck$' -count=1` gives `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` / `semaphore.(*Weighted).Acquire(0x0, ...)` / `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish.func1()`. Second, the whole package at HEAD (RUN/verify/vn06/daemon-head.json.gz) showed started 609 of 3,446 (`go test -list`): pass 589, fail 5, and 15 started but never finished. Positive control: with the temporary guard `|| d.applySem == nil` (RUN/verify/vn06/probes/guard-probe.diff, reverted, tree clean), the run showed started 3,446, pass 3,386, fail 36, skip 24, and 0 panics (daemon-guard.json.gz). 31 of the 36 failures are tests that never started at HEAD, for example TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790, TestEarlyInputBarrierHandoffFollowsEnforcement10751, seven TestAttribution*9641 cells, three TestLo0FlexMatch*14394 cells, six TestRxVlanAudit*11446 cells and TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433. Run alone at HEAD, TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433, TestRxVlanAuditRechecksParentOnLinkUp11446 and TestAttributionFallbacksKeepThePromotedAnswer9641 all FAIL, so these are genuine reds and not order effects. Third, the test-race-dp pkg/daemon -run set panicked in the same frame under -race (race-ctl.txt) and without -race (race-norace-ctl.txt). TestReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot alone panics in 2 of 3 runs. Limits: the 28 untriaged failures may include fixture rot as well as real regressions.

## Acceptance / fix direction
add `d.applySem == nil` to the `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` guard, like its siblings, or build test Daemons through one helper that always sets applySem. Then triage the 31 unmasked failures. Acceptance: a whole-package `go test -json ./pkg/daemon/` starts as many tests as `go test -list` reports (3,446 today). A unit cell must show that a store-only `&Daemon{}` driven through demotion does not panic. The test-race-dp pkg/daemon leg must pass 10/10 without a panic.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn06.md)</summary>

### R3-N06-07 — pkg/daemon test binary panics on a nil applySem in scheduleConnectedRGRepublish (since #15745); whole-package runs and the test-race-dp leg stop early and hide 31 failing cells

A whole-package `go test ./pkg/daemon/` stops after 609 of 3,446 tests. `make test-go`'s prerequisite `test-race-dp` also panics in its pkg/daemon leg. Together these hide 31 cells that genuinely fail.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker n06 (Test/reliability engineer (new harnesses)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vn06
- **Severity:** Medium — this is a broad assurance loss with no production effect. About 82% of the largest daemon package (host-inbound, HA, IPsec attribution, flex-match, rx-vlan audit) has not executed in any whole-package run since 2026-10-19. 31 of the hidden cells fail when run on their own. Production is safe because the only store-bearing constructor sets `applySem`. Demonstrated, not potential. [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High — the panic is deterministic in the whole-package run, and the started/unstarted counts were reproduced with a positive-control guard. Three of the 31 hidden failures were confirmed in isolation. The other 28 were not triaged.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — I ran the single panicking test, the whole package at HEAD, the whole package with a temporary reverted nil guard, the test-race-dp pkg/daemon -run set with and without -race, and three hidden failures in isolation.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — the documented local gate and the CI-selected pkg/daemon run cannot run most of the package, and real reds are hidden behind a test-fixture panic.
- **Contract:** `make test` / `make test-go` and the CI affected-package job are the Go regression gates (CLAUDE.md Quick Start, docs/ci-gate-contract.md). A test that never starts gives no signal. Every other background applySem consumer nil-checks the semaphore before `Acquire`, for example daemon_dhcp.go:156, daemon_ra_reconcile.go:176, daemon_syslog_retry_14597.go:57 and rxvlan_audit_11446.go:172. The sibling `scheduleFRRHAReconcile` stays out of these fixtures through its `d.frr != nil` gate.
- **Adversarial analysis:** No adversary is involved. The fault is an ordinary code change that widened a call path into fixtures built as `&Daemon{store: ..., cluster: ...}` without `applySem`. The protection at stake is the regression gate's ability to run and report the package. The goroutine panics after the test body returns, so it crashes the whole test binary rather than one test, and every later test is silently dropped. The challenged assumption is that a per-test panic only reds that test.
- **Evidence:** pkg/daemon/daemon_route_listener.go:304-313 @d1ea69f9aa: `if d == nil || d.store == nil || d.isResetting() { return }` ... `go func() { if err := d.applySem.Acquire(ctx, 1); err != nil {` has no applySem guard. The call sites are daemon_ha.go:544 and :760 ("cluster-state") and :1469 ("rg-state-reconcile"). The fixture daemon_ha_actuation_6371_test.go:98-105 builds `&Daemon{store: fenceTestStore(...), cluster: cm, vrrpMgr: ..., rgStates: ..., failoverActuations: ..., userspaceDemotionPrepUntil: ...}` with no applySem. Production uses daemon.go:2210 `applySem: semaphore.NewWeighted(1)`. The other production `&Daemon{}` (daemon_ha.go:1952) has no store and returns at the first guard. The test-race-dp -run list at Makefile:392 includes `ReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot`, which selects TestReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot (reconcile_one_snapshot_6743_test.go:103).
- **Probe:** First, `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run '^TestFailoverActuation_FailedRGActiveClearDoesNotAck$' -count=1` gives `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` / `semaphore.(*Weighted).Acquire(0x0, ...)` / `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish.func1()`. Second, the whole package at HEAD (RUN/verify/vn06/daemon-head.json.gz) showed started 609 of 3,446 (`go test -list`): pass 589, fail 5, and 15 started but never finished. Positive control: with the temporary guard `|| d.applySem == nil` (RUN/verify/vn06/probes/guard-probe.diff, reverted, tree clean), the run showed started 3,446, pass 3,386, fail 36, skip 24, and 0 panics (daemon-guard.json.gz). 31 of the 36 failures are tests that never started at HEAD, for example TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790, TestEarlyInputBarrierHandoffFollowsEnforcement10751, seven TestAttribution*9641 cells, three TestLo0FlexMatch*14394 cells, six TestRxVlanAudit*11446 cells and TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433. Run alone at HEAD, TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433, TestRxVlanAuditRechecksParentOnLinkUp11446 and TestAttributionFallbacksKeepThePromotedAnswer9641 all FAIL, so these are genuine reds and not order effects. Third, the test-race-dp pkg/daemon -run set panicked in the same frame under -race (race-ctl.txt) and without -race (race-norace-ctl.txt). TestReconcilePassUsesOneDataplaneSnapshot alone panics in 2 of 3 runs. Limits: the 28 untriaged failures may include fixture rot as well as real regressions.
- **Trace:** test fixture `&Daemon{store, cluster}` → HA demotion or promotion handler (daemon_ha.go:544/760) or the RG reconcile (:1469) → `scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` passes its guards → goroutine → `(*Weighted).Acquire` on nil → SIGSEGV in a non-test goroutine → the test binary exits → `go test` reports FAIL with a panic, and every later test in the package is neither run nor reported.
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for a fixture helper that always sets applySem: there is none, and the panic moves to the next fixture family (TestRethDemotionFenceWaitsForVIPRelease_6177) when one fixture is patched (n06 evidence probe-actuation-applysem.diff). I looked for a production path with a nil applySem: none. I checked whether the race gate avoids the panic. It does not, which corrects the reporter: the reporter said test-race-dp "stays green", but its pkg/daemon leg panics, and with `-count=2` it will almost always panic. I checked whether CI blocks on it: the Go job is advisory and documented red (.github/workflows/test.yml:2-10). So the consequence is lost signal, not a blocked merge.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — test-binary lifetime only. The production goroutine always has a non-nil semaphore, and the guard would only add a nil check on a cold path.

## #16656 — R3-A50-03: A feed-server URL whose host is an internal IP literal passes strict commit without error or warning, but the SSRF block (#10177/#14177) refuses every fetch. Nothing… [OPEN]

## Summary

A feed-server URL whose host is an internal IP literal passes strict commit without error or warning, but the SSRF block (#10177/#14177) refuses every fetch. Nothing documents that destination policy. Any enforced policy over the binding makes every snapshot unrepresentable: previous-good is retained, or default-deny on a fresh boot.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — Once the binding is referenced, commits are accepted but never reach the dataplane, including unrelated rule, NAT and zone changes, until the reference is removed. On a fresh install the result is default-deny. This is fail-closed and discoverable through per-feed LastError and the snapshot-rejection status, and the trigger is an operator's URL choice, so it is not High. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A50-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va50.md` (finding `R3-A50-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa. `pkg/feeds/fetch.go:144-160` `feedDestinationBlocked`: `ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsUnspecified() || !ip.IsGlobalUnicast()`, plus the prefixes at `:111-126` (100.64/10, 198.18/15, fc00::/7, ...). `:196-211` refuses the whole answer set unless `feedDestinationAllowed(ip, allowlist)`, and `resolveFeedIPs` returns an IP literal unchanged (`:162-165`). The allowlist is set only by `SetPrivateFeedAllowlist` (`pkg/feeds/feeds.go:394-405`, "intentionally a manager-level escape hatch"), which has no non-test caller in the repository. `validateDynamicAddressFeedServerEndpointStrict` (`compiler_validate_strict_observability.go:164-285`) checks emptiness, malformed URLs, scheme and path, but not the destination class. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:30-46` documents the `__unsupported_address__` whole-snapshot reject.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_observability.go:140-145`: a server whose feeds can never register makes bound names fail closed (whole-snapshot reject → previous-good or fresh-boot default-deny), and "this gate still turns the silent default-deny into an operator-visible commit error at the feed-server root". Other can-never-install classes were moved to commit by #3300, #5183, #14385 and #14723. pkg/feeds/README.md:320-330 and :475-490 state that later commits are not enforced while a referenced binding is omitted. The README does not state the destination policy at all.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a never-installable configuration that commit-time code could decide passes the gate built to reject that outcome, and the consequence is a freeze of policy publication.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/config strict CompileConfig probe and pkg/feeds Manager.Apply/fetch probe. The whole-snapshot rejection is STATIC (policies_lower.go/policies.go plus README) and pinned by TestUnresolvedFeedBindingWithStaticAliasFailsClosed.

**Confidence:** High — both the commit half and the runtime half were executed with controls. The whole-snapshot consequence is the pinned and documented #5645 behaviour, not re-executed end to end on a helper.

## Impact

An operator integrating an on-prem feed gets a successful commit and then a firewall whose policy publication is frozen at previous-good from that commit on. Later changes are accepted but not enforced, and a fresh install is default-deny. Recovery is to remove the reference. The only clues are LastError and the snapshot-rejection status, neither of which names the cause class.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `validateDynamicAddressFeedServerEndpointStrict`, reject (strict) or warn (lenient) when the URL host is an IP literal that the shared destination predicate would refuse. Move the predicate somewhere pkg/config can use without importing pkg/feeds. Document the destination policy in pkg/feeds/README.md. Optionally add an explicit config leaf wired to `SetPrivateFeedAllowlist`. Acceptance: the six private literals fail commit with a message naming the destination class; the public-hostname and `http://` controls behave as today; with any override leaf set, the runtime arm installs.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A50-03`, part `parts/va50.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16657 — #15218 residual: the shim build recipe scrubs only RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS and records a constant "scrubbed" codegen-env digest, so cargo-honoured overrides (release profile, target linker/rustflags, RUSTC, RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS, $CARGO_HOME config) reach a "pinned" build whose verdict both consumer gates accept as clean [OPEN]

## Summary

#15218 residual: the shim build recipe scrubs only RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS and records a constant "scrubbed" codegen-env digest, so cargo-honoured overrides (release profile, target linker/rustflags, RUSTC, RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS, $CARGO_HOME config) reach a "pinned" build whose verdict both consumer gates accept as clean

**Finding ID:** `R3-A31-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the impact is on build-provenance integrity. The durable verdict that the freshness and release-retention gates trust can say `pinned=true`, `bpf_linker=0.10.2` and "scrubbed env" for a build that used a different rustc, linker or optimisation profile. The kernel verifier still gates loadability at build and at deploy (verify-dataplane). The actor is a contributor or CI host with an ambient variable or a user-level cargo config. The impact is potential; no tainted object was produced [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the closed #15218 fix's stated invariant ("the only codegen env a gated build can have is the empty one") is demonstrably false, and its consumers trust it.

## Mechanism

An ambient `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_OPT_LEVEL` (or `RUSTC`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, the target linker or rustflags, or `~/.cargo/config.toml` `[profile.release]`) passes through `build-userspace-xdp.sh:126` and cargo builds different codegen. shimverify passes, or headroom is OVERRIDDEN. The verdict then records `toolchain=<pin>, pinned=true, bpf_linker=0.10.2, codegen_env_digest=<constant>`. `verdictProvenanceClean` returns true, so the freshness gate adopts the digest, and `retain_shim_verdict.py` retains the verdict for release.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

In `build-userspace-xdp.sh` (all lines at d1ea69f9aa):

## Impact

The durable record the release pipeline trusts says "pinned, scrubbed, pinned linker" for a build that may be none of those. A future #1864-class verifier-cap regression would be diagnosed from a false premise, and the retention gate's promise is unkept. Blast radius: build provenance only. The deploy verifier still decides loadability.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Run cargo under `env -i` with an explicit allowlist (PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, MAX_INTERFACES), pointing `CARGO_HOME` at a repo-controlled empty config, or pass `--config` overrides for `profile.release.*` and `target.bpfel-unknown-none.linker`. Compute `codegen_env_digest` from the environment actually passed to cargo, and refuse if any `CARGO_*`, `RUSTC*` or `RUSTFLAGS*` variable remains. Correct the `userspace_xdp_manifest.go:176-179` comment. Acceptance: the stand-in-cargo probe shows none of the listed variables at cargo, and a test pins the scrub against the Cargo env families.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/dataplane/build-userspace-xdp.sh:115-120`: "a pinned build under them is not the pinned build. Scrub both ... so the only codegen env a gated build can have is the empty one". `pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_manifest.go:176-179`: "everything else that can steer codegen for the bpfel target lives in hashed files (.cargo/config.toml, Cargo.toml, the build recipe)". `scripts/dist/retain_shim_verdict.py:85-87`: "an unpinned or RUSTFLAGS-tainted install must not reach a release as a PASS". #15218 acceptance: "an unpinned or RUSTFLAGS install produces a rejected or OVERRIDDEN verdict".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A31-02` (parts file `parts/va31.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A31-02 | Low | #15218 residual: the shim build recipe scrubs only RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS and…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #15218 (CLOSED, f1b492dc7c) covers RUSTFLAGS and CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS only, and this entry is its residual. #10909/#13963 (verdict override and hand-run manifest) and #1864 (pin) are different mechanisms. `gh issue list --search CARGO_PROFILE` found nothing. Grep for CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE, RUSTC_WRAPPER and CARGO_TARGET_BPFEL across `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/`, `prior-headings.tsv` and the in-run parts found nothing. The only hit is `prior-r2-002.md:2931`, the original A31-01 probe.

## #16658 — The #15021 deferred worker never clears `pending.wakeAt`, so after the first deferred edge or budget deferral it spins on zero-length timers for the rest of the daemon's life [OPEN]

## Summary

The #15021 deferred worker never clears `pending.wakeAt`, so after the first deferred edge or budget deferral it spins on zero-length timers for the rest of the daemon's life

**Finding ID:** `R3-A14-05`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. xpfd burns about one CPU core (0.76–1.19 s of CPU per wall second measured) indefinitely, with nothing pending. On every spin it also takes `pendingMu` and `e.mu`, which RPM probe goroutines (`HandleEvent`) and every commit's `Apply` need. The trigger is ordinary: any event-options edge park…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable, everyday trigger produces an unbounded busy loop in the control-plane daemon for the rest of its lifetime.

## Mechanism

event-options policy commits (cooldown armed) → RPM event within 30 s → `evaluateEventMode` → `maybeDeferCooldownLocked` parks and nudges → `deferredWorker` computes wake = anchor+30 s and stores it in `pending.wakeAt` → timer → `drainDeferred` replays, and the map is empty → next iteration seeds wake from the stale past `wakeAt` → `d=0` → immediate timer → `drainDeferred` (pendingMu+e.mu) → repeat until process exit. The `deferBudget` path is equivalent: it stores the oldest-slot expiry in `wakeAt`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/eventengine/engine.go:959-960` `if !e.pending.wakeAt.IsZero() { wake = e.pending.wakeAt }`. The loops at `:961-984` can only lower it (`cand.Before(wake)`, `exp.Before(wake)`). `:985` `e.pending.wakeAt = wake`. The only other writes are `:1557/:1559` in `deferBudget`; `drainDeferred` (`:1060-`) never resets it. `:993-1004` `d := wake.Sub(now); if d < 0 { d = 0 }` … `timerC, stopTimer = e.newRetryTimer(d)`. The `globalActionBudgetWindow` cap applies only to large d. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:834` creates the engine once per boot, and `Close` runs only at shutdown (`daemon_run_shutdown.go:386`).

## Impact

Any deployment using event-options with RPM, including the shipped lab failover/restore pair, reaches this on the first re-fire inside a cooldown. From then on, xpfd runs a core at 100% until restart. That competes with commit/apply, HA heartbeat/sync goroutines and RPM probes, and hides real CPU regressions in monitoring.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Recompute `wake` from zero on each iteration, as the minimum over current cooldown anchors plus the budget expiry, and only when the respective maps are non-empty. Set `pending.wakeAt` to zero when both maps are empty. Acceptance: the DEFECT arm of `TestProbeVA14WakeSpin` measures CPU within the same order as the control (sub-millisecond per second). The #15021/#15945 replay tests stay green. A regression test should count deferred-worker timers after a replay over a real-clock idle second.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/eventengine/README.md` "Cross-policy global action budget": deferred actions wait "until the oldest slot expires" or are "replayed after the 30 s cooldown". That describes a bounded wait, not a poll. `docs/engineering-style.md` background-work discipline forbids unbounded busy work.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A14-05` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A14-05 | Medium | The #15021 deferred worker never clears pending.wakeAt, so after the first deferred edge or… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:43: - **R3-A14-05 — MATERIAL (Medium, CPU cost measured only at base).** **Defect:** the worker seeds `wake` from old `pending.wakeAt`, replaces it only with *earlier* candidates and stores it back (`pkg/eventengine/engine.go:955-988`); `drainDeferred` removes pending entries without clearing that time (`:1062-1158`). Once the old wake is in the past, `d` is clamped to zero and `time.NewTimer(d)` repeats indefinitely (`:991-1025`, `:591-596`). Previous real-clock cause/control measured roughly a core of CPU after a single fully drained defer. **Best alternative:** not a dataplane hot-loop or proven NUMA contention; engine mutex hold can be short, and no magnitude on target appliance CPUs was measured. **Remaining check:** current wall-clock/rusage control after cooldown *and* budget deferral, verifying no other writer clears wakeAt; measure rather than asserting dataplane throughput impact.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L30: | R3-A14-05 wakeAt never cleared busy-spin | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A14-01 parked direction skips windowing, until ceiling defeated | MATERIAL | Medium-Low | | R3-A14-04 within children escape closed-world gate | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A14-02 e.mu unlock pairs old pol/new semRev | COHORT | Low | | R3-A14-03 parked maps not reconciled on Apply | COHORT | Low | | R3-A15-01 chassis cluster{} spelling escapes raw-AST gates | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A15-02 global-weight omitted =0 not 255 | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A15-03 fused node priority same-keyword exemption | COHORT | Low | | R3-A16-01 inline VPN named as gateway folds connections | MATERIAL | Medium (not High) |

**Wonder:** wonder batch01 L38: | **R3-A14-04** | **MATERIAL** | Inert validator descends into `events` and `then`, not `within` children (`pkg/config/event_options_inert_14660.go:267-339`); compiler reads only `trigger` children inside the `within` branch (`pkg/config/compiler_services.go:3061-3085`). Positive control rejects policy-level bogus child but supplied strict/Store probes report `within ... not events` commits and disappears, causing unconditional action. | `trigger after` itself is correctly rejected; defect is non-trigger children inside `within`. No runtime test was needed to establish the dropped condition because `EventWithin` has no field for it; no attempt to implement correlation is assumed. | | **R3-A14-05** | **MATERIAL** | Deferred worker seeds wake from stale `pending.wakeAt` (`pkg/eventengine/engine.go:961-987`), clamps past time to zero delay (`:995-1006`), and drain does n…

## #16660 — #15117 residual: a unicast NS to an IPv6 static-NAT/DNAT external that is not an interface address is LocalDelivered into the `xpf-usp0` TUN, where the kernel's per-device proxy-NDP lookup misses, so no NA is ever sent [OPEN]

## Summary
#15117 residual: a unicast NS to an IPv6 static-NAT/DNAT external that is not an interface address is LocalDelivered into the `xpf-usp0` TUN, where the kernel's per-device proxy-NDP lookup misses, so no NA is ever sent

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — this is a liveness and neighbour-discovery defect with no enforcement loss. The demonstrated part is that the firewall never answers the unicast NUD probe. The traffic impact is potential: during DELAY and PROBE the upstream router keeps forwarding with its cached lladdr, then marks the entry FAILED and re-resolves by multicast. Multicast NS still reaches the kernel through the shim's multicast early pass and is answered there. The cost is periodic neighbour churn and a short re-resolution window, with packets queued or dropped there, once per NUD cycle for every IPv6 NAT external on a directly connected segment. That matches the parent finding's bounding. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A77-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va77.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Every IPv6 static-NAT or DNAT service published on a directly connected segment gets a recurring neighbour-failure cycle on the upstream router. The issue is closed, and both the operator doc and the code comment tell the next investigator the v6 path is correct, which steers diagnosis away from the dataplane.

**Contract:** `docs/log/15117.md` says on-link NDP to a NAT external must reach the kernel proxy-NDP rather than be translated. RFC 4861 §7.3.3 NUD sends unicast NS in PROBE state and expects the target (here the proxy) to answer. `docs/feature-gaps.md:1172-1179` says "v6 static-NAT / NAT64 external proxy is functional end-to-end". `pkg/cluster/arp_responder_8621.go:59-68` says "The kernel answers v6 proxy NDP for a same-subnet target correctly", which is why no v6 userspace responder exists.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
In the shim, the session-miss arm passes NDP to the kernel only for `is_interface_nat_destination` (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1071-1085`) or a local destination (`lib.rs:2629-2649`). The comment at `lib.rs:1013-1025` confirms there is no type-only NDP pass (#10640). The interface-NAT map holds only SNAT-egress interface addresses (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1601-1626`, `:1821-1845`, `:2271-2310` `pickInterfaceSnapshotV6(*iface)`). The local map holds interface addresses plus kernel `AddrList` addresses (`maps_sync.go:1426-1475`). No proxy or NAT external reaches either (grep for proxy in `maps_sync.go`: none). In the helper, `flowless_base_resolution` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flowless_verdict.rs:283-313`) calls `flowless_local_resolution` (ingress-interface or interface-NAT only, `:401-421`), then the plain `lookup_forwarding_resolution_in_table_with_dynamic`. The external is in `local_v6` (`afxdp/forwarding_build/mod.rs:1016-1030`), so the result is LocalDelivery. `flowless_ndp_nat_tests_15117.rs:108-146` asserts exactly that for external `2001:db8:0:1::10`, which is not an interface address in `nat_snapshot`. In the outlet, LocalDelivery is the `Trusted` `xpf-usp0` outlet (`afxdp/tx/dispatch/slow_path.rs:156-166`), a TUN opened `IFF_TUN|IFF_NO_PI` (`userspace-dp/src/slowpath.rs:35-38`). `docs/host-inbound-multicast.md:163-169` says such a packet is "not passed through on its ingress NIC". In the kernel install, `pkg/dataplane/proxyarp.go:411-427` keys desired entries by `proxyKey{ifindex, addr}`, so the pneigh entry sits on the configured interface only. The helper has no NS responder: a grep of `userspace-dp/src` for NDP-proxy or NA builders finds none, and `poll_stages.rs:149-160` only learns from NA.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED for the kernel receive-device behaviour (unprivileged netns probe, 3 reruns plus an order-varied variant). STATIC for the shim and helper chain. The end-to-end lab capture was not run.
