## #16661 — A `commit confirmed` that removes or renames a dynamic-address feed can never roll back. The #9615 fire-time check waits for a feed producer that only the rollback's own apply would restart. It then drops a forwarding box into bootstrap. [OPEN]

## Summary

A `commit confirmed` that removes or renames a dynamic-address feed can never roll back. The #9615 fire-time check waits for a feed producer that only the rollback's own apply would restart. It then drops a forwarding box into bootstrap.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A32-01`
**Severity (source report):** High. This breaks the operator's lost-contact safety net. When the window expires, the box does not revert to C1. It keeps enforcing the abandoned C2 for 2 more minutes and then runs `enterBootstrapMode()`, which retires the takeover `.network` files, clears the FRR managed section, detaches the dataplane, and resigns every RG and stops cluster comms. On a standalone box that is a full transit outage. On a cluster, transit moves to the peer and this node stays in bootstrap. An ordinary authenticated change triggers it, together with the very event the feature exists for (not confirming). Bootstrap entry is demonstrated in-process. The end-to-end teardown was not run in a lab. [reporter: High]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. A reachable operator workflow turns the commit-confirmed auto-revert into an outage, and no guard covers it.

## Mechanism

C1 binds `dyn1` to feed `malware` and policy p1 uses dyn1; its feed is fetched. `commit confirmed 1` of C2 then removes or renames the feed. The arm gate checks C1 with the live overlay and passes. The apply of C2 runs reconcileFeeds(C2) and the producer for `malware` is cancelled with its snapshot discarded. The deadline arrives and `executeConfirmedRollback` calls `confirmRollbackTargetHandledAtFire`. `SnapshotForBindings(C1)` omits dyn1, so `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` refuses C1 as feed-only. Deferral runs 24 × 5 s while C2 stays enforced. Then PromoteRollback(C1) persists it as committed and enterBootstrapMode runs.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

The gate at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:983-987` (arm time) is `rollbackTarget := d.store.ActiveConfig(); rollbackTargetAppliablePreflight(rollbackTarget, d.feedSnapshotsForConfig(rollbackTarget))`. C1's feed is live, so it passes. Next, `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:145` runs `d.reconcileFeeds(cfg)` on C2's apply. `daemon_feeds.go:210-223` calls the hash-gated `d.feeds.Apply`. `feeds.go:607-640` cancels every old producer and builds `newFeeds` only from C2's plan. The only `reconcileFeeds` call sites in production are `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:145` and boot (`daemon_run.go:514`), observed by grep. At fire time, `confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:82` gets the refusal. At :87, `rollbackTargetRefusedOnlyForFeeds(target)` is true (it substitutes a synthetic overlay, :40-53), so `DeferConfirmTimer` runs up to `confirmRollbackFeedRetryMax = 24` times at 5 s (:31-35). At :101-133 it runs `PromoteRollback` → peer re-sync → `enterBootstrapMode()`. `bootstrap.go:449-` performs the teardown steps.

## Impact

Any feed-using deployment that edits feeds under `commit confirmed`, which is the workflow the docs recommend for risky changes, can get a full transit outage on a standalone box, or an RG resign on a cluster node, 2 minutes after the deadline. The store and log then claim the target was "refused by the dataplane". Recovery needs a reboot or daemon restart (see R3-A32-02), after which the box comes up on C1 normally.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At fire time, before classifying a feed-only refusal, reconcile the feed producers for the pending TARGET (or apply the target normally and let the async feed fetch converge through onUpdate, as on a real apply). Never reach the bootstrap branch for a feed-only refusal whose producer is absent. Acceptance: the defect and rename arms above apply `c1-feed-target` with `bootstrap=false`, and both controls are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/daemon README #6707 says the promise of `commit confirmed` is "this reverts cleanly if I lose contact". `confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:20-26,37-39` says deferral exists for a target that waits only on a feed with no installed snapshot yet, that is, a feed that is late rather than gone. `pkg/feeds/feeds.go` Apply comment: "A feed GENUINELY REMOVED from config has no entry in the new plan, so it gets no replacement and its snapshot is dropped".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A32-01` (parts file `parts/va32.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A32-01 | High | A commit confirmed that removes or renames a dynamic-address feed can never roll back. The…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #9615 (closed) and #15056 (closed, fix 253a9bf852, an ancestor of d1ea69f9aa) are the code under test. Their feed-only transient predicate does not cover a cancelled producer. gemini D67-01 (`/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-500-001.md:55555`) names feed removal only as a precondition for its separate host-auth and peer-resync claim. R3-N09-04 (this run) is the dns-name trigger on a recovered window, with a different fix point. #5282/#5036 cover the producer swap. No gh issue matches a search for commit-confirmed with feed.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A32-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16662 — Packed hierarchical `time-wait-state session-timeout N;` / `time-wait-state session-ageout;` (#15753 knobs, runtime-wired by #15946) pass strict commit and compile to nothing [OPEN]

## Summary
Packed hierarchical `time-wait-state session-timeout N;` / `time-wait-state session-ageout;` (#15753 knobs, runtime-wired by #15946) pass strict commit and compile to nothing

**Finding ID:** R3-N08-06
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — an authored TIME_WAIT session policy is silently not applied (the helper keeps its default close-window handling) while commit and show say it is configured. Bounded to session-table retention. No policy bypass [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
An operator tuning TIME_WAIT retention for session-table pressure believes it is applied, and it is not. The default handling continues.

**Contract:** CLAUDE.md "Compiler must handle both shapes", and the #8939 rationale at compiler_security_flow.go:741-751.

**Trace:** hierarchical text -> parser packs Keys -> SchemaValidate accepts -> compile reads Children only -> TCPSession field zero -> flow.go snapshot -> Rust session timeouts keep their defaults.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
compiler_security_flow.go:796-812 iterates only `twNode.Children`; the packed node carries the leaf on `twNode.Keys[1:]`. pkg/dataplane/userspace/flow.go:124-130 consumes TimeWaitStateSessionTimeout/Ageout/ApplyToHalfClosed.

**Probe:** `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestR3N08TCPSessionJunosSpellings -v` (RUN/workers/n08/evidence/zz_r3n08_tcpsession_test.go; re-run as RUN/verify/vn08/tcpsession-rerun.out):

## Acceptance / fix direction
Read the time-wait-state Keys run (expandFlatRun with the time-wait-state schema, or packedBodyChildren), as the tcp-session loop does. Acceptance: both packed rows compile to the braced values.

## #16663 — The chassis-cluster raw-AST commit gates walk only `chassis { cluster { } }`, so a `chassis cluster { }` spelling that #6672 made compile commits typo'd monitor weights, duplicate monitors, malformed RG/node ids and `preempt delay` that the… [OPEN]

## Summary

The chassis-cluster raw-AST commit gates walk only `chassis { cluster { } }`, so a `chassis cluster { }` spelling that #6672 made compile commits typo'd monitor weights, duplicate monitors, malformed RG/node ids and `preempt delay` that the container spelling rejects

**Finding ID:** `R3-A15-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — a strict-commit enforcement gate is bypassed by a spelling the compiler explicitly supports. The demonstrated consequences are: an interface-monitor weight typo committed as weight 0, so a link-down deducts nothing and the RG never demotes (failover fail-open); a malformed `redundancy-group…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable strict-commit gate escape with fail-open HA consequences and no owner

## Mechanism

`load override` text `chassis cluster { ... interface-monitor { ge-0/0/1 weight 25O; } }` -> parser Node{Keys:[chassis cluster], Children: body} -> runPreWalkGates: forEachChild(chassis.Children,"cluster") finds nothing -> SchemaValidate (normalized; interface-monitor entries are untyped, `children: nil`) passes -> compileChassis via normalizedClusterNode -> compileRGInterfaceMonitors Atoi fails, so weight 0 -> validateChassisClusterStrict sees 0 (in range) -> commit -> pkg/cluster monitor deducts 0 on link-down.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

The gates walk `forEachChild(nodes, "chassis", ... forEachChild(chassis.Children, "cluster", ... namedInstances(cluster.FindChildren("redundancy-group"))` at compiler_chassis_monitor_weight.go:175-177, compiler_chassis_identity.go:98-100, compiler_chassis_rg_arity.go:74-76 and compiler_chassis_garp_count.go:37-39. They are invoked on the raw tree from compiler_prewalk.go:820/851/859/872. Normalization happens only in compileChassis (`clusterNode := normalizedClusterNode(node)`, compiler_chassis.go:367) and in SchemaValidate (`tree = normalizePackedChassisCluster(tree)`, schema_walk.go:170). For `chassis cluster {`, normalizedClusterNode handles `chassisNode.Keys[1] == clusterKeyword` (compiler_chassis_cluster_packed.go:281-283), which the gates' `forEachChild(chassis.Children,"cluster")` never sees. Observation: the gates fire in the container spelling and stay silent in the brace-top-level spelling. Inference: the same holds for the packed spellings, which the a15 compile-level run showed and va15 did not re-run.

## Impact

These gates exist because the compiled struct cannot tell a typo from the 0 default. The fail-open direction is "monitor never demotes" or "RG silently absent / node priority dropped", and both the commit and `show configuration` look clean. Any startup, day-0 or `load override` file written in the shorthand is exposed. Recovery requires noticing, then fixing the text and recommitting.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Run the four gates over `normalizePackedChassisCluster(tree)`, or over `normalizedClusterNode(chassis)` per chassis node, exactly as SchemaValidate does. Add a table test asserting that every chassis prewalk gate rejects the same fixture in all `clusterSpellings`. Acceptance: the brace-top-level and packed rows of TestVA15Spellings reject with the container message.

## Contract (where cited)

compiler_chassis_cluster_packed.go:23-34 ("TWO CONSUMERS, ONE SPLITTER ... making the packed spelling COMPILE without also making it VALIDATE would open a range-gate escape"). compiler_prewalk.go:805-819 (#5694: "Strict (commit / commit-check): the first malformed identity hard-rejects"). compiler_prewalk.go:854-860 (#6588 monitor-weight gate). The #6672 issue body itself says the packed spelling dropped the cluster body for the "compiler and validation gates alike".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A15-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A15-01 | Medium | The chassis-cluster raw-AST commit gates walk only chassis { cluster { } }, so a chassis… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:51: - **R3-A15-01 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** raw prewalk identity/monitor-weight gates descend only through a `cluster` *child* of `chassis` (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis_identity.go:98-105`, `pkg/config/compiler_chassis_monitor_weight.go:175-183`, `pkg/config/compiler_prewalk.go:806-863`), but compiler accepts `chassis cluster { ... }` on the *chassis node's Keys* (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis_cluster_packed.go:281-289`). Prior `LoadOverride` commit tests showed typoed monitor weights becoming zero, malformed RGs disappearing and preempt tails accepted in the shorthand. **Best alternative:** normal `set` and `load merge` node shapes expose these tokens to prewalk, and compiled strict validation still catches many *well-formed numeric out-of-range* values; the bypass applies to malformed tokens erased by tolerant Atoi/default. **Remaining check:** current Store.LoadOverride strict checks for shorthand versus nested twin, including duplicate-monitor and RG-node identity gates.

## #16664 — R3-A51-01: diagcmd.VRFDeviceName leaves a `vrf-`-prefixed instance name unprefixed while the daemon/FRR always prefix, so ping/traceroute, DDNS SO_BINDTODEVICE and HA… [OPEN]

## Summary

diagcmd.VRFDeviceName leaves a `vrf-`-prefixed instance name unprefixed while the daemon/FRR always prefix, so ping/traceroute, DDNS SO_BINDTODEVICE and HA routing-readiness FRR queries for instance `vrf-X` target instance `X`'s VRF or a nonexistent one

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — this is bounded wrong-VRF behaviour across three control-plane consumers. When a sibling instance `X` exists, DDNS update traffic configured for `vrf-X` leaves through `X`'s VRF, and HA routing-transfer readiness judges `vrf-X` on `X`'s adjacencies. When there is no sibling, those operations fail against an absent device. There is no dataplane enforcement change, and it requires an operator to choose a `vrf-`-prefixed instance name, which is legal. Demonstrated: the name derivation and the FRR query string. Inferred: the on-box egress VRF. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A51-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va51.md` (finding `R3-A51-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/diagcmd/diagcmd.go:197-205: `if strings.HasPrefix(name, vrfPrefix) { return name }; return vrfPrefix + name`. Its consumers: diagcmd.go:321 and :352 (`ip vrf exec <dev>`) pkg/frr/status_parse.go:139-141 `frrVRFName` → `vrfShowCommand` :153-161 pkg/ddns/backend_bind.go:134 `b.bindDevice = diagcmd.VRFDeviceName(c.RoutingInstance)` pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_routing_readiness.go:165-177 (`d.frr.GetOSPFNeighborsVRF(ctx, vrf)` etc., whose results feed dynamicRoutingReady)

**Contract / expected behaviour:** A routing-instance N is realised as kernel/FRR VRF `vrf-`+N without canonicalisation: pkg/routing/vrf.go:89 `vrfName := "vrf-" + name`, pkg/frr/config_render.go:646, pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:221, pkg/rpm/rpm.go:109-114, pkg/routing/tunnel_keepalive.go:119-124. backend_bind.go:120-123 and status_parse.go:132-138 both state that they must resolve to that same device.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a committable config gives silently wrong-instance results on a DDNS egress binding and an HA readiness decision.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — va51 config probe, plus the reporter's frr probe re-run with a positive control. Static: the DDNS and HA-readiness consumer chain.

**Confidence:** High — I executed both halves (commit acceptance and the consumer mapping). The remaining assumption is that operators use `vrf-`-prefixed instance names, which Junos permits.

## Impact

Tenants using `vrf-`-style instance names get DDNS updates egressing another tenant's VRF, or failing outright. HA planned transfers may be approved or refused on the wrong instance's adjacencies. Operator diagnostics silently probe the wrong table.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Map a configured instance name to `vrf-`+name always, through one helper shared with pkg/routing. If ping must accept typed device names, resolve against the configured instance set first, with an exact instance match winning. Acceptance: the frr probe passes for `vrf-cust` with and without a sibling `cust`, and an instance named `vrf-mgmt` does not map onto the management VRF.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16665 — The #9615 refused-target bootstrap safe state has no commit exit. Bootstrap refuses plain `commit`, and the #6707 gate refuses `commit confirmed` on the very target that caused the bootstrap. [OPEN]

## Summary

The #9615 refused-target bootstrap safe state has no commit exit. Bootstrap refuses plain `commit`, and the #6707 gate refuses `commit confirmed` on the very target that caused the bootstrap.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A32-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. This is an operator recovery and API contract failure on a box that is already degraded. Every commit route (CLI, gRPC, REST) is refused, and each refusal message points at the other route. The only way out is an appliance reboot (`request system reboot`) or a daemon restart. After that the box boots NORMAL on the refused target, with a fail-closed dataplane, until a plain commit lands. The impact is bounded because a CLI-reachable reboot exists. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. A reachable degraded state, entered by three triggers (upgrade refusal, feed removal, dns-name), has no commit-surface exit, which contradicts the documented recovery instruction.

## Mechanism

A window's target is refused at fire time (upgrade refusal class, R3-A32-01 feed removal, or R3-N09-04 dns-name). PromoteRollback and enterBootstrapMode run. The operator loads a corrected candidate. A plain commit hits the bootstrap refusal. `commit confirmed` hits the #6707 refusal on the active, refused target. No commit-surface route remains.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/daemon/confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:101-133` runs `PromoteRollback` (active := the refused target) and then `enterBootstrapMode()`, which sets the flag at `bootstrap.go:450`. `daemon_apply_commit.go:209-220` and `:238-242` refuse a plain commit when `inBootstrap()`, both before and under applySem. `daemon_apply_commit.go:983-987` runs `rollbackTargetAppliablePreflight(d.store.ActiveConfig(), ...)` with no bootstrap exemption, and `rollback_target_appliable_6707.go:75-77` exempts only a nil target. `daemon_apply.go:152-156` refuses background applies in bootstrap. The cluster is relinquished before bootstrap (#6742), so peer SyncApply is not an exit.

## Impact

An operator who reaches the box after the #9615 outage cannot apply a fix through the product's own commit surface, as the log instructs. They must reboot the appliance, which extends the outage, and then commit while the box runs the refused target fail-closed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When bootstrap was entered from the #9615 refused branch, either allow a plain commit (the target is already the persisted committed config, so the #1922 first-takeover risk does not apply) or skip the #6707 rollback-target gate while `inBootstrap()` (a timeout would return to the same safe state). Acceptance: in the defect arm, a corrected candidate commits by at least one route, and the healthy control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

The log at `confirm_rollback_preflight_9615.go:109-112` says "fix the configuration from the CLI". `rollback_target_appliable_6707.go:66-70` and the README #6707 say "A plain `commit` of B is unaffected and remains the way forward". The enterBootstrapMode and bootstrap refusal messages say to "commit the takeover config with 'commit confirmed <minutes>'".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A32-02` (parts file `parts/va32.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A32-02 | Medium | The #9615 refused-target bootstrap safe state has no commit exit. Bootstrap refuses plain…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #9615 and #15056 own the branch. #15055 owns the bootstrap-gate TOCTOU. #6707 and #9588 own the gate. None covers the lockout. I searched `gh-issues.tsv`, `prior-headings.tsv`, `prior-r2-002.md`, earlier reports, other parts in this run, and gh search for errRollbackTargetUnappliable or a bootstrap commit-confirmed refusal, with no hit. The finding is independent of R3-A32-01 (a different fix point) and also covers the upgrade and dns-name triggers.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A32-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16666 — The PTB arm of `translate_icmpv6_message_to_icmpv4` advertises `PTB_MTU - 20` unconditionally. When the packet in error is a translated IPv6 fragment, which carries a Fragment Header and is therefore `v4_len + 28` byt... [OPEN]

## Summary
The PTB arm of `translate_icmpv6_message_to_icmpv4` advertises `PTB_MTU - 20` unconditionally. When the packet in error is a translated IPv6 fragment, which carries a Fragment Header and is therefore `v4_len + 28` bytes, the relayed next-hop MTU is 8 bytes too large. Every retry at that MTU still exceeds the IPv6 bottleneck.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — Wire-correctness violation of an RFC MUST, with a non-converging PMTUD black hole for one bounded population: DF-clear IPv4 datagrams larger than the path MTU, translated to IPv6 clients behind an IPv6 hop smaller than the translator's egress MTU (PPPoE, tunnels). There is no enforcement loss, and those packets would be dropped without PMTUD anyway. The defect is that recovery never succeeds. [reporter: Low-Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A78-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va78.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Large DF-clear UDP (SIP, media and game UDP, fragmented IKE, large DNS from IPv4 servers) through NAT64 to IPv6 clients on a reduced-MTU access link never recovers: the first fragment of every datagram is lost, so the whole datagram is lost. Operators see PTB and Frag-Needed exchanges and assume PMTUD works. The problem persists for as long as the flow lives.

**Contract:** RFC 7915 §5.2 (fetched text, lines 1127-1135; the section heading "5.2. Translating ICMPv6 Headers into ICMPv4 Headers" was verified at line 1052) says: "Packet Too Big (Type 2): Translate to an ICMPv4 Destination Unreachable (Type 3) with Code 4 ... The MTU field MUST be adjusted for the difference between the IPv4 and IPv6 header sizes, taking into account whether or not the packet in error includes a Fragment Header". FEATURES.md claims RFC 7915 ICMP-error translation (#2219/#6472).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
Observed at d1ea69f9aa. `userspace-dp/src/nat64/icmp.rs:286-290`: `let mtu = u32::from_be_bytes([src[4], src[5], src[6], src[7]]); ... let v4_mtu = mtu.saturating_sub(NAT64_HEADER_DELTA).clamp(68, 0xffff) as u16;`, with `NAT64_HEADER_DELTA: u32 = 20` (`nat64/translate.rs:45`). The `embedded` quote is not inspected for a Fragment Header. `embedded_v6_to_v4_layout` (`icmp.rs:143-205`) rejects only `ipv6_is_non_first_fragment` and copies first-fragment geometry, and `parse_embedded_v6_l4` (`afxdp/icmp_embed/parse.rs`) refuses only `non_first_fragment_offset_seen`, so a first-fragment quote reaches this arm. The production chain is `afxdp/poll_descriptor/nat64_icmp_error.rs:253` → `build_nat64_v6_to_v4_icmp_error_frame_into` → `write_v6_to_v4_icmp_error_into` (`translate.rs:557`) → `write_v6_to_v4_translate` → `translate.rs:720` `translate_icmpv6_message_to_icmpv4`. The translator adds an 8-byte Fragment Header for every IPv4 fragment (`translate.rs:1052,1083-1090`). `fragment_nat64_ipv6_frame` (`afxdp/frame/mod.rs:572-640`) splits DF-clear output at the egress MTU rather than the RFC 7915 §4 1280 default (#14658 comment at :591-597). The only test, `nat64_v6_to_v4_packet_too_big_becomes_frag_needed_with_mtu` (`nat64_tests.rs:2615`), quotes an unfragmented packet.

**Verification (research):** STATIC — The source chain was read at base. A Rust cell was written (`RUN/verify/va78/probes/va78_ptb_probe.rs`) but not run, because the shared cargo lock had about 16 queued holders when the run deadline came.

## #16667 — An omitted `ip-monitoring global-weight` compiles to 0 instead of the Junos default 255, so RG ip-monitoring that relies on the default commits clean and never demotes (aggregate mode, and unweighted targets in independent mode) [OPEN]

## Summary

An omitted `ip-monitoring global-weight` compiles to 0 instead of the Junos default 255, so RG ip-monitoring that relies on the default commits clean and never demotes (aggregate mode, and unweighted targets in independent mode)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A15-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the RG's ip-monitoring protection is silently off: probe loss deducts 0, the commit is clean with no warning, and `show chassis cluster` keeps reporting weight 255. Bounded because only configs that omit `global-weight` are affected, targets with an explicit weight in independent mode still…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — documented Junos default diverges in the fail-open direction with a clean commit and no owner

## Mechanism

`redundancy-group N { ip-monitoring { global-threshold 100; family inet { 10.0.0.1 weight 100; } } }` -> compileRGIPMonitoring sets GlobalWeight=0 -> strict gates pass, since 0 is in range and absent is legal -> pkg/cluster Monitor: the target goes down, cumulative 100 >= threshold 100, aggregate debt = GlobalWeight 0 -> RG weight stays 255 and no failover happens. In independent mode, `10.0.0.1;` gives target weight 0 -> GlobalWeight 0 -> debt 0.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

compiler_chassis.go:1150-1167: `ipm := rg.IPMonitoring; if ipm == nil { ipm = &IPMonitoring{} }`, and GlobalWeight is assigned only `if gwNode := findNamedNode(ipmEntries, "global-weight"); gwNode != nil`. pkg/cluster/monitor.go:928-934 has `if raw == 0 { raw = rg.IPMonitoring.GlobalWeight }`, and its aggregate arm sets `desired[ipAggregateMonitorName] = w` with `w = ClampInterfaceMonitorWeight(GlobalWeight)`. compiler_chassis_monitor_weight.go:86-92 says an absent token is "legal: the documented 0 default". The same file's globals comment states that an unusable global-weight "is zero demotion debt for the WHOLE group, so no number of failing probes demotes it".

## Impact

Every RG that uses ip-monitoring without an explicit global-weight believes it fails over when its upstream probes die, and it never does. The status display shows a healthy group throughout. This lasts until someone notices during a real upstream outage.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Default GlobalWeight to 255 when `ip-monitoring` is present and `global-weight` is absent (Junos parity), or at minimum warn at commit naming any RG whose effective monitor debt is 0 for every target. Update the GlobalsAbsent test, the schema desc and docs/feature-coverage.md. Acceptance: the omitted-aggregate and omitted-indep rows demote to weight 0, or the commit warns naming the RG.

## Contract (where cited)

The Juniper `global-weight` statement page (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/chassis-cluster-security-devices/topics/ref/statement/chassis-edit-global-weight.html, fetched by va15) says: "This is the weight that is subtracted from the redundancy group weight for all of the hosts being monitored ... Range: 0 through 255 ... Default: 255". xpf claims Junos/vSRX syntax and semantics (CLAUDE.md "What This Is"). The schema desc ("Default weight deducted when a monitored IP fails (0..255)") and docs/feature-coverage.md:258-300 state no xpf default and document no divergence. The per-target `weight` leaf says "0 = use global-weight" (schema_chassis.go:342-345).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A15-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A15-02 | Medium | An omitted ip-monitoring global-weight compiles to 0 instead of the Junos default 255, so… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/NEEDS_VALIDATION`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:52: - **R3-A15-02 — MATERIAL (Medium; intentional-code-default counterweight).** **Defect:** missing `global-weight` leaves newly allocated `IPMonitoring.GlobalWeight` at Go zero (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:1160-1175`); zero-weight targets inherit that zero (`pkg/cluster/monitor.go:928-935`), so health failures accrue no RG demotion. Juniper specifies [255 by default](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/chassis-edit-ip-monitoring.html); prior cluster fake-probe showed omitted weight stays at 255 RG weight while an explicit 255 demotes. **Best alternative:** code deliberately labels absent token as *legal, documented zero default* (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis_monitor_weight.go:85-92`), and an existing test pins it, so this is not a previously unseen compiler accident; explicit target weight/explicit global weight can work. The user-facing `schema_chassis.go:319-347` calls it “default weight” but does not advertise the absent=0 Junos divergence. **Remaining check:** obtain a deliberate operator-facing xpf default contract or change the default/warn for clean Junos migrations; reproduce current aggregate and unweighted-independent debt with explicit-255 controls.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L36: | R3-A15-02 global-weight omitted =0 not 255 | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A15-03 fused node priority same-keyword exemption | COHORT | Low | | R3-A16-01 inline VPN named as gateway folds connections | MATERIAL | Medium (not High) | | R3-A16-02 hostname address pins FQDN remote.id | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-VA16-S1 shared local PSK owner verifies every peer | MATERIAL | High | | R3-A17-01 peer-slot DHCP group renders on peer, Kea refuses family | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-02 expired-leases maxima missing | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-03 server+relay same iface commit clean | COHORT | Low | Dispositions/sampled in parts: A09-02 NEG upheld (agree); A10-03 DUP of A11-03 (agree); VA13-S1 DUP of A13-01 (agree); A13 sampled user-class NEG confirmed; A14/A15/A16/A17 sampled dismissals — agree except as noted per claim. ## #16668 — A nested `commit confirmed` pre-flights the unconfirmed active config instead of the store's retained original rollback target, so extending a window is falsely refused. [OPEN]

## Summary

A nested `commit confirmed` pre-flights the unconfirmed active config instead of the store's retained original rollback target, so extending a window is falsely refused.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A32-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low. This is a misleading refusal with a workaround. Re-issuing `commit confirmed N` to extend a window is refused whenever the UNCONFIRMED config is not appliable by the mirror (for example, it binds a feed that has not fetched yet), and the error falsely says that config is what the timer would restore. Plain `commit` confirms. The opposite direction, where the true target is never re-checked at the nested arm, adds no consequence beyond R3-A32-01's mechanism. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (commit-confirmed rollback-target pre-flight residuals: R3-A32-01, R3-A32-02, R3-N09-04). It is real but bounded, with a plain-commit workaround.

## Mechanism

C1 is committed. `commit confirmed` of C2 binds a feed whose first fetch is pending. A nested `commit confirmed` of C3 runs the arm gate on ActiveConfig (C2), the mirror refuses dyn1, and the arm is refused, although the store would restore C1.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

At `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:983-987`, `rollbackTarget := d.store.ActiveConfig()` and `d.deviceMapCommitPreflight(cand, d.store.ActiveConfig())` run with no `IsConfirmPending()` / `PendingRollbackTarget(gen)` branch. `store_commit.go:724-728` keeps `confirmPrevCfg` when `confirmTimer != nil`. `pkg/cli/cli_config.go:346-378` sends `commit confirmed N` straight to `runCommitConfirmed` with no pending-window intercept.

## Impact

Operators who extend windows, standard Junos practice, get a refusal and a wrong explanation when the pending config is feed-bound and not yet fetched. They must confirm with a plain commit or wait.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When a window is pending, pre-flight the store's `PendingRollbackTarget(ConfirmGen)` for both the appliability and device-map gates. Acceptance: the probe's nested arm succeeds, and a nested arm over an unappliable C1 is refused naming C1.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:724-728` says "Nested confirmed commit: cancel the pending timer but keep the original rollback target (last confirmed config)". `rollback_target_appliable_6707.go:16-19` describes the target as "the currently-active config, restored when the confirm timer expires", which is true only for a non-nested arm.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A32-03` (parts file `parts/va32.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A32-03 | Low | A nested commit confirmed pre-flights the unconfirmed active config instead of the store's…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): #12532 (nested rollback session invalidation) is different. No issue or prior heading covers daemon-side target selection on a nested arm. a19 (this run) checked only the store side.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A32-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16669 — R3-A51-03: LLDP Stop()/re-Apply cannot wake the RX goroutine parked in AF_PACKET Recvfrom, so an LLDP config change, a disable, or daemon shutdown blocks until a frame arrives… [OPEN]

## Summary

LLDP Stop()/re-Apply cannot wake the RX goroutine parked in AF_PACKET Recvfrom, so an LLDP config change, a disable, or daemon shutdown blocks until a frame arrives on every LLDP interface (forever on a silent link)

**Severity:** High (source report) — High — the defect wedges the daemon's config-apply pipeline indefinitely. reconcileLLDP runs inside applyConfigLocked while applySem is held, so the triggering commit never finishes and every later commit, rollback and HA config-sync apply queues behind it until restart. The restart then hangs until systemd's TimeoutStopSec=20 SIGKILL, which skips the graceful HA shutdown steps that follow LLDP stop. Demonstrated: Stop and re-Apply block on a silent veth. Inferred from the code chain: the whole-pipeline wedge and the shutdown SIGKILL. [reporter: High]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A51-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va51.md` (finding `R3-A51-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

In pkg/lldp/lldp.go @d1ea69f9aa: :261 `// No SO_RCVTIMEO: recv blocks indefinitely and is unblocked by closing the fd in close()` :285 `n, from, err := unix.Recvfrom(s.rxFD, buf, 0)` :319-327 `close()`: `_ = unix.Shutdown(s.rxFD, unix.SHUT_RDWR); unix.Close(s.rxFD)` :640-656 stopLocked: `m.cancel(); for _, s := range sessions { s.close() }; m.wg.Wait()` :788-870 rxLoop: `n, pkttype, err := sess.recv(buf)`. The success path has no ctx check and loops back into recv on the same int fd. Apply calls stopLocked first (lldp.go:362), so a re-Apply hits the same wait. On the daemon side: pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:347 `d.reconcileLLDP(cfg)` runs inside applyConfigLocked. :738 `d.lldpMgr.Stop()` (disable) and :750 `d.lldpMgr.Apply(ctx, want)` (change or recovery). pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:411-413 calls `d.lldpMgr.Stop()` before the RA, VIP and VRRP teardown. test/incus/xpfd.service:33 `TimeoutStopSec=20`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/lldp/README.md "Socket lifecycle (#2035)" (line 69 on) says Stop closes every session, which "unblocks the parked `Recvfrom` immediately". The stopLocked comment (lldp.go:631-639) says "Closing the fds BEFORE the wait is what makes Stop bounded".

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable operator action (an ordinary LLDP config change) or an automatic #6794 recovery wedges config apply. The documented "close unblocks recv" guard does not work on AF_PACKET.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — va51 probe `TestVA51StopSilentVsChatty`/`TestVA51ReapplyChangedConfigSilent` in an unprivileged user+net namespace with two veth pairs. Static: the daemon apply/shutdown call chain.

**Confidence:** High — the hang was executed with the real Manager on kernel 7.2.8, against a chatty-peer positive control. Remaining assumptions: a production LLDP interface sees no inbound LLDPDU during the wait (always true for `interface all` members such as em0/fab/VLAN/virtual devices, and true for up to the peer's TX interval on a real switch port). The fd-reuse consequence rests on the reporter's executed run and was not re-run by va51.

## Impact

Any operator who edits `protocols lldp` on a box where an LLDP-enabled link is silent loses the commit pipeline until a daemon restart, and that restart then takes the 20 s SIGKILL path. `interface all` (which expands to control, fabric and virtual devices) makes the silent-link case the norm. The #6794/`all` inventory-growth recovery can trigger it with no operator action. On HA nodes, a planned shutdown loses its graceful VIP/VRRP/cluster stop sequence.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make recv cancellable: ppoll on rxFD plus an eventfd/pipe signalled by Stop, or a non-blocking fd driven through the Go netpoller with SetReadDeadline, or SO_RCVTIMEO with a ctx check. Close rxFD only after rxLoop has returned (signal → wait → close), and check ctx after every successful recv. Replace the socketpair-only seam with a namespace-gated AF_PACKET test. Acceptance: TestVA51StopSilentVsChatty reports the SILENT arm returning in <1 s, and the reporter's fd-reuse probe shows no foreign-fd read.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A51-03`, part `parts/va51.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16670 — Regression from #15675: the new `port <N>` wildcard on the source-NAT pool `port` node splits the flat `port range <lo> to <hi>`, so a pool port range cannot be committed via `set` (the repo's own TestCompileTreeStrict_StandaloneCleanSNAT_5 [OPEN]

## Summary
Regression from #15675: the new `port <N>` wildcard on the source-NAT pool `port` node splits the flat `port range <lo> to <hi>`, so a pool port range cannot be committed via `set` (the repo's own TestCompileTreeStrict_StandaloneCleanSNAT_5876 is red at base)

**Finding ID:** R3-N08-08
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — a NAT pool port window, a common SNAT feature, cannot be configured from the CLI, gRPC `set` or `load set`. It fails closed with a misleading "unknown configuration keyword \"to\"" error, and the accepted `set` leaves a split two-node candidate behind. Hierarchical text still works. No wrong translation is installed. Any automation that replays `display set` loses every pool with a port range.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators configure NAT from the CLI. The documented Junos command fails with a misleading error, the configstore suite is red at master (so the gate that should have caught the merge did not run or was ignored), and replaying set-format backups drops pool port ranges. Recovery: author the pool hierarchically.

**Contract:** The Junos source-pool `port { range port-low <to port-high>; }` and the schema's own comment at pkg/config/schema_security.go:690-692 ("#3906: `range <low> to <high>` (Junos) and the legacy `range low <lo> high <hi>` both collapse onto this multi leaf; the compiler parses both via parseSourcePoolPortRange", compiler_nat_source.go:562).

**Trace:** `set security nat source pool P port range 1024 to 2047` -> ParseSetCommand/SetPath against setSchema (the port wildcard swallows `1024`) -> tree `port range` + `port 1024 to 2047` -> SchemaValidate closed-world walk rejects `to` -> commit check fails. CompileConfig without the schema walk still parses it (TestGroupedRangePlusRandomAllocation15935 passes), which is why pkg/config tests stayed green.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/config/schema_security.go:689 `"port": {..., wildcard: &schemaNode{desc: "Single translated source port (1..65535)", placeholder: "<port>"}, children: ...{"range": {..., multi: true}`. Added by c3f63fe146 (#15675); base 51d355c1d:587 had no wildcard. pkg/configstore/peer_effective_snat_5876_test.go:73-92 `TestCompileTreeStrict_StandaloneCleanSNAT_5876` uses `set security nat source pool P port range 1024 to 2048`.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestVN08NATPoolPort|TestR3N08NATPoolPortRange' -v` (RUN/verify/vn08/probes/zz_vn08_natport_test.go; output natport.out). `flat range lo to hi` gives REJECT "security nat source pool p2 port 1024: unknown configuration keyword \"to\""; the legacy low/high form gives REJECT; `hier port { range 1024 to 65535; }` gives OK 1024-65535; the controls `port 3000` (OK 3000-3000) and `no-translation` (OK) pass. Mutation (RUN/workers/n08/evidence/natport-mutation.diff reapplied, then reverted, `git diff --stat` empty; natport-mutated.out): with the wildcard removed, the flat range gives OK 1024-65535 and `port 3000` is rejected. Existing test, run with all probe files moved out of the package (existing-5876-clean.out): `peer_effective_snat_5876_test.go:92: standalone clean SNAT config must compile: security nat source pool P port 1024: unknown configuration keyword "to" under closed-world subtree` --- FAIL.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Keyword children and multi-leaf absorption must take precedence over the numeric wildcard: treat `port <N>` as a wildcard only when the token directly after `port` is numeric, and never re-home tokens that belong to `range`. Acceptance: the flat and legacy rows commit with the same PortLow/PortHigh as the hierarchical row; `port 3000` still yields [3000,3000]; TestCompileTreeStrict_StandaloneCleanSNAT_5876 passes.

## #16671 — On a fail-closed boot of a committed firewall, the main-table default-route NIC (the WAN, since fxp0 lives in vrf-mgmt) becomes the management lifeline: the persisted lifeline record is overwritten, the bootstrap input guard admits the WAN NIC whole, and the live-address fence withholds the WAN addresses [OPEN]

## Summary

On a fail-closed boot of a committed firewall, the main-table default-route NIC (the WAN, since fxp0 lives in vrf-mgmt) becomes the management lifeline: the persisted lifeline record is overwritten, the bootstrap input guard admits the WAN NIC whole, and the live-address fence withholds the WAN addresses

**Finding ID:** `R3-A33-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The mechanism is real, but it does not reach High. I re-ran the probe at d1ea69f9aa in RUN/wt/a33 (`go test ./pkg/daemon -run TestA33R3Fail`) and it PASSES with both WITNESS arms. The record was overwritten from pci=0000:67:00.1 to 0000:67:00.2. The guard set went from [em0 eno2 fab0 fab1 fxp0] to [em0 eno3 fab0 fab1 fxp0]. The fence gave fenced=[] for a default route on the WAN. The code confirms it. bootstrap.go:1580-1590 writes the lifeline record from detectLifelineInterface, which reads onl] Verifier text: (potential) — the box is in its #1960/#10297 fail-closed state after a cold reboot. Host-inbound enforcement on the Internet-facing NIC is gone: neither the input barrier nor the fence drops new connections to the WAN address. sshd and IKE are exposed to the untrust side, and the state lasts until an operator commits a compilable config (unbounded). The record also stays poisoned afterwards. Bounds: the exposed services still authenticate. The #1993 FRR clear removes BGP peers unless forwarding is armed. REST and gRPC are loopback-only. A daemon restart, as opposed to a reboot, keeps the previous real host-inbound table and is mitigated. The cold-boot route timing is inferred, not run [reporter: High (potential)]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — on the one boot class that has a committed config, the route heuristic replaces a verified identity and defeats the documented fence contract. The probe shows both effects against controls.

## Mechanism

The committed edge firewall has fxp0 in vrf-mgmt and `routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop <ISP>` on untagged ge-0-0-1. An upgrade or DB event leaves the config uncompilable (#1960) or active.json absent with history (#10297). On cold reboot, networkd applies the retained `.network` files and FRR installs the main-table default. xpfd computes bootClass=bootstrap. setupBootstrapLifeline then overwrites the record with ge-0-0-1 and refuses the rename (index > 0). In manager-init the fence marks ge-0-0-1 management and fences nothing on it, and the bootstrap guard admits `iifname`/`sdifname ge-0-0-1` whole. New SSH or IKE connections from the Internet to the WAN address are accepted until a compilable commit, and the record still names ge-0-0-1 afterwards.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_run_naming.go:79-93 runs `d.setupBootstrapLifeline()` on every bootstrap boot unless FirstCommitTeardownOwed is set. In pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:1520 `routeIface, _, routeErr := detectLifelineInterfaceFn()` reads the main table (:1329-1369). Then :1580-1590 `if rec, ok := pciAddrForInterface(lifeline); ok { if err := writeLifelineRecord(rec) ...` writes the record before the enumeration and index-0 refusal at :1594-1655, with no EverCommitted gate (only the appliance fallback is gated). In pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1554-1556, `if config.IsManagementIfName(ifName) { mgmtVRFName = config.ManagementVRFDeviceName }`; pkg/config/ifname_class_6731.go:154-158 matches the fxp/fab/em prefixes; pkg/networkd renders `VRF=` but no `Gateway=`. In pkg/daemon/input_barrier_gate_10751.go:126-141, the record name joins the set (`protectedInterfacesWith(mgmtLeaf, recordName)`), and a detected NIC is excluded only while a different record resolves. pkg/daemon/daemon_failclosed_boot.go:40-56 runs `protected := d.resolveProtectedInterfaces(); if found && lifeline != "" { protected[lifeline] = true }`, and :97-100 sends protected-link addresses to `managed`, which both fences withhold. :168-173 installs the fences and then the guard in manager-init, after naming.

## Impact

The fail-closed state exists to keep a broken box safe while it waits for recovery, and on an edge firewall it can last days. During it, the management plane is offered to the Internet, while logs call the WAN NIC the "management NIC". The poisoned record also puts the WAN in the #1922 protected set and the pre-handoff guard on every later boot. Recovery is a compilable commit plus manual removal of `/etc/xpf/lifeline-interface`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When `EverCommitted()` is true, never write or replace the lifeline record from route detection. In installFailClosedBootHostFences, derive management from the persisted record plus management-class names (fxp*/em*/fab*) only, never from a main-table default route. Acceptance: the probe's WITNESS arms flip (record unchanged, guard set excludes eno3, ge-0-0-0 addresses fenced), and the never-committed foreign-host cell (default-route NIC admitted when no record exists) stays green.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/daemon/README.md (#1960) says the fail-closed box stays reachable "at its EXISTING management address". daemon_failclosed_boot.go says the fence treats "all non-management local addresses" as host-inbound drop destinations (#10732). input_barrier_gate_10751.go:100-106 says: "Detected default-route NIC: recovery fallback ONLY when no verified distinct identity exists ... Otherwise an unlisted detected NIC is data until proven management and stays closed." The README #7114 paragraph says the `!everCommitted` gate exists so the fail-closed box (which may carry "a device-map that wants no auto-fxp0") gets no positional claim.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A33-01` (parts file `parts/va33.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A33-01 | Medium | On a fail-closed boot of a committed firewall, the main-table default-route NIC (the WAN,…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked #15220 (CLOSED, mask only), #6789, #12205 and #4815 (other lifeline shapes), #15286 (vrf-mgmt master admit), #10751, muse-spark A7-05 (zero-identity whole-NIC admit, an accepted residual covering never-verified boxes) and A7-07 (fence aborts on netlink error, NEG). I grepped gh-issues.tsv for lifeline/fail-closed/default-route and prior-headings.tsv, and checked the in-run parts and worker reports. None covers replacing a verified record or the fence's default-route exemption on a committed box.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A33-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16672 — A missing `;` between two `node <n> priority <p>` statements commits (the #8437 fused-statement gate exempts a same-keyword repeat) and writes the second priority onto the first node, which can invert RG primary placement [OPEN]

## Summary

A missing `;` between two `node <n> priority <p>` statements commits (the #8437 fused-statement gate exempts a same-keyword repeat) and writes the second priority onto the first node, which can invert RG primary placement

**Finding ID:** `R3-A15-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — RG ownership differs from the authored config after a clean commit. The trigger is a one-character typo, and only the `node 1 ... node 0 ...` order inverts placement; the reverse order keeps placement and only changes the priority value. A per-node priority that is simply missing already commi…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (RG node-priority statement validation gaps, together with gemini parity-001 V34-03: missing/malformed/trailing priority tokens) — real and bounded, and it shares the acceptance surface "each RG node statement is exactly `node <0|1> priority <1..254>`"

## Mechanism

text `redundancy-group 1 { node 1 priority 100 node 0 priority 200; }` -> one node with Keys=[node 1 priority 100 node 0 priority 200] -> #8437 skips `node` (same keyword), and `priority` is a child of node, not a sibling -> compileRGNodePriority gives {1:200} -> the #4880 range gate iterates present keys only -> runtime: node 0 is clamped to 1, so node 1 wins the RG.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

schema_walk.go:990-992 `if tok == keyword { continue // a repeat of this leaf, not a foreign statement }`. compiler_chassis.go:1018-1046 compileRGNodePriority takes `nodeID` from `nodeVal(child)` and then runs `for i := 2; i < len(child.Keys)-1; i++ { if child.Keys[i] == "priority" { ... rg.NodePriorities[nodeID] = n } }`. Every priority token goes to the first id, last wins, and the second `node` id is never read. pkg/cluster/group_state.go clamps the absent node's 0 priority to 1.

## Impact

RG placement decides which chassis carries the RETH VIPs. An inverted placement after a routine edit moves traffic to the intended backup, and with `preempt` it stays there. `show configuration` shows the fused line, which the operator may read as correct.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In compileRGNodePriority, reject (strict) or split a second `node` token. Alternatively, have the #8437 gate treat a repeat of an instance-keyed keyword as fused. Together with V34-03, require that every RG node statement carry exactly one valid priority. Acceptance: both fused orders are rejected at Store.Commit, and the separate-statement control still commits.

## Contract (where cited)

schema_walk.go:941-947 (#8437): a missing semicolon fuses two statements, "the compiler ... silently drops the second statement" while `show configuration` still renders it, and the gate exists to reject that. In Junos, `node (0|1) priority <1..254>` is one statement per node.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A15-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A15-03 | Low | A missing ; between two node <n> priority <p> statements commits (the #8437 fused-statement… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:53: - **R3-A15-03 — COHORT (Low, RG node-priority validation).** **Defect:** same-keyword repeats bypass the sibling-fusion gate (`pkg/config/schema_walk.go:386-405`) and `compileRGNodePriority` assigns *every* inline `priority` occurrence to the *first* node ID (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:1025-1053`), so fused `node 1 priority 100 node 0 priority 200` writes priority 200 to node 1 and omits node 0. **Best alternative:** a missing node's priority is already legal, only one fused ordering inverts winner, and the reported older V34-03 node-priority validation cohort is a closer shared remediation than an independent issue. **Remaining check:** current Store.LoadOverride both fused orders and separate controls, then compare election priorities; reject only malformed/fused syntax, not legitimate omission without a separate contract.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L37: | R3-A15-03 fused node priority same-keyword exemption | COHORT | Low | | R3-A16-01 inline VPN named as gateway folds connections | MATERIAL | Medium (not High) | | R3-A16-02 hostname address pins FQDN remote.id | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-VA16-S1 shared local PSK owner verifies every peer | MATERIAL | High | | R3-A17-01 peer-slot DHCP group renders on peer, Kea refuses family | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-02 expired-leases maxima missing | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-03 server+relay same iface commit clean | COHORT | Low | Dispositions/sampled in parts: A09-02 NEG upheld (agree); A10-03 DUP of A11-03 (agree); VA13-S1 DUP of A13-01 (agree); A13 sampled user-class NEG confirmed; A14/A15/A16/A17 sampled dismissals — agree except as noted per claim. No FIXED/STALE found at origin/master for any batch-01 claim.

**Wonder:** wonder batch01 L41: | **R3-A15-02** | **NEEDS_VALIDATION** | Compiler leaves absent `GlobalWeight` at struct zero (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:1154-1174`); runtime uses zero as effective debt (`pkg/cluster/monitor.go:928-934` per va15), so omitted aggregate/independent global can fail open. Juniper official CLI reference explicitly gives `global-weight` default **255**, range 0–255 (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/chassis-edit-ip-monitoring.html, read in this lane). ## #16673 — R3-A51-04: LLDP Chassis/Port IDs of binary subtypes (MAC-address port ID, network-address chassis ID) are stored as lossy-sanitized text with the subtype dropped, so distinct… [OPEN]

## Summary

LLDP Chassis/Port IDs of binary subtypes (MAC-address port ID, network-address chassis ID) are stored as lossy-sanitized text with the subtype dropped, so distinct same-chassis neighbors share one key and display as garbage

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — the impact is limited to LLDP neighbour display and accounting. Port IDs of subtype 3 and chassis IDs of subtype 5 render as unreadable text (`"RT �� "`). Genuinely distinct neighbours with the same chassis and binary port IDs merge into one entry, and one's TTL=0 removes the other. There is no enforcement impact, and a hostile LLDP peer can already forge any key, so the collision adds no new attacker capability. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A51-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va51.md` (finding `R3-A51-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

In pkg/lldp/lldp.go @d1ea69f9aa: :1248 `n.ChassisID = sanitizeTLVString(string(value[1:]))` for non-MAC chassis subtypes. :1251-1258: for every port subtype, `n.PortID = sanitizeTLVString(string(value[1:]))`, with the subtype byte discarded. :1189-1199 sanitizeTLVString maps controls to ' ', and strings.Map turns invalid UTF-8 into U+FFFD. :150-152 neighborKeyFor keys on those strings.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** The LLDP MSAP identity is the chassis ID plus the port ID, each with its subtype (IEEE 802.1AB; clause not re-verified). lldp.go:118-136 (#7176) says the key must make collisions between distinct neighbours unrepresentable.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (LLDP neighbor identity/display fidelity) — real and cheap to fix, but bounded to display and neighbour bookkeeping.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the reporter's probe re-run by va51.

**Confidence:** High — executed with an ifname-subtype positive control.

## Impact

Hosts advertising MAC port IDs, and devices with network-address chassis IDs, show as garbage in `show lldp neighbors`. Multi-NIC hosts behind one port collapse into one flapping entry.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Decode the binary subtypes (port 3 and chassis 4 as a MAC, 5 as IANA family plus address) into canonical text, hex-encode other non-printable values, and include the subtype in neighborKey. Acceptance: the probe keys differ and display `52:54:00:aa:bb:01`.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A51-04`, part `parts/va51.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16674 — `config.NPTv6OverlapConflict`, the #7078 predicate behind the #4960 apply pre-pass, treats every static-NAT rule with a non-empty match and then as an NPTv6 rule. Two ordinary IPv6 block static-NAT rules where a /64 s... [OPEN]

## Summary
`config.NPTv6OverlapConflict`, the #7078 predicate behind the #4960 apply pre-pass, treats every static-NAT rule with a non-empty match and then as an NPTv6 rule. Two ordinary IPv6 block static-NAT rules where a /64 sits inside a /48 (`then static-nat prefix`, the #3031 block-to-block feature, resolved by longest prefix in the helper) pass strict commit. Every later apply then aborts in `dataplane.CompileConfig` with "the userspace helper rejects the whole NPTv6 snapshot on an overlapping prefix pair". This happens even when the config contains no NPTv6 rule at all.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — Bounded availability and operator-contract failure. A supported, strict-commit-accepted configuration cannot be applied. Every later apply, including unrelated policy, NAT or interface changes, fails at the pre-pass until the operator deletes a correct rule. The running dataplane stays on the previous snapshot while `show configuration` shows the new one. The error names NPTv6 even with zero NPTv6 rules, which points the operator at the wrong cause. Nothing becomes less enforced: the old snapshot keeps running. The boot-time consequence was not executed. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A78-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va78.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
IPv6 block static NAT with a more-specific carve-out is a supported, longest-prefix-resolved feature. With this predicate it can be committed but never applied, and it blocks every other change queued behind it, so committed config and running dataplane diverge silently until someone reads the apply error. Recovery is to delete a correct rule.

**Contract:** `pkg/config/nptv6_overlap.go:8-17,46-48` calls NPTv6OverlapConflict "the single source of truth for 'would the helper refuse this rule set for overlap'" and says "Rules the snapshot builder DROPS are skipped: an excluded rule never reaches try_from_snapshots". `pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:1086-1102` says the pre-pass keeps the #4960 over-rejection properties, so it must never hard-fail a config the helper installs. The helper's NPTv6 snapshot holds only `IsNPTv6` rules (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_nptv6.go:36`: `if rule == nil || !rule.IsNPTv6 { continue }`). Block static rules go to the static table instead (#3031).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
Observed at d1ea69f9aa. `pkg/config/nptv6_overlap.go:69-71`: `if rule.Then == "" || rule.Match == "" { continue // not an NPTv6 rule }`, with no `IsNPTv6` test anywhere in the loop. `nptv6PrefixWords` (`:142-160`) accepts any IPv6 /48 or /64. By contrast, the sibling `compileNPTv6` loop (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:928`) uses `if !rule.IsNPTv6 || rule.Match == "" || rule.Then == "" { continue }`. Call site: `compiler_nat.go:1103`, `if conflict := config.NPTv6OverlapConflict(cfg); conflict != "" { return fmt.Errorf("%s; the userspace helper rejects the whole NPTv6 snapshot ...") }`. The helper's block table (`userspace-dp/src/nat/static_nat.rs:1041-1066`) picks the best tier and then `prefix_len > best_prefix_len`, which is longest-prefix resolution with no rejection. History: the skip has been missing since the predicate was created in 28ca26a866 (#7078) and survived #9877 (2456a1fcba) and #15266 (41f7fcf10e). `compiler_validate_4960.go:4-8`: configstore never imports pkg/dataplane, so commit check does not reach this pre-pass.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — `dataplane.CompileConfig` with the test `recordingDP` on a strict-compiled config: the defect cell, three controls and a reverted one-line fix mutation. The daemon apply loop and boot apply are STATIC.

| R3-A79-01 VLAN domain sync update-first E2BIG, fail-closed + restart wedge | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A79-03 GRE inner DNAT/local lookups dead verifier cost | COHORT | Low |
| R3-A80-01 NAPI bootstrap UDP probes cannot spread RSS (ICMP L3-only, rate-limited) | NEEDS_VALIDATION | Medium (potential) / Low if lab clears |
| R3-A80-03 shim headroom measured on build kernel only, README stale | COHORT | Low |

## #16675 — Bootstrap exit renames a non-index-0 foreign-host lifeline positionally, and a timed-out first `commit confirmed` keeps that rename and its `.link`, so the rollback cannot restore a management NIC addressed by a kernel-name-keyed host config [OPEN]

## Summary

Bootstrap exit renames a non-index-0 foreign-host lifeline positionally, and a timed-out first `commit confirmed` keeps that rename and its `.link`, so the rollback cannot restore a management NIC addressed by a kernel-name-keyed host config

**Finding ID:** `R3-A33-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the outcome is console-only lockout that persists across reboots, on exactly the event commit confirmed exists to survive. It is bounded to a foreign (non-appliance) host whose default-route management NIC is not enumeration index 0, whose own network config matches that NIC by kernel name, and whose operator's first commit loses reachability so the window expires [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the rollback reports success while leaving the management NIC renamed, with no config that addresses it. The design rationale (renames are "cosmetic") is hollow for this shape.

## Mechanism

A foreign host runs netplan `ethernets: enp6s0: {addresses: [...], routes: [default]}`, rendered as `[Match] Name=enp6s0`, with enp5s0 at index 0. After `apt install xpf`, bootstrap finds the lifeline enp6s0 at index 1, refuses the rename, and SSH keeps working. The operator `commit confirmed`s a config without that addressing on ge-0-0-0. Bootstrap exit renames enp6s0 to ge-0-0-0 (a link cycle), netplan's `Name=enp6s0` file no longer matches, and SSH is lost. The window expires. The teardown removes `10-xpf-ge-0-0-0.network` and keeps the `.link`. The NIC stays ge-0-0-0 with no matching config, comes back as ge-0-0-0 on every reboot (the 10-xpf `.link` matches OriginalName), and bootstrap then finds no default route. The operator needs the console.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_run_naming.go:247-268 `runBootstrapExitStartup` calls `applyStartupNamingForConfig`, which reaches pkg/daemon/device_map.go:101-136 `applyStartupNamingPolicy`. In positional mode that calls `notePositionalIgnoresProtected(protected)` and then `enumerateAndRenameInterfacesFn`, which claims every NIC including the lifeline (#7205). pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:965-1000 `runBootstrapTeardownSteps` removes the `10-xpf-*.network` files but skips names ending in `.link`, with the comment "Keep .link files so names remain stable". No rename back exists. bootstrap.go:433-436 says "Renames persist deliberately — reverting them would link-cycle a degraded box for cosmetic benefit." The only lifeline restore is `restoreBootstrapLifelineNetwork` for `10-xpf-fxp0.network`, which for a non-index-0 lifeline is a captured absence. The only strand pre-flight is the device-map one (device_map.go:561 `deviceMapStrandsManagement`); positional mode has none.

## Impact

commit-confirmed rollback is the operator's only remote safety net on first takeover. Here it logs success while the management NIC stays renamed and unaddressed across reboots. Recovery requires console access.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At bootstrap exit, snapshot the lifeline's pre-takeover kernel name and the takeover `.link` set, and on the first-commit rollback remove the takeover `.link` and rename back. Alternatively, refuse at exit to rename a non-fxp0 lifeline whose addressing xpf did not author. Acceptance: the probe's WITNESS flips (no `10-xpf-ge-0-0-0.link`, a ge-0-0-0->enp6s0 rename issued), and the index-0 fxp0 rollback cells stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/daemon/README.md says SAFE-BOOTSTRAP means "the daemon can never lock an operator out of a remote box it manages". Under "First-commit rollback", a timed-out first commit confirmed re-enters bootstrap, retiring takeover state. docs/install-images.md says that on a foreign host "the operator's own network configuration is the lifeline". The bootstrap.go non-index-0 warning tells this exact operator to `commit confirmed` a change, which makes the rollback the advertised safety net.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A33-02` (parts file `parts/va33.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A33-02 | Medium | Bootstrap exit renames a non-index-0 foreign-host lifeline positionally, and a timed-out…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked #12154, #12155, #12505 and #14993 (fxp0 `.network` content and durability), #12151 and #12205 (index-0 remedy text and test), #7205 (positional ignores protected: it documents the rename, not the rollback consequence), #5868 (teardown error reporting), gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv and the in-run parts. No owner.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A33-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16676 — Since #15024 a VPN with an inline endpoint (`ike gateway <ip|fqdn>`) gets a swanctl connection named after the VPN, and a VPN that references a gateway object gets one named after the gateway. Both names share one namespace, and nothing checks… [OPEN]

## Summary

Since #15024 a VPN with an inline endpoint (`ike gateway <ip|fqdn>`) gets a swanctl connection named after the VPN, and a VPN that references a gateway object gets one named after the gateway. Both names share one namespace, and nothing checks for a clash. When an inline VPN's name equals a gateway object's name, the two fold into one connection. The first VPN in sort order supplies the peer address, auth and proposals; the other VPN's peer is dropped silently. Its child SA, including the st0 if_id that carries its route-based traffic, is then negotiated with the wrong peer. Strict commit accepts the config.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A16-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The defect is real and is not a duplicate, but High overstates it. I re-read the code at d1ea69f9aa in RUN/wt/a16. pkg/ipsec/policy.go:53-65: gatewayKeyFor returns the gateway name for a defined gateway and the VPN name for an in…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable through strict commit, the consequence was executed, and no gate covers the gateway-name/VPN-name overlap.

## Mechanism

`set security ike gateway siteA address 10.200.0.3` + `vpn zzz ike gateway siteA bind-interface st0.0` + `vpn siteA ike gateway 10.200.0.1 bind-interface st0.1` -> strict CompileConfig OK -> renderConfig groups both under key `siteA`, and the first sorted member supplies the endpoint -> swanctl.conf holds one connection -> charon trap/initiate for child zzz (if_id 1, st0.0) dials 10.200.0.1 -> xfrm state toward site B carries st0.0 traffic.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:53-65` @d1ea69f9aa: `gatewayKeyFor` returns `sanitizeSwanctlValue(vpn.Gateway)` for a defined gateway, else `sanitizeSwanctlValue(name)`. `:516-530`: `gc, exists := groups[connKey]; if !exists { gc = &gatewayConn{... remoteAddr: remoteAddr, localAddr: localAddr, authMethod: authMethod, ikeProposals: ...} }` and then `gc.children = append(gc.children, enriched...)`, so a later member's endpoint, auth and proposals are discarded. `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go:989-997` accepts an inline literal or dotted hostname (`IsUsableIPsecEndpointList`). `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_sa_collision_9624.go:41-52` builds owners only from `ipsecname.SANames(vpn, selectors)`, which are VPN and child names, never gateway connection names. `SANameIndex.Collisions()` (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1143`) does detect `aaa=[aaa zzz]`, but its only consumer is a slog.Warn (`pkg/daemon/ipsec_sa_rg_9139.go:192`).

## Impact

This hits hub configs that mix legacy inline VPNs with gateway-object VPNs. Site A traffic routed into st0.0 is encrypted to site B, or both sites stay down, with no commit error. It persists until an object is renamed and the SAs are terminated.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make connection keys collision-free by construction (for example, distinct prefixes for inline and gateway connections), or add a strict gate plus a render belt: VPNs sharing a `gatewayKeyFor` key must resolve to the same gateway object, otherwise reject or skip. Consumers: renderConfig, ConnectionNamesForVPN, ExpectedLoadedConns, reinitiate and HA attribution. Acceptance: the DEFECT cell fails strict commit (and on tolerant load renders two connections or skips one), the CONTROL cell is unchanged, and the lab initiate of `zzz` never reaches 10.200.0.1.

## Contract (where cited)

The #15024 commit (cf08e51c25) says "VPNs referencing a defined gateway render as children of the gateway-named connection ... Inline literal/hostname and empty endpoints keep per-VPN connections" (`pkg/ipsec/README.md:341-348`), so different peers never share a connection. The #9624 gate's stated purpose is that two VPNs never render one swanctl name. Each VPN negotiates only with its configured peer.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A16-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A16-01 | Medium | Since #15024 a VPN with an inline endpoint (ike gateway <ip/fqdn>) gets a swanctl… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:57: - **R3-A16-01 — MATERIAL (Medium, not High on present evidence).** **Defect:** named gateway connections and inline-endpoint VPN connections both key one `groups` map by the same sanitized string (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:69-80,181-186,288-296`). On a collision, only the first sorted member supplies endpoint/auth/IKE parameters; later members still append child selectors and PSKs (`:531-563`). SA-name collision gate checks VPN/child names, not this *IKE connection namespace* (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_sa_collision_9624.go:30-70`). Prior source-to-strongSwan run sent one child's SA to the other VPN's configured peer. **Best alternative:** misdelivery of usable traffic additionally needs compatible credentials/selectors and a peer accepting the child; with distinct PSKs both may instead fail. The namespace collision is operator-authored, not attacker-controlled remotely. **Remaining check:** current strict commit/render both VPN-name sort orders and child→peer binding, with shared-credential positive and distinct-credential negative controls.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L38: | R3-A16-01 inline VPN named as gateway folds connections | MATERIAL | Medium (not High) | | R3-A16-02 hostname address pins FQDN remote.id | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-VA16-S1 shared local PSK owner verifies every peer | MATERIAL | High | | R3-A17-01 peer-slot DHCP group renders on peer, Kea refuses family | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-02 expired-leases maxima missing | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A17-03 server+relay same iface commit clean | COHORT | Low | Dispositions/sampled in parts: A09-02 NEG upheld (agree); A10-03 DUP of A11-03 (agree); VA13-S1 DUP of A13-01 (agree); A13 sampled user-class NEG confirmed; A14/A15/A16/A17 sampled dismissals — agree except as noted per claim. No FIXED/STALE found at origin/master for any batch-01 claim. ---

**Wonder:** wonder batch01 L42: | **R3-A15-03** | **COHORT** with gemini parity-001 V34-03 | Fused repeated `node` tokens escape same-keyword fused-statement guard and compiler assigns second priority to first node (`pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:1028-1061`); supplied probe reports `node 1 priority 100 node 0 priority 200` becomes `{1:200}`, inverting placement. | Missing priority is already legal and separately contributes to same acceptance gap; severity Low and grouped with V34-03, which covers missing/malformed/trailing priority statements. Separate-statement control maps both priorities correctly. | | **R3-A16-01** | **MATERIAL** | Inline VPN keys by VPN name while named-gateway VPN keys by gateway name (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:69-80`); when same string collides, existing connection group retains first member’s remote/local/auth/proposals (`:532-547`) and only appends children/PSKs. Supplied stro…
