## #16677 — R3-A51-05: gRPC ShowText `flow-statistics` runs an unadmitted, uncancellable full v4+v6 session-table walk and prints a walk error as `Current sessions: 0` (#15577 regression;… [OPEN]

## Summary

gRPC ShowText `flow-statistics` runs an unadmitted, uncancellable full v4+v6 session-table walk and prints a walk error as `Current sessions: 0` (#15577 regression; pkg/diagcmd #7294 census RED at base)

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — it reopens the bounded resource-exhaustion class that #5708/#7294 closed. Any principal authorised for `show` can drive concurrent full-table walks outside the shared MaxConcurrentSessionWalks budget, on context.Background(), so a disconnecting client does not stop them. Separately, a walk failure is reported as a clean zero, which is the exact operator lie the in-function #3345 comment forbids. It needs an authenticated caller and costs CPU and map-lock time, with no enforcement loss. The walk cost itself was not measured. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A51-05`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va51.md` (finding `R3-A51-05`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/grpcapi/server_show_flow.go:96-101: `v4, v6, _ = backendSessionCountContext(context.Background(), dp)` with no Acquire. :123-125: `v4Cur, v6Cur := grpcSessionCount(s.dp)` … `"Current sessions:", v4Cur+v6Cur`. pkg/grpcapi/server_show.go:256-258: `case "flow-statistics": s.showFlowStatistics(&buf)`. backendSessionCountContext (runtime.go:15-60) → LegacyDataPlaneAdapter.SessionCountContext (pkg/dataplane/userspace/legacy_dataplane.go:1253-1258) → dataplane.Manager.SessionCountContext (pkg/dataplane/maps_session.go:399-430), which does a full `Iterate()` of `sessions` and `sessions_v6`. The siblings acquire first, e.g. server_show_status.go:40-46 `release, err := sessionWalkLimiter.Acquire()`. That comment records that this walk is the live session count on the userspace dataplane.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/diagcmd/limiter.go:160-170 says SessionWalkLimiter is shared by the ShowText surfaces, and records that "a gRPC caller could issue unbounded full-table scans" before #5708. server_show_flow.go:109-110 (#3345): "surface a counter-read failure rather than emitting clean zeros".

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a regression of a closed DoS-cap guarantee, on a PermView surface, with a false-zero display. The guard cell meant to catch it is red.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the census RED at base and GREEN under a one-site admission mutation (reverted). Static: the ShowText dispatch chain.

**Confidence:** High — the mechanism is proven by the repo's own census, and a mutation control isolates this as the only reacher. Medium on the magnitude, because the per-walk cost at production table size was not measured.

## Impact

NMS polling or several view-class users can stack full-table walks on a large session table. A failed walk tells the operator there are zero sessions. The red census also masks the next regression of this class.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Take `sessionWalkLimiter.AcquireCtx(ctx)` in showFlowStatistics and return ResourceExhausted on contention, as showBuffers does. Pass the ShowText ctx, and render an explicit error instead of 0. Acceptance: TestEverySessionScanSurfaceIsAdmitted7294 is green, and ShowText `flow-statistics` with 4 slots held returns ResourceExhausted.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A51-05`, part `parts/va51.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16678 — The first-commit `commit confirmed` rollback to bootstrap leaves the abandoned config's Router Advertisement senders (executed), Kea DHCP server units and DHCP relay (static) running, while it closes transit and logs "config-driven takeover removed" [OPEN]

## Summary

The first-commit `commit confirmed` rollback to bootstrap leaves the abandoned config's Router Advertisement senders (executed), Kea DHCP server units and DHCP relay (static) running, while it closes transit and logs "config-driven takeover removed"

**Finding ID:** `R3-A33-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — after the rollback the box keeps advertising itself as an IPv6 default router (RAs refreshed every MaxRtrAdvInterval) and keeps leasing DHCP with itself as gateway on the abandoned config's segments. Meanwhile it forwards nothing, because the same rollback closes transit and detaches the dataplane. Hosts that follow the RA or lease blackhole through this box, and on a foreign host it acts as a rogue router or DHCP server. It lasts until the next commit or an xpfd restart, and is bounded to the first-commit and nil-target rollback paths [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the rollback violates its own stated post-state ("zero config-driven claims"), with a concrete LAN-facing consequence.

## Mechanism

On a fresh box the operator runs `commit confirmed 5` with `protocols router-advertisement interface ge-0/0/0 prefix 2001:db8:1::/64` and a dhcp-local-server pool. The bootstrap-exit apply starts the RA sender and the Kea units. The window then expires, and executeConfirmedRollback takes the first-commit branch, closing transit and clearing FRR. The RA sender keeps advertising and Kea keeps leasing, so LAN hosts install this box as router or gateway and blackhole.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:1131-1213, the first-commit branch, runs `d.dhcp.Reconcile(nil)` (clients only), `enterBootstrapModeWithLifeline`, the host-auth closeout and `reconcileManagementAfterPromotion`, then `return`, with no applyConfigLocked. bootstrap.go:449-545 and :965-1060 cover debt discharge, the NAT alarm, cluster relinquish, `.network` removal, lifeline restore, reload, `frr.Clear`, `markDataplaneNotArmed` and `rt.Teardown`. Neither touches `d.ra`, `d.dhcpServer` or `d.dhcpRelay`. An exhaustive grep finds the d.ra/dhcpServer/dhcpRelay call sites only in daemon_apply_routing.go:40-52,127-152, daemon_apply_reset.go:137-159, daemon_apply_tail.go:593-594, daemon_run_shutdown.go:314,421-424, and daemon_ra_reconcile.go. The cluster reconcile returns early when the active config has no cluster stanza (:54-58), which is the case after the rollback promotes the empty tree. Background applies are fenced in bootstrap (#15054).

## Impact

the rollback is the operator's undo. It reports a clean bootstrap while still attracting the segment's IPv6 default route and new DHCP clients into a node that forwards nothing.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Bootstrap mode suppresses every takeover action. pkg/dhcpserver/README.md (#6787) says the Kea units outlive xpfd and must be stopped explicitly.

## #16680 — For a PSK gateway addressed by a hostname (`address peer.example.test`) with no `remote-identity`, xpf renders `remote { id = "peer.example.test" }` (an FQDN identity). It does not use the resolved IP that Junos defaults to. A peer that keeps the… [OPEN]

## Summary

For a PSK gateway addressed by a hostname (`address peer.example.test`) with no `remote-identity`, xpf renders `remote { id = "peer.example.test" }` (an FQDN identity). It does not use the resolved IP that Junos defaults to. A peer that keeps the Junos/strongSwan default identity (its own IP) is refused when it initiates. It is also refused when xpf initiates, unless the peer adopts the requested IDr. The DNS-addressed site-to-site VPN never comes up, and commit gives no warning.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A16-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — total availability loss for one supported, commit-clean VPN shape (an FQDN `address`, the usual form for a dynamic-DNS or cloud peer) against default-identity peers. There is no enforcement loss, and a workaround exists (an explicit remote-identity, which a dynamic-address peer cannot expre…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable through strict commit, with a total tunnel outage executed against default-identity peers.

## Mechanism

`set security ike gateway gw1 address peer.example.test` (PSK, no remote-identity) -> strict CompileConfig OK -> render `remote_addrs = peer.example.test`, `remote { id = "peer.example.test" }` -> the peer presents IDi/IDr = its IP -> charon's identity constraint fails -> AUTH_FAILED.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1321-1330` @d1ea69f9aa: `defaultRemoteID` returns `addrs[0]` of `SplitIPsecEndpointList(gw.Address)` for any single entry, with no IP-literal check. `:615-632` renders it as `remote.id`. The sibling inline arm `:633-637` pins `addrs[0]` for an inline hostname endpoint (static). The secret selectors at `pskIDSelectorsLocal` (`:1257-1300`) also carry the hostname string as the peer owner.

## Impact

This hits every PSK VPN to a DNS-addressed peer that keeps the default identity. The tunnel never establishes in either direction, there is no commit or apply signal, and it lasts until the operator adds an explicit identity.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `defaultRemoteID` and the inline arm, return "" unless the single address parses as an IP (`netip.ParseAddr`). For a hostname, either leave the IDr to negotiation or pin the resolved address, and give the secret a peer selector that matches the identity actually presented (not the hostname string). Coordinate with R3-VA16-S1, because the local owner cannot be the scoping mechanism. Acceptance: the FQDN cell renders no hostname `remote.id`, both lab directions establish against a fixed-IP-identity peer, and the IP control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

Junos `remote-identity` (juniper.net CLI reference): "the device uses the IPv4 or IPv6 address corresponding to the remote endpoint by default". `local-identity`: "...the local endpoint by default", so a Junos peer presents its IP. `pkg/ipsec/README.md:547-548`: "A peer that should be dialed by name is expressed with gateway `address <fqdn>`", which is a supported shape.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A16-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A16-02 | Medium | For a PSK gateway addressed by a hostname (address peer.example.test) with no… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:58: - **R3-A16-02 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** `defaultRemoteID` returns a single *address token* without checking IP literal (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1320-1344`); PSK `remote { id = ... }` and secret peer selector then pin that *hostname string* (`:620-653,1282-1300`), while the peer may present its resolved IP as its default identity. Prior strongSwan two-direction run saw AUTH_FAILED for FQDN and success for IP literal. Junos [remote-identity reference](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/security-edit-remote-identity.html) says default is the remote endpoint IP address. **Best alternative:** a peer intentionally presenting the hostname FQDN, or explicit remote-identity matching it, can establish; removing only `remote.id` without fixing secret selectors does not necessarily repair this. Earlier pre-#15193 shape also failed, so do not assert this *originated* in #15193. **Remaining check:** current hostname-vs-IP renderer and both IKE directions on supported strongSwan, with consistent identity/PSK selector fix-shape.

## #16682 — `writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork` turns a failed `.network` write into `(false, nil)` (the #5842 shape), so bootstrap still renames and cycles the management NIC to fxp0 with no fxp0 `.network` to re-address it [OPEN]

## Summary

`writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork` turns a failed `.network` write into `(false, nil)` (the #5842 shape), so bootstrap still renames and cycles the management NIC to fxp0 with no fxp0 `.network` to re-address it

**Finding ID:** `R3-A33-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the consequence can be a bootstrap management lockout (nothing committed to roll back to), but the trigger is a filesystem write failure under /etc/systemd/network (ENOSPC/EROFS/EIO) at the moment of the bootstrap rename [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (#5842 error-laundering residuals / bootstrap write-path refusals) — real but low-reach; it belongs with the sibling-writer error-channel fixes.

## Mechanism

On a bootstrap boot, the default route is on index-0 NIC enp5s0 with a static 192.0.2.10/24. The snapshot succeeds, the `.network` write fails and returns `(false, nil)`, and the code still writes the `.link`, renames enp5s0 to fxp0 and reloads. The host's name-keyed config no longer matches, no xpf fxp0 `.network` exists, and the link cycle flushed the default route, so the box is unreachable.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:1832-1837 `if err := fsatomic.WriteFileAtomic(path, []byte(content), 0644); err != nil { slog.Warn("bootstrap lifeline: failed to write fxp0 .network", ...); return false, nil }`. The caller at :1667-1675 refuses only on a non-nil error. :1683-1745 then writes `10-xpf-fxp0.link`, runs `renameInterfaceFn(lifeline, defaultMgmtInterface)` (LinkSetDown/SetName/SetUp) and runs `networkctlReloadFn()`.

## Impact

a bootstrap box reachable only over that NIC goes console-only on a storage fault, when the documented posture is to change nothing.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Return the write error and have setupBootstrapLifeline refuse (no `.link`, no rename, no reload), exactly as for an observation failure. Acceptance: the WITNESS arm reports `renamed=false` and both controls are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/daemon/README.md #5842 says `writeLinkFile` and `writeBootstrapFxp0Network` return `(changed, error)` because "a single bool made `false` mean BOTH 'already correct' and 'the write failed'". README #6789 says an incomplete lifeline observation aborts setupBootstrapLifeline "before the `.link` write, the rename and the reload". bootstrap.go:1658-1666 says the refusal must happen "before anything is mutated".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A33-04` (parts file `parts/va33.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A33-04 | Low | writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork turns a failed .network write into (false, nil) (the #5842…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): I checked #5842 (CLOSED, sibling writers), #6789 (observation), #12152 (mixed-family content), #12153 (networkd-active precheck), gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv and the in-run parts. No owner names this writer.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A33-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16683 — R3-A52-01: The local console handler for `request system configuration rescue delete` has an empty `if err != nil {}` block left by #15897. It prints the success line and… [OPEN]

## Summary

The local console handler for `request system configuration rescue delete` has an empty `if err != nil {}` block left by #15897. It prints the success line and returns nil when rescue.conf is absent, cannot be unlinked, or its directory fsync fails. The gRPC twin returns codes.Internal for the same errors.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a false success receipt on a durable-state mutation. Demonstrated: the success line is printed while rescue.conf is still on disk. That file is a full copy of the active config (the #4056 secret class). The "file remains" case needs an unlink or dir-fsync failure, which is uncommon. The absent-file case is trivially reachable but has no harmful consequence. No enforcement effect. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A52-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va52.md` (finding `R3-A52-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/cli/cli_request_system.go:403-410` @d1ea69f9aa: `if err := c.store.DeleteRescueConfig(); err != nil {` / `}` / `fmt.Println("Rescue configuration deleted")` / `return nil`. `git show 766cfaa6c4` (#15897, "reject trailing request system arguments", an ancestor of d1ea69f9aa) shows `-			return err` removed from inside that block while the `len(args) > 2` check was added above it. The sibling `save` case (`:393-399`) still returns its error. Observation: no test pins the console output (grep of `*_test.go`). `cmd/cli/request_verb_parity_8597_test.go` covers only the gRPC action mapping.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** The handler's own success line asserts the mutation happened. `DeleteRescueConfig` (`pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:2741-2748`) deliberately returns "no rescue configuration exists", "delete rescue config: %w" or "sync dir after delete rescue config: %w" so the caller can report them. The gRPC sibling (`pkg/grpcapi/server_request_parity_8597.go:83-87`) maps them to codes.Internal "delete rescue configuration: %v". The pkg/cli README treats a console/remote divergence on a request verb as a bug.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable regression that turns a failed durable mutation into a printed success; one-line fix.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go unit probe in pkg/cli driving `CLI.handleRequest([system configuration rescue delete])` against a real configstore. The gRPC twin behaviour is STATIC (code read).

**Confidence:** High — executed through the real `handleRequest` dispatch, with a positive control and a fix mutation that turns the probe green. The only assumption is that unlink/fsync failures happen in the field (EROFS/EIO/EACCES).

## Impact

An on-box console operator deleting rescue.conf to remove a cleartext config copy, or to stop a stale rescue being restored, is told it is gone while it remains. The remote `cli` on the same box reports the error, so the two surfaces disagree. Recovery is to check the file manually or retry via the remote CLI.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Restore `return fmt.Errorf("delete rescue configuration: %w", err)` inside the block (matching the gRPC wording). Acceptance: a pkg/cli regression in which the absent and undeletable rows return non-nil errors and print no success line, while the regular-file row still prints "Rescue configuration deleted".

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A52-01`, part `parts/va52.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16685 — Cluster DHCP filter keeps a peer-slot node-local group member on both nodes; the peer's Kea refuses the family file and serves nothing, including RETH segments after failover [OPEN]

## Summary

Cluster DHCP filter keeps a peer-slot node-local group member on both nodes; the peer's Kea refuses the family file and serves nothing, including RETH segments after failover

**Finding ID:** `R3-A17-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — after a clean commit, the peer node gets a whole-family DHCP outage. This is the consequence class #15206/#15028/#15029/#14601 were accepted at as Medium. It becomes visible when the peer takes over an RG: every RETH segment of that family then loses its DHCP server. In the symmetric layout…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable, clean-committing config shape makes the peer's Kea refuse its file; it survives refutation and dedup.

## Mechanism

shared `interfaces ge-0/0/3 unit 0 family inet address …` + `dhcp-local-server group gL interface ge-0/0/3.0` → CompileConfigForNode(1) is clean → `desiredClusterDHCPConfigWithMasters` keeps `ge-0-0-3` (not RG-scoped) → the #15206 belt keeps it (declared) → generateKea4Config renders subnet `"interface": "ge-0-0-3"` plus the interfaces-config entry → kea-dhcp4 on node 1 refuses the file → the restart fails → the #6535 converger re-drives the same desired state indefinitely → after RG takeover, node 1 serves no DHCPv4 on reth segments either.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:2160-2166` builds `rgScoped` only from `rethInterfacesMatchingRG`. At `:2186-2188`, `if masterIfaces[norm] || !rgScoped[norm] { kept = append(kept, norm) }` keeps every non-RETH member on both nodes. `:2265-2270` runs `dhcpserver.FilterKeaInterfaces15206` on the result. `pkg/dhcpserver/kea_phantom_interface_15206.go:29-31` says "It is deliberately NOT a kernel-existence test", and `:101-108` builds `usable` from `active.Interfaces.Interfaces`, where top-level `ge-0/0/3` is present on node 1 too (observed: `compiledHasGe-0/0/3=true` on node 1). There are no InterfaceByName/LinkByName/sysfs checks in pkg/dhcpserver or daemon_ha.go. The slot→node predicate exists and is used elsewhere: `pkg/cluster/monitor.go:552-553` (`if slot >= 0 && config.SlotToNodeID(slot) != mon.mgr.NodeID()`), `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:878-879`, and `pkg/config/types.go:212-228` (RethToPhysical). `docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf:13-56` declares ports inside `groups nodeN`, which is the safe shape.

## Impact

This hits clustered deployments that keep a per-node data or LAN port in the shared section with a DHCP group. The peer node silently runs with Kea refused; its only signal is a logged apply error. The failure shows at the worst moment: failover leaves every RETH segment without DHCP. Recovery is to move the group and port under `groups nodeN`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `filterDHCPConfigForMasterRGsWithMasters` (and the RA sibling `clusterRAConfigSets`; see R3-A26-03), drop a non-RG member whose `InterfaceSlot` is ≥0 and maps to `SlotToNodeID != localNodeID`, and set `MembersFiltered`. Acceptance: in the probe's shared shape, node 1 renders no `ge-0-0-*` name and Kea accepts with node 1's devices; node 0 is unchanged; the grouped shape is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go` #6520 doc says a node-local interface is served by its node ("Redundancy-group mastership … says nothing about an interface that has no redundant peer"). The pkg/dhcpserver README (#15206/#15028/#9785) holds that a clean commit must not render a name Kea refuses, because Kea refuses the whole family file. CLAUDE.md: node 1 names its ports FPC 7 (`ge-7-0-x`), so node 0's `ge-0-0-x` ports do not exist on node 1. The product already resolves peer-slot names by slot for interface monitors.

## Validation provenance

## #16686 — `addStableRethLinkLocal` installs the cluster stable router link-local for unit 0 only on the bare member netdev. It reaches VLAN sub-interfaces only for `unitNum > 0`. A tagged unit 0 (`reth0 vlan-tagging; unit 0 vlan-id 100`) therefore never carries the address on `<member>.100`. The RA builder nevertheless binds that unit's sender to the stable LL on `<member>.100`, so `ndp.Listen` fails and the RG owner sends no RAs on that VLAN, on either node and across failover. [OPEN]

## Summary

`addStableRethLinkLocal` installs the cluster stable router link-local for unit 0 only on the bare member netdev. It reaches VLAN sub-interfaces only for `unitNum > 0`. A tagged unit 0 (`reth0 vlan-tagging; unit 0 vlan-id 100`) therefore never carries the address on `<member>.100`. The RA builder nevertheless binds that unit's sender to the stable LL on `<member>.100`, so `ndp.Listen` fails and the RG owner sends no RAs on that VLAN, on either node and across failover.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A34-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — IPv6 hosts on that VLAN lose their default router and SLAAC prefixes, and it persists across failover because both nodes run the same code. The scope is bounded to a commit-clean shape (tagged RETH unit 0 with IPv6, router-advertisement, and no configured link-local) and to RA. Only the address/bind mismatch is demonstrated. The missing RA on the wire is derived from the mdlayher/ndp source.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable via a Junos-valid committed shape, with a concrete IPv6 default-router outage, and it survives dedup as a residual of #15684.

## Mechanism

The trace runs from `set interfaces reth0 vlan-tagging; unit 0 vlan-id 100 family inet6 address …; protocols router-advertisement interface reth0.0`, through commit, to the RG1 owner. There, VIP reconcile puts the global VIP on `ge-0-0-0.100`, while `addStableRethLinkLocal(1)` puts `fe80::bf72:1:1` only on `ge-0-0-0`. `reconcileClusterRAServices` then builds the RA for `ge-0-0-0.100` with source `fe80::bf72:1:1`. `ndp.Listen` fails, and there is no periodic or solicited RA on VLAN 100. The same happens on the peer after failover.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:317-318 @d1ea69f9aa: `if !rethUnitHasConfiguredLinkLocal(ifc, 0) { addStableLLToInterfaceFn(linuxName, stableLL) }` — `linuxName` is the bare member. Lines :322-335: `for unitNum := range ifc.Units { if unitNum > 0 && rethUnitHasIPv6(ifc, unitNum) { … subIface = linuxName.VlanID … } }`, so unit 0 is never sub-interfaced. daemon_ra.go:148-156 sets `ra.SourceLinkLocal = cluster.StableRethLinkLocal(clusterID, rg)` when no LL is configured, and :169 `ra.Interface = cfg.ResolveKernelIfName(ra.Interface)` yields `ge-0-0-0.100` for `reth0.0` with vlan-id 100. pkg/ra/sender.go:396-399 binds `ndp.Addr(s.cfg.SourceLinkLocal)`; :297-306 logs "failed to open NDP connection (giving up after retries)" and returns false. mdlayher/ndp@v1.1.0/addr.go literal match: `match = func(check netip.Addr) bool { return ip == check }`, then `ndp: address %q not found on interface %q`. `ensureLinkLocal` (sender.go:1284-1300) returns early because an EUI-64 LL is already present. Census: stable-LL producers are only daemon_ha_vip.go (add/remove/direct GARP) and its callers at daemon_ha.go:1010/1421 and daemon_apply_dataplane.go:1075/1095. All of them go through the same function. pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:138 mirrors the same base-netdev rule.

## Impact

Every SLAAC/RA host on a tagged unit-0 VLAN of an RG never learns its default router, or loses it at router-lifetime expiry. The failure is silent apart from one Warn per sender start, and it survives failover. Recovery requires renumbering the unit or configuring an explicit link-local.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Select the netdev by `unit.VlanID > 0` (the `RethVIPsForRG`/`ResolveKernelIfName` rule) in `addStableRethLinkLocal`, `removeStableRethLinkLocal`, the router-NA leg of `directSendGARPs`, and `stableRethLinkLocalTargets`. Install the parent stable LL only for an untagged unit 0 with IPv6. Acceptance: the probe's unit-0 row shows the LL on `ge-0-0-0.100` and not on `ge-0-0-0`, and the unit 10/50/60/70 rows are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

daemon_ra.go:148-156 says "RETH HA startup installs a stable router link-local on the active member. Bind RA to that address". #15684 made the stable LL per-unit so each VLAN unit carries the shared router identity. pkg/daemon/README.md "Per-RG Router-Advertisement reconcile" uses the shared stable router identity across failover. Junos permits `vlan-tagging` with `unit 0 { vlan-id N; }`.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A34-01` (parts file `parts/va34.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A34-01 | Medium | addStableRethLinkLocal installs the cluster stable router link-local for unit 0 only on the…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): This is a residual of #15684 (CLOSED, fix 4847bf092c, ancestor of d1ea69f9aa): its per-unit predicate still keys the VLAN branch on `unitNum > 0`. The prior gemini vsrx-parity-003 H24-04 is the per-unit LL-suppression claim that became #15684, not this shape. #10303, #14978, #10779 and #2996 are different consumers. No in-run part or worker report covers a tagged unit 0.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A34-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A34-01 — A VLAN-tagged RETH unit 0 (`unit 0 vlan-id N`) never gets the stable router link-local on its VLAN sub-interface, yet its RA sender is bound to that address there, so no Router Advertisements are sent on that VLAN
- **Finding ID:** R3-A34-01

## #16687 — Residual of #15933 C5: the apply path still writes dns-name answers in place into the published active config. This races `show security match-policies` readers outside applySem and leaves the pointer-keyed policymatch cache stale. [OPEN]

## Summary
Residual of #15933 C5: the apply path still writes dns-name answers in place into the published active config. This races `show security match-policies` readers outside applySem and leaves the pointer-keyed policymatch cache stale.

**Finding ID:** R3-N09-05
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium. There is a Go data race on `Address.DNSAddresses` slice headers in the control daemon; torn reads are possible, but a crash was not demonstrated. There is also an operator-visible lie: `show security match-policies` keeps the dataplane-refusal verdict that was cached for a config pointer after the in-place answers change. It can report REFUSED after the helper accepted, or ACCEPTED after the helper began refusing.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Any deployment with dns-name objects whose operators use the policy simulator is affected. The daemon has a memory-unsafe race, and the troubleshooting tool can claim the dataplane accepted policy that it is refusing (see R3-N09-01), or the reverse.

**Contract:** `address_forms_15673.go:111-117` says "cfg MUST NOT be a published active config (#15933): a config handed out by configstore (ActiveConfig / ActiveSnapshot) is shared with concurrent applies and readers". The #15933 closing comment says "no mutation of the published config during concurrent apply".

**Trace:** background apply (holding applySem) → line 150 writes the published `Address.DNSAddresses` ‖ gRPC/CLI `MatchPolicies` (no applySem) → `ActiveConfig()` (same pointer) → `UsableValues` reads it, which is the race. The first query caches the verdict per pointer, and later in-place writes do not invalidate it.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:150` `config.RefreshDNSAddressBooks(cfg)`, where cfg is the published pointer: `daemon_apply_commit.go:851` `applyConfigLocked(..., compiled)`, `daemon_apply.go:263-267` `cfg := d.store.ActiveConfig(); d.applyConfigLocked(...)`, plus feed and debt applies. `address_forms_15673.go:100-103` writes `a.DNSAddresses` in place. `grpcapi/server_cluster.go:153` `cfg := s.store.ActiveConfig()` → `policymatch.Match` → `querySnapshotFor` (`policymatch.go:131-150`, cache keyed on `entry.cfg != cfg`) → `policyContentRejectionReasons` → `UsableValues` (`types_security.go:1921`).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test -race ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestN09ApplyPathDNSWriteRacesShowReader -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/n09/evidence/zz_n09_dns_apply_race_probe_test.go). The writer arm gives 4× `WARNING: DATA RACE` at address_forms_15673.go:103 against types_security.go:1921, then `race detected during execution of test`, FAIL. The control arm (reader only) gives `--- PASS ... control-reader-only`. Cache probe (`go test ./pkg/policymatch/ -run TestN09`): before `ContentRejected=true`; after an in-place recovery on the same pointer `ContentRejected=true answers=[198.51.100.20/32]`; control on a fresh pointer `ContentRejected=false`. Outputs are in RUN/verify/vn09/race-rerun.out and cache-rerun.out. Limits: a synthetic goroutine pair stands in for the daemon goroutines.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Resolve into a private copy before publication, or move answers into a daemon-owned, generation-stamped answer table, and never write through a published `*Config`. Key derived caches on content or answer generation. Acceptance: the race probe passes under -race, and the cache probe reports `ContentRejected=false` after recovery.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn09.md)</summary>

### R3-N09-05 — Residual of #15933 C5: the apply path still writes dns-name answers in place into the published active config, which races `show security match-policies` readers outside applySem and leaves the pointer-keyed policymatch cache stale
- **Finding ID:** R3-N09-05
- **Title:** Residual of #15933 C5: the apply path still writes dns-name answers in place into the published active config. This races `show security match-policies` readers outside applySem and leaves the pointer-keyed policymatch cache stale.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker n09 (A7 daemon-delta engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vn09
- **Severity:** Medium. There is a Go data race on `Address.DNSAddresses` slice headers in the control daemon; torn reads are possible, but a crash was not demonstrated. There is also an operator-visible lie: `show security match-policies` keeps the dataplane-refusal verdict that was cached for a config pointer after the in-place answers change. It can report REFUSED after the helper accepted, or ACCEPTED after the helper began refusing.
- **Confidence:** High for the race (race detector, with a control arm) and for the cache staleness (probe, with a fresh-pointer control). Medium for production timing: the writer/reader pairing was established by reading the code.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — `go test -race` in pkg/dataplane/userspace and a policymatch cache probe. The production writer and reader call sites are STATIC.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — the closing claim of the fixed issue ("no mutation of the published config during concurrent apply") is falsified on a reachable path.
- **Contract:** `address_forms_15673.go:111-117` says "cfg MUST NOT be a published active config (#15933): a config handed out by configstore (ActiveConfig / ActiveSnapshot) is shared with concurrent applies and readers". The #15933 closing comment says "no mutation of the published config during concurrent apply".
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection at stake is control-daemon memory safety and the truthfulness of the policy simulator. The actor is a low-privilege operator running `show security match-policies` while any background apply runs (a feed update, a debt reassert, boot, or a commit). The code assumes that holding applySem makes the in-place write safe; readers do not take applySem.
- **Evidence:** `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:150` `config.RefreshDNSAddressBooks(cfg)`, where cfg is the published pointer: `daemon_apply_commit.go:851` `applyConfigLocked(..., compiled)`, `daemon_apply.go:263-267` `cfg := d.store.ActiveConfig(); d.applyConfigLocked(...)`, plus feed and debt applies. `address_forms_15673.go:100-103` writes `a.DNSAddresses` in place. `grpcapi/server_cluster.go:153` `cfg := s.store.ActiveConfig()` → `policymatch.Match` → `querySnapshotFor` (`policymatch.go:131-150`, cache keyed on `entry.cfg != cfg`) → `policyContentRejectionReasons` → `UsableValues` (`types_security.go:1921`).
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test -race ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestN09ApplyPathDNSWriteRacesShowReader -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/n09/evidence/zz_n09_dns_apply_race_probe_test.go). The writer arm gives 4× `WARNING: DATA RACE` at address_forms_15673.go:103 against types_security.go:1921, then `race detected during execution of test`, FAIL. The control arm (reader only) gives `--- PASS ... control-reader-only`. Cache probe (`go test ./pkg/policymatch/ -run TestN09`): before `ContentRejected=true`; after an in-place recovery on the same pointer `ContentRejected=true answers=[198.51.100.20/32]`; control on a fresh pointer `ContentRejected=false`. Outputs are in RUN/verify/vn09/race-rerun.out and cache-rerun.out. Limits: a synthetic goroutine pair stands in for the daemon goroutines.
- **Trace:** background apply (holding applySem) → line 150 writes the published `Address.DNSAddresses` ‖ gRPC/CLI `MatchPolicies` (no applySem) → `ActiveConfig()` (same pointer) → `UsableValues` reads it, which is the race. The first query caches the verdict per pointer, and later in-place writes do not invalidate it.
- **Refutation attempt:** `TestDNSRefreshConcurrentApplyNeverMutatesPublished15933` models only a reader under applySem (`dns_refresh_15933_test.go:192-205`), so it cannot detect this. The policymatch cache is invalidated only by pointer. #15962 moved the refresher's writer but not the apply path's writer. f14 (this run) inspected the same line and found no unsynchronized reader; the MatchPolicies path is that reader.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Ownership violation: a published immutable generation is mutated after publication, and a derived cache keyed on identity assumes that it is immutable.

## #16688 — R3-A52-02: `ParseEventFilterArgs` stores the protocol token raw, and `EventFilter.matches` compares it with `EqualFold` against the rendered name (TCP/ICMPv6/ESP), never… [OPEN]

## Summary

`ParseEventFilterArgs` stores the protocol token raw, and `EventFilter.matches` compares it with `EqualFold` against the rendered name (TCP/ICMPv6/ESP), never `ProtocolNum`. So `protocol 6` (the value the view prints as `protocol-id="6"`), `58`, `50`, `icmp6`, and a typo like `tcpx` all yield an empty answer with no error. The local CLI, remote ShowText, gRPC GetEvents and REST share this matcher.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a forensic false negative on the security-event query surface. The operator is told "no events recorded" for events that are in the buffer. It is recovered by retrying with the protocol name. No enforcement effect. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A52-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va52.md` (finding `R3-A52-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

@d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/logging/event_filter_args.go:62-67` `case "protocol": ... filter.Protocol = args[i]` (no validation). `pkg/logging/eventbuf.go:434` `if f.Protocol != "" && !strings.EqualFold(rec.Protocol, f.Protocol) { return false }`. `pkg/logging/ringbuf.go:1311-1320` `protoName` renders upper-case names, and `ringbuf.go:676,1126` also populate `ProtocolNum`. `pkg/cli/proto.go:42-57` `protoNameToID` makes RT_FLOW print `protocol-id="6"` for TCP. The same filter is built raw at `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_events.go:51` (`Protocol: req.Protocol`) and `pkg/api/security.go:619`, and the remote ShowText path calls `ParseEventFilterArgs`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `docs/junos-cli-reference.md:2159-2167` says `show security log ... [protocol <proto>]` parsing fails closed (#3347), because "silently broadening a scoped forensic query is worse than failing the query". Silently narrowing a query to nothing is the same class of misreport. `pkg/logging/eventbuf.go:18` documents `ProtocolNum` as the key "The matcher compares ... directly rather than re-parsing the rendered name". Every sibling selector now normalises via `appid.ProtocolNumber`: `pkg/cli/monitor.go:255-271` (flow filter and packet-drop after #15236) and the trace filter (#15679).

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (event/monitor protocol-selector parity) — real and minor. It is the remaining sibling of the #13553/#15236 A52-07/#15679 protocol-normalisation fixes.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/cli probe through `showSecurityLog`, and the pkg/logging parser+matcher probe. The gRPC/REST consumers are STATIC (they build the same `EventFilter` from the raw string).

**Confidence:** High — executed end to end through `CLI.showSecurityLog`, with the sibling #13553 monitor filter as a control on the same record.

## Impact

An incident responder asking "any denies for protocol 50/58?" gets a confident empty answer on every surface, including automation using gRPC/REST, while the same buffer holds matching events.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `ParseEventFilterArgs`, and in the GetEvents/REST builders, resolve the token via `appid.ProtocolNumber` and reject an unknown token with a usage error. Store the number and match on `rec.ProtocolNum`, falling back to the rendered name when ProtocolNum==0, as `monitorFlowFilter.matches` does. Acceptance: `protocol 6`/`58`/`50`/`icmp6` return the matching events, `protocol tcpx` is an error, and the name rows are unchanged on all four surfaces.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A52-02`, part `parts/va52.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16689 — The `userspace_ingress_domains_vlan` sync writes the new rows before it deletes the stale ones. An accepted VLAN re-plan whose union with the pinned plan exceeds 8192 rows hits E2BIG. The result is a transient transit... [OPEN]

## Summary
The `userspace_ingress_domains_vlan` sync writes the new rows before it deletes the stale ones. An accepted VLAN re-plan whose union with the pinned plan exceeds 8192 rows hits E2BIG. The result is a transient transit outage plus an unapplied commit, and at the next daemon restart a durable ctrl-disabled outage.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium. The demonstrated consequence (on a capacity-faithful fake map) is that every commit attempt of such a plan sets ctrl Enabled=0, so all transit drops until the next ~1 s helper status tick re-syncs the old plan. The commit returns an error, and the store-active P2 is never enforced. The potential consequence is a full appliance transit outage at the next daemon restart, crash or upgrade, which persists until rollback, reboot or a manual unpin. The trigger is bounded: it needs a VLAN plan whose old+new union exceeds 8192 rows (about 2 rows per VLAN unit, roughly 2,050 or more units changed at once, or a near-capacity plan plus a modest change). [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A79-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va79.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
VLAN-dense multi-tenant deployments that renumber or move trunk VLANs see a commit that fails with what looks like a transient map error and briefly drops all transit. The commit stays in the store unapplied, so the dataplane diverges from the active config. The latent consequence is that the next xpfd restart, crash or upgrade takes the box down with ctrl disabled. On an HA pair, the peer receives the same config (`applyErrSkipsPeerSync` does not suppress this error class; static) and is exposed the same way.

**Contract:** #13724 (fixed in 52e29404ec) made the shim classifier-map reconcile prune stale keys before it adds replacements "so map occupancy never exceeds max_entries" (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1307-1308`, `reconcileAddressMapKeys`). `docs/log/14842.md` says capacity (8192) is preflighted before any classifier write and that the fail-closed caller leaves ctrl unchanged on refusal. A plan the preflight accepts must therefore be programmable, and a plan that cannot be programmed must leave the old plan forwarding.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:268-279` @d1ea69f9aa runs `for k, v := range desired { if err := domainMap.Update(k, v, ebpf.UpdateAny); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("update userspace_ingress_domains_vlan ...") } }` and only then `for k := range current { ... domainMap.Delete(k) }`. `maps_sync.go:232-238` (`checkIngressDomainCapacity`, called at :493) bounds only `len(desired)`. `maps_sync.go:520-529`: only the preflight message keeps ctrl, and every other error goes to `failClosedUserspaceCtrlMapLocked` (Enabled=0). `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:549-551` declares `HashMap::with_max_entries(8192, 0)`, a preallocated hash whose new-key insert on a full map returns E2BIG. `maps_sync.go:353-366`: `programBootstrapMapsLocked` writes ctrl Enabled 0 and then syncs the classifier maps (:419). `manager_compile.go:705-714` returns that error before `ensureProcessLocked`. `pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go:196-202,866-899`: `reconcileDisposableCollectionPin` keeps a shape-matching pin across restarts. `maps_sync.go:808` is the status tick that re-syncs `m.lastSnapshot`. `manager_compile.go:678,764` assign `lastSnapshot` only on success.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED. The production `buildUserspaceIngressDomainEntries`, `checkIngressDomainCapacity`, `syncUserspaceClassifierMapsFailClosedLocked`, `applyHelperStatusLocked` and `reconcileAddressMapKeys` ran via their seams. The update/delete loop of `syncIngressDomainMapLocked` was transcribed onto a bounded fake. The restart ordering (bootstrap sync before helper start) is STATIC.

## #16690 — `reconcileIPMonGating` has one caller, gated on `anyRGChanged`, which comes from the reconcile pass's own `tr.Changed`. `handleClusterEvent` (and `watchVRRPEvents`) apply the rg-state edge first and never call it. So after a normal failover the new RG owner keeps the probe set computed while it was secondary, with HA-gated tests off, and keeps its old publish gate. The new standby keeps its gated probes running and its gate open. [OPEN]

## Summary

`reconcileIPMonGating` has one caller, gated on `anyRGChanged`, which comes from the reconcile pass's own `tr.Changed`. `handleClusterEvent` (and `watchVRRPEvents`) apply the rg-state edge first and never call it. So after a normal failover the new RG owner keeps the probe set computed while it was secondary, with HA-gated tests off, and keeps its old publish gate. The new standby keeps its gated probes running and its gate open.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A34-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the trigger is every ordinary cluster failover. After it, `services ip-monitoring` WAN failover stops following RG ownership: the forwarding node runs none of its gated probes, so a later WAN next-hop failure is not failed over. Its publish gate stays wrong until a reconcile-observed RG edge. A commit restores the probe set but never the gate. The harm needs a second fault (the WAN failure), which bounds it below High. [reporter: Medium (borderline High)]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the shipped HA gating contract is never actuated on the normal failover path. The trigger is reachable and the consequence concrete.

## Mechanism

RG1 fails over A→B. On B, `watchClusterEvents` → `handleClusterEvent` → `SetCluster(true)` sets active. The next reconcile gets `Reconcile(true, …)` with `Changed=false`, so `anyRGChanged=false` and `reconcileIPMonGating` is not called. B keeps the effective RPM set from its secondary era (gated tests dropped; daemon_rpm.go:160-163 logged "RPM probe tests gated off while secondary") and keeps its old gate. A keeps probing from VIP-less RETHs, which fail structurally, and keeps its gate as it was. If A is still primary for any RG (for example RG0), it may publish preferred routes from those failures.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:593-614 @d1ea69f9aa: `reconcileIPMonGating` → `reconcileRPMForHATransition(cfg)` … `d.ipmon.SetPublishEnabled(d.ipmonPublishAllowed(cfg))`. The callers census found only daemon_ha.go:1467-1470 `if anyRGChanged { … d.reconcileIPMonGating() }`. `anyRGChanged = true` is set only at :1412, under `if tr.Changed` of `tr := s.Reconcile(clusterPri, vrrp)` (:1283). rg_state.go:438-459 `changed := desired != s.active; s.active = desired`. `handleClusterEvent` runs `tr := s.SetCluster(isPrimary)` (:539) and schedules only `scheduleFRRHAReconcile`/`scheduleConnectedRGRepublish` (:542-545, :756-760). `filterRPMForHAGating` evaluates `d.cluster.IsLocalPrimary(rgID)` (daemon_rpm.go:144-147) only when `reconcileRPMMode` runs, and its callers are the apply paths (daemon_apply_tail.go:363, daemon_run.go:523) plus the missing hook. The pin-retry loop rebuilds from the cached `d.rpmEffective` (daemon_rpm.go:512-768), not from the gating filter. The engine starts with `publishEnabled: true` (pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:263) and withholds the overlay while it is false (:649-651).

## Impact

Clusters using probe-driven WAN failover effectively follow the node that was primary at the last commit or reconcile-observed edge, not the RG owner. After any HA failover the forwarding node does not react to a WAN next-hop failure, and nothing tells the operator.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Schedule `reconcileIPMonGating` off the event goroutine, like `scheduleFRRHAReconcile`. Call it from `handleClusterEvent`'s ownership-edge branches and from the `tr.Changed` arms of `watchVRRPEvents`. Alternatively, make the reconcile pass compare the gating inputs against the last-applied gated set rather than its own `tr.Changed`. Acceptance: both directions of both probes report `publishEnabled == predicate` with events delivered, and an RPM fake shows the gated test set swapped on both nodes after a delivered failover, with the #11414 burst firing on the new owner.

## Contract (where cited)

daemon_ha.go:1464-1466 says "#1827 §4.4: on any RG transition, re-evaluate ip-monitoring HA gating — gated probes run (and the overlay publishes) only on the data-RG primary; the standby reverts to the config baseline". The #11414 takeover burst (`reconcileRPMForHATransition`, daemon_rpm.go:786-801) assumes this hook runs on takeover. CLAUDE.md lists probe-driven WAN failover (`services ip-monitoring`, #1827) as a shipped feature.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A34-02` (parts file `parts/va34.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A34-02 | Medium | reconcileIPMonGating has one caller, gated on anyRGChanged, which comes from the reconcile…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked #1827, #3764, #11414 (takeover burst, fix c9f511b1f0 — its burst is reached only via this hook), #15038 (chassis-cluster RG ip-monitoring, a different subsystem) and #15074 (per-test gating predicate). gh-issues has no hit on the trigger. In-run parts and worker reports (a14, a49, b23) mention the hook or publish gates only in other contexts. No prior heading covers the event-path trigger.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A34-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A34-02 — ip-monitoring HA gating (#1827 §4.4 probe set + overlay-publish gate) is re-evaluated only when `reconcileRGState` itself observes an rg-state edge, so an ordinary event-delivered failover never re-gates either node
- **Finding ID:** R3-A34-02

## #16691 — expired-leases-processing max-time/reclaim-timer/flush-timer/unwarned-cycles/hold-time/max-leases lack Kea's maxima; a clean commit stops every pool of the family on the node(s) [OPEN]

## Summary

expired-leases-processing max-time/reclaim-timer/flush-timer/unwarned-cycles/hold-time/max-leases lack Kea's maxima; a clean commit stops every pool of the family on the node(s)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A17-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — after a clean commit, a whole-family DHCP outage follows on the node, and on both cluster nodes because the block is synced and, since #9348, rendered on clustered nodes. This is the #15029/#14601 class. Bounded: the operator must author an out-of-range tuning value. `max-time` is in millis…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the commit gate accepts values the runtime consumer refuses, and the consequence is a family-wide outage.

## Mechanism

`set system services dhcp-local-server expired-leases-processing max-time 30000` → schema min-only OK → compile Atoi → render `"expired-leases-processing": {"max-reclaim-time": 30000}` → Kea refuses the file → the fail-closed restart fails → no DHCPv4 on any segment of the node (the cluster peer behaves the same through the tolerant sync path).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/schema_system.go:1194-1248` uses `ValidateIntegerMin(1)` for reclaim-timer, flush-timer and hold-time, and `ValidateIntegerMin(0)` for max-leases, max-time and unwarned-cycles. `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:883-900` uses `strconv.Atoi` with no range check. `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:1143-1156` renders the values verbatim (`m["max-reclaim-time"] = c.MaxReclaimTime`). A grep finds no other consumer or gate. pkg/configstore adds no DHCP gate. No `kea -t` pre-check exists (grep `"-t"` in pkg/dhcpserver and pkg/daemon finds only sshd). `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go:137-155` reports only a generic `apply DHCP server config:` error after the config is already active.

## Impact

A lease-reclamation tuning knob becomes a DHCP kill switch for every segment of the family on the node, or on both nodes in a cluster. The operator sees only a generic restart error, and the peer sees nothing at all. Recovery requires reading the Kea journal and rolling back.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Use `ValidateIntegerRange` in the schema: reclaim-timer and flush-timer 1..65535, unwarned-cycles 0..65535, max-time 0..10000, hold-time 1..4294967295, max-leases 0..4294967295. Fix the schema comment. Clamp or omit with a warning in the renderer for the tolerant path. Acceptance: every out-of-range probe row is refused at commit naming the leaf; the boundary control still commits and Kea accepts.

## Contract (where cited)

The `docs/config-schema.md` range policy says the binding bound is what the runtime actually consumes. The pkg/dhcpserver README's #14601 doctrine says a value Kea refuses must be refused at commit. The schema's own comment (`schema_system.go:1188-1191`, "Kea has no documented hard upper bound on these knobs, so min-only validation is correct") is factually wrong.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A17-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A17-02 | Medium | expired-leases-processing… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:64: - **R3-A17-02 — MATERIAL (Medium; Kea-version check).** **Defect:** all expired-lease knob validators are minimum-only, with a comment asserting no upper bound (`pkg/config/schema_system.go:1182-1255`); compiler `Atoi` and renderer emit values without cap (`pkg/config/compiler_services.go:884-906`, `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:1138-1160`). Prior Kea 3.0.4 oracle rejected `max-time=10001`, timer/unwarned=65536 and hold/max-leases=2^32, despite clean strict compile, taking the family config down. **Best alternative:** xpf deploys Kea 3.0.3 (not exercised in the previous report), and at-boundary/disabled-block cases worked; no arbitrary schema-only limit should be adopted without consumer-version evidence. **Remaining check:** inspect/run the *deployed* Kea version's `-t` for each boundary and both families against current render; validate min/max plus tolerant-load behavior.

## #16692 — In legacy `no-private-rg-election` mode, `watchVRRPEvents` never refreshes the #15258 sync-hold mirror. The preempt MASTER event that `ReleaseSyncHold` itself triggers is therefore judged against `syncHold=true`: there is no rg_active write and no services. `syncRGSyncHold` then discards the transition its own `SetSyncHold` produced, so neither the cluster promotion nor any reconcile pass sees `tr.Changed`, and the RG's service edge is lost. [OPEN]

## Summary

In legacy `no-private-rg-election` mode, `watchVRRPEvents` never refreshes the #15258 sync-hold mirror. The preempt MASTER event that `ReleaseSyncHold` itself triggers is therefore judged against `syncHold=true`: there is no rg_active write and no services. `syncRGSyncHold` then discards the transition its own `SetSyncHold` produced, so neither the cluster promotion nor any reconcile pass sees `tr.Changed`, and the RG's service edge is lost.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A34-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the new owner of a preempt failback (or a lone node taking a dead master during the hold) serves no RG-scoped Kea DHCP until the next RG edge or commit, which is a DHCP outage on those segments. Its RG-anchored IPsec SAs are not re-initiated, and rg_active lags VIP ownership by up to one reconcile tick. Bounded to legacy mode, not the private-RG default.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the documented post-release activation runs no service edge, and nothing level-triggered repairs it.

## Mechanism

Node B (higher priority, preempt) restarts. `SetSyncHold(30s)` runs (daemon_run_bringup.go:272) and the first reconcile mirrors `syncHold=true`. Bulk sync triggers `ReleaseSyncHold` → `triggerPreemptNow`, and B's RETH instance becomes MASTER (VIPs + GARP). `watchVRRPEvents` then runs `SetVRRP(true)` against the stale mirror: desired=false, `Changed=false`, nothing runs. Next, either the cluster event or the reconcile pass runs `syncRGSyncHold`, which flips desired true and discards the transition, so `SetCluster`/`Reconcile` report `Changed=false`. rg_active is re-driven by the NeedsApply retry, but services, FRR, ip-monitoring and connected republish edge work never run.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:99-104 @d1ea69f9aa: `d.forEachRGState(func(_ int, s *rgStateMachine) { s.SetSyncHold(held) })`, which ignores the returned transition. rg_state.go:424-429 `SetSyncHold` → `reconcileLocked()` (:438-459, `changed := desired != s.active; s.active = desired`). The `syncRGSyncHold()` callers are :495 (handleClusterEvent) and :1169 (reconcileRGState) only, not `watchVRRPEvents` (:961-1045). The MASTER arm runs rg_active, `addStableRethLinkLocal` and `applyRethServicesForRG` only under `tr.Changed && tr.Active` (:991-1012). pkg/vrrp/manager.go:456-470 `releaseSyncHoldWithReason` calls `triggerPreemptNow()` on every instance. daemon_ha_sync.go:99-125 `onSessionSyncBulkReceived` triggers no daemon reconcile. Reconcile services gate: :1404-1412. The Kea converger re-drives only on `ClaimApplyRetry` (a failed attempt) (:2106-2121).

## Impact

In the documented failback, the returning owner serves no RG-scoped DHCP until something else edges the RG, so clients fail renewals and lose leases. RG-anchored IPsec tunnels wait for traffic, or stay down for `establish-tunnels immediately`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

(1) Call `syncRGSyncHold()` at the top of `watchVRRPEvents`' per-event handling, mirroring `handleClusterEvent`. (2) Propagate the mirror refresh's transitions: return them and have the callers run the edge side effects, or OR them into the reconcile pass's `tr`. A level-triggered service converger keyed on `snapshotRethMasterState` vs the last-applied services would cover this and R3-A34-04 together. Acceptance: the probe's held row shows services=true on the VRRP MASTER event, and a release-only pass with VRRP already MASTER runs `applyRethServicesForRG` once.

## Contract (where cited)

daemon_ha.go:491-495 (#15258): "refresh the sync-hold mirror before any state-machine input — … without this refresh a post-release event would stay suppressed". rg_state.go:418-423: "clearing re-derives desired … so a promotion suppressed while held activates on clear". pkg/daemon/README.md (#6535): `applyRethServicesForRG` / `clearRethServicesForRG` run only under `if tr.Changed`.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A34-03` (parts file `parts/va34.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A34-03 | Medium | In legacy no-private-rg-election mode, watchVRRPEvents never refreshes the #15258 sync-hold…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #15258/A89-02 (the mirror itself; fix e4a067242c, ancestor) is the origin. It refreshed the mirror on the cluster and reconcile paths but neither on the VRRP path nor with transition propagation. #14406, #2082 and #4084 concern hold bypass and preempt gating, not the lost edge. #6535's converger is failure-keyed (I2 asked for desired != applied), so this is also a residual of #6535. No in-run part covers it. It is related to R3-A34-04 (shared level-trigger fix), but this finding has a distinct producer.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A34-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A34-03 — Legacy RETH-VRRP mode: the #15258 sync-hold mirror swallows the post-release takeover, so `applyRethServicesForRG` (Kea RG groups, data-RG IPsec re-initiate) never runs for it
- **Finding ID:** R3-A34-03

## #16693 — R3-A52-03: `cliPolicyStats` constructs `NewPolicyCounterReader` inside the per-policy call, so the local detail view takes one full `ReadAllPolicyCounters` snapshot (m.mu, an… [OPEN]

## Summary

`cliPolicyStats` constructs `NewPolicyCounterReader` inside the per-policy call, so the local detail view takes one full `ReadAllPolicyCounters` snapshot (m.mu, an O(C) copy and index, an O(P) walk) per policy. This happens even when policy-stats is off and nothing is read. Both callers discard the returned stats-disabled count and read error, so the #8177 note and the #3408 warning that gRPC prints never appear on the console.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a quadratic performance regression on a read-only console view, plus a local/remote display divergence. Measured one-snapshot cost with the real Manager: 1.15 ms at P=C=1000 and 10.2 ms at P=C=10000 (loadavg 6.7). By linearity the detail view costs about 1.2 s and about 1m42s versus one snapshot for gRPC/hit-count; these totals are extrapolated, not timed end to end. The missing note is live under the compiler-default posture. The dropped read-failure warning is reachable only on a non-bulk/fallback dataplane, because the userspace `ReadAllPolicyCounters` never errors. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A52-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va52.md` (finding `R3-A52-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

@d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:357-382` `cliPolicyStats(...)` contains `rp := dpuserspace.NewPolicyCounterReader(c.dp, cfg, c.dp.ReadPolicyCounters)`. It is called per policy at `:476-482` and `:547-553`, each followed by `_ = sd` / `_ = rerr`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policycounters.go:288-309` `NewPolicyCounterReader` calls `provider.ReadAllPolicyCounters(cfg)` eagerly. `:206-260` takes `m.mu`, copies `m.lastStatus.PolicyRuleCounters`, builds the index and walks every zone-pair and global policy, and has no error return path. `pkg/config/show_ssot_15649.go:135-163` `PolicyDetailStats` reads only `if (statsEnabled || pol.Count) && read != nil`. It returns statsDisabled=true otherwise and prints nothing for a non-unpublished error. `cfg.Security.PolicyStatsEnabled` is a plain bool (`types_security.go:203`) that defaults to false. Introducing commit 15c8ef5ca9 (#15799) is an ancestor.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #3965/#4344 require reading the policy set "from ONE snapshot (O(P+C)) ... instead of a per-policy loop" (`pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:44-51`; `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_policies_text.go:447-455`). #8177/#7776 say the stats-disabled note's "wording is byte-identical to the three sibling renderers" (`server_show_policies_text.go:660-668`). #3408 says a counter read failure is surfaced as a warning (`:656-658`). The pkg/cli README treats console/remote divergence as a bug.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable regression reintroduces a fixed O(P·(P+C)) cliff and a console/remote divergence under the default configuration.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/cli counting-fake probes (detail vs hit-count control), my stats-off probe, and a pkg/dataplane/userspace bulk-cost probe on the real `Manager.ReadAllPolicyCounters`.

**Confidence:** High — executed for the snapshot count, the cost per snapshot and the output. Medium for the absolute end-to-end time (extrapolated from per-snapshot cost).

## Impact

On a large rule base the console detail view pins a daemon core for seconds to minutes and repeatedly takes the Manager mutex. With the default policy-stats-off posture, the console shows no statistics block and no explanatory note, while the remote `cli` on the same box explains why.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Build the reader once in `showPoliciesDetail` (only when stats are enabled or some policy has `count`), pass it into `cliPolicyStats`, accumulate `sd`/`rerr`, and print the same warning and note lines as `server_show_policies_text.go:655-668`. Acceptance: the counting-fake detail snapshot count is 1 for P=100, and 0 when stats are off with no `count` policies. The stats-off detail output contains the #8177 note and the read-fail row contains the warning.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16694 — No commit-time correlation between DHCP-server and DHCP-relay interfaces; one of the two services is silently dead on a shared interface while status reads healthy [OPEN]

## Summary

No commit-time correlation between DHCP-server and DHCP-relay interfaces; one of the two services is silently dead on a shared interface while status reads healthy

**Finding ID:** `R3-A17-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the operator authored a contradictory config. The result is one service dead on one segment, with no enforcement loss and nothing at commit to flag it. A started Kea with no sockets still passes the unit-active check [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (DHCP commit-time cross-config validation gaps) — real and bounded. It groups with commit gates that refuse DHCP configs the runtime cannot honour.

## Mechanism

commit (clean) → `dhcprelay.Manager.Apply` starts a per-interface listener on 0.0.0.0:67 bound to ge-0-0-1 → `dhcpserver.Manager` (re)starts Kea on every DHCP change, RG takeover and converger retry → whichever binds second gets EADDRINUSE. Kea continues with no sockets, or the relay supervisor fails its session → that segment is unserved by one of the configured services.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

I found no validator comparing `cfg.System.DHCPServer.*.Groups[].Interfaces` with `cfg.ForwardingOptions.DHCPRelay.Groups[].Interfaces` (grep in pkg/config and pkg/configstore). `pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:741-776` shows the relay client listener `ListenPacket("udp4", …)` with SO_REUSEADDR+SO_REUSEPORT and SO_BINDTODEVICE (`sockopt_linux.go:7,17-20`). Kea binds `<iface-addr>:67`: the fallback socket in raw mode, the service socket in udp mode.

## Impact

A leftover stanza produces a segment whose DHCP behaviour depends on start order. Clients either get no lease or are served by the wrong service. Commit shows nothing, and status reads healthy.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Add a strict commit gate that refuses a resolved kernel device appearing in both a dhcp-local-server group and a dhcp-relay group of the same family (v6: dhcpv6-local-server vs dhcp-relay dhcpv6); the tolerant path should warn. Acceptance: the probe's both-row is refused naming the interface, and the single-service rows still commit.

## Contract (where cited)

xpf docs state no coexistence contract. Commit-clean implying runtime-honoured is the #14601/#15206 doctrine. The reporter's Junos claim (commit refuses server+relay on the same interface) was not verified against juniper.net, so it is not used here and gets no parity label.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A17-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A17-03 | Low | No commit-time correlation between DHCP-server and DHCP-relay interfaces; one of the two… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`

## #16695 — The native-GRE inner classifiers' post-session DNAT, interface-NAT and local lookups cannot change any disposition. They spend verifier budget on a shim shipped OVERRIDDEN below its headroom floor, and their comments ... [OPEN]

## Summary
The native-GRE inner classifiers' post-session DNAT, interface-NAT and local lookups cannot change any disposition. They spend verifier budget on a shim shipped OVERRIDDEN below its headroom floor, and their comments misstate the steering contract.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low. No packet's fate changes. The value is verifier headroom (unmeasured) and an accurate contract in the comments. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A79-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va79.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
The shim already ships OVERRIDDEN below its floor, and the guest kernel measured thinner than the build host (#15645), so recoverable budget has value. The misleading comments invite future dependence on a steering role that does not exist.

**Contract:** The `pkg/dataplane/README.md` #1864 gate requires the tracked object to keep at least 15% verifier headroom. `pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_gate_verdict.json` @d1ea69f9aa records `"verdict": "OVERRIDDEN"`, `headroom_pct` 14.3354 and slack -6646 insns. Comments are expected to describe the mechanism that actually steers.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1175-1194` (the only healthy consumer) acts only when `inner_action == USERSPACE_SESSION_ACTION_PASS_TO_KERNEL`. `lib.rs:1976-1983` (the degraded consumer) feeds `gre_classify.rs:85-93`, which tests `inner_action.0 == USERSPACE_SESSION_ACTION_PASS_TO_KERNEL`. In `lib.rs:1533-1557` (v4), after `session_action_for_key` returns 0, the code calls `dnat_lookup_v4` (exact plus port-0 wildcard, :1561-1580), then `USERSPACE_INTERFACE_NAT_V4.get` and `USERSPACE_LOCAL_V4.get`, each `return USERSPACE_SESSION_ACTION_REDIRECT`, else `0`. `lib.rs:1686-1700` (v6) has the same shape. The only callers of `classify_native_gre_inner` are lib.rs:1175 and :1980 (grep). The comments at :1538-1556, :1582-1591 and :1679-1688 describe these lookups as keeping packets off the kernel path.

**Verification (research):** STATIC. Both consumers and both classifier bodies were read. No shimverify run was possible (no CAP_BPF).
