## #16696 — In legacy non-strict mode, rg-state desired = clusterPri || allVrrpMaster. Only the `watchVRRPEvents` and reconcile `tr.Changed` arms run `applyRethServicesForRG` / `clearRethServicesForRG`; `handleClusterEvent` makes rg-state edges but runs neither. When the cluster event is the input that flips desired, the services edge is lost and no later pass repairs it. The old owner keeps Kea RG groups and RG-anchored IPsec SAs (the #15194 terminate is skipped), and a cluster-first new owner never applies them. [OPEN]

## Summary

In legacy non-strict mode, rg-state desired = clusterPri || allVrrpMaster. Only the `watchVRRPEvents` and reconcile `tr.Changed` arms run `applyRethServicesForRG` / `clearRethServicesForRG`; `handleClusterEvent` makes rg-state edges but runs neither. When the cluster event is the input that flips desired, the services edge is lost and no later pass repairs it. The old owner keeps Kea RG groups and RG-anchored IPsec SAs (the #15194 terminate is skipped), and a cluster-first new owner never applies them.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A34-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — legacy `no-private-rg-election` mode only. The demotion shape (VRRP BACKUP before cluster demotion) is the ordinary preempt-failback order on the old owner. It skips the #15194 SA terminate and leaves Kea RG groups configured. The promotion shape skips the new owner's Kea RG config and data-RG IPsec re-initiate. RA self-heals. Whether the old owner's stale Kea answers clients is not established, nor is how often cluster-first promotion occurs in the field. [reporter: Low–Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the service edges are not driven from every rg-state edge producer, there is no converger, and both directions are reachable.

## Mechanism

In a preempt failback on old owner A, B's advert makes A's instance BACKUP: `SetVRRP(false)` with clusterPri still true leaves desired true, so nothing runs. A's cluster demotion follows: `SetCluster(false)` sets desired false and `Changed=true`, and the handler writes rg_active and resigns but runs no clear. The reconcile pass then sees `Changed=false`, so Kea keeps the RG groups and the SAs remain. In a cluster-first promotion on B, `SetCluster(true)` gives `Changed=true` and rg_active=true. `ForceRGMaster` leads to VRRP MASTER, where `SetVRRP(true)` reports `Changed=false`, so no apply, and the reconcile pass also reports `Changed=false`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

daemon_ha.go @d1ea69f9aa: the `handleClusterEvent` primary branch (:545-610) sets rg_active, removes blackholes and runs `UpdateRGPriority`/`ForceRGMaster`. The secondary branch (:614-696) runs preflight, `resignRethRG`, blackholes, rg_active and the fence. Neither calls `applyRethServicesForRG` or `clearRethServicesForRG`; the only callers are daemon_ha.go:1011/1041/1407/1409 and the direct-mode daemon_ha_vip.go:165/191. In the `watchVRRPEvents` BACKUP arm (:1015-1043), clear runs only under `tr.Changed && !tr.Active`. With the cluster still primary, `SetVRRP(false)` leaves desired true. The reconcile services gate is :1404-1412 on its own `tr.Changed`. `terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs` is at :2037 and the data-RG `reinitiateIPsecSAs` at :1887, both inside the skipped functions.

## Impact

After a legacy-mode failback, the old owner may keep a Kea config for an RG it no longer owns (a dual-DHCP risk the code itself names), and keeps RG-anchored SAs whose duplication #15194 fixed as a failback black hole. A cluster-first takeover leaves the new owner with no RG-scoped DHCP and no SA re-initiate. This persists until the next RG edge or commit.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Drive the service edges from the rg-state edge in `handleClusterEvent`'s VRRP-mode branches (on `tr.Changed`). Better, add a level-triggered per-RG service converger that compares `snapshotRethMasterState` against the last-applied service ownership every reconcile pass; that also covers R3-A34-03. Acceptance: both order rows of both probes report ran=true, and no double-apply occurs when both inputs arrive (idempotence cell).

## Contract (where cited)

`applyRethServicesForRG` doc (daemon_ha.go:1772-1775): services "must only run on the primary to avoid dual-router / dual-DHCP issues". clearRethServicesForRG/#15194 (daemon_ha.go:2026-2037): "terminate the IKE/CHILD SAs anchored on the demoted RG". The #6535 I2 contract asks for a converger with predicate desired != applied.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A34-04` (parts file `parts/va34.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A34-04 | Medium | In legacy non-strict mode, rg-state desired = clusterPri // allVrrpMaster. Only the…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #15194 (terminate on demotion, fix f7bcca0291, ancestor) and #6535 (Kea converger, failure-keyed) own the services, not the trigger. This is a residual of #6535 I2. R3-A34-03 is the sync-hold mirror producer of the same lost-edge class, with a shared fix option. I checked in-run parts va26/vf08 and worker reports a35/b03/f08: they discuss these functions' internals, not the trigger.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A34-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A34-04 — Legacy RETH-VRRP mode: `handleClusterEvent` never runs the RG service edges, so whenever the cluster input makes the rg-state edge (VRRP-first demotion of a preempt failback, or a cluster-first promotion) `apply/clearRethServicesForRG` is skipped permanently
- **Finding ID:** R3-A34-04

## #16697 — R3-A52-04: `sessionHAActive` returns known=false for unresolvable ownership, but GetSessions stamps `HaActive=false` and the wire field is a plain bool. `cmd/cli` and the… [OPEN]

## Summary

`sessionHAActive` returns known=false for unresolvable ownership, but GetSessions stamps `HaActive=false` and the wire field is a plain bool. `cmd/cli` and the console's peer-session block therefore render "Backup" for a session the console's local rows label "unknown". The #15577 commit and docs/log/15236.md claim "unknown when unresolvable" in CLI, gRPC and REST.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a display-only HA mislabel used in failover triage. It re-creates, on two of three renderers, the guessed label #15236 was written to remove. In a cluster with no RETH (private-RG / no-reth posture), every session is "unknown" and the remote CLI shows all of them as "Backup". No ownership or forwarding effect. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A52-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va52.md` (finding `R3-A52-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

@d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:257-261` (and :319-323, :946-950, :979-983) `if active, known := s.sessionHAActive(...); known { se.HaActive = active } else if s.cluster != nil { se.HaActive = false }`. `proto/xpf/v1/*.proto:594` `bool ha_active = 29;` has no state or known field. `cmd/cli/show_flow.go:292-297` `if se.HaActive { "Active" } else { "Backup" }`. `pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:770-772` `peerHAState := "Backup"` / `if se.HaActive { "Active" }`. `pkg/api/sessions.go:1675-1685` maps `state == "unknown"` to false. `pkg/config/reth_rg_owner.go:118-125` returns "unknown" when cfg has no RETH owners. No grpcapi test asserts HaActive.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** 2b08ebffb0 (#15236/#15577, an ancestor) says "config.SessionHAState derives owning data RG ... (unknown when unresolvable); wired in CLI, gRPC and REST". `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:132-134` says "ok=false means ownership is unknown and the caller must not stamp a guessed Active/Backup onto the entry". `pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:278-281` says "Unresolvable ownership renders "unknown" instead of an inverted Active/Backup".

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (session display HA labelling, residual of #15236) — real and display-only. It belongs with the round-2 A52-03 group.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/grpcapi probe driving `GetSessions` with and without a cluster manager. The `cmd/cli` and console peer-block rendering is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High — executed through the real `Server.GetSessions` legacy path. The renderer branch is a two-line read.

## Impact

During failover triage a remote operator, or the console's peer block, sees sessions labelled "Backup" whose ownership is actually unknown. On a no-RETH cluster that is every session, which suggests the node owns nothing. The console's local rows say "unknown", so the surfaces contradict each other.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Add an additive tri-state to `SessionEntry` (for example `string ha_state` or `bool ha_state_known`), set it from `sessionHAActive`'s known bit in all four stamping sites and in REST, and render "unknown" in `cmd/cli/show_flow.go` and the console peer block when it is unknown. Acceptance: the probe's cluster row renders "unknown" on all three renderers, and Active/Backup rows are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A52-04`, part `parts/va52.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16698 — `ClassifyLoadContent` sends the whole body to flat replay if any uncommented line is a flat-verb line. The box renders an unquoted `change-configuration commands` entry as `set system host-name pwned;` on its own line, so `load override` an [OPEN]

## Summary
`ClassifyLoadContent` sends the whole body to flat replay if any uncommented line is a flat-verb line. The box renders an unquoted `change-configuration commands` entry as `set system host-name pwned;` on its own line, so `load override` and `load merge` of its own `show` output fail with `line 1: is not a set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate command`.

**Finding ID:** R3-VA01-S1
**Severity (source):** Low — Low. The failure is loud and fail-closed. HA SyncApply, rollback and DB reload parse hierarchically and are unaffected. It does break `show`-to-`load` restore for any config that holds a hierarchically authored unquoted event command, which the compiler accepts and the event engine applies.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
`show configuration > file` followed by `load override file` is the ordinary backup and restore workflow. With such a policy present, the restore fails with an error that points at line 1 rather than at the event command.

**Contract:** The #7527 comment in `LoadOverrideAsPlantClass` (store_command.go:466-490) says misclassification "fails loud" and that `show`-style files reload. The pkg/config README Node-modifier section says the box's output round-trips through reload.

**Trace:** A hierarchically authored `commands { set ...; }` is stored with no quote provenance. `ShowCandidate` or `Format` prints it bare at line start. `ClassifyLoadContent` then sets `flat=true`, and flat replay rejects `system {` on line 1.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go:193-198` loops over lines and sets `flat = true` on the first `IsFlatLoadLine(strings.TrimSpace(line))`. No brace-depth or hierarchical-context check exists. `QuotedKeyPath` re-quotes only authored quotes (`keyNeedsAuthoredQuote`), so a hierarchically authored bare command renders bare.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/va01/probes/zz_va01_classify_test.go` (`TestVA01ShowRoundTripEventCmd`). In the unquoted case, `show` prints `                        set system host-name pwned;` and reloading that output gives `override=line 1: is not a set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate command` and `merge=` the same error. The quoted twin (`"set system host-name pwned";`) gives `override=<nil> merge=<nil>`. The same rule forced my R3-A01-04 probe to keep the command on the `commands {` line.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Classify as hierarchical when the uncommented body has brace structure, for example a flat-verb line found at brace depth greater than 0, or when the first non-blank line is not a flat verb. As an alternative, make `Format` quote a value whose first token is a flat verb. The acceptance criterion is that the probe's unquoted case reloads through both paths and that the #7527 and #10305 classifier tests stay green.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (va01.md)</summary>

### R3-VA01-S1 — Load classification routes a hierarchical file to flat replay if any line starts with a flat verb, so the box's own `show` output of an unquoted event-options command cannot be reloaded
- **Finding ID:** R3-VA01-S1
- **Title:** `ClassifyLoadContent` sends the whole body to flat replay if any uncommented line is a flat-verb line. The box renders an unquoted `change-configuration commands` entry as `set system host-name pwned;` on its own line, so `load override` and `load merge` of its own `show` output fail with `line 1: is not a set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate command`.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; found by verifier va01 while sample-checking worker a01's refuted hypothesis "Load classifier vs lexer comment desync"; model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by va01
- **Severity:** Low. The failure is loud and fail-closed. HA SyncApply, rollback and DB reload parse hierarchically and are unaffected. It does break `show`-to-`load` restore for any config that holds a hierarchically authored unquoted event command, which the compiler accepts and the event engine applies.
- **Confidence:** High. The classifier rule is read, and the probe has a quoted twin.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED. Store-level `LoadOverride`, `ShowCandidate`, `LoadOverride` and `LoadMerge`.
- **Gate verdict:** COHORT (load and restore round trip of the box's own output: R3-A01-02, R3-A01-03, R3-VA01-S1). The round-trip contract fails on the box's own output, with a bounded, fail-loud consequence.
- **Contract:** The #7527 comment in `LoadOverrideAsPlantClass` (store_command.go:466-490) says misclassification "fails loud" and that `show`-style files reload. The pkg/config README Node-modifier section says the box's output round-trips through reload.
- **Adversarial analysis:** No adversary is required. This is a reliability defect. The challenged assumption is that only flat files contain lines starting with `set` or `delete`. A hierarchical value can legitimately start with such a token. Event-options commands are the in-tree case, and the box itself renders it unquoted.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go:193-198` loops over lines and sets `flat = true` on the first `IsFlatLoadLine(strings.TrimSpace(line))`. No brace-depth or hierarchical-context check exists. `QuotedKeyPath` re-quotes only authored quotes (`keyNeedsAuthoredQuote`), so a hierarchically authored bare command renders bare.
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/va01/probes/zz_va01_classify_test.go` (`TestVA01ShowRoundTripEventCmd`). In the unquoted case, `show` prints `                        set system host-name pwned;` and reloading that output gives `override=line 1: is not a set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate command` and `merge=` the same error. The quoted twin (`"set system host-name pwned";`) gives `override=<nil> merge=<nil>`. The same rule forced my R3-A01-04 probe to keep the command on the `commands {` line.
- **Trace:** A hierarchically authored `commands { set ...; }` is stored with no quote provenance. `ShowCandidate` or `Format` prints it bare at line start. `ClassifyLoadContent` then sets `flat=true`, and flat replay rejects `system {` on line 1.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked whether the compiler rejects the unquoted hierarchical form. It does not: R3-A01-04's probe compiles it to one command. I checked whether `Format` quotes values beginning with a flat verb. It does not. I checked whether the worker's NEG (no authorization bypass) still stands. It does: both the gate and the store re-lex, so this is a fidelity defect only. I found no owner in gh-issues.tsv, #14145, prior headings or in-run parts.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Not applicable. This is a control-plane load classifier.

## #16699 — The capture generation is bounded to 32 route-based VPNs (`ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels`), but no commit-time limit exists. A 33rd VPN commits cleanly, `stageIpsecCapture` discards the bound error and returns a QuarantineAll(QUEUE_OPEN) runtime with a nil error, and `commitIpsecCaptureStage` installs it. All non-loopback, non-lifeline kernel INPUT/FORWARD is then dropped on every apply until the config changes (residual of #15068). [OPEN]

## Summary

The capture generation is bounded to 32 route-based VPNs (`ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels`), but no commit-time limit exists. A 33rd VPN commits cleanly, `stageIpsecCapture` discards the bound error and returns a QuarantineAll(QUEUE_OPEN) runtime with a nil error, and `commitIpsecCaptureStage` installs it. All non-loopback, non-lifeline kernel INPUT/FORWARD is then dropped on every apply until the config changes (residual of #15068).

**Finding ID:** `R3-A35-01`
**Severity (source report):** High — an authenticated commit that strict validation accepts causes a persistent, box-wide fail-closed outage of host-bound and kernel-forwarded traffic. Every IKE exchange (so all VPNs, not only the 33rd), BGP/OSPF/BFD on data ports and host services on data addresses are dropped, and the commit and every later apply report success. Demonstrated at component level (compile, stage, install spec); the on-wire effect is inferred from the rendered quarantine rules. AF_XDP transit over static routes does not traverse netfilter and is not directly hit (inference). Management survives on lo and the #14696 lifeline netdevs. [reporter: High]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the trigger is a reachable, strict-valid config; the consequence is a box-wide outage with a false-success commit; it survives refutation and dedup.

## Mechanism

`set security ipsec vpn vNN bind-interface st0.NN` ×33 (+ IKE gateway/policy) → configstore strict Commit OK → `applyConfigLocked` → `stageIpsecCapture` (`buildIpsecCaptureQueuePlan`: 132 keys) → the 129th handle hits the per-generation bound → staged QuarantineAll(QUEUE_OPEN), err nil → `commitIpsecCaptureStage` installs the `xpf_ipsec_quarantine*` tables (inet+bridge input/forward DROP) → commit reported successful → each later apply re-stages the same quarantine.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at @d1ea69f9aa.

## Impact

A hub with 33 or more spokes is an ordinary deployment. The operator sees a clean commit while all IKE, routing protocols and host services on data ports drop. HA config sync carries the same config to the peer, so failover does not help. It persists across reboots and applies until VPNs are removed via fxp0/console.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Reject at strict commit and commit-check, and warn on the lenient load/peer-sync path, when the route-based VPN (distinct capture tunnel) count exceeds `ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels`, naming the limit (mirror #10638). Alternatively raise the capacity. Independently, make a QUEUE_OPEN stage return a non-nil error so a runtime over-cap fails the commit visibly, and document the limit. Consumers: pkg/config compiler, pkg/daemon stage, docs. Acceptance: strict Commit of the 33-VPN fixture fails with a message naming the limit; the 32-VPN control commits and stages without quarantine; the lenient path warns and still boots.

## Contract (where cited)

The repo already hard-rejects at strict commit a config whose consequence is exactly "every apply installs a box-wide capture quarantine dropping all non-loopback traffic". See #10638, `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_bindiface.go:226-244` (strict rejects, lenient warns to keep #1960 boot). #15068's fix direction (r2 A35-03, `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md:3774`) also required "add a commit-time limit equal to the real supported count". No README or docs state a 32-VPN limit.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A35-01` (parts file `parts/va35.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A35-01 | High | The capture generation is bounded to 32 route-based VPNs (ipsecCaptureMaxTunnels), but no…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): This is a residual of #15068 (CLOSED, fix c8231163dc, `merge-base --is-ancestor` = yes). The fix's predicate (allocator sized for two generations, a per-generation bound) covers the 17-32 add/rezone shape. It omits the commit-time limit its own fix direction required, and its log acknowledges the over-32 quarantine. I searched gh-issues.tsv (capture/quarantine/QUEUE_OPEN/route-based), prior-r2-002, prior-headings, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports and RUN drafts/parts and workers: no owner for over-32 commit acceptance. va24 notes "supported route-based count is 32 per capture generation" only as a reachability bound. Distinct from #10638 (no-bind shape), gemini H17-02 (shared bind) and R3-F01-01 (lifeline on fallback guards).
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A35-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16700 — HA sweep resends wipe the per-application inactivity-timeout (incl. `never`) and per-policy `then log` flags on the standby: the helper publishes `app_timeout: 0` / `log_flags: 0` to the conntrack mirror, and unlike policy identity (#14359) these… [OPEN]

## Summary

HA sweep resends wipe the per-application inactivity-timeout (incl. `never`) and per-policy `then log` flags on the standby: the helper publishes `app_timeout: 0` / `log_flags: 0` to the conntrack mirror, and unlike policy identity (#14359) these fields have no send/receive memo

**Finding ID:** `R3-A18-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — HA corruption of an enforcement dimension, session lifetime. After failover, a session admitted by an app with a short `inactivity-timeout` keeps its permit for the global window (TCP established 1800 s, #15127). A session admitted by an `inactivity-timeout never` app (#15207) is reaped on …
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable trigger (every HA pair with per-app timeouts or `then log`; the sweep runs every 15 s in userspace mode), a concrete lifetime and audit consequence, and no existing owner

## Mechanism

`applications application A inactivity-timeout 30` → policy snapshot `InactivityTimeout` (`capabilities.go:523`) → helper install with `inactivity_timeout_ns=Some(30s)` → Open delta (`app_timeout=30`) → `daemon_ha_userspace_convert.go:680` `val.AppTimeout = delta.AppTimeout` → peer installs with 30 → ≤15 s later the sweep reads the mirror row (`app_timeout 0`, `log_flags 0`), stamps a newer generation and restores policy identity only → the peer's generation guard accepts it → `req.InactivityTimeout=0` → the helper replaces the entry with `None` → global window. A promoted standby's own mirror resends also carry 0, so the error is sticky across failback

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

Observed @d1ea69f9aa: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bpf_map/publish_conntrack.rs:262` `app_timeout: 0,` and `:301` `log_flags: 0,` (v6 `:509`, `:531`). The only non-zero producer is the delta record (`afxdp/session_delta.rs:439` `app_timeout: inactivity_timeout_secs`). The userspace store wraps the legacy adapter (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager.go:1057-1061`), so `GetV4` is a BPF lookup (`pkg/dataplane/maps_session.go:92-104`). The sweep is `s.sessions.ForEachV4` → `stampSweepV4` (re-reads `s.sessions.GetV4`, then `stampInstallGenV4`) → `encodeSessionV4` (`pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go:89-106,276-310`). The profile is `return true, 15 * time.Second, 60 * time.Second` (`manager.go:1150`). The send stamp ends with `// #14359: policy identity is sync-only; restore last sent / received.` and has no AppTimeout/LogFlags memo (`sync_conn_gen.go:946-1000`). The receive side restores install table, SNAT ICMP and policy identity, then calls `s.sessions.PutClusterSyncedV4(key, val)` (`:1777-1799`). `req.InactivityTimeout = view.val4.AppTimeout` (`manager_sessionsync_request.go:376`, v6 `:424`). `req.LogSessionInit/Close = view.logFlags()&...` (`:352-356`). Rust: `if req.inactivity_timeout != 0 { Some(..) } else { None }` (`session_sync.rs:562-567`), then `self.remove_entry(&key, RemovalKind::Replace)` (`session/install.rs:950`), and `expires_after_ns` is computed from `metadata.inactivity_timeout_ns` (`:1046-1055`). Inference: the standby's entry ages on the global window from the first sweep after install

## Impact

Every HA deployment using per-app idle timeouts or `then log session-close`. The blast radius is all such sessions on the standby within 15 s of creation, and it is silent: no counter and no warning. After failover, short-timeout services keep stale permits about 60× longer, `never` services drop long-idle connections at 1800 s, and session-close audit records vanish. Recovery: none until the session closes, or a new delta for a close-class change

## Acceptance / fix direction

Publish the real `app_timeout` (seconds, with the 86401 `never` sentinel) and `log_flags` in `publish_conntrack.rs` v4/v6 from the session metadata. Or extend the #14359 memo family (send and receive, keyed by SessionID) to AppTimeout and LogFlags. Consumers: sweep, storeBulkWalk, and promoted-standby resends. Acceptance: the v4/v6 cells above pass; a stamp-less resend does not clear a recorded value; a new incarnation (new SessionID) does not inherit it; `never` round-trips as 86401

## Contract (where cited)

#3227/#3301 put the per-application idle timeout on the HA wire so that "a short-timeout app session therefore ages out on the app's value after failover" (`userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/session_sync.rs:556-561`). #2785 carries the `then log` selection "so the synced session logs the same RT_FLOW records after failover" (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_sessionsync_request.go:353-356`). The #14359 doctrine says a sync-only field that the BPF mirror cannot supply must be memo-restored on mirror-sourced resends (`pkg/cluster/sync_policy_identity_14359.go`). `docs/log/15207.md` says HA sync preserves the `never` sentinel

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A18-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A18-01 | Medium | HA sweep resends wipe the per-application inactivity-timeout (incl. never) and per-policy… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch02:7: - **R3-A18-01 — MATERIAL.** D: the userspace mirror initializes `app_timeout`/`log_flags` to zero for both families (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bpf_map/publish_conntrack.rs:262,301,509,531`); `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go:89-123,276-310` re-reads that mirror and stamps a new install generation. The send/receive memo in `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_gen.go:815-841,962-1018` restores **policy identity**, not these two fields. The standby can lose the application's timeout (including never) and the policy log selection on a subsequent eligible mirror sweep. R: this is not every 15-second sweep of every existing flow: only `Created >= threshold` rows are considered (`sync_conn_sweep.go:95-100,263-287`); cold table-truth bulk and a later incremental update may provide correct values until such a resend. The packet's v4/v6 component probes at the old revision support overwrite, not an observed failover. **Check:** a current-revision creation→delta→eligible sweep→standby install cell, then observe actual failover expiry/logging; don't infer a policy bypass.

**SMR:** smr batch02 L14: | R3-A18-01 HA sweep wipes app_timeout/log_flags | **MATERIAL** | Mirror is the only sweep source and hard-codes 0; no memo for these two fields unlike #14359 policy identity; generation guard accepts fresher sweep stamp → standby loses `never`/short timeout + close-logging within 15 s, sticky across failback. | Mirror publication could be intentional projection if some other path re-derives timeout on promote — none found in claim census; [INFERENCE] standby revalidation might re-derive from policy — refutation (e) says it only stamps gen. | `publish_conntrack.rs:262,301,509,531` still `app_timeout: 0 / log_flags: 0` at 8c61ac5770 (v4 245/284 at dirty HEAD); no AppTimeout/LogFlags memo in `sync_policy_identity_14359.go`/`sync_conn_sweep.go` (grep empty). | Lab failover `show sessions` + RT_FLOW close after sweep; Rust synced-install replace-from-None re-read at 8c61. | | R3-A18-03 modeled ALG sub-statements rejected | **COHORT** | Closed-world `disable`-only children for dns/ftp/sip/tftp/pptp reject Junos-valid `doctoring none` etc. at commit in both AST shapes, while unmodeled classes pass with advisory — inverted parity, fail-visible. | Only `dns doctoring/maximum-message-length` externally verified; other five rest on reporter SRX syntax; could be deliberate typo-guard (#12833) if product intends disable-only — but then advisory path should exist per #4232 doctrine. | `schema_security.go:1422` pptp still `{"disable":…}` only; dns/ftp/sip same shape at :1079-1082 (dirty HE

**Wonder:** wonder batch02 L27: ### R3-A18-01 — HA sweep wipes per-app inactivity-timeout + `then log` flags — **MATERIAL** - Defect case: mirror publisher hard-codes the two fields the BPF mirror cannot carry; the 15 s sweep re-stamps them with a fresh generation; the receiver replaces the entry, losing the app timeout (incl. the 86401 `never` sentinel) and the log selection. Unlike policy identity (#14359) there is no send/receive memo for AppTimeout/LogFlags. - Strongest refutation: generation guard / revalidation re-derives the timeout — refuted in-part: the sweep draws a *newer* generation so the guard accepts, and policy revalidation only stamps a generation, never re-derives `inactivity_timeout_ns`. - Decisive evidence @8c61ac5770: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bpf_map/publish_conntrack.rs:262` `app_timeout: 0,`, `:301` `log_flags: 0,` (v6 `:509`/`:531`) — identical literals at the tip; only non-ze…

## #16701 — `cmd/shimverify` applies the 15% headroom floor to the processed-insn count measured on the build host (7.2.8). The provenance in `userspace_xdp_gate_verdict.json` records toolchain, linker and codegen env, but no ker... [OPEN]

## Summary
`cmd/shimverify` applies the 15% headroom floor to the processed-insn count measured on the build host (7.2.8). The provenance in `userspace_xdp_gate_verdict.json` records toolchain, linker and codegen env, but no kernel release. `pkg/dataplane/README.md` still headlines "Processed-insn counts did NOT vary by kernel" and says there is "No evidence either way for a wider version gap". Repo records since then show the loss-cluster guest kernels (7.0.0 and 7.0.0-rc7+) charging the same object 3.8–6.1% more. The recorded 14.34% headroom is therefore roughly 9% on the deployment kernel. Twice, a passing or overridden verdict on the host hid a REJECT on the guest until the deploy pre-flight refused it.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — there is no outage path. The guest-side `xpfd verify-dataplane` pre-flight and the bake's in-guest gate catch an outright REJECT and fail closed by blocking the deploy. What is lost is the floor's purpose: an early warning, on the kernel that actually loads the object, before the next roughly 87k-insn structural change. That loss has recurred: #15645 and #15854 each blocked the lab deploy of master. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A80-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va80.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
The next shim edit is planned against a host figure that overstates guest headroom by about 5 points. The floor that is meant to warn first did not warn either time. Each time the result was a blocked deploy followed by an emergency shim restructure (#15645, #15854).

**Contract:** `pkg/dataplane/README.md:551-562`: "**Processed-insn counts did NOT vary by kernel, measured (#6884).** ... No evidence either way for a wider version gap (6.x vs 7.x); the measurement above bounds only 7.0.0-rc7 → 7.0.13". `UserspaceShimMinVerifierHeadroomPct = 15.0` (`verify_userspace_shim.go:98`), whose #6884 purpose is to fire before the next structural change.

- #15645 lab-acceptance comment, re-read via `gh issue view 15645 --comments`: "merged object `d2b6b59b`: LOADS on both guests — 977241 processed insns, 2.28% headroom ... guest headroom (2.28%) is thinner than the build-host figure (7.93%) recorded in the gate verdict — worth watching". ## #16702 — R3-A53-01: `top exit`/`up N exit` restore the pre-exit edit cursor after config mode is released; the remote CLI's next `configure` prints `[edit]` but prefixes later commands… [OPEN]

## Summary

`top exit`/`up N exit` restore the pre-exit edit cursor after config mode is released; the remote CLI's next `configure` prints `[edit]` but prefixes later commands with the stale cursor (console: config `#` prompt left in operational mode)

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — the trigger is an operator typing shape. A misplaced statement only commits when it is also valid under the stale cursor (for example under `routing-instances RI1` or `groups G`), and `show | compare` before commit exposes it. There is no authz effect, because the server gates the wire path it executes. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A53-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va53.md` (finding `R3-A53-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

cmd/cli/shared.go:717-719 `c.editPath = append([]string{}, target...)` / `err := c.dispatchConfig(innerLine)` / `c.editPath = saved`, unconditional. :511-513: the inner top-level exit runs `c.configMode.Store(false)` / `c.editPath = nil`, which is then overwritten. :200-215: remote `configure` never touches editPath. Local twin pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:710-715 restores `SetEditPath(saved)` and the config prompt after exitConfigureTop; local re-entry is safe because EnterConfigureSession sets `s.editPath = nil` (pkg/configstore/store_lock.go:203).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** Junos `configure` starts at `[edit]`, and the CLI prints `[edit]` as that promise (cmd/cli/shared.go:214). #15082 restores the cursor after a top/up-prefixed command, which is correct only while still in configuration mode.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (CLI config-mode navigation/session state) — real client-state bug with bounded consequence.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — cmd/cli dispatch with a recording gRPC fake; the local prompt half is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High — executed with a positive control.

## Impact

An operator told `[edit]` may commit a root change into a VRF or group body, and the intended change is absent. Recovery is to notice it in compare or show.

## Acceptance / fix direction

in both dispatchTopUp15082 copies, restore cursor and prompt only if still in config mode (`c.configMode.Load()` / `c.configOwned`). Separately, make remote `configure` set `c.editPath = nil`. Acceptance: the probe's DEFECT arm sends the root path, and both CLIs show the operational prompt after `top exit`.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A53-01`, part `parts/va53.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16703 — The #14696 fix emits `meta sdifname {lifelines} accept` on the bridge-family quarantine input chain. Kernel nf_tables rejects that with EOPNOTSUPP, so no lifeline-carrying QuarantineAll (that is, every plan-level quarantine) can be installe [OPEN]

## Summary
The #14696 fix emits `meta sdifname {lifelines} accept` on the bridge-family quarantine input chain. Kernel nf_tables rejects that with EOPNOTSUPP, so no lifeline-carrying QuarantineAll (that is, every plan-level quarantine) can be installed. On an existing divert, the failed transition orphans the old divert onto stopped NFQUEUE listeners.

**Finding ID:** R3-VF01-S1
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium (potential High). Demonstrated: the D1b deny-first quarantine contract cannot be established for any quarantine reason (link-lookup, if_id-underivable, queue-open including queue exhaustion, owner-contested, domain-overlap). On a box with a working divert, the failed guarded transition stops the old capture actor while its divert table stays in the kernel with no bypass flag, so all existing route-based VPN traffic is dropped for as long as the quarantine reason persists. Every apply reports an IPsec error, so the failure is not silent. Potential: on a box with no prior divert, nothing fences the capture-unknown state; whether uncaptured st0 traffic can then be forwarded is not verified.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Any IPsec deployment that hits a quarantine reason after the #14696 fix loses either the deny-first fence (fresh box) or all existing tunnels (box with a running divert), and every commit fails until the reason is cleared. Recovery requires removing the quarantine cause. It also changes the real-kernel consequence of other quarantine findings in this run (R3-A35-01 assumes this guard installs).

**Contract:** #9506 D1b: when capture posture is unknown, a verified two-family QuarantineAll DROP guard is installed (`docs/log/9506.md:239`). #14696 (`docs/log/14696.md`) claims "emit iifname+sdifname ACCEPT only on `input`" for that guard, and its log records GREEN only from render-level cells. Daemon comment `ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1694`: "The guarded installer retains its deny authority on every post-ACK failure."
**Trace:** config yields a quarantine reason → `stageIpsecCapture` plan `addQuarantine` + `finalize` stamps lifelines → `commitIpsecCaptureStage` → `InstallIpsecDivert` (old==nil) or `InstallIpsecDivertWithDrain` (old!=nil) → `installIpsecQuarantineTableAtomic` → bridge input chain gets `meta sdifname` → kernel EOPNOTSUPP → atomic flush rejected, nothing installed → daemon rolls back (old==nil) or retires old with a live old divert table (old!=nil) → apply returns an IPsec error. With an unchanged config, the next apply restages the same quarantine and fails again.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert.go:699-701` `if hook == "input" && len(spec.LifelineNetdevs) > 0 { p.rule().iifname(...); p.rule().sdifname(spec.LifelineNetdevs)... }`. The function is called for both families from `installIpsecQuarantineTableAtomic` `:771-772` (`{gnft.TableFamilyINet,...}, {gnft.TableFamilyBridge, "bridge", ...}`), with one atomic `c.Flush()` at `:798`. `pkg/daemon/ipsec_capture_wiring_9506.go:1027-1028` stamps `LifelineNetdevs = HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs(p.cfg)` (always contains fxp0) on every QuarantineAll plan. Guarded path: `:1690-1702` closes old (`_ = old.close()`), marks orphaned and restores nil. `:875-876` divert queue rules have "No bypass flag ... intentional". Kernel `net/netfilter/nft_meta.c`: `case NFT_META_SDIF: case NFT_META_SDIFNAME: return nft_meta_get_validate_sdif(ctx);` → `default: return -EOPNOTSUPP;` for non-ipv4/ipv6/inet families.
**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf01/probes/zz_vf01_sdif_bridge_test.go`, run as `go test -c` then `unshare -Urn nft.test -test.run TestVF01SdifnameFamilyMatrix`. Output `vf01-s1-sdif-matrix.out`: inet iifname/sdifname and bridge iifname return nil, and "family=bridge iifname=false sdifname=true -> flush err=conn.Receive: netlink receive: operation not supported". Daemon probe `zz_vf01_quarantine_kernel_test.go` (output `vf01-s1-daemon-kernel.out`). First, with a LinkLookup plan quarantine and cfg present: "lifelines=[fxp0] QuarantineAll=true -> commit err=ipsec capture: install divert: quarantine guard install: nftables flush xpf_ipsec_quarantine_guard: ... operation not supported" and "kernel tables after commit: []". Positive control, the identical plan without cfg (no lifelines): "commit err=<nil>", tables [xpf_ipsec_divert xpf_ipsec_divert]. Second, on the guarded path (seeded normal generation, then an OwnerContested quarantine): "guarded divert transition: quarantine guard install: ... operation not supported", then "tables=[xpf_ipsec_divert xpf_ipsec_divert] active-runtime=<nil> orphaned=true oldActorActive=false". Limits: no packets were sent, so the drop of queued tunnel traffic is inferred from the no-bypass queue rules and the stopped listener.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Emit the `sdifname` lifeline rule only in inet-family chains. The bridge family can use iifname only, or no lifeline, since bridge input is not host management. Add a kernel-netns cell that installs QuarantineAll with lifelines through `InstallIpsecQuarantineGuard`, `InstallIpsecDivert` and `InstallIpsecDivertWithDrain`. Make the daemon's guarded-failure path re-verify that a guard table actually exists before retiring the old actor. Acceptance: the daemon probe's lifeline cell commits with err=nil and the guard input chain shows fxp0 iif/sdif accepts in inet; the no-lifeline control is unchanged.

## #16705 — The only runtime enforcement of api-auth `expires` between AuthConfig rebuilds is two terms: the Basic check at pkg/api/auth.go:383 and the API-key/Bearer check at :435. Deleting either term leaves the whole pkg/api s... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-24)

## Summary
The only runtime enforcement of api-auth `expires` between AuthConfig rebuilds is two terms: the Basic check at pkg/api/auth.go:383 and the API-key/Bearer check at :435. Deleting either term leaves the whole pkg/api suite at the same 887/33 result with an identical failing set. The one cell that asserts an expired credential is refused (#13241) uses a test-supplied resolver that reimplements the expiry check.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — this is an assurance gap on an authentication property. The production code is correct at HEAD. If the regression happened, an expired Basic user or API key (up to super-user class) would keep authenticating until the next AuthConfig rebuild (a commit or restart). That reopens part of #10826's remedy, so it is potential, not demonstrated. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A83-07`
**Source part:** `parts/va83.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
This is the "a cell with the right name that cannot detect its defect" class on an authentication remedy. Every cell stays green if expiry is dropped.

**Contract:** pkg/api/README.md:605 "Every identity needs a UTC `expires YYYY-MM-DD` date" and :729 "an unexpired matched credential". #10826 (CLOSED, 5c7c57c54f) added the expiry and claims "RED-on-revert".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
auth.go:383 `if !exists || expected == "" || !credentialExpiryActive(cfg.UserExpires[user]) || !passMatch {`, :404 `credentialExpiryActive`, :435 `if !equal || !credentialExpiryActive(cfg.APIKeyExpires[key]) {`. authz_13241_test.go:33-42 installs `credentialResolver` with its own `credentialExpiryActive(expiry)` check, and :84-89 asserts "expired credential was accepted" against that closure. credentialExpiryActive is referenced only in auth.go and that test. pkg/daemon/daemon_run_servers.go:443-447 filters expired entries only at build (`now.Before(expires)`).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — I ran whole-package `go test ./pkg/api/ -json` for HEAD, MUT-B and MUT-K, compared the results by test name, and ran the probe under HEAD and both mutants.

## #16706 — AB-BA lock inversion between HTTPS leg rebuild (lifeMu → tlsCertificateMu) and the TLS monitor's leg recovery (tlsCertificateMu → lifeMu) can permanently wedge the config-apply path [OPEN]

## Summary
AB-BA lock inversion between HTTPS leg rebuild (lifeMu → tlsCertificateMu) and the TLS monitor's leg recovery (tlsCertificateMu → lifeMu) can permanently wedge the config-apply path

**Finding ID:** R3-N10-02
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — when it fires, the outcome is a permanent deadlock: the management reconcile runs inside applyConfigLocked, so every later commit/apply blocks, and xpfd must be restarted. But it needs an hourly monitor tick that actually reinstalls a certificate to overlap, within that tick's millisecond critical section, a concurrent apply that rebuilds an HTTPS leg. That is too narrow to rate the impact higher.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A rare coincidence permanently freezes configuration apply (CLI/REST/gRPC commits, HA peer config sync, DHCP-driven reapply), and the only recovery is a daemon restart, which itself waits on the systemd stop timeout. The exposure rises on boxes whose custom certificate is rotated on disk while management addresses change (e.g. DHCP fxp0).

**Contract:** `pkg/api/tls_certificate_10827.go:603-607` documents recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked as "the only place that nests lifeMu inside tlsCertificateMu". Correctness requires one canonical lock order. Commits must not hang (engineering-style: no unbounded blocking on the apply path).
**Trace:** commit / peer-sync apply / DHCP mgmt-address change → `reconcileWebManagement` → `managementReconciler.reconcileTo` (`management.go:723-724`, which calls ReconcileHTTPSAddrs on a TLS/address/degraded change or whenever `!HTTPSServing()`) → lifeMu → new leg → `buildHTTPSServer` waits on tlsCertificateMu. Concurrently, the hourly monitor tick, when a certificate is (re)installed (custom pair rotated or repaired on disk, generated cert expired, or recovery from the #15667 boot-failure state), holds tlsCertificateMu during keygen or load → `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` waits on lifeMu.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
Order A: `pkg/api/listener.go:672` `s.lifeMu.Lock()` in `ReconcileHTTPSAddrs` → `reconcileLegsLocked` → `listener.go:796` `s.planHTTPSLeg(addr)` → `pkg/api/server.go:1527` `s.tlsCertificateMu.Lock()` in `buildHTTPSServer`. Order B: `tls_certificate_10827.go:522` `s.tlsCertificateMu.Lock()` in `refreshManagementTLSCertificate` → `refreshManagementTLSCertificateLocked` → install/publish → `:580` / `:785` `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` → `:618` `s.lifeMu.Lock()`. The recovery takes lifeMu BEFORE it checks whether any leg is serving. `ReconcileTLSCertificate` (`:701-702`) takes the same B path, but on the apply goroutine. A lock census of non-test pkg/api finds no other lock serializing the two paths. The B path is gated: the valid steady state returns early (`:540-542` generated cert still valid; `:779-781` same custom fingerprint). Inference from the `management.go:1213` contract comment: management reconcile runs under applyConfigLocked.
**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestN10TLSLockOrderInversion -count=1 -v`, with `RUN/verify/vn10/probes/zz_n10_lockorder_probe_test.go` (the worker's probe, re-run unchanged). Output is in `RUN/verify/vn10/lockorder_rerun.out`. The positive control (same two operations run sequentially) gives `interleave=false both completed (no deadlock)`. The interleaved run gives `interleave=true DEADLOCK: monitor-refresh done=false reconcile done=false after 3s`, with one goroutine in `sync.Mutex.Lock` at `tls_certificate_10827.go:618` and one at `server.go:1527` ← `listener.go:796`. Limits: the seams widen the windows to make the race deterministic, so the probe shows the inversion, not its natural frequency.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Make one order canonical. For example, return a "recover needed" flag from the refresh and run `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` after releasing tlsCertificateMu. Alternatively, load the certificate state before taking lifeMu in `ReconcileHTTPSAddrs`, so `buildHTTPSServer` never takes tlsCertificateMu under lifeMu. Correct the `:603-607` comment. Acceptance: the probe's interleaved case completes, and a test pins that no code path holds lifeMu when acquiring tlsCertificateMu.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn10.md)</summary>

### R3-N10-02 — AB-BA lock inversion between HTTPS leg rebuild (lifeMu → tlsCertificateMu) and the TLS monitor's leg recovery (tlsCertificateMu → lifeMu) can permanently wedge the config-apply path
- **Finding ID:** R3-N10-02
- **Title:** AB-BA lock inversion between HTTPS leg rebuild (lifeMu → tlsCertificateMu) and the TLS monitor's leg recovery (tlsCertificateMu → lifeMu) can permanently wedge the config-apply path
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker n10 (A8 API-delta engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vn10
- **Severity:** Low — when it fires, the outcome is a permanent deadlock: the management reconcile runs inside applyConfigLocked, so every later commit/apply blocks, and xpfd must be restarted. But it needs an hourly monitor tick that actually reinstalls a certificate to overlap, within that tick's millisecond critical section, a concurrent apply that rebuilds an HTTPS leg. That is too narrow to rate the impact higher.
- **Confidence:** High that the inversion exists and deadlocks (stacks captured). Low on production frequency.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — component test using real `NewServer`+`Start` with TLS. The interleaving is forced only through the existing `ListenFunc`/`certGen` seams, and no lock is added. Production frequency is not measured.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — a real lock-order defect introduced by the #15667 fix, whose comment asserts a single nesting direction that the code contradicts. The consequence (wedged commit plane) is concrete, although the trigger is rare.

- **Adversarial analysis:** This is a reliability fault, not attacker-driven. Two internal goroutines can trigger it: the TLS monitor (`startManagementTLSCertificateMonitor`, hourly) and the daemon apply path (commit, peer config sync, DHCP lease change on the management interface → `reconcileWebManagement`). The challenged assumption is that `buildHTTPSServer` is never reached under lifeMu. It is reached under lifeMu on every leg rebuild.
- **Evidence:** Order A: `pkg/api/listener.go:672` `s.lifeMu.Lock()` in `ReconcileHTTPSAddrs` → `reconcileLegsLocked` → `listener.go:796` `s.planHTTPSLeg(addr)` → `pkg/api/server.go:1527` `s.tlsCertificateMu.Lock()` in `buildHTTPSServer`. Order B: `tls_certificate_10827.go:522` `s.tlsCertificateMu.Lock()` in `refreshManagementTLSCertificate` → `refreshManagementTLSCertificateLocked` → install/publish → `:580` / `:785` `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` → `:618` `s.lifeMu.Lock()`. The recovery takes lifeMu BEFORE it checks whether any leg is serving. `ReconcileTLSCertificate` (`:701-702`) takes the same B path, but on the apply goroutine. A lock census of non-test pkg/api finds no other lock serializing the two paths. The B path is gated: the valid steady state returns early (`:540-542` generated cert still valid; `:779-781` same custom fingerprint). Inference from the `management.go:1213` contract comment: management reconcile runs under applyConfigLocked.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestN10TLSLockOrderInversion -count=1 -v`, with `RUN/verify/vn10/probes/zz_n10_lockorder_probe_test.go` (the worker's probe, re-run unchanged). Output is in `RUN/verify/vn10/lockorder_rerun.out`. The positive control (same two operations run sequentially) gives `interleave=false both completed (no deadlock)`. The interleaved run gives `interleave=true DEADLOCK: monitor-refresh done=false reconcile done=false after 3s`, with one goroutine in `sync.Mutex.Lock` at `tls_certificate_10827.go:618` and one at `server.go:1527` ← `listener.go:796`. Limits: the seams widen the windows to make the race deterministic, so the probe shows the inversion, not its natural frequency.
- **Trace:** commit / peer-sync apply / DHCP mgmt-address change → `reconcileWebManagement` → `managementReconciler.reconcileTo` (`management.go:723-724`, which calls ReconcileHTTPSAddrs on a TLS/address/degraded change or whenever `!HTTPSServing()`) → lifeMu → new leg → `buildHTTPSServer` waits on tlsCertificateMu. Concurrently, the hourly monitor tick, when a certificate is (re)installed (custom pair rotated or repaired on disk, generated cert expired, or recovery from the #15667 boot-failure state), holds tlsCertificateMu during keygen or load → `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` waits on lifeMu.
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for an outer lock that serializes the monitor and the apply. There is none: the monitor runs on its own goroutine, and `m.mu` belongs to the daemon reconciler only. I looked for whether `buildHTTPSServer` could be reached only outside lifeMu. It cannot: `reconcileLegsLocked` calls it under lifeMu by contract. I checked the steady state: the B path does not take lifeMu while the cert is valid and unchanged, which narrows reachability (my correction to the reporter's "production always passes the gates": the gates at `:612-617` pass, but the earlier early-returns usually prevent reaching them). The generated cert lasts 10 years (`server.go:2601`) with P-256 keygen (`server.go:2528`), so the B window is milliseconds.
- **HPC/invariant check:** This is a lock-ordering invariant. Two mutexes are acquired in opposite orders on two goroutines, and there is no timeout, try-lock, or context on either acquisition. Once wedged, lifeMu is held forever, so `HTTPSServing`/`EffectiveHTTP(S)Addrs`/`ServingLegAddrs`/shutdown drain also block.
- **Why it matters:** A rare coincidence permanently freezes configuration apply (CLI/REST/gRPC commits, HA peer config sync, DHCP-driven reapply), and the only recovery is a daemon restart, which itself waits on the systemd stop timeout. The exposure rises on boxes whose custom certificate is rotated on disk while management addresses change (e.g. DHCP fxp0).
- **Fix direction:** Make one order canonical. For example, return a "recover needed" flag from the refresh and run `recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked` after releasing tlsCertificateMu. Alternatively, load the certificate state before taking lifeMu in `ReconcileHTTPSAddrs`, so `buildHTTPSServer` never takes tlsCertificateMu under lifeMu. Correct the `:603-607` comment. Acceptance: the probe's interleaved case completes, and a test pins that no code path holds lifeMu when acquiring tlsCertificateMu.

## #16707 — #15086 U+FFFD label sanitization is many-to-one: two committed identifiers that differ only in invalid bytes emit duplicate series and every /metrics scrape answers 500 [OPEN]

## Summary
#15086 U+FFFD label sanitization is many-to-one: two committed identifiers that differ only in invalid bytes emit duplicate series and every /metrics scrape answers 500

**Finding ID:** R3-N10-03
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — total, persistent loss of the Prometheus surface (500, zero samples), but no crash and no enforcement impact. It needs an operator-committed config holding two same-scope identifiers that differ only in raw invalid bytes.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Monitoring goes fully blind (all xpf_* series and health counters) for as long as the config stands, with no daemon-side signal beyond the 500 body. Recovery means renaming one identifier.

**Contract:** `pkg/api/README.md` (#15086 bullet, ~:2419-2437): a committed identifier with raw non-UTF-8 bytes "is therefore still published, sanitized". Here neither sample is published and the whole scrape fails. #15086's filed acceptance allowed "200/500", so the README contract is the stronger promise.
**Trace:** a config file with raw bytes → `load override/merge` (ingress cited in #15086) → commit → `xpfCollector` policy-hit emit → `emitConstMetric` sanitizes each value → two metrics with identical label sets → `Registry.Gather` duplicate error → promhttp 500 for the whole exposition.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/api/metrics_emit_15086.go:33-38` `return strings.ToValidUTF8(s, "�"), false`. `pkg/api/metrics_handler.go:37` `promhttp.HandlerFor(registry, promhttp.HandlerOpts{Timeout: timeout})` keeps the default `HTTPErrorOnError`. There is no commit-time UTF-8 check: `utf8.Valid*` appears in pkg/config, pkg/configstore and pkg/cli only in a display sanitizer and a persist truncation helper.
**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestN10UTF8SanitizeCollision -count=1 -v`, using `RUN/verify/vn10/probes/zz_n10_utf8_collision_probe_test.go`; output in `RUN/verify/vn10/utf8_rerun.out`. Positive controls: two valid names give `status=200`, and one invalid name gives `status=200` (#15086 working). Collision: `web\xffallow` + `web\xfeallow` in trust→untrust gives `status=500` with "collected metric \"xpf_policy_hits_total\" {... rule=\"web�allow\" ...} was collected before with the same name and label values". Limits: shown for policy names only; other label sources follow the same choke point.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Make the sanitized spelling injective, for example by escaping invalid bytes as `\xNN` or by appending a short hash of the raw value when sanitization changed it. As the systemic fix for the whole class, serve with `promhttp.ContinueOnError` and count the dropped series. Acceptance: the probe's colliding case answers 200 with two distinct series, and the Y49-03 zone-vs-global same-name case also answers 200.

## Full validated claim

## #16708 — #15193 adds a local owner to every non-responder PSK secret: `%any`, or the pinned local address or local-id, which all VPNs on a box share. Every such secret therefore matches the responder's own side of the shared-key lookup. When charon  [OPEN]

## Summary
#15193 adds a local owner to every non-responder PSK secret: `%any`, or the pinned local address or local-id, which all VPNs on a box share. Every such secret therefore matches the responder's own side of the shared-key lookup. When charon verifies a peer's PSK AUTH it accepts any matching secret, so the per-peer selectors (#3952) no longer keep VPNs apart. Measured cases: (a) a peer at a fixed gateway's address, holding a different VPN's PSK, is authenticated as that gateway's peer; (b) a peer at any address, holding a fixed VPN's PSK and claiming a responder-only `dynamic hostname` VPN's identity, is authenticated into that VPN. In both cases the responder installs the child SA on the victim's st0 if_id. Case (b) reopens #14591's threat.

**Finding ID:** R3-VA16-S1
**Severity (source):** High — High — loss of per-VPN authentication isolation. The holder of the weakest or lowest-trust PSK on the box gets an IKE SA and a CHILD_SA bound to another site's st0 interface, so it can inject traffic into that site's zone and receive its outbound route-based traffic. Case (b) needs no address control. Bounded by: the actor must hold some PSK configured on the box, and case (a) also needs the victim peer's source address.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
This affects any box with two or more PSK VPNs in the default shape. The weakest key on the box opens every responder-only dynamic VPN from anywhere, and opens fixed VPNs to anyone who can source from their peer's address. It persists for as long as the config is loaded, with no log beyond a normal "established".

**Contract:** #3952/#14139: "Each id-<n> narrows the secret to a peer whose IKE identity matches ... the discriminator between two PSK VPNs to different peers" (`pkg/ipsec/README.md:900-905`). #14591 (CLOSED): a holder of one VPN's PSK must not authenticate into a responder-only VPN by claiming the other site's identity. #15193's own comment, `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1238-1242`: "%any as one owner AMONG peer selectors keeps #3952/#14591 isolation ... can never cause a wrong-peer match".
**Trace:** Two PSK VPNs commit cleanly -> renderConfig -> pskIDSelectorsLocal adds a shared local owner to each fixed-gateway secret -> charon loads secrets whose owners match (me = local) for every peer -> the responder selects the peer config by address/identity -> the PSK authenticator accepts an AUTH computed with any matching secret -> IKE SA established and CHILD_SA installed with the victim VPN's if_id -> route-based traffic on that st0 is exchanged with the actor.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/ipsec/policy.go:1289-1300` @d1ea69f9aa (`pskIDSelectorsLocal`): `case !responderOnlyGateway(gw): if a := strings.TrimSpace(localAddr); a != "" && a != "%any" { add(a) } else { add("%any") }`, and `case gw != nil && gw.LocalIDValue != "": add(formatIdentity(...))`. These owners are shared by every VPN with the same local side. `:719` emits them as `id-<n>`. Rendered secrets (probe): `ike-gw1 { secret = "keyOne"; id-1 = "10.200.0.3"; id-2 = "%any" }` beside `ike-gwd { secret = "keyTwo"; id-1 = "@site-d.example" }`. Introduced by a3a455d0b2 (#15193), an ancestor of the base. Observation, not inference: the charon log shows `authentication of 'site-d.example' with pre-shared key successful` for a peer holding keyOne.
**Probe:** RUN/verify/va16/probes/zz_va16_probe_test.go (TestVA16DumpTwoPSK, TestVA16DumpDynPSK) writes the HEAD renders, and probes/run2.sh runs the netns lab, with nft dropping the initiator's <150-byte AUTH_FAILED notify. sample-twopsk-dropnotify.out (case a, peer at 10.200.0.1 holding keyTwo): xpf side `selected peer config 'gw1'`, `authentication of '10.200.0.1' with pre-shared key successful`, `gw1: ESTABLISHED`, `vpn1: INSTALLED`, xfrm `if_id 0x1`. Pre-#15193 control (`id-2 = "%any"` removed): `N(AUTH_FAILED)` from the xpf side. Correct key keyOne: established. sample-dynpsk-lab.out (case b, peer at unrelated 10.200.0.1 holding keyOne, IDi `@site-d.example`): `selected peer config 'gwd'`, `authentication of 'site-d.example' with pre-shared key successful`, `gwd: ESTABLISHED`, `vpnd: INSTALLED`, xfrm `if_id 0x2`. Pre-#15193 control: AUTH_FAILED. Correct key keyTwo: established. sample-twopsk-lab.out shows the same R-side acceptance without the nft drop. Limit: not run with an IKEv1 or Junos peer.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Do not use a box-shared owner to scope PSKs. Where #15193 needs the initiator lookup to hit, render a per-connection identity pair the secret can be keyed on: the pinned peer `remote.id` already makes the IKEv2 initiator lookup carry the other id, so the local owner can be dropped there. Use a unique local id only where one is configured. Re-measure the #15193 initiator cells after the change. Acceptance: in both lab cases the wrong-key attempt gets AUTH_FAILED from the xpf side, the correct-key and xpf-initiated cells still establish, and a regression test asserts that no secret carries an owner shared with another secret on the same box unless it is the only VPN.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (va16.md)</summary>

## #16709 — `web-management http|https interface fxp0.0` can never bind IPv4 or global IPv6, because fxp0 is enslaved to vrf-mgmt and the REST listener is an unbound `net.Listen` on the interface address (EADDRNOTAVAIL) [OPEN]

## Summary
`web-management http|https interface fxp0.0` can never bind IPv4 or global IPv6, because fxp0 is enslaved to vrf-mgmt and the REST listener is an unbound `net.Listen` on the interface address (EADDRNOTAVAIL)

**Finding ID:** R3-VA45-S1
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — web management bound to the management interface, the usual Junos idiom, does not work for IPv4 or global IPv6. For HTTP, the IPv4 leg is first, and a first-address bind failure fails Start with nothing serving (pkg/api/listener.go:462-466). Bounded and fail-visible: the leg is reported Failed and re-driven by the re-assert owner, loopback and data-zone interface bindings work, and an fxp0 link-local leg binds because its zone sets the bound device.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators who follow the Junos idiom of putting web management on the management port get no IPv4 web/REST access there, and the HTTP plane fails to start entirely. The visible workaround (loopback or a data-zone interface) moves the management plane off the isolated management network.

**Contract:** web-management `interface` must serve on that interface's addresses. Per #14583, one leg is served per family, and show must report the actual listener state (pkg/daemon/management.go:351-406). fxp0 is the management interface and xpf always places it in vrf-mgmt (pkg/config/routinginstance_reserved_name_9622.go:28-33, docs/config-schema.md:12183-12185).
**Trace:** `set system services web-management https interface fxp0.0` -> compile HTTPSInterface -> daemon_run_servers/reconcileWebManagement resolves fxp0's IPv4 (and global IPv6) -> net.Listen("tcp", "<fxp0-ip>:443") -> kernel inet_bind checks the main local table, where the VRF-slave address is absent -> EADDRNOTAVAIL -> the leg is retained/failed and re-asserted every 30 s with the same result.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/daemon/daemon_run_servers.go:404-425 `httpsHosts, degraded = resolveInterfaceAddrsDegraded(cfg, wm.HTTPSInterface, "127.0.0.1")`, `apiCfg.HTTPSAddrs = joinBindAddrs(...)`. pkg/api/server.go:956-959 `s.listen = net.Listen`, with no override in pkg/daemon (grep ListenFunc: none). pkg/api/listener.go:462 / :482 / :785 `ln, err := s.listen("tcp", ...)`. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:509-523 `managementVRFIfaceSet` puts fxp0 in the mgmt set, and :263 / :310 `BindInterfaceToVRF(ifName, config.ManagementVRFInstanceName)`. pkg/networkd/networkd.go:84,1670 renders `VRF=` so the binding survives reconfigure. The only SO_BINDTODEVICE listeners are in grpcapi/ddns/snmp, not pkg/api.
**Probe:** `go test -c ./pkg/daemon/` then `unshare -Urn bash verify/va45/probes/va45_webmgmt_vrf_bind.sh daemon.test`. Source: verify/va45/probes/zz_va45_webmgmt_vrf_bind_test.go. Output: verify/va45/probes/va45_webmgmt_vrf_bind.out. Observed: `managementVRFIfaceSet=map[fxp0:true]`; `interface=fxp0.0 degraded=false addr=192.0.2.5:443 listen err=listen tcp 192.0.2.5:443: bind: cannot assign requested address`. Positive control in the default VRF: `interface=ge-0/0/0.0 degraded=false addr=10.0.1.10:443 listen err=<nil>`. A zoned fxp0 link-local leg binds. Limits: the full api.Server/reconciler was not run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
When the resolved interface (or its address) belongs to a VRF, bind with a ListenConfig whose Control sets SO_BINDTODEVICE to the VRF device (as grpcapi/server.go:1072 does for its VRF listener). Keep the unbound bind for default-VRF interfaces. Acceptance: the va45 netns probe run through the production listener factory binds 192.0.2.5:443 on fxp0-in-vrf-mgmt, a client connection through the VRF is served, and the ge-0/0/0 control is unchanged.

## #16710 — Every RG takeover edge (RG0 at `daemon_ha.go:877`, data RG at `:1887`) runs the same unscoped `reinitiateIPsecSAs`. Its #15194 belt terminates (`--force`) any owned name already live locally. A later edge therefore tears down and renegotiates tunnels an earlier edge of the same takeover sequence restored, whenever the peer's advertised set still lists them. [OPEN]

## Summary

Every RG takeover edge (RG0 at `daemon_ha.go:877`, data RG at `:1887`) runs the same unscoped `reinitiateIPsecSAs`. Its #15194 belt terminates (`--force`) any owned name already live locally. A later edge therefore tears down and renegotiates tunnels an earlier edge of the same takeover sequence restored, whenever the peer's advertised set still lists them.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A35-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — bounded availability loss during HA recovery. Each killed tunnel (and, because the terminate is per IKE SA, its sibling CHILD SAs) gets one extra forced teardown and renegotiation per later edge. The same pass re-initiates it immediately, so it self-heals within the renegotiation time, which grows with tunnel count because passes are sequential swanctl execs. Potential, not lab-measured. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable ordering (progressive RG ownership); concrete consequence (healthy IKE SAs force-terminated); introduced by #15194 on top of the unscoped re-initiation.

## Mechanism

The peer advertises {vpn-rg1, vpn-rg2, vpn-plain} → this node gains RG1 → `applyRethServicesForRG(1)` → `go reinitiateIPsecSAs()` → list-sas = {} → initiate the owned names → tunnels up → this node gains RG2 later (next failover step, or a later edge of the wave) → `go reinitiateIPsecSAs()` → list-sas includes the names just raised → belt → `swanctl --terminate --ike --force` each → initiate again.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at @d1ea69f9aa.

## Impact

HA takeover and per-RG maintenance failovers are routine. Multi-RG deployments with tunnels on several RGs (or RG plus plain) get healthy tunnels flapped on an unrelated RG's edge, lengthening outage during the exact recovery window.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Pass the transitioning RG into `reinitiateIPsecSAs`, and initiate/belt only names whose RG set is that RG (on the RG0 edge, only RG0/unanchored names). Alternatively, record the names this node initiated in the current ownership epoch and exclude them from the belt. Acceptance: the va35 shape-A and reporter wave probes terminate 0 live SAs and initiate each name once; the shipped #15194 belt cells and the C02-02 scope expectation stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

The #9139 design comment at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1880-1881`: "ownsIPsecConn scopes the set to this RG ... RG0's own transition still handles RG0-anchored connections, and neither leg touches the other's". The #15194 belt (`:2640-2647`) is meant only for a STALE duplicate left by a demotion terminate that raced or failed.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A35-02` (parts file `parts/va35.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A35-02 | Medium | Every RG takeover edge (RG0 at daemon_ha.go:877, data RG at :1887) runs the same unscoped…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): 
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A35-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A35-02 — The #15194 "stale local duplicate" belt in reinitiateIPsecSAs force-terminates IKE SAs that an earlier, unscoped re-initiation edge just raised, when takeover edges are spaced wider than an IKE exchange
- **Finding ID:** R3-A35-02

## #16711 — The userspace WireGuard transit encap sizes its IPv6 outer to the local egress link MTU (or a static route `mtu` metric). It emits the outer as one unfragmentable datagram, and nothing learns the underlay path MTU fro... [OPEN]

## Summary
The userspace WireGuard transit encap sizes its IPv6 outer to the local egress link MTU (or a static route `mtu` metric). It emits the outer as one unfragmentable datagram, and nothing learns the underlay path MTU from an ICMPv6 Packet-Too-Big. A smaller MTU beyond the first hop therefore drops every inner packet whose outer exceeds it. No PTB goes to the inner source and no xpf counter moves.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — availability of permitted WireGuard transit traffic, bounded by topology. It needs an IPv6 underlay (a peer endpoint `[v6]:port`) and a path MTU beyond the first hop smaller than the local egress MTU. Inside that shape it is a permanent, silent black hole for large inner packets: TCP full-size segments stall and large non-TCP datagrams are lost. A documented static workaround exists (operator `mtu` on the wg interface, `docs/wireguard-interop.md:272-275`), and there is no enforcement or isolation loss. The black hole itself is potential: it follows from demonstrated component behaviour plus standard IPv6 router behaviour and was not observed in a lab. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A81-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va81.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
WireGuard over an IPv6 transport (v6-only and cloud underlays) silently stalls bulk TCP and loses large UDP after any downstream underlay MTU reduction. The operator sees healthy xpf counters, so the fault presents as an unexplained application hang. It lasts until an operator manually lowers the wg MTU, and it recurs whenever the path changes, for example on failover onto a narrower underlay.

**Contract:** A tunnel entry point must learn the tunnel path MTU and either signal the original source or fragment the outer. RFC 2473 §6.7 (fetched): "The tunnel MTU is set dynamically to the Path MTU between the tunnel entry-point and the tunnel exit-point nodes ... The tunnel entry-point node performs Path MTU discovery on the path between the tunnel entry-point and exit-point nodes". §7.1(a) adds that an oversize original IPv6 packet gets a PTB carrying the tunnel MTU, and §7.1(b) that a packet ≤ 1280 is encapsulated and the outer fragmented to the path MTU. RFC 2003 §5.1 (fetched, verbatim) is the IPv4 IP-in-IP analogue: "all encapsulator implementations MUST support Path MTU Discovery soft state within their tunnels". Both apply to WireGuard/UDP by analogy only; neither is normative for WireGuard. Project basis: issue #13957 ("... nothing learns underlay path MTU") and `docs/log/13957.md:76-79` ("IPv6 outers remain subject to IPv6 Packet Too Big behavior. A two-hop underlay lab verification with reduced path MTU remains outstanding."). RFC 8200 §4.5: only source nodes fragment, so an IPv6 underlay router cannot rescue an oversize outer.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
Read at d1ea69f9aa:
  - `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/wg.rs:815-819`: `let interface_mtu = egress.map(|e| e.mtu).filter(|m| *m > 0).unwrap_or(1500); let outer_mtu = crate::afxdp::forwarding::min_nonzero_mtu(interface_mtu, outer_resolution.resolution.route_mtu as usize);` This is the sole budget.
  - `wg.rs:836-853`: `if wg_encapped_size(inner_packet.len(), outer_v6) > outer_mtu { ... encap_mtu_drops ...; return None; }`. Otherwise the frame is emitted whole.
  - `wg.rs:956-967`: `(true, IpAddr::V6(dst)) => { ... write_ipv6_header(..., PROTO_UDP, outer_tos, 0, endpoint.ttl, payload_len)` writes no Fragment header, and `frame/wg.rs` has no fragmentation path.
  - Twin `wg.rs:936-945`: `write_ipv4_tunnel_header(..., total_len, false)`, DF clear (#14085).
  - Route MTU producer: `pkg/routing/fibimport.go:207` ("MTU is the kernel route-wide RTA_METRICS/RTAX_MTU constraint"), learned protocols only, so no PMTU exceptions; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:1009-1026` (overlay `mtu`).
  - Census: `grep -rn -i 'RECVERR|IPV6_MTU|IP_MTU|MTU_DISCOVER|PMTUDISC|path_mtu|pmtu' userspace-dp/src` finds only NAT64/embedded-ICMP test comments, with no consumer of a PTB quoting a WG outer. `pkg/` hits are nft accept comments and metric descriptors only.
  - Transit vs kernel socket: `afxdp/coordinator/wg_control/mod.rs` module doc says Egress from the TUN goes through the kernel socket and "The transit AF_XDP egress is the other encap site", so transit never uses the kernel's PMTU-aware UDP socket.
  - Reachability: `pkg/config/types_routing.go:1000` `WgOuterFamilyV6` drives `pkg/dataplane/userspace/tunnels.go:122` → `outerFamily = "inet6"`.
  - Inference, not executed: the far-side router drops the 1488-byte outer and returns a PTB to the firewall's outer source. That PTB can only update the kernel's route cache.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a component cell built a real `ForwardingState` with an IPv6 WG peer and an established engine, then ran `wg_encap_frame`. The 1405-byte inner produced a 1488-byte IPv6 outer with next-header UDP (17) and no Fragment header, and an outer larger than the local 1500 was refused. The IPv4-outer twin (DF clear) ran as the family control. The missing PTB consumption and the downstream drop are STATIC.
