## #16734 — #15038 residual: a node demoted by ip-monitoring never re-measures as secondary, so its DOWN state and weight-0 debt stay frozen after the upstream recovers (survivor cannot promote; two demotions leave the RG ownerless) [OPEN]

## Summary

#15038 residual: a node demoted by ip-monitoring never re-measures as secondary, so its DOWN state and weight-0 debt stay frozen after the upstream recovers (survivor cannot promote; two demotions leave the RG ownerless)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A21-01`
**Severity (source report):** High — HA ownership loss that never self-recovers. A transient upstream outage that demotes the primary leaves that node pinned at weight 0 for the life of the process. A later loss of the new primary then leaves the RG with no owner while the upstream is healthy. An outage long enough to demote both nodes (about 2 x fail-threshold polls) leaves zero owners at once. Recovery needs an xpfd restart or removing the RG/ip-monitoring. Shown at component level with real Managers and the real probe path; not shown on a cluster [reporter: High]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable with an ordinary ip-monitoring config and an upstream flap; the ownership loss is permanent; no owner.

## Mechanism

`chassis cluster redundancy-group 1 ip-monitoring { global-weight 255; global-threshold 255; family inet 10.0.0.1 { weight 255; interface reth0.0; } }` -> compileRGIPMonitoring -> Monitor.pollCycle on both nodes. On the primary, the probe from the VIP fails three times -> st.down=true -> aggregate debt 255 -> SetMonitorWeight -> recalcWeight -> weight 0 -> electRG "Local weight 0" -> secondary. The peer sees weight 0 and becomes primary. Upstream recovers. The demoted node's probes are now not completed (no VIP; secondary address not installed) -> `continue` -> st.down stays true -> debt 255 -> weight 0 forever. Peer loss -> handlePeerTimeout -> electSingleNode -> weight 0 -> stays secondary.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/monitor.go:491-496 `if !res.completed { ... continue }` (dampening left untouched); :684-705 probeSourceFor returns the VIP only when `mon.mgr.IsLocalPrimary(rg.ID)`, otherwise `target.SecondaryIPAddress` or ""; :1252-1260 a dial/bind error returns `false, false`; :1318-1326 a WriteTo error with `!mon.mgr.IsLocalPrimary(task.rgID)` returns `false, false`; :1412-1426 defaultICMPDialer is a plain `icmp.ListenPacket(network, listenAddr)` (no freebind) and BindToDevice is a no-op. `SecondaryIPAddress` is read only at monitor.go:701; no code installs it. ipState is purged only for removed RGs (:399-401), and reconcileRGIPDebts derives the debt from `st.down` (:1045, :1085). election.go:165-170 `if localWeight <= 0 { ... "Local weight 0" }` and the peer-lost arm :143-149 only promote when `localWeight > 0`.

## Impact

Every site that uses RG ip-monitoring loses its standby after the first upstream flap, silently, until xpfd restarts. The next primary failure becomes a full RG outage, or a longer outage makes both nodes non-owners at once. `show chassis cluster` keeps reporting the ip-monitoring failure for a target that is reachable.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When a node cannot measure a target (not primary and probe not completed), drop that target's dampened DOWN state and the installed ip debt for the RG, so the probe is neutral rather than frozen. Alternatively, install secondary-ip-address on the local member so the secondary really measures. Acceptance: the reporter's two production rows and the va21 survivor twin end with exactly one owner, and the #15038 tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

docs/feature-coverage.md:285-291 (#15038): a probe that cannot be sent from this node's source "installs no debt and leaves dampening untouched, so the survivor stays promotable instead of being pinned at weight 0 with the RG ownerless after a primary loss". #15038's acceptance criterion says the "survivor promotes after peer loss". The Juniper interface-monitoring page says weight is restored when the monitored object recovers ("If interface ge-0/0/1 is brought back up, the weight of RG1 in node 0 becomes 255").

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A21-01` (parts file `parts/va21.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).

Its predicate covers only a secondary that has never measured. gemini vsrx-parity-003 H23-03 is about compiling and validating secondary-ip-address. R3-F05-03 (part-vf05) is the probe address family on the primary. R3-A15-02 (part-va15) is the global-weight default. #5271/#5990/#5301 are other dimensions. No in-run or prior owner.

## #16735 — R3-A45-02: `show system services` prints `root-login: deny` for an ssh stanza with no root-login leaf, while sshd enforces prohibit-password (root key login accepted) [OPEN]

## Summary

`show system services` prints `root-login: deny` for an ssh stanza with no root-login leaf, while sshd enforces prohibit-password (root key login accepted)

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — an operator-visible misstatement of root SSH posture. It matters only when root keys are installed (`system root-authentication ssh-*`), in which case key login as root is accepted while both show surfaces say "deny". Password root login stays refused, and setting the leaf explicitly makes display and enforcement agree. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A45-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va45.md` (finding `R3-A45-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/cli/cli_show_system.go:399-404 and pkg/grpcapi/server_show_system.go:269-274 `rootLogin := cfg.System.Services.SSH.RootLogin; if rootLogin == "" { rootLogin = "deny" }`. pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1338-1351 emits `PermitRootLogin` only `if ssh.RootLogin != ""`. scripts/image/bake.py:353 `PermitRootLogin prohibit-password` (factory drop-in). The managed drop-in is 00-xpf.conf (:940), so with no line the later default applies.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/sysservices/listeners.go:7-16 and the #6385 lineage: `show system services` reports what services actually do, not assumed values.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (show system services SSH-row truthfulness, with R3-A45-03) — real but bounded display defect. Its fix shares the renderer with A45-03.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — reporter probes re-run: grpcapi showSystemServices, and daemon buildSSHDConfig for the leaf values "", deny and deny-password.

**Confidence:** High — both legs executed. The effective sshd default comes from the factory drop-in or OpenSSH's compiled default (prohibit-password).

## Impact

The operator's only status view of root SSH access states the most restrictive value when a weaker one is in force.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Either render `PermitRootLogin no` when the leaf is unset (if deny is the intended default), or display `deny-password (default)`. Acceptance: for each of "", deny, deny-password, allow, the show row and the effective PermitRootLogin agree.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16736 — When both nodes' monitors take a redundancy group to weight 0, no node owns it; Junos makes the lower node ID primary [OPEN]

## Summary

When both nodes' monitors take a redundancy group to weight 0, no node owns it; Junos makes the lower node ID primary

**Finding ID:** `R3-A21-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — zero owners for the RG while both nodes are at threshold 0. Every RETH VIP of the RG is withdrawn, so forwarding stops on the RG's unaffected interfaces too. A single physical fault can trigger it (both nodes' monitored members on one switch). It self-heals when either monitor recovers [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a grounded parity divergence with a concrete ownership-loss consequence; no owner.

## Mechanism

interface-monitor ge-0/0/1 weight 255 and ge-7/0/1 weight 255 on RG1 -> both links down -> Monitor.pollInterfaceMonitors -> SetMonitorWeight -> recalcWeight -> weight 0 on both -> heartbeat -> electRG "Local weight 0" on both -> both secondary -> VIPs removed on both.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/election.go:165-170 `if localWeight <= 0 { if rg.State != StateSecondary { return electLocalSecondary, "Local weight 0" } ... }` runs before the `peerWeight <= 0` arm (:172-178), so each node takes "Local weight 0". The peer-lost arm (:143-149) requires `localWeight > 0`. runElection's degraded and #9452 fallbacks (:502-526) run only when `result == electLocalPrimary`.

## Impact

The operator configured monitors to move traffic to the healthier node. When neither node is healthier, Junos keeps one owner so the RG's other links (LAN to DMZ, management VIPs) keep forwarding. xpf drops the whole RG for the duration of the fault.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When the peer is alive and both local and peer weight are 0 from monitor debt (not kernel hold or explicit resignation, which the fix must distinguish on the wire or by state), elect the lower node ID. Acceptance: the both-zero row gives exactly one owner (node0), the control rows are unchanged, and the #12164/#9452/kernel-hold tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper "Monitoring Chassis Cluster Interfaces" (juniper.net security-chassis-cluster-interface-monitoring): "If the monitored interfaces of a redundancy group on both nodes reach their thresholds at the same time, the redundancy group becomes primary on the node with the lower node ID". docs/phases.md:760 calls electRG a "Full Junos-style election".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A21-02` (parts file `parts/va21.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A21-02 | Medium | When both nodes' monitors take a redundancy group to weight 0, no node owns it; Junos makes…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): Grepped gh-issues for weight (#6549, #5478, #12164, #9842, #10245, #390), prior-headings and the full reports. Y42-01, r2 A15-03 and r2 A21-01 reach both-weight-0 only as a consequence of other defects; no report owns the tie rule. No in-run part covers it.

## #16737 — R3-A45-03: Removing `system services ssh` leaves sshd serving on zones admitting `ssh`/`all` (an undocumented divergence from Junos service semantics), and `show system… [OPEN]

## Summary

Removing `system services ssh` leaves sshd serving on zones admitting `ssh`/`all` (an undocumented divergence from Junos service semantics), and `show system services` drops the SSH row while sshd still serves

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — management SSH stays reachable (authentication still required) after an operator removes the stanza the Junos way, and the status surface stops mentioning SSH. Narrowed: xpf documents that sshd runs independently of the stanza, so the main residual defect is the misleading show output plus the unstated parity gap. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A45-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va45.md` (finding `R3-A45-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1096-1150 handles an absent stanza by removing the drop-in and reloading only ("SSH config drop-in removed (reverted to defaults)"). pkg/config/host_inbound_tokens.go:735-751: the `all` expansion takes no config input, and :750 `case "ssh": return []L4Match{hiTCP(22)}`. cli_show_system.go:399 and server_show_system.go:269 print the SSH row only when the stanza exists.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** Junos: `[edit system services] ssh` enables the service. xpf: docs/feature-gaps.md:1060 says removing the stanza removes the drop-in "so sshd reverts to base-image defaults", and pkg/daemon/README.md:3504-3507 says the factory drop-in applies "regardless of whether `system services ssh` is configured". Neither states that removing the stanza leaves SSH enabled. sysservices/listeners.go:7-20 requires show to report actual state.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (show system services SSH-row truthfulness, with R3-A45-02) — real, bounded. Its show-side fix shares the renderer with A45-02, and the enablement question needs an owner decision.

**Verification in source report:** STATIC for sshd continuing to listen (no unit stop/disable/mask exists). EXECUTED: host-inbound `all` admits tcp/22 (TestA45AllAdmitsSSH re-run), and the SSH row is absent with no stanza (TestA45ShowRootLoginUnset).

**Confidence:** Medium — the mechanism is clear. Whether xpf intends to own SSH enablement is a design question the docs answer only by implication.

## Impact

Junos-trained operators decommissioning SSH on a data zone keep it reachable with no visible signal.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At minimum, make show print the effective state (e.g. `SSH: running (not managed — no system services ssh)`), document the divergence, and add a commit advisory when host-inbound admits ssh with no stanza. Optionally, own the service by restricting ListenAddress to the lifeline when the stanza is absent. Acceptance: with `system-services all` and no stanza, either tcp/22 is refused from the zone or show plus the advisory state that it is served.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16739 — Under preempt, election scales priority by weight (priority*weight/255), so a partial monitor loss with threshold still above 0 fails the RG over and back; Junos fails over only at threshold 0 [OPEN]

## Summary

Under preempt, election scales priority by weight (priority*weight/255), so a partial monitor loss with threshold still above 0 fails the RG over and back; Junos fails over only at threshold 0

**Finding ID:** `R3-A21-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — unrequested failovers: two ownership moves per partial-monitor flap, with GARP churn and disruption to sessions not yet synced. They happen on configs sized the Junos way to tolerate a single link loss. No enforcement loss [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a grounded parity break with a concrete consequence (failover the operator did not configure); no owner and no documented divergence.

## Mechanism

RG1 preempt, node priorities 200/150, interface-monitor ge-0/0/2 weight 100 -> link down -> SetMonitorWeight -> weight 155 -> EffectivePriority 121 < 150 -> node0 "Preempt: lower priority" -> node1 "Preempt: higher priority" -> failover. Link up -> 200 > 150 -> failback.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/election.go:17-22 `return basePriority * weight / 255`. The preempt arm (:280-298) `if localEff > peerEff {...} else if localEff < peerEff { ... return electLocalSecondary, "Preempt: lower priority" }` has no weight-0 gate. The same scaled values drive non-preempt dual-active resolution (:357-361) and cold-start choice (:388-394). Non-preempt incumbents keep the RG (:376), which matches Junos.

## Impact

A Junos config migrated as written, with several monitors sized to tolerate one failure, gets a failover and a failback on each such failure. Each move costs session state on flows not yet synced and churns upstream ARP.

## Acceptance / fix direction

While weight > 0, elect on raw priority under preempt; keep weight decisive only at 0 and in the #12164 arm-debt rule. Otherwise document the divergence prominently and warn at commit when preempt and sub-255 monitors coexist. Acceptance: the partial-loss row keeps node0 primary, and the #12164 tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper "Monitoring Chassis Cluster Interfaces": "Interface failover occurs only when the redundancy group's threshold reaches zero" (fetched). xpf's docs/phases.md:759-763 describes the `base * weight / 255` scaling but calls the election "Junos-style"; no divergence note exists in feature-coverage or the README.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A21-03` (parts file `parts/va21.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A21-03 | Medium | Under preempt, election scales priority by weight (priority*weight/255), so a partial…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): No issue or prior heading on effective-priority scaling (grepped "effective priority", "weight", "partial" in gh-issues, prior-headings and the reports). The root cause differs from R3-A21-02 (tie at 0 vs scaling above 0). No in-run part covers it.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A21-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16740 — R3-A45-04: ssh-ed25519/ssh-rsa/ssh-dsa leaves have no commit-time validator: a trailing token (e.g. `from 10.1.1.1`) or malformed key commits clean and durable, then apply… [OPEN]

## Summary

ssh-ed25519/ssh-rsa/ssh-dsa leaves have no commit-time validator: a trailing token (e.g. `from 10.1.1.1`) or malformed key commits clean and durable, then apply refuses all of that principal's keys and the previously installed key stays live

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — fail-visible at apply, but the durable config has already advanced, so a key rotation carrying one bad value leaves the old key working on every later apply until the config is corrected.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A45-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va45.md` (finding `R3-A45-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism

pkg/config/schema_system.go:138-140 (root) and :422-424 (users): `"ssh-ed25519": {desc: ..., args: 1, multi: true, placeholder: "<key>", children: nil}` has no validator. pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:108-115 validateAuthorizedSSHKeys is the only check and runs at apply. :264-267 sets `keysValid = false`. :377-379 `if provisionBlocked { continue }` skips both install and revoke.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** CLAUDE.md and docs/config-schema.md: typed leaves are validated at strict commit through setSchema validators. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:237-241: the commit is "the one that ADVANCES the durable config".

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (commit-time typed-leaf validation gaps / host-auth key lifecycle) — real, bounded, fail-visible.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED (schema/compile leg, TestA45SSHKeyFromProbe re-run). STATIC: the apply skip.

**Confidence:** High — the config leg was executed. The apply leg comes from source and the existing #14694 tests.

An operator rotating a compromised key, who sees an apply error and does not fix it immediately, keeps the compromised key valid while the committed config no longer lists it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Move validAuthorizedSSHKey into pkg/config and attach it as the leaf validator applied to every multi value. Acceptance: the probe's second row returns a schema error naming the leaf, and the first row stays clean.

## #16741 — Residual of #14406/#7162: under preempt, the incumbent yields to a rejoining higher-priority peer that is armed but still in the startup sync hold, so no node owns the RG until the hold releases (up to 30 s) [OPEN]

## Summary

Residual of #14406/#7162: under preempt, the incumbent yields to a rejoining higher-priority peer that is armed but still in the startup sync hold, so no node owns the RG until the hold releases (up to 30 s)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A21-04`
**Severity (source report):** High — HA ownership loss on a routine planned operation. Every reboot or upgrade of the preferred node of a preempt RG blackholes that RG from the rejoiner's dataplane arm until bulk sync completes or the 30 s hold times out. Other readiness terms on a higher-priority secondary can stretch this to the 2-minute degraded fallback. Shown at component level; the end-to-end blackhole was not run in a lab [reporter: High]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the #14406 fix keeps the rejoiner secondary but leaves the incumbent's preempt yield in place, so the RG has zero owners for a bounded window.

## Mechanism

node0 (priority 200, preempt) reboots while node1 (100) owns RG1 -> node0 bringup arms the #7162/#14406 hold -> XDP arm -> applyTransitElectionDebt clears the arm debt -> weight 255 -> heartbeat -> node1 electRG: eff 100 < 200 -> "Preempt: lower priority" -> secondary, VIPs removed. node0 electRG returns electLocalPrimary -> readiness gate blocked by "session sync startup hold" -> continue. Both nodes are secondary until releaseNoRethSyncHold / ReleaseSyncHold (bulk sync complete or 30 s).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/election.go:295-298 `} else if localEff < peerEff { if rg.State != StateSecondary { return electLocalSecondary, "Preempt: lower priority" } }`. heartbeat_manager.go:539-555 sends GroupID/Priority/Weight/State only (clamped to 0 only under kernel hold). election.go:502-526: the rejoiner's promotion is blocked ("election blocked by readiness gate"), and peerYieldedOwnership does not match a Secondary/255 peer. pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go:239-252 (#14406) and daemon_ha_vip.go:36-53 (#7162) add the hold reason. daemon_transit_gate.go:418-423 clears the arm debt when `dataplaneReady` alone is true, so the held node advertises 255.

## Impact

Preempt is the Junos way to pin an RG to the preferred node, so every maintenance reboot of that node turns its rejoin into an RG outage of up to 30 s, instead of the session-preserving handover the hold was added to protect. The same yield happens for any not-ready reason on a higher-priority secondary (VIP interface down, fabric not ready, R3-A06-04's disabled unit), bounded there only by the 2-minute degraded timeout.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Do not let the incumbent yield to a peer that cannot take over. Either advertise a not-takeover-ready marker or an effective election weight while the readiness gate is closed (as the kernel hold already clamps the wire weight), or install an election debt for the startup hold the way the arm debt works. Acceptance: in the held-armed row the incumbent stays the single owner until release, then node0 takes over; the #14406/#7162/#9452/#12164 tests stay green. Lab: loss cluster with `preempt` on RG1, reboot fw0 under iperf3, and observe no interval with RG1 secondary on both nodes.

## Contract (where cited)

The startup hold exists to delay the rejoiner's takeover until it has session state (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_noreth_hold.go:8-41; daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go:239-252). It does not exist to remove the current owner. #9452 (election.go:1081-1110) states that holding a node secondary while the peer has given up the RG leaves it "owned by NEITHER node" and is the wrong trade.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A21-04` (parts file `parts/va21.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A21-04 | High | Residual of #14406/#7162: under preempt, the incumbent yields to a rejoining…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #14406 (CLOSED, fix 53924798ba is an ancestor) and #7162 gate only the rejoiner; #14406's regression criterion asserts only that the rejoiner stays secondary. #9452 (peerYieldedOwnership) covers a manual failover into a held node; its predicate misses a preempt yield at full weight. #10776 (preempt dual primary on a requested transfer), #7579 and r2 A89-02 are different mechanisms. R3-A21-06 is the same peer-side preempt yield with a different cause, and fixing either leaves the other. No in-run part owns it.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A21-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16742 — R3-A46-01: After #16303, the close exports only if THIS exporter object recorded the open. Flows that span an RG failover (the promoted node gets no CREATE) or a commit that… [OPEN]

## Summary

After #16303, the close exports only if THIS exporter object recorded the open. Flows that span an RG failover (the promoted node gets no CREATE) or a commit that rebuilds the exporters are never exported at close.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. Routine events (a failover/failback, or any flow-export knob edit) silently drop the close record of every live flow, while the sampler still advertises 1-in-N. Enforcement is unaffected.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa.
  - `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:987` "an unsampled/absent open exports nothing", and `:998-1001` / `:1079-1082`: `s, p, by, rp, rb := b.groups[k].exp.CloseFlow(key); if !s { continue }`.
  - `pkg/flowexport/exporter_core.go:292-304` returns `tracked || inSampledSet`, which is per object.
  - `daemon_flowexport.go:372` / `:696`: a hash change rebuilds every group with `NewExporter`/`NewIPFIXExporter`. `netflow.go:604-607`: Run only `flushBatches()` on cancel.
  - `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:1084` gates CREATE on `delta.is_admission`. The only `is_admission: true` site is `session/install.rs:778`; bulk export `:1212`, `ha/export.rs:350` and `session/mod.rs:4185,4724` are false.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** IPFIX sampler Options say 1-in-N of flows are exported (`pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:77-108`). The parent of the base commit made a close-time `ShouldExportIface` decision (`git show d1ea69f9aa^:pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:885`), so these flows were exported before #16303.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. A reachable trigger (a commit editing `flow-active-timeout`, or a failover) produces a concrete loss of export records.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED for the close-without-open and reconcile arms, with controls. STATIC for the HA promote arm.

**Confidence:** Medium-High. The reconcile trigger was executed. The HA trigger is STATIC from `is_admission` gating. The restart trigger is plausible but unverified.

## Impact

After a failback, every established flow on the cluster is missing from the collector. Each flow-export commit also drops every live flow's close. Volume and session forensics have holes exactly around operational events.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When no open state exists for the key anywhere, make one close-time 1-in-N decision. Also carry the tracker/sampled state to the replacement exporter with the same group key, and treat a promote Open as an open for flow export (without a syslog CREATE). Acceptance: (a) open → exporter-replacing reconcile → close exports exactly one record. (b) A close with no open at rate 1 exports one record. (c) `TestDualFormatOpenConsumesOneSlotPerInstance16303` stays green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16743 — The ISSU drain's weight-0 pin (ForceSecondary) is undone by the next recalcWeight (any commit or peer config sync with interface monitors); under preempt the peer then yields to the still-parked drained node and no node owns the RG [OPEN]

## Summary

The ISSU drain's weight-0 pin (ForceSecondary) is undone by the next recalcWeight (any commit or peer config sync with interface monitors); under preempt the peer then yields to the still-parked drained node and no node owns the RG

**Finding ID:** `R3-A21-06`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — HA ownership loss during the ISSU drain window, with no self-recovery until the drained node restarts or is reset. It needs `preempt` with the drained node at higher priority (the usual "upgrade the preferred node" case) and a recalcWeight trigger during the drain (a commit or a config sync from the new RG0 primary when interface-monitor is configured, or any monitor or arm edge). The window is bounded by the operator-paced drain-to-stop interval [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable during a documented operator procedure; zero owners after the CLI has said the drain is complete; no owner.

## Mechanism

node0 (200, preempt) primary -> CLI ISSU -> ForceSecondary -> weight 0 -> node1 "Peer weight 0" -> primary (drain confirmed) -> commit on node1 synced to node0 -> apply tail SetMonitorWeight(ge-0/0/2, up) -> recalcWeight -> weight 255 -> heartbeat -> node1 preempt 100 < 200 -> secondary; node0 ManualFailover -> NoChange -> zero owners.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/failover.go:337-353 ForceSecondary: `rg.Weight = 0; rg.ManualFailover = true; ... rg.State = StateSecondary` (not SecondaryHold, so the peer's "Peer transfer out" arm does not apply). election.go:901-917 recalcWeight sets `rg.Weight = rgWeightFromDebt(totalLost)` unconditionally. SetMonitorWeight (:727-817) always ends in `m.recalcWeight(rg)`, even for an up report on a never-down monitor. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:399-405 calls `d.cluster.SetMonitorWeight(rgID, st.Interface, !st.Up, st.Weight)` for every monitor on every apply. election.go:70-128: the drained node's ManualFailover arm returns NoChange (peer not resigned, not in hold, not commit-pinned). The peer's :295-298 "Preempt: lower priority" demotes it.

## Impact

The operator is told the drain is complete and safe. A routine commit on the new primary during the maintenance window blackholes every preempt RG until the drained node is restarted (which the ISSU then does, after which R3-A21-04's rejoin window follows) or reset.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make the drain pin a state fact: a forced-secondary flag honoured by recalcWeight and debtDerivedWeightLocked, cleared by ResetFailover and peer loss. Alternatively, have ForceSecondary use the SecondaryHold transfer-out shape the peer already honours. Acceptance: in the preempt row of both probes owners stays 1 after the feed, and the #10004/#10245/#9640 tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/cluster/failover.go:218-224: "ForceSecondary sets weight to 0 for all redundancy groups, forcing this node to become secondary. Used by ISSU to drain traffic to the peer". pkg/cli/cli_request_system.go:345-361 waits for the peer takeover and then tells the operator it is safe to stop the node, which implies the peer stays the single owner until then.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A21-06` (parts file `parts/va21.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A21-06 | Medium | The ISSU drain's weight-0 pin (ForceSecondary) is undone by the next recalcWeight (any…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #10245 (CLOSED) and #10004 concern the abort/restore predicate for stacked ForceSecondary and ManualFailover, not the recalc erasure or the peer's preempt yield. R3-A21-04 shares the peer-side yield but has a different cause. r2 B22-01/B22-02 (#15164 family) are about aborted failovers. No in-run part covers it.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A21-06` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16744 — R3-A46-02: Only SessionClose received the #14609 8192/s budget. SessionCreate, the sole open-side input since #15946/#16303, is GCRA-shed at 1000/s per zone, and a close whose… [OPEN]

## Summary

Only SessionClose received the #14609 8192/s budget. SessionCreate, the sole open-side input since #15946/#16303, is GCRA-shed at 1000/s per zone, and a close whose open was shed exports nothing.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. This is the same consequence class as #14609 (Medium): systematic under-export at ordinary connection rates, plus a false scale factor. Enforcement is unaffected.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa.
  - `producer.rs:19-20`: `DEFAULT_DATAPLANE_EVENT_RATE_PER_SEC = 1_000`, burst `1_024`. `:165-169`: `SessionClose => self.session_close_limit, _ => self.limit`.
  - `event_stream/mod.rs:301`: production uses `DataplaneEventRateLimitConfig::default()`.
  - `rt_flow.rs:211-213` emits SessionCreate through `try_emit_dataplane_frame`. `session_delta.rs:1084-1105` emits on every fresh admission.
  - Go side: `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:998-1001`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `userspace-dp/src/event_stream/producer.rs:22-35` says flow-export input "must not share the 1000/s deny-flood GCRA". The #14609 acceptance was "5000 closes in 1 s from one zone all reach the Go callback". Since #16303 the open is the only decision point.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. A reachable sustained new-session rate produces a measured shed and lost export records.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. A Rust cargo probe ran under `DataplaneEventRateLimitConfig::default()` with a close-kind control, and the Go close-without-open probe was re-run.

**Confidence:** High. The Rust shed was executed under the production-default config, and the Go drop was executed. The end-to-end rate behaviour in a lab is not measured.

## Impact

Busy edges routinely exceed 1000 cps per zone. At exactly the loads where forensics matter, most flows are missing and collector scale-ups are wrong by the shed factor.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Give SessionCreate a separately sized GCRA, as SessionClose has. Or make the close-time fallback of R3-A46-01 decide for opens that were shed. Surface CREATE shed counts in flow-export status. Acceptance: under the default config, 5000 creates/s from one zone all reach Go (or are made up by the fallback), and the exported fraction at rate N stays about 1/N.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;

## #16745 — A comms restart (StopHeartbeat followed by StartHeartbeat) drops the receiver's peer-liveness seed. The peer's RGs are never taken over if the peer is silent from the restart onward. If the peer dies after being heard once, takeover is up to 30 s late. [OPEN]

## Summary

A comms restart (StopHeartbeat followed by StartHeartbeat) drops the receiver's peer-liveness seed. The peer's RGs are never taken over if the peer is silent from the restart onward. If the peer dies after being heard once, takeover is up to 30 s late.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A22-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The mechanism is real at d1ea69f9aa and I confirmed it by reading the code. StartHeartbeat passes restartSeed 0 (heartbeat_manager.go:55-57). armRestart returns early when lastSeen==0 (heartbeat.go:1065-1071). checkTimeout then takes the never-seen arm (heartbeat.go:1380-1385). handlePeerNeverSeen returns on peerEverSeen (heartbeat_manager.go:1128-1130). The only peerAlive=false writers are heartbeat_manager.go:876 and fence_confirm_7147.go:225. stopClusterComms (daemon_ha_sync.go:1762-1789) and] Verifier text: — the consequence is HA ownership loss. In the default private-RG mode, the dead peer's RGs keep no primary until the peer returns or xpfd restarts. This is demonstrated at component level with the real start/stop code. The likelihood is narrow: the peer must die within the detection window, about 0.5–2 s and at most the 5 s sync-suppression cap, before a transport-endpoint comms restart. The second arm (the peer is heard once and then dies) gives a bounded 30 s late takeover, which is #9722's Medium class.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — #9722's fix seeds only `RestartHeartbeat`. The production comms-restart path still takes the cold-start path, and the peer's death is never detected.

## Mechanism

Peer alive, primary for RG1. An operator commit changes a `clusterTransportKey` field (control/fabric/fab1 interface or peer address, or the sync VRF device), or a sticky BindingChanged is consumed by the #11448 reassert (`mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:82-89`), or a bootstrap rollback is followed by the corrected commit (#7901). Then `reconcileClusterTransportBinding` → `stopClusterComms` → `StopHeartbeat` → `startClusterComms` → `startHeartbeatWithRetryForEpoch` → `StartHeartbeat` installs a receiver with lastSeen=0. (a) If the peer is already dead (it died within the old receiver's detection window or the restart gap), every tick takes the never-seen arm. That arm returns on peerEverSeen, so the peer is never declared lost. (b) If the peer is heard once and then dies, `seenThenLostGrace()` is 30 s.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go:55-57` `StartHeartbeat` → `m.startHeartbeat(..., 0, time.Time{})`. `:178` `receiver.armRestart(restartSeed, inheritedHold)`. `heartbeat.go:1065-1071` `armRestart`: `if lastSeen == 0 { return }`. `heartbeat.go:1366-1386` `checkTimeout`: `if lastNano == 0 { if neverSeenConfirmed(...) { r.mgr.handlePeerNeverSeen() }; return }`. `heartbeat_manager.go:1128-1130` `if m.peerEverSeen || m.peerConfirmedAbsent { return }`. The only `peerAlive = false` writers are `heartbeat_manager.go:876` (handlePeerTimeout) and `fence_confirm_7147.go:225`, which runs downstream of it. On the daemon side, `daemon_apply_tail.go:556` `d.stopClusterComms()` → `daemon_ha_sync.go:1788` `d.cluster.StopHeartbeat()`, and the next epoch's `daemon_ha_sync.go:1704` `d.cluster.StartHeartbeat(localIP, peerAddr, vrfDevice, controlIface)`. Only `RestartHeartbeat` (`heartbeat_manager.go:416-475`) reads `receiver.lastSeen` and `inheritedHold`. Inference: while peerAlive stays true, `runElection` keeps the stale `peerGroups` (peer PRIMARY), because election.go has no peer-age guard.

## Impact

This hits clusters in default private-RG mode when a transport-endpoint commit (which also applies on the peer through config sync) or a reassert-driven comms restart lands within a couple of seconds of a peer failure. The result is no takeover at all for the dead peer's RGs. A maintenance sequence of "commit transport change, then reboot the peer within 30 s" gives up to 30 s of outage. Recovery comes only from the peer returning, or from an xpfd restart on the survivor (a fresh Manager runs the never-seen path).

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make the comms-restart start a restart. Hand the outgoing receiver's `lastSeen` and grace end from `StopHeartbeat` to the next `StartHeartbeat` in the same Manager lifetime, or seed from Manager state when `peerEverSeen && peerAlive`. Also make the never-seen arm call `handlePeerTimeout` when `peerEverSeen && peerAlive`. Acceptance: the DEFECT row of `TestVA22CommsRestartSilentPeer` flips to `peerAlive=false localPrimary=true` within restart grace plus timeout. The CONTROL row and the #4386/#11566 cold-boot cells are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:38-51` (#9722) says a receiver "that REPLACED one which had already seen the peer" holds only `heartbeatRestartGrace` (5 s), and that the 30 s cold-boot grace there meant "a peer that died within 30s after a commit was declared lost up to 30s late". CLAUDE.md "Unplanned peer loss — default private-RG election" gives about 0.5–2.1 s detection, and says heartbeat loss is what promotes the survivor.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A22-01` (parts file `parts/va22.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A22-01 | Medium | A comms restart (StopHeartbeat followed by StartHeartbeat) drops the receiver's…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #9722 (CLOSED; fixes 705c2b4e32 and 0d8af4bd9e, both `merge-base --is-ancestor` of d1ea69f9aa) seeds only the `RestartHeartbeat` site its body names. #9751 is restart debt, #7257/#4033 are start/stop races, #7164/#5081 are restart-key contents, #4386/#11566/#12165 tune the never-seen/suppression timing. gemini-4-argon-high D90-01 is RestartHeartbeat resurrection and inheritedHold clobbering, a different mechanism. R3-F13-06 (vf13) is the fabric-mode sync churn loop, a different mode with no heartbeat. Nothing in gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv, the earlier reports, or other parts covers this site.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A22-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A22-01 — A cluster-comms restart installs an unseeded heartbeat receiver, so a peer that is silent from the restart onward is never declared lost, and a peer heard once and then lost is held for the 30 s cold-boot grace (#9722 residual at the stopClusterComms/StartHeartbeat site)
- **Finding ID:** R3-A22-01

## #16746 — A chassis cluster with no complete control link (`control-interface` and `peer-address`) commits cleanly, but under default private-RG election it has no peer detector. With no control-interface, the result is permanent dual-primary. With control-interface set but no peer-address, the result is a permanent no-primary. [OPEN]

## Summary

A chassis cluster with no complete control link (`control-interface` and `peer-address`) commits cleanly, but under default private-RG election it has no peer detector. With no control-interface, the result is permanent dual-primary. With control-interface set but no peer-address, the result is a permanent no-primary.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A22-02`
**Severity (source report):** High — the consequence is HA ownership. Without control-interface (the documented fabric-transport shape, or the peer-address-only shape), both nodes elect PRIMARY for every RG while RETH VRRP is suppressed. That means both forward and NAT under duplicate VIPs. With control-interface but no peer-address, non-preempt RGs never get a primary. The trigger is a configuration that strict commit accepts with no warning. The election and compile layers are demonstrated; the daemon end to end is potential.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a silently accepted configuration reaches dual-primary or a permanent no-primary through the default election mode.

## Mechanism

`set chassis cluster` with RGs, reths and fabric, but no `control-interface` and/or no `peer-address`. Then strict compile OK (`PrivateRGElection=true`) → both nodes boot → `startClusterComms` starts no heartbeat → `UpdateConfig` → `electSingleNode`/`electRG`. (a) controlInterface empty: weight > 0 gives PRIMARY on both nodes, with RETH VRRP suppressed, so nothing arbitrates. (b) controlInterface set: `peerConfirmedAbsent` is never set, so non-preempt RGs stay SECONDARY with no timer (the hold precedes the readiness gate).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:1286` `if cc.ControlInterface != "" && cc.PeerAddress != "" { go d.startHeartbeatWithRetryForEpoch(...) }` is the only heartbeat start. The only producers of `handlePeerHeartbeat`/`handlePeerNeverSeen` are heartbeat.go:1343/1383 (plus test_seams.go). `pkg/cluster/election.go:133-135` and `:635` hold with `!rg.Preempt && !m.peerEverSeen && !m.peerConfirmedAbsent && rg.State == StateSecondary && m.controlInterface != ""`; otherwise the result is `electLocalPrimary, "Peer lost"`. `pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:493` sets `PrivateRGElection = true` by default. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:135` suppresses RETH VRRP under PrivateRGElection. `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:618-660` pairs fabric1 leaves and checks that the control-interface exists, but never checks that the control-interface/peer-address pair is complete. Outside the heartbeat, `peerGroups` writers are only the explicit transfer paths (`failover.go:687,1338,1408,1431`). The no-RETH sync hold (`daemon_run_bringup.go:276-284`) is bounded and releases on its own timer.

## Impact

Any operator running the documented fabric-transport shape (it is also the only dual-fabric sync shape; see vf13's R3-F13-06), or who omits one of the two leaves, gets either two nodes forwarding with the same VIPs (ARP/ND flapping, asymmetric state, NAT collisions, two session-sync "owners") or no node forwarding, while `commit` reports success. Recovery is to add both leaves and restart comms, or to set `no-private-rg-election`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

When a cluster has redundancy groups and private-RG election is in effect, strict-reject a config lacking a complete control link, or fall back to `no-private-rg-election` with a loud warning. Never let `controlInterface == ""` mean "only node present" for a configured two-node cluster. A Manager-owned never-seen clock (see R3-A22-04) closes arm (b) independently. Acceptance: the three non-control compile arms error or warn, and no election arm yields dual-primary or a timerless permanent hold.

## Contract (where cited)

CLAUDE.md "Unplanned peer loss — default private-RG election (#12173)": the default "uses control-link private-RG election and suppresses RETH VRRP". `pkg/config/compiler_chassis.go:491-492`: "Private RG election is the default — suppress RETH VRRP, elect over control link only". `docs/ha-no-hitless-restart.md:295-303` documents fabric-transport clusters, where "the heartbeat does not start at all in that shape". A two-node cluster is owed exactly one primary per RG.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A22-02` (parts file `parts/va22.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A22-02 | High | A chassis cluster with no complete control link (control-interface and peer-address)…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #10783 (CLOSED) is the fabric-gRPC auth-arming consequence of the same "heartbeat never starts" fact; its fix (auth arming) does not touch election or commit. #9178/#8987/#9121/#8965 gate live transport moves. #16024 (OPEN) is a partition of a correctly configured pair. #15669 is control-interface latching on delete. #4386/#11566 cover never-seen timing with a configured link. In-run, R3-F13-06 (vf13) has the same transport shape and a different defect, and vf13 recommends triaging the two together. There is no match in prior-headings.tsv or the earlier reports.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A22-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A22-02 — A cluster committed without a complete control link (control-interface + peer-address) has no peer detector under default private-RG election: both nodes primary when control-interface is absent, both secondary forever when only peer-address is absent; strict commit accepts every shape silently
- **Finding ID:** R3-A22-02

## #16747 — R3-A46-03: The tracker deletes an idle flow on inactive expiry, and nothing re-admits it. Resumed traffic is never polled, and the real close reports not sampled. [OPEN]

## Summary

The tracker deletes an idle flow on inactive expiry, and nothing re-admits it. Resumed traffic is never polled, and the real close reports not sampled.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. Volume is lost for every idle-then-resumed session, which is common (SSH, DB pools, keepalive). It is also a deterministic way to keep a transfer out of flow monitoring: open, idle for 16 s, then transfer. Enforcement is unaffected.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa.
  - `pkg/flowexport/tracker_15655.go:164-167`: `delete(t.flows, key)` on inactivity.
  - `:110-116` and `:134-139`: Touch returns for an unknown key.
  - `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:102-120`: the feed polls only `TrackedKeys()`.
  - `exporter_core.go:309-312`: `MarkFlowSampledAtOpen` is a no-op when the tracker is non-nil. It always is, because `manager.go:500-512` falls back to 60 s/15 s.
  - `daemon_flowexport.go:998-1001`: the close is dropped.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** Active flow monitoring exports and removes a flow after the inactive timeout. Later packets of the same session should produce a new flow record, not silence. The design comment at `tracker_15655.go:21-25` covers only duplicate suppression.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. It has a reachable trigger, the default timeouts apply, and the root cause is independent of R3-A46-08 (it remains after 08 is fixed).

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED at the exporter level with a no-idle-gap control. The daemon feed path is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High for the exporter mechanism. Daemon reachability is STATIC and straightforward.

## Impact

Interactive and pooled sessions idle for more than 15 s routinely. Their bulk volume, the part forensics care about, goes unreported, and exporter health stays green.

## Acceptance / fix direction

On inactive expiry keep a bounded sampled-idle marker. Re-arm the marker when the feed or the close shows progress. Export the post-expiry remainder at close, which is the lifetime total minus the final-record baseline. Acceptance: open → idle ≥ inactive → resume N packets → close exports the N-packet remainder exactly once.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16748 — The session-sync pre-auth accept path logs one INFO per accepted connection, ahead of the #5303 rate limiter, and one WARN per failed handshake. A PSK-less host on the sync segment drives about two journal lines per connection. [OPEN]

## Summary

The session-sync pre-auth accept path logs one INFO per accepted connection, ahead of the #5303 rate limiter, and one WARN per failed handshake. A PSK-less host on the sync segment drives about two journal lines per connection.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A22-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — this is log and journald pressure from an unauthenticated host that can reach the sync listener on the control/fabric segment. journald rate limiting can then drop genuine HA diagnostics. There is no protection or ownership impact.
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (pre-auth log-rate limiting on HA control-plane listeners; sibling of #10316) — real, and it contradicts the #5303 "cannot itself become a log flood" contract, but the consequence is bounded.

## Mechanism

Host → TCP connect :4785 → acceptLoop INFO → beginSetup admits → handleNewConnection → performSyncHandshake fails on 12 bytes of garbage (bad magic) → finishSetup frees the slot → WARN → close. Repeat.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:1392` `slog.Info("cluster sync: peer connected", "remote", conn.RemoteAddr(), "fabric", fabricIdx)` runs before `if !s.beginSetup(conn, true) { s.notePreAuthRejected(conn) ...}` at :1400-1404. `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:888-890` `slog.Warn("cluster sync: auth handshake failed, dropping connection", ...)` runs on every handshake error.

## Impact

An on-segment host can flood the journal and push journald into rate limiting, and that hides real failover and sync logs during the event the attacker would time this with. The scope is limited to hosts on the dedicated control/fabric segment.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Move "peer connected" after successful authentication, or log it at Debug pre-auth. Route the handshake-failure WARN through a per-SessionSync limiter like `heartbeatRejectWarnLimiter`, with a counter in sync stats. Acceptance: the probe's DEFECT line shows about 2 records/s or fewer under flood, and the counters reflect all rejections.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/cluster/sync_admission.go:137-150` (#5303): cap rejections log "at most ~1/sec so a sustained flood cannot itself become a log flood". The CLAUDE.md Logging Rules say never `slog.Info` per-session in a hot loop. #10316 established rate-limited pre-auth reject logging for the heartbeat siblings.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A22-03` (parts file `parts/va22.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A22-03 | Low | The session-sync pre-auth accept path logs one INFO per accepted connection, ahead of the…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): #10316 (CLOSED) fixed the heartbeat UDP pre-auth warns only. #10724 (CLOSED cohort) A5-F5 is the post-auth malformed-record WARN in sync_conn_read.go, a different site. #5303/#14371 cover the admission cap and reserve, not logging. muse-spark A5-16 notes that accept is not IP-pinned and makes no logging claim. There is no in-run duplicate.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A22-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16749 — A flat-set run headed by a valueless BGP flag (`passive`, `remove-private`, `log-updown`) carries typed leaves past the strict validators; `group G passive hold-time 1` renders `timers 1 1`, frr-reload.py fails, and every later reload is… [OPEN]

## Summary

A flat-set run headed by a valueless BGP flag (`passive`, `remove-private`, `log-updown`) carries typed leaves past the strict validators; `group G passive hold-time 1` renders `timers 1 1`, frr-reload.py fails, and every later reload is degraded; chained unknown keywords get no #10707 advisory

**Finding ID:** `R3-A11-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — a commit-clean config renders a line bgpd refuses. frr-reload.py exits 1, xpf falls back to the additive `vtysh -f` load and returns ErrFRRReloadDegraded on every reload until the line is found, and the configured hold-time is never applied. The same blind spot makes chained unknown keyword…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — one supported spelling (#8939 flat runs) bypasses every BGP schema value gate and reproduces the #14585 reload-poisoning state.

## Mechanism

`set protocols bgp group G passive hold-time 1` → SetPath chain `passive { hold-time 1; }` → SchemaValidate walks `hold-time` under `passive`'s nil schema and skips it (open world) → no error, no advisory → compile `expandFlatRun` hoists `hold-time 1` → `HoldTime=1` → render `timers 1 1` → frr-reload.py rc=1 → `vtysh -f` fallback → ErrFRRReloadDegraded on this and every later commit.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/schema_routing.go:511,519,556,564,493`: `passive`, `remove-private`, `log-updown` are childless leaves with no valueType or validator. `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:673` (`expandFlatRun(packedBodyChildren(groupInst.node, groupSchema), groupSchema)`) and `compiler_bgp_neighbor_merge_9192.go:306` (`expandFlatRun(expandResolvingRuns9792(...))`) hoist and apply the chained `hold-time`. `pkg/frr/protocols_render_bgp.go:126-130`: `keepalive := n.HoldTime / 3` ... `neighbor %s timers %d %d`, with no 1/2 belt. `pkg/config/compiler_openworld_10707.go:128-133`: the advisory walker `continue`s at a leaf with no declared children. `pkg/frr/manager.go:1693-1755`: a non-zero frr-reload.py exit leads to `vtysh -f` and `ErrFRRReloadDegraded`.

## Impact

The commit gate is the documented protection against reload-poisoning values. Once this line is committed, every subsequent commit reports a degraded FRR reload, and `show configuration` displays it as `passive { hold-time 1; }`, which is hard to spot. The chained-unknown silence also removes the only signal for dropped statements such as `authentication-key-chain`.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In the strict walker and the #10707 walker, when an untyped childless leaf has children inside a container whose compiler uses `expandFlatRun`/`flattenChainedChildren` (BGP top, group, neighbor), validate those children at the PARENT schema, the same expansion the compiler applies. Add a hold-time 1/2 render belt. Acceptance: the chained rows strict-reject with the separate-line message, chained unknown keywords warn, the 9156 gate gains a strict-path column, and the `hold-time 9` control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

`ValidateBGPHoldTime` (its own message: "FRR rejects 1/2 and a rejected timers line fails the whole reload"); #14585 (a commit-check-clean config must not render a line bgpd refuses); #9156 (an untyped leaf must not be an admission head that carries a run past the strict gate); #10707 (unknown leaves in routing subtrees must warn).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A11-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:21: - **R3-A11-02 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** scalar-arity validation only reaches typed or `scalar` leaves (`pkg/config/schema_walk.go:196-284,308-310`); valueless `passive`/`remove-private` flags under BGP have neither. The compiler hoists a flat-run child `hold-time 1` (`pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:673`), and renderer emits `neighbor ... timers 1 1` (`pkg/frr/protocols_render_bgp.go:122-130`), which the earlier FRR run rejected; the generic unknown-leaf walker likewise skips a flag's descendants (`pkg/config/compiler_openworld_10707.go:128-133`). **Best alternative:** separately authored `hold-time 1` is rejected, and most configurations will not chain modifiers under valueless flags; reloader's fallback error is *degraded* unless its `vtysh` load fails as well (`pkg/frr/manager.go:1699-1772`). **Remaining check:** current-version strict `Store.CommitCheck` for flat chained and separate controls, then FRR 10.6 reload for the generated `timers` line.

## #16750 — R3-A46-04: `deltaRecord` subtracts baselines without saturation, and Touch overwrites per-field counters with lower values. This is latent at the base revision because the live… [OPEN]

## Summary

`deltaRecord` subtracts baselines without saturation, and Touch overwrites per-field counters with lower values. This is latent at the base revision because the live feed never hits (R3-A46-08).

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low. At the base revision it is unreachable: the tracker record is fed only by the live feed, which misses every lookup, so record and baseline both stay 0. It becomes a Medium data-integrity problem (one record of about 2^64 poisons collector aggregates) as soon as R3-A46-08 is fixed, if live readings can move backward. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism

`pkg/flowexport/tracker_15655.go:192-195` @d1ea69f9aa: `r.Packets = f.record.Packets - f.lastPackets` (and the Bytes/Rev fields), unchecked. `:145-148`: TouchBidirectional overwrites each field. The activity test compares sums only (`:142`).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `exporter_core.go:176-205`: the close remainder uses `satSub` "Saturating at zero guards a close whose counters raced backwards … from wrapping". The authors' own invariant expects backward readings.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (flow-export tracker fidelity; must land with the R3-A46-08 fix). The defect is real, but there is no trigger at base.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED at unit level. Reachability is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High for the arithmetic. Low-Medium for post-08 reachability: mirror-row alternation between workers' copies is STATIC.

## Impact

Make Touch monotonic per field (max) and use `satSub` in `deltaRecord`, in the same change as R3-A46-08. Acceptance: the probe's second interim reports 0 forward and 900 reverse, never more than the lifetime total.

A fix should:

## #16751 — If the heartbeat receiver never starts, nothing confirms peer absence. A lone survivor whose control link has no address (for example, a direct control cable to a powered-off peer under networkd's ConfigureWithoutCarrier=false default) keeps every non-preempt RG SECONDARY indefinitely after a cold boot or xpfd restart. [OPEN]

## Summary

If the heartbeat receiver never starts, nothing confirms peer absence. A lone survivor whose control link has no address (for example, a direct control cable to a powered-off peer under networkd's ConfigureWithoutCarrier=false default) keeps every non-preempt RG SECONDARY indefinitely after a cold boot or xpfd restart.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A22-04`
**Severity (source report):** High — the consequence is HA availability and recovery. The surviving node of a dead pair forwards nothing for as long as the peer stays down, which is exactly the case HA exists for. Not even the 2-minute degraded fallback applies. The Go mechanism is demonstrated; the networkd trigger is documented but not executed.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable lifecycle trigger (peer chassis down, survivor reboot or restart, control cable without carrier) gives an unbounded forwarding outage on the survivor.

## Mechanism

The node0 chassis is dead, and node1 reboots or restarts xpfd, giving a fresh Manager (`peerEverSeen=false`). em0 has no carrier, so networkd does not configure it and there is no address. The heartbeat start loop exhausts, so no receiver is installed and `peerConfirmedAbsent` is never set. Every non-preempt RG (the shipped config sets no preempt) stays SECONDARY with no timer. In control-link mode the sync address poll also exhausts and marks `BindingChanged` (`daemon_ha_sync.go:1316-1337`). The #11448 reassert then restarts comms about every 30 s and repeats the same 60 s loop, which never succeeds while the peer is down.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:1681-1731` `startHeartbeatWithRetryForEpoch`: `localIP := resolveClusterInterfaceAddr(...)`. When it is empty, the loop sleeps 2 s and retries, 30 times, then calls `slog.Error("cluster heartbeat failed after retries")` and returns. `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go:1135` `m.peerConfirmedAbsent = true` is the only true-writer, and its only caller chain is `heartbeat.go:1383` in the receiver's checkTimeout. `pkg/cluster/election.go:133-135` and `:635` hold before the readiness gate, so `armDegradedTimerLocked` is never reached. `readiness.go:115/138` and `kernel_selfrecover.go:198` re-enter electSingleNode under the same hold. For the trigger: `pkg/networkd/networkd.go` emits no `ConfigureWithoutCarrier=`/`IgnoreCarrierLoss=`, and `keepConfigurationValue` (`networkd.go:1762-1772`) gives em0 no KeepConfiguration. systemd 262 systemd.network(5) (`RUN/workers/a22/evidence/systemd262-ConfigureWithoutCarrier.txt`) says ConfigureWithoutCarrier "Defaults to false" and IgnoreCarrierLoss "When false, systemd-networkd drops both the static and dynamic configuration".

## Impact

This hits bare-metal pairs with back-to-back control cables (the SRX-style deployment): power loss where only one node returns, or a survivor rebooted or upgraded while the peer is being repaired. The survivor never forwards, and status shows both RGs secondary with no degraded marker explaining why. Recovery needs the peer to return, a manual `preempt`, or a cable or bridge workaround.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Own the never-seen clock in the Manager, armed at UpdateConfig when a control link is configured, so absence is confirmed after the floor whether or not a receiver started. Alternatively, treat "heartbeat could not start" as never-seen evidence. Consider `ConfigureWithoutCarrier=yes` (and `IgnoreCarrierLoss=yes`) for the cluster control and fabric links. Acceptance: the DEFECT cells promote (degraded if not ready) after the floor, and the #4386/#11566 cells are unchanged. Lab: power off node0 of a direct-cabled pair, reboot node1, check `ip addr show em0` (expect no address) and the journal for `cluster heartbeat failed after retries`, and confirm both RGs are still secondary after 2 min.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:22-37`: the never-seen floor exists so that "a genuinely-absent peer (single-node deployment) still promotes once it elapses". The #7161/#10697 readiness gate promises a lone node promotion, at worst degraded after `DefaultDegradedPromoteTimeout` (2 min, `manager.go:773`).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A22-04` (parts file `parts/va22.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A22-04 | High | If the heartbeat receiver never starts, nothing confirms peer absence. A lone survivor…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): R3-F14-02 (vf14, MATERIAL Medium) is the bounded 2-minute fabric-readiness hold, which presumes the receiver's never-seen arm runs; here the arm never runs. #9751 (CLOSED) is restart-failure debt on a running node. #4386/#10697/#11566 tune the never-seen arm itself. vf02 cites a22's carrier-loss point only as a distinct HA-control-link item. Nothing in gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv or the earlier reports covers a lone node with no receiver.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A22-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16753 — The #7194 fail-closed delta-schema gate is not applied in `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig`. Under a mismatched helper delta-schema fingerprint the stream, drain and FullResync paths withhold, but every cold-prime, resync, retry and inventory bulk still frames the same `SessionDeltaInfo` export for the peer's authoritative reconcile. [OPEN]

## Summary

The #7194 fail-closed delta-schema gate is not applied in `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig`. Under a mismatched helper delta-schema fingerprint the stream, drain and FullResync paths withhold, but every cold-prime, resync, retry and inventory bulk still frames the same `SessionDeltaInfo` export for the peer's authoritative reconcile.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A23-02`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. A documented fail-closed HA integrity protection is missing on the one path the receiver treats as authoritative, and the operator is told that sync is withheld while the bulk keeps sending. The precondition is a running helper whose session-delta schema differs from the daemon's (upgrade/rollback skew, which #7194 itself calls "not hypothetical"). The demonstrated defect is the bypass. Zero-filled identity on the standby is the potential consequence #7194 describes, and it occurs only when the helper lacks a field the daemon expects. [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. The same export output is refused on three producers and shipped on the fourth, which is also the authoritative one. No guard or rationale for the exclusion exists.

## Mechanism

The running helper advertises a foreign `session_delta_schema_fingerprint` in ProcessStatus. The drain loop records it (`daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:1115/1129`). Stream, drain and FullResync batches are withheld, with a warning. A sync sweep, reconnect cold prime, survivor re-drive, unacked-bulk retry or peer inventory request runs `doBulkSyncWithBulkSend` -> `BulkSnapshotSource` -> `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig` -> `ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` (JSON `SessionDeltaInfo`, the transport on which a missing field decodes as 0) -> `walkUserspaceSessionDeltas` -> BulkStart/rows/BulkEnd. The peer installs the rows and authoritatively reconciles its table against that window.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

At d1ea69f9aa, `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_export.go:133-139` reads `deltas, _, err := exporter.ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged(rgIDs)` ... `d.walkUserspaceSessionDeltas(ss, buildZoneIDs(cfg), deltas, sink)` / `return sink.snapshot(), nil`, with no `userspaceDeltaSchemaAdmits` call, and the ProcessStatus is discarded. The only production callers of `userspaceDeltaSchemaAdmits` are `daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:1071` and `full_resync_transaction_9767.go:87`. `daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:468` sets `ss.BulkSnapshotSource = d.userspaceBulkSnapshot`. `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:89-130` calls `snap, err := src()` and fails closed only when `err != nil`. Observation: `UserspaceDeltaSchemaWithheldCount` (`daemon_ha_delta_schema_7194.go:126-131`) has no production reader at base, so the only operator signal is the once-per-episode warning "withholding session-delta sync".

## Impact

During the skew window the gate was built for, the operator sees "withholding session-delta sync" while the standby keeps receiving full authoritative snapshots built from the unvalidated decode. A failover then runs on those rows. The blast radius is every RG primed or re-driven during the skew, and it lasts until the helper and daemon agree. The outcome is the opposite of the "loud, fail-closed" posture #7194 documents.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig`, record the export's returned ProcessStatus fingerprint (`recordUserspaceDeltaSchema`) and return an error when `userspaceDeltaSchemaAdmits` refuses. That makes `doBulkSync` fail closed and leaves the cold-prime/resync obligation armed. Update the `docs/session-sync-architecture.md` #7194 section to list the bulk producer, and give the withheld counter a real `show`/status reader. Acceptance: the probe's mismatch arm returns a non-nil error with `framed_v4=0` and advances the withheld counter, the match arm still frames 1, and the existing *6031*/*7194*/*9767* tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)
