## #16755 — `deprovisionLoginUser` infers shell ownership from the account marker, but `reconcileUserPassword` writes that marker for any pre-existing account whose password xpf sets. A pre-existing account whose shell already equals the class... [OPEN]

## Summary
`deprovisionLoginUser` infers shell ownership from the account marker, but `reconcileUserPassword` writes that marker for any pre-existing account whose password xpf sets. A pre-existing account whose shell already equals the class shell (e.g. /bin/bash for super-user) therefore gets `usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin` although xpf never set its shell.

**Finding ID:** R3-F01-03
**Severity (source):** Low — the only loss is the operator's out-of-band SSH-key login on an account they removed from xpf config; the xpf-set password is legitimately locked anyway. Recoverable as root. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
It regresses the overclaim axis #5841/#6797 closed: an operator's own key-based access to a host account is disabled by a config deletion of an xpf user whose shell xpf never touched.

**Contract:** `pkg/daemon/login_password.go` deprovision doc: revoke "only ... a login shell it set (or granted at useradd)" and "never an operator-managed credential it did not provision". The account-marker doc (`:40-43`) itself says the marker records the UID "at the time xpf created it or set its password".

**Trace:** pre-existing `bob` (/bin/bash, own authorized_keys) → `set system login user bob class super-user authentication encrypted-password ...` → shell unchanged (no shell marker), password applied (password + account markers) → user removed → `deprovisionLoginUser` locks the password and, via `ownsAccount`, resets the shell to nologin.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/daemon/login_password.go:832` `ownsShell = ownsShell || ownsAccount`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:849` `acctClaim, err = claimOwnershipFenced14969(provisionedUsersDir, user.Name, curUID)` in `pwApply` for existing accounts. `daemon_hostauth_apply.go:325-345` claims the shell marker only `if found && currentShell != shell`. `loginShellForClass` maps super-user to `/bin/bash` (`:141-145`).

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf01/probes/zz_vf01_shell_bash_test.go` (f01's probe with the pre-existing shell set to /bin/bash, equal to the super-user class shell), `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestVF01S -v`, output `vf01-03-daemon.out`: "account-marker=true shell-marker=false usermod=[]", then on removal "usermod calls=[[usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin -- bob]] shell=\"/usr/sbin/nologin\"". Control (key-only marker) gives "usermod=[] shell=\"/bin/bash\"". Limit: `applySystemLogin` itself was not run; that it writes no shell marker when shells are equal is a static read.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Write a shell marker in the useradd branch (where xpf chooses `-s`) and derive shell ownership only from the shell marker. Acceptance: the class-shell-equal cell keeps /bin/bash; `TestDeprovisionLoginUserResetsInteractiveShellToNologin` (useradd-created) still resets.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf01.md)</summary>

### R3-F01-03 — #14695 resets a pre-existing operator account's login shell to nologin on removal because the password path writes the "account" marker that deprovision now reads as shell ownership
- **Finding ID:** R3-F01-03
- **Title:** `deprovisionLoginUser` infers shell ownership from the account marker, but `reconcileUserPassword` writes that marker for any pre-existing account whose password xpf sets. A pre-existing account whose shell already equals the class shell (e.g. /bin/bash for super-user) therefore gets `usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin` although xpf never set its shell.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker f01 (Fix-residual hunter (delta group 01)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vf01
- **Severity:** Low — the only loss is the operator's out-of-band SSH-key login on an account they removed from xpf config; the xpf-set password is legitimately locked anyway. Recoverable as root. [reporter: Low]
- **Confidence:** High — EXECUTED with the realistic class-shell-equal shape; the `applySystemLogin` shell-claim condition is read statically.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — Go daemon test with fake passwd/shadow/chpasswd/usermod.
- **Gate verdict:** COHORT (login-account provenance / deprovision overclaim, with #5841/#6797/#14695) — real, but a minor violation of the never-touch-non-xpf-credentials invariant.
- **Contract:** `pkg/daemon/login_password.go` deprovision doc: revoke "only ... a login shell it set (or granted at useradd)" and "never an operator-managed credential it did not provision". The account-marker doc (`:40-43`) itself says the marker records the UID "at the time xpf created it or set its password".
- **Adversarial analysis:** Protection: the #5841 per-resource ownership split. Actor: an operator managing a host account partly outside xpf. Challenged assumption: "account marker ⇒ xpf created the account at useradd".
- **Evidence:** `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:832` `ownsShell = ownsShell || ownsAccount`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:849` `acctClaim, err = claimOwnershipFenced14969(provisionedUsersDir, user.Name, curUID)` in `pwApply` for existing accounts. `daemon_hostauth_apply.go:325-345` claims the shell marker only `if found && currentShell != shell`. `loginShellForClass` maps super-user to `/bin/bash` (`:141-145`).

Control (key-only marker) gives "usermod=[] shell=\"/bin/bash\"". Limit: `applySystemLogin` itself was not run; that it writes no shell marker when shells are equal is a static read.
- **Trace:** pre-existing `bob` (/bin/bash, own authorized_keys) → `set system login user bob class super-user authentication encrypted-password ...` → shell unchanged (no shell marker), password applied (password + account markers) → user removed → `deprovisionLoginUser` locks the password and, via `ownsAccount`, resets the shell to nologin.

## #16756 — The #9569 config-stale gate requires a type-40 config-apply ACK and has no peer-capability fallback. Against a connected peer whose build predates 28556c2b19, the bare ISSU verb and untargeted/batch failover refuse forever with a misleading reason. The rolling and kernel-drain verbs do the same only against a pre-#7990 peer on an unkeyed pair. [OPEN]

## Summary

The #9569 config-stale gate requires a type-40 config-apply ACK and has no peer-capability fallback. Against a connected peer whose build predates 28556c2b19, the bare ISSU verb and untargeted/batch failover refuse forever with a misleading reason. The rolling and kernel-drain verbs do the same only against a pre-#7990 peer on an unkeyed pair.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A24-01`
**Severity (source report):** Low — fail-closed. No enforcement loss and no dual-primary. The trigger is confined to a mixed-version window. Planned handover off the new node is blocked, and so is the rolling rollback in the pre-#7990 case. The escape is an unplanned stop of xpfd, which gives up the drain barrier. The operator is sent looking for a config-apply failure that never happened. [reporter: Low (borderline Medium)]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (HA mixed-version handover gating) — real fail-closed refusal with a misleading reason; reachable only in a narrowed mixed-version window, with an unplanned-failover escape.

## Mechanism

unkeyed pair, base node N is RG0 primary, peer O runs a pre-2026-08-29 build (or any pre-28556c2b19 build for the ungated verbs) -> O connects (an unkeyed N never handshakes) -> `reconcileConfigSyncToPeer` pushes (cleartext to a pre-#6629 peer) -> lastSentConfigGen=G -> O applies but has no type-40 frame -> peerAppliedConfigGen stays 0 -> on N, `request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group K`, the batch form, bare `request system software in-service-upgrade`, or `xpfd upgrade --rollback --rolling` / kernel drain (wire 0 permitted) -> ErrPeerConfigStale "standby has not acknowledged applying config generation G". The state persists until O is upgraded or N's comms restart. A node-targeted request from O lands in N's OnRemoteFailover, which calls the same gated ManualFailover (daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:491-501).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/peer_config_stale_9569.go:52-58 `sent := s.lastSentConfigGen.Load(); applied := s.peerAppliedConfigGen.Load(); if sent != 0 && applied < sent { return true, ...}`, with no capability term. The daemon wrapper pkg/daemon/peer_config_stale_9569.go:7-12 passes it straight through. pkg/cluster/failover.go:131, :232 and :989 run `peerConfigStaleRefusal` first. sync_conn_config.go:344/:472/:497 record the sent generation on every push. sync_config_recv.go:65-69 is the only advance of peerAppliedConfigGen. `git grep syncMsgConfigApplyAck 28556c2b19^ -- pkg/cluster` returns nothing, and 28556c2b19 (2026-09-28) is an ancestor of the base. Narrowing evidence: pkg/cluster/sync.go:69 `SessionSyncWireVersion = uint16(3)` was bumped 2->3 at 6556ce24d8 (2026-10-19). Builds from 2026-08-29 (cbe601c4fa, v2) through 6556ce24d8 are wire 2. pkg/upgrade/rolling.go:332-338 (rollback) and :493-504 (forward) refuse a wire mismatch before ForceSecondary (:348/:529), as does kernel_drain.go:93. rolling.go:35-37 and sync_wire_version_7990.go:82-87 permit peer wire 0. cli_request_system.go:345 and grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:676 call ForceSecondary with no wire gate. sync_auth.go:28-29: "a node with no key never handshakes and is byte-for-byte a legacy peer".

## Impact

Operators mid-upgrade or mid-rollback from an old unkeyed build cannot move RGs off the new node in a controlled way. The error points at a config-apply failure that did not happen. Recovery is to finish upgrading the old node, or to force an unplanned failover by stopping xpfd.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Have the peer advertise ACK support as an incarnation-scoped bit in syncMsgPeerCapabilities. For a peer that does not advertise it, fall back to the pre-28556c2b19 semantics (stale iff the newest sent generation was NACKed), and name the reason as "peer predates config-apply ACK". Acceptance: the legacy-peer probe passes ForceSecondary/ManualFailover when the capability is absent and no NACK was received, while an ACK-capable peer that NACKs or stays silent is still refused.

## Contract (where cited)

pkg/cluster/peer_config_stale_9569.go:8-26 says the gate refuses only a standby that "did not apply the newest config generation this node sent". pkg/cluster/sync_wire_version_7990.go:64-96 deliberately PERMITS a peer that advertises no wire version (pre-#7990), "refusing here would block the very rolling upgrade that introduces the advertisement". So rolling from a pre-#7990 build is a supported procedure. docs/in-place-upgrade.md documents the rolling forms and `--rollback --rolling` as the guarded HA path.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A24-01` (parts file `parts/va24.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A24-01 | Low | The #9569 config-stale gate requires a type-40 config-apply ACK and has no peer-capability…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): I checked #9569 (CLOSED; it introduced the gate), D61-04 (gemini 500-001: ACK lost on fabric loss), G24-03 (gemini vsrx-002: CarryingGen and fabric switchover), D34-03 (gemini 200-001: gate bypass in the opposite direction) and r2 A24-02 (the #9530 mark keyed on reachability). None names the mixed-version / missing-capability cause, so this is distinct. Greps of gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports and drafts/parts for apply-ack, PeerConfigStale and legacy peer found nothing else.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A24-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A24-01 — Some handovers refuse permanently against a connected peer that predates the config-apply ACK, and the refusal wrongly says the standby did not apply the config: the bare ISSU verb and untargeted/batch failover against any such peer, and the rolling and kernel-drain verbs only against a pre-#7990 peer on an unkeyed pair
- **Finding ID:** R3-A24-01

## #16757 — R3-A46-07: The "is my source still assigned" canary uses prefix containment. A DHCP/SLAAC renumber within the same subnet leaves IPv4 export parked on the dead socket, and IPv6… [OPEN]

## Summary

The "is my source still assigned" canary uses prefix containment. A DHCP/SLAAC renumber within the same subnet leaves IPv4 export parked on the dead socket, and IPv6 export is never re-dialed while health reads healthy.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. This is the same consequence as r2 A46-01/#15073 (Medium), for the most common renumber shape. IPv4 export stops until a commit or restart. On IPv6, the #15073 canary redial never fires and health stays healthy.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-07`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-07`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/flowexport/transport.go:113` @d1ea69f9aa: `if pfx, err := netip.ParsePrefix(v.String()); err == nil && pfx.Contains(needle) { return true }`. `sourceStale` (`:153-172`) returns `!addrIsAssigned(host)` after the 2-minute grace. The #15073 fixture builds only host masks (`collector_redial_15073_test.go:101`, `CIDRMask(bits, bits)`).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/flowexport/transport.go:481-489` (#15073): "a still-healthy collector whose implicit source was renumbered away … Re-dial those canary-stale sockets BEFORE the write fan-out". The write-failure path re-dials only if `sourceStale()` (`:560-567`).

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. The #15073 fix is effective only for cross-prefix renumbers. The same-prefix case is reachable on DHCP/SLAAC management sources.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. Defect arms and host-mask control arms ran for v4 and v6, and the real `net.InterfaceAddrs` was shown returning on-link masks.

**Confidence:** High for the predicate (executed with the production `*net.IPNet` shape). Medium for the IPv6 on-wire behaviour after address removal, which depends on the kernel and is inherited from the r2 finding without re-measurement.

## Impact

fxp0/management-sourced export on DHCP or SLAAC is a common branch setup. Export silently stops (v4) or keeps an un-owned source (v6) after an ordinary lease change.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Treat the source as assigned only when an assigned address's IP equals it, ignoring the mask. Optionally cache the address set with netlink-event refresh. Acceptance: both a46 defect arms flip (v6 unhealthy plus redial; v4 redial plus delivery), and the host-mask controls stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A46-07`, part `parts/va46.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16758 — An IPsec SA full set over 4096 names is refused whole, and the sender neither fits the bound nor alarms, so the standby keeps a stale set and re-initiates it on takeover [OPEN]

## Summary

An IPsec SA full set over 4096 names is refused whole, and the sender neither fits the bound nor alarms, so the standby keeps a stale set and re-initiates it on takeover

**Finding ID:** `R3-A24-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — the consequence is missed or stale re-initiation on RG takeover, not lost enforcement. Tunnels still recover through the remote peer, DPD or trap traffic. Reaching it needs more than 4096 distinct active child-SA names. [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (HA full-set sync bounds without a sender-side fit or alarm) — real and silent on the primary, but limited reach and recoverable consequence.

## Mechanism

primary with more than 4096 active child SAs -> advertise loop -> QueueIPsecSA (about 78 KB, far below the 16 MiB frame cap) -> standby decode refuses -> peerIPsecSAs frozen at the last set of 4096 or fewer (or empty) -> RG takeover -> reinitiateIPsecSAs initiates the frozen set.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

pkg/cluster/sync_protocol.go:1131-1135 `maxIPsecSANames = 4096` ("far outside what this product targets"), :1174 `if len(names) >= maxIPsecSANames { return nil, true }`. pkg/cluster/sync_lease_recv.go:36-46: when malformed, Warn "refusing a malformed IPsec SA full set" and return, keeping the prior set and leaving the sequence unconsumed and IPsecSAStaleIgnored unchanged. Sender: pkg/cluster/sync.go:2793 `QueueIPsecSA` has no count check, and pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:2549-2575 advertises `ipsecActiveNames()` unbounded. Reinit uses the held set at daemon_ha.go:2627.

## Impact

At extreme selector counts, failover silently leaves current tunnels uninitiated and can resurrect old ones. The only signal is a repeating Warn on the standby.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Chunk the set as #15160 does, or raise the bound and make the sender refuse visibly and raise an alarm on the PRIMARY above it. Count the refusal in a receiver stat. Acceptance: a 5000-name set round-trips to the standby, and an over-bound set raises an operator-visible alarm and counter.

## Contract (where cited)

daemon_ha.go IPsec SA advertise/reinit (#4385/#9139): the standby must hold the primary's current active set, so that takeover re-initiates what the peer held and does not resurrect dropped tunnels. The repo's own rule for full sets, stated in the decoder comment, is that "a full set REPLACES", so the sender has to fit the receiver's bound (the precedent is #15160 DHCP chunking).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A24-02` (parts file `parts/va24.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A24-02 | Low | An IPsec SA full set over 4096 names is refused whole, and the sender neither fits the…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): Greps of gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports and drafts/parts for maxIPsecSANames, "4096 names" and IPsec SA set refusal found only passing mentions. #9061 introduced the bound and #13541 (CLOSED) concerns sequence admission order, so neither is the owner. New.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A24-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16759 — `compileIPsec` and the traffic-selector shape validator read `traffic-selector` as a direct child only. A selector chained after `gateway`/`ipsec-policy`/`bind-interface` in one set command is therefore lost, with no error, while the... [OPEN]

## Summary
`compileIPsec` and the traffic-selector shape validator read `traffic-selector` as a direct child only. A selector chained after `gateway`/`ipsec-policy`/`bind-interface` in one set command is therefore lost, with no error, while the display-set view keeps showing it.

**Finding ID:** R3-F01-04
**Severity (source):** Medium — the authored IPsec SA scope is silently replaced. On a route-based VPN the negotiated and installed selectors widen from the authored prefixes to any↔any, which breaks against narrow-selector peers (TS_UNACCEPTABLE) or widens the inbound inner-address scope; zone policy on st0 still applies. The selector's own validation (#4098 injection and shape gate) is also bypassed for the dropped values, though they never reach swanctl. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The operator sees a clean commit, and `show configuration` shows the selector, while the tunnel negotiates any↔any. Against narrow-selector peers the tunnel fails to establish; otherwise the SA accepts any inner address. Diagnosis is hard because the config appears correct.

**Contract:** #9088/#10327: a packed run under `security ipsec vpn` keeps every declared leaf (`compiler_ipsec.go:843-849` comment). #14684 required the chained form to match the braced and split verdict. #8704 treats silent loss of an authored traffic-selector as a defect.

**Trace:** `set security ipsec vpn v1 gateway gw1 ipsec-policy epol1 bind-interface st0.0 traffic-selector ts1 local-ip 10.1.0.0/24 remote-ip 10.2.0.0/24` → SetPath nests `traffic-selector` inside the run → SchemaValidate and strict compile pass → `vpn.TrafficSelectors` empty → `EffectiveTrafficSelectors` (shared by swanctl render and the dataplane selector fence) → `local_ts = remote_ts = 0.0.0.0/0,::/0`.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go:850` `for _, p := range expandIPsecVPNRun9088(inst.node)` (run-aware leaves). `:925` `for _, tsInst := range namedInstances(inst.node.FindChildren("traffic-selector"))` (direct only). `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_trafficselector.go:84` uses the same direct `FindChildren`. `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:871-940`: with no TS and `xfrmiIfID(vpn.BindInterface) > 0` (`:933`), both sides default to `config.IPsecRouteBasedDefaultTrafficSelector`.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf01/probes/zz_vf01_chained_ts_test.go`, `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestVF01ChainedTS' -v`, output `vf01-04-config.out`. "chained-full" and "chained-bind-only" give "strict OK gw=\"gw1\" pol=\"epol1\" bind=\"st0.0\" TS=0" for the set tree, the hierarchical round trip and the display-set round trip. Controls "ts-chained-own-run" and "split" give TS=1 `{ts1 10.1.0.0/24 10.2.0.0/24}`. `TestVF01ChainedTSSchemaValidate`: chained `local-ip not-a-prefix` gives "SchemaValidate err=<nil> strict err=<nil>", while the split form is rejected by the #4098 selector gate. f01's ipsec probe re-run (`vf01-04-ipsec-rerun.out`): chained gives "effective=[{Name:v1 LocalTS:0.0.0.0/0,::/0 RemoteTS:0.0.0.0/0,::/0}]"; split gives `{v1-ts1 10.1.0.0/24 10.2.0.0/24}`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Read `traffic-selector` instances from `expandIPsecVPNRun9088(inst.node)` (including the compact tail) in both `compileIPsec` and `validateIPsecTrafficSelectorsStrict`, or strict-reject a selector nested in a run. Acceptance: the chained cells compile to TS=1 with the authored prefixes (and an invalid chained local-ip is rejected); the split controls are unchanged.

## #16760 — R3-A46-08: The live counter feed builds `dataplane.SessionKey` with host-order ports, but the map keys carry `__be16` ports. Every lookup misses, so with the default 60 s/15 s… [OPEN]

## Summary

The live counter feed builds `dataplane.SessionKey` with host-order ports, but the map keys carry `__be16` ports. Every lookup misses, so with the default 60 s/15 s timeouts every sampled flow longer than 15 s is exported as one 0-packet/0-byte inactive record and its real close is suppressed.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. NetFlow/IPFIX volume is lost for every flow longer than 15 s in the default configuration, which is where most bytes are. Collectors receive a zero-byte record, and exporter stats still count it as exported. Enforcement is unaffected. The demonstrated impact is monitoring/forensic accounting, so the severity is not High.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A46-08`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va46.md` (finding `R3-A46-08`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

All at d1ea69f9aa.
  - `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:150-153`: `store.GetV4(dataplane.SessionKey{SrcIP: src, DstIP: dst, SrcPort: key.SrcPort, DstPort: key.DstPort, Protocol: key.Protocol})`. The v6 twin is at `:144`. FlowKey ports come from `parseSrcPort` (host numbers, `:1099`).
  - Store chain: `userspace/manager.go:1057-1061` → `dataplane/session_store.go:289-294` → `dataplane/maps_session.go:92-105` `sm.Lookup(key, &val)`, with no conversion anywhere.
  - Writer: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bpf_map/mod.rs:608-623` `src_port: src_port.to_be(), // __be16 on the wire; SessionKey holds host order`.
  - Convention witnesses: `daemon_ha_userspace_convert.go:261-265` `userspaceHostToNetwork16`, and `grpcapi/server_sessions.go:676` `ntohs(key.SrcPort)`.
  - Miss path: `feedFlowLiveCounters` (`:102-120`) skips Touch, so `lastActivity` stays at the open. `tracker_15655.go:164-167` evicts at 15 s with a 0/0 `deltaRecord`, and the close's `CloseFlow` then reports not tracked (`daemon_flowexport.go:998-1001`).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:70-74` (#16303 F5) says the live poll exists so that "the active timer [does not export] zero counters for long-lived flows and the inactive timer [does not forget] continuously-active flows as idle". This is the fix for H14-03/V17-02 ("TouchFlow never called in production"), closed by #15946 at the base commit.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. The default configuration reaches it, and the consequence (volume loss plus a suppressed close) is concrete. It survived the guard search and dedup.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. Go production `liveFlowCounters` (seam nil) ran against a fake byte-keyed store. The existing Rust test `bpf_conntrack_key_port_byte_order` ran and passed. The a46 end-to-end consequence probe was re-run.

**Confidence:** High. The production lookup was executed against a byte-keyed map with the Rust layout, and the Rust layout is pinned by an existing passing Rust test. The only unexecuted link is the real kernel `bpf_map_lookup_elem`, which compares key bytes exactly as the fake does.

## Impact

Every deployment with flow export reports every long TCP/UDP session (bulk transfer, VPN, streaming, exfiltration) as zero bytes. Active interims never fire because flows are evicted at 15 s, before the 60 s active timer. It persists until a fix ships, and nothing is operator-visible.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Convert both ports with `userspaceHostToNetwork16` (v4 and v6). Add a live-feed miss counter. Add a test that runs the real `liveFlowCounters` against a key written through the production encoder. Fix R3-A46-04 in the same change. Acceptance: the probe's Rust-layout arm returns `ok=true`, and a lab flow longer than 60 s shows non-zero active interims plus a close remainder.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## Summary

**Finding ID:** `R3-A24-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — an operator-facing contradiction. It prescribes a controlled single-node outage plus permanent out-of-band dual-node config management to avoid a passive-observer exposure that no longer exists between same-vintage peers. [reporter: Low]

## Mechanism

operator reads "Generating and distributing the key" -> deletes configuration-synchronize and runs the controlled-outage sequence -> keeps config sync off indefinitely, waiting for #6629, which closed two months before the base.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

It no longer does against a peer of the same vintage", and :3112-3116 "On an AUTHENTICATED (Noise-keyed) connection there is no cleartext fallback at all (#15041)". `gh issue view`: #6629 CLOSED 2026-08-22, #15041 CLOSED 2026-10-19.

## Impact

Operators keying a running cluster follow this section. It steers them to an outage and to giving up config sync for no current benefit.

## Contract (where cited)

CLAUDE.md and docs/engineering-style.md treat module READMEs as part of the contract, which must be updated in the same change. ## #16762 — A term's route-filters render as one first-match FRR prefix-list (walkup/OR semantics) instead of the Junos default longest-match, so a more-specific filter whose match type fails no longer ends evaluation [OPEN]

## Summary

A term's route-filters render as one first-match FRR prefix-list (walkup/OR semantics) instead of the Junos default longest-match, so a more-specific filter whose match type fails no longer ends evaluation

**Finding ID:** `R3-A11-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — routing-policy enforcement diverges from Junos for the common "aggregate orlonger plus more-specific exact/upto exception" pattern. Import accept terms admit more-specifics Junos rejects (hijack/leak protection lost), export terms advertise routes Junos withholds, and reject terms drop rout…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — commit-clean Junos policy is evaluated with the opposite of the Junos default semantics, and no diagnostic is issued.

## Mechanism

`term cust from { route-filter 192.168.0.0/16 orlonger; route-filter 192.168.100.0/24 exact; } then accept; term last then reject` → `PolicyTerm.RouteFilters` → inline prefix-list seq 5/10 → `route-map IMPORT permit 10 match ip address prefix-list` → 192.168.100.128/25 hits seq 5 → term matches → accepted (Junos: rejected by `last`).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/frr/prefix_list_render.go:33` `renderRouteFilterEntry` emits each filter as an independent `seq (idx+1)*5 permit` line in authored order, into one list per term and family. `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1080-1081` states the OR model. There is no longest-match or overlap handling in `pkg/config` or `pkg/frr`, and no warning for overlapping filters.

## Impact

"Accept the customer /16 and longer, but only the exact /24 for this block" and "reject the bogon aggregate except an exact more-specific" are standard Junos idioms. Migrated configs commit clean and admit or advertise prefixes the operator meant to exclude.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Per term and family, emit entries in descending base-prefix-length order (stable for equal prefixes), and after each distinct prefix P emit `deny P le <max>`, so that a route under P that fails P's match type cannot fall through to a broader entry. Alternatively, strict-reject overlapping filters with differing match types until this is implemented. Acceptance: 192.168.100.128/25 first-matches a deny, 192.168.100.0/24 and 192.168.5.0/24 permit, and single or disjoint lists render byte-identically.

## Contract (where cited)

Juniper, "Understanding Route Filters for Use in Routing Policy Match Conditions" (fetched): "The policy framework software performs a longest-match lookup"; "The route filter stops evaluating other prefixes, even if the match type fails"; walkup (opt-in) changes the behaviour from "if one fails, then the term fails" to "if one matches, then the term matches". xpf does not model walkup.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A11-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A11-03 | Medium | A term's route-filters render as one first-match FRR prefix-list (walkup/OR semantics)… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:15: - **R3-A10-03 — DUP of R3-A11-03.** **Defect:** broader filter wins in FRR where Junos more-specific `exact` filter should stop matching. **Refutation to separate filing:** same ordered prefix-list renderer, same input, fix and acceptance as A11-03 (`pkg/frr/prefix_list_render.go:23-33,175-184`). **Remaining check:** fold its previous independent route-filter example into A11-03 coverage rather than creating a second issue.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L19: | R3-A11-03 route-filter longest-match vs OR | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-04 community `\| ` vty pipe refusal | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-05 community regex per-community vs joined | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A11-06 RR allow-outbound-policy missing | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-01 duplicate OSPF router-id in RG split | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-03 RIP per-group export flattened | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-05 VL-only area on standby hard-fails apply | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-02 BFD-default perpetual --test diff | COHORT | Low | | R3-A12-04 OSPF key >16/>8 truncation + perpetual diff | COHORT | Low |

## #16764 — An RFC 5798 address owner (virtual-address equal to its own unit address, priority 255) commits strict-clean, then sends no IPv4 advertisements and deletes its own interface address at every start and stop [OPEN]

## Summary

An RFC 5798 address owner (virtual-address equal to its own unit address, priority 255) commits strict-clean, then sends no IPv4 advertisements and deletes its own interface address at every start and stop

**Finding ID:** `R3-A25-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — for as long as the config stays in place, the owner sends no IPv4 VRRP advertisement. Every other router in the group therefore times the owner out and also claims MASTER, which gives a duplicate gateway IP and an ARP fight. The node also loses its own unit address for about 3 s on every instance start, and keeps it lost after a stop. The impact is bounded to standalone `vrrp-group` IPv4 owners; RETH-derived instances never have VIP == unit address. The dual-MASTER outcome on a second router is potential, not demonstrated.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a committable, RFC-defined owner configuration silently produces a non-advertising MASTER and strips the node's own address.

## Mechanism

`interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24 { vrrp-group 1 { virtual-address 10.0.1.1/24; priority 255; } }` → strict `CompileConfig` accepts → `CollectInstances` builds VIP 10.0.1.1/24 → `run()` removeVIPs deletes the unit address and sits in BACKUP for about 3 s (not straight to Master per §6.4.1) → becomeMaster re-adds it → every IPv4 `sendAdvert` fails, Debug-logged → peers hear nothing → on Stop resignForShutdown deletes the address again.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/vrrp/instance_addr.go:152-155` `if ip4 == nil || vipSet[ip4.String()] { continue }` (the source selector drops VIPs; for an owner that is its only address). `pkg/vrrp/instance_send.go:160-173` lazy re-resolve, then `return fmt.Errorf("no IPv4 address on %s", ...)`; `instance_send.go:101-103` logs it at `slog.Debug` only. `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1205` `staleErr := vi.removeVIPs()` at run start; `instance_transition.go:215` `removeVIPsLocked(nil)` in becomeBackup; `instance.go:1346` in resignForShutdown. Each deletes every VIP, which for an owner is the real unit address. Commit gates: `pkg/config/dup_host_local_address.go:403-423` records unit addresses and VIPs only for the cross-zone check; the vipprefix/vipcount/vipcrossgroup/vipempty/timers/identity validators never compare a VIP with its own unit's addresses (observed by reading each).

## Impact

Any operator who configures the RFC/textbook owner gets a gateway that is MASTER on two routers at once, silently: `show vrrp` reports MASTER and the advert failure is Debug-only. BGP/SSH/DHCP sessions bound to that address drop on every xpfd restart. It persists until the config changes.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Either reject at commit a virtual-address equal to any address of its own unit, with a named error, or implement owner semantics: when a VIP is also a configured unit address, use it as the advert source, never `AddrDel` it on BACKUP/stop, and transition straight to MASTER at start (§6.4.1). Acceptance: in the probe, the subject row shows adverts sent > 0 and `present=true` at every checkpoint, or the strict compile rejects the shape, with the control row unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

RFC 5798 (rfc-editor.org text, section numbers verified): §1.6 "IP Address Owner: The VRRP router that has the virtual router's IPvX address(es) as real interface address(es)"; §5.2.4 the owner's priority "MUST be 255"; §5.1.1.1 the IPv4 advert source "is the primary IPv4 address of the interface"; §6.4.1 an owner in Initialize sends an ADVERTISEMENT and transitions to Master at once. pkg/vrrp/README.md:283-288 says an explicit 255 "is how an operator declares the address owner".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A25-01` (parts file `parts/va25.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A25-01 | Medium | An RFC 5798 address owner (virtual-address equal to its own unit address, priority 255)…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): gh-issues.tsv: #4116 (CLOSED) is the owner no-preempt reclaim rule; #14407 is cross-group VIP overlap; #15050/#15061/#6779/#7577 cover other VIP shapes. None covers VIP == own unit address. Checked prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports (the "address owner" hits are unrelated WireGuard/IPv6-PD uses), and all RUN/drafts/parts and worker reports (va06, vf11, a21, a60, a69 and f11 mention "owner" in other senses). New.

## #16765 — #14720 predecessor backup is taken after PREFLIGHT, so a failed re-stage of the committed predecessor permanently replaces its rollback DB snapshot with the live (newer-era) DB [OPEN]

## Summary
#14720 predecessor backup is taken after PREFLIGHT, so a failed re-stage of the committed predecessor permanently replaces its rollback DB snapshot with the live (newer-era) DB

**Finding ID:** R3-F02-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — durable rollback-state corruption: the predecessor's `.<ver>.dbsnap` silently holds the wrong-era DB, so a later rollback from that version restores the wrong config into the older binary (or is refused by the envelope gate). Demonstrated at the snapshot level; the multi-step rollback consequence is traced, not executed. Bounded by a rare trigger (failed predecessor re-stage, then a two-step rollback).
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
The operator is told the rollback target was preserved; the corruption is silent and durable, and surfaces only at the next rollback down the chain, when the box restores config from the wrong era or refuses the rollback.

**Contract:** Commit be8b2bc8a4 (#14720) preserves the committed predecessor's stamp and `.<ver>.dbsnap` across a failed re-stage; pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:1939-1941 says "The restore above already reinstalled the backup copy if this cut's PREFLIGHT overwrote it". `.<V>.dbsnap` is the DB to restore when rolling back FROM V (rollback.go:169).

**Trace:** live 2.0.0 (committed predecessor 1.0.0) → stage tag 1.0.0 → Run → PREFLIGHT rewrites `.1.0.0.dbsnap` := live DB → backup copies it → COPY → VERIFY fails → cleanupFailedVerifyCopy skips removal → restore is a no-op (snapshot exists) → later rollback 2.0.0→1.0.0 (uses `.2.0.0.dbsnap`, fine) → rollback 1.0.0→its stamped predecessor restores `.1.0.0.dbsnap` = 2.0.0-era DB.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:754 `if err := r.preflight(j)` → cutover.go:1468 `return r.snapshotConfigDB(j)` → cutover.go:1504 `snapDir := … "."+j.TargetVersion+".dbsnap"`, then `_ = os.RemoveAll(snapDir)` + `os.Rename(snapPartial, snapDir)` (copy of the LIVE DB). cutover.go:818 `predecessorBackup = r.backupCommittedPredecessor(j, j.TargetVersion)` runs only after that. commit_stamp.go:123-147 copies whatever `.<ver>.dbsnap` holds now; commit_stamp.go:183 restores only `if _, err := os.Stat(snap); os.IsNotExist(err)`. The resume branch cutover.go:796 also re-snapshots before the backup. rollback.go does not rewrite `.<to>.dbsnap`, so the bad copy persists. Observation: content swap. Inference: the wrong-era restore on the second rollback.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -run 'TestProbeR3F02|TestVerifyFailure_PreservesCommittedPredecessor14720' -count=1 -v` (fixture RUN/workers/f02/evidence/probe_r3f02_predbak_test.go, copy + output RUN/verify/vf02/probes/02-upgrade.out): `original .1.0.0.dbsnap/active.json = "#xpf-config-envelope v=1 writer=test ast=1 min-reader=1 rollback-fmt=1\n{}"`, `after .1.0.0.dbsnap/active.json = "{\"marker\":\"LIVE-2.0.0-ERA-DB\"}"`, `DEFECT: failed re-stage replaced the committed predecessor's DB snapshot`. Positive controls: live DB unchanged; the existing existence-only `TestVerifyFailure_PreservesCommittedPredecessor14720` PASSes in the same run (it cannot see content). Limits: verify-fail arm only; pre-STOP and START-failure arms share the same backup/restore code (static).

## Acceptance / fix direction
Take the predecessor backup before PREFLIGHT (and before the #6556 resume re-snapshot), or have snapshotConfigDB write a cut-scoped path when the target is a committed predecessor; restore the backup unconditionally on every failure arm. Acceptance: the probe's `after` equals `original` on verify-fail, pre-STOP refusal and START-failure arms, and the #14720 test asserts content rather than existence.

## Full validated claim

## #16766 — A preemptNowCh token posted while an instance is MASTER is never drained; after the next forced resignation the first BACKUP iteration consumes it and re-promotes the node at priority 0 [OPEN]

## Summary

A preemptNowCh token posted while an instance is MASTER is never drained; after the next forced resignation the first BACKUP iteration consumes it and re-promotes the node at priority 0

**Finding ID:** `R3-A25-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — in legacy RETH-VRRP mode with RG `preempt`, the node that was just demoted re-adds the VIPs, publishes a MASTER event and advertises priority 0, then steps down when the new master's advert arrives (normally milliseconds). This is a short dual-owner window and an extra MASTER/BACKUP event pair. The window is longer only if the peer cannot take MASTER; the 10 s posture reconcile is the backstop. Duration not measured.
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (VRRP run-loop one-shot signal/marker hygiene, with R3-F08-04) — a real state leak with a bounded, self-healing consequence.

## Mechanism

legacy mode, RG1 preempt → boot under SetSyncHold, peer absent → master-down (3 s shield) promotes → hold released (bulk sync or 30 s timeout) while MASTER → token parked → later a manual failover or weight drop → ResignRG → stepMaster resignCh → becomeBackup (stashed 0 applied) + 3× priority 0 → stepBackup consumes the stale token → `shouldPreemptObservedMaster` sees no live master within the horizon → becomeMaster at priority 0.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/vrrp/manager.go:467-470` `vi.restorePreempt(); vi.triggerPreemptNow()` for every instance. `instance_preempt.go:39-44` non-blocking send into the capacity-1 channel (instance.go:479). `instance.go:1260-1333` stepMaster selects stopCh/rxCh/advertTimer.C/configUpdatedCh/resignCh only. `instance.go:1108-1123` stepBackup consumes it: `force || vi.shouldPreemptObservedMaster()` → `becomeMaster()`. `instance_transition.go:92-` becomeMaster has no priority-0 or resign-pending refusal. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:628-633` resigns on every Primary→Secondary edge regardless of preempt. ForceRGMaster (manager.go:1071-1077) filters `getState() != StateMaster` at call time, which races a master-down promotion.

## Impact

The first planned failover after a boot where the node was MASTER at hold release flaps ownership back briefly. Operators see a spurious MASTER/BACKUP pair and GARP churn. Unlikely to drop traffic for long.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Drain `preemptNowCh` and clear `forcePreemptOnce` on every MASTER entry (or in stepMaster), and/or skip `triggerPreemptNow` for MASTER instances under the instance lock. Acceptance: the probe's subject row reads `[BACKUP]` with 0 extra priority-0 adverts and the control is unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

`ResignRG` doc (manager.go:940-966): "masterDownInterval at the stashed 0 keeps the resigned instance from winning a re-election". #2082/README: the preemptNowCh shortcut is a sync-hold-release action for a BACKUP.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A25-02` (parts file `parts/va25.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A25-02 | Low | A preemptNowCh token posted while an instance is MASTER is never drained; after the next…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): #2082 (CLOSED) is the release priority gate for a BACKUP; #14406 is ForceRGMaster during hold; #14706 is the lastMasterPriority overwrite (gemini 100/200/500 reports). R3-F08-04 (part-vf08, COHORT) is the leaked `resignPending` marker, a sibling in the same cohort with a different root cause. No owner for the undrained token.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A25-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16767 — R3-A47-01: `applySystemSyslog` rebuilds every `system syslog host` client on every apply and every retry tick (no fingerprint, no per-host reuse). During a DNS outage an… [OPEN]

## Summary

`applySystemSyslog` rebuilds every `system syslog host` client on every apply and every retry tick (no fingerprint, no per-host reuse). During a DNS outage an unrelated commit closes a working hostname collector's client and installs nothing, stalls the commit 5 s per hostname host, and arms a retry that holds applySem for the same stall every 30 s.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. Off-box forwarding of daemon, authorization and commit-audit records to a hostname collector stops for the length of any DNS outage that overlaps a commit, even though the existing connected-UDP socket was still delivering. Each commit in that window pays 5 s per hostname host. The 30 s retry holds the shared apply semaphore for the same time, so queued commits wait. This was demonstrated in a netns with a blackholed resolver. There is no enforcement loss, and IP-literal hosts are cheap, so the impact is bounded. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A47-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va47.md` (finding `R3-A47-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1721-1863 `applySystemSyslog`: for each host it calls `logging.NewSyslogClientWithSource(host.Address, port, host.SourceAddress)` (:1840), then `d.setSystemSyslogRetryOwed(skippedSystem15231 > 0)` and `d.slogHandler.SetClients(clients)` (:1861-1862). There is no hash or cache. pkg/logging/slog_handler.go:109-124 `SetClients` closes every old client. pkg/logging/syslog.go:1078-1079 performs the no-source UDP dial `dialer := &net.Dialer{Timeout: syslogDialTimeout}; return dialer.Dial("udp", s.remoteAddr)`, and the hostname lookup runs inside it, bounded to 5 s. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:216-217 runs step 10 on every apply. pkg/daemon/daemon_syslog_retry_14597.go:56-70 acquires applySem, and :96-100 `rebuildSyslog` calls `d.applySystemSyslog(cfg)` whenever `systemSyslogRetryOwed()` is set (interval 30 s, :13). The contrast is daemon_system.go:44-79 `syslogClientFingerprint`, which hashes only `cfg.Security.Log`.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #9326 acceptance criterion 1 says "Applying an unchanged `system syslog` / `security log` stanza performs zero dials". Criterion 2 says an unreachable host "does not block the apply". pkg/logging/README.md says the idempotence gate skips the rebuild "when nothing the client set depends on has changed" and that "a fully built identical config still performs zero rebuilds". #15231 (A47-06) says the retry must not replace healthy clients on every tick. Every one of these was implemented for `security log stream` only.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL. There is a reachable trigger (any commit while DNS is down, with a hostname host configured) and a concrete consequence (working remote logging is torn down, plus commit and applySem stalls). It survives dedup as a residual of #9326 and #15231.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. The unit/netns probe drives the real `applySystemSyslog`, the real `SyslogSlogHandler` and the security-log stream twin. The retry-tick semaphore hold and the end-to-end commit wall time are STATIC.

**Confidence:** High. Executed with a positive control. The applySem hold during the retry tick is static: the tick calls the same function inside `applySem.Acquire`.

## Impact

Operators lose the remote system and authorization log during exactly the incident window in which they are committing changes. Commits slow by 5 s per hostname host, and the semaphore stall repeats every 30 s until DNS recovers. Recovery is automatic when DNS returns (the retry rebuilds), but the records in between are not sent.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Give `applySystemSyslog` the stream treatment. Use a fingerprint over `cfg.System.Syslog.Hosts`, the system hostname and the facility/severity derivation, with an early return when unchanged. Use a per-host cache keyed by (address, port, source, facility, min-severity) so that the retry rebuilds only unbuilt hosts and never closes a working client. Optionally resolve outside applySem. Acceptance: two applies of an unchanged stanza perform zero dials (count through a seam), with a changed-stanza control that does dial. In the DNS-loss probe, the unchanged apply #2 gives `same-client=true received-during=true` and takes about 0 s. A retry tick with one bad host leaves the healthy host's client pointer unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A47-01`, part `parts/va47.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16768 — The fixed 3 s deafness shield replaces Master_Down_Interval for non-preempting instances, so with advertise-interval above ~3 s a no-preempt node promotes into a live master on every start (and at sync-hold release) [OPEN]

## Summary

The fixed 3 s deafness shield replaces Master_Down_Interval for non-preempting instances, so with advertise-interval above ~3 s a no-preempt node promotes into a live master on every start (and at sync-hold release)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A25-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — `no-preempt` is the operator's explicit request that a live master is not displaced. With an advertise-interval I > 3 s, each xpfd restart or instance rebuild of a higher-priority node takes mastership from the healthy master with probability about (I−3)/I (an unplanned failover plus GARP). A lower-priority restart instead runs dual-MASTER with an ARP fight until the master's next advert (up to I−3 s, about 37 s at 40 s). Bounded to non-preempting instances with long intervals. Demonstrated at the state-machine level.
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a configured `no-preempt` is violated deterministically by a timer that is shorter than the RFC horizon it claims only to extend.

## Mechanism

`vrrp-group 7 { priority 200; no-preempt; advertise-interval 5; }` → CollectInstances (seconds→ms, vrrp.go:146-149) → run() arms `initialMasterDownInterval()` = 3 s → the live master's (priority 100) next advert is up to 5 s away → the timer fires at 3 s → becomeMaster (VIPs, advert 200, GARP) → the master hears 200 > 100 and steps down.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/vrrp/instance.go:102` `const deafMasterDownInterval = 3 * time.Second`. `pkg/vrrp/instance_timing.go:17-22` `if !vi.getPreempt() { return deafMasterDownInterval }` (replacement, no max). `instance_timing.go:36-41` returns `deafMasterDownInterval, true` for the release re-arm, applied at `instance.go:1162-1168` with `masterDownTimer.Reset(d)`. `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:434-442` advertise-interval `ValidateInteger(1, 40)` seconds; `pkg/config/schema_chassis.go:170-176` reth-advertise-interval `ValidateInteger(10, 40959)` ms.

## Impact

Operators use long intervals with `no-preempt` to keep mastership stable across restarts and upgrades. Instead, each restart of the preferred node yanks traffic back, and each lower-priority restart causes a dual-MASTER GARP fight for seconds. In legacy RETH-VRRP mode with a raised `reth-advertise-interval` the sync-hold release reproduces it on every boot.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Arm `max(deafMasterDownInterval, vi.masterDownInterval())` in both `initialMasterDownInterval` and `masterDownAfterSyncHoldRelease`. Acceptance: in the probe, the subject stays BACKUP, the fix-twin behaviour becomes production behaviour, the positive and 1 s controls are unchanged, and the release helper returns ≥ masterDownInterval().

## Contract (where cited)

RFC 5798 §6.4.1 (non-owner: "Set the Master_Down_Timer to Master_Down_Interval") and §6.1 (`Master_Down_Interval = (3 * Master_Adver_Interval) + Skew_time`), verified on rfc-editor.org. `no-preempt` (schema_interfaces.go:432). The code's own contract (instance.go:1209-1216, "An extended initial timer gives enough time...") and the #7579 comment ("a peer that is actually alive costs nothing", instance.go:1155-1160) promise only a lengthening.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A25-03` (parts file `parts/va25.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A25-03 | Medium | The fixed 3 s deafness shield replaces Master_Down_Interval for non-preempting instances,…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #7579 (CLOSED) introduced the release re-arm with this constant (30 ms context only, root cause unrelated to long intervals); the startup shield predates it per the #7579 comment at instance.go:1133-1135 ("run() already extends the masterDown timer at STARTUP"). No issue, prior heading, earlier report or RUN part covers interval-dependent shortening (grep of `deafMasterDownInterval` across /var/tmp/deep-review-reports finds no hits; RUN hits are only this worker and b22's dedup pointer). ## #16769 — R3-A47-02: The #9165 drop-metric reader snapshots only the security-log stream clients. `system syslog host` clients count write drops (UDP ECONNREFUSED, #16083 queue overflow)… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #9165 drop-metric reader snapshots only the security-log stream clients. `system syslog host` clients count write drops (UDP ECONNREFUSED, #16083 queue overflow) that no metric or show surface exports.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low. This is an observability gap with no enforcement impact. When a dead system-syslog collector loses authorization or daemon records, the metric shows no series for it, and the only remaining signal is the rate-limited journald WARN. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A47-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va47.md` (finding `R3-A47-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/daemon_syslog_drops_9165.go:17-22 `return d.eventReader.SyslogDropStats()`. pkg/logging/syslog_drop_stats_9165.go:37-58 iterates `er.syslogClients`. System-syslog clients are installed only through `d.slogHandler.SetClients` (daemon_system.go:1862). A census of production `DroppedWrites()`/`DroppedDials()` readers finds only syslog_drop_stats_9165.go:51-52 and the in-package warn at syslog.go:323. `slogHandler.Clients()` has no production caller.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #9165 requires that the drop counters have "at least one production reader — a Prometheus gauge or a `show system syslog` line". The metric help reads "Remote syslog messages dropped, by collector and reason." (pkg/api/metrics_syslog_drops_9165.go:19). daemon_syslog_drops_9165.go:5 says the reader "snapshots every installed remote-syslog client's drop counters".

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (system-syslog sibling of the security-log stream fixes; file with R3-A47-01). It is a real residual with a bounded, observability-only impact.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. The unit probe drives the real applySystemSyslog, the slog handler and `d.syslogDropStats()`.

**Confidence:** High. Executed with a positive control, plus a grep census of readers.

## Impact

The metric gives an all-clear for exactly the collectors that carry authorization and commit records, while it correctly reports the security-log collectors beside them. An alert built on it misses a dead system-syslog collector.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Append the `d.slogHandler.Clients()` rows to `syslogDropStats`, labelled by sink (`system` vs `security`), and keep the counters per destination across rebuilds. Acceptance: the probe's system-host case yields one row with `Writes>0`, and the stream control is unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;

## #16770 — #14692 "no valid entries → leave the existing file untouched" keeps revoked or removed host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts after a clean commit (regression of the #5112 revocation contract) [OPEN]

## Summary
#14692 "no valid entries → leave the existing file untouched" keeps revoked or removed host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts after a clean commit (regression of the #5112 revocation contract)

**Finding ID:** R3-F02-03
**Severity (source):** Medium — outbound SSH trust revocation silently fails: the file governs the config-archive scp transfer (StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, #10298), whose payload is the full active config, so a holder of the rotated-out (e.g. compromised) host key can impersonate the archive host on the next transfer. Bounded: requires every configured key in the replacement commit to fail validation; demonstrated at the file level.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Key rotation is exactly when a compromised key must stop being trusted; the operator sees a clean commit and an updated `show`, while the box keeps trusting the old key for the transfer that carries all config secrets. It persists until a later commit with at least one valid key.

**Contract:** pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1425-1430 (function doc, #5112): "a revoked or compromised host key can never outlive the config that trusted it … applied durable trust must not outlive desired trust."

**Trace:** commit 1 trusts host H key A → file renders A → commit 2 deletes A and sets H (or a new host) with a key whose type/blob fails validation → commit succeeds → applySSHKnownHosts skips every entry → `valid == 0` → return → A remains trusted for H → next archive scp accepts A.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
daemon_system.go:1470-1472 `if valid == 0 { slog.Warn("ssh known hosts: no valid entries; leaving existing file untouched", …); return }`; only the empty-config branch removes the file (daemon_system.go:1440-1442). Commit does not validate: pkg/config/schema_security.go:1890-1897 makes the `host` body `closedWorldOpaque`; compiler_security.go:80 copies `SSHKnownHostKey{Type: name, Key: v}` verbatim. The closed type table is only at render time (daemon_system.go:1301 `sshKnownHostTypes`, validated by `validSSHKnownHostKey`).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestProbeR3F02Known -count=1 -v` (fixture RUN/workers/f02/evidence/probe_r3f02_known_hosts_revoke_test.go; output RUN/verify/vf02/probes/03-daemon.out). Positive control: a valid replacement key replaces the old one. Defect: replacement typed `ssh-ed25519` → `WARN … no valid entries; leaving existing file untouched skipped=1`, file still `archive.example ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAII+33r…` (old key). Twin: archive host removed, a different host added with a malformed key → removed host still trusted. Limits: the scp consumer was not driven; the file is its trust source.

## Acceptance / fix direction
When entries are configured but none validate, render a header-only managed file (trust nothing) or remove the managed file, consistent with #5112; additionally validate type/blob at commit so the operator sees the error. Acceptance: the probe's c3/c4 files no longer contain the old key while the valid-replacement control still renders the new key. The #14694 sibling (daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1515 `if !keysValid { return retErr }` keeps prior authorized_keys on one bad key) needs the same review; not executed here.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf02.md)</summary>

Bounded: requires every configured key in the replacement commit to fail validation; demonstrated at the file level.
- **Confidence:** High — executed with real ed25519 keys; the remaining assumption is that operators mistype or paste an OpenSSH type spelling (e.g. `ssh-ed25519`), which the opaque schema accepts.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — real `applySSHKnownHosts` against a temp path, positive control included.

Twin: archive host removed, a different host added with a malformed key → removed host still trusted. Limits: the scp consumer was not driven; the file is its trust source.

## #16771 — A priority-0 advert arms a 1 ms master-down on every BACKUP instead of RFC 5798 §6.4.2 Skew_Time, so in a standalone group with three or more routers all backups claim MASTER at once [OPEN]

## Summary

A priority-0 advert arms a 1 ms master-down on every BACKUP instead of RFC 5798 §6.4.2 Skew_Time, so in a standalone group with three or more routers all backups claim MASTER at once

**Finding ID:** `R3-A25-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low — only standalone `vrrp-group`s with two or more xpf backups (or xpf backups next to other routers) are affected. On a planned resignation, every xpf backup promotes in the same millisecond, giving a short multi-MASTER and GARP storm that converges through handleMasterRx. Neighbor-cache outcome not measured. HA RETH pairs (two nodes) are the designed case and are unaffected.
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (RFC 5798 timer conformance for standalone vrrp-groups) — a documented deliberate deviation whose stated premise ("only 2 HA nodes") does not hold for the standalone consumer.

## Mechanism

standalone `vrrp-group` on a segment with an xpf master and two or more xpf backups → the master stops or resigns → 3× priority 0 → each backup's handleBackupRx arms 1 ms → all promote, add the VIP, advertise and GARP → the lower-priority ones step down on hearing the higher advert.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/vrrp/instance_rx.go:252-276`: on `pkt.Priority == 0` the handler logs "immediate takeover", disarms the hold and calls `masterDownTimer.Reset(time.Millisecond)`, with the comment "RFC 5798 says use skew timer, but with only 2 HA nodes there's no contention risk". There is no `isRethInstance`, priority or preempt condition.

## Impact

Planned maintenance on a multi-router standalone VRRP segment produces a short multi-MASTER storm instead of a single deterministic handover. This is an RFC-visible behaviour difference on the wire.

## Acceptance / fix direction

For non-RETH instances arm Skew_Time (from the local effective priority and the learned interval), and keep the 1 ms fast path for `isRethInstance`. Otherwise document the standalone deviation in README. Acceptance: in the probe, a standalone 250 backup fires at about 23 ms and a 50 backup at about 805 ms; RETH stays at 1 ms.

## Contract (where cited)

RFC 5798 §6.4.2 step (425)/(430) "If the Priority in the ADVERTISEMENT is zero, then: Set the Master_Down_Timer to Skew_Time"; §6.1 Skew_Time = ((256 − priority) × Master_Adver_Interval)/256 (rfc-editor.org, verified). pkg/vrrp/README.md:393-395 documents the 1 ms arm only for legacy RETH shutdown.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A25-04` (parts file `parts/va25.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A25-04 | Low | A priority-0 advert arms a 1 ms master-down on every BACKUP instead of RFC 5798 §6.4.2…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): #10786 (CLOSED) is the untested 1 ms fast path, not its RFC deviation for standalone groups; #16018 (OPEN) and #10719 cover forged priority 0. No prior heading or report covers Skew_Time on priority 0. New.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A25-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16772 — R3-A47-03: `resolveSyslogSource` warns when the source-interface is empty, and the fingerprint helpers call it unconditionally. Every default-shaped stream therefore logs a… [OPEN]

## Summary

`resolveSyslogSource` warns when the source-interface is empty, and the fingerprint helpers call it unconditionally. Every default-shaped stream therefore logs a false "leaving the syslog source unbound (#15078)" WARN on every apply, and twice more per rebuild.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low. This is a false operator diagnostic. The actual bind is correct, because the build arms guard `!= ""`. The WARN repeats per stream per commit, is forwarded to `system syslog host` collectors, and makes the genuine #15078 IPv6 audit-loss warning indistinguishable by message. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A47-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va47.md` (finding `R3-A47-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/config/syslog_source.go:63-117. `srcIface` is trimmed, but there is no early return for "". `net.InterfaceByName("")` fails, and then `if family != "" { slog.Warn(... "source_interface", srcIface, "family", family) }` runs. pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:73-75 (`syslogClientFingerprint`, the `rsi=` term, before the hash gate) and :92-95 (`syslogStreamFingerprint15231`, the `rsi=` and `gsrc=` terms) call `ResolveSyslogSourceAddrForCollector(cfg, st.SourceInterface, st.Host)` without a `!= ""` guard.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** The #15078 WARN is meant for a configured source-interface that has no address of the collector's family (pkg/config/syslog_source.go:112-116). pkg/logging/README.md (#5797/#6829) treats a warning on a correct config as a defect: the "train-operators-to-ignore-it" failure.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (syslog operator diagnostics: false warning introduced by #15078). It is real, but it degrades only operator signal.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. The unit probe drives the real `applySyslogConfig` and counts the WARN records.

**Confidence:** High. Executed with a positive control.

## Impact

Every typical deployment gets a permanent stream of WARNs that read like an audit-loss condition, so a real IPv6 source-family failure no longer stands out in journald or at the collector.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Return "" without warning when the trimmed `srcIface` is empty, or emit the WARN only from the build arm that resolves a configured interface. Acceptance: the probe's defect case gives 0 WARNs, and an IPv6 collector with a v4-only configured source-interface still warns.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16773 — Standalone DHCPv6-PD: a same-lifetime renewal moves the stored Obtained but no RA applier runs. The live sender keeps the first lease's absolute expiry, deprecates the LAN PIO at its preferred expiry, and omits it after its valid expiry. [OPEN]

## Summary

Standalone DHCPv6-PD: a same-lifetime renewal moves the stored Obtained but no RA applier runs. The live sender keeps the first lease's absolute expiry, deprecates the LAN PIO at its preferred expiry, and omits it after its valid expiry.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A26-01`
**Severity (source report):** High — every standalone appliance that re-advertises a DHCPv6-PD prefix to a LAN, with a server granting fixed lifetimes, is affected. That is the common server behaviour, and the code's own comment says so. Its downstream hosts lose SLAAC global IPv6 addressing on schedule: deprecated at the first preferred expiry, removed at the first valid expiry. The loss is permanent until an unrelated commit, a PD content change or a daemon restart, and nothing logs at Warn. This is a loss of a supported forwarding service for a whole segment. It is a regression introduced by a fix (#15057). Demonstrated: the DHCP signal gap and the sender's countdown to omission. Potential: the host-side address loss, which follows from RFC 4862 §5.5.3 and §5.5.4 but was not lab-captured. Dual-stack IPv4 is unaffected. [reporter: High]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable and common configuration silently loses downstream IPv6 addressing; nothing guards the standalone path.

## Mechanism

Config `dhcpv6-client ia-pd` + RA mapping → T0 Reply → commitLease (new PD) → `scheduleRecompile` → `onDHCPAddressChange` → `applyActiveConfig` → `buildRAConfigs` stamps ValidExpiresAt=T0+valid → `ra.Apply` starts the sender. At T1, a Renew Reply with identical lifetimes → `reconcileDelegatedPDs` stores Obtained=T1 → `pdChanged=false` and the lease content is unchanged → only `onDHCPUnchangedLease`, which does nothing without host-inbound debt → the sender keeps T0+valid. At T0+preferred, PIO preferred=0 (deprecated). At T0+valid, `buildRA` omits the PIO and hosts' addresses expire. Every later renewal is equally silent.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa:

## Impact

This hits home and branch CPE and any standalone appliance delegating PD to LANs. The whole segment loses global IPv6 silently, starting one valid lifetime after boot or the last commit (often 1–2 days, or hours on short-lease ISPs). `show` still lists an active sender, and the WAN lease shows as renewed. Recovery is an unrelated commit or a restart, and it recurs after each one.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Give standalone mode an RA-scoped change signal on PD renewal: include ExpiresAt/Obtained in a PD-for-RA digest that triggers an RA-only re-apply, not a full recompile. Alternatively run the digest-gated RA reconcile in standalone too. Consumers: `pkg/dhcp` commitLease and notify, `pkg/daemon` RA appliers. Acceptance: a standalone daemon cell renews a PD with identical lifetimes and asserts that the applied RA config carries the renewed ValidExpiresAt, and that the wire PIO at the original expiry is present with the renewed remaining lifetime. It must be RED on d1ea69f9aa. The cluster no-churn cell (#15057) must stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/ra/README.md:571-578` (#15057) says the sender "is NOT restarted as time advances, but IS restarted when a renewal moves the expiry". `pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:441-447` (#9239) says that in standalone mode "this full-apply path is the ONLY RA applier", and that the 30s loop retries only dead senders, "not live ones holding stale desired state". RFC 9096 L-15 (cited at `sender.go:928`) requires advertised lifetimes not to exceed what remains. It does not license advertising less than the delegation still holds.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A26-01` (parts file `parts/va26.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A26-01 | High | Standalone DHCPv6-PD: a same-lifetime renewal moves the stored Obtained but no RA applier…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked gh-issues.tsv for RA, delegat, PD, renew and 15057 (#15057, #9239, #14598, #14606, #15224 and #1777 are all closed with different predicates). I also checked prior-r2-002 (A26-01 is the cluster churn that #15057 fixed), prior-headings.tsv, `/var/tmp/deep-review-reports/*` (grep for `delegatedPrefixesChanged` and `ValidExpiresAt`: only unrelated or refactoring mentions), and this run's `drafts/parts/*` and `workers/*/report.md`: no owner. This is a regression residual of #15057 (`e210817d0d`, in base) combined with the #1777 silent-renewal rule.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A26-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A26-01 — Standalone DHCPv6-PD: a same-lifetime PD renewal never re-applies RA, so since #15057 the LAN PIO decays to 0 and is omitted at the first lease's expiry while the delegation is still held
- **Finding ID:** R3-A26-01
