## #16792 — #11391 residual: an L2-only bridge-domain whose derived device `br-<name>` exceeds IFNAMSIZ commits strict-clean; networkd discards the `.netdev`, so the bridge never exists and no member is enslaved [OPEN]

## Summary

#11391 residual: an L2-only bridge-domain whose derived device `br-<name>` exceeds IFNAMSIZ commits strict-clean; networkd discards the `.netdev`, so the bridge never exists and no member is enslaved

**Finding ID:** `R3-A37-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — any bridge-domain name of 13 bytes or more (e.g. `customer-vlan-100`) gives a strict-clean config that can never be realised, and the bridge domain bridges nothing. This is the same impact class #11391 was adjudicated in. It is fail-closed (no isolation loss) and bounded to L2-only domains: a `routing-interface irb.N` is already rejected through the #5832 gate [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the reachable, operator-authored config commits clean and is silently non-functional.

## Mechanism

`set bridge-domains customer-vlan-100 vlan-id-list 100; interface ge-0/0/1.100` → SchemaValidate (name OK) → strict compile (no derived-name gate) → `buildBridgeDomainModels` row `br-customer-vlan-100` → `10-xpf-br-customer-vlan-100.netdev/.network` plus member `.network` with `Bridge=br-customer-vlan-100` → networkd ignores the `.netdev` and never creates the bridge → the member is never enslaved. The absent row also poisons the reconfigure batch (R3-A37-02).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/schema_validators_bridge_domain_9494.go:17-31`: `ValidateBridgeDomainName` checks `/\\\x00`, whitespace and glob metacharacters only, with no length or `:` check. `pkg/config/types.go:674-681`: `IRBToBridge` maps `br-`+name only when `bd.RoutingInterface != ""`, and that map is the only route by which the #5832 gate sees `br-*`. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:2032-2077`: `bridgeName := "br-" + bd.Name` becomes an `IsBridge` managed row. The `.netdev` renders `Name=br-<name>`.

## Impact

The operator sees a clean commit, `show configuration` and normal-looking generated files, while the segment bridges nothing. The only signal is a networkd journal line. Recovery is a rename, but nothing points to it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Apply the #11391-style derived-device validator to `br-`+name (≤15 bytes, dev_valid_name: no `:`). Strict-reject, and on lenient load warn and quarantine. Acceptance: the L2-only probe case is rejected at strict compile, and a 12-byte name (`br-` + 12 = 15) still commits.

## Contract (where cited)

#11391 (CLOSED) acceptance is to strict-reject names whose derived Linux device exceeds 15 bytes. #5832 sets `maxLinuxIfNameLen = 15` for authored and derived device names (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ifname_collision.go:8-14`). `docs/feature-gaps.md` lists bridge-domain kernel bridge + `.netdev/.network` generation as Done.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A37-03` (parts file `parts/va37.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A37-03 | Medium | #11391 residual: an L2-only bridge-domain whose derived device br-<name> exceeds IFNAMSIZ…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): #11391 (CLOSED, RI-only, eded89815e), #9494/#10089 (CLOSED, name separators/globs) and #5832 (authored/derived interface names via irb) do not cover this. gh-issues.tsv (bridge-domain), prior-headings.tsv and the RUN parts have no IFNAMSIZ owner for `br-<bd>`.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A37-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16793 — R3-A53-05: In-process console Ctrl-D / double Ctrl-C call the unscoped `store.ExitConfigure()` on the global `InConfigMode()` flag, discarding another session's candidate and… [OPEN]

## Summary

In-process console Ctrl-D / double Ctrl-C call the unscoped `store.ExitConfigure()` on the global `InConfigMode()` flag, discarding another session's candidate and releasing its lock

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — the in-process console is xpfd's own foreground TTY. There, Ctrl-D at the operational prompt is by design the "end the daemon" key, which discards every session's candidate anyway, and double Ctrl-C also ends the daemon. So the console actor already holds a strictly stronger capability through the same key, and no authority boundary is crossed. Residual harm: a remote colleague's staged candidate is wiped and the lock is freed for a third session while the daemon stays up, with a false "Exiting configuration mode" message. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A53-05`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va53.md` (finding `R3-A53-05`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/cli/cli.go:676-684 `if err == io.EOF { if c.store.InConfigMode() { c.store.ExitConfigure(); ... "Exiting configuration mode"; continue }; return nil }`. :650-654 double Ctrl-C: `if c.store.InConfigMode() { c.store.ExitConfigure() }; close(exitCh)`. pkg/configstore/store_lock.go:380-392: ExitConfigure clears the candidate and holder fields unconditionally. pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1014-1024: shell.Run returning ends the main wait, and runShutdownSequence follows.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #14986 (pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:25-30, 71-108): the store's config mode is global, so the console must not act on another holder's session. `ExitConfigureSession` (store_lock.go:263-283, #3979) releases only the caller's own lock.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (session-scoped release on console exit paths) — real holder-model violation, minor because the actor's intended key already ends the daemon.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/cli probe driving the real REPL over a real configstore.Store.

**Confidence:** High — executed through `CLI.Run`; the shutdown consequence of an op-mode Ctrl-D is STATIC.

## Impact

In foreground/debug deployments, a routine keystroke silently drops a colleague's uncommitted work and opens the lock to another session while the box stays up.

## Acceptance / fix direction

in both branches act only when `c.configOwned`, then call `c.store.ExitConfigureSession(localConfigSessionID)` and clear configOwned. Otherwise treat EOF as an operational-mode exit. Acceptance: the probe keeps `locked=true holder="grpc-peer-1"`, and a console that entered `configure` itself still leaves config mode on Ctrl-D.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A53-05`, part `parts/va53.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16794 — #15287 re-enabled on-disk CLI history behind a denylist that misses plain-text-password(-value) and every edit-context spelling of the context-gated secrets (snmp community, md5 key) [OPEN]

## Summary
#15287 re-enabled on-disk CLI history behind a denylist that misses plain-text-password(-value) and every edit-context spelling of the context-gated secrets (snmp community, md5 key)

**Finding ID:** R3-F03-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — a cleartext root/login password, SNMP v1/v2c community or OSPF/IS-IS MD5 key typed by an operator is written durably to `~/.xpf_history` (local CLI) or `~/.xpf_cli_history` (remote CLI); the file is 0600 in the operator's home, so exposure is to later readers of that home, backups or support bundles. This is the same class and grade as #10743; it is not High because the file is not world-readable. Demonstrated at the component level.
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
every operator who configures SNMP communities or routing MD5 keys hierarchically, or types the Junos `plain-text-password-value` spelling, leaves the secret on disk. The secret persists indefinitely, up to the 10000-line bound, and survives restarts. Recovery is a manual wipe plus credential rotation.

**Contract:** #10743 required that typed credentials never persist to the CLI history file. 27078305ec (#15287) made persistence safe only through `IsSensitiveHistoryLine`, whose doc comment says it "mirrors the secret-leaf signatures in pkg/config/ast_redact.go (secretIndices)" and is "fail-closed (over-suppress, never under-suppress)".

**Trace:** operator input (config mode, possibly inside an `edit` context) -> readline returns line -> `RecordHistoryLine` -> `IsSensitiveHistoryLine` false -> O_APPEND to 0600 history file -> next session `ReadHistorySeed` reloads it, filtered by the same predicate, so it is re-seeded too.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`pkg/cliterm/terminal.go:227-251` @d1ea69f9aa: exact-token switch; `community` true only when `fields[i-1]=="snmp"`; `key` only when `fields[i-2]=="md5" && fields[i-3]=="authentication"`; no `plain-text-password`, `plain-text-password-value`. `pkg/config/ast_redact.go:857-862` lists `"plain-text-password", "plain-text-password-value"` (also `client-secret`, `shared-secret`, `radius-shared-secret`); `pkg/config/secret.go:443-444` `secretLeafKeywords` includes both plain-text leaves. `pkg/config/schema_plain_password_15053.go:14-23` the leaf takes `args: 1`, `placeholder: "<password>"` (refused at commit, but the line is already recorded). `pkg/cli/cli.go:692` and `cmd/cli/main.go:323` call `cliterm.RecordHistoryLine(..., line)` on the raw line before dispatch, with no edit-path argument.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cliterm/ -run TestVF03HistoryLeak -count=1 -v`; fixture RUN/verify/vf03/probes/zz_vf03_history_probe_test.go, output RUN/verify/vf03/history_probe.out. Controls persisted=false: flat `set snmp community S3cretA ...`, flat `... authentication md5 1 key S3cretB`, `encrypted-password`, `edit snmp community S3cretC`. Defect rows persisted=true: `set system root-authentication plain-text-password-value S3cretD`, `... authentication plain-text-password S3cretE`, `set community S3cretF authorization read-only` (after `edit snmp`), `set key S3cretG` (after `edit ... authentication md5 1`), `set md5 1 key S3cretH` (after `edit ... authentication`). Limits: the probe calls the recorder directly, not through a live readline session. The reporter's own probe (RUN/workers/f03/evidence/history_probe.out) agrees.

## Acceptance / fix direction
evaluate the line against the full path (`store.GetEditPath()` / remote `c.editPath` + lexed tokens), using `config` secretIndices/IsSecretLeafKeyword as the single SSOT. Fail closed for any config-mode `set`/`edit` whose resolved path contains a secret leaf. Acceptance: the five defect rows report persisted=false with the controls unchanged, and a test pins the history predicate against `secretLeafKeywords ∪ secretIndices` keywords so it cannot drift.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vf03.md)</summary>

### R3-F03-01 — #15287 re-enabled on-disk CLI history behind a denylist that misses plain-text-password(-value) and every edit-context spelling of the context-gated secrets (snmp community, md5 key)
- **Finding ID:** R3-F03-01
- **Title:** #15287 re-enabled on-disk CLI history behind a denylist that misses plain-text-password(-value) and every edit-context spelling of the context-gated secrets (snmp community, md5 key)
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker f03 (Fix-residual hunter (delta group 03)); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vf03
- **Severity:** Medium — a cleartext root/login password, SNMP v1/v2c community or OSPF/IS-IS MD5 key typed by an operator is written durably to `~/.xpf_history` (local CLI) or `~/.xpf_cli_history` (remote CLI); the file is 0600 in the operator's home, so exposure is to later readers of that home, backups or support bundles. This is the same class and grade as #10743; it is not High because the file is not world-readable. Demonstrated at the component level.
- **Confidence:** High — executed against the real `RecordHistoryLine`; the only assumption is that operators use the `edit` hierarchy or the `plain-text-password(-value)` spellings, both of which the schema accepts on the line.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — Go probe through `cliterm.RecordHistoryLine` + on-disk read-back, with positive controls; the interactive end-to-end session (`edit snmp`, `set community x`, `cat ~/.xpf_history`) is not run.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — regression of the #10743 fix: before 27078305ec nothing new reached disk, now credential lines do.
- **Contract:** #10743 required that typed credentials never persist to the CLI history file. 27078305ec (#15287) made persistence safe only through `IsSensitiveHistoryLine`, whose doc comment says it "mirrors the secret-leaf signatures in pkg/config/ast_redact.go (secretIndices)" and is "fail-closed (over-suppress, never under-suppress)".
- **Adversarial analysis:** Protection is credential confidentiality at rest on the appliance. The actor is no attacker at typing time: an operator types a secret normally, and anyone who later gets read access to that account's home (a backup, a support bundle, a later tenant, a compromised low-privilege account that shares the home) gets the secret. The predicate is assumed to cover the population of secret leaves. Challenged: it is a hand-copied token list that ignores the edit path, so context-gated keywords are structurally uncoverable.
- **Evidence:** `pkg/cliterm/terminal.go:227-251` @d1ea69f9aa: exact-token switch; `community` true only when `fields[i-1]=="snmp"`; `key` only when `fields[i-2]=="md5" && fields[i-3]=="authentication"`; no `plain-text-password`, `plain-text-password-value`. `pkg/config/ast_redact.go:857-862` lists `"plain-text-password", "plain-text-password-value"` (also `client-secret`, `shared-secret`, `radius-shared-secret`); `pkg/config/secret.go:443-444` `secretLeafKeywords` includes both plain-text leaves. `pkg/config/schema_plain_password_15053.go:14-23` the leaf takes `args: 1`, `placeholder: "<password>"` (refused at commit, but the line is already recorded). `pkg/cli/cli.go:692` and `cmd/cli/main.go:323` call `cliterm.RecordHistoryLine(..., line)` on the raw line before dispatch, with no edit-path argument.
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cliterm/ -run TestVF03HistoryLeak -count=1 -v`; fixture RUN/verify/vf03/probes/zz_vf03_history_probe_test.go, output RUN/verify/vf03/history_probe.out. Controls persisted=false: flat `set snmp community S3cretA ...`, flat `... authentication md5 1 key S3cretB`, `encrypted-password`, `edit snmp community S3cretC`. Defect rows persisted=true: `set system root-authentication plain-text-password-value S3cretD`, `... authentication plain-text-password S3cretE`, `set community S3cretF authorization read-only` (after `edit snmp`), `set key S3cretG` (after `edit ... authentication md5 1`), `set md5 1 key S3cretH` (after `edit ... authentication`). Limits: the probe calls the recorder directly, not through a live readline session. The reporter's own probe (RUN/workers/f03/evidence/history_probe.out) agrees.
- **Trace:** operator input (config mode, possibly inside an `edit` context) -> readline returns line -> `RecordHistoryLine` -> `IsSensitiveHistoryLine` false -> O_APPEND to 0600 history file -> next session `ReadHistorySeed` reloads it, filtered by the same predicate, so it is re-seeded too.
- **Refutation attempt:** Looked for a second filter: `ReadHistorySeed` re-filters with the same predicate (no help); `SecureReadlineHistory` only sets 0600; zeroize (#11105) wipes only at factory reset. Confirmed with the commit message that the prior state persisted nothing new ("no new command ever persisted"), so this is a regression. Narrowed the reporter's claim: `client-secret`/`radius-shared-secret` are not modelled schema leaves (they appear only in ast_redact), so they are kept as a drift note, not a core row.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — operator CLI path, no hot path; the invariant broken is "one SSOT for secret leaves" (the copy is not wired to `secretIndices`/`secretLeafKeywords`).

## #16795 — Untagged unit 0 on a tagged non-RETH, non-VRRP parent: the netlink reconcile installs its address on the parent, the parent's networkd row renders none and no keep, and xpf's own reconfigure tail strips it (#9721 residual) [OPEN]

## Summary

Untagged unit 0 on a tagged non-RETH, non-VRRP parent: the netlink reconcile installs its address on the parent, the parent's networkd row renders none and no keep, and xpf's own reconfigure tail strips it (#9721 residual)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A37-05`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — the native-VLAN unit's address, connected prefix and host reachability vanish at the end of every apply whose networkd tail runs: any changed generated file, outstanding debt, or a tail owed after an external reload. The address returns only on a later quiet apply. The unit's zone still binds the parent, so that subnet is dead while commits report success. It is bounded to a shape outside Junos idiom (Junos requires a vlan-id on tagged interfaces), which xpf nonetheless supports elsewhere (#9721, #15061, #15113, #12055) [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a strict-clean config loses an L3 address because of xpf's own activation tail.

## Mechanism

`ge-0/0/1 vlan-tagging; unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/24; unit 50 vlan-id 50 ...`, both zoned → strict compile OK → planPhysDesired puts 10.0.0.1/24 on `ge-0-0-1` → netlink add during compile → networkd.Apply writes the parent `.network` with no address and no keep → when files changed or debt is owed, `reload` then `reconfigure -- <all>` → networkd removes the foreign address → the address is absent until a later apply where the tail does not run.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:209-305`: a zone ref with `vlanID == 0` appends `unit.Addresses` to the PARENT plan `pd.addrs`. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1388`: `reconcileInterfaceAddresses(physName, pd.addrs, ...)` installs them. `:1674-1706`: `if effectiveCfg.TaggingEnabled()` emits the parent row with `VLANParentAddresses: vlanParentVRRPSource(...)` (RETH-VRRP only) and `KeepAddresses` only for that source or standalone VRRP. `pkg/networkd/networkd.go:1696`: `if !ifc.IsVLANParent {` gates all `Address=` rendering, and `:1732` renders only `VLANParentAddresses`. `:1762-1773`: `keepConfigurationValue` returns "" for this row. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:377` runs `networkd.Apply` after the compile, so the strip is the last word of the apply.

## Impact

Hosts on the native VLAN lose their gateway and the box loses that connected route. The state flaps with commit cadence (absent after a reconfiguring apply, present after a quiet one), which makes it hard to diagnose. Recovery is another commit that does not touch networkd files.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Pick one owner. Either render untagged-unit addresses on the VLAN-parent row (extend `VLANParentAddresses` beyond the VRRP source, which then gives keep=static), or strict-reject an addressed untagged unit on a tagged non-RETH parent, in line with Junos and #15034. Acceptance: the probe config either fails strict compile, or the parent `.network` carries `Address=10.0.0.1/24` and the netns run keeps it across reload + reconfigure.

## Contract (where cited)

CLAUDE.md: "xpfd manages ALL interfaces ... configures addresses". #9721's own issue text records that for a tagged parent with an addressed unit lacking vlan-id, "The unit's addresses are also never rendered, so this shape is broken beyond VRRP". The doctrine of #14574/#15034 (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces_vlan_tagging.go:10-60`) is that the networkd model and the dataplane writers must agree on which netdev carries a unit's address.

In-run R3-A06-01/R3-A05-04 cover a NON-ZERO untagged unit (#15034 residual) with a different device and fix, and va06 already recorded that this entry is distinct. #15113/#15121/#12055 concern zone and mirror consumers of unit 0, not the address owner.

## #16796 — R3-A54-01: `xpfd upgrade` installs no signal disposition, so SIGINT/SIGHUP during the STOP window kills the runner after `systemctl stop xpfd` and leaves the standalone daemon… [OPEN]

## Summary

`xpfd upgrade` installs no signal disposition, so SIGINT/SIGHUP during the STOP window kills the runner after `systemctl stop xpfd` and leaves the standalone daemon down with nothing to restart it

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — this is an appliance availability loss on a standalone node. Transit forwarding and every daemon-owned service stay down until a human re-runs `xpfd upgrade`, runs `systemctl start xpfd` or reboots. It is bounded: the stopped daemon fails closed, and the journal makes a manual re-run resume. That is why it is not High. The outage was demonstrated at the Runner level. The end-to-end systemd outage is inferred.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A54-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va54.md` (finding `R3-A54-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

A grep for `os/signal|signal.(Notify|Ignore|Reset)|NotifyContext|SIGINT|SIGHUP|Setsid|Setpgid|systemd-run` over non-test `cmd/xpfd` and `pkg/upgrade` returns nothing. Repo-wide, Notify/Ignore exist only in `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go` (a comment), `pkg/cli/cli.go` and `cmd/cli/main.go`, which is the positive control. `cmd/xpfd/main.go:282-289` routes `upgrade` to `runUpgradeSubcommand`. `cmd/xpfd/upgrade.go:28-125` calls `r.Run(upgrade.Options{})`, `RunRolling` and `RollbackTo` with no signal setup. `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:974-980` has `r.logf("upgrade: stopping %s ...")` then `r.cfg.Sys.StopUnit(r.cfg.Unit)` (a blocking `systemctl stop`). The later StartUnit sites are `cutover.go:985,1050,1156` and `flip.go:427,493`, all in-process. `test/incus/xpfd.service` has `Restart=on-failure` (no restart after an explicit stop job) and no ExecStopPost. The postinst safety net `if ! "$STAGED/xpfd" upgrade; then ... systemctl start xpfd` runs in the same process tree. An inference, not executed: under `dpkg -i`, the postinst `sh` receives the same SIGINT.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:1116-1122` says "The daemon must not be left offline (AGY-5)". `docs/in-place-upgrade.md` says "The ONLY live-state mutations are STOP and FLIP-then-START" and that re-running `xpfd upgrade` resumes. The postinst safety net (`debian/xpf.postinst:523-538`) exists "so the node is not left offline after `apt upgrade`". The project treats default-signal death of xpfd itself as a defect (#5807, #15084).

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — an ordinary operator action (Ctrl-C during the visible stop wait, or an SSH drop) on a documented recovery/rollback path leaves the firewall daemon stopped, against the cut's stated "never left offline" invariant.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — an independent re-exec probe drove the real `Runner.Run` (fakeSystem from pkg/upgrade tests) and delivered SIGINT/SIGHUP while StopUnit was blocked. That covers the Runner component. The systemd stop-job persistence and the `systemctl is-active` result on a real node are STATIC.

**Confidence:** Medium — the mechanism is High: the Runner was executed with a fake system, and the signal census found nothing. Delivery depends on the invocation path. A direct shell invocation (`xpfd upgrade`, re-run/resume, `--rollback`) and `dpkg -i` put the runner in the operator's foreground process group. The apt-driven postinst cut is probably shielded, because libapt-pkg runs dpkg in a new session on a pty and apt ignores SIGHUP. That shielding was established STATICALLY from strings in the installed libapt-pkg and was not executed.

## Impact

in-place upgrade and rollback are the supported version-change paths. The one deliberate down window is exactly where an impatient Ctrl-C or a flaky SSH link lands. A standalone appliance forwards nothing until someone notices. If the operator's session dropped, they must reconnect, possibly via console, to restart it.

## Acceptance / fix direction

capture SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGTERM in `runUpgradeSubcommand` (and in the kernel sub-verb) for the whole run. Log a "signal deferred" message, abort cleanly only before STOP, and after STOP finish START/rollback first. Alternatively, run the cut via `systemd-run --unit=xpf-upgrade --collect` so it leaves the terminal's session. Acceptance: a Runner test that signals the process mid-StopUnit observes the cut completing or rolling back with the unit running (the probe's production rows must match the twin), and on a lab VM `kill -INT -<pgid>` during "upgrade: stopping xpfd" leaves `systemctl is-active xpfd` = active.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A54-01`, part `parts/va54.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16797 — The #14701 fix encodes `Name=!a !b` as vetoing both names and rejects IP-literal `MACAddress=`; systemd-networkd 262 does neither, so xpf's external-ownership verdict diverges from networkd's [OPEN]

## Summary

The #14701 fix encodes `Name=!a !b` as vetoing both names and rejects IP-literal `MACAddress=`; systemd-networkd 262 does neither, so xpf's external-ownership verdict diverges from networkd's

**Finding ID:** `R3-A37-06`
**Severity (source report):** Low — this is an ownership disagreement limited to exotic third-party `.network` files. With `Name=!eth0 !eth1`, xpf treats eth1 as its own (strip/always-down) while networkd applies the external file to it, which can oscillate if the file sorts first. With `MACAddress=<tunnel local IP>`, xpf ignores the file while networkd configures the tunnel. It is also an assurance defect: the README and `negated_match_14701_test.go` pin the wrong semantics [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (networkd external-ownership parity with systemd matching: #12135/#14593/#14701 family) — real but minor.

## Mechanism

external `/etc/systemd/network/05-ext.network` → `FindExternallyManaged` → compile `stripUnmanagedInterfaces` and Apply always-down decisions use the xpf verdict → networkd uses its own verdict → they disagree on eth1 (or gre1).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/networkd/networkd.go:969-989`: `for strings.HasPrefix(pattern, "!") { negative = true; pattern = pattern[1:] }`, so a run of `!` collapses (#14701). `:1325` `parseExternalMACAddress` rejects IP literals. Fix 1c0cdbf805 (#14701) is an ancestor of the base. The #14701 issue body shows the premise was code-derived, not checked against networkd.

## Impact

The direct impact is limited. The bigger risk is that the module documents systemd semantics wrongly exactly where they were last "fixed", so later work inherits a false contract, and a correct fix would be reverted by its own regression test.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Restore single-`!` stripping. Accept IPv4/IPv6 literal `MACAddress=` words compared against raw 4/16-byte hardware addresses. Correct the README and test, and add a real-networkd parity cell (the netns harness). Acceptance: xpf's `Matches` equals networkd's verdict for both probe files on eth0/eth1/eth2/gre1/eth9.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/networkd/networkd.go:961-967`: `externalPatternListMatches` "implements systemd's net_condition_test_strv". The premise of #12135/#14593 is that compile and networkd agree on external ownership.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A37-06` (parts file `parts/va37.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A37-06 | Low | The #14701 fix encodes Name=!a !b as vetoing both names and rejects IP-literal MACAddress=;…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): Regression of #14701 (CLOSED, fix 1c0cdbf805). No other issue, prior heading or RUN part covers it. Prior headings for FindExternallyManaged are #12135/#14593/#14701 only.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A37-06` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A37-06 — The #14701 fix encodes `Name=!a !b` as vetoing both names and rejects IP-literal `MACAddress=`; systemd-networkd 262 does neither, so xpf's external-ownership verdict diverges from networkd's
- **Finding ID:** R3-A37-06

## #16798 — R3-A54-02: `cli -c` exits 0 having done nothing when a keyword-only node gets an unknown or unimplemented subcommand (32 nodes, incl. `clear security ike… [OPEN]

## Summary

`cli -c` exits 0 having done nothing when a keyword-only node gets an unknown or unimplemented subcommand (32 nodes, incl. `clear security ike security-associations`, `request system software add`, misspelt `failover`)

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — this is an automation exit-status lie. No RPC is issued, so nothing is changed or widened, and a help listing goes to stdout. A script or runbook step reports success for an IKE SA flush, software add, config sync or failover that never happened. There is no enforcement impact. [reporter: Low-Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A54-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va54.md` (finding `R3-A54-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`cmd/cli/main.go:209-217` maps `err != nil && err != errExit` to `os.Exit(1)` and everything else to exit 0. Help-then-`return nil` arms exist at `cmd/cli/request.go:119-123` (`software` without `in-service-upgrade`), `:182-185` (`request chassis` without `cluster`), `:196-198` (`request chassis cluster` default arm) and `cmd/cli/clear.go:278-280` (`clear security` default). `cmd/cli/shared.go:105-177` (dispatch/dispatchOperational) has no cmdtree canonicalization or validation before routing. `clear security ike` is absent from `pkg/cmdtree/tree.go`, so the verb is unimplemented, not just unrouted.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `cmd/cli/README.md:22-23` says `-c` "Exits with the command's status. Useful for scripted operations.". README:91-95 says "Never silently discard a selector ... REFUSE the command with an error naming it". 61 sibling nodes in the same dispatcher already refuse an unknown token (`request zzqqbogus` gives `unknown request target`).

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (remote-CLI fail-closed token handling and `-c` exit status, with the #5459/#15775/#15723 per-site fixes) — real and cheap to fix once, but the consequence is a visible no-op, not lost protection.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `cmd/cli` dispatcher census with a nil gRPC client (any RPC nil-panics and is recovered). The process exit mapping is STATIC from `cmd/cli/main.go:209-217`.

**Confidence:** High — an executed census through the real dispatcher, with refusing and wire-reaching controls.

## Impact

a runbook step like `cli -c "clear security ike security-associations"` (the standard Junos IKE recovery step) reports success while the tunnel stays wedged. A typo in a scripted failover reports success while no failover occurs. The operator learns only by reading the help text a script discards.

## Acceptance / fix direction

in `dispatchOperational`, consult `cmdtree.Canonicalize` (the operational SSOT). Refuse any line whose first unrecognised token sits under a keyword-only node, with `unknown <path> command: <token>` and exit 1, while keeping help for bare nodes. Acceptance: the census reports `SILENT-SUCCESS=0`, and the Junos-verb table exits 1 naming the token.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A54-02`, part `parts/va54.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16799 — The helper treats every rib-group RETURN row (kernel priority 1001–1999, after the l3mdev VRF lookup at 1000) as a stage-1 leak that runs before the source VRF table's own longest-prefix match. If tenant A has a default route or any route covering a co-leaking tenant B's prefix, the AF_XDP path forwards A's traffic into B, while the kernel, and Junos, use A's own route. [OPEN]

## Summary

The helper treats every rib-group RETURN row (kernel priority 1001–1999, after the l3mdev VRF lookup at 1000) as a stage-1 leak that runs before the source VRF table's own longest-prefix match. If tenant A has a default route or any route covering a co-leaking tenant B's prefix, the AF_XDP path forwards A's traffic into B, while the kernel, and Junos, use A's own route.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A38-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — The fast path and the kernel disagree about routing-instance separation. Executed in the production Rust FIB: A's own default, and even a MORE-SPECIFIC /25 in A, lose to the return row into B. The impact is bounded for two reasons. Transit into B still needs an A-zone→B-zone policy permit, and without one the traffic is dropped instead of following A's route, which is an availability loss for A's own destinations. The trigger also needs two or more instances whose interface-routes rib-groups import inet.0, plus a covering route in A [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — The trigger is a reachable, strict-commit-clean shared-services config. The fast-path egress demonstrably differs from the kernel answer, which the code claims to mirror.

## Mechanism

Tenants A and B each have `interface-routes rib-group inet X-to-main` with `import-rib [ X.inet.0 inet.0 ]`, and A has `static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop <A-WAN>`. ApplyRibGroupRules installs `to 10.20.0.0/24 iif|oif vrf-A lookup <B> pref 1225`. buildRouteSnapshots (from netlink.RuleList) emits the A.inet.0→B.inet.0 NextTable row. forwarding_build puts it into `leak_rules_v4["A.inet.0"]`. A packet ingressing an A interface for 10.20.0.5 resolves through the stage-1 leak to B's egress, while the kernel resolves rule 1000 to table A to A's WAN.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/routing/rules.go:689-695` and `:706-760`: each tenant gets return rules for every other leaking tenant's connected prefixes. `pkg/routing/rib_group_return_9819.go:112-123` installs `to <peer-prefix> iif|oif vrf-A lookup <peer-table>` at 1001..1897. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:566-581` mirrors each rule as `RouteSnapshot{Table: A.inet.0, Destination: <peer-prefix>, NextTable: B.inet.0, RulePriority: <prio>}`. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/fib.rs:658-671` enters with `evaluate_leaks = true`. `fib.rs:969-1009` walks `state.leak_rules_v4.get(table)` and returns the target resolution whenever the target has a route, and only afterwards does `:1011` run `select_v4_route(..., table, ...)`, the source table's own LPM. Only local delivery (`:944-951`) precedes the leak walk. `tests_leak_overlap_9955.rs:265-334` pins "the leak rule must run before main-table LPM" with an inet.0 fixture only.

## Impact

In shared-services designs, each tenant has its own default and leaks into inet.0. On the fast path, tenant A's traffic for B's subnets, and for any A-internal block overlapping a B prefix, is steered into B or dropped by policy, instead of following A's own route as the kernel and slow path do. Fast-path and slow-path behaviour differ, and VRF separation on the fast path becomes a pure zone-policy question.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Give VRF-scoped return rows "after source-table LPM" semantics in the helper, for example by keying off `rule_priority` in (1000,2000) or an explicit flag on RouteSnapshot so that they are evaluated only when the source table misses. Alternatively, R3-A10-02's fix (stop installing peer-return rules no import-rib authorizes) removes these rows altogether, so file the two together. Acceptance: the va38 Rust probe yields 20/20 with A's routes present and 21 in the control, matching the kernel probe's three cases, and the v6 twin agrees.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/routing/README.md` (ip-rule priorities) says the return rules sit in (1000,2000), "after the kernel's l3mdev rule at 1000", and look up the peer table only for leaked peer-prefix destinations, that is, only when the source VRF table misses. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:557-563` says the mirror orders returns "exactly as the kernel RPDB does". Under Junos, nothing imports B's routes into A.inet.0, so A's own routes decide.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A38-01` (parts file `parts/va38.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A38-01 | Medium | The helper treats every rib-group RETURN row (kernel priority 1001–1999, after the l3mdev…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked gh-issues.tsv, prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports and the in-run parts. R3-A10-02 (va10, MATERIAL) is the related return-rule REACH on an A-table miss. It has a different mechanism and a different acceptance, and its proposed fix would also remove this trigger, so they should be cross-linked or filed together. R3-A10-01 is next-table versus inet.0 (main context). #9819, #11062, #14975 and #9955 (CLOSED), gemini D33-02, G19-NEG-01, H19-04 and r2 A38-01 do not cover source-table versus return-row order. 291ddb0066 (#14975) is an ancestor of the base.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A38-01` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

<details><summary>Full validated claim (source part)</summary>

### R3-A38-01 — The AF_XDP FIB evaluates #9819/#14975 rib-group RETURN rows before the source VRF's own routes, but the kernel consults the VRF table first (l3mdev pref 1000), so the fast path sends tenant-A traffic into tenant B even when A has its own covering route
- **Finding ID:** R3-A38-01

## #16800 — On an xpf route reflector, export-policy set clauses (the #5115 `then next-hop self` lowering, local-preference, community) are discarded by bgpd on reflected iBGP routes because `bgp route-reflector allow-outbound-policy` is never rendered… [OPEN]

## Summary

On an xpf route reflector, export-policy set clauses (the #5115 `then next-hop self` lowering, local-preference, community) are discarded by bgpd on reflected iBGP routes because `bgp route-reflector allow-outbound-policy` is never rendered (#2977 blackhole returns for reflected routes)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A11-06`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — RR clients receive reflected routes with the original next-hop and attributes despite `next-hop self` / `local-preference` / `community` in the export policy. Clients without an IGP path to that next-hop blackhole the traffic (the #2977 failure), and traffic engineering on reflected routes …
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the code's own documented guarantee (#2977 stays fixed on RR-reflected routes) is false for every RR config.

## Mechanism

client A advertises 10.9/16 NH 192.0.2.99 → RR best path (iBGP from client) → advertisement to client B (iBGP) → `route-map NHS out` applied to a dummy attribute copy → B receives NH 192.0.2.99, LP 100 → B forwards toward an unreachable next-hop.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1318-1344`: `then next-hop self` becomes `set ip next-hop peer-address` / `set ipv6 next-hop peer-address`, replacing `next-hop-self force` (2004bd1375 / merge c500aacf83, ancestor of the base). `pkg/frr/protocols_render_bgp.go:47` renders `bgp cluster-id`; neighbor `route-reflector-client` and `route-map <export> out` are rendered. `grep -rn allow-outbound pkg/frr` finds no hit. FRR `bgpd/bgp_route.c` (stable/10.6, reporter's `evidence/rr/bgp_route_10.6.c:2826-2835`): with IBGP→IBGP and no `BGP_FLAG_RR_ALLOW_OUTBOUND_POLICY`, the route-map runs on `dummy_attr`.

## Impact

"RR sets next-hop self toward clients" and "RR re-tags or sets local-pref on reflected routes" are common designs. The operator sees the policy attached and the `set` lines present, while clients get unreachable next-hops or wrong preferences. The project already fixed the non-RR half twice (#2977, #5115).

## Acceptance / fix direction

Render `bgp route-reflector allow-outbound-policy` in every `router bgp` stanza (default and VRF) that has a `route-reflector-client` neighbor, or at least when an export chain on such a stanza has modifying terms. Acceptance: in the probe topology with the xpf render, the RR's adj-RIB-out to B shows NH self and LP 777 for 10.9/16; non-RR stanzas render byte-identically.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1336-1340`: "Like the old `force`, an outbound `set` overrides the next-hop on iBGP / route-reflector-reflected routes too, so the #2977 iBGP blackhole stays fixed". #2977 itself. Junos applies BGP export policy, including `next-hop self`, to reflected advertisements.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A11-06` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A11-06 | Medium | On an xpf route reflector, export-policy set clauses (the #5115 then next-hop self… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:25: - **R3-A11-06 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** RR cluster-id and export route maps are rendered but `then next-hop self` lowers to outbound `set ... peer-address` (`pkg/frr/protocols_render_bgp.go:43-47`, `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1297-1325`). ## #16801 — R3-A54-04: runShutdownSequence calls the signal context's stop() before wg.Wait and the fail-closed block, so a second SIGTERM/SIGINT in that window kills xpfd before kernel… [OPEN]

## Summary

runShutdownSequence calls the signal context's stop() before wg.Wait and the fail-closed block, so a second SIGTERM/SIGINT in that window kills xpfd before kernel transit is closed, rg_active cleared and (HA) Kea stopped

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — this needs a deliberate second termination signal from root (`systemctl kill xpfd`, `kill <pid>`) inside a narrow window: after `stop()`, during `wg.Wait()` and the IPsec capture shutdown. The consequence is the #10643/#6787 hazard: standalone kernel transit legs are left open for the downtime, and in HA Kea is left answering beside the promoted peer. When `wg.Wait()` itself is the slow step and would exceed 20s, the TimeoutStopSec SIGKILL already produces the same outcome. [reporter: Low-Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A54-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va54.md` (finding `R3-A54-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:114-115` has `ctx, stop := startupSignalContext(ctx); defer stop()`. Lines `:1120-1122` have `signal.NotifyContext(parent, daemonSignals(isInteractive())...)`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:160-162` has `// Cancel context to stop background goroutines ... stop()  wg.Wait()`, and then `:166` `d.shutdownIpsecCapture()`, `:248-255` `d.markDataplaneNotArmed(...)`, `:257-280` rg_active clear and `:312-319` `d.dhcpServer.Shutdown()`. No other SIGTERM/SIGINT Notify is live in daemon mode (daemon_apply_commit.go:502 is a comment, and pkg/cli's Notify exists only inside the interactive shell). `test/incus/xpfd.service` has no ExecStopPost backstop.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:168-198` (#9035) says "THE FAIL-CLOSED ACTIONS RUN FIRST ... Exactly two actions must have completed". `:221-255` (#9686/#10643) closes kernel transit before detach. `:282-319` (#6787) stops Kea before relinquishing. #15084 keeps SIGHUP captured for the whole Run so a stray signal cannot skip the sequence.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (process signal-disposition residuals of #5807/#15084, with R3-F06-03 helper SIGHUP) — real and trivial to fix. The trigger needs root plus a timed second signal.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — a re-exec probe using the production `ignoreSIGHUP` and `startupSignalContext` seams in Run's order, with a twin sink and a HUP control. The consequence chain through markDataplaneNotArmed/Kea is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High for the signal mechanism. Medium for how often the trigger occurs.

## Impact

an operator who resends a stop signal to a slow-stopping node can turn the fail-closed stop that #9686/#10643/#6787 built into a fail-open one: the standalone kernel forwards under a stale fence, and an HA node's Kea keeps serving beside the peer's Kea.

## Acceptance / fix direction

cancel background goroutines with a separate CancelFunc, or before `stop()` install a long-lived `signal.Notify` sink for SIGTERM/SIGINT that logs "shutdown already in progress" until runShutdownSequence returns. SIGKILL then remains the only hard stop. Acceptance: the probe's production rows report `completed-fail-closed=true`.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A54-04`, part `parts/va54.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16802 — #15271 residual. `accountPBRWindowExhausted` identifies the triggering attachment by filter name and resumes at the first attachment of that name. When a filter attached on several interfaces exhausts the PBR window, attachments that were installed, and the trigger itself, are counted again as degraded. [OPEN]

## Summary

#15271 residual. `accountPBRWindowExhausted` identifies the triggering attachment by filter name and resumes at the first attachment of that name. When a filter attached on several interfaces exhausts the PBR window, attachments that were installed, and the trigger itself, are counted again as degraded.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A38-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — The defect is an operator-visible over-count in `xpf_pbr_degraded_terms` and in the degraded error list, which shows duplicate, indistinguishable lines. The installed kernel rule set is correct, so enforcement does not change [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (#15271 PBR degraded-reporting residuals) — The miscount is real and reachable but counter-only.

## Mechanism

The input filter is attached on N units. collectAttachedInputFilters produces N attachments, sorted. The build exhausts the window at attachment k. accountPBRWindowExhausted then re-accounts attachments 2..N of the same name. PBRBuildRulesAndStats counts the joined errors, and the metric and commit warning report them.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/routing/rules.go:1379-1399` has `pastTrigger := skipFilter == ""; ... if att.Filter == skipFilter { pastTrigger = true }; continue`, which flips on the first attachment of that name. Attachments are sorted (filter, iif) (`:1483-1490`), so the trigger at the last iif re-accounts every earlier-built attachment after the first.

## Impact

Operators sizing FBF against the 500-rule window see inflated losses and duplicate messages, and cannot tell which interface actually lost steering.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Pass the trigger attachment's index or its (filter, iif) pair and resume strictly after it. Acceptance: both probe arms report degraded=1.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/routing/rules.go:1209-1216` comment (#5683/#15271 block) and the #15271 / a99ba0b428 intent: the degraded error and count must "name all that is lost — not only the term that crossed". The accountPBRWindowExhausted doc (`:1364-1378`) says "accounting resumes at the NEXT attachment".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A38-02` (parts file `parts/va38.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A38-02 | Low | #15271 residual. accountPBRWindowExhausted identifies the triggering attachment by filter…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): This is a residual of #15271 (CLOSED, fix a99ba0b428 in base), which addressed the r2 B21-02 under-count; this is the over-count its predicate introduced. f09 and vf09 cover a different #15271 aspect (budget shadowing, NEG). No other report names it.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A38-02` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16803 — R3-A55-02: `show security match-policies` / `test policy` / REST / gRPC certify a policy verdict for IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 tuples (source or destination, transit… [OPEN]

## Summary

`show security match-policies` / `test policy` / REST / gRPC certify a policy verdict for IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 tuples (source or destination, transit and host-bound) that the helper drops at ingress before any policy (#10686/#11669)

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — an operator-visible false verdict on every match-policies surface. The box is stricter than the answer (an unconditional ingress drop), the daemon's enforcement consumers of `policymatch.Match` (rename rebind, rollback re-authorization) reject mapped tuples themselves, and no protection is hidden. Demonstrated at the simulator, with the runtime drop read statically. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A55-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va55.md` (finding `R3-A55-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

Observed at d1ea69f9aa:
  - `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1119-1133`: `if !is_injected && ipv6_frame_has_v4_mapped_or_compat(raw_frame, meta.addr_family) { … if !wg_underlay { … v4_mapped_ipv6_dropped += 1; … continue; } }`. This runs before the VLAN, zone, session, NAT and policy stages. Decapsulated and injected frames are dropped at `:1376-1382`.
  - `afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:877-963` checks SRC OR DST, `::ffff:0:0/96` plus IPv4-compatible `::/96`, excluding `::` and `::1`. Its doc names "Go simulator parity" as one reason it drops instead of folding.
  - `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:1115-1167`: `transitMartianClass` folds a mapped address through `To4()` and leaves a compat address as ordinary v6, so neither gets a route-drop class.
  - `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:1505-1516` and the tier walk that follows then evaluate these addresses normally.
  - The fix commit 2211a437ac (#11669) is an ancestor of the base.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/policymatch/README.md` "Ground truth": where the runtime and the simulator disagree, the runtime wins. The package already models other pre-policy drops through `RouteDropBeforePolicy` / `RouteDropClass` (the martian advisory, #15238). `pkg/policymatch/README.md:690-700` still says a mapped v6 tuple "should be evaluated normally", but #10686 made that false.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (policymatch verdicts for traffic the runtime never policy-evaluates — with R3-A55-03; sibling R3-B09-03, the NAT commit gates that are also unaware of the #10686 identity rule) — real and reproduced, but a bounded diagnostic lie where the box is stricter than the answer.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the Go probe drives `ParseSelectorArgs` → `Match` → `DisplayAction` in `pkg/policymatch`. The Rust ingress drop is STATIC (source read; not executed in this pass).

**Confidence:** High — the drop gate is unconditional except for the WireGuard underlay and is pinned by Rust tests. The simulator side was executed through the operator grammar with positive controls. The only assumption is that operators actually query these address shapes.

## Impact

An operator verifying that an IPv4 deny covers v4-mapped IPv6 sources is told the v6 permit admits them. They may then add rules or file a false bypass report, and automation that trusts the REST verdict will mis-inventory reachable services. Impact is limited to these address shapes, lasts while the query is believed, and needs no recovery.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `Match`, before tier evaluation, classify any v6-family side in `::ffff:0:0/96` or IPv4-compatible `::/96` (excluding `::` and `::1`), mirroring `ipv6_addr_is_v4_mapped_or_compat`. Return a first-class "dropped at ingress (v4-mapped/compatible IPv6, #10686)" verdict for both transit and host-bound queries, surfaced through `DisplayAction` and the REST/gRPC fields. Also update README:690-700 and the #6377 tests. Acceptance: the four defect rows and the host-bound row report the ingress drop, while the v4, ordinary-v6 and link-local controls are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16804 — systemd-networkd keeps its default `ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=yes`, and xpf never overrides it. networkd therefore deletes every xpf ip rule when xpf runs `networkctl reconfigure` and whenever networkd restarts. xpf re-asserts only the #9819 VRF miss terminator. The management-DNS steering rules are installed before the networkd activation and are lost on every commit that changes a networkd file, which takes the management DHCP name-servers out of resolv.conf. After a networkd restart, the next-table, rib-group and PBR rules have no owner until the next commit. [OPEN]

## Summary

systemd-networkd keeps its default `ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=yes`, and xpf never overrides it. networkd therefore deletes every xpf ip rule when xpf runs `networkctl reconfigure` and whenever networkd restarts. xpf re-asserts only the #9819 VRF miss terminator. The management-DNS steering rules are installed before the networkd activation and are lost on every commit that changes a networkd file, which takes the management DHCP name-servers out of resolv.conf. After a networkd restart, the next-table, rib-group and PBR rules have no owner until the next commit.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A38-03`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — The commit arm is deterministic but bounded. It fails closed: the management resolver is dropped from resolv.conf and nothing leaks. It recovers on the next lease change or on a commit that changes no networkd file. The restart arm silently removes every inter-VRF leak and every kernel FBF steer, and the userspace FIB mirror loses them on its next republish, which is High-shaped. Its trigger, though, is external (a systemd upgrade, an admin restart or a watchdog restart) and its frequency is unmeasured, so the finding stays at Medium [reporter: Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — An ordinary interface commit reaches it on the shipped mgmt-VRF + fxp0 DHCP layout, and the consequence is concrete: host DNS is lost. The project already knows the mechanism (#10421) but fixed only one rule.

## Mechanism

A commit changes a generated `.network` file. applyMgmtDNSRules installs the 2500–2503 pairs. networkd.Apply runs reload and reconfigure, and networkd removes all foreign rules except proto kernel. The terminator is re-asserted and applyRoutingRules re-adds the leaks and PBR rules. The tail reconcileDNSLocked finds no mgmt-DNS lookup rule and resolv.conf loses the fxp0 DHCP resolvers. On a networkd restart, all rules go, and only the terminator (30 s tick) and the probe pins (#1895 loop) heal. The next routes-only snapshot republish (routes.go reads `netlink.RuleList`) also drops the leaks from the AF_XDP FIB.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/networkd/networkd.go:643-695`: when files change or debt is owed, xpf runs `networkctl reload` and then `networkctl reconfigure -- <every managed, non-bond-member iface>`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:633` has `mgmtRouteErr := errors.Join(mgmtRouteApplyErr, d.applyMgmtDNSRules())`, which runs before `:676 core := d.applyDataplaneAndHACore(ctx, cfg)`, where `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:376` calls `d.networkd.Apply(...)`. The only post-activation rule re-asserts are `ReassertVRFMissTerminator` at `:389-395` and `:650-660`, and `applyRoutingRules` (`daemon_apply.go:744`), whose next-table, rib-group and PBR Apply clears and re-adds (`pkg/routing/rules.go:123-260`). The tail `reconcileDNSLocked` (`daemon_apply_tail.go:186`) calls `mgmtDNSRuleReadiness` (`daemon_dns.go:523`) and drops any management lease server without a ready rule (`daemon_dns.go:244-246`, "skipping management DHCP name-server without an installed host-routing rule"). The only other `applyMgmtDNSRules` caller is `reconcileDNSFromDHCP` (`daemon_dns.go:557-570`), which runs on a lease change. `routing_reconcile_debt_9693.go:204-232`: the 30 s tick runs only `vrfMissTerminatorReconcileFn` unless `routingDebt.owed`, which only a failed apply sets. Repo-wide grep finds no `ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules` and no networkd.conf drop-in.

## Impact

On the shipped mgmt-VRF + `fxp0 family inet dhcp` layout, any commit that touches interface addressing silently removes the box's own resolvers, so package updates, feeds and NTP-by-name break until the next lease change. A systemd upgrade or a networkd restart silently removes every inter-VRF leak and FBF steer, on the kernel path and, after the next republish, in the helper, while status stays green until the operator commits again.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Ship `/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/xpf.conf` with `[Network] ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no`, installed by the package and the image bake. In addition, either move applyMgmtDNSRules after the activation, or re-assert all xpf rule bands after networkd.Apply and on a periodic readback, like the terminator. Acceptance: in the netns probe, all rules survive reconfigure and restart. The Go order probe shows MGMT-DNS-RULES-INSTALL after NETWORKD-RECONFIGURE. A restart cell shows the next-table and rib-group rules restored without a commit.

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/routing/README.md` documents the ip-rule priority bands as xpf-owned state that must be present after a successful apply. The 2500–2503 management-DNS lookup/shadow pairs exist so that management DNS is steered into table 999 and cannot fall through to main. `daemon_apply_dataplane.go:389-391` already records that "networkd's foreign-rule cleanup can remove the VRF miss terminator that applyVRFReconcile installed before activation".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A38-03` (parts file `parts/va38.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A38-03 | Medium | systemd-networkd keeps its default ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=yes, and xpf never…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL
- Dedup note (source): I checked gh-issues.tsv (foreign/networkd/reconfigure/rule), prior-headings.tsv, /var/tmp/deep-review-reports and the in-run parts and reports. #10421 (CLOSED) re-asserts only the terminator and does not generalize. #14594 and #15061/A37-02 are networkd stripping ADDRESSES. The #12539 log covers foreign ROUTES. b21 defers this to R3-A38-03. No prior entry names foreign routing-policy-rule cleanup for the other bands.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A38-03` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16805 — R3-A55-03: A host-originated query (`from-zone junos-host`) is answered with the unknown-ingress-zone deny ("transit on an interface in no zone is denied unconditionally"),… [OPEN]

## Summary

A host-originated query (`from-zone junos-host`) is answered with the unknown-ingress-zone deny ("transit on an interface in no zone is denied unconditionally"), although host-originated traffic is never policy-evaluated

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a false DENY with a false mechanism on a documented-unsupported query direction. There is no enforcement effect. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A55-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va55.md` (finding `R3-A55-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

Observed at d1ea69f9aa:
  - `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:2082-2090` `zoneKnown` requires membership in `cfg.Security.Zones`, so `junos-host` fails.
  - `:1514-1516`: `if !zoneKnown(cfg, q.FromZone) { return Result{UnzonedIngress: true, Action: config.PolicyDeny} }`.
  - `:1251` `UnzonedIngressActionString` = "deny (ingress zone unknown — transit on an interface in no zone is denied unconditionally; default-policy NOT applied)".
  - The host gate branch handles only `ToZone == junos-host`.
  - REST passes `from_zone` through unchanged (`pkg/api/security.go:781-790`, `:949`).
  - The #12684 fix (596764a7ec, an ancestor) added the junos-host arm only to `GlobalPolicyAppliesToZonePairInZones`, the view filter.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `docs/junos-cli-reference.md:890-900`: `from-zone junos-host` (host-originated) rules "are NOT consulted: locally-generated traffic … egresses via the kernel TX path", and both forms are rejected at strict commit (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:589-608`, #3611 Piece A / #4230). The simulator's own display helper already encodes this at `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go:1966-1975`: "from-zone junos-host with a transit to-zone selects nothing (host-originated traffic never traverses the RX policy gate)". The true answer is "not subject to security policy", not an unknown-zone deny.

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (policymatch verdicts for traffic the runtime never policy-evaluates — with R3-A55-02) — real but bounded diagnostic.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the Go probe uses the operator grammar and has controls. The claim that no host-egress policy hook exists is STATIC (commit gate and docs).

**Confidence:** High — executed, and the runtime fact is stated by the commit gate and the CLI reference. The remaining assumption is that SRX-trained operators issue this query, because Junos treats `from-zone junos-host` as a real self-traffic context.

## Impact

An operator asking whether the firewall may reach its NTP or DNS server is told an unknown-zone condition blocks it. They may add zone bindings or `from-zone junos-host` policies that strict commit rejects or that never match. This is a bounded diagnostic cost with no recovery needed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `Match` (or in `ParseSelectorArgs` and the REST/gRPC validators), treat `FromZone == junos-host` as a first-class "host-originated: not evaluated by security policy (kernel TX path, #3611/#4230)" verdict, distinct from `UnzonedIngress`, on every surface. Acceptance: the probe's junos-host row renders the new verdict, and the `from-zone nosuch` and `to-zone junos-host` controls are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;

## #16806 — #15944 (H23-02) residual. `mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces` still maps the authored control/fabric reference with `LinuxIfName`, which only converts "/". A unit-suffixed `control-interface em0.0` is therefore not recognised as a mgmt-VRF member, and the #11362 classless fence protects no interface. [OPEN]

## Summary

#15944 (H23-02) residual. `mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces` still maps the authored control/fabric reference with `LinuxIfName`, which only converts "/". A unit-suffixed `control-interface em0.0` is therefore not recognised as a mgmt-VRF member, and the #11362 classless fence protects no interface.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A38-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low — The loss is a documented "never" fence, but it bites only when the operator has set `XPF_DHCP_TRUST_CLASSLESS_OVERRIDE=1` and uses the unit spelling. Without the override, the generic #11383 connected-subnet check still suppresses the route. Device-bound HA sockets should not select a route out fxp0, so harm to HA traffic is not demonstrated [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (#15944 H23-02 authored-ref → kernel-name resolution residuals) — This is a real gap at a site that H23-02 itself named, and the merged fix skipped it. It is minor because it sits behind an explicit trust override.

## Mechanism

`set chassis cluster control-interface em0.0` is accepted by commit, and the cluster comms resolve it to em0 since #15944. An fxp0 DHCP lease carries option 121 for a prefix inside em0's 10.99.0.0/24. applyMgmtVRFRoutesTo calls mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces, which returns [], so the fence has no links. With the override set, the #11383 check yields and the route is installed in table 999.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/daemon/mgmtvrf_routes.go:36-63` reads `name = config.LinuxIfName(name); if name == "" || !mgmtSet[name] { continue }`, so for "em0.0" the result is `em0.0`, which is not in `{em0, fxp0}` and is skipped. `pkg/daemon/daemon_flow.go:512-515` feeds the result into `mgmtVRFControlFabricLinkIndexes`. `daemon_flow.go:699-711` is the control/fabric fence (no override check). `:716-731` is the #11383 check, which yields to `trustClassless`. `git show b758ac914b --stat` shows the fix touched daemon_cluster_bind.go, daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go, daemon_ha_sync.go and dupaddr_watch, but not mgmtvrf_routes.go. gemini vsrx-parity-003 H23-02 lists `pkg/daemon/mgmtvrf_routes.go:36-63 (mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces)` among its sites.

## Impact

Clusters that author unit spellings and deliberately trust their management DHCP server lose the one fence documented as unconditional. Blast radius is the mgmt-VRF table, including control-link-subnet routing for non-device-bound traffic.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Use `cfg.ResolveKernelIfName(name)` in mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces, as transportVRFBinding does now. Acceptance: the probe's em0.0 arm returns [em0], and a #11362 cell with the override and a unit spelling suppresses the control-prefix classless route.

## Contract (where cited)

CLAUDE.md DHCP bullet: #11362 suppresses a classless route contained in a configured cluster control/fabric connected prefix "regardless of the classless trust override ... never cluster control/fabric connected-prefix routes". #15944 / b758ac914b commit text: authored control/fabric refs must go through `ResolveKernelIfName`, because "the '/'→'-'-only LinuxIfName handles neither unit/VLAN netdevs nor device-map aliases".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A38-04` (parts file `parts/va38.md` in research-work.mx0fDlYpEK, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A38-04 | Low | #15944 (H23-02) residual. mgmtVRFControlFabricInterfaces still maps the authored…`
- Validated-by: three research lanes (codex, smr, wonder) — votes: codex/smr/wonder=codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT
- Dedup note (source): This is a residual of gemini vsrx-parity-003 H23-02, fixed by #15944 (CLOSED, b758ac914b, ancestor of d1ea69f9aa per `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), whose change set omits this named site. #11362 and #11383 (CLOSED) introduced the fences. No in-run part covers it.
- Dedupe re-check at filing: searched GitHub open+closed issues for finding ID and for `**Finding ID:** R3-A38-04` in source:deep-review issue bodies — no existing owner found at filing time (any incidental cross-reference is not an owner issue for this claim).

## #16807 — R3-A56-01: `isPkgInstalled` matches only `install ok installed`, so a held package (`hold ok installed`) reads as confirmed-absent. Every prune of the always-held candidate… [OPEN]

## Summary

`isPkgInstalled` matches only `install ok installed`, so a held package (`hold ok installed`) reads as confirmed-absent. Every prune of the always-held candidate skips `apt-get purge` and sweeps the package-owned files, which makes the #5076/#5428 guard inert.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. Every discarded roll (firmware fell back) and every revert entered off the candidate leaves the candidate's linux-image/modules/modules-extra/headers recorded by dpkg as held and installed, while their /boot and /lib/modules payload is deleted, their maintainer scripts never run, and /usr/src/linux-headers-<cand> leaks. That is durable package-DB/filesystem divergence that accumulates per roll. Demonstrated: the divergence and the skipped purge. Not demonstrated: any downstream apt breakage. The #5076 re-arm brick does not follow, because a same-version re-arm unholds first and forces --reinstall. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A56-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va56.md` (finding `R3-A56-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/upgrade/kernel_linux.go:1107-1115` contains `out, err := captureCmd("dpkg-query", "-W", "-f=${Status}", pkg)` … `return strings.Contains(out, "install ok installed"), nil`. At `:1031-1038` the pre-purge loop adds a package only `if qerr != nil || ok`; `:1039` `if len(installed) > 0 {` is then skipped; `:1079-1088` `os.RemoveAll(/lib/modules/<cand>)` plus every `/boot/*-<cand>`. The only caller is `kernel_run.go:915`, reached when running != candidate. The only unhold is `kernel_linux.go:312` (inside InstallCandidateKernel), so nothing unholds between arm and prune. Observation: real dpkg-query prints `hold ok installed|installed` for a held package and `install ok installed|installed` for an unheld one.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/upgrade/kernel_linux.go:1064-1078` says "manual deletion of package-owned files must ONLY follow a CONFIRMED removal" and that the sweep runs only when the candidate packages are "confirmed ABSENT". `:1010-1013` says "The candidate kernel packages are HELD … so `apt-get purge` must be allowed to change held packages". #5076 and #5428 are the issues that established this contract.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a reachable, consequential state-corruption defect in a guard whose stated contract is never to desync dpkg.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. The production `isPkgInstalled` and `PruneInactiveSlot` ran against the real dpkg-query 1.23.11 with a fake admindir. The verifier independently checked `${Status}` and `${db:Status-Status}` for a held and an unheld package.

**Confidence:** High for the mechanism (real dpkg-query semantics executed twice, independently). Medium for operational consequence beyond divergence and leak. On a dpkg DB that carries stray not-installed linux-* names, R3-A56-04 currently stops arm before any prune can be reached.

## Impact

Every appliance that discards or reverts a roll off the candidate accumulates gutted, held kernel packages. Package audits (`dpkg -V`) on an image whose validation relies on package identity report missing files, and root-fs space leaks under /usr/src. The safety tests stay green because they bypass the real query.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Classify by the status word, for example `-f=${db:Status-Status}` == `installed`, and treat half-installed/unpacked/half-configured/triggers-* as possibly installed. Share one helper with R3-A56-04's enumeration. Acceptance: with a real-dpkg admindir fixture holding `hold ok installed` candidates, PruneInactiveSlot issues `apt-get purge … --allow-change-held-packages`, and it keeps the files if the re-query still reports installed.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A56-01`, part `parts/va56.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).
