## #16809 — R3-A56-02: ARMING is classified everywhere as "firmware one-shot never set", but two paths reach ARMING with BootNext actually queued. (a) Process death between SetBootNext… [OPEN]

## Summary

ARMING is classified everywhere as "firmware one-shot never set", but two paths reach ARMING with BootNext actually queued. (a) Process death between SetBootNext (`kernel_run.go:470`) and the ARMED rename (`:506`). (b) A SetBootNext error after the write landed, for example the 10 s kill timeout: the error branch does not clear BootNext. The next boot runs the candidate kernel while Promote, the outer hop, the daemon election hold and the status surface all treat it as an ordinary boot.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. An unverified candidate kernel (verify-dataplane and beacon never run) forwards traffic on a standalone box, or joins the HA election with no kernel-upgrade hold, until the next reboot. In variant (b) the failed arm makes xpf-deploy rejoin the node, and the candidate is queued for an arbitrary later reboot. This is the hazard #6758 was filed for (High). It is bounded: a fault in a short window is required, firmware clears BootNext so there is only one candidate boot, and the next plain reboot returns to known-good. Potential, not demonstrated on hardware. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A56-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va56.md` (finding `R3-A56-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`kernel_run.go:466` transitions to ARMING. `:470-478`: `if err := sys.SetBootNext(inactiveID); err != nil { … return false, disarmWatchdogAfterArmFailure(sys, …) }`, with the comment "BootNext was not set" and no `ClearBootNext`. `:485-512`: only the GetBootNext error, readback mismatch, recordPromoteBinary and ARMED-rename failures use `disarmAfterArmFailure` (which clears BootNext). `kernel_linux.go:446-448` SetBootNext = `runCmdTimeout(kernelNVRAMTimeout, "efibootmgr", "--bootnext", id)`. `kernel_run.go:623` `if !j.State.atLeast(KernelStateArmed) { … "ordinary boot, nothing to promote"; return … nil }`. `scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote:62` `JOURNAL_ARMED_STATE="ARMED"`. `pkg/daemon/kernel_selfrecover.go:83-110` gates the hold on `IsArmed()` (ARMED only).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/upgrade/kernel.go:67-76` (KernelStateArming) says a journal stuck at ARMING "is NOT a genuine in-flight trial: the firmware still boots the known-good default". The #6758 commit 60ed1fa42c says "BootNext stayed armed while every durable software gate classified the node as unarmed … a drained node could rejoin with an untested candidate kernel queued". The `kernel_status.go:194-197` operator text says "the next boot is the KNOWN-GOOD kernel".

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — a residual of #6758 whose clear-on-failure predicate covers only the four post-SetBootNext error returns, not process death and not SetBootNext's own error.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. Production `KernelRunner.Arm` then `Promote` ran with the package fake system: the reporter's panic-injection probe for (a), and the verifier probe for (b). The firmware and efivarfs timing for (b) is NEEDS_VALIDATION.

**Confidence:** High for the state-machine mechanism, both variants executed. Medium for incidence: (a) needs process death in a window of a few efibootmgr execs, and (b) needs firmware whose SetVariable outlasts 10 s, or an efibootmgr non-zero exit after the write, and the write must still land.

## Impact

Gate 3 (verify-dataplane) exists to catch a candidate kernel that breaks AF_XDP. Here that kernel serves traffic: standalone, the box blackholes until someone reboots it; in HA, the node runs without the election hold. Variant (b) can surface days after a "failed" arm the operator already wrote off.

## Acceptance / fix direction

(1) In the SetBootNext error branch, use `disarmAfterArmFailure` (clear BootNext unconditionally; clearing an absent BootNext is already a success). (2) On boot, treat `ARMING && BootCurrent == entries[InactiveSlot] && uname -r == CandidateVersion` as a genuine trial: run the gates or revert, have the daemon hold fail closed on the same predicate, and make xpf-kernel-promote and kernel_status stop asserting "next boot is known-good" without reading BootNext. Acceptance: both probe defect rows end reverted (or gated) with the hold set, and the control rows are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A56-02`, part `parts/va56.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16810 — In an active/active RG split, both cluster nodes run OSPF under the same router-id (an explicit or inherited `routing-options router-id`), so the routing domain keeps only one node's RETH prefixes at a time and ECMPs them to both nodes [OPEN]

## Summary

In an active/active RG split, both cluster nodes run OSPF under the same router-id (an explicit or inherited `routing-options router-id`), so the routing domain keeps only one node's RETH prefixes at a time and ECMPs them to both nodes

**Finding ID:** `R3-A12-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — while data RGs are split across nodes (the supported active/active state), the OSPF area sees one router-id announced by two routers. A neighbouring router keeps one node's router-LSA at a time: the other node's RETH prefixes disappear from the whole area, the surviving ones are ECMP'd to b…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — the trigger is reachable through strict commit and routine per-RG failover, the consequence (domain-wide loss and mis-ECMP of RETH prefixes) is concrete, and no guard or owner exists.

## Mechanism

One config is config-synced to both nodes. `routing-options router-id X` goes through `resolveRoutingOptionsRouterID` into OSPF.RouterID. On each node, `assembleFRRConfig` calls `newFRRHADemotionState` and then `filterProtocols`, which keeps the RG1 RETH unit on the RG1 owner and the RG2 RETH unit on the RG2 owner. Both managed frr.conf files then carry `router ospf / ospf router-id X` with an active `ip ospf area`. Both ospfd processes originate router-LSAs with Advertising Router X. Neighbours keep the newest one, the other node's links vanish, and the self-originated-LSA conflict flips at refresh.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_frr_rg_shutdown_11415.go:322-345` @d1ea69f9aa: `filterOSPF` does `filtered := *source` (RouterID retained) and drops only interfaces where `inactiveInterface` is true. `:382-394`: `filterISIS` keeps `NET`. `pkg/config/compiler_routing.go:1585-1607` `resolveRoutingOptionsRouterID`: `if ospf != nil && ospf.RouterID == "" { ospf.RouterID = routerID }` for the global instance and every routing instance (and the same for OSPFv3 and BGP). `pkg/frr/protocols_render_ospf.go:25-26`: `fmt.Fprintf(b, " ospf router-id %s\n", ospf.RouterID)`. `pkg/frr/protocols_render_isis.go:91`: ` net %s`. Observation: I found no cluster-mode uniqueness check for router-id or NET in pkg/config or pkg/daemon, and pkg/frr/README.md and docs/config-schema.md:16243-16273 give no per-node requirement.

## Impact

Per-RG failover is the routine HA operation, and the split state is exercised by the project's own active/active gate. During every split, half the IGP-advertised RETH prefixes behind the cluster flap out of the whole area, and the rest are load-shared toward a node that does not own them. Recovery is to rejoin the RGs or configure per-node router-ids. The same shape applies to OSPFv3 (inherited router-id) and IS-IS (shared NET).

## Acceptance / fix direction

In cluster mode, either reject at strict commit (warn on tolerant load) a non-node-specific OSPF/OSPFv3 router-id and IS-IS NET when IGP interfaces span RETHs of more than one data RG, or derive or require a node-specific identity (for example via `${node}` groups), or run each IGP instance only where Junos semantics put it. Acceptance: the split render yields distinct identities (or a single participating node), and the three-router check shows both stub prefixes, each via its owner.

## Contract (where cited)

RFC 2328 §1.2 (fetched): Router ID is "A 32-bit number assigned to each router running the OSPF protocol. This number uniquely identifies the router within an Autonomous System." The #11415 contract (`pkg/daemon/daemon_frr_rg_shutdown_11415.go:53-57`) says dynamic routing follows per-RG ownership, which puts both nodes into the IGP at once during a split. Active/active is a supported cluster state (#9139 "supported active/active cluster"; the `test-active-active` smoke).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A12-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A12-01 | Medium | In an active/active RG split, both cluster nodes run OSPF under the same router-id (an… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch01:29: - **R3-A12-01 — MATERIAL (Medium; OSPF verified at base).** **Defect:** shared global router ID propagates into OSPF even across VRFs (`pkg/config/compiler_routing.go:1581-1606`); active/active RG demotion copies OSPF structs (including RouterID) and filters interfaces *per node* (`pkg/daemon/daemon_frr_rg_shutdown_11415.go:322-344`). Both active routers can originate LSAs with one router ID; the prior FRR multi-router topology observed missing/flapping RETH prefixes. **Best alternative:** active/passive, no configured ID, or node-specific `groups nodeN` IDs avoid the trigger; IS-IS shared-NET is only a source-level analogue, not shown to have the same observed LSA effect. **Remaining check:** current assembled HA split with two owned RGs and a router receiving both LSAs on the deployment FRR, plus per-node ID control.

**SMR:** smr batch01 L23: | R3-A12-01 duplicate OSPF router-id in RG split | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-03 RIP per-group export flattened | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-05 VL-only area on standby hard-fails apply | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A12-02 BFD-default perpetual --test diff | COHORT | Low | | R3-A12-04 OSPF key >16/>8 truncation + perpetual diff | COHORT | Low | | R3-A13-01 deny-* bracket list first-token only | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A13-02 permission fold widens to PermView vs doc | COHORT (doc/advisory only) | Low | | R3-A14-05 wakeAt never cleared busy-spin | MATERIAL | Medium | | R3-A14-01 parked direction skips windowing, until ceiling defeated | MATERIAL | Medium-Low |

## #16811 — R3-A56-03: When revert runs while the candidate is the running kernel, restoreKnownGood correctly defers the prune (#14165), but revert then clears the journal… [OPEN]

## Summary

When revert runs while the candidate is the running kernel, restoreKnownGood correctly defers the prune (#14165), but revert then clears the journal (`kernel_run.go:849`, `:855-857`). Nothing persists "prune owed", so every failed candidate kernel stays installed, held and on disk permanently.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low. A root-fs leak of hundreds of MB per failed roll, plus a stale GRUB 10_linux entry, on the common failure path (verify-dataplane REJECT, beacon fail, BootOrder write fail). There is no enforcement impact, and the next preflight checks only /boot and the ESP. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A56-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va56.md` (finding `R3-A56-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`kernel_run.go:912-913` defers when `running == j.CandidateVersion`. `:855` `_ = r.ktransition(j, KernelStateReverted)`, `:857` and `:849` `_ = r.clearKernelJournal()`. `:623` returns early on the next boot. `kernel_run.go:915` is the only PruneInactiveSlot caller.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** The `kernel_run.go:878-884` restoreKnownGood doc says the deferral is safe because "a later gate pass (journal still armed if the clear failed, or the operator) can prune safely". `kernel.go:35-36`: "GC removes only the un-promoted candidate".

**Gate verdict (validated):** COHORT (LANE-1 kernel-channel cleanup/fail-direction, with R3-A56-05) — real but minor: a broken in-code promise that leaks disk.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. Production Arm, Promote (gate fail on the candidate) and a second Promote ran with the package fake system.

**Confidence:** High; executed, and the single PruneInactiveSlot caller was confirmed.

## Impact

Repeated failed trials, the scenario LANE-1 exists to absorb, steadily consume root-fs space on a fixed appliance disk. When the prune is eventually made to run, it will also hit R3-A56-01.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Persist a "prune-owed {slot, candidate, known-good}" record when deferring, and consume it on the next boot where uname != candidate. Alternatively, leave a terminal REVERTED journal for the next Promote to finish. Acceptance: the probe's gate-fail row shows exactly one prune on boot 2.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A56-03`, part `parts/va56.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16812 — R3-A56-04: `currentLinuxPackages` passes not-installed dpkg names (e.g. `linux-headers-3.0`, `linux-image-fb-generic` on the Ubuntu 26.04 base) to `apt-mark hold`, which exits… [OPEN]

## Summary

`currentLinuxPackages` passes not-installed dpkg names (e.g. `linux-headers-3.0`, `linux-image-fb-generic` on the Ubuntu 26.04 base) to `apt-mark hold`, which exits 100. The rehold after the candidate install is fatal, and `KernelHeld` can never be true, so `xpfd upgrade kernel arm` fails after installing the candidate and leaves a PREFLIGHT journal.

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium. The verify-gated LANE-1 channel, documented as the kernel-CVE path, cannot complete on a DB carrying any not-installed name that passes the kernel-prefix filter. Each attempt still mutates the box: the candidate packages are installed and update-initramfs and update-grub run. The PREFLIGHT journal then makes the resume guard refuse any other version until the operator deletes it, and an orchestrated HA kernel roll aborts on its first node. It fails closed: no enforcement loss and no brick. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A56-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/va56.md` (finding `R3-A56-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see `synthesis.md` §1; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/upgrade/kernel_linux.go:1217-1218` `captureCmd("dpkg-query", "-W", "-f=${binary:Package}\n", "linux-*")`, with only `isKernelPkg` (:1202-1215, prefixes include `linux-image-` and `linux-headers-`). `:1188-1194` holdLinuxPackages is `apt-mark hold <all>`. `:374-375` treats a rehold failure as FATAL. `:286-305` KernelHeld requires every enumerated name in `apt-mark showhold`. `kernel_run.go:253-332` preflight has no KernelHeld check, so the failure comes after the install. `db:Status-Status` appears nowhere in pkg/ or cmd/. The test fake's `KernelHeld` returns `f.held` (`kernel_test.go:108`), so no test exercises the real enumeration.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `scripts/image/bake.py:948-968` (#1930 INC-0, fixed in 6e85c28653): "`dpkg-query -W` matches every package dpkg KNOWS OF, not just the installed ones … `apt-mark hold` errors on those … Filter on `${db:Status-Status}`". `pkg/upgrade/kernel.go:61-65` and `kernel_run.go:374-381`: INSTALLED means "(unhold -> install -> rehold)" with the kernel set held again. docs/in-place-upgrade.md (LANE-1) makes this the kernel-patching path.

**Gate verdict (validated):** MATERIAL — the product's only in-place kernel-patch channel is unavailable on the shipped image, and a residual of a fix whose predicate was applied to the bake only.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED. Production `currentLinuxPackages`, `KernelHeld` and `InstallCandidateKernel` ran against real dpkg-query and apt-mark through PATH shims and a fake root; apt-get, update-initramfs and update-grub were no-ops. The verifier independently checked dpkg-query enumeration semantics.

**Confidence:** High for the mechanism (real dpkg-query plus real apt-mark 3.3.3). Medium-High that shipped appliances carry such names: 6e85c28653 measured them on the Ubuntu 26.04 base in a real bake, and this host's Debian DB independently carries `linux-image-6.18.5+deb14-amd64-unsigned` and `linux-image-generic` as not-installed. Not checked on a baked image.

## Impact

Every operator or orchestrator kernel roll on the appliance fails after partially mutating it, which pushes kernel CVE remediation to LANE-2 image replacement. It also currently shadows R3-A56-01, which becomes reachable once this is fixed, so the two fixes should land together.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Enumerate with `-f='${db:Status-Status} ${binary:Package}\n'` and keep `installed` only, mirroring bake.py, in one helper used by hold, unhold, KernelHeld and the prune. Optionally move a KernelHeld-feasibility check into preflight. Acceptance: a Go test with a real dpkg-query admindir fixture containing not-installed `linux-headers-*`/`linux-image-*` names passes InstallCandidateKernel and KernelHeld like the control.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Provenance / dedup

- Provenance: source report `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A56-04`, part `parts/va56.md`; validated by three lanes (codex+smr+wonder ledgers in research-work `ledger-*-batch*.md`, synthesis §1).

## #16813 — The #15203 benign-reload re-check can never certify convergence when a BFD profile uses FRR-default values (or an OSPFv3 BFD profile is rendered), because those lines are a perpetual `frr-reload.py --test` diff, so the #15203 IS-IS removal still… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #15203 benign-reload re-check can never certify convergence when a BFD profile uses FRR-default values (or an OSPFv3 BFD profile is rendered), because those lines are a perpetual `frr-reload.py --test` diff, so the #15203 IS-IS removal still reports a degraded reload

**Finding ID:** `R3-A12-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low — this is a false non-convergence signal (`ErrFRRReloadDegraded`, degraded gauge, retry) on a change whose end state converged, which is exactly the Low consequence #15203 was filed to remove. There is no enforcement loss, and the next retry or commit behaves as before.
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (FRR reload diff-stability / #15203 certification residuals, with R3-A12-04) — real but minor. It is a status-signal accuracy defect sharing one fix theme: render only what FRR keeps in running-config, or normalise default-elided lines in the re-check.

## Mechanism

An IS-IS interface with BFD timers goes through `bfd.addProfile` into a `bfd / profile` block with default-valued lines, which ends up in the managed frr.conf. FRR running-config omits those lines, so every `--test` lists them as additions. On an IS-IS interface removal the primary reload fails benignly, the re-check sees a diff, the additive `vtysh -f` runs, and `ErrFRRReloadDegraded` is returned, so `applyFRRFull` fails the commit as "did not fully converge".

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/frr/bfd.go:150-164` @d1ea69f9aa: for every profile, `fmt.Fprintf(&b, " detect-multiplier %d\n", multiplier)`, `receive-interval`, `transmit-interval`, with defaults substituted (3/300/300). `pkg/frr/manager.go:1717` `} else if m.reloadTestConverged15203() {` and `:1757-1766` return `FrrReloadPyTest(...) == nil`. `pkg/frr/protocols_render_ospfv3.go:120-124` renders only ` ipv6 ospf6 bfd profile P` for a timed interface.

## Impact

Any box with a BFD-timed IGP interface at a default multiplier or interval still gets a degraded report and retry on the routine IS-IS interface removal that #15203 was meant to certify. That erodes trust in the convergence gauge.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Emit BFD profile lines only for non-default values (and the OSPFv3 `ipv6 ospf6 bfd` line FRR holds), or normalise FRR-default-elided lines before `reloadTestHasDiff15203`. Acceptance: the isisrm scenario with profile xpf-300-3 certifies convergence against real FRR (`--test` empty after reload), and the no-change boot `--test` is empty.

## Contract (where cited)

#15203 (CLOSED; `pkg/frr/manager.go:1704-1724`): "Re-check with `frr-reload.py --test`: an empty diff proves the failure benign — certify convergence instead of reporting a degraded reload". Acceptance in #15203: "a commit removing IS-IS from such an interface returns nil."

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A12-02` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A12-02 | Low | The #15203 benign-reload re-check can never certify convergence when a BFD profile uses… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

Claimed IS-IS default-elision and OSPFv3 session churn were not validated, and the virtual-link first-load subcase overlaps an earlier review. **Remaining check:** deployed FRR 10.6 `--test` after a no-change boot/reload with a default-valued BFD profile, with/without profile controls.

## #16814 — Junos-valid sub-statements of the five modeled ALG classes (`dns doctoring`, `dns maximum-message-length`, `ftp ftps-extension`, `sip inactive-media-timeout`, `sip application-screen`, `pptp traceoptions`) are rejected at commit in both AST… [OPEN]

## Summary

Junos-valid sub-statements of the five modeled ALG classes (`dns doctoring`, `dns maximum-message-length`, `ftp ftps-extension`, `sip inactive-media-timeout`, `sip application-screen`, `pptp traceoptions`) are rejected at commit in both AST shapes, while unmodeled ALG classes with arbitrary bodies commit with an advisory

**Finding ID:** `R3-A18-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — fail-visible vSRX drop-in blocker. A config with the common `set security alg dns doctoring none` will not commit. No enforcement change [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (vSRX drop-in config parity: Junos-valid statements rejected at commit) — real, minor, fail-visible

## Mechanism

`set security alg dns doctoring none` → `SetPath` → configstore commit → `SchemaValidateWithDefinitions` → `validateALGPackedTokens` / closed-world child check → commit refused. CompileConfig alone would accept it and silently ignore it

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/schema_security.go:1415-1420`: `"dns": {..., packedTail: true, nodeValidator: validateALGPackedTokens, children: map[string]*schemaNode{"disable": ...}}` (the same for ftp/sip/tftp/pptp), and the wildcard for other classes is `closedWorldOpaque`. `pkg/config/compiler_security_alg.go:21-27`: `case "dns", "ftp", "sip", "tftp", "pptp": ... if token != "disable" { return fmt.Errorf("unknown configuration keyword ...") }`. The commit path calls `config.SchemaValidateWithDefinitions` (`pkg/configstore/store.go:1090,1099`)

## Impact

vSRX/SRX operators migrating configs that tune modeled ALGs (DNS doctoring is commonly disabled; SIP media timeout is commonly set) must hand-edit them out. The failure is loud, so there is no silent enforcement drift

## Acceptance / fix direction

Add the known Junos sub-statements of dns/ftp/sip/tftp/pptp as opaque accepted-but-inert children carrying the existing not-implemented advisory, and keep rejecting unknown tokens. Acceptance: the six lines commit with an advisory in both shapes, and `ftp desable` still rejects

## Contract (where cited)

The #4232/#4337 doctrine: Junos ALG stanzas xpf does not model are accepted-but-inert with an advisory (`compiler_security_alg.go` #4232 block; wildcard "Unsupported ALG class (accepted-only; compiler warning)", `schema_security.go:1420`). #12833 aimed to reject misspellings ("A misspelling is invalid Junos syntax"). juniper.net "dns (Security ALG)" lists `doctoring` (`none` | `sanity-check`) and `maximum-message-length`

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A18-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).

- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch02:9: - **R3-A18-03 — COHORT** (Junos ALG admission parity). D: five modeled classes accept only `disable` (`pkg/config/schema_security.go:1410-1425`), whereas other classes are admitted opaquely; Juniper's [DNS ALG documentation](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/alg/topics/topic-map/security-dns-algs.html) describes doctoring. Thus an otherwise valid migration stanza can be refused rather than accepted-with-advisory. R: these ALG options are not implemented, and the refusal is loud and safe; the packet independently established full Junos syntax only for DNS, not every listed FTP/SIP/PPTP variant or release. **Check:** version-pin each additional statement to a primary Junos grammar and check strict flat/braced acceptance without permitting typo forms.

## #16815 — Residual of #15207 (R2 A18-02): ~19 Junos default applications (junos-mail, -echo, -lpr, -ymsg, -chargen, -discard, -biff, -who, -uucp, -nfs, -sql-monitor, ...) are still absent from the predefined table so referencing policies fail commit, and… [OPEN]

## Summary

Residual of #15207 (R2 A18-02): ~19 Junos default applications (junos-mail, -echo, -lpr, -ymsg, -chargen, -discard, -biff, -who, -uucp, -nfs, -sql-monitor, ...) are still absent from the predefined table so referencing policies fail commit, and junos-snmp-agentx lacks its default `inactivity-timeout 7560`

**Finding ID:** `R3-A18-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low — mostly fail-visible: a policy citing a missing name is refused at commit. The one silent part is that `junos-snmp-agentx` sessions idle out on the global 1800 s instead of Junos's 7560 s (version-bounded basis) [reporter: Low]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (predefined junos-defaults parity gaps, with #4102/#5634/#11340/#11341/#15207) — real, minor residual

## Mechanism

policy `match application junos-mail` → ResolveApplication (user, then predefined) → miss → strict commit error (#3144 gate)

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

A grep of `pkg/config/*.go` (non-test) for each of the 19 quoted names returns 0. `pkg/config/predefined.go:47` `"junos-snmp-agentx": {Name: "junos-snmp-agentx", Protocol: "tcp", DestinationPort: "705"},`. No predefined entry sets `InactivityTimeout`. #15207's fix 39ee7f7c8c is an ancestor of base

## Impact

vSRX configs that cite these defaults (e.g. `junos-mail`, `junos-lpr`) cannot load and need user-defined replacements. AgentX sub-agent connections idle out about 4× earlier than on Junos

## Acceptance / fix direction

Complete the simple tcp/udp members from a cited, version-stated junos-defaults capture (multi-term ones as predefined sets), carry the default inactivity-timeouts, and document the omitted rpc/uuid names in docs/feature-gaps.md. Acceptance: a table-vs-capture diff test, and the probe names commit

## Contract (where cited)

`pkg/config/predefined.go:12-13` "Based on the official Junos OS predefined application list". The 12.1X44-D35.5 capture (https://www.51sec.org/2014/09/21/juniper-junos-pre-defined-applications-and-application-sets-details/) defines `junos-mail { term t1 protocol tcp destination-port 25; }`, `junos-echo` udp/7, `junos-lpr` tcp/515, `junos-ymsg` (4 terms tcp/udp 5000-5010 + 5050), and `junos-snmp-agentx { term t1 protocol tcp destination-port 705 inactivity-timeout 7560; }`

## #16818 — R3-F08-01: An aborted node-targeted failover leaves the requester primary: `abortRequestedPeerFailover` never demotes the requester that `commitRequestedPeerFailover` already promoted, so… [OPEN]

## Summary

An aborted node-targeted failover leaves the requester primary: `abortRequestedPeerFailover` never demotes the requester that `commitRequestedPeerFailover` already promoted, so `RequestPeerFailover` reports failure while the RG has moved (whenever the requester outranks the owner, or whenever the owner's hold heartbeat landed before the commit)

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — HA ownership moves contrary to the reported outcome on a supported operator path (`request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group N node <local>`, CLI and gRPC); when the abort cause is the local commit-ready settle timeout, the node left primary is the one whose activation did not settle, which is the fail-closed guarantee #15164 was filed to restore; with the abort frame lost the owner later restores at lease expiry and a second, unrequested move follows. Bounded: operator-initiated, needs a post-ACK abort, no dual-primary steady state (dual-active resolution converges). Demonstrated at the cluster-manager level, not on the lab.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F08-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf08.md` (finding `R3-F08-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/cluster/failover.go:607-646 `commitRequestedPeerFailover` applies the override, `delete(m.abortedPeerTransferReqID, rgID)` (:630) and `m.runElection()` (:635), promoting the requester via election.go:207 `return electLocalPrimary, "Peer transfer out"`. failover.go:587-600 then calls `abortRequestedPeerFailover` on a commit-ready or commit-send failure; :650-669 sets the marker, restores the peer snapshot (`restorePeerTransferOutOverrideLocked`, :1419-1443) and re-runs election — no `rg.State` demotion anywhere. Outcome is decided by electRG arms: snapshot PRIMARY -> election.go:361 "Dual-active: lower priority yields" only when the requester is lower, else :378 "Dual-active: winner stays"; snapshot SECONDARY-HOLD -> :380 `return electNoChange, "" // non-preempt: incumbent stays` for either ordering. The #15164 guard (election.go:198-211) is never the deciding arm. Observation: the probe history; inference: production frequency of the hold-before-commit ordering.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/cluster/README.md:4006-4025 (#15164, B22-01): "A requester-side abort must not re-promote the requester ... the requester had reported the failover as failed and demoted"; issue #15164 acceptance: "in the b22 probes the requester stays non-primary after the abort, and the owner is restored promptly".

**Trace:** CLI/gRPC `request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group N node <self>` (pkg/cli/cli_request_chassis.go:102, pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:898) -> `Manager.RequestPeerFailover` -> owner ACK (owner in SECONDARY-HOLD, #5079 lease) -> `commitRequestedPeerFailover` promotes requester -> `localTransferCommitReadyFn` timeout or `commitFn` error -> `abortRequestedPeerFailover` (no demotion) -> electRG retains PRIMARY -> CLI prints the error; owner restored by abort frame then yields by dual-active priority, or restores at lease expiry.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go probe driving `RequestPeerFailover` with two real `cluster.Manager`s, owner callbacks wired as the daemon does (`ManualFailover` + `ArmRemoteTransferOutLease`, `AbortRemoteTransferOut`), both abort causes, both orderings, frame delivered/lost, hold heartbeat before/after commit; final ownership observed after heartbeats in both directions.

**Confidence:** High — executed against the real Manager with a twin control; remaining assumption is how often the owner's hold heartbeat precedes the commit in production (one heartbeat interval vs the ACK + settle latency).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run TestProbeVF08Abort15164 -count=1 -v` with RUN/verify/vf08/probes/zz_probe_vf08_15164_test.go; output RUN/verify/vf08/probes/probe_15164_output.txt. Positive control (shipped fixture shape, owner 200 > requester 100, hold not yet seen): `err=true reqPrimaryAfterAbort=false FINAL reqPrimary=false ownPrimary=true | ... Peer transfer out ; primary->secondary, reason: Dual-active: lower priority yields`. Subject (requester 200 > owner 100): `err=true reqPrimaryAfterAbort=true FINAL reqPrimary=true ownPrimary=false | ... dual-active resolved: winner reaffirm` for both causes and both frame outcomes. Shipped ordering with the hold seen before commit, frame lost: `err=true reqPrimaryAfterAbort=true FINAL reqPrimary=true ownPrimary=false` (no demotion at all). Reporter's probe RUN/workers/f08/evidence/zz_probe_f08_15164_test.go reproduces the subject rows. Limits: in-process managers, no VIP/rg_active actuation.

## Impact

Operators and failover automation (e.g. `make test-failover`-style cycling) read the error as "nothing moved" and retry or stop; the RG has moved, possibly to a node whose dataplane did not settle, and a lost abort frame adds a second move at lease expiry (30 s default). Recovery: another manual failover.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Record in the requester that this request promoted it (e.g. the reqID with the pre-request local state) and have `abortRequestedPeerFailover` demote it back (and hold secondary while the peer advertises the aborted hold), instead of relying on election ordering; keep the "Peer transfer out" guard. Accept the documented ownerless window up to lease expiry when the abort frame is lost, or shorten it. Acceptance: all 16 rows of the vf08 probe report `FINAL reqPrimary=false`, with `ownPrimary=true` on delivered-frame rows; shipped `TestAbortedPeerFailoverDoesNotRepromoteRequester15164` stays green; add both orderings and the hold-before-commit shape to the shipped test.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;

## #16819 — R3-F08-02: `clamp_tcp_mss` declines every SYN carrying a TCP-MD5 (kind 19) option although the RFC 2385 digest excludes TCP options; configured `security flow tcp-mss all-tcp|gre-in|gre-out` is silently not… [OPEN]

## Summary

`clamp_tcp_mss` declines every SYN carrying a TCP-MD5 (kind 19) option although the RFC 2385 digest excludes TCP options; configured `security flow tcp-mss all-tcp|gre-in|gre-out` is silently not applied to MD5-authenticated flows, and the shipped 15119 MD5 clamp cell pins the wrong behaviour

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a configured PMTU-avoidance knob is silently skipped for a whole flow class (MD5-authenticated BGP and other TCP-MD5 transit sessions, including over GRE where `gre-in/gre-out` is configured), with no counter or log; any host can also exempt its SYNs by adding a kind-19 option. Not an enforcement or isolation loss, and the firewall's own egress still emits PTB for DF traffic, so a session stall additionally needs a PMTUD failure elsewhere on the path (potential Medium in that topology). [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F08-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf08.md` (finding `R3-F08-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/tcp.rs:449-452 comment "TCP-MD5 (kind 19) digests cover the pseudo-header + header + data likewise"; tcp.rs:458-460 `if tcp_header_has_auth_option(tcp, data_offset) { return false; }`; tcp.rs:82 `if kind == TCP_OPTION_KIND_MD5 || kind == TCP_OPTION_KIND_AO { return true; }`. Callers: frame/mod.rs:670 (copy-build) and tcp.rs:964 `clamp_tcp_mss_frame` (in-place). Shipped cell userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/tcp_tests.rs:579-591 `clamp_tcp_mss_no_op_on_tcp_md5_syn_15119` asserts "TCP-MD5 SYN must not be clamped". dcc31bea75 message: "Sibling: clamp_tcp_mss rewrote the MSS of a TCP-AO SYN or an IPv6 AH-protected SYN".

**Contract / expected behaviour:** RFC 2385 s2.0 (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2385.txt, lines 71-84): the digest covers "1. the TCP pseudo-header (in the order: source IP address, destination IP address, zero-padded protocol number, and segment length) 2. the TCP header, excluding options, and assuming a checksum of zero 3. the TCP segment data (if any)". Rewriting the MSS value changes none of these. RFC 5925 s5.1 (TCP-AO) covers the header including options by default, so the AO decline is right. #15119's own sibling clause asked only for AO SYNs and IPv6 AH SYNs.

**Trace:** `set security flow tcp-mss all-tcp mss N` -> compiled flow config -> helper `selected_tcp_mss` -> forward path `clamp_tcp_mss` (frame/mod.rs:670 or tcp.rs:964) -> early `return false` for kind 19 -> SYN forwarded with the original MSS.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — temporary `#[cfg(test)]` cell run with cargo (`cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vf08_probe_md5`) at d1ea69f9aa: subject, unauthenticated twin control, and an RFC 2385 digest-input oracle.

**Confidence:** High — RFC text read at the source, the decline and its twin control executed; the end-to-end stall depends on topology.

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vf08/probes/vf08_md5_clamp_probe.rs.diff (appended to tcp_tests.rs, then reverted); output RUN/verify/vf08/probes/probe_15119_md5_output.txt: `VF08 SUBJECT md5 clamped=false bytes_unchanged=true | CONTROL kind253 clamped=true mss_after=1200 | ORACLE rfc2385_digest_input_identical_after_mss_rewrite=true options_inclusive_input_identical=false`. Control: identical option layout with unauthenticated kind 253 clamps, so only the kind-19 test blocks. Oracle: the RFC 2385 digest input (pseudo-header, option-less header with zero checksum, data) is byte-identical after an MSS rewrite, while an options-inclusive (AO-style) input changes. Limits: no live MD5 peer validation.

## Impact

BGP-MD5 across a GRE or IPsec tunnel is exactly the deployment that sets `tcp-mss gre-in/gre-out/all-tcp`; without the clamp, full-size UPDATEs rely on PMTUD, and with ICMP filtered upstream the session establishes and then stalls (hold-timer flaps). The operator sees a configured clamp and no indication that it is skipped.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Decline only kind 29 (TCP-AO) and IPv6 AH in `clamp_tcp_mss`; keep `tcp_header_has_auth_option` (19 and 29) for the segmentation gates; correct the comment; invert `clamp_tcp_mss_no_op_on_tcp_md5_syn_15119` to assert the clamp applies with a valid TCP checksum. Acceptance: MD5 SYN clamped, AO SYN and AH SYN untouched, segmentation still declines MD5 and AO.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16820 — R3-F08-03: `terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs` is a fire-and-forget goroutine that never re-checks RG ownership or serializes with `reinitiateIPsecSAs`; if the RG fails back while the sweep is still running, the… [OPEN]

## Summary

`terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs` is a fire-and-forget goroutine that never re-checks RG ownership or serializes with `reinitiateIPsecSAs`; if the RG fails back while the sweep is still running, the sweep force-terminates the SA the now-primary node just re-initiated, recreating the failback IPsec black hole #15194 fixed

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — route-based VPN outage on the owning node after failback, bounded only by DPD, rekey or peer initiation (the #15194 consequence); needs a demotion followed by re-promotion of the same RG within the sweep's runtime, which grows with SA count because each terminate re-lists all SAs. Potential, not lab-measured.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F08-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf08.md` (finding `R3-F08-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

daemon_ha.go:2037 `go d.terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs(rgID)` and :922 `go d.terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs(0)`; :2743-2760 lists live SAs once (`d.ipsecActiveNames()`), filters by `d.ipsecSAsForRG(names, rg)` and terminates each — no `IsLocalPrimary`, epoch or cancellation. Promotion launches `go d.reinitiateIPsecSAs()` (:877, :1887), whose belt (:2640-2668) terminates a stale local duplicate BEFORE initiating and cannot see a terminate issued after. pkg/ipsec/ike.go:986-1012 `TerminateConnection` re-runs `--list-sas` and issues `--terminate --ike <conn> --force` by name at terminate time.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #15194 and the function's own doc (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:2735-2742): terminate the SAs of an RG "which this node has just lost"; #9139 `ownsIPsecConn` scoping: a node must not tear down connections of an RG it owns.

**Trace:** RG1 demotion -> `clearRethServicesForRG(1)` -> async sweep starts `swanctl --list-sas` -> RG1 re-promoted -> `applyRethServicesForRG` -> `go reinitiateIPsecSAs()` initiates `vpn-rg1` (or the remote re-establishes to the VIP) -> sweep resumes and `TerminateConnection("vpn-rg1")` -> `--terminate --ike vpn-rg1 --force` on the owning node.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go probe in pkg/daemon driving `clearRethServicesForRG` (real sweep launch) and `reinitiateIPsecSAs` (real takeover leg) with swanctl seams; effect order recorded with a twin control.

**Confidence:** Medium — the race is executed with both real daemon legs; the production window size (how long the sweep runs relative to a demote/re-promote cycle) is not measured.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestProbeVF08DemotionSweepRace15194 -count=1 -v` with RUN/verify/vf08/probes/zz_probe_vf08_15194_test.go; output RUN/verify/vf08/probes/probe_15194_output.txt: CONTROL (sweep completes before failback) `events=[terminate:vpn-rg1@primary=false terminate:vpn-rg1@primary=true initiate:vpn-rg1] LAST=initiate:vpn-rg1`; SUBJECT (failback during the sweep's live-SA read) `events=[terminate:vpn-rg1@primary=true initiate:vpn-rg1 terminate:vpn-rg1@primary=true] LAST=terminate:vpn-rg1@primary=true`. The reporter's probe (RUN/workers/f08/evidence/zz_probe_f08_15194_test.go) showed only the primary flag at terminate; its "control" also terminated, so it could not distinguish the end states — replaced. Limits: swanctl seams; no charon.

## Impact

HA failback of route-based VPNs — the case #15194 was filed for — can again end with the owning node's tunnel down until DPD/rekey; many-tunnel deployments widen the window to seconds.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Capture an RG ownership epoch at demotion and re-check `!IsLocalPrimary(rg)` plus the epoch immediately before each terminate; or serialize sweep and reinitiate per RG and cancel the sweep on promotion. Acceptance: the vf08 probe SUBJECT ends with `initiate:vpn-rg1`; shipped 15194 cells stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16821 — R3-F08-04: The stepBackup resign arm consumes the resign token without clearing `resignPending`, so an already-BACKUP instance keeps its pre-resign priority (contrary to the ResignRG doc) and a later… [OPEN]

## Summary

The stepBackup resign arm consumes the resign token without clearing `resignPending`, so an already-BACKUP instance keeps its pre-resign priority (contrary to the ResignRG doc) and a later unrelated step-down silently installs priority 0

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — legacy VRRP-backed RETH mode only (`no-private-rg-election` without `no-reth-vrrp`); the stale 0 needs a later MASTER step-down not driven by a cluster demotion, and the posture reconcile re-sends priority 200 after a 10 s mismatch; the retained pre-resign priority only shortens master-down skew.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F08-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf08.md` (finding `R3-F08-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

manager.go:994-995 `vi.beginResign(); vi.triggerResign()` regardless of state; instance.go:1055-1068 resign arm calls only `vi.notifyResigned(vi.staleVIPResignErr())`; instance_resign.go:40-52 `applyPendingResign` (only caller instance_transition.go:221 in becomeBackup); track.go:32-60 getPriority returns pre-resign `cfg.Priority` while pending; instance_timing.go:121-128 masterDownInterval uses getPriority; instance_rx.go:321-323 step-down to a higher-priority advert calls becomeBackup; UpdateRGPriority (manager.go:1004-1035) never clears the marker.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/vrrp/manager.go:940-996 (ResignRG, #15213 A25-06): the stash is applied by becomeBackup and "masterDownInterval at the stashed 0 keeps the resigned instance from winning a re-election"; instance.go:1055-1067 (#6177): a resign on an already-BACKUP instance is an expected path.

**Trace:** cluster RG demotion (legacy mode) -> daemon_ha.go:383 `ResignRG` -> instance already BACKUP -> stepBackup arm consumes token, marker stays -> later MASTER tenure -> higher-priority advert -> becomeBackup -> `applyPendingResign` writes 0.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — reporter's probe re-run (`go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run TestProbeF08StaleResignMarker15213 -race`), control and subject.

**Confidence:** High — executed with the shipped fixture and the real stepBackup arm under -race; end-to-end ownership effect not measured.

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vf08/probes/zz_probe_f08_15213_test.go (reporter's), output RUN/verify/vf08/probes/probe_15213_output.txt: `CONTROL (no resign while BACKUP): pending=false priAfterBackupResign=200 priAfterLaterStepDown=200`; `SUBJECT (ResignRG while already BACKUP): pending=true priAfterBackupResign=200 priAfterLaterStepDown=0`; no data race. Limits: state set directly for the later MASTER tenure.

## Impact

Legacy-mode operators can get a router that later advertises priority 0 (or sits BACKUP while the cluster says primary under non-preempt) for a resignation resolved long before; diagnostics show the configured priority.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In the stepBackup resign arm call `applyPendingResign()` (or clear the marker); clear `resignPending` in UpdateRGPriority/updateConfig; fix the masterDownInterval doc or make it use the stash. Acceptance: probe SUBJECT reports `pending=false`, priority 0 immediately after the BACKUP resign and 200 after the later step-down once restored.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16822 — R3-F08-05: `deterministicPoolBlockCapacity` / `deterministicSubscriberCapacity` hard-code the NAT64 1024-65535 window for IPv6 subscribers, so `xpf_nat_pool_deterministic_info{host_count}` and the… [OPEN]

## Summary

`deterministicPoolBlockCapacity` / `deterministicSubscriberCapacity` hard-code the NAT64 1024-65535 window for IPv6 subscribers, so `xpf_nat_pool_deterministic_info{host_count}` and the deterministic block total/allocated gauges overstate a range-limited NAT64 deterministic pool (645 vs 10 in the probe)

pkg/api/metrics_nat.go:158-171 `if ipv6Subscriber { rangeForBlocks = 65535 - 1024 + 1 }`; :194-209 IPv6 capacity delegates to it; pkg/nat/deterministic.go:466-487 mode 2 uses `poolPortRangeV4(pool)` and `portRange / det.BlockSize`.

**Trace:** `source pool P { address ...; port range 2000 to 3000; deterministic { block-size 100; host address 2001:db8::/32; } }` referenced by NAT64 -> allocator/wire use 2000-3000 (#15283) -> Prometheus collector computes with 1024-65535.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestProbeF08Mode2GaugeIgnoresPoolPortRange` re-run.

## #16823 — R3-F09-02: #15264 kernel-truth recheck marks host-inbound stale on a detected `nft flush ruleset` but leaves `hostInboundEnforced`/`hostInboundCoveredAddrs` set, so a re-apply whose real install fails takes… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15264 kernel-truth recheck marks host-inbound stale on a detected `nft flush ruleset` but leaves `hostInboundEnforced`/`hostInboundCoveredAddrs` set, so a re-apply whose real install fails takes the day-2 retention branch and installs neither the cold-boot fence nor a gap fence for previously covered local addresses

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the kernel nftables host-inbound default-deny for every previously covered firewall-local address stays open after the documented recovery step if the re-apply's real install fails; it needs a privileged out-of-band flush plus an independent install failure (a double fault), the commit itself fails (H7) and applied state shows LastApplyFailed, and userspace-dp's own host-inbound gate still covers XDP-ingress traffic, so the exposure is the kernel-path host-input surface (non-XDP and XDP_PASS paths); potential, demonstrated at component level [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F09-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf09.md` (finding `R3-F09-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/host_kernel_truth_15264.go:69-84 (observed): the host-inbound arm on `enErr == nil && !enforcing` runs only `d.noteHostInboundApplyFailed(now); drift = true`. `hostInboundEnforced` and `hostInboundCoveredAddrs` are untouched. :93-100: the lo0 arm runs `d.lo0Enforced.Store(false); d.lo0LastFailed.Store(true)`. pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:1078 `if !d.hostInboundEnforced.Load() { ... installHostInboundColdBootFence ... } else {` the day-2 branch computes `hostInboundUncoveredDropAddrs(views, unzonedV4, unzonedV6, d.hostInboundCoveredAddrs)`, so with the stale covered set the uncovered set is empty and no gap spec is built. Inference: no other owner re-drives a fence. The recheck deliberately does not re-apply, and the gap reassert loop only re-asserts an existing gap spec.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:920-929 (teardown): "Leaving hostInboundEnforced sticky-true is FAIL-OPEN: if a later generation becomes enforceable and its FIRST real load fails, the stale true would take the day-2 retention branch — which assumes a retained table still protects the addresses — and SKIP the cold-boot/fresh-install fence". The #15264 recheck applies this reasoning to lo0 (host_kernel_truth_15264.go:86-92: "the next failed install must take the cold-boot fence path rather than the day-2 retention branch (#6476/#5790 parity)") and documents "re-apply to converge" as the operator step after a flush (scripts/image/xpf-input-closed.service, quoted in the file header).

**Trace:** commit → applyHostInboundFilter installs xpf_hostinbound (covered={10.0.0.1}, hostInboundEnforced=true) → out-of-band `nft flush ruleset` → 30 s hostKernelTruthLoop15264 → TableDropsInput=false, TableEnforcing=false → stale is marked, latch kept → operator re-applies → InstallHostInbound fails → daemon_nft.go:1078 takes the day-2 branch → uncovered={} → no cold-boot fence and no gap fence → no nft deny for 10.0.0.1 until a later successful install.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go component test through `recheckHostKernelTruth15264` and `applyHostInboundFilter` with a fake nft installer (DEFECT arm plus a positive control); no live kernel or lab run.

**Confidence:** High — the mechanism was executed against the real `applyHostInboundFilter` with a scripted nft installer; the remaining assumption is how often the re-apply's real install fails after a flush on real kernels.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestR3F09 -count=1 -v` with workers/f09/evidence/zz_r3_f09_flush_latch_probe_test.go (copy in worktree pkg/daemon/), output RUN/verify/vf09/probes/f09-02-go.out. DEFECT arm: `after recheck: hostInboundEnforced=true lo0Enforced=false covered=1`, then `FLUSH arm: coldBootFence installs=0 gapSpecs=0 10.0.0.1-in-gap=false enforced=true`, giving `--- FAIL`. Positive control (latch and covered set reset as teardown does, same failed install): `coldBootFence installs=1` and the "fallback succeeded with address- and ingress-scoped DROPs" log, giving PASS. Limits: fake installer, so this shows the selected branch, not kernel packet behavior.

## Impact

any appliance where an operator flushes nftables (the documented service-file scenario) and then hits a transient install failure on re-apply. Host services on firewall-local addresses lose the kernel default-deny until a later apply succeeds. The fix's own recovery step is the trigger.

## Acceptance / fix direction

on detected host-inbound drift, mirror lo0 and teardown: `hostInboundEnforced.Store(false)`, clear `hostInboundCoveredAddrs`/`hostInboundDHCPRetainedAddrs`, and clear `hostInboundGapFenceActive` when the gap table is also gone. Consumers to re-check: the HostInboundApplied projection (Established after drift) and the recheck's own `hostInboundEnforced` probe gate, which then needs a separate "stale-established" bit so the warn de-dupe still works. Acceptance: the DEFECT arm installs the cold-boot fence (or puts 10.0.0.1 in a fence), the control stays green, and the six existing #15264 cells stay green with the Established-after-drift expectation updated.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16825 — R3-F09-04: #15757's bare-destination fix makes `AuthorizeConfigMutation` adjudicate a NON-bare `copy`/`rename` destination without the edit cursor, while the local CLI executor prepends it. Under `[edit… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15757's bare-destination fix makes `AuthorizeConfigMutation` adjudicate a NON-bare `copy`/`rename` destination without the edit cursor, while the local CLI executor prepends it. Under `[edit system]`, `copy login user operator to login user root` passes an anchored `deny-configuration "^system login user root"` and commits, because the expanded commit gate is a no-op on a groupless config.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — demonstrated end to end: a documented RBAC control (anchored `deny-configuration`, including the explicitly supported restricted-root console class) fails open and the denied subtree reaches the active config. The only affected surface is the in-process xpfd console, though, and its login class comes from the xpfd process uid (`osident.Current()`), so the restricted actor already owns the daemon process and its store. SSH, gRPC, REST and event-engine callers are unaffected. Anchored `allow-configuration` false-denies in mirror. [reporter: Low; f12 addendum argued High, rejected because of the actor bound]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F09-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf09.md` (finding `R3-F09-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:150-152 (observed): `resolvedDst := strings.Join(ResolveBareCopyRenameDestination(append(append([]string{}, editPath...), src...), dst), " ")`, which before 609d36f264 was `resolve(dst)` (editPath+dst). pkg/config/ast_edit.go:124-128: `if !ok || !bare { return dst }`. pkg/cli/cli_config.go:102: `dstPath = config.PrependEditPathForCopyDst(editPath, srcPath, dstPath)` prepends the cursor for every non-bare destination. pkg/config/authz_config_groups_14981.go:78-81: `if t == nil || !treeHasGroupStanzas14981(t) { return nil, nil }`. pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1012: `applyCLILoginClass(shell, d.store.ActiveConfig(), osident.Current())`. cmd/cli/shared.go:400-405: the remote CLI prepends the cursor itself before `client.Set`, so the server gate sees a full destination.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go copy/rename comment (#14147): "the endpoints adjudicated here are the endpoints acted on". The #15757 comment itself says "Full destinations are unaffected". docs/system-login.md: "uid 0 with an explicit `system login user root class <c>` → <c> — an explicit restriction is honoured". Junos semantics: `deny-configuration` refuses the configuration path at edit time.

**Trace:** console line `copy login user operator to login user root` at `[edit system]` → `dispatchConfig` → `checkConfigRegex` → `AuthorizeConfigMutation(cfg, class, ["system"], line)` → configMutationPaths tests src `system login user operator` and dst `login user root`, the anchored deny misses, so the line is allowed → `handleCopyRename` writes `system login user root` → `handleCommit` → `checkExpandedConfigRegex14981` returns no lines on a groupless tree → commit → active config.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/config gate cell (f09) and a pkg/cli end-to-end cell through `dispatchConfig` and `handleCommit` (from f12, re-run by vf09), each with positive controls.

**Confidence:** High — both the gate cell and the full dispatcher-and-commit path were executed. The remaining assumption is how far the in-process console counts as a principal boundary, which docs/system-login.md treats as one (#6701).

**Probe:** (1) `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestR3F09 -count=1 -v` (workers/f09/evidence/zz_r3_f09_copy_dst_cursor_probe_test.go), output RUN/verify/vf09/probes/f09-04-go.out: `executor destination = "system login user root"`, then `DEFECT: [edit system] copy ... was ALLOWED` and the same for `rename`. Controls, both denied: the root-spelled `copy system login user operator to system login user root` and the bare `copy login user operator to user root`. (2) `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/cli/ -run TestVF09CopyUnderCursorE2E -count=1 -v` (RUN/verify/vf09/probes/zz_vf09_copy_cursor_e2e_test.go, a renamed copy of f12's cell; removed from the worktree after the run), output probes/f09-04-e2e.out. Control at top level: `permission denied: login class "limited" denies copy under "system"`. Under `[edit system]`: `err=<nil>`, then `candidate: set system login user root class super-user`, `commit-time expanded gate: <nil>`, `commit complete: 3 statement(s) changed`, `BYPASS COMMITTED: active config now has system login user root`. Limits: the cell uses an in-memory store, not a live console.

## Impact

operators who restrict the console class (including restricted root) with anchored regexes, the Junos-documented idiom for complex expressions, can have the restriction bypassed by typing the destination relative to the cursor. This is the third fix in this family (#9938, #14147, #15757) whose predicate covered one destination shape and regressed the other. Anchored allows false-deny legitimate copies.

## Acceptance / fix direction

in `configMutationPaths`, resolve the destination exactly as the executor does: `PrependEditPathForCopyDst(editPath, fullSrc, dst)`, then `ResolveBareCopyRenameDestination(fullSrc, thatDst)`. Ideally both should call one shared helper so gate and executor cannot diverge. Acceptance: both probe cells pass (copy and rename denied under the cursor, nothing committed), and the #15757 bare cells and the root-spelled controls stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16826 — R3-F10-01: The #15176 NAT-scope fold drops the VLAN unit on both ends, so HA-imported sessions on a tagged RETH unit are revalidated against the parent's interface/RI scope and revoked on their first hit on… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #15176 NAT-scope fold drops the VLAN unit on both ends, so HA-imported sessions on a tagged RETH unit are revalidated against the parent's interface/RI scope and revoked on their first hit on the new primary (regression vs pre-fix)

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — HA continuity loss. Established flows matched by a `from interface <reth>.<vlan>` (or `from routing-instance`) scoped SNAT/DNAT/static-NAT rule on a VLAN-tagged RETH unit are revoked as StaleSourceNat on the new primary after failover. The shipped HA topology uses tagged RETH units (reth0.50/reth0.80). Zone-scoped rules are not affected, because the zone is still derived from (ingress ifindex, vlan). It fails closed (no enforcement loss). The revocation verdict was demonstrated through the production revalidation function; the end-to-end teardown after failover is static. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F10-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf10.md` (finding `R3-F10-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/cluster/sync.go:2347-2352 `stampNatScopeFold(ifindex int32)` -> `s.stampIngressIfaceFold(uint32(ifindex), 0)`. pkg/daemon/ingress_fold_7095.go:142-151: the fold is `StableIfaceID(cfg.ClusterStableIfaceName(nameByIndex[ifindex], vlan))`. pkg/config/stable_iface_7095.go:184-230 `selectStableIfaceOwner`: RETH members carry no units, so `ge-0-0-2.80` falls to the legacy first-cut and yields `reth0`. pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_sessionsync_request.go:305-308 `if ifindex, _, ok := m.resolveIngressFoldLocked(view.natScopeFold()); ok { req.NatScopeIfindex = int32(ifindex) }` drops the vlan, unlike :301-304, which keeps `IngressVLANID`. Rust: userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/session_sync.rs:581 stores it. userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/nat.rs:36-39 `logical_ingress = fabric_ingress_scope_ifindex.unwrap_or_else(|| resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex(...))`, so the recorded scope overrides the correctly derived logical unit. policy_revalidation.rs:845 and :411-420 consume it. :1294-1297 keeps the session only when `identity_absent` (fabric or ingress_ifindex==0) and the scope is None. Imported rows have neither, so they are judged under the wrong scope. userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:1002 (`upsert_synced_with_origin`) installs synced rows with `source_nat_revalidated: None`, so the first hit after takeover revalidates.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** c65a353e8b (#15176): "session-hit NAT revalidation rebuilds the SAME interface/RI scope admission used". The scope crosses the HA wire as a cluster-stable fold of the LOGICAL unit, and the peer "resolves it back to its own logical unit" (pkg/cluster/sync.go:2342-2346 comment).

**Trace:** `set security nat ... rule-set X from interface reth0.80` -> node0 admits on (ge-0-0-2, vlan 80) and records `nat_scope_ifindex = ifindex(ge-0-0-2.80)` (poll_descriptor/mod.rs:7129-7140) -> helper delta -> Go `NatScopeIfindex` -> fold("reth0") -> wire `nat_scope_fold` -> node1 resolve -> (ge-7-0-2, 0), vlan discarded -> `NatScopeIfindex = ifindex(ge-7-0-2)` -> Rust import `nat_scope_ifindex=Some(parent)` -> first hit after takeover -> scope ifname is the parent's config name, not `reth0.80` -> no rule match -> StaleSourceNat revocation.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go: sender fold and receiver resolve on real two-node compiled cluster configs. Rust: an imported SNAT session judged by `source_nat_revocation_on_session_hit` under the three scope shapes. Not run end-to-end on the lab cluster.

**Confidence:** High — both Go legs and the Rust verdict were executed with controls. Remaining assumption: the logical-unit ifindex on the sender is the kernel VLAN child, as built by `ensureVLANSubInterface` for zone-bound RETH VLAN units. In the logical-only synthetic shape the fold is 0, the scope is None, and the session is safe.

**Probe:** Go: `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestF10NatScopeFoldVlanUnit -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/f10/evidence/zz_f10_natscope_fold_probe_test.go; rerun output RUN/verify/vf10/probes/go_daemon.out). Control: `sender ingress-fold name (ge-0-0-2,80) = "reth0.80"`. Defect: `sender nat-scope-fold name (ge-0-0-2.80,0) = "reth0"`, and `receiver resolve("reth0.80") = ifindex=20 vlan=80` -> NatScopeIfindex 20 (parent `ge-7-0-2`), never 22. Rust: temporary cell `vf10_imported_reth_vlan_scope_probe` (RUN/verify/vf10/probes/vf10_rust_probes.rs, output rust_vf10.out). Fixture: SNAT rule `from interface reth0.80`, ingress (20, vlan 80) -> logical 22 `reth0.80`. Results: `pre-fix import (scope None): KEPT`, `correct logical scope Some(22): KEPT`, `post-fix import scope Some(parent 20): REVOKED stale_snat=true`. A first run with a missing egress-zone ledger revoked all three arms; it was VOID and fixed before the decisive run.

## Impact

Every operator with interface- or RI-scoped NAT on a tagged RETH unit loses those established sessions at failover. That is the symptom #15176 set out to remove, now introduced for imported sessions that previously survived. It recurs on every failover until fixed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Fold the NAT scope as (parent physical, vlan), the same shape as the ingress fold (have the helper delta carry the scope VLAN, or derive it from the logical row), and on import map fold -> (ifindex, vlan) -> logical unit through the snapshot (or ship the vlan and let Rust `resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex`). Acceptance: a two-node Go cell where a reth0.80 session's NatScopeFold resolves to node1's `ge-7-0-2.80` logical ifindex, and a Rust cell where an imported reth0.80 session with `from interface reth0.80` survives its first hit.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16827 — R3-F10-02: The #15278 undefined-scope gate accepts a unit-less NAT `from/to interface <ifd>`, which is stored raw and can never equal the logical unit name the dataplane compares, so the rule-set is inert… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #15278 undefined-scope gate accepts a unit-less NAT `from/to interface <ifd>`, which is stored raw and can never equal the logical unit name the dataplane compares, so the rule-set is inert with no commit warning

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — same harm class and grade as the parent D02-02 (Low COHORT). It needs the operator to write the unit-less spelling. The scoped rule-set then never matches, so a scoped SNAT does not translate (or a later rule-set does) and a scoped DNAT/static rule never fires. Security policy still applies. Inertness was demonstrated in Rust; downstream traffic consequences are inferred. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F10-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf10.md` (finding `R3-F10-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:150-172 `if !split.HasUnit { if _, ok := cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces[base]; ok ... { return true }`. pkg/config/compiler_nat_helpers.go:296 `rs.FromInterface = s.value` (no `.0` canonicalization). pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:308, nat_destination.go:661 and nat_static.go:67 copy it raw. Rust exact compare: userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:1100 `self.from_interface != scope.ingress_ifname`, nat/destination.rs:148, nat/static_nat.rs:122. The ifname is `ifindex_to_config_name[logical]`, and the unit row claims that name (forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:781-800). In contrast, Go's `snapshotInterfaceNameMatches` (pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_iface_pool_overlap.go:159-167) treats a bare name as matching any unit, an internal inconsistency.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** 41c18d7deb (#15278 D02-02) added the gate because the dataplane "silently never matches" an undefined scope (compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:144-149 comment). A ref the gate admits must be matchable.

**Trace:** `set security nat source rule-set rs1 from interface ge-0/0/1` -> gate: defined -> `FromInterface="ge-0/0/1"` -> snapshot `from_interface` -> Rust `SourceNatRule.from_interface` -> traffic on unit 0 has ingress_ifname `ge-0/0/1.0` -> exact compare fails -> rule-set never matches.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go strict compile of bare, unit and undefined refs. Rust `source_nat_revocation_on_session_hit` judges a rule with each spelling against the unit ifname. The existing contract test `contract_undotted_control_pair_matches` pins the unit row owning the ifindex name.

**Confidence:** High — Go acceptance, Rust exact-match non-match and the unit-row name ownership were all executed.

**Probe:** Go: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestF10NATBareFromInterface -v` (RUN/workers/f10/evidence/zz_f10_nat_bare_iface_probe_test.go; rerun RUN/verify/vf10/probes/go_config.out): `ref="ge-0/0/1": strict commit OK; source FromInterface="ge-0/0/1" ... warnings=0`; `ref="ge-0/0/1.0"` OK; positive control for the gate `ref="ge-0/0/9": strict commit REJECTED`. Rust: temporary cell `vf10_bare_from_interface_probe` (RUN/verify/vf10/probes/vf10_rust_probes.rs, rust_vf10.out): `from_interface="ge-0/0/0.0" vs unit ifname ge-0/0/0.0: MATCHES (kept)`; `from_interface="ge-0/0/0" ...: NO MATCH (revoked)`. `contract_undotted_control_pair_matches ... ok` (rust_contract_9821.out).

## Impact

The gate added to close "inert NAT scopes commit clean" explicitly blesses a spelling that is equally inert, so an operator gets no signal. A scoped NAT exemption or translation silently does nothing.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Canonicalize a unit-less NAT interface scope to `<ifd>.0` at compile (as zone bindings are canonicalized, #5878), or treat it as undefined for NAT (strict reject, lenient warn). Align `snapshotInterfaceNameMatches` with whichever is chosen. Acceptance: the probe's unit-less rule-set either compiles to `ge-0/0/1.0` or is rejected, and the Rust cell's bare arm then matches or never reaches the dataplane.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.
