## #16828 — R3-F10-03: The #15281/#5742 commit classifier treats `compiled == nil` as "not committed", but applyAndSyncCommitted returns `(nil, err)` after store promotion for the protocol-gate and policy-READ-authority… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #15281/#5742 commit classifier treats `compiled == nil` as "not committed", but applyAndSyncCommitted returns `(nil, err)` after store promotion for the protocol-gate and policy-READ-authority aborts, so a persisted config is reported as REST 400 / gRPC InvalidArgument

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — operator/API contract misreport, the same class and grade as the parent D08-02 (Low). The client is told "invalid config, not committed" for a config the store has promoted and persisted (live on the next apply/boot). The failure itself is still reported. Triggers are rare: helper protocol skew (required-protocol gate) or a policy-session READ authority race. The context-cancel class is mapped to 503 first and is not affected. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F10-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf10.md` (finding `R3-F10-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:405-415 `if applyErrSkipsPeerSync(applyErr) { ... return nil, applyErr }`, inside a function documented (:334-337) to run for a config "the store has ALREADY promoted+persisted". :538-545 `applyErrSkipsPeerSync` = `compileErrorMustAbortApply(err)` || Canceled || `ErrPolicyReadAuthority`. pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:72-84 `commitApplyStatus`: Canceled/Deadline first, `compiled != nil` -> Unavailable, default -> InvalidArgument. pkg/api/config.go:886-903 `writeCommitError`: the same split, default -> 400.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** 31ccbf9c2a / #5742: compiled == nil means "the config was NOT committed" (pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go:62-67). But pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:870-876: Store.Commit/CommitConfirmed/SyncApply "have ALREADY promoted+persisted the compiled config before applyConfigLocked runs, so the abort does not unwind store promotion".

**Trace:** REST/gRPC commit -> commitAndApply -> store promote+persist -> applyAndSyncCommitted -> apply returns a protocol-gate or READ-authority error -> `(nil, err)` -> writeCommitError / commitApplyStatus default arm -> 400 / InvalidArgument "not committed".

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `applyAndSyncCommitted` with an injected ErrPolicyReadAuthority returns compiled==nil, and the store active config is not unwound. Classifier arms static. Protocol-gate leg static (same return).

**Confidence:** High — the post-promotion `(nil, err)` return was executed on the production function, and the no-unwind property is stated in source. The classifier mapping is a single switch (static).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestF10CommitAbortReportedAsReject -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/f10/evidence/zz_f10_commit_abort_classify_probe_test.go; rerun RUN/verify/vf10/probes/go_daemon.out): `mode=read-authority-refusal err=policy session invalidation authority refusal: policy session READ authority unavailable ... compiled==nil:true activeHasPromoted:true`. Control `mode=tail-error-control err=<nil> compiled==nil:false`. Limit: the probe's "active" check shows only that the function does not unwind the store (the promotion is the probe's own SyncApply); the no-unwind contract is corroborated by the daemon_apply.go doc.

## Impact

Automation that sees InvalidArgument/400 treats the config as rejected (edits or abandons it), while the box's persisted active config is the new one and becomes live on a later apply or boot. This is the #15281 harm on a rarer path.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Return the promoted config alongside the fatal post-promotion error, with an explicit "committed, not applied" marker or sentinel so the classifier can distinguish it from a true pre-promotion reject. Correct the #5742 doc. Acceptance: an authority-refusal or protocol-gate commit yields REST `data.committed:true` (non-400) and a non-InvalidArgument gRPC code; a pre-promotion reject still yields 400/InvalidArgument.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16829 — R3-F10-04: #15265 made the default-instance BGP status query `vrf all`; HA transfer readiness for a default-instance BGP requirement is satisfied by an Established same-address peer in any other routing-instance [OPEN]

## Summary

#15265 made the default-instance BGP status query `vrf all`; HA transfer readiness for a default-instance BGP requirement is satisfied by an Established same-address peer in any other routing-instance

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — false positive in the HA routing-readiness interlock. A transfer can proceed to a node whose default-instance BGP session is down, which blackholes RG traffic until BGP converges. It needs the same neighbor address configured in the default instance and another instance on RG-served interfaces, the default session down while the other is Established, and no BGP-learned route yet in table 254. The prerequisites are narrow and recovery is automatic. The predicate result was demonstrated; the failover consequence is static. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F10-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf10.md` (finding `R3-F10-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/frr/status_parse.go:393-398 `GetBGPSummary` -> `m.vtysh(ctx, "show bgp vrf all summary json")`. :413-416 `GetBGPSummaryVRF`: `if vrf == "" { return m.GetBGPSummary(ctx) }`. pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_routing_readiness.go:167-168 `adjacencies.bgp[vrf], statusErr = d.frr.GetBGPSummaryVRF(ctx, vrf)`. :82-87 `for _, peer := range status.bgp[requirement.vrf] { if strings.EqualFold(peer.State, "Established") && hasName(requirement.neighbors, peer.Neighbor) { return true } }`. There is no `peer.Instance` check, although the parser stamps it (status_parse.go:491-494, `routingInstanceName`). Consumer: pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go:129 (`userspaceTransferReadiness` -> `haRoutingTransferReadiness`).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `dynamicRoutingReady` "requires evidence independently for every dynamic protocol/table that can serve the RG. A route learned by another protocol or in another table cannot make this RG's protocol ready" (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_routing_readiness.go:38-40). Requirements and adjacency maps are keyed per VRF.

**Trace:** BGP neighbor 10.0.0.1 in the default instance and in routing-instance tenant, both on RG interfaces -> requirement {bgp, vrf:"", neighbors:[10.0.0.1]} -> no learned default BGP route -> `GetBGPSummaryVRF("")` -> `vrf all` -> peers from every VRF -> the tenant peer is Established -> ready=true -> transfer allowed.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — `frr.ParseBGPSummaryAllJSON` + `dynamicRoutingReady` with a two-instance fixture and a default-only control. The vtysh call itself is static: one function, at status_parse.go:393-398.

**Confidence:** High — executed on the production parser and predicate. b08 in this run captured real FRR 10.7.1 `vrf all` JSON with the same nesting.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestF10BGPAllVRFReadiness -count=1 -v` (RUN/workers/f10/evidence/zz_f10_bgp_allvrf_readiness_probe_test.go; rerun output RUN/verify/vf10/probes/go_daemon.out). `default-down+tenant-up: ... {Neighbor:10.0.0.1 ... Instance: ... State:Active} {Neighbor:10.0.0.1 ... Instance:tenant ... State:Established}] ready=true`. Control `control-default-down-only: ... ready=false reasons=[bgp routing not ready in table 254 ...]`. Limit: no live FRR; the JSON shape is corroborated by b08's capture.

## Impact

The readiness interlock exists to stop a failover onto a routing-blind node. With overlapping tenant/default addressing, the gate certifies readiness on the wrong instance's evidence and the RG's default-table traffic blackholes until BGP converges.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Have `GetBGPSummaryVRF("")` keep querying `show bgp summary json` (default only), or filter `Instance == ""`. Also make `hasEstablishedAdjacency` require `peer.Instance == requirement.vrf`. Acceptance: the probe's mixed case reports not-ready, the default-only control stays not-ready, and a default peer Established stays ready.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16830 — R3-F11-01: #15539 stale-owner refusal triggers UNFENCED compensating rollbacks: a superseded host-auth owner withdraws the newer authority's key provenance marker (a revocation committed next leaves the key… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15539 stale-owner refusal triggers UNFENCED compensating rollbacks: a superseded host-auth owner withdraws the newer authority's key provenance marker (a revocation committed next leaves the key installed) and strips the PAM faillock

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the consequence class is privileged authority: an SSH key the config no longer grants keeps granting login while the deprovision reports success. Reach is narrow. It needs an abandoned closeout owner (budget expiry, #14356) parked between its fenced claim and its fenced write while a newer authority completes. My narrowing probe adds that the durable miss happens only when the next host-auth apply after the stale owner resumes is the revocation itself; any intervening apply re-writes the marker. The faillock strip heals at the next applySSHConfig.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F11-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf11.md` (finding `R3-F11-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:417` `keyClaim, err := claimOwnershipFenced14969(...)` then `:498-503` `if err := guardedWriteFileDurable14969(keysFile, ...); err != nil { ... keyClaim.rollback()`. `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:409-418` `rollback()` calls `removeProvenanceMarker` and `:421-426` is a raw `os.Remove`. The fenced variant `removeProvenanceMarkerFenced14969` (`hostauth_fence_14969.go:218-223`) is not used there. PAM: `daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1014` `faillockInstalled, err := applySSHPAMFaillockChanged()`, then the deferred `:1036-1042` `stripSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback(faillockInstalled)` on any `retErr`, which writes via unfenced `sshdPAMWriteFile = fsatomic.WriteFileAtomic` (`ssh_faillock_11492.go:41,259`). Exec seam: `exec_timeout.go:87-90` `out, err := body(ctx); if staleErr := checkHostAuthSeam14969(); staleErr != nil { return nil, staleErr }` discards a completed child's result, and `daemon_hostauth_apply.go:857-865` then rolls back the password/account claims.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/daemon/hostauth_fence_14969.go:36-56` (and the pkg/daemon README #15539 section): "Once a newer authority has advanced the token, the stale seam returns errHostAuthStaleOwner14969 WITHOUT performing the syscall, and the owner abstains ... no interleaving lets a stale syscall land after the newer authority's final seam for the same target." Key provenance markers gate key revocation (`login_password.go`, `#6797`).

**Trace:** commit N's closeout owner (gen G) claims alice's key marker (absent, so preExisting=false) and parks; budget expiry abandons it; commit N+1 advances to G+1 and applySystemLogin(K2) sees the marker (preExisting=true) and writes K2; the stale owner resumes, the fenced write returns stale, and the unfenced rollback unlinks the marker; commit N+2 removes alice's keys, the retained-user empty-key reconciler is marker-gated, and K2 stays installed while the commit succeeds.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/daemon production reconcilers with the #15539 supersede harness (key-marker and faillock arms, plus controls and a heal probe). STATIC: the chpasswd arm.

**Confidence:** Medium — the mechanism is executed through production `applySystemLogin` and `applySSHConfig`. Field frequency of closeout abandonment overlapping a commit is unmeasured. The password/account-marker arm (exec seam reporting stale after a completed chpasswd) is static only.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestF11|TestVF11StaleRollbackHealedByInterveningApply' -count=1 -v`; sources `RUN/workers/f11/evidence/zz_f11_keymarker_probe_test.go`, `zz_f11_faillock_probe_test.go`, `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/zz_vf11_keymarker_heal_test.go`; outputs `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/daemon_f11.out`, `keymarker_heal.out`. Observed: `stale owner err = write authorized_keys for alice: host-auth mutation refused ... (stale=true)`; `marker present after stale return = false; authorized_keys after key removal = "ssh-ed25519 NEWKEY alice@b\n"`. PAM: `after NEWER authority completed: faillock present=true` ... `stripped managed PAM faillock rules on SSH apply rollback` ... `final faillock present = false`. Controls (no supersession): `keys-after-removal=""` and `faillock present = true`. Heal probe: `intervening-apply=true: ... before removal=true, authorized_keys after removal=""` versus `intervening-apply=false: ... "ssh-ed25519 NEWKEY alice@b\n"`. Limits: the faillock probe parks the stale owner in a test-wrapped drop-in seam that reproduces the production check-then-write ordering. It is not a real fs stall.

## Impact

A super-user key or password that config revoked can keep working, with xpf's status saying it was removed. Or host-wide SSH lockout protection silently disappears until the next commit. Both arise exactly in the abandonment interleaving #15539 was written to make safe.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Treat `errors.Is(err, errHostAuthStaleOwner14969)` as "abstain entirely": rollback(), the faillock strip and forget must no-op on a stale trigger, or route through the fenced helpers (`removeProvenanceMarkerFenced14969`, a fenced `sshdPAMWriteFile`). The exec seam should return a completed child's real result, or a distinct completed-but-superseded error that callers do not roll back on. Acceptance: both TestF11 defect cells keep the newer authority's marker and faillock; the controls stay green.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16831 — R3-F11-02: `functional-zone management` compiles into an ordinary transit zone indistinguishable from `security-zone management`, so global and zone-pair permit policies forward traffic into and out of the… [OPEN]

## Summary

`functional-zone management` compiles into an ordinary transit zone indistinguishable from `security-zone management`, so global and zone-pair permit policies forward traffic into and out of the management interface, which Junos never does

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — isolation of the out-of-band management segment from data zones is lost whenever a global permit, or a zone-pair permit naming `management`, covers it. That is a common shape in imported Junos configs. The operator sees a Junos-valid commit and believes the port is host-only. It is bounded to configs that use the functional zone and carry such a permit. The compile and publication are demonstrated; the Rust forwarding of such a flow is inferred from the documented global-rule scope. [reporter: Medium, High with a global permit]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F11-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf11.md` (finding `R3-F11-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:548-557` `compileZoneBody15668(mgmt, "management", functionalZoneManagementSchema15668(), sec)` writes into the same `sec.Zones["management"]` find-or-create as a security-zone. `ZoneConfig` (`pkg/config/types_security.go:477`) carries no functional flag. No `"management"` zone special case exists in pkg/dataplane, pkg/daemon or userspace-dp/src (grep, with the functional-zone schema/compile hits as positive control). `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:200-201` publishes global rules as `FromZone: "junos-global", ToZone: "junos-global"`; `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:1859-1866` evaluates global rules for every pair. Commit 661366b4b2 Risk: "Policies may now reference from/to-zone management, which previously could not compile."

**Contract / expected behaviour:** Juniper, Security Zones configuration topic (fetched 2026-10-23, juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/security-policies/topics/topic-map/security-zone-configuration.html): "Traffic entering management zones does not match policies; therefore, traffic cannot transit out of any other interface if it was received in the management interface." and "Management zones can only be used for dedicated management interfaces." README/CLAUDE.md claim native Junos/vSRX configuration parity.

**Trace:** `set security zones functional-zone management interfaces ge-0/0/1.0` -> `compileZones` -> `sec.Zones["management"]` (ordinary) -> userspace zone snapshot binds ge-0/0/1.0 as a transit zone -> global permit (junos-global) and any management zone-pair rule publish -> helper policy admits management<->data flows.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/config strict compile plus pkg/dataplane/userspace `buildPolicySnapshots`. STATIC: the Rust global-rule scope.

**Confidence:** High for the compile and snapshot shape (executed, DeepEqual against the security-zone twin). Medium for the end-to-end transit: Rust policy evaluation was not re-run, and it rests on `junos-global` rules applying to every zone pair.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestVF11FunctionalZoneIndistinguishable|TestF11FunctionalZoneManagementIsTransitZone' -count=1 -v`; sources `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/zz_vf11_mgmtzone_test.go`, `RUN/workers/f11/evidence/zz_f11_mgmtzone_probe_test.go`; output `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/mgmtzone.out`. Observed: `functional-zone ZoneConfig == security-zone ZoneConfig (DeepEqual): true`; `policy snapshots identical: true`; `functional-zone published rule g1 junos-global->junos-global action=permit`; f11 arm: `published rule p1 management->trust action=permit`. Control: the twin config with ge-0/0/1.0 in an ordinary `security-zone management`, where transit is the intended behaviour, yields byte-identical zone and policy output. So nothing downstream can apply functional semantics. Limits: no Rust forwarding run.

## Impact

functional-zone management is the standard SRX/vSRX stanza for a dedicated OOB management port. Under an imported global permit, data-zone hosts can reach the management network, and management hosts can transit into data zones, with no visible indication.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Mark the compiled zone as functional (for example `ZoneConfig.Functional`). Reject zone-pair policies naming it at commit, exclude it from global and default policy matching, and drop transit ingress/egress on its interfaces while keeping host-inbound. Acceptance: the probe's management->trust rule is rejected at strict commit; a transit flow ingressing the functional-zone interface under a global permit is dropped; and host-inbound ssh to the interface address is still admitted.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16832 — R3-F11-03: #15667 preflight rejects every CA:TRUE leaf, including the self-signed certificate the stock OpenSSL 3 `req -x509` command emits, so an upgrade takes a working custom management HTTPS certificate… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15667 preflight rejects every CA:TRUE leaf, including the self-signed certificate the stock OpenSSL 3 `req -x509` command emits, so an upgrade takes a working custom management HTTPS certificate offline

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — the management HTTPS/REST listener is not installed, and every handshake on that slot is refused, for operators using the most common hand-made self-signed certificate. It persists until the certificate is reissued. SSH, the console and the loopback gRPC are unaffected, the error is logged, and there is no crypto weakening. This is bounded availability loss on the management plane.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F11-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf11.md` (finding `R3-F11-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/api/tls_certificate_10827.go:171-173` `if leaf.IsCA { return fmt.Errorf("leaf certificate is a CA certificate ...") }`, called at custom load (`:380-383`, `failManagementTLSCertificate`), custom refresh (`:776-779`) and per handshake (`managementTLSGetCertificateFromSlot`, `:487-516`, marks the slot invalid). There is no fallback to the generated pair for a configured custom certificate. `git show a88e050183^:pkg/api/tls_certificate_10827.go` contains zero `IsCA` references.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #15667's intent was to stop serving invalid chains (expired or not-yet-valid intermediates, broken links, non-ServerAuth leaves). The commit's own Risk states that self-signed single-leaf certs are unaffected, but it checked only generated pairs. RFC 5280 does not forbid cA=TRUE on a self-signed certificate used as its own trust anchor, and Go and curl accept it when pinned. Before a88e050183 the file had no IsCA check, so these certificates were served.

**Trace:** `system services web-management https` with a custom certificate/key -> `NewServer` -> `loadManagementTLSCertificateWithGen` -> preflight error -> `failManagementTLSCertificate` -> no HTTPS leg built; the monitor refresh repeats the rejection; any live slot refresh marks the state invalid and the selector refuses handshakes.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/api `NewServer` custom-certificate load plus the certificate selector, with a real handshake twin.

**Confidence:** High — executed with a real OpenSSL 3.6.4 certificate through the production server constructor. A stock Go TLS client pinning that certificate handshakes successfully against a plain Go server.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/api/ -run TestVF11OpenSSLDefaultSelfSignedCustomLoad -count=1 -v`; source `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/zz_vf11_tls_ca_leaf_test.go`, certs `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/certs/` (`openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -subj /CN=fw -addext subjectAltName=DNS:fw`, which `openssl x509 -ext basicConstraints` reports as `critical CA:TRUE`), output `probes/tls.out`. Observed: `openssl req -x509 default (CA:TRUE): stock Go server+pinned Go client handshake err=<nil>`; `xpf httpsServer installed=false getCertificate err=management TLS certificate is unavailable: leaf certificate is a CA certificate`. Positive control: the identical command with `-addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE` gives `installed=true err=<nil>`. Limits: the browser-specific treatment of CA:TRUE leaves was not tested.

## Impact

Operators with a hand-made management certificate lose HTTPS/REST management after upgrading. Nothing at commit time warns them, because the certificate files are external to the config. Recovery requires reissuing the certificate.

## Acceptance / fix direction

For a single-entry self-signed chain, downgrade CA:TRUE to a logged diagnostic. Keep rejecting a CA:TRUE leaf that is not self-signed (a mis-installed intermediate). Acceptance: the probe's CA:TRUE self-signed certificate loads with a warning; the existing `CA leaf` chain cell (issued by an intermediate) is still rejected.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16833 — R3-F11-04: Every commit's netlink address reconcile deletes a standalone `vrrp-group` MASTER's VIP (untagged and VLAN units); VRRP stays MASTER and nothing re-adds it [OPEN]

## Summary

Every commit's netlink address reconcile deletes a standalone `vrrp-group` MASTER's VIP (untagged and VLAN units); VRRP stays MASTER and nothing re-adds it

**Severity:** High (source report) — High — on any node running a standalone (non-RETH) Junos VRRP group, the next commit of any change removes the gateway VIP from the elected MASTER. The MASTER keeps advertising from its real address, so the BACKUP never takes over, and hosts behind the segment lose their first-hop gateway once ARP/ND ages out. It lasts until a VRRP state change or a daemon restart. HA cannot recover it on its own. Bounded to standalone vrrp-group deployments (RETH, DHCP and fabric are excluded by the existing `skipAddrs`). The deletion is demonstrated; the end-to-end gateway loss is inferred from the static no-re-add chain.

**Finding ID:** `R3-F11-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf11.md` (finding `R3-F11-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go:250-252` `if ifCfg.RedundancyGroup > 0 || ifCfg.LocalFabricMember != "" { pd.skipAddrs = true }` and `:273-275` (DHCP) are the only suppressions; `:276-282` desired is `unit.Addresses` only. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go:1385-1390` `if pd := st.physDesired[physName]; pd != nil && !pd.skipAddrs { if reconcileInterfaceAddresses(physName, pd.addrs, ...)`. The VLAN arm `:1060-1083` `if !isDHCPSub && !isReth { if reconcileInterfaceAddresses(subName, addrs, ...)`. `planAddressReconcile` `:653` `del = append(del, addr)` for every non-link-local address not in `want`. The only VRRP consult in pkg/dataplane is `compiler_iface_vrrp_keep.go` (networkd keep). On the re-add side: `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:755` `continue // No change.` for an unchanged instance; `pkg/vrrp/addrwatch.go` `reresolveAddrFor` only re-resolves the advert source; `ReconcileVIPs` is called only when `needLinkCycleRecovery` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:1084-1086`); `ReconcileVIPsForRG` is RG-keyed (`:1103`). Observation: delete demonstrated. Inference: the gateway outage, from the static re-add census.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** CLAUDE.md (networkd section): "standalone `vrrp-group` rows carry the static keep via `KeepForeignStatic` (#15061) — their VIPs are installed by pkg/vrrp and never rendered as `Address=`". `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_vrrp_keep.go` (#15061) records the VIP as a genuine kernel address owned by pkg/vrrp that must survive reconfigure. The zone planner already honours that ownership rule for RETH, where `skipAddrs` is set because "those addresses belong to the DHCP client, VRRP, or the IPVLAN overlay" (`compiler_iface.go:1383-1384` comment).

**Trace:** commit -> `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:222 rt.ApplyConfig` -> `CompileUserspaceShim` (`pkg/dataplane/loader.go:275-285`) -> `CompileConfig` -> `compileZones` -> `mapZoneInterface` -> `reconcileInterfaceAddresses(ge-0-0-1, [10.0.1.10/24])` -> AddrDel 10.0.1.1/24 (logged "removed stale address from interface") -> apply tail `vrrpMgr.UpdateInstances` (`daemon_apply_tail.go:156`) sees no change -> instance stays MASTER, advertising, with no VIP in the kernel.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — component scope: `planPhysDesired` plus the production `reconcileInterfaceAddresses` actuation via its netlink seams (untagged arm via the planner; VLAN arm with the unit's addresses as the zone loop passes them). STATIC: the daemon apply chain and the absence of any VIP re-add.

**Confidence:** High — the delete was executed through the production reconcile function on a strict-compiled config, with two controls. Medium-High for "nothing re-adds it". That part is a static census of every VIP add path in pkg/vrrp and pkg/daemon, which a28 repeated independently. No live netlink run.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run 'TestVF11StandaloneVRRPVIPReconcile|TestF11StandaloneVRRPVIPDeletedByNetlinkReconcile' -count=1 -v`; source `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/zz_vf11_vrrp_vip_test.go`, output `RUN/verify/vf11/probes/vrrp_vip.out`. Strict-compiled `set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.10/24 vrrp-group 1 virtual-address 10.0.1.1/24` (+ priority, zone). Observed: `vrrp instance iface (CollectInstances resolver)=ge-0-0-1`; `plan ge-0-0-1 addrs=[10.0.1.10/24] skipAddrs=false`; `MASTER (VIP + link-local present): deleted=[10.0.1.1/24]`; `VLAN vrrp instance iface=ge-0-0-1.100`, `VLAN MASTER: deleted=[10.0.100.1/24]`. Positive controls: `CONTROL BACKUP (no VIP): deleted=[]` (converged) and `CONTROL stale non-VIP: deleted=[10.0.9.9/24]`, which shows the harness sees deletes and the VIP is handled exactly like operator-stale debris. A bare VIP without a prefix is rejected at strict commit, so the prefixed form is the only committable shape. Limits: no real netlink and no live VRRP instance.

## Impact

Standalone firewalls or pairs using Junos VRRP for a LAN gateway lose the gateway at the first routine commit, such as a policy edit. `show vrrp` keeps reporting MASTER and the peer stays BACKUP. The outage is durable until a VRRP transition or a restart, and it repeats on every later commit after recovery.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `planPhysDesired` and the VLAN-unit arm, collect each enabled unit's `VRRPGroups[*].VirtualAddresses` into a per-netdev foreign-keep set that `planAddressReconcile` never deletes. Do not add them to `desired`. As a belt, pkg/vrrp could re-add on RTM_DELADDR while MASTER. Acceptance: the probe's MASTER and VLAN arms plan zero deletes with the VIP present; the stale-address control still deletes 10.0.9.9/24; and removing a vrrp-group still withdraws its VIP via pkg/vrrp.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16834 — R3-F12-01: A VRRP group on a disabled unit or interface still runs, claims MASTER, and installs its VIP, while #15763 and #13149 removed that VIP from every host-inbound drop scope (kernel input path fails open) [OPEN]

## Summary

A VRRP group on a disabled unit or interface still runs, claims MASTER, and installs its VIP, while #15763 and #13149 removed that VIP from every host-inbound drop scope (kernel input path fails open)

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — this is a loss of host-inbound enforcement for one firewall-local address. Every host service listening on a wildcard socket (SSH, NETCONF, HTTPS, SNMP and so on) answers new connections on the VIP no matter what the zone's `host-inbound-traffic` says. Two things bound it. First, the trigger is an operator `disable` on a unit or interface that carries a `vrrp-group`. Second, the demonstrated exposure is the kernel-delivered host path that the nft table exists to guard: kernel-terminated GRE/IPsec tunnel ingress and interfaces not under XDP. The AF_XDP ingress path most likely does not deliver the packet, because the VIP is also missing from the shim's local-address map (static reading, not executed) [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F12-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf12.md` (finding `R3-F12-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

Observations at d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:95-97` (`unit := ifc.Units[unitNum]; if unit == nil { continue }`, with no Disable gate); `pkg/vrrp/instance_transition.go:92-130` (`becomeMaster` → `setState(StateMaster)` → `addVIPsLocked()`, gated only by the kernel-upgrade hold and the advert-capacity check, not by link state); `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:627,637` (zoned VIP walk `iface.Disable` / `unit.Disable` skip); `:1074,1084` (unzoned walk); `:1606-1608` (the live snapshot walk skips `snap.AdminDisabled`, so even the VIP live on the netdev is skipped); `:1625,1635` (`forEachFirewallLocalAddrFromSnaps` VRRP walk). `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:604` sets `AdminDisabled: iface.Disable || unit.Disable`. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1777-1779` also skips AdminDisabled rows when building the shim's USERSPACE_LOCAL map (an inference about XSK behaviour; not executed).

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound.go:603-614` (#3172) says VIPs must be in the host-inbound destination set "or `chain input` would fall through to `policy accept` (FAIL-OPEN) for VIP-destined host-bound traffic". `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:818-822` says an unscoped local address "would fall through the chain's `policy accept` and reach the host stack with no host-inbound admission (fail-open)". #15763 and #13149 drop a disabled unit's or interface's VIP from scope on the premise that a disabled unit owns no address. Under Junos, a disabled interface or unit carries no active VRRP group.

**Trace:** `set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 3 disable` on a unit with `vrrp-group 30 virtual-address 10.0.30.254/24` passes strict commit. networkd renders the netdev `ActivationPolicy=always-down` with no Address= (`pkg/networkd/networkd.go:1617-1625`). `applyTailReconciles` → `CollectInstances` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:107`) → `Manager.UpdateInstances` → `openSocket` succeeds on the down netdev → no adverts are heard → master-down → `becomeMaster` adds the VIP; the kernel installs a `local` route. `BuildInterfaceSnapshots` marks the row AdminDisabled, and `BuildZoneHostInboundViews`, `BuildUnzonedHostInboundAddrs` and `BuildFenceAddrSets` all omit the VIP. The nft chain then has no drop for it, so the packet reaches `policy accept` and the host socket.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — four executed pieces, each in an unprivileged user+net namespace except the strict commit (an in-process compile): (1) strict commit of the config; (2) the production `CollectInstances`, `Manager.UpdateInstances` and run loop on a real DOWN VLAN netdev; (3) kernel local delivery of an address on a down netdev; (4) the production host-inbound payload built from the live snapshot, loaded with real nft and tested with TCP SYNs. The XSK/userspace-dp disposition is STATIC.

**Confidence:** High for the chain from commit to VRRP MASTER to VIP to nft verdict (all executed on a real kernel). Medium for which production ingress paths reach the kernel input chain with this destination. Remaining assumption: networkd reconfigures of the always-down link may strip the foreign VIP between VRRP re-adds, so the VIP may be present only intermittently.

**Probe:** (a) `RUN/verify/vf12/probes/zz_vf12_disabled_unit_netns_test.go`, run as `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run TestVF12DisabledUnitVRRPRunsOnRealKernel -v` (output in `probes/vrrp_netns.out`). It applies the set-syntax config (strict CompileConfig; the VIP must carry a prefix, `10.0.30.254/24`) and runs the production `NewManager`/`UpdateInstances`. With `disable=true` it logs `CollectInstances=[ge-0-0-0.30/vrid30/[10.0.30.254/24]]`, `transitioning to MASTER`, `added VIP vip=10.0.30.254/24`, `GARP failed ... network is down`, `states=map[VI_ge-0-0-0.30_30_inet:MASTER]`, `ge-0-0-0.30@ge-0-0-0 DOWN 10.0.30.254/24` and `local 10.0.30.254 dev ge-0-0-0.30 proto kernel scope host`. (b) `probes/kernel_down_vip.out` shows that from an up interface, `ip route get` for v4 and v6 addresses on a down VLAN or veth returns `local ... dev lo`; the control (a non-local address) gives `Network is unreachable`. (c) `probes/zz_vf12_disabled_vip_nft_netns_test.go`, run as `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestVF12DisabledUnitVIPHostInboundOnRealKernel -v` (output in `probes/nft_netns.out`). It builds the payload with `sampleHostInboundSnapshots` and the production builders and loads it with real nft; an untrust-zone client sends an SSH SYN, and both zones allow only ping. Enabled twin: `ssh->10.0.20.1(control)=timeout ssh->VIP=timeout payload mentions VIP=true`. Disabled: `ssh->10.0.20.1(control)=timeout ssh->VIP 10.0.30.254=connected payload mentions VIP=false`. The no-table baseline is `connected` in both cases (reachability control). Limits: the client arrives on a plain kernel VLAN netdev, not through AF_XDP. f12's own Go-side probe and mutation control (`RUN/workers/f12/evidence/zz_r3f12_disabled_unit_vrrp_probe_test.go`) agree.

## Impact

An operator who disables a unit to take it out of service gets a live, unfiltered local address on the box, reachable on the kernel host path (for example over a tunnel). `show vrrp` reports MASTER for that unit. The state persists until the unit is re-enabled or the group is removed.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make `CollectInstances` skip `ifc.Disable || unit.Disable`; the existing manager reconcile then stops the instance and withdraws its VIPs. Keep the #15763/#13149 scope exclusion consistent with that. Acceptance: in the vf12 pkg/vrrp probe, the disabled case has 0 instances and no VIP on the netdev; the enabled twin is still MASTER; in the nft probe the disabled row gets `timeout` (no VIP is present); re-enabling restores the instance; a whole-interface-disable row is added.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16835 — R3-F12-02: #15779's ordered permutation entries cannot match a route whose literal members sit next to each other (or one community that satisfies two regex members), so `from community X` misses routes that… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15779's ordered permutation entries cannot match a route whose literal members sit next to each other (or one community that satisfies two regex members), so `from community X` misses routes that carry every member

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — routing-policy enforcement is wrong for an ordinary shape: a multi-member `community` with at least two literal members plus at least one regex member, at most 4 distinct members. A route carrying every member, with the two literals consecutive in the sorted community string, fails every entry. A `then reject` term then lets the route through to later terms (a filter bypass), and an accept or modify term skips it. Bounded to BGP policy on that shape; no crash [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F12-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf12.md` (finding `R3-F12-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

`pkg/frr/policy_render.go:212-214` (a literal becomes `` `(^| )` + factor + `( |$)` ``), `:226-231` (`joined = prefix + ".*" + factor`), `:330-333` (emitted as `bgp community-list expanded <name> permit <pattern>`). FRR master `bgpd/bgp_clist.c:531-544` (`regexec` on `community_str(com, false)`), `bgpd/bgp_community.c:293-301` (values joined with a single `" "`, sorted by `qsort` at `:162`), and `bgpd/bgp_regex.c:54` (`regcomp(..., REG_EXTENDED | REG_NOSUB)`); I fetched and read all three.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** `pkg/frr/README.md:1688-1691` says "each entry requires every factor in its order, so the set matches exactly the routes satisfying every member"; `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:74-82` makes the same claim, adding "in whatever position". Junos semantics (Juniper's routing-policy community evaluation, as quoted in R3-A11-05): each member is evaluated against each community on the route, one community can satisfy a member, and every member must be satisfied.

**Trace:** `set policy-options community MIX members [ 65000:100 65000:200 65001:.* ]` plus `from community MIX; then reject` → `communityExpandedConjunctionPatterns` → 3! expanded permit lines → `route-map IMP deny 10 / match community MIX` → bgpd `community_regexp_match` on `"65000:100 65000:200 65001:5"` → no entry matches → the term is skipped → the route falls through to later terms or the default.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — set syntax → strict CompileConfig → `generatePolicyOptions` → rendered lines → regexec oracle. Not executed against a running bgpd.

**Confidence:** High for the render and its regex semantics: executed with Go POSIX and with a glibc `regcomp(REG_EXTENDED|REG_NOSUB)` oracle mirroring FRR, plus positive and negative controls. The live bgpd outcome is currently masked by R3-A11-04 (see Adversarial analysis).

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vf12/probes/zz_vf12_community_e2e_probe_test.go` (`go test ./pkg/frr/ -run TestVF12CommunityE2E -v`, output in `probes/community_e2e.out`) renders 6 entries for `[ 65000:100 65000:200 65001:.* ]`. Results: literals separated `match=true`, lit2 absent `false`, regex absent `false`, regex-only list `true`; the ADJACENT row `65000:100 65000:200 65001:5` gives `match=false want=true`. The glibc oracle (`probes/regexec_frr.c`, output in `probes/glibc_regexec.out`) gives the same verdicts, and the double-spaced twin `65000:100  65000:200 65001:5` gives `match=1`, which isolates separator consumption as the cause. The pipe-free spelling A11-04 proposes (`probes/mix_patterns_pipefree.txt`, output in `glibc_regexec_pipefree.out`) still gives adjacent `match=0`. For the shared-token shape (`probes/shared_token.out`), `[65000:.* .*:100]` against a route carrying only `65000:100` gives `match=0`, while the control `65000:7 1:100` gives `match=1`. A candidate fix shape (`probes/fix_shape.out`) matches the adjacent and separated rows and correctly rejects `165000:200`, `65000:2000` and the case with a member absent. Limit: no running bgpd.

## Impact

Operators commonly combine exact tags with a regex (`[ 65000:100 65000:200 65000:3.* ]`), and numerically close exact values sort next to each other. A reject term built on such a list silently passes the routes it targets, with no warning, and `show` displays the configured semantics. If R3-A11-04 is fixed by respelling alone, this becomes the live behaviour.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Generate factors so that consecutive literal factors share a separator. For example, join a literal factor that follows a literal as `(.* )?m( |$)` instead of `.*(^| )m( |$)`. Alternatively, express the literal members as a separate standard list AND-ed in the route-map. Coordinate this with the R3-A11-04 pipe-free spelling and the R3-A11-05 per-token semantics. Acceptance: the adjacent row and the shared-token row match, while the separated, absent-member and substring (`65000:2000`, `165000:200`) controls keep their verdicts; the patterns compile under `regexp.CompilePOSIX` and glibc regcomp, contain no `| `, and install in a running bgpd.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16837 — R3-F13-01: `then static-nat prefix-name` resolves through singular UsableValue(): a multi-host range-address or multi-answer dns-name commits as 1:1 NAT to its first host, and a dns-name target is frozen at… [OPEN]

## Summary

`then static-nat prefix-name` resolves through singular UsableValue(): a multi-host range-address or multi-answer dns-name commits as 1:1 NAT to its first host, and a dns-name target is frozen at the compile-time answer

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — a strict-clean commit installs an inbound static NAT whose target is not what the referenced object denotes, with no warning. For dns-name, after a DNS change the NAT keeps the old host while the policy book follows DNS, so inbound service is misdirected or blackholed with no commit. Bounded to static NAT naming a range/dns-name object

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-01`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-01`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

compiler_nat_static.go:532-535 `if value := a.UsableValue(); value != "" { return value, true }` has no multiplicity check, unlike the set branch at :542 (`len(members) != 1` -> false), and :545-548 repeats it for a one-member set whose member is a range. pkg/config/types_security.go:1893-1906: UsableValue returns `a.ExpandedPrefixes[0]` / `a.DNSAddresses[0]`. compiler_nat_static.go:596-606 writes Then once and skips rules with `rule.Then != ""`. pkg/daemon/daemon_dnsaddr.go:156-169 refreshes via CloneForDNSRefresh + RefreshDNSAddressBooks + applyConfigLocked, which does not re-resolve Then.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/config/compiler_nat_static.go:517-523: "anything else (undefined, an address with no prefix, an empty / multi-member set, dangling) is not a valid scalar 1:1 target and returns ok=false … the strict guard rejects it". #15673's own intent was to consume Address.UsableValues in every resolver.

**Trace:** `address r range-address 10.0.0.5 to 10.0.0.8` -> ExpandedPrefixes (4 x /32) -> resolveStaticNATThenPrefixNames (compiler_earlystrict.go:241) -> UsableValue -> rule.Then="10.0.0.5/32" -> validateStaticNATThenTargetStrict passes (Then non-empty) -> static NAT snapshot. dns-name: compile-time answer -> Then -> 5-minute refresh updates book entries only.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/config strict compile plus RefreshDNSAddressBooks; the daemon refresh path (daemon_dnsaddr.go) reasoned statically

**Confidence:** High — compile results executed; the end-to-end translated-host behaviour follows directly from rule.Then and was not lab-tested

**Probe:** workers/f13/evidence/zz_r3f13_static_prefix_name_test.go re-run by vf13 (RUN/verify/vf13/f13-01-02-config.out): `CONTROL two-member set strict commit REJECTED … does not resolve to a single address-book prefix (#4290)`; `CONTROL single prefix strict commit OK: Then="10.0.0.5/32"`; `range-address 4 hosts strict commit OK: Then="10.0.0.5/32" (entry usable=[10.0.0.5/32 10.0.0.6/32 10.0.0.7/32 10.0.0.8/32])`; `range-address in 1-member set … Then="10.0.0.5/32"`; dns: `compile: answer=[10.0.0.5 10.0.0.9] Then="10.0.0.5/32"` -> `after DNS change+refresh: answer=[10.0.0.77] Then="10.0.0.5/32" usable=[10.0.0.77/32]`.

## Impact

Inbound 1:1 NAT silently maps to a single host other than what the object denotes. With dns-name the misdirection appears later, with no commit and no warning, and policy and NAT disagree about the server's address.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In resolveStaticNATThenPrefixName use UsableValues() and require exactly one value with DNSName=="" (a dynamic object is not a static 1:1 target), otherwise ok=false. Acceptance: the range, 1-member-set and dns-name probe rows are all rejected strict and warned lenient, and the single-prefix control still resolves.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16838 — R3-F13-02: #15685 dynamic-address/static name-collision gate does not cover #15672 named address books: an attached named-book entry sharing a binding's name commits strict-clean and the userspace policy… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15685 dynamic-address/static name-collision gate does not cover #15672 named address books: an attached named-book entry sharing a binding's name commits strict-clean and the userspace policy snapshot is refused while the feed is unready

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — this brings back the exact #15685 failure: whole-snapshot publication is refused, so the previous-good policy is retained (or default-deny on a fresh boot) until the feed is fetched, and after that the name enforces feed ∪ static, all after a clean strict commit. It fails closed and is bounded to configs combining named books with dynamic-address

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-02`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-02`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

compiler_validate_strict_addrbook.go:157-226 iterates `cfg.Security.AddressBook` and `cfg.Security.Zones[*].AddressBook` only. The file's other gates reference NamedAddressBooks, this one does not. compiler_earlystrict.go:164 runs the gate, then :218 `resolveNamedAddressBooks15672(&cfg.Security)` folds the named book into the zone, and :233 `resolveZoneLocalAddressBooks` mints `zone-local/trust/blocked`, which dynamicAddressLookupName (pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:353) unqualifies back to the binding name `blocked`. No later gate compares bindings against folded entries.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_addrbook.go:124-156 (#15685) rejects a dynamic-address binding sharing its name with a static entry "in the global book or in ANY zone-local book … MUST run on the PRISTINE books". compiler_earlystrict.go:214-217 (#15672) says "the pristine gates above already validated the named books' own entries". Junos also forbids the name ambiguity at commit.

**Trace:** `security address-book eng-book address blocked …; attach zone trust` plus `dynamic-address address-name blocked` -> pristine gates (no NamedAddressBooks walk) -> named-book fold -> zone-local fold -> policy token zone-local/trust/blocked -> userspace lowering checks the declared binding first -> feed overlay absent -> unrepresentable -> PolicyContentRejectionReasons non-empty -> snapshot publication refused.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — pkg/config strict compile and pkg/dataplane/userspace PolicyContentRejectionReasons; the helper-side refusal and its previous-good retention are covered by the existing #15685 chain, not re-run

**Confidence:** High — executed at compile and at the lowering boundary with positive controls; the post-ready "union" meaning is taken from #15685's own documented analysis, not re-probed

**Probe:** workers/f13/evidence/zz_r3f13_named_book_dynaddr_test.go and zz_r3f13_named_book_dynaddr_runtime_test.go, re-run by vf13 (RUN/verify/vf13/f13-01-02-config.out, f13-02-04-userspace.out): `CONTROL zone-local book strict commit REJECTED … collides with security zone "trust"`; `CONTROL global book strict commit REJECTED`; `named book attached to trust strict commit OK: policy source tokens=[zone-local/trust/blocked] folded zone-local entry present=true binding=true`. Runtime: `CONTROL no collision … feed unready reasons=0`; `named-book collision … feed unready reasons=1 [policy trust->untrust/p1 … source-address "zone-local/trust/blocked"]`.

## Impact

A migrated config combining a named book with a threat-feed binding re-arms the #15685 publication abort. Every later policy commit "succeeds" while the helper keeps the previous snapshot (or default-deny on a fresh boot) until the feed is ready.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Iterate cfg.Security.NamedAddressBooks in validateDynamicAddressStaticCollisionStrict, naming the book in the error, and add a cross-gate census test asserting that every pristine gate walks all three book kinds. Acceptance: the probe's named-book row is rejected strict and warned lenient, and both controls are unchanged.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16839 — R3-F13-03: #15727 raw-priority RST-drop chain also drops RSTs from live, conntrack-tracked local sockets on interface-NAT addresses (no nfct exists before the -200 conntrack hook), and the fix's tracked-RST… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15727 raw-priority RST-drop chain also drops RSTs from live, conntrack-tracked local sockets on interface-NAT addresses (no nfct exists before the -200 conntrack hook), and the fix's tracked-RST control cannot fail

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — abortive closes (SO_LINGER 0, close with unread data) of the firewall's own TCP sockets bound to an interface-NAT address lose their RST, and the peer holds the connection until its own timer. Enforcement is unaffected and graceful FIN closes are unaffected. The upper bound is Medium only if a control-plane protocol on that address depends on RST delivery, which is not shown

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-03`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-03`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

rst_suppress.go:134 `Priority: nftables.ChainPriorityRaw` on ChainHookOutput, and :222-246 matches `ct state & INVALID == INVALID`, `tcp flags & rst != 0`, counter, drop. pkg/nftables/rst_suppress_live_15727_test.go:96-127: the "tracked" control aborts the client socket (source 127.0.0.1, "outside the rule's saddr scope as well as tracked"), so it passes regardless.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/nftables/rst_suppress.go:27-34: "Conntrack-tracked RSTs from the same addresses -- nft reject-with-tcp-reset … and local control-plane socket RSTs -- are legitimate and must survive." :124-125 gives the premise "a local socket's RST carries its socket conntrack entry (attached before OUTPUT)".

**Trace:** interface-NAT address set (pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go interface-NAT collection) -> InstallRSTSuppression -> output chain at -300 -> local socket abort -> tcp_send_active_reset -> ip_local_out -> raw hook: no nfct -> INVALID -> drop.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — live kernel in an unprivileged user+net namespace (`unshare -rn`), loopback addresses standing in for the interface-NAT address

**Confidence:** High — the kernel behaviour was measured directly with a witness that has no drop rule

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vf13/probes/zz_vf13_rst_witness_test.go installs witness counters only (no drop), `go test -c ./pkg/nftables/ && unshare -rn nft.test -test.run TestVF13RSTWitness -test.v` (RUN/verify/vf13/f13-03.out): `server-abort RST from 127.0.0.2: raw(-300) ct-invalid=1 filter(0) ct-established=1 filter(0) ct-invalid=0 … connection reset by peer`. The same RST is ESTABLISHED (tracked) after conntrack and INVALID at raw. f13's cell (workers/f13/evidence/zz_r3f13_rst_tracked_live_test.go), re-run: control `rst-drop counter 0 -> 0; client saw RST (ECONNRESET)`; with xpf_dp_rst `0 -> 1; client saw NOTHING (RST dropped; read timed out)`. The existing 15727 live test still passes (`after tracked RST: packets=3`), which shows its control is blind to this. Limits: loopback rather than a NIC, and the default sysctls of the namespace.

## Impact

Peers of the firewall's own sockets on a WAN interface-NAT address get no reset on abort and hold half-open state. Operator troubleshooting is misled because the counter attributes these to "spurious" RSTs.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Exclude socket-owned packets at raw (for example match `meta sk`/socket presence, since tcp_v4_send_reset's control socket is not a full socket), or move the rule after conntrack and match the no-entry signature there. Acceptance: a live cell whose RST is SOURCED from the protected address by a live server socket is delivered, while the existing socket-less spurious-RST cell is still dropped.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);

## #16840 — R3-F13-04: #15675 charges 0 port slots for `port no-translation` pools in the Go aggregate budget, but the Rust apply still defaults them to 1024-65535 and charges/builds the full PAT bitmap: strict-clean… [OPEN]

## Summary

#15675 charges 0 port slots for `port no-translation` pools in the Go aggregate budget, but the Rust apply still defaults them to 1024-65535 and charges/builds the full PAT bitmap: strict-clean configs have later pools refused OverBudget at runtime

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — a config the commit gate accepts and the Go snapshot builder does not poison is refused by the helper's independent #6812 budget. The over-budget pool's rules get pool_failure=OverBudget, so its subscribers' traffic fails closed after a clean commit. Within budget, each address-only pool also materialises a 64,512-slot bitmap per address that the address-only path never uses. Bounded to large address-only pools (more than about 133k addresses in aggregate at the 2^33-slot budget)

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-04`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-04`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

Go: compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:4416-4418 `if pool.PortNoTranslation { return 0, 0, true }`, and :4693-4701 `var portCap uint64; if !pool.PortNoTranslation { … }`. pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go ships PortLow=0/PortHigh=0 with PoolNoTranslation=true. Rust: userspace-dp/src/nat/source/mod.rs:1898 sets `pool_mode` true for a named pool. :2025-2033 defaults 0 to 1024 and 65535. :2088-2097 pushes a PendingPoolAllocator for every healthy pool-mode rule with no `no_translation` exclusion. :628-640 charges `allocator_capacity(total_pool, port_low, port_high)`. The budget is 1<<33 at :482-486, and :978-982 does `used.admitted_with(charge, budget)`, which on refusal gives OverBudget at :946-949.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:4716-4735 says the Go walk mirrors "the Rust apply boundary [which] independently enforces the same budgets … same charge". The comment at :4680-4685 names this very defect class: a pool that "charged zero port slots and was admitted, while … the dataplane charged 64,512 per address".

**Trace:** `source pool pN address 100.6x.0.0/16; port no-translation` x 3 -> SourceNATAggregateOverBudgetPools charges 0 port slots -> strict commit OK, nothing poisoned -> snapshot wire port 0/0 + pool_no_translation -> Rust parse defaults to 1024-65535 -> PendingPoolAllocator charge 65536 x 64512 per pool -> first-fit admits p0+p1 (8.46e9 ≤ 8.59e9) -> p2 OverBudget -> rules on p2 fail closed.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — Go: strict compile + snapshot builder (pkg/dataplane/userspace). Rust: `parse_source_nat_rules_with_budget` (the same resolve path as production) with a scaled budget and a temporary cargo test; the production 2^33 budget is reasoned arithmetically, as the existing #6812 suite does

**Confidence:** High — both halves executed at d1ea69f9aa

**Probe:** Go, workers/f13/evidence/zz_r3f13_notranslation_budget_test.go re-run (RUN/verify/vf13/f13-02-04-userspace.out): `CONTROL PAT pools strict commit REJECTED: … 12683575296 total port slots … over the aggregate budget of 8589934592`; `no-translation pools strict commit OK; Go over-budget pools=map[]`, wire `PortLow=0 PortHigh=0 noTranslation=true`. Rust, RUN/verify/vf13/probes/vf13_notrans_budget.rs, temporarily appended to src/nat/tests_aggregate_budget.rs and reverted, `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vf13_no_translation_pool_charge_skew` (RUN/verify/vf13/f13-04-rust.out): three /29 no-translation pools at wire 0/0 under a budget of 2 x 8 x 64512 give `r0 … port=1024-65535 failure=None occupancy_words=8064`, `r1 … failure=None occupancy_words=8064`, `r2 … failure=Some(OverBudget) occupancy_words=0`. The unbounded-budget twin installs all three. Go charges these pools 0, so it would admit any number of them. Limits: a scaled budget stands in for 2^33, and no lab run.

## Impact

CGNAT-style address-only pools are exactly the configs with very large pools. The commit succeeds, the snapshot publishes, and a later pool's subscribers are dropped by the helper, visible only as an over_budget pool failure. Memory is also wasted on bitmaps the address-only path never touches.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Make the two sides agree on the same unit. The preferred fix is Rust: skip the port bitmap and charge 0 port slots for `no_translation` rules (and key their allocator without the port range). The alternative is Go charging what Rust builds. Acceptance: a Rust cell applying three no-translation pools at wire 0/0 under the real budget gets no OverBudget, plus a Go/Rust charge-parity cell for a no-translation pool.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16841 — R3-F13-05: `no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit` is implemented as "suppress transit ICMPv6 Time Exceeded"; Junos defines it as "accept hop-limit-0 packets addressed to the local host", and the Junos default… [OPEN]

## Summary

`no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit` is implemented as "suppress transit ICMPv6 Time Exceeded"; Junos defines it as "accept hop-limit-0 packets addressed to the local host", and the Junos default (reject them) is enforced nowhere

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — a Junos statement gets a different meaning. With the knob unset, xpf accepts hop-limit-0 IPv6 to its own addresses (Junos rejects it). With it set, the only change is that transit expiry no longer draws Time Exceeded, which is behaviour the statement does not govern and which RFC 4443 §3.3 requires. There is no transit enforcement change

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-05`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-05`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp.rs:234-238 and :660-664 are the only behavioural consumers (they return None when the arrived hop limit is 0 and the flag is set). pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1233-1245 takes no kernel action. A grep for `packet_hop_limit_v6`, `hop_limit == 0` and nft `hoplimit` finds no local-delivery check in userspace-dp/src or pkg/nftables. pkg/config/schema_system.go:188 help text is "Do not reject IPv6 packets with zero hop limit".

**Contract / expected behaviour:** Juniper "Configuring the Acceptance of IPv6 Packets with a Zero Hop Limit" (juniper.net/documentation/en_US/junos13.1/topics/task/configuration/ipv6-acceptance-packets-zero-hop-limit-configuring.html): "By default, such packets are rejected both when they are addressed to the local host and when they are transiting the router or switch." "To accept zero hop-limit packets addressed to the local host, include the no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit statement". "Transit packets are still dropped." The page has no ICMP text. RFC 4443 §3.3: "If a router receives a packet with a Hop Limit of zero … it MUST discard the packet and originate an ICMPv6 Time Exceeded message with Code 0".

**Trace:** `set system internet-options no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit` -> compiler_system.go:908-917 -> builder.go:283 NoIPv6RejectZeroHopLimit -> snapshot -> forwarding_build/mod.rs:672 -> icmp.rs Time Exceeded suppression only. The local-delivery path has no consumer.

**Verification in source report:** STATIC — consumer census over Go and Rust, plus the vendor page and the RFC section read

**Confidence:** High — the vendor text was fetched, and the code census of the flag and of any hop-limit-0 local check is complete

**Probe:** none executed (no Rust cell needed for a census). The settling cells would be a Rust test where ICMPv6 echo with hop limit 0 to a local address is dropped with the knob off and delivered with it on, plus a cell asserting that transit expiry Time Exceeded is unaffected by the knob.

## Impact

Migrated configs get different host-bound admission than Junos documents, and `show system` output claims a semantics the dataplane does not apply. Setting the knob also suppresses an RFC-mandated error. The blast radius is small.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Drop hop-limit-0 IPv6 addressed to local host addresses by default (XDP local-delivery and kernel input), let the knob admit them, and restore unconditional transit Time Exceeded (subject to the rate limiter). Acceptance: the two Rust cells above, plus the existing #15707 cells updated to the corrected contract.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## #16842 — R3-F13-06: #15687 fab1 transport debt makes the #11448 reassert loop tear down and rebuild session sync every 30 s, indefinitely, while fab1 has no address (fabric-transport dual-fabric clusters) [OPEN]

## Summary

#15687 fab1 transport debt makes the #11448 reassert loop tear down and rebuild session sync every 30 s, indefinitely, while fab1 has no address (fabric-transport dual-fabric clusters)

**Severity:** Medium (source report) — Medium — continuous session-sync churn (with a full cold-prime bulk each reconnect, plus aux/config/IPsec/DHCP sync and fabric loops restarted) on a cluster that has lost one of its two fabrics, which is the fault dual fabric exists to absorb; bounded because it only happens in fabric-transport mode (no `control-interface`/`peer-address`), the heartbeat is not involved (it never runs in that mode), and sync is up for part of every cycle; no loss of RG ownership was shown [reporter: High]

**Finding ID:** `R3-F13-06`
**Source report:** `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`
**Source part:** `parts/vf13.md` (finding `R3-F13-06`)
**Validated by:** three research lanes (codex / smr / wonder) — votes: `codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL` (see addendum to finished report; at least 2/3 MATERIAL or COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)
**Verified against:** `d1ea69f9aa` (origin/master at review time); file:line evidence below is from ledgers/parts at that base — re-verify line numbers at current master before fixing.

## Mechanism

pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:1349 `if syncTransport == "fabric" && cc.Fabric1Interface != "" && cc.Fabric1PeerAddress != ""` guards the fab1 poll, and :1380 `d.markClusterCommsFab1Debt(commsGen)` runs on poll exhaustion. :1148-1158 sets the sticky BindingChanged flag. pkg/daemon/mgmt_vrf_reassert_11448.go:13 sets the interval to 30 s. :39-47 lets the quick gate pass on `bindingChanged` alone, and :82-89 then calls `reconcileClusterTransportBinding(cfg, false)`. pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:545-561: the config-derived key (BindingChanged=false) != active (true) -> stopClusterComms + startClusterComms. pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_comms_wiring.go:187-201 shows that fabric transport is used only when control-interface or peer-address is empty. daemon_ha_sync.go:1286 starts the heartbeat only when both are set.

**Contract / expected behaviour:** #15687 (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:1167-1178) says the fab1 debt exists so "the next apply restarts comms and a late fab1 address upgrades to dual". That is one upgrade retry. Nothing says a working single-fabric epoch should be torn down every tick. docs/feature-gaps.md:707 lists "dual-fabric sync transport" as supported. Before #15687, an unaddressed fab1 meant a stable single-fabric epoch.

**Trace:** The config has fabric-interface + fabric1-interface and no control-interface. startClusterComms -> clusterSyncTransport = "fabric" -> fab0 address resolves -> fab1 poll exhausts -> markClusterCommsFab1Debt -> single-fabric SessionSync starts -> the 30 s reassert tick sees BindingChanged -> reconcileClusterTransportBinding -> stopClusterComms (SessionSync.Stop) -> startClusterComms -> new epoch clears the flag -> about 30 s fab1 poll (no SessionSync yet) -> re-mark -> repeat.

**Verification in source report:** EXECUTED — the daemon-package probe drives startClusterComms plus five reassertMgmtVRFOnce calls (one call = one 30 s tick) with the #15687 poll seam shortened; the lab duty cycle is not measured

**Confidence:** High for the restart loop and its scope (executed, with both twins); Medium on the production duty cycle (reasoned from 15 x 2 s fab1 poll and the 30 s tick, not measured on the lab)

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vf13/probes/zz_vf13_fab1_debt_test.go, `GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run TestVF13Fab1DebtChurn -count=1 -v` (output RUN/verify/vf13/f13-06.out): `CONTROL fabric-mode single fabric restarts/5 ticks=0 debt=false`; `fabric-mode dual, fab1 unaddressed restarts/5 ticks=5 debt=true`; `control-link dual, fab1 unaddressed restarts/5 ticks=0 debt=false`. f13's original probe (workers/f13/evidence/zz_r3f13_fab1_debt_churn_test.go) also reproduces 5/5. The limit is that the poll timing is shortened, so the exact production down-window is not observed.

## Impact

This hits operators running dual fabric with sync over the fabric when one fabric dies. Session sync is down for roughly the 30 s fab1 poll of every cycle. A failover inside that window loses sessions created since the last completed bulk, and there are WARN/INFO logs every tick. It recovers only when fab1 gets an address back or is removed from config.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Retry the fab1 upgrade without tearing down the working epoch: a background fab1 address watcher that restarts comms only once resolveClusterInterfaceAddr(fab1) is non-empty, or exclude the fab1 debt from the reassert gate and back it off. Acceptance: the probe's fabric-mode dual row shows 0 restarts over N ticks while fab1 stays unaddressed and exactly 1 once it becomes addressed. The existing #15687 late-address test still passes.

A fix should:
- address the mechanism above (not only the symptom), with a regression test that fails pre-fix (RED) and passes post-fix for the defect cell, plus the cited positive/control cell unchanged;
- re-verify cited file:line at current master (line numbers may have drifted since `d1ea69f9aa`);
- not regress the adjacent/residual issues cited in the dedup note.

## Summary

The send-site gates added by #15919 and #15937 kill 7 existing regression cells at setup (proven by a gate-disable control). Combined with the census exemptions, dropping the Flow or StaticNAT builder literal survives the whole pkg/dataplane/userspace suite.

**Severity:** Low (source report) — Low — assurance only, with no live-traffic defect. The consequence is potential: a regression of two known fail-open classes would merge with no new red. Those classes are #6986 (a deferred snapshot swallowed by content-hash dedup, so the helper keeps stale enforcement) and the 670274c712 dropped-section class (a dropped `Policies:` literal default-denied all transit). The package is already documented as red and CI does not require it [reporter: Medium].

**Finding ID:** `R3-F14-01`
